Oranga Tamariki-Ministry for Children is known as "Oranga Tamariki". It came into existence on 1 April 2017, and replaced what was known as "Child, Youth and Family" or CYF.
Its original name, from 1 April 2017 until 18 January 2018, was the "Ministry for Vulnerable Children, Oranga Tamariki".

chunks.title: osteopath
chunks.text:
## osteopath
An osteopath is a health practitioner who is registered with the Osteopathic Council of New Zealand. Osteopathy is based on the belief that the body is able to rectify itself against toxic conditions when it has favourable environmental circumstances and satisfactory nourishment.
A wide variety of treatment techniques are used, which could include manipulation and mobilisation to joints and soft tissues, muscle energy stretches, and cranial-sacral therapy.

chunks.title: other authorised agency
chunks.text:
## other authorised agency
Other authorised agencies include:
- iwi social services
- cultural social services
- child and family support services
These services must be approved under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki.
For the purposes of Unsupported Childs Benefit, however, other iwi or cultural involvement may be sufficient (a hui or cultural meeting, for example).

chunks.title: other benefit payments
chunks.text:
## other benefit payments
This includes:
- Emergency Benefit
- Jobseeker Support
- Sole Parent Support
- Supported Living Payment
- Youth Payment
- Young Parent Payment and
- Accommodation Supplement

chunks.title: other people
chunks.text:
## other people
People living at the property who are not:
- the tenant
- the tenants' partner
- dependent children or
- additional occupants
They can include friends, other children who are financially independent, relatives, boarders or flatmates.

chunks.title: Out-of-cycle payment
chunks.text:
## Out-of-cycle payment
An information share Child Support payment paid by Inland Revenue to a receiving carer on any day other than the second business day after the 19th of a month (i.e. not an in-cycle payment).
These payments generally relate to Child Support that a liable parent has not paid on time.
They may relate to any liability period in the past, other than the immediately preceding month (unless the due date for that month has passed).

chunks.title: output tax
chunks.text:
## output tax
A legal term usually called GST (Goods and Services Tax) payable or GST collected.

chunks.title: paediatrician
chunks.text:
## paediatrician
A paediatrician is a medical practitioner who is concerned with the physical, emotional and social health of children from birth to young adulthood (about 16 years old).

chunks.title: parent
chunks.text:
## parent
Funeral Grants for children
Parents or any person/s liable in law to maintain the deceased child on the date of death.

chunks.title: parental home
chunks.text:
## parental home
The parental home is the home where a student is living with a parent. They are not sharing accommodation with them.
There will be situations where even though a parent is living in the same home as the student, it is not the parental home.
There are a number of questions to consider when deciding if the home is the parental home.
Not all of the questions below will be applicable in every case. There may also be other matters that need to be considered in particular cases.
Some questions to consider
- Who owns the property? How long have they owned it? If the ownership changed recently, why?
- Who is on the tenancy agreement or mortgage agreement and why, and how long has this been the case?
- If both a parent and the student are on the tenancy or mortgage agreement, why is this?
- If they are both on the tenancy or mortgage agreement, do they have a shared responsibility? If not, why not?
- How many rooms ‘belong’ to the people living in the home? Why?
- Where are the shared spaces in the home and does their design and size reflect a shared approach to the use of the property between those living there?
- Are the furniture and chattels in the shared spaces owned by a parent?
- Do people outside the family understand that the property is the parental home, or a shared home or residence?
- Who is responsible for and manages or organises and pays for the maintenance, outgoings and any improvements? How long has this been the case?
The answer to these and any other relevant questions will provide a picture of the situation, and therefore assist to determine whether the home is the parental home.

chunks.title: part-time employment
chunks.text:
## part-time employment
Part-time employment is paid employment that averages not less than 20 hours per week, calculated over the preceding 3 month period.
## Exception
Part-time work is employment that averages not less than 15 hours per week, calculated over the preceding 3 month period, for the following purposes:
- appropriate hours of work for people with a limited capacity to work full-time because of a health condition, injury, or disability
- eligibility for temporary deferrals from work obligations because of a health condition, injury, or disability

chunks.title: Participation Allowance
chunks.text:
## Participation Allowance
Clients (or their partners) who are participating in an Activity in the Community are paid a Participation Allowance of up to $21.00 a week.
Participation Allowance is not paid for Voluntary Work.
A further amount of up to $20.00 a week can be paid for actual and reasonable costs over the $21.00.
Participation Allowance and Actual and Reasonable costs are not regarded as income.

chunks.title: partly subsidised
chunks.text:
## partly subsidised
Partly subsidised (also referred to as partially subsidised), in relation to a pharmaceutical product, means that the cost of the product is partly funded under the New Zealand Public Health and Disability Act 2000.
This means that for partly subsidised pharmaceutical items, people are required to pay the government prescription charge (often referred to as a co-payment), a part-charge, and an additional dispensing charge, referred to as a "mark-up", which the pharmacy adds on.
Some pharmacies charge a higher mark-up on partly subsidised pharmaceuticals than others do. This means that the final price for a partly subsidised pharmaceuticals may vary between pharmacies.
A part charge is the difference between the subsidised amount and the cost to manufacture the item.

chunks.title: passive income
chunks.text:
## passive income
Passive income means an amount paid to a person from:
- interest or
- dividends or
- a taxable Māori authority distribution other than a retirement scheme contribution or
- a replacement payment paid to a person under a share-lending arrangement
Note this is the same definition as resident passive income.

chunks.title: Patient Referral Scheme
chunks.text:
## Patient Referral Scheme
A Patient Referral Scheme (also known as a Medical Referral Scheme) is the agreement between a New Zealand District Health Board and Tokelau, Niue or the Cook Islands where clients from these countries can come to New Zealand to access the secondary and tertiary health services provided by the Ministry of Health.
Under the scheme the Island country government may meet the airfares of the client and, if appropriate, an attendant.
The health services can include (but not limited to):
- Dialysis
- Heart operations
- Organ donation
- Diabetes
- Maternity care

chunks.title: Pay in lieu of accumulated leave
chunks.text:
## Pay in lieu of accumulated leave
This is a payment that represents a leave entitlement an employee had accrued but not taken at the time their employment was terminated.
Employers are not legally required to pay out unused sick leave, family violence leave, long service leave, bereavement leave, or other leave entitlements specified in a person's employment agreement, but some choose to include it in their final pay.
Note family violence leave is also known as domestic violence leave.

chunks.title: Pay in lieu of notice
chunks.text:
## Pay in lieu of notice
When an employer terminates a person's employment, they must give the employee a period of notice unless they are being terminated due to misconduct. Notice periods are often 2 to 4 weeks.
Usually an employee works out their notice period, however an employer can choose to:
- not require the employee to work out any of their notice period or
- only require the employee to work out part of their notice period
In all cases, the employer must pay the employee as if they were continuing to work during the notice period. This known as pay in lieu of notice.

chunks.title: paying parent
chunks.text:
## paying parent
A person is a paying parent of a child if they are not a carer of that child and are any of the following:
- the natural mother of the child
- a person named on the birth certificate
- a person legally married to the natural mother of the child at the time of conception or birth
- a person named by a court declaration or a paternity order as the parent of the child
- the adoptive parent
- a legal step-parent (if declared by the Family Court)
- a person who has acknowledged they are the parent of a child in any court proceeding and the court did not find to the contrary
- a person who has been appointed as a guardian of the child by a court as they are the father of the child
Note the natural mother may be any gender but must have been pregnant with the child.

chunks.title: payments by a trustee
chunks.text:
## payments by a trustee
Payments by a trustee are by definition made to beneficiaries of a trust (not the settlor) and as such are generally taxable. A settlor cannot withdraw their earlier investment in a trust by way of a payment by the trustee as they no longer have ownership of that investment. Therefore, a payment by a trustee cannot be a payment of a capital amount.

chunks.title: Payments dependent on the completion of a fixed term contract
chunks.text:
## Payments dependent on the completion of a fixed term contract
When a person enters into a fixed-term contract or engagement, instead of receiving salary or wages, they may be paid at the end of the term of the contract or on completion or the work specified in the contract.
In some cases contractors are paid in instalments and the final instalment is paid on completion of the contract. This is often the case for people hired to complete a specific task eg tradespeople.

chunks.title: payments
chunks.text:
## payments
Any payments including board payments paid for a child in the direct care or sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki.

chunks.title: pecuniary damages
chunks.text:
## pecuniary damages
A portion of a compensation payment made by the Crown may include payment for:
- non-pecuniary losses and
- pecuniary losses
Non-pecuniary losses include payments for:
- loss of liberty
- loss of reputation
- mental harm and
- emotional harm
These payments or portions of payments are considered ex gratia or compensation payments, and must be exempt from the income and cash asset tests for 12 months from date of payment. Any income derived from the cash asset must not be treated as chargeable income for benefit purposes for 12 months from date of payment.
Pecuniary losses include payments for:
- loss of livelihood
- loss of property
- future earnings
- costs in obtaining an acquittal and
- costs in obtaining a pardon
These payments or portions of payments are not exempt from the income and cash assets test. Any income derived from the cash asset will be treated as chargeable income for benefit purposes.

chunks.title: people trafficking
chunks.text:
## people trafficking
People trafficking is a crime that involves the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring or receipt of a person, using coercion or deception, for the purpose of exploitation.
People trafficking may involve crossing a border (e.g. entering or leaving New Zealand) or may happen entirely within a country.
Common types of exploitation that people are trafficked for include:
- forced labour or labour exploitation
- sexual exploitation
- domestic servitude
- forced marriage
- debt bondage
- forced criminality

chunks.title: periodic dental care
chunks.text:
## periodic dental care
Periodic dental care is the check-up and cleaning of teeth done by a dentist. Generally these are undertaken on a regular basis.

chunks.title: periodically
chunks.text:
## periodically
This means regular or intermittent. This generally means more than once a year.

chunks.title: period of Maltese contributions
chunks.text:
## period of Maltese contributions
Period of Maltese contributions means a period of insurance in terms of the Social Security Act.

chunks.title: permanent resident visa
chunks.text:
## permanent resident visa
A permanent resident visa is a type of residence class visa.
A permanent resident visa allows the holder to leave and re-enter New Zealand without any visa restrictions.
People may qualify for a permanent resident visa if they meet specific requirements set by Immigration New Zealand and have had a resident visa in New Zealand for at least 2 years.

chunks.title: permanently and severely
chunks.text:
## permanently and severely
Permanent means the health condition, injury or disability your client has is expected to continue for at least 2 years. Your client's health condition, injury or disability is also considered permanent when they have been diagnosed with a terminal illness (where your client is not expected to live for more than 2 years).
Severely means that your client cannot regularly work 15 hours or more per week in open employment.

chunks.title: permanently restricted
chunks.text:
## permanently restricted
To be permanently restricted, MSD must be satisfied that:
- the restricting health condition, injury, or disability is expected to continue for at least the period set out in regulations made under this Act for the purposes of this section or
- the person is not expected to live for the period set out in the regulations, because the person's health condition is terminal

chunks.title: Personal resources
chunks.text:
## Personal resources
Resources can mean:
- a definite offer of employment (supported in writing)
- financial support from family members in New Zealand (supported in writing) or
- personal cash assets

chunks.title: pharmacist
chunks.text:
## pharmacist
A pharmacist is a health practitioner who is registered with the Pharmacy Council of New Zealand and holds a current Annual Practising Certificate.
Pharmacists are trained to advise people on how medicines and pharmaceutical products may contribute to their health and well-being.
They may also prepare, dispense, and monitor the safe use of prescription and non-prescription medicine therapies and therapeutic aids.

chunks.title: physiotherapist
chunks.text:
## physiotherapist
A physiotherapist is a health practitioner who is registered with the Physiotherapy Board of New Zealand and holds a current Annual Practising Certificate.
Physiotherapists are trained to treat people in restoring muscle function.
Physical therapists evaluate and treat those with musculoskeletal disorders, neurological dysfunctions and those with other types of health condition, injury or illness.
They co-ordinate treatment plans with health practitioners, doctors, nurses, social workers and occupational therapists.

chunks.title: Portfolio Investment Entity
chunks.text:
## Portfolio Investment Entity
A Portfolio Investment Entity (PIE) is a type of entity that invests the contributions from investors in different types of investments. PIEs came into existence on 1 October 2007.

chunks.title: practice notes
chunks.text:
## practice notes
Guidelines for the procedures that must be followed in any proceedings before the Student Allowance Appeal Authority.

chunks.title: pre-paid funeral trust fund or account
chunks.text:
## pre-paid funeral trust fund or account
A pre-paid funeral trust fund or account is money put aside (usually in a trust) exclusively for the payment of funeral expenses of that person.
If the money can be accessed and used by the client for other purposes, it is not considered exclusively for funeral expenses.

chunks.title: Primary Industry
chunks.text:
## Primary Industry
A Primary Industry includes, but is not limited to, the primary production of meat, wool, or dairy products, arable farming, aquaculture, sharemilking, an orchard, bee-keeping, herb or flower growing, a market garden, and poultry farming but does not include hobby farming.

chunks.title: principal caregiver
chunks.text:
## principal caregiver
The principal caregiver is the person who has the permanent primary responsibility for the day-to-day care of the child, other than on a temporary basis. It does not include proprietors or employees of any childcare home or institution.

chunks.title: principal temporary caregiver
chunks.text:
## principal temporary caregiver
For Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, the principal temporary caregiver is the person who has the primary responsibility for the day-to-day care of the child for a short-term, unknown, or uncertain period, and is not the natural or adoptive parent of the child.

chunks.title: Private arrangement of Child Support
chunks.text:
## Private arrangement of Child Support
Payments similar to Child Support where parents agree who pays and how much.
The paying parent pays directly to the carer and there is no involvement from Inland Revenue.
This may be money paid, goods and services provided, or in-kind assistance.

chunks.title: programme (students)
chunks.text:
## programme (students)
In terms of study, a programme means:
- for secondary school, a full time course
- for tertiary studies, the combination of courses, classes and work required to complete a degree, diploma, certificate or other qualification awarded by the provider. It does not mean a group of separate courses that are not part of the same qualification

chunks.title: protected person
chunks.text:
## protected person
A protected person under the Immigration Act 2009 means a person recognised as a protected person in New Zealand under the:
- Convention Against Torture or
- Covenant on Civil and Political Rights

chunks.title: psychiatrist
chunks.text:
## psychiatrist
A psychiatrist is a medical specialist who specialises in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of mental, addictive, and emotional disorders (for example, psychoses, depression, anxiety disorders, substance abuse disorders, developmental disabilities, sexual dysfunctions and adjustment reactions).
They understand the biological, psychological and social components of illness, and can prescribe medications, as well as evaluate and treat psychological and interpersonal problems.

chunks.title: psychologist
chunks.text:
## psychologist
A psychologist is a health practitioner who is registered under the Health Practitioners Competence Assurance Act 2003 and with the New Zealand Psychologists Board. Psychologists are concerned with the study of behaviour.
Psychologists must be listed on the New Zealand Psychologists Board's Register and hold a current practising certificate.
Psychology is a broad field of practice and research which applies psychological principles to:
- the assessment, prevention, improvement, and rehabilitation of psychological distress, disability, dysfunctional behaviours, and health-risk behaviours and
- the enhancement of psychological and physical well-being
Not all practitioners with the title psychologist have the same skillset or scope of practice. The New Zealand Psychologists Board has identified what scopes of practice can be practised by psychologists in New Zealand.
Each scope of practice has a unique focus and requires specific qualifications and experience.
The scopes of practice identified are:
- Psychologists
- Clinical Psychologists
- Counselling Psychologist
- Educational Psychologist
- Neuropsychology
- Trainee or intern psychologists (these are psychologist who have not yet completed their full training and are working under supervision)
Note although some psychologists will provide counselling, counsellors are not the same as psychologists and most counsellors will not be registered with the New Zealand Psychologists Board.

chunks.title: PYECI
chunks.text:
## PYECI
SWIFTT Payee/Client Inquiry
Use this screen to see all payees linked to a client.

chunks.title: qualifying benefit
chunks.text:
## qualifying benefit
Clients and their partners qualify for Winter Energy Payments if they are getting one of the following qualifying benefits:
- Emergency Benefit
- Emergency Maintenance Allowance
- Jobseeker Support
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Sole Parent Support
- Supported Living Payment (caring for a person)
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury and disability)
- Veteran's Pension
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
Note client's not getting a qualifying benefit are not eligible for a Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: rateable valuation
chunks.text:
## rateable valuation
This is the house and land value that is used to set your rates. The rateable valuation is provided on the rates statement issued by the local city or district council. Depending on which local city/district council you belong too will depend on how the rateable valuation is assessed. This could be as follows:
- Capital Value The estimated value that would have been paid for the property if it had been sold at the date of the last general revaluation
- Land value The estimated value that would have been paid for the land if it had been sold at the date of the last general revaluation
- Mixed value The estimated amount of the capital and land values combined
- Annual value This value only applies to the Auckland City Council where valuer's assess what a rating unit would be if a property is rented for over a 12 month period
Rateable valuation previously known as the GV or Government valuation.

chunks.title: Receiving carer
chunks.text:
## Receiving carer
A caregiver who is owed Child Support, payable through Inland Revenue, in respect of a child. They may or may not be a parent of the child.
A person can be a receiving carer, without meeting the definition of a carer.

chunks.title: Reciprocal Agreements
chunks.text:
## Reciprocal Agreements
An agreement on social security between New Zealand and another country.
Reciprocal Agreements allow some New Zealand benefits and pensions to be paid overseas and/or earlier access to benefits and pensions in New Zealand and the agreement.

chunks.title: recognised relationship
chunks.text:
## recognised relationship
For Student Allowance, a partner or spouse is someone who the student is in a recognised relationship with.
A recognised relationship is when either:
- the student and their partner are both 24 and over or
- one or both of them are under 24, and they have a dependent child or
- they are legally married or in a de facto relationship, if they have consent from the family court

chunks.title: recognised student hostel
chunks.text:
## recognised student hostel
A recognised student hostel in one that is registered and approved with StudyLink for Student Allowance purposes.

chunks.title: referee's declaration
chunks.text:
## referee's declaration
At the time of application, clients are required to supply the details of two referees who can confirm the client's residence in New Zealand. Any information supplied, in writing, by the referee is called the referee's declaration.

chunks.title: refugee
chunks.text:
## refugee
A refugee means a person recognised under the Immigration Act 2009 as:
- a refugee outside New Zealand and
- brought to New Zealand under a government programme on the basis of that recognition
or
- a refugee in New Zealand within the meaning of the Refugee Convention, and cannot be deported except for circumstances set out in the Immigration Act 2009

chunks.title: refund period
chunks.text:
## refund period
If the tenant meets the criteria, you can consider backdating to any earlier date.
The refund period is from:
- the start date of the tenancy, but cannot be any earlier or
- the date that full and correct information was subsequently provided or
- the rent charge date following the date the change in circumstance occurred
The refund period is to the rent effective date that the correct rate of Income Related Rent was applied.

chunks.title: registered charities and charitable trusts
chunks.text:
## registered charities and charitable trusts
A registered charity means a society, institution, and trustees of a trust, registered as a charitable entity under the Charities Act 2005. A charitable trust means any trustees or a society that has been incorporated as a board under the Charitable Trusts Act 1957.
These groups must exist for a charitable purpose that is beneficial to the community such as supporting disabled people, emergency and disaster relief, and sports and recreation. Examples of registered charities and charitable trusts include:
- Barnardos New Zealand
- Scouts Association New Zealand
- The Stroke Foundation of New Zealand
- Volunteer Fire Brigades

chunks.title: relevant tax year
chunks.text:
## relevant tax year
The relevant tax year is the tax year that is most current to when the student:
- starts study or
- makes an application for and is approved a Student Allowance
whichever is the later.
## Example 1
If a student starts study in and is approved Student Allowance for February 2018, the parental income that would need to be assessed should be for the tax year 1 April 2017 to 31 March 2018, as this is the "relevant tax year" for that study.
## Example 2
If a student starts study in and is approved Student Allowance for July 2018, the parental income that would need to be assessed should be for the tax year 1 April 2018 to 31 March 2019, as this is the "relevant tax year" for that study.

chunks.title: remediation work
chunks.text:
## remediation work
Remediation work means the repair or refurbishment of:
- any building in which the home is located (eg apartment within an apartment building)
- the land on which the land is located
- any infrastructure required to provide essential services to the home
It also includes the demolition and rebuilding of any building comprising the home or in which the home is located.

chunks.title: rent charge date
chunks.text:
## rent charge date
This is the date the housing provider charges the rent. It does not change; it is a regular day of every week or fortnight.
Note that the rent effective date of an increase in rent is aligned with the charge date.

chunks.title: rent effective date
chunks.text:
## rent effective date
The rent effective date is the one-off date on which an increased rate of Income Related Rent is charged.
The rent effective date is aligned with the next charge date.

chunks.title: rent period
chunks.text:
## rent period
Rent periods are either weekly or fortnightly (as agreed to in the Tenancy Agreement).

chunks.title: Rental housing (Housing Support Programme)
chunks.text:
## Rental housing (Housing Support Programme)
Rental housing for Housing Support Products is housing that is, was or will be occupied by a tenant with a tenancy agreement under the Residential Tenancies Act 1986.
This includes private rentals, boarding house tenancies and social housing.

chunks.title: Republic of Ireland
chunks.text:
## Republic of Ireland
The 'Republic of Ireland' means that territory governed by the Government of Ireland.

chunks.title: Reserve Bank six-month term deposit rate
chunks.text:
## Reserve Bank six-month term deposit rate
Once a month, the Reserve Bank publishes the Retail interest rates on lending and deposits (B3).
Six-month term deposit rate
This rate is the average of the advertised interest rates paid for a new 6-month term deposit of $10,000.

chunks.title: residence class visa
chunks.text:
## residence class visa
A residence class visa means a:
- resident visa or
- permanent resident visa
A residence class visa allows people to live in New Zealand indefinitely. The visa also lets people work and study in New Zealand. There are different travel conditions based on the type of residence class visa.
Residence class visas are granted by Immigration New Zealand.
For the purpose of deciding if a person meets the residence criteria for financial assistance from MSD, people who were granted a residence permit under the Immigration Act 1987 and some British citizens who arrived in New Zealand before 1 January 1962 are deemed to hold a residence class visa.

chunks.title: Resident passive income
chunks.text:
## Resident passive income
Passive income means an amount paid to a person from:
- interest or
- dividends or
- a taxable Māori authority distribution other than a retirement scheme contribution or
- a replacement payment paid to a person under a share-lending arrangement
Note this is the same definition as passive income.

chunks.title: resident visa
chunks.text:
## resident visa
A resident visa is a type of residence class visa.
Resident visas have travel conditions that state how many times a person can travel in and out of New Zealand over a stated period of time.
There are different types of resident visas with different conditions based on a person's circumstances.

chunks.title: residential disability care
chunks.text:
## residential disability care
Residential disability care is the level of care provided for the care and attention of children, young people and adults whose needs cannot be met in their own home with home-based services, generally because of their disability/impairment related needs.

chunks.title: rest home care
chunks.text:
## rest home care
Rest home care is the level of care provided for the care and attention of people whose needs cannot be met in their own home with home-based services, generally because of their age-related needs.
This may be rest home care, continuing care (commonly called hospital-level care), dementia care, or specialised hospital care (commonly called psychogeriatric care).

chunks.title: Rest of New Zealand
chunks.text:
## Rest of New Zealand
For the purposes of calculating Special Transfer Allowance, any location that is not contained in Area 1 or Area 2, is considered to be in the Rest of New Zealand.
These areas are different from the areas used for Accommodation Supplement.

chunks.title: retirement savings scheme contribution tax
chunks.text:
## retirement savings scheme contribution tax
Retirement savings scheme contribution tax is a tax payable on contributions to a retirement savings scheme.
A person can choose not to pay this tax and make a final withholding tax payment when the contributions are distributed.
If a person makes a final withholding tax payment, the amount of income distributed from the retirement scheme is not considered parental income for Student Allowances purposes.

chunks.title: retirement savings scheme
chunks.text:
## retirement savings scheme
Retirement savings schemes are Inland Revenue approved schemes that restrict withdrawals before a person reaches an age of retirement.
Contact Inland Revenue for more information.

chunks.title: RoS - Results of Study
chunks.text:
## RoS - Results of Study
Results of Study
This data match enables MSD to get a student's study results from the Ministry of Education.
The Ministry of Education gets the information from education providers.
The RoS match is used to assess both Student Loan and Student Allowance entitlement.
It confirms details of relevant study a student has completed.
The specific information differs depending on what the information is being received for, but generally includes:
- the title and programme code of study
- the start and end date of study
- the institution ID for the study
- the EFTS value of the study
- whether the EFTS were passed, failed or the result is still pending
Note if a student thinks the results of their study information MSD gets is incorrect, they will need to resolve this with their education provider(s), not the Ministry of Education.
## Legal authority
RoS is an authorised information matching programme under the Privacy Act 2020.
It is authorised by Clause 7 of Schedule 9 of the Education and Training Act 2020, and must comply with the requirements set out in Subpart 4 of Part 7, and Schedule 6 of the Privacy Act 2020.

chunks.title: SADTA
chunks.text:
## SADTA
Accommodation Supplement/Tenure Protection Allowance data add/change screen.
Use this screen to add, change, delete or inquire on details relating to the assessment of Accommodation Supplement or Tenure Protection Allowance for a client or their partner.
The weekly accommodation costs are maintained by this screen.

chunks.text:
## SADVI
Advance history inquiry.
Use this screen to:
- see recommended, approved and declined advances
- select an advance to be approved or declined through SSNAA (Special Needs Grant/advance/lump sum approve/decline) screen
- select an advance to be changed (only if you are the recommending officer) through SSNAR (Special Needs Grant/advance recommend) screen

chunks.title: SAHPI
chunks.text:
## SAHPI
Swiftt Adhoc Payment Inquiry screen.
Use this screen to view or select an adhoc payment.

chunks.title: SAL
chunks.text:
## SAL
Student Allowances and Loans system.
SAL is the computer system that is used for the assessment and payment of Student Allowances and Student Loans.
It does not link directly to other MSD systems.
SAL has a direct link to online services such as ODS (Online Decision Support) and MyStudyLink. Information provided by students online can be automatically downloaded into SAL and the student's entitlement reassessed without any manual intervention.

chunks.title: sanction
chunks.text:
## sanction
A sanction is a penalty imposed on a client's benefit for failure to fulfil their obligations.

chunks.title: SASA

Accommodation Supplement register/grant/decline screen.
Use this screen to register, grant or decline an application for Accommodation Supplement.

Use this screen to change details on a current Accommodation Supplement.

chunks.title: SATRI

## SATRI

Use this screen to select a payment needing authorisation.

chunks.text:
## Designated health practitioner referral screen
This screen will:
- record designated health practitioner referrals
- automatically extend medical coverage to ensure entitlement while waiting the outcome of the designated health practitioner referral
- record the outcome of designated health practitioners appointment

chunks.title: SBFTZ
chunks.text:
## SBFTZ
SWIFTT Benefit/Pension Cancel screen.
Use this screen to:
- Cancel a parent benefit or pension
- Exclude a partner included in the benefit or a non-qualified partner included in the pension

chunks.title: SBSR
chunks.text:
## SBSR
SWIFTT Benefit/pension Suspend/Resume screen.
Use this screen to suspend or resume a benefit to a client and/or their partner, or to suspend or resume a pension for a pensioner and/or their non-qualified partner included in the pension.

chunks.title: SBSRC
chunks.text:
## SBSRC
SWIFTT Benefit/pension Suspend Change screen
Use this screen to change the reason code for a current suspension and the comment field for a current suspension.

chunks.title: SBZC
chunks.text:
## SBZC
SWIFFT Benefit/pension Cancellation Change screen.
Use this screen to change the effective date of cancellation, change the reason for cancellation or to cancel the terminal benefit.

chunks.title: SCHIE
chunks.text:
## SCHIE
SWIFTT Child Inclusion/Exclusion screen.
Use this screen to include/exclude a child in the client's parent benefit or pension.

chunks.title: schizophrenia
chunks.text:
## schizophrenia
Disorders that involve disturbances in the form and content of thought (e.g. delusions, hallucinations), in mood, behaviour and sense of relationship between self and the external world.
There are different types of schizophrenia including paranoid, reactive and undifferentiated. The symptoms differ between types. (A common misconception is that schizophrenia involves multiple personalities - this is a different condition - Multiple Personality Disorder.)

chunks.title: SDAWA
chunks.text:
## SDAWA
SWIFTT Disability Allowance Weekly costs
Use this screen to add, delete or inquire into the Disability Allowance weekly costs for a client, partner or child.

chunks.title: SDBTC
chunks.text:
## SDBTC
SWIFTT Debt Change screen
Use this screen to change the status, amount and/or period of any manually established debt.

chunks.title: SDOCS
chunks.text:
## SDOCS
SWIFTT Doctor Search Screen
Use this screen to search and link to your client's health practitioner (doctor).

chunks.title: SDPAA
chunks.text:
## SDPAA
SWIFTT Debtor Paying Arrangements Add/change
At benefit cancellation, paying arrangement details loaded onto this screen will transfer to debtor's DMS record.

chunks.title: Seasonal worker
chunks.text:
## Seasonal worker
Seasonal worker means a person employed on a seasonal basis in the horticultural or viticultural industries.

chunks.title: secondary health service
chunks.text:
## secondary health service
Whenever a medical practitioner refers a patient on for further assessment or treatment at a hospital (inpatients or outpatients), they are accessing secondary health services. This treatment may not always be located in a hospital, e.g. it may be a private medical laboratory.

chunks.title: secondary school
chunks.text:
## secondary school
A secondary school for the purposes of Student Allowance eligibility means:
- a secondary school established under Part 3 or registered under section 200 of the Education and Training Act 2020 or
- a school that provides secondary instruction and is designated as a distance school under section 196 of the Education and Training Act 2020 or
- a specialist school established under section 197, or a specialised institution listed in Schedule 2 of the Education and Training Act 2020

chunks.title: self-contained residence
chunks.text:
## self-contained residence
A self-contained residence (whether attached or detached) is an additional residence on a property, which allows the occupant to live separately and without the need for access to the main residence on the property.
To determine if a student is living in a self-contained residence, MSD needs to consider the particular circumstances of the student’s living situation and how separate they are from their parent(s)’ main residence.
A self-contained residence will generally have:
- separate access from the main residence and therefore allow the occupant to enter and exit the self-contained residence separately
- its own kitchen with cooking facilities, shower/bathroom and laundry facilities
- a separate meter for power/gas. If it is not separately metered, the occupant will need to be paying a contribution towards their power/gas use
A basic caravan or sleep-out that does not have these facilities or features is not a self-contained residence.

chunks.title: SELXT
chunks.text:
## SELXT
Sell Exchange Rates Table screen
You can use this screen to convert foreign currency into an estimate of New Zealand dollars.

chunks.text:
