However, because James contacted MSD after his Mandatory Review date, he will need to respond to the Mandatory Review to confirm his circumstances before MSD can resume the Accommodation Supplement.
On 8 September 2027 James responds to his Mandatory Review and confirms there is no change in circumstances. MSD resumes James' Accommodation Supplement at the same rate from 6 September 2027.
MSD completes the Mandatory Review on 8 September 2027 and sets the next review date 52-weeks from the date the Mandatory Review was completed.
James' next Mandatory Review date is 6 September 2028.

chunks.title: Action on return to New Zealand — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Action on return to New Zealand
MSD must look at the circumstances of the client's absence from and subsequent return to New Zealand to decide when to recommence their Accommodation Supplement and when to treat it as a new application.
Consider the following:
- the client's intention at the time of their departure, for example, did they cancel their Accommodation Supplement before leaving New Zealand because they did not intend to return?
- did the client remain ordinarily resident during the period of absence?
- the length of time that they have been absent
- the reason for the absence
- if their circumstances changed significantly during their absence
## Payment can recommence
If a client returns to New Zealand on or before the 29th day (where continued payment of benefit was allowed) Accommodation Supplement can recommence without any break in payment, as long as their accommodation costs have continued.
Generally, for other short periods of absence (where continued payment was not approved) Accommodation Supplement payments can recommence from:
- the date the client returned to New Zealand as long as they contact MSD within 14 days of their return or
- the date they contacted MSD to advise they have returned if more than 14 days after date of return
## New application
In all other circumstances the client may need to reapply using a new application after reviewing the circumstances above.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Accommodation Supplement it is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising Work and Income of a change in circumstances within 14 days you may reduce, suspend or cancel Accommodation Supplement from the first available date.
## False or misleading information
If the client gives false or misleading information you must review Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Accommodation Supplement it is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
Note income for non-beneficiaries must be charged against the Accommodation Supplement for the week(s) in which the income is earned or represents.
For more information see:
- Change in income
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event and does not have a good and sufficient reason, you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information you must review Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Accommodation Supplement it is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. A reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event MSD should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising MSD of a change in circumstances within 14 days MSD may reduce, suspend or cancel Accommodation Supplement from the first available date.
## False or misleading information
If the client gives false or misleading information MSD must review Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Avoiding a debt — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Avoiding a debt
When a non-beneficiary client dies, Accommodation Supplement generally stops from the day after the date of death. You must take all possible steps to stop payments from this date.
When payment cannot be stopped from the day after the date of death there is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days after the date of death. You can use this discretion to stop payment from the first available date, that is, the earliest date that you can stop payments from so that no overpayment is established.
If the period between the date of death and the first available date to cancel payment from (to avoid creating a debt) is more than 28 days, you will have to establish an overpayment from the 29th day after death.
However, when there has been a deliberate intent to delay advising Work and Income of the client's death you should stop payment from the day after the date of death and establish an overpayment.
Note under no circumstances can payment continue for more than 28 days after the date of death.
For more information see:
- Terminal benefit

chunks.title: Calculating the period of absence — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Calculating the period of absence
The period of an absence from New Zealand for which payment of Accommodation Supplement can continue (if approved or when approval is not needed) is up to 28 consecutive days, that is, Saturdays and Sundays are included.
In all cases, when assessing the period of absence do not include:
- the date of departure from New Zealand and
- the date of return to New Zealand
If a client is absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period the Accommodation Supplement should be suspended from the 29th day (unless they are receiving a main benefit and meet the criteria to pay for longer than 28 days).
Note if a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, the Accommodation Supplement must be cancelled from the day after departure.
## Calculating 52 week period
When a client who is receiving a main benefit is paid an Accommodation Supplement while they are absent from New Zealand, a client can receive a payment for up to 28 days in total in a 52 week period. The 52 week period is counted in the following way:
- identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand
- count back 52 weeks from this date
- identify any periods of paid absence they have used (counting from the day after they have left New Zealand to the day before they returned to New Zealand)
- subtract the number of days absent from New Zealand from 28 days. The remainder is the client's entitlement to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand
- pay the client the days they have available up to the period of absence. This may not be the whole of the time they intend to be absent from New Zealand depending on how many days of their entitlement they have left.
For more information see:
- Return to New Zealand
- Permanent absence

chunks.title: Change in accommodation — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Change in accommodation
You will need to review Accommodation Supplement to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the clients:
- accommodation costs
- part of the property they live in
- type of accommodation rent, board or home ownership or
- residential area (region)
Note if a client is a social housing tenant they are no longer able to receive an Accommodation Supplement.
The date to review Accommodation Supplement from will depend on the action involved. Generally, you should:
## Increase
- increase Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances
## Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Accommodation Supplement from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event

chunks.title: Change in accommodation income — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Change in accommodation income
Clients must tell MSD when they start getting accommodation income or there is a change in accommodation income they get from renters or boarders so the correct rate of Accommodation Supplement can be paid.
When there is a change in accommodation income that a client gets, review their Accommodation Supplement to make sure they still meet the qualifications and are getting the correct rate of payment. The date to review Accommodation Supplement from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:
Increase
- increase Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances
Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Accommodation Supplement from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information MSD must review Accommodation Supplement from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Mismatch of information
When the renter or boarder also gets Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, MSD will check the details match what information is held. Where there is a mismatch of information, the mismatch process must be followed.
For more information see:
- Mismatch of accommodation income and accommodation costs
- Weekly qualifying accommodation costs
- Change in income
- Rent and board payments

chunks.title: Change in assets — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Change in assets
You will need to review Accommodation Supplement to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's cash assets.
The date to review Accommodation Supplement from will depend on the action involved. Generally, you should:

chunks.title: Change in family circumstances — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Change in family circumstances
MSD should review Accommodation Supplement to check that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the clients:
- relationship status or
- the number of dependent children in the client's care
The date to review Accommodation Supplement from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:
## Care and protection concerns
When a child has come into a client's care, MSD should consider if there are any care and protection concerns.
If MSD believes any child has been, or is likely to be harmed (physically, emotionally or sexually), ill-treated, abused, neglected, deprived or MSD has concerns about the wellbeing of the child, the case must be referred to Oranga Tamariki.
MSD staff must notify Oranga Tamariki if they are aware that the child’s sole caregiver has been remanded in custody and/or sentenced to a term of imprisonment.
## Child turns 18
When a dependent child turns 18, they can no longer be included in their parent or caregiver's payments, unless they are continuing in education and are not financially independent.

chunks.title: Change in income — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When there is a change in a client’s income, review their Accommodation Supplement to make sure they still meet the qualifications and are getting the correct rate of payment.
Income for non-beneficiaries must be charged against the Accommodation Supplement in the week(s) the income is earned or represents.
## Information share Child Support payments
Information share Child Support payments are treated differently as they are automatically charged forward as income for a period of 4 or 5 weeks.
For more information see:
## Variable income
When a client has variable income, (for example wages for a client who works different hours each week) the income is charged for the week the income was earned.
If the client is unsure of the exact amount of income they will earn, they need to provide an estimate of their income. This will help to reduce the risk of a debt being established for the client.
If a client's actual income differs from the estimate given, they must tell MSD the correct amount and their rate of benefit needs to be reviewed.
The correct amount of income must still be charged for the week the income was earned.
Note the automated income charging rules still apply to information share Child Support payments, even if their Child Support income varies.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Accommodation Supplement or the rate payable.
MSD may also review Accommodation Supplement at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment (if applicable).
## Mandatory Review for Accommodation Supplement
MSD must review a client's Accommodation Supplement within 52 weeks of when this assistance commenced, or within 52 weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed.
Clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend.
Generally, all clients getting Accommodation Supplement will have a Mandatory Review for this assistance (except clients also getting Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment).

chunks.title: Child leaves sole parents care suddenly — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When a child stops being a dependent child of a sole parent because of a sudden change of circumstances beyond the control of the client, payment of Accommodation Supplement for the child leaving care may continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child stopped being dependent. This is to allow a period of transition for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances. For example when a child suddenly goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki, payment of Accommodation Supplement may continue to be assessed using a sole parent threshold for 28 days from the date the child is no longer dependent on the client. During the 28 days continuation of payment, if the client has other changes of circumstances such as a change in accommodation costs, the rate of Accommodation Supplement will need to be reassessed accordingly using the sole parent threshold.

chunks.title: Mandatory Reviews — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: Generally, clients getting Accommodation Supplement must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date or their payments will suspend. If a child leaves a sole parent's care suddenly and the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement after the 28-day continuation period, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client is unable to respond to the review (even if they had more time) based on their individual circumstances, they may qualify for an exemption. Generally, when the Mandatory Review is only for Accommodation Supplement the benefit will stop at the end of the continuation period e.g. if they are over the income limit, and the review is due, an exemption will apply. The client must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: Generally, clients getting Accommodation Supplement must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will no longer be considered a dependent child and will be excluded from their payments. If Accommodation Supplement is continuing at the existing rate for 28 days because a child has left a sole parent's care suddenly, and that child turns 18 during that period, the client is not required to respond to the notice and the child will not be excluded during the continuation of payment period. However, if Accommodation Supplement is continuing at the existing rate for 28 days because a child has left a sole parent's care suddenly, and a different child in their care turns 18, the client must respond to the notice, or the 18-year-old will be excluded from their payments.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in the assessment of their parent or caregiver's Accommodation Supplement.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Accommodation Supplement from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in the assessment of their parent or caregiver's Accommodation Supplement for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier
## Getting a main benefit
If a parent or caregiver is getting a main benefit , and their main benefit is suspended due to their child turning 18, their Accommodation Supplement will also suspend.
Note main benefits do not include Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Surviving partner or dependent child — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Surviving partner or dependent child
When a client dies (and there is a surviving partner or dependent child) before a decision is made on an application or review for Accommodation Supplement, you can continue the application or review process as if the client had not died.

chunks.title: Client does not return — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Client does not return
If a client's benefit is suspended because they are absent from New Zealand and they do not return their benefit record will automatically cancel in SWIFTT 8 weeks after the date of suspension.
Note if the client had been approved continued payment of benefit for the first 28 days of the absence, this is not established as a debt.
For more information see:
- Payment
- Return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Clients receiving a main benefit — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving a main benefit
Accommodation Supplement can continue to be paid to the client for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital.
When the client's benefit is reduced to the hospital rate, their Accommodation Supplement will need to be stopped.
## Single clients and sole parents
Accommodation Supplement must be stopped from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation.
You will need to check if the client still has to meet their continuing accommodation costs.
If so, increase the hospital rate to meet the accommodation costs.
## Married, civil union or de facto couples (without dependent children)
For a married, civil union or de facto client (without dependent children) you still treat the couple as married, in a civil union or de facto relationship and take into account the income and assets of both.
You can pay the full Accommodation Supplement to the partner not in hospital.
For more information see 'Hospitalisation' in the relevant Main Benefit

chunks.title: Court attachment orders — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Court attachment orders
All court attachment requests are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing. Court attachments are administered via the CORBI screen in SWIFTT.
The Ministry of Justice has the authority to make attachment orders on benefits to meet outstanding court fines.
The attachment order may include:
- court finesthese are fines payable to the District Court
- civil attachmentsthese are generally paid to a private individual or organisation that is owed money. Occasionally the District Court will act as a collection agent for civil debts.
Attachment Orders issued by the Ministry of Justice can be made under either the Insolvency Act 2006 or the District Court Act 2016.
## Protected earnings rate
No attachment order can, whether on its own or when combined with other attachment orders, Child Support deduction, or Ministry of Social Development debt repayment, take a client's total income below the protected earnings rate. For more information see:
- Protected earnings rate
## Priority for deductions
Court attachment orders do not take priority over:
- Child Support deductions
- Ministry of Social Development deductions
- Inland Revenue deductions or
- any attachment order made under the Family Proceedings Act
For more information see:
- Priority for deductions
## Information provided by the Court
The information that will be received from the Court, Ministry of Justice will have:
- the client's name
- the amount to be deducted from the benefit
- the fine's reference number
If a client is suffering undue hardship because of the amount of the attachment order then they should be directed to a Registrar of the District Court for a reassessment of the rate.
For more information see:
- Court request for information
## Transferring or cancelling and re-granting benefits
When transferring or cancelling and re-granting benefits when there are court attachments on the record please email the Central Processing Unit. Include the clients name and client number, and a request to review and reload court attachments as necessary.

chunks.title: Court request for information — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Court request for information
The Ministry of Justice can request the following information when they are considering either making an attachment order or assessing the client's protected earnings rate under section 87AA of the Summary Proceedings Act 1957:
- the amount of any benefit paid to the client
- the amount of any attachment orders or deduction notices issued under the following Acts: Social Security Act 2018Family Proceedings Act 1980Child Support Act 1991Tax Administration Act 1994
- Social Security Act 2018
- Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Child Support Act 1991
- Tax Administration Act 1994
- any Ministry of Social Development debt that is being recovered from the client
- the composition of the client's family, including the number of family members who are dependent on the client, as known by Work and Income
This information is used to determine how much the client can reasonably be expected to pay each week on any outstanding fines.
For more information see:
- Protected earnings rate
## Information that can be provided
Work and Income can provide the Courts, Ministry of Justice with the last known address and telephone number of a client under Schedule 6, clause 13 of the Social Security Act 2018.
This only applies when the Courts, Ministry of Justice is unable to locate a client who is in default of a court fine.
## Information that cannot be provided
The following information cannot be provided to the Courts, Ministry of Justice:
- the client's benefit number
- the benefit type and
- employer details

chunks.title: Getting a main benefit — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Getting a main benefit
When a client who is getting a main benefit dies, their Accommodation Supplement stops from the same date as the main benefit.
## Non-beneficiaries
For non-beneficiary clients, Accommodation Supplement generally stops from the day following the date of death. However, there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days after the date of death:
- to avoid creating a debt or
- as terminal benefit when there are other circumstances that justify payment
## Cost of funeral
The person responsible for the cost of the funeral may be able to get a Funeral Grant.
## Mandatory Reviews
There are no Mandatory Reviews of Accommodation Supplement when the client has died.
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Accommodation Supplement when the child turns 18 during the terminal benefit period.

chunks.title: Death of a dependent child — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Death of a dependent child
When a dependent child dies, Accommodation Supplement needs to be reviewed to check that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
There is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the date of death. To help decide whether to continue payment see:
- Terminal benefit
## Mandatory Reviews
Clients must still respond to a Mandatory Review for Accommodation Supplement during the 28-day continuation of payment. They may be able to get an extension or an exemption.
## Child turns 18
Generally, clients getting Accommodation Supplement must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will no longer be considered a dependent child and will be excluded from their payments.
If Accommodation Supplement is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because the client's child has died, and the child that died was due to turn 18 during that period, the client is not required to respond to the notice and the child will not be excluded during the continuation of payment period.
However, if Accommodation Supplement is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because the client's child has died and a different child in their care turns 18, the client must respond to the notice, or the 18-year-old will be excluded from their payments.

chunks.title: Death of a married, civil union or de facto client — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Death of a married, civil union or de facto client
When a married, civil union or de facto client dies you will need to review the surviving partner's Accommodation Supplement to ensure they still meet the qualifications and are receiving the correct rate of payment.
The Accommodation Supplement should be reviewed from the day following death.

chunks.title: Debt recovery maximum — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Debt recovery maximum
The recommended maximum recovery rate for clients currently receiving income support is set at no more than $40.00 a week, unless the client volunteers to pay more.
Debt types included in this maximum recovery rate are:
- Special Needs Grant
- Advance Payment of Benefit and
- overpayments of benefit
For more information see:
- Debt types not included

chunks.title: Debt Repayment Orders — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Debt Repayment Orders
All Debt Repayment Orders are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
Debt Repayment Orders are issued by the Ministry of Justice under the Insolvency Act 2006. These can be issued when the client is an undischarged bankrupt.
Unlike other Ministry of Justice attachment orders, Debt Repayment Orders do not have a protected earnings rate. Payment is generally made to the supervisor of the debt but occasionally the District Court will act as an agent for collection of the debt.
Payment continues for 3 years or until further notice is received from either the supervisor or the District Court.
Unlike other Ministry of Justice attachment orders, Debt Repayment Orders are administered via PYECI, not CORBI.

chunks.title: Debt types not included — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Debt types not included
Debt types not included in the maximum recovery rate of debt of $40.00 a week are:
- Child Disability Allowance debt
- Family Benefit Capitalisation debt
- Fraudulent Student Loans
- Liable Parent Contributions (LPC)
- Maintenance debt
- Major Repairs Advances (MRA)
- Residential Support Services debt
- Student Allowance debt
- Suspensory Loans
- Work Services debt

chunks.title: Deductions — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Deductions
In certain circumstances Work and Income can be required to pay part of the client's benefit to another party.
Work and Income is legally required to make such deductions when served with a properly issued Deduction Notice or Attachment Order. In these cases, the consent of the client is not required.
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others. For more information see:
- Priority for deductions
Deductions include the following:
- Court attachment orders
- Debt Repayment Orders
- Ministry of Social Development debt repayments
- Student Loans
- Inland Revenue deduction notices
Note the Central Processing Unit deals with Child Support, Debt Repayment Orders, Court attachment orders, and Inland Revenue deduction notices.

chunks.title: Examples of Mandatory Review outcomes — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: MSD must review a client's Accommodation Supplement within 52 weeks of the commencement date of Accommodation supplement, or 52 weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed. The Mandatory Review is completed when MSD has determined the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement and confirms the rate payable (if applicable). When a client responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined if the client qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g. client has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: Outcomes of a Mandatory Review Examples Client declares no change (exception doesn't apply) Rita is single with no dependent children. Rita is getting Accommodation Supplement and pays rent of $300.00 per week in Area 1. Rita's Mandatory Review is due on 11 November 2027. Rita responds to their Mandatory Review on 5 November 2027 to confirm they have had no change in circumstances. Because Rita has declared no change in circumstance, and an exception doesn't apply, MSD must continue the payment at the same rate. MSD completes Rita's Mandatory Review on 5 November 2027 and sets the next review date 52 weeks from the date the Mandatory Review was completed. Rita's next Mandatory Review date is 3 November 2028. Client declares no change (exception applies) Rachel is single with no dependent children. Rachel is getting Accommodation Supplement and pays rent of $350.00 per week in Area 1. Her Mandatory Review is due on 9 June 2027, and she responds on 7 June 2027 to confirm she has had no change in her circumstances. Because Rachel has been getting Accommodation Supplement and declared no change in her accommodation costs for three consecutive years, MSD must consider whether further information is required before completing the Mandatory Review. MSD considers Rachel's circumstances and sees that she hasn't provided verification of her accommodation costs since moving to her current apartment in 2024. Given Rachel lives in an area where rental accommodation is very limited and rents have increased significantly, MSD determines that it is reasonable to request verification of her accommodation costs to confirm that the information is correct before making a decision about her entitlement. Rachel is asked to provide this information before 7 July 2027 (her new deadline for the review) or her Accommodation Supplement will stop. Rachel contacts MSD on 1 July 2027 with the evidence requested. MSD determines that Rachel's circumstances have changed as her rent increased in January 2027. MSD adjusts the rate of payment for Accommodation Supplement and exercises discretion to backdate the payment to the date of the increase in costs. MSD completes Rachel's Mandatory Review on 1 July 2027. Rachel's next Mandatory Review date is set for 52 weeks in the future on 29 June 2028. Client declares a change in circumstances Tyrese is single with no dependent children. Tyrese is getting Accommodation Supplement and pays rent of $265.00 per week in Area 2.

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: Tyrese's Mandatory Review is due on 19 March 2027. He responds to the Mandatory Review on 17 March 2027 and tells MSD their rent will go up by $20.00 to $285.00 per week from 20 March 2027. MSD determines that Tyrese still qualifies for Accommodation Supplement based on the new change declared. His Accommodation Supplement rate is updated from 20 March 2027 with the new rent of $285.00 per week. MSD completes the Mandatory Review on 17 March 2027 and set's Tyrese's next review 52 weeks from the date the review was completed. Tyrese's next Mandatory Review date is 15 March 2028. Mandatory Review was not completed, and benefit has suspended Yvonne is single with no dependent children. Yvonne is getting Accommodation Supplement and pays rent of $155.00 in Area 3. Yvonne's Mandatory Review is due on 12 April 2027. Yvonne doesn't respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date and their Accommodation Supplement suspends on 12 April 2027. Yvonne does not contact MSD or respond to the Mandatory Review for 8 weeks after their Accommodation Supplement payment was suspended. Because of this Yvonne's Accommodation Supplement is cancelled from the date it suspended. Not enough information to complete Mandatory Review Susan has a partner and 1 dependent child. Susan is getting Accommodation Supplement and is paying $600.00 per week for their home ownership costs in Area 2. Susan's Mandatory Review is due on 17 March 2026. Susan responds to the Mandatory Review on 12 March 2026 and tells MSD that their mortgage payments have decreased due to an adjustment in their interest rate. However, MSD cannot complete the Mandatory Review as more information is needed from Susan. MSD asks Susan to provide evidence of when their mortgage payments changed. MSD tells Susan she needs to provide the information by her existing review date as this is a reasonable timeframe to get the evidence. Susan's Accommodation Supplement will continue to be paid during this time. However, if Susan does not provide information before this date, their Accommodation Supplement will suspend on 17 March 2026. Susan contacts MSD on 13 March 2026 and provides evidence that confirms her mortgage costs changed on 10 January 2026. MSD updates Susan's rate of Accommodation Supplement with the new home ownership costs from 10 January 2026 and a debt is established.

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: MSD completes the Mandatory Review on 13 March 2026 and sets the next review date 52 weeks from the date the review was completed. Susan's next Mandatory Review date is 12 March 2027. Note when there is a change in circumstances that means a client no longer qualifies for Accommodation Supplement, MSD should consider if they qualify for other types of assistance.

chunks.title: Exceptions when a client declares no change in circumstances for Mandatory Review — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have no change in circumstances, MSD must generally continue their Accommodation Supplement at the same rate. However, there are some exceptions when MSD can request further information from the client to determine if they continue to qualify for Accommodation Supplement or that the rate of payment is correct. Exceptions include when, at the time the client responds to their Mandatory Review, they: - have been getting Disability Allowance and have had no change in their disability related costs for three consecutive years or - have been getting Accommodation Supplement and have had no change in their accommodation costs for three consecutive years or - have had no change to their confirmed income amount for three consecutive years or - are a non-beneficiary and have confirmed no income If a client has one or more of these exceptions, MSD must consider if further information is required from the client before deciding the outcome of the Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Requesting further information — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: The decision to request further information from the client should be assessed on a case-by-case basis. Consider additional factors such as: - the type of costs the client has (e.g. accommodation costs vary with economic conditions and would be unlikely to have no change over an extended period) - when the client last provided verification of their costs (if it was required e.g. home ownership costs or accommodation costs that are unusually high) - other resources available to meet their costs (e.g. when the client has no income declared and is only getting assistance for some of their expenses, or when the client's income has not changed over an extended period)

chunks.title: Further information is needed to complete the Mandatory Review — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: If further information is needed to determine if the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement or that the rate of payment is correct, MSD must give a reasonable timeframe for the client to provide it. The date the client is given to provide the information by becomes the client's new deadline to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client does not provide the information that was asked for, MSD must suspend the Accommodation Supplement from the new deadline date. If the client provides the information that was asked for and MSD determines the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement (including the rate payable), the future Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Example Owen gets Accommodation Supplement to help with his accommodation costs of $375 per week. Owen is getting the maximum rate of Accommodation Supplement for the area he lives in. He recently stopped working and declared no income to MSD on 5 September 2027. Owen's Mandatory Review is due on 10 December 2027. He responds to his review before the review date and confirms he has had no change in his circumstances. As Owen is a single non-beneficiary (he is not getting a main benefit) and has confirmed no income at the time the Mandatory Review is returned, MSD must consider whether further information is required before completing the Mandatory Review. MSD considers Owen's circumstances and notes that he has $210 a week that he needs to pay in his rent, after getting Accommodation Supplement. As he has not declared a change in his income, MSD determines that it is reasonable to request further information about how Owen is meeting those costs as he may qualify for other assistance. Owen is asked to provide this information by 24 December (his new deadline for the review) or his Accommodation Supplement will stop. Two weeks is a reasonable amount of time because Owen only needs to contact MSD to confirm the details, he does not need to provide evidence. Owen contacts MSD on 15 December 2027 and confirms that he is renting from his uncle who is only charging him $165 a week since he was made redundant from his job. MSD reassess his Accommodation Supplement accordingly. MSD invites Owen to apply for Jobseeker Support if he is actively seeking full-time employment. Owen doesn't want to apply right now but says he will get in contact with MSD if he decides that he does want to apply for Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Further information is needed to complete the Mandatory Review — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: Owen's rate of Accommodation Supplement reduces from $165 to $72 a week, he will use his savings to make up the shortfall in his rent. MSD completes the Mandatory Review and his next review date is set for 52 weeks in the future (13 December 2028).

chunks.title: Further information not needed to complete the Mandatory Review — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: In some situations, there may be good reason for the client having no change in their costs or income, or no income, and further information may not be needed. For example, the client may have provided recent evidence of their costs or income, they may have recently discussed their circumstances with MSD or a non-beneficiary client with no income may be in the process of applying for a main benefit. If no further information is needed for MSD to determine the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement (including the rate payable), the future Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Example Marique is getting Accommodation Supplement for help with her accommodation costs of $550 rent per week. Marique's Mandatory Review for Accommodation Supplement is due 9 November 2026 and she responds on 5 November 2026 to confirm she has had no change in her circumstances. The last change she declared was in July 2023 when she moved into her rental property. As Marique has been getting Accommodation Supplement and declared no change in her accommodation costs for three consecutive years at the time the Mandatory Review is returned, MSD must consider whether further information is required before completing the Mandatory Review. MSD considers Marique's circumstances and sees that she recently provided verification of these costs in the form of a letter from her landlord when applying for assistance with rent arrears. This confirms that Marique's current accommodation costs are the same as they were in 2023. MSD determines that no further information is required to determine Marique continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement. Her Accommodation Supplement continues at the same rate, and her next review date is set for 52 weeks in the future (4 November 2027).

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a client getting Accommodation Supplement is admitted to hospital payment can continue at the existing rate for the first 13 weeks if their accommodation costs are continuing.
From the start of 14th week of hospitalisation the Accommodation Supplement will need to be reviewed.
The date of admission and the date of discharge are not included in the 13-week calculation.
Couples with dependent children do not have their Accommodation Supplement reduced regardless of how long they are in hospital.
## Client in hospital during Mandatory Review
Generally, clients getting Accommodation Supplement must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date or their payments will suspend.
However, when a client is in hospital (for 13 weeks or less) and needs more time to respond to the Mandatory Review, they may be able to get an extension. If a client is unable to respond to the review, they may be able to get an exemption.
The client must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption.
Note clients who are in hospital for more than 13 weeks do not have a Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Imprisonment — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
Accommodation Supplement is generally not paid when a client in prison. Accommodation Supplement should stop from the day following the date of imprisonment.
However, clients on home detention may qualify. For more information, see "Home Detention" in the appropriate main benefit manual.
In some circumstances Accommodation Supplement can continue when a:
- married, civil union or de facto client, or a single client with dependent children, is imprisoned or
- client is on remand
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances of the client before making a decision.

chunks.title: Inland Revenue deduction notices — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
Inland Revenue may request for a client's unpaid taxes to be directly deducted from their benefit payments.
Note all Inland Revenue deduction notices are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
The instructions of the deduction notice will be to deduct the lowest of either:
- 10% of the total debt which Inland Revenue specify in the notice, on a weekly basis or
- 20% of the client's gross earnings on a weekly basis
Where there are insufficient funds to cover the deduction, Work and Income must advise Inland Revenue immediately that the deduction will not start or will start at a reduced rate.
Inland Revenue deductions have a lower priority than Child Support deductions.
For more information see:
- Priority for deductions

chunks.title: IRD number for partner who is not apportioned assistance — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: As part of a review of Accommodation Supplement, MSD may make a written request to the client for evidence of a partner's IRD number when the: - partner is not being apportioned the primary client's Accommodation Supplement, and - partner's income is relevant to a client's Accommodation Supplement.

chunks.title: Setting or extending the period for providing evidence — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: MSD can request a client to provide evidence of a partner's IRD number within a reasonable time period (usually 10 working days). MSD can set a different period or extend the period to provide evidence of an IRD number when it is expected to take longer to get the evidence. This includes considering factors outside the client or partner's control that may cause delays, including, but not limited to: - the client or partner has a family emergency that caused a delay - processing delays with an external agency (e.g. Inland Revenue, Department of Internal Affairs, etc) - the client or partner does not speak English as a first language and has difficulty navigating evidence requirements - the client or partner has limited access to the internet, a device, or their local service centre - the client or partner has a physical or intellectual disability that makes accessing services difficult.

chunks.title: Notice following an unsuccessful match — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about a partner's IRD number. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information, or there's an error, MSD should ask the client (in writing) to provide evidence of their partner's IRD number, unless there are significant barriers to providing this. In the written request for evidence of the IRD number, MSD must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and the match was unsuccessful, and - giving the client a minimum of 10 working days to provide their partner's IRD number evidence or the client's assistance may be suspended. Example Isla is receiving Accommodation Supplement. Isla's partner, Ariki, has income that is included in MSD's income test to determine eligibility for Accommodation Supplement and MSD holds an IRD number for Ariki. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Ariki's IRD number. As part of a review of Isla's assistance, MSD provides a notice in writing giving 10 working days for Isla to provide evidence of Ariki's IRD number. MSD's decision to give 10 working days to provide evidence is based on: - Ariki already having an IRD number - Ariki not having any significant barriers to getting evidence of their IRD number - MSD's obligation to provide a minimum of 10 working days to provide the information.

chunks.title: MSD may suspend assistance if evidence is not received — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: MSD may suspend all taxable and/or income tested assistance the client is getting, including their Accommodation Supplement, if a partner's IRD number evidence is not provided within a reasonable timeframe (usually 10 working days) or within the extended period if this has been applied, the client's assistance may be suspended. In rare cases, depending on the client's circumstances, MSD may consider cancelling or varying the client's assistance. Note suspension does not apply to Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: IRD number not requested in some circumstances — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: MSD may not ask for evidence of an IRD number when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - significant factors, that are outside the client's or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of their IRD number, (e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence), and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided. A partner's IRD number and evidence of their IRD number does not need to be provided when they are not a New Zealand tax resident. MSD can determine a later point to request the evidence of the IRD number. For more information see: - Non-tax resident partner's IRD number not required Note there is different guidance for requesting evidence of an IRD number for clients and partners who are apportioned assistance, or when a client is applying for Accommodation Supplement.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review dates for Accommodation Supplement — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review dates for Accommodation Supplement
MSD must review a client's Accommodation Supplement within 52 weeks of the commencement date of Accommodation Supplement, or within 52 weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed.
The next review date is set for 52 weeks from the date MSD determined the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement and the rate of benefit payable (i.e. when MSD completes the review).
Clients who are getting a main benefit that is subject to a Mandatory Review will have their Accommodation Supplement reviewed at the same time as that benefit (this includes the initial review).
Note when MSD has an interaction with a client that confirms all of the same circumstances as a Mandatory Review, this can push out the client's Mandatory Review date by 52 weeks. This is known as a specific engagement.
## Initial review dates for Accommodation Supplement
Accommodation Supplement commencement date
Mandatory Review dates
Benefit commenced before 2 March 2026
Clients whose Accommodation Supplement commenced before 2 March 2026 will have their initial Mandatory Review either:
- 52 weeks from the commencement date of the Accommodation Supplement
or
- 52 weeks from when their last periodic review was completed
or
- 52 weeks from when MSD last contacted the client to confirm if the information MSD holds about their circumstances is correct (annual circumstances letter)
Whichever of the dates is later.
Benefit commenced on or after 2 March 2026
If a client's Accommodation Supplement commenced on or after 2 March 2026, their initial Mandatory Review date is either:
- 52 weeks from the commencement date of the Accommodation Supplement
or
- 52 weeks from the completion of a specific engagement

chunks.title: Mandatory Review not required — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review not required
There is no Mandatory Review for Accommodation Supplement for clients in the following circumstances:
- the client is hospitalised for more than 13 weeks
- the client is in residential disability care or rest home care
- the client has died
- the client is living in or visiting a region affected by an emergency or adverse event and are unable to reasonably leave the area
- the client is living in or visiting a region affected by an outbreak of a quarantinable disease and an epidemic notice has been given and is in force
or when:
- there is a system outage that prevents MSD or the client from completing the review
MSD will also stop the review for any clients who are in these circumstances after they have been notified about their Mandatory Review.
MSD will notify the client when they are not required to complete the review. The Mandatory Review date will be reset to 52 weeks from the client's original review date.
Note a notification will not be sent when the client has died.

chunks.title: Married, civil union or de facto clients — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Married, civil union or de facto clients
Where one partner is overseas and their Accommodation Supplement will not be paid, the partner remaining in New Zealand should still be assessed using the entry threshold for a married, civil union or de facto couple.
Pay the full amount to the partner remaining in New Zealand.

chunks.title: Ministry of Social Development debt repayments — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Ministry of Social Development debt repayments
When a client has a Ministry of Social Development debt, this can be recovered by regular deductions from their current benefit.
Note Income Related Rent historical Housing New Zealand debt should be given equal priority to Ministry of Social Development debt.
For more information see:
- Core policy Negotiating repayment of debt

chunks.title: Mismatch of accommodation income and accommodation costs — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: Clients must tell MSD when: - they start getting rent or board or - there is a change in the rent or board amount they get, or - their accommodation costs change

chunks.title: When clients can be matched — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When a client declares the rent or board payments they get, or the accommodation costs they pay, MSD will check the details match between two clients when: - a head tenant or homeowner client and their renter or boarder client both get Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, or - a social housing tenant who pays Income Related Rent gets contributions from a client who lives with them and that client gets Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit

chunks.title: Moving house — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When a client moves house, it is possible for there to be two separate mismatches at the same time. For example, when the client is a boarder and their previous landlord pays Income Related Rent and their new landlord gets Accommodation Supplement. In this case, there could be a mismatch process for the client and their old landlord and a mismatch process for the client and their new landlord.

chunks.title: Mismatch process — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When there is a mismatch of the accommodation type or amounts, the mismatch process below must be followed.

chunks.title: Step one - Mismatch identified — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: A mismatch of information will be identified when a client's accommodation type or amount differs from what a client who is a head tenant or homeowner has declared they are getting, or a renter or boarder has declared they are paying. MSD must try to contact both clients within one working day of identifying the mismatch to check and confirm the correct details. If one or both clients are uncontactable within one working day, but a message is left for the client/s to make contact, MSD must consider whether it is reasonable to allow the one working day to lapse before moving to the next step in the process. When one or both clients have been contacted, and it is clear the mismatch cannot be resolved within one working day, or one or both clients are uncontactable and a message cannot be left, MSD can continue to the next step in the process. Note the one working day ends on the close of the working day following the day the mismatch is identified. Example: Englebert lives with Alphonse, and they both get Accommodation Supplement. Englebert pays his rent to Alphonse who owns the property. On Wednesday 6 May, Englebert advises MSD his rent will be increasing from $350 per week to $360 per week from next Monday. Alphonse has not yet advised MSD of this change. On Thursday 7 May (within one working day of identifying the payment amount mismatch), MSD contacts Englebert to confirm he intended to declare a change in his rent amount. Alphonse contacts MSD later that day to advise that Englebert's rent will be increasing to $360 from next Monday. MSD updates both clients' payments from next Monday and the mismatch has been resolved.

chunks.title: Step two - Notification of mismatch — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When the mismatch is not resolved within one working day after it was identified, MSD must notify both clients of the mismatch and advise they have 10 working days to resolve it. MSD will also advise if the mismatch is not resolved within 10 working days after the date of notification, any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit will be suspended from the 11th working day. If the client is a social housing tenant, they will be notified that the Income Related Rent will be set to market rent if they have not resolved the mismatch within 10 working days after the date of notification. Note the 10 working days starts from the day after the letter is sent.

chunks.title: Step three - Response to the notification of mismatch — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: Contact from client/s and mismatch resolved within 10 working days When the client/s make contact and resolve the mismatch within 10 working days, the details should be updated and any assistance reviewed accordingly. This means the mismatch is now resolved. No contact from client/s When one or both clients don't make contact within 10 working days to confirm their rent or board payment information, the mismatch is unable to be resolved, and both clients Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit must be suspended. If the client is a social housing tenant and the mismatch is not resolved, MSD will notify the housing provider that the client's Income Related Rent must be set to market rent for the property. Community Housing Providers have a discretion not to set the client's rent to the market rent rate. The standard 60-day notice period will apply. Example: Astrid and Rex live together, and Rex pays board to Astrid. They both get Accommodation Supplement as non-beneficiaries. Astrid receives a mandatory review for her Accommodation Supplement. On Tuesday 9 June, she responds before her review due date confirming that she receives $10 more in board from Rex. The new amount is different from what MSD holds for Rex. MSD checks with Astrid on Wednesday 10 June (within one working day of identifying the mismatch) to see if she advised of the increase in error. She confirms the increase is correct. On Wednesday 10 June, MSD tries contacting Rex to confirm the new rate, but he doesn't respond. On Thursday 11 June (after the one working day has lapsed), MSD sends both Astrid and Rex notification of the mismatch and provides 10 working days to resolve it and advise MSD. Rex does not respond to the request for information by close of day Tuesday 23 June (within 10 working days). MSD suspends Rex's Accommodation Supplement from Wednesday 24 June (11th working day). Astrid's Accommodation Supplement is also suspended from Wednesday 24 June as MSD cannot verify the information she has declared is correct. If Rex does not respond within 8 weeks, both Astrid and Rex's Accommodation Supplement will be cancelled.

chunks.title: Disputes — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: If both clients can't reach an agreement or provide the requested evidence within 10 working days from being notified of the mismatch, both clients' Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit must be suspended. If the client is a social housing tenant and they can't reach an agreement or provide the requested evidence within 10 working days from being notified of the mismatch, MSD will notify the housing provider that the client's Income Related Rent must be set to market rent for the property. Community Housing Providers have a discretion not to set the client's rent to the market rent rate. The standard 60-day notice period will apply. If both clients agree and/or provide evidence confirming the correct rent or board payment information while the assistance is suspended or Income Related Rent is at the market rent rate, the details should be updated and any assistance resumed and reviewed accordingly. For more information see: - Change in accommodation income - Change in accommodation If the mismatch has not been resolved within 8 weeks of being suspended, the Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit will be cancelled. In this case, clients can reapply for Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, however if both clients apply and the same mismatch of information is identified, the disputes process will start again.

chunks.title: Non-beneficiaries — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Non-beneficiaries
Accommodation Supplement can continue to be paid to the client for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital.
From beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation the Accommodation Supplement will need to be reviewed.
## Single clients and sole parents
If client still has to meet their continuing accommodation costs Accommodation Supplement can continue at the existing rate.
You will need to check how they are supporting themselves. The client may qualify for a benefit if their income has reduced or stopped.
## Married, civil union or de facto couples (without dependent children)
For a married, civil union or de facto client (without dependent children) you still treat the couple as married, in a civil union or de facto relationship and take into account the income and assets of both. You can pay the full amount to the partner not in hospital.
You will need to check if the client's income has changed because of being in hospital. The client may qualify for a benefit if their income has reduced or stopped.

chunks.title: Obligation to advise of departure from New Zealand (main beneficiaries only) — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Obligation to advise of departure from New Zealand (main beneficiaries only)
All clients getting a main benefit must tell the Ministry of Social Development before they leave New Zealand.
If the client or partner does not tell the Ministry before they go overseas, their benefit payments will stop from the day after they leave New Zealand.
If a client tells us they will be absent from New Zealand, and they have an approved travel reason, they may be able to keep getting their main benefit payments for up to 28 days.
Clients who do not keep getting a main benefit while overseas may still be able to get their Accommodation Supplement, if their absence does not affect the client's eligibility for this assistance and they told the Ministry of their absence before they travelled overseas. They must have ongoing accommodation costs and this assistance is limited to 28 days in any 52 week period.
For more information about absence from New Zealand see:
- Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period in relevant main benefit
## Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service
The Ministry of Social Development has an Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service that identifies clients getting a benefit who have left New Zealand.
Once identified, the client's eligibility to keep getting their benefit payments while they are absent from New Zealand is automatically determined by Ministry systems.
## Client does not advise of departure
If the client did not tell the Ministry they were leaving New Zealand, their benefit will be suspended immediately from the day after they left New Zealand. As a result, their Accommodation Supplement will also stop.
The Integrity Intervention Centre will determine if any overpayment has occurred, establish any debt and advise the client.
If a client challenges the information match refer them to Integrity Intervention Centre.
For more information see:
- Paying benefit when client failed to advise of absence in relevant main benefit
- Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit
- Action on return to New Zealand
- Calculating the period of absence

chunks.title: Outcomes of a Mandatory Review — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: Clients must respond to their Mandatory Review before their Mandatory Review date, or their payments will suspend. When a client responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined if the client qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g. client has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies The Mandatory Review is completed when MSD makes a decision about the client’s eligibility for Accommodation Supplement and the rate of benefit payable (if applicable). MSD may also carry out a separate review of the Accommodation Supplement at any time, where there is good reason.

chunks.title: Client declares no change — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have had no change in circumstances, MSD must generally continue their Accommodation Supplement at the same rate. The client's next review date will be set for 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Exceptions when a client declares no change When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have no change in circumstances, there are some situations when MSD can request further information from the client before deciding whether to continue Accommodation Supplement e.g. the client is a non-beneficiary and has no income.

chunks.title: Client declares a change in circumstances — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When a client responds to the Mandatory Review with a change in circumstances, MSD must use the information provided to determine if the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement, or any other benefits they get that are subject to a Mandatory Review (excluding Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit) and the rate payable. MSD may request further information from the client where it’s unclear whether the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement. Date of change When a client declares a change in circumstances, MSD will need to assess if the client still qualifies for Accommodation Supplement and determine the rate payable and from what date, depending on when the change in circumstances happened or will happen. Client is also getting other assistance When the client has provided information as part of the Mandatory Review that could affect their entitlement to or the rate payable of any other assistance (e.g. Temporary Additional Support or Flexible Childcare Assistance), MSD may use this information to review that assistance. When the other assistance is affected by the outcome of the Mandatory Review, MSD must change the rate, suspend or cancel that assistance where appropriate. For example, if the outcome of the Mandatory Review is that the client is no longer entitled to Accommodation Supplement, their Temporary Additional Support must be reviewed, and the rate may change or stop if they no longer qualify.

chunks.title: Further information is needed to complete the Mandatory Review — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: When a client has responded to the review and further information is needed to determine if the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement or that the rate of payment is correct, MSD must give a reasonable timeframe for the client to provide it. The date the client is given to provide the information by will become the client's new deadline to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client does not provide the information that was asked for before the deadline, MSD must suspend the Accommodation Supplement from the new deadline date. If the client provides the information that was asked for and MSD determines the client continues to qualify for Accommodation Supplement (including the rate payable), the next Mandatory Review date is set 52-weeks from the date MSD completed the review.

chunks.title: Completing Mandatory Reviews in specific circumstances — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: A client may provide all the information required to complete the Mandatory Review but advise of a change in accommodation costs that has not been confirmed by the client they pay rent or board to. This means there is either a mismatch of the accommodation type (e.g. rent or board) or the amount. In this situation MSD can continue paying the Accommodation Supplement at the existing rate and complete the Mandatory Review. Before the client's Accommodation Supplement can be updated to reflect the change in amount or accommodation type, the mismatch of information must be resolved. Example Rowan and Luca live together. They both get Accommodation Supplement as non-beneficiaries, and Rowan pays board to Luca. Rowan gets a Mandatory Review for his Accommodation Supplement. He responds before his review date and advises MSD that his board has increased by $10 a week. The new board value does not match the board amount MSD holds for Luca. Outcome As part of the Mandatory Review, MSD determines that Rowan still qualifies for Accommodation Supplement. However, because the change in accommodation costs hasn't been confirmed with Luca, the rate of Accommodation Supplement cannot be updated through the Mandatory Review. MSD continues Rowan's Accommodation Supplement at the existing rate and completes the Mandatory Review. MSD must then follow the mismatch process to resolve the mismatch.

chunks.title: Completing a Mandatory Review when there are new costs — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text: In some circumstances MSD can still complete the Mandatory Review when a client has declared a change in circumstances that does not affect the client's eligibility for Accommodation Supplement, e.g. a new cost relating to a disability. Example Hana is getting Accommodation Supplement and Disability Allowance (non-beneficiary) and has a Mandatory Review for both. Hana responds to the Mandatory Review to confirm their circumstances. Hana tells MSD they have a new disability cost but nothing else has changed. MSD completes the Mandatory Review and continues the Accommodation Supplement and Disability Allowance at the existing rate. MSD advises Hana that she needs to provide a medical certificate from her medical or nurse practitioner to confirm the additional cost, and she must provide proof of the cost to have the new cost included in her Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Client getting a main benefit — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Client getting a main benefit
When a client is paid their main benefit while they are absent from New Zealand (either because they meet the criteria for approved travel or the requirement to approved travel does not apply to them) they can continue getting their main benefit and their Accommodation Supplement for up to 28 days in any 52 week period, unless they meet the criteria to be paid their main benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.
They must have ongoing costs.
Clients who do not continue getting a main benefit while overseas may still be able to continue to get Accommodation Supplement, if their absence:
- does not affect the client's eligibility for this assistance and
- they advised MSD of their absence before their international travel and
- they have ongoing accommodation costs
This is limited to 28 days in a 52 week period.
For more information about Absence from New Zealand see:
- Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period in relevant main benefit
## Information required from client when advising they intend to travel
When a client contacts you to advise that they intend travelling overseas you need to obtain the following information:
- date of departure
- date of return
- whether their accommodation costs are continuing
## Non-beneficiary Extra help payment will not continue
Where payment of Accommodation Supplement will not continue because they do not meet the eligibility criteria due to their absence you will need to suspend the benefit from:
- the day after departure

chunks.title: Permanent absence — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
If the client is leaving New Zealand permanently Accommodation Supplement must be cancelled from the day after departure.

chunks.title: Priority for deductions — extra help > accommodation supplement > changes and reviews accommodation supplement
chunks.text:
## Priority for deductions
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others; the following list gives the order of priority, highest to lowest:
Highest priority
- Inland Revenue tax deductions (including Student Loan repayments)
- Child Support deductions made under the Child Support Act 1991
- Ministry of Social Development debt repayments including Liable Parent Contributions (LPC), child maintenance debts and Major Repairs Advances (MRA), Student Allowance debt, Student Loan debt converted to Ministry of Social Development debt, Income Related Rent historical Housing New Zealand debt, Income Related Rent Ministry of Social Development debt
- Attachment orders made under the Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Court attachment orders issued under the Summary Proceedings Act 1957
- Court attachment orders issued under the District Court Act 2016
- Student Loan repayments
Lowest priority
Determining the priority of deductions is necessary when a client has more than one order issued in respect of their benefit. Also each order and deduction notice is subject to its own protected earnings rule.
