chunks.title: Amount payable during absences — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Amount payable during absences
The usual weekly amount that the centre receives when the child attends is the amount that is paid to the centre during absences.
For example if a centre usually receives $100 when the child attends this is the amount they will receive when the child is absent regardless of the actual absence fee charged by the centre.
Note if a centre or service knows that a child will not be returning the Subsidy must be cancelled from that date.

chunks.title: Amount payable during absences — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Amount payable during absences
The usual weekly amount that the centre receives when the child attends is the amount that is paid to the centre during absences.
For example if a centre usually receives $100 when the child attends this is the amount they will receive when the child is absent regardless of the actual absence fee charged by the centre.
Note if a centre or service knows that a child will not be returning the OSCAR subsidy must be cancelled from that date.

chunks.title: Amount payable during COVID-19 absence or closure — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Amount payable during COVID-19 absence or closure
When a child is absent or a centre is closed due to COVID-19 requirements, the usual weekly amount the centre got before the absence or closure is the amount they will continue to get. This is regardless of whether a fee is charged to hold the child's place, and how much the fee is.
For example, if a centre usually gets $100 when the child attends, this is the amount they will get when the child is absent, or the centre is closed, regardless of the actual fee charged by the centre.
Note if during an absence or closure, the client decides their child will not return, payment must be stopped.
If a change in circumstance happens during an absence or closure, the Childcare Subsidy must be reviewed, and the rate of payment may change.

chunks.title: Approved early childhood education programme or service — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Approved early childhood education programme or service
An approved early childhood education programme means, early childhood education, provided by any of the following:
- a licensed early childhood service which includes: early childhood education and care centre (eg daycare centre, kōhanga reo, playcentre, kindergarten)home-based education and care servicehospital-based education and care service
- early childhood education and care centre (eg daycare centre, kōhanga reo, playcentre, kindergarten)
- home-based education and care service
- hospital-based education and care service
- a playgroup certificated by the Ministry of Education (this means a playgroup funded by the Ministry of Education and will meet certain standards)
and
- for which a fee is charged for the children to participate in the programme
Note under no circumstances can we make a payment for childcare provided informally (for example through family or friends who are not licensed to provide a home-based education and care service) or a childcare centre or service that is not approved (not licensed).

chunks.title: Approved OSCAR programmes — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Approved OSCAR programmes
An approved OSCAR programme is one that has been approved as a community service by Te Kāhui Kāhu (Social Services Accreditation).
For more information see:
- Accreditation and approval overview
Under no circumstances can MSD pay a subsidy for a programme that is not approved.
The OSCAR provider is given a letter of approval by Te Kāhui Kāhu detailing their current certification.
The programme's approval status must be checked before OSCAR subsidy can be granted as programme approval can be revoked by Te Kāhui Kāhu.
If a programme is not on the directory, the client will need to provide a copy of the programme's approval letter before OSCAR subsidy can be granted. This should only be when there has been a delay between the programme being approved and the directory being updated.
For a list of approved centres see:
- Family Services Directory - OSCAR providers
Approved OSCAR programmes may provide childcare at different times:
- before school or
- after school or
- during school holidays or
- a combination of the above

chunks.title: Assessing travel time — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Assessing travel time
Travel time can be included in the assessment of Childcare Subsidy.
The clients travel time is calculated from the time the child is dropped off/picked up at the centre and the time the client arrives/departs work, study or training.
Note the hours of travel included in the assessment of Childcare Subsidy must not be more than the maximum of hours the client qualifies for.

chunks.title: Assessing travel time — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Assessing travel time
Travel time can be included in the assessment of OSCAR Subsidy.
Calculate the client's travel time from:
- the time the child is dropped off at the centre and the time the client arrives at work and
- the time the client departs work and the time the client picks up the child
If the client has work obligations you can calculate the client's travel time from:
- the time the child is dropped off at the centre and the time the client arrives at their employment related training (or an activity included in an existing Job Seeker Agreement) and
- the time the client departs the employment related training (or an activity included in an existing Job Seeker Agreement) and the time the client picks up the child
Note the hours of travel included in the assessment of OSCAR Subsidy must not be more than the maximum of hours the client qualifies for.

chunks.title: Change of ownership — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Change of ownership
When an existing childcare centre is sold, the new owners will need to meet the criteria set down by the Ministry of Education.
The new centre will need to supply the information requested under new centres.
Under no circumstances can we pay a subsidy to a centre that is not approved.
All subsidies may be transferred to the new centre using the CCTFR screen in SWIFTT. The transfer screen (CCTFR) will allow users to transfer all children linked to a childcare provider record to a new centre in one action, rather than individually by child record.
The new centre should confirm by letter or fax the children who will be attending the centre.
For more information see:
- New centres

chunks.title: Change of ownership — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Change of ownership
When an existing OSCAR centre is sold, the new owners will need to meet the criteria set down by Ministry of Social Development Approvals.
The new centre will need to supply the information requested under new centres.
Under no circumstances can we pay a subsidy to a centre that is not approved.
All subsidies may be transferred to the new centre using the CCTFR screen in SWIFTT. The transfer screen (CCTFR) will allow users to transfer all children linked to a childcare provider record to a new centre in one action, rather than individually by child record.
The new centre should confirm by letter or fax the children who will be attending the centre.
For more information see:
- New centres

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: If a child is absent from New Zealand we can continue paying Childcare Subsidy for up to 28 days from the day after the date the child leaves the country if the client: - continue to meet the qualifications and - a fee is being charged to hold the child's place with the childcare service or centre while they are temporarily absent from New Zealand Paying Childcare Subsidy while the client is absent from New Zealand depends on whether the client is also getting a main benefit.

chunks.title: Clients getting a main benefit — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: All clients getting a main benefit must tell the Ministry of Social Development before they leave New Zealand. If the client or partner does not tell the Ministry before their international travel, their benefit payments (including Childcare Subsidy) must stop. When a client is still being paid their main benefit while they are absent from New Zealand (either because they qualify for approved travel or the requirement for approved travel does not apply to them) they can continue getting their main benefit and their Childcare Subsidy for up to 28 days in any 52 week period. Clients who do not continue to get their main benefit while overseas (because they do not qualify for approved travel) may keep getting Childcare Subsidy, if: - their absence does not affect the client qualifying for this assistance and - they advised the Ministry of their absence before their international travel Payment while a client is absent from New Zealand is limited to 28 days in a 52 week period. For more information about Absence from New Zealand see: - Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit - Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period in relevant main benefit

chunks.title: Clients getting non-beneficiary Extra help — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: Clients who are getting Childcare Subsidy, but do not get a main benefit: - must advise of their departure from New Zealand and - can be absent and paid their Childcare Subsidy for up to 28 days per absence where the client remains eligible for Childcare Subsidy. They must be required to pay to hold the child's place at the childcare service or centre if the child is not attending while the parent or caregiver is absent from New Zealand.

chunks.title: Information required from client when advising they intend to travel — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: When a client contacts you to advise they intend travelling overseas you need to obtain the following information: - date of departure - date of return - whether the child or young person is remaining in New Zealand - whether the child or young person will continue attending the childcare centre and - whether a fee is being charged to hold the child's place while they are not attending

chunks.title: Non-beneficiary Extra help payment will not continue — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: When payment of Childcare Subsidy is stopped because the client does not qualify due to their absence, you need to suspend the benefit from: - the day after departure

chunks.title: Board payments - Childcare Subsidy — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Board payments - Childcare Subsidy
Some clients will get board payments for children in their care from Oranga Tamariki or via a 3rd party e.g. Barnardos.
These payments are not treated as income when assessing entitlement to Childcare Subsidy or OSCAR.

chunks.title: Change in childcare centre — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Change in childcare centre
When a client changes centres they are required to complete a Change of circumstances form R24.
The provider will need to verify the number of hours that the child will be attending, fee charge, and date the child started care.

chunks.title: Change in clients income — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Change in clients income
If a client's income changes the Childcare Subsidy must be reviewed to ensure that the correct rate of subsidy is being paid.
The reason for this is that the amount of subsidy paid depends on the family income.

chunks.title: Change in hours — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Change in hours
If a child changes the hours that they attend their centre, the Childcare Subsidy must be reviewed.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Childcare Subsidy.
You may also review Childcare Subsidy at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.

chunks.title: Child that the subsidy is for — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Child that the subsidy is for
The Childcare Subsidy must be stopped from the day after the date that the child leaves the client's care.
## Other child in family
The Childcare Subsidy must be reviewed from the day after the date that the child leaves the client's care to ensure that the correct rate is being paid. The reason for this is that the amount of subsidy that can be paid depends on how many children are in the family. This is because the rate of subsidy payable is based on household income and the number of dependent children remaining, if any.

chunks.title: Child leaves the centre — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Child leaves the centre
When a child leaves the centre, Childcare Subsidy should be cancelled from the day after the child's last day at the centre.
The Childcare Subsidy cannot be used to pay for a notice period if the child is no longer attending.
## Child leaves the centre - centre unsure if child is returning
Where the provider is aware that the child will no longer be attending the centre the subsidy must cease from the day after the last date of attendance.
The payment of Childcare Subsidy can continue for up to 3 weeks if the provider is not sure if a child has left the centre. In these cases Childcare Subsidy must cease from the earlier of:
- 3 weeks of non attendance or
- when the centre becomes aware that the child will not be returning
## Child changes centre
A client should complete a change in circumstances form confirming when their child has changed to a new centre. Childcare Subsidy must cease from the earlier of:
- when the centre becomes aware that the child will not be returning or
- the day prior to Childcare Subsidy being granted for the new centre or
- after 3 weeks of non attendance

chunks.title: Client debt — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Client debt
Debts should be recovered from the parent when the child continues to be present at the centre and a debt has arisen as a result of one of the following circumstances:
- change in client's income
- absences - when no charge is made for absences by the childcare centre
- change in application typeexample if a client finishes training or ceases work and is now only eligible for 9 hours
- change in care arrangement
- if the child or parent goes overseas we can only pay the subsidy if the costs are continuing. For example if an absence fee is charged. If the costs are not continuing the debt must be established from the day after the parent leaves the country.
- admitted/discharged from hospital
- imprisoned/held in custody
Note it is important that clear notes are put on CMS to show how the debt was created and who is responsible for the refund.

chunks.title: Client takes up Twenty hours Early Childhood Education — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Client takes up Twenty hours Early Childhood Education
When a client takes up Twenty hours Early Childhood Education hours, you must reduce, suspend or cancel their Childcare Subsidy.
## Notification within 28 days
When you are advised that a child is taking up Twenty hours Early Childhood Education within 28 days of the event, the new rate is effective from the week you process (the first available date) providing you are notified by the client or provider within 28 days.
Generally where a child is taking up the Twenty hours Early Childhood Education we would not establish Childcare Subsidy overpayments.
## Notification after 28 days
When you are advised a child is taking up the Twenty hours Early Childhood Education more than 28 days after the event, you should reduce, suspend or cancel the Childcare Subsidy from the actual date.
Overpayments will need to be established where appropriate.

chunks.title: Death of a client — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
When a client getting a Childcare Subsidy dies the subsidy generally stops from the day after death.
There is discretion to continue paying until the next pay date following the date of death if the child is still attending the centre.
After this date the subsidy must be cancelled.
## Death of a child
When a child who is receiving Childcare Subsidy dies the subsidy generally stops from the day after death.
## Death of another child
The Childcare Subsidy must be reviewed to ensure that we are paying the correct rate for the family size.

chunks.title: Debts — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Debts
A debt is created when a client or childcare centre is overpaid.
Debts can be recovered from the client or provider depending on the reason why the debt was created.

chunks.title: If the child is in hospital — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## If the child is in hospital
The client can choose to have the Childcare Subsidy suspended or for the subsidy to be paid as an absence.
## If the parent is in hospital
If the child is still attending the Childcare centre you can continue to pay the Childcare Subsidy.
However, you will need to see how long the parent will be in hospital, as it may mean the child will be in someone else's care.
If this is the case the subsidy will have to be cancelled and then granted to the new caregiver.

chunks.title: Partner's IRD number — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: As part of a review of Childcare Subsidy, when the client also receives any other taxable assistance, MSD may make a written request to the client for evidence of a partner's IRD number when the partner's income is relevant to a client's assistance.

chunks.title: Setting or extending the period for providing evidence — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: MSD can request a client to provide evidence of their partner's IRD number within a reasonable time period where the client also receives any other taxable assistance (usually 10 working days). MSD can set a different period or extend the period to provide evidence of an IRD number when it is expected to take longer to get the evidence. This considers factors outside the client or partner's control that may cause delays, including, but not limited to: - the client or partner has a family emergency that caused a delay - processing delays with an external agency (e.g. Inland Revenue, Department of Internal Affairs, etc) - the client or partner does not speak English as a first language and has difficulty navigating evidence requirements - the client or partner has limited access to the internet, a device, or their local service centre - the client or partner has a physical or intellectual disability that makes accessing services difficult.

chunks.title: Notice following a No Match result — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about IRD numbers. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information, MSD should ask the client (in writing) to provide evidence of their partner's IRD number, unless there are significant barriers to providing this. The request for evidence of the IRD number must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and the match was unsuccessful, and - giving the client or partner a minimum of 10 working days to provide their partner's IRD number evidence or the client's assistance may be suspended, cancelled or varied. Example Isla is working part-time and receiving Childcare Subsidy. Isla's partner, Ariki, is also working part-time. Ariki's income is included in MSD's income test to determine Isla's eligibility for Childcare Subsidy and MSD holds an IRD number for Ariki. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Ariki's IRD number. MSD contact Isla to informally check Ariki's IRD number but because Isa is only receiving Childcare Subsidy and no other taxable income, no further request for Ariki's IRD number is made.

chunks.title: MSD may suspend assistance if evidence is not received — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: MSD may suspend all taxable and income tested assistance except Childcare Subsidy the client is getting if a partner's IRD number evidence is not provided within a reasonable timeframe (usually 10 working days) or within the extended period if this has been applied. In rare cases, depending on the client's circumstances, MSD may consider cancelling or varying the assistance.

chunks.title: IRD number not required in some circumstances — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text: MSD may not need evidence of an IRD number when the client is only receiving the Childcare Subsidy. MSD can still informally ask for an IRD number. In addition, IRD number evidence may not be required when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - significant factors, that are outside the client or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of their IRD number (e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence), and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided or - significant factors related to a health, injury or disability that are outside the client's control that prevents them from providing evidence of an IRD number, and - an agent cannot be appointed to act on the client's behalf. A partner's IRD number and evidence of their IRD number does not need to be provided when they are not a New Zealand tax resident. MSD can determine at a later point to request evidence of the IRD number. For more information see: - Non-tax resident partner's IRD number not required Note there is different guidance for requesting evidence of an IRD number for clients or when a client is applying for Childcare Subsidy.

chunks.title: Provider debt — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Provider debt
Debts should be recovered from the provider, when a debt has arisen from one of the following circumstances:
- child leaves the centre permanently - the childcare centre knowing the child has left cannot accept the money in good faith
- childcare centre is closed - centres may close during school holiday periods. This excludes statutory holidays
- caregiver is unavailable - for home based care providers there are occasions when the caregiver cannot provide childcare
- as a result of Twenty hours Early Childhood Education being paid to the centre for hours for which they also receive Childcare Subsidy
Note it is important that clear notes are put on CMS to show how the debt was created and who is responsible for the refund.

chunks.title: Review — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Review
Childcare Subsidy is reviewed every 52 weeks.
The purpose of this review is to check that:
- the client still qualifies for the subsidy
- all of the child's absences are recorded and
- the correct rate of subsidy is being paid

chunks.title: Study — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews childcare subsidy
chunks.text:
## Study
If a client starts or finishes study the Childcare Subsidy must be reviewed from that date.
A review is necessary to ensure:
- we are paying the correct number of hours and
- paying at the correct rate

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — extra help > childcare assistance programme > changes and reviews oscar subsidy
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
If a child is absent from New Zealand we can continue paying the OSCAR subsidy for up to 28 days from the day after the date the child leaves the country if the client:
- continue to meet the qualifications and
- a fee is being charged to hold the child's place with the OSCAR provider while they are temporarily absent from New Zealand
The OSCAR subsidy must be suspended from the 29th day after the child left the country.
If the child or client is leaving New Zealand permanently OSCAR subsidy must be cancelled from the day after departure.
Paying OSCAR Subsidy while the client is absent from New Zealand depends on whether the client is also getting a main benefit.
## Clients getting a main benefit

- their absence does not affect the client qualifying for this assistance and
- they advised the Ministry of their absence before their international travel
Payment while a client is absent from New Zealand is limited to 28 days in a 52 week period.
For more information about Absence from New Zealand see:
- Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit

Clients who are getting OSCAR subsidy, but do not get a main benefit:
- must advise of their departure from New Zealand and
- can be absent and paid their OSCAR subsidy for up to 28 days per absence where the client remains eligible for OSCAR subsidy. They must be required to pay, to hold the child's place with the OSCAR provider if the child is not attending while the parent or caregiver is absent from New Zealand.
## Non-beneficiary Extra help payment will not continue
When payment of OSCAR subsidy is stopped because the client does not qualify due to their absence, you need to suspend the benefit from:
- the day after departure

chunks.title: Child Disability Allowance — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Child Disability Allowance
The Childcare Subsidy is for children under 5 years old except for children for whom Child Disability Allowance is paid. These children can get a Childcare Subsidy until they are 6 years of age.
Childcare Subsidy may be paid for up to 50 hours a week if the qualifications are met (except the requirement that the child is under 5 years old) and
- the child is under 6 years old and
- the child is one for whom Child Disability Allowance is paid
This category of subsidy recognises that many of these children benefit from an extra year in pre-school.
The subsidy will cease either when the child turns 6 years old or when they start school, whichever is earlier.
The other parent or partner is not required to provide childcare in these cases.
## Child turns 5 years old
When a child for whom Child Disability Allowance is paid turns 5 years old, they can either get a Childcare Subsidy or OSCAR subsidy but cannot get both.

chunks.title: Child not living at home — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Child not living at home
The child doesn't have to be living with the client to be a dependent child. To help you decide, consider the following:
- why the child is living away from home
- how permanent the arrangement is and
- what payments the client makes towards the child's care

chunks.title: Child getting Child Disability Allowance — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Child getting Child Disability Allowance
Children who get a Child Disability Allowance are eligible for the OSCAR Subsidy.
OSCAR may be paid for up to 20 hours a week in term time or 50 hours a week in the school holidays if:
- the qualifications are met (but not the additional qualifications) and
- the child is one for whom Child Disability Allowance is paid
The other parent or partner is not required to provide childcare in these cases.
The subsidy will stop when:
- the child can no longer get Child Disability Allowance or
- the child turns 18 and is not continuing in education or is no longer financially dependent or
- the child is 18 and: they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education orthey are no longer attending school or tertiary education as required orthey are financially independent orthey leave the parent or caregiver's care orit is later than 31 December of the year they turned 18 or
- they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education or
- they are no longer attending school or tertiary education as required or
- they are financially independent or
- they leave the parent or caregiver's care or
- it is later than 31 December of the year they turned 18 or
- the qualifications are no longer met
whichever is earliest.

chunks.title: Childcare Providers and GST — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Childcare Providers and GST
The Childcare Subsidy does not include GST as the payment is being made to the childcare provider on behalf of the client.
If the childcare provider is registered, they are required to include GST as part of the fee for the service provided.
For any queries about GST the provider should contact Inland Revenue to discuss the childcare centres liability.

Childcare Subsidy is a non-taxable payment that aims to assist clients with dependent children to undertake and remain in employment, education or training.
It also assists client's access pre-school care if they or their child are seriously disabled or ill.
For more detailed information see:

chunks.title: Child's caregiver also cares for a child in hospital - OSCAR — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Child's caregiver also cares for a child in hospital - OSCAR
OSCAR Subsidy may be paid for up to 20 hours a week during term time and 50 hours a week during the school holidays where the eligible child has a sibling who has been admitted to hospital.
There are extra pressures on caregivers when a child is admitted to hospital. It is usually difficult for the caregiver to arrange childcare for other children so that the caregiver can visit the child in hospital.
This is why up to 20 or 50 hours OSCAR Subsidy may be granted in respect of other children in these situations, regardless of how many hours the caregiver spends visiting the hospital.
Note the client and their partner (if any) do not need a good and sufficient reason why they are not able to care for the eligible child.
The subsidy will stop when:
- the hospitalised child is discharged or
- the dependent child turns 14 and Child Disability Allowance is not paid for them or
- Child Disability Allowance is paid for the child and the child: turns 18 and is not continuing in education or is no longer financially dependent oris 18 and: they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education orthey are no longer attending school or tertiary education as required orthey are financially independent orthey leave the parent or caregiver's care orit is later than 31 December of the year they turned 18 or
- turns 18 and is not continuing in education or is no longer financially dependent or
- is 18 and: they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education orthey are no longer attending school or tertiary education as required orthey are financially independent orthey leave the parent or caregiver's care orit is later than 31 December of the year they turned 18 or
- they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education or
- they are no longer attending school or tertiary education as required or
- they are financially independent or
- they leave the parent or caregiver's care or
- it is later than 31 December of the year they turned 18 or
- the qualifications are no longer met
whichever is earliest.
## Evidence of hospitalisation
A letter from the hospital social worker or the treating hospital doctor should be requested verifying that the child has been or will be admitted to hospital.
This letter should show the:
- date of admission and
- expected date of discharge

chunks.title: Child's principal caregiver also cares for a child in hospital — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Child's principal caregiver also cares for a child in hospital
Childcare Subsidy may be paid for up to 50 hours per week where the eligible child's principal caregiver has another dependent child who has been admitted to hospital. This includes a principal temporary caregiver of a child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid.
There are further pressures on caregivers when a child is admitted to hospital. It is usually difficult for the caregiver to arrange childcare for other children so the caregiver, can visit the child in hospital.
Therefore up to 50 hours Childcare Subsidy may be granted in respect of other children in such families, regardless of how many hours the caregiver spends visiting the hospital.
Payment ceases when the hospitalised child is discharged.
Note the client and their partner (if any) do not need any further reason why they are not able to care for the eligible child.
A letter from the hospital social worker should be requested verifying that a dependent child has been, or will be admitted to hospital.
This letter should show:
- the date of admission and
- the expected date of discharge

- has a sibling for whom a Child Disability Allowance is paid
Note the client and their partner (if any) do not need a good and sufficient reason why they are not able to care for the eligible child.
The subsidy will cease when:
- the Child Disability Allowance child no longer get Child Disability Allowance or
- the dependent child turns 14 years of age or

chunks.title: Child's caregiver also cares for a child receiving Child Disability Allowance — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Child's caregiver also cares for a child receiving Child Disability Allowance
Childcare Subsidy may be paid for up to 50 hours per week when the eligible child's principal caregiver also cares for a child:
- for whom a Child Disability Allowance is paid
This includes a principal temporary caregiver of a child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid.
The subsidy will cease when:
- that other dependent child can no longer receive Child Disability Allowance or
- the eligible child turns 5 years of age or
- up to 4 weeks after the eligible child turns 5 years old and not yet attending school or
- the qualifications are no longer met
whichever is earliest.
Note the client and their partner (if any) do not need any further reason why they are not able to care for the eligible child.

chunks.title: Client Activities — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Client Activities
An OSCAR subsidy for a child is available only to enable the child's principal caregiver to undertake one of the following:
- employment (whether full-time or part-time, and whether permanent, temporary, or casual)
- any employment related training (for a client with work obligations)
- an activity included in an existing Job Seeker Agreement
- an employment-related training course offered by a course-provider accredited by the New Zealand Qualifications Authority or
- a course of study at a secondary school or a tertiary educational institution
This includes a principal temporary caregiver of a child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid.
The subsidy will only be paid for the hours the client is participating in an activity. This will include any travel time that is involved.

chunks.title: Client's IRD number — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: MSD may make a written request for evidence of an IRD number for a client who is being paid Childcare Subsidy and any other type of taxable assistance.

chunks.title: Setting or extending the timeframe for providing evidence — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: MSD must provide the client with a minimum of 10 working days to provide IRD number evidence that has been requested in writing. MSD can extend the 10 working day period (in writing) if the client has a reasonable explanation for requiring more than 10 days to provide evidence of their IRD number. This considers factors outside the client's control that cause delays, including, but not limited to: - client has a family emergency that caused a delay - processing delays with an external agency (e.g. Inland Revenue, Department of Internal Affairs, etc) - client does not speak English as a first language and has difficulty navigating evidence requirements - client has limited access to the internet, a device, or their local service centre - client has a physical or intellectual disability that makes accessing services difficult - client is injured, disabled, or has a medical condition that makes accessing services difficult.

chunks.title: Notice following a No Match result — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about client's IRD numbers. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information, or there's an error, MSD should ask the client (in writing) to provide evidence of their IRD number. In the written request for evidence of the IRD number, MSD must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and the match was unsuccessful, and - giving the client a minimum of 10 working days to provide their IRD number evidence or the client's assistance must be suspended. Note suspension does not apply to Childcare Assistance. Example Isla is working and receiving Childcare Subsidy. MSD holds an IRD number on record. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Isla's IRD number. MSD provides 10 working days in writing, for Isla to provide evidence of their IRD number. MSD's decision to give 10 working days to provide evidence is based on: - Isla already having an IRD number - Isla not having any significant barriers to getting evidence of their IRD number - MSD's obligation to provide a minimum of 10 working days to provide the information.

chunks.title: MSD must suspend assistance if evidence of IRD number is not received — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: MSD must suspend all taxable and income tested assistance the client is getting, except their Childcare Subsidy, if evidence of an IRD number is not provided within 10 working days from the written (adverse action) request, or extended period if this has been applied. Example Koa has been receiving Childcare Subsidy and Sole Parent Support for 1 year. MSD does not have an IRD number on file for Koa. MSD sends a written request giving 10 working days for Koa to provide evidence of their IRD number because they receive Sole Parent Support which is a taxable benefit. MSD receives no response to this request. MSD suspends Koa's Sole Parent Support (but not Koa's Childcare Subsidy) because Koa has not supplied MSD with evidence of their IRD number within the timeframe provided.

chunks.title: IRD evidence may not be required in some circumstances — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: MSD may not need evidence of an IRD number when the client is only receiving the Childcare Subsidy. MSD can still informally ask for an IRD number. In addition, IRD number evidence may not be required when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - significant factors, that are outside the client or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of their IRD number (e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence), and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided or - significant factors related to a health, injury or disability that are outside the client's control that prevents them from providing evidence of an IRD number, and - an agent cannot be appointed to act on the client's behalf. MSD can determine at a later point to request evidence of the IRD number. Example Sienna is 23 and receiving Childcare Subsidy. Sienna's mother (Sara) is Sienna's agent and acts on Sienna's behalf with MSD. Sienna does not have an IRD number and Sara is not a recognised agent for Sienna for Inland Revenue. Sienna has a serious head injury, is unconscious and expected to be in hospital for at least 8 weeks. Due to their injury, Sienna is not able to give consent to appoint Sara as an agent for Inland Revenue to apply for an IRD number. MSD can request this information later when Sienna's situation has changed. Note there is different guidance for requesting evidence of an IRD number for partner's whose income is relevant to a client's Childcare Subsidy or when a client is applying for Childcare Subsidy.

chunks.title: Clients with partners — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Clients with partners
If a client has a partner, they are generally expected to provide care for the child while the client is in employment, training, study or other activity.
However, a Childcare Subsidy can be paid for up to 50 hours per week where the partner cannot look after the child because:
- the partner is in employment (including full-time, part-time, temporary or casual) or
- the partner is participating in a rehabilitation programme or
- the partner is attending employment related training or
- the partner is participating in a suitable activity under section 102A(1)(f) or
- the partner is participating in a suitable activity under section 123B or
- the partner is attending a course of study at a secondary school or a tertiary educational institute or
- there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner cannot look after the child
As a guideline, good and sufficient reasons would include situations where the partner may be able to get an exemption from their work obligations. For example, where the partner is ill or is caring for someone who is ill.
Note when a Child Disability Allowance is paid for that child or another dependent child, or one of the dependent children is in hospital, then a good and sufficient reason is not required at that time.

chunks.title: Clients with partners — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Clients with partners
If a client has a partner, they are generally expected to provide care for the child while the client is in employment, training, study or undertaking employment related training.
However, an OSCAR Subsidy can be paid up to 20 or 50 hours per week where the partner cannot look after the child because:
- the partner is in employment (including full-time, part-time, temporary or casual) or
- the partner is undertaking employment related training or
- the partner is participating in a suitable activity under section 102A(1)(f) or
- the partner is participating in a suitable activity under section 123B or
- the partner is attending a course of study at a secondary school or a tertiary educational institute or
- there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner cannot look after the child
As a guideline, good and sufficient reasons would include situations where the partner has an exemption from their work obligations.
For more information see:
- Core policy Relationship status for benefit

chunks.title: Closures due to COVID-19 requirements — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Closures due to COVID-19 requirements
When a childcare centre is closed due to COVID-19 requirements, Childcare Subsidy can continue being paid if the client still qualifies. A fee does not need to be charged to hold the child's place open for payment to continue.
A centre may close due to COVID-19 requirements because they:
- must close due to COVID-19 Alert Level 4
- are connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19 and have been instructed to close
- are not able to operate safely and within public health guidelines
- temporarily do not have any children needing childcare because of COVID-19
This is not an exhaustive list. If a centre has closed and you are unsure if it is due to COVID-19 requirements, please check the COVID-19 Alert System website for the most up to date COVID-19 guidelines.
Note Childcare Subsidy cannot continue being paid to a centre that is closed because it is not financially viable for them to stay open, or for any other reason that is not related to COVID-19 requirements.
## Number of weeks payment can continue
There is no limit on how long Childcare Subsidy can be paid when a child is absent due to COVID-19 requirements.
However, the subsidy can only be paid for a period that relates to COVID-19 requirements.
If a centre is closed for longer than what is needed due to COVID-19 requirements, Childcare Subsidy can only be paid for the period that relates to COVID-19 requirements.
## Example
Liam's daughter usually goes to a small, family run childcare centre. They had to close for 4 weeks when New Zealand was at COVID-19 Alert Level 4. They then stayed closed for an extra 2 weeks due to a family bereavement.
Liam's Childcare Subsidy continued for the first 4 weeks the centre was closed because this was due to COVID-19 requirements. Childcare Subsidy was stopped for the extra 2 weeks because the centre was closed for a reason not related to COVID-19 requirements.

chunks.title: COVID-19 absences and closures — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: When a child is absent from childcare or the childcare centre is closed due to COVID-19 requirements, Childcare Subsidy can continue being paid if the client still qualifies. A fee does not have to be charged to hold the child's place open for payment to continue.

chunks.title: COVID-19 requirements — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: COVID-19 requirements means New Zealand's COVID-19 Alert System. The alert system is designed to manage and minimise the risk of COVID-19. There are 4 alert levels and each one sets out the public health and social measures we must take. For example, at Alert Level 3 people generally need to stay home except for essential activities like grocery shopping. Each alert level places restrictions on things like travel, business activity and personal movement. Alert levels can apply to the whole country, or to parts of it. Different areas of New Zealand may be at different alert levels at the same time.

chunks.title: How COVID-19 requirements affect childcare — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: COVID-19 requirements can affect childcare in a number of ways. Children may need to be absent because they are unwell, connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19, or are at high risk of severe illness if they contract COVID-19. Centres may need to close because they are unable to operate within public health guidelines, they are connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19, or an Alert Level 4 lockdown is in place. An absence or closure due to COVID-19 requirements means that a child is absent, or a centre is closed because it is required by the COVID-19 Alert System guidelines. Generally verification about the reason for an absence or closure due to COVID-19 requirements is not required. However if you have doubts about the situation, you can ask the client or centre for verification.

chunks.title: Client must continue to qualify — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: The client must continue to qualify for Childcare Subsidy for it to be paid during an absence or closure due to COVID-19 requirements. If the client has a change in circumstances that affects their eligibility, their Childcare Subsidy must be reviewed. If they no longer qualify, Childcare Subsidy must be stopped.

chunks.title: Example — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: Katie has been getting Childcare Subsidy of 25 hours per week because her son attends childcare while she works. 20 hours are for the time Katie is at work and 5 hours are for the time she spends travelling between work and the centre. During Alert Level 3 Katie worked from home but her work hours stayed the same. Her son did not go to childcare because Katie's mum looked after him. Katie's Childcare Subsidy continued during her son's absence, but it reduced to 20 hours per week because she did not need to travel between work and the centre. Katie has now lost her job and her last day will be this Friday. She intends to send her son back to childcare at Alert Level 2. Katie's Childcare Subsidy will be reduced to 9 hours per week because she is no longer engaged in an approved activity.

chunks.title: Debts — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Debts
A debt is created when a client or childcare centre is overpaid.
Debts can be recovered from the client or provider depending on the reason why the debt was created.
Debts should be recovered from the parent when the child continues to be present at the centre, and a debt has arisen as a result of one of the following circumstances:
- change in parent's income
- absences - when no charge is made for absences by the childcare centre
- change in parent's circumstances i.e. relationship status
- change in application typeExample if a client finishes training or ceases work and is now only eligible for 9 hours
- change in care arrangement
- if the child or parent goes overseas, we can only pay the subsidy if the costs are continuing. For example if an absence fee is charged. The debt must be established from the day after the parent leaves the country.
- admitted/discharged from hospital
- imprisoned/held in custody
Debts should be recovered from the provider, when a debt has arisen from one of the following circumstances:
- child leaves the centre permanently - the childcare centre knowing the child has left cannot accept the money in good faith
- childcare centre is closed - centres may close during school holiday periods. This excludes statutory holidays
- caregiver is unavailable - for home based care providers there are occasions when the caregiver cannot provide childcare
- as a result of Twenty hours Early Childhood Education being paid to the centre for hours for which they also receive Childcare Subsidy
Note it is important that clear notes are put on CMS to show how the debt was created and who is responsible for the refund.

chunks.title: Debts — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Debts
A debt is created when a client or centre is overpaid.
Debts can be recovered from the client or provider depending on the reason why the debt was created.
## Client debt
Debts should be recovered from the parent when the child continues to be present at the centre, and a debt has arisen as a result of one of the following circumstances.
- change in parent's income
- change in parent's circumstances i.e. relationship status
- change in application typeExample if a client finishes training or ceases work and is now only eligible for 9 hours
- change in care arrangement
- admitted or discharged from hospital
- imprisoned or held in custody
## Provider debt
Debts should be recovered from the provider when a debt has arisen from one of the following circumstances:
- child leaves the centre permanently - the OSCAR centre knowing the child has left cannot accept the money in good faith
- OSCAR centre is closed - centres may close during school holiday periods. This excludes statutory holidays
- caregiver is unavailable - for home based care providers there are occasions when the caregiver cannot provide childcare
Note it is important that clear notes are put on CMS to show how the debt was created and who is responsible for the refund.

chunks.title: Declarations — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Declarations
Declaration forms are sent to clients receiving an OSCAR subsidy 28 days before each school term ends.
They are issued to check if the care arrangements for a child are changing and to obtain details of any school holiday programme the child may be attending.

chunks.title: Dependent child — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
A dependent child for Childcare Subsidy is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of the client
- maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
- not a child for whom Orphan's Benefit or an Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid
- in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but has been returned to their parent's care
A dependent child for Childcare Subsidy does not include a:
- child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 and
- young person getting a Young Parent Payment and their child (see Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples)
In some situations, a child may not be living at home but is still considered to be a dependent child

chunks.title: Eligible child — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Eligible child
To receive a Childcare Subsidy, the client's child must be:
- dependent on the caregiver applying for the subsidy (this includes a child for whom Unsupported Childs Benefit or Orphans Benefit is being paid)
- under the age of 5 years old or
- aged over 5 years and enrolled to attend a cohort entry school on the term or mid-term start date, on or immediately after the child's 5th birthday (whichever is closer)
- aged less than 5 years and 4 weeks and not yet attending a school with continuous entry or
- under the age of 6 years old if a Child Disability Allowance is paid and
- attending an approved early childhood education programme or service
- for 3 hours a week or more
For more information see:
- Dependent child
- Approved early childhood education programme or service

chunks.title: Eligible child — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Eligible child
To get an OSCAR Subsidy, the client's child must be:
- dependent on the caregiver who is applying for the subsidy (this includes when the caregiver is getting Unsupported Child's Benefit or Orphan's Benefit for the child)
- aged: from 5 to 13 years old orbetween 14 and 18 years old and getting Child Disability Allowance and
- from 5 to 13 years old or
- between 14 and 18 years old and getting Child Disability Allowance and
- attending an approved OSCAR programme for a total of 3 or more hours a week

chunks.title: Fees — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Fees
Some childcare centres charge a flat fee and other centres charge a fee based on the hours of attendance of a child.
## Centre charges a fee based on the attendance of a child
When a childcare centre charges a fee based on the hours attended by the child, we need to calculate the hourly fee.
To get an hourly fee the weekly fee must be divided by the number of hours the child attends.
Example 1
Fee for attending
$100.00
Divided by hours attending each week
25 hours
Hourly fee equals
$4.00
The amount payable in this example is $4.00 per hour.
Example 2
Fee for attending
$350.00
Divided by hours attending each week
50 hours
Hourly fee equals
$7.00
The fee is higher than the maximum rate we can pay $6.72 (as at 1 April 2026). This client would be entitled to receive the maximum hourly rate of the subsidy.
We cannot pay more than the maximum rate.
## Centre charges a flat fee
If the childcare centre charges a flat fee, calculate the amount of Childcare Subsidy payable by dividing the centre's weekly fee by the number of hours the child is enrolled for.
Enrolled hours means, the number of hours the child is booked to attend the centre for, and the parent pays for, (whether or not the child attends).
## Example 3
Step 1
Weekly childcare centre fee
$240.00
Divided by enrolled hours
35 hours
Hourly fee equals
$6.85
The fee is higher than the maximum rate payable. We can only pay at the maximum rate.
Step 2
maximum hourly rate payable equals
$6.72 (as at 1 April 2026)
multiply by eligible hours
35 hours
weekly Childcare Subsidy equals
$235.20
## Maximum subsidy paid per hour
We cannot pay out more than the maximum hourly rate.
Example if a childcare centre charges $7.00 per hour we can only pay out the current maximum hourly rate $6.72 (as at 1 April 2026).

chunks.title: Fifty hours a week subsidy — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Fifty hours a week subsidy
In addition to the Childcare Subsidy qualifications, up to 50 hours a week subsidised childcare may be available to clients who are:
- in paid employment (including full-time, part-time, temporary and casual) or
- participating in an employment-related training course offered by a course provider accredited by the New Zealand Qualifications Authority or
- participating in an activity to improve work readiness or
- attending a course of study at a Tertiary Institution or Secondary School or
- temporarily unable to continue employment because of illness or injury or
- attending an approved rehabilitation programme or
- seriously disabled or ill caregivers or
- getting a Child Disability Allowance for a child or their sibling or
- caregivers of a sibling who is in hospital
Note if a client has a partner there must be a good and sufficient reason why they are not able to care for the child. Exception when the parents qualify for a Child Disability Allowance for the child attending the childcare service.

chunks.title: Four week extension — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Four week extension
Children who attend a continuous entry school at age 5 will be paid up until the Monday following the child's birthday unless they have applied for the 4 week extension.
We can continue to pay a Childcare Subsidy for up to 4 weeks after the child turns 5 years old, unless they are attending a school with cohort entry.
If a child is going to a school with cohort entry, Childcare Subsidy is payable until the school term or mid-term start date immediately on or after their 5th birthday, whichever is closer.

chunks.title: Guidelines to financial assistance for childcare costs — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Guidelines to financial assistance for childcare costs
The following forms of assistance are available to help people with childcare costs.
Financial assistance
Purpose
Childcare Subsidy
Childcare Subsidy is a non-taxable payment that aims to assist clients with pre-school aged dependent children to undertake and remain in employment, education or training.
People who do not meet the specific activity criteria may still be able to get up to 9 hours a week of Childcare Subsidy.
It can also be used for families where the principal caregiver, or the child or children of the principal caregiver are experiencing, serious ill health or disability.
Early Learning Payment
Early Learning Payment is a non-taxable payment to provide earlier access to early childhood education for families with specific needs.
Early Learning Payment helps with the costs of early childhood education for children aged 18 months to 3 years, who are from families enrolled in Family Start or Early Start programmes.
Flexible Childcare Assistance
Flexible Childcare Assistance provides financial assistance for informal childcare costs to support caregivers who are considered at risk of long-term benefit receipt and unable to access formal childcare while participating in a specified employment activity.
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment is a non-taxable payment providing financial assistance with childcare costs for pre-school aged children to enable young parents who are:
- getting Young Parent Payment or is a partner of a specified beneficiary to meet their youth activity obligations or
- not getting a main benefit to return to, or remain in, secondary education
OSCAR
OSCAR (Out of School Care and Recreation Subsidy) is a non-taxable payment that aims to assist low income caregivers with school aged dependent children enter and remain in employment.
It can also be used for families where the principal caregiver, or the child or children of the principal caregiver are experiencing, serious ill health or disability

chunks.text: Below are examples of using Childcare Subsidy to pay for home-based educator top up payments.

chunks.title: Example 2 - working couple qualify for Childcare Subsidy for 50 hours a week — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: Reina and Nick both work full-time (50 hours a week) and earn $2500 gross per week. They have 3 children Dave is 9, Steph is 6, and Gina is 4 years old. Dave and Steph are already at school. Gina attends a total of 50 hours of home-based early childhood education while Reina and Nick are at work. She is enrolled with 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE) which covers her attendance for 5 hours a day, 4 days a week. The home-based educator charges $12 per hour for the 30 remaining (standard) early childhood education and childcare hours that Gina is in home-based childcare. This is a weekly fee of $360. The educator also charges a home-based educator top up payment of $4 per hour for the same hours as 20 Hours ECE. This is an additional charge of $80 a week. Reina and Nick qualify for Childcare Subsidy at a rate of $2.09 per hour (as at 1 April 2026) for 50 hours a week. They get Childcare Subsidy for the 30 hours outside of 20 Hours ECE. This is a total of $60.90 a week. They also get Childcare Subsidy for the home-based educator top up payment charged for the same hours as 20 Hours ECE. This is a total of $40.60 a week Total hours in home-based childcare 50 Hours enrolled in 20 Hours ECE (4 hours x 5 days) 20 Standard childcare charge $12 per hour (for 30 hours outside of 20 Hours ECE) $360 per week (30 hours x $12 per hour) Childcare Subsidy entitlement (for 30 hours outside of 20 Hours ECE) $62.70 per week (30 hours x $2.09 per hour as at 1 April 2026) Home-based educator top up payment charge $4 per hour (for the 20 hours of 20 Hours ECE) $80 per week (20 hours x $4 per hour) Childcare Subsidy entitlement (for 20 hours home-based educator top up payment charge) $41.80 per week (20 hours x $2.09 as at 1 April 2026) Total Childcare Subsidy entitlement $104.50 per week

chunks.title: Home-based educator top up payments — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: Home-based educators can charge a home-based educator top up payment for the same hours as 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE). This is to cover the difference between the 20 Hours ECE funding and the educator's usual hourly rate. Home-based early childhood education providers may charge the top up payment on the educator's behalf. Example a home-based educator charges $10 per hour per child for hours outside of 20 Hours ECE. The service they are contracted to passes on $6 per hour for each child from the 20 Hours ECE funding. The educator can charge a home-based educator top up payment of $4 per hour. Eligible clients can choose to take up Childcare Subsidy to pay for: - standard childcare hours only or - home-based educator top up payments charged for 20 Hours ECE hours only or - a combination of the two, but not for the same hours

chunks.title: Hours payable for home-based educator top up payments — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: Eligible clients can get Childcare Subsidy to help pay for home-based educator top up payments charged for the same hours as 20 Hours ECE. If a client uses Childcare Subsidy to pay for home-based educator top up payments, these hours are deducted from the total hours of Childcare Subsidy the client is eligible for. This means a client who is eligible to 50 hours of Childcare Subsidy can get the subsidy for 20 hours of home-based educator top up payments and 30 hours of standard childcare fees. For more information see: - Home-based educator top up payments examples - 20 Hours Early Childhood Education and up to 9 hours Childcare Subsidy - 20 Hours Early Childhood Education and up to 50 hours Childcare Subsidy

chunks.title: Rate payable for home-based educator top up payments — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: When Childcare Subsidy is used to help pay for home-based educator top up payments, the amount payable for those hours is the lesser of the: - maximum hourly rate of Childcare Subsidy available to the client or - actual hourly home-based educator top up payment charged Note Childcare Subsidy for home-based educator top up payments may be paid at a different rate to the fees for standard childcare hours.

chunks.title: Example - rate payable for home-based educator top up — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: A client has their child enrolled for 20 hours of 20 Hours ECE and 30 hours of standard childcare with a home-based educator. The educator charges $10 per hour but for 20 Hours ECE, they get $7 per hour passed through from their provider. This leaves $3 per hour that they charge as a home-based educator top up payment. The client is entitled to a maximum Childcare Subsidy rate of $6.72 per hour (as at 1 April 2026). This means that they can get $3 per hour for the home-based educator top up payment and $6.72 per hour for the standard childcare hours. chunks.title: Hours of attendance — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Hours of attendance
Generally, the number of hours of Childcare Subsidy payable is the same as a child’s hours of attendance, up to a maximum of 50 per week.
The rate of Childcare Subsidy payable cannot be more than the fee charged.
Childcare Subsidy is not payable for hours of attendance if those hours are funded through another government programme except when Childcare Subsidy is being used for home-based educator top-up payments for the same hours that 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE) is paid.
Example if a child gets 20 Hours ECE for centre-based childcare, they cannot get Childcare Subsidy for the same hours.
## Exception
If a child gets 20 Hours ECE for childcare provided by a home-based educator they may be able to get Childcare Subsidy for the same hours if they are eligible.

chunks.title: Hours of attendance — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Hours of attendance
MSD can only pay for the maximum hours the OSCAR subsidy can be paid.
## School term time maximum hours
The maximum number of hours payable is 20 hours per week.
Example if during the school term a child attends for 25 hours per week, the most we can pay is for 20 hours per week.
## Holiday time maximum hours
The maximum number of hours payable is 50 hours per week.
Example if during holiday time a child attends for 55 hours per week, we cannot pay more than the maximum of 50 hours a week.
Also the OSCAR subsidy cannot exceed the fee charged.

chunks.title: In study — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## In study
Childcare Subsidy may be paid for up to 50 hours per week if the qualifications are met and the caregiver:
- is in education
- needs assistance with childcare to be able to undertake the education and
- does not have a partner who can provide childcare or there is a good reason why a partner is unable to provide childcare
The subsidy will only be paid for the time that the client is required to study (including travel time).
For more information see:
- Clients with partners
- Assessment of travel time
## Client on school holidays
It is generally accepted that students who are undertaking a full-time study course will be required to study during vacation periods. Therefore the subsidy may continue during these periods.
The Christmas break and summer vacation would not usually be included as study time, the subsidy should be reviewed at the time to ensure the client meets all qualifications.

chunks.title: In study - OSCAR — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## In study - OSCAR
OSCAR Subsidy may be paid for up to 20 or 50 hours per week if the qualifications are met and the caregiver:
- is in education
- needs assistance with childcare to be able to undertake the education and
- does not have a partner who can provide childcare or there is a good reason why a partner is unable to provide childcare
The subsidy will only be paid for the time that the client is required to study (including travel time).
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Clients with partners
- Assessing travel time
- Hours of attendance

chunks.title: In training — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## In training
Childcare Subsidy may be paid for up to 50 hours per week if the qualifications are met and the caregiver:
- is in approved employment-related training
- needs assistance with childcare to be able to undertake the employment-related training and
- does not have a partner who can provide childcare or there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner is unable to provide childcare
The subsidy will only be paid for the time that the client is in training (including travel time).
For more information see:
- Clients with partners
- Assessing travel time
## Approved employment related training
A course is considered employment-related if it is designed to increase employment potential by developing greater work skills.
The training provider should be accredited with the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA).
Rehabilitation programmes provided by reputable organisations would generally be regarded as providing appropriate employment potential. Therefore they would meet the Childcare Subsidy qualification.
Only if the client would otherwise be denied an employment-related training opportunity, should courses that do not meet the above criteria be considered for Childcare Subsidy.

chunks.title: In training - OSCAR — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## In training - OSCAR
OSCAR Subsidy may be paid for up to 20 or 50 hours per week if the qualifications are met and the caregiver:
- is in approved employment-related training
- needs assistance with childcare to be able to undertake the employment-related training and
- does not have a partner who can provide childcare or there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner is unable to provide childcare
The subsidy will only be paid for the time that the client is in training (including travel time).
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Clients with partners
- Assessing travel time
## Approved employment related training
A course is considered employment-related if it is designed to increase employment potential by developing greater work skills.
The training provider should be accredited with the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA).
Rehabilitation programmes provided by reputable organisations would generally be regarded as providing appropriate employment potential. Therefore they would meet the OSCAR subsidy qualification.
Only if the client would otherwise be denied an employment-related training opportunity, should courses that do not meet the above criteria be considered for OSCAR subsidy.
