chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The objectives of the childcare assistance programme are to assist:
- low income parents with pre-school children to enter employment, training or education and
- caregivers and/or children to access licensed childcare centres, family day care projects or chartered Te Kohanga Reo and
- low income parents with school aged children to enter employment or participate in an activity to improve work readiness and
- access approved out of school care and school holiday programmes (OSCAR)
## Community Services Cards
Community Services Cards are not automatically issued to clients who get non-beneficiary assistance (unless they get Accommodation Supplement) and they must make a separate application for a card.
Clients who get Accommodation Supplement qualify for a Community Services Card and are sent a card automatically without having to make a separate application. See:

chunks.title: Ministry of Education +10 funding — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Ministry of Education +10 funding
The Ministry of Education pay a number of different payments to Licensed ECE providers.
The funding model is made up of many parts and is explained fully in the ECE Funding Handbook.
This handbook is designed to be a "one-stop-shop" for all providers of payment information about early childhood funding including:
- 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE)
- +10 funding
The +10 hours is one method of funding, this payment is made based on child places, not children.
We do not pay subsidy for the same hours that a child is being funded by 20 Hours ECE funding, but +10 funding does not have any impact on Childcare Subsidy payments.
For more information see:

chunks.title: New childcare centres — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## New childcare centres
The following proof is required from any new centre that wants to be paid a Childcare Subsidy:
- proof that they are a licensed centre (issued by the Ministry of Education)
- proof of bank account
- details of their postal and residential address
- service providers name, phone number and a copy of their signature
- fee structure which includes any centre closures over the year
Childcare centres also need to tell us whether they are receiving Twenty hours Early Childhood Education funding.
Fax the details to Data Integrity, who will enter the information on SWIFTT.
Ensure a file is set up for the childcare centre, a liaison officer is assigned and forms and pamphlets made available.
Under no circumstances can we pay a Childcare Subsidy to a childcare centre that is not approved.

chunks.title: New OSCAR centres — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## New OSCAR centres
The following proof is required from any new centre that wants to be paid an OSCAR subsidy:
- proof that they are an approved centre (available from Ministry of Social Development Approvals)
- proof of bank account
- details of their postal and residential address
- service providers name, phone number and a copy of their signature
- fee structure which includes any centre closures over the year
Fax these details to Data Integrity, who will then enter the information on SWIFTT.
Ensure a file is set up for the centre, a liaison officer is assigned and forms and pamphlets are made available.
Under no circumstances can we pay a subsidy to a provider that is not approved.

chunks.title: Absences due to COVID-19 requirements — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Absences due to COVID-19 requirements
When a child is absent due to COVID-19 requirements, OSCAR Subsidy can continue being paid if the client still qualifies. A fee does not need to be charged to hold the child's place open for payment to continue.
A child may be absent due to COVID-19 requirements because they are:
- unwell and cannot attend OSCAR while unwell
- at high risk of severe illness if they contract COVID-19
- in self-isolation or quarantine due to COVID-19 public health requirements
- connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19
- being kept home during Alert Level 3
This is not an exhaustive list. If a child is absent and you are unsure if it is due to COVID-19 requirements, please check the COVID-19 Alert System website for the most up to date COVID-19 guidelines.
## Number of weeks payment can continue
There is no limit on how long OSCAR Subsidy can be paid when a child is absent due to COVID-19 requirements. However the subsidy can only be paid for a period that relates to COVID-19 requirements.
If a child is absent for other reasons, you will need to check the general absence guidelines to see how long they can be paid.
## Example
Jian's daughter Jenny was absent from OSCAR care for 7 weeks because she was sick. At COVID-19 Alert Level 2, parents to be stricter about keeping sick children home from childcare and OSCAR.
Because Jenny's absence was due to COVID-19 requirements, OSCAR Subsidy continued being paid for the full 7 weeks.

chunks.title: Amount payable during COVID-19 absence or closure — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Amount payable during COVID-19 absence or closure
When a child is absent or a provider is closed due to COVID-19 requirements, the usual weekly amount the provider got before the absence or closure is the amount they will continue to get. This is regardless of whether a fee is charged to hold the child's place, and how much the fee is.
For example, if a provider usually gets $100 when the child attends, this is the amount they will get when the child is absent, or the provider is closed, regardless of the actual fee charged by the provider.
Note if during an absence or closure, the client decides their child will not return, payment must be stopped.
If a change in circumstance happens during an absence or closure, the OSCAR Subsidy must be reviewed, and the rate of payment may change.

chunks.title: OSCAR closures due to COVID-19 requirements — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## OSCAR closures due to COVID-19 requirements
When an OSCAR provider is closed due to COVID-19 requirements, OSCAR Subsidy can continue being paid if the client still qualifies.
A fee does not need to be charged to hold the child's place open for payment to continue.
A provider may close due to COVID-19 requirements because they:
- must close due to COVID-19 Alert Levels 3 or 4
- are connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19 and have been instructed to close
- are not able to operate safely and within public health guidelines
- temporarily do not have any children needing OSCAR care because of COVID-19.Note OSCAR Subsidy cannot continue being paid to a provider that is closed because it is not financially viable for them to stay open, or for any other reason that is not related to COVID-19 requirements
This is not an exhaustive list. If a provider has closed and you are unsure if it is due to COVID-19 requirements, please check the COVID-19 Alert System website for the most up to date COVID-19 guidelines.
Note OSCAR Subsidy cannot continue being paid to a provider that is closed because it is not financially viable for them to stay open, or for any other reason that is not related to COVID-19 requirements.
## Number of weeks payment can continue
There is no limit on how long OSCAR Subsidy can be paid when a provider is closed due to COVID-19 requirements. However, the subsidy must only continue for periods that relate to COVID-19 requirements.
If a provider is closed for longer than what is needed due to COVID-19 requirements, OSCAR Subsidy can only be paid for the period that relates to COVID-19 requirements.
## Example
Maria's son usually goes to a small, family run OSCAR provider. They had to close for 2 weeks when New Zealand was at COVID-19 Alert Level 3. They then stayed closed for an extra 2 weeks due to a family bereavement.
Maria's OSCAR Subsidy continued for the first 2 weeks the provider was closed because this was due to COVID-19 requirements. OSCAR Subsidy was stopped for the extra 2 weeks because the provider was closed for a reason not related to COVID-19 requirements.

chunks.title: COVID-19 absences and closures — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: When a child is absent from OSCAR care or the provider is closed due to COVID-19 requirements, OSCAR Subsidy can continue being paid if the client still qualifies. A fee does not have to be charged to hold the child's place open for payments to continue.

chunks.title: COVID-19 requirements — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: COVID-19 requirements means New Zealand's COVID-19 Alert System. The alert system is designed to manage and minimise the risk of COVID-19. There are 4 alert levels and each one sets out the public health and social measures we must take. For example, at Alert Level 3 people generally need to stay home except for essential activities like grocery shopping. Each alert level places restrictions on things like travel, business activity and personal movement. Alert levels can apply to the whole country, or to parts of it. Different areas of New Zealand can be at different alert levels at the same time.

chunks.title: How COVID-19 requirements affect OSCAR — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: COVID-19 requirements can affect OSCAR in a number of ways. Children may need to be absent because they are unwell, connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19, or are at high risk of severe illness if they contract COVID-19. Providers may need to close because they are unable to operate within public health guidelines, they are connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19, or an Alert Level 4 lockdown is in place. An absence or closure due to COVID-19 requirements means that a child is absent, or a provider is closed because it is required by the COVID-19 Alert System guidelines. Generally verification about the reason for an absence or closure due to COVID-19 requirements is not required. However if you have doubts about the situation, you can ask the client or provider for verification.

chunks.title: Client must continue to qualify — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: The client must continue to qualify for OSCAR Subsidy for it to be paid during an absence or closure due to COVID-19 requirements. If the client has a change in circumstances that affects their eligibility, their OSCAR Subsidy must be reviewed. If they no longer qualify, OSCAR Subsidy must be stopped.

chunks.title: Example — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: Aroha has been getting OSCAR Subsidy of 20 hours per week because her son attends OSCAR care while she works. Her payments continued while the OSCAR provider was closed at Alert Level 3 because Aroha's work situation stayed the same and the closure was due to COVID-19 requirements. Aroha has now lost her job and her last day will be this Friday. Her OSCAR Subsidy will stop from the beginning of next week as Aroha is no longer engaged in an approved activity.

chunks.title: OSCAR Providers and GST — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## OSCAR Providers and GST
The OSCAR Subsidy does not include GST as the payment is being made to the Childcare provider on behalf of the client.
If the Childcare provider is registered, they are required to include GST as part of the fee for the service provided.
For any queries about GST the provider should contact Inland Revenue to discuss the centres liability.

chunks.title: OSCAR subsidy and overnight camps — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: During the school holidays parents may choose to enrol their children in overnight camps. Children generally stay all week, and most parents have an entitlement of 50 hours' OSCAR subsidy. Entitlement is either: - 50 hours OSCAR subsidy or - the camp fees whichever is the lesser. Some families either: - don't have entitlement to 50 hours OSCAR subsidy per week, but still want their child to attend the camp or - don't necessarily want to leave their child for a whole week Examples of both types of payment are detailed below.

chunks.title: Example A — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: The child is enrolled in a holiday camp which costs $250.00 for the full week. The child's parent works 50 hours per week and is entitled to a subsidy of $6.72 per hour (maximum weekly payment for 50 hours is $336.00 as at 1 April 2026). Payment in this case is $250.00 as the camp fee is the lesser amount.

chunks.title: Example B — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: The child is enrolled in a holiday camp which costs $150.00 for the full week. The child's parent works 50 hours per week and is entitled to a subsidy of $5.36 per hour (maximum weekly payment for 50 hours is $268.00 as at 1 April 2026). Payment in this case is $150.00 as the camp fee is the lesser amount.

chunks.title: Example A — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: The child is enrolled in a holiday camp which costs $250.00 for the full week and the child will be attending for the week. The child's parent works 35 hours per week and is entitled to a subsidy of $6.72 per hour as at 1 April 2026 (maximum weekly payment for 35 hours is $235.20). Payment in this case is $235.20 as at 1 April 2026. The parent would need to make up the difference of $14.80 to pay for the camp in full.

chunks.title: Example B — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: The child is enrolled in a holiday camp which costs $200.00 for the full week. The child's parent works 20 hours per week, and is entitled to a subsidy of $6.72 per hour as at 1 April 2026 (maximum weekly payment for 20 hours is $134.40). The child attends camp for 2 days only but the camp still charges for the whole week. The subsidy paid is $134.40 (20 hours' subsidy). The parent still needs to pay the additional $65.60 as at 1 April 2026.

chunks.title: OSCAR Subsidy — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## OSCAR Subsidy
OSCAR (Out of School Care and Recreational Subsidy) is a non-taxable payment that aims to assist low income caregivers to enter and remain in employment.
This includes a principal temporary caregiver of a child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid.
It can also be used for families where the principal caregiver, or the child or children of the principal caregiver are experiencing, serious ill health or disability.

chunks.title: Paid employment — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Paid employment
Childcare Subsidy may be paid up to 50 hours a week if the qualifications are met and the caregiver is
- in paid employment
- needs assistance with childcare to undertake employment and
- does not have a partner who can provide childcare or there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner is unable to provide childcare
The subsidy will only be paid for the time that the client is participating in employment (this includes lunch breaks), training or education (including travel time).
If the client's employment is during the night the subsidy will be paid for the time that the client needs to sleep during the day.
Note paid employment includes when the client is still employed, but not at work such as sick, annual leave, or when weather conditions do not permit them to work. It does not cover periods of parental leave.
For more information see:
- Clients with partners
- Assessing travel time
## Between employment
If the current employment ceases and the parent has further confirmed employment, the subsidy can be paid for a further 10 working days between employment.
If the break is for a longer period than 10 working days then the childcare subsidy must be stopped from the date after employment ceased.

chunks.title: Paid employment — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Paid employment
OSCAR subsidy can only be paid during the time that the caregiver is in employment (including travel time and lunch breaks) up to a maximum of:
- 20 hours a week (outside of school hours) during the school term or
- 50 hours a week (during the day) throughout the school holidays
If the client's employment is during the night the subsidy will be paid for the time that the client needs to sleep during the day.
Note paid employment includes when the client is still employed, but not at work, such as sick leave, annual leave, or when weather conditions do not permit them to work. It does not cover periods of parental leave.
For more information see:
- Clients with partners
- Assessing travel time
- Weather conditions
If the client is in employment but becomes temporarily sick, OSCAR can be paid for a maximum of 12 weeks. For more information see:
- Temporary illness
## Between employment
If the current employment ceases and the parent has further confirmed employment, the subsidy can be paid for a further 10 working days between employment. If the break is for a longer period than 10 working days then the subsidy must be stopped from the date after employment ceased.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Payment
The rate of payment of Childcare Subsidy depends on the number of children, and the level of income, of the client.
For the current rates of Childcare Subsidy see:
- Deskfile Income limits and maximum rates
The Childcare Subsidy is paid directly to the pre-school facility that the child attends on a weekly basis. Payment must not be more than the fee the pre-school facility charges (including the fee charged to keep the child's place open), and for no more than 50 hours a week.
The number of hours attended by the child must be calculated on a weekly basis.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Payment
The OSCAR Subsidy rate of payment depends on the number of children and the client's income.
For the current rates of OSCAR Subsidy see:
- Deskfile Income limits and rates of payment
The OSCAR Subsidy is paid directly to the provider. Payment must not be more than the fee the approved OSCAR programme provider charges (including the fee charged to keep the child's place open).
The number of hours attended by the child must be calculated on a weekly basis.

chunks.title: Payment during holidays — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Payment during holidays
We can pay Childcare Subsidy for statutory holidays e.g. the Sovereign's birthday and a regional anniversary day, but we cannot pay for the break between Christmas and New Year if the centre is closed.

chunks.title: Payment during holidays - OSCAR — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Payment during holidays - OSCAR
We can pay for statutory holidays e.g. the Sovereign's birthday and a regional anniversary day, but we cannot pay for the break between Christmas and New Year if the centre is closed.

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
A client may qualify for assistance for subsidised childcare of up to 9 hours a week if:
- they are the principal caregiver or principal temporary caregiver of a dependent child
- they meet an income test
- the child is under 5 years old orunder 6 years old and qualifies for Child Disability Allowance oraged 5 years old and whose parent intends to enrol them at school with a cohort entry policy, but that child is not yet able to enrol (start), payments end at the mid-term or term start date on or immediately after their 5th birthday (whichever is closer)Note children are not considered 'enrolled' unless they are attending school.
- under 6 years old and qualifies for Child Disability Allowance or
- aged 5 years old and whose parent intends to enrol them at school with a cohort entry policy, but that child is not yet able to enrol (start), payments end at the mid-term or term start date on or immediately after their 5th birthday (whichever is closer)Note children are not considered 'enrolled' unless they are attending school.
- the child attends an approved early childhood education programme or service
- the child attends for at least 3 hours per week
- they are a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder (i.e. not be in New Zealand unlawfully, or here on a temporary entry class visa) and
- they are generally ordinarily resident in New Zealand
Some clients may be able to get '20 hours Early Childhood Education'.
## Childcare Subsidy of more than 9 hours per week
To get a Childcare Subsidy of more than 9 hours per week, the client must meet additional qualifications.

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
A client may qualify for an OSCAR Subsidy for up to 20 hours a week during a school term and up to 50 hours a week during school holidays if:
- they are the principal caregiver or principal temporary caregiver of a dependent child aged: from 5 to 13 years old orthey are the principal caregiver of a dependent child aged between 14 and 18 years old if the dependent child gets Child Disability Allowance and
- from 5 to 13 years old or
- they are the principal caregiver of a dependent child aged between 14 and 18 years old if the dependent child gets Child Disability Allowance and
- the child attends an approved OSCAR programme for a minimum of 3 hours a week and
- they meet an income test and
- they don't have a partner who can provide childcare and
- they are a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder (i.e. they are not in New Zealand unlawfully, or here on a temporary entry class visa) and
- they are generally ordinarily resident in New Zealand
In some circumstances there are additional qualifications a client must meet to qualify for an OSCAR Subsidy.
## Sole parent is attending a personal development programme
If a Sole Parent Support client is attending a personal development programme and needs childcare assistance for this reason, they do not qualify for an OSCAR subsidy.
If clients do not qualify for an OSCAR subsidy, they should arrange their personal development programme at practical times e.g. during school hours.

chunks.title: Residence — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Residence
To get Childcare Subsidy, a client must:
- be a New Zealand citizen or
- have a residence class visa in New Zealand under the Immigration Act 2009 or
- be deemed to hold a residence class visa in New Zealand under the Immigration Act 2009 and
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they first apply for benefit and
- generally be ordinarily resident in New Zealand
Note for Childcare Subsidy no period of residence is required.
People who are in New Zealand unlawfully or here on a temporary entry class visa generally do not qualify for a benefit.
## Clients without citizenship or a residence class visa
If a client does not have New Zealand citizenship or a residence class visa, they cannot get Childcare Subsidy.
However, if a client in this situation has childcare costs, they may be able to get Temporary Additional Support if they are:
- a person who has refugee or protected person status in New Zealand or
- awaiting the outcome of their application for refugee or protected person status and are lawfully in New Zealand (i.e. they have a valid temporary entry class visa under the Immigration Act 2009) or
- applying for a residence class visa under the Immigration Act 2009 and are compelled to remain in New Zealand through unforeseen circumstances
Once the client has been granted citizenship or a residence class visa and they meet all the other qualifications, Childcare Subsidy can be granted.
## Australian clients
Australian citizens or residents are lawfully allowed in New Zealand as they hold a residence class visa.
However, they must still be ordinarily resident in New Zealand and meet all other criteria to qualify for Childcare Subsidy.

chunks.title: Residence — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Residence
To get OSCAR Subsidy, a client must:
- be a New Zealand citizen or
- have a residence class visa in New Zealand under the Immigration Act 2009 or
- be deemed to hold a residence class visa in New Zealand under the Immigration Act 2009 and
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they first apply for benefit and
- generally be ordinarily resident in New Zealand
Note for OSCAR Subsidy no period of residence is required.
People who are in New Zealand unlawfully or here on a temporary entry class visa generally do not qualify for a benefit.
## Clients without citizenship or a residence class visa
If a client does not have New Zealand citizenship or a residence class visa, they cannot get OSCAR Subsidy.
However, if a client in this situation has childcare costs, they may be able to get Temporary Additional Support if they are:
- a person who has refugee or protected person status in New Zealand or
- awaiting the outcome of their application for refugee or protected person status and are lawfully in New Zealand (i.e. they have a valid temporary entry class visa under the Immigration Act 2009) or
- applying for a residence class visa under the Immigration Act 2009 and are compelled to remain in New Zealand through unforeseen circumstances
Once the client has been granted citizenship or a residence class visa and they meet all the other qualifications, OSCAR Subsidy can be granted.
## Australian clients
Australian citizens or residents are lawfully allowed in New Zealand as they hold a residence class visa.
However, they must still be ordinarily resident in New Zealand and meet all other criteria to qualify for OSCAR Subsidy.

chunks.title: Rounding of hours — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Rounding of hours
The number of hours a child is receiving Childcare Subsidy for can be rounded up on a weekly basis to the next whole hour.
## Example
If a child attends a centre for 35 hours and 15 minutes a week, we can pay the subsidy for 36 hours.

chunks.title: Rounding of hours — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Rounding of hours
The amount of hours a child is receiving an OSCAR Subsidy for can be rounded up on a weekly basis to the next whole hour.
Example
If a child attends a centre for 19 hours and 15 minutes a week we can pay the subsidy for 20 hours.

chunks.title: Seriously disabled or ill caregivers — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Seriously disabled or ill caregivers
Childcare Subsidy may be paid for up to 50 hours a week if the principal caregiver of a dependent child:
- has an illness or disability that reduces their independent function and
- that illness or disability is expected to continue for at least 6 months and
- that illness or disability is so serious they need additional childcare for more than 9 hours a week and
- at least 1 of the following applies the principal caregiver does not have a partner or there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner cannot provide childcare (e.g. they are employed) orthe child qualifies for Child Disability Allowance
- the principal caregiver does not have a partner or there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner cannot provide childcare (e.g. they are employed) or
- the child qualifies for Child Disability Allowance
This includes a principal temporary caregiver of a child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid.
The client does not need to have been getting Childcare Subsidy before becoming seriously ill or disabled.
The Childcare Subsidy will stop when the child is no longer an eligible child. That is when whichever of the below happens first:
- the child turns 5 or 6 years old or
- the child starts school or
- the caregiver no longer requires childcare for their child
## Supporting medical evidence
Caregivers getting Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability, and some caregivers getting Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability, will already have sufficient medical evidence to indicate that childcare is required for more than 9 hours a week.
Points to note when considering a medical certificate already held for another benefit are whether the health condition, injury or disability is:
- likely to continue for at least 6 months and
- so serious as to warrant additional childcare
If sufficient medical evidence is not already available, a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must certify that the caregiver meets the above requirements.
The cost of a medical examination is to be covered by the client.
## ACC or employment related insurance
If the caregiver's disability is due to an accident, ACC or another insurer would generally meet any childcare costs.

chunks.title: Seriously disabled or ill caregivers — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: OSCAR Subsidy may be paid for up to 20 hours a week in term time or 50 hours a week in the school holidays if the qualifications are met (but not the additional qualifications) and the principal caregiver of a dependent child: - has an illness or disability that reduces their independent function and - that illness or disability is expected to continue for at least 6 months and - that illness or disability is so serious they need additional childcare for more than 3 hours a week and - at least 1 of the following applies: the principal caregiver does not have a partner or there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner cannot provide childcare (e.g. they are employed) orthe child qualifies for Child Disability Allowance - the principal caregiver does not have a partner or there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner cannot provide childcare (e.g. they are employed) or - the child qualifies for Child Disability Allowance This includes a principal temporary caregiver of a child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid. The client does not need to have been getting OSCAR Subsidy prior to becoming seriously ill or disabled. OSCAR Subsidy will stop when the child is no longer an eligible child. That is when whichever event below happens first: - the child turns 14 and Child Disability Allowance is not paid for them or - Child Disability Allowance is paid for the child, and the child: turns 18 and is not continuing in education or is not financially dependent oris 18 and: is no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education oris no longer attending school or tertiary education as required oris financially independent orthey leave the parent or caregiver's care orit is later than 31 December of the year they turned 18 or - turns 18 and is not continuing in education or is not financially dependent or - is 18 and: is no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education oris no longer attending school or tertiary education as required oris financially independent orthey leave the parent or caregiver's care orit is later than 31 December of the year they turned 18 or - is no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education or - is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required or - is financially independent or - they leave the parent or caregiver's care or - it is later than 31 December of the year they turned 18 or

chunks.title: Seriously disabled or ill caregivers — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: - the caregiver no longer requires childcare for their child or - the qualifications are no longer met

chunks.title: Supporting medical evidence — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: Caregivers getting Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability and some caregivers getting Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability, will already have sufficient medical evidence to indicate that the caregiver has a serious disability or illness. Points to note when considering a medical certificate already held for another benefit are whether the health condition, injury or disability is: - likely to continue for at least 6 months and - so serious as to warrant additional childcare If sufficient medical evidence is not already available, a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must certify the caregiver meets the above requirements. The cost of a medical examination is to be covered by the client.

chunks.title: Client has a partner — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text: If the client has a partner, they are generally expected to provide care for the siblings (or other dependent children) of a seriously disabled child while the client is in employment, training, study or other activity. However, if the role is particularly demanding the partner may need extra support and breaks from caring.

chunks.title: Shared care - principal caregiver — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Shared care - principal caregiver
To be considered the 'principal caregiver' of the child the client must have:
- the primary responsibility for the day to day care of the child, other than on a temporary basis
If it is difficult to assess who is the principal caregiver, review the decision guidelines for:
- Childcare and OSCAR Subsidy shared care [no link find out why]
Exception a principal temporary caregiver getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is considered to have primary responsibility for the child and may get Child Disability Allowance while the child is in their care. However, they cannot be considered a principal caregiver for the purposes of decisions on shared care.
## Shared care - deciding principal caregiver
Shared care only applies when the parents or caregivers of a child are living apart, the child lives 40% of the time with each parent and both parents apply for an OSCAR subsidy for that child.
Only one parent or caregiver (defined as the principal caregiver) is entitled to get the OSCAR subsidy. It cannot be paid to two parents/caregivers. The parent or caregiver must meet the qualifications.

chunks.title: Principal caregiver — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Principal caregiver
To be considered the 'principal caregiver' of the child the client must have:
- the primary responsibility for the day to day care of the child, other than on a temporary basis
If it is difficult to assess who is the principal caregiver, review the decision guidelines for:
- Childcare and OSCAR Subsidy shared care [no link find out why]
## Exception
A principal temporary caregiver receiving Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is considered to have primary responsibility for the child and may receive Child Disability Allowance while the child is in their care. However, they cannot be considered a principal caregiver for the purposes of decisions on shared care.
## Shared care - deciding principal caregiver
Shared care/carer only applies when the parents or caregivers of a child are living apart, the child lives at least 40% of the time with each parent and both parents apply for a Childcare Subsidy for that child.
Only one parent or caregiver (defined as the principal caregiver) is entitled to receive the subsidy. It cannot be paid to two parents/caregivers. The parent or caregiver applying must meet the qualifications.

chunks.title: Temporary illness — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Temporary illness
Childcare Subsidy may be paid for up to 50 hours a week if the qualifications are met and the caregiver:
- is in paid employment and
- is unable to attend their employment due to sickness or injury and
- has a child who has been attending an early childhood service while the parent worked and
- does not have a partner who can provide childcare or there is a good and sufficient reason why the partner is unable to provide childcare
Note when Childcare Subsidy is being paid temporarily because of sickness or injury it can only be paid to clients who have had to completely stop working. It cannot be paid where the client has reduced their hours.
This type of subsidy may only be paid for a maximum of 12 weeks.
If the illness is for more than 5 working days it must be verified by a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner. A copy of this certificate should be kept on the client's file. Where the illness is 5 working days or less a medical certificate is not required.
Payment can continue when client returns to work if they were getting it before they became ill.
If the caregiver is unable to participate in employment or training due to an injury, ACC or another workplace insurer may pay for childcare. If this is the case, then the subsidy is not payable.

chunks.title: Temporary illness — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Temporary illness
An OSCAR subsidy can continue being paid for a maximum of 12 weeks if the qualifications are met and the caregiver:
- is in paid employment
- is unable to attend their employment due to sickness, injury or disability
- has a child who has been attending an approved OSCAR programme while the parent worked and
- does not have a partner who can provide childcare
If the illness is for more than 5 working days it must be verified by a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner. A copy of this certificate should be kept on the client's file.
When the illness is for 5 working days or less a medical certificate is not required.
ACC or employment-related insurance
If the caregiver is unable to participate in employment due to an injury, and childcare is paid by ACC or another workplace insurer they do not qualify for OSCAR subsidy.

chunks.title: 20 Hours Early Childhood Education and Childcare Subsidy — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## 20 Hours Early Childhood Education and Childcare Subsidy
Children aged 3, 4 and 5 years old attending early childhood education services (kindergartens, centre based, home-based, kōhanga reo and playcentres) offering 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE) may be able to get up to 6 hours per day, 20 hours per week of subsidised early childhood education.
Generally, clients eligible for Childcare Subsidy will be better off getting 20 Hours ECE when their provider offers it.
This is because 20 Hours ECE fully funds early childhood education for up to 20 hours a week.
Childcare Subsidy helps pay for childcare up to a maximum amount per hour, meaning clients may still have costs to pay after the subsidy is paid.
However, clients can choose to take up either:
- 20 Hours ECE only or
- Childcare Subsidy if they qualify or
- a combination of both, but generally not for the same hours
## When a client takes up 20 Hours ECE
- They can get Childcare Subsidy for any other hours not covered by 20 Hours ECE up to a combined total of 9 hours or 50 hours depending on their activities.
- Childcare Subsidy cannot be paid for the same hours that 20 Hours ECE is paid except when home-based educator top-up payments are charged for those hours.
## Client does not take up 20 Hours ECE
If a client is enrolled with a provider that does not offer 20 Hours ECE or the client chooses not to take up 20 Hours ECE, they can apply for Childcare Subsidy under the current qualifications.

chunks.title: 20 Hours Early Childhood Education and up to 50 hours Childcare Subsidy — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## 20 Hours Early Childhood Education and up to 50 hours Childcare Subsidy
Clients who are getting 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE) and qualify for 50 hours a week subsidy, can get Childcare Subsidy for attendance over 20 hours but only up to 50 hours combined.
The maximum total Childcare Subsidy would be 30 hours per week or up to the total number of hours of their activity (including travel time).
The only exception is when a client is being charged a home-based educator top up payment.
Clients who qualify for up to 50 hours of Childcare Subsidy can access Childcare Subsidy for 20 hours of home-based educator top up payments as well as 30 hours of standard early childhood education and childcare fees.

chunks.title: 20 Hours Early Childhood Education and up to 9 hours Childcare Subsidy — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## 20 Hours Early Childhood Education and up to 9 hours Childcare Subsidy
Generally, clients who are getting 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE) cannot get 9 hours Childcare Subsidy.
There are 2 exceptions to this:
## Less than 9 hours of 20 Hours ECE
If a client is getting less than 9 hours of 20 Hours ECE they can get Childcare Subsidy for the remaining standard childcare hours (up to the maximum number of hours they qualify for).
For example, if a client qualifies for 9 hours Childcare Subsidy and is getting 6 hours of the 20 Hours ECE, they can get up to 3 hours of Childcare Subsidy.
For these clients, if their child is attending early childhood education for more than 9 hours a week, they are likely to be better off getting the full 20 Hours ECE entitlement instead of Childcare Subsidy for those hours.
## Home-based educator top up payments
If a client is charged home-based educator top up payments, they can get Childcare Subsidy and 20 Hours ECE.
In this situation, it doesn't matter how many hours of 20 Hours ECE the client is getting for their child.
If a client is getting 9 hours or more of 20 Hours ECE, the 9 hours of Childcare Subsidy can only be used for home-based educator top up payments.
Example
A client has their child enrolled with a home-based educator for 10 hours of 20 Hours ECE and is being charged a home-based educator top up payment for those hours.
The client can get 9 hours of Childcare Subsidy to use towards home-based educator top up payments.
## Less than 9 hours and home-based educator top up payments
If a client is getting less than 9 hours of 20 Hours ECE, the 9 hours of Childcare Subsidy can be used for a combination of both home-based educator top up payments and standard childcare hours.
Example
A client has their child enrolled with a home-based educator for 6 hours of 20 Hours ECE and is being charged a home-based educator top up payment for those hours.
Their child is also enrolled for 3 hours of standard childcare.
The client can get Childcare Subsidy to use towards 6 hours of home-based educator top up payments and 3 hours of standard childcare.

chunks.title: 20 Hours Early Childhood Education — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## 20 Hours Early Childhood Education
20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE) makes early childhood education more affordable for families. It is available for all families regardless of their income and working hours.
Children aged 3,4 and 5 years old attending an early childhood education service (e.g. kindergartens, centre based, home-based, kōhanga reo and playcentres), offering 20 Hours ECE may be able to get up to 6 hours per day, 20 hours per week free childcare.
The funding is available for all licensed early childhood education providers, including centre-based and home-based providers.
Note playgroups cannot get 20 Hours ECE funding.
## Payment to providers
The funding is paid directly to the provider by the Ministry of Education. Families have the choice of taking up 20 Hours ECE if their child is attending an early childhood education service offering 20 Hours ECE funding.
Families who take up 20 Hours ECE complete an 'attestation' form with the provider that sets out information about which hours they wish to get 20 Hours ECE funding for. Families can get 20 Hours ECE in more than one service, but the total number of hours cannot be more than 20 hours a week.
20 Hours ECE is not mandatory. Providers do not have to offer 20 Hours ECE.
## Provider fees
Providers cannot charge fees for the same hours as 20 Hours ECE, but they can ask families to make an optional payment for other hours of enrolment that are not covered by the 20 Hours ECE funding. Clients can choose whether to pay this or not.
The only exception is when a home-based educator charges a home-based educator top up payment for the same hours as 20 Hours ECE. Providers may charge these payments on behalf of a home-based educator.

chunks.title: 20 Hours Early Childhood Education optional payments — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## 20 Hours Early Childhood Education optional payments
Optional payments may be charged by providers for costs not covered in the hourly fee for childcare funded by Childcare Subsidy and 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE).
There are 2 types of optional payments that providers may charge.
## Donations
Donations are voluntary payments.
There is no obligation for a caregiver to pay these charges and the childcare provider cannot enforce payment.
Examples of donations include requests for extra funds to help pay for a school mural or a gift for a leaving teacher.
## Optional charges
Optional charges are costs for a specific purpose that a caregiver can choose whether to pay or not.
They can be one-off or ongoing costs.
Providers formally agree optional charges with caregivers and may enforce charges if a caregiver does not pay.
Optional charges must reflect the real and actual cost of the item or activity.
Childcare Subsidy cannot be used to pay for optional payments.

chunks.title: Weather conditions - Childcare Subsidy — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Weather conditions - Childcare Subsidy
Some clients may have a job that is affected by weather conditions and they are unable to work their standard hours.
As these clients may still be called back to work at any time Childcare Subsidy can continue to be paid for a period of up to 3 weeks, if the child continues to attend the childcare centre.
The types of occupations affected may include (but are not limited to):
- Shearer - cannot shear the sheep if they are wet
- Mussel farmer - it is impossible to gather mussels when the water is too murky
- Road worker - affected by storms, they cannot continue with certain tasks like tar sealing as the tar seal will not set in the rain
A clients ability to work their standard hours may also be affected by a weather event, such as flooding or earthquakes.

chunks.title: Weather conditions - OSCAR — extra help > childcare assistance programme
chunks.text:
## Weather conditions - OSCAR
Some clients may have a job that is affected by weather conditions and they are unable to work their standard hours.
As these clients may still be called back to work at any time OSCAR can continue to be paid for a period of up to 3 weeks, if the child continues to attend the OSCAR provider.
The types of occupations affected include (but are not limited to):
- Shearer - cannot shear the sheep if they are wet
- Mussel farmer - it is impossible to gather mussels when the water is too murky
- Road worker - affected by storms, they cannot continue with certain tasks like tar sealing as the tar seal will not set in the rain
A clients ability to work their standard hours may also be affected by a weather event, such as flooding or earthquakes.

chunks.title: Accommodation costs — extra help > civilian amputee assistance
chunks.text:
## Accommodation costs
A client (and attendant) can receive assistance for accommodation costs if their appointment time or the distance travelled means that an overnight stay is reasonable.
Clients applying for Civilian Amputee Assistance to attend a limb centre must provide:
- confirmation of the accommodation booking and
- details of the cost
Note payment should be made to the supplier where possible.
The maximum payment a client can receive is:
- the actual cost of the accommodation or
- $100.00 per night
whichever is less.
Note accommodation costs should not be paid for more than 10 days per assessment.

chunks.title: Appointments at a limb centre — extra help > civilian amputee assistance
chunks.text:
## Appointments at a limb centre
Appointments to attend a limb centre can be made by the:
- client
- client's medical practitioner or specialist or
- limb centre
The limb centre will decide whether the client needs to attend a centre or a regional clinic and issue an appointment card to the client that states:
- the date of the appointment and
- where the client needs to attend
There may be situations when a client requires an urgent appointment to attend a limb centre or regional clinic due to a breakage or malfunction of the artificial limb. In these situations it is likely that the client will not have an appointment card. You should obtain authorisation from the client to contact the limb centre to confirm the appointment.

chunks.title: Attendant — extra help > civilian amputee assistance
chunks.text:
## Attendant
Assistance can be granted to reimburse the costs of one attendant if:
- the person travelling to the limb centre is a child aged under 15 years old or
- medical evidence is provided stating that the person cannot travel by themselves
Note the loss of earnings of an attendant cannot be met by Civilian Amputee Assistance.

chunks.title: How to apply — extra help > civilian amputee assistance
chunks.text:
## How to apply
A client should complete the Application for Civilian Amputee Assistance form and provide an appointment card or certificate of attendance from the limb centre.
For dependent children the application form should be completed by the parent, guardian or primary caregiver and payments should be made on parents, guardian's or primary caregiver's record.
## Evidence of costs
Clients will need to provide:
- estimates of their costs if applying before they attend the Limb Centre or
- verification of their actual costs once the appointment has been completed

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > civilian amputee assistance
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Civilian Amputee Assistance is available for clients to help with some of the costs when they are required to attend a limb centre to have an artificial limb fitted, adjusted or repaired. It applies equally to amputees or people who were born without a limb.
Assistance is not subject to an income or asset test.
This assistance is provided under the Disabled Community Welfare Act 1975, with payment administered by the Ministry. Assistance is paid for costs that cannot be met by the District Health Boards or any other funding scheme. Generally, the District Health Boards will cover initial artificial limb fitting travel costs if the client is still in hospital.
Assistance is paid prior to the client's appointment based on the estimated cost. A client can apply for a reimbursement of costs when:
- the estimated amount paid in advance did not meet all their costs or
- the client elects to pay the costs themselves and apply for reimbursement after they have attended the limb centre

chunks.title: Limb centres — extra help > civilian amputee assistance
chunks.text:
## Limb centres
Limb centres are administered by the New Zealand Artificial Limb Service (NZALS).
The New Zealand Artificial Limb Service is a Crown Entity, and is the single national provider of prosthetic limbs services to New Zealand amputees and provides 5 limb centres.
Each limb centre is responsible for regional clinics:
