chunks.title: Action on return to New Zealand — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Action on return to New Zealand
MSD must look at the circumstances of the client's absence from and subsequent return to New Zealand to decide when to recommence their Disability Allowance and when to treat it as a new application.
Consider the following:
- the client's intention at the time of their departure, for example, did they cancel their Disability Allowance before leaving New Zealand because they did not intend to return?
- did the client remain ordinarily resident during the period of absence?
- the reason for the absence
- the length of time that they have been absent
- if their circumstances changed significantly during their absence
## Payment can recommence
If a client returns to New Zealand on or before the 29th day (where continued payment of benefit was approved) Disability Allowance can recommence without any break in payment, as long as their costs have continued.
For other short periods of absence (where continued payment was not allowed) the Disability Allowance payments can recommence from:
- the date the customer returned to New Zealand as long as they contact MSD within 14 days of their return or
- the date they contacted MSD to advise they have returned if more than 14 days after date of return

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Disability Allowance it is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Disability Allowance from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising Work and Income of a change in circumstances within 14 days you may reduce, suspend or cancel Disability Allowance from the first available date.
## False or misleading information
If the client gives false or misleading information you must review Disability Allowance from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: False or misleading information — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information you must review Disability Allowance from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Disability Allowance it is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event and does not have a good and sufficient reason, you should generally cancel Disability Allowance from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising Work and Income of a change in circumstances within 14 days you may cancel Disability Allowance from the first available date.

chunks.title: Avoiding a debt — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Avoiding a debt
When a non-beneficiary client dies, Disability Allowance generally stops from the day after the date of death. You must take all possible steps to stop payments from this date.
When payment cannot be stopped from the day after the date of death there is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days after the date of death. You can use this discretion to stop payment from the first available date, that is, the earliest date that you can stop payments from so that no overpayment is established.
If the period between the date of death and the first available date to cancel payment from (to avoid creating a debt) is more than 28 days, you will have to establish an overpayment from the 29th day after death.
However, when there has been a deliberate intent to delay advising Work and Income of the client's death you should stop payment from the day after the date of death and establish an overpayment.
Note under no circumstances can payment continue for more than 28 days after the date of death.
For more information see:
- Terminal benefit

chunks.title: Calculating the period of absence — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Calculating the period of absence
The period of an absence from New Zealand for which payment of Disability Allowance can continue (if approved or when approval is not needed) is up to 28 consecutive days, that is, Saturdays and Sundays are included.
In all cases, when assessing the period of absence do not include:
- the date of departure from New Zealand and
- the date of return to New Zealand
If a client is absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period the Disability Allowance should be suspended from the 29th day (unless they are receiving a main benefit and meet the criteria to pay for longer than 28 days).
Note if a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, the Disability Allowance must be cancelled from the day after departure.
## Calculating 52 week period
When a client who is receiving a main benefit is paid a Disability Allowance while they are absent from New Zealand, a client can receive a payment for up to 28 days in total in a 52 week period. The 52 week period is counted in the following way:
- identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand
- count back 52 weeks from this date
- identify any periods of paid absence they have used (counting from the day after they have left New Zealand to the day before they returned to New Zealand)
- subtract the number of days absent from New Zealand from 28 days. The remainder is the client's entitlement to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand.
- pay the client the days they have available up to the period of absence. This may not be the whole of the time they intend to be absent from New Zealand depending on how many days of their entitlement they have left.
For more information see:
- Return to New Zealand
- Permanent absence

chunks.title: Change in costs — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Change in costs
When there is a change in the client's existing costs you will need to review Disability Allowance to make sure the client is getting the correct rate of payment.
For more information see:
- costs paid for and
- costs not included
Note when the client has applied for new costs to be included, you should follow the commencement date rules. Allowable costs can only be added from the date the client applied to include the new cost.
The date to review Disability Allowance from will depend on the action involved. Generally, you should:
## Increase
- increase Disability Allowance from the actual date of the change in circumstances
## Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Disability Allowance from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event

chunks.title: Change in family circumstances — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Change in family circumstances
MSD should review Disability Allowance to check that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the clients:
- income or
- the dependent children in the client's care
The date to review Disability Allowance from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:
## False or misleading information
If the client gives false or misleading information MSD must review Disability Allowance from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Child turns 18
When a dependent child turns 18, the parent or caregiver can no longer get Disability Allowance for them, unless they are continuing in education and are not financially independent.

chunks.title: Change in income — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When there is a change in the client's income and they are not getting a main benefit, you will need to review the Disability Allowance to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications.
Generally, when a client no longer qualifies for Disability Allowance you should cancel Disability Allowance from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Disability Allowance or the rate payable.
MSD may also review Disability Allowance at any time to check the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment (if applicable).
## Mandatory Review for Disability Allowance
MSD must review a client's Disability Allowance within 52-weeks of when this assistance commenced, or within 52-weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed.
Clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend.
Generally, all clients getting Disability Allowance will have a Mandatory Review for this assistance (except clients also getting Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment).

chunks.title: Child leaves sole parents care suddenly — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Child leaves sole parents care suddenly
When a child stops being a dependent child for a sole parent because of a sudden change of circumstances beyond the control of the client, Disability Allowance paid for the child leaving care may continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child stopped being dependent.
This is to allow a period of transition for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.
For example when a child suddenly goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki payments will continue for 28 days from the date the child is no longer dependent on the client.
## Mandatory Reviews
Generally, clients getting Disability Allowance must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date or their payments will suspend.
If a child leaves a sole parent's care suddenly, but the Disability Allowance will continue at a different rate because a client also gets this payment for someone else, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to respond to the Mandatory Review.
If the client is unable to respond to the review (even if they had more time) based on their individual circumstances, they may qualify for an exemption.
Generally, when the Mandatory Review is only for Disability Allowance and the benefit will stop at the end of the continuation period, and the review is due, an exemption will apply.
The client must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption.
## Child turns 18
Generally, clients getting Disability Allowance must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or Disability Allowance paid for the child will stop.
If Disability Allowance paid for a child is continuing for 28 days because the child has left a sole parent's care suddenly, and that child turns 18 during that period, the client is not required to respond to the notice and Disability Allowance paid for the child will not stop during that period.
However, if Disability Allowance paid for a child is continuing for 28 days because a child has left a sole parent's care suddenly, and a different child in their care (that Disability Allowance is paid for) turns 18, the client must respond to the notice, or Disability Allowance for the 18-year-old will stop.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 for a parent or caregiver to get Disability Allowance for them.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and Disability Allowance paid to a parent or caregiver for them must stop from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and have Disability Allowance paid for them for a limited period.
In these situations, Disability Allowance must stop from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier.
Note if the parent or caregiver also gets Disability Allowance for other people, the payments for the other people will not be affected by the child turning 18.
## Getting a main benefit
If a parent or caregiver is getting a main benefit , and their main benefit is suspended due to their child turning 18, their Disability Allowance will also suspend.
Note main benefits do not include Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
## Disability Allowance may cancel
Disability Allowance will cancel when a parent or caregiver is:
- only getting Disability Allowance for the child that gets excluded and no other Disability Allowance payments and
- not getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit for that child
If the parent or caregiver contacts MSD within 8 weeks after the cancellation, and MSD is satisfied that Disability Allowance can continue to be paid for the 18-year-old for a limited period, MSD may regrant it if there is sufficient evidence, including a current Disability Allowance medical certificate.

chunks.title: Surviving partner or dependent child — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Surviving partner or dependent child
When a client dies (and there is a surviving partner or dependent child) before a decision is made on an application or review for Disability Allowance, you can continue the application or review process as if the client had not died.

chunks.title: Clients receiving a main benefit — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving a main benefit
Disability Allowance can continue to be paid to the client for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital. When the client's benefit is reduced to the hospital rate, their Disability Allowance will need to be stopped.
## Single clients and sole parents
Disability Allowance must be stopped from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation. You will need to check if the client still has continuing costs. If so, increase the hospital rate to meet the costs.
## Married, civil union or de facto couples (without dependent children)
Disability Allowance must be stopped from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation for the client who is in hospital. You will need to check if the client still has continuing costs. If so, increase the hospital rate to meet the costs.
When a benefit is reduced the partner not in hospital may receive Special Disability Allowance.
For more information see:
- Special Disability Allowance
- Hospitalisation in relevant Main Benefit

chunks.title: Court attachment orders — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Court attachment orders
All court attachment requests are sent directly to the Housing Processing Hub for processing. Court attachments are administered via the CORBI screen in SWIFTT.
The Ministry of Justice has the authority to make attachment orders on benefits to meet outstanding court fines. The attachment order may include:
- court finesThese are fines payable to the District Court
- civil attachmentsThese are generally paid to a private individual or organisation that is owed money. Occasionally the District Court will act as a collection agent for civil debts.
Attachment Orders issued by the Ministry of Justice can be made under either the Summary Proceedings Act 1957 or the District Court Act 2016.
## Protected earnings rate
No attachment order can, whether on its own or when combined with any other attachment order, Child Support deduction, or Ministry of Social Development repayment, take a client's total income below the protected earnings rate. For more information, see:
- Protected earnings rate
## Information provided by the court
The information that will be received from the Ministry of Justice will have:
- the client's name
- the amount to be deducted from the benefit
- the fine's reference number
If a client is suffering undue hardship because of the amount of the attachment order then they should be directed to a Registrar of the District Court for a reassessment of the rate.
For more information see:
- Court request for information
## Transferring or cancelling and re-granting benefits
When transferring or cancelling and re-granting benefits when there are court attachments on the record please email the Housing Processing Hub. Include the clients name and client number, and a request to review and reload court attachments as necessary.

chunks.title: Court request for information — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Court request for information
The Ministry of Justice can request the following information when they are considering either making an attachment order or assessing the client's protected earnings rate under section 87AA of the Summary Proceedings Act 1957:
- the amount of any benefit paid to the client
- the amount of any attachment orders or deduction notices issued under the following Acts: Social Security Act 2018Family Proceedings Act 1980Child Support Act 1991Tax Administration Act 1994
- Social Security Act 2018
- Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Child Support Act 1991
- Tax Administration Act 1994
- any Ministry of Social Development debt that is being recovered from the client
- the composition of the client's family, including the number of family members who are dependent on the client, as known by the Ministry of Social Development
This information is used to determine how much the client can reasonably be expected to pay each week on any outstanding fines.
## Information that cannot be provided
The following information cannot be provided to the Ministry of Justice:
- the client's benefit number
- the benefit type and
- employer details

chunks.title: Receiving a main benefit — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Receiving a main benefit
When a client is getting a main benefit, Disability Allowance stops from the same date as the main benefit.
## Non-beneficiaries
For non-beneficiary clients Disability Allowance generally stops from the day following the date of death. However, there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days after the date of death:
- to avoid creating a debt or
- as terminal benefit when there are other circumstances that justify payment
## Mandatory Reviews
There are no Mandatory Reviews of a client's or their partner's (if applicable) Disability Allowance when the client has died.
However, the deceased client's surviving partner will have a Mandatory Review of their Disability Allowance in the future.

chunks.title: Death of a dependent child — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Death of a dependent child
When a dependent child (that Disability Allowance is paid for) dies, payment generally stops from the day after death.
There is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the date of death. To help decide whether to continue payment see:
- Terminal benefit
When a dependent child dies the client's Disability Allowance needs to be reviewed to check that they still meet the qualifications.
## Mandatory Reviews
There are no Mandatory Reviews for a Disability Allowance that is paid for a dependent child who has died. All other Mandatory Reviews, including a Disability Allowance paid for someone else, must still be completed.
The client may be able to get an extension if they need more time to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client is unable to respond to the review (even if they had more time) based on their individual circumstances, they may qualify for an exemption.
## Child turns 18
Generally, clients getting Disability Allowance must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or Disability Allowance paid for the child will stop.
If Disability Allowance paid for a child is continuing for up to 28 days because the child died, and the child that died was due to turn 18 during that period, the client is not required to respond to the notice and Disability Allowance paid for the child will not stop during that period.
However, if Disability Allowance paid for a child is continuing for up to 28 days because a child has died, and a different child in their care (that Disability Allowance is also paid for) turns 18, the client must respond to the notice or Disability Allowance for the 18-year-old will stop.

chunks.title: Death of a married, civil union or de facto client — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Death of a married, civil union or de facto client
When a married, civil union or de facto client dies the surviving partner's Disability Allowance needs to be reviewed to check they still meet the qualifications and are getting the correct rate of payment.
The Disability Allowance should be reviewed from the day following death.
## Mandatory Reviews
There are no Mandatory Reviews of a client's or their partner's Disability Allowance when the client has died. However, the surviving partner will have a Mandatory Review of their Disability Allowance in the future.

chunks.title: Debt recovery — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Debt recovery
When a client has arrears owing to them at the time of their death and they have an outstanding debt balance, you should attempt to recover the debt, in full, from the final payment.
When a client has an outstanding debt balance and terminal benefit is payable, you should not attempt to recover the debt in full, from the terminal benefit payment.

chunks.title: Disability Allowance suspended before Mandatory Review date — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Disability Allowance suspended before Mandatory Review date
Clients getting Disability Allowance are always notified about their Mandatory Review, even if their Disability Allowance is suspended, unless it is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison.
MSD must not undertake the Mandatory Review unless the client contacts MSD to resume their Disability Allowance.
If the client contacts MSD before their review date to resume their Disability Allowance, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to do their Mandatory Review. MSD can resume the benefit before the Mandatory Review has been responded to.
However, if the client contacts MSD on or after their Mandatory Review date, the review must be completed before MSD can resume the benefit.
Example
MSD was notified by NZ police that Wilfred has a warrant for their arrest (risk to public safety) on 1 December 2026. Wilfred's Disability Allowance is suspended on this date.
Wilfred's Mandatory Review date is due on 15 January. Wilfred's Disability Allowance is still suspended when he would have been notified about the review, so he does not get notified.
On 17 January Wilfred tells MSD that they have resolved their warrant to arrest and provides a notice of hearing as evidence.
MSD advises Wilfred's his Mandatory Review for his Disability Allowance was due on 15 January 2027 and that he will need to respond to the Mandatory Review and confirm his circumstances before MSD can resume his Disability Allowance.
On 19 January 2027 Wilfred responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms he has had no change in circumstances and that his costs are still the same.
MSD determines Wilfred continues to qualify for Disability Allowance and the rate payable and completes the Mandatory Review on 19 January 2027. Wilfred's Disability Allowance is resumed from 17 January.
MSD sets Wilfred's next review date 52-weeks from the date the review was completed. Wilfred's next Mandatory Review date is 18 January 2028.

chunks.title: Disability due for reassessment — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Disability due for reassessment
When a client applies for Disability Allowance, their general medical practitioner or nurse practitioner confirms if the client’s (or their partner or dependent child, if any) disability is permanent or needs to be reassessed in:
- 6 to 12 months
- 1 to 2 years or
- 2 to 3 years.
When a client's disability is due for reassessment, a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must confirm if the client's (or their partner or dependent child, if any) has:
- a disability that is likely to last for at least 6 months or
- a life expectancy of less than 6 months because of a terminal illness and
- state the ongoing costs arising from that disability and that those costs are of therapeutic value
As part of the reassessment, a client is required to confirm their ongoing additional costs arising from that disability and to provide any evidence of a cost that:
- has increased or
- is a new cost
If a client has a new cost to be included in their Disability Allowance, the client must provide a new medical certificate completed by their registered medical or nurse practitioner that confirms the new cost is a result of the client's disability, on-going and of therapeutic value.
Verification of a disability cost is not required if the client states a particular cost already included in their Disability Allowance is unchanged or has reduced.
If the cost has reduced, accept this and review the client's (or family members) Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Examples of Mandatory Review outcomes — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: MSD must review a client's Disability Allowance within 52 weeks of the commencement date of the Disability Allowance, or 52 weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed. The Mandatory Review is completed when MSD has determined if the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance and confirms the rate payable (if applicable). When a client responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined if the client qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g. client has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Outcomes of a Mandatory Review Examples Client declares no change (exception doesn't apply) Monica is single with no dependent children and is getting Disability Allowance to help with their gardening costs. Monica responds to their Mandatory Review on 5 November 2026 and confirms she has had no change in circumstances. Because Monica has declared there has been no change to her circumstances and an exception doesn't apply, MSD must continue their Disability Allowance at the same rate. MSD completes Monica's Mandatory Review on 5 November 2026 and sets the next review date 52 weeks from the date the Mandatory Review was completed. Monica's next Mandatory Review is 4 November 2027. Client declares no change (exception applies) Ricky is single with no dependent children. Ricky is getting Accommodation Supplement and Disability Allowance and pays rent of $350.00 per week in Area 1. His Mandatory Review is due on 9 June 2027, and he responds on 7 June 2027 to confirm he has had no change in his circumstances. While his Disability Allowance costs were updated last year, he hasn't declared a change in rent since January 2024. Because Ricky has been getting Accommodation Supplement and declared no change in his accommodation costs for three consecutive years, MSD must consider whether further information is required before completing the Mandatory Review. MSD considers Ricky's circumstances and sees that he hasn't provided verification of his accommodation costs since moving to his current apartment in 2024. Given Ricky lives in an area where rental accommodation is very limited and rents have increased significantly, MSD determines that it is reasonable to request verification of his accommodation costs to confirm that the information is correct before making a decision about his entitlement. Ricky is asked to provide this information before 7 July 2027 (his new deadline for the review) or his Accommodation Supplement and Disability Allowance will stop. Ricky contacts MSD on 1 July 2027 with the evidence requested. MSD determines that Ricky's circumstances have changed as his rent increased in January 2027. MSD adjusts the rate of payment for Accommodation Supplement and exercises discretion to backdate the payment to the date of the increase in costs, and continues Disability Allowance at the same rate. MSD completes Ricky's Mandatory Review on 1 July 2027, and his next Mandatory Review date is set for 52 weeks in the future on 29 June 2028. Client declares a change in circumstances Nate is single with no dependent children, and is getting Disability Allowance for their counselling and prescription costs.

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Nate's Mandatory Review is due on 19 March 2027. Nate responds to their Mandatory Review on 24 February 2027 and tells MSD they stopped going to counselling from 20 February 2027. MSD reassesses Nate's Disability Allowance from 20 February and removes the counselling costs. MSD also determines that that Nate is still eligible for Disability Allowance for their prescription costs. MSD completes the Mandatory Review on 24 February 2027 and sets Nate's next review date 52 weeks from the date MSD completes the Mandatory Review. Nate's next Mandatory Review date is 23 February 2028. Mandatory Review was not completed, and benefit has suspended Vince is single with no dependent children, and is getting Disability Allowance for special foods due to his dietary needs. Vince's Mandatory Review is due on 8 September 2027. However, Vince does not respond to the Mandatory Review before his review date and Disability Allowance suspends on 8 September 2027. Vince does not contact MSD or respond to the Mandatory Review for 8 weeks after his Disability Allowance suspended. Because Vince didn't respond during those 8 weeks after his benefit was suspended, Vince's Disability Allowance is cancelled from 8 September 2027 (the date it was originally suspended). Not enough information to complete Mandatory Review Angie is a single client with 1 dependent child. Angie is getting Disability Allowance (non-beneficiary) for her power, heating and her daughter's prescription costs. Angie's Mandatory Review is due on 16 August 2026. Angie responds to the Mandatory Review on 13 August 2026 and tells MSD that their child left their care (a planned change in circumstances) and is now living with their father full time. Angie has declared a change which affects their Disability Allowance. However, MSD does not have enough information to determine if Angie is getting the correct rate of Disability Allowance as she can't confirm the date her daughter left her care. MSD cannot complete the Mandatory Review without requesting more information from Angie. MSD sets a new reasonable deadline of 18 August 2026 for Angie to provide further information. Angie's Disability Allowance will continue to be paid during this time. If Angie does not provide information before the 18 August 2026, her Disability Allowance will suspend on this date.

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Angie contacts MSD on 17 August 2026 and confirms that her daughter left her care on 5 August 2026. MSD updates Angie's rate of Disability Allowance by removing her daughter's prescription costs from 5 August 2026. MSD completes the Mandatory Review on 17 August 2026 and sets Angie's next review date 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Angie's next review date is 16 August 2027. Note when there is a change in circumstances that means a client no longer qualifies for Disability Allowance, MSD should consider if the client is eligible for other types of assistance.

chunks.title: Exceptions when a client declares no change in circumstances for Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have no change in circumstances, MSD must generally continue their Disability Allowance at the same rate. However, there are some exceptions when MSD can request further information from the client to determine if they continue to qualify for Disability Allowance or that the rate of payment is correct. Exceptions include when, at the time the client responds to their Mandatory Review, they: - have been getting Disability Allowance and have had no change in their disability related costs for three consecutive years or - have been getting Accommodation Supplement and have had no change in their accommodation costs for three consecutive years or - have had no change to their confirmed income amount for three consecutive years or - are a non-beneficiary and have confirmed no income If a client has one or more of these exceptions, MSD must consider if further information is required from the client before deciding the outcome of the Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Requesting further information — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: The decision to request further information from the client should be assessed on a case-by-case basis. Consider additional factors such as: - the type of costs the client has (e.g. food, transport and power costs vary with economic conditions and would be unlikely to have no change over an extended period) - when the client last provided verification of their costs (if it was required e.g. new or increased disability related costs and those that were previously included on the basis of a quote and there is no evidence of receipts or invoices being provided) - whether other assistance is available to cover or partly cover the additional cost, e.g. client has additional public transport costs, but they have not changed even though they are a Community Services Card holder and can get a 50% discount on public transport fares - other resources available to meet their costs (e.g. when the client has no income declared and is only getting assistance for some of their expenses, or when the client's income has not changed over an extended period)

chunks.title: Further information is needed to complete the Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: If further information is needed to determine if the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance or that the rate of payment is correct, MSD must give a reasonable timeframe for the client to provide it. The date the client is given to provide the information by becomes the client's new deadline to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client does not provide the information that was asked for, MSD must suspend the Disability Allowance from the new deadline date. If the client provides the information that was asked for and MSD determines the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance (including the rate payable), the future Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Example Duncan gets Disability Allowance to help with his disability related costs, which includes transport costs. Duncan pays $10 for the bus fare to get to and from physiotherapy each week. Duncan's Mandatory Review is due on 10 December 2027. He responds to his review before the review date and confirms he has had no change in his circumstances. As the last change he declared was in July 2024 when the transport costs were first included in his Disability Allowance, MSD must consider whether further information is required before completing the Mandatory Review. MSD considers Duncan's circumstances and notes that he has the full bus fare included in his Disability Allowance. As Duncan is a Community Services Card Holder, he can get a 50% discount on public transport fares through Community Connect. MSD determines that it is reasonable to request further information about his travel costs and whether there is a good reason for not applying for the 50% discount. Duncan is asked to provide this information by 24 December (his new deadline for the review) or his Disability Allowance will stop. Two weeks is a reasonable amount of time because Duncan only needs to contact MSD to confirm the details. Duncan contacts MSD on 15 December 2027 and advises that he didn't know about the 50% discount. Duncan confirmed that he now uses his Community Services Card to get the 50% discounted bus fare and pays $5 a week to get to and from the physiotherapist. MSD reassess his Disability Allowance accordingly and his next review date is set for 52 weeks in the future (13 December 2028).

chunks.title: Further information not needed to complete the Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: In some situations, there may be good reason for the client having no change in their costs or income, or no income, and further information may not be needed for MSD to determine whether they continue to qualify for Disability Allowance. For example, the client may have provided recent evidence of their costs or income, they may have recently discussed their circumstances with MSD or a non-beneficiary client with no income may be in the process of applying for a main benefit. If no further information is needed for MSD to determine the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance (including the rate payable), the future Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Example Martha is getting Disability Allowance for help with a range of ongoing costs arising from her disability, including the cost of fortnightly lawn-mowing at her home. Martha's Mandatory Review for Disability Allowance is due 9 November 2026 and she responds on 5 November 2026 to confirm she has had no change in her circumstances. The last change she declared was in July 2023 when the lawn-mowing costs were first included in her Disability Allowance. None of her other costs have changed. As Martha has been getting Disability Allowance and declared no change in her Disability Allowance costs for three consecutive years at the time the Mandatory Review is returned, MSD must consider whether further information is required before completing the mandatory review. MSD considers Martha's circumstances and sees that she recently provided verification of these costs in the form of the receipt from the service provider. This confirms that Martha's current lawn-mowing costs are the same as they were in 2023. The other costs included in her Disability Allowance are unlikely to change. MSD determines that no further information is required to determine Martha continues to qualify for Disability Allowance. Her Disability Allowance continues at the same rate, and her next review date is set for 52 weeks in the future (4 November 2027).

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a client receiving Disability Allowance is admitted to hospital payment can continue at the existing rate for the first 13 weeks if their costs are continuing.
From the start of 14th week of hospitalisation their Disability Allowance will need to be reviewed.
The date of admission and the date of discharge are not included in the 13-week calculation.
Note a couple with dependent children do not have their Disability Allowance reduced regardless of how long they are in hospital.
## Clients in hospital during Mandatory Review
Generally, clients getting Disability Allowance must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend.
However, when a client is in hospital (for 13 weeks or less) and needs more time to respond to the review, they may be able to get an extension. If a client is unable to respond to the Mandatory Review, they may be able to get an exemption.
The client must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption.
Note clients who are in hospital for more than 13 weeks do not have a Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Imprisonment — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
Disability Allowance is generally not paid when a client is in prison. Disability Allowance should stop from the day following the date of imprisonment.
However, clients on home detention may qualify. For more information see: 'Home Detention' in the appropriate main benefit manual.
In some circumstances Disability Allowance can continue when, a:
- married, civil union or de facto client, or a single client with dependent children, is imprisoned or
- client is on remand
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances of the client before making a decision.

chunks.title: Inland Revenue deduction notices — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
Inland Revenue may request for a client's unpaid taxes to be directly deducted from their benefit payments.
Note all Inland Revenue deduction notices are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
The instructions of the deduction notice will be to deduct the lowest of either:
- 10% of the total debt which Inland Revenue specify in the notice, on a weekly basis or
- 20% of the client's gross earnings on a weekly basis
Where there are insufficient funds to cover the deduction, the Ministry of Social Development must advise Inland Revenue immediately that the deduction will not start or will start at a reduced rate.
Inland Revenue deductions have a lower priority than Child Support deductions.
For more information see:
- Priority for deductions

chunks.title: Mandatory Review dates for Disability Allowance — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review dates for Disability Allowance
MSD must review a client's Disability Allowance within 52-weeks of the commencement date of Disability Allowance, or within 52-weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed.
The next Mandatory Review date will be set for 52-weeks from the date MSD determined the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance and the rate of benefit payable (if applicable) i.e. when MSD completes the review.
Clients who are getting a main benefit that is subject to a Mandatory Review will have their Disability Allowance reviewed at the same time as that benefit (this includes the initial review).
Note when MSD has an interaction with a client that confirms all of the same circumstances as a Mandatory Review, this can push out the client's Mandatory Review date by 52 weeks. This is known as a specific engagement.
## Initial review dates for Disability Allowance
Disability Allowance commencement date
Mandatory Review dates
Disability Allowance commenced before 2 March 2026
Clients whose Disability Allowance commenced before 2 March 2026 will have their initial Mandatory Review either:
- 52 weeks from the commencement date of the Disability Allowance
or
- 52 weeks from when they were last notified about their periodic review.
Whichever of the dates is later.
Disability Allowance commenced on or after 2 March 2026
If a client's Disability Allowance commenced on or after 2 March 2026, their initial Mandatory Review date will be either:
- 52 weeks from the commencement date of the Disability Allowance
or
- 52 weeks from the completion of a specific engagement.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review for Disability Allowance — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: MSD must review a client's Disability Allowance within 52-weeks of when this assistance commenced or from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed. Clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend. The purpose of a Mandatory Review for Disability Allowance is to: - check for any changes to the client's circumstances - determine if the client stills meets the qualifications for Disability Allowance (except for the medical qualifications, they are reviewed separately) - check for any changes to a client's ongoing costs for Disability Allowance (e.g. including or removing a cost, an increase in cost, or a decrease in cost) and - review the rate of Disability Allowance payable. The Mandatory Review will check a client's circumstances but will not be a reassessment of their disability, known as a medical review. Medical reviews will take place separately. Generally, all clients getting Disability Allowance will have a Mandatory Review for this assistance (except clients also getting Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment). Note New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension clients and non-beneficiaries getting Disability Allowance must meet the income test. This also applies to clients not getting a main benefit who get Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, and get Disability Allowance for those children.

chunks.title: Mandatory Reviews of only Disability Allowance and Accommodation Supplement — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: When clients are getting Disability Allowance and Accommodation Supplement, the initial Mandatory Review date is determined by which assistance commenced first. This will only apply to clients getting who are getting: - non-beneficiary assistance - Veterans Pension - New Zealand Superannuation (unless they have a grandparented non-qualified partner included in their benefit). Example Gabriella has been getting Disability Allowance since 23 June 2026. Gabriella applied for Accommodation Supplement, which commenced on 13 July 2026. Because the initial Mandatory Review date is determined by which assistance commenced first, the review for both Disability Allowance and Accommodation Supplement will be set for 52 weeks from 23 June 2026.

chunks.title: Client is getting a benefit that is subject to a Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Clients who are getting some benefits that are subject to a Mandatory Review will have their Disability Allowance reviewed at the same time as that benefit. These benefits are: - Supported Living Payment - Emergency Benefit (when the expiry date for the benefit is more than 52-weeks or there is no expiry date) - Emergency Maintenance Allowance (when the expiry date for the benefit is more than 52-weeks or there is no expiry date) - New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner Example Justin was granted Disability Allowance on 11 March 2026. He was diagnosed with a serious illness that will last and restrict his capacity for work for longer than 2 years and was granted Supported Living Payment on 5 May 2026. Because the review date is based on the commencement date of Justin's main benefit, the Mandatory Review for Justin's Disability Allowance and Supported Living Payment is reset to 52 weeks from 5 May 2026.

chunks.title: Clients getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: A client getting Disability Allowance for a child who Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid for will have their Disability Allowance reviewed at the same time as their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit. If a client is getting Disability Allowance for someone else, they will have a Mandatory Review for their Disability Allowance at least once in a 52-week period, but it will be separate to the Mandatory Review for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Clients getting Jobseeker Support and Sole Parent Support — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Clients getting Sole Parent Support or Jobseeker Support have a reapplication process they must complete to continue getting their benefit. These clients will have a Mandatory Review for Disability Allowance when they: - are completing the reapplication process for the benefit and - their disability costs have not been reviewed in the last 44 weeks If a client's disability costs have been reviewed in the last 44 weeks, there will be no Mandatory Review for Disability Allowance until their next Mandatory Review is due or at their next reapplication.

chunks.title: Client is getting a benefit that does not have a Mandatory Review, 26-week, or 52-week reapplication — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: If a client is getting a benefit that does not have a Mandatory Review and are also getting Disability Allowance, they will still have a Mandatory Review for Disability Allowance at least once in a 52-week period. Clients getting Youth Parent Payment or Youth Payment do not have a Mandatory Review of their Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Notice period for a Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Clients are notified at least 20 working days before their Mandatory Review date, unless their Disability Allowance is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison. The notice period allows sufficient time for clients to respond to the Mandatory Review. Note if a client's Disability Allowance is suspended when the Mandatory Review notice is sent, they are not required to respond to their Mandatory Review until their Disability Allowance is to be resumed.

chunks.title: Responding to the Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: To respond to the Mandatory Review, the client must: - confirm or provide current information about their circumstances and - provide further information to MSD if requested. Clients must confirm the information MSD holds is correct or provide any new information before their review date. When a client has responded to the Mandatory Review and MSD has determined they continue to qualify for Disability Allowance, their next review date is 52 weeks from the date their Mandatory Review was completed.

chunks.title: Client does not respond to the Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: When a client does not respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, the Disability Allowance will suspend. If the client does not respond to the Mandatory Review to confirm their circumstances within 8 weeks after their payments have suspended, the Disability Allowance will be cancelled. A client can still do their Mandatory Review during those 8 weeks. However, once the Disability Allowance has cancelled, the client will need to apply for Disability Allowance if they need this assistance. A client's Disability Allowance cannot be resumed before they have responded to their Mandatory Review during the 8-week suspension period.

chunks.title: Disability Allowance suspends — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: If a client's Disability Allowance suspends as the result of not responding to a Mandatory Review, all of their assistance will also suspend, except for the following payments: - Child Disability Allowance - Orphan's Benefit - Unsupported Child's Benefit - Childcare Subsidy - OSCAR (Out of School Care and Recreational Subsidy) - New Zealand Superannuation (unless they have a grandparented non-qualified partner included) - Veteran's Pension - Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment

chunks.title: When the Mandatory Review is completed — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: The Mandatory Review is complete when MSD makes a decision about the eligibility for Disability Allowance and the rate of benefit payable. MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g., client has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Mandatory Reviews for clients with partners — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: When a client has a partner, both the client and partner's circumstances are included in the review. Changes to the partner's circumstances (e.g. disability costs, income and other factors) must be included in the Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review not required — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review not required
There is no Mandatory Review for Disability Allowance for clients in the following circumstances:
- the client is hospitalised for more than 13 weeks
- the client is in residential disability care or rest home care
- the client has died
- living in or visiting a region affected by an emergency or adverse event and are unable to reasonably leave the area
- the client is living in or visiting a region affected by an outbreak of a quarantinable disease and an epidemic notice has been given and is in force
or when:
- there is a system outage that prevents MSD or the client from completing the review.
MSD will also stop the review for any clients who are in these circumstances after they have been notified about their Mandatory Review.
MSD will notify the client when they are not required to complete the review. The Mandatory Review date will be reset to 52 weeks from the client's original review date.
Note a notification will not be sent when the client has died.

chunks.title: Married, civil union or de facto clients — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Married, civil union or de facto clients
Where one partner is overseas and their Disability Allowance will not be paid, the partner remaining in New Zealand should still be assessed as a married, civil union or de facto couple (including their partner's income).

chunks.title: Price changes — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Price changes
MSD reviews MSD-accredited medical alarm suppliers every 2 years. During this process MSD-accredited medical alarm suppliers can negotiate price changes.
Clients with medical alarms from MSD-accredited medical alarm suppliers will have their Disability Allowance costs adjusted if prices change.
Clients who have a non MSD-accredited medical alarm supplier need to let us know if they have a change in cost.
This is an opportunity to discuss with them changing to an MSD-accredited supplier

chunks.title: Ministry of Social Development debt repayments — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Ministry of Social Development debt repayments
When a client has a Ministry of Social Development debt, this can be recovered by regular deductions from their current benefit.
Note Income Related Rent historical Housing New Zealand debt should be given equal priority to Ministry of Social Development debt.
For more information see:
- Debt recovery maximum

chunks.title: Non-beneficiary clients — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Non-beneficiary clients
Disability Allowance can continue to be paid to the client for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital. From the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation the Disability Allowance will need to be reviewed.
## Single clients and sole parents
If client still has to meet their continuing costs Disability Allowance can continue at the existing rate.
You will need to check how the client is supporting themselves. The client may qualify for a benefit if their income has reduced.
## Married, civil union or de facto couples (without dependent children)
If client still has to meet their continuing costs Disability Allowance can continue at the existing rate.
You will need to check if the client's income has changed because of being in hospital. The client may qualify for a benefit if their income has reduced.

chunks.title: Obligation to advise of departure from New Zealand (main beneficiaries only) — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Obligation to advise of departure from New Zealand (main beneficiaries only)
All clients getting a main benefit must tell the Ministry of Social Development before they leave New Zealand.
If the client does not tell the Ministry before they go overseas, their benefit payments will stop from the day after they left New Zealand.
If a client tells us they will be absent from New Zealand, and they have an approved travel reason, they may be able to keep getting payments for up to 28 days.
Clients who do not keep getting a main benefit while overseas may be still be able to get Disability Allowance, if their absence does not affect the client's eligibility for this assistance, and they told the Ministry they were going before they left New Zealand. They must have ongoing disability costs and this assistance is limited to 28 days in a 52 week period.
For more information about absence from New Zealand see:
- Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period in relevant main benefit
## Does not advise of departure
If the client did not tell the Ministry they were leaving New Zealand, their benefit will be suspended immediately from the day after they left New Zealand. Their Disability Allowance will also stop.
The Integrity Intervention Centre will determine if there has been an overpayment, establish any debt and advise the client.
If a client challenges the information match, refer them to the Integrity Intervention Centre.
## Client contacts us from overseas
Clients may contact us from overseas to advise of their travel.
When they do this their benefit may be:
- resumed if their travel is allowed, from the date they told the Ministry of their absence or
- backdated to the departure date (in limited circumstances)
For more information about absence from New Zealand see:
- Payment benefit when client failed to advise of absence in relevant main benefit
- Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit
- Action on return to New Zealand
- Calculating the period of absence

chunks.title: Outcomes of a Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their Mandatory Review date to continue getting Disability Allowance, or their payments will suspend. When a client responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined if the client qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g. client has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies The Mandatory Review is complete when MSD makes a decision about if the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance and the rate of benefit payable (if applicable). MSD may also carry out a separate review of the Disability Allowance at any time, where there is good reason. This could be where MSD is unsure about a cost e.g. a change in pharmaceutical subsidies has happened and the client has not advised of that change.

chunks.title: Client declares no change — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have had no change in circumstances, MSD must generally continue their Disability Allowance at the same rate. The client's next review date will be set for 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Exceptions when a client declares no change When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have no change in circumstances, there are some situations when MSD can request further information from the client before deciding whether to continue Disability Allowance e.g. the client is a non-beneficiary and has no income.

chunks.title: Client declares a change in circumstances — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: When a client responds to the Mandatory Review with a change in circumstances, MSD must use the information provided to determine if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, or any other benefits they get that are subject to a Mandatory Review (excluding Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit, unless Disability Allowance is paid for the child that Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid for) and the rate payable. MSD may request further information from the client if it is unclear if the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance. Date of change When a client declares a change in circumstances, MSD will need to assess if the client still qualifies for Disability Allowance and determine the rate payable and from what date, depending on when the change in circumstances happened or will happen. Client is also getting other assistance When a client has provided information as part of the Mandatory Review that could affect their entitlement to or the rate payable for any other assistance (e.g. Temporary Additional Support or Flexible Childcare Assistance), MSD may use this information to review that assistance. When the other assistance is affected by the outcome of the Mandatory Review, MSD must change the rate, suspend or cancel that assistance where appropriate. For example, if the outcome of the Mandatory Review is that the client is no longer entitled to Disability Allowance, their Temporary Additional Support must be reviewed, and the rate may change or stop if they no longer qualify.

chunks.title: Further information is needed to complete the Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: When a client has responded to the review and further information is needed to determine if the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance or if the rate of payment is correct, MSD must give a reasonable timeframe for the client to get the information. The date the client is given to provide the information by will become the client's new deadline to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client doesn't provide the information that was asked for before the deadline, MSD must suspend the Disability Allowance from the new deadline date. If the client provides the information that was asked for and MSD determines the client continues to qualify for Disability Allowance (including the rate payable), the next Mandatory Review date will be set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review.;

chunks.title: Completing a Mandatory Review when there are new costs — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: In some circumstances MSD can still complete the Mandatory Review when a client has declared a new costs and this does not affect the client's eligibility for Disability Allowance. Example 1 Jennifer is getting Disability Allowance (non-beneficiary) and has a Mandatory Review for this assistance. Jennifer responds to the Mandatory Review to confirm her circumstances. She tells MSD she has a new disability cost but nothing else has changed. MSD completes the Mandatory Review and continues the Disability Allowance at the existing rate. MSD advises Jennifer that she needs to provide a medical certificate from her medical or nurse practitioner to confirm the additional cost, and she must provide receipts or invoices to have the new cost included in her Disability Allowance. Example 2 Denzel is getting an Emergency Benefit and Disability Allowance and has a Mandatory Review for both. Denzel responds to the Mandatory Review to confirm his circumstances. Denzel tells MSD he now has accommodation costs but nothing else has changed. MSD completes the Mandatory Review and continues the Emergency Benefit and Disability Allowance at the existing rate. The change declared by Denzel doesn't affect his eligibility for the Emergency Benefit or Disability Allowance. Denzel can apply for Accommodation Supplement based on his new accommodation costs. This application is separate to the Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Partner's IRD number — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: As part of a review of Disability Allowance, MSD may make a written request to the client for evidence of a partner's IRD number when the: - partner is not being apportioned the primary client's Disability Allowance, and - partner's income is relevant to a client's Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Notice following an unsuccessful match — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about a partner's IRD number. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information, or there's an error with the data match, MSD should ask the client (in writing) to provide evidence of their partner's IRD number, unless there are significant barriers to providing this. In the written request for evidence of the IRD number, MSD must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and some of this information hasn't matched, and - giving the client a minimum of 10 working days to provide their partner's IRD number evidence or the client's assistance may be suspended. Example Isla is receiving Disability Allowance. Isla's partner, Ariki, has income that is included in MSD's income test to determine eligibility for Disability Allowance and MSD holds an IRD number for Ariki. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Ariki's IRD number. As part of a review of Isla's assistance, MSD provides a notice in writing, giving 10 working days for Isla to provide evidence of Ariki's IRD number. MSD's decision to give 10 working days to provide evidence is based on: - Ariki already having an IRD number - Ariki not having any significant barriers to getting evidence of their IRD number - MSD's obligation to provide a minimum of 10 working days to provide the information.

chunks.title: MSD may suspend assistance if evidence is not received — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: If a partner's IRD number evidence is not provided within a reasonable timeframe (usually 10 working days) or within the extended period if this has been applied, the client's taxable and/or income tested assistance may be suspended. In rare cases, depending on the client's circumstances, MSD may consider cancelling or varying the client's assistance. Note suspension does not apply to Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: IRD number not requested in some circumstances — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: MSD may not ask for evidence of an IRD number when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - significant factors, that are outside the client's or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of their IRD number, (e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence), and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided. A partner's IRD number and evidence of their IRD number does not need to be provided when they are not a New Zealand tax resident. MSD can determine a later point to request the evidence of the IRD number. For more information see: - Non-tax resident partner's IRD number not required Note there is different guidance for requesting evidence of an IRD number for a client, or when a client is applying for Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Client receiving a main benefit — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Client receiving a main benefit
When a client is paid their main benefit while they are absent from New Zealand (either because they qualify for approved travel or the requirements for approved travel do not apply to them) they can continue to receive their main benefit and their Disability Allowance for up to 28 days in any 52 week period. This applies unless they qualify to be paid their main benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. They must have ongoing costs while they are away.
Clients who do not continue getting their main benefit while overseas (because they do not qualify for approved travel) may still be able to keep getting Disability Allowance, if their absence does not affect the client's eligibility for this assistance, and they advised Work and Income of their absence before their international travel.
They must have ongoing disability costs and this assistance is limited to 28 days in a 52 week period.
For more information about Absence from New Zealand see:
- Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period in relevant main benefit
## Information required from client when advising they intend to travel
When a client contacts you to advise they intend travelling overseas you need to obtain the following information:
- date of departure
- date of return
- whether their disability costs are continuing
## Non-beneficiary Extra help payment will not continue
When Disability Allowance payments are not continuing because the client does not qualify due to their absence, you will need to suspend the benefit from:
- the day after departure
For more information see:
- Permanent absence
- Client does not return
- Married, civil union or de facto clients
- Return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Permanent absence — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
If the client is leaving New Zealand permanently Disability Allowance should be cancelled from the day after departure.

chunks.title: Permanent disability — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text:
## Permanent disability
When a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner has confirmed a client (or their partner or dependent child, if any) has a permanent disability that never needs to be reassessed, the client is still required to confirm their ongoing additional costs arising from that disability and to provide evidence of any cost that:
- has increased or
- is a new cost.
Note if a client has a change in circumstances, MSD will need to assess the client’s eligibility for Disability Allowance and determine the rate payable depending on when the change in circumstances happened or will happen.
## New cost to be included
If a client has a new cost to be included in their Disability Allowance, they must provide a new medical certificate completed by their registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner that confirms the new cost is a result of the client's disability, on-going and of therapeutic value.
## Cost included has reduced
Verification of a disability cost is not required if the client states a cost that is already included in their Disability Allowance has reduced. If the cost has reduced, accept this and review the client's (or their partner or dependent child, if any) Disability Allowance.
## Cost is unchanged
Generally, verification is not required if a cost included in a client’s Disability Allowance is unchanged. However, MSD may carry out a separate review of the Disability Allowance at any time, where there is good reason. This could be where MSD is unsure about a cost e.g., a change in pharmaceutical subsidies has happened and the client has not advised of that change.
For more information see:
- Change in costs

chunks.title: Protected earnings rate — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Both the District Court Act and the Summary Proceedings Act provide that every attachment order must specify a 'protected earnings rate'. The protected earnings rate is usually 60% of the client’s net earnings after PAYE tax has been deducted or withheld. If the attachment order will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate, then the order will not operate, and you must cancel or return the attachment order to the Ministry of Justice. Calculating the client's income differs between attachment orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act and the District Court Act, as different benefits are taken into account. It is important to determine what type of attachment order has been issued. Summary Proceedings Act 1957 For orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act, the calculation of the client's income does not include Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support, Disability Allowance, Child Disability Allowance, Winter Energy Payment, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit. District Court Act 2016 For orders made under the District Court Act, the client's income includes Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support and Disability Allowance but does not include Child Disability Allowance, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Example — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: An attachment order is received from the Ministry of Justice for $70.00 per week. The attachment order shows that the client's protected earnings rate is $307.83 per week. The client's attachment order falls under the District Court Act 2016. The client's Disability Allowance is therefore included as income. We need to calculate whether adding the deduction of $70.00 will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate: Calculate protected earnings rate Jobseeker Support - single person 25+ years net rate (as at 1 April 2026) $372.55 Plus Accommodation Supplement (area 2) $105.00 Plus Disability Allowance $35.50 Total net earnings $513.05 60% of total net earnings (= protected earnings) $307.83 Calculate if Attachment Order will exceed protected earnings Total net earnings $513.05 Less Child Support deduction $75.00 Less Ministry of Social Development debts $75.00 Sub-total $363.05 Less Court Order $70.00 Total $293.05 The court order takes the client's income to $293.05, which is below the protected income rate of $307.83 per week. The attachment order will not operate therefore you must return it to the Ministry of Justice for the order to be amended.

chunks.title: Reviews of Disability Allowance — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Disability Allowance is reviewed to check a client’s (or their partner’s or dependent child’s, if any) disability assessment, and any ongoing costs related to that disability are still accurate. MSD may review Disability Allowance at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment. There are two types of periodic reviews a client can have for Disability Allowance: - Medical Review - Mandatory Review Note for Mandatory Reviews, New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran’s Pension clients, and non-beneficiaries receiving Disability Allowance must also confirm their income.

chunks.title: Medical Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: The Medical Review occurs when a client’s (or their partner’s or dependent child’s, if any) disability is due for reassessment. A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must check if the client (or their partner or dependent child, if any): - still meets the qualifications for Disability Allowance (this includes confirming if the disability duration will be for 6 months or more) and - has ongoing costs arising from that disability and that those costs are of therapeutic value. A client will not have a reassessment of their disability when a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner has confirmed that the client or their family member has a permanent disability. Note if the registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner indicates the duration is less than 6 months, the client is not eligible for Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review — extra help > disability allowance > changes and reviews disability allowance
chunks.text: Clients getting Disability Allowance must respond to the Mandatory Review at least once every 52-weeks.
