In some cases, family tax credit and Best Start tax credits may be stopped for an indefinite period because the main benefit is suspended. Stopping the family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments with the main benefit is not covered by the Ministry’s review and appeal process.
The client should be advised to contact Inland Revenue for continued payment of Best Start tax credit and family tax credit.
The review rights for the main benefit still apply.

chunks.title: Commencement date — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
Family tax credit starts from the date the main benefit is granted if the client is not getting their family tax credit payments from Inland Revenue.
If the client is still getting their family tax credit paid by Inland Revenue but want to get it from the Ministry of Social Development instead, it will start from the beginning of the next full pay period after the benefit has been granted.
Family tax credit is paid with the main benefit.

chunks.title: Dependent child — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
For family tax credit a dependent child of any client means a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of that client
- maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
- not getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989
- not a child for whom Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid
- in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but has been returned to their parent's care

chunks.title: Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples
To help you identify when there is a dependent child, please see the examples below:
Household
Payments
Outcome
Parent and young person, aged between 16-18 years old.
Parent receiving Sole Parent Support (SPS), young person receiving no assistance.
Young person is a dependent child.

Parent and young person aged between 16-18 years old and young person’s baby.

Both the young person and the young person’s baby are dependent children of the parent.
Couple (parents) and young person aged between 16-18 years old and young person’s baby.

Both the young person and the young person’s baby are dependent children of the parents.
Couple (parents) and young person aged between 16-18 years old and young person’s baby.
Parents receiving Jobseeker Support half married rate, young person receiving Young Parent Payment.
Young person is no longer dependent on their parents however the baby is a dependent child of the young person.

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Family tax credit is one of 5 income-tested tax credits administered by Inland Revenue that make up Working for Families Tax Credits for low-income families.
The Ministry of Social Development pays family tax credit on behalf of Inland Revenue to clients receiving a main benefit. Inland Revenue has overall legislative and administrative responsibility for this assistance.
When a client is receiving a main benefit they can get family tax credit and Best Start tax credit, but cannot receive any other Working for Families Tax Credits.
The income threshold for family tax credit is higher than the main benefits income thresholds. This means that a client's main benefit will stop due to their income level before the family tax credit income threshold is reached. If a client receives a main benefit the Ministry can pay the maximum rate of family tax credit.
Inland Revenue is responsible for all payments of family tax credit to families:
- who receive a main benefit but choose to get their family tax credit from Inland Revenue or
- not receiving a main benefit
New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension clients with dependent children must apply to Inland Revenue for payment of family tax credits and Best Start tax credits.
On 1 July 2018 the 5 separate rates of family tax credit were merged into 2 rates, for the eldest child, and the second or subsequent children.
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Payment
- Commencement date
- Changes and reviews
- Deskfile Family tax credit rates

chunks.title: Payment from Ministry of Social Development or Inland Revenue — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Payment from Ministry of Social Development or Inland Revenue
Main benefit clients can choose to have their family tax credit and Best Start tax credit paid by Inland Revenue or Ministry of Social Development.
This would be more practical for clients who are expecting to get a main benefit for only a short period of time. Best Start tax credit and family tax credit must be paid together, by either Inland Revenue or Ministry of Social Development.
Foster care parents that receive a main benefit and have children of their own, will have their family tax credit and Best Start tax credit paid by Inland Revenue.
Note clients getting Young Parent Payments cannot choose to have their Best Start tax credit and family tax credits paid by Inland Revenue.

chunks.title: Payment to partner — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Payment to partner
SWIFTT automatically pays family tax credit to the primary client. However, there are cases when the partner is the 'principal caregiver' and the partner should receive the family tax credit payment.
When the family tax credit payments are made to the partner:
- obtain written verification from the couple that the partner is the principal caregiver and family tax credit is to be paid to the partner
- use the SNSRA screen (of the primary client) to pay family tax credit to the partner
When there is a formal shared care agreement both partners may be able to receive a share of the family tax credit payment.
For more information see:
- Principal caregiver
- Shared care

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Payment
The Ministry of Social Development will pay the maximum rate of family tax credit when a client is receiving a main benefit.
Depending on the client's individual circumstances the Ministry can continue to pay a family tax credit up to 8 weeks after a benefit is suspended or cancelled. This allows Inland Revenue time to contact the client and start paying Working for Families Tax Credits.
The family tax credit rates depend on the number of children in the client's care and their children's age.

chunks.title: Principal caregiver — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Principal caregiver
Family tax credit is paid to the principal caregiver of a dependent child.
The definition of a principal caregiver for family tax credit is defined under the Income Tax Act 2007. This is different to the definition of principal caregiver used for other payments made by the Ministry of Social Development.
For family tax credit, a principal caregiver is the person who:
- has primary responsibility for the day-to-day care of the child, not on a temporary basis
The principal caregiver cannot be:
- a group of people (whether incorporated or unincorporated) or
- the partner of a transitional resident under the Income Tax Act 2007 or
- a person who is the owner of or employed in: a residence established under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989a residential disability care institution under the Health and Disability Services (Safety) Act 2001 orany other institution where a child is being cared for
- a residence established under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989
- a residential disability care institution under the Health and Disability Services (Safety) Act 2001 or
- any other institution where a child is being cared for
Family tax credit is automatically paid in full to the primary client. When the partner of the primary client is the principal caregiver, family tax credit payments should be paid to the partner.
In a sole parent family, family tax credit is paid in full to the parent who has the most day-to-day care of the child or children.

chunks.title: Protected family tax credit while getting a main benefit — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Protected family tax credit while getting a main benefit
Family tax credit is part of an annual tax system - payment is assessed using a family's income in the whole of the tax year.
## Client is getting a main benefit
A client will get the maximum rate of family tax credit and Best Start tax credits while they are getting a main benefit.
If the client had a high income before going on benefit or after moving off benefit they still qualify for the maximum rate of family tax credit while they are getting a benefit.
Note this protection applies for the whole of a calendar month if the client receives benefit at any time during that month (provided their gross income in that month does not exceed $3,741 as at 1 April 2026).
For example, if a client gets a main benefit in the first week of the month only, they will still receive protected family tax credit for the whole of that calendar month.
Important exception - Do not include any income from a main benefit, pension or employment obtained in the calendar month because of an extra pay in that month.
## Family tax credit is paid by Inland Revenue
The family tax credit protection rules also apply if Inland Revenue pays the family tax credit when the client is getting a benefit.
## Example of protected family tax credit
A client is married with 2 children. He was a seasonal worker at the local freezing works, worked full-time from April to end of July, and then again from December to end of March and earned $925.00 gross per week ($4,008 per month).
From August to the end of November, he was on Jobseeker Support during his off-season and earned no other income.
This means that while the client was getting Jobseeker Support, he could get the maximum rate of family tax credit because his total gross income was below $3,741 for each calendar month, even though his total income for the tax year was more than $44,900 (as at 1 April 2026).

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
The Ministry of Social Development can pay a family tax credit to the client if they are the principal caregiver of a dependent child or children, and
the client is getting one of the following benefits:
- Jobseeker Support
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship
- Sole Parent Support
- Emergency Benefit
- Emergency Maintenance Allowance
- Supported Living Payment
- Young Parent Payment
New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension clients with dependent children must apply to Inland Revenue for assessment and payment of family tax credits.

chunks.title: Shared care — extra help > family tax credit
chunks.text:
## Shared care
For family tax credit purposes when there is shared care, there can be more than one principal caregiver. Both parents of a dependent child can qualify as a principal caregiver in shared care cases and be entitled to family tax credit if:
- they are living apart and
- they both qualify and
- they care for the dependent child for at least a third of the time throughout the tax year
If a child is under the care of each parent for more than 2 days of a week then Inland Revenue recognises the shared care arrangement and each parent can be paid the appropriate amount of family tax credit.
For the Ministry of Social Development to pay family tax credit in shared care cases, the client must have a formal agreement and supply a copy of either:
- the signed care agreement or
- the court order stating the arrangement
For information about how to process family tax credit in shared care cases in SWIFTT contact Helpline.
When one parent has care of the child(ren) for 2 days or less they cannot receive the family tax credit. In this situation all of the family tax credit is paid to the parent with the majority of the care.
Note when there is an informal care agreement refer the client to Inland Revenue for any family tax credit payments.
For more information see:
- Principal caregiver

chunks.title: Age — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Age
To qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance, a client must be:
- a young person or
- of working-age
Note people who are getting Youth Payment and people who are younger than 15 years old do not qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: At risk of long-term benefit receipt — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: To qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance, MSD must consider the client to be at risk of long-term benefit receipt. This means there is a risk the client will get or continue getting a main benefit for an indefinite period. To decide if a person is at risk of getting a benefit long-term, several factors need to be considered. These include: - demographic information e.g. age, gender, ethnicity and location - level of skills, employment experience and education - specific barriers to employment e.g. medical conditions, caring responsibilities - benefit status and history e.g. current period they have been getting a main benefit, time spent on and off benefit, age when they first started getting a benefit - previous times they got, or participated in, MSD employment programmes and services

chunks.title: Example 1 — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: Lani is the principal caregiver for 10 year old, Huia. She used to get Jobseeker Support, but cancelled her benefit so that she could increase her hours at work. She works multiple casual jobs. Lani has been offered a new permanent role. If she accepts this, she only needs to work for one employer and would have a more stable income. However, this position requires her to regularly work on weekends and she can't afford a private babysitter for Huia. Lani has low job security, got a benefit in the past and if she doesn't get Flexible Childcare Assistance, she won't be able to accept the new role. These factors mean Lani is at risk of long-term benefit receipt and may be able to get Flexible Childcare Assistance if she meets the other qualifications.

chunks.title: Example 2 — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: Jess and Meka have a 2 year old son, Rawiri. Rawiri attends playcentre for 25 hours a week. Jess often works night shifts and Meka has recently cancelled her Jobseeker Support to take up part-time work. She picks up Rawiri after she finishes work and looks after him in the evenings. Meka has been offered some extra hours involving evening work. She needs someone to look after Rawiri and her Mum has offered to help for free when his playcentre closes. Meka could be considered at risk of long-term benefit receipt because she got a benefit in the past. However, she would not be able to get Flexible Childcare Assistance because she doesn't need this to help her accept the extra hours at work.

chunks.title: Getting or qualifying to get a main benefit — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: Generally, a person at risk of long-term benefit receipt is either: - getting (or qualifies to get) a main benefit or - has a partner who is getting (or qualifies to get) a main benefit

chunks.title: On a main benefit and not at risk of long-term benefit receipt — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: Not everyone getting a main benefit is at risk of long-term benefit receipt. For example, a person who is work ready is considered capable of getting into and staying in work without our help and only needs a benefit for a short time while they find work. These people would not qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance because they are not at risk of long-term benefit receipt.

chunks.title: Not on a main benefit but at risk of long-term benefit receipt — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: Sometimes people who are not on a main benefit and are in employment are at risk of long-term benefit receipt. For example, the client: - has applied for and been assessed as eligible for a main benefit - has previously received a main benefit - is underemployed (i.e., available for full-time work but are unable to secure full-time job opportunities) - has low job security (e.g., they are a casual or fixed-term worker) Note this list is not exhaustive. A person who is not currently getting a main benefit may only qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance if: - they are considered at risk of long-term benefit receipt and - not getting help with their informal childcare costs would mean they cannot participate in the specified employment activity

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
Generally, clients cannot continue getting Flexible Childcare Assistance while they are absent from New Zealand because they won't be participating in a specified employment activity or have informal childcare costs.
If a client is temporarily absent from New Zealand, Flexible Childcare Assistance payments can only continue for up to 28 days from the day after the date they leave the country if the client continues to meet the qualifications.
Payment while a client is absent from New Zealand is limited to 28 days in a 52 week period.
Clients who are getting Flexible Childcare Assistance:
- must advise of their departure from New Zealand and
- can be absent and paid their Flexible Childcare Assistance for up to 28 days per absence where the client remains eligible for Flexible Childcare Assistance
If the client leaves New Zealand permanently, Flexible Childcare Assistance payments stop from the day after departure.

chunks.title: Absence from specified employment activity — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Absence from specified employment activity
Clients must advise of any change in circumstances that affects their entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance, such as being absent from their specified employment activity.
When a client is absent from their specified employment activity, Flexible Childcare Assistance may only continue during a temporary absence.
This includes (but is not limited to) when the absence is due to:
- illness, injury, or disability
- hospitalisation
- weather conditions
- school holidays (provided the education provider requires the client to continue studying during the vacation period)
- paid employment leave, e.g. sick leave or annual leave. This does not include periods of paid parental leave.
To continue getting Flexible Childcare Assistance during a temporary absence, clients must still meet all the other qualifications, including having informal childcare costs.
If the absence is no longer considered temporary, entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance stops on the date MSD considers the absence to be permanent.
Any change in circumstances that lasts for more than 8 weeks are generally considered to be a permanent change for Flexible Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews - Flexible Childcare Assistance — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews - Flexible Childcare Assistance
A client is obliged to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance.
Flexible Childcare Assistance may also be reviewed by MSD at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
Note clients do not need to tell MSD if their costs change, provided they continue to have ongoing costs associated with informal childcare.

chunks.title: Changes in living situation or childcare arrangements — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Changes in living situation or childcare arrangements
Clients must advise MSD of any change in circumstances that affects their entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance, such as a change in their childcare or living arrangements.
This includes (but is not limited to):
- change of address
- dependent children entering or leaving their care
- a change in shared care arrangements
- formal childcare becoming available
- no longer having costs associated with informal childcare
Generally, relationship status changes do not affect a client's entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance. However, the following situations may mean that entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance stops, e.g. when a client:
- separates from their partner and moves to an area where there are formal childcare options while they are at work
- separates from their partner and is no longer the child's (or children's) principal caregiver
- is no longer considered at risk of long-term benefit receipt because of a change in relationship status (e.g. they start a relationship with someone who can financially provide for them and their family)
Note this list is not exhaustive.
## Care and protection concerns
When a child has come into a client's care, MSD should consider if there are any care and protection concerns.
If MSD believes any child has been, or is likely to be harmed (physically, emotionally or sexually), ill-treated, abused, neglected, deprived or MSD has concerns about the wellbeing of the child, the case must be referred to Oranga Tamariki.
MSD staff must notify Oranga Tamariki if they are aware that the child's sole caregiver has been remanded in custody and/or sentenced to a term of imprisonment.

chunks.title: Changes in specified employment activity — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Changes in specified employment activity
Clients must advise of any change in circumstances that affects their entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance, such as changes to their hours or their specified employment activity ending.
If a client is transferring to a different activity, they must check with MSD if the new activity is a qualifying specified employment activity.
To continue getting Flexible Childcare Assistance, clients must still meet all the other qualifications, including having costs associated with informal childcare for at least 3 hours a week while they are participating in the specified employment activity.
If a client leaves their specified employment activity or if the activity ends (e.g., because their course has finished), they are no longer entitled to Flexible Childcare Assistance from the day after the change occurs.

chunks.title: Child changes — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Child changes
Clients must advise MSD of any changes in a dependent child's circumstances that may affect the client's entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance.
Generally, entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance stops when a client no longer has informal childcare costs for that child. For example, when a child turns 14 and can stay home alone or when a child who cannot stay home alone turns 18.
If other children still need informal childcare, then the client's rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance is reduced to reflect the remaining number of children that still require informal childcare.
## Temporary absence
Flexible Childcare Assistance can be paid for up to one week while a child does not need informal childcare temporarily (e.g. because the child is unwell).
If a child no longer needs informal childcare or is unwell for more than one week, entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance should be reviewed from the day the change occurs.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
To be included in the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance, dependent children must generally be under the age of 14 years old. This is because children aged 14 and older can legally be left at home alone for short periods of time without supervision.
The only exception is when their individual circumstances mean the child requires supervision and cannot safely be left home alone, e.g. because of a health condition or disability. In these situations, a child can generally continue to be included in the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance until their 18th birthday.
## Continuing in education and not financially independent
An 18-year-old child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance for a limited period if they require supervision and cannot safely be left home alone and they are:
- continuing in education and
- not financially independent
If the client is getting a benefit or Community Costs, the 18-year-old must be excluded from the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance from the same date they are excluded from the parent or caregiver's benefit.
If the client does not get a benefit or Community Costs, the 18-year-old must generally be excluded from the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance from the date they no longer meet the above criteria. They must not be included any later than the start of the week following 31 December of the year they turn 18.
## Getting a main benefit
If a parent or caregiver is getting a main benefit, and their main benefit is suspended due to their child turning 18, their Flexible Childcare Assistance will also suspend.
Note main benefits do not include Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Death of a client — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
When a client who is getting Flexible Childcare Assistance dies, entitlement stops from the day after death.
## Death of a child
When a child for whom Flexible Childcare Assistance is being paid dies, entitlement stops from the day after death.
## Death of other child in family
Flexible Childcare Assistance must be reviewed to ensure the client is getting the correct rate.

chunks.title: Debts — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Debts
A debt is created when a client is overpaid Flexible Childcare Assistance.
When a debt is created, it must be checked against the debt write-off criteria to decide if the debt or part of the debt is recoverable.

chunks.title: Ending the payment — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Ending the payment
Eligible clients can get Flexible Childcare Assistance for a maximum of 52 weeks.
If a client does not get the full 52 week duration of Flexible Childcare Assistance, they can get the remaining amount for a later application if they meet all the qualifications.
However, if the client has previously been paid 52 weeks of Flexible Childcare Assistance, they are not eligible to get Flexible Childcare Assistance again.
## Example 1
Rob is the principal caregiver for 9-year-old Christine and 7-year-old Harlow.
He cancelled his benefit to take up a new job and gets Flexible Childcare Assistance to help with the costs associated with informal childcare for Christine and Harlow when he is working night shifts.
Rob's Flexible Childcare Assistance commenced on Monday 15 April 2024.
Rob can keep getting Flexible Childcare Assistance as long as he continues to meet all qualifications.
He can get up to a maximum of 52 weeks of Flexible Childcare Assistance, or until Sunday 13 April 2025.
## Example 2
Cam is the principal caregiver of 6-year-old Katie.
Cam recently completed a 12 week workplace communication course. This took place every Sunday from 12 May until 28 July and each session was 6 hours.
He got 12 weeks of Flexible Childcare Assistance to help with the informal childcare costs for Katie (while he was in employment-related training). His Flexible Childcare Assistance payments stopped when the course ended.
Cam has now been offered a permanent position at his work from 5 August and this will involve a weekly 4 hour Sunday shift. He will have informal childcare costs associated with Katie's care while he is at work on Sundays.
Cam has already received 12 weeks of Flexible Childcare Assistance for his previous course. If he applies and qualifies for Flexible Childcare Assistance again, he can get a maximum of another 40 weeks.
Cam applies for, qualifies for, and is granted Flexible Childcare Assistance from the week starting 5 August (for Katie's informal childcare costs on Sundays).
He can keep getting Flexible Childcare Assistance as long as he continues to meet all qualifications for a maximum of 40 more weeks, or until the week ending Sunday 11 May.

chunks.title: Imprisonment — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
When a Flexible Childcare Assistance client is imprisoned or detained in custody, they are generally no longer entitled to get Flexible Childcare Assistance.
Entitlement to Flexible Childcare Assistance stops from the day after either, the date:
- of imprisonment or
- they are remanded in custody
## Remanded in custody
Generally, when a client is remanded in custody awaiting a further court appearance their financial assistance should be stopped.
However, there is discretion to continue payment of Flexible Childcare Assistance after taking the client's financial circumstances and commitments into account.
When considering whether to continue paying Flexible Childcare Assistance for the period for a client, consider the following:
- has the client been remanded pending a further court hearing or for sentencing
- are the client's informal childcare costs continuing
- is the client still primarily responsible for the day-to-day care of their dependent child (or children)
Every situation should be looked at on a case-by-case basis.
Clients must meet all qualifications to keep getting Flexible Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: Temporary illness — extra help > flexible childcare assistance > changes and reviews flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Temporary illness
Flexible Childcare Assistance can continue being paid for a maximum of 8 weeks if the qualifications are met and the client:
- is participating in a specified employment activity and
- is unable to participate in their specified employment activity due to sickness, injury or disability and
- still has informal childcare costs for at least 3 hours per week
## Example
Tākuta starts work at 6.00am on Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. He gets Flexible Childcare Assistance to help with the cost of having his friend look after his son Jaxson from 5.30am to 8.00am on these days (2.5 hours per day before school).
Tākuta injures his leg and requires 3 weeks off work. He provides MSD with a medical certificate. As he is unable to drive while he recovers, his friend helps care for Jaxson and gets him to and from school each day for Tākuta. This takes 5 hours per week.
Tākuta still qualifies for Flexible Childcare Assistance because his absence from work is expected to be temporary and he still meets all the other qualifications (including having costs associated with informal childcare for at least 3 hours a week).

chunks.title: Childcare arrangements — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: To qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance, a client must have costs associated with informal childcare because they are unable to access formal childcare while participating in a specified employment activity. For school-aged children, Flexible Childcare Assistance is generally not payable for informal childcare during school hours during school terms as the child is required to be in education.

chunks.title: Unable to access formal childcare — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: Formal childcare is generally provided by a licensed or certified early childhood service and is available during standard business hours (e.g. between 7am and 6pm, Monday to Friday). Unable to access formal childcare means there are no places available in formal childcare, or formal childcare options are not suitable for the client's situation. This may include situations when the client is participating in a specified employment activity at times when: - formal childcare services are closed (e.g. during the evening or on weekends) or - there are no available places in formal childcare services within a reasonable distance (e.g. if the client lives rurally and the local services are full) If there are no available places in formal childcare, MSD may consider: - how the client is travelling (public transport or private vehicle) - how far the location of care is from their home or workplace - what time the specified employment activity starts

chunks.title: Formal childcare not suitable — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: There may also be some situations when a child has a health condition or disability that means formal childcare is not suitable for their individual circumstances. For example, a neurodiverse child may have difficulty attending centre-based early childhood education and may require one-on-one care, or care outside of a limited number of hours the centre can provide.

chunks.title: Costs associated with informal childcare — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: Informal childcare is any childcare not provided by a licensed early childhood education service or certified playgroup. This generally means care arranged by the client either in the child's home or elsewhere, provided by relatives, friends, neighbours, or babysitters. To qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance, a client must have ongoing costs associated with informal childcare. The amount and type of cost may vary from week to week and can include one-off costs such as: - travel (e.g. fuel or public transport costs to drop off or pick up a child from the place of care) - food (e.g. the cost of meals while a child is being cared for) - reimbursement for the carer's time (including in-kind payments and babysitting fees) - groceries (for the carer in lieu of a cash payment) Note this is not an exhaustive list. MSD has discretion to determine if the informal childcare costs are acceptable, considering the client's individual circumstances.

chunks.title: Suitable and safe childcare — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text: Clients are responsible for choosing and organising appropriate care for their child (or children). This could include the client: - asking the person who will be caring for their child for a reference or a copy of their criminal record - thinking about the safety of the environment where their child will be cared for, (e.g. other people who will be there, animals, swimming pools or stairs) - checking if their child will be travelling in the person's vehicle, whether the person has a driver licence, and whether the vehicle is safe - talking to the person about how they want their child looked after, including discussing any specific needs or medical conditions

chunks.title: Commencement date — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
The commencement date for Flexible Childcare Assistance depends on a client's entitlement date and the date of application.
The entitlement date is the date all qualifications are met.
If a client applies for Flexible Childcare Assistance within a reasonable period of their entitlement date, the commencement date is the entitlement date. A reasonable period is generally considered to be 28 days or less.
If a client does not apply for Flexible Childcare Assistance within a reasonable period of their entitlement date, the commencement date is the date of application.
Note if a client applies for Flexible Childcare Assistance before their entitlement date, the commencement date is the future entitlement date.
## Example 1
A client became eligible for Flexible Childcare Assistance on 1 April but does not apply for this until 26 April.
They have applied for Flexible Childcare Assistance within a reasonable period of their entitlement date (within 28 days).
This means Flexible Childcare Assistance can be backdated to commence from 1 April.
## Example 2
A client became eligible for Flexible Childcare Assistance on 1 April but does not apply for this until 30 April.
They have not applied for Flexible Childcare Assistance within a reasonable period of their entitlement date (more than 28 days since meeting all the qualifications).
This means Flexible Childcare Assistance payments can commence from 30 April.
## Example 3
A client starts a specified employment activity on 1 January, and they have access to free informal childcare until 21 January.
Their entitlement date is the day that their childcare costs start.
This means Flexible Childcare Assistance payments can commence from 22 January.

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Flexible Childcare Assistance provides financial assistance for informal childcare costs to support caregivers who are:
- considered at risk of long-term benefit receipt and
- participating in or entering into a specified employment activity for at least 3 hours a week and
- have costs associated with informal childcare because they are unable to access formal childcare during those hours

chunks.title: Other childcare assistance — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Other childcare assistance
Clients who get other assistance for the same informal childcare costs do not qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance.
However, a client can get multiple types of childcare assistance if their costs are not fully covered by one type of assistance.
This includes but is not limited to:
Note other childcare assistance can be paid if that assistance is not for the same hours as Flexible Childcare Assistance, including:

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Payment
The Flexible Childcare Assistance rate of payment depends on the number of dependent children a client has informal childcare costs for and the age of the children. This is paid at a flat rate for each week.
Flexible Childcare Assistance can be paid for a maximum of 52 weeks (per client) after the payment commences.
Flexible Childcare Assistance is paid directly to the client or their agent (if authorised).
The client is responsible for paying the informal childcare costs themselves.
## Age of children
To be included in the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance, dependent children must generally be under the age of 14.
This is because children aged 14 and older can legally be left at home alone for short periods of time without supervision. There is no lower age limit.
Exceptions
Children aged 14 to 17 may be able to be included in the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance when they require supervision and cannot safely be left home alone (e.g. because of a health condition or disability).
Children aged 18 may also be able to be included in the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance when they are considered a dependent child and require supervision, are financially dependent on a principal caregiver, and continuing in education.
## Child turns 18
When a dependent child turns 18, they can no longer be included in the rate of Flexible Childcare Assistance, unless they are continuing in education and are not financially independent.

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
To qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance, a client must:
- meet the residence requirements and
- meet the age qualifications and
- are the principal caregiver or principal temporary caregiver of a dependent child and
- are considered at risk of long-term benefit receipt and
- have costs associated with informal childcare because they are unable to access formal childcare and
- are participating in or entering into a specified employment activity and
- are in the specified employment activity for at least 3 hours a week when they require informal childcare
Note there are no income or asset limits for Flexible Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: Residence — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Residence
To get Flexible Childcare Assistance, a client must:
- be a New Zealand citizen or
- have a residence class visa in New Zealand under the Immigration Act 2009 that allows the client to work in New Zealand or
- be deemed to hold a residence class visa under the Immigration Act 2009 that allows the client to work in New Zealand or
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they first apply for assistance and
- generally be ordinarily resident in New Zealand
Note for Flexible Childcare Assistance no period of residence is required.
People who are in New Zealand unlawfully or here on a temporary entry class visa generally do not qualify for assistance from MSD.
## Clients without citizenship or a residence class visa
If a client does not have New Zealand citizenship or a residence class visa, they can only get Flexible Childcare Assistance if they:
- are a person who has refugee or protected person status in New Zealand or
- hold a temporary entry class visa under the Immigration Act 2009 that allows the person to work in New Zealand and are: awaiting the outcome of their application for refugee or protected person status orapplying for a residence class visa under the Immigration Act 2009 and are compelled to remain in New Zealand through unforeseen circumstances
- awaiting the outcome of their application for refugee or protected person status or
- applying for a residence class visa under the Immigration Act 2009 and are compelled to remain in New Zealand through unforeseen circumstances
## Australian clients
Australian citizens or residents are lawfully allowed in New Zealand, as they hold a residence class visa.
However, they must still be ordinarily resident in New Zealand and meet all other criteria to qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: Shared care - principal caregiver — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Shared care - principal caregiver
To qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance, a client must be the principal caregiver or principal temporary caregiver of a dependent child.
Only one parent or caregiver (defined as the principal caregiver) can get Flexible Childcare Assistance. It cannot be paid to 2 parents or caregivers for the same child.
The parent or caregiver applying must meet the qualifications.

chunks.title: Specified employment activity — extra help > flexible childcare assistance
chunks.text:
## Specified employment activity
To qualify for Flexible Childcare Assistance, a client must be participating in or entering into a specified employment activity. This means:
- paid employment or
- employment-related education or
- employment-related training or
- rehabilitation programmes where their participation is necessary to retain or obtain employment
A client must be participating in a specified employment activity for at least 3 hours a week when they are unable to access formal childcare. The 3 hours can include lunch breaks, travel time, and contact study time.
## Paid employment
If the client won't be getting a main benefit while working, the paid employment (or change in hours if they are already working) must be sustainable employment. This means it must be expected to last for at least 13 weeks.
If a client will keep getting a main benefit while working, there is no minimum duration for the employment.
## Employment-related education or training
Employment-related education or employment-related training includes industry training, sector training, job-specific training, or on-the-job training.
There is no minimum course duration for clients who are entering into or participating in employment-related education or training.
Note if a client is applying for Flexible Childcare Assistance for a course that is for 13 weeks or longer, it must be Level 3 or below on the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF).
## Rehabilitation programmes
If a client is attending a rehabilitation programme, they may be able to get Flexible Childcare Assistance if the programme will help them prepare for or return to employment. They do not have to currently be in paid employment or have a specific offer of employment to qualify.
Rehabilitation programmes are considered on a case-by-case basis and may include:
- programmes aimed at enabling people with ill health and disabled people to reach and maintain their optimal level
- drug and alcohol rehabilitation programmes
- ex-offenders' rehabilitation programmes
Note this list is not exhaustive.
Flexible Childcare Assistance cannot be paid for a client to participate in a residential rehabilitation programme. Clients in this situation may be able to get Community Costs. For more information see:

chunks.title: Application requirements — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Application requirements
A client may be able to get Flexible Funding Assistance if the MSD is satisfied:
- they have an immediate need for assistance
- the client meets the qualifications and
- they have provided any supporting evidence MSD has reasonably required

chunks.title: Assistance for the period client is staying in emergency housing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Assistance for the period client is staying in emergency housing
Flexible Funding Assistance is paid for the client or their immediate family's needs only when they are staying in accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant.
It cannot be used to cover costs after the:
- Emergency Housing Grant has ended, or
- client has left the accommodation (if the assistance has not already been paid)
If the immediate need continues and the client is paid another Emergency Housing Grant, Flexible Funding Assistance can be paid again if the client meets the qualifications.
## Calculating period to pay assistance
Mandy is paid an Emergency Housing Grant for 7 nights on 1 March (1 March - 7 March). As their child's school is not on the school bus route nearest the emergency housing, they need additional help to pay for public transport ($15 per day). The client is unable to pay for this cost themselves and do not qualify for other assistance.
Mandy is granted Flexible Funding Assistance on 4 March to pay for public transport for the remainder of their stay (4 March - 7 March).
After the first 7 nights Mandy still needs emergency housing and is paid another Special Needs Grant for emergency housing for 7 nights (8 March - 14 March). Mandy is also granted Flexible Funding Assistance again as she still needs help with public transport for their child, Flexible Funding Assistance is paid again for 7 days.
## Example
1 March to 7 March (Grant 1)
8 March to 14 March (Grant 2)
Emergency Housing Grant
7 nights from 1 March
7 nights from 8 March
Flexible Funding Assistance
4 days from 4 March
Cost to meet the need per day: $15
Flexible Funding Assistance granted, and provider makes payment of $60
7 days from 8 March
Cost to meet the need per day: $15
Flexible Funding Assistance granted, and provider makes payment of $105
## Client leaves emergency housing before assistance ends
Sometimes a client will leave emergency housing before the period of their grant, and the period that Flexible Assistance Payment has been paid.
In these cases, the client cannot get any further grants of Flexible Funding Assistance but as the assistance has already been paid for a service for the grant period, this can continue to be used (e.g. the school lunches have already been paid for).

chunks.title: Benefit sanctioned due to an obligation failure - applying for an Emergency Housing Grant — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Benefit sanctioned due to an obligation failure - applying for an Emergency Housing Grant
A client cannot get Flexible Funding Assistance if their benefit is sanctioned as they do not qualify for an Emergency Housing Grant. This includes financial sanctions and non-financial sanctions.
This applies even if they were getting it before and an Emergency Housing Grant had been made.
The client must resolve the failure and have an Emergency Housing Grant granted, to again qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance.
## Benefit sanctioned due to an obligation failure - currently getting an Emergency Housing Grant
If a client is already in emergency housing and their benefit is sanctioned due to an obligation failure, this will not affect their Flexible Funding Assistance before the end of the grant period.
However, MSD may need to review the need and amount of assistance provided.
## Reduced or suspended on other grounds
If a client has their benefit reduced or suspended for any other reason than an obligation failure e.g. income, this will generally not affect their Flexible Funding Assistance.
However, MSD may need to review their needs, and amount of assistance provided.
There are situations where MSD cannot pay an Emergency Housing Grant and the grant must be declined. If a client is declined an Emergency Housing Grant for 1 of these reasons, they will not qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance.

chunks.title: Cash asset limit — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Cash asset limit
To qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance, the cash assets of the client and their partner (if any) generally must not exceed the appropriate asset limit.
## Cash asset limit for Flexible Funding Assistance
The appropriate cash asset limit for
for Flexible Funding Assistance is the same cash asset limit used for an Emergency Housing Grant for:
- a couple (with children), or
- sole parents
Note a bank overdraft facility is not considered a cash asset or resource available to a client for Flexible Funding Assistance.
## Exceptions for paying Flexible Funding Assistance when over income and asset limits
In exceptional circumstances, MSD can pay Flexible Funding Assistance if the client and/or their partner (if any) have income and assets over the relevant limits.

chunks.title: Client can meet their need from other sources of assistance — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: Flexible Funding Assistance can only be paid when the client's immediate need cannot be met from other available sources of assistance. Before granting Flexible Funding Assistance, MSD needs to consider whether other assistance is or might be available to the client to meet their immediate need (i.e. from both MSD and non-MSD assistance).

chunks.title: Other assistance provided to the dependent child — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: When other assistance to fully meet the need is, or can be, provided directly to the dependent child, such as school lunches or transport funded through another agency, the need will be considered able to be met through other forms of assistance.

chunks.title: Other assistance will not fully meet the need — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: When there is other assistance available that will partially meet the need, Flexible Funding Assistance can be granted to meet any shortfall. For example, where the Ministry of Health or Ministry of Education funding will meet some of any additional travel costs due to the family being in emergency housing, Flexible Funding Assistance can be used to pay for the unsubsidised portion only.

chunks.title: Other MSD assistance — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: Clients must be made aware of all of the financial assistance from MSD available to them to help meet the need and alleviate hardship. If a client qualifies for other assistance from MSD to meet the specific need, that assistance must be granted before Flexible Funding Assistance. Flexible Funding Assistance should only be considered as the last option available after all other sources of assistance to meet the need have been exhausted. The following assistance should be considered (including using discretion to exceed limits in exceptional circumstances where appropriate) before granting Flexible Funding Assistance: If a client's existing debt level or inability to repay the assistance would mean that a Recoverable Assistance Payment or Advance Payment of Benefit cannot be granted, then it would be reasonable to use the Flexible Funding Assistance as an alternative, if all criteria are met. Where the client or partner (if any) is getting MSD assistance with other needs (i.e. needs that are not covered by Flexible Funding Assistance), this will not affect their eligibility for Flexible Funding Assistance.

chunks.title: Student assistance — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: When the client or their partner (if any) are a student, staff will consider the balance of any Student Loan living costs or course-related costs available (where appropriate). Under no circumstances will students be referred to institution hardship funds (e.g. funds administered by universities for students in hardship).

chunks.title: Civil Defence Payments — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: Civil Defence payments are available to meet the immediate needs of people who are affected by a civil defence emergency or adverse event. This includes paying for accommodation where the client has been required to leave their home, or who was away from home at the time of the emergency and is unable to return to their home, due to the emergency. A client getting a Civil Defence payment will not be paid an Emergency Housing Grant during this time and Flexible Funding Assistance won't be paid for people in accommodation funded by Civil Defence Payments.

chunks.title: Client can meet their need from their own resources — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Client can meet their need from their own resources
To have an immediate need for Flexible Funding Assistance, you must be satisfied the client and their partner (if any) does not have enough resources available to them to meet the need.
A client may be able to meet their immediate need from their own available resources when the client (and their partner, if any):
- has sufficient income left after essential expenses to meet the need from their next income, benefit or pension payment without causing serious hardship
- has cash assets that can be used to meet the need (that are not needed for essential expenses)
- can arrange automatic payments or negotiate payment by instalments, including hire purchase
- can access assistance from other government agencies to meet the need eg from the Ministry of Health or Ministry of Education
Note this list is not exhaustive.
A bank overdraft facility is not considered a cash asset or resource available when determining whether the client has an immediate need that can be paid for by Flexible Funding Assistance.
When you consider the client can meet their immediate need from their own resources or other sources, Flexible Funding cannot be paid.
## Use of resources to meet the need would cause serious hardship
When you consider the client or their immediate family would be in serious hardship if they used their available resources to meet the immediate need, the Ministry may still grant Flexible Funding Assistance for that need.
Serious hardship is when the client would be unable to meet their own or their immediate family's other immediate and essential needs (eg food or health costs) from their remaining resources. Their remaining resources includes any other assistance they are getting (or qualify to get) from the Ministry (eg Extra help).
Example
The client and her partner only have $30 left each week, after meeting their immediate and essential needs.

chunks.title: Client dies while in emergency housing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Client dies while in emergency housing
If a client dies while staying in emergency housing and has been granted Flexible Funding Assistance before their death, the assistance can continue being paid to the relevant suppliers until the end of the client's current Emergency Housing Grant.
At the end of the deceased client's Emergency Housing Grant period, their partner may be able to apply for another grant and Flexible Funding Assistance.

chunks.title: Client leaves emergency housing before assistance ends — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Client leaves emergency housing before assistance ends
Clients who have been paid an Emergency Housing Grant for the current period but have moved elsewhere before the end of the grant period, cannot get any further grants of Flexible Funding Assistance. However, as the assistance has already been paid for a service for the grant period, this can continue to be used (e.g. the school lunches needed for the week have already been paid).
Example
Ropata was paid an Emergency Housing Grant for 2 weeks (9 November to 23 November). Ropata was also granted Flexible Funding Assistance to help with their child’s additional childcare costs from being in emergency housing. On 18 November, Ropata moved into a private rental so no longer qualifies for Flexible Funding Assistance for childcare costs from this date. However, if the childcare has already been paid for 18-23 November, Ropata can use this service.
## Flexible Funding Assistance for past periods
Flexible Funding Assistance can be paid to cover past periods covered by the Emergency Housing Grant in certain circumstances. For example, it can be paid when a client is already staying in emergency housing and applies late for an Emergency Housing Grant to cover a past period (and has not caused or contributed to their immediate need).
Example
Ana is working full-time and receiving non-beneficiary assistance. Her 2-year-old daughter Georgia is staying with her in emergency housing. They have been there for 5 days as their accommodation ended and they were not able to find any other permanent accommodation.
Ana thought she had the funds to pay for this accommodation but then they had to pay for their car repairs which she needed to be able to get to work. Ana was worried about how she was going to pay the motel and so met with a case manager who advised them about the Emergency Housing Grant.
Based on this client's circumstances, the case manager agrees to grant the Emergency Housing Grant from the first day the client entered the emergency housing. Flexible Funding Assistance for additional travel to their child's daycare can also be considered from the day they moved into emergency housing if the client hasn't paid for this already.

chunks.title: Client on non-entitlement period for emergency housing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Client on non-entitlement period for emergency housing
Clients who are on a 13 week non-entitlement period for emergency housing do not qualify for an Emergency Housing Grant. These clients also do not qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance because they cannot get an Emergency Housing Grant.
However, clients (and their dependent children) who meet the limited circumstances criteria can be granted an Emergency Housing Grant while they are on their 13 week non-entitlement period. If the client meets the limited circumstances criteria, their 13 week non-entitlement period will be paused.
If a client meets the limited circumstances criteria and is granted an Emergency Housing Grant during their 13 week non-entitlement period they may be eligible for Flexible Funding Assistance during the grant period. They may continue to qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance as long as they are in emergency housing under limited circumstances.
If the clients 13 week non-entitlement period for emergency housing resumes they will not qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance.

chunks.title: Dependent child staying with client in emergency housing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: To get Flexible Funding Assistance, the client must have at least 1 dependent child in their care and staying with them in the same accommodation paid for by an Emergency Housing Grant. The dependent child must be included in the Emergency Housing Grant and not just be a visitor to the client's accommodation. A client does not qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance when: - they do not have any dependent children or - their dependent child(ren) are not staying with them in the same emergency accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant. This includes when the client remains financially responsible for them.

chunks.title: Example — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: Tim has 3 dependent children, who are staying elsewhere with other family members while Tim is in a motel paid for by an Emergency Housing Grant. The children are included in Tim's Sole Parent Support and visit him in the motel most days after school. Tim does not qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance as his dependent children are not staying with him in the motel. For more information see:

chunks.title: Dependent children in both the accommodation and elsewhere — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: If the client has dependent child(ren) not staying with them in accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant and also has at least 1 dependent child staying, they can get Flexible Funding Assistance for the child/children staying with them (if they meet the criteria). Flexible Funding Assistance cannot be paid to meet the needs of the dependent children not staying in the emergency housing. Example: Tiana has 3 dependent children, 2 are staying with the client in emergency housing and 1 is not. Tiana needs assistance with transport to school for the children. They may qualify for Flexible Funding Assistance for school transport for the 2 children who are staying in emergency housing. Flexible Funding Assistance cannot be paid for school transport for the dependent child not in emergency housing.

chunks.title: Client in emergency housing has a shared care arrangement — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: When the client has a shared care arrangement for their dependent child(ren) and their dependent child stays with them in emergency housing for some of the time and elsewhere for the rest of the time, Flexible Funding Assistance may still be granted if the client qualifies. In a shared care situation, Flexible Funding Assistance can only be paid to meet the needs specific to the period the dependent child is staying with the client in their accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant. Example Mera is 10 years old and her parents Simon and Francesca share their daughter's care. Mera stays in emergency housing with Simon for 4 nights a week. Mera spends the rest of the week with Francesca in a rental apartment in the next suburb. Simon's emergency housing is an additional 12km away from Mera's school and too far away from the school bus route. Simon needs help paying the additional cost for transport. MSD decides he meets the qualifications for Flexible Funding Assistance. MSD finds a shuttle service for Mera which costs $50 a week ($12.50 x 4 days = $50 a week) to meet Mera's additional need for transport due to the location of the emergency housing. Mera's transport is arranged and the Contracted Provider pays the shuttle service company.

chunks.title: Dependent child turns 18 while staying in emergency housing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Dependent child turns 18 while staying in emergency housing
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer eligible to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's future Emergency Housing Grants. If they are the only child included in the parent or caregiver's Emergency Housing Grant, Flexible Funding Assistance can no longer be paid. The child is also no longer included as a dependent child if the client applies for an Emergency Housing Grant again.
## Continuing in education and not financially independent
An 18-year-old child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's future Emergency Housing Grants for a limited period if they are:
- continuing in education and
- not financially independent
If the client is getting a benefit or Community Costs, the 18-year-old must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Emergency Housing Grants from the same date they are excluded from the benefit.
If the client does not get a benefit or Community Costs, the 18-year-old must generally be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Emergency Housing Grants from the date they no longer meet the above criteria. They must not be included any later than the start of the week following 31 December of the year they turn 18.

chunks.title: Dependent child — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
A dependent child for Flexible Funding Assistance is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of the client
- being maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
- not a child for whom Orphan's Benefit or an Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid
- in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki and has been returned to their parent's care
A dependent child for Flexible Funding Assistance does not include:
- a child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 are being made or
- a young person getting a Young Parent Payment and their child
Note if the young person applies for Flexible Funding Assistance, their child is a dependent child.

chunks.title: Examples of dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step-parent — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Examples of dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step-parent
To help you identify when there is a 'dependent child', please see the examples below:
Household
Payments

chunks.title: Examples of immediate needs for Flexible Funding Assistance — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: The below table shows examples of additional or increased costs for immediate needs that may be included in Flexible Funding Assistance (note this is not an exhaustive list).

chunks.title: Additional (or increased) costs for immediate needs related to education, early childhood and wellbeing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: Additional (or increased) costs for immediate needs - education, early childhood and wellbeing Examples Participation in education, including early childhood education School costs The child has moved to a school with a uniform, and existing assistance is not available, for example: - existing assistance is insufficient to meet the immediate need eg the child needs additional clothing due to health or disability needs - the client has been declined existing assistance because: - their income is over the limit for Recoverable Assistance Payment or - their debt level is over the advance guidelines Food storage The client has additional costs for their child's school lunch as storing food for packed lunches is unreasonable in emergency housing (eg, there is no fridge). Flexible Funding Assistance can be provided to the: - school canteen for the student to use or - early childhood centre to buy the food and have lunch provided to the child each day Travel Extra costs associated with travel due to the location of the emergency housing in relation to: - university/school/early childhood - before/after school activities, including: sports practice and gamesschool clubs or groupstutoringother before/after school activities - sports practice and games - school clubs or groups - tutoring - other before/after school activities These costs are likely to be seen when: - a school is further away and it is unreasonable to expect the child/parent to walk this distance - the public transport options are unsuitable eg due to child's age or health condition - public transport costs are higher due to the location of the emergency housing Access childcare After school care or holiday programme Costs for after school care or holiday programmes due to the accommodation environment not being suitable for the child. Example, the motel room is small and everyone in the family is sharing one bedroom. Note Flexible Funding Assistance cannot be used for additional costs of school holiday activities to get the child out of the emergency housing where there are appropriate free activities the family can access Additional childcare costs Additional childcare costs due to the accommodation environment not being suitable due to the age of the child or their additional special needs due to disability. For example, a beneficiary client can only access 9 hours childcare assistance, so we pay more hours for childcare which gives the child a place to play and learn and gives the client a break or time to search for other accommodation Additional travel

chunks.title: Additional (or increased) costs for immediate needs related to education, early childhood and wellbeing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: Extra costs associated with travel because the location of the emergency housing is further away from the child's usual childcare, after school care or holiday programme. Accessing health services Increased doctor fees It may be impractical to go to their existing doctor due to location so the client (or immediate family member) needs to go to a closer medical centre or after-hours clinic. Additional prescription costs Additional prescription costs as the current medication or script was unable to be accessed from the former home due to circumstances outside of their control, eg family violence or immediate eviction. Travel to their usual doctor Additional travel to their existing medical centre because of how far the doctor is from the emergency accommodation. Finding suitable social or alternative housing Childcare expenses If the client needs to view properties that are outside of school hours. Transport costs - extra transport costs to attend property viewings due to the location of the emergency housing - extra travel costs for the client/partner/dependent child to go to work Mobile phone or internet costs Additional costs associated with finding suitable social housing or alternative housing in the rare circumstances when: - making phone calls from the emergency housing landline is less cost effective or - there is no free internet at the accommodation or - internet at the accommodation is limited Limited licence or car impound fees This help can only be granted where: - not assisting would impact on the client's ability to find suitable social or alternative housing - the wellbeing of children is impacted due to their need for the transport while staying in emergency housing. The process for granting limited license or car impound fees [no link find out why] Car repairs This can be considered if other hardship assistance cannot be used and the vehicle is needed to find suitable social or alternative housing or transport to school. Warrant of fitness and registration costs may also be considered if the need is directly related to staying in emergency housing Laundry costs Having to use the laundromat as there is no access to other laundry facilities. Additional storage for food Assistance may be provided if the family is unable to safely store enough food for their daily needs in the accommodation eg buying a small fridge. However, this can only be considered when: - the emergency housing provider agrees - there is no other assistance available eg where it is not practical to use a preferred supplier for whiteware [no link find out why] - it is the last resort and all other options have been exhausted Other wellbeing costs

chunks.title: Additional (or increased) costs for immediate needs related to education, early childhood and wellbeing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text: Other additional or increased costs relating to wellbeing will be considered on a case by case basis. This could include: - help so clients/immediate family members can continue to participate in regular activities they were doing before their stay in emergency housing. For example, those relating to education, employment, health, social, religious or cultural pursuits - help so clients/immediate family can participate in additional activities while staying in emergency housing. For example, enrolling the child into Karate, swimming lessons etc.

chunks.title: Immediate need for Flexible Funding Assistance — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Immediate need for Flexible Funding Assistance
To get Flexible Funding Assistance, a client or their immediate family must have an immediate need.
For Flexible Funding Assistance to be paid, MSD must be satisfied:
- the client or their immediate family has an immediate need for Flexible Funding Assistance and
- the immediate need has been created from the client or their immediate family staying in accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant and
- the client and their partner (if any) do not have enough resources available to them to meet the need and
- the immediate need cannot be met by other assistance available (i.e. from both MSD and non-MSD assistance) and
- a payment of Flexible Funding Assistance to help the client with the immediate need would be consistent with the purpose of the Flexible Fund Programme (i.e. the need has happened because of where they are living and they now have additional costs related to education, early childhood or wellbeing costs for the client or their immediate family)

chunks.title: Immediate need — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Immediate need
To get Flexible Funding Assistance, the client must have an immediate need for the assistance.
An immediate need is:
- a need of the client or their immediate family that must be met, generally within the next 7 days of the need being identified and
- which the client or their immediate family have additional costs that need to be paid while they are staying in accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant
## Needs that are not 'immediate'
A need is generally not considered 'immediate' when it does not have to be met within 7 days time.
Example
A client is paid an Emergency Housing Need on 25 May. They ask for assistance to help pay for their children to go on a holiday programme to get them out of the motel during the upcoming school holidays (10 July to 25 July).
However, the holiday programme does not start for 6 weeks (10 July) and payment is not required to secure a place for the children in the holiday programme until 2 weeks before the holidays (26 June).
As the need is not immediate, Flexible Funding Assistance cannot be granted at this time. If the family are still in emergency housing in mid-June and they qualify, Flexible Funding Assistance may be granted closer to the payment date for the holiday programme, when the need is immediate.
## Ongoing needs
In some cases, there may be a need that is likely to continue for the duration of the client's stay in emergency housing e.g. school lunches, afterschool care or transport to early childhood activities.
When there is an immediate need at the time of granting Flexible Funding Assistance and that need is expected to be ongoing, Flexible Funding Assistance can be granted for the duration of the current Emergency Housing Grant. This includes when the Emergency Housing Grant is for more than 7 nights.
Example
A client with 2 dependent children is paid an Emergency Housing Grant for 15 nights. Their 2 children will remain in the same school for the grant period but there are no appropriate food storage facilities in the emergency accommodation. Flexible Funding Assistance for school lunches can be granted for the duration of the Emergency Housing Grant.
Note if the client leaves emergency housing before their grant period ends and the ongoing costs have already been paid a client can continue to use these services but will not be granted any further Flexible Funding Assistance.

chunks.title: Income limit — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Income limit
A client cannot get Flexible Funding Assistance unless their income (and any partner's income) is below the appropriate income limit.
## Income limit for Flexible Funding Assistance
The appropriate income limits for Flexible Funding Assistance are the same income limits used for an Emergency Housing Grant, for:
- a couple (with children) or
- sole parents (with 1 child, or 2+ children)
The income limit depends on the client's relationship status.
## What is considered income for Flexible Funding Assistance
For Flexible Funding Assistance, income includes:
- Core policy Types of income
- any of the following paid to the client or their partner: New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pensionany payments made under the following programmes: New Employment Transition Grant Programme orSeasonal Work Assistance Programme orWork Bonus Programme
- New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
- any payments made under the following programmes: New Employment Transition Grant Programme orSeasonal Work Assistance Programme orWork Bonus Programme
- New Employment Transition Grant Programme or
- Seasonal Work Assistance Programme or
- Work Bonus Programme
Winter Energy Payment is not considered income when assessing whether a client qualifies for Flexible Funding Assistance.
If a client is getting a main benefit, they would generally meet the income test for Flexible Funding Assistance.
## Exceptions for paying Flexible Funding Assistance when over income and asset limits
In exceptional circumstances, MSD can pay Flexible Funding Assistance if the client and/or their partner have income and assets over the category limits.

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > flexible funding assistance
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Flexible Funding Assistance is a last resort, non-taxable and non-recoverable financial assistance for clients with dependent children staying in accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant.
It is discretionary assistance paid under the Flexible Funding Programme. The purpose of the Flexible Funding Programme is to help with meeting the educational, early childhood and wellbeing needs of families with children when additional costs have happened because they are staying in emergency housing.
The client must be unable to pay for the additional costs from their own resources or other sources of assistance.
MSD determines who can receive a payment of Flexible Funding Assistance and generally confirms who the supplier of the goods and services will be to meet the client's needs.
Payments of Flexible Funding Assistance are made by Contracted Providers to suppliers on MSD's behalf.

chunks.title: Need created as the client and their immediate family are in emergency housing — extra help > flexible funding assistance
