- a licensed early childhood service which includes: early childhood education and care centre (eg daycare centre, kohanga reo, playcentre, kindergarten)home-based education and care servicehospital-based education and care service
- early childhood education and care centre (eg daycare centre, kohanga reo, playcentre, kindergarten)
- home-based education and care service
- hospital-based education and care service
- a playgroup certificated by the Ministry of Education (this means a playgroup funded by the Ministry of Education and they meet certain standards)
and
- for which a fee is charged for the children to participate in the programme.
Note under no circumstances can we make a payment for childcare provided informally (for example through family or friends who are not licensed to provide a home-based education and care service) or a childcare centre or service that is not approved (not licensed).

chunks.title: Calculating hourly rate — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: The calculation of the hourly rate for childcare may vary for different early childhood education programmes or services. Some services charge a flat fee and other services charge a fee based on the hours of attendance of a child.

chunks.title: Maximum subsidy paid per hour or week — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: The rate of payment must not exceed the maximum levels per child, which are: - up to $6.72 per hour (as at 1 April 2026) and - up to 50 hours per week ($336 per week)

chunks.title: Weekly flat fee — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: To calculate the hourly rate for an early childhood education programme or service that charges a weekly flat fee, divide the weekly flat fee by the number of hours the child is enrolled. Enrolled hours means the number of hours the child is booked to attend the early childhood education programme or service, whether the child attends or not.

chunks.title: Example 1 — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Number of hours the child is enrolled in the early childhood education programme or service each week 31 hours Total weekly hours of attendance payable for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment (school time plus travel time) 31 hours Early childhood education programme or service flat fee $180 per week Hourly rate equals $5.80 per hour

chunks.title: Fee based on the hours of attendance of a child — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: When an early childhood education programme or service charges a fee based on the hours attended by the child, the hourly rate needs to be calculated. To get an hourly rate, the weekly fee must be divided by the number of hours the child attends the early childhood education programme or service. Example 2 Number of hours the child is attending the early childhood education programme or service each week 34 hours Total weekly hours of attendance payable for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment (school time plus travel time) 34 hours Early childhood education programme or service weekly fee $153 per week Hourly fee equals $4.50 per hour

chunks.title: Fee exceeds the maximum subsidy paid per hour or week — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: When an early childhood education programme or service charges a flat fee that is more than the maximum hourly rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment, the rate payable needs to be calculated. To calculate the hourly rate of the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment, the flat fee must be divided by the number of hours the child attends the early childhood education programme or service.

chunks.title: Example 3 — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Early childhood education programme or service flat fee $319 per week Total weekly hours of attendance payable for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment (activity time plus travel time) 45 hours Number of hours the child is enrolled in the early childhood education programme or service each week 45 hours Hourly fee equals $7.08 per hour Hourly rate payable of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment (as at 1 April 2026) $6.72 per hour Rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment per week (45 hours x $6.72 at 1 April 2026) $302.40 per week In this example the calculated hourly fee is higher than the maximum rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment per hour. In this example the rate of payment per week is $302.40 and the young parent is responsible for the additional cost of $16.60 per week.

chunks.title: Attending childcare for more than the number of hours payable — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: When the maximum number of hours of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment payable is less than the number of hours the child attends childcare, the young parent is responsible for the additional costs of the childcare.

chunks.title: Example 4 — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Hours spent travelling between childcare service and school 8 hours per week Hours spent at school and part-time work 47 hours per week Number of hours the child is enrolled in the early childhood education programme or service each week 55 hours Total 'weekly hours of attendance payable' for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment 50 hours Early childhood education programme or service weekly fee $250 per week Hourly fee equals $4.54 per hour Maximum rate of payment per week (50 hours x $4.54) $227 per week Additional costs $23.00 per week In this example the weekly rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment is $227, and the young parent is responsible for the additional cost of $23 a week.

chunks.title: Provider does not charge an absence fee — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Provider does not charge an absence fee
If the childcare centre or service does not charge a fee for holding places open during absences of children, the young parent must inform of the child's absence within a reasonable time to either:
- YSSU via the contact centre (for those not receiving a main benefit) or
- their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service
A debt may be created for any overpayment to the childcare centre or service where an absence is not notified to us.
The young person's service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service must report this information along with any other changes in young parent's circumstances via the Activity Reporting Tool (ART) on a daily basis.
## Providers who charge an absence fee
Most providers charge a fee when a child is temporarily away. The fee is charged to hold the child's place open at the service or centre. We cannot pay more than what the childcare centre or service charges per week.
For example if a young parent is receiving the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment for a child of $70.20 a week and the provider charges a $50.20 a week whilst the child is away, the most we can pay is $50.20 per week.

chunks.title: Absences due to COVID-19 requirements — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Absences due to COVID-19 requirements
When a child is absent due to COVID-19 requirements, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can continue being paid if the client still qualifies. A fee does not need to be charged to hold the child's place open for payment to continue.
A child may be absent due to COVID-19 requirements because they are:
- unwell and cannot attend childcare while unwell
- at high risk of severe illness if they contract COVID-19
- in self-isolation or quarantine due to COVID-19 public health requirements
- connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19
- being kept home during Alert Level 3
This is not an exhaustive list. If a child is absent and you are unsure if it is due to COVID-19 requirements, please check the COVID-19 Alert System website for the most up to date COVID-19 guidelines.
## Number of weeks payment can continue
There is no limit on how long Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be paid when a child is absent due to COVID-19 requirements.
However, the payment can only be paid for a period that relates to COVID-19 requirements. If a child is absent for other reasons, you will need to check the general absence guidelines to see how long they can be paid.
## Example
Amina's son Gabriel suffers from a respiratory condition which means he is at high risk of severe illness if he contracts COVID-19. Due to this, Amina withdrew him from childcare for 7 weeks while New Zealand was at Alert Level 3.
Because the COVID-19 Alert Level 3 guidelines state that high risk people should stay home if they can, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can continue for the full period of Gabriel's absence.

chunks.title: Fee is charged — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Fee is charged
If a fee is charged, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment will be paid based on the child's enrolled hours and the fee charged by the centre. See: Payment
## No fee is charged
If no fee is charged, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment will continue at the usual weekly amount before the absence or closure.
Note if during an absence or closure, the client decides their child will not return, payment must be stopped.
If a change in circumstance happens during an absence or closure, the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment must be reviewed, and the rate of payment may change.

chunks.title: Centre is closed and no childcare is available — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Centre is closed and no childcare is available
When a centre has closed for a specific period of time and there is no childcare available for the child to attend, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment should not be paid.
Providers should advise YSSU when this occurs.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A young parent client is obliged to advise the Ministry or their service provider of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment.
The Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be reviewed at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A change in a young parent's circumstances may also mean that the young parent qualifies for another benefit.

chunks.title: Child leaves the centre — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Child leaves the centre
When a child leaves the centre, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment must be cancelled from the day after the child's last day at the centre.
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment cannot be used to pay for a notice period if the child is no longer attending.

chunks.title: Closures due to COVID-19 requirements — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Closures due to COVID-19 requirements
When a childcare centre is closed due to COVID-19 requirements, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can continue being paid if the client still qualifies. A fee does not need to be charged to hold the child's place open for payment to continue.
A centre may close due to COVID-19 requirements because they:
- must close due to COVID-19 Alert Level 4
- are connected to a confirmed or probable case of COVID-19 and have been instructed to close
- are not able to operate safely and within public health guidelines
- temporarily do not have any children needing childcare because of COVID-19
This is not an exhaustive list. If a centre has closed and you are unsure if it is due to COVID-19 requirements, please check the COVID-19 Alert System website for the most up to date COVID-19 guidelines.
Note Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment cannot continue being paid to a centre that is closed because it is not financially viable for them to stay open, or for any other reason that is not related to COVID-19 requirements.
## Number of weeks payment can continue
There is no limit on how long Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be paid when a child is absent due to COVID-19 requirements.
However, the payment can only be paid for a period that relates to COVID-19 requirements.
If a centre is closed for longer than what is needed due to COVID-19 requirements, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can only be paid for the period that relates to COVID-19 requirements.
## Example
Liam's daughter usually goes to a small, family run childcare centre. They had to close for 4 weeks when New Zealand was at COVID-19 Alert Level 4. They then stayed closed for an extra 2 weeks due to a family bereavement.
Liam's Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment continued for the first 4 weeks the centre was closed because this was due to COVID-19 requirements. Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment was stopped for the extra 2 weeks because the centre was closed for a reason not related to COVID-19 requirements.

chunks.title: Example — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Example
Kerry has been getting Early Learning Payment of 20 hours per week because she is enrolled in the Early Start Programme.
Her son has stayed home from childcare during Alert Level 3 and Early Learning Payment has continued. From next week Kerry’s son will be going to live with his father and he will no longer be dependent on Kerry.
Her Early Learning Payment will stop from the beginning of next week because Kerry no longer qualifies.

chunks.title: Debts — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Debts
Overpayment of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be recovered from the young person or the childcare centre or service.
In most cases, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment is paid direct to the childcare centre or service and so any overpayments should be recovered direct from them.
## Debts for childcare centre or service
Debts can be recovered from the childcare centre or service depending on the reason the debt was created. Debts should be recovered from the childcare centre or service when a debt has arisen due to one of the following circumstances:
- child leaves the centre permanently - the childcare centre knowing the child has left cannot accept the money in good faith
- childcare centre is closed and they do not charge a holding fee - centres may close during school holiday periods. This excludes statutory holidays
- caregiver is unavailable - for home based care providers there are occasions when the caregiver cannot provide childcare
## Debts for childcare centre or service in SWIFTT
Payments for the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment are made through Childcare Subsidy Screen or through a miscellaneous subsidy code for non-beneficiaries under 16 years old (Teen Payment - 512). It is important that any debt created on the young parent's record is transferred to the childcare centre or service in TRACE.
Full notes should be entered into CMS to explain why the debt was created. You should note that it is the childcare centre or service that is responsible for refunding the debt.
You should follow up with the childcare centre or service to recover the debt. You also need to email your local contact from Client_Support_Debt_Management@msd.govt.nz with details of the debt.

chunks.title: Ending the payment — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Ending the payment
The Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment will stop for a person granted a payment because they have youth activity obligations when:
- the child turns 5 years old or within 4 weeks after the child turns 5 years, when they are transitioning between pre-school and primary school or
- for children over 5 years whose parent intend to enrol them at a school with a cohort entry policy, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment ends at the mid-term or term start date on or immediately after their 5th birthday (whichever is closer)or
- the young parent no longer has an eligible child attending an approved childcare centre or service or
- the young parent turns 20 years old:
- when the young parent turns 20 mid-way through a year and their child remains eligible, the payment may continue until the end of the course or if the course ends in December, until 31 March the following year or
- when the parent turns 20 years old and is still subject to youth activity obligations, payment will continue until those obligations cease, this would be 6 months following the date they where granted Young Parent Payment or
- the young parent has stopped attending the course or secondary institution
whichever is earlier.
Note children are not considered 'enrolled' unless they are 'attending' school.
For more information on when a young parent receiving Young Parent Payment can continue to get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment after they turn 20 years old. See:
## Young parent not getting a main benefit
When a young parent is not getting a main benefit and is attending a full-time secondary institution, and they are still eligible for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can keep getting payments until:
- the child turns 5 years and 4 weeks old (if transitioning to school)and will be starting at a continuous entry school or
- the child is aged over 5 years and enrolled in a cohort entry school until the term or mid-term start date on or after the child's 5th birthday (whichever is closer) or
- the young parent no longer has an eligible child attending an approved childcare centre or service or
- they stop attending the secondary institution
whichever is earlier.
Note children at cohort entry schools are not considered 'enrolled' unless they are 'attending' school.
Parents do not need to formally apply for an extension of 4 weeks when their child turns 5 years old, if the school is a continuous entry school. However the client needs to tell us if their child will be starting at a cohort entry school.

chunks.title: Payment can continue - young parent over 20 years — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Payment can continue - young parent over 20 years
Generally a young parent receiving Young Parent Payment would no longer be eligible to receive Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment once they reach the age of 20 years. There are two situations where a young parent can continue to receive Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment past this age.
These are where a young parent:
- has reached the age of 20 years and has not received Young Parent Payment for 6 months
They must remain on Young Parent Payment until they have completed 6 months.
- is meeting their youth activity obligations to participate in education, training or work-based learning when they turn 20 and choose to remain on this payment to complete their course

chunks.title: Child absent for up to 15 working days — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Child absent for up to 15 working days
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be paid for a continuous period of up to 15 working days at any one time when a child is absent for any reason. The childcare centre or service must be open and charge a fee for holding the child's place during their absence.
This can occur more than one time in a 52-week period. If a child is consistently absent, their hours of attendance should be reviewed to ensure the rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment reflects this.
Note while the child is absent from childcare, the young parent must still meet the qualifications for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment. This includes:
- participating in activities to meet their youth activity obligations, or
- attending, or about to be attending, secondary school (if they're not getting an income-tested main benefit)
## Child absent for more than 15 days
Generally, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment must stop if an eligible child has been absent from the childcare centre or service for a continuous period of 15 working days or more.
In some cases, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be paid for up to 30 days where reasonable circumstances exist.

chunks.title: Public holidays — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Public holidays
The Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can also be paid for statutory holidays (e.g. the Sovereign's birthday and a regional anniversary day).
Payment is made regardless of whether an absence fee is charged or not.

chunks.title: Reasonable circumstances for paying up to 30 days — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Reasonable circumstances for paying up to 30 days
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be paid for a continuous period of up to 15 working days at any one time when a child is absent for any reason. The childcare centre or service must charge a fee for holding the child’s place during their absence.
In some situations, the child may need to be temporarily absent for a longer period. Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can continue during a child’s absence for up to 30 working days if the child:
- is injured or ill or
- has a family bereavement or
- is on holiday or
- has another reasonable circumstance for their absence
The young parent must be charged a fee by the childcare centre or service during the child’s absence and must continue to meet all the qualifications for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment to keep being paid.
## Reasonable circumstances
Young parents may face a range of challenges when managing their education, employment, and family responsibilities. Reasonable circumstances for the child's absence may include (but are not limited to), the young parent being temporarily unable to:
- transport the child to or from the childcare centre or service for reasons outside of their control (e.g. their vehicle has broken down, their home has been damaged or isolated by an emergency event, or another member of the household is unwell), or
- provide the child with clothing or shoes that are size or weather appropriate, or
- provide the child with food that the childcare provider has said is appropriate
What is considered a reasonable circumstance will depend on the young parent's individual situation.
MSD must also consider:
- the likelihood of the child returning to the childcare centre or service within 30 working days and
- whether another person would consider it reasonable to continue to pay Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment for the reason the child is absent (for example would other MSD staff consider it reasonable)

chunks.title: School holidays and holding fees — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## School holidays and holding fees
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment is paid during the full year (up to 52 weeks) when the young parent is attending activities to meet their youth activity obligations, part-time work or full-time secondary school (where they are not receiving a main benefit).
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can continue to be paid during the school term and summer vacation period when:
- the young parent intends to return to school and/or training the following year
- a fee is charged for holding the child's place open
Note where no holding fee is charged, the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment must be suspended in SWIFTT during the school holiday period. The payment must be resumed in SWIFTT when school starts again.
## Exception
A young person who is in part-time work can continue to receiving Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment for their part-time work hours when their centre doesn't charge a holding fee where they are intending to return to education, training or work-based learning when their holiday ends.
## Holding fee is less than normal fee charged
If the holding fee is less than the amount normally paid then the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment must be reduced in SWIFTT to the fee charged during the school holiday period.
## Returning to education or training the following year
All young parents receiving Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment will be contacted in the first three weeks of December each year to confirm their intentions of returning to education or training the following year.
When a young parent is managed by a service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service, they will make this contact and record the results in the Activity Reporting Tool (ART).
When the young parent does not have a service provider because they are not receiving a main benefit, the YSSU will make contact to ask about the young parent's intentions for the following year.

chunks.title: Young parent leaves the secondary institution — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment > changes and reviews guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Young parent leaves the secondary institution
When a young parent is getting the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment as a non-beneficiary, it must be cancelled when the young parent has stopped attending the secondary institution.

chunks.title: Commencement date — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
The Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment commences on the date:
- the child begins attending the approved early childhood education programme
- the young parent started participating in education, training or work-based learning or other activities to meet their youth activity obligations
- the young parent starting attending or participating in full-time secondary education (where they are not receiving a main benefit)
- of application or
- 20 August 2012
whichever is the later.
Note the Childcare Subsidy (or Early Learning Payment) should be cancelled from the commencement date.

chunks.title: Deciding ordinarily resident — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Deciding ordinarily resident
Generally a young parent must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand to receive a Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment.
## What is ordinarily resident?
Ordinarily resident means someone who is normally and lawfully in New Zealand and intends to stay here, that is, they consider New Zealand to be their home.
Whether a person is ordinarily resident is a question of fact and degree and their intentions during any period of absence is the most important factor.
Where it is not clear if the young parent is ordinarily resident, consider the following:
(a) the young parent's intentions toward New Zealand (that is, the reasons for their absence from New Zealand and the reasons for their return). Are they going overseas for a holiday or are they intending to live overseas permanently? (sighting return air tickets is a good indication)
(b) the length of time they spend in New Zealand on a continual basis
(c) property ownership (as this tends to suggest permanent ties with a place), including other asset ownership (for example boats, cars or caravans)
(d) where are their cash assets held?
(e) is their income earned in New Zealand or overseas, and do they pay New Zealand taxes?
(f) do they still vote (or are they eligible to vote) in the New Zealand election?
(g) their commitment to New Zealand (for example their involvement in the community, community events, clubs and other groups)?
Note a young parent cannot be ordinarily resident in two places at the same time.
## Australian clients
Australian citizens or residents are lawfully allowed in New Zealand, as they are deemed to hold a residence class visa.
However, they must still be ordinarily resident in New Zealand and meet all other criteria to be eligible for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment.

chunks.title: Full-time secondary education — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Full-time secondary education
A young parent can get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment when they are enrolled in a full-time course of secondary education.
This means a course of secondary education in a composite school, distance school, secondary school, or teen parent unit.
For Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment, a private training establishment (PTE) is not considered a secondary institution.
For secondary school, a full-time secondary education course is defined as:
- 20 class hours a week
Te Kura o Te Aho Pounamu - Distance school
For young people studying at Te Kura - Distance school full-time is:
- 4 subjects at NCEA level 1 or
- 3 subjects at NCEA levels 2 and 3
## Full-time tertiary education
Some young parents can get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment when they are participating in a course of tertiary education.
Tertiary programmes have an equivalent full-time student (EFTS) value assigned to them. The EFTS value determines if the course of study is full-time or not.
To be considered enrolled in a full-time course of tertiary education, a young person must be studying the minimum EFTS in regards to weeks, as used for assessing full-time for Student Allowance purposes.
For Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment, a Private Training Establishment is not considered tertiary education.
For more information see:
- Table of weeks for EFTS
## Work-based learning and other approved training
For work-based learning and all other types of training, full-time means the young parent's spouse or partner must be engaged for 30-40 hours.
Note a young parent can get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment while they are working for up to 15 hours per week if this work is during times they are not required to be participating in a youth activity obligation.

chunks.title: Eligible child — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Eligible child
An eligible child is a child of the young parent for whom they have the primary responsibility for the day to day care.

chunks.title: Good and sufficient reason for partner not providing care — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Good and sufficient reason for partner not providing care
A good and sufficient reason for not providing childcare while the young parent is undertaking activities or attending full-time secondary school may include (but is not limited to):
- the partner is in full-time or part-time employment during the young parent's school hours
- the partner is in full-time secondary or tertiary education or other training themselves
- the partner also receives Young Parent Payment and is required to undertake activities to meet their obligation at the same time
- the partner is incapacitated due to sickness, injury or disability
- the partner receives a main benefit and is expected to meet work obligations

chunks.title: Home-based educator top up payments examples — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Below are examples of using Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment to pay for home-based educator top up payments.

chunks.title: Example 1 - hours of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment payable for home-based educator top up payments — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Hours in childcare Hours payable before 3 June 2024 Hours payable from 3 June 2024 20 Hours ECE 20 0 20 (home-based educator top up payments only) Standard hours 30 30 30 Total 50 30 50 (20 home-based educator top up payment + 30 standard fees)

chunks.title: Example 2 - Young parent qualifies for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment for 25 hours per week — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Scott is 18 and is getting Young Parent Payment while he finishes high school. He is the principal caregiver for his 3-year-old son, Fran. Fran attends a home-based early childhood education service for 25 hours per week while Scott is at high school. Fran is enrolled with 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE) for 4 hours each day (a total of 20 hours each week). The home-based educator charges $12 per hour for the hours outside of 20 Hours ECE. This is a charge of $60 each week (for the 5 standard hours). The educator also charges a home-based educator top up payment of $2 per hour for the same hours as 20 Hours ECE. This is an additional charge of $40 a week. Scott qualifies for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment for the 25 hours a week that Fran is in childcare. He can get the full rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment ($6.72 per hour as at 1 April 2026) for the 5 hours outside of 20 Hours ECE. This is a total of $33.60 per week. Scott can also get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment for the home-based educator top up payment. Because the amount charged ($2 per hour) is less than the maximum hourly rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment, Scott gets the lower amount of $2 for those hours. This is a total of $40 per week, which fully covers those costs. Hours in childcare 25 20 Hours ECE (4 x 5 days) 20 Standard childcare charge $12 per hour (for 5 hours outside of 20 Hours ECE) $60 per week (5 hours x $12 per hour) Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment entitlement (for 5 hours outside of 20 Hours ECE) $33.60 per week (5 hours x $6.72 per hour) Home-based educator top up payment charge $2 per hour (for 20 hours of 20 Hours ECE) $40 per week (20 hours x $2) Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment entitlement (for 20 hours of home-based educator top up payment charge) $40 per week (20 hours x $2) Total Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment entitlement $73.60 per week

chunks.title: Home-based educator top up payments — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Home-based educators can charge a home-based educator top up payment for the same hours as 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE). This is to cover the difference between the 20 Hours ECE funding and the educator's usual hourly rate. Home-based early childhood education providers may charge the top up payment on the educator's behalf. Example a home-based educator charges $10 per hour per child for hours outside of 20 Hours ECE. The service they are contracted to passes on $6 per hour for each child from the 20 Hours ECE funding. The educator can charge a home-based educator top up payment of $4 per hour. Eligible young parents can choose to take up Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment to pay for: - standard childcare hours only or - home-based educator top up payments charged for 20 Hours ECE hours only or - a combination of the two, but not for the same hours

chunks.title: Hours payable for home-based educator top up payments — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Eligible young parents can get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment to help pay for home-based educator top up payments charged for the same hours as 20 Hours ECE. If the young parent uses Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment to pay for home-based educator top up payments, these hours are deducted from the total hours of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment the young parent is eligible for. This means a young parent who is eligible to 50 hours of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can get the payment for 20 hours of home-based educator top up payments and 30 hours of standard childcare fees. For examples of hours payable for home-based educator top up payments see: - Home-based educator top up payments examples

chunks.title: Rate payable for home-based educator top up payments — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: When Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment is used to help pay for home-based educator top up payments, the amount payable for those hours is the lesser of the: - maximum hourly rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment available to the young parent or - actual hourly home-based educator top up payment charged Note Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment for home-based educator top up payments may be paid at a different rate to the fees for standard childcare hours.

chunks.title: Example - rate payable for home-based educator top up payments — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: A client has their child enrolled for 20 hours of 20 Hours ECE and 30 hours of standard childcare with a home-based educator. The educator charges $10 per hour but for 20 Hours ECE, they get $7 per hour passed through from their provider. This leaves $3 per hour that they charge as a home-based educator top up payment. The client is entitled to a maximum Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment rate of $6.72 per hour (as at 1 April 2026). This means that they can get $3 per hour for the home-based educator top up payment and $6.72 per hour (as at 1 April 2026) for the standard childcare hours. Hours child is in home-based childcare per week Hourly amount charged by educator Maximum hourly Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment entitlement Weekly amount charged by educator Weekly Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment rate payable to young parent 20 Hours ECE 20 $3 home-based educator top up payment $6.72 (as at 1 April 2026) $3 x 20 hours ($60) $3 x 20 hours ($60) Standard fees 30 $10 $6.72 (as at 1 April 2026) $10 x 30 hours ($300) $6.72 x 30 hours ($201.60) Total 50 (20 hrs top up payment + 30 hrs standard) - - $360 (2x top up payments + standard fees) $261.60

chunks.title: Unable to provide visa or permit — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Unable to provide visa or permit
When a client is unable to provide an immigration visa or permit they may provide other Immigration New Zealand documents to verify their immigration status.
MSD can also undertake an immigration status check directly with Immigration New Zealand.
Note Immigration New Zealand may be unable to verify immigration status for clients of British nationality who arrived in New Zealand before 2 April 1974 and do not have a passport.

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment is a non-taxable payment providing financial assistance with childcare costs to enable young parents who are:
- getting a main benefit to meet their youth activity obligations or
- not getting a main benefit to return to, or remain in, secondary education
All applications and review actions for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment are processed by the Youth Services Support Unit (YSSU).

chunks.title: Number of hours paid for childcare — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Number of hours paid for childcare
The Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment will only be paid for the time that the young parent is:
- required to be in activities to meet their youth activity obligations or part-time work (including travel time) or
- attending secondary school (including travel time) for young parents not receiving a main benefit
Travel time is determined by calculating the weekly amount of hours spent travelling to and from the early childhood education programme or service, and the activities to meet youth activity obligations or work or secondary school (for those not receiving a main benefit).
To work out the 'total weekly hours of attendance' payable for the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment add the number of hours travel time and the number of hours the child is attending the early childhood education programme or service.
When the number of hours the child is attending the early childhood education programme or service is greater than the total number of hours the young parent spends in activities to meet their youth activity obligations or full-time secondary school (for those not receiving a main benefit) or part-time work up to 15 hours, the young parent is expected to pay for the extra hours.
Note the 'number of hours paid for Early Childhood Education' can be rounded up on a weekly basis to the next whole hour.
## The Correspondence School
If a young parent is undertaking secondary education by correspondence, their teacher will need to confirm how many hours the young parent is required to be in schooling (or studying for) each week.

chunks.title: Partner getting a main benefit — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Partner getting a main benefit
Where the young parent is included in their partner's main benefit, they can receive Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment if they have youth activity obligations and are participating in education, training or work-based learning in order to meet their obligations.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Payment
The rate of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment for each eligible child the young parent has depends on the number of hours paid for childcare and the fee the early childhood education programme or service charges.
The rate payable is the lesser of the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment rate and the actual fee charged.
The rate of payment must not exceed the maximum levels per child, which are:
- up to $6.72 per hour (as at 1 April 2026) and
- up to 50 hours per week ($336 per week)
Payment includes travel time which is in addition to the hours to undertake activities to meet youth activity obligations and paid employment, or secondary school (for those not receiving a main benefit).
Note paid employment includes when the client is still employed, but not at work, such as sick or annual leave. It does not cover periods of parental leave.
The Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment is paid directly to the approved early childhood education programme or service that the child attends on a weekly basis.
Payment must not be more than the fee the early childhood education programme or service charges.
Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment is not payable for:
- full-time employment or
- for any additional part-time work hours over 15 hours per week
Note some early childhood education services attached to Teen Parent Units receive financial assistance to reduce the childcare costs for young parents attending the unit. In this case the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment should only be paid for the reduced amount of childcare costs (i.e. the actual hourly fee payable).

chunks.title: Permanent residence — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Permanent residence
Generally applicants need to have permanent residence or New Zealand citizenship to get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment.
To get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment, a young parent must:
- be a New Zealand citizen or
- have a residence class visa under the Immigration Act 2009 (which can either be a resident visa or a permanent resident visa) or
- have a residence permit under Immigration Act 1987 or
- be deemed to hold a residence class visa in New Zealand under the Immigration Act 2009 (e.g. Australian citizens or residents)
If MSD needs further information about a young parent's application for permanent residence the young parent must give consent for MSD to contact Immigration New Zealand or the young parent can get the information themselves. MSD must not collect or disclose information about a young parent's application without the young parent's consent.
Note refugees or protected persons who do not have permanent residence cannot get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment.

chunks.title: Primary responsibility for day to day care — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Primary responsibility for day to day care
The young parent must have the primary responsibility for the day to day care of their child.
Primary responsibility for the day to day care means that the young parent has all the responsibilities of looking after their child.
For example, the young parent:
- cares for the child during the day and night
- feeds the child
- changes the child's nappies
- nurtures the child and
- wakes up during the night for the child
Exception the young parent does not have to be financially responsible for their child.

chunks.title: Proof of residence — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Proof of residence
All documents should be originals. Photocopies and/or documents that have been changed in any way cannot be accepted.
Where the young parent (or partner) cannot provide proof or proof is unclear, MSD should ask the young parent (or partner) to obtain confirmation of their residence status from Immigration New Zealand (for permanent residence) or the Department of Internal Affairs (for citizenship).
Proof of citizenship and/or permanent residence in New Zealand can be a:
- New Zealand birth certificate
Generally, a person born in New Zealand is a New Zealand citizen by birth.
- New Zealand passport
To hold a New Zealand passport you must be a citizen of New Zealand.
- Certificate of Registration
A child born outside New Zealand (to a parent who is a New Zealand citizen) may be a New Zealand citizen from birth. However, the child must apply for a Certificate of Registration to confirm their New Zealand citizenship.
- Grant of Citizenship
People who have permanent residence, may (normally after 5 years residence in New Zealand) apply for a Grant of Citizenship. They must meet the conditions of the Grant.
- Certificate of Confirmation
This is a certificate issued to confirm that the holder is a New Zealand citizen by birth, descent or Grant of Citizenship.
- Passport (other than a New Zealand passport) containing a residence class visa granted under the Immigration Act 2009
- Passport (other than a New Zealand passport) containing a residence permit granted under the Immigration Act 1987
Note that a visa issued before 29 November 2010 does not allow a person to stay in New Zealand
- Letter of confirmation of permanent residence from Immigration New Zealand
- Australian citizens
Australian citizens are lawfully allowed in New Zealand without a residence class visa or residence permit and their date of entry into New Zealand is generally not recorded. Where possible supporting evidence should be sought, such as, tenancy agreements, bank statements or old utility bills to show that the client has been ordinarily resident for two continuous years.

chunks.text: - generally be ordinarily resident in New Zealand Note there is no income or asset test to get Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment. If a young parent does not meet the qualifications for Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment they may be able to get other assistance. However, Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment cannot be paid if other assistance for Early Childhood Education costs is being paid for the same child.

chunks.title: Activity requirements — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text: Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment will stop (unless there are exceptional circumstances) if the young parent: - is not participating in activities to meet their youth activity obligations, or - is not attending, or about to be attending, full-time secondary school (if they are not getting an income-tested main benefit).

chunks.title: Getting a Childcare Subsidy (or Early Learning Payment) — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Getting a Childcare Subsidy (or Early Learning Payment)
The Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment cannot be granted, if other assistance for childcare is being paid for the same child.
## Getting a Childcare Subsidy
If a young parent or their parent or guardian is currently receiving a Childcare Subsidy for the eligible child, this must be cancelled before the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be paid.
You must get permission to cancel the Childcare Subsidy from the person who has been granted the Childcare Subsidy before it is cancelled.
## Getting the Early Learning Payment
If a young parent or the parent or guardian is currently getting the Early Learning Payment for the eligible child this must be cancelled before the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment can be paid. Contact the Central Processing Unit to cancel the payment.
The young parent would remain enrolled in the Family Start or Early Start Programme and the family or whanau worker will continue to work with them.
Note the Childcare Subsidy (or Early Learning Payment) should be cancelled from the commencement date of Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Programme.

chunks.title: Secondary institutions — extra help > guaranteed childcare assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Secondary institutions
A young parent can get the Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment when they are enrolled to attend a secondary institution. These are institutions that run a course of education at a secondary level.
This includes:
- a composite school or a secondary school (as established and defined under the Education and Training Act 2020)
- Teen Parent Units and Activity Centres attached to those schools and
- Te Kura (distance school)
For Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment, a Private Training Establishment is not considered as a secondary institution.
