Generally, receiving a Student Loan (including the living cost component) does not mean a child is financially independent. For more information see:
- Gets a Student Loan

chunks.title: Full-time employment — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance > changes and reviews clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Full-time employment
When a child starts full-time employment the child is no longer a dependent child.
Note a child is still considered a dependent child if they are working full-time during the school holidays and they will be returning to school after the holidays.
## Date of review
Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, and Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children should stop from the beginning of the next pay period in which the child started work.
There is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the event. This discretion is generally used to avoid financial hardship for the family when the change has been unexpected or when processing deadlines have passed.

chunks.title: Hospitalisation of caregiver or child — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance > changes and reviews clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation of caregiver or child
If the caregiver or the child (that Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, and Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported Children is paid for) is admitted to hospital there is no change to the rate of payment.
While the caregiver or child is in hospital you will need to ensure that the child continues to meet the definition of dependent child and the caregiver continues to be the principal caregiver or principal temporary caregiver.
When a child is admitted to hospital (depending on the nature of the child's injury, illness or disability) the caregiver may be able to receive Child Disability Allowance.
Child Disability Allowance is a non-taxable allowance paid to the principal caregiver of a child with a serious disability, who is in need of constant care and attention for a period longer than 12 months.

chunks.title: New caregiver applies for benefit — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance > changes and reviews clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## New caregiver applies for benefit
When a new caregiver applies for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, you will need to obtain verification from the previous caregiver that the child is no longer in their care.
If the new caregiver meets the all qualifications, and there has been no change in the circumstances of the child's parents, then Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, and Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children can be paid to the new caregiver.
When any application for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is granted, and Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children is also granted, and entitlement to an Establishment Grant can be considered.
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Establishment Grant [no link find out why]
- Child Support

chunks.title: Permanent absence — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance > changes and reviews clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
If the caregiver or the child (that Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid for) is leaving New Zealand permanently, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, and Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children must be cancelled from the day after departure. Except for countries where a reciprocal agreement is in place.
If the child is remaining in New Zealand:
- the new caregiver may meet the qualifications [no link find out why] for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit or
- if the new caregiver is receiving a main benefit the child may be included as a dependent child [no link find out why] in the benefit
For more information see:
- Permanent absence
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Reciprocal Agreements

chunks.title: Gets a Student Allowance — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance > changes and reviews clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Gets a Student Allowance
When a child gets a Student Allowance or an Independent Circumstances Allowance under the Student Allowances Regulations 1998 they are no longer a dependent child and Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, and Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children must stop from:
- the start of the pay period following the date the event took place or
- the date the child's Student Allowance is granted
whichever is earlier.
Wherever possible (and in appropriate circumstances) the date the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, and Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children stops and the commencement date of the Student Allowance should coincide.
There is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the date of event to allow for a period of financial adjustment, generally to avoid hardship for the client.
Note there are specific rules for excluding an 18-year-old child when they are continuing in education.

chunks.title: Gets a Student Loan — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance > changes and reviews clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Gets a Student Loan
Getting a Student Loan (including the living cost component) does not mean the child is financially independent.
If the child continues to be the caregiver's primary responsibility and maintained as a member of their family and financially dependent (that is, the caregiver is meeting some of the costs for the child) Orphan's or Unsupported Child's Benefit, and Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children can continue to be paid until the start of the pay period following:
- the date they turn 18 or
- where the child is 18 and continuing in education, the earlier of: the date they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education orthe date the child is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required orthe date the child is financially independent orthe date the child leaves the parent or caregiver's care or31 December of the year they turn 18
- the date they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education or
- the date the child is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required or
- the date the child is financially independent or
- the date the child leaves the parent or caregiver's care or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18

chunks.title: Reciprocal Agreements — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance > changes and reviews clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Reciprocal Agreements
New Zealand has Reciprocal agreements with some countries.
Clothing Allowance for Orphans or Unsupported children cannot be made when Orphans Benefit is paid under a reciprocal agreement.
Reciprocal agreements apply to Orphans Benefit only and allow residence and/or periods of insurance contributions in one of the following countries to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for Orphans Benefit purposes:
- Hellenic Republic (Greece)
- Ireland
- United Kingdom
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Reciprocal Agreements
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Absence from New Zealand
- Permanent absence

chunks.title: Child in the care of Oranga Tamariki — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Child in the care of Oranga Tamariki
Depending on the circumstances when a child is in care, custody or sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, the cost of care is generally the responsibility of Oranga Tamariki.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Child in care of Oranga Tamariki

chunks.title: Child Support — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Child Support
Child support does not affect payment of Clothing Allowance
For more information see:

chunks.title: Childs income — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Childs income
Personal earnings of the child do not affect the rate of payment of Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit or the amount of Clothing Allowance.
Note a child in full-time employment and financially independent is not treated as a dependent child for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
For more information see:
- Changes and reviews Child in full time employment
## Other income
A child may receive other income that is not personal earnings.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Childs other income
## Rate reduces below family tax credit rate
If the income received by a child reduces Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit to below the level of family tax credit that the caregiver can get, consider:
- cancelling the benefit and including the child as a dependent in a parent benefit or
- advising the caregiver to seek family tax credit payments through Inland Revenue.
When the Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit reduces to nil no Clothing Allowance can be paid.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Child starts work
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Childs income

chunks.title: Effect of Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Effect of Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children
Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children is not considered as income when assessing other benefit assistance where an income test is applied;
- Advance Payment of Benefits (including the calculation of the Advance Balance calculation)
- Childcare Subsidy or OSCAR
- Special Benefit
- Special Needs Grants
- Temporary Additional Support
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Advance Payment of Benefits and Special Needs Grants
- Deskfile Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children rates
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children provides weekly financial assistance to caregivers getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit. This benefit is not taxed.
The payment provides assistance for:
- a reasonable range of clothing
- a travel bag
- replacement school clothing
These cover the same costs that clothing allowance for Oranga Tamariki caregivers receive.
The Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children is paid in addition to the School and Year Start-up Payment (SAYSUP).
The Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children can also assist caregivers to replace items that wear out or are lost etc.

chunks.title: Multiple children — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Multiple children
Some caregivers may be granted Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for multiple children.
A caregiver will receive Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children for each child they receive an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Qualifications
- Siblings

chunks.title: Emergency Benefit — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Emergency Benefit
If the caregiver is eligible for Emergency Benefit (including meeting the hardship test), this should usually be granted at the Jobseeker Support rate they would have received if they were available for full-time work.
They can continue to receive Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for the care of the child and also continue to receive Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children.
- Emergency Benefit Single and caring for a child

chunks.title: Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children
From 1 July 2018 weekly payments of Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children are paid to all caregivers who are getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit. The allowance is based on the age of the child and adjusted annually with the Consumer Price Index.
Clothing Allowance is paid weekly on a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday at the same time that Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit payments are made.
Payment is made one week in arrears and covers a 7 day period.
The payment is made at different rates depending on the age of the child.
For the age groups and clothing allowance rates see:
- Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported Children rates
## End date
Payment of Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children will stop when the client is no longer getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for that child.
## Other payments made to carers getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child Benefit
The Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children payment is in addition to:
- School and Year Start Up Payment
- Establishment Grant
- Extraordinary Care Fund

chunks.title: Agencies meeting — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Agencies meeting
When considering a permanent placement, the caregiver and social worker will meet with a case manager to discuss any income support that may be available to the caregiver.
Generally this meeting will take place before any court orders in favour of the caregivers have been made.
Because Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children is available from 1 July 2018, any court ordered support from Oranga Tamariki should exclude this assistance.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Process for children in permanency
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Oranga Tamariki child discharged to caregiver
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Definition of discharged from Oranga Tamariki care

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
To receive a Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported Children, caregivers must be receiving Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
Payment is automatically made when Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is granted.
## Child Support
Child Support does not affect payment of Clothing Allowance. See: Core policy Child Support
For more information see:

chunks.title: Siblings — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > clothing allowance
chunks.text:
## Siblings
When the children have siblings and the caregiver is receiving Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for every sibling, each child is entitled to a Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit Qualifications
- Multiple children

chunks.title: Application forms can be left at a service centre — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text: Clients can take their completed application form and supporting documents directly to a service centre. Clients do not need to meet with us to apply for Extraordinary Care Fund. If a client would like to talk to someone before submitting their application they will need to make an appointment. Clients need to provide proof of the costs they are applying for, e.g. a quote, receipt or letter from the service provider. They also need to provide proof of how the item or activity will help the child. This could be a letter of support from a teacher, coach or doctor. If the client is applying for $500 or more for items not relating to sports or arts they need to provide a second letter of support from another independent person. We do not need a letter of support as evidence for costs to do with sports and arts, if the application is for less than $1,000 in a financial year. If a client has a change in circumstances at any time they should tell their local service centre. If their quotes change while waiting for their Extraordinary Care Fund application to be processed, they will need to provide a new quote.

chunks.title: Payment of Extraordinary Care Fund to clients with guardianship of more than one child — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text: The Extraordinary Care Fund is paid per child. If a client is caring for more than one child they are able to apply for a grant for each child.

chunks.title: Paying in advance and retrospective applications — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text: When a cost needs to be paid in stages or over a period of time the client can request a grant to cover up to a year's costs. For example, a trip that requires $500 in October and $500 in March, or music lessons that have weekly or monthly payments. If the panel considers there are circumstances where a grant should be allowed retrospectively (ie the client has already paid for the costs and then applies) they can approve that grant. Retrospective applications will need to show evidence of the costs incurred.

chunks.title: Applicants not eligible — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text: Applicants who won't be eligible for the Extraordinary Care Fund include: - clients whose Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is not current at the time the panel considers applications (suspended, registered, expired or cancelled) - applicants who have already received an Extraordinary Care Fund grant for the respective child within the current financial year (1 July to 30 June) - this is regardless of how much the grant approved was for

chunks.title: Costs excluded from the Extraordinary Care Fund — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text: The Extraordinary Care Fund excludes: - costs that the Establishment Grant or the School and Year Start-up Payment are designed to assist with, such as clothing, school fees and stationery - everyday common costs (eg vehicles, legal costs, school trips, childcare) - costs funded by from other agencies such as: everyday health and medical costs (eg treatment, medication that is covered by the Ministry of Health)teacher aides - everyday health and medical costs (eg treatment, medication that is covered by the Ministry of Health) - teacher aides - overseas travel and any other overseas travel related costs (eg hotels, overseas courses) - costs less than $100. These costs may be considered under other emergency hardship grants. For more information see: - Eligibility - Payment - Reconsideration of an Extraordinary Care Fund decision

chunks.title: Eligibility — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text:
## Eligibility
To be considered for a grant from the Extraordinary Care Fund the applicant must meet the following criteria.
Be caring for a child who is:
- experiencing difficulties that significantly impact on their development or
- showing promise
## Experiencing difficulties that significantly impact on their development
The following are examples, and don't limit what may be covered by the fund for a child who is experiencing difficulties that significantly impact on their development:
- extra tutoring (not funded by the Ministry of Education) for a child who is unable to keep up in school
- attending an emotional or physical confidence programme to build self-esteem
- swimming lessons
- orthodontic work for a child who is not eligible for funding through the Ministry of Health
- house modifications (not be funded by the Ministry of Health) for safety reasons (eg a special gate for a child who runs away)
- social skills course eg through support groups
- private counselling
## Showing promise
The following are examples, but don't limit what may be covered by the fund for a child who is showing promise:
- national Kapa Haka competitions
- attending national sports competitions
- attending a New Zealand youth orchestra/youth choir event or the Royal New Zealand Ballet's mentoring programme
- cost of advanced coaching, tutoring or lessons - this could include the cost of lessons and musical instruments
For more information see:
- Applications
- Payment
- Reconsideration of an Extraordinary Care Fund decision

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The Extraordinary Care Fund provides non-taxable financial assistance to carers who receive the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
The grant is not included in the hardship count, and does not affect eligibility for other payments such as Working for Families or Extra help supplementary assistance.
The Extraordinary Care Fund has up to 4 funding rounds each year. Grants are made as one-off, ad-hoc payments.
Applications can be accepted at any time during the year, however decisions will be made 4 times a year at the end of each funding round.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text:
## Payment
The Extraordinary Care Fund is a discretionary grant for an amount between $100 to $2000.
Clients who submit a successful application are able to receive one grant per financial year (1 July to 30 June) for each child in their care.
## The Panel
The Extraordinary Care Fund is administered by an expert panel. The panel assesses each application and makes recommendations to approve or decline the application and the amount.
## The Secretariat
The Secretariat is the national co-ordinator of the application process and is based in the Partnerships and Services team at National Office.
The Secretariat co-ordinates with the panel, sends completed applications to the panel for consideration before the review meeting, and manages any Extraordinary Care Fund applications which are escalated.
## The Budget Manager
The Panel's recommendations are made to the manager of Partnerships and Services (the budget manager) who approves the payment.
## Repayment of Extraordinary Care Fund
We can request the client refunds any payments from the Extraordinary Care Fund when:
- the client advises they no longer need the Extraordinary Care Fund payment or
- we became aware that the payment was not used for the reason it was paid.
For more information see:
- Eligibility
- Applications
- Reconsideration of an Extraordinary Care Fund decision

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
To apply for a grant from the Extraordinary Care Fund, an applicant must be receiving:
- Orphan's Benefit or
- Unsupported Child's Benefit
For more information see:
- Eligibility
- Applications
- Payment

chunks.title: Reconsideration of an Extraordinary Care Fund decision — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > extraordinary care fund
chunks.text:
## Reconsideration of an Extraordinary Care Fund decision
The Extraordinary Care Fund decisions are not subject to the rights to review under the Social Security Act 2018. However, a client may request that the original decision is reconsidered.
A decision can be reconsidered based on the following:
- was all relevant information provided and duly considered
- was there a good and sufficient reason for not providing the information
- the amount of funding available for that round
For more information see:
- Extraordinary Care Fund - Reconsideration of a Decision [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Caregiver not entitled to an allowance on entitlement date — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Caregiver not entitled to an allowance on entitlement date
The Birthday Allowance and Holiday Allowance are paid to a caregiver in advance of the entitlement date.
If, on the entitlement date, the caregiver no longer qualifies for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit for the child for whom an Allowance was paid, the Allowance payment will become a debt.
The debt must be assessed against the debt write-off criteria to determine whether the debt is recoverable or not.
Note when a caregiver has a change in circumstances and they no longer qualify for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, there is discretion to continue the benefit payments for up to 28 days following the event. If the caregiver is still getting Orphans Benenfit or Unsupported Childs Benefit on the entitlement date for a Birthday Allowance or Holiday Allowance, they still qualify for the Allowance
## Example - caregiver not entitled to Holiday Allowance
Naisi is 5 years old and lives with her caregiver, Paul.
Naisi returns to live with her mother on 5 November, but Paul did not tell the Ministry of Social Development of the change in circumstances and continues getting Unsupported Childs Benefit for Naisi.
The Holiday Allowance is paid on 10 December, and on 15 December Paul advises the Ministry, Naisi has returned to live with her mother.
The Ministry uses discretion to avoid financial hardship for Paul, and continues paying Unsupported Childs Benefit for 28 days from the date Naisi left his care, until 3 December.
As Paul’s entitlement to Unsupported Childs Benefit ended on 3 December, the Ministry establishes a debt the Holiday Allowance.
Any payments of the Unsupported Child’s Benefit from 4 December also become a debt for Paul.

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance > changes and reviews holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
When the caregiver, or the child, is absent from New Zealand, the caregiver may still be paid the Birthday Allowance and/or Holiday Allowance for a child if:
- they meet all the qualifications and
- the absence from New Zealand is temporary
See:
- Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit Absence from New Zealand

chunks.title: Change of caregiver — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance > changes and reviews holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Change of caregiver
To get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit the caregiver must be an eligible caregiver of the child.
Any changes in circumstances that result in Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit no longer being paid for the child, mean the caregiver is not entitled to get a Holiday Allowance or Birthday Allowance in respect of the child.
## Two caregivers getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for the same child
There may be circumstances when, due to the discretion for extending entitlement to Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for up to 28 days, more than one caregiver qualifies to get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for the same child.
In these circumstances, both caregivers may get the Holiday Allowance and/or Birthday Allowance if they are both getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit on the entitlement date for the Allowance.
## Example – caregivers with Unsupported Childs Benefit entitlement overlap in respect of the same child
Henderson is getting Unsupported Childs Benefit while caring for Ana, who has her 15th birthday on 1 October. Henderson notifies the Ministry of Social Development that Ana is leaving his care on 20 September to go and live with her kuia (grandmother) Marama. The Ministry uses discretion to avoid financial hardship and continues paying Henderson the Unsupported Childs Benefit for 28 days after Ana leaves Henderson's care.
Marama applies for and is granted Unsupported Childs Benefit from the day Ana comes into her care, 20 September.
Both Henderson and Marama are entitled to get Unsupported Childs Benefit on Ana's birthday (1 October), and both caregivers get a Birthday Allowance in respect of Ana.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance > changes and reviews holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
Caregivers must tell the Ministry of Social Development about any changes in circumstances that may affect their qualification to get Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit.
These changes may also affect a caregiver's qualification to the Birthday Allowance and Holiday Allowance.
A benefit may also be reviewed at any time to make sure the caregiver still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.

chunks.title: Child changes — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance > changes and reviews holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Child changes
For Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit to be paid for a child, the child must meet the definition of a dependent child.
Any changes in circumstances that result in Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit no longer being paid for the child, mean the caregiver will also not get a Holiday Allowance or Birthday Allowance for the child.
Change to a dependent child's circumstances is generally going to affect the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
## Unsupported Childs Benefit only
- Temporary return to parents
- Permanent return to parents

chunks.title: Permanent absence — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance > changes and reviews holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
The Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance cannot be paid to any caregiver when the child or caregiver permanently leaves New Zealand.
The caregiver will generally no longer qualify for an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit from the day after departure if they or the child leave New Zealand permanently, therefore the caregiver will not qualify for the Holiday Allowance or Birthday Allowance.
A caregiver may continue to qualify for an Orphans Benefit if they are going to live in a country with a reciprocal agreement in place, but the Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance are not payable under any reciprocal agreement.
If the child is staying in New Zealand:
- the new caregiver may meet the qualifications for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit or
- if the new caregiver is getting a main benefit the child may be included as a dependent child in the benefit

chunks.title: Reciprocal Agreements — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance > changes and reviews holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Reciprocal Agreements
New Zealand has reciprocal agreements with some countries. Reciprocal agreements only apply to the payment of Orphans Benefit.
Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance cannot be paid when Orphans Benefit is paid under a reciprocal agreement.

chunks.title: Effect of Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance on other assistance — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Effect of Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance on other assistance
Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance are not considered income when assessing eligibility:
- to any assistance provided under the Social Security Act 2018
- for Social Housing or calculating the rate of Income Related Rent
- to or calculating the rate payable of any Student Allowance

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance are 2 individual annual, non-taxable payments to caregivers getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
The Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance help with the costs of preparing a celebration, purchasing gifts, or planning an event or experience for the child, or children, in the caregiver's care.
Clients do not apply for this assistance, payments are made automatically.
These allowances cover the same costs as the Birthday Allowance and Christmas Allowance paid to Oranga Tamariki caregivers.

chunks.title: Payment made in arrears — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Payment made in arrears
The Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance can be paid after the entitlement date, known as payment in arrears.
This may happen when retrospective entitlement to Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is established on, or before the entitlement date for the Holiday Allowance or/and Birthday Allowance.
The client does not need to apply for the Birthday Allowance or Holiday Allowance.
## Example - child comes into caregivers care with retrospective entitlement to Unsupported Childs Benefit
On 10 February Maria applies for Unsupported Childs Benefit for her grandson Mata who is in her care following a breakdown in the family.
Maria is granted Unsupported Childs Benefit for her grandson, Mata, on 24 February.
The commencement date is 10 February (the application date). Mata's birthday is on 15 February.
Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid in arrears for the retrospective entitlement, and includes the Birthday Allowance, as Maria qualified for Unsupported Childs Benefit on Mata's birthday.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Payment
The Birthday Allowance and Holiday Allowance are non-taxable, annual payments.
The allowances are paid at half the weekly rate of Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit the caregiver will get for the child, on the entitlement date for the allowance.
If the weekly rate of Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit cannot be divided equally by 2, the half rate is rounded up to the nearest cent.
Caregivers do not need to apply for this assistance. Payments are automatically made to each caregiver getting an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
For the payment rates see:
- Deskfile Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance rates

chunks.title: Holiday Allowance — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Holiday Allowance
To get the Holiday Allowance, a caregiver must be getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit on the entitlement date.
The entitlement date for the Holiday Allowance is 25 December each year.
## Birthday Allowance
To get the Birthday Allowance, a caregiver must be getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit on the entitlement date.
The entitlement date for the Birthday Allowance is the date of each child's birthday, except for birthdays on 29 February in leap years.
## Multiple children
Some caregivers may be getting an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for multiple children.
The caregiver will get both a Holiday Allowance and a Birthday Allowance for each child they get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for.

chunks.title: Rate of payment adjusted — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## Rate of payment adjusted
The Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance rates may increase on 1 April each year if there is a percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index affecting the rate of Unsupported Childs Benefit and Orphans Benefit.
## Birthday Allowance and 1 April change in rate
As the Birthday Allowance is generally paid in advance of the entitlement date, the rate payable may increase if the payment is made before 1 April for birthdays on or just after 1 April.
When a Birthday Allowance is paid before 1 April, caregivers will get a top-up payment after 1 April, if there was an increase in the Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit rate on 1 April.

chunks.title: When payment is made — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > holiday allowance and birthday allowance
chunks.text:
## When payment is made
The Holiday Allowance and Birthday Allowance are paid to a caregiver a short time before the entitlement date when the Ministry of Social Development expects the caregiver will qualify for the allowance.
Generally, the payment is made automatically about 2 weeks before the allowance entitlement date, and is paid with the caregiver's weekly Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit payments.
## Example – Birthday Allowance
Latisha gets Orphans Benefit while caring for Moana, who is 14 years old on 23 March. Latisha is automatically paid the Birthday Allowance on 9 March with Latisha's weekly benefit payment, before the Birthday Allowance entitlement date (23 March). The Birthday Allowance is paid at half the weekly rate of Orphans Benefit that Latisha will get on Moana's birthday.
Note the entitlement date for the Birthday Allowance is the child's birthday.
## Example - Holiday Allowance
Rebecca is getting Unsupported Childs Benefit for 2 children, Boston and Christen. Rebecca is automatically paid 2 Holiday Allowances on 13 December for both Boston and Christen with her weekly benefit payment, 2 weeks before the entitlement date.
Note the entitlement date for the Holiday Allowance is 25 December.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > school and year start up payment
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise the Ministry of Social Development of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a School and Year Start-up Payment.

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > school and year start up payment
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The School and Year Start-up Payment provides non-taxable, non-recoverable financial assistance to assist with school related costs or other costs relating to the care of the child.
These costs may result in additional financial pressure such as clothing, costs associated with sports club memberships, Scouts, or Kapa Haka etc.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > school and year start up payment
chunks.text:
## Payment
The School and Year Start-up Payment is a one-off payment that a client can apply for every year between the first Monday after 10 January and the last day of February.
The maximum amount of School and Year Start-up Payment will depend on the child's age as at the last day of February and is paid directly to the client's bank account.

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit products > school and year start up payment
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
To receive a School and Year Start-up Payment:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit must be payable on the last day of February or
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit would be payable on the last day of February but for the child's temporary absence from New Zealand
and
- the client must have applied for the School and Year Start-up Payment between the first Monday after 10 January and last day of February each year, unless the client has a good and sufficient reason for not applying within these dates
## Good and sufficient reason
When a client has good and sufficient reason that prevented them from applying for a School and Year Start-up Payment in the specified time period, a payment may still be considered if they were receiving Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit on the last day of February.
The guiding principle in determining "good and sufficient" reason is one of "reasonableness". Having considered the client's circumstances, would it have been "reasonable" for the client to have applied for the School and Year Start-up Payment between the first Monday after 10 January and the last day of February.
The list of good and sufficient reasons (but not limited to) are:
- death of a close relative
- severe illness or hospitalisation of client or family member
- essential overseas travel
- where a child comes into care after the last day of February and has costs associated with starting a new school
Decide in favour of the client if any doubt remains.
## Multiple children
Some clients may be granted Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for multiple children.
A client can get a School and Year Start-up Payment for each child included in their Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit and listed on the application form for School and Year Start-up Payment.
## Absence from New Zealand
A client may apply for a School and Year Start-up Payment when the Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is suspended as the child is overseas.
An application for School and Year Start-up Payment may be paid if the child meets all the qualifications and the absence from New Zealand is temporary and the child is returning to New Zealand.
The Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit must be current as at the last day of February for a School and Year Start-up Payment to be made.

chunks.title: Ambulance subscription fees — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Ambulance subscription fees
Instead of paying one-off ambulance fees, clients can pay a one-year subscription to St John. The subscription gives the client and their families' unlimited access to emergency services for one year.
If the client meets all qualifications, they may be able to receive a Recoverable Assistance Payment for subscription fees.
As a Recoverable Assistance Payment is for items of particular immediate need, you should consider the following:
- whether the client and/or their family is likely to require ambulance services
- how regular an ambulance would be required by the client and/or their family
- whether there is a history of expectation of the requirement to use an ambulance
As a guideline, a Recoverable Assistance Payment for Ambulance Subscription fees should not be more than $200.

chunks.title: Applying hardship obligations to partners — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Applying hardship obligations to partners
Hardship obligations can apply to a client and/or their partner.
It may be appropriate to apply hardship obligations to a partner when:
- previous assistance has been provided to meet the need of both the client and partner (eg food grants have been provided because both the client and partner need food)
- the partner has contributed to the need for assistance (eg where assistance with a power bill is required because both the client and partner have not paid a previous bill)
- the partner's actions are adversely affecting the client's ongoing financial position
Generally, when a partner has failed to take reasonable steps or not completed a budgeting activity, an application from the client for a Special Needs Grant, Advance Payment of Benefit or Recoverable Assistance Payment will be declined unless exceptional circumstances exist.
For more information see:
- Hardship obligations
- Reasonable steps obligation
- Budgeting activity obligation
- Failure to meet hardship obligations
- Exceptional circumstances

chunks.title: Assignment, subletting or ending a tenancy early — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Assignment, subletting or ending a tenancy early
If a client qualifies for a Recoverable Assistance Payment, they may get assistance under the 'other emergency payment' category to meet the actual and reasonable costs charged by their landlord for assignment, subletting or ending a tenancy early when:
- special circumstances exist and
- the client, their partner (if any) or dependent children (if any) would suffer serious hardship without that item or service
Verification of the amount required for each cost, and the landlord's full name and address, must be seen.
When deciding if there are special circumstances or if the client, their partner or dependent children would suffer serious hardship, also consider the reason the person needs to assign, sublet or end the tenancy early, and the impacts if they do not move.
This includes considering the following:
- Is the person moving to: reduce their ongoing rent costsleave a situation of family violencebe closer to work or essential services (eg moving closer to a tertiary hospital for specialist treatment or moving to a new area to take up a job offer) ora property that better meet their needs (eg moving to an accessible property or one with more bedrooms so they are no longer overcrowded)?
- reduce their ongoing rent costs
- leave a situation of family violence
- be closer to work or essential services (eg moving closer to a tertiary hospital for specialist treatment or moving to a new area to take up a job offer) or
- a property that better meet their needs (eg moving to an accessible property or one with more bedrooms so they are no longer overcrowded)?
- If they did not move, would the client be: in danger or at risk of harm orunable to meet their other immediate and essential needs (eg food or power costs) from their remaining resources, including other assistance from the Ministry of Social Development?
- in danger or at risk of harm or
- unable to meet their other immediate and essential needs (eg food or power costs) from their remaining resources, including other assistance from the Ministry of Social Development?
## Payment
Except when exceptional circumstances exist, payment cannot exceed:
- 6 weeks of the appropriate rate of Supported Living Payment the client would be entitled to get or
- $200
whichever is the least amount.

chunks.title: Attendance at funerals and tangihanga — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Attendance at funerals and tangihanga
If a client meets all qualifications, a Recoverable Assistance Payment can be made for bereaved relatives towards the expenses of attending Funerals or Tangihanga and are limited to the deceased's:
- parents (including step-parents and foster parents)
- partner (providing they were living with the deceased at the time of death)
- grandparents
- children (including grandchildren, stepchildren, foster children, mokopuna - those grandchildren who have been raised by the grandparents as the principal caregivers, and whāngai - children who have been raised, normally by a relation or other person within the wider whānau to which the child belongs) or
- siblings (including half siblings and step siblings, but excluding members of organisations/gangs referring to themselves as 'blood brothers and sisters')
Assistance is not available to the deceased's:
- parents' siblings (including aunts and uncles)
- siblings' children (including nieces and nephews)
- cousins
- in-laws or
- friends
Recoverable Assistance Payments approved for funerals and tangihanga are not to include:
- assistance toward costs arising as a result of a funeral/tangihanga
- costs associated with unveiling ceremonies or
- the cost of contributing toward a koha (for example, food)
For assistance toward the cost of a funeral/tangihanga itself, see:
- Funeral Grants
## Payment
Except where exceptional circumstances exist, payment cannot exceed:
- 6 weeks of the appropriate rate of Supported Living Payment that the client would be entitled to receive or
- $200
whichever is the least amount.

chunks.title: Budgeting advice requirements — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Budgeting advice requirements
Clients will often attend budgeting advice services on an ongoing basis. Clients can be considered to be completing their budgeting activity if they can show that they have seen their budgeting advisor at least once since their last grant date, or that they are following a current budgeting advice programme or individual plan.
For more information see:
- Building Financial Capability services [no link find out why] procedures
- Adding plan items and resulting activities in CMS [no link find out why] procedures

chunks.title: Acceptable budgeting course or seminar — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Acceptable budgeting course or seminar
A budgeting course or seminar does not have to be provided by a budgeting service (eg it may be provided by another community organisation or a bank).
To be considered a budgeting activity the course or seminar must include information on:
- learning how to budget or
- developing a budget or
- improving budgeting skills
For more information see:
- Attending a budgeting advice service
- Completing a budgeting worksheet
- Budgeting activity obligation
- Reasonable steps obligation
- Failure to meet hardship obligations
- Adding plan items and resulting activities in CMS [no link find out why] procedures
- Building Financial Capability services [no link find out why] procedures

chunks.title: Beds, chairs, and tables — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Beds, chairs, and tables
If a client meets all qualifications, a Recoverable Assistance Payment may be made for the purchase of the most economical items of essential beds, chairs, and tables.
Note that beds include cots, bassinets and pepi-pods.
Quotes are to be produced from new or second-hand dealers or retailers. Payment should not be approved for purchases of furniture through private sales.

chunks.title: Budgeting activity obligation — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text: Clients who frequently access Special Needs Grants, Advance Payments of Benefit and Recoverable Assistance Payments may need to meet a budgeting activity obligation. This obligation requires clients to take part in activities that will help them improve their ability to budget and make the most of the resources available to them. Clients may be required to: - complete or review a budgeting worksheet - attend a budgeting course or seminar or - attend a budgeting advice service The specific activity the client is required to complete should be the activity that is most likely to meet their needs and be helpful given their personal situation Note you must make sure the client is getting their correct entitlement at every interaction with them.

chunks.title: Applying budgeting activity obligation — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text: Generally clients are not required to complete a budgeting activity until after they have received Special Needs Grants, Advance Payments of Benefit and/or Recoverable Assistance Payments on at least 3 grant dates during the past 12 months. Before applying a budgeting activity obligation, you need to ensure that you understand the client’s circumstances and how applying the obligation could help them. A budgeting activity obligation should only be applied if you have been in contact with the client and determined: - the client is likely to benefit from completing a budgeting activity - the client’s financial situation could improve as a result and - the client has previously: been offered services to help them build their financial capability, understood how they could benefit from participating, and chose to not take up the services orused a building financial capability or similar service and their circumstances have substantially changed from when they used the service - been offered services to help them build their financial capability, understood how they could benefit from participating, and chose to not take up the services or - used a building financial capability or similar service and their circumstances have substantially changed from when they used the service Before applying a budgeting activity obligation, also consider: - the number of previous applications for hardship assistance and why the assistance was needed eg is there a pattern of not being able to meet regular, ongoing costs or were there a number of separate unforeseeable events? - eg is there a pattern of not being able to meet regular, ongoing costs or were there a number of separate unforeseeable events? - if the current need is related to unforeseeable events, or circumstances out of the client’s control eg a recent bereavement or separation, emergency or other adverse event, etc - eg a recent bereavement or separation, emergency or other adverse event, etc - why the client has not taken up services to help them build their financial capability if previously offered If you have decided that the client should have a budgeting activity obligation, discuss which budgeting activity will be most helpful for them, make sure they know the activity they choose is an obligation and explain the consequence if they do not complete the activity. Note in some circumstances partners must also complete a budgeting activity. For information on when it would not be appropriate to require a client to complete a budgeting activity see: - Budgeting activity obligation not applied

chunks.title: Applying budgeting activity obligation before third grant date — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text: Generally clients are only required to complete a budgeting activity after they have received Special Needs Grants, Advance Payments of Benefit and/or Recoverable Assistance Payments on at least 3 grant dates during the past 12 months. However, you can apply the budgeting activity obligation before 3 grant dates. When deciding whether to apply the budgeting activity obligation before their third grant date you must also consider if the client has: - received repeated grants for the same costs - a history of receiving multiple hardship payments - a significant debt with the Ministry of Social Development

chunks.title: Budgeting activity obligation not applied — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Budgeting activity obligation not applied
You should not apply a budgeting activity obligation if it is unlikely to help the client and their financial situation would not improve as a result.
Clients applying for a Special Needs Grants, Advance Payments of Benefit or Recoverable Assistance Payments who should not be required to complete a budgeting activity for a period of time, or until their circumstances change, include those who:
- have high unavoidable costs and are unlikely to benefit from the budgeting activity
- previously completed the same budgeting activity and their circumstances have not substantially changed since completing that activity
- had a recent sudden change in circumstances eg a recent bereavement or separation
- had a temporary change in their situation eg an unforeseen drop in income or a change in needs due to family, or family violence

chunks.title: Car repairs — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Car repairs
If a client meets all qualifications, a Recoverable Assistance Payment may be made for repairs to a vehicle, when the use of a car is essential for the client or their dependent partner and children. The car should be considered essential due to illness, disability, employment, or lack of access to public transport.
The car should be owned by the client or their partner, not another family member or a friend.
Assistance should not be given to approve foreseen costs (for example, fuel, warrant of fitness, car insurance, and car registration) or for regular servicing costs.
## Car insurance excess
Car insurance excess is the cost a person has to pay towards their insurance claim, with the insurance company meeting the remaining cost.
If the client meets all qualifications, a Recoverable Assistance Payment may be made for the cost of car insurance excess.
## Payment
Except where exceptional circumstances exist, payment cannot exceed:
- 6 weeks of the appropriate rate of Supported Living Payment that the client would be entitled to receive or
- $400
whichever is the least amount.

chunks.title: Cash asset limits — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Cash asset limits
A client (and any partner) cannot get Recoverable Assistance Payments if their cash assets exceed the following appropriate asset limit:
Single person
Asset limit for a single person without dependent children
Married, civil union or de facto couple, with or without dependent children or
Sole parents
Asset limit for a married, civil union or de facto couple, with or without dependent children, and sole parents

chunks.title: Cash assets include — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Cash assets include
- bills of exchange or promissory notes
- building society shares
- money in bank accounts, including fixed and term deposits with any bank, friendly society, credit union, or building society
- money invested with or lent to any bank, other financial institution or person
- mortgage investments and other long-term loans
- shares, stocks, debentures, bonus bonds, and other bonds
- the client's share in any partnership and
- the net equity held in any property or land not used as the person's home
## Cash assets do not include
- the home property and land on which it is situated
- a caravan, boat, or other vehicle with a net equity of less than $2,000, or which is used by the person or a member of their family for day to day accommodation
- Christchurch mosques attack support payments
- Crown funds provided directly to clients to purchase Support Services and Direct Disability Support payments
- funds locked into KiwiSaver and other retirement scheme accounts
- Information share Child Support payments currently being charged as income
- motor vehicle principally used by the client for private use
- MSD lump sum payments for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Payments of Accommodation Supplement arrears due to system processing error from 1993 to 2014
- Payments of arrears to Special Benefit clients better off on Temporary Additional Support for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Payments to clients whose Kāinga Ora tenancy was terminated due to methamphetamine contamination for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- personal effects
- Residential Care Subsidy historic review refunds for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Severe weather event payments for the first 12 months from when payment is received (and any interest earned on the payment)
- specified Ex gratia and Compensation payments
- FamilyBoost Tax Credit payments for the first 12 months after payment is received
A bank overdraft facility is not considered a cash asset or resource available to a client.
Canterbury earthquake related payments
Payments made by the Crown, Earthquake Commission, insurance companies or the Canterbury Earthquake Commission (Red Cross) relating to the Canterbury earthquake are generally excluded for the first 12 or 24 months following the date the client received the payment.

chunks.title: Child restraints for motor vehicles, and safety helmets — extra help > recoverable assistance payment
chunks.text:
## Child restraints for motor vehicles, and safety helmets
If a client meets all qualifications, a Recoverable Assistance Payment can be made to:
- purchase a new approved child restraint for a motor vehicle, for each child under 7 years of age who is dependent child of the client
- hire an approved child restraint for a motor vehicle from reputable agencies, for each child under 7 years of age who is a dependent child of the client or
- purchase a new cycle safety helmet for each school aged dependent child of the client
Where the motor vehicle needs an attachment to fit the child restraint, this cost can be included in the purchase.
## Payment
Except where exceptional circumstances exist, payment for each dependent child cannot exceed:
- 6 weeks of the appropriate rate of Supported Living Payment that the client would be entitled to receive or
- $200
whichever is the least amount.
