Note if the client in care is getting Residential Care Subsidy, any income that is included in the means assessment of income is not charged against New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension (when they are income tested) or Emergency Benefit.

chunks.title: Trust decisions — extra help > residential care subsidy
chunks.text:
## Trust decisions
The assets held, income generated, and decisions made by the trust cannot be attributed to the client.
## Role of trustee
A trustee is appointed to take care of the assets and income of the trust in a way that supports the needs of the trust beneficiaries. Trustees have a duty to make decisions in line with the terms of the trust deed.
## Client is a trustee
Decisions made by a trust cannot be attributed to a single trustee. When the client is a trustee, decisions made by the trust cannot be attributed solely to the client. Decisions are being made in the role of trustee and not in the client's personal capacity.
## Exception
The only time we can attribute trust decisions to the client is when they have full unrestricted control over the entire trust. This control must not be limited by the terms of the trust deed or the involvement of any other trustee.

chunks.title: Trusts — extra help > residential care subsidy
chunks.text:
## Trusts
A trust is a legal arrangement established by the settlor who usually sells or gifts assets to be held 'on trust' by specified persons (the trustees) for the benefit of specified persons (the beneficiaries). Any assets gifted or sold to the trust are legally owned by the trust.
Trusts can be established for a variety of reasons. A common reason is to preserve assets for future generations. Reasons for the trust establishment and conditions around distributions will generally be provided for in the trust deed.
## Common types of trusts
Family trusts: established to keep asset ownership in the family and support family members in need.
Testamentary trusts: trusts established by provision in a will when a person passes away.
Mirror trusts: trusts, generally established by couples, where each partner is the settlor/trustee of the trust that the other partner is a beneficiary of.
Institutional constructive trusts: when a property transaction denies one party their property entitlement it might be considered their interest is being held 'on trust'.
For more information see:
- Key words within trusts
## Beneficiary of a trust
A trust can have an impact on Residential Care Subsidy because clients need to use the resources available to them before seeking financial assistance. We might expect a trust to provide resources to the client to help pay for their care.
When the client is a beneficiary of a trust, they will generally be expected to request support from it.
## Deprivation has been identified
If a specific act of deprivation has been identified the trust can be looked to as a source of other resources available to help meet the cost of care. This is an essential consideration before deciding if discretion should be used to count deprived assets or income back into the financial means assessment.
There is an assumption that resources are available from a family trust unless there is evidence to the contrary. If the client is a beneficiary of a trust, their partner (if any) is a beneficiary of a trust or they have received regular support from a trust they will generally be expected to request support.

chunks.title: Using discretion — extra help > residential care subsidy
chunks.text:
## Using discretion
The means assessment is to ensure that where appropriate people use the resources available to them before getting Residential Care Subsidy. People should use the resources available to them to meet the cost of their care before they get additional financial support.
There is discretion to count amounts of assets or income a client or their partner (living or deceased) deprived themselves of into the financial means assessment. Deprivation can be direct or indirect and may have happened at any time.
Note there is no discretion for excess gifting within the 5-year gifting period.
When considering using discretion to count back deprived assets or income, the circumstances of the client should be taken into account. There is no set criteria. Consider the reasons for their decisions, as well as their current situation and access to resources.
## Discretion not always used
Discretion can be used to count deprived amounts back into the financial means assessment as if the deprivation had not occurred.
There are some restraints when using discretion, and it should not be used automatically. Each case needs to be assessed on the facts and consideration given to whether counting deprivation back into the financial means assessment would result in the client having to use their assets below the threshold to pay for their care.
Factors to consider may include (but are not limited to):
- what resources are available to the client?
- who a gift was made to (i.e. family, trust, charity organisation)?
- why the client deprived themselves?
- who benefitted from the deprivation?
- did the client receive anything in return for depriving themselves?
- the total value of the client's assets
- what would the client's position be if they had not deprived themselves?

chunks.title: Accommodation Supplement — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Accommodation Supplement
If a client is in an approved Ministry of Health contracted facility and receiving residential care because of a physical, intellectual, psychiatric disability or alcohol and drug problem, they cannot receive an Accommodation Supplement.
Accommodation Supplement should be stopped from the day the client entered residential care. If the client has entered residential care and their partner in the community has accommodation costs, the Accommodation Supplement needs to be re-assessed.
The exception to this is when the client has ongoing accommodation costs in the community that they are still required to meet. The client should be invited to apply for Community Costs. If Community Costs is granted, any Accommodation Supplement should stop from the day the client entered care. For more information see: Community Costs
## Partner's accommodation costs
Accommodation Supplement may be paid to the partner in the community who is continuing to meet accommodation costs. The Accommodation Supplement needs to be manually re-assessed at the single or sole parent rate, but taking the income and assets of both the client and the partner into consideration.
## Non contracted facilities
If the client is in a residential care facility that is not contracted or funded by the Ministry of Health, they cannot receive a Residential Support Subsidy. They may be able to receive assistance through Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance.
For more information see:
- Increased payment to partner in community
- Extra Help Disability Allowance
- Extra help Accommodation Supplement

chunks.title: Advance Payment of Benefit — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Advance Payment of Benefit
A client granted Residential Support Subsidy may be able to receive an Advance Payment of Benefit if they meet all of the qualifications.
Before considering an Advance Payment of Benefit, check that the item that they are applying for is not paid by, or the responsibility of the service provider.
When processing a recoverable Advance Payment of Benefit in SWIFTT, the Residential Support Subsidy must be suspended first to access the appropriate screen in SWIFTT and recommend/approve/decline the Advance Payment of Benefit. You must contact the Residential Subsidy Unit in Whangarei who will do this for you. They will be responsible for resuming the Residential Support Subsidy and redirecting the benefit contribution.
## Please note
When recommending an Advance Payment of Benefit an offset amount is required to be entered in SWIFTT. This offset amount is then removed by the Residential Subsidy Unit when resuming the Residential Support Subsidy.
The Advance Payment of Benefit must not be recovered from the client's Personal Allowance unless the client gives their permission. Do not commence recovery of an Advance Payment of Benefit until the client is released from care, or in the event of death, seek recovery from the client's estate.
If the client gives their permission to recover the Advance Payment of Benefit from their Personal Allowance the appropriate MSD Collections is added as a payee on the client's record.

chunks.title: Application form incomplete — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Application form incomplete
If there is likely to be any delay in completing the Residential Support Subsidy application form beyond 24 hours, for example the client has not been assessed or assessment details are not readily available, then the residential service provider should in the first instance, send Senior Services - residential care a Resident's Details Notification. This form is available online.
If an incomplete Residential Support Subsidy authorisation form is received, it will be treated as a notification of entry only.
A non-standard rate, equal to the appropriate Personal Allowance rate, should be added on the client's record immediately. The residential service provider will then, as soon as possible, forward the authorisation form to Senior Services - residential care so that the clients main benefit can be adjusted accordingly.
For more information see:
- Application process

chunks.title: Application process — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Application process
All residential service providers in New Zealand are required to use the Residential Support Subsidy authorisation form to advise Work and Income when a client in their care has been assessed and will be subsidised by the Ministry of Health.
The Residential Support Subsidy Authorisation Form is available online.
When the residential service provider fully completes the form, providing full details of the assessment for residential care, it is accepted that:
- authorisation has been given by the Ministry of Health
- the client is in the target group and meets the qualifications for Residential Support Subsidy
- their service co-ordinator has arranged a suitable care facility
- the service provider is contracted by the Ministry of Health
- Ministry of Health funds are available to pay for the cost of the client's care
and
- if the client is getting a benefit they must contribute towards the cost of their care

chunks.title: Application received after death — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Application received after death
If the client is receiving a main benefit prior to their death and a Residential Support Subsidy application form is received after the death of the client, but before the main benefit has been cancelled, we can only redirect the benefit contribution to the service provider if:
- the client authorisation portion of the application form has been signed by the client or their approved agent and
- a needs assessment was carried out before death
As we are only assigning the redirection of benefit to the provider from the first available pay day, then we would not expect there to be any benefit due to the service provider after the client had died unless the client had applied for benefit and the grant action was not completed prior to death.
The service provider would need to seek payment from the estate if they have not completed the necessary application form prior to the death of the client.
For more information see:
- Application process

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client must advise the Ministry of Social Development of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement or rate of benefit payable.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
When there has been a change to the client's benefit entitlement, and as a result of this change the amount of benefit contribution has increased or decreased, the Residential Subsidy Unit must give written advice of the new amount of benefit contribution and the effective date of change to:
- the client
- the service provider (if applicable) and
- the Ministry of Health
Information given to the Ministry of Health should provide details of the change and the relevant dates only. Details of the client's financial affairs are confidential and must be discussed with the client or their agent only.
For more information see:
- Core policy Agents
- Client enters public hospital
- Client leaves care
- Client transfers to a new service provider
- Death of a client
- Debts
- Historical information
- Core policy Redirection of benefit payment
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals
- Temporary absence

chunks.title: Client enters public hospital - process — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text: If the residential service provider advises that the client has entered public hospital, you must find out whether the client is expected to be returning to the service provider's care within 13 weeks. The redirection to the service provider should only remain in place if: - the client is expected to be in hospital for less than 13 weeks - the service provider is holding the client's bed - the service provider is continuing to provide support to the client (such as maintaining contact, visiting, checking on their condition etc) and - the client has not withdrawn their consent for the redirection to continue If the client is to be in hospital less than 13 weeks, and the service provider is holding the client's bed and providing support to the client, the benefit contribution can continue to be paid. On receipt of the Resident's Details Notification form from the service provider, the date of admission to hospital needs to be added to the SHODA screen for the client, and a Client Event added.

chunks.title: When to resume full benefit payments and cancel redirection — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text: The client should be paid their full benefit entitlement and the redirection of benefit to the service provider should be cancelled from the earliest of the following dates: - the date the client enters hospital if it is known at the time that the client will not be returning to the residential care facility or - the date the service provider is advised the client will not be returning to their care, if this occurs after the client entered hospital or - the date the service provider stops holding the client's bed and providing support to the client or - the date the client withdraws their consent in writing for the redirection of benefit payment to the service provider or - the beginning of the 14th week in hospital (at which time the benefit being paid to the client will reduce to the hospital rate of payment, unless they have dependent children)

chunks.title: Client in hospital for more than 13 weeks — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text: An Exception Notification will be generated for the beginning of the 14th week. From the beginning of the 14th week, you should stop the Residential Support Subsidy and the benefit contribution. From that date, the client's benefit reduces to the hospital rate of payment. This reduction does not apply to clients who have dependent children or clients receiving Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Client returns to the community — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text: If the client returns to live in the community, advise the client to contact Work and Income to update their change in circumstances. For more information see: - Changes and reviews, hospitalisation in relevant Main benefits

chunks.title: Client leaves care — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Client leaves care
Pay the client their full benefit entitlement from the date of departure. Any redirection of benefit authorised by the client to the service provider ceases on the client's discharge date.
If the client returns to live in the community, reassess eligibility for benefit assistance, and invite applications for Extra Help if appropriate.

chunks.title: Client transfers to a new service provider — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Client transfers to a new service provider
If a client transfers from one service provider to another, cancel the redirection of Residential Support Subsidy from the date the client leaves the previous service provider. The transfer is treated as a new 'application', please refer to the Application process
If the Residential Support Subsidy application form is received within the current pay period, redirect the clients benefit contribution from:
- the date of entry / admission / authorisation or
- from the first available payday if the current processing deadline has passed
## Client responsibility
The client is responsible for payment of benefit contribution from the date of entry or admission up until such time as the redirection is made to the new service provider.

chunks.title: Death of a client — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
When a client dies, the redirection of the benefit contribution to the service provider should be cancelled from the day after death. In some cases a further 28 days may be paid to the client's estate.
For more information see:
- Death of a client, changes and reviews Main benefits
- Supported Living Payment Terminal benefit rate

chunks.title: Debts — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Debts
A debt is created when a client or service provider is overpaid.
When a client enters and leaves residential care it is important that any changes in benefit payment are completed as soon as possible to avoid any overpayments for the client or the service provider.
## Client moves into care
When a client enters residential care it is important to stop payment of any Extra Help as soon as possible to avoid any overpayment.
When the client requests that their benefit contribution be paid directly to the service provider, the redirection should be added from the first available date.
The client will need to make their own arrangement to meet the cost of their care prior to the commencement of the redirection to the service provider.
## Client moves out of care
Pay the client their full benefit payment from the date they leave care.
Establish a third party debt against the service provider for any portion of benefit contribution paid after the client leaves care.
SWIFTT initially establishes the debt against the client for the service provider, and then transfers it overnight to the Debt Management System. This means that the debt is not held against the client.

chunks.title: Historical information — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Historical information
Residential care for people with age-related disabilities has been the responsibility of the Ministry of Health since 1 July 1993 when Residential Care Subsidy was created.
Residential care services for people with physical, intellectual or psychiatric disabilities (including drug and alcohol rehabilitation) was paid for by Income Support (now Work and Income) through 'maximised benefit'.
The 'maximised benefit' payment was a 'fee for service' payment made up of a number of different types of benefits (main benefit paid at single Invalids Benefit for 18 years and over, Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance and Special Benefit). The 'fee for service' rate was set by Government and varied according to the type and level of disability of the people in care.
This continued until 1 July 1995, when the funding from maximised benefits was transferred to Regional Health Authorities who later became known as Transitional Health Authorities, Health Funding Authorities and are now known as Ministry of Health.
For more information see:
- Residential Support Subsidy

chunks.title: Temporary absence — extra help > residential support subsidy > changes and reviews residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Temporary absence
If the service provider or Ministry of Health advise Work and Income that the client will be absent for a temporary period, continue paying the client's benefit contribution. This can continue for up to 3 weeks while the client is absent.
## Removal of benefit redirection
If the client withdraws their authorisation for benefit redirection Work and Income are obliged to increase their benefit payment as requested by the client, however, every effort should be made to verify this with the service provider.

chunks.title: Client authorisation for benefit redirection — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Client authorisation for benefit redirection
If a client can receive Residential Support Subsidy from the Ministry of Health the client must contribute any benefit they receive (less a Personal Allowance) towards the cost of their care. This is done through a redirection of benefit directly to the service provider.
To do this the client needs to sign the "client authorisation" section of the Residential Support Subsidy application form or complete the Residential Support Subsidy - client authorisation form.
The amount you should redirect to the service provider is the client's main benefit less the Personal Allowance.
## Please note
The granting of a "redirection of benefit" does not give the recipient of the payments any other decision-making powers over the client's affairs, or grant them access to personal information about the client.
For more information about redirecting the clients benefit see:
- Redirection of benefit payment
- Application process
- Payment
- Personal Allowance
- Processing Standards Redirection of benefit payment [no link find out why]
Also see:
- Core policy Agents
- Processing standards Agents [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Client has debts or payees — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Client has debts or payees
When a client is in residential care and getting Residential Support Subsidy any existing client benefit debt recovery and payee links will need to be reviewed.
## Payees
The following payee deductions are required by legislation or court order and should not be stopped:
- Child Support
- Court deductions
- Court fines
- Debt Repayment Orders
- Liable Parent Contributions
- Maintenance
If a client entering residential care has any of these payments to a payee, encourage the client (or their agent) to approach the relevant agency to review the amount they need to pay.
Any payee deductions that are continuing will need to be deducted from the client's Personal Allowance.
For more information see:
- Supported Living Payment Deductions
## Kāinga Ora or community housing provider, and partner in the community
The Housing Processing Hub will identify when a tenant goes into residential care. The Housing Processing Hub will delete the payee and reassess the Income Related Rent rate for the person remaining in the community.
## Existing client benefit debt
Benefit debt, Special Needs Grants, and Advance debt repayments are suspended for the duration of the residential care, unless the client gives their permission to continue recovery from their Personal Allowance. In this case the appropriate MSD Collections is then added as a payee on the client's record. In the event of death, seek recovery from the client's estate.
For more information see:
- Personal Allowance
## Client leaves residential support care
The client's original debt repayment should be resumed when the client moves back into the community and Residential Support Subsidy has been cancelled.

chunks.title: Client has other income — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Client has other income
Any income the client receives may affect their benefit. If the income is in excess of the exemption amount the main benefit will be reduced.
If the client has authorised the redirection of their benefit payment to the service provider, the amount paid to the service provider will be affected when the benefit rate is reduced due to the clients' income. If the income reduces their benefit rate below the benefit contribution amount, then the client will be paid the balance of the benefit payment as Personal Allowance.
The client will need to make their own arrangements with the service provider to pay the balance of their care costs.
For more information see:
- Definition of income
- Changes and reviews, Treatment of income, relevant Main benefit
- Application process

chunks.title: Clients not receiving a main benefit — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Clients not receiving a main benefit
If a client enters residential care and is not receiving a main benefit, the client should be invited to apply for the appropriate main benefit at the nearest Work and Income service centre. Consider eligibility to Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability, Supported Living Payment on the ground of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness or Emergency Benefit.
If all qualifying criteria are met and the benefit is to be granted, the Residential Subsidy Unit in Whangarei must be informed as soon as the benefit has been authenticated. This is to ensure the client receives the correct rate of benefit while in residential care.
If the client does not qualify for a benefit or chooses not to apply for a main benefit they may not have to contribute towards the cost of their care. This is at the discretion of the Ministry of Health.

chunks.title: Disability Allowance — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Disability Allowance
Clients receiving Residential Support Subsidy who have ongoing disability related costs may qualify for Disability Allowance.
Disability Allowance cannot be paid for costs covered by the client's contract with their residential support service provider or through other funding services.
Due to the complexity of assessing Disability Allowance for Residential Support Subsidy clients, all Disability Allowance applications, reviews and inquiries from clients receiving Residential Support Subsidy are managed by the Residential Subsidy Unit.
For more information see:
- Extra help Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Extra help — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Extra help
A client who is in residential care may be able to get Extra help if they have ongoing costs in the community.
Clients in residential care because of physical, intellectual or psychiatric disabilities cannot get:
- the annual Clothing Allowance for Residential Care Subsidy or
- Special Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Increased payment to partner in community — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Increased payment to partner in community
If the client is granted Residential Support Subsidy and has a partner, the partner's rate of payment is increased to the appropriate single rate or the sole parent rate if there are dependent children.
Increase the partner's rate of benefit from the date the client's Residential Support Subsidy is granted.
Likewise, if the partner of the client enters residential care then the primary client is increased to the appropriate single rate or the sole parent rate if there are dependent children.
## SWIFTT
This does not automatically happen in SWIFTT and must be actioned by the Residential Subsidy Unit in Whangarei.
For more information see:
- Application process

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Residential Support Subsidy is the name given to payments made by the Ministry of Health for people with physical, sensory, intellectual, psychiatric disabilities (including drug and alcohol rehabilitation) or disabling chronic health conditions who are receiving residential support services.
Clients with age-related disabilities are not paid Residential Support Subsidy but may be able to receive a Residential Care Subsidy.
Residential Support Subsidy for all of New Zealand is administered by Senior Services - residential care.
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Payment
- Extra Help
- Changes and reviews

chunks.title: Main benefit assistance — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Main benefit assistance
If a client is currently getting a main benefit you will need to check that the client can still meet the qualifications of that benefit while in residential care.
If not, the client may need to transfer to a more appropriate benefit for the duration of residential care, such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or a disability, Supported Living Payment on the grounds of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness, or Emergency Benefit.
Clients applying for or transferring to Jobseeker Support on the grounds of a health condition, injury or a disability will continue to be required to provide an initial medical certificate as proof of their health condition. No further verification is required while the client remains in care.
Clients applying for or transferring to Supported Living Payment on the grounds of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness will continue to be required to provide proof of their health condition. No further verification is required while the client remains in care.
If the client is receiving Sole Parent Support, they may be able to continue to receive their benefit.
For more information see:
- Sole parents
## Extra help
If a client is getting Extra help, it should be stopped from the day the client enters care. Clients may be able to access Extra help only if they have additional ongoing costs in the community.
The Residential Subsidy Unit in Whangarei will ensure any Extra help is reviewed and the appropriate action taken.

chunks.title: Non beneficiaries — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Non beneficiaries
Work and Income does not pay Extra Help payments towards the cost of residential care where the client does not receive a main benefit.
The only payment a non beneficiary may be able to receive is assistance for ongoing costs in the community while residing in residential care.
For more information see:
- Extra Help

chunks.title: Partner enters residential care — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Partner enters residential care
Residential Support Subsidy cannot be linked on a partner's SWIFTT record, except for clients receiving New Zealand Superannuation. When a partner included in a main benefit enters residential care, they are required to apply for a benefit in their own right.
The partner in care will need to complete a full application such as, Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability, Supported Living Payment on the ground of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness or Emergency Benefit, and forward it to their local Work and Income office.
If all qualifying criteria are met, they will then be granted a main benefit in their own right at the half married or civil union rate. The client that is still living in the community should continue to receive their original benefit at the appropriate single rate or the sole parent rate if there are dependent children.
The Residential Subsidy Unit in Whangarei will ensure the partner in care and the client in the community receives the correct rate of benefit.
For more information see:
- Application process

chunks.title: Payment for children's care — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Payment for children's care
Where the children live with the client in the care facility, the client is paid Personal Allowance, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit if qualified. The service provider receives the remainder of the benefit.
If the care is likely to continue for more than 6 months the entitlement to Sole Parent Support would stop. The caregiver may qualify for assistance for the children such as Emergency Benefit, Unsupported Childs Benefit or Working for Families Tax Credits through Inland Revenue.
If the children are cared for by another caregiver in the community, the client is responsible for paying the family tax credit and Best Start tax credit to the temporary caregiver. If the family tax credit and Best Start tax credit does not cover the additional child care costs, then Community Costs may be considered.
If the client is receiving Special Benefit, then this should be reviewed as Community Costs.
For more information see:
- Sole parents
- Extra Help Community Costs
- Extra Help Family tax credit
- Extra Help Best Start tax credit
- Main benefits Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Main benefits Emergency Benefit

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Payment
When a client is in residential care, they are required to contribute any main benefit they receive (less a Personal Allowance) to the service provider towards the cost of their care. This is usually done by redirection of benefit; however the client may choose to make their own arrangements to pay the service provider.
If the client does not qualify for a benefit or chooses not to apply for a main benefit they may not have to contribute towards the cost of their care. This is at the discretion of the Ministry of Health.
For more information see:
- Personal Allowance
- Client authorisation for benefit redirection
- Increased payment to partner in community
- Sole parents
- Client has other income
- Client has debts or payees
- Extra Help
Also see:
- Application process

chunks.title: Personal Allowance — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Personal Allowance
Clients who are receiving Residential Support Subsidy are able to retain a portion of their main benefit for their personal needs. This is called a Personal Allowance.
The Personal Allowance enables the client to purchase items such as shampoo, magazines and postage stamps. It cannot be paid to cover any of the costs of residential care services when a person is receiving Residential Support Subsidy.
For more information see:
- Rates of Personal Allowance
- Payment
- Application process

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
To get Residential Support Subsidy a person must be needs assessed by a contracted needs assessment service as requiring residential support due to:
- physical disability or
- sensory disability or
- intellectual disability or
- psychiatric disability (including drug and alcohol rehabilitation) or
- disabling chronic health condition
Note the residential service provider must be contracted by the Ministry of Health.
Work and Income is responsible for:
- re-directing the client's benefit contribution if authorised by the client and
- paying a Personal Allowance if the person is getting a benefit
There is no asset test for Residential Support Subsidy.

chunks.title: Residential service providers — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Residential service providers
The residential service provider must be contracted to the Ministry of Health to provide residential support services in order to receive a Residential Support Subsidy from the Ministry of Health.
Details of contracted service providers are recorded in SWIFTT to enable redirection of the client's benefit contribution.
If the Ministry of Health have contracted a new service provider, the information must be forwarded to the Data Integrity Unit at National Office who will add the new provider to SWIFTT. Senior Services - residential care must be informed of the new service provider details.
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Application process

chunks.title: Sole parents — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Sole parents
If a client is getting Sole Parent Support and the expected period in residential care is short term the client can continue to get Sole Parent Support.
Before continuing the benefit, check:
- that the client remains financially responsible for their children
- the child or children are only temporarily out of care and will be returning to the care of the client upon their discharge
- how long the client is likely to be in care
- their financial circumstances
- their continuing commitments and
- any childcare arrangements
If the client is getting another benefit, MSD must check whether the client can still meet the qualifications. If not, consider transferring to a more appropriate benefit such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or a disability or Supported Living Payment on the ground of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness.
## Child moves permanently
Where the child moves permanently from the client's care or is taken into the care, custody or sole guardianship of Oranga Tamariki, there is no continued entitlement to Sole Parent Support.
The client will need to apply for another benefit, such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or a disability. The new caregiver may be entitled to assistance for the child such as:
- Unsupported Child's Benefit
- Main benefits Emergency Benefit or
- Extra help Family tax credit

chunks.title: Special Needs Grants — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Special Needs Grants
A client granted Residential Support Subsidy may be able to receive a Special Needs Grant if they meet all of the qualifications.
Before considering a Special Needs Grant, check that the item that they are applying for is not paid by, or the responsibility of, the service provider.
When processing a recoverable Special Needs Grant in SWIFTT, the Residential Support Subsidy must be suspended first to access the appropriate screen in SWIFTT and recommend/approve/decline the Special Needs Grant. You must contact the Residential Subsidy Unit in Whangarei who will do this for you. They will be responsible for resuming the Residential Support Subsidy and redirecting the benefit contribution.
## Please note
When recommending a recoverable Special Needs Grant an offset amount is required to be entered in SWIFTT. This offset amount is then removed by the Residential Subsidy Unit when resuming the Residential Support Subsidy.
The recoverable Special Needs Grant must not be recovered from the client's Personal Allowance unless the client gives their permission. Do not commence recovery of any recoverable Special Needs Grant until the client is released from care, or in the event of death, seek recovery from the client's estate.
If the client gives their permission to recover the Special Needs Grant from their Personal Allowance the appropriate MSD Collections is added as a payee on the client's record.
## Re-establishment grant
If a client has lived in a hospital, hospital unit or residential home continuously as a patient for the preceding six months or more and are resettling themselves in the community independent of a Residential Care facility, they may be able to receive a re-establishment grant.

chunks.title: Standards — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Standards
If the client has been assessed, and the service provider can fully complete the Residential Support Subsidy application form within 24 hours of the client entering care, then this form should be emailed to Work and Income.
The application form should be actioned within 24 hours of receipt. You must advise the Ministry of Health as follows:
Client name
Client number
Service provider
Service providers residential address
Date RSS granted from
Amount of main benefit
Amount of Personal Allowance
Type of main benefit
This means the total turn around time from receipt to notification is 48 hours. This is very important. If the benefit is not granted straight away or Ministry of Health does not receive the notification, then they do not know how much to pay the service provider.

chunks.title: Training Incentive Allowance — extra help > residential support subsidy
chunks.text:
## Training Incentive Allowance
Clients getting Residential Support Subsidy may qualify for Training Incentive Allowance provided they meet all of the qualifications.

chunks.title: Accommodation Supplement — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Accommodation Supplement
If the client chooses to have Accommodation Supplement stopped:
- stop the payment from the date Social Rehabilitation Assistance is to be granted
Any overpayment of Accommodation Supplement must be recovered from arrears of Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
## Partner's accommodation costs
Accommodation Supplement may be paid to the partner in the community who is continuing to meet accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Advance Payment of Benefit — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Advance Payment of Benefit
A client granted Social Rehabilitation Assistance may be able to receive an Advance Payment of Benefit if they meet all of the qualifications.
Before considering an Advance Payment of Benefit, check that the item or services that they are applying for is not paid by or the responsibility of, the social rehabilitation service provider.

chunks.title: Application form incomplete — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Application form incomplete
If there is likely to be any delay in completing the Social Rehabilitation Assistance application form beyond 24 hours or if an incomplete Social Rehabilitation application form is received, register the Social Rehabilitation Assistance and follow-up with the social rehabilitation provider.

chunks.title: Application process — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Application process
Clients must complete the Social Rehabilitation Assistance application form and have the relevant section of the form completed by the social rehabilitation provider.
The social rehabilitation provider must verify that the client is resident in a social rehabilitation programme.
Clients cannot receive Social Rehabilitation Assistance as well as Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance, Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support. Clients must choose to have their Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance, Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support stopped if they are to be granted Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
Once a fully completed application form has been received, Social Rehabilitation Assistance is paid direct to the social rehabilitation provider via the miscellaneous subsidy screen in SWIFTT.
The grant date is either:
- 1 July 2003 or
- the date their main benefit commenced or
- the date the client entered the social rehabilitation programme
whichever is the later.
When a fully completed application for Social Rehabilitation Assistance is received after the client has left the social rehabilitation programme, grant Social Rehabilitation Assistance from the date of entry, to date of exit, and pay arrears directly to the social rehabilitation provider.

chunks.text:

For a list of approved social rehabilitation programmes in your area, see:

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
Clients who will be absent from New Zealand do not qualify for Social Rehabilitation Assistance. Cancel Social Rehabilitation Assistance from the day after departure.
## Note
Different rules apply to the main benefit the client is receiving. Please refer to Changes and reviews: Absence from New Zealand in relevant main benefit.

chunks.title: Agents and re-direction of benefit — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Agents and re-direction of benefit
The client may wish to appoint any individual or organisation as their agent whilst they are resident in an approved social rehabilitation programme. They will indicate this on the 'Appointment of an Agent' section of the Social Rehabilitation Assistance application form.
If the client wishes to have all of their main benefit or any portion of it re-directed to the service provider they need to indicate this on the 'Your Benefit Payment' section of the Social Rehabilitation Assistance application form.
The client does not need to complete a separate Agent or Re-direction form.
For more information see:
- Application process
- Payment

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise the Ministry of Social Development of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
You may also review Social Rehabilitation Assistance at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
For more information see:
- Absence from New Zealand
- Agents and re-direction of benefit
- Client has debts or payees
- Client leaves social rehabilitation programme
- Death of a client
- Hospitalisation
- Overpayment to social rehabilitation provider
- Residential Parole
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Client has debts or payees — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Client has debts or payees
All benefit deductions and other payee deductions are to continue for the duration of the client's social rehabilitation programme.

chunks.title: Client leaves social rehabilitation programme — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Client leaves social rehabilitation programme
Cancel Social Rehabilitation Assistance from the date the client leaves the programme.
Any redirection of benefit authorised by the client to the social rehabilitation provider ceases on the client's exit date unless the client has authorised that the re-direction is to continue.
## Removing the payee link
If the client leaves the social rehabilitation programme part way through the week then you need to adjust the Social Rehabilitation Assistance payee amount to the correct rate for the part payment via the payee screen in SWIFTT.
The payee link can only be deleted from the beginning of a current pay period; therefore you will need to ensure that the payee link is removed at the next change in processing deadline so that the social rehabilitation provider is not overpaid.
Note clients leaving social rehabilitation programmes do not qualify for a re-establishment grant when leaving this type of programme, regardless of the period they were resident with the provider. Re-establishment grants are provided for patients who have been receiving medical treatment. Social Rehabilitation does not provide medical treatment.
For more information see:
- Special Needs Grant Re-establishment grants

chunks.title: Death of a client — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
When a client dies, the Social Rehabilitation Assistance paid directly to the social rehabilitation provider should be cancelled from the day after death.
For more information see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
If the service provider advises that the client has entered hospital, Social Rehabilitation Assistance is to be cancelled from the date of admission.
For more information see:
- Changes and reviews - hospitalisation for relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Overpayment to Social Rehabilitation Provider — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Overpayment to Social Rehabilitation Provider
A debt is created when the social rehabilitation provider is overpaid Social Rehabilitation Assistance. Debts should be recovered from the social rehabilitation provider.
## CMS notes
It is important that clear notes are put on CMS to show how the debt was created and who is responsible.

chunks.title: Residential parole — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance > changes and reviews social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Residential parole
Clients who have been released on residential parole and enter an Habilitation programme do not receive Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
They may be able to receive an Emergency Benefit.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Qualifications
- Application process

chunks.title: Clients not receiving a main benefit — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Clients not receiving a main benefit
If a client enters an approved social rehabilitation programme and is not receiving a main benefit, the client should be invited to apply for the appropriate main benefit at the nearest Work and Income service centre.
If the client does not qualify for a benefit or chooses not to apply for a main benefit they will not qualify for Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
## Clients aged 16 or 17 years old
Clients aged 16 or 17 years old who are resident in an approved social rehabilitation programme may qualify for either Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment.
## No stand-down
No stand-down applies to clients who:
- are required to pay all or part of a benefit towards the cost of their treatment or care in a residential programme

chunks.title: Disability Allowance — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Disability Allowance
If the client chooses to have Disability Allowance stopped. Stop the payment from the date Social Rehabilitation Assistance is to be granted.
Any overpayment of Disability Allowance must be recovered from arrears of Social Rehabilitation Assistance.

chunks.title: Extra help — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Extra help
Clients cannot get Social Rehabilitation Assistance and the following assistance:
- Accommodation Supplement
- Disability Allowance
- Special Benefit and
- Temporary Additional Support
Clients must choose to have this assistance stopped before they can be granted Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
Exception
Winter Energy Payment can continue being paid to clients who are getting Social Rehabilitation Assistance if they are getting a qualifying benefit.

chunks.title: Income test — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Income test
To get Social Rehabilitation Assistance a client must qualify for and be getting an income tested benefit, or meet a special income test if they are getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
The rate of Social Rehabilitation Assistance is not affected by any income the person is getting.
## Asset test
There is no asset test for Social Rehabilitation Assistance.

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Social Rehabilitation Assistance is paid to clients who are resident in an approved residential social rehabilitation programme and the client's benefit is not sufficient to meet the fees charged.
Social Rehabilitation Assistance is paid through miscellaneous subsidy on SWIFTT.
The social rehabilitation provider must verify that the client is resident in an approved social rehabilitation programme. The payment of Social Rehabilitation Assistance must be paid direct to the social rehabilitation provider.
The rate of payment for Social Rehabilitation Assistance differs depending on which area the social rehabilitation programme is running in. The areas are the same as those specified for Accommodation Supplement.

chunks.title: Main benefit — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Main benefit
If a client is currently receiving a main benefit you will need to check that the client can still meet the qualifications of that benefit while resident in an approved social rehabilitation programme.
If not, the client may need to transfer to a more appropriate benefit for the length of their social rehabilitation such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or a disability, or Supported Living Payment.
Clients applying for or transferring to Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or a disability will continue to be required to provide an initial medical certificate as proof of their medical condition.
Clients applying for or transferring to Supported Living Payment on the ground of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness will continue to be required to provide proof of their medical condition.
If the client's main benefit is less than the single Supported Living Payment rate, then you should increase the rate to that level.
## Note
There is a special income test for clients who are receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
## Extra help
Clients cannot receive Social Rehabilitation Assistance as well as Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance, Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support.
Clients must choose to have their Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance, Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support stopped if they are to be granted Social Rehabilitation Assistance.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension income limit — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension income limit
When assessing eligibility for Social Rehabilitation Assistance the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension that the client, or the client's spouse or partner, is receiving is included as income.
The New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension plus their other income must be below the appropriate income limit.

chunks.title: Payment to partner in community — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Payment to partner in community
If the client is granted Social Rehabilitation Assistance and has a partner, the partner's rate of payment is increased to the appropriate single rate or the sole parent rate if there are dependent children.
Increase the partner's rate of benefit from the date the client's Social Rehabilitation Assistance is granted.
If the partner of the client enters residential care then the primary client is increased to the appropriate single rate or the sole parent rate if there are dependent children.
## Note
This does not automatically happen. Please contact Helpline if you have any queries.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Payment
If the client's main benefit is less than the single Supported Living Payment rate, then you should increase the rate to that level.
For the current Social Rehabilitation Assistance rates see:
- Deskfile Social Rehabilitation Assistance payments
Social Rehabilitation Assistance is paid through miscellaneous subsidy (code 835) and select reason for payment code 501 on SWIFTT. The payment must be paid direct to the social rehabilitation provider.
The social rehabilitation provider is added as a payee to the clients' record. A comment must be entered 'in Social Rehab' into the comment field on the miscellaneous subsidy screen and a 'must view' note must be completed in CMS notes in every case.
The 'must view' note should contain the following details:
- date the client entered social rehabilitation
- name of the social rehabilitation provider and
- any other relevant information, such as the client authorising the social rehabilitation provider to act as their agent for the duration of their residence in the programme and
- whether or not the client has authorised the re-direction of any or all of their benefit payment directly to the social rehabilitation providers resident trust account

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
In order to receive Social Rehabilitation Assistance a person must be:
- resident in an approved social rehabilitation programme and
- eligible for and receiving an income tested benefit or
- receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and meet an income test
If the client is not receiving an income tested benefit, New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, they will need to complete a main benefit application and establish entitlement first before they can be considered for Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
## Residential Parole
Clients in Residential Parole do not qualify for Social Rehabilitation Assistance.

chunks.title: Special Benefit — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Special Benefit
Special Benefit should be assessed in the normal manner having regard to the client's income and expenses.
If the rate of Special Benefit is less than the appropriate rate of Social Rehabilitation Assistance discuss with the client whether they wish to withdraw their application for Special Benefit and apply for Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
If Special Benefit is to be paid and the social rehabilitation provider is not agent, discuss with the client the possibility of re-directing to the social rehabilitation provider the equivalent amount of Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
The commencement date for Special Benefit will be either:
- the date of application or
- the date main benefit commenced or
- the date of the qualifying event, that is, date of entry into an approved social rehabilitation programme
whichever is the later.

chunks.title: Special Needs Grants — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Special Needs Grants
A client granted Social Rehabilitation Assistance may be able to receive a Special Needs Grant if they meet all of the qualifications.
Before considering a Special Needs Grant, check that the item or services that they are applying for is not paid by or the responsibility of, the social rehabilitation service provider.

chunks.title: Temporary Additional Support — extra help > social rehabilitation assistance
chunks.text:
## Temporary Additional Support
Temporary Additional Support should be assessed in the normal manner having regard to the client's income and expenses.
If the rate of Temporary Additional Support is less than the appropriate rate of Social Rehabilitation Assistance discuss with the client whether they wish to withdraw their application for Temporary Additional Support and apply for Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
If Temporary Additional Support is to be paid and the social rehabilitation provider is not agent, discuss with the client the possibility of re-directing to the social rehabilitation provider the equivalent amount of Social Rehabilitation Assistance.
The commencement date for Temporary Additional Support will be either:
- the date of application or
- the date main benefit commenced or
- the date of the qualifying event, that is, date of entry into an approved social rehabilitation programme
whichever is the later.

chunks.title: Abated family tax credit — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Abated family tax credit
Non-beneficiary clients and clients receiving a New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, may have their family tax credit abated by Inland Revenue if they earn income in excess of the abatement threshold ($44,900 as at 1 April 2026).
You would only include the actual or estimated amount of family tax credit that is payable at the time the client applies for Special Benefit. Do not include any payments of family tax credit paid in the past.
## Example
If a client has received the full family tax credit entitlement for the tax year (such as in the first 6 months of that year) before applying for Special Benefit, then this cannot be charged as income when assessing Special Benefit.
The amount of family tax credit you include is the actual or estimated amount payable at the time they apply for Special Benefit.

chunks.title: Weekly qualifying accommodation costs — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: From 2 March 2026, a client's allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs must be determined to assess the rate of Special Benefit a client can get. Special Benefit paid prior to 2 March 2026 will be based on previous settings. The weekly qualifying accommodation cost is calculated based on the client's accommodation costs, the part of the property they live in and any accommodation income they get.

chunks.title: Accommodation costs — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: The following are accommodation costs when assessing the allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs for Special Benefit. Rent - rent including Kāinga Ora and community housing provider rental properties - water rates can be included as a rental cost for the assessment of Special Benefit when the rental property has a separate water meter and the tenancy agreement states the tenant is responsible for this cost Board - the amount allowed is 62% of the board paid (excluding arrears) Home ownership costs - mortgage repayments (including Kāinga Ora and Te Puni Kōkiri Ministry of Māori Development mortgage payments) Interest and principal repayments on mortgages to purchase, alter or extend the home - local authority rates If the applicant receives a rebate on any of these items, this must always be deducted - water rates - house insurance premium on the dwelling only is allowed Note that household contents insurance premium is not an allowable accommodation cost as it is covered in the standard cost calculation - mortgage protection or life insurance, when compulsory - essential repairs and maintenance costs to the home - leasehold rental for leasehold land and for Māori land rent - principal and interest repayments on Loans for Major Repairs Advances to Homes - farm residence But not accommodation costs claimed as expenses against the farm business accounts - businesses attached to the home property Accommodation costs that are claimed against the business cannot be included Emergency housing contribution - an emergency housing contribution. Clients staying in emergency accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant pay this contribution towards their accommodation costs. An emergency housing contribution is generally 25% of a client's (and their partner's, if any) net income. However, if their net income is lower than Jobseeker Support, their emergency housing contribution will be 25% of the Jobseeker Support rate that would apply to them Transitional housing contribution - a transitional housing contribution. Clients staying in transitional housing funded by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development pay this contribution towards their accommodation costs. A transitional housing contribution is generally up to 25% of the client's income. Arrears for emergency housing contribution Arrears for emergency housing contribution can be included as an allowable accommodation cost, when the client is repaying the arrears under a payment arrangement agreed to by MSD. The client needs to be meeting the terms of the payment arrangement. Example:

chunks.title: Accommodation costs — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: A client has emergency housing arrears totalling $210. We have agreed with the client that they will repay the arrears at $10 a week and the client is making those repayments. The amount of $10 a week can be included in the client's Special Benefit assessment. Accommodation costs that cannot be included The following accommodation costs cannot be included in Special Benefit: - accommodation costs that are not for the part of the property the client lives in - arrears of accommodation costs that occurred while the client was getting: Accommodation SupplementAccommodation Benefita rent rebateTenure Protection Allowance orSpecial Transfer Allowance - Accommodation Supplement - Accommodation Benefit - a rent rebate - Tenure Protection Allowance or - Special Transfer Allowance

chunks.title: Not part of property they live in — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: When a client doesn’t live in part of their property, that part of the property is deducted from their accommodation costs when calculating the weekly qualifying accommodation costs. This includes when part of the property is: - primarily used for business purposes - self-contained and rented to another person/s or - rented to another person/s who does not reside there For information on how to calculate part of a property see: - Self-employed claiming home office expenses - Homeowner renting out part of their property

chunks.title: Accommodation income — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: When a client gets rent, board or additional occupant contribution payments from someone living in the same premises, it is accommodation income and is deducted from their accommodation costs when calculating the weekly qualifying accommodation costs. Accommodation income includes: - rent a client gets from another person (not being additional occupants or boarders) residing in the same premises, except where the person paying the rent is in a self-contained part of the premises or the rent payment is part of the income of a business on the premises - 62% of payments for board a client gets from another person residing in the same premises, except where the board payment is part of the income of a business on the premises - 62% of contributions a client gets from an additional occupant residing in the same premises Note when accommodation income is more than the client’s accommodation costs (after the deduction of the cost of any part of the property not being lived in by the client), the excess amount is income and must be charged against any financial assistance the client gets. In this case, the client will have no weekly qualifying accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Calculation — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: When calculating the weekly qualifying accommodation costs to assess Special Benefit, the cost of part of the property not lived in must be deducted from the client's accommodation costs before any accommodation income. If a client is getting Accommodation Supplement, the weekly qualifying accommodation costs used to calculate Accommodation Supplement is the same amount to be used to calculate Special Benefit. For example: Franky rents a 3-bedroom house for $850 per week. He uses his home to run a bespoke boat building business with a workshop in the double garage and a bedroom as an office. He calculates the percentage of home space used for his business to determine the business-related costs from using his home. Franky uses 45 percent of the property where he lives (135sqm/300sqm) for his bespoke boat building business and claims the portion of business home expenses of $19,890 per year ($382.50 per week) in his business accounts. Franky's friend, Chopper, also boards with him and pays $400 per week (62% of the board payment is $248 accommodation income). Franky's weekly qualifying accommodation costs for Accommodation Supplement and Special Benefit exclude the portion of his home that he uses to run his business and are then reduced by 62% of the board payments he gets. His weekly qualifying accommodation costs are calculated as $219.50 per week. Cost of part of property not lived in Total rent costs for property Total A $850.00pw Total square metres Total B 300m2 Square metres of property that is used for business purposes Total C 135m2 Proportion of property used for business purposes Total C ÷ Total B = Total D 0.45 Cost of part of property not lived in Total A x Total D $382.50pw Accommodation income Board payment $400.00 Accommodation income (62% of the board payment) $248.00 Weekly qualifying accommodation costs Accommodation costs (rent) $850.00 Less cost of part of property not lived in $382.50 Less accommodation income $248.00 Equals weekly qualifying accommodation costs $219.50

chunks.title: Advice — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Advice
You must ensure that where it is practical, the client is receiving appropriate advice with the objective that wherever possible, the need for Special Benefit is reduced or eliminated within 6 months.
If a client's rate of payment is over $50 per week you should make them a priority.
Where reasonable and practicable clients are expected to make efforts to:
- negotiate reductions in debt and hire purchase payments
- to seek budget advice and/or
- look at alternative ways of meeting their needs
Information on healthy eating on a tight income, energy saving and alternative ways of meeting needs is freely available in the community.
## Budget advice
There are free budget advice services throughout the country.
Budget advisers can help clients negotiate reductions in repayments of debt and hire purchases and look at alternative ways to meet their needs.

chunks.title: Allowable costs — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Allowable costs
Allowable costs for Special Benefit are any regular essential expenses, calculated on a weekly basis and based on the special circumstances of the client.
These are costs that cannot be readily avoided or varied and include (this list is not exhaustive):
- Weekly qualifying accommodation costs
- Childcare costs
- Counselling
- Disability and personal health
- Transport costs due to a disability
- Hire purchase agreements
- Motor vehicles
- Public transport to work
- Telephone rental
- Formula-assessed Child Support costs
There could be costs other than those listed, and because of the client's circumstances should be included as an allowable cost. For help deciding whether a cost should be included in the Special Benefit assessment as an allowable cost, contact Helpline.
## Debt insurance payment
When a client gets a debt insurance payment in relation to a mortgage, health or disability payment, reduce the allowable cost by the amount of the payment.

chunks.title: Allowable costs not in client's name — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Allowable costs not in client's name
Allowable costs that may be included in the assessment of Special Benefit are any regular essential expenses (on a weekly basis) arising out of the special circumstances of the client and family (if any) which cannot be readily avoided or varied.
Generally, costs not in the client or their partner's name are not included in the assessment of Special Benefit as the client or their partner is not liable for the repayments.
There may be situations where a client or their partner has entered an informal arrangement with another person to purchase an essential item using the other person's name and/or credit rating for the hire purchase agreement.
You need to be satisfied that the client or their partner is the person making the payments and that it was the intention of the parties to the informal arrangement that the client or their partner would have responsibility for the payments and would benefit from the use and control of the item.
Note you must also be satisfied that the client is responsible for the cost and has the use of the goods or service is required. The onus is on the client in the first instance to provide any further information required, ask for further information if you are not satisfied.
A full statement from the client or partner and the other party is required along with a copy of the purchase agreement to determine if the cost can be included in the Special Benefit assessment.
Note in these situations the cost must still be essential, not reasonably avoidable and unable to be varied.
To assist in making a decision as to whether the client is responsible for the cost the following should be considered:
- Why are the goods or service in another person's name? You will need to establish why the goods or service is not in the client's name. For example, but not limited to, is the client bankrupt and cannot obtain this essential goods or service item with their current credit rating?
- Is it possible to transfer the goods or service into the client's name?
- Has any other person contributed to the goods or service payments in any way?
If you need assistance deciding whether or not the cost can be included contact Helpline.

chunks.title: Assessing whether a client's individual circumstances justify payment — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Assessing whether a client's individual circumstances justify payment
After calculating a client's financial deficiency (even in cases where no deficiency exists) you must also consider whether the client's individual circumstances justify payment of Special Benefit and if so at what rate.
Consider the following factors:
- does the client have any special or unusual costs compared to others in a similar general position to the client and what is the extent of those costs
- does the client have any special or unusual reasons for any costs that has caused or contributed to the deficiency
- consider the nature of the financial difficulty and the likely duration of the deficiency
- the age and health of the client and any dependants and any special needs arising from that age or health
- the ability of the client to improve their financial situation
- the causes of the client's financial difficulty
- the extent to which the basic necessities of life for the client, partner and any dependants would be at risk if Special Benefit was not granted or paid at another rate
- and any other circumstances of the client's particular situation you consider relevant
You must consider the nature of the expenses and the reasons behind it. Individual factors may not be out of the ordinary on their own but taken together they may justify payment of Special Benefit and/or departing from the formula assessment.
In addition to the above remember to consider the following:
- that the intention of the benefit is to alleviate financial hardship
- that it would normally only be granted if the applicant has a reasonable deficiency of income over expenditure which is likely to continue for some time
- that a Special Benefit should only be considered in respect of costs that are essential and not reasonably avoided
- the ability of the client to meet that deficiency from their own resources and
- the assistance that might be available from other sources to meet the clients need
When you are satisfied that the client's change of circumstances does not justify ongoing payment of Special Benefit, see:
- Suspending Special Benefit
- Cancelling Special Benefit
If you are unsure whether a client's circumstances continue to justify payment of Special Benefit, or at what rate the grant should be made contact Helpline.
For more information see:
- Guidelines
- Students
- Non beneficiaries
- Self-employed clients
- People not able to receive Special Benefit
- Seasonal workers
- Partners overseas
- Social Rehabilitation programmes
- Residential Support Services

chunks.title: Assessment of income deficiency — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Assessment of income deficiency
Assessing a client's eligibility for Special Benefit requires a picture of their financial circumstances and commitments. This tells you whether the client has a deficiency of income over expenses, and if so how large that deficiency is.
The following formula is used to assess deficiency:
Chargeable income
less allowable costs
= disposable income
$_____________
$_____________
$_____________
Standard Costs
Less Disposable Income
= total A
$_____________
$_____________
$_____________
Allowable costs
x 25% (with children)
or
x 30% (without children)
= total B
$_____________
x 0.25
x 0.30
$_____________
The formula rate of Special Benefit is the lower of totals A or B.
For a detailed assessment see:
- Example with dependent children
- Example without dependent children
The deficiency is the weekly shortfall in the client's income. Special Benefit would not normally be granted unless:
- the deficiency of income over expenses and commitments is reasonably substantial
- the deficiency is likely to continue for a period which justifies Special Benefit being granted
- the costs taken into consideration are essential and not reasonably avoidable
- the client cannot meet the deficiency from their own or other resources
- payment is otherwise justified in relation to the clients individual circumstances
However, every case must be considered individually including consideration of the client's expenses and any other surrounding circumstances. Even when there is minimal or no deficiency of income and/or the expense is not continuing for a reasonable period; consideration must be given to whether the payment of Special Benefit may be justified in the client's particular circumstances.
For more information see:
- Assessing whether a client's individual circumstances justify payment
You must also consider the client's individual circumstances to decide whether or not the rate of assessment justifies being increased or decreased. For more information see:
- Deciding what rate to pay

chunks.title: Cash assets include — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Cash assets include
- bills of exchange or promissory notes
- building society shares
- money in bank accounts, including fixed and term deposits with any bank, friendly society, credit union, or building society
- money invested with or lent to any bank, financial institution or other person
- mortgage investments and other long term loans
- pre-paid funeral expenses (in some circumstances)
- shares, stocks, debentures, bonus bonds, and other bonds
- the client's share in any partnership and
- the net equity held in any property or land not used as the person's home
## Cash assets do not include
- a caravan, boat or other vehicle with a net equity less than $2000 or which is used by the client or a member of their family for day to day accommodation
- a home property and land on which it is situated
- a motor vehicle principally used by the client for private use
- Christchurch mosques attack support payments
- Crown funds provided directly to clients to purchase Support Services and Direct Disability Support payments
- funds locked into KiwiSaver and other retirement scheme account contributions
- income earned on Payments of arrears to Special Benefit clients better off on Temporary Additional Support for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Information share Child Support payments currently being charged as income
- MSD lump sum payments for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- personal effects of the person and their partner
