- Payments of Accommodation Supplement arrears due to system processing error from 1993 to 2014 for the first 12 months after payment is made
- Payments to clients whose Kāinga Ora tenancy was terminated due to methamphetamine contamination for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Residential Care Subsidy historic review refunds for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Severe weather event payments for the first 12 months from when payment is received (and any interest earned on the payment)
- specified Ex gratia and Compensation payments
- FamilyBoost Tax Credit payments for the first 12 months after payment is received
A bank overdraft facility is not considered a cash asset or resource available to a client.
Canterbury earthquake related payments
Payments made by the Crown, Earthquake Commission, insurance companies or the Canterbury Earthquake Commission (Red Cross) relating to the Canterbury earthquake are generally excluded for the first 12 or 24 months following the date the client received the payment.

chunks.title: Cash assets test — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Cash assets test
A client will not normally be able to receive a Special Benefit if they (and their partner if any) have cash assets equal to or more than:
Single person Asset limit for a single person without dependent children Married, civil union or de facto couple orsole parent Asset limit for a married, civil union or de facto couple with or without dependent children
Single person
Asset limit for a single person without dependent children
Married, civil union or de facto couple orsole parent
Asset limit for a married, civil union or de facto couple with or without dependent children
Note the sole parent asset limit is the same as the married, civil union or de facto.
If the client has cash assets but they are less than the maximum, you should still consider whether the client could be expected to meet the costs they face from these cash assets. (Note where the client has committed some of these assets to a reasonable and essential expense then this amount does not form part of their cash assets.) There is no ability to adjust the cash assets test. However, the outcome of the cash assets calculation may be disregarded in the exercise of your discretion if the particular circumstances of the applicant justify granting Special Benefit.
For more information see:
- Cash assets

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
When a client receiving Special Benefit intends to be absent from New Zealand you will need to determine if payment of Special Benefit can continue.
You will need to decide each case on its own merits taking all of the client's circumstances into account.
In no circumstances should payment continue beyond 28 days.
## Permanent Absence
If the client is leaving New Zealand permanently, Special Benefit should be cancelled from the day after departure.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Special Benefit, it is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. A reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event MSD should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising MSD of a change in circumstances within 14 days, MSD may reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the first available date.
## False or misleading information
If the client gives false or misleading information, MSD must review Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Avoiding a debt — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Avoiding a debt
When a non-beneficiary client dies, Special Benefit generally stops from the day after the date of death. You must take all possible steps to stop payments from this date.
When payment cannot be stopped from the day after the date of death, there is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days after the date of death. You can use this discretion to stop payment from the first available date, that is, the earliest date that you can stop payments from so that no overpayment is established.
However, when there has been a deliberate intent to delay advising the Ministry of Social Development of the client's death you should stop payment from the day after the date of death and establish an overpayment.
Note under no circumstances can payment continue for more than 28 days after the date of death.
For more information see:
- Terminal benefit

chunks.title: Cancelling Special Benefit — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Cancelling Special Benefit
Special Benefit should be cancelled when the client:
- chooses to cancel Special Benefit or
- no longer qualifies to receive Special Benefit
## Client chooses to cancel Special Benefit
A client can choose to cancel Special Benefit at any point. However, if a client chooses to cancel their Special Benefit, they cannot be granted Special Benefit at a later date. The only exception to this is when the client applies for ongoing hardship assistance within 26 weeks of the cancellation and has not been granted Temporary Additional Support.
Choosing to cancel Special Benefit is not considered deprivation of income and does not mean that the client has arranged their circumstances to qualify for other ongoing assistance.
## Client no longer qualifies to receive Special Benefit
When a client has a change in circumstances, which is expected to last more than 26 weeks, and their situation does not justify ongoing payments of Special Benefit, you should cancel their Special Benefit payments from the date the client no longer qualifies.
When a client has a change of circumstances that means their situation does not justify ongoing payments of Special Benefit for a temporary period, you should suspend the Special Benefit from the beginning of the temporary period.
For more information see:
## Entitlement to Temporary Additional Support
When you cancel Special Benefit for any reason, you must assess whether the client is entitled to Temporary Additional Support.
The client cannot receive both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support for the same period. However, if Special Benefit has been cancelled and the qualifications for Temporary Additional Support are met, the client may then be granted Temporary Additional Support.
Note clients whose Special Benefit has been cancelled cannot have it reinstated if they choose to receive Temporary Additional Support after that cancellation.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Change in accommodation — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Change in accommodation
MSD will need to review Special Benefit to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's accommodation. This includes when there is a change in the client's accommodation costs and/or a change to the part of the property they live in. MSD will need to update and reassess the client's allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs.
MSD will also need to check whether the client's other allowable costs have changed.
Note MSD must review the client's Accommodation Supplement before reviewing their Special Benefit.
The date to review Special Benefit from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:
Increase
- increase Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances
Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
When MSD is satisfied that the client's change of circumstances does not justify ongoing payment of Special Benefit, see:
- Suspending Special Benefit
- Cancelling Special Benefit
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information MSD must review Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Change in accommodation income — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Change in accommodation income
Clients must tell MSD when they start getting accommodation income or there is a change in accommodation income they get from renters, boarders or additional occupants so the correct rate of Special Benefit can be paid.
When there is a change in accommodation income that a client gets, review their Special Benefit to make sure they still meet the qualifications and are getting the correct rate of payment.
The date to review Special Benefit from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:
Increase
- increase Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances
Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
When MSD is satisfied that the client's change of circumstances does not justify ongoing payment of Special Benefit, see:
- Suspending Special Benefit
- Cancelling Special Benefit
## Mismatch of information
When the renter, boarder or additional occupant also gets Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, MSD will check the details match what information is held. Where there is a mismatch of information, the mismatch process must be followed.
For more information see:
- Mismatch of accommodation income and accommodation costs
- Weekly qualifying accommodation costs
- Change in income
- Rent and board payments
- Additional occupant contributions

chunks.title: Change in assets — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Change in assets
You will need to review Special Benefit to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's cash assets.
The date to review Special Benefit from will depend on the action involved. Generally, you should:
## Increase
- increase Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances
## Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
When you are satisfied that the client's change of circumstances does not justify ongoing payment of Special Benefit, see:
- Suspending Special Benefit
- Cancelling Special Benefit
## Income
Income is charged against the Special Benefit for the week(s) in which the income is earned or represents.
For more information see:
- Change in income
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information, you must review Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Change in costs — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Change in costs
You will need to review Special Benefit to ensure the client is getting the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's costs such as when the client has applied for new costs to be included in their assessment.
For more information see:
- Allowable costs
The date to review Special Benefit from will depend on the action involved. Generally, you should:
## Increase
- increase Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances
Note there are transitional arrangements when including formula-assessed Child Support costs for current Special Benefit clients in the period 1 July 2023 to 29 September 2023.
For more information see:
- Formula-assessed Child Support costs
## Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
Note when a client has a decrease in formula-assessed Child Support costs, this is treated differently. Clients generally must tell MSD of a change within 14 days of the date Inland Revenue notifies the client of the outcome of their reassessment. This is likely to be a different date than the date their costs changed.
When you are satisfied that the client's change of circumstances does not justify ongoing payment of Special Benefit, see:
- Suspending Special Benefit
- Cancelling Special Benefit
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information you must review Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment when appropriate.

chunks.title: Change in family circumstances — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Change in family circumstances
MSD should review Special Benefit to check that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the clients:
- relationship status or
- the number of dependent children in the client's care
The date to review Special Benefit from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:
## Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
When MSD is satisfied that the client's change of circumstances does not justify ongoing payment of Special Benefit, see:
- Suspending Special Benefit
- Cancelling Special Benefit
## Care and protection concerns
When a child has come into a client’s care, MSD should consider if there are any care and protection concerns.
If MSD believes any child has been, or is likely to be harmed (physically, emotionally or sexually), ill-treated, abused, neglected, deprived or MSD has concerns about the wellbeing of the child, the case must be referred to Oranga Tamariki.
MSD staff must notify Oranga Tamariki if they are aware that the child's sole caregiver has been remanded in custody and/or sentenced to a term of imprisonment.
## Child turns 18
A child must generally be under the age of 18 to be considered a dependent child and to be included in their parent or caregiver's Special Benefit.
The parent or caregiver must also complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for their discretionary benefit such as Special Benefit, and the rate payable.

chunks.title: Change in income — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Change in income
MSD will need to review Special Benefit to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's income.
Income for non-beneficiaries must be charged against Special Benefit for the week(s) in which the income is earned or represents.
If income does not represent a specific period or if MSD cannot determine the actual period it represents, MSD must determine the most appropriate period to charge the income. This may be the week it is received, provided or supplied.
## Variable income
When a client has variable income, (for example wages) the income is charged for the week in which the income was earned.
If the client is unsure of the exact amount of income they will earn, they should provide an estimate of their income. This will help to reduce any debt being established for the client.
If a client's actual income differs from the estimate given, they must inform the Ministry of Social Development of the correct amount and their rate of benefit will need to be reviewed.
The correct amount of income should still be charged for the week in which the income was earned.
For more information see:
- Chargeable income
- Change in assets

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Special Benefit.
MSD may also review Special Benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
For more information see:
- Absence from New Zealand
- Core policy Agents
- Cancelling Special Benefit
- Change in accommodation
- Change in accommodation income
- Change in assets
- Change in costs
- Change in family circumstances
- Change in income
- Client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
- Client in new relationship
- Client's relationship ends
- Death of a client
- Hospitalisation
- Imprisonment
- Mismatch of accommodation income and accommodation costs
- Core policy Redirection of benefit payment
- Core policy Relationship status for benefit
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals
- Reviews 3 and 6 monthly
- Study
- Suspending Special Benefit
- Transfer

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Special Benefit.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Special Benefit from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday. The parent or caregiver must also complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for their discretionary benefit such as Special Benefit, and the rate payable.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Special Benefit for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier
Note a parent or caregiver getting Special Benefit must complete a review of circumstances when a dependent child turns 18, and when the child is excluded (if they continued to be included in the parent or caregiver's benefit after the child turned 18). If the parent or caregiver does not complete the review, their Special Benefit will be suspended.

chunks.title: Client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Special Benefit, it is expected they will do so within a reasonable period.
As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days of the date their costs change.
For clients who have a change in formula-assessed Child Support costs, they generally must notify MSD within 14 days of the date Inland Revenue notifies them of the change. This is likely to be a different date from the date their costs changed.
## Good and sufficient reason
When there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising MSD of a change in circumstances within 14 days, you may reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the first available date.
## No good and sufficient reason
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event and does not have a good and sufficient reason, you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances, and establish an overpayment if appropriate.
If a client advises MSD of a decrease in their formula-assessed Child Support costs more than 14 days after the date Inland Revenue notifies them of the change, without a good and sufficient reason for the delay, you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Special Benefit from the date the client was notified of the change. You may need to establish an overpayment if appropriate.
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information you must review Special Benefit from the actual date of the change in circumstances, and establish an overpayment if appropriate.
## Income change advised more than 14 days after the event
Income must be charged against the Special Benefit for the week(s) in which the income is earned or represents.
Note the rules for charging income are different for Information share Child Support payments.

chunks.title: Surviving partner or dependent child — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Surviving partner or dependent child
When a client dies (and there is a surviving partner or dependent child) before a decision is made on an application or review for Special Benefit, you can continue the application or review process as if the client had not died.

chunks.title: Client in new relationship — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: When a client enters into a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship, you will have to determine if the client and their spouse or partner qualify for Temporary Additional Support or Special Benefit. As soon as a client enters into a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship they no longer have entitlement to a single or sole parent rate of benefit. When a client enters into a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship, you will need to determine if the client and their spouse or partner are eligible for Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Clients receiving Special Benefit — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: If either person in a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship was receiving a Special Benefit immediately before they entered into the marriage, civil union or de facto relationship they can: - continue to receive Special Benefit if they continue to qualify or - choose to receive Temporary Additional Support if the couple qualify If the client chooses to continue to receive Special Benefit, you will have to re-assess the rate of Special Benefit based on the couple's circumstances. Note one partner in a current marriage, civil union or de facto relationship cannot choose to receive Temporary Additional Support if the other partner continues to receive Special Benefit. If neither person in a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship is still eligible for a Special Benefit, they should be assessed for Temporary Additional Support as a couple.

chunks.title: Clients receiving Temporary Additional Support — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: If a person in a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship was receiving Temporary Additional Support and their spouse or partner was not receiving Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support immediately before they entered into the marriage, civil union or de facto relationship, they should both be assessed for Temporary Additional Support. If a person in a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship was receiving Temporary Additional Support and their partner was receiving Temporary Additional Support immediately before they entered into the marriage, civil union or de facto relationship, they should both be assessed for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Type of payment to be considered — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: The following table summarises which type of payment you should consider when a client enters into a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship. Type of payment received by client before relationship Type of payment received by partner before relationship Married, civil union or de facto couple may qualify for: Special Benefit Special Benefit Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Special Benefit Temporary Additional Support Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support Special Benefit Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Special Benefit Not receiving Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Not receiving Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Special Benefit Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support Not receiving Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support Not receiving Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support Not receiving Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Not receiving Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support Temporary Additional Support

chunks.title: Example — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: John is a non-beneficiary client who is currently receiving Temporary Additional Support. John enters into a marriage with Susan who receives a main benefit and a Special Benefit. As Susan can continue to receive a Special Benefit, the couple is assessed to see if they qualify for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support. As the couple is eligible for both, but will receive more assistance on Special Benefit, they choose to have Special Benefit continue at the newly assessed rate.

chunks.title: Client's relationship ends — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Client's relationship ends
When a client's marriage, civil union or de facto relationship ends, you will have to determine if the client and their spouse or partner qualify separately for Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support.
If Special Benefit had been paid to the couple, each person's eligibility should be assessed for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support based on that person's circumstances when the relationship ends.
If Temporary Additional Support had been paid to the couple, each person's eligibility should be assessed for Temporary Additional Support based on that person's circumstances when the relationship ends. If the eligibility criteria are met for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support, each person can choose to receive one or the other form of assistance, but not both.
Note if a person chooses to cancel Special Benefit and receive Temporary Additional Support, they cannot be granted Special Benefit at a later date.
## Type of payment to be considered
The following table summarises which type of payment you should consider when a client's marriage, civil union or de facto relationship ends.
Married, civil union or de facto couple
Assess client's eligibility for:
Assess partner's eligibility for:
Special Benefit
Special Benefit
Temporary Additional Support
Special Benefit
Temporary Additional Support
Temporary Additional Support
Temporary Additional Support
Temporary Additional Support
## Example 1
Tane and Maria are in a relationship and together have been receiving a main benefit and Special Benefit as a couple since 2002. In 2018 the relationship ends and each receives a main benefit at the single rate.
Tane is assessed based on his new circumstances and he qualifies for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support. Tane chooses to receive Special Benefit as it is the most appropriate for his circumstances.
After the relationship, Maria also qualifies for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support. Maria chooses to receive Temporary Additional Support as she will receive a higher rate of assistance.
## Example 2
In 2008, Kate and Billy are married. Kate, previously a non-beneficiary, is included in Billy’s main benefit and Special Benefit. In 2018, Kate and Billy end their relationship.
Billy qualifies for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support. He chooses to continue to receive Special Benefit at the newly assessed rate.
Kate is not eligible for Special Benefit as she was not receiving, or had not applied for, Special Benefit immediately before 1 April 2006. She also does not qualify for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Clients receiving a main benefit — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving a main benefit
Special Benefit can continue to be paid to the client for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital.
When the client's benefit is reduced to the hospital rate, their Special Benefit will need to be stopped.
## Single clients and sole parents
Special Benefit must be stopped from beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation.
You will need to check if the client still has to meet their continuing costs. If so, increase the hospital rate to meet the costs.
## Married, civil union or de facto couples (without dependent children)
Special Benefit must be stopped from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation for the client who is in hospital. From the same date you will need to review Special Benefit and pay the full amount to the partner not in hospital.
Generally, no additional costs associated with the hospitalisation should be added to the Special Benefit. However, you would need to consider their individual circumstances.
The partner not in hospital is increased to the single rate of payment and can receive Special Disability Allowance to cover any extra costs.
For more information see:
- Hospitalisation in the relevant main benefit

chunks.title: Getting a main benefit — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Getting a main benefit
When a client is getting a main benefit, Special Benefit stops from the same date as the main benefit.
For more information see:
- Death of a client in the relevant main benefit
## Non-beneficiaries
For non-beneficiary clients Special Benefit generally stops from the day after the date of death. However, there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the date of death:
- to avoid creating a debt or
- as terminal benefit when there are other circumstances that justify payment
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Special Benefit when the child turns 18 during the terminal benefit period.
The review of circumstances for a discretionary benefit such as Special Benefit when their child turns 18 is not required when the client has died.

chunks.title: Death of a dependent child — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Death of a dependent child
When a dependent child dies you will need to review the Special Benefit to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.

chunks.title: Death of a married, civil union or de facto client — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Death of a married, civil union or de facto client
When a client with a partner dies you will need to review the surviving partner's Special Benefit to ensure they still meet the qualifications and are receiving the correct rate of payment.
The Special Benefit should be reviewed from the day following death.

chunks.title: Debt recovery — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Debt recovery
When a client has arrears owing to them at the time of their death and they have an outstanding debt balance, you should attempt to recover the debt, in full, from the final payment.
When a client has an outstanding debt balance and terminal benefit is payable, you should not recover the debt in full, from the terminal benefit payment.

chunks.title: Application received after 8 weeks of cancellation, but within 26 weeks — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Application received after 8 weeks of cancellation, but within 26 weeks
When a client next applies for ongoing hardship assistance after 8 weeks but within 26 weeks of their Special Benefit being cancelled, you must check the previous cancellation to determine if, at that time, the decision to cancel Special Benefit was correct and the process that was followed.
Clients whose Special Benefit has been cancelled and who have subsequently been granted Temporary Additional Support cannot have Special Benefit reinstated if they apply for ongoing hardship assistance.
For more information about the Special Benefit cancellation guidelines see:
- Cancelling Special Benefit
When you are satisfied that the client's Special Benefit should not have been cancelled at that time and they have not been granted Temporary Additional Support, you should:
- reinstate their Special Benefit if they qualify
- review the period from the date of cancellation to the date Special Benefit is reinstated
When you are satisfied that the client's Special Benefit should have been cancelled at that time, you should invite them to apply for Temporary Additional Support.
For more information see:
- Suspending Special Benefit
## Application received after 26 weeks of cancellation
Where a client next applies for ongoing hardship assistance after 26 weeks from the date their Special Benefit was cancelled, they should generally apply for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Client does not receive Temporary Additional Support — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Client does not receive Temporary Additional Support
Where Special Benefit has been cancelled (regardless of the reason) and the client applies for ongoing hardship assistance up to 8 weeks from that cancellation, you must determine if the client is entitled to and would receive more assistance from Temporary Additional Support.
- If the client is not entitled to Temporary Additional Support, or is entitled to Temporary Additional Support but would receive more assistance from Special BenefitSpecial Benefit should be reinstated if their circumstances at the time of their application mean they still qualify.
- If a client is entitled to receive more assistance from Temporary Additional Support The client should be given the opportunity to choose to receive Temporary Additional Support or have Special Benefit reinstated if their circumstances at the time of their application mean they still qualify. The payment that is most appropriate will depend on the client’s individual circumstances and may vary as the client’s circumstances change.
Note only the Data Integrity Unit can approve the Special Benefit grant in SWIFTT.
## Client already receives Temporary Additional Support
Clients whose Special Benefit has been cancelled and who have subsequently been granted Temporary Additional Support cannot have Special Benefit reinstated if they apply for ongoing hardship assistance up to 8 weeks from the cancellation of their Special Benefit.
For more information see:
- Special Benefit Qualifications

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a client receiving Special Benefit is admitted to hospital payment can continue at the existing rate for the first 13 weeks if their costs are continuing.
From the start of 14th week of hospitalisation the Special Benefit will need to be reviewed.
The date of admission and the date of discharge are not included in the 13-week calculation.
Note married, civil union or de facto couples with a dependent child do not have their Special Benefit reduced regardless of how long they are in hospital. You will need to check if their costs have changed.
For more information see:
- Clients receiving a main benefit
- Non-beneficiaries

chunks.title: Imprisonment — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
Special Benefit is generally not paid when a client is in prison. Special Benefit should stop from the day following the date of imprisonment.
However, clients on home detention may qualify. For more information see "Home Detention" in the appropriate main benefit manual.
In some circumstances Special Benefit can continue when, a:
- married, civil union or de facto client, or a single client with dependent children, is imprisoned or
- client is on remand
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances of the client before making a decision.

chunks.title: Mismatch of accommodation income and accommodation costs — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: Clients must tell MSD when: - they start getting rent, board or contributions from additional occupants or - there is a change in the rent, board or contribution amount they get, or - their accommodation costs change

chunks.title: When clients can be matched — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: When a client declares the rent, board or additional occupant contributions they get, or the accommodation costs they pay, MSD will check the details match between two clients when: - a head tenant or homeowner client and their renter or boarder client both get Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, or - a social housing tenant who pays Income Related Rent gets contributions from a client who lives with them and that client gets Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit

chunks.title: Step one - Mismatch identified — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: A mismatch of information will be identified when a client's accommodation type or amount differs from what a client who is a head tenant or homeowner has declared they are getting, or a renter or boarder has declared they are paying. MSD must try to contact both clients within one working day of identifying the mismatch to check and confirm the correct details. If one or both clients are uncontactable within one working day, but a message is left for the client/s to make contact, MSD must consider whether it is reasonable to allow the one working day to lapse before moving to the next step in the process. When one or both clients have been contacted, and it is clear the mismatch cannot be resolved within one working day, or one or both clients are uncontactable and a message cannot be left, MSD can continue to the next step in the process. Note the one working day ends on the close of the working day following the day the mismatch is identified. Example: Englebert lives with Alphonse, and they both get Accommodation Supplement and Alphonse also gets Special Benefit. On Wednesday 6 May, Englebert pays his rent to Alphonse who owns the property. Englebert advises MSD his rent will be increasing from $350 per week to $360 per week from next Monday. Alphonse has not yet advised MSD of this change. On Thursday 7 May (within one working day of identifying the payment amount mismatch), MSD contacts Englebert to confirm he intended to declare a change in his rent amount. Alphonse contacts MSD later that day to advise that Englebert's rent will be increasing to $360 from next Monday. MSD updates both clients'; payments from next Monday and the mismatch has been resolved.

chunks.title: Step three - Response to the notification of mismatch — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: Contact from client/s and mismatch resolved within 10 working days When the client/s make contact and confirm the correct details within 10 working days, the details should be updated and any assistance reviewed accordingly. This means the mismatch is now resolved. No contact from client/s When one or both clients don't make contact within 10 working days to confirm their rent, board or additional occupant contribution payment information, the mismatch is unable to be resolved, and both clients Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit must be suspended. If the client is a social housing tenant and the mismatch is not resolved, MSD will notify the housing provider that the client's Income Related Rent must be set to market rent for the property. Community Housing Providers have a discretion not to set the client's rent to the market rent rate. The standard 60-day notice period will apply. Example: Astrid and Rex live together, and Rex pays board to Astrid. They both get Accommodation Supplement and Special Benefit as non-beneficiaries. Astrid receives a mandatory review for her Accommodation Supplement and Special Benefit. On Tuesday 9 June, she responds before her review due date confirming that she receives $10 more in board from Rex. The new amount is different from what MSD holds for Rex. MSD checks with Astrid on Wednesday 10 June (within one working day of identifying the mismatch) to see if she advised of the increase in error. She confirms the increase is correct. On Wednesday 10 June, MSD tries contacting Rex to confirm the new rate, but he doesn't respond. On Thursday 11 June (after the one working day has lapsed), MSD sends both Astrid and Rex notification of the mismatch and provides 10 working days to resolve it and advise MSD. Rex does not respond to the request for information by close of day Tuesday 23 June (within 10 working days). MSD suspends Rex's Accommodation Supplement and Special Benefit from Wednesday 24 June (11th working day). Astrid's Accommodation Supplement and Special Benefit is also suspended from Wednesday 24 June as MSD cannot verify the information she has declared is correct. If Rex does not respond within 8 weeks, both Astrid and Rex's Accommodation Supplement and Special Benefit will be cancelled.

chunks.title: Disputes — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text: If both clients can't reach an agreement or provide the requested evidence within 10 working days from being notified of the mismatch, both clients' Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit must be suspended. If the client is a social housing tenant and they can't reach an agreement or provide the requested evidence within 10 working days from being notified of the mismatch, MSD will notify the housing provider that the client's Income Related Rent must be set to market rent for the property. Community Housing Providers have a discretion not to set the client's rent to the market rent rate. The standard 60-day notice period will apply. If both clients agree and/or provide evidence confirming the correct rent, board or additional occupant contribution payment information while the assistance is suspended or Income Related Rent is at the market rent rate, the details should be updated and any assistance resumed and reviewed accordingly. For more information see: - Change in accommodation income - Change in accommodation If the mismatch has not been resolved within 8 weeks of being suspended, the Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit will be cancelled. In this case, clients can reapply for the Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, however if both clients apply and the same mismatch of information is identified, the disputes process will start again.

chunks.title: Non-beneficiary clients — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Non-beneficiary clients
Special Benefit can continue to be paid to the client for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital.
From the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation the Special Benefit will need to be reviewed.
## Single clients and sole parents
If client still has to meet their continuing costs Special Benefit can continue at the existing rate.
You will need to check how the client is supporting themselves. The client may qualify for a benefit if their income has reduced.
## Married, civil union or de facto couples (without dependent children)
Special Benefit must be stopped from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation for the client who is in hospital. From the same date you will need to review Special Benefit and pay the full amount to the partner not in hospital.
Generally no additional costs associated with the hospitalisation should be added to the Special Benefit however you would need to have regard to their individual circumstances.
You will need to check if the client's income has changed because of being in hospital. The client may qualify for a benefit if their income has reduced.

chunks.title: Reviews - 3 and 6 month — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Reviews - 3 and 6 month
Special Benefit is reviewed at 3 months following its grant, at 6 months from grant, and then at 6 monthly intervals (that is every 26 weeks).
The intent of the 3 and 6 month reviews of Special Benefit is to:
- check continuing eligibility for Special Benefit
- determine if the client would receive more assistance from Temporary Additional Support, discuss the implications of any potential change in assistance and allow the client to determine which assistance is most appropriate for their circumstances
- discuss steps taken to reduce expenditure and live within their normal income
- complete a DREW assessment to review any circumstances that have taken place or changed that might increase or decrease the need for Special Benefit
- discuss and document in DREW any further steps that could/should be taken
- discuss and document in DREW any advice given to the client as to possible consequences, if no particular action is taken in regard to further steps the client should take
If possible, work on an action plan to reduce the need for Special Benefit before the next review.
If appropriate steps discussed previously with the client have not been undertaken, discuss the reasons for this. This may be taken into account when considering whether payment continues to be justified or the rate of payment remains the same (but is not the only factor)
Where you determine that payment is no longer warranted or the rate of payment should be varied:
- fully document decisions in DREW (including reasons and factors considered)
- inform client and give review and appeal rights
- consider giving the client a lead in time before cancelling Special Benefit in order for them to adjust
When you are satisfied that the client's change of circumstances does not justify ongoing payment of Special Benefit, see:
- Suspending Special Benefit
- Cancelling Special Benefit
For more information see:
- Special Benefit procedures [no link find out why]
- Special Benefit error [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Study — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Study
If a client commences study as a full-time student Special Benefit will need to be reviewed as there are additional criteria for full-time tertiary students.
For more information see:
- Students

chunks.title: Suspending Special Benefit — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Suspending Special Benefit
When a client has a temporary change of circumstances, and their situation does not justify ongoing payments of Special Benefit during the temporary period, you must:
- suspend the client's Special Benefit from the beginning of the temporary period using the appropriate reason code
- fully note CMS, clearly stating that the client has had a temporary change of circumstances, that the client's situation does not justify ongoing payments during this period, and why you made this decision
- send the LSUM letter in SWIFTT
You would complete this process where you are suspending a current Special Benefit.
Note where the client has a change of circumstances that is expected to last more than 26 weeks and that does not justify ongoing payments of Special Benefit, you should cancel their Special Benefit.
## Client is entitled to Temporary Additional Support
If a client is entitled to Temporary Additional Support, you must discuss the implications of any potential change in assistance and give the client the opportunity to choose to receive Temporary Additional Support or Special Benefit.
Note clients whose Special Benefit has been suspended cannot have it restarted if they choose to receive Temporary Additional Support after the suspension.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Terminal benefit — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit
When a non-beneficiary client dies, Special Benefit generally stops from the day after the date of death. However, there is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days. When payment is continued after the date of death, it is referred to as terminal benefit.
Circumstances where MSD might consider continued payment beyond a client's date of death include:
- when the deceased client's domestic situation results in a transition cost for a family member, causing hardship Example accommodation and other household costs when client has been sharing accommodation.
Example accommodation and other household costs when client has been sharing accommodation.
or
- when there are exceptional and justified costs associated with the death of the client Example multiple deaths within 1 family.
Example multiple deaths within 1 family.
MSD should not continue payment for 28 days following the death of a client to meet funeral expenses. A Funeral Grant may be available for this purpose.
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Special Benefit when the child turns 18 during the 28-day continuation of payment period.
The review of circumstances for a discretionary benefit such as Special Benefit when their child turns 18 is not required when the client has died.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit rate — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit rate
The provision to continue the payment for up to 28 days following the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit.
Special Benefit is continued at the rate which was payable to the client at the date of death.
## SWIFTT
If you are paying terminal benefit you will need to manually calculate entitlement and make an adhoc payment in the SAHPA screen.
There is no automatic provision for the payment of terminal benefit for Special Benefit in this case on SWIFTT.

chunks.title: Transfer — extra help > special benefit > changes and reviews special benefit
chunks.text:
## Transfer
When a client receiving Special Benefit:
- transfers between benefit types or
- moves between main benefit and non-beneficiary categories
they do not have to complete a new Special Benefit application form.
You will need to review the Special Benefit to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
For more information see:
- Processing standards Transfers [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Chargeable income — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Chargeable income
Chargeable income is any income or earnings (after tax and/or ACC levies) received by the client or partner, before any deductions or attachment orders on account of debt, liability, sanction, penalty, child support payments or student loan repayments.
Chargeable income includes but is not limited to:
- wages or salary
- Accommodation Benefit paid to students
- Accommodation Supplement
- any net benefit received (except Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit or Childcare Assistance)
- any other income charged against the benefit rate
- any regular periodical payments made under any Welfare Programme (including payments made under the Telephone Costs Payment Programme, the New Employment Transition Grant Programme, or the Seasonal Work Assistance Programme)
- Blind subsidies
- Child Disability Allowance
- Disability Allowance (including the amount of Special Disability Allowance and any Disability Allowance paid for children getting an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit)
- Child Support received directly by the client
- COVID-19 Income Relief Payment
- Independent Circumstances Allowance
- Family tax credit
- Best Start tax credit
- Flexi-Wage Self Employment weekly subsidy (excluding the GST component of 15%) and any income generated from the business
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension
- paid parental leave
- Rent and 62% of board payments a client gets in excess of their accommodation costs (after the deduction of the cost of any part of the property not being lived in by the client)
- 62% of additional occupant contributions a client gets in excess of their market rent
- Student Allowance
- the living costs component of any Student Loan
- Voluntary portion of overseas pensions
- War pension or allowances

chunks.title: Childcare costs — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Childcare costs
Allowable costs are any regular essential expenses, calculated on a weekly basis arising out of the special circumstances of the client. They are costs that cannot be readily avoided or varied.
Costs of essential childcare (after deduction of childcare or OSCAR subsidy that is payable) can be included in the formula assessment of Special Benefit in the following situations:
- to enable the client or their partner to take part in paid employment or
- because the client or their partner is seriously disabled or seriously ill
There may be some instances where a cost does not fit the description detailed above but it may still be considered if the cost meets the definition of an allowable cost.
SWIFTT will not automatically include childcare costs as allowable costs for Special Benefit. You should deduct any Childcare or OSCAR Subsidy paid from the childcare cost before adding them in the SSPWA screen.
If you feel the client's individual circumstances warrant consideration of childcare costs even though the above criteria is not met, you may take this into consideration when deciding, through the use of your discretion, whether or not to grant a Special Benefit and/or at what rate to pay.

chunks.title: Clients not receiving a main benefit — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients not receiving a main benefit
Clients who do not receive a main benefit, and clients receiving New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension will receive their family tax credit from Inland Revenue.
The amount of family tax credit that you include as chargeable income is the actual weekly rate payable to the client. If the client has chosen not to receive family tax credit, they will need to take steps to obtain this assistance, and in most cases, you should encourage them to receive it as a weekly payment.
There may however be circumstances where it would be more beneficial for the client to receive an end of year payment, such as for those who receive fluctuating income, especially those who expect more income at the end of the tax year than the beginning.
If it is more beneficial for them to receive family tax credit as a lump sum at the end of the tax year, you will need to estimate the amount they would receive if paid on a weekly basis. You will need to include this estimated weekly amount of family tax credit as chargeable income and note CMS stating that the client will receive a year end payment and that you have estimated family tax credit for the client.
When assessing family tax credit as chargeable income, the following should be considered:
- Family tax credit Shared care
- Abated family tax credit
- Year end family tax credit
- Estimating weekly family tax credit

chunks.title: Clients receiving a main benefit — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving a main benefit
A client getting a main benefit can only receive family tax credit and Best Start tax credit, which can be paid with their main benefit. They cannot receive any other form of Working for Families Tax Credits.
You should make sure that clients are receiving their full entitlement to Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit before assessing Special Benefit. The amount of Family tax credits that you include as chargeable income is the actual weekly rate payable to the client.
The gross annual abatement threshold for family tax credit is $44,900 ($3,741 per month) as at 1 April 2026 and $79,000 for Best Start tax credit as at 1 April 2024. Clients who are getting a main benefit will be able to get the full amount of their family tax credit or Best Start tax credit.
From 1 April 2026 all three years of the Best Start tax credit are income tested, which is managed by Inland Revenue for clients not getting a main benefit. Main benefit clients continue to receive Best Start tax credit until the child is 3 years old. This is despite any income received before applying for benefit or moving off benefit.
For more information see:
- Protected Family tax credit while receiving a main benefit
- Protected Best Start tax credit while receiving a main benefit
Note clients getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension can only get their family tax credit and Best Start tax credit from Inland Revenue.

chunks.title: Clients with an orphan or unsupported child — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients with an orphan or unsupported child
When a client has an orphan or an unsupported child in their care, consider granting either an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit
If the client is already receiving an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, the benefit payment is not included in the assessment of income deficiency of Special Benefit.
## Assessment of the client's individual circumstances
However, the child's circumstances may be taken into account to decide if a payment of Special Benefit is justified when considering the overall circumstances of the client.
For more information see:
- Assessing whether a client's individual circumstances justify payment

chunks.title: Commencement date — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
Special Benefit is granted from:
- the date of application or
- the date of the qualifying event
whichever is the later.
There is no provision to backdate grants of Special Benefit.
For more information see:
- Core policy Application for assistance

chunks.title: Costs not generally allowed — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Costs not generally allowed
The following costs are not allowed in the calculation of a client's income deficiency.
However, they may still be considered, when using discretion whether to grant a Special Benefit or not and/or at what rate to pay:
- fixed line or pipe charges for telephone, electricity, gas or water(For allowable telephone costs see: Telephone rental)
- the client (or partner's if any) tuition costs such as stationery, books, fees or other course related costs
- debt repayments, fine repayments and other liabilities (other than Allowable costs)These include payments to collection agencies, Inland Revenue, personal loans, visa and bankcard repayments, MSD debts, debt repayment orders, attachment orders, maintenance, court fines, student loan repayments.
- fees charged by banks or other financial institutions
- any regular essential expenses for a child when the client is getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for them
- any temporary accommodation costs covered by Temporary Accommodation Assistance
Note some costs, particularly fines and debt repayments can be renegotiated and the repayment level decreased. MSD debt repayments should generally not exceed $40 per week.
However, if the client's debt repayment is causing or contributing to the client's hardship you should consider reducing the recovery rate.
Some costs are covered by the standard cost calculation and are generally not included:
- clothing, dental costs, electricity, gas, water, food and grocery items, house contents insurance
Costs that are non-essential, and not due to the special circumstances of the client or their partner, or can be reasonably avoided or varied are not allowed in the calculation of a client's deficiency.
However, you may consider these costs using discretion, whether to grant a Special Benefit or not and/or what rate to pay.
If you need assistance deciding whether a client's cost should be included contact Helpline.
## Child Support costs
Child Support costs that are not the current amount of formula-assessed Child Support a client is liable to pay cannot be included as an allowable cost for clients getting Special Benefit. This includes:
- Voluntary agreement Child Support
- Private arrangement of Child Support
- Court ordered lump-sum payments
- Foreign Child Support payments
- any amount of Child Support debt or penalties that a client has to pay to Inland Revenue

chunks.title: Counselling — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Counselling
Allowable costs are any regular essential expenses, calculated on a weekly basis arising out of the special circumstances of the client. They are costs that cannot be readily avoided or varied.
The maximum counselling costs that can be included is the amount paid for that purpose by way of Disability Allowance.
For more information see:
- Disability Allowance Types of costs
There may be some instances where a cost does not fit the description detailed above but it may still be considered if the cost meets the definition of an allowable cost.
If a client is receiving a Disability Allowance for counselling costs, these costs will automatically be included as an allowable cost for Special Benefit. You do not need to add them manually to the SSPWA screen.
For more information see:
- Disability Allowance
If you feel the client's individual circumstances warrant consideration of additional counselling costs even though the above criteria is not met, you may take this into consideration when deciding, through the use of your discretion, whether or not to grant a Special Benefit and/or at what rate to pay.

chunks.title: Deciding what rate to pay — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Deciding what rate to pay
If you consider that your assessment of the client's individual circumstances justifies payment of Special Benefit you could consider:
- granting Special Benefit at the rate assessed by the formula
- granting Special Benefit even though the client has no deficiency or
- granting Special Benefit at a rate other than that assessed by the formula
In SWIFTT you should add the rate you decide on in the SSPBA screen.
Fully document your decision, including the factors you have taken into consideration in reaching your decision.

chunks.title: Disability and personal health — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Disability and personal health
Allowable costs are any regular essential expenses, calculated on a weekly basis arising out of the special circumstances of the client. They are costs that cannot be readily avoided or varied.
Allowable disability and personal health costs are those costs that are allowed for Disability Allowance.
For more information about these costs see:
- Types of costs
There may be some instances where a cost does not fit the description detailed above, but it may be considered if the cost meets the definition of an allowable cost.
If a client is receiving a Disability Allowance, disability costs contained in SWIFTT will automatically be included as allowable costs for Special Benefit. You do not need to add them manually in the SSPWA screen.
For more information see:
- Disability Allowance
If you feel the client's individual circumstances warrant consideration even though the above criteria is not met, you may take this into consideration when deciding, through the use of your discretion, whether or not to grant Special Benefit and/or at what rate to pay.
Also see: Telephone rental

chunks.title: Disposable income — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Disposable income
Disposable income is the amount remaining after deducting allowable costs from the client's weekly chargeable income.

chunks.title: Documenting your decision — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Documenting your decision
Because Special Benefit involves the use of discretion, it is important to show the process used to arrive at that decision.
The Decision Summary form on DREW must be completed with every application and filed.
In particular you must provide details on:
- the reasons for your decision, including the factors you have taken into consideration in reaching your decision
- what costs you have or have not considered at each point in the decision process and why
- the reasons you have paid the formula assessment or departed from the formula assessment
If the client would receive more assistance from Temporary Additional Support, you must also document:
- the amount of assistance the client would be paid if they received Temporary Additional Support instead of Special Benefit
- your discussion with the client regarding the implications of receiving Temporary Additional Support instead of Special Benefit
- the client's decision on which assistance they choose
As Special Benefit is generally intended as short-term assistance, any payments made must be reviewed 3 months after grant and then at 6 month intervals.
These reviews are a reassessment of the application.
You should go through all the steps that were done for the initial application and, then make an assessment of the steps the client has taken to live within their normal income and what further steps could appropriately be taken in the client's circumstances. You then decide whether payment at the current rate continues to be justified.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Estimating weekly family tax credit and Best Start tax credit — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Estimating weekly family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
To estimate a client's weekly family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments from Inland Revenue, you will need to determine the amount of weekly family tax credits that would be payable to that client.
To verify this, the client may provide a Certificate of Entitlement from Inland Revenue or you can have the client phone Inland Revenue in your presence for verbal confirmation of the family tax credit entitlements.
If the client does not have a recent Certificate of Entitlement you can still complete a Special Benefit assessment by including the family tax credit rates determined by:
- estimating a weekly rate by using the Inland Revenue Working for Families chart or Estimate your WFFTC calculator or
- phoning Inland Revenue (the client must be with you to give verbal permission)
Inland Revenue has a dedicated phone line for Ministry of Social Development staff to enquire about Working for Families Tax Credits.
The amount of family tax credits that you would include as chargeable income is the actual weekly rate payable to the client (this is regardless of whether or not the client has chosen to receive family tax credit).
For more information see:
- Clients receiving a main benefit
- Year end family tax credit
- Verification of Family Tax Credit [no link find out why] process

chunks.text:

MSD must then take into consideration whether the client's individual circumstances justify this rate being increased or decreased, or no grant made.

chunks.text:

A single Jobseeker Support client aged 25 years (without dependent children) renting in Accommodation Supplement (Area 2) whose weekly chargeable income is $477.55 (as at 1 April 2026) made up of:

chunks.title: Example 1: Full Special Benefit paid as a lump sum — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: This is a lump sum payment to remove all ongoing payments of Special Benefit. A client's Special Benefit rate of payment has been assessed at $28 per week after taking into consideration all circumstances and financial hardship. One of the client's allowable costs is a hire purchase for a washing machine which is paid at $32 a week. The total owing on the washing machine is $320. The total amount the client would receive for Special Benefit in 3 months would be $364. By paying Special Benefit in a lump sum of $320 to pay off the washing machine eliminates that cost and reduces the client's deficiency meaning the client no longer requires Special Benefit.

chunks.title: Example 2: Portion of Special Benefit paid as a lump sum — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: A lump sum paid to remove the ongoing allowable costs for Hire Purchase, while also continuing payments for other costs. A client's Special Benefit rate has been assessed at $30 per week after taking into consideration all of the client's circumstances and financial hardship. The rate of payment includes 2 significant allowable costs, weekly qualifying accommodation costs and a hire purchase for a fridge that the client bought prior to being on benefit. While receiving a benefit, the client is struggling to budget due to the Hire Purchase account and it is causing significant hardship that would be alleviated somewhat if this account was closed. The total amount the client would receive for Special Benefit in three months would be $390. The total of Hire Purchase amount owing is $195, which would be paid as a lump sum. The remaining Special Benefit ($195) is the ongoing payment, which equals $15 per week ($195 divided by 13 weeks).

chunks.title: Example 3: Portion of Special Benefit paid as a lump sum — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: A lump sum paid to remove the immediate essential cost, example, arrears owing for a Hire Purchase, but does not remove the ongoing cost of the Hire Purchase. A client's Special Benefit formula rate has been assessed at $30 per week after taking into consideration all of the client's circumstances and financial hardship. Consideration was given to pay another $20 per week ($260 divided by 13 weeks) to a total payment of $50 per week Special Benefit for the arrears due on a Hire Purchase. However, because the retailer would not negotiate, it has been decided to pay a lump sum of $260 instead. The rate of payment includes 2 allowable costs, ongoing weekly qualifying accommodation costs and a Hire Purchase for a fridge that the client bought prior to being on benefit plus arrears owing for this. While receiving a benefit, the client has been unable to make the required repayments for the Hire Purchase and the client has received a letter from the retailer to advise of the debt and they require urgent repayment or the item will be repossessed. There are $260 arrears due to bring the client's account up to date. The client is struggling to budget due to the Hire Purchase account and is unable to pay the arrears. This is causing significant hardship that would be alleviated somewhat if the arrears due are paid as a lump sum. The total amount the client would receive for Special Benefit in three months would be $650 if the arrears where included. The total of Hire Purchase arrears owing is $260, which would be paid as a lump sum. The remaining Special Benefit ($390) is the ongoing payment, for the ongoing allowable costs for weekly qualifying accommodation costs and the Hire Purchase monthly repayments, which is the $30 per week. Remember to discuss and document the decision fully.

chunks.title: Expenses — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: All students have expenses such as fees, books and transport etc. Generally, Student Allowance and Student Loan are intended to cover these costs. If they are intended to be covered they generally should not be included as allowable costs.

chunks.title: Example — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: The Student Loan scheme provides for course related costs, which are intended to cover required course items such as books and in some circumstances computer equipment. A student seeks Special Benefit for the hire purchase cost of a computer. The student paid for part of their computer with the $1000 maximum course related costs component of their Student Loan and is paying off the rest. The hire purchase payments for the computer are a type of expense normally covered by the Student Loan scheme, so MSD should generally not include the expense for the purposes of assessment of Special Benefit for a full-time student or Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client. Remember that if the expense is one normally covered by the Student Allowance and Student Loan schemes, the student must also have exhausted all assistance available under these schemes.

chunks.title: Accommodation costs — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: Accommodation costs during the academic year are normally covered by the Student Allowance (Accommodation Benefit) and the living costs component of the Student Loan schemes. Generally, accommodation costs during the academic year should not be included when assessing the allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs for Special Benefit. Only those costs considered extraordinary due to the amount and/or nature can be included when assessing the allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs for Special Benefit. Accommodation costs that are not included in the calculation of weekly qualifying accommodation costs cannot be included in Special Benefit. However, Student Allowance and Student Loan are not available for these costs during the holiday period. They are intended to cover the academic year but not during the main holiday period. This means the accommodation costs of a person on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship may meet the criteria but for that same person during term they do not.

chunks.title: Additional expenses — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: Additional expenses, such as those related to a disability can be regarded as costs not intended to be covered by the schemes or alternatively extraordinary expenses and can be included in the assessment of Special Benefit. As with any assessment of Special Benefit, other avenues for meeting the cost should be explored, e.g. Disability Allowance. When the expense is one that would not usually be covered by the Student Allowance or Student Loan schemes MSD needs to assess the expense under the usual criteria for allowable costs. - Are they costs that cannot be readily avoided or varied? - Has the person accessed all other sources of financial assistance? For example, but not limited to, support from parents and/or other relatives where applicable (that is, if the student is under 24 years old) For more information see: - Extraordinary expenses

chunks.title: Extraordinary expenses — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Extraordinary expenses
If the costs are the type of expense usually covered by the Student Allowance or Student Loan schemes then to consider these costs for Special Benefit they should be:
- an extraordinary expense and
- the student should have exhausted all their entitlements under those schemes
Extraordinary expenses are those that are 'rare'. They are different to or over and above those of other students. Consider any special circumstances leading to the expense which may be 'extraordinary', as that can mean that the expense in itself may be extraordinary.
However, you must consider the individual circumstances of the student. You should consider:
- any special circumstances that have led to the extraordinary expense
- any circumstances that differentiate the student or the extraordinary expenses they have from other students
- access to other sources of financial assistanceFor example, but not limited to, support from parents and/or other relatives.
- other individual circumstances that should be taken into account
Remember the student must also have exhausted all assistance available under the Student Allowance and Student Loan schemes.
For more information see:
- Students chargeable income
- Student Allowance declined due to parental income

chunks.title: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text:
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit are chargeable income for the purpose of assessing Special Benefit.
When assessing family tax credit and Best Start tax credit as chargeable income, the following should be considered:
- Clients receiving a main benefit
- Clients not receiving a main benefit
For more information see:
- Shared care - family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
- Abated family tax credit
- Year end family tax credit
- Estimating weekly family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
You need to take into consideration the client's individual circumstances when deciding, through the use of your discretion, whether or not to grant Special Benefit and/or at what rate to pay.

chunks.title: Formula-assessed Child Support costs — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: Formula-assessed Child Support liability is the only type of Child Support that is an allowable cost for Special Benefit. Formula-assessed Child Support costs are determined by Inland Revenue, using a formula that considers the essential costs that a liable parent must contribute towards supporting their child(ren). These costs must be verified by Inland Revenue.

chunks.title: Child Support liability — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: Only the current amount of formula-assessed Child Support a liable parent is required to pay can be included as an allowable cost. The allowable cost does not include any amount of: - Child Support for a liability period before the commencement date of the Special Benefit - debts or penalties a liable parent may be paying to Inland Revenue along with their regular Child Support liability - court-ordered lump sum payments - Child Support the liable parent does not have to pay (e.g. when their formula assessment is suspended or when the client has an exemption from paying Child Support) Note if the liable parent has an offsetting arrangement, the full amount of formula-assessed Child Support liability may be included. This applies regardless of how much Child Support the liable parent is paying (if any) while the offsetting arrangement is in place.

chunks.title: Date costs can be included — extra help > special benefit
chunks.text: Clients may have their formula-assessed Child Support liability included as an allowable cost in their Special Benefit assessment from 1 July 2023. If a client applies to include Child Support as an allowable cost between 1 July 2023 and 29 September 2023, the inclusion of the cost can be backdated to the later of: - the date the client is liable for the cost or - 1 July 2023 Clients who do not apply to include Child Support as an allowable cost until on or after 30 September 2023 cannot have these costs backdated.
