chunks.title: Applying reasonable steps obligation — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Applying reasonable steps obligation
Generally, clients who have received Special Needs Grants, Advance Payments of Benefit and/or Recoverable Assistance Payments on 3 or more grant dates during the past 12 months must take reasonable steps before they get any additional payments.
Reasonable steps are actions that increase their income, reduce their costs, or improve their financial management.
You should let clients know at their third grant date and each subsequent grant date that they must take reasonable steps before they can get further assistance.
Note in some circumstances partners must also take reasonable steps.

chunks.title: Recovery of payment — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Recovery of payment
If a Special Needs Grant paid is recoverable, repayments must be:
- more than $4.00 a week, unless exceptional circumstances exist
- paid either by lump sum, instalments or through benefit payments
- paid by the parent if the Special Needs Grant was paid for dependent children
## Recovery rate
The rate of recovery must be negotiated with the client taking into account their circumstances.
When setting the rate of recovery, MSD needs to consider the following factors (where relevant):
- the circumstances of the client and their dependents
- the ability of the client to meet their needs and the needs of their dependents
- the amount of the debt - we want clients to pay off their debts as fast as they can, but always bear in mind the circumstances of the client and their ability to repay without placing them in undue hardship. If the debt is large and the client can afford to pay it, MSD should consider a higher repayment rate
- the effect the rate of recovery will have on the client's ability to support themselves
- whether the rate of recovery would cause undue hardship to the client or their dependents
- the effect the rate of recovery would have on the client's ability to fulfil their work and social obligations – e.g. ensuring their child is enrolled with a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner or be enrolled with a medical practice that is part of a Primary Health Organisation if required to do so
- the ability of the debtor to gain access to further advances and recoverable assistance
If the client does not agree with the rate of repayment MSD must record why the set rate has been decided.

chunks.title: Refugee, protected person, Afghan interpreter or Afghan evacuee — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Refugee, protected person, Afghan interpreter or Afghan evacuee
If the client meets all the qualifications they can get a Special Needs Grant for re-establishment costs if they are a refugee, protected person, Afghan interpreter or Afghan evacuee and they do not qualify for other forms of government assistance that are not provided by MSD.
Note a client must apply to MSD within 1 year of their first arrival in New Zealand (or 2 years if they are applying for English language classes assistance).
## Immigration status
A person applying for refugee, protected person status or residence as they were an Afghan interpreter is not entitled to a re-establishment grant unless or until their application, including a residence class visa, is approved by Immigration New Zealand.
An Afghan evacuee is entitled to a re-establishment grant if they are:
- a New Zealand citizen or
- hold a residence class visa (including an Afghan Emergency Resettlement Visa) or
- have applied for an Afghan Emergency Resettlement Visa
## Refugee Family Support Resident Visa
Clients who hold a Refugee Family Support Resident Visa cannot get a re-establishment grant if they are not themselves recognised as a refugee or protected person.
They are considered an immigrant not a refugee or a protected person.

chunks.title: Reinstating driver licences — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Reinstating driver licences
A recoverable Special Needs Grant may be made for a client to reinstate a driver licence of any class if they:
- had their driver licence disqualified and/or
- surrendered their driver licence because they were required to give it up or decided not to drive anymore and handed it in and
- qualify for their driver licence to be reinstated
Note payments can only be made to clients who have completed their suspension/disqualification period and who are eligible to reinstate their licence. This does not include a person who has been disqualified for more than 12 months as they would need to apply for a new licence.
Generally, 1 payment each may be made to the client and their partner during a 52-week period. MSD can use discretion to grant more than 1 Special Needs Grant in a 52-week period if the client has exceptional circumstances.
## Disqualified for longer than 12 months
Clients who have had their driver licence disqualified for longer than 12 months need to complete and pass a test to get their licence back. They will need to pay a requalification fee, which includes the cost of the test.
A Special Needs Grant for the requalification fee cannot be made under the driver licence category, but MSD should consider if the client would qualify under the 'other emergency payment' grant category.
## Dependent children
A parent can apply on behalf of their dependent child for a Special Needs Grant to reinstate their driver licence under the driver licence category.

chunks.title: Renewals of existing driver licences — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Renewals of existing driver licences
A recoverable Special Needs Grant may be made for a client to renew their driver licence if they:
- hold an unexpired driver licence or
- hold an expired driver licence and had a good or sufficient reason why they could not renew it before the expiry date and
- are applying for a renewal of a driver licence of the same or equivalent class or classes
Generally, a client and their partner can get 1 payment each, during a 52-week period. MSD can use discretion to grant more than 1 Special Needs Grant in a 52-week period if the client has exceptional circumstances.
## Actual fees
Special Need Grants to renew a driver licence must not be more than the actual fee payable.
For more information see:
## Assistance cannot be paid
A client will not qualify for a Special Needs Grant for driver licence costs if they:
- are disqualified from holding or getting a driver licence
## Renewals for a client aged 75 or over
A client aged 75 or over may also be required to take an on-road safety test as a condition to renew their driver licence. The cost for this test is included in the renewal fee.

chunks.title: Review of ongoing payments — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Review of ongoing payments
All ongoing payments (e.g. for accommodation costs) are to be reviewed within four weeks following the end of the civil defence emergency or adverse event requiring the activation of the Civil Defence payments. The local authority will usually declare when the civil defence emergency or adverse event is over.
Civil Defence Payments are intended to meet an immediate need during a period of a civil defence emergency or adverse event. While some people may not be able to return to their homes for an extended period and some will never be able to return to their homes, they must make alternative accommodation arrangements as soon as practicable once the civil defence emergency or adverse event is over. Only in exceptional circumstances would we continue payments for longer than four weeks following the end of the emergency or adverse event.
Exceptional circumstances could include:
- lack of alternative accommodation options in the local area or
- a definite date in the near future for returning to their home or moving into alternative accommodation (e.g. a confirmed date for their damaged home to be repaired or declared habitable or a commencement date for a rental agreement or alternative accommodation)
Other ongoing assistance may be available for people who are in temporary accommodation for an extended period. This includes:
- Accommodation Supplement
- Temporary Additional Support
Applicants must meet all the qualifications for these forms of assistance.
When considering eligibility to the Accommodation Supplement for a period of temporary accommodation their home is not considered as a realisable asset (e.g. they are moving back into the damaged property once it is repaired). Neither is the net equity in their damaged home to be considered as the value of the damaged home is likely to be uncertain.

chunks.title: Rural assistance payments — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Rural assistance payments
Rural assistance payments are available when the Minister announces assistance specifically for a Primary Industry in a certain area.
This is usually after the industry in that area has been affected by a:
- natural disaster, e.g. a flood
- climatic event, e.g. a drought
- biosecurity event e.g. a pest, or disease
These payments help farmers who meet all the qualifications and have:
- an approved Primary Industry
- no other significant income and
- no readily realisable assets that are not connected with the Primary Industry
## Assistance currently approved by the Minister
The Minister has approved assistance for the following event:
- North and South Island drought 2025

chunks.title: Second or subsequent separation — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Second or subsequent separation
When a client reconciles with their former partner, and later separates for a second time they will not be required to 'prove' some aspects of eligibility again.
## Work permit or visa
You should confirm their work permit or visa (if granted after 29 November 2010) is still current; Immigration New Zealand will have initially granted this.
Note that a work visa issued before 29 November 2010 does not allow a person to remain in New Zealand.
## Proof of family violence
Provided proof of family violence by the partner was obtained from Immigration New Zealand for the first application, no further proof is required where the client separates for a second time due to family violence.
## Relationship ended and hardship
You will need to confirm the relationship has ended and that the client is suffering hardship. It may also be appropriate to confirm the client's immigration status with Immigration New Zealand. See:
- Immigration New Zealand
## Advise National Office
You must advise National Office when a client 'resumes' applications for weekly Special Needs Grant payments under the Family Violence Programme. See:
- National Office contacts [no link find out why]
## New partner
Where a client forms a 'new relationship' and later separates due to family violence, you would need to refer the client to Immigration New Zealand and when appropriate, to the New Zealand Police to report the incident of violence and/or a refuge organisation for support.

chunks.title: Sector Services process — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Sector Services process
Sector Services is a business unit of the Ministry of Health contracted to manage health claims. One of the services Sector Services provides is for wigs and hairpieces.
To be assisted with a Special Needs Grant for a wig or hairpiece all other assistance from a health agency must be accessed. Only when this assistance is not available can consideration be given to pay a Special Needs Grant.
Generally, contact with Sector Services will be made during the interview with the client. The client should first make contact with Sector Services, giving Sector Services permission to supply details of their entitlement for wigs and hairpieces to Work and Income.
Where contact with Sector Services cannot be made during the interview, a form must be completed giving Work and Income permission to contact Sector Services to discuss the client's wig and hairpiece entitlements. The form is then facsimiled to Sector Services.
Work and Income can contact Sector Services the following day requesting the client's entitlement to wigs and hairpieces.
Note Sector Services do not send clients any details of their entitlement. This is all completed by telephone - Sector Services contact number is: 0800 458 448

chunks.title: Single client — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Single client
If exceptional circumstances exist, a single client with no dependent children may be able to receive a Special Needs Grant during the application process for a benefit and/or during their initial stand-down if they meet all the qualifications.
The client must also:
- be suffering serious hardship and
If the client will be subject to work obligations, they must:
- accept suitable employment when offered or
- participate in an activity that Work and Income considers suitable, which will improve their work-readiness or prospects for employment
You may grant and pay a recoverable Special Needs Grant to the client up until either:
- the date of decline of the benefit or
- the date of grant of the benefit or
- the commencement date of the benefit or
- the date the application for benefit lapses
whichever is the later.
## Payment
More than one payment can be made to a client, but the maximum amount payable, in any one week cannot be more than:
- half the maximum weekly rate of Jobseeker Support the client would have received if they were entitled to that benefit
Special Needs Grants for this purpose are recoverable.
## Restriction on payments
Only when a client has received their maximum entitlement to recoverable assistance during their initial stand-down can you consider providing other assistance, either recoverable or non-recoverable. To receive other emergency grants they or a member of their immediate family must be:
- experiencing an emergency situation or
- in extreme hardship
A client is still required to meet all the qualifications for any other Special Needs Grant assistance they apply for, including non-recoverable assistance.
The exception to the restriction is grants relating to re-establishment situations (eg Steps to Freedom).

chunks.title: Sole parent — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Sole parent
A sole parent client may be able to receive a Special Needs Grant during the application process for a benefit and/or during their initial stand-down if they meet all the qualifications.
A sole parent may be able to receive this type of Special Needs Grant from the date of first contact up until either:
- the date of decline of the benefit or
- the date of grant of the benefit or
- the commencement date of the benefit or
- the date the application for benefit lapses
whichever is the later.
The client must also:
- have no cash assets, cannot obtain credit facilities and
- have taken all reasonable steps to reduce their fixed commitments
## Payment
More than one payment can be made, but the maximum amount payable in any 1 week cannot be more than:
- half the maximum weekly rate of Jobseeker Support the client would have received if they were entitled to that benefit
Special Needs Grants for this purpose are recoverable.

chunks.title: Steps to Freedom — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: A person who meets all the qualifications may be paid a grant to re-establish themselves in the community when they were in prison or held in custody on remand for 31 days or more and they have been: - released from prison (including up to 5 days before release) - released from court after being held in custody or on remand This includes when they are: - released on home detention or - released from prison to a residential facility or - released from a residential facility or - deported from overseas (back to New Zealand) following release from prison A re-establishment grant can also be made to an immediate family member of a person who meets the above criteria.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: A non-recoverable grant, up to a maximum of $350, may be paid towards the cost of: - accommodation, bond, or rent in advance - beds and bedding - essential appliances - connecting telephone, electricity, and gas - food - clothing and toiletry items or - other re-establishment costs For more information see: - Qualifications - Verification for Special Needs Grants - Payment of Steps to Freedom grants - The Prisoner Reintegration team

chunks.title: Specific conditions — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: A re-establishment grant cannot be paid for emergency housing costs. The amount payable must be reduced by any money held by the prison or other custodian on the person's behalf. This includes any money held in the prisoner's trust account, canteen account or earnings account. Generally, Steps to Freedom grants should not be paid when: - they do not have an initial stand-down or - a prisoner has a partner getting benefit assistance, and their partner's benefit is changed to the couple rate from the date of release

chunks.title: Clients returning to their own home — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: Generally, if the client is returning to an established home there would be no re-establishment costs. However, if the client can show that they have valid re-establishment costs then a payment of the Steps to Freedom grant may be appropriate. Some examples are: - a prisoner's partner had moved in with family while their partner was in prison, then upon their release, they needed to set themselves up with new accommodation - a prisoner was returning to their parents' home upon their release, but their parents did not have enough bedding or food - a prisoner was returning to their partner's home, and required assistance for clothing and toiletry items If a prisoner has been released from prison and is entering a residential facility, see: - Entering residential facility

chunks.title: Prisoners with partners — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: If a prisoner has a partner you may need to interview them together to determine what re-establishment costs are required. Note the income and cash assets of a prisoner's partner must be taken into account when checking to see if the client meets the qualifications for a Special Needs Grant before assessing eligibility for a Steps to Freedom grant. For more information see: - Income - Cash assets

chunks.title: Clients deported from overseas — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: New Zealanders deported from overseas (sent back to New Zealand) following the completion of a prison sentence can receive a Steps to Freedom grant. Deportees are required to supply evidence they have served 31 days or more in prison and/or remanded in custody and to supply evidence of any funds they were released with.

chunks.title: Home detention clients — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: Home detainees may qualify for a Steps to Freedom grant when they have been imprisoned for 31 days or more before being released on home detention.

chunks.title: Remand prisoners — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: Remand prisoners are often released from the Court rather than a prison and are usually not issued with a Steps to Freedom form. You must confirm the period that the prisoner has been held on remand with the prison, the District Court or the local PARS office.

chunks.title: Other assistance available — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text: A client who has already received the maximum amount payable for Steps to Freedom who continues to face hardship may qualify for other financial assistance, such as a recoverable Special Needs Grant. When Steps to Freedom does not cover the full amount needed for bond or rent in advance, consider whether the client qualifies for any Housing Support Products for the remaining amount.

chunks.title: SWIFTT requirements — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT requirements
To record ongoing weekly Special Needs Grants, clients must be recorded on SWIFTT as a non-beneficiary with a 'registered' status. A must view note stating the words 'Domestic Violence Programme' must be completed.
Note that it may be appropriate in some circumstances to 'secure' the CMS record.

chunks.title: Terminations for dependent children — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Terminations for dependent children
Dependent children cannot get a Special Needs Grant for termination of pregnancy in their own right. Applications must be made by their parent or caregiver.
If this highlights care and protection concerns, refer the dependent child to Oranga Tamariki.

chunks.title: The Prisoner Reintegration team — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## The Prisoner Reintegration team
Prisoner Reintegration teams work with prisoners before their release. Generally, they are Ministry of Social Development case managers or work brokers.
Their main role is to:
- assist prisoners to find suitable employment upon release
- assist prisoners to make and begin to process applications for any financial assistance they may qualify for when they are released, including Steps to Freedom grants and
- provide in-work support for former prisoners
For more information about the Prisoner Reintegration teams see:
## Steps to Freedom
The Prisoner Reintegration team can pay Steps to Freedom grants up to 5 days before a prisoner's release. This allows the prisoner to pay for their re-establishment costs before they are released from prison. However, it cannot be paid more than 5 days before their release.
For more information see:
## Birth certificates
The application fee for a New Zealand birth certificate can be paid for a prisoner before release when the:
- prisoner meets the qualifications for a Special Needs Grant
- prisoner meets the criteria for other emergency grants and
- birth certificate is required as supporting evidence for an application for a benefit
The Prisoner Reintegration team will organise payment of the application fee with Births, Deaths and Marriages.
If the prisoner's birth was not registered in New Zealand you can pay the application fee for other forms of identification, such as a confirmation letter from Immigration New Zealand.

chunks.title: Personal advisors role — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Personal advisors role
As part of the Transition from Care to Independence pilot, each young person will have a personal advisor contracted by Oranga Tamariki. The personal advisor will help develop a pathway plan and provide support to access a range of programmes and services available to them.
The personal advisor will begin their involvement with the young person:
- before discharge
- during the transition stage and
- support post discharge
The personal advisor will prepare the young person for their discharge from supported care and refer the young person as a participant on the pilot.
Personal advisors will work in partnership with the young person, their social worker and caregivers to develop and review transition plans to ensure the young person is given sufficient opportunities and support to develop independent living skills.
The role of the personal advisor is to:
- mentor
- be a contact point for the young person until they reach 19 years old
- help in accessing safe and affordable accommodation
- help the young person develop life skills
- send them on personal development services

chunks.title: Transition from Care to Independence — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Transition from Care to Independence
Oranga Tamariki has 'Transition from Care to Independence' initiatives in Auckland and Christchurch.
As part of the initiative, eligible clients may be able to get a Special Needs Grant to assist them with the costs of establishing themselves in the community if they:
- are aged 16 years or over
- have been in supported care under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 and
- leaves supported care to live independently and
- have a letter from their personal advisor verifying that they are participating in a Transition from Care to Independence initiative and
- they require a youth transition payment
The personal advisor's involvement with the young person is necessary for the client to get Special Needs Grant assistance for re-establishment of young persons aged 16 to 19, who leave care under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 to live independently.

chunks.title: Types of licence endorsement — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Types of licence endorsement
The recoverable Special Needs Grants for driver licences is not available to pay for the following endorsements on driver licences:
Identifying letter
Endorsement
D
Dangerous goods endorsement
I
Driving instructor endorsement
O
Testing officer endorsement
P
Passenger endorsement
F
Forklift endorsement for use with special-type vehicles that are forklifts
R
Roller endorsement for use with special-type vehicles that run on rollers
T
Tracks endorsement for use with special-type vehicles that run on self-laying tracks
W
Wheels endorsement for use with special-type vehicles that run on wheels and are not forklifts
V
Vehicle recovery endorsement

chunks.title: Vasectomies — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Vasectomies
A client may be able to receive a Special Needs Grant for the cost of a vasectomy when:
- assistance is not available from the District Health Boards or
- only partial funding is available from the District Health Boards
The District Health Board does not always provide for vasectomies. When clients are required to travel away from home to receive this treatment or to pay private hospital fees, Special Needs Grants towards the cost of:
- travel
- accommodation and
- surgery
may be considered.
## Payment
Unless exceptional circumstances exist, the maximum amount payable towards the cost of travel, accommodation and surgery is $300.
Special Needs Grants for this purpose are:
- non-recoverable and
- restricted to one payment in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Vasectomies and termination of pregnancies — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Vasectomies and termination of pregnancies
If the client meets all qualifications, they may be able to receive a Special Needs Grant of up to $300 towards the cost of travel, accommodation and surgery if they require a pregnancy to be terminated or a vasectomy.
Payment may be made in respect of each member of an immediate family.
Deduct any health-related subsidy and/or insurance from the total cost of the vasectomy and termination of pregnancy.

chunks.title: Verification — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Verification
The basic verification required for the application of a Special Needs Grants is:
- identification
- income and cash asset details, if not receiving an income tested benefit
- a quote for goods or services
Note a quote is not required when a client applies for assistance for food or petrol, or there is a preferred supplier arrangement in place.
If a client refuses to purchase from the preferred supplier they cannot get a Special Needs Grant for these items.
## Verification of income and asset details
Applications for Special Needs Grants do not require verification to be provided for income or cash assets when the client is getting ongoing financial assistance, such as an income tested benefit, or second tier assistance.
However, if the client has declared income or assets that are different from what is currently recorded you must update the client's record in SWIFTT.
If an application is made by a person who is not receiving ongoing financial assistance they must provide verification for both income and cash assets.
## Verification hardship obligations have been met
A client must provide verification that they have met any hardship obligations applied to them.

chunks.title: Water tank refill — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Water tank refill
Clients may be able to get a Special Needs Grant to cover the cost of both delivery and refilling of a water tank when they meet all qualifications, and where the property they live in is either:
- owned by them or
- rented by them and they are responsible for refilling the water tank
## Tenancy agreement signed after 1 October 2010
From 1 October 2010, it is the responsibility of the tenant to refill their water tank unless the tenancy agreement specifically states the landlord is responsible for this.
Clients can get a Special Needs Grant to refill their water tank unless their tenancy agreement specifically states that the landlord is responsible.
## Tenancy agreement signed before 1 October 2010
Before 1 October 2010, landlords were responsible for refilling the water tank for their tenants unless the tenancy agreement specifically stated the tenant was responsible for this.
Clients can get a Special Needs Grant to refill their water tank if their tenancy agreement was signed before 1 October 2010, and it specifically states they are responsible for refilling the water tank.
If their tenancy agreement does not state they are responsible for refilling the water tank, the landlord is responsible for this. In this case, the client cannot get a Special Needs Grant to refill the water tank.
## Payment
Unless exceptional circumstances exist:
- the maximum amount payable is $500 and
- is restricted to one payment in any 52 week period
## Payment non-recoverable
Special Needs Grants for water tank refills are always non-recoverable.

chunks.title: Wigs and hairpieces — extra help > special needs grant
chunks.text:
## Wigs and hairpieces
If the client meets all qualifications, they may be able to receive a Special Needs Grant to assist with the cost of wigs and hairpieces if they:
- suffer from a medical condition or are undergoing medical treatment which makes it desirable for the client to wear a wig or hairpiece on cosmetic grounds
- have been provided with financial assistance towards the purchase of a wig or hairpiece through Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora and
- are unable to meet the remaining costs
The client needs to provide evidence Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora has provided assistance and what shortfall the client must meet to purchase the wig or hairpiece.
## Payment
Unless exceptional circumstances exist, the maximum amount payable towards the cost of a wig or hairpiece is $300.
Grants for this purpose are:
- non-recoverable
- are restricted to one payment for the same or similar purpose in any 52-week period
Deduct any health-related subsidy and/or insurance payments from the total payment required.
Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora provides assistance for wigs and hairpieces, and to assist you a process to request a client's entitlement has been developed.

chunks.title: Accommodation Supplement — extra help > special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Accommodation Supplement
Receiving Special Transfer Allowance will affect the rate of Accommodation Supplement payable.
Accommodation costs are determined by the following formula:
actual rent $______ less Special Transfer Allowance $______ Equals accommodation costs $______
actual rent
$______
less Special Transfer Allowance
$______
Equals accommodation costs
$______
Accommodation Supplement is then to be assessed using the normal formula based on the new assessed accommodation costs.
Example a married couple living in Dunedin are receiving New Zealand Superannuation and paying rent of $200. They have just been assessed as being entitled to $50 Special Transfer Allowance.
actual rent $200.00 less Special Transfer Allowance $50.00 Equals $150.00
actual rent
$200.00
less Special Transfer Allowance
$50.00
Equals
$150.00
The rate of Accommodation Supplement payable must now be based on the couple having rental costs of $150.
For information on calculating Accommodation Supplement see:
- Accommodation Supplement

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text: Clients can be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment for the first 28 days if it does not affect the client's eligibility for Special Transfer Allowance, that is, their accommodation costs are continuing. To pay Special Transfer Allowance while the client is absent from New Zealand depends on whether the client is also receiving a main benefit. Note when assessing the period of absence, do not include: - the date of departure from New Zealand and - the date of return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Clients receiving a main benefit — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text: All clients receiving a main benefit must advise Work and Income before they leave New Zealand. If the client or partner does not advise Work and Income prior to their international travel, their benefit payments (including Special Transfer Allowance) must stop. Where a client is paid their main benefit while they are absent from New Zealand (either because they meet the criteria for approved travel or the requirement to approved travel does not apply to them) they can continue to receive their main benefit and their Special Transfer Allowance for up to 28 days in any 52 week period, unless they meet the criteria to be paid their main benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. Clients who do not continue to receive main benefit while overseas (because they do not meet the criteria for approved travel) may still be able to continue to receive Special Transfer Allowance, if their absence does not affect the client's eligibility for this assistance and they advised Work and Income prior to their international travel. This is limited to 28 days in a 52 week period. For more information about Absence from New Zealand see: - Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit - Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period in relevant main benefit

chunks.title: Clients receiving non-beneficiary Extra Help — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text: Clients who are receiving Special Transfer Allowance and who are not also receiving a main benefit: - are required to advise of their departure from New Zealand and - can be absent and paid their Special Transfer Allowance for up to 28 days per absence where it does not affect the client's eligibility for Special Transfer Allowance, that is, where they have continuing accommodation costs

chunks.title: Non-beneficiary Extra Help payment will not continue — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text: Where payment of Special Transfer Allowance will not continue because they do not meet the eligibility criteria due to their absence you will need to suspend the benefit from: - the day after departure

chunks.title: Married, civil union or de facto clients — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text: Where one partner stays in New Zealand, assess Special Transfer Allowance at the full married, civil union or de facto rate and pay the full amount to the partner remaining in New Zealand.

chunks.title: Permanent absence — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text: If the client is leaving New Zealand permanently Special Transfer Allowance should be cancelled from the day after departure.

chunks.title: Cancellation of main benefit — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Cancellation of main benefit
When the parent benefit is cancelled, Special Transfer Allowance may be paid as a non-beneficiary supplementary.
A check should be made at the time of cancellation that the client continues to meet the criteria and that the rental remains unchanged.
Special Transfer Allowance for non-beneficiaries should be reviewed annually to ensure the client remains at the listed address and continues to pay rent.
The same formula used to calculate the rate of payment for beneficiaries is used for non-beneficiaries. For more information on this calculation see:
- Payment

chunks.title: Change in accommodation — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Change in accommodation
A client can continue receiving Special Transfer Allowance each time they move provided they continue to pay rent that is more than the average regional rent.
If the client changes accommodation and they:
- are boarding
- own their own home
- receiving residential care services or
- pay rent to live in a property that is owned or managed by Housing New Zealand or a property let by or on behalf of Housing New Zealand (an income related rent)
Special Transfer Allowance must stop from the day after the client moved out of their previous residence.
## Continuing to pay rent
Where a client continues to pay rent their Special Transfer Allowance must be reviewed to ensure they are receiving the correct payment.
Note the maximum rate payable is the rate of Special Transfer Allowance they were receiving, not the rate of Tenure Protection Allowance they once received. So they either receive:
- Special Transfer Allowance based on their new accommodation costs or
- the rate of Special Transfer Allowance paid on their last home
whichever is the lesser

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise the Ministry of Social Development of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Special Transfer Allowance.
You may also review Special Transfer Allowance at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
For more information see:
- Absence from New Zealand
- Core policy Agents
- Cancellation of main benefit
- Change in accommodation
- Client moves house
- Death of a client
- Hospitalisation
- Core policy Redirection of benefit payment
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals
- Separation of a couple

chunks.title: Client moves house — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Client moves house
Where a client has their Special Transfer Allowance reviewed because they move house again, the maximum rate payable is the rate of Special Transfer Allowance they were receiving, not the rate of Tenure Protection Allowance they once received. So they either receive:
- Special Transfer Allowance based on their new accommodation costs or
- the rate of Special Transfer Allowance paid on their last home
whichever is the lesser.

chunks.title: Death of a client — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
If the client who qualifies for Special Transfer Allowance dies, the allowance is reviewed and may be granted to a partner or family member who has been living with the client prior to death, for:
- up to three months from the date of death or
- to the day the partner, companion or family member vacates the premises
whichever is earlier.

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a client who qualifies for Special Transfer Allowance is admitted to hospital payment can continue as long as the client continues to pay rent.
If the client stops paying rent, Special Transfer Allowance must stop from the day after they stop paying rent.

chunks.title: Separation of a couple — extra help > special transfer allowance > changes and reviews special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Separation of a couple
When a couple separate and they both have been receiving Special Transfer Allowance, either one or both partners may qualify for the allowance.
If only one partner qualifies:
- only the client who qualifies can continue to receive Special Transfer Allowance
If both partners qualify:
- both of them may receive Special Transfer Allowance

chunks.title: Commencement date — extra help > special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
Special Transfer Allowance is granted from when the client is eligible for it.
There is no stand down period for Special Transfer Allowance.
For more information see:
- Core policy Application for assistance

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Special Transfer Allowance provides non-taxable assistance to clients who received a Tenure Protection Allowance but who can no longer receive it because they moved house or because Housing New Zealand sold their house.
The client may have moved into any type of rental accommodation except a Housing New Zealand property. Special Transfer Allowance is not income or asset tested and is not counted as income for high earnings stand down.
Special Transfer Allowance may be paid to students.
A client who rents a Housing New Zealand house cannot receive Special Transfer Allowance.
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Payment
- Commencement date
- Changes and reviews
To see the effect of Special Transfer Allowance on Accommodation Supplement see:
- Accommodation Supplement

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Payment
The rate of Special Transfer Allowance is generally the difference between the client's rent and the average regional rent.
The rate of Special Transfer Allowance payable cannot be higher than the amount of Tenure Protection Allowance or Special Transfer Allowance a client was receiving at 17 November 2000.
If a client moves premises and still qualifies for a Special Transfer Allowance their rate can be no greater than the amount they were receiving for their old house.
To calculate the Special Transfer Allowance use the following formula:
Rental cost $______ less average regional rent $______ Equals $______
Rental cost
$______
less average regional rent
$______
Equals
$______
The country is broken up into 3 regions for the average regional rent. These regions do not correspond to the three regions used for the maximum Accommodation Supplement payable.
For more information see:
- Deskfile Average regional rents
When Special Transfer Allowance is granted, Accommodation Supplement is calculated differently.
For more information see:
- Accommodation Supplement

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
To be able to receive a Special Transfer Allowance (STA) a client must fall into at least one of the following 3 groups:
- the client was receiving a Special Transfer Allowance immediately prior to 17 November 2000 and continues to rent from a landlord other than Housing New Zealand
- the client was receiving Tenure Protection Allowance but had their house sold by Housing New Zealand and continues to live in the house
- the client has moved from premises in which they received Special Transfer Allowance immediately prior to moving and still meets all the other qualifying criteria for Special Transfer Allowance
A client's rent costs must also be higher than the average regional rent.
For more information see:
- Special Transfer Allowance cannot be paid

chunks.title: Special Transfer Allowance cannot be paid — extra help > special transfer allowance
chunks.text:
## Special Transfer Allowance cannot be paid
There are some specific situations where Special Transfer Allowance cannot be paid:
- where the client is a boarder
- where the client lives in a property owned or managed by Housing New Zealand
- where the client has a disability and moves into residential care or
- to any person who did not qualify in their own right for a Tenure Protection Allowance
For more information see:
- Separation of a couple

chunks.title: Calculating the payment — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Calculating the payment
You can use the Income Assessment tab in DREW to estimate the benefit rate with income for clients.
Income must be rounded down to the nearest dollar.
## Weekly income
Income (including any income of a partner) can be charged weekly as it is earned, for the following benefits and at the following rates:
- Jobseeker Support (including Student Hardship)
- Emergency Benefit (equivalent to Jobseeker Support)
70 cents is taken from the benefit for each $1.00 of income over $160.00 before tax a week
except for a client with a partner (with or without dependent children), when the partner is:
- granted any of the main benefits in their own right (other than a Veterans Pension) or
- not entitled to get a main benefit because of voluntary unemployment, misconduct, or on strike
then the rate of:
- 35 cents is taken from the half couple rate of benefit for each $1.00 of the combined income of the client and their partner over $160.00 (before tax) a week
Note Youth Payment and Young Parent Payment clients have their income charged differently and more information can be found here:
- Charging income Youth Payment
- Charging income Young Parent Payment
## Annual income
Income (including any income of a partner) can be charged over a 52 week period for the following benefits:
- Sole Parent Support
- Supported Living Payment
- Jobseeker Support - Sole parent rate or
- grandparented rate for clients who were getting Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women Alone, or Widows Benefit with no children or children over the age of 14 years on 15 July 2013
As the income for these benefits is charged over a 52 week period, you will not need to calculate the abatement for the grant as the abated benefit rate has already been assessed by SWIFTT for the first week's payment.
Deduct any other assistance received for ordinary living expenses from this amount to determine the grant amount payable.

chunks.title: Cash assets include — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Cash assets include
- bills of exchange or promissory notes
- building society shares
- money in bank accounts, including fixed and term deposits with any bank, friendly society, credit union, or building society
- money invested with or lent to any bank or other financial institution
- mortgage investments and other long term loans
- shares, stocks, debentures, bonus bonds, and other bonds
- the net equity held in any property or land not used as the person's home and
- the client's share in any partnership
## Cash assets do not include
- the personal effects of the client and partner (if any)
- the home property and land on which it is situated
- the motor vehicle principally used by the client for their personal use
- a caravan, boat, or other vehicle with a net equity of less than $2000, or which is used by the person or a member of their family for day to day accommodation
- funds locked into KiwiSaver and other retirement scheme accounts
- Crown funds provided directly to clients to purchase Support Services and Direct Disability Support payments
- Christchurch mosques attack support payments
- Information share Child Support payments currently being charged as income
- MSD lump sum payments for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Payments of Accommodation Supplement arrears due to system processing error from 1993 to 2014 for the first 12 months after payment is made
- Payments of arrears to Special Benefit clients better off on Temporary Additional Support for the first 12 months after payment is made
- Payments to clients whose Kāinga Ora tenancy was terminated due to methamphetamine contamination for the first 12 months after payment is made
- Residential Care Subsidy historic review refunds for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Severe weather event payments for the first 12 months from when payment is received (and any interest earned on the payment)
- specified Ex gratia and Compensation payments
- FamilyBoost Tax Credit payments for the first 12 months after payment is received
A bank overdraft is not considered a cash asset or resource available to a client.
Canterbury earthquake related payments
Payments made by the Crown, Earthquake Commission, insurance companies or the Canterbury Earthquake Commission (Red Cross) relating to the Canterbury earthquake are generally excluded for the first 12 or 24 months following the date the client received the payment.

chunks.title: Deduction of other assistance — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Deduction of other assistance
If a client (or their partner) has received any assistance under a welfare programme (such as Special Needs Grant or Recoverable Assistance) for their ordinary living expenses for their stand-down week, the amount paid must be deducted from the grant amount payable.
Note if no other assistance is paid, and the income in the stand-down week and the commencement week are the same (or there is no income), you will not need to calculate the benefit reduction due to income. The benefit rate will have already been assessed by SWIFTT for the first week's payment and this is the Student Allowance Transfer Grant amount payable.
For more information see:
- Examples of assessment

chunks.title: Example 1 — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Example 1
A couple with one dependent child is granted Jobseeker Support.
In their first stand-down week they earn $200.00 gross and get other assistance for ordinary living expenses of $100.00.
To work out the Student Allowance Transfer Grant payment reduction due to income:
Primary client (gross income excluding cents)

$28.00
To work out the Student Allowance Transfer Grant payable:
Maximum benefit (net as at 1 April 2026)
$669.40

Amount payable
$541.40
## Example 2
A single parent with one child and no other income got a Special Needs Grant for food of $75.00 within their stand-down week.
To work out the Student Allowance Transfer Grant payable:
Maximum benefit (net as at 1 April 2026)
$521.52

Amount payable
$446.52

chunks.title: Hardship — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Hardship
A client will generally be considered to be in hardship if they have:
- cash assets less than the maximum allowed and
- no other means of supporting themselves
## Cash asset limit
A client's (and partner's if any) combined cash assets must not be greater than the appropriate asset limit to receive a Student Allowance Transfer Grant.
For more information see:
- Cash assets
- Payment
- Calculating the payment
- Deduction of other assistance

chunks.title: Income limit — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Income limit
To be eligible for the Student Allowance Transfer Grant, the client must have a dependent partner or a dependent child. The income limit for the Student Allowance Transfer Grant applies where the client has a dependent partner but no dependent children.
When the client and their partner's combined gross income is over $569.40 (as at 1 April 2026) during the assessment week, the client will not be eligible for the grant.
If a client has a partner and a dependent child, the income limit is not applicable. The client may be eligible for the grant when they have a dependent child.
## When the income limit is applicable
Family circumstances
Income limit
Client and dependent partner with no dependent children
Yes
Gross income limit $569.40 per week (as at 1 April 2026)
Client with a dependent child
No income limit
Client and partner with a dependent child
No income limit

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The Student Allowance Transfer Grant is a payment that can be made to a client (or their partner) if they are in hardship during the stand-down week between the Student Allowance end date and the commencement of main benefit.
To qualify for this assistance, the client must have a dependent partner or a dependent child on the date that they are entitled to a main benefit.
The grant is equal to one week of the net main benefit rate the client (and partner) would be entitled to less:
- any reduction due to income earned in the stand-down week and
- any assistance paid under a welfare programme for ordinary living expenses (examples, Special Needs Grants or Recoverable Assistance) during that stand-down week
The Student Allowance Transfer Grant is non-recoverable and non-taxable.
Note if the stand-down is for more than one week, then the grant should be paid in the first week of the stand-down.
## Temporary removal of initial stand-downs between 23 March 2020 and 24 July 2021
Due to the impacts of COVID-19, initial stand-downs were temporarily removed for all clients applying for a main benefit when:
- their entitlement date and benefit grant date were on or after 23 March 2020 and
- their application and entitlement date were not later than 24 July 2021
Student Allowance Transfer Grants were not be available during this period.

chunks.title: Main benefit — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Main benefit
For the purposes of a Student Allowance Transfer Grant a main benefit is:
- Jobseeker Support
- Sole Parent Support
- Emergency Benefit (other than an emergency benefit payable under section 17(2)(c) of the New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001)
- Supported Living Payment
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
A main benefit does not include:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veterans Pension
- War Pension
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Orphans Benefit and
- non beneficiary assistance

chunks.title: Ordinary living expenses — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Ordinary living expenses
Examples of 'ordinary' living expenses would include:
- food
- telephone
- electricity / gas
- rent / board
Examples of 'non-ordinary' living expenses which do not affect the amount of this grant would include:
- dental bills
- extra medical expenses
- glasses

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Payment
A client or the partner can apply for the grant. The grant is paid to the applicant's bank account. Applications for the grant must be made on the Student Allowance Transfer Grant application form.
The client's main benefit must be granted before a Student Allowance Transfer Grant can be paid as entitlement to the benefit must be established first.
There is no limit to the number of applications the client or partner may make in a 52-week period. However, the client or partner can only receive one payment each time they transfer from the Student Allowance to a main benefit.
The amount of the grant payable during the stand-down week is:
- one week of the net main benefit rate (excluding supplementary assistance) payable to the client (and partner)
less
- any reduction due to income and
- the amount of any other assistance (Special Need Grants or Recoverable Assistance Payments) received for ordinary living expenses within the stand-down week e.g. food
Do not pay the Student Allowance Transfer Grant before the first day of the stand-down week.
These applications may need to be held until the stand-down week. You should still register the application and have the grant approved in the stand-down week.
Note if the income in the stand-down week and the commencement week are the same, you do not need to manually calculate the income reduction. The benefit rate will have already been assessed by SWIFTT for the first week's payment. Deduct any other assistance received for ordinary living expenses from this amount to determine the amount of Student Allowance Transfer Grant payable.
For more information see:
- Calculating the payment
- Deduction of other assistance
- Examples of assessment
- Student Allowance Transfer Grant application form

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > student allowance transfer grant
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
To be able to receive a Student Allowance Transfer Grant a client must:
- be a specified student (or partner of a specified student)
- be transferring from receiving a Student Allowance to a main benefit (whether or not the Student Allowance was payable because of income)
- on the date the client is entitled to that main benefit, have a dependent partner or a dependent child
- meet an income limit in certain circumstances
- be in hardship
- apply for a main benefit because the Student Allowance will stop for one of the following reasons: client will no longer be a secondary or tertiary studentclients allowance has stopped because the tertiary provider has lost their accreditationclients allowance has stopped because the student is sick, injured or on a break of 3 weeks or moreclients allowance will end because the recognised course of study has ended
- client will no longer be a secondary or tertiary student
- clients allowance has stopped because the tertiary provider has lost their accreditation
- clients allowance has stopped because the student is sick, injured or on a break of 3 weeks or more
- clients allowance will end because the recognised course of study has ended
- apply for a Student Allowance Transfer Grant before or within 28 calendar days after the end date for which the Student Allowance is payable
If the Student Allowance Transfer Grant application is received outside the 28 calendar days - and you can clearly establish the date of intent, you can use the intent date as the date of application and approve the grant.
The 28 calendar days described above took effect from 24 October 2014. Before 24 October 2014, the timeframe was 5 working days.
## Student Allowance suspended
A client cannot get a Student Allowance Transfer Grant if their Student Allowance is suspended due to:
- detention in a penal institution
- failure to attend or perform study
- failure of a full-time course of study (if the Student Allowance is suspended for this reason then a Student Allowance Transfer Grant cannot be granted)
- failure to give a statement when required
For more information see:
- Payment
- Core policy Relationship status for benefit

chunks.title: Abated Working for Families Tax Credits — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Abated Working for Families Tax Credits
Non-beneficiary clients and clients getting a New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension may have their Working for Families Tax Credits abated by Inland Revenue if they earn income in excess of the income threshold.
You would only include the actual or estimated amount of Working for Families Tax Credits that is payable at the time the client applies for Temporary Additional Support. Do not include any payments of Working for Families Tax Credits paid in the past.
## Example
If a client has received the full Working for Families Tax Credits entitlement for the tax year (eg in the first 6 months of that year) before applying for Temporary Additional Support, then this cannot be charged as income when assessing Temporary Additional Support. The amount of Working for Families Tax Credits you include is the actual or estimated amount payable at the time they apply for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Weekly qualifying accommodation costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: From 2 March 2026, a client's weekly qualifying accommodation costs are allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support. Temporary Additional Support paid prior to 2 March 2026 will be based on previous settings. The weekly qualifying accommodation cost is calculated based on the client's accommodation costs, the part of the property they live in and any accommodation income they get. These costs must also be essential to meet the family's daily living needs and could not be easily avoided or changed when the expense was incurred. MSD must check whether the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement. If the client is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement, this must be granted before MSD assesses whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: A client or any member of their family does not have to be getting Accommodation Supplement to have their costs included for Temporary Additional Support. If the client does not qualify for an Accommodation Supplement but has allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs, these costs are included in the assessment for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Accommodation deduction — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: An amount of $34.13 (as at 1 April 2026) is deducted from the total amount of allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs. For example, a client who has allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs of $250.00 per week will have $215.87 per week included in their assessment for Temporary Additional Support. For more information see: - Deskfile Allowable cost limits

chunks.title: Allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: A client's allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs must be determined to assess the rate of Temporary Additional Support a client can get. The weekly qualifying accommodation cost is calculated based on the client’s accommodation costs, the part of the property they live in and any accommodation income they get. Accommodation costs The following accommodation types are accommodation costs that can be assessed as allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs for Temporary Additional Support. Clients must provide verification of their accommodation costs, except for accommodation costs for any emergency housing contribution. - Rent - water rates can be included as a rental cost for the assessment of Temporary Additional Support when the rental property has a separate water meter and the tenancy agreement states the tenant is responsible for this cost. - Board - the amount allowed for Temporary Additional Support is 62% of the amount of board paid (excluding arrears) - Home ownership costs - Transitional housing contribution - clients who are staying in transitional housing funded by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development can include their transitional housing contribution (including any arrears) as an accommodation cost - Emergency housing contribution - clients who are staying in accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant for emergency housing can include their emergency housing contribution (including any arrears) as an accommodation cost Additional information is needed for clients who: - live in relocatable cabins, caravans, and motor homes - were once Idea Services residents - live in a retirement village - are retirement village residents with 'Licence to Occupy' - are in a rent to buy situation - become prisoners Accommodation costs that cannot be included The following accommodation costs cannot be included for Temporary Additional Support: - arrears the client incurred while they were getting an Accommodation Supplement, Accommodation Benefit (students), Rent Rebate Allowance, Tenure Protection Allowance or Income Related Rent - arrears for mortgage, rates and insurance - household consumables for e.g. gas, electricity or water - accommodation costs that are not for the part of the property the client lives in Not part of property they live in When a client doesn't live in part of their property, that part of the property is deducted from their accommodation costs when calculating the weekly qualifying accommodation costs. This includes when part of the property is: - primarily used for business purposes - self-contained and rented to another person/s or - rented to another person/s who does not reside there For information on how to calculate part of a property see: - Self-employed claiming home office expenses

chunks.title: Allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: - Homeowner renting out part of their property Accommodation income When a client gets rent, board or additional occupant contribution payments from someone living in the same premises, it is accommodation income and is deducted from their accommodation costs when calculating the weekly qualifying accommodation costs. Accommodation income includes: - rent a client gets from another person (not being additional occupants or boarders) residing in the same premises, except where the person paying the rent is in a self-contained part of the premises or the rent payment is part of the income of a business on the premises - 62% of payments for board a client gets from another person residing in the same premises, except where the board payment is part of the income of a business on the premises - 62% of contributions a client gets from an additional occupant residing in the same premises Note when accommodation income is more than the client's accommodation costs (after the deduction of the cost of any part of the property not being lived in by the client), the excess amount is income and must be charged against any financial assistance the client gets. In this case, the client will have no weekly qualifying accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Calculation — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: When calculating the weekly qualifying accommodation costs to assess Temporary Additional Support, the cost of part of the property not lived in must be deducted from the client's accommodation costs before any accommodation income. If a client is getting Accommodation Supplement, the weekly qualifying accommodation costs used to calculate Accommodation Supplement is the same amount to be used to calculate Temporary Additional Support. For example: Franky rents a 3-bedroom house for $850 per week. He uses his home to run a bespoke boat building business with a workshop in the double garage and a bedroom as an office. He calculates the percentage of home space used for his business to determine the business-related costs from using his home. Franky uses 45 percent of the property where he lives (135sqm/300sqm) for his bespoke boat building business and claims the portion of business home expenses of $19,890 per year ($382.50 per week) in his business accounts. Franky's friend, Chopper, also boards with him and pays $400 per week (62% of the board payment is $248 accommodation income). Franky's weekly qualifying accommodation costs for Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support exclude the portion of his home that he uses to run his business and are then reduced by 62% of the board payments he gets. His weekly qualifying accommodation costs are calculated as $219.50 per week. Cost of part of property not lived in Total rent costs for property Total A $850.00pw Total square metres Total B 300m2 Square metres of property that is used for business purposes Total C 135m2 Proportion of property used for business purposes Total C ÷ Total B = Total D 0.45 Cost of part of property not lived in Total A x Total D $382.50pw Accommodation income Board payment $400.00 Accommodation income (62% of the board payment) $248.00 Weekly qualifying accommodation costs Accommodation costs (rent) $850.00 Less cost of part of property not lived in $382.50 Less accommodation income $248.00 Equals weekly qualifying accommodation costs $219.50

chunks.title: Clients must take reasonable steps to reduce their accommodation costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: To qualify for Temporary Additional Support, when possible clients must take reasonable steps to reduce their costs, or increase their chargeable income.

chunks.title: Agreed period payments — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Agreed period payments
An agreed period payment is a written agreement of credit under a consumer credit contract or by other regular payments which must:
- be in writing
- have regular payments over an agreed period
- be for the purchase of an essential household item (excluding laundrette costs and telephone rental costs), a vehicle or a dryer
The client must provide satisfactory verification that they have purchased the essential item and that they are making regular repayments towards the item.
## Not included
Agreed period payments do not include:
- revolving credit payments
- Advance Payments of Benefits
- Recoverable Assistance Payments
For more information see:
- Allowable costs
- Hire or rental essential household items
- Consumer credit contract
- Revolving credit payments

chunks.title: Allowable costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Allowable costs
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support must be ongoing and regular expenses, calculated on a weekly basis.
The full list of allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support purposes is grouped in the following categories:
- Essential household items
- Employment-related costs
- Weekly qualifying accommodation costs
- Health and disability costs
- Formula-assessed Child Support costs
Also see:
- Allowable costs not in client's name
- Allowable cost limits
When a client has a cost not on the allowable cost list MSD should consider alternative assistance such as:
- Special Needs Grants
- Advance Payment of Benefit
- Recoverable Assistance Payments
## Hire purchases with deferred payment options
A client may have a hire purchase with a deferred payment option. This means the client doesn't need to make payments for some time. However, the client may decide to start paying for the item before the date stated in the terms of the contract.
Voluntary payments made before the client is required to make repayments cannot be included in Temporary Additional Support.
## Consolidating debt
When a personal loan has been taken out to consolidate debt which includes existing hire purchase repayments, MSD needs to calculate the amount for each allowable cost.
Determine the percentage of the total loan which is allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support to determine the cost to be included.

chunks.title: Allowable costs not in client's name — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Allowable costs not in client's name
Generally, costs not in the client's or partner's name are not included in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support as the client or partner is not liable for the repayments.
There may be situations where a client or their partner has entered an informal arrangement with another person to purchase an essential item using the other person's name and/or credit rating for the hire purchase agreement.
You need to be satisfied that the client or their partner is the person making the payments and that it was the intention of the parties to the informal arrangement that the client or their partner would have responsibility for the payments and would benefit from the use and control of the item.
Note you must also be satisfied that the client is responsible for the cost and has the use of the goods or service is required. The onus is on the client in the first instance to provide any further information required. Ask for further information if you are not satisfied.
A full statement from the client or partner and the other party is required along with a copy of the purchase agreement to determine if the cost can be included in the Temporary Additional Support assessment.
To assist in making a decision as to whether the client is responsible for the cost the following should be considered:
Why are the goods or service in another person's name? You will need to establish why the goods or service is not in the client's name. For example, but not limited to, is the client bankrupt and cannot obtain this essential goods or service item with their current credit rating?
Is it possible to transfer the goods or service into the client's name?
Has any other person contributed to the goods or service payments in any way?
Contact Helpline if you need assistance deciding whether or not the cost can be included.
For more information see:
- Allowable costs
- Qualifications

chunks.title: Alternative treatment — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Alternative treatment
MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for the costs of their alternative treatment.
If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for alternative treatment, it must be granted before MSD assess if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support. The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support when they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because:
- they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or
- their disability will last less than 6 months or
- they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include fees for alternative treatment needed by a client because of their disability.
The disability and need for alternative treatment must be verified by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner on the client's Disability Allowance medical certificate. The alternative treatment must be provided or supervised by a health practitioner.
The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are:
- additional and
- ongoing and
- directly related to the clients disability
Note as the alternative treatment must be provided or supervised by a health practitioner that practitioner must verify the costs of their services
The following cannot be included as allowable costs:
- alternative treatment that is not provided by or supervised by a registered health practitioner or
- treatment that is not additional or directly related to the client's disability
## Proof of alternative treatment costs
The client must provide:
- a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and
- proof of fees and the frequency of the alternative treatment (receipts or quotes from the registered health practitioner providing of the alternative treatment) and
- evidence that the alternative treatment is being supervised by or provided by a registered health practitioner (this can be confirmed by the client’s medical or nurse practitioner)
Note it is not appropriate for MSD to approach the health practitioner directly. The client should provide the receipts or quotes.

chunks.title: Ambulance fees and subscriptions — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Ambulance fees and subscriptions
You must check whether the client qualifies for Disability Allowance. If the client is entitled to a Disability Allowance, it must be granted before you assess whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support where they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because:
- they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or
- their health or disability condition will last less than 6 months or
- they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include ambulance fees or subscription fees, when:
- the fee is directly related to their disability and
- the cost is on an on-going basis
When considering whether to include ambulance fees and subscription fees as an allowable cost consider the following:
- is the client and/or their family likely to require ambulance services
- how regularly an ambulance would be required by the client and/or their family and
- how often the client and/or family have needed an ambulance in the past
The client should provide proof of fees and the frequency of the service.
Note ambulance fees and subscriptions should be treated as 'transport for personal health' for Temporary Additional Support.
## SWIFTT process
If a client or any family members are getting Disability Allowance, the total of their Disability Allowance costs contained in SWIFTT will automatically be included as allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support.
If the client or any family members do not qualify for a Disability Allowance and their ambulance and subscription fees are accepted as allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support you should to manually add them into the STAWA screen using the cost code 255 (Transport personal health).

chunks.title: Applicable excess costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Applicable excess costs
A client's applicable excess costs are the lesser amount of their:
- excess disability costs total and
- excess total costs
## Example
Chez is 17 years old and gets Supported Living Payment of $355.87 a week (as at 1 April 2026). For Chez, the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support is $106.76 (as at 1 April 2026). Chez's income deficiency is $115.00 a week and they have an excess disability costs total of $18.00 a week.
Excess total costs (A)
$8.24 ($115.00 - $106.76)
Excess disability costs total (B)
$18.00
Applicable excess costs
$8.24 (the lesser amount of (A) and (B))
The applicable excess costs of $8.24 are covered in full under the disability exception amount (as up to the first $100.00 of applicable excess costs are fully subsidised)

chunks.title: Application process for medical alarm when client is not getting Disability Allowance — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Application process for medical alarm when client is not getting Disability Allowance
When a client is applying for Temporary Additional Support and has costs for a monitored medical alarm they are not getting Disability Allowance for, they should be told that generally the medical alarm can only be included as an allowable cost for Temporary Additional Support if their medical alarm is provided by an accredited medical alarm supplier.
A current list of MSD-accredited medical alarm companies should be sent with the Disability Allowance - Medical Alarm Assessment form issued to a client applying for the cost of a medical alarm to be included as an allowable cost for Temporary Additional Support.
It is important clients are aware of the service they can expect from an accredited medical alarm supplier.

chunks.title: Assessing additional food costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Assessing additional food costs
Additional food expenditure must be verified by comparing the cost of the special diet with the cost of a regular diet.
Use the following table to assess the cost of additional foods.
