The dietitian recommending the diet should be able to supply details of the expected or average consumption of each item.

chunks.title: Authorised consumables — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for authorised consumables. If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, this must be granted before MSD assess if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support. The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support when they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because: - they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or - their disability will last less than 6 months or - they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include the ongoing cost of consumable items needed by a client because of a disability. A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client's disability, the need for treatment and that consumables are necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are: - additional and - ongoing and - directly related to the client's disability Some examples of consumable items commonly paid for are: - batteries for hearing aids - sensors for diabetic monitors - printer ribbons and paper for computers if the computer is necessary for the client's communications (e.g. a deaf person who doesn't communicate orally) - food, vet's fees etc for guide dog - incontinence pads if they are not provided through the Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support do not include: - items not directly related to the client's disability (e.g. art supplies, even if their registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner recommends them as beneficial for the client) or - one-off costs, such as buying a computer, nebuliser or blood glucose monitor (the client may qualify for assistance through Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora) or - items funded, subsidised, or provided through other agencies (e.g. items such as blood glucose monitoring strips, syringes, needles or pen devices used by diabetics; these items will usually be funded by Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora) If a client applies for Disability Allowance for an item that should be paid for through Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora or ACC, MSD should refer them to the correct organisation.

chunks.title: Authorised consumables — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: If the organisation won't cover the full cost (or there is excess), and the client has a letter from the organisation confirming this and stating why, then the cost can be included in Disability Allowance. An example might be a physiotherapy appointment that is partially funded under ACC.

chunks.title: Proof of authorised consumables costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: The client must provide: - a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and - receipts as proof of actual costs

chunks.title: Before 1 July 2021 - Formula for Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: On 1 July 2021, changes were made to the way the disability exception amount is calculated under the formula for Temporary Additional Support. When a client qualifies for the disability exception amount for a period before 1 July 2021, you will need to assess the client's Temporary Additional Support for that period using the formula for Temporary Additional Support that applied before 1 July 2021. Before 1 July 2021, the formula to calculate the weekly rate of Temporary Additional Support was as follows:

chunks.title: Step 1 - Calculate the client's disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the disposable income of the client and their partner (if any): Weekly chargeable income Less Weekly allowable costs Equals Disposable income

chunks.title: Step 2 - Calculate client's deficiency (or surplus) in their disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate whether there is a deficiency or surplus in the disposable income of the client and their partner (if any): Standard costs Less Disposable income (from step 1) Equals Deficiency (positive amount) or Surplus (negative amount) A client does not qualify for Temporary Additional Support if: - there is a surplus or - the deficiency is less than $1.00 If the client has a deficiency of $1.00 or more in their disposable income, they qualify for Temporary Additional Support. Go to Step 3 below.

chunks.title: Step 3 - Compare deficiency to upper limit of Temporary Additional Support to find lesser amount — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the client's upper limit for Temporary Additional Support then compare this amount to the deficiency. Upper limit 30% of the full net rate of main benefit payable to the client and their partner (if any) or for non-beneficiaries 30% of the appropriate net rate of Jobseeker Support, for the client and their partner if any, (except for certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants) Deficiency from step 2 Compare the above the rate of Temporary Additional Support is the lesser of the deficiency or the upper limit unless the client qualifies for a disability exception amount If the deficiency is less than the upper limit, the rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support is the deficiency. The client will not qualify for the disability exception amount. If the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, go to Step 4 below.

chunks.title: Step 4 - Calculate the disability exception amount (only if client qualifies) — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Determine if the client qualifies for a disability exception amount. The client qualifies for a disability exception amount if the client's deficiency is greater than the upper limit and they or their family have excess disability costs. If the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, calculate the excess disability costs total. This is the total amount of excess disability costs of the client and their family. Total all of the Disability Allowance costs for each family member (including any child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid) who has costs that exceed the maximum amount of Disability Allowance paid $0.00 Less the maximum rate of Disability Allowance paid for each family member (including any child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit) who is getting the maximum amount of Disability Allowance $ Equals excess disability costs total $ Disability exception amount - 30% of the excess disability costs total $ Note the excess disability costs total must not include any costs for counselling (including the costs of transport to attend counselling) that are above the maximum rate of Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Step 5 - Calculate the rate of Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the rate of Temporary Additional Support Upper limit (from step 3) $0.00 Plus disability exception amount (from step 4) $ Equals rate of Temporary Additional Support $

chunks.title: Board — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Board
MSD must check whether the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement in respect of their accommodation costs.
If the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement it must be granted before Temporary Additional Support can be paid for these costs.
If the client has a deficiency of income based on other allowable costs, they can get Temporary Additional Support. However, the accommodation costs must not be included until the Accommodation Supplement has been granted.
Board may still be included in Temporary Additional Support if the client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement.
Board is an arrangement where a person pays a set amount that includes the cost of residing at the premises along with food and may include other costs such as power, water, and internet. When a person pays board, 62% of their total payment is considered to be their accommodation cost (except arrears).
A person is considered to be a boarder when they are:
- making payments for their accommodation and food for residing at the premises and
- the accommodation costs can't be separately identified as part of the amount they pay
or
- living in a commercial boarding house and the amount they pay for residing at the premises includes accommodation and food costs.
## Additional occupant living in a social housing property
Additional occupants may pay a contribution towards accommodation costs while living in the social housing property.
The contribution amount may include food and sometimes other costs. Whether it includes food (and/or other costs) or not, only 62% of the contribution can be considered as their allowable accommodation cost. This means they are treated the same as a boarder.
## Joint tenants with shared food costs
Sometimes joint tenants, for example flatmates, will contribute money to cover shared costs. This could include cleaning suppliers, groceries, and service costs (e.g. power and internet).
When these costs are shared among all tenants, this is not board.
Note a client does not have to have their name on a tenancy agreement to be considered renting.
For more information see:
- Rent
- Rent includes service costs

chunks.title: Body corporate fees — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Body corporate fees
MSD must check whether the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement.
If the client is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement this must be granted before assessing whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
Body corporate fees may still be included in Temporary Additional Support if the client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement.
Body corporate is a term generally used when referring to cross-leased or shared properties where one or more properties are sited on the same land. The body corporate is made up of the owners of a unit-titled property under the Unit Titles Act 2010.
This can include accommodation such as townhouse complexes, apartment blocks and flats. Each unit has a separate legal title and is individually owned.
These homeowners are usually required to pay a regular fee or levy to cover joint expenses for the whole property.
Note body corporate fees can be included as repairs and maintenance in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support.
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their body corporate fees costs.

chunks.title: Calculating the rate for certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Calculating the rate for certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
The rate of Temporary Additional Support payment for certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants is the lesser of the:
- client's income deficiency or
- upper limit for refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
## Rate of payment
If the client is a refugee, protected person or residence applicant and meets the qualifications for Temporary Additional Support, the rate of Temporary Additional Support to pay should be calculated as follows:
Deficiency
Calculate deficiency after deducting the disposable income from the standard costs
Upper limit
30% of the net rate of unabated main benefit or for non-beneficiaries 30% of the appropriate net rate of unabated Jobseeker Support.
Compare the calculated deficiency to the calculated upper limit
If the deficiency is less than the upper limit, this is the rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support.
If the deficiency is greater than the upper limit, continue and compare the deficiency to the 'upper limit for refugees, protected persons or residence applicants'.
Upper limit for refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
Manually calculate the appropriate 'upper limit for refugees, protected persons or residence applicants' which is the greater of:
- the appropriate Accommodation Supplement maximum rate or
- 30% of the net rate of the applicant's unabated main benefit
Compare
Compare the calculated deficiency to the 'upper limit for refugees, protected persons or residence applicants'.
Rate of payment for refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
The rate for Temporary Additional Support is the lesser of the deficiency or the 'upper limit for refugees, protected persons or residence applicants'.
## Disability exception amount
Refugees, protected persons or residence applicant clients (or any family member) do not qualify for the disability exception amount, as they do not qualify for Disability Allowance.
However, if they have a family member who is getting Disability Allowance, the client may qualify for the disability exception amount.

chunks.title: Step 1 - Calculate client's disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the amount of disposal income. MSD needs to determine the client's, and partner's, (if any) weekly amount of chargeable income, and weekly amount of allowable costs. Weekly chargeable income $0.00 Less Weekly allowable costs $ Equals Disposable income $

chunks.title: Step 2 - Calculate client's deficiency (or surplus) in their disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the deficiency or surplus. Standard costs No dependent children - 70% of net full main benefit, New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension rate With dependent children - 70% of net full main benefit, New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension rate plus 70% of full net rate of family tax credit (For non-beneficiaries use 70% of the appropriate full net rate for Jobseeker Support) $0.00 Less Disposable income $ Equals Deficiency (positive amount) Surplus (negative amount) $ A client does not qualify for Temporary Additional Support if: - there is a surplus or - the deficiency is less than $1.00

chunks.title: Step 3 - Compare deficiency to upper limit to find lesser amount — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the client's upper limit for Temporary Additional Support then compare the upper limit amount to the deficiency. Upper limit (30% of the net rate of full main benefit, New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension rate payable to the client or for non-beneficiaries 30% of the appropriate full net rate of Jobseeker Support) $0.00 Deficiency (from step 2) $ Compare: the upper limit to the deficiency. The rate for Temporary Additional Support is the lesser amount unless the client qualifies for a disability exception amount. $ If the deficiency is less than the upper limit, the rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support is the deficiency. The client will not qualify for a disability exception amount. If the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, go to step 4 below.

chunks.title: Step 4 - Calculate the disability exception amount (if client qualifies) — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Determine if the client qualifies for a disability exception amount. The client will qualify for a disability exception amount if the client's deficiency is greater than the upper limit, and they or their family have excess disability costs. Step 4(a) - Calculate the excess disability costs total If the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, calculate the excess disability costs total. This is the total amount of excess disability costs of the client and their family, including any child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid. Family member Total amount of allowable Disability Allowance costs Less the maximum amount of Disability Allowance payable Excess disability costs Client $ $82.85 (maximum as at 1 April 2026) $ Partner $ $82.85 (maximum as at 1 April 2026) $ Child 1 $ $82.85 (maximum as at 1 April 2026) $ Child 2 $ $82.85 (maximum as at 1 April 2026) $ Excess disability costs total $ The excess disability costs total must not include any costs for counselling (including the costs of transport to attend counselling) that are above the maximum rate of Disability Allowance. Step 4(b) - Calculate the excess total costs A client's excess total costs are the client and their partner's (if any) deficiency in their disposable income minus the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support. Excess total costs are the costs that are not already covered by the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support. Deficiency $0.00 Less the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support $ Excess total costs $ Step 4(c) - Calculate applicable excess costs Calculate the client's applicable excess costs to determine what amount to use to calculate the disability exception amount. A client's applicable excess costs is the lesser amount of their: - excess disability costs total and - excess total costs Excess disability costs total $0.00 (A) Excess total costs $0.00 (B) Applicable excess costs Lesser amount of (A) and (B) Step 4(d) - Calculate the disability exception amount using the client's applicable excess costs The disability exception amount provides a full subsidy for a client's applicable excess costs amount of up to $100. If the client has any applicable excess costs remaining after the full subsidy has been applied, these are subsidised at 30% of the remaining applicable excess costs amount.

chunks.title: Step 4 - Calculate the disability exception amount (if client qualifies) — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Applicable excess costs amount will be fully subsidised up to $100 Up to $100 (C) Find 30% of remaining balance of applicable excess costs not covered above (if any) 30% x remaining applicable excess (D) Disability exception amount Add (C) and (D) together

chunks.title: Step 5 - Calculate the rate of Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the rate of Temporary Additional Support. Upper limit (from step 3) $0.00 Plus Disability exception amount (from step 4 (d)) $ Equals rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support $ Note Temporary Additional Support is calculated differently for certain refugee and protected person applicants, and applicants for residence.

chunks.title: Calculating the rate of Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Calculating the rate of Temporary Additional Support
The rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support is the lesser of the:
- client's income deficiency or
- upper limit of Temporary Additional Support
unless the client qualifies for a disability exception amount. If the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, their rate of Temporary Additional Support will be the upper limit plus the disability exception amount.
Note a client does not qualify for Temporary Additional Support if the calculation results in the client's income deficiency being less than $1.00 or in a surplus of income.

chunks.title: Relocatable cabins, caravans, and motor homes — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Relocatable cabins, caravans, and motor homes
MSD must check whether the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement. If the client is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement this must be granted before assessing whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
Relocatable cabin, caravan or motor home costs may still be included in Temporary Additional Support if the client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement.
If a client lives in a relocatable cabin, caravan, or motor home, they may have more than one type of accommodation cost. Temporary Additional Support can only be paid for one accommodation cost type at a time. In these cases, Temporary Additional Support is generally assessed on the cost of the cabin, caravan, or motor home as this is the place the client occupies as a home.
## More than one accommodation cost type
If a client has more than one type of accommodation cost, assess them as a:
- homeowner if they are repaying a loan for the purchase of the cabin, caravan, or motor home
- renter if they are renting the cabin, caravan, or motor home
For example, Enzo pays $180 a week to rent the cabin he lives in. He owns the land the cabin is situated on and pays $4412 a year for local authority rates. Enzo is considered renting, and his Temporary Additional Support is assessed on rent of $180 a week.
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Cash assets test — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Cash assets test
A client will not be able to get Temporary Additional Support if they (and their partner if any) have cash assets equal to or more than:
Single person
Asset limit for a single person without dependent children
Married, civil union or de facto,
and sole parents
Asset limit for a married, civil union or de facto couple with or without dependent children
Note the sole parent asset limit is the same as the married, civil union or de facto rate.

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: When a client receiving Temporary Additional Support intends to be absent from New Zealand, you will need to determine if payment of Temporary Additional Support can continue. Clients can be absent from New Zealand, and continue to receive payment for the first 28 days, if it does not affect the client's eligibility for Temporary Additional Support. To decide if someone still meets the eligibility for Temporary Additional Support, you will need to decide each case on its own merits taking all of the client's circumstances into account. To pay Temporary Additional Support while the client is absent from New Zealand depends on whether the client is also receiving a main benefit. When assessing the period of absence, do not include: - the date of departure from New Zealand and - the date of return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Clients receiving a main benefit — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: All clients getting a main benefit must advise Work and Income before they leave New Zealand. If the client or partner does not advise Work and Income before their international travel, their benefit payments (including Temporary Additional Support) must stop. When a client is paid their main benefit while they are absent from New Zealand (either because they qualify for approved travel, or the requirement for approved travel does not apply to them) they can keep getting their main benefit and their Temporary Additional Support. When a client qualifies they can keep getting payments for up to 28 days in any 52 week period. If a client qualifies they may be paid their main benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. Clients who do not keep getting their main benefit while overseas (because they don't qualify for approved travel) may still be able to continue to keep getting Temporary Additional Support, if their absence does not affect the client's eligibility for this assistance and they advised Work and Income of their absence before their international travel. This is limited to 28 days in a 52 week period. For more information about Absence from New Zealand see: - Approved travel reasons in relevant main benefit - Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period in relevant main benefit

chunks.title: Clients receiving non-beneficiary Extra Help — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: Clients who are receiving Temporary Additional Support, but do not get a main benefit: - must advise of their departure from New Zealand and - can be absent and paid their Temporary Additional Support for up to 28 days per absence when it does not affect the client's eligibility for Temporary Additional Support

chunks.title: Information required from client when advising they intend to travel — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: When a client getting a main benefit contacts you to advise that they intend travelling overseas, you need to obtain the following information: - date of departure - date of return - whether their costs are continuing

chunks.title: Non-beneficiary Extra help payment will not continue — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: When payment of Temporary Additional Support is stopped because the client does not meet the eligibility criteria due to their absence you will need to suspend the benefit from: - the day after departure

chunks.title: Permanent absence — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: If the client is leaving New Zealand permanently, Temporary Additional Support should be cancelled from the day after departure.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
Clients have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Temporary Additional Support and it is expected that they will do so as soon as possible.
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising Work and Income of a change in circumstances within 14 days you may reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the first available date.
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information you must review Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
Clients have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Temporary Additional Support and it is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be 14 days.
Note income must be charged against the Temporary Additional Support for the week(s) in which the income is earned or represents.
For more information see:
- Change in income
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event and does not have a good and sufficient reason, you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Temporary Additional Support, it is expected they will do so within a reasonable period.
As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days of the date their costs change.
For clients who have a change in formula-assessed Child Support costs, they generally must notify MSD within 14 days of the date Inland Revenue notifies them of the change. This is likely to be a different date from the date their costs changed.
## Good and sufficient reason
When there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising MSD of a change in circumstances within 14 days, you may reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the first available date.
## No good and sufficient reason
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event and does not have a good and sufficient reason, you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
If a client advises MSD of a decrease in their formula-assessed Child Support costs more than 14 days after the date Inland Revenue notifies them of the change, without a good and sufficient reason for the delay, you should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the date the client was notified of the change. You may need to establish an overpayment if appropriate.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Temporary Additional Support it is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. A reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
When a client advises of a change in circumstances more than 14 days after the event MSD should generally reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising MSD of a change in circumstances within 14 days MSD may reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the first available date.
## False or misleading information
If the client gives false or misleading information MSD must review Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Avoiding a debt — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Avoiding a debt
When a non-beneficiary client dies, Temporary Additional Support generally stops from the day after the date of death. You must take all possible steps to stop payments from this date.
When payment cannot be stopped from the day after the date of death there is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days after the date of death. You can use this discretion to stop payment from the first available date, that is, the earliest date that you can stop payments from so that no overpayment is established.
However, when there has been a deliberate intent to delay advising Work and Income of the client's death you should stop payment from the day after the date of death and establish an overpayment.
Note under no circumstances can payment continue for more than 28 days after the date of death.
For more information see:
- Terminal benefit

chunks.title: Change in accommodation — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Change in accommodation
MSD will need to review Temporary Additional Support to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's accommodation. This includes when there is a change in the clients accommodation costs and/or a change to the part of the property they live in. MSD will need to update and reassess the clients allowable weekly qualifying accommodation costs.
MSD will also need to check whether the client's other allowable costs have changed.
Note MSD must review the client's Accommodation Supplement before reviewing their Temporary Additional Support.
The date to review Temporary Additional Support from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:
Increase
- increase Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances
Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information MSD must review Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Change in accommodation income — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Change in accommodation income
Clients must tell MSD when they start getting accommodation income or there is a change in accommodation income they get from renters, boarders or additional occupants so the correct rate of Temporary Additional Support can be paid.
When there is a change in accommodation income that a client gets, review their Temporary Additional Support to make sure they still meet the qualifications and are getting the correct rate of payment.
The date to review Temporary Additional Support from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:
Increase
- increase Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances
Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event

chunks.title: Change in assets — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Change in assets
You will need to review Temporary Additional Support to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's cash assets.
The date to review Temporary Additional Support from will depend on the action involved. Generally, you should:
## Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
## Income
Income is charged against the Temporary Additional Support for the week(s) in which the income is earned or represents.
For more information see:
- Change in income

chunks.title: Change in costs — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Change in costs
You will need to review Temporary Additional Support to make sure the client is getting the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's existing costs.
For more information see:
- Allowable costs
Note when the client has applied for new costs to be included, you should follow the commencement date rules. Allowable costs can only be added from the date the client applied to include the new cost.
The date to review Temporary Additional Support from will depend on the action involved. Generally, you should:
## Increase
- increase Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances
Note there are transitional arrangements when including formula-assessed Child Support costs for current Temporary Additional Support clients in the period 1 July 2023 to 29 September 2023.
For more information see:
- Formula-assessed Child Support costs
## Reduce, suspend or cancel
- reduce, suspend or cancel Temporary Additional Support from the first available date except when the client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event.
Note when a client has a decrease in formula-assessed Child Support costs, this is treated differently. Clients generally must tell MSD of a change within 14 days of the date Inland Revenue notifies the client of the outcome of their reassessment. This may be a different date than the date their costs changed.

chunks.title: Change in family circumstances — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Change in family circumstances
MSD should review Temporary Additional Support to make sure that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the:
- client's relationship status or
- the number of dependent children in the client's care
The date to review Temporary Additional Support from will depend on the action involved. Generally, MSD should:

chunks.title: Change in income — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Change in income
MSD will need to review Temporary Additional Support to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment whenever there is a change in the client's income.
Income must be charged against Temporary Additional Support for the week(s) in which the income is earned or represents.
If income does not represent a specific period or if MSD cannot determine the actual period it represents, MSD must determine the most appropriate period to charge the income. This may be the week it is received, provided or supplied.
## Variable income
Where a client has variable income, (for example wages) the income is charged for the week in which the income was earned.
If the client is unsure of the exact amount of income that they will earn, they should provide an estimate of their income. This will help to reduce any debt being established for the client.
If a client's actual income differs from the estimate given they must inform Work and Income of the correct amount and their rate of benefit should be reviewed.
The correct amount of income should still be charged for the week in which the income was earned.
For more information see:
- Chargeable income
- Change in assets

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Temporary Additional Support.
MSD may also review Temporary Additional Support at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.

chunks.title: Child leaves sole parents care suddenly — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Child leaves sole parents care suddenly
When a sole parent client stops caring for a dependent child because of a sudden change of circumstances beyond the control of the client, payment of Temporary Additional Support paid for the child leaving care may continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child stopped being dependent.
This is to allow a period of transition for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.
For example when a child suddenly goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki payments will continue for 28 days from the date the child is no longer dependent on the client.
During the 28 day continuation of payment, if the client has other changes of circumstances such as a change in accommodation costs, the rate of Temporary Additional Support will need to be reassessed using the sole parent threshold rates.
SWIFTT will automate the 28 day extension payment from the effective date of the child being excluded.
Use reason code 331 (Child left care-unforeseen circumstances) to exclude the child in the SCHIE screen.

chunks.title: Client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Client advises of a change more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes that may affect their entitlement to Temporary Additional Support, it is expected they will do so within a reasonable period.
As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days of the date their costs change.
For clients who have a change in formula-assessed Child Support costs, they generally must notify MSD within 14 days of the date Inland Revenue notifies them of the change. This is likely to be a different date from the date their costs changed.
## False or misleading information
If a client gives false or misleading information you must review Temporary Additional Support from the actual date of the change in circumstances and establish an overpayment if appropriate.

chunks.title: Surviving partner or dependent child — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Surviving partner or dependent child
When a client dies (and there is a surviving partner or dependent child) before a decision is made on an application or review for Temporary Additional Support, you can continue the application or review process as if the client had not died.

chunks.title: Client in new relationship — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Client in new relationship
When a client enters into a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship, you will have to determine if the client and their spouse or partner qualify for Temporary Additional Support or Special Benefit.
As soon as a client enters into a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship they no longer have entitlement to a single or sole parent rate of benefit.
## Clients receiving Special Benefit
If either person in a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship was receiving a Special Benefit, immediately before they entered into the marriage, civil union or de facto relationship they can:
- continue to receive Special Benefit if they continue to qualify or
- choose to receive Temporary Additional Support if the couple qualify
If the client chooses to continue to receive Special Benefit, you will have to re-assess the rate of Special Benefit based on the couple’s circumstances.
Note one partner in a current marriage, civil union or de facto relationship cannot choose to receive Temporary Additional Support if the other partner continues to receive Special Benefit.
## Type of payment to be considered
The following table summarises which type of payment you should consider when a client enters into a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship.

Married, civil union or de facto couple may be eligible for:
