## Example
John is a non-beneficiary client who is currently receiving Temporary Additional Support. John enters into a marriage with Susan who receives a main benefit and a Special Benefit.
As Susan can continue to receive a Special Benefit, the couple is assessed to see if they qualify for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support. As the couple is eligible for both, but will receive more on Special Benefit, they choose to have Special Benefit continue at the newly assessed rate.

chunks.title: Client's relationship ends — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Client's relationship ends
When a client's marriage, civil union or de facto relationship ends, you will have to determine if the client and their spouse or partner qualify separately for Temporary Additional Support or Special Benefit.
If Temporary Additional Support had been paid to the couple, each person's eligibility should be assessed for Temporary Additional Support based on that person's circumstances when the relationship ends.
If Special Benefit had been paid to the couple, each person's eligibility should be assessed for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support based on that person's circumstances when the relationship ends. If the eligibility criteria are met for both Temporary Additional Support and Special Benefit, each person can choose to receive one or the other forms of assistance, but not both.
Note if a person chooses to cancel Special Benefit and receive Temporary Additional Support, they cannot be granted Special Benefit at a later date.
## Example 1
Tane and Maria are in a relationship and together have been getting a main benefit and Special Benefit as a couple since 2002. In 2018 the relationship ends and each gets a main benefit at the single rate.
Tane is assessed based on his new circumstances and he qualifies for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support. Tane chooses to get Special Benefit as it is the most appropriate for his circumstances.
After the relationship, Maria also qualifies for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support. Maria chooses to get Temporary Additional Support as she will receive a higher rate of assistance.
## Example 2
In 2008, Kate and Billy are married. Kate, previously a non-beneficiary, is included in Billy's main benefit and Special Benefit. In 2018, Kate and Billy end their relationship.
Billy qualifies for both Special Benefit and Temporary Additional Support. He chooses to continue to get Special Benefit at the newly assessed rate.
Kate is not eligible for Special Benefit as she was not getting, or had not applied for, Special Benefit immediately before 1 April 2006. She also does not qualify for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Court attachment orders — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Court attachment orders
All court attachment requests are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing. Court attachments are administered via the CORBI screen in SWIFTT.
The Ministry of Justice has the authority to make attachment orders on benefits to meet outstanding court fines. The attachment order may include:
- court finesthese are fines payable to the District Court
- civil attachmentsthese are generally paid to a private individual or organisation that is owed money. Occasionally a District Court will act as a collection agent for civil debts.
Attachment Orders issued by the Ministry of Justice can be made under either the Summary Proceedings Act 1957 or the District Court Act 2016.
## Priority for deductions
Court attachment orders do not take priority over any Child Support deductions, Ministry of Social Development deductions, Inland Revenue deductions or any attachment order made under the Family Proceedings Act.
For more information see:
## Information provided by the Court
The information that will be received from the Ministry of Justice will have:
- the client's name
- the amount to be deducted from the benefit
- the fine's reference number
If a client is suffering undue hardship because of the amount of the attachment order then they should be directed to the Registrar of the District Court for a reassessment of the rate.
For more information see:
- Court request for information

chunks.title: Receiving a main benefit — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Receiving a main benefit
When a client is receiving a main benefit, Temporary Additional Support stops from the same date as the main benefit.
For more information see:
- Death of a client in the relevant main benefit
## Non-beneficiaries
For non-beneficiary clients Temporary Additional Support generally stops from the day after the date of death. However, there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the date of death:
- to avoid creating a debt or
- as terminal benefit when there are other circumstances that justify payment
Note when a client has a Community Services or SuperGold Card [no link find out why] , the card must be manually cancelled and death details added to Person Details latch in CMS.
Contact the Card Centre on 0800 999 999 or email csc_enquiries (MSD) if you have trouble with this process.
## Cost of funeral
The person responsible for the cost of the funeral may be able to receive a Funeral Grant.
For more information see:
- Death of a married, civil union or de facto client
- Death of a dependent child
- Client dies before grant or review
- Debt recovery
- Verification

chunks.title: Death of a dependent child — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Death of a dependent child
When a dependent child dies, Temporary Additional Support needs to be reviewed to check that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
There is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the date of death. To help decide whether to continue payment see:
- Terminal benefit

chunks.title: Death of a married, civil union or de facto client — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Death of a married, civil union or de facto client
When a married, civil union or de facto client dies you will need to review the surviving partner's Temporary Additional Support to ensure they still meet the qualifications and are receiving the correct rate of payment.
The Temporary Additional Support should be reviewed from the day following death.

chunks.title: Inland Revenue deduction notices — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
Inland Revenue may request for a client's unpaid taxes to be directly deducted from their benefit payments.
Note all Inland Revenue deduction notices are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
The instructions of the deduction notice will be to deduct the lowest of either:
- 10% of the total debt which Inland Revenue specify in the notice, on a weekly basis or
- 20% of the client's gross earnings on a weekly basis
Where there are insufficient funds to cover the deduction, Work and Income must advise Inland Revenue immediately that the deduction will not start or will start at a reduced rate.
Inland Revenue deductions have a lower priority than Child Support deductions.
For more information see:

chunks.title: IRD number for partner who is not apportioned assistance — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: As part of a review of Temporary Additional Support, MSD may make a written request to the client for evidence of a partner's IRD number when the: - partner is not being apportioned the primary client's Temporary Additional Support, and - partner's income is relevant to a client's Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Notice following an unsuccessful match — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about a partner's IRD number. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information, or there's an error, MSD should ask the client (in writing) to provide evidence of their partner's IRD number, unless there are significant barriers to providing this. In the written request for evidence of the IRD number, MSD must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and the match was unsuccessful, and - giving the client or partner a minimum of 10 working days to provide their partner's IRD number evidence or the client's assistance may be suspended. Example Isla is receiving Temporary Additional Support. Isla's partner, Ariki, has income that is included in MSD's income test to determine eligibility for Temporary Additional Support and MSD holds an IRD number for Ariki. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Ariki's IRD number. As part of a review of Isla's assistance, MSD provides a notice in writing, giving 10 working days for Isla to provide evidence of Ariki's IRD number. MSD's decision to give 10 working days to provide evidence is based on: - Ariki already having an IRD number - Ariki not having any significant barriers to getting evidence of their IRD number - MSD's obligation to provide a minimum of 10 working days to provide the information.

chunks.title: MSD may suspend assistance if evidence is not received — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD may suspend all taxable and income tested assistance the client is getting, including Temporary Additional Support, if a partner's IRD number evidence is not provided within a reasonable timeframe (usually 10 working days) or within the extended period if this has been applied. In rare cases, depending on the client's circumstances, assistance may be cancelled or the rate of payment varied. Note suspension does not apply to Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: IRD number not required in some circumstances — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD may not need evidence of an IRD number when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - significant factors, that are outside the client's or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of their IRD number, (e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence), and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided. A partner's IRD number and evidence of their IRD number does not need to be provided when they are not a New Zealand tax resident. MSD can determine a later point to request the evidence of the IRD number. For more information see: - Non-tax resident partner's IRD number not required Note there is different guidance for requesting evidence of an IRD number for clients and partners who are apportioned part of the client's assistance payments or when a client is applying for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Step one - Mismatch identified — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: A mismatch of information will be identified when a client's accommodation type or amount differs from what a client who is a head tenant or homeowner has declared they are getting, or a renter or boarder has declared they are paying. MSD must try to contact both clients within one working day of identifying the mismatch to check and confirm the correct details. If one or both clients are uncontactable within one working day, but a message is left for the client/s to make contact, MSD must consider whether it is reasonable to allow the one working day to lapse before moving to the next step in the process. When one or both clients have been contacted, and it is clear the mismatch cannot be resolved within one working day, or one or both clients are uncontactable and a message cannot be left, MSD can continue to the next step in the process. Note the one working day ends on the close of the working day following the day the mismatch is identified. Example: Englebert lives with Alphonse, and they both get Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. Englebert pays his rent to Alphonse who owns the property. On Wednesday 6 May, Englebert advises MSD his rent will be increasing from $350 per week to $360 per week from next Monday. Alphonse has not yet advised MSD of this change. On Thursday 7 May (within one working day of identifying the payment amount mismatch), MSD contacts Englebert to confirm he intended to declare a change in his rent amount. Alphonse contacts MSD later that day to advise that Englebert's rent will be increasing to $360 from next Monday. MSD updates both clients' payments from next Monday and the mismatch has been resolved.

chunks.title: Step three - Response to the notification of mismatch — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: Contact from client/s and mismatch resolved within 10 working days When the client/s make contact and confirm the correct details within 10 working days, the details should be updated and any assistance reviewed accordingly. This means the mismatch is now resolved. No contact from client/s When one or both clients don't make contact within 10 working days to confirm their rent, board or additional occupant contribution payment information, the mismatch is unable to be resolved, and both clients Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit must be suspended. If the client is a social housing tenant and the mismatch is not resolved, MSD will notify the housing provider that the client's Income Related Rent must be set to market rent for the property. Community Housing Providers have a discretion not to set the client's rent to the market rent rate. The standard 60-day notice period will apply. Example: Astrid and Rex live together, and Rex pays board to Astrid. They both get Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support as non-beneficiaries. Astrid receives a mandatory review for her Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. On Tuesday 9 June, she responds before her review due date confirming that she receives $10 more in board from Rex. The new amount is different from what MSD holds for Rex. MSD checks with Astrid on Wednesday 10 June (within one working day of identifying the mismatch) to see if she advised of the increase in error. She confirms the increase is correct. On Wednesday 10 June, MSD tries contacting Rex to confirm the new rate, but he doesn't respond. On Thursday 11 June (after the one working day has lapsed), MSD sends both Astrid and Rex notification of the mismatch and provides 10 working days to resolve it and advise MSD. Rex does not respond to the request for information by close of day Tuesday 23 June (within 10 working days). MSD suspends Rex's Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support from Wednesday 24 June (11th working day). Astrid's Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support is also suspended from Wednesday 24 June as MSD cannot verify the information she has declared is correct. If Rex does not respond within 8 weeks, both Astrid and Rex's Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support will be cancelled.

chunks.title: Priority for deductions — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Priority for deductions
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others. The following list gives the order of priority, highest to lowest:
Highest priority
- Child Support deductions made under the Child Support Act 1991
- Inland Revenue tax deductions
- Ministry of Social Development debt repayments including Liable Parent Contributions (LPC), child maintenance debts and Major Repairs Advances (MRA), Student Allowance debt, Student Loan debt converted to Ministry of Social Development debt, Income Related Rent historical Housing New Zealand debt, Income Related Rent Ministry of Social Development debt
- Attachment orders made under the Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Court attachment orders issued under the Summary Proceedings Act 1957
- Court attachment orders issued under the District Court Act 2016
- Student Loan repayments
Lowest priority
Determining the priority of deductions is necessary when a client has more than one order in respect of their benefit. Also each order and deduction notice is subject to its own protected earnings rate.
When you need to reduce deductions you adjust from the lowest priority up to those with a higher priority taking into account the protected earnings rules for each.

chunks.title: Protected earnings rate — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: Both the District Court Act and the Summary Proceedings Act provide that every attachment order must specify a 'protected earnings rate'. The protected earnings rate is usually 60% of the client's net earnings after PAYE tax has been deducted or withheld. If the attachment order will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate, then the order will not operate and MSD must cancel or return the attachment order to the Court, Ministry of Justice. Calculating the client's income differs between attachment orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act and the District Court Act, as different benefits are included. Therefore it is important to determine what type of attachment order has been issued. Summary Proceedings Act 1957 For orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act, the calculation of the client's income does not include Special Benefit, Disability Allowance, Child Disability Allowance, Temporary Additional Support, Winter Energy Payment, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit. District Court Act 2016 For orders made under the District Court Act, the client's income includes Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit and Disability Allowance but does not include Child Disability Allowance, and Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Example — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text: An attachment order is received from the Ministry of Justice for $75.00 per week. The attachment order shows that the client's protected earnings rate is $295.83 per week. The client's attachment order falls under the District Court Act 2016. The client's Temporary Additional Support is therefore included as income. We need to calculate whether adding the deduction of $75.00 per week will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate: Calculate protected earnings rate Jobseeker Support - single person 25+ net rate (as at 1 April 2026) $372.55 Plus Accommodation Supplement (Area 3) $80.00 Plus Temporary Additional Support (Weekly qualifying accommodation costs (Rent) $202.00 less $33.10 accommodation deduction ($168.90) + vehicle repayments ($50.00) and + Television repayments ($20.00)) $40.50 Total net earnings $493.05 60% of total net earnings (= protected earnings) $295.83 Calculate if Attachment Order will exceed protected earnings Total net earnings $493.05 Less Child Support deduction $55.00 Less Ministry of Social Development debt $70.00 Sub total $368.05 Less Attachment Order $75.00 Total net income remaining for the client per week $293.05 The attachment order amount of $75.00 takes the client's total net income remaining to $293.05, which is below the protected earnings rate of $295.83 per week. The attachment order will not operate therefore MSD must return it to the Ministry of Justice for the order to be amended.

chunks.title: Re-applying for Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Re-applying for Temporary Additional Support
Temporary Additional Support can be paid for a maximum period of 13 weeks only.
If the client still needs help with their regular essential living costs and they have received Temporary Additional Support for the maximum 13 week period, they must re-apply.
The client must:
- meet all the qualifications and
- complete a re-application form for Temporary Additional Support

chunks.title: Terminal benefit — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit
When a non-beneficiary client dies, Temporary Additional Support generally stops from the day after the date of death. However, there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days. When payment is continued after the date of death, it is referred to as terminal benefit.
Circumstances where you might consider continued payment beyond a client's date of death include:
- when the deceased client's domestic situation results in a transition cost for a family member, causing hardshipExample: accommodation and other household costs when client has been sharing accommodation
or
- when there are exceptional and justified costs associated with the death of the clientExample: multiple deaths within one family
You should not continue payment for 28 days following the death of a client to meet funeral expenses. A Funeral Grant is available for this purpose.
For more information see:
- Avoiding a debt
- Terminal benefit rate

chunks.title: Terminal benefit rate — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit rate
The provision to continue the payment for up to 28 days following the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit.
Temporary Additional Support is continued at the rate which was payable to the client at the date of death.
## SWIFTT
If you are paying terminal benefit you will need to manually calculate entitlement and make an adhoc payment in the SAHPA screen.
There is no automatic provision for the payment of terminal benefit for Temporary Additional Support in this case on SWIFTT.

chunks.title: Transfers — extra help > temporary additional support > changes and reviews temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Transfers
MSD must review a client’s Temporary Additional Support to ensure they still meet the qualifications and are getting the correct rate of payment when the client moves between the following categories:
- main benefit
- New Zealand Superannuation of Veterans Pension or
- non-beneficiary

chunks.title: Chargeable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Chargeable income
Chargeable income is any income or earnings (after tax and/or ACC levies) the client or partner are getting, before any deductions or attachment orders for debt, liability, sanction, penalty, child support payments or student loan repayments.
Chargeable income includes but is not limited to:
- wages or salary
- the net rate of any benefit received (except Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit or Childcare Assistance)
- Working for Families Tax Credits
- Paid parental leave
- War pensions or allowances
- New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
- Accommodation Supplement
- Rent and 62% of board payments a client gets in excess of their accommodation costs (after the deduction of the cost of any part of the property not being lived in by the client)
- 62% of additional occupant contributions a client gets in excess of their market rent
- Blind subsidies
- Child Disability Allowance
- information share Child Support payments
- non-information share Child Support payments
- formula-assessed Child Support for liability periods before 1 July 2023 paid in excess of the benefit rate
- formula-assessed Child Support paid in excess of the Unsupported Child's Benefit rate (including mixed Child Support payments)
- COVID-19 Income Relief Payment
- Disability Allowance (including the amount of Special Disability Allowance and any Disability Allowance paid for children getting an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit)
- Student Allowance
- Accommodation Benefit paid to students
- Independent Circumstances Allowance
- the living costs component of a Student Loan
- any regular periodical payments made under any Welfare Programmes paid to replace lost income
- weekly amounts of Accident Compensation paid to replace lost income
- Flexi-Wage Self Employment weekly subsidy (excluding the GST component of 15%) and any income generated from the business
- any voluntary portion of an overseas pension
Note chargeable income is the net rate of any benefit received before any deduction or sanction, for example (but not limited to) deductions for overseas pension.

chunks.title: Childcare if the caregiver is incapacitated — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Childcare if the caregiver is incapacitated
The net cost of childcare (after the deduction of any childcare or OSCAR subsidy that is payable) up to a maximum of $6 per hour can be included in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support where the client or their partner is disabled or seriously ill.
In addition, these costs must be essential to meet the family's daily living needs and could not be readily avoided or varied when the expense was incurred.
Allowable childcare costs can be included in Temporary Additional Support where the childcare provider is not a recognised childcare organisation.
## Reasonable steps
You need to consider that if a recognised childcare organisation can be used by the client and would cost less than the childcare provider being used, then a reasonable step could be to change their childcare provider.
For more information about this see:
- Reasonable steps
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their childcare costs.
## SWIFTT process
SWIFTT will not automatically include childcare costs as allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support. You should deduct any Childcare or OSCAR Subsidy paid from the childcare cost before manually adding them into the STAWA screen.

chunks.title: Childcare if the caregiver is working — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Childcare if the caregiver is working
Allowable childcare costs (where the caregiver is working) can be included in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support.
In addition, these costs must be essential to meet the family's daily living needs and could not be readily avoided or varied when the expense was incurred.
The net cost of essential childcare (after the deduction of any childcare or OSCAR subsidy that is payable) up to a maximum of $6 per hour can be included in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support to enable the client or their partner to take part in paid employment.
Allowable childcare costs can be included in Temporary Additional Support where the childcare provider is not a recognised childcare organisation.
## Reasonable steps
You need to consider that if a recognised childcare organisation can be used by the client and would cost less than the childcare provider being used, then a reasonable step could be to change their childcare provider.
For more information see:
- Reasonable steps
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their childcare costs.

chunks.title: Clients not getting a main benefit — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Clients not getting a main benefit
Clients who do not get a main benefit, and clients getting New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension, will get their Working for Families Tax Credits payments from Inland Revenue.
The amount of Working for Families Tax Credits included as chargeable income is the actual weekly rate payable to the client. If the client has chosen not to get Working for Families Tax Credits, they will need to take steps to obtain this assistance, and in most cases you should encourage them to get it as a weekly payment. There may however be circumstances where it would be more beneficial for the client to get an end of year payment, such as for those who have fluctuating income, especially those who expect more income at the end of the tax year than the beginning.
If it is more beneficial for them to get Working for Families Tax Credits as a lump sum at the end of the tax year, you need to estimate the amount they would get if paid on a weekly basis. You need to include this estimated weekly amount of Working for Families Tax Credits as chargeable income and note CMS stating that the client will get a year end payment and that you have estimated Working for Families Tax Credits for the client.
When assessing Working for Families Tax Credits as chargeable income, consider the following:
- Shared care - family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
- Grace period for in-work tax credit
- Abated Working for Families Tax Credits
- Year end Working for Families Tax Credits
- Estimating weekly Working for Families Tax Credits

chunks.title: Clients getting a main benefit — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Clients getting a main benefit
A client getting a main benefit can only get family tax credit and Best Start tax credit, which can be paid with their main benefit. They cannot get any other form of Working for Families Tax Credits.
Make sure that clients are getting their full entitlement to family tax credit and Best Start tax credit before assessing Temporary Additional Support. The amount of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit included as chargeable income is the actual weekly rate payable to the client.
## Family tax credit
The gross annual income threshold for the highest rate of family tax credit is $44,900 ($3,741 per month) as at 1 April 2026.
## Best Start tax credit
The Best Start tax credit is paid at $77.50 a week (as at 1 April 2026) for families supporting a newborn baby.
From 1 April 2026 all three years of the Best Start tax credit are income tested for clients who are not receiving a main benefit.
Clients will get the Best Start tax credit paid at the full (unabated) rate if they earn less than the gross annual income threshold for Best Start tax credit of $79,000 (as at 1 April 2026). This threshold is more than the income cut-out points for main benefits, so clients getting a main benefit are able to get the full Best Start tax credit rate.
## Clients not getting a main benefit
For clients not getting a main benefit, payments of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit are managed by Inland Revenue.
This includes clients getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension. Inland Revenue assess whether the client qualifies for the tax credits and the rate of tax credit payable.

chunks.title: Clients who cannot get Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Clients who cannot get Temporary Additional Support
A client cannot get Temporary Additional Support if:
- they are getting Special BenefitNote a client may choose to cancel Special Benefit and, if they qualify, may be granted Temporary Additional Support. See: Cancelling Special Benefit
- another member of their family is getting Temporary Additional Support
- they are a dependent child or a child for whom an Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paidNote an application may be made by the child's principal caregiver
- they have arranged their circumstances to qualify for Temporary Additional Support
- they have a non-entitlement period
- they are subject to a stand-down period
- they are subject to 100% sanction
- they are a full-time student unless they meet certain criteria

chunks.title: Clients with specific circumstances — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Clients with specific circumstances
There are some situations when it may be unclear if a client and their partner (if any) qualify for Temporary Additional Support, and how to calculate their rate of payment.
## For more detailed information see:
- Partner unlawfully resident in New Zealand or here temporarily
- Partner is overseas
- Partner does not qualify
- Partner gets a different main benefit
- Full-time students
- Striking workers
- Self-employed clients
- Single client in residential care
- Partner in residential care
- Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid
- Client in new relationship
- Client's relationship ends

chunks.title: Clothing — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Clothing
MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for additional clothing costs.
If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, it must be granted before MSD assess if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support where they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because:
- they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or
- their disability will last less than 6 months or
- they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include additional clothing costs that a client has because of their disability.
For example, additional costs may arise because of:
- greater frequency of washing or
- wear and tear resulting from use of a prosthetic aid (e.g. artificial limb or splints) or wheelchair or
- the need to have clothes or shoes made-to-measure
If the clothing is made to measure, the amount of the allowable costs is the difference between having an item made-to-measure and buying normal clothing items through a shop.
Note allowable costs do not include the normal clothing costs for a client.
A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client's disability, need for treatment and that clothing is necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are:
- additional and
- ongoing and
- directly related to the client's disability
## Proof of clothing costs
The client must provide:
- a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and
- receipts or quotes showing the extra costs of the clothing
If the clothing is made-to-measure, the client must provide evidence of how much more it costs than buying a normal item through a shop.
The issue of clothing is not always straightforward and needs to be treated with sensitivity. It can be difficult to quantify their additional costs. MSD should assess clients on a case-by-case basis.

chunks.title: Commencement date — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
Unless a client applies for a main benefit and Temporary Additional Support at the same time, the commencement date for Temporary Additional Support is the later of:
- the application date and
- the date the client became entitled to it
## Applying for a main benefit and Temporary Additional Support at the same time
When a client applies for a main benefit and Temporary Additional Support at the same time, Temporary Additional Support commences from the same date as the main benefit unless the 28-day rule applies to the main benefit.
In some circumstances a client who applies for a main benefit within 28 days of their entitlement date can have their benefit commence earlier than their application date. In these cases, the main benefit commences from the day after the initial stand-down ends.
The 28-day rule does not apply to Temporary Additional Support.
## Effect of initial stand-downs, non-entitlement periods and sanctions
A client is not entitled to Temporary Additional Support during:
- an initial stand-down
- a non-entitlement period
- a 100% suspension sanction

chunks.title: Consumer credit contract (hire purchase) — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Consumer credit contract (hire purchase)
A consumer credit contract (hire purchase) is where a client enters into a contract to purchase personal, domestic or household items, including any agreement where:
- interest charges may be payable under the contract or
- credit fees may be payable under the contract or
- security may be required under the contract and
- the creditor is in the business of providing credit
A client who has used a consumer credit contract to purchase an essential item that is an allowable cost can have this item included in their assessment for Temporary Additional Support.
The client must purchase the item from a supplier and establish a credit contract through that supplier. The credit contract does not have to be with the supplier but the supplier must introduce the client to the creditor.
For example, a client would like to establish a consumer credit contract with a supplier to purchase a washing machine. The supplier then asks the client to complete a credit application form for a finance company.
For more information see:
- Allowable costs
- Agreed period payments
- Revolving credit payments
- Hire or rental essential household items

chunks.title: Day care for the older disabled people — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Day care for the older disabled people
If the client is an older disabled person and needs help with the costs of travelling to, or attending, a day care centre, MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance.
If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, it must be granted before MSD assess if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support where they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because:
- they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or
- their disability will last less than 6 months or
- they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include the costs of an older disabled client (usually aged 65 or over) to attend a day care centre, and/or the cost of transport to the centre.
This is intended to enable the client to remain in or return to their own home, or family/whānau care.
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support do not include:
- the costs of people in residential care services
- if the client is entitled to carer relief through Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora funding (MSD should refer the client to the local Hospital and Health Services to check their entitlement for carer relief)
A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client's disability, the need for treatment and that day care is necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are:
- additional and
- ongoing and
- directly related to the client's disability
Note when a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner indicates on the client's Disability Allowance medical certificate that treatment by another registered health practitioner is necessary, that practitioner must verify the costs of their services.
## Proof of cost of day care for the older disabled person
The client must provide:
- a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and
- receipts to verify the costs of day care (1 receipt is enough proof if it shows the regular cost of each visit)
Note the requirement to get a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner's signature at the client's Review of Circumstances, is waived if the costs are for attendance at an IHC day programme (regardless of whether the costs have changed).

chunks.title: Deficiency — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Deficiency
The deficiency is the amount that a client's standard costs exceed their disposable income.
To qualify for Temporary Additional Support a client must:
- have standard costs that exceeds their disposable income and
- have a deficiency of $1.00 or more
The deficiency is compared to the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support payable to the client to determine the rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support.
Note if the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, the rate of Temporary Additional Support payable is the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support plus the disability exception amount.

chunks.title: Dependent child — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
For the purposes of Temporary Additional Support, a dependent child is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of the client
- maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
- in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but has been returned to their parent's care
A dependent child for Temporary Additional Support does not include a:
- child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989
- child for whom an Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid and
- young person getting a Young Parent Payment and their child (see Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples)

chunks.title: Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples
To help you identify when there is a 'dependent child', please see the examples below:
Household
Payments
Outcome
Parent, and young person aged between 16-18 years old.
Parent getting Sole Parent Support (SPS), young person getting no assistance.
Young person is a dependent child.
Parent, and young person aged between 16-18 years old and young person's baby.
Parent getting Sole Parent Support, young person getting Young Parent Payment (YPP).

chunks.title: Disability exception amount — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Disability exception amount
A disability exception amount is available to the applicant only when:
- the client has a deficiency greater than the upper limit for Temporary Additional Support and
- any member of the client's family, or a child for whom they get an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, is getting the maximum amount of disability allowance and
- any member of the client's family, or a child for whom they get an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, has excess disability costs
If the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, the rate of Temporary Additional Support is:
- the upper limit plus
- the disability exception amount
From 1 July 2021, the disability exception amount covers:
- up to the first $100 of applicable excess costs in full and
- 30% of any remaining applicable excess costs over $100

chunks.title: Disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Disposable income
Disposable income is the amount of income remaining after subtracting the allowable costs of the client and their partner (if any) from their chargeable income.
Disposable income can be a positive or negative amount.
## Example 1
Chargeable income
$421.25
Less: Allowable costs
$168.89
Equals: Disposable income
$252.36 (positive amount)
## Example 2
Chargeable income
$212.68
Less: Allowable costs
$396.02
Equals: Disposable income
($183.34) negative amount

chunks.title: Dryer — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Dryer
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include regular repayments for a clothes dryer, where it is needed because of a client's disability.
The maximum weekly limit for a dryer per family is $31.80 (as at 1 April 2026).
## Dryer purchased before the client became a beneficiary
Temporary Additional Support can be paid when the dryer was purchased before the client became a beneficiary.
Note this includes clients who at the time of their application for Temporary Additional Support, are or have been a beneficiary at some point since purchasing the essential item.
## Dryer purchased when the client was a beneficiary
If the dryer was purchased when the client or their partner (if any) was a beneficiary Temporary Additional Support can only be paid if the cost:
- is essential to meet the family's daily living needs and
- could not be easily avoided or reduced when the expense was incurred (e.g. there were no other options available at the time of purchase)
## Verification
A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client's disability, need for treatment and that a dryer is necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are:
- additional and
- ongoing and
- directly related to the client's disability

chunks.title: Emergency housing contribution — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Emergency housing contribution
Clients staying in accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant pay an emergency housing contribution after the first 7 nights in the accommodation.
The emergency housing contribution is generally 25% of the client's net income (including their partner's income, if any).
However, if the client's income is less than Jobseeker Support, they will pay 25% of the appropriate Jobseeker Support rate that would apply to them (if they were a beneficiary).
Clients staying in accommodation funded by an Emergency Housing Grant and who pay an emergency housing contribution towards their accommodation costs generally do not qualify for Accommodation Supplement.
The emergency housing contribution may still be included in Temporary Additional Support if the client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement.
## Arrears for emergency housing contribution
Arrears for the emergency housing contribution can be included as an accommodation cost, when the client is repaying the arrears under a payment arrangement agreed to by MSD. The client needs to be meeting the terms of the payment arrangement.
Example:
A client has emergency housing arrears totalling $210. We have agreed with the client that they will repay the arrears at $10 a week and the client is making those repayments. The amount of $10 a week can be included in the client's Temporary Additional Support assessment.

chunks.title: Employment-related costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Employment-related costs
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support must be ongoing and regular expenses, calculated on a weekly basis
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their allowable employment-related costs.
## SWIFTT process
If the client or any family members have allowable employment-related costs for Temporary Additional Support, you will need to manually add them into the STAWA screen.
The following employment related costs can be included as allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support:
- Childcare if the caregiver is working
- Public transport to work
- Telephone rental costs for employment
- Vehicle repayments for employment
- Vehicle running costs for employment

chunks.title: Essential household items — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support must be: - ongoing and regular expenses, calculated on a weekly basis and - essential to meet the family's daily living needs and - not easily avoided or reduced when the expense was incurred An essential household item that is considered an allowable cost is a: - bed (including mattress) or mattress - dining suite - combined fridge/freezer, or a fridge and freezer or a fridge or a freezer - lounge suite - portable heater - stove - television - vehicle repayment - washing machine You can only include payments for the essential household items that are listed as allowable costs. Most of the items listed as essential household items have limits on the weekly amounts and the number of items that can be included for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Essential item purchased before the client became a beneficiary — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Temporary Additional Support can be paid where the essential item was purchased before the client became a beneficiary. Note this includes clients who at the time of their application for Temporary Additional Support, are or have been a beneficiary at some point since purchasing the essential item.

chunks.title: Essential item purchased while the client was a beneficiary — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: If an essential item was purchased while the client was a beneficiary Temporary Additional Support can only be paid if: - the cost is essential to meet the family's daily living needs - the cost could not be easily avoided or reduced when the expense was incurred (for example there were no other options available at the time of purchase) Generally, you can include the costs for essential household items in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support if the client purchased the item using a consumer credit contract or any other agreed period payment. In some circumstances a client may include the costs for essential household items in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support if the client purchased the item using a revolving credit payment. For more information see: - Essential household items list - Types of health and disability costs - Hire or rental essential household items

chunks.title: How was the essential item purchased? — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Generally, you can include the costs for essential household items in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support if the client purchased the item using a consumer credit contract or any other agreed period payment. In some circumstances a client may include the costs for essential household items in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support if the client purchased the item using a revolving credit payment. For more information see: - Consumer credit contract - Agreed period payment - Revolving credit payment

chunks.title: Deferring repayments — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: If the consumer credit contract (hire purchase) has a provision to defer repayment when earnings are reduced because of a health condition or accident, this option should be considered. Advice should also be given to the client to explore the possibility of deferring or re-negotiating the terms of repayment to eliminate or reduce the need for Temporary Additional Support. You should consider including the consumer credit contract cost and give the client time to explore their options prior to their next review.

chunks.title: SWIFTT process — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: If the client or any family members have allowable essential household items for Temporary Additional Support, you will need to manually add them into the STAWA screen. For more information see - Allowable costs

chunks.title: Essential repairs and maintenance — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Essential repairs and maintenance
MSD must check the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement. If the client is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement this must be granted before assessing whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
Essential repairs and maintenance may still be included in Temporary Additional Support if the client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement.
Homeowners can claim the cost of essential repairs and maintenance to the house they occupy as accommodation costs. There are some general guidelines to consider when deciding if something is an accommodation cost:
- repairs or maintenance must be essential to maintain the house and property to a habitable standard
- repairs and maintenance should be made to meet the homeowner and families current housing needs
- all costs claimed must be verified with receipts which, if necessary, are detailed enough to verify the work undertaken was essential or needed for maintenance
Note essential repairs and maintenance can be included as an accommodation cost when recoverable assistance has also been paid for the cost. This does not apply when non-recoverable assistance has been paid e.g. a Special Needs Grant for effluent treatment system maintenance or repair.
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their essential repairs and maintenance costs.

chunks.title: Estimating weekly Working for Families Tax Credits — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Estimating weekly Working for Families Tax Credits
To estimate a client's weekly Working for Families Tax Credits payments from Inland Revenue, you will need to determine the amount of weekly Working for Families Tax Credits that would be payable to that client.
To verify this, the client may provide a Certificate of Entitlement from Inland Revenue or you can have the client phone Inland Revenue in your presence for verbal confirmation of Working for Families Tax Credits.
If the client does not have a recent Certificate of Entitlement you can still complete a Temporary Additional Support assessment by including Working for Families Tax Credits determined by:
- estimating a weekly rate using the Inland Revenue Estimate your WFFTC calculator or
- phoning Inland Revenue (the client must be with you to give verbal permission)
Inland Revenue has a dedicated phone line for Work and Income staff to enquire about Working for Families Tax Credits.
The amount of Working for Families Tax Credits that you would include as chargeable income is the actual weekly rate payable to the client (this is regardless of whether or not the client has chosen to get Working for Families Tax Credits).

chunks.title: Example - Orphans or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: A single client aged 45 years old getting Jobseeker Support also receives an Unsupported Child's Benefit for a grandchild. Weekly Chargeable income Weekly Allowable costs Net rate of Jobseeker Support before any deductions (as at 1 April 2026) $372.55 Weekly qualifying accommodation costs (Kāinga Ora rent $88.00) less $34.13 accommodation deduction (as at 1 April 2026) $53.87 Disability Allowance for client $50.00 Disability Allowance costs for client $50.00 Disability Allowance for Unsupported Child (as at 1 April 2026) $82.85 Disability Allowance costs for Unsupported Child $110.00 Bed $38.99 Fridge-freezer $25.00 Vehicle repayments $80.00 Total chargeable income $505.40 Total allowable costs $357.86

chunks.title: Step 1 - Calculate client's disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the amount of disposable income. Chargeable income $505.40 Less Allowable costs $357.86 Equals Disposable income $147.54

chunks.title: Step 2 - Calculate client's deficiency (or surplus) in their disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the deficiency or surplus. Standard costs 70% of the net rate of abated Jobseeker Support (as at 1 April 2026) $260.78 Less Disposable income (from step 1) $147.54 Equals Deficiency $113.24 A client does not qualify for Temporary Additional Support if: - there is a surplus or - the deficiency is less than $1.00

chunks.title: Step 3 - Compare deficiency to upper limit to find lesser amount — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the client's upper limit for Temporary Additional Support then compare this amount to the deficiency. Upper limit 30% of the net rate of unabated Jobseeker Support ($372.55 x 30% as at 1 April 2026) $111.76 Deficiency (from step 2) $113.24 Compare the upper limit to the deficiency. The rate of Temporary Additional Support is the lesser of the deficiency or the upper limit unless the client qualifies for a disability exception amount. $111.76 If the deficiency is greater than the upper limit, the rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support is the upper limit, plus the disability exception amount (if the client qualifies for it).

chunks.title: Step 4 - Calculate the disability exception amount — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Determine if the client qualifies for a disability exception amount. In this case, the client qualifies for a disability exception amount because the upper limit is less than the client's income deficiency and they also have excess disability costs. They have excess disability costs because their grandchild (the unsupported child) has Disability Allowance costs in excess of the maximum amount of Disability Allowance paid. Step 4(a) - Calculate the excess disability costs total Total all of the Disability Allowance costs for each family member who has costs that exceed the maximum amount of Disability Allowance paid (including any child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid) $110.00 (child) Less the maximum rate of Disability Allowance paid for each family member who is getting the maximum amount of Disability Allowance (as at 1 April 2026) including any child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid $82.85 Equals excess disability costs total $27.15 The excess disability costs total must not include any costs for counselling (including the costs of transport to attend counselling) that are above the maximum rate of Disability Allowance. Step 4(b) - Calculate the excess total costs Excess total costs is the amount of the client's income deficiency that is not already covered by the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support. Deficiency $113.24 Less the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support $111.76 Excess total costs $1.48 Step 4(c) - Calculate applicable excess costs The client's applicable excess costs is the lesser amount of their: - excess disability costs total and - excess total costs Excess disability costs total $27.15 Excess total costs $1.48 Applicable excess costs (lesser amount of $27.15 and $1.48) $1.48 Step 4(d) - Calculate the disability exception amount using the client's applicable excess costs The disability exception amount provides a full subsidy for a client's applicable excess costs amount of up to $100.00. If the client has any applicable excess costs remaining after the full subsidy has been applied, these are subsidised at 30% of the remaining applicable excess costs amount. Applicable excess costs amount will be fully subsidised up to $100.00 $1.48 Find 30% of remaining balance of applicable excess costs not covered above (if any) n/a Disability exception amount $1.48

chunks.title: Step 5 - Calculate the rate of Temporary Additional Support. — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the rate of Temporary Additional Support. Upper limit (from step 3) $111.76 Plus Disability exception amount (from step 4) $1.48 Equals rate of Temporary Additional Support $113.24 The rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support is $113.24 (as at 1 April 2026).
