chunks.title: Excess total costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Excess total costs
Excess total costs are the client’s income deficiency minus the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support. These excess costs are the client’s remaining deficiency that is not already covered by the upper limit.
Excess total costs form part of the formula when calculating a client’s disability exception amount.
## Example
A single non-beneficiary who is 25 years old and qualifies for a disability exception amount has an income deficiency of $105 a week. Their excess total costs would be:
Deficiency
Upper limit
Excess total costs
$105.00
$83.55
$21.45

chunks.title: Extra help charged as income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Extra help charged as income
The following financial assistance is charged as income for Temporary Additional Support:
- Civil Defence Payments for lost income
- Employment Transition Assistance
- Live Organ Donors Assistance payments for lost income
- New Employment Transition Grant
- Seasonal Work Assistance
- Special Assistance to the Rural Sector
- Telephone Costs Payment
- Assistance to transition into employment for bridging finance
- Work Bonus.

chunks.title: Formula-assessed Child Support costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Formula-assessed Child Support liability is the only type of Child Support that is an allowable cost for Temporary Additional Support. These costs are essential to help meet the needs of a client's child(ren) and cannot be easily avoided or changed. These costs must be verified by Inland Revenue.

chunks.title: Child Support liability — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Only the current amount of formula-assessed Child Support a liable parent is required to pay can be included as an allowable cost. The allowable cost does not include any amount of: - Child Support for a liability period before the commencement date of the Temporary Additional Support - debts or penalties a liable parent may be paying to Inland Revenue alongside their regular Child Support liability - court-ordered lump sum payments - Child Support the liable parent does not have to pay (e.g. when their formula assessment is suspended or when the client has an exemption from paying Child Support) Note if the liable parent has an offsetting arrangement, the full amount of formula-assessed Child Support liability may be included. This applies regardless of how much Child Support the liable parent is paying (if any) while the offsetting arrangement is in place.

chunks.title: Date costs can be included — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Clients may have their formula-assessed Child Support liability included as an allowable cost in their Temporary Additional Support from 1 July 2023. If a client who was getting Temporary Additional Support on 1 July 2023 applies to include Child Support as an allowable cost between 1 July 2023 and 29 September 2023, the inclusion of the cost can be backdated to the later of: - the date the client is liable for the cost or - 1 July 2023 Clients who do not apply to include Child Support as an allowable cost until on or after 30 September 2023 cannot have these costs backdated. If the client applies on or after 30 September, formula-assessed Child Support costs can be included in their Temporary Additional Support from the later of: - the date the client is liable for the cost or - the date the client applies to have the cost included Normal commencement date rules apply to new applications for Temporary Additional Support. This means clients who are not getting Temporary Additional Support on 1 July 2023 can only include the formula-assessed Child Support cost from the date they apply for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Changes to formula-assessed Child Support liability — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Inland Revenue may reassess how much Child Support a client is liable to pay, based on changes in the liable parent or receiving carer's circumstances. This may mean a client's formula-assessed Child Support costs change. The change may take effect from a date in the past or a date in the future. For changes to formula-assessed Child Support costs, clients generally must notify MSD of a change in their costs within 14 days of the date that Inland Revenue notifies the client of the outcome of their reassessment. This is different to the 14-day rule for changes in other allowable costs, where clients must tell MSD of a change in circumstances within 14 days of the date of the change (i.e. the date of event).

chunks.title: Formula for Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: From 1 July 2021, the formula to calculate the weekly rate of Temporary Additional Support is as follows:

chunks.title: Step 1 - Calculate client's disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the disposable income of the client and their partner (if any): Weekly chargeable income Less Weekly allowable costs Equals Disposable income

chunks.title: Step 2 - Calculate client's deficiency (or surplus) in their disposable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate whether there is a deficiency or surplus in the disposable income of the client and their partner, (if any): Standard costs Less Disposable income (from step 1) Equals Deficiency (positive amount) or Surplus (negative amount) A client does not qualify for Temporary Additional Support if: - there is a surplus or - the deficiency is less than $1.00 If the client has a deficiency of $1.00 or more in their disposable income, they qualify for Temporary Additional Support. Go to Step 3 below.

chunks.title: Step 3 - Compare deficiency to upper limit of Temporary Additional Support to find lesser amount — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the client's upper limit for Temporary Additional Support then compare this amount to the deficiency. Upper limit 30% of the full net rate of main benefit payable to the client and their partner (if any) or for non-beneficiaries 30% of the appropriate net rate of Jobseeker Support for the client and their partner, if any (except for certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants) Deficiency from step 2 Compare the above The rate of Temporary Additional Support is the lesser of the deficiency or the upper limit unless the client qualifies for a disability exception amount If the deficiency is less than the upper limit, the rate of payment for Temporary Additional Support is the deficiency. The client will not qualify for the disability exception amount. If the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, go to Step 4 below.

chunks.title: Step 4 - Calculate the disability exception amount (only if client qualifies) — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Determine if the client qualifies for a disability exception amount. The client qualifies for a disability exception amount if the client's deficiency is greater than the upper limit and they or their family have excess disability costs. Step 4(a) - Calculate the excess disability costs total If the client qualifies for a disability exception amount, calculate the excess disability costs total. This is the total amount of excess disability costs of the client and their family. Total all of the Disability Allowance costs for each family member (including any child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid) who has costs that exceed the maximum amount of Disability Allowance paid $0.00 Less the maximum rate of Disability Allowance paid for each family member (including any child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid) who is getting the maximum amount of Disability Allowance $ Equals excess disability costs total $ Note the excess disability costs total must not include any costs for counselling (including the costs of transport to attend counselling) that are above the maximum rate of Disability Allowance. Step 4(b) - Calculate the excess total costs A client's excess total costs are the client and their partner's (if any) deficiency in their disposable income minus the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support. 'Excess total costs' are the costs that are not already covered by the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support. Deficiency $0.00 Less the upper limit of Temporary Additional Support $ Excess total costs $ Step 4(c) - Calculate applicable excess costs Now find the client's applicable excess costs to determine what amount to use to calculate the disability exception amount. A client's applicable excess costs is the lesser amount of their: - excess disability costs total and - excess total costs Excess disability costs total $0.00 (A) Excess total costs $0.00 (B) Applicable excess costs Lesser amount of (A) and (B) Step 4(d) - Calculate the disability exception amount using the client's applicable excess costs The disability exception amount provides a full subsidy for a client's applicable excess costs amount of up to $100. If the client has any applicable excess costs remaining after the full subsidy has been applied, these are subsidised at 30% of the remaining applicable excess costs amount. Applicable excess costs amount will be fully subsidised up to $100 Up to $100 (C)

chunks.title: Step 4 - Calculate the disability exception amount (only if client qualifies) — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Find 30% of remaining balance of applicable excess costs not covered above (if any) 30% x remaining applicable excess (D) Disability exception amount Add (C) and (D) together

chunks.title: Step 5 - Calculate the rate of Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Calculate the rate of Temporary Additional Support. Upper limit (from step 3) $0.00 Plus disability exception amount (from step 4(d)) $ Equals rate of Temporary Additional Support $

chunks.title: Before 1 July 2021 - Formula for Temporary Additional Support — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: On 1 July 2021, changes were made to the way the disability exception amount is calculated under the formula for Temporary Additional Support. When a client qualifies for the disability exception amount for a period before 1 July 2021, you will need to assess the client's Temporary Additional Support for that period using the formula for Temporary Additional Support that applied before 1 July 2021.

chunks.title: Full-time student's chargeable income — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Full-time student's chargeable income
Chargeable income for students includes:
- Student Allowance
- Accommodation Benefit paid to students
- Independent Circumstances Allowance
- the Living Costs component of any Student Loan
The living costs component of any Student Allowance or Student Loan is included as chargeable income for Temporary Additional Support purposes. This is because the living costs component of a Student Loan is a means of financial assistance available to students to assist with their living costs.
Student Loans for course fees or course-related costs are not to be included as chargeable income.
Students must take all necessary steps to obtain all other sources of assistance that may be available, for example, the availability of financial support during the academic year under the Student Allowance and Student Loan schemes. The student must also take reasonable steps to reduce their costs or increase their income.
You should consider declining, reducing or cancelling Temporary Additional Support if these sources have not been utilised.
Parental income does not affect whether a student qualifies for Temporary Additional Support and questions about parents' income should not be asked. However, any contribution from parents for living costs, excluding lump sum gifts, should be included as chargeable income.

chunks.title: Full-time students — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Full-time students
Full-time students (and their partners) can get Temporary Additional Support when:
- the student or their partner is the principal caregiver or principal temporary caregiver of a dependent child or
- the student or any member of their family is getting the maximum amount of Disability Allowance and has excess disability costs or
- the student is a beneficiary (for example, a Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or total blindness) client studying full-time)
A student getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is not considered a full-time student when assessing whether they qualify for Temporary Additional Support.
If a student and their partner meet the qualifications for Temporary Additional Support you may include all of their allowable costs into the assessment of Temporary Additional Support.
Student Allowance, Accommodation Benefit and the living costs component of the Student Loan are included as chargeable income for Temporary Additional Support purposes.
Student Loans for course fees or course-related costs are not included as chargeable income.
Note to qualify for Temporary Additional Support the student must take all necessary steps to obtain all other sources of assistance available, for example, financial support during the academic year under the Student Allowance and Student Loan schemes. They must also take reasonable steps to reduce their costs or increase their chargeable income.

chunks.title: Gardening, lawns and outside window cleaning — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must check whether the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for help with gardening, lawns or outside window cleaning. If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, this must be granted before MSD assesses whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support. The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support when they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because: - they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or - their disability will last less than 6 months or - they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants. A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client's disability, the need for treatment and that gardening, lawn mowing or outside window cleaning is necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are: - additional and - ongoing and - directly related to the client's disability Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include the costs of gardening, lawn mowing, and outside window cleaning for the client's own home or private residence. These costs can only be included if the client is unable to do these tasks themselves because of their disability but cannot be included solely based on of the client's age. Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support do not include: - house repairs or house painting as these are part of normal living costs, and are not due to the client's disability - indoor household maintenance (e.g. carpet cleaning) as funding for home help is available through Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora MSD should refer the client to the local Hospital and Health Services home support services - gardening, lawn mowing or window cleaning costs that are included in a standard service fee charged to all residents of a retirement village or complex. However there are exceptions, for more information see: Retirement Villages - gardening, lawn mowing or window cleaning carried out by family members. When a client has high gardening costs (e.g. due to the extra work involved in maintaining a large property, or high maintenance gardens) the client should look at other options for meeting or alleviating the cost.

chunks.title: Proof of gardening, lawn mowing and outside window cleaning costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: The client must provide: - a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and - receipts or quotes for the cost of the gardening work - a receipt showing actual costs is preferred Note sometimes gardening costs are covered as part of the client's tenancy agreement. MSD should check if this applies to the client before accepting these as allowable costs. The costs must be reasonable, and consideration given to the client's circumstances and the seasonal demands. Generally, lawns will not require mowing every week throughout the colder months. If the client has difficulty getting a receipt, the client's statement of the hourly rate paid, plus a quote from the gardener stating the time taken per week is acceptable.

chunks.title: Gym and swimming pool fees — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Gym and swimming pool fees
MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for gym or swimming pools fees.
If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, it must be granted before MSD assess if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support where they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because:
- they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or
- their disability will last less than 6 months or
- they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client’s disability, the need for treatment and that exercise-based medical treatment is necessary.
The certificate must also confirm the exercise they are supporting is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are:
- additional and
- ongoing and
- directly related to the client's disability
For example Temporary Additional Support can be paid if the exercise is part of a medical treatment (e.g. hydrotherapy) or exercise in a pool supervised by a physiotherapist.
## Generally gym and swimming pool costs cannot be included
Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support do not include the cost of activities such as swimming at the local pool or workouts at the gym, even if the client's registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner recommends them as beneficial for the client's condition.
This is general exercise, which is a normal cost of everyday living that people without disabilities also have.

chunks.title: Health and disability costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Health and disability costs
Allowable health and disability costs are based on the actual costs arising from a disability of:
- the client and/or any member of their family and
- any child for whom an Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid
These costs must be essential to meet the family's daily living needs and could not be readily avoided or varied when the expense was incurred.
A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client's disability and need for treatment. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are:
- additional and
- ongoing and
- directly related to the client's disability
Note when a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner indicates on the client's Disability Allowance medical certificate that treatment by another registered health practitioner is necessary, that practitioner must verify the costs of their services.
## Client qualifies for Disability Allowance
MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for the health and disability costs.
If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, it must be granted before Temporary Additional Support can be paid for those costs.
If the client has a deficiency of income based on other allowable costs, they can get Temporary Additional Support. However, the health and disability costs must not be included until Disability Allowance has been granted.
## Client does not qualify for Disability Allowance
A client may not qualify for Disability Allowance because:
- they or any member of their family have a disability which is likely to last less than 6 months or
- they do not meet the Disability Allowance income test or
- they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants or
- the health and disability costs are not allowable costs for Disability Allowance (e.g. repayments for the purchase of a dryer)
If the client does not qualify for a Disability Allowance (for the reasons above), MSD can still include these costs in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support if:
- the cost is an allowable cost for Temporary Additional Support and
- the disability and need for treatment have been verified by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner.

chunks.title: Hire or rental essential household items — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Hire or rental essential household items
An essential household item which is acquired through a hire or rental agreement can be included as an allowable cost for Temporary Additional Support provided the agreement requires regular payments over an agreed period. That is, an essential household item which is leased or hired on a fixed term.
Regular ongoing payments are not limited to, but can include:
- hire or rental agreements
- private payment arrangements relating to a specific item
Clients must provide written verification of the item acquired, the initial purchased amount, the term and the amount of regular ongoing payments.
For more information see
- Essential household items
- Consumer credit contract
- Agreed period payment
- Revolving credit payment

chunks.title: Home ownership costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Home ownership costs
MSD must check whether the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement. If the client is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement this must be granted before assessing whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
Home ownership costs may still be included in Temporary Additional Support if the client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement.
Accommodation costs that can be assessed as home ownership costs include:
- mortgage repayments (interest and principal repayments on mortgages to purchase a home)
- payment towards a deposit if included in a rent to buy contract
- retirement village residents with 'Licence to occupy'
- body corporate fees
- local authority rates (if they get a rebate, this must be deducted)
- water rates
- house insurance premiums (must not include contents insurance)
- mortgage protection insurance or life insurance (only if this is compulsory for the mortgage)
- cost of essential repairs and maintenance to the home
Other costs that can be considered accommodation costs are:
- leasehold rental for leasehold land and for Māori rent
- principal and interest repayments made under the Loans for Major Repairs Advances to Homes scheme
- costs of a farm residence (but only if these costs are not claimed as an expense in the farm business account)
- costs of a home that is also being used as a business (but only if these costs are not claimed as an expense for the business)
## Costs that are not accommodation costs
Service costs, mortgage arrears, rates arrears, and insurance arrears cannot be included as accommodation costs.
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Idea Services residents and drug and alcohol abuse facilities — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Idea Services residents and drug and alcohol abuse facilities
MSD must determine whether the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement.
If the client is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement this must be granted before assessing whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
Most Idea Services residents and those staying at a drug and alcohol abuse facility will get a Residential Support Subsidy.
However, if residents at an Idea Services or drug and alcohol abuse facility do not qualify for either a Residential Support Subsidy or Accommodation Supplement, they may be able to get Temporary Additional Support.
When the amount a resident pays for their accommodation includes other costs (e.g. food or service costs) and these costs can be separated out from the amount they pay for accommodation, they are considered renting.
When the resident pays for their accommodation and food, and the food costs can't be separated out from the amount they pay, they are considered boarding.
Former residents of Idea Services facilities may get extra support from Idea Services. Extra support could include:
- someone taking the client grocery shopping
The costs of this support cannot be included as an accommodation cost.
People in approved Social Rehabilitation Programmes may have accommodation costs.
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Introduction — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Temporary Additional Support is non-taxable extra help paid for a maximum of 13 weeks. It is paid as a last resort to help clients with their regular essential living costs that cannot be met from their chargeable income and other resources.
Clients must ensure that they are accessing all other assistance available to them, and take reasonable steps towards reducing their costs and increasing their chargeable income.
A client does not have to be getting a main benefit to qualify for Temporary Additional Support.
## Community Services Cards
Note Community Services Cards are not automatically issued to clients who get non-beneficiary assistance (unless they get Accommodation Supplement), and they must make a separate application for a card.
Clients who get Accommodation Supplement qualify for a Community Services Card, and are sent a card automatically without having to make a separate application. See:
- Card services Community Services Card

chunks.title: IRD number for client or partner who is apportioned assistance — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD may make a written request for evidence of an IRD number for a primary client who is being paid Temporary Additional Support. MSD can also request evidence of an IRD number for a partner when they are apportioned a part of the assistance.

chunks.title: Setting or extending the timeframe for providing evidence — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must provide the client or partner with a minimum of 10 working days to provide IRD number evidence that has been requested in writing. MSD can extend the 10 working day period (in writing) if the client or partner has a reasonable explanation for requiring more than 10 days to provide evidence of their IRD number. This includes considering factors outside the client's control that cause delays, including, but not limited to: - client or partner has a family emergency that caused a delay - processing delays with an external agency (e.g. Inland Revenue, Department of Internal Affairs, etc) - client or partner does not speak English as a first language and has difficulty navigating evidence requirements - client or partner has limited access to the internet, a device, or their local service centre - client or partner has a physical or intellectual disability that makes accessing services difficult - client or partner is injured, disabled, or has a medical condition that makes accessing services difficult.

chunks.title: Notice following unsuccessful match — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about IRD numbers. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information, or there's an error, MSD should ask the client or partner (in writing) to provide evidence of their IRD number, unless there are significant barriers to providing this. In the written request for evidence of the IRD number, MSD must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and the match was unsuccessful, and - giving the client or partner a minimum of 10 working days to provide their IRD number evidence or the client's assistance must be suspended. Example Isla is receiving Temporary Additional Support. MSD holds an IRD number on record. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Isla's IRD number. MSD provides a notice in writing, giving 10 working days for Isla to provide evidence their IRD number. MSD's decision to give 10 working days to provide evidence is based on: - Isla already having an IRD number - Isla not having any significant barriers to getting evidence of their IRD number - MSD's obligation to provide a minimum of 10 working days to provide the information.

chunks.title: MSD must suspend assistance if evidence of IRD number is not received — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must suspend all taxable and income tested assistance the client is getting, including their Temporary Additional Support, if evidence of an IRD number is not provided within 10 working days from the written request, or extended period if this has been applied. If the apportioned partner has not provided evidence of their IRD number, the partner's taxable and income tested assistance must be suspended. Note suspension does not apply to Childcare Assistance. Example Koa has been receiving Temporary Additional Support for 8 weeks. MSD does not have an IRD number on file for Koa. MSD sends a written request giving 10 working days for Koa to provide evidence of their IRD number. MSD receives no response to this request. MSD suspends Koa's Temporary Additional Support because Koa has not supplied MSD with evidence of their IRD number within the timeframe provided.

chunks.title: IRD evidence may not be requested in some circumstances — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD may not ask for evidence of an IRD number when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - significant factors, that are outside the client or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of their IRD number (e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence), and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided or - there are significant factors related to a health, injury or disability that are outside the client or partner's control that prevents them from providing evidence of an IRD number, and - an agent cannot be appointed to act on the client or partner's behalf. MSD can determine at a later point to request evidence of the IRD number. Example Sienna is 23 and receiving Temporary Additional Support. Sienna's mother (Sara) is Sienna's agent and acts on Sienna's behalf with MSD. Sienna does not have an IRD number and Sara is not a recognised agent for Sienna for Inland Revenue. Sienna has a serious head injury, is unconscious and expected to be in hospital for at least 8 weeks. Sienna is not able to give consent to appoint Sara as an agent for Inland Revenue to apply for an IRD number due to their injury. MSD can request this information later when Sienna's situation has changed. Note there is different guidance for requesting evidence of an IRD number for partners who are not apportioned assistance but their income is relevant to the Temporary Additional Support. or when a client is applying for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: KiwiSaver and superannuation scheme account contributions — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## KiwiSaver and superannuation scheme account contributions
To qualify for Temporary Additional Support a client must take all reasonable steps to reduce their costs or increase their income. Reducing costs can include suspending KiwiSaver and superannuation scheme account contributions.
If a client has questions about how to suspend their contributions to KiwiSaver or superannuation scheme accounts, they should contact their scheme provider.

chunks.title: Maintenance — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Maintenance
MSD must check whether the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement. If the client is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement this must be granted before assessing whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
Essential maintenance may still be included in Temporary Additional Support if the client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement.
Maintenance costs that may be considered as accommodation costs includes any reasonable maintenance carried out on the house or grounds, which is necessary to prevent damage to the house or furnishings.
This may include but is not limited to:
- clearing chimneys and gutters
- replacing broken windows
- removing trees
- painting
Maintenance costs will not include:
- mowing lawns or
- work carried out for cosmetic purposes
Note Body Corporate fees can also be included as maintenance.
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their maintenance costs.
For help on deciding whether a repair or maintenance is essential contact Helpline.

chunks.title: Married, civil union or de facto couples in a joint tenancy — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Married, civil union or de facto couples in a joint tenancy
When the premises are occupied by joint tenants and there are one or more married, civil union or de facto couples, each couple is treated as one joint tenant.
The accommodation costs of the couple, as one joint tenant, should be used as the total of the accommodation costs for both partners.
For more information see:
- Cash assets
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Medical alarms — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for a medical alarm. If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, it must be granted before MSD assesses if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support. A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client's disability, the need for treatment and that a medical alarm is necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are: - additional and - ongoing and - directly related to the client's disability Note when a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner indicates on the client's Disability Allowance medical certificate that treatment by another registered health practitioner is necessary, that practitioner must verify the costs of their services.

chunks.title: Client qualifies for Disability Allowance — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: When a client is getting Disability Allowance for the costs of a monitored medical alarm, this cost can be included as a cost for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Client does not qualify for Disability Allowance — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support when they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because: - they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or - their disability will last less than 6 months or - they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include the costs of medical alarm rental and monitoring if: - a medical alarm is necessary for normal daily living, without it the client's life or health would be put at risk, or their disability would get worse and - the need for the monitored medical alarm is an ongoing, additional cost directly related to the client's disability or personal health need and - the monitored medical alarm is supplied by an MSD-accredited medical alarm supplier, unless exceptional circumstances exist and the medical alarm services the client needs are not available through an MSD-accredited medical alarm supplier Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support do not include: - buying medical alarms or smoke alarms (which are often marketed with medical alarms) because this is a one-off cost, not an ongoing cost or - alarms installed for security reasons as this is not a cost directly related to the client's disability or - a medical alarm cost that is included in the standard service fee for a client living in a retirement village or complex

chunks.title: Proof of medical alarm costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: The client must provide a: - Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and - completed Disability Allowance - Medical Alarm Assessment form signed by the registered health practitioner who is providing their treatment or managing their care and - copy of the contract or a receipt for the installation/rental of the medical alarm

chunks.title: Ongoing and additional costs of medical alarm — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD should check the costs claimed are for the rental and monitoring of the medical alarm and do not include: - the cost of installing the medical alarm or - any costs related to smoke alarms and - a medical alarm service provided by an MSD-accredited medical alarm supplier

chunks.title: Clients with a non MSD-accredited medical alarm supplier — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: The client will need to provide a copy of their contract from their supplier, when it has been agreed that a client can have the cost of a medical alarm from a non MSD-accredited supplier included as an allowable cost for Disability Allowance due to their exceptional circumstances. The contract must clearly show the service being provided is a monitored medical alarm service.

chunks.title: Medical fees — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for medical fees. If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, it must be granted before MSD assess if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support. The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support where they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because: - they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or - their disability will last less than 6 months or - they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client's disability and the need for treatment is necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are: - additional and - ongoing and - directly related to the client' disability

chunks.title: Medical fees included — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: If the fees, or a portion of the fees, claimed are not covered by the Community Services Card or the High Use Health Card, ACC or other accident insurers, or medical insurance they can be included in Disability Allowance. Note unless there are exceptional circumstances (e.g. when a public medical specialist doesn't exist in the client's region) Disability Allowance cannot usually be paid for private medical specialist fees. Public specialist fees are free. Medical fees can also include the fee charged by the medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or their teams) to complete a repeat prescription for ongoing conditions without the client attending a consultation (including faxing or electronically sending the prescription to the chemist). This category can also include fees for the following services if a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner verifies the client's disability and the need for the services on the client's Disability Allowance medical certificate: - occupational therapy - physiotherapy - speech-language therapy (for adults) - audio logical - orthotic - podiatry - dental services

chunks.title: Proof of medical fees costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: The client must provide: - a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and - receipts as proof of their medical/therapy fees (1 receipt is enough proof if it shows the regular cost of each visit, and the registered medical or nurse practitioner signing the certificate has indicated how often the treatment happens) Note it is not appropriate for MSD to approach the health practitioner directly. The client should provide the receipts. Example 1 A client is charged $20 for their doctor's visit. This includes an administration fee of $5. This fee is deducted from the total if the account is paid within 7 days, and the account is reduced to $15. If this is not paid within 7 days, the total charge of $20 can be included as a cost for Disability Allowance. Example 2 A client has an overdue account with their doctor and has been charged a $10 late fee. The late fee is not an allowable cost for Disability Allowance as this fee is not a direct result of their health condition or disability but due to the client not paying the overdue account. Example 3 A client goes to see a private rheumatologist specialist and applies for the cost to be covered by Disability Allowance. This is not an allowable cost for Disability Allowance (or Temporary Additional Support) as there is a publicly funded rheumatologist specialist in their region.

chunks.title: Mortgage repayments — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Mortgage repayments
MSD must check whether the client qualifies for Accommodation Supplement. If the client is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement this must be granted before assessing whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
If the client does not qualify for Accommodation Supplement, mortgage repayments for the home they occupy may still be included in Temporary Additional Support. This is limited to mortgage repayments towards:
- the mortgage principal (amount they borrowed) for the purchase of the home
- any mortgage principal for essential repairs and maintenance
- interest (amount the lender charges for providing the loan)
## Increasing a mortgage
A homeowner may increase their mortgage to do things like buy a car, take a holiday, or make improvements to their home. This increases the minimum repayment the homeowner must pay. The increased amount cannot be included in Temporary Additional Support unless it is for essential repairs and maintenance. If the mortgage was increased for more than one reason, only the increased amount for essential repairs and maintenance can be included.
## Refinancing a mortgage
Refinancing means transferring a mortgage to a new lender e.g. from one bank to another. When a homeowner refinances, they pay off their existing mortgage and take out a new one. A homeowner may borrow more than they need to pay off their mortgage to do things like consolidate debt, buy a car, or make improvements to their home.
Only repayments towards the mortgage principal for the original purchase of the home, any essential repairs and maintenance, and any related interest can be included in Temporary Additional Support. The homeowner must provide verification from their lender showing how much of their repayments relate to accommodation costs.
## Joint ownership
If a homeowner has joint ownership with one or more other people but they are the only owner living in the home, the actual costs they are paying can be included in Temporary Additional Support.
Note some homeowners have a mortgage through the Shared Equity Scheme administered by Kāinga Ora. Repayments on these mortgages are voluntary are not an accommodation cost.
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Necessary steps — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Necessary steps
Temporary Additional Support is last resort financial assistance for clients who have regular essential living costs that cannot be met from their chargeable income and other resources.
To qualify for Temporary Additional Support a client must take all necessary steps to obtain financial assistance from all other sources to reduce their costs.
You should consider the following when assessing whether or not a client can receive Temporary Additional Support.
Have other alternatives been explored? For example:
- Is the client getting the correct rate of benefit?
- Can the client get other Extra help such as Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance, Child Disability Allowance or Winter Energy Payment (during the winter period)?
- Would an Advance Payment of Benefit, Recoverable Assistance Payment or a Special Needs Grant be more appropriate?
You may be able to eliminate or reduce a client's hardship by paying a one-off Special Needs Grant or Advance Payment of Benefit for a specific need.
As Advance Payments of Benefit, Recoverable Assistance Payments and some Special Needs Grants are recoverable, the effect on the client's circumstances needs to be taken into account when considering if this is more appropriate
Is there any other assistance available to client? For example:
- Working for Families Tax Credits
- assistance from another government agency
Note a client's decision about applying for or ending a Child Support arrangement cannot be considered when assessing entitlement to Temporary Additional Support.
You should consider declining, reducing or cancelling Temporary Additional Support where the client has not taken all necessary steps to obtain financial assistance from all other resources to reduce their costs. This includes when a client decides not to get Winter Energy Payment when they qualify for it during the winter period.
There will be some situations where the client may not be able to improve their financial circumstances, in these cases a client may still qualify for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Non-beneficiaries — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Non-beneficiaries
Standard costs are the proportion of living costs that the client (and their partner, if any) are expected to meet from their benefit or income.
A client does not have to be getting a main benefit to qualify for Temporary Additional Support, but they must meet the qualifications for Temporary Additional Support.
This includes the client taking all necessary steps to obtain all other sources of assistance that may be available as well as taking reasonable steps to reduce their costs or increase their chargeable income, where possible.
## Standard costs
The following table is used to calculate standard costs for non-beneficiaries for Temporary Additional Support:
Standard costs for a client not getting a main benefit
70%
net rate of Jobseeker Support (before any income reduction or other deduction) according to the client's family circumstances and
70%
family tax credit (before any income reduction or other deduction) payable for 'any children' to the client or their partner according to the client's family circumstances
Note 'any children' includes dependent children and shared care children who qualify for family tax credit. Best Start tax credit is not included in the calculation of the standard costs.
## For example
The standard costs for a non-beneficiary married, civil union or de facto couple with 2 children aged 4 and 9 years is calculated as follows:
70% of the net rate of Jobseeker Support for a married, civil union or de facto couple with 2 children before any income reduction or other deduction ($669.40 as at 1 April 2026)
$468.58
70% of the family tax credit before any income reduction or other deduction payable for any children to the client or their partner ($151.91 + $123.78 = $275.69 as at 1 April 2026)
$192.98
Total amount of standard costs
$661.56

chunks.title: Non-subsidised pharmaceuticals — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance. The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support if they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because: - they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or - their disability will last less than 6 months or - they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants To determine if the cost of a non-subsidised pharmaceutical can be included in as an allowable cost for Temporary Additional Support, it is necessary to consider: - the availability of another suitable subsidised or partly subsidised pharmaceutical item and - if funding from PHARMAC under their Named Patient Pharmaceutical Assessment Policy has been applied for and if so, whether the application has been accepted or declined and the reasons for it being declined (this was previously known as the Exceptional Circumstances Panel Policy) The cost of the non-subsidised pharmaceutical can be included as an additional expense for Temporary Additional Support if the client's registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner verifies the client's disability and their need for the pharmaceutical item. They must verify the item is essential and there are no suitable subsidised or partly subsidised alternatives. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are: - additional and - ongoing and - directly related to the client's disability The client will need to provide a letter from their registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner confirming the following information: - the reasons for prescribing the non-subsidised pharmaceutical and - there is not suitable subsidised or partly subsidised alternative and - the medication is essential and directly related to the client's disability and - if PHARMAC funding has been applied for and declined, the reasons for this decision and - if there is no suitable subsidised or partly subsidised alternative, and if PHARMAC funding has not been applied for, the reasons why funding has not been requested Note MSD should refer applications for non-subsidised pharmaceuticals to the Regional Health Advisor and Regional Disability Advisor [no link find out why] . They will assess if the application qualifies.

chunks.title: Application to PHARMAC not always necessary — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: It’s not always necessary for an application to PHARMAC for funding to be lodged. If the client's registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner confirms funding has not been applied for because they are aware that PHARMACs criteria will not be met, the cost of the non-subsidised pharmaceutical can be included as an allowable cost for Temporary Additional Support. The registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must still verify there is not a suitable subsidised or partly subsidised alternative, and the pharmaceutical item is essential and directly related to the client's disability.

chunks.title: Obtaining proof on behalf of clients — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: There are 3 options for obtaining proof on behalf of the client: - if appropriate MSD can use the Privacy Statement - asking the client to provide further information or seeking consent from the client using the 'consent to release of health or disability information' form - if the client is unable to obtain the information and all other options have been pursued a Schedule 6 request for information can be used in limited cases

chunks.title: Clarifying or verifying information - use the Privacy Statement — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: The privacy statement on application forms permits case managers to contact the registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner who completed the client's Disability Allowance medical certificate health to verify information they have provided. The form does not allow MSD to collect additional information about the client from their original practitioner or any other health practitioner. The part of the Privacy Statement that is relevant is MSD may share information with health practitioners if it needs medical information to assess the client's eligibility. This gives MSD the authorisation to contact the appropriate health practitioners to confirm or clarify the information they have already provided as part of the application process. This includes information that is unclear or hard to read.

chunks.title: Additional information - use Client consent — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must give the client every opportunity to provide the information before the client consent form is used. If further information is required, the 'consent to release of health and disability information' form can be used. Generally, the consent form is valid for a particular purpose.

chunks.title: Additional information in limited circumstances - use a Schedule 6 request — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Before making a Schedule 6 request MSD must take the following steps: 1. MSD must request the information from the client before seeking it from the appropriate health practitioners. 2. The client must be allowed sufficient time to respond. MSD must ensure they are fully aware of the time restriction. 3. MSD must consider all other avenues for obtaining information from the client before a Schedule 6 request is used. A determination will need to be made on a case-by-case basis as to whether there is a legitimate inability to provide proof of information that is requested. If a client is not able to complete the 'consent to release of health or disability information form' due to their disability, for example they are unable to physically sign the form, then a Schedule 6 request for verification can be used to obtain the information. Only Manager Client Service Delivery can contact health practitioners. When requesting information from a client's health providers using a Schedule 6 request the Manager Client Service Delivery must do the following: - make the request in writing and - specify that the request is made under Schedule 6 of the Social Security Act 2018 and - specify the information and/or documents sought and - specify how long they have to provide that information

chunks.title: Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit
When a client (without dependent children) is paid a main benefit and also gets paid an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, use the main benefit only to calculate the standard cost.
For example, a client is getting Sole Parent Support with one child and also gets Unsupported Childs Benefit for another child, you would use the standard cost for a Sole Parent Support client with 1 child.

chunks.title: Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid
When a client is getting an Orphans and/or an Unsupported Childs Benefit and applies for Temporary Additional Support:
- the child is not treated as a dependent child for the purpose of Temporary Additional Support and
- the Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit is not chargeable income in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support
However, a client who is getting an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit can have an essential expense for the child included as an allowable cost for Temporary Additional Support provided the expense cannot be met by the Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit or a Disability Allowance.
## Disability Allowance for orphan or unsupported child
When assessing the rate of Temporary Additional Support where the client is getting a Disability Allowance on behalf of an orphan or unsupported child you must include:
- the amount of Disability Allowance being paid for the child as chargeable income and
- the total amount of Disability Allowance costs for the child as allowable costs
If the child's Disability Allowance costs exceed the maximum amount of Disability Allowance paid, the client may qualify for the disability exception amount.
## Standard costs
When a client is paid a main benefit and also gets paid an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, you would use the standard cost that relates to the main benefit only.

chunks.title: Payment — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Payment
Temporary Additional Support can be paid for a maximum of 13 weeks. It should be paid for a period of less than 13 weeks when the client's circumstances confirm this would be appropriate.
It is paid together with a client's main benefit payment, or weekly for clients not getting a benefit.

chunks.title: Period less than 13 weeks — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Period less than 13 weeks
You can pay Temporary Additional Support for a period less than 13 weeks if you determine that the client's entitlement to Temporary Additional Support will end before the end of the 13 week standard period. The period that you pay Temporary Additional Support will depend on the client's circumstances and whether they still meet the qualifications.
If you pay Temporary Additional Support for a shorter fixed period, the end date should be the day the client is no longer entitled to Temporary Additional Support.
For example, if the client is leaving New Zealand permanently Temporary Additional Support should be cancelled from the day after departure.

chunks.title: Pharmaceutical charges — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance for pharmaceutical charges. If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, this must be granted before MSD assess if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support. The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support when they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because: - they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or - their disability will last less than 6 months or - they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client’s disability, the need for treatment and that pharmaceuticals are necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are: - additional and - ongoing and - directly related to the client's disability Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include the regular, ongoing pharmaceutical charges a client has because of their disability. These costs can only be included for the portion of the costs that are not covered by the Community Services Card, High Use Health Card, Pharmaceutical Subsidy Card, medical insurance, ACC or other accident insurer. Allowable costs for pharmaceutical products are generally only for the cost of pharmaceutical products that are fully or partially subsidised under the Healthy Futures (Pae Ora) Act 2022. When a client has non-subsidised pharmaceutical costs, additional factors must be considered before the cost can be included in Disability Allowance. For example, if there is a fully subsidised or partially subsidised alternative that could be used. The part-charge and pharmacy fees for non-subsidised services such as packaging, mailing out medications and faxing are allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Extra costs in relation to pharmaceutical charges — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: In addition to the charges for medication, clients may have additional charges which can be included as allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support. These can include: - printed reports that list what pharmaceutical charges were paid over a period of time - blister packs (this refers to the way a client's medication may be packaged) - assistance to pick up medication from the pharmacy that incurs a cost (e.g. courier or mailing costs) - the cost to print, fax or electronically send prescriptions

chunks.title: Costs not included — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support do not include: - non-pharmaceutical drugs, even if the items are recommended by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner , as these costs are not additional costs directly related to a disability - pharmaceutical items not related to the client's disability (e.g. a cough suppressant for the flu, as the flu is not an ongoing disability) - illegal drugs used for medical purposes (e.g. recreational cannabis that has not been prescribed by a doctor that may be used for pain relief)

chunks.title: Proof of pharmaceutical costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: The client must provide: - a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and - receipts as proof of their ongoing pharmaceutical costs Note if a fee has been charged by a registered health practitioner or pharmacist for the cost of a report or print out to verify medical fees or pharmaceutical charges; this fee or other administration related cost can be included as a cost for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Pharmaceutical subsidies — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance. If the client is entitled to Disability Allowance, this must be granted before MSD assesses whether the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support. The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support if they do not qualify for Disability Allowance when: - they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or - their health or disability condition will last less than 6 months or - they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include: - the co-payment on fully subsidised prescription items from publicly and privately funded health providers - the cost of partially subsidised prescription items from publicly and privately funded health providers - in certain circumstances non-subsidised prescription items may be considered for Temporary Additional Support allowable costs Allowable costs can also cover the "part-charge" if the cost to manufacture the item is more than the government subsidy. The amount pharmaceuticals are subsidised by will depend on what prescription item is needed, whether it was prescribed by a publicly funded health provider or a privately funded health provider, and if the person holds a Community Services Card, Pharmaceutical Subsidy Card and/or High Use Health Card. From 1 February 2026, prescribers can issue prescriptions for up to 12 months in some cases. Any co-payment charged is per prescription, rather than each time it is dispensed. This means clients may only have to pay for one $5.00 co-payment within a 12-month period. Anyone getting a prescription may have to pay other pharmacy fees that are not subsidised (e.g. packaging, printing and faxing). This includes clients with a Community Services Card or a Pharmaceutical Subsidy Card, and families with children under 14 years. Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support cannot include the portion of pharmaceutical costs covered by the Community Services Card, High Use Health Card, Pharmaceutical Subsidy Card, ACC or other accident insurer, or medical insurance. Allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support can include the co-payment on prescription items that are subsidised by the Government. It can also be used to pay for the 'part-charge' if the cost to manufacture the item is more than the government subsidy.

chunks.title: Publicly funded providers — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Fully subsidised prescription items from publicly funded health providers (including public specialists) are free for people: - under 14 or - holding a Community Services Card (and their dependents aged 14-17 years old) or - 65 years or older (from 1 July 2024) If someone in one of the above groups is prescribed items from a publicly funded health provider, they may still have to pay a fee. For example, if they are prescribed partially subsidised and non-subsidised prescription items. This includes clients who hold a Community Services Card, Pharmaceutical Subsidy Card and/or High Use Health Card. Example 1 - client is not in a subsidised group George has asthma that has been stable for 10 years. He visits a publicly funded specialist for his inhaler. He requests to change from one of the partially subsidised inhalers to a fully subsidised inhaler. His doctor notes that both inhalers do the same thing. At the pharmacy George pays a $5.00 co-payment for his initial inhaler as he does not fall into one of the subsidised groups, and any extra inhalers needed in that 12-month period will not have another co-payment. Example 2 - client is in a subsidised group Tina visits her general practitioner (GP). They prescribe her medication she needs for her on-going disability. The medication prescribed is fully subsidised. At the pharmacy Tina does not have to pay anything for her medication as she has a Community Services Card.

chunks.title: Privately funded providers — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: When prescriptions are prescribed by privately funded health providers (including private specialists) there is a cost. This includes fully subsidised, partially subsidised and non-subsidised prescription items. Prescriptions from privately funded health providers have a: - $10.00 co-payment for people aged 14-17 years old or - $15.00 co-payment for people aged 18 years and older Example Sarah has an ongoing skin condition and visits her private specialist. She prescribed a fully subsidised prescription cream. As Sarah is over 18 years old, she is charged a $15.00 co-payment for her medicine at the pharmacy.

chunks.title: Pharmaceutical Subsidy Card — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: An individual or family unit pays the co-payment for the first 20 prescription items prescribed in any "pharmaceutical year" (defined as 1 February to 31 January). Note this applies to every new prescription and does not apply to repeat supplies on the same prescription. After 20 pharmaceutical items have been purchased by an individual or family from the same pharmacy, the pharmacist issues a Pharmaceutical Subsidy Card. Once a Pharmaceutical Subsidy Card is issued that individual or family unit will not have to pay the co-payment for the rest of the pharmaceutical year.

chunks.title: Non-Subsidised pharmaceuticals — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: When a client has non-subsidised pharmaceutical costs, additional factors must be considered before the cost can be included in Temporary Additional Support. For example, if there is a subsidised or partially subsidised alternative that could be used. Note the part-charge and pharmacy fees for non-subsided services such as packaging and faxing are additional charges that are considered allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Power, gas and heating — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Power, gas and heating
MSD must check if the client qualifies for Disability Allowance.
If the client qualifies for Disability Allowance, it must be granted before MSD assesses if the client qualifies for Temporary Additional Support.
The client may have allowable health and disability costs for Temporary Additional Support where they do not qualify for Disability Allowance because:
- they do not meet the Disability Allowance income limit or
- their disability will last less than 6 months or
- they are certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants
A registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner must complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate confirming the client’s disability, the need for treatment and that additional power is necessary. The certificate must also confirm the treatment is beneficial and of therapeutic value and that the costs are:
- additional and
- ongoing and
- directly related to the client's disability
The amount of the allowable cost is the amount over and above the normal power consumption of similar-sized households in the area at the same time of the year.
The cost of additional electricity, gas or heating costs:
- should not be paid automatically because the client has a disability and lives in a colder part of the country (the additional expense must be due to the client's disability not the area of New Zealand they live in)
- can be paid for the cost of firewood over and above normal usage if the client uses this method of heating
Calculate the amount to be paid by comparing the client's:
- costs with the average costs for your region and
- power, gas etc usage before their disability with their costs incurred now (when appropriate)
If it is unclear what the average power cost is for the region the client is in, MSD should contact Helpline.
## Proof of power, gas and heating costs
The client must provide:
- a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and
- copies of power accounts, and/or receipts for gas, coal, or firewood

chunks.title: Pre-paid funeral expenses — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Pre-paid funeral expenses
A pre-paid funeral trust fund or account is money put aside (usually in a trust) exclusively for the payment of funeral expenses. If the money can be accessed by the client and so used for other purposes, it is not considered exclusively for funeral expenses then this money is a cash asset for Temporary Additional Support.
It is usually clear whether or not the trust fund or account has been genuinely set aside for funeral expenses. Evidence that it has been set aside exclusively for funeral expenses include:
- the trust fund/account is only paid out on production of a death certificate
- the client cannot usually access the funds
- if a client can access the fund, there are limited conditions on withdrawal, such as re-locating overseas
- the trust fund/account is only payable to the funeral director or administrator of the client's estate
- the client cannot generally access the interest earned from the trust fund or account
Where the trust fund or account has been set aside for funeral expenses and cannot be accessed or converted into cash then this money is not a cash asset for Temporary Additional Support.
For more information see:
- Cash assets

chunks.title: Prisoners — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Prisoners
Prisoners and clients on remand cannot generally get Temporary Additional Support while detained.
However, clients on home detention may qualify.
In some circumstances Temporary Additional Support can continue when the client is imprisoned.
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances of the client before making a decision.

chunks.title: Proof of transport costs — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Proof of transport costs
The client must provide:
- a Disability Allowance medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner and
- proof of their ongoing travel costs
The costs of travelling to receive treatment, support services, or to visit their registered health practitioner may be considered as additional expenses arising from the client's disability.
## Travel not specifically stated on the Medical Certificate
Where 'travel' is not specifically written on the Disability Allowance medical certificate it can be included as an allowable cost without further verification if the medical practitioner or nurse practitioner has verified the:
- client will be attending a specific treatment or support service
## Public transport and taxis
If the client is using public transport or taxis they must provide receipts as proof of their costs.
When a client has a Total Mobility card or vouchers, the cost of their travel fares is subsidised.
Clients with a Community Services Card can get a 50% discount on public transport fares through Community Connect.
## Private vehicle
If the client is using their own car, the rates listed in the table below are used to calculate the costs.
The following rates have been set and reflect the reasonable running costs (excluding fixed costs) of a vehicle dependent on engine size.
Running costs include consumables such as, petrol and oil. Fixed costs (not included in the calculation) include costs such as, relicensing, insurance and Warrants of Fitness.
Fixed costs are not included as all clients will incur these costs when they own a vehicle. For example, people without a disability would still incur fixed costs.
Use these rates to calculate the allowable motor vehicle running costs:
cc rating
paid per kilometre
Up to 1000
29 cents per km
1000-1350
30 cents per km
1351-2000
35 cents per km
Over 2000
40 cents per km

chunks.title: Public transport to work — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Public transport to work
Allowable public transport costs can be included in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support.
In addition, these costs must be essential to meet the family's daily living needs and could not be readily avoided or varied when the expense was incurred.
If a client or their partner is in paid employment you can include the costs of public transport to and from their place of work in the assessment of Temporary Additional Support.
Clients who are using public transport and have a Community Services Card can get a 50% discount on public transport fares.
To qualify for Temporary Additional Support, the client must take all necessary steps to obtain financial assistance from all other sources to reduce their costs.
If a client has not used their Community Services Card to apply for the discount, you must discuss their reasons if their actual public transport costs are higher than they would be if the 50% discount was applied.
If the client did not apply for the discount, you must consider their reasons and decide if they had a good reason not to take the necessary steps (e.g. the client has a disability and there are accessibility issues with applying for the Community Connect discount through a public transport provider’s website, and this is the only way to apply).
If there is no good reason, you should consider declining, reducing or cancelling Temporary Additional Support.
## Verification
The client must provide verification of their public transport costs.

chunks.title: Qualifications — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
To qualify for Temporary Additional Support, a client must:
- be aged 16 years or more
- complete a Temporary Additional Support application or re-application form
- meet a cash asset test
- have a minimum deficiency of $1.00 after calculating the formula for Temporary Additional Support
- take all necessary steps to obtain other financial assistance or resources available
- take reasonable steps to reduce their costs or increase their chargeable income
- be a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder (i.e. not be in New Zealand unlawfully, or here on a temporary entry class visa) and
- generally be ordinarily resident in New Zealand

chunks.title: Reasonable steps — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Temporary Additional Support is last resort financial assistance for clients who have regular essential living costs that cannot be met from their chargeable income and other resources. To qualify for Temporary Additional Support a client must take reasonable steps to try to reduce their costs or increase their chargeable income, where possible.

chunks.title: Examples of reasonable steps — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Reasonable steps to try and reduce their costs or increase their chargeable income, may include but are not limited to, the client: - no longer purchasing non-essential items - seeking budgeting advice for help to reduce expenses - re-negotiating debt repayments to a lesser repayment amount - reducing costs by negotiating or applying for reduced payments of court fines - reducing costs by using public transport - requesting debt repayments to be temporarily stopped - refinancing debt, for example a mortgage - consolidating debt to reduce interest and repayment amounts - seeking part-time or full-time paid employment, or increasing hours to increase income - stopping contributions to KiwiSaver and/or other retirement schemes You should consider declining, reducing or cancelling Temporary Additional Support where the client has not taken reasonable steps to reduce their expenses or increase their chargeable income, where possible. There will be some situations where the client may not be able to reduce their expenses or increase their income, in these cases a client may still qualify for Temporary Additional Support.

chunks.title: Reasonable steps generally must have been discussed with client — extra help > temporary additional support
chunks.text: Generally you would not consider a step 'reasonable' if it has not been discussed with the client. This would usually mean not considering discretion to cancel or decline Temporary Additional Support until the client re-applies and you have checked whether they have undertaken the steps identified when they were granted Temporary Additional Support. However, it is not essential that a step has been discussed, and there could be exceptions where the client would have been aware that it was reasonable for them to have taken a particular step. For example, a client turning down paid employment that they were clearly capable of doing. It is important to note that clients do not have to complete all the reasonable steps discussed at application, as long as they take some steps. If the client has not completed the steps, you should consider: - why the client was unable to complete the steps - whether the client has completed steps that were not discussed at the prior application - whether the steps discussed are still relevant for the client to take Where a client was unable to take a reasonable step, you should discuss why this was not taken and note it.
