Unless the person has entered residential care or has been admitted to hospital permanently, the benefit should be stopped from the beginning of the next pay period following the event. MSD will need to determine if the client qualifies for another benefit.

chunks.title: Person enters residential care or hospital — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Emergency Benefit may continue at the existing rate for 28 days from the date the person left the client's care. This is to allow a period of transition for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.

chunks.title: Death of the person being cared for — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: When the person being cared for dies the client no longer qualifies for Emergency Benefit on the ground of caring for a person. The benefit may end 28 days following the date of event and can continue to be paid at the existing rate. At the end of the 28-day period it needs to be determined if the client qualifies for another benefit. Note if the client has other changes of circumstances, such as a change in income, the rate of main benefit and extra help will need to be reassessed.

chunks.title: Mandatory Reviews — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Generally, clients getting Emergency Benefit must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date or their payments will suspend. If the person being cared for temporarily leaves the client's care and Emergency Benefit will continue, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client is unable to respond to the review (even if they had more time) based on their individual circumstances, they may qualify for an exemption. Generally, when the Mandatory Review is only for Emergency Benefit and the benefit will stop at the end of the 28-day continuation period e.g. the person being cared for has entered residential care or hospital, or died, and the review is due, an exemption will apply. The client must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Generally, clients getting a discretionary benefit such as Emergency Benefit must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will be excluded from their payments. The client must also complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for Emergency Benefit and the rate payable, or their payments will suspend. When the person being cared for is a dependent child who turns 18 while they have temporarily left care, the client must complete the review of circumstances or their payments will suspend. When the person being cared for is a dependent child who has entered residential care or hospital, or died, and was due to turn 18 during the continuation of payment period, the client is not required to complete a review of circumstances. However, if Emergency Benefit and any extra help is continuing for up to 28 days because the person being cared for has entered residential care or hospital, or died, and a dependent child turns 18 (who is not the person being cared for), the client must still complete the review of circumstances or their payments will suspend.

chunks.title: Private hospital and homes — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Private hospital and homes
Emergency Benefit can be paid at the full rate regardless of the period of hospitalisation when a client is:
- admitted to a private hospital or
- admitted to a private home that provides residential care disability services
If the client receives Extra Help this will need to be reviewed to see if their costs are continuing.
For more information see:
- Residential Care Subsidy
- Residential Support Subsidy
## Transfer from home to hospital
If a client is a resident of a home and has been transferred to a hospital, their rate of payment can be reduced when they have been in hospital for 13 weeks.
Continue payment to the home unless the client requests otherwise. Increase the client's benefit to the appropriate full rate, if it has been reduced, from the day the client is transferred back to the home.

chunks.title: Protected earnings rate — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Protected earnings rate
Both the District Court Act and the Summary Proceedings Act provide that every Ministry of Justice attachment order must specify a 'protected earnings rate'. The protected earnings rate is usually 60% of the client’s net earnings after PAYE tax has been deducted or withheld.
If the attachment order will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate, then the order will not operate and you must cancel or return the attachment order to the Ministry of Justice.
Calculating the client's income differs between attachment orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act and the District Court Act, in that different benefits are taken into account.
It is important to determine what type of attachment order has been issued.
Summary Proceedings Act
For orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act, the calculation of the client's income does not include Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support, Disability Allowance, Child Disability Allowance, Winter Energy Payment, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
District Court Act
For orders made under the District Court Act, the client's income includes Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support and Disability Allowance but does not include Child Disability Allowance, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
## Example
An attachment order is received from the Ministry of Justice for $60.00 per week. The order lists the client's protected earnings rate as $286.53 per week:
We need to calculate whether adding the deduction of $60.00 will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate:
Calculate protected earnings rate
Jobseeker Support - single person 25+ net rate (as at 1 April 2026)
$372.55
Plus Accommodation Supplement (Area 2)
$105.00
total net earnings
$477.55
60% of total net earnings (= protected earnings)
$286.53
Calculate if Attachment Order will exceed protected earnings
Total net earnings
$477.55
Less Child Support deduction
$80.00
Less Ministry of Social Development debts
$55.00
Sub total
$342.55
Less Court Order
$60.00
Total
$282.55
The attachment order amount of $60 takes the client's total net income remaining to $282.55, which is below the protected earnings rate of $286.53 per week. The attachment order will not operate therefore you must return it to the Ministry of Justice for the order to be amended.

chunks.title: Qualifies for another benefit — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Qualifies for another benefit
A client may qualify for another benefit due to a change in their circumstances. It is also important to determine if the client still qualifies for Emergency Benefit.
For example:
- if a client meets the residential qualification for a particular benefit
If the client qualifies for more than one benefit they must be told which benefit is the most beneficial for their particular circumstances. You will need to advise them of:
- benefit rates
- the effect of any income they may receive (income reduction and any exemptions) and
- benefit obligations
The client must make the final decision on which benefit they receive after being given all relevant information.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit qualifications
- Processing standards Client transfers to another benefit type [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Rate of payment - sole parents — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Rate of payment - sole parents
If payment of Emergency Benefit is to continue while a sole parent client is in prison, you will need to determine the rate to pay to the temporary caregiver.
The Emergency Benefit should generally be paid at the equivalent rate of Unsupported Child's benefit that would be payable if the caregiver qualified for this.
## Discretion
However there is discretion to continue payment at the full sole parent rate.
You can consider including the following costs to calculate the rate to pay the temporary caregiver while the client is in prison:
- rent or outgoings if the children are being cared for in the client's home
- the client's other commitments if these costs are for essential items and they cannot be suspended, such as Child Support payments (where the client does not qualify for an exemption) or hire purchase for an essential item
Note the total amount paid to the temporary caregiver must not exceed the maximum amount of Emergency Benefit payable.
## SWIFTT
The Emergency Benefit, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit should continue in the client's name and be paid to the caregiver as an agent in SWIFTT.
When the temporary caregiver is to be paid less than the maximum rate of Emergency Benefit, you will need to add this as a non-standard rate using the SNSRA screen in SWIFTT.
For more information see:
- Examples - sole parents
- Decision guidelines - sole parents
- Sole parents

chunks.title: Gets a Student Allowance — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Gets a Student Allowance
When a child gets a Student Allowance or an Independent Circumstances Allowance under the Student Allowances Regulations 1998 they are no longer a dependent child.
## Date of review
The child should be excluded from the start of the pay period following the date Student Allowance (or Independent Circumstances Allowance) commences.
Note there are specific rules for deciding whether a child is considered a dependent child when they turn 18 and are continuing in education.
## Family tax credit
Family tax credits should be stopped from the start of the pay period following the date Student Allowance was granted, to avoid an overpayment with Inland Revenue for the client.

chunks.title: Gets a Student Loan — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Gets a Student Loan
Getting a Student Loan (including the living cost component) does not mean the child is financially independent.
If the child continues to be the client's primary responsibility and maintained as a member of their family and financially dependent (that is the parent is meeting some of the costs for the child) the child can continue to be included in the benefit until the start of the pay period following:
- the date they turn 18 or
- where the child is 18 and continuing in education, the earlier of: the date they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education orthe date the child is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required orthe date the child is financially independent orthe date the child leaves the parent or caregiver's care or31 December of the year they turn 18
- the date they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education or
- the date the child is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required or
- the date the child is financially independent or
- the date the child leaves the parent or caregiver's care or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
Note a parent or caregiver getting a discretionary benefit such as Emergency Benefit must complete a review of circumstances when a dependent child turns 18, and when the child is excluded (if they continued to be included in the parent or caregiver's benefit after the child turned 18).
## Extra help
Where the dependent child is required to live away from home to undertake their tertiary study, the client may be able to get assistance for accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Release from prison — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Release from prison
A client may be entitled to Emergency Benefit when they are released from prison. The date to recommence payment depends on the length of time the client has been in prison.
For more information see:
- Prisoners no stand-down applies

chunks.title: Release on bail — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Release on bail
When a client is released on bail, Emergency Benefit can be paid from the date of release providing the client:
- is limited in their capacity or unable to work for a period because of a temporary health condition or
- because of a health condition, cannot work for an indefinite period
A medical certificate is required as proof.
Note if the client has been in custody for more than 31 days an initial stand-down will be imposed.
For more information see:
- Prisoners no stand-down applies

chunks.title: Remanded in custody — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Remanded in custody
Generally, when a client is remanded in custody awaiting a further court appearance their benefit should be stopped. However, there is discretion to continue payment of Emergency Benefit after taking the client's financial circumstances and commitments into account.
When deciding whether to continue paying Emergency Benefit for the period of remand for a particular client consider the following:
- has the client been remanded pending further hearing or for sentencing
- does the client have continuing costs that cannot be avoided, such as rent and hire purchase for essential items
- does the client have client have a partner or dependent children
Every situation should be considered on a case-by-case basis.
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances of the client before making a decision.

chunks.title: Review of Annual Income — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Clients getting Emergency Benefit may have a Review of Annual Income if their equivalent benefit is: - Supported Living Payment - Sole Parent Support - Jobseeker Support - sole parents only - New Zealand Superannuation The Review of Annual Income ensures clients getting Emergency Benefit have been getting the correct rate of payment for the past 52 weeks. Clients do not have a Review of Annual Income if their benefit has not been reduced at any point during the period that income is assessed (the 52-week review period). Clients who did not get any income during this period will also not have a review. Note the Review of Annual Income is a separate review process to a Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Income received during the review period — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Income received during the 52-week period following the client's commencement date, and each 52-week period after that, is assessed against the benefit paid to the client during this time. Most types of income are charged against the Emergency Benefit for the review year the income was earned in or the period it relates to. The relevant period may be a period in the past or a future date. Only income charged during the current review period is considered for the Review of Annual Income. If the client has transferred between benefits, but has continuously been getting a benefit that can have income charged annually, the commencement date is the date they first started getting an annual benefit.

chunks.title: Child Support income for Reviews of Annual Income — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Non-information share Child Support Non-information share Child Support payments are charged as income using the general charging rules used for most other types of income. Any non-information share Child Support payments charged as income during the current review period are included in the Review of Annual Income. Information share Child Support Information share Child Support payments are charged forward as income, using defined rules. The income charge is always for 4 or 5 weeks from when the client gets the payment, regardless of what period the payment relates to. Any information share Child Support payments charged as income during the current review period are included in the Review of Annual Income. Note the amount of information share Child Support payment charged as income may not be the same amount of Child Support a client got in the review period. This could happen if a client gets an information share Child Support payment shortly before the end of the review period. Only the income charged during the review period can be included in the Review of Annual Income. Example Mercutio gets an Emergency Benefit equivalent to Supported Living Payment and gets information share Child Support payments from his child's other parent. Mercutio's review period for his Review of Annual Income is 6 September to 5 September the following year. Mercutio gets an information share Child Support payment on 21 August. This payment is charged forward for 4 weeks, from the week beginning 19 August. Only the income charged from 19 August to 5 September will be included in this years' Review of Annual Income. The remainder of the 4-week income charge related to that Child Support payment will be included in the following year's review.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review for Emergency Benefit — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Mandatory Reviews for Emergency Benefit will only apply to clients whose benefit has an expiry date of more than 52-weeks, or whose Emergency Benefit has no expiry date. MSD must review a client’s Emergency Benefit within 52-weeks of when the benefit commenced, or 52-weeks from when the client’s last Mandatory Review was completed. The purpose of a Mandatory Review for Emergency Benefit is to: - check for any changes to a client’s circumstances - determine if the client still meets the qualifications for Emergency Benefit and - review the rate of Emergency Benefit payable If a client declares a change in circumstances that may affect their conditions of grant, MSD should check if the client continues to meet the conditions of grant for the Emergency Benefit. Note the Review of Annual Income is a separate process to a Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Clients getting Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Clients also getting Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance have these reviewed at the same time as their Mandatory Review for Emergency Benefit. Example: client is getting Emergency Benefit and Disability Allowance Michael has been getting Disability Allowance since 8 December 2025, and his Emergency Benefit commenced on 4 April 2026. Because the initial Mandatory Review date is determined by the Emergency Benefit commencement date, the review date for both Disability Allowance and Emergency Benefit will be reset to 52 weeks from 4 April 2026.

chunks.title: Clients getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: A client getting Emergency Benefit (and the expiry date for the Emergency Benefit is more than 52 weeks from the commencement of the benefit or last Mandatory Review, or there is no expiry date) and Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, will have a Mandatory Review for their Emergency Benefit at least once in a 52-week period, but it will be separate to the Mandatory Review for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Notice period for a Mandatory Review — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Clients are notified at least 20 working days before their Mandatory Review date, unless their Emergency Benefit is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison. The notice period allows sufficient time for clients to respond to the Mandatory Review. Note if a client's Emergency Benefit is suspended when the Mandatory Review notice is sent, they are not required to respond to their Mandatory Review until their Emergency Benefit is to be resumed.

chunks.title: Responding to the Mandatory Review — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: To respond to the Mandatory Review, the client must: - confirm or provide current information about their circumstances and - provide further information to MSD if requested. Clients must confirm the information MSD holds is correct or provide any new information before their review date. When a client has responded to the Mandatory Review and continues to qualify for Emergency Benefit, their next review date is set 52 weeks from the date their Mandatory Review was completed, (if the expiry date for the Emergency Benefit is more than 52 weeks or there is no expiry date).

chunks.title: Client does not respond to Mandatory Review — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: When a client does not respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, the Emergency Benefit will suspend. If the client does not respond to the Mandatory Review to confirm their circumstances within 8 weeks after their payments have suspended, the Emergency Benefit will be cancelled. A client can still do their Mandatory Review during those 8 weeks. However, once the Emergency Benefit has cancelled, the client will need to apply for Emergency Benefit if they still need this assistance. A client's Emergency Benefit cannot be resumed before they have responded to their Mandatory Review during the 8-week suspension period.

chunks.title: Emergency Benefit suspends — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: If a client's Emergency Benefit suspends as the result of the client not responding to their Mandatory Review, all of their assistance will also suspend, except for the following payments: - Child Disability Allowance - Orphan's Benefit - Unsupported Child's Benefit - Childcare Subsidy - OSCAR (Out of School Care and Recreational Subsidy) - Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment

chunks.title: When the Mandatory Review is complete — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: The Mandatory Review is complete when MSD makes a decision about whether the client continues to qualify for Emergency Benefit and the rate of benefit payable. MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g. client has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Mandatory Reviews for clients with partners — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: When a client has a partner, both the client and partner's circumstances are included in the review. Changes to the partner's circumstances (e.g. income, employment, living arrangements and other factors) must be included in the Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Cash assets — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Clients getting Emergency Benefit may have met the exceptional circumstance criteria for having all or part of their cash assets disregarded when they were granted their benefit on the grounds of hardship. If a client has a Mandatory Review for their Emergency Benefit and there has been a change to their assets, MSD may consider if the exceptional circumstances criteria still applies and if the cash assets should still be disregarded.

chunks.title: Shared care — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Shared care
shared care only applies when the parents of a child are living apart, the child lives (for at least 40% of the time) with each parent and both parents apply for a benefit in respect of that child.
In shared care situations you can only pay a sole parent rate of benefit to the parent that has the greater responsibility.
For more information see:
- Decision Guidelines for shared care
Emergency Benefit cannot be paid to the 'other' parent on the basis that they care for the child for part of the time. Parents are expected to arrange care of their children to allow at least one parent to work.
Never pay two sole parent rates of benefit in respect of the same child (that is one child can't be included in 2 benefits at the same time).
## Only one parent applies for benefit
When only one parent applies for a benefit in respect of a child in shared care situations, the child still has to be a dependent child before benefit eligibility in respect of that child can be determined.
For more information see:
- Dependent child
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
For information on the payment of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit in shared care situations see:
- Family tax credit Shared care
- Best Start tax credit Shared care
## Childcare and OSCAR subsidy
For information on the payment of Childcare and OSCAR subsidy in shared care cases see:
- Childcare subsidy Shared care - principal caregiver
- OSCAR subsidy Shared care - principal caregiver
## Child Disability Allowance
For information on the payment of Child Disability Allowance in shared care see:
- Child Disability Allowance Shared care - principal caregiver
## Winter Energy Payment
For information on the payment of Winter Energy Payment in shared care see:
- Single and caring for a child

chunks.title: Sole parents — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Sole parents
When a sole parent client is imprisoned the Emergency Benefit will generally need to be cancelled.
The Emergency Benefit should be cancelled from the day following imprisonment.
Note generally, sole parents on Emergency Benefit receive the Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
For more information see:
- Emergency Maintenance Allowance Imprisonment
You may need to find out who is caring for the client's children and the length of time the client is likely to be in prison. This information can be obtained by contacting the prison liaison officer at the Department of Corrections.
## Exception
There is discretion to pay all or part of the Emergency Benefit to a temporary caregiver caring for the client's children.
There is also discretion to continue payment if the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance.
For more information to help you decide these cases see:
- Decision guidelines - sole parents
- Temporary caregiver
- Rate of payment - sole parents
- Examples - sole parents
- Remanded in custody

chunks.title: Special Disability Allowance — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Special Disability Allowance
A Special Disability Allowance is paid to the partner of a client who is receiving the hospital rate or Residential Care Subsidy. It is paid to the client in the community to help with the extra costs of their partner's hospitalisation, for example travel costs to visit the patient.
Note that Special Disability Allowance is:
- granted without the client having to apply
- paid separately from Disability Allowance and
- not income or asset tested
Special Disability Allowance can start from the date the client in the community starts receiving a single rate of benefit, and their partner starts receiving a hospital rate of benefit or becomes financially eligible for Residential Care Subsidy.
Special Disability Allowance should be stopped from the first available date if the person receiving it is also admitted to hospital.
## SWIFTT
Grant Special Disability Allowance using code 838 on the SSUPI screen.
For more information see:
- Special Disability Allowance
- Rates of Special Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Specific engagements — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Specific engagements
Specific engagements are interactions that can meet the same purpose as the Mandatory Review. These interactions can capture information that confirms if a client still qualifies for Emergency Benefit.
Specific engagements are when a client has an interaction with MSD, and this results in a full review of the client's circumstances.
For example, specific engagements may include when a client contacts MSD to:
- discuss a change in circumstances or
- apply for assistance.
If the specific engagement meets the same purpose as a Mandatory Review and the client still qualifies, their Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from when the specific engagement was completed.

chunks.title: Split care — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Split care
Split care is when parents with 2 or more children are living apart and each parent has the care of at least one of their children on a full-time basis.
The child(ren) that is living with the Emergency Benefit client can be included as a dependent child.
Note in split care situations generally only one parent can receive Sole Parent Support. The other parent must qualify, in their own right, for another benefit.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support Split care

chunks.title: Student Loan repayments — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Student Loan repayments
Clients with a Student Loan must make repayments to Inland Revenue when the income they get is over the repayment threshold. This level is called the 'income threshold'.
A person must make repayments to Inland Revenue when their income is over $464.00 gross per week ($24,128 gross per year) as at 1 April 2026.
Note non-taxable Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Accommodation Supplement and Winter Energy Payments do not count as income.
If the client's income is over the income threshold, the Ministry of Social Development can make the deduction. However, this is only done if the client requests it.
If the client's portion of benefit is below the income threshold, there is no provision to make voluntary repayments through SWIFTT.
The client can make voluntary payments direct to Inland Revenue at any time.
Note the following:
- Student Loan deductions can only be made from taxable benefits
- Student Loan deductions cannot be made if the client's benefit is below the income threshold
- when a client receives a married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit only the client's portion is taken into consideration when assessing Student Loan repayments
- when a client is receiving a reduced rate of payment due to other income, the Student Loan deduction is assessed on the net payment after income deduction
## For more information on Student Loans see:
- Students Student Loans

chunks.title: Study — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Study
Clients (and partners) have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any change in their circumstances that may affect their qualification for Emergency Benefit, such as commencing study.
When an Emergency Benefit client intends to or has commenced study, you will need to find out:
- the date study starts and
- the type of study, that is part-time or full-time
This will help you decide the appropriate review action required.
For more information see:
- Client engaged in study
- Partner engaged in study

chunks.title: SWIFTT process to pay a partner — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT process to pay a partner
When you decide to continue payment of Emergency Benefit to the partner of a client who has been imprisoned, you will need to determine the most appropriate SWIFTT process to enable payment to be made to the partner.
The process for payment will depend on the following:
- the period in prison is in the past
- the client is due to be released from prison shortly
- the client is likely to be in prison for more than 28 days and
- the rate of payment for the partner
Note that there is discretion to pay the full married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit.
## Period in prison has passed or release is imminent
Generally you should use the SBDR screen in SWIFTT to:
- suspend the client's portion of Emergency Benefit for the period in prison and
- pay the appropriate rate of Emergency Benefit to the partner
## Period in prison exceeds 28 days
When the Emergency Benefit is to continue, and be paid to the partner you will need to contact Helpline for advice regarding the SWIFTT process to use.
For more information contact Helpline or see:
- Decision guidelines - clients with a partner

chunks.title: Tax Certificates — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Tax Certificates
Work and Income does not issue tax certificates to clients. If a client requests information about their tax details they must be referred to Inland Revenue to get a "Summary of Earnings" or a "Personal Tax Summary".
## Exception
Tax details can be issued if a client:
- dies - you can provide details to the estate solicitor, administrator, executor etc or
- is paid a New Zealand benefit overseas - details will be automatically sent to the client in April each year

chunks.title: Tax codes — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Tax codes
Emergency Benefit is taxed at the 'M' rate.
Emergency Benefit is always considered the client's primary source of income regardless of the amount paid. If the client has other income this is always considered the client's secondary income. Clients can apply to Inland Revenue for a tailored tax code for their other income.
## SWIFTT
You can view a client's current monthly tax details in STAXQ. The client's tax history can be viewed in STAXI.

chunks.title: Taxation — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Taxation
Emergency Benefit is a taxable benefit. MSD makes payments to clients at the net rate after the deduction of tax. MSD passes the tax on to Inland Revenue.
Generally, MSD will request clients to provide MSD with their Inland Revenue IRD number or evidence of their IRD number.

chunks.title: Temporary care — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Temporary care
Generally a client will not be considered as the person primarily responsible for the child when the period of care is temporary. Examples of temporary care are:
- school holidays
- Christmas or other public holidays
- during the temporary incapacity of the primary caregiver or
- primary caregiver is in prison
## Extra assistance during temporary care
Any assistance for additional costs due to temporary care situations should be met, in the first instance, by the custodial parent. Where this is not available, you can consider Special Needs Grants assistance for the client.
For more information see:
- Special Needs Grants

chunks.title: Temporary caregiver — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Temporary caregiver
When a client is imprisoned, you will need to find out who is caring for the client's children and the length of time the client is likely to be in prison. This information can be obtained by contacting the prison liaison officer at the Department of Corrections.
If another person is caring for the client's dependent children, generally the temporary caregiver will need to apply for financial assistance in their own right.
They may be entitled to:
- have the children included as dependent children in their current benefit
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Emergency Benefit - Caring responsibilities or
- family tax credit and Best Start tax credit through Inland Revenue
## Exception
There is discretion to pay all or part of the Emergency Benefit to a temporary caregiver caring for the patient and client's children.
There is also discretion to continue payment if the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance.
For more information to help you decide, see:
- Decision guidelines - sole parents
- Rate of payment - sole parents
- Examples - sole parents
- Remanded in custody
- Sole parents

chunks.title: Terminal benefit for a single client — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit for a single client
Generally Emergency Benefit stops from the date following the death of a single client with no children, however, there is some discretion to continue the payment of benefit for up to 28 days. When payment is continued after the date of death, it is referred to as terminal benefit.
Circumstances to consider for continued benefit payment beyond a single client's date of death include:
- when the deceased client's domestic situation results in a transition cost for a family member, causing hardship
Example: accommodation and other household costs when client has been sharing accommodation
or
- when there are exceptional and justified costs associated with the death of the client
Example: multiple deaths within one family
Payment should not continue for 28 days following the death of a single client to meet funeral expenses. A Funeral Grant may be available for this purpose.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit payments to surviving person or person caring for the children — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit payments to surviving person or person caring for the children
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children.
## Surviving partner
When the benefit is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person's and the surviving person's portion of the benefit is paid. Payment is the total benefit as well as any ongoing extra help. It does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit.
The deceased person's portion of terminal benefit is paid to their bank account.
A surviving person can apply to have the deceased person's portion of terminal benefit paid to them. When an application is received, terminal benefit (or remaining unpaid balance) can be paid to that applicant.
The surviving person's benefit should be reviewed to determine the best option financially for the person.
## Surviving children
When the deceased client has no surviving partner but has surviving children, the payment of terminal benefit can be made to the person caring for the deceased client's children.
When an application is received, the remaining unpaid balance of terminal benefit can be paid to the carer.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit rate — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: The provision to continue the benefit payment for 28 days following the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit. Benefit payment is continued at the rate which was payable to the client and partner (if any) at the date of death. A terminal benefit includes extra help being paid (for up to 28 days following the date of death) but does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments.

chunks.title: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments do not form part of terminal benefit. If the deceased client was getting these payments and there is a surviving partner, transfer these payments to the partner.

chunks.title: Benefit paid at a reduced rate — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: When the client's benefit was paid at a reduced rate at the date of death, the terminal benefit is also paid at the reduced rate. Benefit payments may have been reduced due to: - hospitalisation The deceased client's benefit was reduced as they were in hospital for more than 13 weeks. - income - debt repayment when benefit arrears are due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit paymentdo not recover debts in full, from terminal benefit payments - when benefit arrears are due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit payment - do not recover debts in full, from terminal benefit payments - Child Support if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewedChild Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenuewhen a surviving partner or family member makes enquiries, refer them to Inland Revenue - if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed - Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenue - when a surviving partner or family member makes enquiries, refer them to Inland Revenue - court attachment orders - redirection of benefit to Kāinga Ora or a community housing provider When the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. For more information see: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client Note all of the above deductions will continue to be made from the terminal benefit payments unless they are manually stopped before cancellation.

chunks.title: Client was money managed — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the deceased client had Money Management imposed, this must be stopped from the day after they passed away. The full amount of terminal benefit will be paid to the person that the benefit is payable to.

chunks.title: Changes to benefit rate payable — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Rates of main benefits being paid as part of Terminal benefit are adjusted to reflect changes in the rate payable arising from legislative amendments, such as the Annual General Adjustment of benefit rates on 1 April each year.

chunks.title: Underpaid — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Underpaid
When a client has been underpaid Emergency Benefit and is owed arrears, MSD will work out the amount of tax and pass this on to Inland Revenue.
From 1 April 2024, if an arrears payment relates to a previous tax year, the arrears will not be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment. This means the client will not have to pay any more tax on the payment.
Only arrears payments relating to the current tax year will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment.
Example
A client is paid arrears on 12 June 2025. This payment represents arrears for 25 March 2025 to 8 June 2025.
The arrears for 25 March to 31 March 2025 represent a past tax year, so they will not be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment. The arrears for 1 April to 8 June 2025 represent the current tax year, so they will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment.
## Overpaid
If a client has been overpaid, the overpayment is always established for the net amount. Inland Revenue will return the tax portion of the overpayment directly to MSD.
The overpayment will reduce the amount of benefit and tax paid in the tax year in which the overpayment was made, that is, the overpayment will directly relate to the tax year(s) in which it occurred.

chunks.title: Verification — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Verification
You must be satisfied that you can accurately identify the deceased client's benefit record.
Generally we will accept verbal notification of a client's death. This advice can be acted on when you determine the relationship of the caller to the deceased client and obtaining sufficient information to provide confirmation of the deceased's identity.
Follow-up verification should generally be requested. A copy of the death certificate or a copy of the death notice is acceptable support documentation.

chunks.title: Verification from Internal Affairs — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Verification from Internal Affairs
If a client can't produce a copy of a birth certificate, you can request one using the "“Request for NZ birth Certificate" form (BDM93B).
Requests for verification of births can be made to:
Certificate TeamBirths, Deaths and Marriages PO Box 10-526 Wellington 6143

chunks.title: Verification of income — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Verification of income
The client will need to provide verification of any income earned over their 52 week period.
If the client cannot provide verification (for example payslips) then you can contact the employer and ask them to complete the Employment and earnings information for reviews form (V26) form.
For further details on how to charge income see:
- Core Policy Income

chunks.title: Weekend leave — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Weekend leave
Emergency Benefit is paid for a seven day period, covering Monday to Sunday. Therefore, where the client is receiving the hospital rate and is on weekend leave you should pay the appropriate full rate of benefit for the number of days they are on weekend leave and subsequently incurring additional expenses in the community.
## Example
If the client is on leave from Friday to Monday, you will need to pay the appropriate full rate of Emergency Benefit for 4 days. Generally, you will do this by completing a back dated review so that SWIFTT will pay the appropriate full rate of Emergency Benefit for 4 days.
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.

chunks.title: When an extension or exemption can be given — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: When a client needs more time to respond to the Mandatory Review, they may be able to get an extension. If a client is unable to respond to the review, they may be able to get an exemption. Clients must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption. A client cannot get an extension or exemption on or after the Mandatory Review date. Note even if a client gets an extension or exemption, they must still advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Emergency Benefit or the rate payable.

chunks.title: Extension - client needs more time to respond to review — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: Clients may be able to get an extension if there is a good and sufficient reason why they cannot complete their Mandatory Review in time. When a client needs more time to complete their review, they must let MSD know before their review date. The extension can only be granted before the review date. If MSD determines the client has a good and sufficient reason, the client can get an extension of up to 20 working days. Good and sufficient reasons may include (but are not limited to): - the client is unexpectedly hospitalised - death or illness in the client's immediate family - the client is experiencing or escaping a family violence situation Note a client can get multiple short extensions, however the maximum amount of time that can be given for an extension is a total of 20 working days from the client's original review date.

chunks.title: Exemption - client is unable to respond to review — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text: A client may be able to get an exemption when they are experiencing an unforeseen event or situation that is beyond their control, and this means they are unable to respond to their Mandatory Review (even if they had more time). The client must let MSD know before their review date to discuss their circumstances. Exemption reasons may include (but are not limited to): - localised natural disaster that affects the client but not the whole region (e.g. the client's property is affected by a landslip) - unexpected serious illness or an accident affecting the client or their immediate family member - the client's benefit is ending because a child has left their care suddenly and the Mandatory Review is due during the 28-day continuation of payment - the client's benefit is ending because the person they are caring for has died or entered residential care or hospital and the Mandatory Review is due during the 28-day continuation of payment Generally, an exemption would also apply when a client's benefit (paid equivalent to Supported Living Payment) is ending within 28 days because they no longer meet the medical qualifications. If MSD determines an exemption applies, the client is not be required to respond to their Mandatory Review, and the review date is reset to 52 weeks from their current review date. Example: Adina is getting Emergency Benefit and has a Mandatory Review due on 12 July 2026. However, Adina's home is damaged by a small-scale flash flooding, and she cannot return home. Because Adina has lost all her possessions and is focused on finding accommodation, MSD determines it is not reasonable for Adina to respond to her Mandatory Review by her review date. In this case, MSD grants an exemption. Adina's next Mandatory Review is set for 52-weeks from the original review date.

chunks.title: Young partner not yet subject to obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Young partner not yet subject to obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning
A young partner of a main beneficiary who is not yet subject to the obligation to be in education, training or work based learning can continue to be paid a benefit for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason if the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet these obligations
## Example (but not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A young person who is not yet subject to the education obligation as their youngest dependent child is less than 12 months (and there is no Teen Parent Unit place available for them) wishes to holiday in Australia.
As long as the travel will not prevent the young person from meeting their other obligations (eg their parenting and budgeting obligations) they can continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Partners of main beneficiaries who have youth activity obligations
- Young partners who are exempt from their youth activity obligations
- Absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days for an approved reason
- Activity failures for young partners

chunks.title: Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations — main benefits > emergency benefit > changes and reviews emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations
A young partner of a main beneficiary who is exempt from all their youth activity obligations can continue to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason.
A young partner who is exempt from some of their youth activity obligations can continue to receive their payment for any reason for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations.
## Example includes (but not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A young person who is exempt from all of their activity obligations advises that they wish to travel to Australia to visit friends.
The young person is able to be absent from New Zealand and continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
Note that a client with a partial exemption is still subject to some obligations and therefore they can only be paid while they are overseas if the travel will not prevent them from meeting their obligations.
For more information see:
- Activity failures for young partners

chunks.title: Charging income — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Charging income
If you are paying Emergency Benefit equivalent to a benefit then you must use the appropriate income test for that benefit. In these instances the income deduction will need to be calculated and the correct manual non-standard rate of Emergency Benefit added to SWIFTT. For more information see:
- Charging income - caring for a person
- Sole Parent Support Charging income
- Supported Living Payment Charging income
- Jobseeker Support Charging income
- Youth Payment Charging income
Remember generally Emergency Benefit is granted on the grounds of hardship. If the client has a change in income, you may need to review the client's entitlement to benefit.
Clients in habilitation programmes may face a different income test. For more information see:
- Charging income residential parole
## Income from Overseas Pensions
Income from overseas pensions is generally treated as a direct deduction from the benefit rate and this requires a separate calculation to charging other types of income.
For more information see:
- To or from overseas Payments from Overseas
For more details on what is income and how to charge it see:
- Core policy Income
Also see:
- Exemption for severe disablement

chunks.title: Single clients - caring — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Single clients - caring
Income is charged weekly as it is earned and at the following rates:
- 30 cents is taken from the benefit for each $1.00 of income the client earns over $160 per week, but not more than $250 per week (as at 1 April 2022)
- 70 cents for each $1.00 of income over $250 per week (as at 1 April 2022)
Note if you are paying Emergency Benefit at the rate of another type of benefit (instead of Supported Living Payment - caring for a person) then you must use the appropriate income test for that benefit.
Remember generally Emergency Benefit is granted on the grounds of hardship. If the client has a change in income, you may need to review the client's entitlement.
## Clients with partners - caring
If a client has a partner (with or without dependent children) and the partner is granted, in their own right any of the main benefits or is working, income is charged weekly as it is earned and at the following rates:
- 15 cents is taken from each of their benefits for each $1.00 of combined income the client and their partner earn over $160 per week, but not more than $250 per week (as at 1 April 2022)
- 35 cents for each $1.00 of combined income over $250 per week (as at 1 April 2022)
## For more details on what is income and how to charge it, see:
- Core policy Definition of income

chunks.title: Charging income - caring for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension partner — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: When a client is getting Emergency Benefit because they are caring for their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension partner on medical grounds, income is charged weekly as it is earned and at the following rates: - 15 cents is taken from the benefit for each dollar of income that the client and their partner earn over $160.00 per week, but not more than $250.00 per week (as at 1 April 2021) - 35 cents for every dollar of income that is more than $250.00 per week (as at 1 April 2021) The income deduction is only applied to the Emergency Benefit client's rate of payment. The partner's New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is not reduced by the couple's income. Note income does not include the rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension paid to the partner.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: Couple (no children), one partner is getting New Zealand Superannuation, the other partner is providing full-time care for the first partner. The couple's income is $340.00 gross per week. Income deduction 35 cents for every $1.00 earned over $250.00 per week $340.00 gross per week Less $250.00 $90.00 x 35 cents = $31.50 deduction Income deduction 15 cents for every $1.00 earned over $160.00 per week but less than $250.00 per week $250.00 gross per week Less $160.00 $90.00 x 15 cents = $13.50 deduction Plus $31.50 (deduction from above table) Total income deduction $45.00 client partner maximum benefit payable (as at 1 April 2026) $360.72 N/A less income deduction $45.00 N/A Benefit payable $315.72 N/A

chunks.title: Example 2 — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: Civil union couple with one child, one partner is getting New Zealand Superannuation, the other partner is providing full-time care for the first partner. The couple's income is $570.00 gross per week. Income deduction 35 cents for every $1.00 earned over $250.00 per week $570.00 gross per week Less $250.00 $320.00 x 35 cents = $112.00 deduction Income deduction 15 cents for every $1.00 earned over $160.00 per week but less than $250.00 per week $250.00 gross per week Less $160.00 $90.00 x 15 cents = $13.50 deduction Plus $112.00 (deduction from above table) Total income deduction $125.50 client partner maximum benefit payable (as at 1 April 2026) $392.94 N/A less income deduction $125.50 N/A Benefit payable $267.44 N/A

chunks.title: Charging income: residential parole — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Charging income: residential parole
Depending on the client's marital status there are different ways that we treat income.
Note if you are paying Emergency Benefit at the rate of another type of benefit (other than Jobseeker Support) then you must use the appropriate income test for that benefit.
## Single clients
When the client is on residential parole and is single the following apply:
- income is charged weekly as it is earned and
- 70 cents is taken from the benefit for each $1.00 of income over $160(before tax) a week
## Partner receives Sole Parent Support
When the client is receiving an Emergency Benefit and their partner in the community is receiving Sole Parent Support, the client is treated as single for the purpose of income.
Only the client's income is taken into account.
Income is charged weekly as it is earned and at the following rate:
- 70 cents is taken from the benefit for each $1.00 of income over $160 (before tax) a week
## Client included in partner's benefit
When the person on parole is included in their partner's benefit, they are treated as a married, civil union or de facto couple and both of their income is taken into account.
Income (includes any income of a partner) is charged weekly as it is earned and at the following rate:
- 70 cents is taken from the benefit for each $1.00 of income over $160(before tax) a week
## Partner in employment
When the partner in the community is in employment, benefit entitlement and income reduction is assessed as a married, civil union or de facto couple.
Income (includes any income of a partner) is charged weekly as it is earned and at the following rate:
- 70 cents is taken from the benefit for each $1.00 of income over $160 (before tax) a week

chunks.title: Child changes and social obligations — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Child changes and social obligations
Sometimes a client will have a change in circumstances that may mean the client is no longer required to comply with their social obligations including where:
- a dependent child changes age and the social obligation that applied for the dependent child in their care is no longer relevant or
- child leaves care (for example starts to live with another parent or caregiver or goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki)

chunks.title: Client and partner fail their social obligations — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Client and partner fail their social obligations
Where a client has a partner, the social obligations apply to the couple. This means that when a social obligation is not complied with the obligation failure is initiated on both the client and their partner's record.
If a client and partner are at different stages in the 24-month failure count they may have to complete different recompliance activities. This is because the client or partner may have failed other obligations such as work obligations in the past 24 months.
## Example 1
Client
Partner
Current 24-month failure count
Obligations failure 1
Obligations failure 2
Social obligations failure
Obligations failure 2
Obligations failure 3
In this situation the client will have to recomply by complying with all their social obligations. The partner will have to recomply by completing a six-week approved activity or programme of activities which includes complying with all their social obligations in order to be granted a provisional benefit..
## Example 2
Client
Partner
Current 24-month failure count
Obligations failure 2
Obligations failure 1
Social obligations failure
Obligations failure 3
Obligations failure 2
In this situation the client will have to recomply by complying with all their social obligations. The partner will have to recomply by completing a six-week approved activity or programme of activities which includes complying with all their social obligations in order to be granted a provisional benefit.

chunks.title: Client in hardship — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Client in hardship
You can consider that a client is in hardship if the client has:
- no other means of supporting themselves and any dependent family
and
- cash assets of or less than: $4,300 if the client is single or$7,464 if the client is married, in a civil union or de facto relationship, or is a sole parent
- $4,300 if the client is single or
- $7,464 if the client is married, in a civil union or de facto relationship, or is a sole parent
See:
## Payment must be justified
Emergency Benefit is a discretionary benefit. There may be situations where a client meets the hardship criteria but their overall circumstances do not justify payment. Also consider:
- to what degree the client has contributed to their hardship
and
- the impact on the client (and any dependent family) if Emergency Benefit is not granted
If you are doubt, before making a decision contact Helpline to discuss.
## Discretion to disregard assets
In exceptional circumstances you can disregard some of the client's cash assets, see:
- Exceptional circumstances for cash assets
## Deprivation
You also need to look at whether the client has recently given away or sold any assets that contributed to them in hardship. When this has happened, consider if the client has deprived them of an asset or income. Any situations where you think a client or partner (if any) has deprived themselves (and any dependent family) of income or an asset, contact Helpline to discuss.

chunks.title: Client in hospital — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Client in hospital
A client's Emergency Benefit rate of payment can be different if they are in hospital.
The rate is reduced to the hospital rate when the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks (not after receiving a benefit for 13 weeks).
If a client is married, in a civil union or de facto relationship with dependent children do not reduce their rate.
The hospital rate allows for the cost of personal items, which patients are expected to provide for themselves.
## Exception
If the client has been in hospital for 13 weeks or more at the commencement date of the benefit, the rate of payment is the hospital rate.
For more information about the hospital rate see:
- Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Client is meeting their social obligations — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Client is meeting their social obligations
If, during any of the Contact Steps of engagement and support, you consider that the client is meeting their social obligations you will need to let the client know that:
- as they are meeting their social obligations, you do not require any more information or contact from them and
- if they require any support regarding their social obligations they can contact Work and Income at any time
The appropriate outcome for the specific social obligations that apply to each of the client's dependent children needs to be recorded in OBMAN.
For more information on the three step process of engagement see:
- Social obligations - Actively engaging with clients [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Client leaves Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Client leaves Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre
No stand-down applies to the commencement of a benefit when a client has left the Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Client's situation changes during regular engagement and support — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Client's situation changes during regular engagement and support
A client and their partner (if any) may have a change of circumstance which means they are no longer subject to a social obligation. These changes may include (but are not limited to):
- a dependent child leaves their care or
- a dependent child changes age and the social obligations that apply for the dependent child in their care are no longer relevant
If this happens during regular engagement and support, the client cannot be failed and they are no longer subject to the social obligation.
For more information see:
- Social obligations - Actively engaging with clients [no link find out why]
- Overview of social obligations according to the age of the child
- Changes and reviews Child changes

chunks.title: Clients aged 16 or 17 years — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients aged 16 or 17 years
Generally, it is expected that parents support their children up to 18 years. However, there is specific assistance available to clients aged 16 or 17 who cannot be supported. These clients may be eligible for:
- Youth Payment
- Supported Living Payment
- Jobseeker Support (partnered clients with a dependent child) or
- Student Allowance Independent Circumstances Allowance
Note sole parent clients aged 16 to 19 years may also be entitled to Young Parent Payment.
Where a client aged 16 or 17 years does not meet all the requirements for any other benefit, they may be eligible for an Emergency Benefit. However, you will need to:
- consider why they are unable to earn a sufficient livelihood to support themselves (and any dependent family)
- confirm the client is in hardship and
- determine they are not eligible for any other benefit
## Young person who is 16 or 17 must be in exceptional circumstances
In addition to the criteria outlined above, you should only grant Emergency Benefit to a young person who is aged 16 or 17 if the young person is in exceptional circumstances. For more information see:
- Aged 16 or 17 years and in exceptional circumstances
## Young person may be required to work with a youth service provider
If it is decided to grant an Emergency Benefit, you may consider it appropriate that as part of the condition of receiving the benefit that the young person must work with a youth service provider.
The reason a client aged 16 or 17 years is in hardship as they are unable to earn a sufficient livelihood will determine the equivalent benefit. For more information see:
- Not lawfully present or resident for youth support payments
- Students aged 16 or 17 years
Also see:
- Determining the reason for insufficient livelihood
- Conditions of grant
- Not eligible for another benefit

chunks.title: Clients aged 65 years or over — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients aged 65 years or over
When clients aged 65 years or over do not qualify for New Zealand Superannuation there are usually a range of reasons that they are unable to earn a sufficient livelihood, such as disability, language or skill barriers as well as their age.
In some circumstances, Emergency Benefit may be considered for a client aged 65 years or over.
Note before considering Emergency Benefit, all other main benefits must be considered.
## Granting Emergency Benefit on grounds of hardship
If a client is not available for or seeking full-time employment, they do not qualify for Jobseeker Support. If the client does not qualify for another benefit such as Sole Parent Support or Supported Living Payment, MSD should consider their eligibility for Emergency Benefit. The client will need to meet all of the qualifications for Emergency Benefit including the hardship test.
For more information see:
- Granting Emergency Benefit on grounds of hardship (65 years or older)
## Granting Emergency Benefit in substitution of Jobseeker Support
Where a client has confirmed that they are willing and available for full-time work but the likelihood of them gaining employment is low, MSD may make a decision through the 26 week reapplication process to grant Emergency Benefit in substitution for Jobseeker Support.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Reapplication process for clients aged 65 or older
## Clients with a partner
If the client has a partner, the partner should also be assessed to see if they meet the qualifications for a benefit. If the partner qualifies for a benefit, this should be granted before Emergency Benefit is considered for the client.
Note that Emergency Benefit may still be considered for the client if the benefit their partner qualifies for is Supported Living Payment on the ground of caring. This is because the client cannot be included in that benefit, there is no couple rate of payment.

chunks.title: Clients compelled to remain in New Zealand — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients compelled to remain in New Zealand
A client compelled to remain in New Zealand through some unforeseen circumstance may be able to receive Emergency Benefit if they are applying for permanent residence. It must be a serious and unforeseen reason that prevents them from leaving New Zealand, for example life maintaining medical treatment.
Note clients applying for permanent residence and compelled to remain in New Zealand through some unforeseen circumstance do not need a current temporary entry class visa or a temporary permit granted by Immigration New Zealand to receive Emergency Benefit or Temporary Additional Support.
## Strong and compelling reasons
It is not possible to detail the circumstances under which this may occur. However, there must be very strong and compelling reasons why the client is unable to leave New Zealand.
Lack of funds is not regarded as a reason for not being able to leave New Zealand. When the client originally arrived in New Zealand on a temporary entry class visa or a temporary permit, a condition of entry required an air ticket to another destination in the world (that is, the ability to leave New Zealand).
If you have a case where you think the client may be eligible for an Emergency Benefit, contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.
For more information see:
- Extra help for clients without permanent residence
- Clients without permanent residence or citizenship

chunks.title: Clients donating an organ income test and asset test — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients donating an organ income test and asset test
Emergency Benefit is income and asset tested. However, different rules apply to the payment of Emergency Benefit when the client has donated a kidney or liver tissue.
## Income test
When a client has been transferred to Emergency Benefit, the applicable Jobseeker Support or Sole Parent Support income test applies to the Emergency Benefit.
## Asset test
Clients donating a kidney or liver tissue must not be disadvantaged by this donation and do not have an asset test applied to their Emergency Benefit.

chunks.title: Clients with dependent children - 50% protection — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients with dependent children - 50% protection
Sanctions are applied differently for:
- couples with dependent children, who both fail their social obligations
- couples with dependent children, when a partner fails their obligations
- couples where one person is youth money managed
Clients in these situations with a financial sanction imposed do not have their whole benefit sanctioned. Instead, a maximum sanction of 50% of the total benefit may be imposed. The balance payable is known as 50% protection.
For more information, including treatment of supplementary assistance, see:
- Sanctions for a couple with dependent children - both fail their obligations
- Sanctions for young partners
The 50% protection also applies to these groups if they have a 13-week non-entitlement period for voluntarily leaving employment without a good and sufficient reason, dismissal due to misconduct, or refusing to accept any offer of suitable employment.
Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.
For more information see:
- Recompliance

chunks.title: Clients with permanent residence or citizenship — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients with permanent residence or citizenship
In order to receive a benefit, a client must normally
- be a New Zealand citizen or
- have a residence class visa granted under the Immigration Act 2009 (which can either be a resident visa or a permanent resident visa) or
- have a residence permit granted under the Immigration Act 1987 (note that this is deemed to be a residence class visa under the Immigration Act 2009) or
- be deemed under the Immigration Act 2009 to hold a residence class visa in New Zealand (eg Australian citizens or residents)
In addition, clients are required to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand, and for some benefits, meet certain period of residence in New Zealand requirements.
If a client does not meet the period of residence requirements for a benefit, in the first instance, consider eligibility to another benefit and then hardship benefits associated to other main benefits
Example 1
A client has just arrived in New Zealand and has been granted New Zealand permanent residence. The client has applied for Jobseeker Support. They meet all the eligibility requirements for Jobseeker Support except the two years residence. In the first instance, Jobseeker Support on grounds of hardships should be considered.
Example 2
A sole parent client has arrived in New Zealand from Australia and has been seeking work. They have not been able to secure employment, are now sick and have applied for a benefit. They meet the all the criteria for Jobseeker Support on ground of health condition, injury or disability except the two year residence requirement. In this instance, Jobseeker Support on grounds of hardship should be considered.
## Hardship benefits associated to other benefits
Consider hardship benefits associated to other benefits when the client is not eligible for another main benefit due to not meeting the period of residence requirements.
Note consider these hardship benefits before an Emergency Benefit.
For more information see:
- Permanent residence
- Jobseeker Support
- Jobseeker Support Granting on grounds of hardship
- Tokelau, Niue and Cook Islands clients
- Australian clients

chunks.title: Clients without permanent residence or citizenship — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Clients without permanent residence or citizenship
To be eligible for a benefit a client must have permanent residence or citizenship. However, if a client does not have permanent residence or citizenship they may be eligible for an Emergency Benefit if the client is:
- a person who has made a claim for refugee or protected person status (also known as an asylum seeker) and
- is waiting for or appealing a decline decision to the Immigration and Protection Tribunal and
- has a valid visa or permit to be lawfully present in New Zealand or
- a person recognised as a refugee or protected person in New Zealand and has a valid visa or permit or
- applying for permanent residence and are compelled to remain in New Zealand due to some unforeseen reason
Generally, clients are not entitled to a benefit if they are unlawfully in New Zealand.
If the client has a partner who is unlawfully in New Zealand (or here on a temporary entry class visa or a temporary permit), is not a refugee and is not applying for permanent residence, you will need to contact the Card Centre when granting the primary client's benefit to ensure that a Community Services Card is not issued to the non-resident partner.

chunks.title: Commencement date — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
To decide when the Emergency Benefit can start you must first find the entitlement date.
This is usually the date that a person no longer has a means of support.
For a list of these dates see:
- Entitlement date
Generally, Emergency Benefits are subject to an initial stand-down period of up to a maximum of two weeks after the entitlement date.
The commencement date is:
- the day after the initial stand-down ends or
- the application date
whichever is the later.
However, if clients apply within 28 days of their entitlement date, the commencement date rules are different, and the 28 day rule can be used when the equivalent benefit is:
- Sole Parent Support
- Supported Living Payment
- Jobseeker Support on the grounds of health condition, injury or disability
- Jobseeker Support granted to a sole parent
- Jobseeker Support granted to a client who has recently lost the financial support of their spouse due to death, commenced living apart (including imprisonment) or ending of a de facto relationship
- Youth Payment
- Young Parent Payment
## No stand-down applies
There are some situations when an initial stand-down is not imposed. When no stand-down applies, the commencement date of the benefit is:
- the entitlement date or
- the application date
whichever is the later.

chunks.title: Commencement of position — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Commencement of position
