A partner can start their Community Work Experience from the first date that the position is available. This must not be more than one week after the 2-week search period has ended.
## Commencement during 2-week search period
A partner may find and start their position within the 2-week search period (after MSD has confirmed the organisation and position are suitable). If they start during this period, the 4-week position period will start from the date they start the position. This allows them to recomply with their obligations more quickly.
Note partners still need to meet the requirements of 5 hours per week for 4 weeks.
## Commencement after 2-week search period
If a partner’s position starts in the first week after the 2-week search period ends, the first day of the position might not be the first day of the week.
If MSD is satisfied the approved position will start within that week, and the partner can still complete their required 5 hours, the position period can start from the first day of the week.

chunks.title: Community Work Experience — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Community Work Experience
Community Work Experience is a non-financial sanction that can be imposed on a partner of an Emergency Benefit client, instead of a Grade 1 financial sanction. It is intended to help clients build work-related skills and confidence, and also build connections in their community.
A partner will work with a community or voluntary organisation, for at least 5 hours a week, for 4 weeks.
A partner will have a 2-week search period before their Community Work Experience begins to find a suitable position and organisation.
MSD will need to confirm whether the organisation and position are suitable before the partner can begin.
Once a partner completes their Community Work Experience, they are considered to have recomplied with their obligation failure and do not need to complete any other recompliance activities.

chunks.title: Conditions of grant — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Conditions of grant
The payment of Emergency Benefit can be subject to certain conditions set by the Chief Executive. Generally, the conditions will reflect the obligations for the Equivalent benefit.
Why the client is in hardship and is unable to earn a sufficient livelihood for themselves (and any dependent family) will determine the appropriate conditions that should be applied to the Emergency Benefit.
The conditions of an Emergency Benefit will vary. It is important that the right conditions be applied to each Emergency Benefit. If the client does not meet the conditions of grant that are applied, the Emergency Benefit may be stopped.
## Advise the client of conditions of grant
All conditions of grant of the Emergency Benefit must be explained to the client, both verbally and in writing, and noted in CMS. The client must understand the conditions before they can be imposed. These conditions of grant must be monitored.
The conditions of grant of an Emergency Benefit may be (but not limited to):
- Job search
- Planning requirements
- Medical assessments
- Any other appropriate conditions
- Benefit paid for a specific period
Not all these conditions of grant will apply to every client but at least one condition must be imposed.
## Client has a partner
If the client has a partner, MSD must consider if the partner should have work or work preparation obligations imposed on them or if they have youth activity obligations. For more information see:
- Work or work preparation obligations - partners
- Youth activity obligations (for partners aged 16 to 18 years)
- Partners 65 years or over
## Rate of payment
The rate of payment and income test are not part of the conditions of grant.
Generally, Emergency Benefit is paid at the maximum rate of the equivalent benefit with the appropriate income test however there is discretion to pay a lower rate of payment where it is justified.
The maximum rate cannot be New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Continued compliance with their obligations — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Continued compliance with their obligations
Generally a young partner will be considered to have demonstrated continued compliance with their obligations when:
- they have earned all the incentives that available to them or
- where a young partner has a full or partial exemption, the service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service is satisfied that the young partner is engaging with the provider as is required and
- the young partner has not had an activity obligations failure in the last 6 months
## Earning all of the incentive payments available to them
For young partners who have Youth Activity obligations to have the option of getting their payment directly, they would need to earn the following incentive payments:
- budgeting
- education and
- parenting (where applicable)
A young partner who has a full or partial exemption for their activity obligations is only able to earn those incentive payments which apply to their current obligations.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Contributed to hardship — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Contributed to hardship
Payment of Emergency Benefit may be considered when a client can show they are in hardship, as they are unable to earn a sufficient livelihood for themselves (and any dependent family).
Where a client has the ability to earn a sufficient livelihood but has chosen not to earn that livelihood the client has imposed their own hardship and Emergency Benefit should not be considered.
Example
A client is married and their partner has gone overseas. They have one child, 14 years of age. The circumstances of the client identifies that it is reasonable to expect them to look for work, however they have stated they will not.
In this situation, the client has imposed their own hardship by choosing not to look for work therefore Emergency Benefit should not be considered.
Note all the client's circumstances must be determined to assess why the client is unable to earn a sufficient livelihood. There may be other reasons why they are in hardship.

chunks.title: Counting previous obligations failures — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: The sanction imposed depends on how often the client or partner has failed to comply with their obligations in the previous 24 months while getting a benefit. Previous failures are only counted if the failure occurred within the last 24 months while continuously getting a benefit. Note this does not apply to young partners who fail their youth activity obligations. These failures are counted for 12 months. The 24-month count starts from the day the obligation failure is imposed. Each obligation failure has its own 24-month count. Example A client fails their first obligation on 1 June 2025. They fail another obligation on 1 October 2025, and have an obligation failure count of two. Their obligation failure count is reset to one on 1 June 2027, 24 months after they failed their first obligation. Their obligation failure count will be reset to zero on 1 October 2027, 24 months after the second obligation failure.

chunks.title: Transfer between benefits — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If a client transfers between benefits, any obligations failures within the previous 24 months are still counted. Failures on a previous benefit type will count toward the failure count on the new benefit, even if the same obligations do not apply.

chunks.title: Failure of different obligations add to failure count — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: The failure count includes all obligation failures. If a partner fails a work obligation and then a later failure related to social obligations in a 24-month period, this would be counted as two failures.

chunks.title: Young person transfers between benefits — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: When a client transfers from Young Parent Payment or Youth Payment to a benefit without youth activity obligations the count will be reset to zero. This is because the sanction regime is different for young people getting these payments. The count does not return to zero when young partners of main beneficiaries with youth activity obligations move to having different obligations.

chunks.title: Examples of transfers between benefits — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: The following table outlines what happens to the failure count and sanction when a youth client transfers between benefit type. From To Failure count Sanction Jobseeker Support Young Parent Payment Re-sets to zero Re-sets to zero Young partner aged 16 or 17 years getting Jobseeker Support Jobseeker Support (work obligations) Carries over Re-set to zero Young partner aged 16 or 17 years getting Jobseeker Support Young partner aged 16 or 17 years getting Supported Living Payment Carries over Carries over

chunks.title: Calculating continuous receipt of benefit — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: To calculate continuous receipt of benefit any employment for less than 10 working days is disregarded.

chunks.title: Transitional arrangements ended on 26 May 2026 — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: From 26 May 2025, the obligations failure count period increased from 12 months to 24 months for working age clients. Any obligation failures that were initiated before 26 May 2025 were only counted for 12 months. Note youth activity obligation failures are still counted for 12 months only.

chunks.title: Grade 1 and 2 sanctions — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Grade 1 and 2 sanctions
The primary client who has met their obligations will continue to get their portion of the assistance.
A first or second failure means suspension of the in-hand allowance and any incentive payments for the young partner, until they recomply with the obligations they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations).
The young partner can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and portion of Winter Energy Payment to which they are entitled.
If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks the whole of their benefit and any incentive payments are suspended along with their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Winter Energy Payment they get. The primary client can be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.
Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.
## Grade 3 sanction
The primary client who has met their obligations will continue to get their portion of the assistance. They will also be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.
If the young partner who is youth money managed fails their obligations for a third time:
- their portion of the benefit, and any incentive payments is cancelled immediately
- their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Winter Energy Payment is cancelled and
- the young partner is subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks from the date of cancellation
The young partner may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities.
If the young partner does not start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of their non-entitlement period to get a benefit.
Note Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period.

chunks.title: Couple, young partner is youth money managed, primary client has work obligations, dependent children, both fail — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: Couples with dependent children who both fail their obligations at the same time do not have their whole benefit sanctioned. Instead, a maximum sanction of 50% of the total benefit may be imposed. If a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligations failures. Note family tax credit continues to be paid at the full rate.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the primary client fails their obligations for the first time, their portion of the benefit is reduced by 50%, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. Their Extra help (including their portion of Winter Energy Payment) is not affected. For more information on non-financial sanctions see: - Non-financial sanctions If the young partner fails for the first time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments will be suspended. Their Extra help (including their portion of Winter Energy Payment) is not affected. If the client or young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks their portion of the benefit is suspended. For young partners, their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks, including their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. While part of the benefit is cancelled, the couple gets 50% of the main benefit and any Extra help to which they are entitled. They can continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the primary client fails their obligations a second time, their portion (50% of the couple's benefit) is reduced by 25%. Their portion of Extra help is also suspended. They will not get their portion of Winter Energy Payment. If the young partner also fails for the second time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments will be suspended. The young partner will continue to get their portion of any Extra help to which they are entitled. In effect the couple gets 50% of the total Extra help to which they are entitled. This is as they have 50% protection for the family unit. The young partner will also continue to be paid the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit. If the client or young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks their portion of the benefit is suspended. For young partners, their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks, including their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. While part of the benefit is cancelled, the couple gets 50% of the main benefit and any Extra help to which they are entitled. They can continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If both clients fail their obligations a third time, 50% of the couple's benefit is cancelled. The couple will continue to get a maximum of 50% of their married rate of benefit until they recomply. The young partner's portion will be paid directly to their bank account, not via youth money management. If both clients are subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks, both clients may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities. While part of the benefit is cancelled, the couple gets 50% of any Extra help to which they are entitled. They can continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment. This is as they have 50% protection for the family unit.

chunks.title: One client recomplies first — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the primary client recomplies first, their portion of the benefit and Extra help must be resumed or re-granted. The young partner's benefit must remain sanctioned until they recomply. If the young partner recomplies first, their portion of benefit and Extra help is not able to be resumed or re-granted as the primary record is not current. The payments must be manually made. If the client or young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks their portion of the benefit is suspended. For young partners, their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks, including their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. While part of the benefit is cancelled, the couple gets 50% of the main benefit and any Extra help to which they are entitled. They can continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the young partner fails their obligations for the first time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments are suspended, until they recomply with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations). The young partner can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and Winter Energy Payment to which they are entitled. Disability Allowance is payable throughout any non-entitlement period. The primary client will continue to get 50% of the couple's benefit entitlement and their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and the Winter Energy Payment. If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks their portion of the benefit is suspended. Their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks, including their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. The primary client will continue to get 50% of their married rate of benefit and their portion of Temporary Additional Support and Accommodation Supplement. The primary client can be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment. Note family tax credit continues being paid at the full rate.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the young partner fails their obligations for the second time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments are suspended, until they recomply with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations). The young partner can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and the Winter Energy Payment to which they are entitled. The primary client will continue to get 50% of the couples benefit entitlement and their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and the Winter Energy Payment. If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks their portion of the benefit is suspended. Their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks, including their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. The primary client will continue to get 50% of their married rate of benefit and their portion of Temporary Additional Support and Accommodation Supplement. The primary client can be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the young partner fails their obligations for a third time, their portion of the benefit and Extra help is cancelled. They are subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks. The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6 week approved activity or programme of activities. If they have not started a 6 week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of the non-entitlement period to get a benefit. The non-sanctioned primary client will continue to get 50% of the couple's benefit entitlement including Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. The non-sanctioned primary client will be paid the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the primary client fails their obligations for the first time, that person's portion of benefit is reduced by half (50%) until they recomply with the obligation they have failed unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. For more information on non-financial sanctions see: - Non-financial sanctions The young partner will have their in-hand allowance of up to $50 and any incentive payments suspended. The couple can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled. They continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit. Disability Allowance can continue being paid during any non-entitlement period. After 4 weeks If the partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks, they will have their portion of the benefit and their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If the primary client fails their obligations for the second time, that person's portion of benefit is suspended until they recomply with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations). Their portion of Extra help is also suspended (including their portion of the Winter Energy Payment). The young partner who is youth money managed, has their in-hand allowance of up to $50 and any incentive payments suspended. Their portion of Extra help is not affected. The young partner can continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit. After 4 weeks If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks, they will have their portion of the benefit and their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and the Winter Energy Payment suspended. Their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: If both people in a couple fail their obligations for a third time: - their benefit and any incentive payments are cancelled immediately - Extra help, including the Winter Energy Payment is cancelled and - subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks from the date of cancellation The client and young partner may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities. If the client or young partner does not start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of their non-entitlement period to get a benefit.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: The young partner who has met their obligations will continue to have their portion (50%) of their assistance paid as usual through youth money management. This will include their incentive payments where these are payable. If the primary client fails their obligations for the first time, that person's portion of benefit is reduced by half (25%) unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. For more information on non-financial sanctions see: - Non-financial sanctions The couple can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled. They can continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment. Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period. If the client does not recomply within 4 weeks, they will have their portion of the benefit suspended (along with their portion of any Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled). Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: The young partner who has met their obligations will continue to have their portion of their assistance (including their incentive payments) paid as usual through youth money management. The young partner can continue getting their portion of any Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support they are entitled to. The young partner can get the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment. If the primary client fails their obligations for the second time, that person's portion of benefit is suspended (along with their portion of any Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled). Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text: The young partner who has met their obligations is due their portion of the main benefit (including their incentive payments) paid as usual. The young partner can also continue to get their portion of any Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled. The young partner can get the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment. If the primary client fails their obligations for a third time: - their portion of the benefit is cancelled immediately and - their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and the Winter Energy Payment is cancelled and - the client subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks from the date of cancellation The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6 week approved activity or programme of activities. If the client does not start a 6 week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of their non-entitlement period to get a benefit. Note Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period.

chunks.title: Court imposed conditions — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Court imposed conditions
This exemption may apply to partners with work or work preparation obligations.
A client serving a sentence of home detention, or who has conditions and requirements of a court sentence or court order that limits their ability to meet all their obligations can be exempt from meeting some or all of their work or work preparation obligations.
This can be a full or partial exemption depending on the conditions imposed by the Courts.
This includes clients who:
- are former prisoners who are have probation or parole conditions which means that they cannot meet all their work obligations and
- have work obligations and are required as part of a sentence of the court or other court order to attend programmes or other activities, or have conditions imposed upon them (e.g. bail conditions) which limit their ability to meet all their work obligations
Home detainees or former prisoners are case managed by their probation officer. Part of this case management includes undertaking appropriate job search and activities to improve their prospects of obtaining paid employment.
In all cases, the case manager should contact the probation officer to facilitate any meetings.
Note this can be a full or partial exemption depending on the conditions imposed by the Courts.
## Proof
The client must provide proof from the Ministry of Justice, the Department of Corrections or the Department of Courts stating that they:
- are serving a sentence of Home Detention or
- have probation or parole conditions which limit their ability to meet all their work obligations or
- are required to attend programmes or other activities which limit their ability to meet all their work obligations or
- have conditions imposed (e.g. bail conditions) which limit their ability to meet all their work obligations and
- the length of time the client should be exempt
## Duration
The duration of the exemption can be for up to 12 months or for a period determined by the court order or conditions placed on the person by the Courts, whichever is earliest.
Note you cannot add an expiry date in SWIFTT, but you must note the duration in CMS.
## SWIFTT process
Use SWIFTT exemption reason 'Court imposed conditions'.
For more information see:
- Full or partial exemptions

chunks.title: Court imposed conditions (young partners) — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Court imposed conditions (young partners)
A young partner serving a sentence of home detention, or who has conditions and requirements of a court sentence or court order that limits their ability to meet their obligations can be exempt from meeting some or all of their activity obligations.
This can be a full or partial exemption depending on the conditions imposed by the Courts.
This includes young people who are:
- former prisoners who are subject to probation or parole conditions which means that they cannot meet all their activity obligations and
- required as part of a sentence of the court or other court order to attend programmes or other activities, or have conditions imposed upon them (eg bail conditions) which limit their ability to meet all their activity obligations
Home detainees or former prisoners are case managed by their probation officer. Part of this case management includes undertaking appropriate activities to improve their prospects of obtaining paid employment.
In all cases, the service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service should contact the probation officer to facilitate any meetings for that young partner.
## Proof
The young partner must provide proof from the Ministry of Justice, the Department of Corrections or the Department of Courts stating that they:
- are serving a sentence of Home Detention or
- are subject to probation or parole conditions which limit their ability to meet all their activity obligations or
- are required to attend programmes or other activities which limit their ability to meet all their activity obligations or
- have conditions imposed (eg bail conditions) which limit their ability to meet all their activity obligations and
- the length of time the young partner should be exempt
## Duration
The duration of the exemption can be for up to 12 months or for a period determined by the court order or conditions placed on the person by the Courts, whichever is earlier.
## SWIFTT process
Use SWIFTT exemption reason 'Court imposed conditions'.
Note you cannot add an expiry date in SWIFTT but you must note the duration in CMS.
For more information see:
- Full or partial exemption
For an overview of the exemptions see:
- Table of exemptions for young partners
