If it is decided that the young partner has failed their activity obligations, the YSSU will initiate an activity obligations failure. The young partner will then be notified by text message (where they have consented to be contacted in this way) or letter that:
- an obligations failure has occurred
- a sanction has been imposed and
- they have five working days to recomply before their payments are affected
All young people have a five working day notice period to dispute or recomply before the sanction is imposed. If a young person recomplies within the five working day notice period their benefit is not sanctioned but the activity obligations failure is recorded.
For more information see:
- Activity failures for young partners
- Recompliance for young partners
- Approved recompliance activities for young partners

chunks.title: Youth Guarantee courses — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Youth Guarantee courses
Youth Guarantee courses are considered to be employment-related training.
## Course information
Youth Guarantee is an education initiative for students. The courses are level 1-3 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF).
The courses provide students with knowledge and information on vocational pathways, and contain a mix of practical, specific and general skill development.

chunks.title: Youth money management — main benefits > emergency benefit
chunks.text:
## Youth money management
Youth money management is where a young partner gets an in-hand allowance of up to $50 a week, with most of their benefit payment being redirected to pay for their everyday living costs and any lawful debts. Any remainder is placed onto their payment card.
A young partner who is required to be youth money managed cannot review the decision on how their benefit payment (or their portion of the benefit payment) is paid to them.
## No longer subject to youth money management
A young partner aged 16 or 17 years (with no children) or 16 to 19 years (with dependent children) will not be subject to youth money management and will have their full payment paid directly to them when they have:
- demonstrated continued compliance with their obligations and been assessed as being financially competent or
- opted out of youth money management because they turned 18 years (for young partners without dependent children) or 20 years (for young partners with dependent children) and have chosen to stay in the Youth Service and complete their course of study, training or work-based learning
For more information see:
- Redirection for young partners
- In-hand allowance
- Incentive payments
- Payment process for a young partner
- Extra help and other payments
- Opting out of youth money management
- Earning the right to receive payment directly
- Continued compliance with their obligations
- Assessed as financially competent
- Returned to youth money management
- Method of payment
- Money management activity

chunks.title: Additional conditions of grant — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text: Clients may need to meet additional conditions of grant before you can grant Emergency Maintenance Allowance. These additional conditions can mirror the obligations that would apply if the client was getting Sole Parent Support. Note if the client is 65 years or older you should treat them the same as a client on Emergency Benefit.

chunks.title: Youngest child under 3 years — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text: If a client getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance has a youngest child under 3 years the conditions of grant should include work preparation obligations that mirror those that would apply if the client was getting Sole Parent Support. When work preparation obligations are set as a condition of grant the client must: - when required to undertake planning for employment - when required to report to Work and Income on progress in meeting their work preparation obligations as often as required - when required to attend and participate in any interview with Work and Income or on behalf of Work and Income and - when required by Work and Income undertake any activity to improve their work readiness and employment prospects, including: any work assessmentany programme or seminarany work experience or work exploration activityany employment related training andrehabilitation (but not medical treatment)an education programme - any work assessment - any programme or seminar - any work experience or work exploration activity - any employment related training and - rehabilitation (but not medical treatment) - an education programme

chunks.title: Youngest child aged between 3 and 13 years — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text: If a client getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance has a youngest child aged between 3 and 13 years the conditions of grant should include work obligations that mirror those that would apply if the client was getting Sole Parent Support. That is part-time work obligations. When work obligations are set as a condition of grant the obligations the client must: - be available for, and take reasonable steps to obtain, suitable employment - accept any offer of suitable employment, including temporary employment or seasonal employment Note suitable employment can include employment that contains an employment trial. - attend and participate in an interview for any opportunity of suitable employment to which the client is referred - when required to attend and participate in any interview with Work and Income or on behalf of Work and Income - when required to undertake planning for employment - report to Work and Income on progress in meeting their work obligations as often as required and - when required by Work and Income, undertake any activity to improve their work readiness and employment prospects, including: any work assessmentany programme or seminarany work experience or work exploration activityany employment related trainingrehabilitation (but not medical treatment) - any work assessment - any programme or seminar - any work experience or work exploration activity - any employment related training - rehabilitation (but not medical treatment) If the client's youngest dependent child is aged between 3 and 13 years their conditions of grant should be part-time. This means they must be available for, and take reasonable steps to find, suitable employment of at least 20 hours per week. For more information see: - Sole Parent Support Work or work preparation obligations - Consequences of failing to meet conditions

chunks.title: Client circumstances mirror reasons for a sole parent exemption — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text: If you think that a client has circumstances that mean they will not be able to meet some or all of the obligations, you should: - check the reasons that clients on Sole Parent Support can be exempt from meeting their work or work preparation obligations - note the client's circumstances in CMS For more information see: - Sole Parent Support Table of Exemptions At the time of grant you must advise the client if these additional conditions apply.

chunks.title: Additional conditions of grant for 16 to 19 year old's — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Additional conditions of grant for 16 to 19 year old's
Sole parents aged 16 to 19 years may need to meet additional conditions of grant before you can grant Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
Young people getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance must advise of any change in circumstances that affect their entitlement or rate of benefit payable.
They also may be required to be:
- enrolled in and undertaking, or be available for, a full-time course of secondary or tertiary education, or approved training or work-based learning leading to a NCEA level 2 qualification or an equivalent or higher qualification
- when required to, attend and participate in any interview with Work and Income (or their Youth Service provider) to discuss their circumstances
- when required to, participate in and complete an approved budgeting programme
- when required to, participate satisfactorily in an approved parenting education programme
- enrol their child with a Primary Health Organisation, where a local provider is available
- keep their child or children under the age of five years up-to-date with their Well Child/Tamariki Ora checks
- ensure their child's attendance at an approved Early Childhood Education (ECE) programme or other suitable childcare, while they are participating in education, training, work-based learning or part-time work
These conditions of grant apply from the time Emergency Maintenance Allowance is first paid except where the young person is caring for a child aged under 12 months. Where the young person is caring for a child under the age of 12 months, the obligation to be in or available for full-time education, training or work-based learning begins to apply:
- when their youngest child is aged between six and twelve months and there is no suitable place available in a Teen Parent Unit or there is a suitable place available but there are special circumstances to justify the obligation applying later
or
- the day on which the child becomes 12 months old
## Client circumstances mirror reasons for a youth exemption
If you think that a client has circumstances that mean they will not be able to meet some or all of their conditions of grant, you should:
- check the reasons that clients getting Young Parent Payment can be exempt from meeting their youth activity obligations
- note the client's circumstances in CMS
For more information see:
- Young Parent Payment Table of Exemptions
At the time of grant you must advise the client if these additional conditions apply.

chunks.title: Additional criteria for sole parents aged 16 or 17 years — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Additional criteria for sole parents aged 16 or 17 years
Parents are expected to support their children until they turn 18 years old.
Where a sole parent aged 16 or 17 years does not meet all the requirements for any other benefit, they may be eligible for an Emergency Maintenance Allowance. However, you will need to:
- confirm that the client is in exceptional circumstances
- consider why they are unable to earn a sufficient livelihood to support themselves (and any dependent family)
- confirm the client is in hardship and
- determine they are not eligible for any other benefit
## Young person who is 16 or 17 must be in exceptional circumstances
You should only grant Emergency Maintenance Allowance to a young person who is aged 16 or 17 if the young person is in exceptional circumstances. For more information see:
- People aged 16 or 17 years in exceptional circumstances
## Young person may be required to work with a Youth service provider
If it is decided to grant an Emergency Maintenance Allowance, you may consider it appropriate that as part of the condition of receiving the benefit that the young person must work with a Youth service provider.
For more information see:
- Additional conditions of grant for 16 to 19 year olds

chunks.title: Age — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Age
To get an Emergency Maintenance Allowance a client must be:
- 20 years or older or
- have been legally married or
- have been in a civil union
## Exception
A 16 to 19 year old sole parent may qualify for an Emergency Maintenance Allowance if they cannot receive Young Parent Payment because they do not have permanent residence or citizenship.
For more information see:
- Sole parents who are 16 to 19 years old

chunks.title: All reasonable steps to meet social obligations — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## All reasonable steps to meet social obligations
There may be some situations where a client can't comply with their social obligations for reasons beyond their control. You can accept that a client has taken all reasonable steps to comply if they:
- have made a commitment to meet their social obligations at a more appropriate time and
- are working towards addressing any barriers they are facing
Every client's situation is different and what may be a barrier to meeting social obligations for one family may not be for another.
The decision about whether a client is taking all reasonable steps to comply lies with Work and Income.
Below are some of the situations you should take into account when considering that the client is taking all reasonable steps:
- Shared care issues in the family or family court proceedings occurring
The parent who is not the principal caregiver does not support their child having to attend recognised early childhood education programmes. It would not be reasonable for the client to be held responsible for the actions of someone else.
- Family violence or safety concerns in the family
A client discloses family violence or they have safety concerns for the child.
- Supply or availability issues
A child is on a waiting list for
an early childhood education programme or
a medical centre and the client has a plan or commitment to ensure their child can access primary health care if it is required
- Additional costs of participation or engagement may put the client in hardship
The travel costs or additional early childhood education programme costs associated with attendance would cause hardship to the family.
- The child has a health condition, injury or disability
A child has an injury or behavioural problems meaning that it would not be reasonable to expect them to participate in an approved programme either temporarily or permanently.
- Family has recently moved to a new area
The family has recently moved and is in the process of establishing networks.
For more information see:
- Social obligations
- Monitoring compliance with social obligations

chunks.title: Amount of income exemption — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Amount of income exemption
When you have determined that a client is severely disabled you must then consider if they should have all or part of their income from employment disregarded for benefit purposes.
The amount of the income exemption depends on the client's individual circumstances after considering the guidelines - for severe disablement and should be:
- a reasonable amount as an incentive to recognise the personal effort that a severely disabled person has made to participate or continue in employment
- any additional costs that a severely disabled person has incurred to participate or continue in employment
- a reasonable amount to ensure that a severely disabled person is not disadvantaged by participating or continuing in employment
Note the client may be entitled to receive other types of assistance, for example Disability Allowance for transport costs to work or employment assistance.
Fully document your decision by recording the reasons and the amount of the exemption in the CMS note template, Income exemption amount.
Contact Helpline if you need help with the assessment.
For more information see:.
- Extra Help

chunks.title: Annual closedown periods — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Annual closedown periods
Employers may close their operation or discontinue the work of one or more of their employees at a certain time every year. This is traditionally done over a holiday period, and is called a closedown period.
During a closedown period the employer requires their employees to take all or some of their annual holidays. If the employee is entitled to leave at the start of the closedown period, the Holidays Act 2003 requires that they take paid leave.
If an employee has no annual holiday entitlement for the period of the closedown, the employer must pay the employee 8% of their gross earnings since they began work or since they last became entitled to annual holidays. Alternatively, an employer and employee can agree that the employee may take annual holidays in advance to cover some or all, of the annual closedown.
## Clients covered by holiday pay not entitled to a main benefit
If a client is covered by holiday pay during the annual closedown period the Holidays Act 2003 requires that they take paid leave. They would not qualify for a main benefit.
## Client not covered by holiday pay
Clients not covered by holiday pay during any period of an annual closedown are unemployed for that period (that is, they are no longer in paid employment) and most clients would generally qualify for Sole Parent Support.
However, in cases where the client's annual income precludes entitlement to the benefit (that is, their income is such that Sole Parent Support would be paid at a disqualifying rate or the rate of payment would be insufficient) and they don't qualify for any other benefit, you should consider paying Emergency Maintenance Allowance on the grounds of hardship.
## Additional criteria
To qualify for Emergency Maintenance Allowance there are other criteria the client must meet.
For more information see:
- Additional conditions of grant
- Age
- Client's circumstances
- Dependent child
- Hardship criteria
- Residence

chunks.title: Approved early childhood education programmes or services — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Approved early childhood education programmes or services
An approved early childhood education programme or service includes:
- a licensed early childhood education service which includes:
- early childhood education and care centre (eg daycare centre, kōhanga reo, playcentre, kindergarten)
- home-based education and care service
- hospital-based education and care service
- a playgroup that has been certificated by the Ministry of Education (this means a playgroup is funded by the Ministry of Education and will meet certain standards)
- if before 1 December 2014, a licence-exempt early childhood education and care centre funded by the Ministry of Education (this means a playgroup is funded by the Ministry of Education and so meets certain standards)
and
- for which a fee is charged for the children to participate in the programme
Most early childhood education services offer 20 Hours Early Childhood Education. This means that children aged 3, 4 and 5 years old may be able to receive up to 6 hours per day, 20 hours per week of free early childhood education.
To help clients meet this social obligation you should discuss childcare assistance that may be available to the client.

chunks.title: Bank — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Bank
An appropriate bank is:
- a private savings bank, a trustee savings bank, or The Co-operative Bank Limited or
- a registered bank which on the 31st March 1987 was a trading bank or
- any other registered bank or a building society approved by the Minister after consultation with the Minister of Finance
For more information see:
- Processing standards Bank account [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Breakdown in the child's family cannot be established — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Breakdown in the child's family cannot be established
If a breakdown in the childs family cannot be established the child cannot be considered dependent for Emergency Maintenance Allowance purposes.
The client should:
- ask the child's parent to contribute financially to the care and support of the child or
- have a good and sufficient reason to include the child in their benefit
Note the child must meet the definition of a dependent child to be included in the client's benefit.

chunks.title: Cash assets — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Cash assets
Cash assets mean any assets the client has that can easily be converted into cash.
## Cash assets do not include
- a caravan, boat or other vehicle with a net equity less than $2000, or is used by the client or a member of their family for day to day accommodation
- a home property and land on which it is situated
- a motor vehicle principally used by the client for private use
- Christchurch mosques attack support payments
- Crown funds provided directly to clients to purchase Support Services and Direct Disability Support payments
- funds locked into KiwiSaver and other retirement scheme accounts
- Information share Child Support payments currently being charged as income
- specified Ex gratia and compensation payments
- MSD lump sum payments for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Payments of Accommodation Supplement arrears due to a system processing error from 1993 to 2014 for the first 12 months after payment is made
- Payments of arrears to Special Benefit clients better off on Temporary Additional Support for the first 12 months after payment is made
- Payments to clients whose Kāinga Ora tenancy was terminated due to methamphetamine contamination for the first 12 months after payment is made
- personal effects
- Residential Care Subsidy historic review refunds for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Severe weather event payments for the first 12 months from when payment is received (and any interest earned on the payment)
- FamilyBoost Tax Credit payments for the first 12 months after payment is received
Note a bank overdraft facility is not considered a cash asset or a resource available to the client.
Payments made by the Crown, Earthquake Commission, insurance companies or the Canterbury Earthquake Commission (Red Cross) relating to the Canterbury earthquake, are generally excluded for the first 12 or 24 months following the date the client received the payment.
In exceptional circumstances you can disregard some of the client's cash assets.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Change in circumstances
Clients must tell us straight away of any changes in their circumstances or their family's situation that may affect entitlement to an Emergency Maintenance Allowance. Clients agree to this by signing the Emergency Maintenance Allowance application form.
A change in circumstance may also affect the client's social obligations.
Examples of changes and how to deal with these can be found in Changes and Reviews.
For more information see:
- Child changes and social obligations
- Changes and reviews Child changes

chunks.title: Change in circumstances during Money Management — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Change in circumstances during Money Management
Clients may have a change in circumstances during Money Management, such as a change in income, which may change their rate of benefit.
If a client declares a change in circumstances after their payment has been issued onto the payment card, it may mean this payment is incorrect resulting in a debt being established or arrears due to the client.
Any debt will generally be repaid from their future benefit payments.
If a client is owed arrears, it will be paid directly to their bank account. This is different when a client's benefit stops during Money Management – for more information see: Period of Money Management.

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
Emergency Maintenance Allowance is an Emergency Benefit. It provides income support for sole parents with 1 or more dependent children under the age of 14 who do not qualify for any other benefit.
## Emergency Maintenance Allowance clients generally cannot be absent and continue to get payment
Clients getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance cannot generally be absent from New Zealand and continue to get payment of their benefit. The Government's obligation to pay income support usually stops when the client leaves New Zealand.
## All clients have an obligation to advise of departure from New Zealand
All clients receiving a main benefit must advise MSD before they leave New Zealand. If the client does not advise MSD before their international travel, their benefit payments will stop from the day after they leave New Zealand.
## Paying Emergency Maintenance Allowance while client is absent from New Zealand
Generally, a client is not entitled to get Emergency Maintenance Allowance while they are absent from New Zealand.
However, in limited circumstances, the Emergency Maintenance Allowance can be paid for up to 28 days in a 52 week period when a client is absent from New Zealand for:
- Approved travel reasons
- Overseas medical treatment
## Payment of benefit while absent for more than 28 days in any 52 week period
Generally, a benefit cannot be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period.
However there are limited circumstances where a benefit can be paid for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.
## Mandatory Review while overseas
Mandatory Reviews apply to clients getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance when their benefit has an expiry date of more than 52-weeks or has no expiry date.
Clients getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance who have temporarily left New Zealand must still respond to the Mandatory Review before their Mandatory Review date.
Temporary absence from New Zealand (e.g. personal travel) does not pause or defer the Mandatory Review.
Clients must contact MSD to talk about their situation if they are unable to respond to the review or if more time is needed to do it.

chunks.title: Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
Generally, a benefit cannot be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period. However there are limited circumstances where a benefit can be paid for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.
These circumstances are:
- travel is required for an approved reason, and either: it is the client's first absence in a 52 week period and the permitted reason the client needs to be absent from New Zealand necessitates a period longer than 28 days orthe client has had other prior approved absences within the 52 week period and they require further approved absences which will require them to be absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- it is the client's first absence in a 52 week period and the permitted reason the client needs to be absent from New Zealand necessitates a period longer than 28 days or
- the client has had other prior approved absences within the 52 week period and they require further approved absences which will require them to be absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- the client is absent from New Zealand for an approved travel reason and their return is prevented by a new circumstances that requires them to be absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period

chunks.title: Action on return to New Zealand — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Action on return to New Zealand
You will need to look at the circumstances of the client's absence from and subsequent return to New Zealand to decide when to recommence their benefit and when to treat it as a new application.
You will need to consider the following:
- the client's intention at the time of their departure for example, did they cancel their benefit before leaving New Zealand because they did not intend to return
- did the client remain ordinarily resident during the period of absence?
- the length of time that they have been absent
- the reason for the absence
- have their circumstances changed significantly during their absence
- is the client eligible to have their benefit backdated to the day after their departure date or date of return?
For more information see:
- Backdating benefit to the day after departure date

chunks.title: Approved travel reasons — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Approved travel reasons
A client receiving Emergency Maintenance Allowance is generally not able to continue to get their main benefit payments while they are absent from New Zealand unless they meet the criteria for approved travel.
Approved travel for clients getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance is:
- travel for a permitted reason
Note clients are not required to meet their job search obligations while absent from New Zealand on approved travel.

chunks.title: Backdating benefit to the day after departure date — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Backdating benefit to the day after departure date
A client who leaves New Zealand without advising MSD of their travel can only have their benefit backdated to the day after their departure date if they:
- have a humanitarian reason that justifies their reason for travel and their failure to tell MSD before they left
- contacted MSD as soon as they could reasonably have been expected to, given their circumstances after they departed and
- meet the criteria to continue to be paid their benefit while overseas (either because they meet the criteria for approved travel, or the requirement that travel be approved does not apply to them)

chunks.title: Birth of a child — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Birth of a child
When a client applies to have their newborn child included in their benefit, the following information is required:
- full birth certificate of the child, or confirmation from Internal Affairs that the child's birth was registered online and permission was given to share the birth registration with MSD
- written statement from the client requesting inclusion of the child
If a child's birth certificate is not available immediately, you can include the child in the benefit (without delay) when the client can provide:
- Plunket records
- birth notices
- confirmation from the client's midwife or doctor of the date of birth of the new child or
- hospital papers
Note you must follow-up to make sure the client produces a copy of the birth certificate.
## Extra help
If a child is born with a mental or physical disability, needs constant care and attention because of a disability, or is likely to require care for at least 12 months, the client should test their eligibility for Child Disability Allowance.
When a child has ongoing additional costs because of a disability they may be able to receive a Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Calculating the period of absence — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Calculating the period of absence
The period of an absence from New Zealand for which payment of Emergency Maintenance Allowance can continue (if approved) is up to 28 consecutive days, that is, Saturdays and Sundays are included.
In all cases, when assessing the period of absence do not include:
- the date of departure from New Zealand and
- the date of return to New Zealand
If a client is absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period the benefit should be suspended from the 29th day (unless they meet the criteria to pay for longer than 28 days).
Note if a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, the benefit must be cancelled from the day after departure.
## Calculating 52 week period
When a client is paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand, a client can receive a payment for up to 28 days in total in a 52 week period. The 52 week period is counted in the following way:
- identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand
- count back 52 weeks from this date
- identify any periods of paid absence they have used (counting from the day after they have left New Zealand to the day before they returned to New Zealand)
- subtract the number of days absent from New Zealand from 28 days. The remainder is the client's entitlement to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand
- pay the client the days they have available up to the period of absence. This may not be the whole of the time they intend to be absent from New Zealand depending on how many days of their entitlement they have left

chunks.title: Verification — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Verification
You must obtain written proof of the new care arrangement.
Written proof could be (but is not limited to):
- statement from the other parent or
- parenting order or
- documentation from Oranga Tamariki
For more information see:
- Child comes into care
## Permanent or long term
To include a child as a dependent child, the change in care arrangements should be with the intent of permanency or at least capable of being a long-term arrangement.

chunks.title: Change in age — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Change in age
A child's age may affect:
- the family tax credit payable
- the Best Start tax credit payable
- whether the child is still a dependent child
- eligibility for Emergency Maintenance Allowance and
- the client's obligations
## Child is not dependent
A child is not a dependent child if they are:
- in full-time employment
Note generally a child is still a dependent child when they start part-time employment.
- getting a basic Student Allowance or an Independent Circumstances Allowance
Note getting a Student Loan does not always mean a child is financially independent.
- getting a benefit in their own right or
- financially independent
## Child turns 14
When a client's last dependent child turns 14, the client no longer qualifies for Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
## Child turns 18
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and can no longer be included in their parent or caregiver's payment, unless they are continuing in education and are not financially independent. The client must complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for their discretionary benefit such as Emergency Maintenance Allowance, and the rate payable.

chunks.title: Change of address — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Change of address
When a client advises that they have changed their address it is important to check that the move does not affect their entitlement to Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
Note you will need to update the address in CMS.
If the client is receiving Extra help this will also need to be reviewed to take into account their new costs.
If the client has a portion of their benefit paid to Kāinga Ora or Te Puni Kokiri this may need to be changed or cancelled.
The change of address may also indicate a change in the client's circumstances.
Examples of changes that may affect entitlement are:
- commencing employment, study or training
- ceased employment, study or training (clients with work obligations)
- marries or starts living with a partner
- dependent children who have come into or left their care

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Emergency Maintenance Allowance or the rate payable.
A change in a client's circumstances may mean that the client qualifies for another benefit.
MSD may also review a benefit at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment (if applicable).
## Mandatory Review for Emergency Maintenance Allowance
Mandatory Reviews for Emergency Maintenance Allowance will only apply to clients whose benefit has an expiry date of more than 52 weeks, or whose Emergency Maintenance Allowance has no expiry date.
MSD must review a client's Emergency Maintenance Allowance within 52 weeks of when the benefit commenced, or within 52 weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed.
Clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend.

chunks.title: Child admitted to hospital — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Child admitted to hospital
When a client's dependent child is admitted to hospital, there is no change to the rate of payment, irrespective of how long the child remains in hospital. Family tax credit payments continue to be paid for a child who is admitted to hospital.
Depending on the nature of the child's injury, health condition or disability the client may be able to get Child Disability Allowance.
Child Disability Allowance is a non-taxable allowance paid to the principal caregiver of a child with a serious disability, who is need of constant care and attention for a period longer than 12 months.

chunks.title: Child applies for a benefit in their own right — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Child applies for a benefit in their own right
When a child applies for a benefit in their own right, exclude the child from the client's Emergency Maintenance Allowance from:
- the start of the pay period following the date of event
Note there is discretion to continue payment for one more payday following the event.
or
- the date the child's benefit is granted
whichever is earlier.
Wherever possible (and in appropriate circumstances) the date of exclusion of the child from the client's benefit and the commencement date of the child's benefit should coincide to avoid financial hardship for the family.
Note there are specific rules for deciding whether a child is considered a dependent child when the child turns 18.

chunks.title: Child changes — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Child changes
The number of dependent children in an Emergency Maintenance Allowance client's care and any change to the circumstances of a child can affect:
- the rate of family tax credit payable
- payment of Best Start tax credit
- the rate of extra help payable
- the client's obligations and
- (in some situations) the client's eligibility to the benefit, for example, last child leaves care
## Including a child in Emergency Maintenance Allowance
For a child to be included in a client's Emergency Maintenance Allowance the child must be a dependent child and generally ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
When the child is not the client's natural or adoptive child, the client may be able to get an Unsupported Child's Benefit (instead of having the child included in their Emergency Maintenance Allowance). This will mainly depend on the care arrangements.
## Changes to a child's circumstances
Change to a dependent child's circumstances is generally going to affect the client's Emergency Maintenance Allowance.

chunks.title: Child comes into care — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Child comes into care
When a client has made an application to have another child included in their benefit and that child was in the care of another person the following information is required:
- full birth certificate of the childSee: Verification from Internal Affairs
- written statement from the applicant stating they are the principal caregiver and requesting inclusion in the Emergency Maintenance Allowance
- (where appropriate) letter from previous caregiver confirming that child has left their careNote if the client cannot get written confirmation from the previous caregiver, the new caring arrangement can be confirmed by a referee such as a teacher, Plunket nurse, minister or a Justice of the Peace.
Any benefit payments the previous caregiver was getting for the child must stop.
## Date of review
Include the child in the benefit from:
- the date the child came into the client's care or
- the date the Emergency Maintenance Allowance was granted
whichever is the later.
## Backdating
When a client requests the backdated inclusion of a child and the previous caregiver was getting a benefit for the child, you will need to review the date the child was excluded from the previous caregivers benefit.
Generally a child cannot be included in multiple benefits for the same period. In some situations, the previous caregiver may continue to get a benefit in respect of that child for up to 28 days.
Consider all the circumstances and decide whether a debt should be established for the previous caregiver.
If the date you are including the child from is a date in the previous tax year, MSD can only pay arrears of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit from the beginning of the current tax year, that is, 1 April. The client will need to apply for any arrears of tax credits before this date from Inland Revenue.
A review of entitlement needs to be completed to determine the amount of any benefit arrears owed to the client for the backdated period.

chunks.title: Personal earnings — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Personal earnings
A dependent child's personal earnings are not charged as income against the Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
However, a child in full-time employment and financially independent cannot be included as a dependent child in the benefit.
## Other income
A child may get other income that is not personal earnings.
For more information about how to treat other forms of child's income see:
- Income

chunks.title: Child leaves care — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Child leaves care
When a dependent child leaves the client's care, the child should be excluded from the start of the pay period following the date the child leaves care and any extra help the client gets should be reassessed at the appropriate rate where applicable.
If the child is the client's last dependent child aged under 14 years Emergency Maintenance Allowance must be cancelled. MSD must determine if the client qualifies for another benefit.
Note different rules apply when a child stops being a dependent child of a sole parent client because of a sudden change of circumstances beyond the control of the client.
## Example
A sole parent client getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance has two dependent children included in their benefit, one aged 11 and the other aged 13 years.
The younger child leaves care to start living with another caregiver as planned and is excluded from the start of the pay period following the date they left care so the client does not incur a debt.
Six months later the remaining child turns 14.
The client no longer meets the qualification for Emergency Maintenance Allowance and MSD must determine if the client qualifies for another benefit.
## Family tax credit
Family tax credits should be stopped from the start of the pay period following the date the event took place to avoid an overpayment with Inland Revenue for the client.

chunks.title: Child leaves care suddenly — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text: When a client getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance stops caring for a dependent child because of a sudden change of circumstances beyond the control of the client, payment of the benefit may continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child stopped being dependent. This is to allow a period of transition for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances. For example when a child suddenly goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki, payment may continue for 28 days from the date the child is no longer dependent on the client. Extra help payments that can be continued for 28 days are: - Accommodation Supplement - Child Disability Allowance - Disability Allowance - Temporary Additional Support - Winter Energy Payment The exception is Childcare Assistance which must be stopped on the day after the client stopped caring for the dependent child. During the 28 days continuation of payment, if the client has other changes of circumstances such as a change in income, the rate of main benefit and extra help will need to be reassessed using sole parent threshold rates.

chunks.title: Mandatory Reviews — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text: Generally, clients getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date or their payments will suspend. If a child leaves a sole parent's care suddenly and Emergency Maintenance Allowance will continue because a client gets this payment for more than one child, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client is unable to respond to the review (even if they had more time) based on their individual circumstances, they may qualify for an exemption. Generally, when the Mandatory Review is only for Emergency Maintenance Allowance and the benefit will stop at the end of the 28-day continuation period, and the review is due, an exemption will apply. The client must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text: Generally, clients getting a discretionary benefit such as Emergency Maintenance Allowance must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will be excluded from their payments. The client must also complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for Emergency Maintenance Allowance and the rate payable, or their payments will suspend. If Emergency Maintenance Allowance and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a child has left a sole parent's care suddenly, and that child turns 18 during that period, the client is not required to complete a review of circumstances. However, if Emergency Maintenance Allowance and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a child has left a sole parent's care suddenly, and a different child in their care turns 18, the client must still complete the review of circumstances or their payments will suspend.

chunks.title: Family tax credit — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text: Family tax credits should be stopped from the start of the pay period following the date the child left care (whether planned or suddenly) to avoid an overpayment with Inland Revenue for the client.

chunks.title: Child under the age of 18 years — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Child under the age of 18 years
When a child under the age of 18 years leaves school or tertiary education, they can continue to be included in the parent or caregiver's Emergency Maintenance Allowance until the start of the pay period following their 18th birthday as long as the child remains a dependent child.
## Child aged 18 years old
When a child aged 18 years old leaves school or tertiary education, they should be excluded from their parent or caregiver's payment from the start of the pay period following the date the child left school or tertiary education. The parent or caregiver must complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for their discretionary benefit such as Emergency Maintenance Allowance, and the rate payable.
## Family tax credit
When a child leaves school or tertiary education, family tax credits should be stopped from the day the child is excluded from the parent or caregiver's Emergency Maintenance Allowance.

chunks.title: Deciding if a child is financially dependent — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Deciding if a child is financially dependent
When a client states that they are receiving payments for a child's expenses you must decide if the child is a dependent child of the client.
A child does not have to be solely financially dependent on a client to be considered a dependent child. All that is required is that the child is financially dependent on the person to some degree.
However, being financially dependent on a client is only part of the qualifications of a dependent child. The child must still meet all the qualifications to be considered dependent.
If another person or body is paying for the child's expenses, including payments for the care provided, the child is not financially dependent on the client.
If a client is receiving payments toward the expenses of a dependent child this is regarded as income for benefit purposes.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Emergency Maintenance Allowance from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday. The parent or caregiver must also complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for their discretionary benefit such as Emergency Maintenance Allowance, and the rate payable.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and included in their parent or caregiver's Emergency Maintenance Allowance for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier
Note a parent or caregiver getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance must complete a review of circumstances when a dependent child turns 18, and when the child is excluded (if they continued to be included in the parent or caregiver's benefit after the child turned 18).
If the parent or caregiver does not complete the review, their Emergency Maintenance Allowance will be suspended.

chunks.title: Client becomes sick — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Client becomes sick
When an Emergency Maintenance Allowance client has a health condition, injury or disability that permanently and severely restricts their ability to work, they may be able to get Supported Living Payment on the ground of a health condition, an injury or a disability.
If the client is admitted to hospital it may affect their rate of payment.

chunks.title: Surviving dependent child — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Surviving dependent child
When a client dies (and there is a surviving dependent child) before a decision is made on an application or review for Emergency Maintenance Allowance you can continue the application or review process as if the client had not died.
## Funeral Grant
In situations when the decision to grant or review Emergency Maintenance Allowance is made after the date of death of the client, you decide any Funeral Grant as if the deceased client were in receipt of Emergency Maintenance Allowance. For more information see:
- Funeral Grant

chunks.title: Client donates a kidney or liver tissue — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Client donates a kidney or liver tissue
When a client is donating a kidney or liver tissue, they can keep getting their Emergency Maintenance Allowance. Exempt the client from any work obligations during the recovery period.
Grant the exemption 'Would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability'.
Manually record the exemption and the client's circumstances in the CMS 'Client Event Note', this exemption cannot be entered in SWIFTT.
The exemption starts from the date of their operation and can continue while the client:
- is recovering from their operation and
- they cannot meet their part-time or full-time work obligations
This exemption must not be more than 12 weeks.
Do not apply any obligation failures:
- for the maximum period of 12 weeks or
- until the client has recovered from the operation
whichever is earlier.
## Client has an obligation failure
If the client currently has an obligation failure, donating a kidney or liver tissue is considered a 'good and sufficient reason'. The work obligations failure must be overturned.
This will remove the failure from the client’s 12 month obligation failure count. No sanction is added.
## Childcare Assistance
Clients may be eligible for Childcare Assistance payments while they are they are recovering.
For more information see:
- Childcare Subsidy Temporary illness
- OSCAR Temporary illness

chunks.title: Absent from New Zealand but benefit not being paid — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Absent from New Zealand but benefit not being paid
Where a client had left New Zealand and their benefit wasn't paid as they didn't qualify for an approved travel reason, and they now qualify for an approved travel reason, their benefit may be started from the date the client became eligible to receive the benefit overseas (where they have sufficient days left from their 28 days within a 52 week period).
## Examples (but are not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A client receiving Emergency Maintenance Allowance was out of New Zealand visiting his father in Australia. His Emergency Maintenance Allowance was suspended the day after he left New Zealand as it wasn't an approved travel reason. The client contacts Work and Income three days later to say that his father is in hospital as he has had a heart attack. The client has been paid for five days in the previous 52 weeks while he was absent from New Zealand leaving a balance of 23 days.
The reason for travel now meets the criteria for approved travel. The benefit is resumed from the date the client became eligible to receive the benefit overseas. The client must contact Work and Income from overseas. The benefit cannot be back-dated if the client advises Work and Income when they return to New Zealand.
A client receiving Emergency Maintenance Allowance left New Zealand to visit her sick mother. Two days before she was due to return, her mother's house burnt down. The client has been paid for 20 days in the previous 52 weeks while she was absent from New Zealand leaving a balance of eight days.
The reason for travel has changed and the client has not been absent from New Zealand for up to 28 days in any 52 week period. The benefit expiry is extended for an additional five days.
If the client hadn't informed Work and Income their benefit would have stopped from the day they were meant to return.
Note that where the client has already been absent for 28 days in a 52 week period, consider whether the client meets the criteria for receiving a payment for more than 28 days in any 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Paying for more than 28 days - delayed return
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Client not returned due to an unforeseeable event (within 28 day maximum) — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Client not returned due to an unforeseeable event (within 28 day maximum)
Generally, a client must advise Work and Income if there is a change in their return date. A client may need to change their return date when:
- they cannot return to New Zealand due to an event or new circumstances
- they couldn't have couldn't have reasonably foreseen the event or circumstance when they left New Zealand and
- the event or circumstance is outside of their control
## Examples include (but are not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A client receiving Emergency Maintenance Allowance left New Zealand to see a sick family member. While she was in Australia there was severe flooding which meant she could not return to New Zealand on the day she was meant to return. She contacts Work and Income. The client has been paid for 20 days in the previous 52 weeks while she was absent from New Zealand, leaving a balance of eight days.
The client cannot return due to circumstances that were not reasonably foreseeable and they were outside the client's control. Work and Income would extend the client's benefit for a reasonable period for her to be able to return.
If the client hadn't informed Work and Income their benefit would have stopped from the day they were meant to return.
A client receiving Emergency Maintenance Allowance has been overseas for five days to attend his father's funeral. He is delayed in Sydney due to fog. He must remain a further three days.
The client cannot return due to circumstances that were not reasonably foreseeable and they were outside the client's control. Work and Income would extend the client's benefit for a reasonable period for him to be able to return. Also consider whether there is any grounds to pay for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Client obtains employment overseas — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Client obtains employment overseas
Where the client:
- is successful in their job prospect or job search overseas and
- they are not returning to New Zealand
the Emergency Maintenance Allowance should be cancelled from the day after the notice of job appointment.
If the client returns to New Zealand for the period between getting the job and actually starting employment, the Emergency Maintenance Allowance can be continued until they leave the country. The benefit must be cancelled from the day after they leave New Zealand to commence the job.

chunks.title: Contacting MSD as soon as the client reasonably can — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Contacting MSD as soon as the client reasonably can
A client who leaves New Zealand without advising MSD of their travel can only have their benefit backdated to the day after departure date if they contact MSD as soon as they could reasonably have been expected to, given the circumstances.
This may be while the client is still absent from New Zealand, or once they have returned.
For more information see:
- Backdating benefit to the day after departure date
## Determining reasonable contact time
In order to determine whether a client contacted MSD as soon as they could reasonably have been expected to, you need to take into account the circumstances of the client.
The reason why the client did not contact MSD until after returning to New Zealand may be the same reason why they left New Zealand without advising MSD of their absence, or a different humanitarian reason.
Reasons for not contacting MSD sooner may include (but are not limited to) that the client:
- did not contact MSD due to the stress of the event that led to them leaving New Zealand without informing Work and Income
- left with a humanitarian reason, and then could not access the technology to communicate with MSD while absent from New Zealand
- left for a humanitarian reason, and then was temporarily medically unfit while overseas and they have a medical certificate that shows this
- left for humanitarian reason, and then had a death or illness in the immediate family while overseas or on return to New Zealand and/or
- left for a humanitarian reason, and then experienced an adverse event or natural disaster while overseas or on return to New Zealand that meant they were unable to contact MSD
## Contacting Work and Income on return to New Zealand
Generally, it would be reasonable to expect a client to contact MSD within 10 working days of returning to New Zealand.
However, you should consider whether the client's circumstances meant they were unable to inform MSD in this period.

chunks.title: Protected earnings rate — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Protected earnings rate
No attachment order can, whether on its own or when combined with any other attachment order, Child Support deduction, or Ministry of Social Development debt repayment, take a client's total income below the protected earnings rate. For more information, see:
- Protected earnings rate

chunks.title: Backdating — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Backdating
Where a client requests the backdated inclusion of a child and the previous caregiver was in receipt of a benefit for the child, you will need to review when the child was excluded from the previous caregivers benefit.
Note a child cannot be included in two benefits for the same period.
Have regard to all the circumstances and decide whether a debt should be established for the previous caregiver.
If the date you are including the child from is a date in the previous tax year, SWIFTT will only pay arrears of family tax credit from the beginning of the current tax year, that is, 1 April. You will need to advise the client that any arrears of family tax credit prior to this date will need to be claimed from Inland Revenue.
You will need to do a backdated review in the SBDR screen to pay any benefit arrears to the client for the previous tax year. A backdated review may be required for the current year if other rate changes have occurred - check the SRAUI screen for details.
For more information see:
- Processing standards Child changes [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Death of a child — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Death of a child
When a dependent child dies, the child should be excluded from Emergency Maintenance Allowance 28 days following the date of the child's death.
Payment of the benefit should continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child died. This provides a transition period for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.
## Best Start tax credit
Best Start tax credit is paid for 28 days following the child's date of death.
Note if the child's third birthday is in the 28-day period the Best Start tax credit stops from the date of the child's third birthday.
## Mandatory Reviews
If the child who has died was the only child in the client's care, the Mandatory Review is not required. When Emergency Maintenance Allowance is paid for multiple children, the Mandatory Review must still be completed. The client may be able to get an extension or an exemption.
## Child turns 18
Generally, clients getting a discretionary benefit such as Emergency Maintenance Allowance must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will be excluded from their payments. The client must also complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for Emergency Maintenance Allowance and the rate payable, or their payments will suspend.
If Emergency Maintenance Allowance and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because the client's child has died, and the child that died was due to turn 18 during that period, the client is not required to complete a review of circumstances.
However, if Emergency Maintenance Allowance and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because the client's child has died and a different child in their care turns 18, the client must complete the review of circumstances or their payments will suspend.

chunks.title: Death of a client — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
Emergency Maintenance Allowance can continue to be paid for 28 days following the death of a client.
The continuation of payment beyond the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit.
## Exception
When the death of the client was the result of an accident, entitlement to a lump sum Accident Compensation payment needs to be decided before terminal benefit can be paid.
If the child is entitled to a survivors grant from the Accident Compensation Corporation there is no entitlement to Emergency Maintenance Allowance beyond the date of death.
When benefit payment has continued beyond the date of death, an overpayment should be established and recovery of the debt should be sought from the estate.
## Mandatory Reviews
There are no Mandatory Reviews of Emergency Maintenance Allowance when the client has died.
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Emergency Maintenance Allowance when the child turns 18 during the 28-day continuation of payment period.
The review of circumstances for a discretionary benefit such as Emergency Maintenance Allowance when their child turns 18 is not required when the client has died.

chunks.title: Arrears — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Arrears
When a client has benefit payment arrears owing to them at the time of their death and they have an outstanding debt balance, you should attempt to recover the debt, in full, from the final benefit payment.

chunks.title: Debt Repayment Orders — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Debt Repayment Orders
All Debt Repayment Orders are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
Debt Repayment Orders are issued by the Ministry of Justice under the Insolvency Act 2006 and can be issued when the client is an un-discharged bankrupt.
Unlike other Ministry of Justice attachment orders, Debt Repayment Orders are not subject to any protected earnings rate. Payment is generally made to the supervisor of the debt but occasionally the District Court will act as an agent for collection of the debt.
Payment continues for 3 years or until further notice is received from either the supervisor or the District Court.
Unlike Ministry of Justice attachment orders, Debt Repayment Orders are administered via the PYECI screen in SWIFTT, not through CORBI.

chunks.title: Decision guidelines for shared care — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines for shared care
The parent with greater responsibility is usually the parent who has the child for most of the time. If a parent has the child for at least 60% of the time they have the primary responsibility.
Where parents have equal time, to help you decide which parent has greater responsibility, consider the following:
- who pays for the child's material support (furniture, clothes etc)
- who decides about the child's daily activities
- who takes them to and from school and supervises leisure activities
- who makes decisions about their education and health
- who pays for which expenses
If it is not clear who has greater responsibility or the parents share the responsibility equally, the parent who was mainly responsible for the day-to-day care of the child prior to the separation is the person who can have the child included.
If you can't decide who is entitled to have the child included, the parents must make the decision. Don't include the child in any income support until they have decided.

chunks.title: Decision guidelines - sole parents — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines - sole parents
When a sole parent Emergency Maintenance Allowance client is imprisoned it is important that financial assistance is available to support any dependent children.
While Emergency Maintenance Allowance should generally be stopped when the client is imprisoned, there is discretion for payment to be continued and paid to the person who is caring for the client's dependent children.
To help you decide whether it is reasonable to pay the Emergency Maintenance Allowance while the client is in prison, consider the following:
- has the period in prison already passed
- is the client due to be released from prison shortly
- is the likely period in prison less than twelve months
- will the children return to the client's care on their release from prison
- has the caregiver ceased work to care for the children
- has the caregiver lost entitlement to their own benefit due to having children in their care
For further help you can contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.
For more information see:
- Examples - sole parents
- Rate of payment
- Remanded in custody
- Temporary caregiver

chunks.title: Dependent child — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
A dependent child for Emergency Maintenance Allowance is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of the client
- maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
- in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but has been returned to their parent's care
A dependent child for Emergency Maintenance Allowance does not include a:
- child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989
- child for whom Orphan's or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid and
- young person getting a Young Parent Payment and their child (see Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples)
## Primary responsibility
The client must be responsible for the day-to-day care of the child and be the person who makes the major decisions concerning the child's life (for example schooling and health care).
There are some situations where the person who has principal responsibility of a child is not clear.
## Maintained as a member of the family
The child should be an integral part of the family, participating in the usual family activities (for example outings and annual holidays).
Dependent children should be included in the assessment of Emergency Benefit.
In some situations, a child may not be living at home but is still considered to be a dependent child.

chunks.title: Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital
When person who has been remanded in custody or is serving a term of imprisonment, is detained in or transferred to a psychiatric hospital you may be able to pay an Emergency Benefit at the hospital rate.
People who are remanded in custody or serving a term of imprisonment who are temporarily hospitalised for treatment of an injury or illness are still considered to be in prison and the Department of Corrections will meet their costs. An Emergency Benefit or any other financial assistance cannot be paid.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Person serving their sentence of imprisonment in a psychiatric hospital
- Release from prison

chunks.title: Discharge from hospital — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Discharge from hospital
Where a client is getting the hospital rate and they are discharged from hospital:
- increase their benefit to the appropriate full rate from the date of discharge and
- review any Extra Help from the same date
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.
## Re-admitted to hospital
When a client (who has been formally discharged from hospital) is re-admitted, the 13 week period starts again from the day after they are re-admitted (even if the client has been re-admitted within 28 days of being discharged).
Note this only refers to clients who are formally discharged from hospital not clients on leave.
For more information about clients on leave from hospital see:
- On leave from hospital

chunks.title: Discharged from Oranga Tamariki care — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Discharged from Oranga Tamariki care
Where Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency has care, custody or sole guardianship of the child, and returns the child to the care of the immediate previous caregiver, they do not make payments for the child.
The child is then a dependent child and can be included in the Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
Where the relationship is not one of care, but more of a boarding arrangement, the young person may be able to receive Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment.
Once a child has been discharged from care the child can be considered a dependent child even when Oranga Tamariki or any other authorised agency involvement continues, for example:
- Additional Guardianship Order
- Support Order or
- Services Order
When there is a Service or Support Order in place, you will need to make sure that the Court's intent allows you to consider the child as a dependent child.
For further details on what discharged from care means see:
- Definition of discharged from Oranga Tamariki care

chunks.title: Effect on benefit — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Effect on benefit
Any inclusion or exclusion of a dependent child from a client's benefit will result in a general review of the client's Emergency Maintenance Allowance and any extra help they are getting.
You may need to review the following:
- Accommodation SupplementChanges to the family composition may result in a change to the Accommodation Supplement entry thresholds.
- Non-standard benefit rateWhere a child is added or removed you may need to manually adjust the non-standard rate of payment.
- Special BenefitAny change to family circumstances will result in a review of Special Benefit. A child included or excluded from the Emergency Maintenance Allowance may result in a change to the allowable costs for Special Benefit.
- Temporary Additional SupportAny change to family circumstances will result in a review of Temporary Additional Support. A child included or excluded from the Emergency Maintenance Allowance may result in a change to the allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support.
- Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Effect on Extra Help — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Effect on Extra Help
Extra Help can continue to be paid to the client for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital. When the client's benefit is reduced to the hospital rate, any Extra Help they receive will need to be stopped.
## Accommodation Supplement
You will need to check whether the client still has to meet their continuing accommodation costs. If so, increase the benefit rate above the hospital rate to meet the accommodation costs.
## Special Benefit
You will need to check whether the client still has to meet their continuing costs. If so, increase the benefit rate above the hospital rate to meet the costs.

chunks.title: Emergency Maintenance Allowance suspended before Mandatory Review date — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Emergency Maintenance Allowance suspended before Mandatory Review date
Clients getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance are always notified about their Mandatory Review, even if their Emergency Maintenance Allowance is suspended, unless it is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison.
MSD must not undertake the Mandatory Review unless the client contacts MSD to resume their Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
If the client contacts MSD before their review date to resume their Emergency Maintenance Allowance, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to do their Mandatory Review. MSD can resume the benefit before the Mandatory Review has been responded to.
However, if the client contacts MSD on or after their Mandatory Review date, the review must be completed before MSD can resume the benefit.
Example
Daisy is getting Emergency Maintenance Allowance. Daisy's Mandatory Review is due on 2 May.
Daisy left New Zealand to go on holiday on 25 April and did not tell MSD that she was leaving. Her Emergency Maintenance Allowance is suspended on 26 April.
On 10 May Daisy contacts MSD and advises that she arrived back in New Zealand on 7 May.
MSD advises Daisy that she will need to respond to the Mandatory Review and confirm her circumstances before MSD can resume her Emergency Maintenance Allowance.
On 11 May Daisy responds to her Mandatory Review and confirms that she has had no change in circumstances.
MSD determines that Daisy continues to qualify for Emergency Maintenance Allowance at the same rate and resumes her benefit from 7 May.
MSD completes Daisy's Mandatory Review on 11 May and sets the next review date for 52 weeks from the date the review was completed.

chunks.title: Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason to travel (within 28 day maximum) — main benefits > emergency maintenance allowance > changes and reviews emergency maintenance allowance
chunks.text:
## Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason to travel (within 28 day maximum)
Where the client is receiving their payments while they are absent from New Zealand because they have an approved travel reason and their return date changes, they must advise Work and Income from overseas, otherwise their payment will be stopped from the day they originally advised they would return to New Zealand.
They may be able to have their benefit backdated if there is an unforeseen reason they cannot notify us. For example, a client boards a plane to return home on schedule and the plane is held up due to fog. There is no way the client could notify Work and Income due to an event outside of their control. The benefit would be resumed from the original date the client was due to return (this will be on the itinerary or e-ticket).
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Client not returned due to an unforeseeable event
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Client does not return
