chunks.text: Sole parent and grandparented clients move to weekly charging from: - their next commencement date, this is when: a client moves to the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle because they completed the 26 week reapplication process before their final 52 week expiry date, and their Jobseeker Support has been regranted ora client transfers to another main benefit and then back to Jobseeker Support ortheir benefit is cancelled for any reason and they later apply for and are granted Jobseeker Support - a client moves to the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle because they completed the 26 week reapplication process before their final 52 week expiry date, and their Jobseeker Support has been regranted or - a client transfers to another main benefit and then back to Jobseeker Support or - their benefit is cancelled for any reason and they later apply for and are granted Jobseeker Support - when they have a change in circumstances that means they are no longer a sole parent or grandparented client, for example: if a sole parents only dependent child leaves their care ora grandparented client has their benefit cancelled for any reason and they later apply for and are granted Jobseeker Support - if a sole parents only dependent child leaves their care or - a grandparented client has their benefit cancelled for any reason and they later apply for and are granted Jobseeker Support If a sole parent or grandparented client has a change in circumstances other than the kind listed above, they can continue to have their income charged annually until they move to the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle. For example, when a client has had their benefit temporarily suspended at any time before their final 52 week expiry date. For more information see: - Completing the 26 week reapplication process

chunks.title: Temporary full-time employment — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: When a client has commenced full-time employment they no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support. However, there is an exception for some clients. For more information see: - Temporary employment period for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026

chunks.title: Applying a subsequent medical expiry extension of more than 4 weeks in exceptional circumstances — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: There may be situations when a client is still unable to produce a current medical certificate within the period of time their medical coverage has been extended ie up to 4 weeks. Subsequent medical expiry extensions are discretionary and should only be considered in exceptional circumstances. This means clients in situations beyond their control due to genuine unforeseen events may be granted a subsequent extension. A subsequent extension must not be granted unless there is a good and sufficient reason due to exceptional circumstances. You must assess if a client has exceptional circumstances to determine if a subsequent extension is appropriate. Note existing medical information can be used when extending coverage. To determine whether a client's situation allows for a subsequent extension of up to another 4 weeks, you must consider if the client's circumstances are additional to, and significantly different from, the approved reason provided when the previous extension was initially applied. See example below: Example A client is unable to get an appointment with their doctor for another 3 weeks due to the unavailability of doctors. The client called to tell us they are unable to provide a medical certificate in time but have booked an appointment. A discretionary medical expiry extension of 4 weeks was initially applied. However, a few days before their doctor’s appointment, there was a death in the family and the client was unable to attend the scheduled appointment. When the appointment was rescheduled, the client was told that the next available appointment would be in 3 weeks. The client accepted the appointment and notified the Ministry. In this situation a subsequent extension is appropriate. The events in this client's situation are unplanned and/or unavoidable. The client has also demonstrated their attempts at re-arranging an appointment but is limited by the lack of appointments at their doctor's surgery. Note a further extension of entitlement should not exceed 8 weeks in total. If the client does not provide a current medical certificate by the subsequent extension date, a discussion with them is needed to review their current circumstances and see if they qualify for Jobseeker Support on another ground or other financial assistance such as another main benefit or extra help.

chunks.title: When extending entitlement is not appropriate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: When a decision is made not to apply a discretionary medical expiry extension, you must ensure you have: - considered the client's individual situation - considered all factors to determine there is no good and sufficient reason for not providing a current medical certificate in time and - fully explained to the client the reasons for the Ministry's decision to not extend payment of their Jobseeker Support

chunks.title: Approved travel reasons — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Approved travel reasons
A client receiving Jobseeker Support (and partners with work obligations or work preparation activities assigned) are generally not able to continue to receive their main benefit payments while they are absent from New Zealand unless they meet the criteria for approved travel.
Approved travel includes:
- travel for a permitted reason
- travel where the absence does not prevent the partner from meeting all of their obligations because the absence is at a time they are not required to attend employment, education or training (whichever applies)
Note clients with work obligations are not required to meet their job search obligations while absent from New Zealand on approved travel.
For more information see:
- Permitted travel reasons
- Absences that do not prevent partner from meeting their obligations
## Length of travel for an approved travel reason
Clients can travel for up to 28 days on Jobseeker Support for an approved travel reason. Discuss with the client the amount of time that they need to be absent from New Zealand as a result of the approved reason. The client should explain the length of their intended absence.
Consider:
- the length of time the event or reason for travel will take
- the duties the client will have as part of their reason (eg if they are travelling for a funeral, do they have responsibilities beyond attending the funeral itself such as estate duties or sorting out the possessions of the deceased?)
- flight availability and travel time
Remember to advise clients that generally they are only able to continue to be paid their benefit for up to 28 days in a 52 week period. This should be taken into account when deciding the approved travel period.
## Client travelling for multiple reasons
Some clients may travel overseas for an approved travel reason but elect to stay longer for another reason that is not an approved travel reason. In this case, the client can generally only receive their main benefit payments for the period of time that the approved travel reason applies to.
For more information see:
- Examples of applying the Absence from New Zealand policy
- Absences from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Travel notifications made while overseas [no link find out why] procedures
- Travel notifications made on return to New Zealand [no link find out why] procedures

chunks.title: Assistance during seasonal work — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Assistance during seasonal work
Where Jobseeker Support client is engaged in seasonal work they may be entitled to additional assistance.
For more information see:
- Extra Help
- Working for Families Tax Credits from Inland Revenue
If the client is eligible for non-beneficiary assistance the benefit must be cancelled.
- Employment and training Seasonal Work Assistance
- Transition to Work [no link find out why]
Note if a client is liable to pay Child Support advise them to contact Inland Revenue to make alternative arrangements for payment.

chunks.title: Backdating benefit to the day after departure date — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Backdating benefit to the day after departure date
A client who leaves New Zealand without advising Work and Income of their travel can only have their benefit backdated to the day after their departure date if they:
- have a humanitarian reason that justifies their reason for travel and their failure to tell Work and Income before they left
- contacted Work and Income as soon as they could reasonably have been expected to, given their circumstances after they departed and
- meet the criteria to continue to be paid their benefit while overseas (either because they meet the criteria for approved travel, or the requirement that travel be approved does not apply to them)
For more information see:
- Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure
- Contacting Work and Income as soon as the client reasonably can
- Approved travel reasons
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Action on return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Benefit has expired — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Benefit has expired
If a client's Jobseeker Support (health condition, injury or disability) has expired and the client has provided medical coverage from the date the benefit expired, the benefit can be resumed from the expiry date as long as the client meets the qualifications during the expired period.
When deciding whether to resume the benefit from the expiry date, where your client does not have medical coverage during the expired period, you should consider:
- the length of time without medical coverage
- how they have financially supported themselves
- the nature of their illness
- any reasons why medical coverage was not supplied and
- whether they need a payment of arrears
If it is reasonably clear that your client meets the qualifications during the expired period and would have had medical coverage, resume the benefit from the expiry date.
If it is not clear, you can ask your client to provide medical coverage for the period. If your client cannot provide evidence, resume the benefit from the date of medical coverage.
As a guideline, if the expiry period is over 28 days, the client may be required to re-apply for the benefit.
## Second opinion
When you are uncertain about the health practitioner's recommended duration for medical coverage, you should refer to your Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor [no link find out why] for advice. They may recommend the client is referred to a designated health practitioner for further assessment.
## Delay in producing a current medical certificate
There may be situations when a client is unable to provide a current medical certificate before the expiry date.
If a client has a good and sufficient reason for the delay, you can consider applying a discretionary medical expiry extension allowing a client more time to produce a current medical certificate and continue getting their benefit during the extension period.
Note existing medical information can be used to extend medical coverage of up to 4 weeks.

chunks.title: Birth of a child — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Birth of a child
When a client applies to have their newborn child included in their benefit, the following information is required:
- full birth certificate of the child, or confirmation from Internal Affairs that the childs’ birth was registered online and permission was given to share the birth registration with MSD
- written statement from the client requesting inclusion of the child
If a child's birth certificate is not available immediately, you can include the child in the benefit (without delay) when the client can provide:
- Plunket records
- birth notices
- confirmation from the client's midwife or doctor of the date of birth of the new child or
- hospital papers
Note you must follow-up to make sure the client produces a copy of the birth certificate.
## Extra help
If a child is born with a mental or physical disability, needs constant care and attention because of a disability, or is likely to require care for at least 12 months, the client should test their eligibility for Child Disability Allowance.
When a child has ongoing additional costs because of a disability, they may be able to receive a Disability Allowance.
For more information see:
- Partner in prison - child support obligations
- Date of review (including backdating)
- Dependent child
- Effect on benefit
- Child should be included
- Family tax credit
- Best Start tax credit
- Verification from Internal Affairs

chunks.title: Calculating the benefit rate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Calculating the benefit rate
SWIFTT will automatically calculate the rate of benefit payable when you add the client's income on the INCMA screen. If income is declared late it may be appropriate to complete a back dated review SBDR. SWIFTT will prompt you when a back dated review is required. You will need to check SRAUI to determine the period the review is required for.
You can use the Income Assessment tab in DREW to estimate the benefit rate with income for the client.
Note income must be rounded down to the nearest dollar.
For more information see:
- Examples of income assessment
- Recording income
- Income for a past period

chunks.title: Calculating the period of absence — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Calculating the period of absence
The period of an absence from New Zealand for which payment of Jobseeker Support can continue (if approved) is up to 28 consecutive days, that is, Saturdays and Sundays are included.
In all cases, when assessing the period of absence do not include:
- the date of departure from New Zealand and
- the date of return to New Zealand
If a client is absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period the benefit should be suspended from the 29th day (unless they meet the criteria to pay for longer than 28 days).
Note if a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, the benefit must be cancelled from the day after departure.
## Calculating 52 week period
When a client is paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand, a client can receive a payment for up to 28 days in total in a 52 week period. The 52 week period is counted in the following way:
- identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand
- count back 52 weeks from this date
- identify any periods of paid absence they have used (counting from the day after they have left New Zealand to the day before they returned to New Zealand)
- subtract the number of days absent from New Zealand from 28 days. The remainder is the client's entitlement to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand
- pay the client the days they have available up to the period of absence. This may not be the whole of the time they intend to be absent from New Zealand depending on how many days of their entitlement they have left
For more information see:
- Examples of calculating absence from New Zealand
- Permanent absence
- Reciprocal Agreements

chunks.title: Carer arrangements — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Carer arrangements
Where parents of a child live apart and the child comes into the care of the other parent it is important to establish that the arrangements made have been agreed to by both parents before you include the child in the other parents benefit.
In some cases the arrangement between both parents may not be of a legal arrangement but the child has been placed with the other parent by mutual agreement.
## Verification
You must obtain written proof of the new care arrangement. Written proof could be (but is not limited to):
- statement from the other parent
- court order or
- documentation from Oranga Tamariki
For more information see:
- Child comes into care
## Permanent or long term
To include a child as a dependent child, the change of carer should be with the intent of permanency or at least capable of being a long-term arrangement.
For more information see:
- Shared care
- Split care
- Temporary care

chunks.title: Change in age — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Change in age
A child's age may affect:
- the family tax credit payable
- the Best Start tax credit payable
- the partner's obligations and
- whether the child is still a dependent child
## Partner's work obligations
Unless a partner qualifies for an exemption from their obligations, they are required to:
- prepare for work (if required) when the youngest dependent child is under 3 years old
- meet the part-time work obligations when the youngest dependent child turns 3
- meet the full-time work obligations when the youngest dependent child turns 14
## Child turns 18
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and can no longer be included in their parent or caregiver's payments, unless they are continuing in education and are not financially independent.
If the parent or caregiver is getting a discretionary benefit such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of hardship, they must complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for their discretionary benefit.

chunks.title: Change of address — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Change of address
When a client advises that they have changed their address it is important to check that the move does not affect their entitlement to Jobseeker Support.
Note you will need to update the address in CMS.
If the client is receiving Extra Help, this will need to be reviewed.
If the client has a portion of their benefit paid to Kāinga Ora or Te Puni Kokiri for accommodation costs this may need to be changed or cancelled.
## Change in circumstances
The change of address may also indicate a change in the client's circumstances.
Examples of changes that may affect the client's entitlement to Jobseeker Support are:
- commencing employment
- commencing study or training
- moving to a remote area where there are few job opportunities
- change of relationship status
- dependent children coming into or leaving care
For more information see:
- Meeting job search requirements
- Limited employment locations
- Approved training
- Students

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Jobseeker Support.
MSD may review a benefit at any time to ensure the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
A change in a client's circumstances may also mean that they qualify for another benefit.

chunks.title: Child admitted to hospital — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child admitted to hospital
Where a client's dependent child is admitted to hospital, there is no change to the rate of payment while the child remains in hospital. Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments continue to be paid for a child who is admitted to hospital. Best Start tax credit will stop when the child turns three even if they are in hospital.
Depending on the nature of the child's injury, illness or disability the client may be able to receive Child Disability Allowance.
Child Disability Allowance is a non-taxable allowance paid to the principal caregiver of a child with a serious disability, who is need of constant care and attention for a period longer than 12 months.
For more information see:
- Child Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Child applies for a benefit in their own right — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child applies for a benefit in their own right
Where a child applies for a benefit in their own right, exclude the child from the client's Jobseeker Support from:
- the start of the pay period following the date of event
Note there is discretion to continue payment for one more payday following the event.
or
- the date the child's benefit is granted
whichever is earlier.
Wherever possible (and in appropriate circumstances) the date of exclusion of the child from the client's benefit and the commencement date of the child's benefit should coincide to avoid financial hardship for the family.
Note there are specific rules for deciding whether a child is considered a dependent child when the child turns 18.

chunks.title: Child changes — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child changes
The number of dependent children in a Jobseeker Support client's care and any change to the circumstance of a child can affect:
- the basic rate of benefit payable
- the rate of family tax credit payable
- payment of Best Start tax credit
- the rate of extra help payable and
- the client's obligations
## Including a child in Jobseeker Support
For a child to be included in a client's Jobseeker Support the child must be a dependent child and generally ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
When the child is not the client's natural or adoptive child, the client may be able to get an Unsupported Child's Benefit (instead of having the child included in their Jobseeker Support). This will mainly depend on the care arrangements.
## Changes to a child's circumstances
Change to a dependent child's circumstances is generally going to affect the client's Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Child comes into care — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child comes into care
When a client has made an application to have another child included in their benefit and that child was in the care of another person the following information is required:
- full birth certificate of the childSee: Verification from Internal Affairs
- written statement from the applicant stating they are the principal caregiver and requesting inclusion in the Jobseeker Support
- (where appropriate) letter from previous caregiver confirming that child has left their careNote when the client cannot get written confirmation from the previous caregiver, the new caring arrangement can be confirmed by a referee such as a teacher, Plunket nurse, minister or a Justice of the Peace.
Any benefit payments the previous caregiver was getting for the child must stop.
## Single client has child come into care
When a single client has a child aged under 14 years come into their care the client may be able to get another benefit such as Sole Parent Support.
For more information see:
- Qualifies for another benefit
## Clients aged under 20 years old
Clients aged under 20 years old who have a child come into their care no longer meet the age qualification for Jobseeker Support.
For more information see:
## Date of review
Include the child in the benefit from:
- the date the child came into the client's care or
- the date the Jobseeker Support was granted
whichever is the later.
## Backdating
When a client requests the backdated inclusion of a child and the previous caregiver was getting a benefit for the child, you will need to review when the child was excluded from the previous caregivers benefit.
Generally a child cannot be included in multiple benefits for the same period. In some situations, the previous caregiver may continue to get a benefit in respect of that child for up to 28 days.
Consider all the circumstances and decide whether a debt should be established for the previous caregiver.
If the date you are including the child from is a date in the previous tax year, MSD can only pay arrears of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit from the beginning of the current tax year, that is, 1 April. The client will need to apply for any arrears of tax credits before this date from Inland Revenue.
A review of entitlement needs to be completed to determine the amount of any benefit arrears owed to the client for the backdated period.

chunks.title: Child in care of Oranga Tamariki — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child in care of Oranga Tamariki
Where a child or young person is in the care, custody or sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, the cost of the child's care is the responsibility of Oranga Tamariki and it is responsible for making payments under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989. The child is not considered a dependent child and Unsupported Childs Benefit cannot be paid.
However, where there is a sole guardianship order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but the child or young person is in the custody of the caregiver, the caregiver may be entitled to Unsupported Childs Benefit if all other criteria are met.
Where Oranga Tamariki is involved, but there are no orders or agreements about care, the child can be considered a dependent child (for example when Oranga Tamariki provides services to family groups under a Family Group Conference plan only).
For information on different orders and whether they mean the child can be considered a dependent child while the order is still in place, see:
- Oranga Tamariki order in place

chunks.title: Personal earnings — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Personal earnings
A dependent child's personal earnings are not charged as income against the Jobseeker Support.
However, a child in full-time employment and financially independent cannot be included as a dependent child in the benefit.
For more information see:
- Full-time employment
- Part-time employment

chunks.title: Child leaves care — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child leaves care
When a dependent child leaves the client's care, the child should be excluded from the start of the pay period following the date the child leaves care. The client's benefit rate and the rates of any extra help the client gets should be reassessed to the appropriate rate where applicable.
Note different rules apply when a child stops being a dependent child of a sole parent client because of a sudden change of circumstances beyond the control of the client.
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit should be stopped from the start of the pay period following the date of event to avoid an overpayment with Inland Revenue for the client.

chunks.title: Child under the age of 18 years — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child under the age of 18 years
When a child under the age of 18 years leaves school or tertiary education, they can continue to be included in the parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support until the start of the pay period following their 18th birthday as long as the child remains a dependent child.
## Child aged 18 years
When a child aged 18 years leaves school or tertiary education, they should be excluded from their parent or caregiver's payment from the start of the pay period following the date the child left school or tertiary education. If the client is getting a discretionary benefit such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of hardship, the parent or caregiver must complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for their discretionary benefit, and the rate payable.
## Family tax credit
When a child leaves school or tertiary education, family tax credits should be stopped from the day the child is excluded from the parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
Generally, clients getting Jobseeker Support must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will be excluded from their payments. When a client is getting Jobseeker Support on the ground of hardship, the client must complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for Jobseeker Support and the rate payable or their payments will suspend.
If Jobseeker Support and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a child has left a sole parent's care suddenly, and that child turns 18 during that period, the child will not be excluded, and the client is not required to respond to the notice or complete a review of circumstances.
However, if Jobseeker Support and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a child has left a sole parent's care suddenly, and a different child in their care turns 18, the client must respond to the notice or the 18-year-old will be excluded from their payments or if required, complete a review of circumstances or their payments will suspend.
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit should be stopped from the start of the pay period following the date the child left care (whether planned or suddenly) to avoid an overpayment for the client with Inland Revenue.

chunks.title: Deciding if a child is financially dependent — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Deciding if a child is financially dependent
When a client states that they are receiving payments to pay for a child's expenses you must decide whether the child is a dependent child of the client.
A child does not have to be solely financially dependent on a client to be considered a dependent child. All that is required is that the child is financially dependent on the person to some degree.
However, being financially dependent on a client is only part of the qualifications of a dependent child. The child must still meet all the qualifications to be considered dependent.
If another person or body is paying for the child's expenses, including payments for the care provided, the child is not financially dependent on the client.
If a client is receiving payments toward the expenses of a dependent child this is regarded as income for benefit purposes.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier
Note if a parent or caregiver is getting a discretionary benefit such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of hardship, they must complete a review of circumstances when a dependent child turns 18, and when the child is excluded (if they continued to be included in the benefit after they turned 18). If the parent or caregiver does not complete the review, their Jobseeker Support will be suspended.

chunks.title: Client becomes sick — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client becomes sick
A client who has a health condition, an injury or a disability they will no longer be able to meet their job search requirements. They may be able to continue to receive Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, an injury or a disability.
A partner with work obligations who has a health condition, injury or disability can be exempt from meeting their work obligations until they are well again.
Where a client (or partner's) health condition permanently and severely restricts their ability to work, they may be able to receive Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability.
If the client (or partner) is admitted to hospital it may affect their rate of payment.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Client has a health condition, injury or disability
- Supported Living Payment Medical qualifications
- Exemptions
- Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Client deferred from their work obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client deferred from their work obligations
The following clients may have a deferral from their work obligations:
- clients with a health condition, injury or a disability or
- clients who are 27 weeks pregnant or more, or have complications with their pregnancy
Clients in these circumstances generally cannot be absent from New Zealand and continue getting benefit payments, unless they meet the criteria for approved travel.

chunks.title: Surviving partner or dependent child — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Surviving partner or dependent child
When a client dies (and there is a surviving partner or dependent child) before a decision is made on an application or review for Jobseeker Support, you can continue the application or review process as if the client had not died.
## Funeral Grant
In situations when the decision to grant or review Jobseeker Support is made after the date of death of the client, you decide any Funeral Grant as if the deceased client were getting Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Partner with child under 14 years old — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Partner with child under 14 years old
When a client dies and the surviving partner has a dependent child under 14 years, the partner may be able to receive Sole Parent Support.
## Partner with a child over 14 years old
If the partner has a dependent child 14 years old or over, they may be able to receive Jobseeker Support, with an exemption from their work obligations to allow them time to adjust to their new circumstances.
Note there is no initial stand-down when a partner applies for Sole Parent Support within 28 days of the client's death. When the partner applies 28 days after the death of the client, there will be an initial stand-down.
## Partner with no dependent children
When there are no dependent children, the surviving partner must apply for a main benefit, in their own right. The surviving partner may be granted a new main benefit (instead of terminal benefit) from the day after their partner's death if they will get more money.
## Delay in granting ACC payments
When the death was the result of an accident, the surviving partner may be able to receive weekly compensation payments from ACC. If there will be a delay in deciding their claim, the partner can apply for a benefit while waiting. The client must acknowledge, in writing, that benefit payments made will be refunded once weekly compensation payments are granted from ACC.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Client does not make contact or provide current medical certificate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client does not make contact or provide current medical certificate
If a current medical certificate is not provided prior to the client's expiry date or the client does not make contact to indicate they wish to be available for full-time employment, their Jobseeker Support will expire.
For more information see:
- Client makes contact and confirms they are available for full-time employment

chunks.title: Client donates a kidney or liver tissue — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client donates a kidney or liver tissue
When a client is donating a kidney or liver tissue, they can keep getting Jobseeker Support. Exempt the client from any work obligations during the recovery period.
When adding the medical certificate information in the SINCC screen in SWIFTT the deferral will be automatically added in SWTDA.
The exemption starts from the date of their operation and can continue while the client:
- is recovering from their operation and
- they cannot meet their part-time or full-time work obligations
This exemption must not be more than 12 weeks.
Do not apply any obligation failures:
- for the maximum period of 12 weeks or
- until the client has recovered from the operation
whichever is earlier.
## Client has an obligation failure
If the client currently has an obligation failure, donating a kidney or liver tissue is considered a 'good and sufficient reason'. The work obligations failure must be overturned.
This will remove the failure from the client’s 12 month obligation failure count and there is no sanction.
## Childcare assistance
Clients may be eligible for Childcare Assistance payments while they are they are recovering.
For more information see:
- Childcare Subsidy Temporary illness
- OSCAR Temporary illness
- Client has a health condition, injury or disability
- Deferrals

chunks.title: Client engaged in study — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client engaged in study
A full-time student cannot get Jobseeker Support other than when they are eligible for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship between the end of one academic year of a programme of study and the start of the next year of that programme.
If MSD is unsure whether a student is full-time or not, they can ask the student to provide verification from their education provider.
Jobseeker Support should be stopped from the:
- day the client commences full-time study if they are not going to get Student Allowance or Student Loan living costs or
- Monday of the week the client commences full-time study if they are going to get Student Allowance or Student Loan living costs (these payments are paid for the full week)
For more information see:
- Client intends to study full time
## Part-time study
When a client commences part-time study and the hours that they study are outside normal working hours, it is accepted that the client is available for full-time work.
If the part-time study is 8 hours or more each week, you must be satisfied that reasonable job search activity is taking place.
When considering the time available for job search you should take into consideration the client's study timetable and whether enough blocks or periods of time are available for job search activity.
To help you decide if a part-time student can get Jobseeker Support see:
- Decision guidelines - part-time students

chunks.title: Client exempt from work obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client exempt from work obligations
Where a Jobseeker Support client has been granted an exemption from their work obligations, to continue to receive Jobseeker Support they must still be:
- available for
- actively seeking and
- willing to undertake suitable employment
The effect of this is that Jobseeker Support clients who are exempt from their work obligations cannot continue to receive payment of benefit while absent from New Zealand unless the absence is for:
- Approved travel reasons
- Overseas medical treatment
- Exemptions
For details about when a partner is exempt see:
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption

chunks.title: Client intends to study full-time — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client intends to study full-time
When a client, getting Jobseeker Support advises they intend to study full-time, they can continue to receive Jobseeker Support until they commence their study (provided they still meet all the qualifications for Jobseeker Support).
## Applying for Student Allowance, Independent Circumstances Allowance or Student Loan
If the client is applying for a Student Allowance, Independent Circumstances Allowance or Student Loan you will need to:
- add a future suspension to the benefit for the Monday of the week that the client advises they will start full-time study using the reason code '032 - Full-time student'
For example, the client starts study on Wednesday 15 June - add the future suspension for Monday 13 June. Student Allowance or Student Loan living costs (if nominated) will commence on Monday 13 June as these are always paid for the full week.
and
- encourage the client to go into the StudyLink website and apply on-line for Student Allowance, Independent Circumstances Allowance or Student Loan with living costs at the earliest opportunity
Where there is early approval of Student Allowance, Independent Circumstances Allowance or Student Loan, StudyLink will check the future suspension date on the Jobseeker Support and advise the case manager of any correction needed.
When the Jobseeker Support has been cancelled from an incorrect date, StudyLink will establish overpayments.
## No Student Allowance, Independent Circumstances Allowance or Student Loan
When a client advises they intend to commence full-time study but do not intend to receive or are not eligible for Student Allowance, Independent Circumstances Allowance or Student Loan, you will need to add a future suspension to the Jobseeker Support.
Note the date for the future suspension in this situation is the date the client commences study.

chunks.title: Examples (but are not limited to) — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Examples (but are not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A primary client on Jobseeker Support was out of New Zealand visiting his father in Australia. His Jobseeker Support was suspended the day after he left New Zealand as it wasn't an approved travel reason. The client contacts Work and Income three days later to say that his father is in hospital as he has had a heart attack. The client has been paid for five days in the previous 52 weeks while he was absent from New Zealand leaving a balance of 23 days.
The reason for travel now meets the criteria for approved travel. The benefit is resumed from the date the client became eligible to receive the benefit overseas. The client must contact Work and Income from overseas. The benefit cannot be back-dated if the client advises Work and Income when they return to New Zealand.
A partner receiving Jobseeker Support with work preparation but no activities assigned left New Zealand to visit her mother. Two days before she was due to return, her mother's house burnt down. The client has been paid for 20 days in the previous 52 weeks while she was absent from New Zealand leaving a balance of eight days.
The reason for travel has changed and the client has not been absent from New Zealand for up to 28 days in any 52 week period. The benefit expiry is extended for an additional five days.
This client can travel for any reason. If the client hadn't informed Work and Income, their benefit would continue to be paid up until the 29th day.
Note that where the client has already been absent for 28 days in a 52 week period, consider whether the client meets the criteria for receiving a payment for more than 28 days in any 52 week period.

chunks.title: Client makes contact and confirms they are available for full-time employment — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client makes contact and confirms they are available for full-time employment
When a client contacts the Ministry and indicates they are available for full-time employment, the qualification for Jobseeker Support will change on the date after their medical coverage expires.
The client will then have full-time work obligations from this date.

chunks.title: Examples include (but are not limited to) — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Examples include (but are not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A partner of someone receiving Jobseeker Support with work preparation but no activities assigned left New Zealand for a holiday in Australia. While she was in Australia there was severe flooding which meant she could not return to New Zealand on the day she was meant to return. She contacts Work and Income. The client has been paid for 20 days in the previous 52 weeks while she was absent from New Zealand, leaving a balance of eight days.
The client cannot return due to circumstances that were not reasonably foreseeable and they were outside the client's control. Work and Income would extend the client's benefit for a reasonable period for her to be able to return.
This client can travel for any reason. If the client hadn't informed Work and Income, their benefit would continue to be paid up until the 29th day.
A client on Jobseeker Support has been overseas for five days to attend his father's funeral. He is delayed in Sydney due to fog. He must remain a further three days.
The client cannot return due to circumstances that were not reasonably foreseeable and they were outside the client's control. Work and Income would extend the client's benefit for a reasonable period for him to be able to return. Also consider whether there is any grounds to pay for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Client obtains employment overseas — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client obtains employment overseas
Where the client:
- is successful in their job prospect or job search overseas and
- they are not returning to New Zealand
the Jobseeker Support should be cancelled from the day after the notice of job appointment.
If the client returns to New Zealand for the period between getting the job and actually starting employment, the Jobseeker Support can be continued until they leave the country. The benefit must be cancelled from the day after they leave New Zealand to commence the job.

chunks.title: Client or partner remains in New Zealand — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client or partner remains in New Zealand
Qualification for Jobseeker Support may be affected for a married, civil union or de facto couple when one of them remains in New Zealand. This will depend on whether:
- it is the primary client or their partner who remains in New Zealand and
- payment has been approved to continue if it is the primary client overseas
## Partner remains in New Zealand
If the partner remains in New Zealand, they can continue to receive the half married, civil union or de facto rate of Jobseeker Support as long as payment to the primary client has been approved and is continuing to be paid while they are overseas for up to 28 days.
If payment will not continue to the primary client, or has been stopped, the partner will no longer qualify to receive any payment. You will need to determine if the partner qualifies for another benefit in their own right, or they may be able to receive an Emergency Benefit.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefits
Note the partner can only receive the half married, civil union or de facto rate of Jobseeker Support while the client is overseas, unless the couple are living apart with the intention of ending their marriage or civil union. If the primary client is receiving any income while overseas this must be charged against the benefit.
## Exception
However, there are some situations that allow Jobseeker Support client to be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment for a period of absence.
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Overseas medical treatment

chunks.title: Client with part-time work obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client with part-time work obligations
A client who has been assessed as having part-time work obligations because of the impact of their health condition, injury or disability on their capacity for full-time work generally cannot be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment of their benefit, unless they meet the criteria for approved travel.
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons

chunks.title: Client with work obligations, exemption or deferral — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client with work obligations, exemption or deferral
Clients receiving Jobseeker Support cannot generally be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment of their benefits unless they have an approved reason for travel.
This includes:
- clients exempt from work obligations
- clients deferred from their work obligations
- clients with part-time work obligations
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Clients exempt from work obligations
- Clients deferred from their work obligations
- Clients with part-time work obligations
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption

chunks.title: Clients changing between annual and weekly income charging before 30 June 2026 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients changing between annual and weekly income charging before 30 June 2026
Sole parent and grand-parented Jobseeker Support clients whose benefit commenced (or last commenced) before 1 July 2025 may move between annual and weekly income charging. At the point of change, a part year income assessment (due paid assessment) should be considered.
Note from 30 June 2026 all sole parent and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients will have moved to weekly income charging and if applicable, will have had their final Review of Annual Income.
## Example
Sophie is a sole parent getting Jobseeker Support. Her last dependent child leaves her care on 18 August 2025. From 18 August 2025 Sophie's income is charged weekly. A part year income assessment (due paid assessment) should be considered to determine whether there are benefit arrears due to Sophie.
For more information see:
- Annual income for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
- Period over which to charge income

chunks.title: Clients with a partner — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients with a partner
When a married, civil union or de facto client is imprisoned the Jobseeker Support will generally need to be cancelled to enable the partner to be granted a benefit in their own right.
The Jobseeker Support should be cancelled from the day after imprisonment.
If the primary client is imprisoned, the partner should be invited to apply for an alternative benefit in their own right, for example Sole Parent Support (where they have dependent children under the age of 14 years) or Jobseeker Support (when they have no children or their youngest dependent child is over 14 years of age). Where the partner has children, they can be granted a sole parent rate of benefit while their partner is in prison, even if they are still in a relationship.
If the partner is imprisoned the Jobseeker Support can continue provided the primary client is still able to meet their work obligations. The Jobseeker Support will be paid at the single or sole parent rate.
Where there are dependent children and the primary client is no longer able to meet the eligibility for Jobseeker Support because they are no longer available for and seeking full-time work, they will need to test their eligibility for another benefit, for example Sole Parent Support (where their youngest dependent child is under the age of 14 years).
## Exception
Where a client has a partner and/or dependent children there is discretion to continue payment of the Jobseeker Support for a limited period in some circumstances.
There is discretion to pay all or part of the Jobseeker Support to the partner of the person who has been imprisoned. This will depend on the length of time imprisoned. Where the length of imprisonment is short, using discretion to continue to pay the benefit prevents having to re-grant the benefit.
There is also discretion to continue payment if the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance. For example, this may be considered where the client may end up receiving a sentence of home detention and needing to have the benefit re-granted to the couple anyway.
For more information to help you decide these cases see:
- Work obligations
- Decision guidelines - clients with a partner
- SWIFTT process to pay a partner
- Remanded in custody

chunks.title: Commission work — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Commission work
If a client commences full-time commission work (even if there is no or minimum income being earned) they will no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support.
If the client has a partner who meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support in their own right, the partner can apply for Jobseeker Support as the primary client.
Note there is an exception for some clients, see:
- Temporary employment period for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
- Annual income for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
## Part-time commission work
If a client starts part-time commission work, they may still be able to get Jobseeker Support, as long as they continue to meet their job search requirements. Any offer of suitable employment takes precedence over any part- time activity or commission work that does not meet their work obligations.
For more information see:
- Suitable employment
## Partner
If the person who has commenced commission work (either part-time or full-time) is the partner, then the Jobseeker Support can continue with their earnings being charged as income against the benefit.
This is regardless of whether the partner has work obligations.
Note if the partner has full-time work obligations and is working 30 hours per week, or has part-time work obligations and is working 20 hours or more, then they must be receiving an income from this employment to be meeting their work obligations. If they are not receiving any income from their commission work, they must still be available for and actively seeking suitable employment.
For more information see:
- Charging income
- Employment related income

chunks.title: Determining reasonable contact time — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Determining reasonable contact time
In order to determine whether a client contacted Work and Income as soon as they could reasonably have been expected to, you need to take into account the circumstances of the client.
The reason why the client did not contact Work and Income until after returning to New Zealand may be the same reason why they left New Zealand without advising Work and Income of their absence, or a different humanitarian reason.
Reasons for not contacting Work and Income sooner may include (but are not limited to) that the client:
- did not contact Work and Income due to the stress of the event that led to them leaving New Zealand without informing Work and Income
- left with a humanitarian reason, and then could not access the technology to communicate with Work and Income while absent from New Zealand
- left for a humanitarian reason, and then was temporarily medically unfit while overseas and they have a medical certificate that shows this
- left for a humanitarian reason, and then had a death or illness in the immediate family while overseas or on return to New Zealand and/or
- left for a humanitarian reason, and then experienced an adverse event or natural disaster while overseas or on return to New Zealand that meant they were unable to contact Work and Income
## Contacting Work and Income on return to New Zealand
Generally, it would be reasonable to expect a client to contact Work and Income within 10 working days of returning to New Zealand. However, you should consider whether the client's circumstances meant they were unable to inform Work and Income in this period.
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure
- Client with work obligations, exemption or deferral
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Examples of applying the Absence from New Zealand policy

chunks.title: Couple under 24 years - partner not granted an exemption in non-approved study — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Couple under 24 years - partner not granted an exemption in non-approved study
The following process is for a couple (one or both of whom are under 24 years) with no dependent children, when a partner starts full-time study and can no longer meet their work obligations. If the partner does not meet the criteria for an exemption you may need to initiate an obligations failure.

chunks.title: Court request for information — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Court request for information
The Courts, Ministry of Justice can request the following information when they are considering either making an attachment order or assessing the client's protected earnings rate under section 87AA of the Summary Proceedings Act 1957:
- the amount of any benefit paid to the client
- the amount of any attachment orders or deduction notices issued under the following Acts: Social Security Act 2018Family Proceedings Act 1980Child Support Act 1991Tax Administration Act 1994
- Social Security Act 2018
- Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Child Support Act 1991
- Tax Administration Act 1994
- any Ministry of Social Development debt that is being recovered from the client
- the composition of the client's family, including the number of family members who are dependent on the client, as known by Work and Income
This information is used to determine how much the client can reasonably be expected to pay each week on any outstanding fines.
## Information that can be provided
Work and Income can provide the Ministry of Justice with the last known address and telephone number of a client under schedule 6, clause 13 of the Social Security Act 2018. This only applies when the Ministry of Justice is unable to locate a client who is in default of a court fine.

chunks.title: Backdating — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Backdating
Where a client requests the backdated inclusion of a child and the previous caregiver was in receipt of a benefit for the child, you will need to review when the child was excluded from the previous caregivers benefit.
Note a child cannot be included in two benefits for the same period.
Have regard to all the circumstances and decide whether a debt should be established for the previous caregiver.
If the date you are including the child from is a date in the previous tax year, SWIFTT will only pay arrears of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit from the beginning of the current tax year, that is, 1 April. You will need to advise the client that any arrears of family tax credit prior to this date will need to be claimed from Inland Revenue.
You will need to do a backdated review in the SBDR screen to pay any benefit arrears to the client for the previous tax year. A backdated review may be required for the current year if other rate changes have occurred - check the SRAUI screen for details.
For more information see:
- Processing standards Child changes [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Date payment should be reduced — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Date payment should be reduced
The hospital rate is paid when the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks. Reduce the client's benefit to the hospital rate or appropriate higher rate from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation.
Note the rate of benefit paid to a couple with dependent children is not affected by the client's hospitalisation.
The rate of benefit payable to a sole parent is dependent on their circumstances.
For more information see:
- Sole Parents
## Absence of 28 days or less
Any periods of leave from hospital of 28 days or less are ignored when deciding the date the benefit will be reduced. Calculate the period in hospital from the original admission date. If the client has been allowed out of hospital for more than 28 days, the calculation of the period in hospital begins again after the client has been re-admitted.
## Absence of 28 days or more
If the client has been out of hospital for more than 28 days and is readmitted, the calculation of the period in hospital starts again.
## Client formally discharged
If the client has been formally discharged from hospital and then readmitted to the same or a different hospital, even if the absence is less than 28 days, the 13 week calculation starts again.
However, if the client is formally discharged from 1 hospital with the intention that they immediately transfer to another hospital, the client is treated as not being discharged (transferred). Ensure that SHODA is updated to show the new hospital details.

chunks.title: Couple — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Couple
When a dependent child dies, the child should be excluded from a couple's Jobseeker Support from the start of the pay period following the date of the child's death.
## Sole parents
When a dependent child dies they should be excluded from a sole parent's Jobseeker Support 28 days following the date of the child's death.
Payment of the benefit may continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child died.
This provides a transition for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.
Note during the 28-day continuation of payment, if the client has other changes of circumstances such as a change of income, the rate of any benefit will need to be reassessed using the sole parent threshold rates.
## Child turns 18
Generally, clients getting Jobseeker Support must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will be excluded from their payments. When a client is getting a discretionary benefit such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of hardship, the client must complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for their discretionary benefit and the rate payable, or their payments will suspend.
If Jobseeker Support and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a sole parent's child has died, and the child that died was due to turn 18 during that period, the child will not be excluded, and the client is not required to respond to the notice or complete a review of circumstances.
However, if Jobseeker Support and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a sole parent's child has died and a different child in their care turns 18, the client must respond to the notice or the 18-year-old will be excluded from their payments or if required, complete a review of circumstances or their payments will suspend.
## Family tax credit
Family tax credit payments should be stopped from the start of the pay period following the date the child died, to avoid an overpayment with Inland Revenue for the client.

chunks.title: Death of a client — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
The date benefit payment stops following the death of a client depends on whether the client has:
- a partner or
- a dependent child
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support when the child turns 18 during the terminal benefit period.
The review of circumstances for a discretionary benefit such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of hardship when their child turns 18 is not required when the client has died.

chunks.title: Death of a client with a partner or child — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Jobseeker Support can continue to be paid for 28 days after the death of a client when there is a surviving partner or child, and the surviving partner is not entitled to a survivor's grant from ACC. Jobseeker Support can also continue to be paid for 28 days following the death of a single client who is a: - liable person and paying Child Support payments or - caregiver getting Unsupported Child's Benefit or Orphan's Benefit Continuing payments after the date of death is known as terminal benefit. When terminal benefit is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person and the surviving person's portion of the benefit continues to be paid. The total benefit, including the surviving person's portion, plus any ongoing extra help continues for 28 days.

chunks.title: Surviving partner will get more money on other assistance — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Sometimes the surviving person, or the caregiver of the child would get more money (based on their new circumstances) on: - a new main benefit or - their existing benefit at a higher rate instead of getting their portion of their current assistance for 28 days.

chunks.title: New benefit paid at a higher rate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the surviving person’s benefit is reviewed and they qualify for a new benefit at a higher rate, they may be granted the new benefit instead of terminal benefit from the day after a client's death. If the deceased person qualified for terminal benefit their portion will continue to be paid.

chunks.title: Current benefit paid at a higher rate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the surviving person's current benefit is reviewed and they qualify for a higher rate, their benefit rate increases from the day after their partner's death. MSD pays this instead of their portion of the terminal benefit as they will get more money. If the deceased person qualified for terminal benefit their portion of the benefit will continue to be paid.

chunks.title: Surviving person is entitled to survivor's grant from ACC — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: When the death of a person was the result of an accident, entitlement to a survivor's grant from ACC needs to be decided before terminal benefit can be paid. If the surviving person or child are entitled to a survivor's grant from ACC, there is no entitlement to terminal benefit. If Jobseeker Support payments have continued after the date of death, an overpayment is established and the debt should be recovered from the estate.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support when the child turns 18 during the 28-day continuation of payment. The review of circumstances for a discretionary benefit such as Jobseeker Support on the ground of hardship when their child turns 18 is not required when the client has died.

chunks.title: Death of a single client — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Death of a single client
When a single client (with no children) dies, payment generally stops from the day after the date of death, but there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days.
Payment should stop from the first available date if we have been notified within 28 days of the date of death. This will avoid creating a debt.
Where there are other circumstances that justify payment of terminal benefit, payment should continue for the full 28 days after death.
For more information see:
- Avoiding a debt
- Terminal benefit for a single client
Note a single client who is a liable person and paying Child Support payments, or a principal caregiver receiving Unsupported Childs Benefit or Orphans Benefit is regarded as having children.
For more information see:
- Death of a client with a partner or child
## Cost of funeral
The person responsible for the cost of the funeral may be able to receive a Funeral Grant.
For more information see:
- Funeral Grant
- Verification

chunks.title: Deciding if surviving person would be better off getting terminal benefit or a new benefit — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Deciding if surviving person would be better off getting terminal benefit or a new benefit
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or child.
When the benefit is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person and the surviving person’s portion of the benefit is paid. Payment is the total benefit including any ongoing Extra help. It does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit.
Sometimes the surviving person or the caregiver of the children would get more money (based on their new circumstances) on a new benefit or their existing benefit at a higher rate, instead of their portion of their current assistance for 28 days.
Compare the surviving person’s potential new benefit and any ongoing Extra help (from the date after death) against the surviving person’s portion of benefit and ongoing Extra help they were getting before their partner’s death.
Generally, the surviving person will get more money if they change to a single rate of benefit.
If the deceased person qualified for terminal benefit, their portion will continue to be paid to their bank account.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Decision guidelines - clients with a partner — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines - clients with a partner
While Jobseeker Support should generally be stopped when the primary client is imprisoned, there is discretion for payment to be continued and paid to the partner not in prison. This discretion allows payment of all or part of the Jobseeker Support to the partner.
If you feel that payment should be continued, and paid to the partner, this should generally be at the single or sole parent rate. However, you can pay the full married, civil union or de facto rate if you feel this is warranted after having regard to the particular circumstances of the client and their partner.
To help you decide whether it is reasonable to pay the Jobseeker Support to the partner while the client is in prison, and the rate to pay, consider the following:
- has the period in prison already passed
- is the client due to be released from prison shortly
- is the likely period in prison less than six months
- does the partner qualify for a statutory benefit in their own right
- do they intend to live together when the partner is released
- has the partner in prison applied for Home Detention
- are there exceptional circumstances that warrant paying the full married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit to the partner who is not in prison
For further help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.
For more information see:
- SWIFTT process to pay a partner

chunks.title: Decision guidelines for shared care — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines for shared care
The parent with greater responsibility is usually the parent who has the child for most of the time. If a parent has the child for at least 60% of the time they have the primary responsibility.
Where parents have equal time, to help you decide which parent has greater responsibility, consider the following:
- who pays for the child's material support (furniture, clothes etc)
- who decides about the child's daily activities
- who takes them to and from school and supervises leisure activities
- who makes decisions about their education and health
- who pays for which expenses
If it is not clear who has greater responsibility or the parents share the responsibility equally, the parent who was mainly responsible for the day to day care of the child prior to the separation is the person who can have the child included.
If you can't decide who is entitled to have the child included, the parents must make the decision. Don't include the child in any income support until they have decided.

chunks.title: Decision guidelines - sole parents — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines - sole parents
When a sole parent Jobseeker Support client is imprisoned it is important that financial assistance is available to support any dependent children.
While Jobseeker Support should generally be stopped when the client is imprisoned, there is discretion for payment to be continued and paid to the person who is caring for the dependent children.
To help you decide whether it is reasonable to pay the Jobseeker Support while the client is in prison, you should consider the following:
- has the period in prison already passed
- is the client due to be released from prison shortly
- is the likely period in prison less than twelve months
- will the children return to the client's care on their release from prison
- has the caregiver ceased work to care for the children
- has the caregiver lost entitlement to their own benefit due to having children in their care
For further help you can contact the Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.
For more information see:
- Rate of payment - sole parents
- Examples - sole parents
- Remanded in custody
- Sole parents

chunks.title: Definition of 'support' from a family member residing overseas — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Definition of 'support' from a family member residing overseas
'Support' means assistance that the young person could not reasonably obtain from a family member in New Zealand, and includes (but is not limited to):
- emotional support
- educational support
- mentoring/guidance
- any other assistance that is beneficial to the welfare of the young person
Note in assessing whether the young person could not reasonably obtain the support from a family member in New Zealand, you should consider:
- the type and nature of the relationship with the family member residing overseas
- whether there are features of the young person's relationship with that family member that are absent from their relationships with other family members residing in New Zealand (such as shared experiences and the nature of the relationship)

chunks.title: Dependent child — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
A dependent child for Jobseeker Support is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of the client
- maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
- in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but has been returned to their parent's care
A dependent child for Jobseeker Support Allowance does not include a:
- child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989
- child for whom Orphan's or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid and
- young person getting a Young Parent Payment and their child (see Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples)
## Principal responsibility
The client must be responsible for the day-to-day care of the child and be the person who makes the major decisions concerning the child's life (for example schooling and health care).
There are some situations where the person who has principal responsibility of a child is not clear.
## Maintained as a member of the family
The child should be an integral part of the family, participating in the usual family activities (for example outings and annual holidays).
In some situations, a child may not be living at home but is still considered to be a dependent child.
Dependent children should be included in the assessment of Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Continuing dependent partner's portion of benefit — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Continuing dependent partner's portion of benefit
When the partner of a Jobseeker Support client dies, the partner's portion of the benefit is continued for 28 days at the same rate that was being paid on the date their partner died. Benefit payments that continue after the day a client has died are called 'terminal benefit'.
## Dependent children
When there are dependent children included in the benefit, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments should be transferred to the primary client. Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments are not part of the terminal benefit.
A surviving partner with dependent children, can choose to remain on Jobseeker Support if they can meet their work obligations.
If their youngest child is under 14 years old they may be able to receive Sole Parent Support from the date following the death of their partner. It is important that the different entitlements of Jobseeker Support and Sole Parent Support are explained to the client so they can make the best decision for their circumstances.
## No dependent children
A client would stay on Jobseeker Support if they have no dependent children.
Note clients staying on Jobseeker Support may be given an exemption from their work obligations to allow them time to adjust to their new circumstances.
## Date of review
When the surviving client remains on Jobseeker Support, review the client's benefit from the date following the death of their partner.
You need to:
- increase their benefit to the single or sole parent rate and
- adjust any Extra help to the single or sole parent rate
When the client applies for (and is granted) Sole Parent Support, cancel their Jobseeker Support from the day after their partner's death.
Note when the surviving client decides to receive a new main benefit or their existing benefit at the increased rate, the deceased partner’s portion of the benefit continues for 28 days at the rate being paid at the date of death (if the deceased person qualifies for terminal benefit).
## Funeral costs
