The person responsible for the cost of the funeral may be able to receive a Funeral Grant.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital
When person who has been remanded in custody or is serving a term of imprisonment, is detained in or transferred to a psychiatric hospital you may be able to pay an Emergency Benefit at the hospital rate.
People who are remanded in custody or serving a term of imprisonment who are temporarily hospitalised for treatment of an injury or illness are still considered to be in prison and the Department of Corrections will meet their costs. Therefore an Emergency Benefit or any other financial assistance cannot be paid.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Person serving their sentence of imprisonment in a psychiatric hospital
- Release from prison

chunks.title: Discharged from Oranga Tamariki care — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Discharged from Oranga Tamariki care
Where Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency has care, custody or sole guardianship of the child, and returns the child to the care of the immediate previous caregiver, they do not make payments for the child.
The child is then a dependent child and can be included in Jobseeker Support.
Where the relationship is not one of care, but more of a boarding arrangement, the young person may be able to receive Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment.
Once a child has been discharged from care the child can be considered a dependent child even when Oranga Tamariki or any other authorised agency involvement continues, for example:
- Additional Guardianship Order
- Support Order or
- Services Order
When there is a Service or Support Order in place, you will need to make sure that the Court's intent allows you to consider the child as a dependent child.
For further details on what discharged from care means see:
- Definition of discharged from Oranga Tamariki care

chunks.title: Effect of income on Extra help — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Effect of income on Extra help
When income is added or changed you will also need to review any Extra help the client may be receiving.
Some Extra help is not income tested such as Child Disability Allowance and Winter Energy Payment. It is the client's obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances.
Income is charged against Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support and Childcare Subsidy or OSCAR on a weekly basis.
- Temporary Additional Support Chargeable income
- Childcare Subsidy Income test
- Special Benefit Assessment of income deficiency
- Income change
- Extra Help

chunks.title: Effect on benefit — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Effect on benefit
Any inclusion or exclusion of a dependent child from a client's benefit will result in a general review of the client's Jobseeker Support and any extra help they are getting.
You may need to review the following:
- the rate of Jobseeker Support, you will need to review the rate payable if the child being excluded is the client's last or only dependent child
- Jobseeker SupportPartner's work obligations may change. Where a partner has a change in work obligations as a result of the change in circumstances, this will need to be reviewed.
When a single client has a child come into their care they may no longer be able to meet their work obligations. Depending on the age of the child, they may be able to get Sole Parent Support or an Emergency Benefit Single and caring for a child.
- Accommodation SupplementChanges to the family composition may result in a change to the Accommodation Supplement entry thresholds.
- Non-standard benefit rateWhere a child is added or removed you may need to manually adjust the non-standard rate of payment.
- Special BenefitAny change to family circumstances will result in a review of Special Benefit. A child included or excluded from the Jobseeker Support may result in a change to the allowable costs for Special Benefit.
- Temporary Additional SupportAny change to family circumstances will result in a review of Temporary Additional Support. A child included or excluded from the Jobseeker Support may result in a change to the allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support.
- Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Effect on Extra Help — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Effect on Extra Help
Extra Help can continue to be paid to the client for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital. When the client's benefit is reduced to the hospital rate, any Extra Help they receive will need to be reviewed.
## Accommodation Supplement
For a single client stop the Accommodation Supplement from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation. Check whether the client still has to meet their continuing accommodation costs. If so, increase the benefit rate above the hospital rate to meet the costs.
For a married , civil union or de facto client (without dependent children) you still treat the couple as married, in a civil union or de facto relationship and take into account the income and assets of both. You can pay the full Accommodation Supplement to the partner not in hospital.
For more information see:
- Accommodation Supplement
## Temporary Additional Support
For a single client stop Temporary Additional Support from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation. Check whether the client still has to meet their continuing costs. If so, increase the benefit rate above the hospital rate to meet the costs.
For a married, civil union or de facto couple, Temporary Additional Support must be stopped from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation for the client who is in hospital. From the same date you will need to review Temporary Additional Support and pay the full amount to the partner not in hospital.
No additional costs associated with the hospitalisation should be added to Temporary Additional Support for a married, civil union or de facto client. However you will need to have regard to their individual circumstances taking into consideration that the partner not in hospital is increased to the single rate of payment and can receive Special Disability Allowance to cover any extra costs.
## Family tax credit
As long as the child continues to be a dependent child, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments continue to be paid whilethe client is in hospital. For best start tax credit the payments cannot be paid past the child’s third birthday.

chunks.title: Employment — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Employment
Clients must advise of any change in circumstances that affects their entitlement to Jobseeker Support, such as commencing employment.
When a client, or partner (if any), advises they have commenced employment, MSD must check that they are still entitled to Jobseeker Support and are getting the correct rate of payment.
To review the client's Jobseeker Support, MSD needs to know:
- the date their employment commenced
- the type of employment - meaning casual, part-time or full-time
- the name and address of the employer
- the hours they will be working.
MSD will determine the appropriate review action based on this information.
For more information see:
- Full-time employment
- Part-time employment
- Self-employment
- Seasonal work
- Commission work
- Voluntary Work
- Income stops
- Applying for Jobseeker Support after finishing employment

chunks.title: Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason to travel (within 28 day maximum) — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason to travel (within 28 day maximum)
Where a client or partner is receiving their payments while they are absent from New Zealand for an approved reason their payments will suspend automatically on their agreed return date.
For example, a client has been approved travel to attend a job interview in Sydney. They are approved three days. The benefit will suspend automatically on the day they were meant to return.
Where the client or partner is receiving their payments while they are absent from New Zealand because they have an approved travel reason and their return date changes, they must advise Work and Income from overseas, otherwise their payment will be stopped from the day they originally advised they would return to New Zealand.
## Benefit can be backdated once back in New Zealand in very limited circumstances
A client who is continuing to be paid while they are absent from New Zealand for an approved reason may be able to have their benefit backdated if there is an unforeseen reason they cannot notify Work and Income while they are overseas.
For example, a client boards a plane to return home on schedule and the plane is held up due to fog. There is no way the client could notify Work and Income due to an event outside of their control. When the client contacts Work and Income once they are back in New Zealand, their benefit would be resumed from the original date they were due to return (this will be on the itinerary or e-ticket).
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Client not returned due to an unforeseeable event
- Absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Partner may need to be absent for more than 28 days — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Partner may need to be absent for more than 28 days
A partner may be required to be absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days.
For more information see:
- Paying for more than 28 days - delayed return
- Ending payments for client who needs an approved reason to travel
- Absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Essential travel — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Essential travel
A client not otherwise entitled to be paid their Jobseeker Support while they are absent from New Zealand may have their payments continue for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if they have to travel outside of New Zealand to attend a significant event relating to a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family).
These events are ones which the client or partner would reasonably be expected to attend. That is, the travel is essential to them and where not attending the event would cause the person emotional distress. This may include, but is not limited to, travel that allows the client to:
- be with a seriously ill or dying person who is a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family)
- attend a funeral or an unveiling in relation to a family member
- pay respect to a family member of the deceased in the event of the client missing the funeral
- attend to legal matters in relation to the affairs of the deceased family member
- attend a birth of a family member or be with a family member around the time of their giving birth
- provide support to a party or witness to a court case
- attend a wedding of a family member - the client does not need to be a member of the bridal party or play a significant part in the wedding in order for the payment of benefit to continue while they are absent from New Zealand
- travel for a court ordered custody arrangement
For more information see:
- Definition of family member
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Job interviews or follow up on a job prospect
- Permitted travel reasons
- Absences that do not prevent partner from meeting their obligations
- Paying benefit when client failed to advise of absence
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes (within a 28 day maximum)

chunks.title: Estimated income — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Estimated income
Clients must advise MSD of any change in their circumstances that affects their entitlement or rate of Jobseeker Support, such as commencing employment.
If a client has one-off, fluctuating or casual income, it may be necessary to estimate their earnings to prevent a debt. When the client under or over estimates their income they should confirm the actual amount earned as soon as possible.
If the actual income is different to the estimated amount, it must be charged against Jobseeker Support for the week it was earned or the period that it represents.
This may result in arrears or a debt for the client.
For more information about income see:
- Income change
- Calculating the benefit rate
For information about debt recovery, see:
- Debt treatment procedures [no link find out why] Doogle

chunks.title: Examples for paying more than 28 days for an approved reason — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: The following examples show situations where a benefit may be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period (but are not limited to): Client's reason for travelling for 28 days within 52 week period Client's current reason for travel within 52 week period Outcome Essential travel reasons Essential travel reason eg a seriously ill family member Generally consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if reasonable in the circumstances Job interview or job prospect Essential travel reason eg a funeral Generally would consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if reasonable in the circumstances Partners of Jobseeker Support with work obligations, or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. The client wishes to be absent from New Zealand for another general holiday This is not an approved reason for paying for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. The client would not be able to receive a benefit while absent from New Zealand for this reason even if the travel will not prevent them meeting their obligations (eg even if they had further annual leave from their employment or for partners even if the travel is at a time when they are not required to be in education, training or work-based learning) Partners of Jobseeker Support with work obligations or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. To provide aid or assistance to a family member immediately following a natural disaster or similar adverse event. Generally would allow further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. This is an unforeseen event and it is reasonable for them to help their family member. Partners of Jobseeker Support with work obligations or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. Essential travel reason Generally would consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if the essential travel reason was unforeseen. Partners of Jobseeker Support with work obligations or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. Needs to attend a wedding of a family member. Generally would not consider allowing a further period of payment for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.

chunks.title: Examples for paying more than 28 days for an approved reason — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Weddings are usually known about in advance and this should have been planned for when they used the 28 days to go on holiday. However, where the wedding is genuinely unforeseen, consideration could be given to allowing travel for a period of more than 28 days in a 52 week period. Partners of Jobseeker Support with work obligations or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations had to spend four days at a funeral overseas. The partner had booked a holiday prior to the attendance at the funeral overseas. This holiday was booked for 28 days because they are able to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with their obligations. The client does not have the full 28 days left Travelling for a general holiday is not an approved reason for paying a benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period The benefit will only be paid for the number of days the client has available (that is, 24 days).

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Carlos contacts MSD on 19 November to advise that he has returned from travelling to Malaysia to be with his dying mother. He left in a hurry and didn't contact MSD before his departure. His Jobseeker Support stopped on 4 November, the day after he left the country. He returned to New Zealand on 14 November, but then had to organise a New Zealand-based funeral for his mother, as a large number of people are based in New Zealand. Carlos didn't advise MSD of his travel before leaving New Zealand, but he has a humanitarian reason that justifies his travel and the reason he didn't contact MSD before he left. Given Carlos' circumstances, he contacted MSD as soon as it would have been reasonable to expect him to and he meets the criteria for an approved travel reason. Carlos' Jobseeker Support can be backdated to 4 November.

chunks.title: Example 2 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Sanjay left New Zealand for India on 7 December because his father had become suddenly seriously ill and been hospitalised. While in India, Sanjay's father passed away and Sanjay stayed in India for the funeral. Sanjay returned on 16 December, after staying for 2 weeks for the Hindu funeral and mourning period. On 19 December, Sanjay contacts MSD to explain that he has been overseas after learning of his father's illness, and that he stayed for the funeral. On return, Sanjay spent time mourning with his own family and has been distraught. He explains that he only realised last night that he had not informed MSD of his absence. Sanjay's reason for leaving New Zealand is a humanitarian reason and he meets the criteria for backdating his payment to the day after departure. Given Sanjay's circumstances, he informed MSD as soon as he reasonably could. Sanjay's Jobseeker Support can be backdated to 8 December, the date it was suspended.

chunks.title: Example 3 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Tusila calls MSD on 5 October to tell them she will leave New Zealand on 7 October to help her sister, who just lost her house in a flood. When asked how long she will be gone for, Tusila says that she hasn't bought a return ticket yet and was considering staying on to catch up with family and see how her sister is going. MSD informs Tusila that she can only keep getting her Jobseeker Support if she is absent for essential travel. Helping her sister after a flood is considered essential travel, however if she is going to stay longer for a holiday, she won't be able to get Jobseeker Support during the time she is on holiday. Tusila returns to MSD the next day with an airline quote showing that the cheapest return flight is on 14 October. She thinks it will take her a week to ensure her sister has sorted out insurance, medium-term accommodation, and access to basic goods like clothing and food. She has decided not to stay on for the holiday. MSD agrees this is reasonable and tells Tusila she can keep getting Jobseeker Support from 7 to 14 October, while she is overseas helping her sister.

chunks.title: Example 4 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Christy is getting Jobseeker Support and contacts MSD to advise that her sister is getting married in Australia on 8 September. Christy is going to Australia to her sister's wedding but intends to stay on for a further 2 weeks to visit other family. Christy is leaving New Zealand on 4 September as she has to help her sister prepare. She will stay until 10 September to help clean up. Christy then begins the holiday leg of her trip, returning to New Zealand on 25 September. Christy's travel is divided as follows: - 5 September to 10 September period meets the essential travel criteria - 11 September to 24 September period is considered other travel (holiday) and does not meet the essential travel criteria Christy's Jobseeker Support can only be paid until 10 September, for the period that meets the essential travel criteria.

chunks.title: Example 5 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Graeme left New Zealand on 16 August to help his sister in Australia after she lost her house in a fire. He returns to New Zealand on 23 August. A week later, on 30 August he attends an appointment and asks why he hasn't been getting his Jobseeker Support. His case manager informs him that his payments stopped when he left the country and asks why he didn't contact MSD sooner. Graeme explains that he left to help his sister after a house fire, and he meant to contact MSD once he had helped his sister sort out accommodation and insurance , but he forgot. The case manager explains that because he didn't contact MSD as soon as he reasonably could have been expected to (i.e. once he had helped his sister), his Jobseeker Support can only be backdated to 23 August, the date he returned to New Zealand.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Example 1
A client applies for benefit to be paid for 10 days when they are going to be absent from New Zealand. In the past 52 weeks the client has had 10 days absence from New Zealand and continued being paid their benefit
Step
Calculation
Identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand.
14 September 2019
Count back 52 weeks from this date.
15 September 2018
Count the number of days the client continued getting their benefit while they were overseas in this 52 week period
Days client continued getting their benefit while absent from New Zealand between 14 September 2018 and 15 September 2019 = 10 days
Subtract the number of days the client was paid their benefit while absent from New Zealand from 28 days.
28 - 10 days = 18 days available
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay the client for the days they have available.
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay them for the 10 days they are out of the country.
## Example 2
A client applies for benefit to be paid for 10 days when they are going to be absent from New Zealand. In the past 52 weeks the client had 20 days absence from New Zealand and continued being paid their benefit
Step
Calculation
Identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand.
14 September 2019
Count back 52 weeks from this date.
15 September 2018
Count the number of days the client continued getting their benefit while they were overseas in this 52 week period.
Days client continued getting their benefit while absent from New Zealand between 14 September 2018 and 15 September 2019 = 20 days
Subtract the number of days the client was paid their benefit while absent from New Zealand from 28 days.
28 - 20 days = 8 days available
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay the client for the days they have available
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay them for the 8 days they are out of the country. For 2 of the days they are absent from New Zealand they will not get their payments.
Check if the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period - if they meet these criteria, they may be able to continue getting their payment for the additional 2 days of absence.

chunks.title: Examples of income assessment — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: A married client (with no children) is getting Jobseeker Support, and their partner works for 2 weeks earning $390.53 gross in the first week and $795.00 gross in the second week. To work out the income deduction: Week 1 Week 2 Gross income (excluding cents) $390.00 $795.00 Less income allowed before benefit is affected $160.00 $160.00 Equals income $230.00 $635.00 Amount benefit reduced on account of income (Income over $160.00 reduces benefit by 70 cents per $1.00) ($230 x 0.7) $161.00 ($635 x 0.7) $444.50 To work out the benefit rate payable: Week 1 Week 2 Maximum benefit (net as at 1 April 2026) $633.94 $633.94 Less reduction due to income $161.00 $444.50 Benefit rate payable $472.94 $189.44

chunks.title: Example 2 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: A client is getting Jobseeker Support (with no children) at the half married, civil union or de facto rate as their partner has a voluntary unemployment stand-down imposed. The client also works and is earning $220.00 gross a week on a regular basis. To work out the income deduction: Gross income (excluding cents) $220.00 Less income allowed before benefit is affected $160.00 Equals income $60.00 Amount benefit reduced on account of income (Income over $160.00 reduces benefit by 35 cents per $1.00) ($60 x 0.35) $21.00 To work out the benefit rate payable: Maximum net benefit (as at 1 April 2026) $316.97 Less reduction due to income $21.00 Benefit rate payable $295.97

chunks.title: Example 3 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: A sole parent getting Jobseeker Support is working and earning $300.00 gross per week. To work out the income deduction: Gross income (excluding cents) $300.00 Less income allowed before benefit is affected $160.00 Equals income $140.00 Amount benefit reduced on account of income Income over $160.00 reduces benefit by 30 cents per $1.00 ($90.00 x 0.30) = $27.00 Income over $250.00 reduces benefit by 70 cents per $1.00 over $250.00 ($50.00 x 0.70) = $35.00 $62.00 To work out the benefit payable: Maximum net benefit (as at 1 April 2026) $521.52 Less reduction due to income $62.00 Benefit rate payable $459.52 Note sole parent and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients whose benefit commenced (or last commenced) before 1 July 2025 may be able to have their income charged annually. For more information see: - Annual income for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026

chunks.title: Examples of job interviews and prospects overseas — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Some examples of job interviews and prospects overseas are: Client situationOutcomeClient on Jobseeker Support has a job interview for a maintenance position with a mining company in Kalgoorlie, Western Australia. He has a definite job interview for an advertised position and has an email confirming this.This client can continue to be paid his Jobseeker Support for the five days he is absent from New Zealand to attend the job interview.An employer in Sydney has asked a client to come over and meet him to discuss a job prospect in his factory. It is not a formal interview, but a discussion about what the role would involve. If the client meets the employer and they agree, there may be a job offer.The client can continue to be paid their Jobseeker Support for three days while he is absent from New Zealand.A client has made appointments with specific recruitment companies in Melbourne, Australia.There are interview times booked with specific consultants.This client can continue to be paid their Jobseeker Support for the three days while they are absent from New Zealand.A client advises they are heading to the Gold Coast to 'look for work' and undertake job search. They do not have a job interview or a specific job prospect. Their aim is to undertake general job search and go and see a few employers which they will find when they get there.This provision cannot be used to allow general job search overseas and the client will not be able to continue to receive payment if they are absent from New Zealand for this reason. Client situation Outcome Client on Jobseeker Support has a job interview for a maintenance position with a mining company in Kalgoorlie, Western Australia. He has a definite job interview for an advertised position and has an email confirming this. This client can continue to be paid his Jobseeker Support for the five days he is absent from New Zealand to attend the job interview. If the client meets the employer and they agree, there may be a job offer. The client can continue to be paid their Jobseeker Support for three days while he is absent from New Zealand. A client has made appointments with specific recruitment companies in Melbourne, Australia. There are interview times booked with specific consultants.

chunks.title: Examples of job interviews and prospects overseas — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: This client can continue to be paid their Jobseeker Support for the three days while they are absent from New Zealand. A client advises they are heading to the Gold Coast to 'look for work' and undertake job search. They do not have a job interview or a specific job prospect. Their aim is to undertake general job search and go and see a few employers which they will find when they get there. This provision cannot be used to allow general job search overseas and the client will not be able to continue to receive payment if they are absent from New Zealand for this reason.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: A client has two casual part time jobs both are paid on a weekly basis. - Job 1 $150.00 gross paid weekly earned for the period Wednesday 05/04/2017 to Friday 07/04/2017 - Job 2 $210.00 gross paid weekly earned for the period Sunday 09/04/2017 to Tuesday 12/04/2017 The client phones the contact centre and declares all of this income. Although the income declared is received from two different part-time jobs the amounts are added together for the week the income is earned and charged against the benefit as follows: Period income earned Monday 27/03/2017 to Sunday 02/04/2017 Job 1 27/03/2017 to 29/03/2017 = (3 days) Job 2 01/04/2017 to 03/04/2017 = (1 day) $150.00 gross $70.00 gross Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support for week 27/03/2017 to 02/04/2017 $220.00 gross Period income earned Monday 03/04/2017 to Sunday 09/04/2017 Job 2 05/04/2017 to 07/04/2017 = (2 days) $140.00 Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support for week 03/04/2017 to 09/04/2017 $140.00

chunks.title: Example 2 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: A client's partner has two casual part time jobs. - Part-time Job 1 $150 gross for the period worked Tuesday 04/04/2017 to Friday 07/04/2017 paid on the following Thursday 13/04/2017. - Part-time Job 2 $375 gross for the period worked Wednesday 05/04/2017 to Tuesday 18/04/2017 paid fortnightly on Tuesday 18/04/2017. Client earns $15.00 per hour and works 5 hours per day. The client's partner phones the contact centre on Tuesday 18/04/2017 and declares all of this income. Although the income declared is received from two different part-time jobs the amounts are added together for the week the income is earned and charged against the benefit as follows: Period income earned Monday 27/03/2017 to Sunday 09/04/2017 Job 1 = 04/04/2017 to 06/04/2017 = 2 days Job 2 = 05/04/2017 to 08/04/2017 = 3 days $150 gross $225 gross Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support for week 27/03/2017 to 09/04/2017 $375 gross Period income earned Monday 10/04/2017 to Sunday 16/04/2017 Job 2 = 10/04/2017 to 16/04/2017 = (5 days) $375.00 Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support for week 10/04/2017 to 16/04/2017 $375.00 Period income earned Monday 17/04/2017 to Sunday 23/04/2017 Job 2 = 13/04/2017 to 14/04/2017 = (2 days) $150.00 Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support for week 13/04/2017 to 19/04/2017 $150.00 For more information see: - Period over which to charge income

chunks.title: Young partner of a main beneficiary generally won't meet requirements of obtaining support — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Young partner of a main beneficiary generally won't meet requirements of obtaining support
A partner of a main beneficiary who has youth activity obligations would generally not meet the requirements to be paid a benefit in this circumstance because usually they would be receiving the support of their spouse or partner. If they are receiving the support of their spouse or partner it could not be justified for them to travel overseas to receive the support of a different family member.
## Young partner of main beneficiary may meet the requirements in some circumstances
However, they may be able to be paid their payment for more than 28 days for the purposes of obtaining support from a family member if:
- the support they require can't be given by their partner because the main beneficiary themselves is absent from New Zealand or
- it is support the young partner cannot receive from their partner (for example, it is support from a parent or grandparent or the partner and the young person are having relationship difficulties)

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Example 1
The temporary caregiver is paid Jobseeker Support - sole parent at the equivalent Unsupported Childs Benefit rate while caring for 1 child aged 14 years, during the sole parent client's imprisonment.
Unsupported Child's Benefit (as at 1 April 2026)
$350.58
Less family tax credit (as at 1 April 2026)
$151.91
Equals amount to add as a non-standard rate
$195.71
## Example 2
The temporary caregiver is paid Jobseeker Support - Sole parent at the equivalent Unsupported Childs Benefit rate while caring for 2 children aged 14 and 10 years during the sole parent client's imprisonment.
Unsupported Childs Benefit (as at 1 April 2026):
- $350.58 for 14-year old and
- $327.16 for 10-year old
$677.74
Less family tax credit (as at 1 April 2026):
- $151.91 for first child and
- $123.78 for second child
$275.67
Equals amount to add as a non-standard rate
$402.07
## Example 3
The temporary caregiver is to be paid Jobseeker Support - sole parent while caring for 2 children aged 14 and 10 years during the sole parent client's imprisonment. It has been agreed to include the rent of the client's home of $180.00.
Unsupported Childs Benefit (as at 1 April 2026):
- $350.58 for 14-year old and
- $327.16 for 10-year old
$677.74
Plus rent on client's home
$180.00
Sub total
$857.74
Less family tax credit (as at 1 April 2026):
- $151.91 for first child and
- $123.78 for second child
$275.67
Equals calculated amount required to assist the temporary caregiver to care for the client's children (rent included)
$582.07
Maximum Jobseeker Support - sole parent rate (net as at 1 April 2026)
$521.52
In this case the amount payable is the maximum Jobseeker Support - sole parent rate of $521.52. You don't need to add a non-standard rate.

chunks.title: Extending medical coverage when there is no medical certificate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Clients are notified before their medical coverage expires, that they need to produce a current medical certificate if they want to continue getting Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability. There may be instances where clients are having difficulty in providing a current medical certificate before their medical coverage expiry date. To avoid hardship, you may consider applying a discretionary period of up to 4 weeks that extends a client's medical coverage past the expiry date, while waiting for them to provide a current medical certificate. You must be sure that the client: - continues to meet the qualifications for Jobseeker Support and - has a good and sufficient reason for the delay in providing a new medical certificate Note a medical expiry extension is only available to primary clients getting Jobseeker Support because of a health condition, injury or disability. It cannot be applied for those that have an exemption due to a health condition, injury or disability. When deciding whether it is appropriate to extend medical coverage past the expiry date, you need to discuss with the client their circumstances and why they are unable to provide a current medical certificate. Examples of good and sufficient reasons are (but not limited to): - unplanned emergency surgery - hospitalisation - an emergency or adverse event - a death or illness in the immediate family - client tested positive for COVID-19 or is a close contact and is required to self-isolate at home or in a managed isolation facility - lack of health practitioner appointments in some circumstances eg unusually longer waiting periods for an appointmentunavailability of health practitionerssudden rescheduling of a scheduled appointment. - unusually longer waiting periods for an appointment - unavailability of health practitioners - sudden rescheduling of a scheduled appointment. Each client’s situation must be assessed on a case-by-case basis. See example below: Example A client gets a reminder letter from the Ministry advising their medical certificate is due to expire in 2 weeks. Client arranges to see a doctor, but the first available appointment is in 5 weeks. Client manages to get an earlier doctor’s appointment in 3 weeks once they explained about their benefit situation. The client tells the Ministry about their situation and asks what can be done to prevent their benefit from stopping. In this situation, the Ministry may consider the client has made reasonable efforts to access the earliest doctor's appointment and made contact with us to confirm their situation.

chunks.title: Extending medical coverage when there is no medical certificate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Therefore, discretion can be used to apply an extension allowing time to attend their appointment and to provide a current medical certificate.

chunks.title: Duration of extension — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: When applying discretion to extend the medical expiry period, you should consider a reasonable and realistic extension timeframe. For example, if a client tells the Ministry that they are booked in to see their doctor in 10 days' time, you may consider applying a discretionary expiry extension of up to 2 weeks. This allows for sudden or unpredictable events that may prevent the client from providing the Ministry with their current medical certificate on the same day as the appointment.

chunks.title: Number of extensions — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: There is no limitation as to how many times a client can get a medical expiry extension. A client may ask for an extension each time they are asked to provide a current medical certificate. Clients who repeatedly need an extension will need to have their entitlement reviewed to assess if they are getting their full and correct entitlement or whether there are other barriers that are preventing them from providing a subsequent medical certificate within the required timeframe.

chunks.title: Additional extension - up to 4 weeks after medical expiry date — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: There may be situations when a client was initially granted an extension of less than 4 weeks but needs more time to provide a current medical certificate (up to 4 weeks after medical expiry date) due to unforeseen circumstances. Example A client was given a discretionary extension of 1 week due to a lack of available appointments to see a doctor. At the appointment, the client was told that the doctor's clinic booked the wrong date and the client could not be seen urgently due to staff shortages. Another appointment had to be arranged for a later date in 2 weeks. The client contacted the Ministry again to see what can be done to ensure their benefit does not stop. Due to circumstances beyond the client's control, benefit entitlement can be extended by another 2 weeks allowing time to attend the appointment and provide a current medical certificate. There may be situations where a client is still unable to produce a current medical certificate within the period that their medical coverage has been extended ie up to 4 weeks. For more information see:

chunks.title: When extending entitlement is not appropriate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: When a decision is made not to apply a discretionary medical expiry extension, you must make sure you have: - considered the client's individual situation - considered all factors to determine there is no good and sufficient reason for not providing a current medical certificate in time and - fully explained to the client the reasons for the Ministry's decision to not extend payments of Jobseeker Support

chunks.title: Date of review — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Date of review
Where a child becomes financially independent it should be excluded from the benefit payment from the start of the next pay period in which the child became financially independent.
There is discretion to continue payment for one payday following the event.
This discretion only applies when the exclusion of the child affects the rate of payment of Jobseeker Support and is generally used when processing deadlines have passed.
## Not financially independent
Generally, receiving a Student Loan (including the living cost component) does not mean a child is financially independent.

chunks.title: Date of review — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Date of review
Exclude the child from the Jobseeker Support from the beginning of the next pay period in which the child started work.

chunks.title: Client — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the client has commenced full-time employment, they will no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support. Jobseeker Support should be stopped from the date the client commences full-time employment. If a client commences full-time employment they may qualify for Extra Help as a non-beneficiary such as: - Accommodation Supplement - Disability Allowance - Assistance to transition into employment - Transition to Work [no link find out why] - Working for Families Tax Credits from Inland Revenue - Childcare Assistance Programme Exception for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026 Sole parent and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients whose benefit commenced (or last commenced) before 1 July 2025 can have their income charged annually, until they reach their final 52 week expiry date. Sole parent and grandparented clients who have their income charged annually may be able to undertake full-time employment for a temporary period of up to 26 weeks if their income, when assessed over 52 weeks, does not reduce their benefit to zero. This is a transitional arrangement. These clients move to weekly income charging when they complete their reapplication before their final 52 week expiry date and moved to the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle, once their Jobseeker Support has been regranted. If a client is working full-time at the time of their reapplication, Jobseeker Support cannot be regranted as they no longer qualify For more information see: - Annual income for sole parents and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026 - Temporary employment period for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026 Note if the client has outstanding debt when their benefit is cancelled, MSD is responsible for arranging repayments with the client. If a client is cancelling their benefit to commence full-time employment, their debt recovery can be suspended for a 3 month period provided the client remains in employment. MSD can still accept repayments if the client wishes to start paying the outstanding debt straight away. For more information see: - Arranging repayments at cancellation To determine whether the benefit should be suspended or cancelled when a client commences full-time employment, see: - Guidelines for suspension or cancellation

chunks.title: Partner — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the person who has commenced full-time employment is the partner, then the Jobseeker Support can continue with the partner's earnings being charged as income against the benefit. This is regardless of whether the partner is subject to work obligations. Note if the partner has full-time work obligations and is working 30 hours per week, or has part-time work obligations and is working 20 hours or more, then they will be meeting their work obligations.

chunks.title: Guidelines for paying a higher rate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Guidelines for paying a higher rate
Payment can be increased above the hospital rate to a rate that (together with the client's other income) will be sufficient to meet the client's continuing commitments.
Use the following guidelines to assess whether the client's rate should be higher.
1. Have the client complete an Increased payment while you are in hospital form.
2. Accept stated expenses where they appear reasonable, but ask for proof if there is doubt.
3. If the client is a sole parent and has childcare costs:
- include the child care costs when assessing whether a higher rate should be paid
- include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments as income (as these payments will continue)
4. If a client is married, in a civil union or de facto relationship, do not include home outgoings or accommodation expenses. These are the responsibility of the partner not in hospital. (The partner may qualify for Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support.)
5. Check that all possible action has been taken to reduce expenses. For example, giving up the lease on a flat where the hospital stay is indefinite.
6. If the increase in payment request is for one-off items such as clothing, you can pay the increase by:
- a backdated review of the benefit rate to create a lump sum payment or
- increasing the benefit rate for a limited time

chunks.title: Guidelines for suspension or cancellation — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a client has commenced full-time employment they cannot get Jobseeker Support. Generally, their benefit must be suspended or cancelled from the date they commenced employment. If their full-time employment is for a limited period, there are different ways to treat the benefit depending on: - the proposed length of employment - the client's circumstances - whether they qualify for Extra help such as Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance, Family Tax Credit, Best Start tax credit or in-work tax credit In determining whether the Jobseeker Support should be suspended or cancelled, MSD will consider: - if the employment is likely to last for less than 8 weeks - if the client qualifies for Extra help during the period of employment - whether the client gets Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit - if the client qualifies for Working for Families Tax Credits from Inland Revenue. Note when the client's employment is likely to last for less than 8 weeks, the Jobseeker Support should generally be suspended and not cancelled, so the client can have their benefit resumed once their employment ends.

chunks.title: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit can be paid for a maximum of 8 weeks after a benefit is suspended or cancelled when a client commences full-time employment. Payment of tax credits will continue at the same rate that was paid while the client was getting a benefit. For more information see: - Family tax credit [no link find out why] - Best Start tax credit

chunks.title: Extra help — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a client commences full-time employment they may qualify for Extra Help as a non-beneficiary. The client does not need to complete an application form if they were already getting the Extra Help with their main benefit. If they continue to qualify, the rate payable should be reviewed. If the client qualifies for Extra help they are not already getting with their main benefit, a new application is generally required.

chunks.title: Clients on the social housing register and social housing tenants — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: All clients on the social housing register, or renting social housing, must continue to declare any change in their circumstances, including their income, when their main benefit has been cancelled, that may affect the following: - whether they still qualify for social housing while on the register - the need to be allocated, assigned or let any particular social housing property - whether they still qualify for social housing when they are a current tenant - the need for particular property requirements in the place they are renting - their calculated rate of Income Related Rent MSD will record any changes in circumstances when cancelling the benefit, including the client's new income details. If the client does not yet know their new income details, MSD will ask them to provide the information as soon as possible. For more information see: - Social housing - duty to advise changes in circumstances - Change in circumstances for current tenants - Register management and referrals - change in circumstances

chunks.title: Home Detention — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Home Detention
A client may be in prison for a short time before being released on home detention.
- Home detainees can apply for an exemption from their Work obligations
## Period in prison less than 31 days
If the period in prison is less than 31 days the client can be transferred to Emergency Benefit from the date of release if they apply for a benefit immediately after their release.
## Period in prison 31 days or more
If the period in prison is 31 days or more, an initial stand-down will be imposed.
## Partner
When the partner of a person in prison has been receiving a benefit, this will be reviewed from the date of release.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Court imposed conditions
- Transfer between benefits
- Release from prison

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a Jobseeker Support client (or their partner) is admitted to hospital, their benefit can continue at the full rate for the first 13 weeks. The rate of payment will need to be reduced to the hospital rate after the client (or their partner) has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks (not after getting a benefit for 13 weeks).
## Exception
Married, civil union or de facto couples with dependent children do not have their benefit payment reduced regardless of how long they are in hospital.
Note if a client (or partner) is getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for a child in their care, this child is regarded as a dependent child.
## Hospital rate
The hospital rate allows for the cost of personal items, which patients are expected to provide for themselves. The net weekly hospital rate is $58.34 (as at 1 April 2026).
You can pay an amount above the hospital rate where there are financial circumstances to warrant paying at a higher rate.
Note you cannot pay an amount less than the hospital rate.

chunks.title: Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure
Where a client does not advise of their departure from New Zealand before they go, they may be able to have their benefit paid from the day after their departure date if the client has a humanitarian reason that justifies their reason for travel and their failure to tell Work and Income before they left.
Humanitarian reasons are:
- to provide aid or assistance to a family member (or a person to whom they have a relationship similar to a family member) immediately following a natural disaster (for example, flood, earthquake, bush fires) or similar adverse event (eg house fire)
- to be with a suddenly seriously ill, or dying family member (or a person to whom they have a relationship similar to a family member)
- to attend the sudden funeral of a family member (or a person to whom they have a relationship similar to a family member)
For more information see:
- Client not returned due to an unforeseeable event (within 28 day maximum)
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes (within 28 day maximum)
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Backdating benefit to the day after departure date

chunks.title: Imprisonment — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
Generally, when a Jobseeker Support client is imprisoned or detained in custody, they are no longer entitled to get Jobseeker Support.
Jobseeker Support should stop from the day following the date of imprisonment.
MSD must decide whether to suspend or cancel the benefit after considering the likely period in prison and whether the client has a partner and/or dependent children.
In some circumstances Jobseeker Support can continue when the client is imprisoned.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Example 1
A client getting Jobseeker Support has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks.
This client has other income which reduces the main benefit rate to $20.00 per week.
In this case we pay the rate $20.00 per week which is lower than the hospital rate of $58.34 (as at 1 April 2026).
## Example 2
A client getting Jobseeker Support has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks.
This client has other income which reduces the main benefit rate to $70.00 per week.
In this case we pay the hospital rate of $58.34 per week (as at 1 April 2026) which is the lower rate.

chunks.title: Income change — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Income change
Clients must advise MSD of any change in circumstances that affects their entitlement or rate of benefit payable, such as when they receive or earn income.
Any income a Jobseeker Support client or their partner (if any) receives must be charged against the benefit for the period in which the income was earned or represents.
If income does not represent a specific period or if MSD cannot determine the actual period it represents, MSD must determine the most appropriate period to charge the income. This may be the week it is received, provided or supplied.
When a client or their partner (if any) declares a change in income, MSD must check that they still qualify for Jobseeker Support. and reassess any Extra help they get.
## Sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
Sole parent and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients whose benefit commenced (or last commenced) before 1 July 2025 can have their income charged annually, until they reach their next 52 week expiry date. This is a transitional arrangement.
When a sole parent or grandparented client with annual income charging declares a change in income, their income should be updated from the first available date.
These clients move to weekly income charging and the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle when they complete their final 52 week reapplication, and their Jobseeker Support is regranted.
Note by 30 June 2026 all sole parent and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients will have moved to weekly income charging. This means that when they declare a change in their income, it will be charged for the period it represents.
## Deductions or redirections
When adding income to a client's record MSD should check that there is enough benefit to cover any deductions or redirections. Any deductions or redirections may need to be reduced depending on the amount of benefit payable.
For more information see:
- Redirection of benefit payment

chunks.title: Income for a past period — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Income for a past period
If a client declares income for a past period and there is either no income or there is a different amount previously declared for that period, the client's Jobseeker Support must be reviewed for that period.
Income must be charged against the Jobseeker Support for the week in which it is earned or the period it represents. Any Extra Help the client gets must also be reviewed.
## Information share Child Support payments
Information share Child Support payments are treated differently as they are automatically charged forward as income for a period of 4 or 5 weeks.
For more information see:
- Information share Child Support payments
- Automated income charging rules
## Sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
Generally, any income a client receives should be charged against the benefit for the period in which the income was earned or represents.
However, sole parent and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients whose benefit commenced (or last commenced) before 1 July 2025 can have their income charged annually until their next 52 week expiry date. This is a transitional arrangement.
For clients with annual income charging, MSD will estimate the prospective income the client is likely to receive over the next 52 weeks and update income from the first available date. If the client declares a change in income for a past or current period their prospective income should be reviewed.
For more information see:
- Annual income for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
- Review of Annual Income - sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026

chunks.title: Income from employment — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Income from employment
Clients must advise MSD of any change in their circumstances that affects their entitlement or rate of Jobseeker Support, such as commencing employment.
## Full-time employment
If a client has commenced full-time employment, the Jobseeker Support must be stopped from the date they commenced employment.
If the client has a partner who meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support in their own right, the partner can apply for Jobseeker Support as the primary client.
If the person who has commenced full-time employment is the partner, then the Jobseeker Support can continue with their earnings being charged as income against the benefit.
Note sole parents and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients may be treated differently when they commence full-time employment. For more information see:
- Temporary employment period for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
- Annual income for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
## Part-time employment
If a client or their partner commences part-time or casual employment that is less than 30 hours a week, the Jobseeker Support can continue. This is because the client or partner will still be able to meet their job search requirements.
The income from part-time or casual employment will be charged against the benefit for the week in which the income was earned or represents.
However, if the earnings from the part-time or casual employment reduce the Jobseeker Support to zero when charged against the benefit, the benefit must be suspended.
## Weekend work
If a client or partner is working weekends regularly, casually or 'one-off' then the income is charged against the benefit from the previous Monday.
For more information see:
- Estimated income

chunks.title: Income reduces the benefit payable to zero — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Income reduces the benefit payable to zero
If the client or partner has earnings or income for a period that will reduce the Jobseeker Support payable to zero, then the Jobseeker Support will need to be suspended or cancelled.
There is an exception for some clients, see:
- Annual income for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
- Temporary employment period for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
Although the main benefit may be stopped a client may still qualify for Extra help.
For more information see:
- Effect of income on Extra help
- Income from employment
- Income change
Note clients will not qualify for the Winter Energy Payment if their income reduces their benefit payable to zero.

chunks.title: Income stops — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Income stops
If a Jobseeker Support client advises that their income has stopped, MSD must review their Jobseeker Support and any Extra help they are getting from the day after the income stopped.
MSD will need to determine why the income has stopped for example, a client may advise that the interest payments from their investment have stopped. MSD should find out what the client has done with the money that was invested.
## Deprivation of income or assets
MSD has discretion to reduce or decline a benefit (or Extra help) where clients have deprived themselves of income or assets.
For more information see:
- Core policy Income
## Stops work
If a Jobseeker Support client or partner (if any) ceases employment, MSD needs to decide when to review their Jobseeker Support from.
MSD will need to find out:
- the date they ceased employment
- the reason they ceased employment
- final pay details (including any holiday pay, redundancy etc)
Note if the client or partner gets any holiday pay, the holiday pay should be charged as ongoing income over the period it represents.
## Example
Kaya has been getting Jobseeker Support with her partner Brennan included.
Brennan is working and has been earning $720 gross per week. He ceases work on 1 April 2026 and gets holiday pay of $1,440.
Brennan's holiday pay is equivalent to 2 weeks of his normal pay. MSD continue to charge $720 per week as income against the Jobseeker Support, for the 2 weeks from 1 April 2026.

chunks.title: Income test — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Income test
The family circumstances of a client will determine how the income (including any income of a partner, if any) is charged.
## Single clients and couples
Clients whose weekly income is over $160 gross per week will have their benefit reduced by 70 cents for every $1.00 of income that is over $160 gross per week.
If a client is getting a half-married rate of benefit because their partner is:
- granted a main benefit in their own right, or
- not entitled to get a benefit because they have a 13-week non-entitlement period, have a financial sanction imposed, or they are on strike.
Then, their benefit will be reduced by 35 cents for every $1.00 of the total combined income that is over $160 gross per week.
## Sole parents and grandparented clients
Sole parents and grandparented clients whose weekly income is over $160 gross per week will have their benefit reduced by:
- 30 cents for every $1.00 of income that is between $160 and $250 gross per week
- 70 cents for every $1.00 of income that is more than $250 gross per week.
## Sole parents and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026
Sole parents and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients whose benefit commenced (or last commenced) before 1 July 2025 can have their income charged annually, until they reach their next 52 week expiry date. This is a transitional arrangement.
These clients move to weekly income charging, and the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle, when they complete the 26 week reapplication process before their final 52 week expiry date and have their Jobseeker Support regranted.
By 30 June 2026 all Jobseeker Support clients will have moved to weekly income charging.
For more information see:
- Annual income for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026

chunks.title: IRD number for partner who is not apportioned assistance — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: As part of a review of benefit, MSD may make a written request to the client for evidence of their partner's IRD number when the: - partner is not apportioned the primary client's Jobseeker Support, and - partner's income is relevant to a client's Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Setting or extending the period for providing evidence — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: MSD can request a client to provide evidence of their partner's IRD number within a reasonable time period (usually 10 working days). MSD can set a different period or extend the period to provide evidence of an IRD number when it is expected to take longer to get the evidence. This includes considering factors outside the client or partner's control that may cause delays, including, but not limited to: - the client or partner has a family emergency that caused a delay - processing delays with an external agency (e.g. Inland Revenue, Department of Internal Affairs, etc) - the client or partner does not speak English as a first language and has difficulty navigating evidence requirements - the client or partner has limited access to the internet, a device, or their local service centre - the client or partner has a physical or intellectual disability that makes accessing services difficult.

chunks.title: Adverse Action Notice following an unsuccessful match — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about a partner's IRD number. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information or there's an error, MSD should ask the client (in writing) to provide evidence of their partner's IRD number, unless there are significant barriers to providing this. In the written request for evidence of the IRD number, MSD must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and the match was unsuccessful, and - giving the client or partner a minimum of 10 working days to provide their partner's IRD number evidence or the client's assistance may be suspended. Example Isla is receiving Jobseeker Support. Isla's partner, Ariki, has income that is included in MSD's income test to determine eligibility for Jobseeker Support and MSD holds an IRD number for Ariki. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Ariki's IRD number. As part of a review of Isla's benefit, MSD provides a notice in writing, giving 10 working days for Isla to provide evidence of Ariki's IRD number. MSD's decision to give 10 working days to provide evidence is based on: - Ariki already having an IRD number - Ariki not having any significant barriers to getting evidence of their IRD number - MSD's obligation to provide a minimum of 10 working days to provide the information.

chunks.title: MSD may suspend assistance if evidence is not received — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: MSD may suspend all taxable and/or income tested assistance the client is getting, including Jobseeker Support, if evidence of a partner's IRD number evidence is not provided within a reasonable timeframe (usually 10 working days) or within the extended period if this has been applied. In rare cases, depending on the client's circumstances, MSD may consider cancelling or varying the client's assistance. Note suspension does not apply to Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: IRD number not requested in some circumstances — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: MSD may not ask for evidence of an IRD number when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - significant factors, that are outside the client's or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of the IRD number, e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence, and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided. A partner's IRD number and evidence of their IRD number does not need to be provided when they are not a New Zealand tax resident. MSD can determine at a later point to request evidence of the IRD number. For more information see: - Non-tax resident partner's IRD number not required Note there is different guidance for requesting evidence of an IRD number for clients and partners apportioned Jobseeker Support or when a client is applying for Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Medical reviews — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: The Ministry of Social Development requires clients on Jobseeker Support (health condition, injury or disability) to have their medical eligibility reviewed regularly. The date of a client's medical review is generally based on the expiry of the medical coverage period their health practitioner has recorded in their current medical certificate. When a client is applying for (or transfers to) Jobseeker Support with part-time or deferred work obligations (granted on the ground of health condition, injury or disability) they will need to provide a current medical certificate with their medical coverage. Before the end of the medical coverage period, a client must provide a current medical certificate with a new medical coverage period to continue getting Jobseeker Support. The client may no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support (health condition, injury or disability) from the date their medical coverage in their medical certificate expires. Clients are notified before their expiry date telling them, if they are still unable to work full-time, they must see their health practitioner. Clients who are still unable to work, need to provide another medical certificate to keep getting Jobseeker Support with part-time or deferred work obligations on the ground of a health condition, injury or a disability. For more information see: - Client does not make contact or provide current medical certificate - Client makes contact and confirms they are available for full-time employment

chunks.title: Exceptions — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: There are situations when a maximum medical review period is applied for clients with specific health conditions, including a: - pregnant client who is over 26 weeks pregnant or - client who is donating a kidney or liver tissue The medical certificate coverage for these exceptions is either the duration specified by a health practitioner or the maximum review period for these specific health conditions, whichever is the lesser. For more information see:

chunks.title: Further medical certificates — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: Medical certificates need to be current to help you determine or review your client's benefit entitlement or capacity to work part-time. The medical certificate must include: - a diagnosis - the impact of the condition on your client's ability to work - the likely duration of that effect and - any other information the Ministry requires For more information see: - Medical certificates

chunks.title: Delay in producing a current medical certificate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: There may be situations where a client is unable to provide a current medical certificate in time. If a client has a good and sufficient reason for the delay, you could consider applying a discretionary medical expiry extension, allowing a client more time to get a current medical certificate. For more information see:

chunks.title: Refer to Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the information about the client's medical coverage is unclear, ie the information is conflicting or ambiguous, you should refer to your Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor for advice. For more information see: - Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor [no link find out why] process

chunks.title: Second opinion — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text: In some circumstances you may need to refer your client to a designated health practitioner for another assessment. If the health practitioner indicates on the certificate that a second opinion is appropriate you can require your client to be assessed by a designated health practitioner. The health practitioner may indicate that a medical specialist or a hospital doctor or some other person is best placed to provide the information for your client. When the certificate indicates 'other', refer to your Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor [no link find out why] for advice.

chunks.title: Ministry of Social Development debt repayments — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Ministry of Social Development debt repayments
When a client has a Ministry of Social Development debt, this can be recovered by regular deductions from their current benefit.
Note Income Related Rent historical Kāinga Ora debt should be given equal priority to Ministry of Social Development debt.
For more information see:
- Current client debt Negotiating repayment of debt

chunks.title: Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service
The Ministry of Social Development has an Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service that identifies clients who have left New Zealand if they are getting a benefit.
Once identified, the client's eligibility to keep getting their benefit payments while they are absent from New Zealand is automatically determined by Ministry systems.
## Does not advise of departure
If the client did not tell the Ministry they were leaving New Zealand their benefit will be suspended immediately from the day after they left New Zealand.
The Integrity Intervention Centre will determine if there has been an overpayment, establish any debt and advise the client.
If a client questions the information match refer them to the Integrity Intervention Centre.
For more information see:
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Approved travel reasons
- Backdating benefit to the day after departure
- Action on return to New Zealand
- Examples of applying the Absence from New Zealand policy
- Contacting Work and Income as soon as the client reasonably can

chunks.title: On leave for 28 days or less — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## On leave for 28 days or less
Where a client who is receiving the hospital rate is on leave from hospital for 28 days or less:
- increase their benefit to the appropriate full rate from the date of discharge on leave
- for married, civil union or de facto clients reduce the partner's benefit to the half married, civil union or de facto rate and suspend Special Disability Allowance and
- review any Extra Help from the same date
On re-admission to hospital:
- reduce the benefit to the rate payable prior to the period of leave
- for married, civil union or de facto clients increase the partner's benefit and resume Special Disability Allowance and
- review any Extra Help from the same date
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.

chunks.title: On leave for more than 28 days — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## On leave for more than 28 days
Where a client who is receiving the hospital rate is on leave from hospital for more than 28 days:
- increase their benefit to the appropriate full rate from the date of discharge on leave
- for married, civil union or de facto clients reduce the partner's benefit to the half married, civil union or de facto rate and suspend Special Disability Allowance and
- review any Extra Help
On re-admission to hospital continue to pay the full rate of benefit and any Extra Help for a further 13 weeks of hospitalisation.
Note calculation of the 13 week period in hospital begins again after the client has been re-admitted when on leave for more than 28 days.
The dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.

chunks.title: On leave from hospital — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## On leave from hospital
Jobseeker Support is paid at the full rate for any period of leave from hospital. Where the client has been receiving the hospital rate increase their benefit for any period they are on leave.
The benefit action to take, on the client's re-admission to hospital, will depend on how long they were on leave.
## Effect of leave on thirteen week count
Any periods of leave from hospital of 28 days or less are to be ignored when deciding the date from which the benefit is to be reduced to the hospital rate. Calculate the period in hospital from the original admission date.
If the client has been allowed out of hospital for more than 28 days, the calculation of the 13 week period in hospital begins again after the client has been re-admitted.
For more information see:
- On leave for 28 days or less
- On leave for more than 28 days
- Weekend leave
- Discharge from hospital
