You should not continue payment for 28 days following the death of a single client to meet funeral expenses. A Funeral Grant is available for this purpose. For more information see:
- Funeral Grant
## SWIFTT
If you are paying terminal benefit for a single client you will need to manually calculate entitlement and make an adhoc payment. There is no automatic provision for the payment of terminal benefit (for a single client) on SWIFTT.
Wherever possible you should enter the next of kin or the executor of the deceased's estate on SWIFTT.
For more information see:
- Avoiding a debt
- Terminal benefit rate

chunks.title: Terminal benefit payments to surviving person or person caring for a child — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit payments to surviving person or person caring for a child
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children.
## Surviving partner
When Jobseeker Support is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person's and the surviving person's portion of the benefit is paid. Payment is the total benefit as well as any ongoing extra help. It does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit.
The deceased person's portion of terminal benefit is paid to their bank account.
A surviving person can apply to have the deceased person's portion of terminal benefit paid to them. When an application is received, terminal benefit (or remaining unpaid balance) can be paid to that applicant.
The surviving person's benefit should be reviewed to determine the best option financially for the person.

chunks.title: Benefit paid at a reduced rate — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Benefit paid at a reduced rate
When the client's benefit was paid at a reduced rate at the date of death, the terminal benefit is also paid at the reduced rate.
Benefit payments may have been reduced due to:
- hospitalisation The deceased client's benefit was reduced as they were in hospital for more than 13 weeks.
- income
- debt repayments when benefit arrears are due at the date of death, attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit paymentdo not recover debts, in full, from terminal benefit payments
- when benefit arrears are due at the date of death, attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit payment
- do not recover debts, in full, from terminal benefit payments
- Child Support if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewedChild Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenuewhen a surviving partner or family member makes enquiries, refer them to Inland Revenue
- if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed
- Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenue
- when a surviving partner or family member makes enquiries, refer them to Inland Revenue
- court attachment orders
- redirection of benefit to Kāinga Ora or a community housing providerWhen the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. For more information see: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client
Note all of the above deductions will continue to be made from the terminal benefit payments unless they are manually stopped before cancellation.

chunks.title: Treatment of income — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Treatment of income
When a client (or their partner) is receiving Jobseeker Support and declares any income you need to:
- determine the source and the amount of income
- the family circumstances of the client
- check the client still qualifies for the and meets the job search requirements
- check the client's income is below the Jobseeker Support cut-out point
- check the period over which to charge income
- check the client is still entitled to receive family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
- review the rate of payment, see Income test and Income change
- review any Extra help Effect of income on Extra help
- check any Exemption for severe disablement
For information on how to charge specific types of income for example, Accident Compensation Payments, see: Types of income
When a client (or their partner) advises that they have commenced employment, you will need to find out more specific information about their employment see: Changes and reviews Employment
## Benefit stopped, suspended or expired
Where a benefit is stopped (suspended or expired) and the client has declared income for a period where no benefit has been paid, you need to determine the client's entitlement to benefit first and then charge the income accordingly.
For more information see
- Processing standards Income and asset details [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Underpaid — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Underpaid
When a client has been underpaid Jobseeker Support and is owed arrears, MSD will work out the amount of tax and pass this on to Inland Revenue.
From 1 April 2024, if an arrears payment relates to a previous tax year, the arrears will not be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment. This means the client will not have to pay any more tax on the payment.
Only arrears payments relating to the current tax year will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment.
Example
A client is paid arrears on 12 June 2025. This payment represents arrears for 25 March 2025 to 8 June 2025.
The arrears for 25 March to 31 March 2025 represent a past tax year, so they will not be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment. The arrears for 1 April to 8 June 2025 represent the current tax year, so they will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment.

chunks.title: Verification from Internal Affairs — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Verification from Internal Affairs
If a client can't produce a copy of a birth certificate, you can request one using the "Birth Verification" form (V02W).
Requests for verification of births can be made to:
Computer RegistryBirths, Deaths and Marriages PO Box 10-526 Wellington 6143

chunks.title: Voluntary Work — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Voluntary Work
A Jobseeker Support client or their partner may elect to participate in voluntary work to obtain work experience.
This is an acceptable activity however it should not take precedence over the primary client's availability for paid work.
When clients in receipt of a work obligated benefit engage in one of these activities it is essential that they continue to meet their job search requirements and obligations.
It is not sufficient to only be available for work. There is also the requirement to be actively seeking work.
Clients can undertake voluntary work while continuing to meet the job search requirements and obligations of Jobseeker Support. Each case has to be considered on its merits, but if the part-time 'non' job search activity reaches in excess of 12 to 15 hours per week, there should be careful scrutiny of the person's benefit eligibility.
A client's part-time voluntary work must allow enough time for them to actively seek work as required by their job search requirements.

chunks.title: Weekend leave — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Weekend leave
Jobseeker Support is paid for a seven day period, covering Monday to Sunday. Therefore, where the client is receiving the hospital rate and is on weekend leave you should pay the appropriate full rate of benefit for the number of days they are on weekend leave and subsequently incurring additional expenses in the community.
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.
## Example
If the client is on leave from Friday to Monday, you will need to pay the appropriate full rate of Jobseeker Support for 4 days. Generally, you will do this by completing a back dated review so that SWIFTT will pay the appropriate full rate of Jobseeker Support for 4 days.

chunks.title: Young partner not yet subject to obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Young partner not yet subject to obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning
A young partner of a main beneficiary who is not yet subject to the obligation to be in education, training or work based learning can continue to be paid a benefit for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason if the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations.
## Example (but not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A young person who is not yet subject to the education obligation as their youngest dependent child is less than 12 months (and there is no Teen Parent Unit place available for them) wishes to holiday in Australia.
As long as the travel will not prevent the young person from meeting their other obligations (eg their parenting and budgeting obligations) they can continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Young partners meeting their youth activity obligations
- Young partners who are exempt from their youth activity obligations
- Absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Activity failures for young partners

chunks.title: Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support > changes and reviews jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations
A young partner of a main beneficiary who is exempt from all of their youth activity obligations can continue to be paid a benefit for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason.
A young partner who is exempt from some of their youth activity obligations can continue to receive their payment for any reason for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations.
## Example (but not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A young person who is exempt from all of their activity obligations advises that they wish to travel to Australia to visit friends.
The young person is able to be absent from New Zealand and continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
Note that a client with a partial exemption is still subject to some obligations and therefore they can only be paid while they are overseas if the travel will not prevent them from meeting their obligations.
For more information see:
- Activity failures for young partners

chunks.title: Charging income — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: A client (and their partner, if any) getting Jobseeker Support have their income assessed and charged weekly. MSD must charge income for the period it is earned or relates to. If a payment does not represent a specific period or if MSD cannot determine the actual period it represents, MSD must determine the most appropriate period to charge the income. This may be the week it is received, provided or supplied. When a client declares any income MSD needs to: - determine the source and the amount of income - check the client is still entitled to get Jobseeker Support and meets the job search requirements - check if the client qualifies for Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit. For information on how to charge specific types of income for example, Accident Compensation Payments, see: Types of income.

chunks.title: Single clients and couples — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Clients whose weekly income is over $160 gross per week will have their benefit reduced by 70 cents for every $1.00 of income that is over $160 gross per week. If a client is getting a half-married rate of benefit because their partner is: - granted a main benefit in their own right, or - not entitled to get a benefit because they have a 13-week non-entitlement period, have been sanctioned due to an obligations failure or they are on strike. Then, their benefit will be reduced by 35 cents for every $1.00 of the total combined income that is over $160 gross per week. For more information see: - Weekly income example - single clients and couples

chunks.title: Sole parents and grandparented clients — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Sole parent and grandparented clients whose weekly income is over $160 gross per week will have their benefit reduced by: - 30 cents for every $1.00 of income that is over $160 to $250 gross per week - 70 cents for every $1.00 of income that is more than $250 gross per week. For more information see: - Weekly income example - sole parents

chunks.title: Sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026 — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Sole parent and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients whose benefit commenced (or last commenced) before 1 July 2025 can have their income charged annually, until they reach their next 52 week expiry date. This is a transitional arrangement. These clients move to weekly income charging when they complete the 26 week reapplication process before their final 52 week expiry date and move to the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle once their Jobseeker Support has been regranted. Note from 30 June 2026 all sole parent and grandparented Jobseeker Support clients will have moved to weekly income charging. For more information see: - Annual income for sole parent and grandparented clients before 30 June 2026

chunks.title: Childcare costs income exemption — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a sole parent has to pay childcare costs because they are working, they can get an additional income exemption. For more information see: - Childcare cost income exemption - sole parents

chunks.title: Information share Child Support payments — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Information share Child Support payments are treated differently than other types of income as they are automatically charged forward as income for a period of 4 or 5 weeks. For more information see: - Information share Child Support payments - Automated income charging rules

chunks.title: Income from overseas pensions — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Income from overseas pensions is generally treated as a direct deduction from the benefit rate, and this requires a separate calculation to charging other types of income. For more information see: - Payments from overseas

chunks.title: Child changes and social obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child changes and social obligations
Sometimes a client will have a change in circumstances that may mean the client is no longer required to comply with their social obligations. This includes where:
- a dependent child changes age and the social obligation that applied for the dependent child in their care is no longer relevant or
- child leaves care (for example starts to live with another parent or caregiver or goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki)
For more information see:
- Changes and reviews Child changes
- Clients situation changes during engagement and support process

chunks.title: Child to be included — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Child to be included
A client is obliged to tell us of all their circumstances including the number of children in their care.
If a child is considered to be dependent that child is to be included in the caregiver's benefit.
## Client doesn't want to include a child
In cases where the client has genuine concerns about including the child in their benefit (such as concerns about violence from the other parent) advise the client all information contained in their benefit record is confidential.
If you have any concerns regarding the welfare of the child, the case should be referred to Oranga Tamariki.
## Deciding if a child is financially dependent
When a client states they are receiving payments to pay for a child's expenses you must decide if the child is a dependent child of the client.
A child does not have to be solely financially dependent on a client to be considered a dependent child. All that is required is that the child is financially dependent on the person to some degree.
However, being financially dependent on a client is only part of the qualifications of a dependent child. The child must still meet all the qualifications to be considered dependent.
If another person or body is paying for the child's expenses, including payments for the care provided, the child is not financially dependent on the client.
If a client is receiving payments toward the expenses of a dependent child this is regarded as income for benefit purposes.

chunks.title: Childcare cost income exemption - sole parents — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Childcare cost income exemption - sole parents
There is an additional $20.00 per week income exemption for a sole parent who is receiving Jobseeker Support when they have to pay childcare costs while they are working.
It is not necessary for the child to attend an approved childcare centre, private arrangements can be accepted.
Entitlement to a Childcare Subsidy or OSCAR must be assessed first. If the total cost of childcare is not covered by the subsidy the client can receive the additional income exemption.
The exemption would be the lesser of:
- the amount the client pays for childcare or
- the cost of childcare not covered by a subsidy or
- $20.00 per week
The exemption only applies for the weeks the sole parent pays for childcare while they are working.

chunks.title: Recurring illness — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Recurring illness
No stand-down is imposed for clients who have a chronic recurring health condition if:
- their registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist or midwife where relevant) has confirmed they are suffering from a chronic health condition and
- this is a second or subsequent application for Jobseeker Support (on the ground of a health condition, injury or a disability)
Accept subsequent applications for Jobseeker Support as a re-application of the initial application.
Note this also applies if the client had previously been receiving Sickness Benefit.

chunks.title: Client accepts the results of a failed screening test — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client accepts the results of a failed screening test
A client will be asked by the employer, training provider or the drug test provider to confirm that they accept the result of the failed screening test. They can accept the result of the failed drug test by:
- signing the Pre-employment Drug Test Result Confirmation Form or
- verbally accepting the result
When a client has accepted the results, this means that they understand:
- there is no requirement to send the failed screening test sample to a laboratory for evidential testing
- this may result in a sanction being imposed and
- they may have to repay Work and Income for the cost of the failed drug test
Before you initiate an obligations failure for a client because they have failed a drugs test, without having a good and sufficient reason, you must receive confirmation from the employer that the client has failed the test.
Once you have received confirmation from the employer or training provider that a client has failed the screening test, and all testing has been completed, an obligations failure should be initiated.
Although the client can still dispute other parts of the decision, by providing a good and sufficient reason for the obligations failure, they cannot dispute the result of the screening drug test because they have already accepted the failed result.
For more information see:
- Informing a client of the drug test obligation failure
- Reimbursement to employers and debt recovery
- Drug test obligation failures - Good and sufficient reasons
- Recompliance for drug test obligation failures

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Example 1
Client
Partner
Current 24-month failure count
Obligations failure 1
Obligations failure 2
Social obligations failure
Obligations failure 2
Obligations failure 3
In this situation the client will have to recomply by complying with all their social obligations. The partner will have to recomply by completing a six-week approved activity or programme of activities which includes complying with all their social obligations in order to be granted a provisional benefit.

chunks.title: Client does not accept the results of a failed screening test — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client does not accept the results of a failed screening test
If the client does not accept the results of failed screening test the employer, training provider or drug test provider may decide to send the failed sample to the laboratory for evidential testing.
If you have received information back from the employer, training provider or drug test provider that the client has subsequently failed the evidential drug test you must initiate a drug test obligations failure. Centralised Services will organise the debt recovery of both the screening and evidential drug tests (if the test was being conducted for a suitable job).
## Sample sent for evidential test
Some employers, training providers, or drug test providers, will send all screening test samples for evidential testing, regardless of whether the client accepted the result of the failed screening test or not.
If the client passes the evidential drug test, then the client is not required to repay the Ministry of Social Development for the cost of either the failed screening drug test or the evidential drug test.
If the client also fails the evidential drug test, the client is required to repay the Ministry for the costs of both the failed tests (screening and evidential).
## Client disputes the results of an evidential drug test
A client can dispute the result of a failed evidential test.

chunks.title: Client does not need to complete the reapplication process — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Clients do not need to complete the reapplication process if, at any the time from the date their ‘initial notice to reapply’ letter is sent, until their expiry date, they are: - in hospital care, or - in residential disability care or rest home care, or - living in or visiting a region affected by an emergency or adverse event and they are unable to reasonably leave the area Clients in one of these specific circumstances will have their expiry date automatically cleared and reset to the end of the next 26 week period. The client and their partner (if any included in their Jobseeker Support) do not need to complete a reapplication until the next expiry date, if they still need Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Partner not required to complete reapplication — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If only the partner is in one of the specific circumstances listed above, they do not need to complete any part of the reapplication process. The client must still complete their reapplication before their expiry date, as the expiry date will not be cleared in this situation.

chunks.title: Client in hospital — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If MSD is aware a client is in hospital when the 'initial notice to reapply' letter is due to be sent, the letter will not be sent. If the client is in hospital at any time during their notice period, they do not need to complete the reapplication process. MSD will generally review the client’s Jobseeker Support and any Extra Help they get when the client is discharged from hospital. For more information see: - Discharge from hospital

chunks.title: Client in residential disability care or rest home care — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If MSD is aware a client is in residential disability care or rest home care when the 'initial notice to reapply' is due to be sent, the letter will not be sent. If the client is in residential disability care or rest home care at any time during their notice period they do not need to complete the reapplication process. This includes but is not limited to clients who are getting Residential Care Subsidy or Residential Support Subsidy. For more information see: - Residential Care Subsidy - Residential Support Subsidy

chunks.title: Emergency or adverse events — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: During an emergency or adverse event it may be unreasonable to expect clients to complete the reapplication process. This is limited to clients who, at any point during the notice period are: - living in or visiting a region affected by an emergency or adverse event, and - they are unable to reasonably leave the area. An area affected by an emergency or adverse event means that: - a local state of emergency or national emergency is in force in the area (e.g. because of a natural disaster such as a flood or earthquake), or - an epidemic notice is in force in the area (i.e. because of an outbreak of a quarantinable disease that is affecting or may affect the area), or - other exceptional circumstances are affecting the area As an emergency or adverse event affects a whole area or region, or is nationwide, it is likely that multiple clients will be affected by the event. Generally, in an emergency or adverse event, MSD will be able to determine which clients have been affected as a result of the emergency or adverse event.

chunks.title: Client has a health condition, injury or disability — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client has a health condition, injury or disability
To get Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability, the client must meet certain medical qualifications.
The client must be:
- limited in their capacity or unable to work full-time due to a health condition, injury or disability or
- in employment, but because of a health condition, injury or disability cannot work or can only work at a reduced level
To support their application for a Jobseeker Support (health condition, injury or disability) a client must:
- provide a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist or midwife where relevant) and
- attend an appointment with a designated health practitioner, if required

chunks.title: Client has failed a screening drug test — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client has failed a screening drug test
If a client fails a screening drug test with an employer, training provider or drug test provider, they will be advised that they have failed and they will be asked if they:
- accept the results of the screening drug test or
- do not accept the result of the screening drug test
For more information see:
- Informing a client of the drug test obligation failure
- Client accepts the results of a failed screening test
- Client does not accept the results of a failed screening test
- Drug test obligation failures - Good and sufficient reason

chunks.title: Client has part-time work obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client has part-time work obligations
If you have decided that the client has the capacity for work of at least 15 hours per week, the client will have part-time work obligations.
You should consider the client's work capacity and any restrictions or support needs the client may have as a result of their health condition, injury or disability when considering what activities you will require your client to complete.
## Client does not agree with decision to apply work obligations
Once you have decided that the client will have part-time work obligations, the client will be sent a letter. The letter advises the client that they have a right to review any decisions made relating to medical capacity to work with the Medical Appeals Board.
For more information see:
- Work obligations
- Core policy Medical Appeals Board
- Date when work obligations apply from (health condition, injury or disability
- Informing clients of their obligations
- Client no longer eligible for part-time work obligations or deferral

chunks.title: Client is granted a deferral and has work preparation obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client is granted a deferral and has work preparation obligations
If you have decided that the client should be deferred from their work obligations, they will be subject to work preparation obligations.
You should consider the client's work capacity and any restrictions and support needs the client may have as a result of their health condition, injury, or disability when considering what activities you will require your client to complete.
For more information see:
- Work preparation obligations
- Deferrals
- Date when work obligations apply from
- Informing clients of their obligations
- Client no longer eligible for part-time work obligations or deferral

chunks.title: Client is meeting their social obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client is meeting their social obligations
If, during any of the Contact Steps of engagement and support, you consider that the client is meeting their social obligations you will need to let the client know that:
- as they are meeting their social obligations, you do not require any more information or contact from them and
- if they require any support regarding their social obligations they can contact Work and Income at any time
The appropriate outcome for the specific social obligations that apply to each of the client's dependent children needs to be recorded in OBMAN.
For more information on the three step process of engagement see:
- Contact steps - social obligations [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Client leaves Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client leaves Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre
No stand-down applies to the commencement of a benefit when a client has left the Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre.
For more information see:
- Refugee or protected person
- Commencement date
- No stand-down applies

chunks.title: Client no longer eligible for part-time work obligations or deferral — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client no longer eligible for part-time work obligations or deferral
A client's obligations will change when:
- the client's medical certificate indicates that their work capacity has changed
- the client's medical certificate is no longer current
- the client informs Work and Income that they are available for and seeking full-time work
When this occurs, you need to review the client's benefit entitlement and work obligations, and determine whether the client will now have full-time work obligations.
If a person requests to have full-time work obligations, and their medical certificate suggests this is not appropriate, you may refer to a Regional Health and Disability advisor for clarification of a person's capacity for work and limitations. This will assist to determine what the appropriate obligations for the client are.
For more information see:
- Ending a deferral [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Client receiving youth support payments — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client receiving youth support payments
A young person who is receiving Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment when they reach the qualifying age for Jobseeker Support can only be granted that benefit if they have been receiving Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment for 6 months.
## Young Parent Payment or Youth Payment was cancelled
Where a young person was previously receiving Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment and this was cancelled because, for example, they moved into employment or went overseas, and they now require financial assistance, the young person can be granted Jobseeker Support if they meet all the qualifications.

chunks.title: Client's job ceases during an employment trial period — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client's job ceases during an employment trial period
When determining eligibility for Jobseeker Support, any employment that has an employment trial period included in a client's employment agreement is assessed the same as any other employment.
A client's job can cease during the employment trial period for any number of reasons, such as:
- the employer not being able to afford the client's wages
- the employer's belief that the client lacks the necessary skills
- misconduct
- any other reason the employer decides to cease the client's employment or
- the client leaving of their own accord
When a client ceases work during an employment trial period, assess the client's eligibility to Jobseeker Support and commencement date the same as any other employment arrangement.
When an employer gives the client notice during the employment trial, they are not required to advise why they have decided to end the client's employment. They are however, required to provide details of their last date of employment and the date they will be paid to.
If the employer gave notice to the client of ending their employment after the employment trial, the employer must provide the client with the reason for ending their employment (i.e. the employment trial rules do not apply).
To determine eligibility and commencement date of the Jobseeker Support, the client needs to provide evidence and reasons for ceasing their employment, their last day of duty and last date paid to.
If the client cannot provide this evidence and reason for their employment ceasing, their last day of duty or last date paid to, you can ask the employer to complete the Employment and earnings information for applications (V06) form.
If the client's employer does not provide the reason for the client's employment ceasing during the employment trial, accept the client's reasons for the termination and continue with the application process. However, the employer must complete the date ceased and last pay details.

chunks.title: Client's situation changes during regular engagement and support — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Client's situation changes during regular engagement and support
A client and their partner (if any) may have a change of circumstance which means they are no longer subject to a social obligation. These changes may include (but are not limited to):
- a dependent child leaves their care or
- a dependent child changes age and the social obligations that apply for the dependent child in their care are no longer relevant
If this happens during regular engagement and support, the client cannot be failed and they are no longer subject to the social obligation.
For more information see:
- Social obligations - Actively engaging with clients [no link find out why]
- Overview of social obligations according to the age of the child
- Changes and reviews Child changes
- Good and sufficient reasons for failing to comply with a social obligation

chunks.title: Clients aged 18 or 19 years — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients aged 18 or 19 years
Clients aged 18 or 19 years living at home with their parents or caregiver are paid a lower rate of Jobseeker Support.
Clients must state on their application form if they live at home or away from home. Proof can be requested from the client if doubt exists.
There are certain situations where the lower rate does not apply.

chunks.title: Clients aged 65 years and over — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients aged 65 years and over
Clients aged 65 years or older may receive Jobseeker Support provided they meet all the qualifications, including work or work preparation obligations and the 26 week reapplication process.
For Jobseeker Support granted on the grounds of a health condition, injury or disability, they must confirm they would be available for and seeking full-time work, if not for a health condition, injury or disability.
If the client has circumstances which mean an exemption or deferral from their work obligations should be granted, this must be considered.
## Work and work preparation obligations for Jobseeker Support
Clients aged 65 or older who are eligible for Jobseeker Support have the same obligations as other clients. Clients may have:
- full-time work obligations
- part-time work obligations (for those granted on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability where they have capacity to work part-time)
- work preparation obligations (for those granted on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability where their obligations have been deferred)
MSD will determine appropriate activities for the client to undertake to meet their work and work preparation obligations depending on their circumstances. Generally it is unlikely that MSD would assign activities to clients aged 65+. However, the client is still subject to the obligations and may be assigned activities where appropriate.
## Client is not available for or seeking full-time employment
When a client is not available for or seeking full-time employment (and does not qualify on other grounds such as a deferral due to a health condition) Jobseeker Support cannot be granted or continued.
If the client does not qualify for Jobseeker Support or any other benefit, Emergency Benefit may be considered in substitution of Jobseeker Support.
The client will need to meet all of the qualifications for Emergency Benefit including the hardship test. This must be decided on a case-by-case basis, taking the clients full circumstances into consideration.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Clients aged 65 years and over
- Obligations
- Qualifications

chunks.title: Clients currently living in a limited employment location — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients currently living in a limited employment location
This applies to clients who are living in a limited employment location, and are:
- getting Jobseeker Support
- transferring from a benefit with no work obligations to Jobseeker Support or
- applying for Jobseeker Support
It does not include clients already getting Jobseeker Support who:
- move to a limited employment location or
- move from one limited employment location to another
A client who is living in a limited employment location and applying for Jobseeker Support, or transferring from a benefit with no work obligations to Jobseeker Support, must meet the Jobseeker Support eligibility criteria.
For more information see:
- Qualifications
A client who is living in a limited employment location and receiving Jobseeker Support through their local Service Centre must continue to meet the work obligations. These include being available for, and taking reasonable steps to obtain, suitable employment.
## Meeting the work obligations
To determine whether a client is meeting their work obligations, you should consider if the client:
- is available for work for 30 hours or more a week
- accepts any reasonable job offers within their abilities
- does not restrict their job search to vacancies in their chosen occupation
- makes applications for suitable jobs and
- contacts employers about vacancies
It is up to the client to demonstrate to you how they are meeting their work obligations. If they are unable to do this, they will fail the work obligations.
## Assistance to transition into employment
Assistance to transition into employment may be available to help clients, including those living in a limited employment location, with the essential costs of attending a job interview or taking up paid employment.

chunks.title: Clients from overseas — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients from overseas
If the client was born in another country or has lived and worked overseas this needs to be recorded on CMS. International Services follow up any entitlement to an overseas pension once the details are recorded in CMS.
## Cook Island, Niue and Tokelau clients
Clients born in the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau are automatically New Zealand citizens (by birth). Generally they will travel to New Zealand on a New Zealand passport.
However, they must still have lived continuously in New Zealand for two years at any one time before they can receive the Jobseeker Support.
Other residents of the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau will be required to produce a proof of residence document and meet the two years continuous residence requirement in New Zealand.
## Australian clients
Australian citizens are lawfully allowed in New Zealand as they are deemed to hold a residence class visa. However, they must still meet the two years residence qualification to qualify for Jobseeker Support.
## British clients
Clients of British nationality who arrived in New Zealand prior to 2 April 1974 were allowed residence in New Zealand without a visa or a permit. However they must still meet the residence requirement for Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Clients investigating self-employment options — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients investigating self-employment options
Jobseeker Support may be paid to clients investigating self-employment options if they continue meeting their job search requirements.
There are several types of assistance available to clients investigating self-employment options. These are:
## Pacific Island Employment Development Scheme (PIEDS)
Pacific Island Employment Development Scheme loans are offered to small businesses to encourage employment creation by the Pacific Island Employment Development Board.
Jobseeker Support cannot be paid to clients who have received this loan.
## Flexi-wage Self Employment
A Flexi-wage Self Employment subsidy is paid by MSD to eligible clients who are starting a small business.
The subsidy is paid for a set period of 28 weeks. In exceptional circumstances it can be extended up to a maximum of 52 weeks.
In most cases Jobseeker Support cannot be paid to clients who are getting this assistance.
The only exception is a work obligated partner of a Jobseeker Support client getting Flexi-wage Self Employment.
In these cases it is charged as income against Jobseeker Support.
Up to $5,000 of the Flexi-wage Self Employment can be capitalised. This amount is not charged as income.
## Business Training and Advice Grant
A one-off Business Training or Advice Grant of up to $5,000 per client per project is also available.
This amount is considered a capital payment and is not charged as income against Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Clients moving to a limited employment location — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients moving to a limited employment location
If a client is thinking of moving to a limited employment location (or from one limited employment location to another), you must tell them that moving to a limited employment location means they may not be able to meet their work obligations, including to be available for, and take reasonable steps to obtain, suitable employment in that location. This is because of a lack of employment opportunities in that area.
To meet the work obligations, clients moving to a limited employment location must demonstrate that they have access to reliable transport and are willing, and realistically able, to commute to a nearby town or centre where employment is available.
Continued residence in a limited employment location without meeting this requirement means they will fail the work obligations.
Note we do not want clients to put themselves in a situation where they will fail the work obligations. You need to work with all clients planning to move to a limited employment location, as appropriate, to explore:
- why they want to move
- whether and how the need to move could be alleviated without their having to move to a limited employment location
- how they plan to meet their work obligations should they move to a limited employment location
For more information see:
- Why is the client moving to a limited employment location?
- Decision guidelines - clients moving to a limited employment location
- Deskfile Limited employment locations

chunks.title: Clients released from prison — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients released from prison
Clients who have been released from prison can receive Jobseeker Support. You must confirm the clients release date. Usually the client receives release information (such as a Steps to Freedom grant) confirming the date of release from prison.
If the client has been in prison for less than 31 days, the initial stand-down may be waived.
For more information see:
- No stand-down applies
- Imprisonment
- Special Needs Grants Steps to Freedom
For more information see:
- Court imposed conditions

chunks.title: Clients taking periods of leave without pay — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients taking periods of leave without pay
People may sometimes be in a situation where they take periods of leave without pay from their employment. To do this, employees' must have agreed with their employer to alter the conditions of their employment.
People who are on a period of unpaid leave are not considered to be employed and therefore if they meet all of the qualifications they can receive Jobseeker Support.
## Voluntary unemployment stand-down
You need to consider the reason that a person is on a period of unpaid leave.
It is considered a good and sufficient reason to become unemployed if you are satisfied that an employee has agreed to take a period of leave without pay to protect their job in the future. This may be due to a downturn in the economy or because of an unexpected temporary closure at the premises (such as flood or fire).
You may consider imposing a voluntary unemployment stand-down if the person decided to take leave without pay without a good and sufficient reason (for example, if a person just decided they wanted to have a break from their job).
For more information see:
- Voluntary unemployment - good and sufficient reason
## Work obligations
To receive Jobseeker Support, people on a period of unpaid leave must still meet their work obligations and be available for, and take reasonable steps to obtain suitable employment and accept any offer of suitable employment, whether full-time, part-time, temporary or seasonal employment.
A person who decides not to search for other work while on a period of unpaid leave would not be entitled to receive Jobseeker Support as they do not meet the job search requirements.
Note that if the person has an essential need during this time we could assist with a Special Needs Grant. Recoverable Assistance Payment may be appropriate as long as the client meets the annual income test.
For more information see:
- Work obligations
- Extra help Special Needs Grant
- Extra help Recoverable Assistance Programme

chunks.title: IRD number for client or partner who is apportioned assistance — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: MSD may make a written request for evidence of an IRD number for a primary client who is being paid Jobseeker Support. MSD can also request evidence of an IRD number for a partner when they are apportioned a part of the primary client's assistance payment.

chunks.title: Notice following an unsuccessful match — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about a client or their partner's IRD number. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information, or there's an error, MSD should ask the client or partner (in writing) to provide evidence of their IRD number, unless there are significant barriers to providing this. In the written request for evidence of the IRD number, MSD must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and the match was unsuccessful, and - giving the client or partner a minimum of 10 working days to provide their IRD number evidence or their assistance must be suspended. Example Isla is receiving Jobseeker Support and MSD holds an IRD number on record. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Isla's IRD number. MSD provides a notice in writing, giving 10 working days for Isla to provide evidence of their IRD number. MSD's decision to give 10 working days to provide evidence is based on: - Isla already having an IRD number - Isla not having any significant barriers to getting evidence of their IRD number - MSD's obligation to provide a minimum of 10 working days to provide the information.

chunks.title: MSD must suspend assistance if evidence of IRD number is not received — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: MSD must suspend all taxable and/or income tested assistance the client is getting, including their Jobseeker Support, if evidence of an IRD number is not provided within 10 working days from the written request, or extended period if this has been applied. If the partner has not provided evidence of their IRD number, the partner's taxable and/or income tested assistance must be suspended. Note suspension does not apply to Childcare Assistance. Example Koa is receiving Jobseeker Support and MSD does not have an IRD number on record. MSD sends a written request giving 10 working days for Koa to provide evidence of their IRD number. MSD receives no response to this request. MSD suspends Koa's taxable and/or income tested assistance because Koa has not supplied MSD with evidence of their IRD number within the timeframe provided.

chunks.title: IRD number evidence may not be requested in some circumstances — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: MSD may not ask for evidence of an IRD number when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - there are significant factors, that are outside the client's or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of their IRD number (e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence), and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided or - there are significant factors related to a health, injury or disability that are outside the client or partner's control that prevent them from providing evidence of an IRD number, and - an agent cannot be appointed to act on the client or partner's behalf. MSD can determine a later point to request the evidence of the IRD number. Example Sienna is 23 and receiving Jobseeker Support. Sienna's mother (Sara) is Sienna's agent and acts on Sienna's behalf with MSD. Sienna does not have an IRD number and Sara is not a recognised agent for Sienna for Inland Revenue. Sienna has a serious head injury, is unconscious and expected to be in hospital for at least 8 weeks. Sienna is not able to give consent to appoint Sara as an agent for Inland Revenue to apply for an IRD number due to their injury. MSD can request this information later when Sienna's situation has changed. Note there is different guidance for requesting an IRD number or evidence of an IRD number for partners who are not apportioned but their income is relevant to a clients Jobseeker Support, or when a client is applying for Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Clients undertaking Voluntary Work — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients undertaking Voluntary Work
Clients (or partners) who do voluntary work can still receive the Jobseeker Support as long as they continue to meet their work or work preparation obligations.
Clients (or partners) with work preparation or work obligations may have to give up some or all of their voluntary activities if a work preparation activity is required or if a suitable job becomes available.
For more information see:
- Work experience, activity in the community and voluntary work
- Suitable employment
## Community Service
Clients (and their partners) who are required to do Community Service as the result of a Court imposed sentence can still receive the Jobseeker Support as long as they are engaged in active job search and follow up all employment opportunities.

chunks.title: Clients who have a health condition or are injured or disabled — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients who have a health condition or are injured or disabled
A client can be deferred from their work obligations and be subject to work preparation obligations, when they have a health condition, injury or disability and have:
- no capacity to work or
- capacity to work less than 15 hours per week
## Capacity to work at least 15 hours per week
Clients who have a health condition, injury or disability and have the capacity to work at least 15 hours per week are subject to part-time work obligations.
The information contained in the Work Capacity Medical Certificate will help MSD determine if the client should be either:
- deferred from work obligations or
- subject to part-time work obligations
## Live Organ Donor
When a client or partner have decided to donate a kidney or liver tissue they can continue to receive their current benefit. The client or partner must provide evidence they have been accepted as a live organ donor.
Medical evidence must be signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner.
The medical certificate coverage can be up to 12 weeks.
## Unable to meet work preparation obligations
Clients who have a health condition, injury or disability may be granted an exemption from their work preparation obligations if it is unrealistic that they be required to plan.
For example when a client is:
- in hospital or
- is unable to attend an interview with MSD due to their condition
Consider the information on the client's Work Capacity Medical Certificate to see if the registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist or midwife where relevant) has advised of any restrictions to a client's capacity to plan.

chunks.title: Clients who have an ‘in-flight’ 52 week reapplication on 1 July 2025 — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients who have an ‘in-flight’ 52 week reapplication on 1 July 2025
On 1 July 2025 some clients (and any partner included in their Jobseeker Support) will have an 'in-flight' 52 week reapplication and will complete the 52 week reapplication process, rather than the 26 week reapplication process.
This applies to clients, who on 1 July 2025, had already been sent their 'initial notice to reapply' letter before 1 July 2025. Their letter outlined the 52 week reapplication process.
When these clients complete the reapplication process before their final 52 week expiry date and Jobseeker Support is regranted, they move to the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle.

chunks.title: Clients with dependent children - 50% protection — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients with dependent children - 50% protection
Sanctions are applied differently for:
- sole parent clients who fail their obligations
- couples with dependent children who both fail their obligations
- couples where one person is youth money managed
Clients and partners in these situations with a financial sanction imposed do not have their whole benefit sanctioned. Instead, a maximum sanction of 50% of the total benefit may be imposed. The balance payable is known as 50% protection.
For more information, including treatment of supplementary assistance, see:
- Sanctions for sole parents
- Sanctions for a couple with dependent children - both fail their obligations
- Sanctions for young partners
The 50% protection also applies to these groups if they are subject to a 13-week non-entitlement period for voluntarily leaving employment without a good and sufficient reason, dismissal due to misconduct, or refusing to accept any offer of suitable employment.
Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.
For more information see:
- Recompliance

chunks.title: Clients with specific circumstances — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Clients with specific circumstances
A client with specific circumstances may be able to get Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Commencement date — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
To decide when the Jobseeker Support can start you must first find the entitlement date.
This is usually the date that a person no longer has a means of support.
For a list of these dates see:
- Entitlement Date
Jobseeker Support is subject to an initial stand-down period of up to a maximum of two weeks after the entitlement date.
Generally, the commencement date is:
- the day after the initial stand-down ends or
- the application date
whichever is the later.
However, if clients in the following circumstances apply within 28 days of their entitlement date the commencement date rules are different and the twenty-eight day rule can be used:
- clients who have a health condition, injury or disability
- sole parents
- clients who have lost the financial support of their partner due to death, separation, or ending of a de facto relationship, or partner going into prison

chunks.title: Commencement of position — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Commencement of position
A client can start their Community Work Experience from the first date that the position is available. This must not be more than one week after the 2-week search period has ended.
## Commencement during 2-week search period
A client may find and start their position within the 2-week search period (after MSD has confirmed the organisation and position are suitable). If they start during this period, the 4-week position period will start from the date they start the position. This allows them to recomply with their obligations more quickly.
Note clients still need to meet the requirements of 5 hours per week for 4 weeks.
## Commencement after 2-week search period
If a client's position starts in the first week after the 2-week search period ends, the first day of the position might not be the first day of the week.
f MSD is satisfied the approved position will start within that week, and the client can still complete their required 5 hours, the position period can start from the first day of the week.

chunks.title: Community Work Experience — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Community Work Experience
Community Work Experience is a non-financial sanction that can be imposed on a client or their partner instead of a Grade 1 financial sanction. It is intended to help clients build work-related skills and confidence, and also build connections in their community.
A client will work with a community or voluntary organisation, for at least 5 hours a week, for 4 weeks.
A client will have a 2-week search period before their Community Work Experience begins to find a suitable position and organisation.
MSD will need to confirm whether the organisation and position are suitable before the client can begin.
Once a client completes their Community Work Experience, they are considered to have recomplied with their obligation failure and do not need to complete any other recompliance activities.

chunks.title: Completing the 26 week reapplication process — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Clients must complete the 26 week reapplication process before the expiry date of their Jobseeker Support, unless they have exceptional circumstances. If a client does not do this, their benefit will stop. To complete the 26 week reapplication process the client and their partner (if any included in their Jobseeker Support) must: - confirm their circumstances for the purposes of an eligibility check and - participate in and complete and appropriate employment engagement (including their partner, if they have part-time or full-time work obligations) and - agree to their obligations and confirm their intent to reapply for Jobseeker Support. If MSD is satisfied that the client and their partner have completed all relevant parts of the reapplication before their expiry date, and the client continues to qualify for Jobseeker Support, MSD must regrant their benefit. For more information see: - Eligibility part of the 26 week reapplication - Employment part of the 26 week reapplication - Employment part of the reapplication not required - Exceptional circumstances for reapplication

chunks.title: Completing the reapplication — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: A client and partner may complete the parts of the reapplication separately or at the same time. The eligibility and employment parts of the reapplication may be completed in the 13 weeks before their expiry date through specific engagements. Clients must agree to their obligations and confirm their intent to reapply for Jobseeker Support when they submit their 26 week reapplication. They can do this at any time from the start of their notice period.

chunks.title: Specific engagements — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Specific engagements are interactions or discussions that a client or partner can have with MSD in the 13 weeks before their expiry date that satisfy either the eligibility or employment part of the reapplication process. A specific engagement may include: - an interaction with MSD where the client confirms the same circumstances that apply to the Jobseeker Support qualifications, as required for the reapplication, and - a discussion with MSD about what the client is doing or needs to do to find or prepare for suitable employment If a client and their partner have satisfied the eligibility and employment parts of the reapplication through specific engagements, they only need to confirm if there have been any changes in their circumstances since they completed a specific eligibility engagement, agree to their obligations and confirm their intention to reapply to complete the reapplication. Note agents may complete the eligibility, obligations and intent to reapply parts of the reapplication on behalf of the client or partner if they have been given the appropriate rights to act on their behalf. Agents cannot complete the employment engagement unless MSD decides there is a reason that this is unavoidable. For more information see: - Specific engagements - What an agent can do - What an agent cannot do

chunks.title: Automated decision making — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the client has satisfied all parts of the reapplication (including where in the 13 weeks before their expiry date, specific engagements for eligibility and employment are completed to satisfy parts of the reapplication) and continues to qualify for Jobseeker Support, their benefit may be regranted automatically using Automated Decision Making. This applies when all of the following requirements are met: - a client has confirmed their circumstances for the purposes of an eligibility check and - the client has completed an appropriate employment engagement and - the client has agreed to their obligations and confirmed their intent to reapply and - the client has declared no change of circumstances since their specific engagements, and - the outcome is that the client continues to meet the qualifications for Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Exceptions — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: There are situations where a client or partner do not need to complete the reapplication process. For more information see: - Client does not need to complete the reapplication process

chunks.title: Comprehensive Work Assessment for 52 week reapplication process — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Comprehensive Work Assessment for 52 week reapplication process
The Comprehensive Work Assessment is a compulsory part of the 52 week reapplication process. It is designed to support in-depth conversations with clients to help them prepare for and find suitable employment.
The 52 week reapplication process and Comprehensive Work Assessment apply to the following clients only:
- clients who have an 'in-flight' 52 week reapplication on 1 July 2025.
Clients and partners with work obligations must participate in and complete the Comprehensive Work Assessment. Clients who have a deferral or exemption from work obligations must still participate in and complete the Comprehensive Work Assessment.
Note partners with no work obligations do not need to complete the Comprehensive Work Assessment.
## Client does not complete Comprehensive Work Assessment
If a client does not complete the Comprehensive Work Assessment the reapplication cannot be processed.
## Partner does not complete Comprehensive Work Assessment
A partner with work obligations should be encouraged to complete the Comprehensive Work Assessment before the expiry date.
Partners with work obligations
If a partner with work obligations has not completed the Comprehensive Work Assessment, MSD will book an appointment with them to complete it. If they do not attend, an obligations failure will be initiated for the partner. To recomply the partner must participate in and complete the Comprehensive Work Assessment.
Partners without work obligations
Partners who do not have work obligations do not need to complete the Comprehensive Work Assessment. The 52 week reapplication process can be completed, provided that the client has completed the Comprehensive Work Assessment.
For more information see:
- Obligations failures
- Effect of sanctions on assistance
## Completing the 52 week reapplication process
When these clients complete the 52 week reapplication process before their final 52 week expiry date and Jobseeker Support is regranted, they move to the 26 week expiry and reapplication cycle.

chunks.title: Contact made but reapplication not completed before expiry date — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Contact made but reapplication not completed before expiry date
When a client makes contact to complete the reapplication process before their expiry date, but it cannot be completed before the expiry date through no fault of their own, an extension may be granted.
An extension may be granted for up to 10 working days starting on their expiry date, on the condition that the client completes the reapplication as soon as possible and within the extension period.
Generally, this extension can be granted when:
- a client contacts MSD for an employment engagement or for support to complete the reapplication, but there are no available appointments before their expiry date, or
- there are delays in MSD processing the reapplication, or
- a client has an employment engagement or reapplication appointment booked but the MSD service centre has closed unexpectedly, for example in an emergency.
Note if a client is granted an extension and completes the reapplication process within 10 days of the expiry date, the benefit should be regranted from the expiry date.
If a client does not complete the reapplication process within the extension period or no longer qualifies for Jobseeker Support, their benefit will be stopped from their expiry date. The amount of benefit (including any Extra Help) that was paid during the extension period must be established as a debt.
## Applying as a new applicant
If the client does not complete their reapplication within the extension period, or were not granted an extension, they will need to apply as a new applicant if they still need Jobseeker Support. Their expired benefit must be cancelled from the expiry date before they can be granted Jobseeker Support as a new applicant.
The client will be subject to the usual commencement date rules, including the initial stand-down.
For more information see:
- Commencement date
- Initial stand-down
Note if the client advises they want to apply for Jobseeker Support as a new applicant and completes the reapplication form, MSD can use their reapplication form as their new application.

chunks.title: Earning all of the incentive payments available to them — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Earning all of the incentive payments available to them
For young partners who have Youth Activity obligations to have the option of getting their payment directly, they would need to earn the following incentive payments:
- budgeting
- education and
- parenting (where applicable)
A young partner who has a full or partial exemption for their activity obligations is only able to earn those incentive payments which apply to their current obligations.

chunks.title: Failure of different obligations add to failure count — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Failure of different obligations add to failure count
The failure count includes all obligation failures. If a client or partner fails a work obligation and then a later failure related to social obligations in a 24-month period, this would be counted as two failures.
## Examples of transfers between benefits
The following table outlines what happens to the failure count and sanction when a youth client transfers between benefit types.
From
To
Failure count
Sanction
Jobseeker Support
Young Parent Payment
Re-sets to zero
Re-sets to zero
Young partner aged 16 or 17 years getting Jobseeker Support
Jobseeker Support (work obligations)
Carries over
Re-set to zero
Young partner aged 16 or 17 years getting Jobseeker Support
Young partner aged 16 or 17 years getting Supported Living Payment
Carries over
Carries over
## Calculating continuous receipt of benefit
To determine whether a client has been in continuous receipt of a main benefit, MSD must disregard any period that their benefit was suspended or cancelled because:
- the client was in employment, and
- that employment was less than 10 working days.
## Transitional arrangements
From 26 May 2025, the obligations failure count period increased from 12 months to 24 months for working age clients.
Any obligation failures that were initiated before 26 May 2025 will only be counted for 12 months.
Obligation failures (except youth activity obligation failures) initiated from 26 May 2025 onwards will be counted for 24 months.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Grade 3 sanction
The primary client who has met their obligations will continue to get their portion of the assistance. They will also be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.
If the young partner who is youth money managed fails their obligations for a third time:
- their portion of the benefit, and any incentive payments is cancelled immediately
- their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Winter Energy Payment is cancelled and
- the young partner is subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks from the date of cancellation
The young partner may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6 week approved activity or programme of activities.
If the young partner does not start a 6 week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of their non-entitlement period to get a benefit.
Note Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period.

chunks.title: Couple, young partner is youth money managed, primary client has work obligations, dependent children, both fail — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Couples with dependent children who both fail their obligations at the same time do not have their whole benefit sanctioned. Instead, a maximum sanction of 50% of the total benefit may be imposed. If a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligations failures. Note family tax credit and Best Start tax credit continue to be paid at the full rate.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the primary client fails their obligations for the first time, their portion of the benefit is reduced by 50%, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. Extra help (including their portion of Winter Energy Payment) is not affected. For more information on non-financial sanctions see: - Non-financial sanctions If the young partner fails for the first time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments will be suspended. Their Extra help (including their portion of Winter Energy Payment) is not affected.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the primary client fails their obligations a second time, their portion (50% of the couple's benefit) is reduced by 25%. Their portion of Extra help is also suspended. They will not get Winter Energy Payment. If the young partner also fails for the second time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments will be suspended. The young partner will continue to get their portion of any supplementary assistance to which they are entitled. In effect the couple gets 50% of the total Extra help to which they are entitled. This is as they have 50% protection for the family unit. The young partner will also continue to be paid the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If both clients fail their obligations a third time, 50% of the couple's benefit is cancelled. The couple will continue to get a maximum of 50% of their married rate of benefit until they recomply. The young partner's portion will be paid directly to their bank account, not via youth money management. If both clients are subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks, both clients may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities. While part of the benefit is cancelled, the couple gets 50% of any Extra help to which they are entitled. They can continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment. They have 50% protection for the family unit.

chunks.title: One client recomplies first — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the primary client recomplies first, their portion of the benefit and Extra help must be resumed or re-granted. The young partner's benefit must remain sanctioned until they recomply. If the young partner recomplies first, their portion of benefit and Extra help is not able to be resumed or re-granted as the primary record is not current. The payments must be manually made.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Grade 1 sanction
If the young partner fails their obligations for the first time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments are suspended, until they recomply with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations).
The young partner can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and Winter Energy Payment to which they are entitled.
The primary client will continue to get 50% of the couple's benefit entitlement and their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and Winter Energy Payment.
Note family tax credit and Best Start tax credit continue to be paid at the full rate.
## Grade 2 sanction
If the young partner fails their obligations for the second time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments are suspended, until they recomply with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations).
The young partner can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and Winter Energy Payment to which they are entitled.
The primary client will continue to get 50% of the couples benefit entitlement and their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and Winter Energy Payment.
## Grade 3 sanction
If the young partner fails their obligations for a third time, their portion of the benefit and Extra help is cancelled. They are subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks. The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities.
If they have not started a 6-week approved activity, they may reapply at the end of the non-entitlement period to get a benefit.
The non-sanctioned primary client will continue to get 50% of the couple's benefit entitlement including Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. The non-sanctioned primary client will be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Grade 1 sanction
If the primary client fails their obligations for the first time, that person's portion of benefit is reduced by half (50%) until they recomply unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed.
For more information on non-financial sanctions see:
- Non-financial sanctions
The young partner will have their in-hand allowance of up to $50 and any incentive payments suspended.
The couple can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled. They continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit. Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during any non-entitlement period.
After 4 weeks
If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks, they will have their portion of the benefit and their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support suspended. Their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended.
Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.
## Grade 2 sanction
If the primary client fails their obligations for the second time, that person's portion of benefit is suspended until they recomply with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations). Their portion of Extra help is also suspended (including their portion of the Winter Energy Payment).
