Medical treatment may be part of the rehabilitation process but a client cannot be required to complete medical treatment as an activity as part of their obligations.
If you are uncertain whether an activity would be considered as medical treatment, rehabilitation or other activity you should seek advice from your Regional Health or Regional Disability Advisor before you require a client to undertake the activity.
## Rehabilitation activities
Requiring clients to undertake rehabilitation activities must be done with care. Generally you would ensure that they are willing and able to undertake activities.
Important before you require the client to undertake a rehabilitation activity you must discuss the situation with your manager client service delivery.
The client must be advised that if they are required to complete a rehabilitation activity and they fail to do this without a good and sufficient reason a sanction may be imposed.

chunks.title: Reimbursement to employers and debt recovery — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Reimbursement to employers and debt recovery
The potential employer can be reimbursed for a failed drug test for a client only when Work and Income receives confirmation a drug test has been completed that was part of the pre-employment process and the potential employer has completed the Pre-employment drug test claim form for employers which includes details such as:
- the name of the employer
- the type of test - whether it was a screening or evidential test
- confirmation that the drug test was to the drug test standard
- confirmation of a failed test result and
- the cost of the failed test and the payment rate they are claiming
At the same time that the employer is reimbursed, a debt for the cost of the drug test will be manually added to the clients SWIFTT record by NPCU/NAC.
For more information see:
- Reimbursement and claims for Employers/Drug Test Agencies [no link find out why]
A training provider cannot be reimbursed for the costs of a failed drug test. In most cases the contract with the provider will have already factored these costs into account.
Although a drug test provider may conduct the testing the employer will be the one to be reimbursed for the costs relating to the failed drug test.
The information provided related to the failed drug tests is not to be shared with other employers, and is only to be used for the purposes of establishing whether a client has failed, without good and sufficient reason, to meet the drug test obligations.
The reimbursement of failed drug tests only apply to jobs where
- the client with work obligations has been referred by Work and Income
- the vacancy is listed with Work and Income and
- the vacancy requires a pre-employment drug test
## Debt recovery
Once the cost of the failed drug test is reimbursed to the employer, it must be established as a debt to the client. The amount of the debt is the amount that has been reimbursed to the employer.
For more information see:
- Reimbursement and claims for Employers/Drug Test Agencies [no link find out why]
Debt repayment options must be discussed with the client giving consideration to any other debts the client may have. Add notes to the client's record about the negotiated debt repayment.

chunks.title: Removing incentive payments — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Removing incentive payments
Incentive payments should be removed when the young partner:
- is subject to a grade 1, 2 or 3 sanction
- is in hospital for longer than 13 weeks and they are receiving the hospital rate of payment
- no longer has a dependent child (Parent education incentive only)
- has intentionally acted in a way that is inconsistent with the purpose of the incentives
Note young people can continue to receive their incentive payments once they are earned if they are granted an exemption from their obligations, unless the reason the exemption is needed is because they have acted in a way that is inconsistent with the purpose of the incentive.
For more information see:
- Examples of actions inconsistent with purpose
- Incentive payments can continue
- Restoring incentive payments

chunks.title: Report Job Search — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Report Job Search
Report Job Search is a non-financial sanction that can be imposed on a client or their partner instead of a Grade 1 financial sanction. It is intended to help clients actively participate in finding suitable employment.
In a 4-week period, a client must:
- do at least 3 job search activities a week and
- report to MSD on the job-search activities they have done each week and
- provide MSD with evidence of their job-search activities at the end of the 4-week period
MSD must be satisfied the evidence provided is sufficient.
Once a client completes 4 weeks of Report Job Search, they are considered to have recomplied with their obligations and don't need to complete any other recompliance activities.

chunks.title: Report to service provider or Work and Income on progress — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Report to service provider or Work and Income on progress
A young partner is required to report to their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service on how they are satisfactorily meeting their obligation to be:
- in education, training or work-based learning
- participating in a budgeting programme and
- (if a parent) participating in a parenting education programme and other parenting obligations
A service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service can ask a young partner to report to them by either phone, email or in person and will determine how often the young partner must report.
The frequency of reporting must be reasonable and take into account:
- the length of the activity
- how often the young partner is required to attend
- whether a young partner has failed to comply with their obligations in the past
Generally a young partner should not be required to report more than once a week.
Example
The service provider sets an activity for a young partner to attend a budgeting programme and asks that they report on their progress when they commence the programme and when they attend each week.
A young partner undertakes the budgeting programme. They phone their service provider when they commence the programme and report in each week of the programme to confirm their attendance.
For more information see:
- Money management activity
- Youth activity obligations

chunks.title: Reporting progress — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Reporting progress
You can require your client to report on their job search progress in meeting their work or work preparation obligations.
You must advise the client that if they fail to comply with this obligation without a good and sufficient reason, they have an obligations failure.
## Example
You have asked a partner with a 3 year old child to research child care options and training options available in their community and to call you in a month to update you on their progress. If the client does not contact you, you should initiate an obligations failure.
## Clients and partners with work obligations
You can require a client with work obligations to report on their job search progress.
A client can report by either phone, email or in person. Generally a client should not be required to report more than once a week.
## Example
You have asked the client to register with various recruitment agencies and call you weekly to update on their job search progress.
If the client does not contact you, you should initiate an obligations failure.

chunks.title: Residence — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Residence
To be granted Jobseeker Support, a client must:
- be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident (ie not be in New Zealand unlawfully, here on a temporary entry class visa or a temporary permit) or
- be deemed to hold a residence class visa in New Zealand under the Immigration Act 2009 (eg Australian citizens or residents) and
- have lived continuously in New Zealand for 2 years or more at any one time since becoming a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident and
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they first apply for benefit and
- generally be ordinarily resident in New Zealand
For more information see:
- Deciding ordinarily resident
Note clients who are a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident but have not lived in New Zealand continuously for 2 years may be eligible for Jobseeker Support on grounds of hardship.
If a client is from overseas or is a refugee or protected person special provisions may apply, see:
- Refugee or protected person
## Sponsored clients
Some clients have been granted permanent residence on condition that they will be supported by a New Zealand sponsor.
Before a decision can be made about the client's application for benefit, any reasons why their sponsor can no longer support the client must first be determined and verified.
For more information see:
- Sponsored clients [no link find out why]
## Clients without permanent residence
If a client does not have permanent residence they cannot receive Jobseeker Support or Jobseeker Support on the grounds of hardship (even if they have lived in New Zealand continuously for 2 years). They may be able to receive an Emergency Benefit if they:
- are lawfully present in New Zealand and are awaiting the outcome of their application for refugee or protection status in New Zealand or
- are applying for a residence class visa under the Immigration Act and are compelled to remain in New Zealand through unforeseen circumstances

chunks.title: Resident in New Zealand — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Resident in New Zealand
To qualify for Jobseeker Support a client must have lived continuously in New Zealand for 2 years at any one time since becoming a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident.
To be resident in New Zealand at a particular time means that the client either:
- makes their home in New Zealand, that is, they have been living in New Zealand on a permanent basis or
- has an intention to make their home in New Zealand for the foreseeable future
Note 'resident' is not the same as being ordinarily resident.
Remember you must be satisfied that the client has been resident in New Zealand continuously for at least two years at any one time since becoming a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident.
## Client makes their home in New Zealand
A client will be resident in New Zealand if they make their home in New Zealand. You should look for evidence that the client makes their home in New Zealand. Relevant factors you should consider include:
- a fixed abode in New Zealand?
- ownership of property in New Zealand?
- frequent absences from New Zealand, and what is the duration of and reason for those absences?
- involvement with New Zealand society such as (but not limited to):- community activities- employment- membership of clubs and- local churches
For more information see:
- Calculating the period of residence
- Deciding ordinarily residence
- Reciprocal Agreements
- Proof of residence

chunks.title: Restoring incentive payments — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Restoring incentive payments
The service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service can recommend that an incentive payment be returned to the young partner, if they are satisfied that the young partner is now acting in a way that is consistent with the aims of the incentive payment.
When the incentives will be returned depends on:
- the reason that the incentive was removed
- whether the young partner has undertaken or completed steps to address their actions
- whether the service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service is satisfied that the young partner is now acting in a way that is consistent with the aims of the incentive payment
For more information see:
- Removing incentive payments
- Examples of actions inconsistent with purpose
- Payment Incentive payments

chunks.title: Restricted circumstances guidelines — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Restricted circumstances guidelines
You must consider the following factors in relation to the restricted circumstances that make the child's attendance at school unreasonable.
It can be unreasonable for that child to attend school:
- if there is a no school bus or
- no suitable transport and
- there is a significant distance between their home and school
It may also be unreasonable for the child to attend the nearest school because the child has particular needs that prevent them from attending the nearest school, for example:
- special needs such as physical or intellectual disability; chronic or recurring illness
- learning or behavioural difficulties or
- exclusion from the school

chunks.title: Before expiry date — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Before expiry date
If a client has a suspended (other than due to a grade 2 sanction) or an expired benefit, they will not be sent the 'initial notice to reapply' letter. This is because they are not currently getting a benefit.
For more information see:
- Notice to clients with a suspended or expired benefit
If the client's benefit is resumed before the reminder letter is due to be sent, and the client has not completed the reapplication process, MSD must advise them of what they need to do to complete their reapplication.
MSD should consider whether the client will be able to complete the reapplication process before their expiry date and if an extension may be appropriate.
## On or after expiry date
If a client makes contact to have their benefit resumed on or after their expiry date and does not have an exceptional circumstance for not reapplying before the expiry date, their benefit must be cancelled from the expiry date.
If the client still needs Jobseeker Support, they will need to apply as a new applicant and will be subject to the usual commencement date rules, including the initial stand-down.
## Exception
If the resumption date of the client's benefit would have been before the expiry date, but due to their circumstances the client was unable to complete the reapplication process before the expiry date, MSD will consider whether the client had exceptional circumstances.
For more information see:
- Situations where extensions can be given
- Exceptional circumstances for reapplication

chunks.title: Retirement — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Retirement
Retirement is any situation where a person's contract of employment has fully ceased due to retirement. This applies to all types of retirement including age-related retirement, medical retirement, early retirement, and temporary retirement.
If a person retires from employment, they voluntarily cease work. Under the Humans Rights Act, employment contracts can no longer state an age of retirement so a person can retire at any age.
If a client with work obligations has voluntarily given up work even if they have retired we would generally impose a voluntary unemployment stand-down unless they had a good and sufficient reason for giving up work. For example they gave up work due to ill health, or the job may be outside the client's capabilities.

chunks.title: Removing incentive payment as a result of an activity obligations failure — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Removing incentive payment as a result of an activity obligations failure
If a young partner has a grade 1 or grade 2 sanction and they are getting an incentive payment, these payments are also suspended until the young partner recomplies with the obligation they failed.
If a young partner has a grade 3 sanction imposed, any incentive payment they are receiving is cancelled.

chunks.title: Review of decision - 26 week reapplication process — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Review of decision - 26 week reapplication process
The client cannot review the requirement to complete the 26 week reapplication process as it is a statutory requirement to reapply - rather than a reviewable decision made by MSD.
However a client can apply for a Review of Decision of the 26 week reapplication process when:
- they do not agree with a decision regarding the regrant of their Jobseeker Support, such as the benefit or supplementary assistance being paid at a different rate or being declined, or
- they have provided a reason for not reapplying in time which was not deemed by MSD to be an exceptional circumstance.
Note this is also applicable for clients who are required to complete the 52 week reapplication process on or after 1 July 2025 as a transitional arrangement.
## Automated decision making
Where Automated Decision Making is used to determine that a client has satisfied all parts of the reapplication and continues to qualify for Jobseeker Support, their benefit is automatically regranted.
If MSD or the client does not agree with the decision to automatically regrant the benefit, MSD can review the decision.
A client can then apply for a Review of Decision if they do not agree with the outcome of MSD's review of the decision made through Automated Decision Making.
For more information see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals
- Automated
- Clients who have an 'in-flight' 52 week reapplication on 1 July 2025

chunks.title: Review period for a client who has a job to return to — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Review period for a client who has a job to return to
If a client identifies that they have a job to return to, they will not need to have a medical review until their recommended return to work date indicated on their medical certificate by their registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist or midwife where relevant).
If a client advises they are returning to full-time work before their return to work date, MSD must advise the client that their benefit will stop.

chunks.title: Review period for client referred to a contracted service provider — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Review period for client referred to a contracted service provider
If a client has been referred to a contracted service provider for case management, the client will continue to have a medical review.

chunks.title: Review period for clients who are over 26 weeks pregnant — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Review period for clients who are over 26 weeks pregnant
If a client is over 26 weeks pregnant (in their 27th week of pregnancy or over) they do not need to have another medical review until 4 weeks after the expected due date of the birth of their child.
Pregnant clients who are less than 27 weeks pregnant will follow the standard medical certification process.

chunks.title: Reviewing or disputing the drug test failure and sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Reviewing or disputing the drug test failure and sanction
A client has the right to dispute or review any decision they disagree with relating to:
- an obligations failure or
- a sanction being imposed
A client can do this by:
- disputing the decision or
- lodging a formal Review of Decision
A Review of Decision can be lodged at any stage within 3 months of the obligations failure being initiated, or within 3 months of the sanction being imposed.
If a client disputes their obligations failure or sanction more than 20 working days after it is initiated or imposed, you need to advise the client to lodge a formal Review of Decision in writing.
## Appealing to the Medical Appeal Board
A client can only lodge an appeal to the Medical Appeal board for a decision relating to a drug test failure when a decision was made that they:
- did not have a good and sufficient reason for failing a drug test obligation and
- the reason given for the failure was that the client was either addicted to controlled drugs ordependent on controlled drugs
- addicted to controlled drugs or
- dependent on controlled drugs
A client is not required to dispute a decision before lodging a review of decision or appealing to the Medical Appeal Board (drug test failure only).
For more information see:
- The disputes process
- Recording decisions on a dispute
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Samoan Quota Scheme — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Samoan Quota Scheme
This category is run by ballot and is available to Samoan citizens. Either the principal applicant or their partner must have an offer of employment in New Zealand.
Where the offer of employment was withdrawn or employment terminated through circumstances beyond the control of the client, you may consider granting Jobseeker Support where the client meets the 2 year residence criteria.
If you find that there was no job or that the job fell through you need to advise Immigration New Zealand after consulting with Legal Services regarding any privacy law implications with doing this.
Immigration New Zealand will decide on any action to be taken with regard to the client's residence status. In the meantime you need to look at all the circumstances of the client as to whether you can grant benefit assistance.
Note if the client has permanent residence and has lived continuously in New Zealand for 2 years at any one time since becoming a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident, assess the client's entitlement to Jobseeker Support in the usual manner.
Jobseeker Support on grounds of hardship is income and asset tested. To assess a client's entitlement confirmation of the client's income and assets declared on application for permanent residence is required from Immigration New Zealand. The client's current income and assets is also required.
Once confirmed, assess Jobseeker Support on grounds of hardship in the usual manner taking into account all other information provided by Immigration New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Permanent residence
- Definite offer of employment
- Qualifications
- Granting on grounds of hardship

chunks.title: Sanctions and the Jobseeker Support reapplication process — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Sanctions and the Jobseeker Support reapplication process
All clients with grade 1 or 2 sanctions, and clients with dependent children with a grade 3 sanction, can complete the Jobseeker Support reapplication process before their expiry date in order to continue getting their benefit.
Note the sanction continues to apply to the re-granted benefit.
Primary clients with a partner and single clients who have a grade 3 sanction have their benefit cancelled. This means they cannot complete the reapplication process.

chunks.title: Sanctions for a couple with dependent children - both fail their obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Couples with dependent children who both fail their obligations at the same time do not have their whole benefit sanctioned. Instead, a maximum financial sanction of 50% of the total benefit may be imposed. The balance of the benefit payable is known as 50% protection.

chunks.title: Young partners — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: The effect of the sanction for a young partner depends on whether the client is youth money managed or not. For more information see: - Sanctions for young partners Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If both clients fail their obligations for the first time, each person's portion of the benefit is reduced by 50%, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. The couple will continue to get a maximum of 50% of their married rate of benefit until they recomply. While their benefit is reduced, the couple can continue to get Extra help. The couple will continue to get the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit. For more information see: - Recompliance - Non-financial sanctions

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If both clients fail their obligations a second time, 50% of the couple's benefit is suspended. The couple will continue to get a maximum of 50% of their married rate of benefit until they recomply. While part of the benefit is suspended, the couple can get 50% of any Extra help they are entitled to. However, they can get the full rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit. Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If both clients fail their obligations a third time, 50% of the couple's benefit is cancelled. The couple will continue to get a maximum of 50% of their married rate of benefit until they recomply. If both clients are subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks, both clients may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities. While part of the benefit is cancelled, the couple gets 50% of any Extra help they are entitled to. However, they can get the full rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit. For more information see: - Recompliance

chunks.title: Processing 50% payments — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: When both clients fail their obligations at the same time and a financial sanction is imposed for each person, the couple must continue to get a maximum of 50% of their married rate of benefit until they recomply. This must be paid manually, and will depend on which client failed their obligations first. For more information see: - Imposing a manual sanction [no link find out why]

chunks.title: One client recomplies first — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the primary client recomplies first, their portion of benefit and Extra help must be resumed or re-granted. The primary client will get the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment. The partner's benefit must remain sanctioned until they recomply. If the partner recomplies first, their portion of benefit and Extra help is not able to be resumed or re-granted as the primary record is not current. For information on how to process this see: - Processing a manual sanction [no link find out why]

chunks.title: 50% protection and reduction of income — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: The 50% protection is applied to half the main benefit rate (eg the married rate) before any reduction of income. Any income will reduce benefit by 35 cents for every $1 of total income over $160 per week from the 50% protection payment. For more information see: - Charging income

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If both partners fail their obligations for the first time, each person's portion of the benefit is reduced by 50% unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. For more information on non-financial sanctions see: - Non-financial sanctions The couple will continue to get a total of 50% of the married rate. While their benefit is reduced, the couple can continue to get Extra help. Winter Energy Payment can continue to be paid as the client is still getting a qualifying benefit. If either partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks, they will have their portion of the benefit and Extra help suspended. Winter Energy Payment cannot continue to be paid to the client who has not recomplied as they are not getting a qualifying benefit. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks. Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If both partners fail their obligations for the second time, each person's portion of the benefit is suspended. While the benefit is suspended, the couple's Extra help is also suspended. Winter Energy Payment cannot continue to be paid as they are not getting a qualifying benefit. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks. Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If both partners fail their obligations for a third time, each person's portion of the benefit is cancelled. They are subject to a non-entitlement period for a period of 13 weeks. The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities. If they have not started a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of the non-entitlement period to get a benefit. When the client's benefit is cancelled, Extra help is also cancelled. Winter Energy Payment cannot continue to be paid as they are not getting a qualifying benefit.

chunks.title: Young partners — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: The effect of a sanction on a young partner's assistance depends on whether the client has children, and is youth money managed or not. For more information see: - Recompliance

chunks.title: Sanctions for couples where one person is youth money managed — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Sanctions for couples where one person is youth money managed
Young partners (16 or 17 with no children and 16 to 19 with children) who are included in a client's Jobseeker Support may be youth money managed.
Sanctions will differ for couples depending on who has failed their obligations.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If one partner fails their obligations for the first time, that person's portion of the benefit is reduced by 50% until they recomply, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. For more information on non-financial sanctions see: - Non-financial sanctions While the benefit is reduced, the couple can continue to get Extra help. Winter Energy Payment can continue to be paid as the client is still getting a qualifying benefit. Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If one partner fails their obligations a second time, their portion of the benefit is suspended until they recomply. While their portion of the benefit is suspended, their portion of Extra help is also suspended. They cannot get Winter Energy Payment. The other person continues to get their portion of the main benefit and Extra help. The full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment can be paid to the partner who hasn't failed. Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures. For their partner's entitlements see: - Payments to the non-sanctioned client For more information see: - Recompliance

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If one partner fails their obligations for a third time, their portion of the benefit and Extra help is cancelled. They cannot get their portion of Winter Energy Payment. They are subject to a non-entitlement period for a period of 13 weeks. The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities. If they have not started a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of the non-entitlement period to get a benefit. For their partner's entitlements see: - Payments to the non-sanctioned client

chunks.title: Young partners — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: The effect of a sanction on a young partner's assistance depends on whether the client has children, and is youth money managed or not. For more information see: - Recompliance - Sanctions for young partners

chunks.title: Client does not recomply — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the client has not recomplied after 2 weeks, MSD will contact them to discuss financial assistance and recompliance. If the client has still not recomplied after 4 weeks, MSD will need to send a letter advising that they need to attend an appointment to discuss ongoing entitlement to benefit. For more information on this process see: - Sanction period - Two week intervention [no link find out why] - Sanction period - Four week intervention [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If one partner fails their obligations for the first time, that person's portion of the benefit is reduced by 50%, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. For more information on non-financial sanctions see: - Non-financial sanctions While the benefit is reduced, the couple can continue to get Extra help. Winter Energy Payment can continue to be paid as the client is still getting a qualifying benefit. If the person being sanctioned has not recomplied within 4 weeks, they will have their portion of the benefit and Extra help suspended. Winter Energy Payment cannot continue to be paid to the client who has failed as they are not getting a qualifying benefit. The full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment can be paid to the partner who hasn’t failed. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks. Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If one partner fails their obligations a second time, their portion of the benefit is suspended. While their portion of the benefit is suspended, their portion of Extra help is also suspended. Winter Energy Payment cannot continue to be paid to the client who has failed as they are not getting a qualifying benefit. The full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment can be paid to the partner who hasn’t failed. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks. Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If one partner fails their obligations for a third time, their portion of the benefit and Extra help is cancelled. Winter Energy Payment cannot continue to be paid to the client who has failed as they are not getting a qualifying benefit. The full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment can be paid to the partner who hasn't failed. They are subject to a non-entitlement period for a period of 13 weeks. They may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities. If they have not started a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of the non-entitlement period to get a benefit. For their partner's entitlements see: - Payments to the non-sanctioned client or partner

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Grade 1 sanction
A first obligations failure means the client's benefit is reduced by 50%, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed.
For more information on non-financial sanctions see:
- Non-financial sanctions
While their benefit is reduced, the client can continue getting Extra help. Winter Energy Payment can continue to be paid as the client is still getting a qualifying benefit.
If the client has not recomplied within 4 weeks, they will have their benefit suspended along with all Extra help (including Winter Energy Payment).
Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.
Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligations.
## Grade 2 sanction
A second obligations failure means the client's benefit is suspended. When their benefit is suspended, any Extra help the client was getting is also suspended. Winter Energy Payment cannot continue to be paid as the client is not getting a qualifying benefit.
Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.
Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligations.
## Grade 3 sanction
A third obligations failure means the client's benefit is cancelled and they are subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks. The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities.
When the client's benefit is cancelled, Extra help is also cancelled. Winter Energy Payment cannot continue to be paid as the client is not getting a qualifying benefit.
If they have not started a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of the non-entitlement period to get a benefit.

chunks.title: Sanctions for sole parents — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Sanctions for sole parents
When sole parents fail their obligations and have a financial sanction imposed, they do not have their whole benefit sanctioned. Instead, a maximum financial sanction of 50% of the total benefit may be imposed. The balance payable is known as 50% protection.
Sole parents who are sanctioned can continue to get full Extra help, regardless of the grade of sanction. This includes the Winter Energy Payment.
For more information on what a client can continue to get when sanctioned, see:
- Paying other assistance during a sanction
If the client has not recomplied after 2 weeks, MSD will contact them to discuss financial assistance and recompliance. If the client has still not recomplied at 4 weeks MSD must send the client a letter advising they need to attend an appointment to discuss ongoing entitlement to benefit.
For more information on this process see:
- Sanction period - Two week intervention [no link find out why]
- Sanction period - Four week intervention [no link find out why]
## Grade 1 and 2 sanctions
For a first and second obligations failure, a sole parent's benefit is reduced by 50% until they recomply, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed (for a first failure only).
For more information on non-financial sanctions see:
- Non-financial sanctions
They continue to receive full Extra help (including the full rate of Winter Energy Payment).
Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.
## Grade 3 sanction
For a third obligations failure a sole parent is subject to a non-entitlement period for a period of 13 weeks and will have 50% of their benefit cancelled. The sole parent may get a provisional benefit and have their benefit increased to 100% if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities.
They continue to get full Extra help (including the full rate of Winter Energy Payment).
For more information see:
- Recompliance

chunks.title: Sanctions for young partners — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: The effect of the sanction of the client's assistance for a young partner depends on whether the client is youth money managed or not.

chunks.title: Grade 1 and 2 sanctions — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: The client who is not required to get Youth Services and is not youth money managed will continue to get their portion of the assistance. They can continue to get their portion of the Winter Energy Payment. For a client who is required to get Youth Services and is youth money managed, a first or second failure means suspension of the in-hand allowance and any incentive payments, until the client recomplies with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations). The client can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled. The young partner can continue to get their portion of the Winter Energy Payment. If the client has not recomplied within 4 weeks the whole of their benefit and any incentive payments are suspended along with any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Winter Energy Payment they get. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: The client who is not required to get Youth Services and is not youth money managed will continue to get their portion of the assistance. The client will get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment. If the person who is required to get Youth Services and is youth money managed fails their obligations for a third time: - their portion of the benefit, and any incentive payments, are cancelled immediately - their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and Winter Energy Payment is cancelled and - the young person is subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks from the date of cancellation The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6 week approved activity or programme of activities. If the client does not start a 6 week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of their non-entitlement period to get a benefit. Note Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period. For more information see:

chunks.title: Client is not youth money managed — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: When a client is not youth money managed, has an obligations failure and has not recomplied within the 5 working day notice period, the effect of the sanction on the client's assistance is the same as for their main benefit except that any incentive payments being paid will also stop. Unlike Youth Payment clients who have earned the right to get their payment directly, a young partner will not be returned to youth money management after they have been sanctioned. For more information see:

chunks.title: Self-employed — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: People who are self-employed may be able to get Jobseeker Support. This depends on whether they meet all the qualifications. MSD must be satisfied that a self-employed person who is still working, is available for and seeking full-time employment, is willing and able to undertake it and has taken reasonable steps to find it. A self-employed person cannot get Jobseeker Support if they are working full-time, even if they are not earning income, or their income is less than the income limit. Note there is an exception for some clients, see: If the business is continuing with other staff being paid to run it, you need to look at the following before granting Jobseeker Support: - was the client working and supporting themselves beforehand? - if yes, what has changed and why has the client ceased working? - can the client begin supporting themselves again? When will they be able to do so? If the client is sick, injured or disabled, they may be able to get Jobseeker Support (health condition, injury or disability) for a specified period.

chunks.title: Example (Jobseeker Support, Health Condition, Injury or Disability) — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Brian is a sole trader operating as 'Brian Lawnmowing' Brian is temporarily unable to work following back surgery and applies for Jobseeker Support as he has no income. Brian has a medical certificate stating he will not be able to resume work for 13 weeks and has a deferral on his work obligations. Brian provided a copy of his most recent business accounts and bank statements with his application for benefit. These accounts show that Brian's business has a net loss for 2023 and is not generating enough income to support him, due to a combination of bad weather and illness. Brian is sure he will be able to support himself again when he is well again. Brian has employed his nephew Kevin to do some of the lawnmowing work while he's recovering from his operation. The wages Brian pays Kevin are a business expense which has further reduced Brian's income.

chunks.title: Part-time self-employed — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a person is only working part-time hours in self-employment they may be able to get Jobseeker Support. Examples of clients who may be in part-time self-employment include clients operating small retail business such as handmade soaps, knitwear, candles, part-time commission salespeople and hobby farmers.

chunks.title: Self-employed with no further work available — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Some small businesses have a drop in earnings and no scheduled work in the near future. When these businesses have no funds or cannot access any funds until further work becomes available, a client can get Jobseeker Support if they meet the qualifications.

chunks.title: Example — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: A contract weed sprayer who has been unable to get any work for 4 weeks and has no work available for the next 4 weeks can be classified as being available for work. Obtain confirmation that business activities have reduced or stopped, and no income is being received. If, before the client applies, business has significantly reduced and/or has now stopped, you can disregard income from the business when assessing the rate of Jobseeker Support that can be paid. However, the income must be taken into account for the initial stand-down assessment.

chunks.title: Work commences — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a regular pattern of income or work starts to emerge or a future contract of 3 - 4 weeks is obtained, the Jobseeker Support should be reviewed. If the client is working full-time their Jobseeker Support should be suspended or cancelled, unless they are covered by the exception. Note One-off contract work should be charged in the same way as casual earnings (less any business expenses).

chunks.title: Seriously sick or injured — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Seriously sick or injured
It may be determined that a client has an exceptional circumstance for not completing their reapplication before their expiry date, on the ground of being seriously sick or injured during their notice period which affected their ability to reapply before the expiry date.
## Evidence
MSD may require the client to provide evidence that they were seriously sick or injured. This could include a medical certificate or other medical information signed by a health practitioner, stating:
- what the illness or injury was, and
- the length of time it affected the client.

chunks.title: Setting appropriate activities for clients — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Setting appropriate activities for clients
After a discussion with a client, you will need to determine the most appropriate activities for them to undertake. To decide what activities are most appropriate, you should consider:
- client's individual circumstances
- whether the activity is suitable for the client
- whether the client has work preparation obligations or work obligations
Note you do not need to seek the client's or partner's agreement to the activities that you require them to complete.
Once you and the client have discussed what activities will be appropriate, include them in the client's Service Plan.
## Types of activities
You should refer the client to activities to improve their work-readiness or prospects for employment.
Activities may include (but are not limited to):
Work obligations
Work preparation obligations
A job interview
Contacting employers
Developing or updating a C.V.
Developing or updating a C.V.
Obtaining a driver's licence
Obtaining a driver's licence
Work assessment
Work assessment
Programme or seminar to increase particular skills or enhance motivation
Programme or seminar to increase particular skills or enhance motivation
Work experience or work exploration activity
Work experience or work exploration activity
Employment related training
Employment related training
Completing a high school qualification
Completing further study
Completing further study
Researching childcare options available in the community
Researching childcare options available in the community
You must take reasonable steps to arrange for the client to undertake an activity.
Note a client must not be required to undertake an Activity in the Community. If a client would like to undertake an Activity in the Community you may include it in their Service Plan. However, if the client fails to complete the activity you must not initiate an obligations failure.
For more information see:
- Process for deciding appropriate activities
- Work preparation obligations
- Work obligations
- Rehabilitation
- Activity Summary

chunks.title: Single and caring for an Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit child — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: A client who applies for or is getting Jobseeker Support, and also caring for a child aged under 14 years who meets the qualifications to get Orphan's Benefit or an Unsupported Child's Benefit, must meet the qualifications for Jobseeker Support to get this benefit. Many clients who apply for, or who are getting Jobseeker Support, and care for a child aged under 14 years for whom Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid, can meet the eligibility criteria to be willing and able, available and seeking full-time employment. In this case, they should be granted Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Cannot meet the eligibility criteria for Jobseeker Support — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If the client is not willing and able, or available for and actively seeking full-time work because of their caring duties, then they do not qualify for Jobseeker Support. Clients who are in this position and are single or are sole parents whose own dependent children are aged 14 years or over will need to assess their entitlement to other financial assistance.

chunks.title: Things to consider when discussing benefit options with the client — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: When discussing the benefit options available to a client, you need to consider the impact the benefit type has on other types of assistance and obligations. For more information see: - Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit Other benefit assistance

chunks.title: Consider if appropriate to include Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit child in Sole Parent Support — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Generally, a client is only eligible for Sole Parent Support if they have at least one dependent child aged less than 14 years. Once their youngest dependent child is 14 years or older, they will automatically transfer to Jobseeker Support. It may be appropriate to include the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit child into the client's benefit as the client's dependent child. A sole parent whose own dependent children are aged 14 or over, or a single client caring for one or more Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit children may be able to include one or more of the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit children as their own in Sole Parent Support . They cannot continue to get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for children who are included in their Sole Parent Support although they may decide to exclude the child in the future and get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit instead. For more information see: - Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit Getting UCB/OB for a child after the child has been included in a benefit

chunks.title: Two or more Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit children — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Where a single client is caring for two or more Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit children, the client may consider including the youngest child into the client's benefit as their own and being granted or transferring to Sole Parent Support. They can continue to receive Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit payments for the other child or children.

chunks.title: Not appropriate to include Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child Benefit child as a dependent child in Sole Parent Support — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If it is considered not appropriate to include the child as their own dependent child, their eligibility to Emergency Benefit, on the grounds of hardship, should be considered. For more information see: - Emergency Benefit Single and caring for a child

chunks.title: Situations where extensions can be given — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Situations where extensions can be given
Generally, all clients (and partners, if any) getting Jobseeker Support need to complete the reapplication process before their expiry date.
If a client does not complete the reapplication process before their expiry date their Jobseeker Support will stop, as they will no longer be entitled to get it.
There are limited situations where a client may complete the reapplication process on or after their expiry date and have their Jobseeker Support regranted. These are:
- when a client makes contact to reapply before their expiry date but the reapplication process cannot be completed before the expiry date through no fault of the client
- when a client has an exceptional circumstance that has affected their ability to reapply or contact MSD before their expiry date.
For more information see:
- Contact made but reapplication not completed before expiry date
- Exceptional circumstances for reapplication
## Client does not qualify for extension
If the client does not qualify for an extension but still needs Jobseeker Support, they must apply as a new applicant. Their expired benefit must be cancelled from their expiry date before they can be granted Jobseeker Support as a new applicant.
They will be subject to the usual commencement date rules, including the initial stand-down.
For more information see:
- Commencement date
- Initial stand-down
Note if the client advises they want to apply for Jobseeker Support as a new applicant and completes the reapplication form, MSD can use their reapplication form as their new application.

chunks.title: Skilled/Business Stream — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Skilled/Business Stream
The purpose of the Skilled/Business stream is to help talented and entrepreneurial migrants gain residence in New Zealand. The categories in this stream are the:
- Skilled Migrant Category
- Business Categories (Long Term Business, Migrant Investment, Entrepreneur, Entrepreneur Plus, Employees of Relocating Businesses) and
- Residence from Work Categories (Talent (Accredited Employers), Talent (Arts, Culture, and Sports) and Long Term Skill Shortage List instructions)
For clients granted permanent residence under the Skilled/Business Stream the client has signed a Declaration of Personal Resources statement they have funds to support themselves and family (if any) for the first 2 years residence in New Zealand. Generally the client would have had a work/study visa for at least 2 years before permanent residence was granted.
## Exception
Clients granted permanent residence under the Skilled Migrant Category should already have had employment for their 5 years of residence in New Zealand.
Clients must have 2 years continuous residence in New Zealand to be entitled to Jobseeker Support. Until they have met this requirement Jobseeker Support on grounds of hardship may be considered.
Note if a client has permanent residence and already meets the 2 years continuous residence, assess the client for Jobseeker Support in usual manner.
Jobseeker Support on grounds of hardship is both income and asset tested. To assess a client's entitlement to Jobseeker Support confirmation of the client's income and assets declared on the application for permanent residence is required from Immigration New Zealand.
If the client has a change in personal resources, confirmation of that change is required.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support on grounds of hardship
- Change in personal resources

chunks.title: Social obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Social obligations
A client and their partner (if any) getting Jobseeker Support have social obligations that apply for each dependent child in their care. This includes any children for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid.
A client and their partner (if any) must take all reasonable steps to meet all of the social obligations that apply for each child. The social obligations that apply for each child depend on the age of the child.
When the client is in a relationship the social obligations apply to both the client and their partner.
When required, clients and their partner (if any) must take all reasonable steps to meet the following social obligations. The child must be:
- enrolled with a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner, or a medical practice that is part of a Primary Health Organisation and
- up-to-date with their core Well Child/Tamariki Ora checks (for children aged under 5 years) and
- enrolled in and attending 1 of the following from 3 years of age until they start school: an approved early childhood education programme orTe Kura (distance school) oranother approved parenting and early childhood home education programme
- an approved early childhood education programme or
- Te Kura (distance school) or
- another approved parenting and early childhood home education programme
- enrolled in and attending school from 5 or 6 years of age (depending on when they start school)
When required, a client and their partner (if any) must:
- attend and participate in interviews with MSD to discuss meeting their social obligations and
- advise on progress where they have not been able to meet their social obligations
A client is only required to meet social obligations from the time they begin to get a benefit. Clients in the process of applying for Jobseeker Support or who have a future commencement date of their Jobseeker Support are not required to meet their social obligations.
Clients are also not required to meet social obligations that would have been relevant prior to them getting a benefit.
For example a client who starts getting Jobseeker Support when their child is between 3 and 4 months old cannot be sanctioned for not having completed the core Well Child/Tamariki Ora checks a child should have at ages 4 to 6 weeks.

chunks.title: Social obligations recompliance (13 week non-entitlement period) — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a client or partner fails their obligations for a third time, their benefit is reduced or cancelled. For the client or partner to increase their benefit they must undertake a six week recompliance activity or programme of activities and reapply for a benefit. If the third obligation failure is a social obligation failure, the standard six week recompliance activities may not be appropriate as some partners do not have work obligations and cannot work or be in training for a period of 6 weeks. In this situation, a programme of short-term approved activities may be more appropriate for the client.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Short term approved activities to consider for a Jobseeker Support client with part-time work obligations and social obligations, where the third failure was a social obligations failure. Week 1 Take reasonable steps to talk to providers of an appropriate recognised early childhood education programme Week 2 Take reasonable steps to enrol their child in a recognised early childhood education programme Week 3 CV seminar Week 4 Attend presentation seminar approved by Work and Income Week 5 Attend a local parenting programme that provides support for families Week 6 Meet with case manager to talk about what reasonable steps have been taken to enrol the child in a recognised early childhood education programme and discuss how the other activities went Week 1 Take reasonable steps to talk to providers of an appropriate recognised early childhood education programme Week 2 Take reasonable steps to enrol their child in a recognised early childhood education programme Week 3 CV seminar Week 4 Attend presentation seminar approved by Work and Income Week 5 Attend a local parenting programme that provides support for families Week 6 Meet with case manager to talk about what reasonable steps have been taken to enrol the child in a recognised early childhood education programme and discuss how the other activities went Note a programme of suitable activities for a client with part-time work obligations should be: - for no more than 15 hours per week for clients with limited capacity to work because of a health condition, injury or disability - for no more than 20 hours per week for all other clients with part-time work obligations

chunks.title: Example 2 — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Example of short term approved activities to consider for a Jobseeker Support client with social obligations, where the third failure was a social obligations failure. Week 1 Make contact with the local Family Start whanau worker and arrange a meeting with them Week 2 Family Start whanau worker visit Week 3 Contact a Well Child/Tamariki Ora provider and arrange a visit Week 4 Contact the local medical centre to ensure the children are enrolled in primary health care Week 5 Talk to appropriate providers of recognised early childhood education programmesWell Child/Tamariki Ora provider visit Week 6 Meet with a case manager about what steps have been taken Week 1 Make contact with the local Family Start whanau worker and arrange a meeting with them Week 2 Family Start whanau worker visit Week 3 Contact a Well Child/Tamariki Ora provider and arrange a visit Week 4 Contact the local medical centre to ensure the children are enrolled in primary health care Week 5 Talk to appropriate providers of recognised early childhood education programmes Well Child/Tamariki Ora provider visit Week 6 Meet with a case manager about what steps have been taken

chunks.title: Sole parents with sanction applied — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Sole parents with sanction applied
Sole parents and single clients getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit who have any sanction imposed will be sent the "notice to reapply" letter. They must complete the reapplication process before their expiry date to continue getting Jobseeker Support.
When sole parents and single clients getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit fail their obligations and have a sanction imposed, their benefit remains current because 50% protection applies.
Note if the client completes their reapplication before the expiry date and their Jobseeker Support is regranted, the financial or non-financial sanction will continue to apply to the regranted benefit until they recomply.

chunks.title: Special circumstances justifying delay in activity obligation — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Special circumstances justifying delay in activity obligation
A young partner may have special circumstances that justify not having to attend a Teen Parent Unit when their youngest dependent child is 6 months old even if there is a suitable place available.
Special circumstances include, but are not limited to, the:
- young partner's child having an uncontrolled health condition, such as asthma, or the child having special needs
- young partner’s ability to return to school because of a health condition or disability
- young partner struggling with the challenge of being a new parent (supported by information received from their Well Child/Tamariki Ora or a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner) and returning to education or training being detrimental to them and/or their child
- young partner having difficulty bonding with their child (supported by information received from their Well Child/Tamariki Ora or a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner) and returning to education or training being detrimental to them and/or their child
- dynamics with the other participants of the Teen Parent Unit making the young partner's attendance at the Teen Parent Unit inappropriate
## Special circumstances exist
If the service provider or MSD are satisfied there are special circumstances that justify the delay in the obligation to return to education at the Teen Parent Unit, the obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning would apply from the earliest of either:
- a suitable place becoming available and there no longer being special circumstances that delay the obligation to return to education at the Teen Parent Unit or
- the young partner's youngest child reaching the age of 12 months

chunks.title: Special Needs Grants for strikers — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Special Needs Grants for strikers
Where hardship has been established, you can provide assistance by way of a Special Needs Grant if there are dependent children. These have to be approved by a manager client service delivery and except when the client is a sole parent, payment must be made to the partner of the striking employee.
It is important to establish that a client:
- is not receiving any payment or assistance from their union or from any other source and
- must be able to prove that they require immediate financial assistance and have no cash assets
Use the Special Needs Grant provision sparingly and only in cases where the industrial dispute is obviously placing the family in desperate financial difficulties. You must tell the client that the grant is not to replace income or wages lost as a result of the dispute, and that they will have to repay it.
The maximum amount payable must not be more than the under 25 year old rate of the Jobseeker Support. Also see:
## Single clients on strike
Special Needs Grant assistance for single clients on strike can only be considered under the Serious Hardship provisions.
However, being on strike should not be considered an exceptional circumstance in itself.

chunks.title: Specific eligibility engagement — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Specific eligibility engagements are engagements that clients have with MSD in the 13 weeks before their expiry date that satisfy the eligibility part of the reapplication. This is because they capture information that can be used to confirm that the client still qualifies for Jobseeker Support. Specific eligibility engagements include (but are not limited to): - applying for and being granted certain assistance such as: Temporary Additional SupportAccommodation SupplementChildcare Subsidy or OSCAR subsidy (except when the client is getting Jobseeker Support on the grounds of hardship)some types of hardship assistance, such as a Special Needs Grant - Temporary Additional Support - Accommodation Supplement - Childcare Subsidy or OSCAR subsidy (except when the client is getting Jobseeker Support on the grounds of hardship) - some types of hardship assistance, such as a Special Needs Grant - applying for social housing and being added to the Social Housing register, - participating in active case management and has an assigned case manager - assigned work obligations because they no longer have a health condition, injury or disability that limits their capacity to work full-time - any interaction with MSD in which qualifications for Jobseeker Support are reviewed and continued eligibility is confirmed For more information see: - Granting on ground of hardship - Specific Engagements [no link find out why] Doogle

chunks.title: Clients with partners — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Specific eligibility engagements may be completed by the client or their partner (if any included in their Jobseeker Support) for the 26 week reapplication. This means that if a client or their partner completes a specific eligibility engagement in the 13 weeks before their expiry date, both the client and their partner are considered to have satisfied the eligibility part of the reapplication. If a specific eligibility engagement has not been completed by the client or the partner in the 13 weeks before their expiry date, they must both complete the eligibility part of the reapplication.

chunks.title: Specific eligibility engagement has been completed — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a client or their partner has completed a specific eligibility engagement in the 13 weeks before their expiry date, they will only need to complete the remaining parts of the reapplication when they reapply: - confirm if there have been any changes in their circumstances since they completed a specific eligibility engagement, and - participate in and complete an employment engagement (where appropriate) and - agree to their obligations and confirm their intent to reapply for Jobseeker Support. Example Asha's Jobseeker Support commenced on 15 August 2025, with her partner Shea included in her benefit. Her expiry date is 13 February 2026. She and her partner have full-time work obligations. In January 2026, Asha applies for Social Housing. As part of the assessment of eligibility, MSD checks Asha's and her partner's combined income and assets, and Asha confirms information about their relationship. Asha and Shea are added to the social housing register on 15 January 2026. From the information provided for the Social Housing application, MSD can confirm that Asha continues to meet the qualifications for Jobseeker Support. Because Asha had this specific eligibility engagement in the 13 weeks before her expiry date and covered information about both herself and her partner, the engagement satisfies the eligibility part of the reapplication. If Asha still needs Jobseeker Support in February 2026 she and her partner only need to confirm if there have been any changes in their circumstances since they completed a specific eligibility engagement, complete the employment part of the reapplication, agree to their obligations and confirm their intent to reapply for Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: Specific eligibility engagement has not been completed — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a client or their partner have not completed a specific eligibility engagement in the 13 weeks before their expiry date, they must complete the eligibility part of the reapplication when they reapply. Example Jai's Jobseeker Support commenced on 28 October 2026. His expiry date is 28 April 2027. On 1 March 2027 Jai applies for Disability Allowance. Jai provides MSD with his Disability Allowance application form, his Disability Allowance medical certificate and verification of his costs. MSD grants his Disability Allowance without needing to get in touch with Jai, and his Disability Allowance commences on 12 March 2027. Because Jai is getting Jobseeker Support, his Disability Allowance is not income tested. This means MSD cannot confirm that Jai meets all the qualifications for Jobseeker Support based on his Disability Allowance being granted. This is not a specific eligibility engagement for the purposes of the 26 week reapplication. If Jai still needs Jobseeker Support in April 2027 and has not completed any other specific eligibility engagements, he will need to complete all parts of the 26 week reapplication process.

chunks.title: Specific employment engagement — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Specific employment engagements are engagements clients have with MSD in the 13 weeks before their expiry date that satisfy the employment part of the reapplication. This is because they are discussions with MSD about what the client is doing or needs to do to find or prepare for suitable employment. Specific employment engagements include (but are not limited to): - engaging with MSD to apply for jobs (e.g. has been referred to a vacancy by MSD) - participating in one of MSD's employment services (e.g. Rapid Return to Work) - discussing job search activities with MSD as part of recomplying a work obligations failure - participating in active case management and has an assigned case manager - getting Course Participation Assistance or Training Incentive Allowance to undertake employment-related education or training - discussing what steps they need to take to move towards or into work with MSD and what supports they need from MSD - participating in an engagement that is considered suitable for improving their work readiness, such as discussing their job search activities or help with removing barriers that prevent work readiness. For more information see: - Specific Engagements [no link find out why] Doogle

chunks.title: Clients with partners — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Employment engagements only count for the person who completes the engagement. This means that specific employment engagements must be completed by the client and their partner separately. If a client has completed a specific employment engagement in the 13 weeks before their expiry date, only the client is considered to have met the employment part of the reapplication. The partner must complete the employment part of the reapplication separately.

chunks.title: Specific employment engagement has been completed — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a client or their partner has completed a specific employment engagement in the 13 weeks before their expiry date, that person will only need to complete the remaining parts of the reapplication when they reapply: - confirm their circumstances for the purposes of an eligibility check and - agree to their obligations and confirm their intent to reapply for Jobseeker Support Example Hana's Jobseeker Support commenced on 23 February 2026, with her partner included in her benefit. Her expiry date is 24 August 2026. She and her partner have full-time work obligations. On 18 June 2026, Hana contacts MSD about potential job opportunities in her area and MSD refers her to a vacancy. Hana applies for the role but is unsuccessful. From the conversation held on 18 June 2026 about her job search MSD can confirm that Hana is available for and seeking full-time employment. She is also taking reasonable steps to find work and is willing and able to undertake employment. As this specific engagement happened in the 13 weeks before her expiry date, the engagement satisfies her employment part of the reapplication. If Hana still needs Jobseeker Support in August 2026 she will only need to complete the eligibility part of the reapplication, agree to her obligations and confirm her intent to reapply. Hana's partner had no engagements with MSD recently and attends an appointment with MSD to discuss their job search activities and any support they need from MSD. At the appointment the partner also completes the eligibility part of the reapplication, agrees to their obligations and confirms their intent to reapply. For more information see: - Specific engagements - Completing the 26 week reapplication process

chunks.title: Specific employment engagement has not been completed — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: If a client or their partner have not completed a specific employment engagement in the 13 weeks before their expiry date, they must complete the employment part of the reapplication when they reapply. During the notice period if the client or partner still need to complete the employment part of the reapplication, they may need to attend an appointment or seminar. The client and their partner will still need to complete the employment part of the reapplication before their expiry date. If they do not do this, their benefit will stop. This applies even if one person in the couple has completed their reapplication process on time. Note not all clients and partners need to complete the employment part of the reapplication. For more information see: - Effect on payments due to not completing the reapplication process - Employment part of the 26 week reapplication - Employment part of the reapplication not required Example Nahani's Jobseeker Support commenced on 8 December 2025, with their partner included in their benefit. Their expiry date is 8 June 2026. Nahani and their partner both have full-time work obligations. Nahani and their partner attend a work seminar soon after they start getting Jobseeker Support. However, they have no other interactions with MSD. On 1 May 2026 they are sent a letter advising what they and their partner need to do to complete their reapplication. Because they have had no employment engagements with MSD recently (in the last 13 weeks), both Nahani and their partner attend an appointment with MSD to discuss their job search activities and any support they need from us (such as help with removing barriers preventing work readiness). They also complete the eligibility part of the reapplication, agree to their obligations, and confirm their intention to reapply.

chunks.title: Specific engagement completed for both eligibility and employment — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Specific engagement completed for both eligibility and employment
If a client (and their partner if any included in their Jobseeker Support) have satisfied both the eligibility and employment parts of the reapplication through specific engagements, they only need to confirm whether they have had any changes in their circumstances since those specific engagements, agree to their obligations and confirm their intention to reapply to complete the reapplication.
