They must: - be enrolled in and undertaking, or be available for, a full-time course of secondary or tertiary education, or approved training or work-based learning leading to a NCEA level 2 qualification or an equivalent or higher qualification - when required to, participate in and complete an approved budgeting programme - when required to, participate satisfactorily in an approved parenting education programme - report to their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service on progress in meeting their education, parenting and budgeting obligations (above) as often as required - when required to, attend and participate in regular budgeting discussions with their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service - when required to, attend and participate in any interview with their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service - when asked, provide within 20 working days, to their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service, details of the young person's accommodation costs, service costs and lawful debts or other liabilities - co-operate with their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service in managing the spending of their benefit or portion of benefit and - attend and participate in regular discussions on budgeting at any discussion, or when asked, provide details on their: accommodation costs and service costs such as power and phonelawful debts and liabilitieshow they spent any in-hand allowance and any money credited to their payment card or any other device - accommodation costs and service costs such as power and phone - lawful debts and liabilities - how they spent any in-hand allowance and any money credited to their payment card or any other device A young partner with a dependent child or children also has the following obligations. They must: - enrol their child with a Primary Health Organisation, where a local provider is available - keep their child or children under the age of 5 years up-to-date with their Well Child/Tamariki Ora checks - ensure their child's attendance at an approved Early Childhood Education (ECE) programme or other suitable childcare, while they are participating in education, training, work-based learning or part-time work These obligations apply from the time the benefit is first paid except where the young partner is caring for a child aged under 12 months. For more information see:

chunks.title: Young partner (with dependent children) turns 20 years old — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Generally, when a young partner with a dependent child or children turns 20 years old the youth activity obligations no longer apply. However, there are 2 situations where the obligations will continue to apply after they turn 20 years old. These are where a young partner: - is aged under 20 years when they first have youth activity obligations applied and must undertake Youth Activity obligations for a minimum of 6 months, even if they turn 20 years during this period - chooses to continue to have youth activity obligations so they can remain in education, training or work-based learning When a young partner with a dependent child or children reaches the age of 20 and has already had youth activity obligations for 6 months and does not choose to continue to have these obligations because they are not in education, training or work-based learning, the youth activity obligations no longer apply. Instead they will have the work or work preparation obligations applicable for their main benefit.

chunks.title: Choose to have Youth Activity obligations past 20 years of age — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Generally, when a young partner turns 20 years old the obligations for them to comply with youth activity obligations will no longer apply. However, to give a young partner a chance to complete the qualification they have started while having Youth Activity obligations, a young partner can choose to continue to have youth activity obligations and continue to participate in the Youth Service after they turn 20 if they remain in education, training or work-based learning. Attending secondary school When a young partner reaches the age of 20 years and is attending secondary school they will continue to have Youth Activity obligations and continue to participate in the Youth Service until the following 31 March. For example, a young partner attending school who turns 20 years old in June will continue in the Youth Service until the following 31 March. Attending tertiary education, training or work-based learning When a young partner is attending tertiary education, training or work-based learning and they turn 20 years old, they may choose to continue to have youth activity obligations and participate in the Youth Service until the course finishes, unless their course ends in December. If their course ends in December, they will continue to have youth activity obligations and participate in the Youth Service until 31 March the following year. Examples: - a young partner is part-way through a training course when they turn 20 years old. The training course finishes on 20 November. The young partner will be exited from the Youth Service on 21 November - a young partner is part-way through a training course when they turn 20 years old. The training course finishes on 20 December. The young partner will continue to have Youth Activity obligations and remain in the Youth Service until the following 31 March

chunks.title: Must have Youth Activity obligations for 6 months — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: A young partner who is aged under 20 years when they first have Youth Activity obligations applied must undertake these obligations for a minimum of 6 months, even if they turn 20 during this period. This ensures that the young partner is able to have a reasonable chance to move towards a qualification by participating in education, training or work-based learning and other youth activity obligations before they focus on obligations attached to other main benefits. For example, a young partner first has Youth Activity obligations applied at the age of 19 years and 8 months old. When they turn 20 years old they will need to continue to have these Youth Activity obligations and participate in the Youth Service for another 2 months to complete the 6 month minimum period. After this point, the Youth Activity obligations will no longer apply and instead they will have the work obligations applicable to main benefit (unless they choose to continue to have Youth Activity obligations because they are in education, training or work-based learning). For more information see: - Deciding education, training or work-based learning activities - Approved budgeting programme activity - Report to service provider or Work and Income on progress - Money management activity - Youth activity obligations failures - Parenting obligations - Work or work preparation obligations

chunks.title: Young partner without children — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Young partners aged 16 or 17 years old without dependent children have the following youth activity obligations. They must: - be enrolled in and undertaking, or be available for, a full-time course of secondary or tertiary education, or approved training or work-based learning leading to a NCEA level 2 qualification or an equivalent or higher qualification - when required to, participate in and complete an approved budgeting programme - report to their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service on progress in meeting their education and budgeting obligations (above) as often as required - when required to, attend and participate in regular budgeting discussions with their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service - when required to, attend and participate in any interview with their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service - when asked, provide within 20 working days, to their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service, details of the young person's accommodation costs, service costs and lawful debts or other liabilities - co-operate with their service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service in managing the spending of their benefit or portion of benefit and - attend and participate in regular discussions on budgeting at any discussion, or when asked, provide details on their: accommodation costs and service costs such as power and phonelawful debts and liabilitieshow they spent any in-hand allowance and any money credited to their payment card or any other device - accommodation costs and service costs such as power and phone - lawful debts and liabilities - how they spent any in-hand allowance and any money credited to their payment card or any other device The activity obligations cannot be enforced until the main benefit commencement date.

chunks.title: Young partner (no dependent children) turns 18 years old — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Generally, when a young partner with no dependent children turns 18 years old the youth activity obligations no longer apply. However, there are two situations where the obligations will continue to apply after they turn 18 years old. These are where a young partner: - is aged under 18 years when they first have youth activity obligations applied and must undertake Youth Activity obligations for a minimum of 6 months, even if they turn 18 years during this 6 month period - chooses to continue to have youth activity obligations so they can remain in education, training or work-based learning When a young partner reaches the age of 18 years and has already had youth activity obligations for 6 months and does not choose to continue to have these obligations because they are not in education, training or work-based learning, the youth activity obligations no longer apply. Instead they will have the work obligations applicable to the main benefit.

chunks.title: Choose to have youth activity obligations past 18 years of age — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: Generally, when a young partner turns 18 years old the obligations for them to comply with Youth Activity obligations will no longer apply. However, to give a young partner a chance to complete the qualification they have started while having youth activity obligations, a young partner can choose to continue to have youth activity obligations and continue to participate in the Youth Service after they turn 18 years old if they remain in education, training or work-based learning. Attending secondary school When a young partner reaches the age of 18 years and is attending secondary school they will continue to have youth activity obligations and continue to participate in the Youth Service until the following 31 March. For example, a young partner attending school who turns 18 years old in June will continue in the Youth Service until the following 31 March. Attending tertiary education, training or work-based learning When a young partner is attending tertiary education, training or work-based learning and they turn 18 years old, they may continue to have youth activity obligations and continue to participate in the Youth Service until their course finishes, unless their course ends in December. If their course ends in December, they will continue to have youth activity obligations and participate in the Youth Service until 31 March the following year. Examples: - a young partner is part-way through a training course when they turn 18 years old. The training course finishes on 20 November. The young partner will be exited from the Youth Service on 21 November - a young partner is part-way through a training course when they turn 18 years old. The training course finishes on 20 December. The young partner will continue to have Youth Activity obligations and remain in the Youth Service until the following 31 March

chunks.title: Must have Youth Activity obligations for 6 months — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text: A young partner who is aged under 18 years when they first have Youth Activity obligations applied must undertake these obligations for a minimum of 6 months even if they turn 18 years old during this period. This ensures that the young partner is able to have a reasonable chance to move towards a qualification by participating in education, training or work-based learning and other youth activity obligations before they focus on obligations attached to other main benefits. For example, a young partner first has Youth Activity obligations applied at the age of 17 years and 8 months old. When they turn 18 years old they will need to continue to have these Youth Activity obligations and participate in the Youth Service for another 2 months to complete the 6 month minimum period. After this point, the youth activity obligations will no longer apply and instead they will have the work obligations applicable as the partner of a Jobseeker Support client (unless they choose to continue to have youth activity obligations because they are in education, training or work-based learning). For more information see: - Deciding education, training or work-based learning activities - Approved budgeting programme activity - Report to service provider or Work and Income on progress - Money management activity - Youth activity obligations failures

chunks.title: Young partners would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Young partners would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability
If a young partner meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability, they can be exempt from meeting some or all of their activity obligations until their capacity for education, training and work-based learning improves.
The young partner must be limited in their capacity to undertake activities because of a health condition, injury or disability.
If the young partner is partially exempt they are able to:
- plan for education, training or work-based learning and
- undertake other activities such as budgeting
If a young partner qualifies for a full exemption this means they are unable to meet any of their activity obligations, including planning.
## Evidence
To support their exemption, the young partner must provide a medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist or midwife where relevant).
The information required on the medical certificate includes:
- a diagnosis (what the illness is) and
- the impact of the condition on their ability to undertake activity obligations and
- the likely duration of the impact and
- their capacity for education, training and work-based learning and
- any other information that is required
## Duration
This exemption is initially granted until the earlier of either:
- 13 weeks or
- the next reassessment date recorded by the registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist or midwife where relevant) on the medical certificate
This exemption should then be reviewed.
At the review MSD should consider the young partner's circumstances and whether it is appropriate to extend the exemption. MSD can ask the young partner to provide evidence that their exemption should be extended.

chunks.title: Young partners would qualify for Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Young partners would qualify for Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability
If a young partner meets the qualifications for Supported Living Payment on the ground of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness, they can be exempt from meeting some or all of their activity obligations.
The young partner must be:
- both permanently and severely restricted in their capacity for education, training and work-based learning because of a health condition, or injury or disability from an accident, or condition they have had since birth or
- totally blind
Note totally blind and legally blind are not the same.
For more information see:
- Supported Living Payment
This can be a full or partial exemption depending on the whether the young partner can plan for a return to education, training or work-based learning.
MSD should discuss with the young partner whether they can still:
- plan for education, training or work-based learning and
- undertake other activities such as budgeting
If it is unclear whether a full or partial exemption should be granted seek advice from the Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor.
Note when appropriate MSD should consider the young partner's eligibility for Supported Living Payment.
## Evidence
The young partner must provide either a medical certificate or medical information signed by a registered medical practitioner, nurse practitioner or psychologist stating:
- a diagnosis (what the illness is) and
- the impact of the condition on their ability to undertake activities and
- the likely duration of the impact and
- their capacity for planning and undertaking activities part-time and
- any other information that is required

chunks.title: Youngest dependent child is aged under 12 months — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Youngest dependent child is aged under 12 months
Youth activity obligations apply from the time the benefit is first paid except where the young partner is caring for their youngest dependent child, and that child is aged under 12 months old.
In these cases, the obligation to be in or available for full-time education, training or work-based learning begins to apply on the earlier of:
- the day the child becomes six months old if there is a suitable place available for the young partner in a teen parent unit andthe Chief Executive is satisfied that there are no special circumstances justifying the obligation starting at a later date
- if there is a suitable place available for the young partner in a teen parent unit and
- the Chief Executive is satisfied that there are no special circumstances justifying the obligation starting at a later date
or
- the day on which the child becomes 12 months old
For more information see:
- Deciding if suitable place at Teen Parent Unit available
- Special circumstances justifying delay in activity obligation
- Deciding education, training and work-based learning activities
- Parenting obligations
- Exemptions for young partners

chunks.title: Youth activity obligations — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Youth activity obligations
A young partner is subject to youth activity obligations instead of work or work preparation obligations if they are:
- aged 16 or 17 years old without dependent children or
- aged 16 to 19 years old with a dependent child and
- married, in a civil union, or de facto relationship with a person getting Jobseeker Support
Note young partners may qualify for an exemption from some or all obligations if it is unreasonable to expect them to meet their obligations for a specified period.
## Aged 16 or 17 in a de facto relationship
A 16 or 17 year old can only be treated as in a de facto relationship if they have an order from a Family Court Judge giving consent for the de facto relationship. This applies even when the couple has a dependent child.

chunks.title: Youth activity obligations failures — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Youth activity obligations failures
If a young partner fails to comply with their youth activity obligations, an activity obligations failure needs to be considered.
The service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service:
- must be satisfied the young partner would have had no good and sufficient reason for their failure and
- if the young partner has no good and sufficient reason, recommend an activity obligations failure be imposed
The Youth Service Support Unit (YSSU):
- makes the decision to apply a sanction, based on the recommendation of the service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service and
- initiates the activity obligations failure in the system
If it is decided that the young partner has failed their activity obligations, the YSSU will initiate an activity obligations failure. The young partner will then be notified by text message (where they have consented to be contacted in this way) or letter that:
- an obligations failure has occurred
- a sanction has been imposed and
- they have 5 working days to recomply before their payments are affected
All young people have a 5 working day notice period to dispute or recomply before the sanction is imposed. If a young person recomplies within the 5 working day notice period their benefit is not sanctioned but the activity obligations failure is recorded.

chunks.title: Course information — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Course information
Youth Guarantee is an education initiative for students. The courses are level 1-3 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF). The courses provide students with knowledge and information on vocational pathways, and contain a mix of practical, specific and general skill development.
For more information see:
- Tertiary Education Commission Youth Guarantee
- Approved training (young partners)

chunks.title: Youth money management — main benefits > jobseeker support
chunks.text:
## Youth money management
Youth money management is when a young partner gets an in-hand allowance of up to $50 a week, with most of their benefit payment being redirected to pay for their everyday living costs and any lawful debts. Any remainder is placed onto their payment card.
A young partner who is required to be youth money managed cannot review the decision on how their benefit payment (or their portion of the benefit payment) is paid to them.
## No longer subject to youth money management
A young partner aged 16 or 17 years (with no children) or 16 to 19 years (with dependent children) will not be subject to youth money management and will have their full payment paid directly to them when they have:
- demonstrated continued compliance with their obligations and been assessed as being financially competent or
- opted out of youth money management because they turned 18 years (for young partners without dependent children) and have chosen to stay in the Youth Service and complete their course of study, training or work-based learning

chunks.title: Abbeyfield houses — main benefits > new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Abbeyfield houses
Abbeyfield is an incorporated, non-profit organisation that provides housing for older people.
An Abbeyfield house is styled as a large family home, where each of the eight to ten residents has a separate bedroom with ensuite facilities. A live-in housekeeper/cook prepares the main meals and cares generally for the residents.
A client living in an Abbeyfield house may receive the single living alone rate as long as they meet the definition of living alone and the Abbeyfield house meets the definition of a boarding house.
Abbeyfield residents may also receive an Accommodation Supplement provided they meet the usual criteria.

chunks.title: ACC weekly compensation and grandparented non-qualified partner included — main benefits > new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## ACC weekly compensation and grandparented non-qualified partner included
When a client (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) gets weekly compensation from ACC, these payments are charged as income.

chunks.title: Age — main benefits > new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Age
Clients must be 65 years old to meet the age qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
The applicants age must be verified before New Zealand Superannuation is granted.

chunks.title: Amount of income exemption — main benefits > new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Amount of income exemption
When you have determined that a client is severely disabled you must then consider if they should have all or part of their income from employment disregarded for benefit purposes.
The amount of the income exemption depends on the client's individual circumstances after considering the guidelines - for severe disablement and should be:
- a reasonable amount as an incentive to recognise the personal effort that a severely disabled person has made to participate or continue in employment
- any additional costs that a severely disabled person has incurred to participate or continue in employment
- a reasonable amount to ensure that a severely disabled person is not disadvantaged by participating or continuing in employment
Note the client may be entitled to receive other types of assistance, for example Disability Allowance for transport costs to work or employment assistance.
Fully document your decision by recording the reasons and the amount of the exemption in the CMS note template, Income exemption amount.
Contact Helpline if you need help with the assessment.

chunks.title: Bank account — main benefits > new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Bank account
Unless there are special circumstances, it is a condition of New Zealand Superannuation that the client provides or opens a bank account or membership to a credit union to receive their New Zealand Superannuation payment.
## Bank
An appropriate bank is:
- a private savings bank, a trustee savings bank, or The Co-operative Bank Limited (formerly the Public Service Investment Society, or PSIS)
- a registered bank which on the 31st March 1987 was a trading bank or
- any other registered bank or a building society approved by the Minister after consultation with the Minister of Finance

chunks.title: Boarding houses — main benefits > new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Boarding houses
Clients living alone in a room in a boarding house can receive the single living alone rate, as long as all other qualifications are met.
This can include houses that are styled as a large family home where the residents have a separate bedroom along with facilities for communal use by all the other residents, such as Abbeyfield Houses or some Selwyn Foundation community houses.
If you are unsure whether the premises meet the definition of a boarding house contact Helpline for advice.

chunks.title: Boats — main benefits > new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Boats
Clients, who are living alone on a boat or craft moored within New Zealand, can receive the single living alone rate as long as all other qualifications are met. In this situation, New Zealand includes:
- the territorial sea around New Zealand and
- lakes, rivers, estuaries within New Zealand
The boat does not have to remain in the same location.

chunks.title: Caravan parks and motor camps — main benefits > new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Caravan parks and motor camps
A client living alone in a caravan park, motor camp or camping ground may qualify for a single living alone rate of New Zealand Superannuation.
This accommodation includes cabins, flats and caravans. The unit of accommodation does not have to be self-contained, the client can share facilities.
## Travelling between caravan parks or motor camps
A client travelling between different motor camps or caravan parks would need to be living in a self-contained mobile home (caravan, house bus etc) to remain eligible for this rate.

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation in their own right can be absent from New Zealand and keep getting their payments for up to 26 weeks.
If a client is overseas for more than 30 weeks, they do not qualify for New Zealand Superannuation from when they left New Zealand.
However, they may qualify for the payments they got for the first 26 weeks if the client's return to New Zealand is delayed due to circumstances beyond the client's control, that could not have be expected before their departure.
For grandparented couples getting the non-qualified partner rate of New Zealand Superannuation, the grandparented rate ends if the qualified partner is absent from New Zealand, and they do not qualify for payment during the period of absence or any part of the absence from New Zealand. See: Effect of absence overseas on grandparented clients.
The client must remain ordinarily resident during any absence from New Zealand.
Clients may continue getting payment for a longer period if the reason they are overseas is for:
- Overseas medical treatment
- Humanitarian work
## Single living alone rate
The single living alone rate can keep being paid for absences overseas of up to 26 weeks if the client still qualifies.
## Extra help
Clients who are absent from New Zealand can keep getting their ongoing payments for 28 days.
Extra help cannot continue for more than 28 days when the client is absent from New Zealand. See: Absence from New Zealand in the relevant Extra help.
## Mandatory Review while overseas
Only clients getting New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included have a Mandatory Review for their New Zealand Superannuation.
However, all New Zealand Superannuation clients getting Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance have a Mandatory Review for this assistance.
Clients who are overseas must still respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or the assistance being reviewed will suspend.
Temporary absence from New Zealand (e.g. personal travel or humanitarian work) does not pause or defer the Mandatory Review.
Clients must contact MSD before their review date to talk about their situation if they are unable to respond to the review or if they need more time to do it.

chunks.title: Payment to continue — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Payment to continue
Where you have confirmed the client will be absent for less than 26 weeks make full notes in CMS. This is important for anyone else looking at the client's record, for example the National Data Match Centre.
You will also need to create a bring-up on BRUPA screen for the expected date of return to check that the client has returned.
Advise the client to contact the Ministry of Social Development to confirm their return to New Zealand.
## Payment will not continue
Where the client is leaving New Zealand permanently or for more than 26 weeks the case is usually referred to International Services

chunks.title: Action on return to New Zealand — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Action on return to New Zealand
The action to take will depend on how long the client was overseas.
## 26 weeks or less
The absence will not have effected payments.
## Between 26 and 30 weeks
Payment for the pay days that fall within the first 26 weeks of absence can be confirmed. In no circumstances should payment continue beyond 26 weeks.
If the qualified client of a grandparented non-qualified couple is absent for more than 26 weeks the grandparented non-qualified partner rate will end. If the qualified client is entitled to payment for the first 26 weeks, the grandparented rate will end from the beginning of the 27th week of absence.
## More than 30 weeks
If the client was overseas for 30 weeks or more there is no qualification from when the client left New Zealand unless the client's return to New Zealand was delayed due to circumstances beyond the client's control that could not have been foreseen before departure.
If the qualified client of a grandparented non-qualified couple is absent for more than 26 weeks the grandparented non-qualified partner rate will end. If the qualified client is unavoidably delayed but entitled to payment for the first 26 weeks of their absence the grandparented rate will end from the beginning of the 27th week of their absence.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
As clients have an obligation to advise Senior Services of any changes that may affect the rate of payment of New Zealand Superannuation. It is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
When a client advises of a change in living situation more than 14 days after the event you should generally reduce New Zealand Superannuation from the actual date of the change in living situation and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising Senior Services of a change in living situation within 14 days you may reduce New Zealand Superannuation from the first available date.
## False or misleading information
If the client gives false or misleading information you must review New Zealand Superannuation from the actual date of the change in living situation and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Annual income due paid assessment over 27 September 2010 period — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Annual income due paid assessment over 27 September 2010 period
When completing a due paid assessment of New Zealand Superannuation over the 27 September 2010 period you need to:
1. Calculate the income deduction for the weeks prior to 27 September 2010.
2. Calculate the income deduction for the weeks from 27 September 2010.
3. Add the two deductions from step 1 and 2 together to get the annual income deduction.
The income to be charged for each of these periods must be totalled and compared with actual income for the year to establish whether an underpayment or overpayment has occurred.
## Annual income prior to 27 September 2010
Prior to 27 September 2010:
- income less than $4160 gross per year will not affect their benefit
- income over $4160 gross per year reduced benefit by 70 cents for every $1.00 of income
For more information see:
- Example of due paid assessment over 27 September 2010 period
- Charging income

chunks.title: SWIFTT — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT
You will need to cancel New Zealand Superannuation payments from the earliest possible date (but not more than 28 days after the date of death) in SBFTZ. However, the date of death entered in CMS must be the client's actual date of death. You must make full notes in CMS of your actions.
Wherever possible you should enter the next of kin or the executor of the deceased's estate on SWIFTT.
For more information see:
- Terminal benefit for a single client

chunks.title: Calculating the period of absence — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Calculating the period of absence
In all cases, when assessing the period of absence does not include:
- the date of departure from New Zealand and
- the date of return to New Zealand
As New Zealand Superannuation payments do not cover any specific period, you must look at the pay days that fall within the 26 weeks when confirming payment.

chunks.title: Change in living situation — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Change in living situation
MSD should review the rate of payment of New Zealand Superannuation whenever there is a change in the clients living situation such as:
- change in relationship status e.g. getting married, starting or ending a de facto relationship or a civil union which may affect a grandparented non-qualified partner or a partner getting a main benefit
- death of a partner
- partner enters long term residential care or hospital
- starts or stops living alone
- has a visitor who stays for more than 13 weeks in any 26 week period
- change in the number of children supported (child comes into or leaves their care)

chunks.title: Change of address — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Change of address
When a client advises that they have changed their address it is important to check that the move does not affect their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation.
If the client is receiving Extra Help this will also need to be reviewed to take into account their new costs.
If the client has a portion of their benefit paid to Kāinga Ora or Te Puni Kokiri this may need to be changed or cancelled.
The change of address may also indicate a change in the client's circumstances.
Examples of changes that may affect entitlement are:
- client or partner commences or ceases employment (grandparented non-qualified partner included)
- change of relationship status
- dependent children who have come into or left their care
For more information see:
- Payment
- Change in living situation
- Core policy Relationship status for benefit

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or the rate payable.
MSD may also review New Zealand Superannuation at any time to check that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment (if applicable).
## Mandatory Reviews for New Zealand Superannuation clients
Only clients getting New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included have a Mandatory Review for their New Zealand Superannuation.
Clients who do not have a non-qualified partner included in their benefit do not have a Mandatory Review for their New Zealand Superannuation.
However, all New Zealand Superannuation clients getting Disability Allowance or Accommodation Supplement have a Mandatory Review for this assistance.
Clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or the assistance being reviewed will suspend.

chunks.title: Surviving partner or dependent child — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Surviving partner or dependent child
When a client dies (and there is a surviving partner or dependent child) before a decision is made on an application or review for New Zealand Superannuation you can continue the application or review process as if the client had not died.
## Funeral Grant
In situations when the decision to grant or review New Zealand Superannuation is made after the date of death of the client, you decide any Funeral Grant as if the deceased client were in receipt of New Zealand Superannuation.

chunks.title: Client does not return — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Client does not return
If a client does not return to New Zealand payments must be cancelled from the day after the departure date.

chunks.title: Client donates a kidney or liver tissue — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Client donates a kidney or liver tissue
Clients receiving the New Zealand Superannuation can keep getting their payments if they are donating a kidney or liver tissue.
## Childcare assistance
Clients may be eligible for Childcare Assistance payments while they are recovering.
For more information and the additional qualifications see:
- Childcare Subsidy Temporary illness
- OSCAR Temporary illness
- Partner donates a kidney or liver tissue

chunks.title: Client or partner in prison — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Client or partner in prison
There is discretion to continue New Zealand Superannuation for clients in prison, for 2 instalments following imprisonment.
There is further discretion to continue payments beyond the initial 2 instalments where the Ministry of Social Development can pay all or part of the New Zealand Superannuation to:
- the partner of the person in prison
- any person responsible for the spouse or partner or any dependent children of the person in prison or
- to the client in prison beyond the 2 instalments that have already been paid
A decision on making payment beyond the date of imprisonment must consider the couples’ full circumstances.
## Grandparented non-qualifying partner included
When a client is imprisoned and has a grandparented non-qualified partner included in their New Zealand Superannuation, the New Zealand Superannuation will generally need to be cancelled from the day following imprisonment to enable the partner to get a benefit in their own right.
However, there is discretion to continue payment of the client's New Zealand Superannuation beyond the date of imprisonment.
Note if the grandparented non-qualified partner rate ends, the qualifying partner cannot get it again.
## Partner qualifies for New Zealand Superannuation
When a married, civil union or de facto client is imprisoned and has a partner who qualifies for New Zealand Superannuation in their own right, the client's New Zealand Superannuation will generally be stopped form the day following imprisonment. However, there is discretion to continue payment of the client's New Zealand Superannuation for two pay days after the date of imprisonment.

chunks.title: Clients on leave from hospital — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Clients on leave from hospital
New Zealand Superannuation is paid at the full rate for any period of leave from hospital. Where the client has been receiving the hospital rate increase their New Zealand Superannuation for any period they are on leave.
The action to take, on a client's re-admission to hospital, will depend on how long they were on leave.
## Effect of leave on thirteen week count
Any periods of leave from hospital of 28 days or less are to be ignored when deciding the date from which New Zealand Superannuation is to be reduced to the hospital rate. Calculate the period in hospital from the original admission date.
If the client has been allowed out of hospital for more than 28 days, the calculation of the 13 week period in hospital begins again after the client has been re-admitted.
For more information see:
- On leave for 28 days or less
- On leave for more than 28 days
- Weekend leave
- Discharge from hospital

chunks.title: Date payment should be reduced — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Date payment should be reduced
The hospital rate of payment is paid when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks not after receiving a benefit for 13 weeks.
Reduce the client's benefit to the hospital rate or appropriate higher rate from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation.
## Client in hospital when benefit commences
If the client has been in hospital for 13 weeks or more at the commencement date of the benefit, the rate of payment is the hospital rate or a higher rate (if applicable).
If the client has been in hospital for less than 13 weeks at the commencement date of the benefit, the full rate of payment is paid until the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation.
Note the date of admission and the date of discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital and are not included in the 13-week calculation.
## SWIFTT
Add the client's admission date on the SHODA screen. SWIFTT will automatically reduce the client's rate of payment to the hospital rate from the beginning of the 14th week after the admission date.
## Transfer between hospitals
Transfer from one hospital to another does not interrupt the period of hospitalisation, which can be taken as continuous from the original admission date. Ensure that SHODA is updated to show the new hospital details.
## Consider any short-term leave
Any periods out of hospital of 28 days or less are to be ignored when deciding the date from which the benefit is to be reduced. Calculate the period in hospital from the original admission date.
If the client has been allowed out of hospital for more than 28 days, the calculation of the period in hospital begins again after the client has been re-admitted.
## Client formally discharged
If the client has been formally discharged from the hospital and then re-admitted, the 13 week calculation starts again from the day after they are re-admitted (even if the client has been re-admitted within 28 days of being discharged).
For more information see:
- Discharged from hospital
- Clients on leave from hospital

chunks.title: Death of a client — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
The date payment stops following the death of a client depends on whether the client has:
- a partner or
- a dependent child
## Mandatory Reviews
There are no Mandatory Reviews when a client with a non-qualifying partner included in their New Zealand Superannuation has died.
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's New Zealand Superannuation when the child turns 18 during the terminal benefit period.

chunks.title: Death of a client with a partner or child — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: New Zealand Superannuation can continue to be paid for 28 days after the death of a client when there is a surviving partner or child, and the surviving partner (including a grandparented non-qualified partner) is not entitled to a survivor's grant from ACC. New Zealand Superannuation can also continue to be paid for 28 days following the death of a single client who is a: - liable person and paying Child Support payments or - caregiver getting Unsupported Child's Benefit or Orphan's Benefit Continuing payments after the date of death is known as terminal benefit. When New Zealand Superannuation is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person and the surviving partner's payment continues to be paid. The total amount, including the surviving partner's portion, plus any on-going extra help continues for 28 days.

chunks.title: Surviving partner will get more money on other assistance — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Sometimes the surviving person, or the caregiver of the child would get more money (based on their new circumstances) on: - a new main benefit or - their existing benefit or New Zealand Superannuation at a higher rate instead of getting their portion of their current assistance for 28 days.

chunks.title: New benefit paid at a higher rate — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If the surviving person’s New Zealand Superannuation or main benefit is reviewed and they qualify for a higher rate, they may be granted the new rate instead of terminal benefit from the day after a client's death. If the deceased person qualified for terminal benefit, their portion will continue to be paid.

chunks.title: Current benefit paid at a higher rate — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If the surviving person's New Zealand Superannuation or main benefit is reviewed and they qualify for a higher rate, their rate increases from the day after their partner's death. MSD pays this instead of their portion of the terminal benefit if they get more money. If the deceased person qualified for terminal benefit, their portion will continue to be paid.

chunks.title: Changing benefits or the benefit rate — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: The effect the client's death has on the surviving partner's payments will depend on whether the surviving partner: - qualifies in their own right for New Zealand Superannuation or - is included in New Zealand Superannuation as a grandparented non-qualified partner or gets a main benefit If the surviving partner is a grandparented non-qualified partner they will need to apply for a main benefit as they will not qualify for the grandparented non-qualified rate of New Zealand Superannuation. If the surviving partner gets a main benefit the rate and type of benefit should be reviewed to check they are getting the correct benefit and rate of payment.

chunks.title: Surviving person is entitled to survivor's grant from ACC — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When the death of the person was the result of an accident, entitlement to a survivor's grant from ACC needs to be decided before terminal benefit can be paid If the surviving person or child is entitled to a survivor's grant from ACC there is no entitlement to terminal benefit. If the New Zealand Superannuation payments have continued after the date of death, an overpayment is established and the debt should be recovered from the estate.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's New Zealand Superannuation when the child turns 18 during the 28-day continuation of payment.

chunks.title: Death of a single client — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Death of a single client
When a single client (with no children) dies, payment generally stops from the day after the date of death, but there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days.
Payment should stop from the first available date if we have been notified within 28 days of the date of death. This will avoid creating a debt.
Where there are other circumstances that justify payment of terminal benefit, payment should continue for the full 28 days after death.
For more information see:
- Avoiding a debt
- Terminal benefit for a single client
Note a single client who is a liable person and paying Child Support payments, or a caregiver receiving Unsupported Childs Benefit or Orphans Benefit is regarded as having children.
For more information see:
- Death of a client with a partner or child

chunks.title: Deciding if grandparented non-qualified partner or main benefit partner would be better off getting terminal benefit or another benefit — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Deciding if grandparented non-qualified partner or main benefit partner would be better off getting terminal benefit or another benefit
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children. Depending on the client's circumstances, they may be better off getting other assistance instead of Terminal Benefit.
Terminal Benefit
When New Zealand Superannuation is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person and the surviving person's portion of superannuation should be paid if it is decided that terminal benefit is the best option for the surviving partner. Payment is the total superannuation including any ongoing Extra help. It does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit.
A surviving grandparented non-qualified partner who does not have on-going entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation payments would generally get more money by getting terminal benefit.
Other assistance
Sometimes the surviving person or the caregiver of the child would get more money (based on their new circumstances) on a new main benefit instead of getting their portion of their current assistance for 28 days.
Compare the surviving person's potential new main benefit or increase of their main benefit if they get one and ongoing Extra help (from the date after death) against the surviving person's portion of benefit and ongoing Extra help they were getting before their partner's death.

chunks.title: Decision guidelines - married, civil union or de facto clients — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines - married, civil union or de facto clients
While New Zealand Superannuation should generally be stopped when the qualifying client is imprisoned, there is discretion for payment to be continued to the qualifying client in prison or in full or part to the partner not in prison. This discretion allows payment of all or part of the New Zealand Superannuation to the partner.
If you feel that payment should be continued, and paid to the partner, this should generally be at the half married, civil union or de facto rate. However, you can pay the full married, civil union or de facto rate if you feel this is warranted after having regard to the particular circumstances of the client and their partner.
To help you decide whether it is reasonable to pay the New Zealand Superannuation to the client in prison or to the partner of the client in prison, consider the following:
- has the period in prison already passed?
- is the client due to be released from prison shortly?
- is the likely period in prison less than 6 months?
- does the partner qualify for a statutory benefit in their own right?
- do they intend to live together when the partner is released?
- has the partner in prison applied for Home Detention?
- are there exceptional circumstances that warrant paying the full married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit to the partner who is not in prison?
- are there exceptional circumstances to treat the partner in the community as single (eg the client does not intend resuming the relationship with their partner when they are released or has decided to end the relationship due to the imprisonment)?
For further help you can contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.
Note imprisonment can affect the grandparenting status of non-qualified partner couples.

chunks.title: Deductions — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Deductions
In certain circumstances MSD can be required to pay part of the client's benefit to another party.
MSD is legally required to make such deductions when served with a properly issued Deduction Notice or Attachment Order. In these cases, the consent of the client is not required.
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others.

chunks.title: Departure from New Zealand — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Departure from New Zealand
A client should advise the Ministry of Social Development of any change of circumstances that may affect the payment of their New Zealand Superannuation, for example, if they are going to be absent from New Zealand.
When a client or their partner contacts you to advise that they intend travelling overseas you need to obtain the following information:
- date of departure (flight numbers if possible)
- date of return (flight numbers if possible)
You need to make sure that you have told the client about their portability options and their need to return to New Zealand within 26 weeks, and if they do not return within 30 weeks they may be overpaid from the day after they left New Zealand.
Note couples getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate of New Zealand Superannuation will lose their grandparenting if the qualified client is not entitled to payment during their absence, or any of the period of their absence.

chunks.title: Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital
When a New Zealand Superannuation client has been remanded in custody, or is serving a term of imprisonment, is detained in or transferred to a psychiatric hospital they can receive New Zealand Superannuation.
This will also apply to people who turn 65 while in prison and who are then transferred to a psychiatric hospital provided they meet the eligibility criteria.
People who are aged 65 or over, and are not eligible for New Zealand Superannuation may be able to receive Emergency Benefit. For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Person serving their sentence of imprisonment in a psychiatric hospital
Clients remanded in custody or serving a term of imprisonment who are temporarily hospitalised for treatment of an injury or health condition are still considered to be in prison and the Department of Corrections will meet their costs. An Emergency Benefit or any other financial assistance cannot be paid.
## Payment rate
New Zealand Superannuation can be paid at the full rate for 13 weeks following admission to a psychiatric hospital.
New Zealand Superannuation must be reduced to the hospital rate 13 weeks after admission to a psychiatric hospital. You can consider paying a higher rate in some circumstances.
For more information see:
- Definition of imprisonment
- Release on bail
- Qualifications
- Hospitalisation
- Paying at a higher rate

chunks.title: Discharge from hospital — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Discharge from hospital
Where a client is receiving the hospital rate and they are discharged from hospital:
- increase their New Zealand Superannuation to the appropriate full rate from the date of discharge
- for married, civil union or de facto clients reduce the partner's New Zealand Superannuation, benefit, or pension to the married, civil union or de facto rate and cancel Special Disability Allowance and
- review any Extra help from the same date
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.
## Re-admitted to hospital
Where a client (who has been formally discharged from hospital) is re-admitted, the 13 week period starts again from the day after they are re-admitted (even if the client has been re-admitted within 28 days of being discharged).
Note this only refers to clients who are formally discharged from hospital not clients on leave.
For more information about clients on leave from hospital see:
- Clients on leave from hospital

chunks.title: Effective date of review due to change in relationship — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: New Zealand Superannuation should be reviewed when the client: - marries, starts a de facto relationship or enters a civil union - reconciles with a former partner - separates - qualified partner elects to cancel the grandparented non-qualified couple rate - has a partner who enters long term residential care or - has a partner who dies

chunks.title: Couple rate of payment when client enters relationship — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: The rate of New Zealand Superannuation should be changed to the couple rate from the first available date if the client has advised the change in circumstances within a reasonable time (generally within 14 days). You should only establish an overpayment if: - the client has failed to advise of a change in living situation within 14 days of the event or - they have deliberately mislead the Ministry of Social Development Note if the couple getting grandparented non-qualified couple rate of New Zealand Superannuation, separate the grandparenting non-qualified rate is cancelled (and if they then reconcile again, they won't be able to be included again). The non-qualified partner will be able to apply for a main benefit relevant to their circumstances.

chunks.title: Single sharing accommodation rate of payment in situations the client is now single — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: The single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation can be paid from the: - day after their relationship ends or - day that their partner enters long-term residential care (though there is no change in relationship status) If the relationship has ended, the partner who does not qualify for New Zealand Superannuation in their own right will need to test their eligibility to other assistance.

chunks.title: Single living alone rate of payment when the client becomes single — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When the client meets the definition of living alone, the single living alone rate of New Zealand Superannuation can be paid from the: - date the client meets the definition of living alone - day that their partner enters long-term residential care (though there is no change in the relationship status) - day after the relationship ends - day after their partner died or - 2 September 2013 whichever is the later.

chunks.title: Exception where spouse or partner died before 2 September 2013 — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If the client was living alone before 2 September 2013 as their partner died and they contacted the Ministry of Social Development within 28 days from the date of death, the client may be able to get the Living Alone Payment from the day after the date of death. The client will need to complete a Living Alone Payment application form. If the application for Living Alone Payment is received more than 28 days following the partner's death, or no application is received, the client will be paid the single living alone rate from: - the date the client meets the definition of living alone or - 2 September 2013 whichever is the later.

chunks.title: Example of due paid assessment over 27 September 2010 period — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Below are examples of how to calculate the annual income when the client's annual income year falls across the 27 September 2010 period.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: A client receiving New Zealand Superannuation has a grandparented non-qualified partner who works for 12 hours each week and earns $13 per hour ($156 per week). Their annual income year began on 5 July 2010 and ended on 4 July 2011. 1. Calculate the weeks prior to 27 September 2010 (12 weeks) Client's annual gross income ($156 x 12 weeks) $1,872 Less income allowed before benefit is affected - $80.00 per week $1,872 - $960 ($80 x 12 weeks) $912 Equals annual income that will reduce benefit payment (income over $4,160) $912 Annual reduction in benefit rate: Income over $4,160 = 70% of every $1 (70% of $912) $912 x 0.70 = $638.40 Reduction in benefit rate $638.40 2. Calculate the weeks from 27 September 2010 (40 weeks) Client's annual gross income ($156.00 x 40 weeks) $6,240 Less income allowed before benefit is affected - $115 per week $6,240 - $4,000 ($115 x 40 weeks) $2,240 Equals annual income that will reduce benefit payment (income over $5,980) $2,240 Annual reduction in benefit rate: Income over $5,980 = 70% of every $1 (70% of $2,240) $2,240 x 0.7 = $1,568 Reduction in benefit rate $1,568 3. Add the Reduction in benefit rate from steps 1 and 2 to get the total annual reduction in benefit $638.40 + $1,568 = $2,206.40

chunks.title: Example 2 — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: A client receiving New Zealand Superannuation has a grandparented non-qualified partner who is self-employed and earns $14,500. Their annual income year began on 9 August 2010 and ended on 7 August 2011. 1. Calculate the weeks prior to 27 September 2010 (7 weeks) Clients annual gross income ($14,500 divided by 52 x 7 weeks) $1,951.92 Less income allowed before benefit is affected - $80 per week ($4,160 annually) $1,951.92 - $560 ($80 x 7 weeks = $560) $1,391.92 Equals annual income that will reduce benefit payment (income over $4,160) $1,391 Annual reduction in benefit rate: Income over $4,160 = 70% of every $1 (70% of $1,391) $1,391 x 0.7 = $973.70 Reduction in benefit rate $973.70 2. Calculate the weeks from 27 September 2010 (45 weeks) Clients annual gross income ($14,500 divided by 52 x 45 weeks) $12,548.08 Less income allowed before benefit is affected - $115 per week $12,548.08 - $4,500 ($115 x 45 weeks) $8,048.08 Equals annual income that will reduce benefit payment (income over $5,980) $8,048 Annual reduction in benefit rate: Income over $5,980 = 70% of every $1 (70% of $8,048) $8,048 x 0.7 = $5,633.60 Reduction in benefit rate $5,633.60 3. Add the Reduction in benefit rate from steps 1 and 2 to get the total annual reduction in benefit $973.70 + $5,633.60 = $6,607.30

chunks.title: Examples of Mandatory Review outcomes — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: MSD must review a client's New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) within 52 weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed. The Mandatory Review is complete when MSD has determined if the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) and the rate payable (if applicable). When a client responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined whether the client qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Outcomes of a Mandatory Review Examples Client declares no change (exception doesn't apply) Blair and Georgia are getting New Zealand Superannuation as a couple. Georgia is included as a grandparented non-qualifying partner. Blair's Mandatory Review is due on 14 December 2026. Blair responds to the Mandatory Review on 11 December and confirms they have had no change in circumstances. Because Blair has declared no change in circumstances and an exception doesn't apply, MSD must continue the benefit at the same rate. MSD completes Blair's Mandatory Review on 11 December and sets the next review date for 52 weeks later (10 December 2027). Client declares no change (exception applies) Mavis and Donald are getting New Zealand Superannuation as a couple. Donald is included as a grandparented non-qualifying partner. They also get Accommodation Supplement and Disability Allowance and pay rent of $350.00 per week in Area 1. Mavis' Mandatory Review is due on 9 June 2027, and she responds on 7 June 2027 to confirm they have had no change in their circumstances. While their Disability Allowance costs were updated last year, they haven't declared a change in rent since January 2024. Because they have been getting Accommodation Supplement and declared no change in their accommodation costs for three consecutive years, MSD must consider whether further information is required before completing the Mandatory Review. MSD considers their circumstances and sees that they haven't provided verification of their accommodation costs since moving to their current apartment in 2024. Given they live in an area where rental accommodation is very limited and rents have increased significantly, MSD determines that it is reasonable to request verification of their accommodation costs to confirm that the information is correct before making a decision about their entitlement. Mavis is asked to provide this information before 7 July 2027 (the new deadline for the review) or their New Zealand Superannuation, Accommodation Supplement and Disability Allowance will stop. Mavis contacts MSD on 1 July 2027 with the evidence requested. MSD determines that their circumstances have changed as their rent increased in January 2027. MSD adjusts the rate of payment for Accommodation Supplement and exercises discretion to backdate the payment to the date of the increase in costs, and continues New Zealand Superannuation and Disability Allowance at the same rate.

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: MSD completes Mavis' Mandatory Review on 1 July 2027, and the next Mandatory Review date is set for 52 weeks in the future on 29 June 2028. Client declares a change in circumstances Arin and Daphney are getting New Zealand Superannuation as a couple. Daphney is included as a grandparented non-qualifying partner. Arin's Mandatory Review is due on 20 April 2027. Arin responds to the Mandatory Review on 16 April and tells MSD that they are no longer in a relationship with Daphney. Arin tells MSD that their relationship ended on 10 April 2027, and they now live alone. Because Arin has declared they are no longer in a relationship, the rate of Arin's New Zealand Superannuation will need to be reassessed. MSD reassesses Arin's rate of New Zealand Superannuation to a single living alone rate from 10 April 2027. There is no future Mandatory Review date for the New Zealand Superannuation as Arin no longer has a non-qualifying partner included. Not enough information to complete Mandatory Review Courtney and Chris are getting New Zealand Superannuation as a couple. Chris is included as a grandparented non-qualifying partner. Courtney's Mandatory Review is due on 17 August 2026. Courtney responds to the Mandatory Review on 12 August and tells MSD they are no longer in a relationship with Chris. Courtney has not told MSD when the relationship ended. Courtney has declared a change in circumstance that affects their New Zealand Superannuation. MSD cannot complete the Mandatory Review without requesting more information from Courtney. MSD sets a new reasonable deadline of 25 August 2026 for Courtney to provide more information about when her relationship ended and her living arrangements. Courtney's New Zealand Superannuation will continue to be paid during this time. If Courtney does not provide the information by the new deadline, her New Zealand Superannuation will suspend from this date. Courtney contacts MSD on 20 August and confirms that she left her relationship and moved to live with family on 10 August 2026. Based on this, MSD reassesses Courtney's New Zealand Superannuation and updates the rate to single, sharing accommodation from 10 August 2026. Note when a client's New Zealand Superannuation stops because they did not respond to the Mandatory Review, their New Zealand Superannuation will cancel after 2 years.

chunks.title: Exceptions when a client declares no change in circumstances for Mandatory Review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have no change in circumstances, MSD must generally continue their New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) at the same rate. However, there are some exceptions when MSD can request further information from the client to determine if they continue to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) or that the rate of payment is correct. Exceptions include when, at the time the client responds to their Mandatory Review, they: - have been getting Disability Allowance and have had no change in their disability related costs for three consecutive years or - have been getting Accommodation Supplement and have had no change in their accommodation costs for three consecutive years or - have had no change to their confirmed income amount for three consecutive years If a client has one or more of these exceptions, MSD must consider if further information is required from the client before deciding the outcome of the Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Further information is needed to complete the Mandatory Review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If further information is needed to determine if the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) or that the rate of payment is correct, MSD must give a reasonable timeframe for the client to provide it. The date the client is given to provide the information by becomes the client's new deadline to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client does not provide the information that was asked for, MSD must suspend the New Zealand Superannuation from the new deadline date. If the client provides the information that was asked for and MSD determines the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included (including the rate payable), the future Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review.

chunks.title: Further information not needed to complete the Mandatory Review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: In some situations, there may be good reason for the client having no change in their costs or income, and further information may not be needed for MSD to determine whether they continue to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included). For example, the client may have provided recent evidence of their costs or income, or they may have recently discussed their circumstances with MSD. If no further information is needed for MSD to determine the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) including the rate payable, the future Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Example Riley is getting New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) and his wife Susan works 10 hours a week as a caregiver with a local employer. Susan is paid more than the minimum wage in this role in recognition of her skills and experience. Riley's Mandatory Review for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) is due on 12 February 2027 and he responds on 10 February 2027 to confirm they have had no change in their circumstances. This includes no change in Susan's income (which has remained unchanged since she moved into her current role in 2024). As Riley has been getting New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) and declared no change in their income for three consecutive years at the time the mandatory review is returned, MSD must consider whether further information is required before completing the Mandatory Review. MSD considers their circumstances and notes that Riley recently contacted MSD for a food grant and as part of that conversation, MSD confirmed he has no income and Susan's income hadn't changed. MSD determines that no further information is required to determine that Riley continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included). His New Zealand Superannuation continues at the same rate, and his next review date is set for 52 weeks in the future (9 February 2028).

chunks.title: Extra help — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Extra help
Extra help can be paid to clients for the first 13 weeks that they are in hospital or until their rate of payment is reduced.
After the client has been in hospital for 13 weeks, Extra help is no longer payable. If the client has continuing financial costs, such as accommodation, consider increasing their rate of payment to a rate higher than the hospital rate.
For more information see:
- Guidelines for paying at a higher rate
If a client is married, in a civil union or de facto relationship with no dependent children and they qualify for Accommodation Supplement or Winter Energy Payment, you can pay the full Accommodation Supplement or Winter Energy Payment to the partner not in hospital. For Accommodation Supplement, take into account income and assets of both of the couple.
## Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit
If a client is receiving an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, continue payment if it is a short-term admission. If requested, apportion the benefit to cover the cost of alternative care or accommodation for the child.
If it appears likely that the client will be in hospital for longer than 13 weeks, check what the continuing care arrangements are for the child/children and if necessary review the client's entitlement to the benefit.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Winter Energy Payment

chunks.title: Fails to advise of absence — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Sometimes a client does not tell the Ministry of Social Development they intend to travel overseas.

chunks.title: Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: The Ministry of Social Development has an Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service that identifies clients who have left New Zealand. If the client has not returned to New Zealand after 26 weeks the client is sent a letter requesting they contact the Integrity Intervention Centre within 10 working days.

chunks.title: Client does not respond — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If the client fails to make contact, the Integrity Intervention Centre will suspend the New Zealand Superannuation from the first available date after the 10 working days have lapsed. Notes are added in CMS stating that the client needs to confirm their date of return to New Zealand before their New Zealand Superannuation can be resumed. If the client fails to make contact within 2 pay cycles, the Integrity Intervention Centre will establish an overpayment from the day after the departure date.

chunks.title: Client makes contact before New Zealand Superannuation suspended — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
