chunks.text: If the client contacts the Ministry when they received the first letter, that is, before the New Zealand Superannuation is suspended, take the following action: - confirm the date they returned to New Zealand - make full notes in CMS to prevent their New Zealand Superannuation being suspended at a later date by the Integrity Intervention Centre - remind your client of their obligation to tell the Ministry of any change in their circumstances that may affect their New Zealand Superannuation payments - a grandparented non-qualified couple must be informed that their grandparented non-qualified partner rate will end if the qualified partner is not entitled to payment for the period of absence or any part of the absence.

chunks.title: Client makes contact after New Zealand Superannuation suspended — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If a client contacts after their New Zealand Superannuation has been suspended it will also mean that a debt has been established by the Integrity Intervention Centre, from the day after the client left New Zealand up to the date their payments were suspended. If the overpayment period is incorrect, ask your client the following information and forward it to the Integrity Intervention Centre: - verification of travel dates, for example, photocopy of passport details - any other relevant information The Integrity Intervention Centre will reassess the overpayment if there is more information which suggest the overpayment is incorrect. Note clients may be asked to provide proof of the circumstances of their absence. If you need any help contact the Integrity Intervention Centre.

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualified partner becomes sick — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Grandparented non-qualified partner becomes sick
When a grandparented non-qualifying partner cannot work due to health condition, injury or disability they can continue to be included in their partners New Zealand Superannuation. However, they may also qualify for Jobseeker Support or Supported Living Payment.
Depending on the couples other income, the income exemption and abatement rate, the client and partner may be financially better off with the New Zealand Superannuation and main benefit if the:
- client gets the married or civil union person rate of New Zealand Superannuation and
- partner gets Jobseeker Support or Supported Living Payment at the half married or civil union rate
The client and partner must decide which option best meets their needs and you must tell the client and partner:
- the benefit rates
- the effect of income (income reduction and any exemptions) on the benefit
- about any benefit obligations and
- the implications if they choose to no longer be a grandparented non-qualified partner (that is they will not be able to re-include them again)

chunks.title: Guidelines for paying a higher rate — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Guidelines for paying a higher rate
Payment can be increased above the hospital rate to a rate that (together with other income) will be sufficient to meet the cost of continuing commitments.
Use the following guidelines to assess whether the client's rate should be higher.
1. Have the client complete an Increased payment while you are in hospital form.
2. Accept stated expenses where they appear reasonable, but ask for proof if there is doubt.
3. A liberal attitude can be allowed for costs but purchases such as presents for the family must be met from the basic grant.
4. If the client is a sole parent and has childcare costs:
- include the childcare costs when assessing whether a higher rate should be payable
- include family tax credit and any Best Start tax credit payments as income
Note the client will need to provide details of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit.
5. If a client is married, in a civil union or de facto relationship, do not include home outgoings or accommodation expenses. These are the responsibility of the partner not in hospital. (The partner may qualify for Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support.)
6. Check that all possible action has been taken to reduce expenses. For example, giving up the lease on a flat where the hospital stay is indefinite.
7. If the increase payment request is for one-off items such as clothing, you can pay the increase by:
- a backdated review of the benefit rate
- increasing the benefit rate for a limited time or
- by a lump sum payment
## Example
Continuing commitments per week
$55.00
less other income (bank interest)
$5.00
rate of increase
$50.00
plus hospital rate (net, at 1 April 2026)
$58.34
rate of benefit payable
$108.34
Add the rate payable as a non-standard rate on the SNSRA screen.
A parent benefit reassessment SPBR may also be required.

chunks.title: Home detention — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Home detention
A client may be in prison for a short time before being released on home detention.
Note New Zealand Superannuation does not have an initial stand-down.
Where the partner of a person in prison has been receiving a benefit, this will need to be reviewed from the date of release.

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a client is admitted to hospital, their New Zealand Superannuation can continue at the existing rate for the first 13 weeks.
The rate will need to be reduced to the hospital rate of payment after the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks (not after receiving New Zealand Superannuation for 13 weeks).
## Exception
Couples with a dependent child do not have their New Zealand Superannuation payment reduced regardless of how long they are in hospital.
Note if a client (or partner) is getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for a child in their care, this is regarded as a dependent child.
## Hospital rate
The hospital rate payment allows for the cost of personal items, which patients are expected to provide for themselves. The net weekly hospital rate is $58.34 as at 1 April 2026.
An amount above the hospital rate can be paid where there are financial circumstances to warrant paying at a higher rate.
Note MSD cannot pay an amount less than the hospital rate.
## Client in hospital during Mandatory Review
Generally, clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend.
Only clients getting New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included have a Mandatory Review for their New Zealand Superannuation.
All New Zealand Superannuation clients getting Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance have a Mandatory Review for this assistance.
When a client is in hospital (for 13 weeks or less) and needs more time to respond to the review, they may be able to get an extension. If a client is unable to respond to the Mandatory Review, they may be able to get an exemption.
A client must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption.
Note clients who are in hospital for more than 13 weeks do not have a Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Humanitarian work — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: A client can get payment while overseas if they are undertaking full-time voluntary and unpaid humanitarian work for a recognised aid agency, and - the absence is not more than 156 weeks - the work the client has been engaged in has not deprived another person of paid employment and - the client has remained ordinarily resident in New Zealand during this time If all the conditions are not met the usual absence overseas conditions apply. If the client is overseas for more than 156 weeks, payments must stop from the day after departure from New Zealand.

chunks.title: Recognised aid agency — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: A recognised aid agency is an organisation that has as its principal function 'the giving of aid and assistance to less advantaged communities in one or more other countries' or similar. Aid agencies would include (but are not limited to) organisations such as: - Red Cross - United Nations Volunteers - Volunteer Services Abroad and - World Vision Whether an aid agency meets the criteria above, is determined by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. If you need assistance deciding if the agency is a 'recognised aid agency' please contact Helpline.

chunks.title: Partners — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Payment can continue up to 156 weeks for the partner of a married, civil union or de facto superannuitant if they are also undertaking humanitarian work. If the partner is absent from New Zealand and not undertaking humanitarian work, they can only get payment for up to 26 weeks, provided they return to New Zealand within 30 weeks.

chunks.title: Grandparented couples doing humanitarian work overseas for recognised aid agencies — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Grandparented couples who are both undertaking humanitarian work with an approved aid agency can be absent for up to 156 weeks and get payment of their New Zealand Superannuation. If their absence is over 156 weeks they will not be entitled to payments from the date after their departure from New Zealand and grandparenting will end from the same date.

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualified partner couples where only one partner is undertaking humanitarian work — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When only the qualified partner is undertaking humanitarian work the client can get their payments for up to 156 weeks. The grandparented non-qualified partner not undertaking humanitarian work can get payments for up to 26 weeks, provided they return to New Zealand within 30 weeks. If the grandparented non-qualified partner is the only partner undertaking humanitarian work then neither client is entitled to be paid under the 156 week absence provision for humanitarian aid agency workers. If the grandparented non-qualified partner is the only partner undertaking humanitarian work, the qualified partner and non-qualified partner's payments can continue for up to 26 weeks, provided they return to New Zealand within 30 weeks. Note a grandparented non-qualified partner cannot retain their grandparenting if the qualifying partner is absent from New Zealand for more than 26 weeks. For more information see: Effect of absence overseas on grandparented clients.

chunks.title: Proof — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Clients must supply proof of their absence from the Aid Agency (on their letterhead) confirming: - the name(s) of the people concerned - the period of their absence - detail of the work being undertaken and that it is voluntary, full-time and unpaid - that the work the person has been engaged to do has not deprived another person of paid employment and - the principal function of the aid agency

chunks.title: Advice of departure — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When you have determined that payment can continue for up to 156 weeks you must make full notes in CMS. For further help you can contact the Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.

chunks.title: Imprisonment — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
When a New Zealand Superannuation client is imprisoned or detained in custody they are generally no longer entitled to get New Zealand Superannuation.
New Zealand Superannuation should stop from the day following the date of imprisonment. However, there is discretion to continue 2 payments following imprisonment.
Further ongoing payments for the period of imprisonment are also discretionary.
MSD must decide whether to suspend or cancel the benefit after considering the likely period in prison and whether the client has a partner and or dependent children.

chunks.title: Inland Revenue deduction notices — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
Inland Revenue may request that a client's unpaid taxes be directly deducted from their benefit payments.
Note all Inland Revenue deduction notices are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
The instructions on the deduction notice are to deduct the lowest of either:
- 10% of the total debt which Inland Revenue specify in the notice, on a weekly basis or
- 20% of the client's gross earnings on a weekly basis
Where there are insufficient funds to cover the deduction, Work and Income must advise Inland Revenue immediately that the deduction will not start or will start at a reduced rate.
Inland Revenue deduction notices for unpaid taxes have a lower priority than Child Support deductions.
For more information see:
- Priority for deductions
- Inland revenue deductions

chunks.title: Inland Revenue deductions — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Inland Revenue deductions
There are a number of Inland Revenue deductions. These include tax, student loan repayments and deduction notices.
## Tax
New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension is part of a person's taxable income and must be taken into account when a person is calculating their tax rate. Tax deductions are made in line with the tax code entered in the system and are the first priority for deductions. See:
- New Zealand Superannuation Tax codes
## Student Loan repayments
New Zealand Superannuation clients with a student loan must use a tax code with the student loan ("SL") repayment code. This will ensure that student loan repayments are deducted every pay period if required. Student loan repayments are part of a person's tax liability and are first priority for deductions. See:
- Student Loan repayments
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
These are notices that Inland Revenue issue when a person has a tax debt. They are separate from and additional to their current tax liability, and are second priority deductions. See:
- Inland Revenue deduction notices
For more information see:
- Priority for deductions

chunks.title: Mandatory Review dates for New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review dates for New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included in the benefit have a Mandatory Review for their New Zealand Superannuation.
MSD must review the client's New Zealand Superannuation within 52 weeks from the date:
- the client's last Mandatory Review was completed, or
- their benefit recommenced after it was cancelled as a result of the Mandatory Review
The next review date will be set for 52-weeks from the date MSD determined the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) and the rate of benefit payable (i.e. when MSD completes the review).
Note when MSD has an interaction with a client that confirms all of the same circumstances as a Mandatory Review, this can push out the client's Mandatory Review date by 52-weeks. This is known as a specific engagement.
## Initial Mandatory Review dates
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) have an initial Mandatory Review date on or after 2 March 2026 of either:
- 52 weeks from when their last periodic review was completed or
- 52 weeks from when MSD last contacted the client to confirm whether the information MSD holds about their circumstances is correct (annual circumstances letter)
Whichever of the dates is later.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review not required — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review not required
There is no Mandatory Review for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) in the following circumstances:
- the client is hospitalised for more than 13 weeks
- the client is in residential disability care or rest home care
- the client has died
- the client is living in or visiting a region affected by an emergency or adverse event and they are unable to reasonably leave the area
- the client is living in or visiting a region affected by an outbreak of a quarantinable disease and an epidemic notice has been given and is in force
or when:
- there is a major system outage that prevents MSD from carrying out mandatory reviews of specified benefits
MSD will also stop the review for any clients who are in these circumstances after they have been notified about their Mandatory Review.
MSD will notify the client when they are not required to complete the review. The Mandatory Review date is reset to 52 weeks in the future from the client's original review date.
Note a notification will not be sent when the client has died.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) suspended before Mandatory Review date — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) suspended before Mandatory Review date
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation (with a non-qualified partner included) are always notified about their Mandatory Review, even if their New Zealand Superannuation is suspended, unless it is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison.
MSD must not undertake the Mandatory Review unless the client contacts MSD to resume their New Zealand Superannuation.
If the client contacts MSD before their review date to resume their benefit, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to do their Mandatory Review. MSD can resume the benefit before the Mandatory Review has been responded to.
However, if the client contacts MSD on or after the Mandatory Review date, the review must be completed before MSD can resume the benefit.
## Example
Pete and Sam are getting New Zealand Superannuation as a couple. Sam is included as a grandparented non-qualifying partner. Pete's Mandatory review is due on 2 September 2027.
MSD is notified by New Zealand Police that both Pete and Sam have warrants to their arrest. Pete and Sam do not take reasonable steps to resolve their warrant to arrest for 10 working days, and MSD suspends their New Zealand Superannuation on 25 August.
For MSD to resume their New Zealand Superannuation, both Pete and Sam must resolve or take steps to resolve the warrant to arrest and provide evidence of this.
On 6 September 2027 both Pete and Sam tell MSD that they resolved their warrants to arrest and provide notices of hearing as evidence.
However, because Pete contacted MSD after his Mandatory Review date, he will need to respond to the Mandatory Review and confirm both his and Sam's circumstances before MSD can resume the New Zealand Superannuation.
On 8 September 2027 Pete responds to this Mandatory Review and confirms there is no change in circumstances. MSD resumes their New Zealand Superannuation at the same rate from 6 September 2027.
MSD to completes the Mandatory Review on 8 September 2027 and sets the next review date 52-weeks from the date the Mandatory Review was completed.
Pete's next Mandatory Review date is 6 September 2028.

chunks.title: On leave for 28 days or less — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## On leave for 28 days or less
Where a client who is receiving the hospital rate is on leave from hospital for 28 days or less:
- increase their New Zealand Superannuation to the appropriate full rate from the date of discharge on leave
- for married, civil union or de facto clients reduce the partner's New Zealand Superannuation, benefit or pension to the married, civil union or de facto rate and suspend Special Disability Allowance and
- review any Extra Help from the same date
On re-admission to hospital:
- reduce New Zealand Superannuation to the rate payable prior to the period of leave
- for married, civil union or de facto clients increase the partner's New Zealand Superannuation, benefit or pension and resume Special Disability Allowance and
- review any Extra Help from the same date
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.

chunks.title: On leave for more than 28 days — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## On leave for more than 28 days
Where a client who is receiving the hospital rate is on leave from hospital for more than 28 days:
- increase their New Zealand Superannuation to the appropriate full rate from the date of discharge on leave
- for married, civil union or de facto clients reduce the partner's New Zealand Superannuation, benefit or pension to the married, civil union or de facto rate and suspend Special Disability Allowance and
- review any Extra Help
On re-admission to hospital continue to pay the full rate of New Zealand Superannuation and any Extra Help for a further 13 weeks of hospitalisation.
Note calculation of the 13 week period in hospital begins again after the client has been re-admitted when on leave for more than 28 days.
The dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.

chunks.title: Ongoing assistance for surviving partner — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: The effect the client's death will have on the surviving partner's payments will depend on whether the surviving partner: - qualifies in their own right or - is included in New Zealand Superannuation as a grandparented non-qualifying partner; or - gets a main benefit

chunks.title: Qualified in own right — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When the surviving partner qualifies for New Zealand Superannuation in their own right, they can get the single sharing accommodation rate or the single living alone rate from the day after their partner's death. Any ongoing extra help should then be adjusted to the appropriate single rate. The rate of payment will depend on whether they: - are sharing accommodation with any person aged 18 years or over who is not a dependent child or a visitor who stays less than 13 weeks in any 26 week period or - meet all the qualifications for the single living alone rate For more information see: - Single sharing accommodation rate - Single living alone rate - Effective date of review due to change in relationship Note when the surviving client qualifies for New Zealand Superannuation in their own right and gets the single sharing accommodation or single living alone rate from the day after their partner's death, the deceased client is paid the payments they were getting at the date of their death. This includes if they were being paid the full amount of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Winter Energy Payment for the couple.

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualifying partner with no dependent children — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When there are no dependent children, the surviving partner must apply for the appropriate benefit, in their own right. The surviving partner may be granted a new benefit (instead of terminal benefit) from the day after their partner's death if they will get more money.

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualifying partner with dependent children — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When a qualifying New Zealand Superannuation client dies and the surviving partner has a dependent child, they may be able to get Sole Parent Support, Jobseeker Support or Supported Living Payment depending on the age of the youngest dependent child. Note there is no initial stand-down when a partner applies for Sole Parent Support or Jobseeker Support within 28 days of the client's death. When the partner applies 28 days or more after the death of the client, there will be an initial stand-down.

chunks.title: Delay in granting ACC payments — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When the death was the result of an accident, the surviving partner may be able to get weekly compensation payments from ACC. If there will be a delay in deciding their claim, the partner can apply for a benefit while waiting. The surviving partner must acknowledge, in writing, that benefit payments made will be refunded once weekly compensation payments are granted.

chunks.title: Outcomes of Mandatory Review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation (who have a grandparented non-qualified partner included in their benefit) must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend. When a client responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined if the client qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies The Mandatory Review is completed when MSD makes a decision about whether the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) and the rate of benefit payable(if applicable). MSD may also carry out a separate review of the New Zealand Superannuation at any time, where there is good reason.

chunks.title: Client declares no change — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When a client responds to the Mandatory Review and confirms they have had no change in circumstances, MSD must generally continue their New Zealand Superannuation at the same rate. The client's next review date will be set for 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Exceptions when a client declares no change When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have no change in circumstances, there are some situations when MSD can request further information from the client before deciding whether to continue New Zealand Superannuation.

chunks.title: Client declares a change in circumstances — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When a client responds to the Mandatory Review with a change in circumstances, MSD must use the information provided to determine if the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included, or any other benefits they get that are subject to a Mandatory Review (excluding Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit) and the rate payable. MSD may request further information from the client if it is not possible to determine if the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation. Date of change When a client declares a change in circumstances, MSD must assess whether the client still qualifies for New Zealand Superannuation and the rate payable and from what date, depending on when the change in circumstances happened or will happen. Client is also getting other assistance When the client has provided information as part of the Mandatory Review that could affect their entitlement to and the rate payable of any other assistance (e.g. Temporary Additional Support), MSD may use this information to review that assistance. When the other assistance is affected by the outcome of the Mandatory Review, MSD must change the rate, suspend or cancel that assistance where appropriate. For example, if the outcome of the Mandatory Review is that the client is no longer entitled to New Zealand Superannuation, their Temporary Additional Support must be reviewed, and the rate may change or stop if they no longer qualify.

chunks.title: Further information is needed to determine whether the client continues to qualify — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If further information is needed to determine if the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) or that the rate of payment is correct, MSD must give a reasonable timeframe for the client to provide it. The date the client is given to provide the information by becomes the client's new deadline to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client does not provide the information that was asked for before the deadline, MSD must suspend the New Zealand Superannuation from the new deadline date. If the client provides the information that was asked for and MSD has determined the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) including the rate payable, the future Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review.

chunks.title: Completing the Mandatory Review when there are new costs — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: In some circumstances MSD can still complete the Mandatory Review when a client has a change in circumstances that doesn't affect the client's eligibility for New Zealand Superannuation. Example Marama is getting New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included in her benefit) and Disability Allowance. Marama has a Mandatory Review due for both New Zealand Superannuation and Disability Allowance. Marama responds to the Mandatory Review to confirm her circumstances. Marama tells MSD she has a new disability cost but nothing else has changed. MSD completes the Mandatory Review and continues New Zealand Superannuation and Disability Allowance at the existing rate. MSD advises Marama that she needs to provide a medical certificate from her medical or nurse practitioner to confirm the additional cost, and she must provide proof of cost to have the new cost included in her Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Overseas medical treatment — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Overseas medical treatment
When a client is receiving assistance for overseas medical treatment from the Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora - High Cost Treatment Pool, the client can continue to get payment of New Zealand Superannuation for up to 2 years while absent from New Zealand.
Payment can also continue if the partner, dependent child, or sibling of a client is the person who is being assisted under the High Cost Treatment Pool. Payment may also continue for partners and siblings when they are required to accompany the client overseas.
## Grandparented non-qualified partner couples
Grandparented couples who are absent from New Zealand under the overseas medical treatment programme will lose their grandparenting if the qualified partner is absent for more than the maximum 2 years. Partners usually accompany the person receiving the treatment which could be either partner of the grandparented couple.

chunks.title: Partner donates a kidney or liver tissue — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Partner donates a kidney or liver tissue
Partners of clients receiving New Zealand Superannuation can keep getting their payments if they are donating a kidney or liver tissue.
## Childcare assistance
Clients may be eligible for Childcare Assistance payments while they are recovering.
For more information and the additional qualifications see:
- Childcare Subsidy Temporary illness
- OSCAR Temporary illness

chunks.title: Partner has left New Zealand permanently — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Partner has left New Zealand permanently
When a partner has left New Zealand permanently and the other partner remains in New Zealand, their qualification for New Zealand Superannuation depends on whether they are:
- qualified in their own right or
- a grandparented non-qualified partner
## Both qualified in own right
When payment has stopped for a client, as they are overseas, the partner who remains in New Zealand can continue to get the married, civil union or de facto person rate. The partner remaining in New Zealand cannot get the single rate unless there is a breakdown in the relationship.
## Grandparented non-qualified partner is overseas
When the grandparented non-qualified partner is overseas permanently, the qualified client remaining in New Zealand will continue getting the half couple rate.
If the grandparented non-qualified partner is not returning to New Zealand, the grandparented non-qualified rate must end as the non-qualified partner will not be ordinarily resident.
## Grandparented non-qualified partner remains in New Zealand
When the grandparented non-qualified partner remains in New Zealand and the qualifying partners New Zealand Superannuation has stopped as they are overseas for more than 26 weeks, the grandparented rate ends because the qualifying partner is not entitled to payment for their absence or part of their absence.
The non-qualified partner can test their eligibility for a main benefit if they need financial assistance.

chunks.title: Paying at a higher rate — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Paying at a higher rate
You can make payment at a rate higher than the hospital rate where the client's continuing costs cannot be met by the hospital rate of payment and any other income they receive. Take into consideration:
- the client's financial commitments and
- access to other income
If a client is required to make Child Support payments and does not qualify for an exemption from Inland Revenue Child Support, increase the rate of payment to the hospital rate plus any Child Support payments that are required to be apportioned from the client's payments.
## Maximum amount payable
You can pay at a rate higher than the hospital rate up to the maximum that would otherwise be payable.
## When not to pay at a higher rate
If the client's rate of payment should be paid at a rate that is lower than the hospital rate, do not increase the rate to the hospital rate (or any other higher rate).
For example, do not pay a higher rate if the client is to receive a lower rate because of:
- the client's income
- maintenance deductions or
- overseas pension deductions
For more information about paying at a higher rate see:
- Guidelines for paying a higher rate

chunks.title: Payment to partners — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Payment to partners
When a client with a partner (with no dependent children) has their New Zealand Superannuation reduced to the hospital rate, their partner in the community from the same date can:
- get a Special Disability Allowance and
- have their portion of pension increased by the difference between the maximum half married, civil union or de facto rate and the single living alone rate for New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension partners (including grandparented non-qualified partners) or
- have their portion of benefit increased by the maximum half married, civil union or de facto rate and the single rate for main benefit partners
Note couples with dependent children do not have their rate reduced to the hospital rate.
## Partner is also in hospital
If the partner is also in hospital, the same rules apply as when the client is in hospital. If they have been in hospital for more than 13 weeks their benefit or pension is also reduced to the hospital rate.
Note if the partner is receiving Veteran's Pension and is in hospital for more than 13 weeks, their payment must not be reduced to the hospital rate. This is because Veteran's Pension is not affected by hospitalisation. The partner of the Veteran's Pension client cannot have their payments increased or get Special Disability Allowance.
## Charging income with a grandparented non-qualified partner included
You need to charge any income the couple gets against the married, civil union or de facto rate before you can determine the amount to pay.
The partner in the community will receive the half married, civil union or de facto rate (after charging income) plus the difference between the maximum married, civil union and de facto rate and single rate.
The client in the hospital will get the lesser of the:
- half married, civil union or de facto rate (after charging income) or
- hospital rate of payment
## Charging income with a main benefit partner
You need to charge any income the couple gets against the main benefit using the half abatement rule for that benefit type. The rate paid to the client in hospital will not be affected by any income the couple gets.

chunks.title: Permanent absence — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
Generally, if a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, payments must be cancelled from the day after the client leaves New Zealand.
If the client is moving to a country that has a Reciprocal agreement with New Zealand they may qualify for a benefit or pension in that country.
If the client is moving to country that New Zealand does not have a Reciprocal agreement with, they may be able to receive part of their New Zealand Superannuation payments.
If the client wishes to receive part of their New Zealand Superannuation overseas, then it is important that they apply for 'portability' before they leave New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Reciprocal agreements
- To or from overseas Payment overseas of New Zealand Superannuation
- To or from overseas Special portability arrangements with Pacific countries

chunks.title: Person detained under a Public Protection Order — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Person detained under a Public Protection Order
A person who has a Public Protection Order may get New Zealand Superannuation if they meet the qualifications.
A Public Protection Order is when a person has finished their sentence in prison but for public safety they must remain in a secure residence. This is to protect members of the public from the almost certain harm from serious sexual or violent offences. Corrections fund the costs of the person being detained in a residence within the prison compound.
For more information see:
## Rate of payment
The hospital rate of New Zealand Superannuation is paid from the date of grant.
## Entitlement date
The entitlement date for New Zealand Superannuation for a person held under a Public Protection Order is generally the date of release. The usual stand-down provisions for prisoners apply when determining the commencement date.
## Emergency Benefit
A person who has a Public Protection Order may get Emergency Benefit if they meet the basic eligibility criteria.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Person detained under a Public Protection Order

chunks.title: Priority for deductions — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Priority for deductions
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others; the following list gives the order of priority, highest to lowest:
Highest priority
- Child Support deductions made under the Child Support Act 1991
- Inland Revenue tax deductions (including Student Loan repayments)
- Inland Revenue deduction notices (for unpaid taxes)
- Ministry of Social Development debt repayments including Liable Parent Contributions (LPC), child maintenance debts and Major Repairs Advances (MRA), Student Allowance debt, Student Loan debt converted to Ministry of Social Development debt, Income Related Rent historical Kāinga Ora debt, Income Related Rent Ministry of Social Development debt
- Attachment orders made under the Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Court attachment orders issued under the Summary Proceedings Act 1957
- Court attachment orders issued under the District Court Act 2016
Lowest priority
Determining the priority of deductions is necessary where a client has more than one order issued in respect of their benefit. Also each order and deduction notice is subject to its own protected earnings rule.
When you need to reduce deductions you adjust from the lowest priority up to those with a higher priority taking into account the protected earnings rules for each.

chunks.title: Private hospitals and rest homes — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Private hospitals and rest homes
Payment of New Zealand Superannuation can be paid at the full rate when a client is:
- admitted to a private hospital or
- admitted to a private rest home that provides residential care disability services
If the client receives Extra Help, this will need to be reviewed to see if the costs are continuing.
For more information see:
- Residential Care Subsidy
- Residential Support Subsidy
## Transfer from rest home to hospital
If a client is a resident of a rest home and has been transferred to a hospital, their rate of payment can be reduced when they have been in hospital for 13 weeks.
Continue payment to the rest home unless the client requests otherwise. Re-instate the New Zealand Superannuation, if it has been reduced, to the original rate from the day the client is transferred back to the home.

chunks.title: Example — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Example
An attachment order is received from the Ministry of Justice for $50.00 per week. The order lists the client's protected earnings rate as $396.09 per week.
We need to calculate whether adding the deduction of $50.00 will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate.
Calculate protected earnings rate:
New Zealand Superannuation paid at the single living alone rate (net at 'M' tax rate as at 1 April 2026)
$555.15
Plus Accommodation Supplement (Area 2)
$105.00
Total net earnings
$660.15
60% of total net earnings (= protected earnings)
$396.09
Calculate if Attachment Order will exceed protected earnings
Total net earnings
$660.15
Less Child Support deduction
$95.00
Less Ministry of Social Development debt
$130.00
Sub total
$435.15
Less Court order
$50.00
Total
$385.15
The court order takes the client's income to $385.15, which is below the protected income rate of $396.09.
The attachment order will not operate, you must return it to the Ministry of Justice for the order to be amended.

chunks.title: Qualification if one partner remains in New Zealand — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Qualification if one partner remains in New Zealand
A client qualified for New Zealand Superannuation in their own right can be temporarily absent from New Zealand for up to 26 weeks and continue to get New Zealand Superannuation.
When a partner has left New Zealand permanently and the other partner remains in New Zealand, their qualification for New Zealand Superannuation depends on whether they are qualified in their own right or are a grandparented non-qualified partner.

chunks.title: Qualification starts during absence — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Qualification starts during absence
If a client applies for New Zealand Superannuation and becomes qualified while overseas, their absence before qualification is not taken into account. The allowable absence period starts from when the client qualified, not from when they went overseas and is treated the same as other clients.

chunks.title: Release on bail — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Release on bail
When a client is released on bail, New Zealand Superannuation can be paid from the date of release providing the client still meets the qualifications for the New Zealand Superannuation and reapplies for New Zealand Superannuation immediately after their release.
A grandparented non-qualified partner cannot be reincluded on release if the grandparented non-qualified partner rate was cancelled due to the imprisonment.
Note there is no initial stand-down when clients apply for New Zealand Superannuation. New Zealand Superannuation commences from:
- date of application or
- date of release

chunks.title: Remanded in custody — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Remanded in custody
Generally, when a client is remanded in custody awaiting a further court appearance the client's New Zealand Superannuation should be stopped. There is discretion to continue payment for 2 pay days following imprisonment.
There is also discretion to continue payment of New Zealand Superannuation after taking the client's financial circumstances and commitments into account.
When deciding whether to continue paying New Zealand Superannuation for the period of remand, consider the following:
- has the client been remanded pending further hearing or for sentencing
- does the client have continuing costs that cannot be avoided, such as rent and hire purchase for essential items
- does the client have a partner (either qualified in their own right or a grandparented non-qualified partner)
Every situation should be considered on a case-by-case basis.
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances of the client before making a decision.

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When the client returns to New Zealand you will need to confirm the following:
- date of return to New Zealand
- date of departure (if client did not advise before leaving New Zealand) and
- did the client apply for or get any benefit or pension in the country that they travelled to, or an increase in the benefit or pension that they already get from that country during their stay there?
Note couples getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate of New Zealand Superannuation will lose their grandparenting, if the qualified client is not entitled to payment during their absence, or any part of their absence.

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand is delayed — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand is delayed
If unexpected circumstances, beyond the client's control, prevent their return to New Zealand within 30 weeks, payment for the paydays that fall within the first 26 weeks of absence can be confirmed. The client must also either:
- return to New Zealand
- apply under a reciprocal agreement or
- apply for payment overseas
In no circumstances should payment continue beyond 26 weeks.
You will need to carefully investigate the circumstances that caused the delay. Circumstances beyond the control of the client would include (but are not limited to):
- aircraft breakdowns
- industrial disputes
- bereavement and
- illness/injury to the client, their partner or other relatives
You will need to find out whether or not travel arrangements were affected by such circumstances. Consider the following factors:
What were the booking arrangements before departure?
Was a return passage or flight within the allowable period arranged?
Could an earlier return have reasonably been expected despite the circumstances that arose?
When the extended absence was caused by unforeseen circumstances beyond the control of the client, payment can be confirmed for the pay days that fall within the first 26 weeks.
Note if the qualified client of a grandparented non-qualified couple is absent for more than 26 weeks, and is not entitled to payment for their absence, or any part of the absence, the grandparented non-qualified partner rate ends.
## Single living alone rate
The single living alone rate can continue to be paid for absences overseas of up to 26 weeks provided the client is otherwise entitled to get it.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review for New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Client getting New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included in the benefit have a Mandatory Review for their New Zealand Superannuation. Both the client and partner's circumstances are included in the review. MSD must review the client's New Zealand Superannuation within 52 weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed. Clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend. The purpose of a Mandatory Review for New Zealand Superannuation is to: - check for any changes to a client's circumstances and - review the rate of New Zealand Superannuation payable Note clients who do not have a grandparented non-qualified partner included in their benefit do not have a Mandatory Review for their New Zealand Superannuation.

chunks.title: Clients getting Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: All New Zealand Superannuation clients getting Disability Allowance or Accommodation Supplement have a Mandatory Review for this assistance. Clients who are getting New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included will have a Mandatory Review for Accommodation Supplement and Disability Allowance at the same time as their Mandatory Review for New Zealand Superannuation. For New Zealand Superannuation clients who only have a Mandatory Review for Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance, different rules apply.

chunks.title: Clients getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: A client getting New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified partner included and Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit will have a Mandatory Review for their New Zealand Superannuation at least once in a 52-week period, but it will be separate to the Mandatory Review for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Notice period for a Mandatory Review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Clients are notified at least 20 working days before their Mandatory Review date, unless their Accommodation Supplement is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison. Note if a client's New Zealand Superannuation is suspended when the Mandatory Review notice is sent, they are not required to respond to their Mandatory Review until their New Zealand Superannuation is to be resumed.

chunks.title: Responding to the Mandatory Review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: To respond to the Mandatory Review, the client must: - confirm or provide current information about their circumstances and - provide further information to MSD if requested Clients must confirm the information MSD holds is correct or provide any new information before their review date. When a client has responded to the Mandatory Review and MSD has determined they continue to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation, their next review date is 52 weeks from the date their Mandatory Review was completed.

chunks.title: Client does not respond to Mandatory Review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When a client does not respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, the New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) will suspend. If the client does not respond to the Mandatory Review to confirm their circumstances within 2 years after their payments have suspended, their benefit will be cancelled. A client can still do their Mandatory Review during those 2 years. However, once the benefit has cancelled, the client will need to apply for New Zealand Superannuation if they still want this assistance. A client's New Zealand Superannuation cannot be resumed before they have responded to their Mandatory Review during the 2-year suspension period.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) suspends — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If a client's New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) suspends as a result of the client not responding to their Mandatory Review, all of their assistance will also suspend, except for the following payments: - Child Disability Allowance - Orphan's Benefit - Unsupported Child's Benefit - Childcare Subsidy - OSCAR (Out of School Care and Recreational Subsidy) - Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment

chunks.title: When the Mandatory Review is completed — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: The Mandatory Review is completed when MSD makes a decision about whether the client continues to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation (with a grandparented non-qualified partner included) and the rate of benefit payable. MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g., client has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Single living alone rate and absences from New Zealand — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Single living alone rate and absences from New Zealand
The single living alone rate can continue to be paid during temporary absences from New Zealand if the client:
- still meets the definition of living alone and
- is eligible for and receiving New Zealand Superannuation
## Not entitled to the single living alone rate
If the client is not entitled to the single living alone rate while they are absent from New Zealand, their New Zealand Superannuation should be reduced to the single sharing accommodation rate from the day after departure from New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Single living alone rate
- Definition of living alone
- Absence from New Zealand
- Overseas medical treatment
- Humanitarian work

chunks.title: Sole Parents — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Sole Parents
For the first 13 weeks in hospital, sole parent clients are entitled to the full rate of payment. If a sole parent requests, apportion part of their payment to cover the cost of alternative care or accommodation for the client's dependent children.
For more information on apportionments, see:
- Agents
Check:
- whether the client is likely to be in hospital for longer than 13 weeks
- how long the client is likely to be in hospital
- their financial circumstances
- their continuing commitments and
- any childcare arrangements
If the client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the client has continuing financial costs including supporting their children, you can pay at a rate higher than the hospital rate up to the maximum otherwise payable.
For more information see:
- Guidelines for paying a higher rate
If there are no other continuing financial costs and it is likely that the client will remain in hospital long term, consider other means of income support for the children. For example, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit or including the child/children in the new caregivers benefit.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit

chunks.title: Special Disability Allowance — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Special Disability Allowance
A Special Disability Allowance can be paid to the partner of a client in hospital or residential care who is receiving a reduced rate of New Zealand Superannuation or receiving Residential Care Subsidy.
It is paid to the partner in the community to help with extra costs because of their partner's hospitalisation.
No application form is needed, and it is not income or asset tested.
Special Disability Allowance should be stopped from the first available date if the person receiving it is also admitted to hospital or residential care.
Note if a Veteran's Pension client is in hospital for more than 13 weeks their payments are not reduced to the hospital rate and their partner cannot get Special Disability Allowance. This is because Veteran's Pension is not affected by hospitalisation.
For the rate of Special Disability Allowance see:
- Deskfile Special Disability Allowance rates

chunks.title: Specific engagements — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Specific engagements
Specific engagements are interactions that can meet the same purpose as the Mandatory Review. These interactions can capture information that confirms whether a client still qualifies for New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualifying partner included.
Specific engagements are when a client has an interaction with MSD, and this results in a full review of the client's circumstances.
For example, specific engagements may include when a client contacts MSD to:
- discuss a change in circumstances or
- apply for assistance
If the specific engagement meets the same purpose as a Mandatory Review, and the client still qualifies, their Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from when the specific engagement was completed.

chunks.title: Student Loan repayments — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Student Loan repayments
Clients on New Zealand Superannuation with a Student Loan must use a tax code with the Student Loan ("SL") repayment code. This will ensure that Student Loan repayments are deducted every pay period if required.
A Student Loan repayment is required when:
- the client's gross weekly payment of New Zealand Superannuation is over the Student Loan repayment threshold or
- the client is on secondary tax code, regardless of the client's rate of payment
For more information see:
- Repayment thresholds (current)
If the client's New Zealand Superannuation is over the Student Loan repayment threshold, the Student Loan repayments will automatically be deducted from their fortnightly payment.
Deductions are calculated weekly but made fortnightly.
If the client's New Zealand Superannuation is below the Student Loan repayment threshold, no Student Loan repayments will be made from the client's payment, unless the client is on a secondary tax code.
Clients can make voluntary payments direct to Inland Revenue at any time.
For more information on Student Loans see:
- Student Loan
- Student loan tax codes [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Study — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Study
If a New Zealand Superannuation client (or partner) starts full-time or part-time study it does not affect their New Zealand Superannuation.
For any study commencing on or after 1 January 2011:
- a client will not be able to receive Student Allowance if the client or their partner is receiving New Zealand Superannuation
- a client will not be able to receive Student Loan Living Costs if the client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or is included in their partners' New Zealand Superannuation

chunks.title: SWIFTT process to pay a partner — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT process to pay a partner
When you decide to continue payment of New Zealand Superannuation to the partner of a client who has been imprisoned, you will need to determine the most appropriate SWIFTT process to enable payment to be made to the partner.
The process for payment will depend on the following:
- the period in prison is in the past
- the client is due to be released from prison shortly
- the client is likely to be in prison for more than four weeks and
- the rate of payment for the partner
Note there is discretion to pay the full married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit.
## Period in prison has passed or release is imminent
Generally you should use the SBDR screen in SWIFTT to:
- suspend the client's portion of New Zealand Superannuation for the period in prison and
- pay the appropriate rate of New Zealand Superannuation to the partner
## Period in prison exceeds 4 weeks
When the New Zealand Superannuation is to continue, and be paid to the partner you will need to contact Helpline for advice regarding the SWIFTT process to use.

chunks.title: Exception — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Exception
Tax details can be issued if a client:
- dies - you can provide details to the estate solicitor, administrator, executor etc or
- is paid New Zealand Superannuation overseas - details will automatically be sent to the client in April each year

chunks.title: Tax codes — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Tax codes
New Zealand Superannuation clients must choose a tax code appropriate to their circumstances. The client can change their tax code at any time.
All queries about correct tax codes must be referred to Inland Revenue.
As a general guideline:
- if New Zealand Superannuation is the client's highest or only source of income, the 'M' tax code should be used
- if New Zealand Superannuation is not the client's highest or only source of income, a secondary or 'S' tax code should be used or
- clients with a Student Loan must use a tax code with the Student Loan (SL) repayment code or
- a tailored tax code can also be used when the client has other income
## Tailored tax codes
Clients need to apply to Inland Revenue for a tailored tax code. The client needs to provide proof of their tailored tax code for example, a letter from Inland Revenue, for this to be added to their New Zealand Superannuation record.
A tailored tax code should only be added to a client's New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension at grant if verification from Inland Revenue of the tailored tax code is provided by the client.
The tailored tax code only applies for the year in which it is issued. Each year all clients with a tailored tax code need to re-apply to Inland Revenue to get a tailored tax code.
Instructions are provided each year in March on the 'end of tax year' process required for clients with a tailored tax code.
## SWIFTT
You can view a client's current monthly tax details in STAXQ. The client's tax history can be viewed in STAXI.
For more information see:
- Payment
- Taxation
- Tax codes and tax rates for individuals Inland Revenue

chunks.title: Tax codes for hospital rate — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Tax codes for hospital rate
The hospital rate for New Zealand Superannuation (after tax) must be equal to the hospital rates for other benefits. This means that the client's tax code may need to be changed.
If the client's usual rate of payment (after tax) is below the hospital rate, ask the client what tax code they prefer.
Restore the tax code to the pre-hospital code on discharge if it has been changed.
For more information about tax codes see:
- Taxation

chunks.title: Taxation — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Taxation
New Zealand Superannuation is a taxable benefit. MSD makes payments to clients at the net rate after the deduction of tax. MSD passes the tax on to Inland Revenue.
Generally MSD will request a client or partner who is included in the New Zealand Superannuation (grandparented non-qualified partner) to provide MSD with their IRD number or evidence of their IRD number.

chunks.title: Temporary absence — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Temporary absence
When a client is going to be temporarily overseas (i.e. they are still ordinarily resident in New Zealand) there are a number of options available to the client depending on how long they will be overseas.
You should also advise the client that while payment can continue for up to 26 weeks, provided they return to New Zealand within 30 weeks, they must remain ordinarily resident in New Zealand. In addition, if the client
- leaves New Zealand temporarily, eg on holiday, but does not return to New Zealand and decides to live permanently overseas
- is simply returning to New Zealand every 26 weeks in order to remain qualified for New Zealand Superannuation but is no longer ordinarily resident in New Zealand and
- if they decide to remain overseas for longer than 30 weeks
an overpayment will be established.
As payments can continue for up to 26 weeks, provided the client returns to New Zealand within 30 weeks, you should advise a client intending to be overseas for more than 26 weeks that if they are staying in a country that:
- has a Reciprocal agreement with New Zealand they may qualify for a benefit or pension in that country or
- New Zealand does not have a Reciprocal agreement with, they may be able to get part of their New Zealand Superannuation payments
Note couples getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate of New Zealand Superannuation will lose their grandparenting if the qualified client is not entitled to payment during their absence, or any part of their absence.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit for a single client — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit for a single client
When a single client (with no children) dies, payment generally stops from the day after the date of death. However, there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days. When payment is continued after the date of death, it is referred to as terminal benefit.
Circumstances where you might consider continued payment beyond a single client's date of death include:
- when the deceased client's domestic situation results in a transition cost for a family member, causing hardshipExample: accommodation and other household costs when client has been sharing accommodation
or
- when there are exceptional and justified costs associated with the death of the clientExample: multiple deaths within one family
You should not continue payment for 28 days following the death of a single client to meet funeral expenses. A Funeral Grant is available for this purpose.
## SWIFTT
If you are paying terminal benefit for a single client you will need to manually calculate entitlement and make an adhoc payment. There is no automatic provision for the payment of terminal benefit (for a single client) on SWIFTT. You should make notes in CMS with the adhoc amount and the period it represents.
Wherever possible you should enter the next of kin or the executor of the deceased's estate on SWIFTT.
For more information see:
- Avoiding a debt
- Terminal benefit rate

chunks.title: Terminal benefit payments to surviving partner or person caring for the child or children — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit payments to surviving partner or person caring for the child or children
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children. The surviving partner could be a grandparented non-qualified partner or getting a main benefit.
## Surviving partner
When New Zealand Superannuation is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person and the surviving person's portion of New Zealand Superannuation is paid. Payment is the total New Zealand Superannuation payment as well as any ongoing extra help.
The deceased person's portion of terminal benefit is paid to their bank account.
A surviving person can apply to have the deceased person's portion of terminal benefit paid to them. Where an application is received, terminal benefit (or remaining unpaid balance) can be paid to that applicant.
The surviving partner's New Zealand Superannuation or main benefit should be reviewed to determine the best option financially for the person.
## Surviving children
When the deceased client has no surviving partner but has surviving children, the payment can be made to the person caring for the deceased client's children.
When an application is received, the remaining unpaid balance of terminal benefit can be paid to the carer.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit rate — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: The provision to continue payment for 28 days following the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit. Benefit payment is continued at the rate which was payable to the client and partner (if any) at the date of death and includes any extra help being paid (for up to 28 days following the date of death).

chunks.title: Payments at a reduced rate — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: If the client's New Zealand Superannuation payment is being paid at a reduced rate when the client dies, the terminal benefit is also paid at the reduced rate. Payments may have been reduced due to: - hospitalisation - income (if a grandparented non-qualifying partner is included or surviving partner gets a main benefit) - debt repayment if there are benefit arrears due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit paymentdo not recover debts, in full, from terminal benefit payments - if there are benefit arrears due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit payment - do not recover debts, in full, from terminal benefit payments - Child Support if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed.Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however, MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenuewhen a surviving partner or family member makes enquires, refer them to Inland Revenue - if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed. - Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however, MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenue - when a surviving partner or family member makes enquires, refer them to Inland Revenue - redirection to Kāinga ora or a community housing providerWhen the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. For more information see: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client - court attachment orders Note all of the above deductions will continue to be made from the terminal benefit payments unless they are manually stopped before cancellation.

chunks.title: Underpaid — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Underpaid
When a client has been underpaid New Zealand Superannuation and is owed arrears, MSD will work out the amount of tax and pass this on to Inland Revenue.
The amount is included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment for the current tax year, regardless of the period that the underpayment covers. This is different to how arrears payments for main benefits are taxed.
Example
A client is paid arrears on 12 June 2026. This payment represents arrears for 25 March 2026 to 3 June 2026.
The whole arrears payment will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (the current tax year).
## Overpaid
If a client has been overpaid, the overpayment is always established for the net amount. Inland Revenue will return the tax portion of the overpayment directly to MSD.
The overpayment will reduce the amount of benefit and tax paid in the tax year in which the overpayment was made, that is, the overpayment will directly relate to the tax year in which it occurred.

chunks.title: Verification — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Verification
You must be satisfied that you can accurately identify the deceased client's New Zealand Superannuation record.
Generally we will accept verbal notification of a client's death. This advice can be acted on when you determine the relationship of the caller to the deceased client and obtaining sufficient information to provide confirmation of the deceased's identity.
Follow-up verification should generally be requested. A copy of the death certificate or a copy of the death notice is acceptable support documentation.

chunks.title: Verification of income — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Verification of income
When a client has a review, MSD may require verification of income earned for the 52 weeks since the last anniversary of their New Zealand Superannuation commencement date.
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension who also get Disability Allowance are not required to provide verification of their income if it is below the relevant income limit by at least $20 per week ($1040.00 per annum).
If a client has a grandparented non-qualified partner included in their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, they are not required to provide verification of their income if it is below the grandparented non-qualified partner income exemption by at least $20.00 per week ($1040.00 per annum).
If the client cannot provide verification (for example payslips) then you can contact the employer and ask them to complete the Employment and earnings information for reviews (V26) form.
Once we have confirmed income details a due/paid income assessment will need to be done.

chunks.title: Weekend leave — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text:
## Weekend leave
New Zealand Superannuation is paid for a fourteen day period, covering Wednesday to Tuesday.
Therefore, where the client is receiving the hospital rate and they are on weekend leave you should pay the appropriate full rate of New Zealand Superannuation for the number of days the client is on leave and subsequently incurring additional expenses in the community.
## Example
Client is on leave from Friday to Monday, you will need to pay the appropriate full rate of New Zealand Superannuation for 4 days. Generally, you will do this by completing a back dated review so that SWIFTT will pay the appropriate full rate of New Zealand Superannuation for 4 days.
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.

chunks.title: When an extension or exemption can be given — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: When a client needs more time to respond to the Mandatory Review, they may be able to get an extension. If a client is unable to respond to the review, they may be able to get an exemption. Clients must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption. A client cannot get an extension or exemption on or after the Mandatory Review date. Note even if a client gets an extension or exemption, they must still advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation (with a non-qualified partner included) or the rate payable.

chunks.title: Extension - client needs more time to complete review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
chunks.text: Clients may be able to get an extension if there is a good and sufficient reason why they cannot respond to their Mandatory Review before the review date. When a client needs more time to complete their review, they must let MSD know before their Mandatory Review date. The extension can only be granted before the review date. Good and sufficient reasons may include (but are not limited to): - the client is unexpectedly hospitalised - death or illness in the client's immediate family - the client is experiencing or escaping a family violence situation If MSD determines the client has a good and sufficient reason, the client can get an extension of up to 20 working days. Note a client can get multiple short extensions, however the maximum amount of time that can be given for an extension is a total of 20 working days from the client's original review date.

chunks.title: Exemption - client is unable to complete review — main benefits > new zealand superannuation > changes and reviews new zealand superannuation
