- Social Security Act 2018
- Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Child Support Act 1991
- Tax Administration Act 1994
- any Ministry of Social Development debt that is being recovered from the caregiver
- the composition of the caregiver's family, including the number of family members who are dependent on the caregiver, as known by the Ministry
This information is used to determine how much the caregiver can reasonably be expected to pay each week on any outstanding fines.
For more information see:
- Protected earnings rate
## Information that can be provided
The Ministry of Social Welfare can provide the Ministry of Justice with the last known address and telephone number of a caregiver under schedule 6, clause 13 of the Social Security Act 2018. This only applies when the Ministry of Justice is unable to locate a caregiver who is in default of a court fine.
## Information that cannot be provided
The following information cannot be provided to the Ministry of Justice:
- the caregiver's benefit number
- the benefit type and
- employer details

chunks.title: Death of a caregiver or child — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Death of a caregiver or child
When the caregiver or child dies, Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit payments can continue for up to 28 days following the date of death.
## Verification
MSD must be satisfied that the deceased caregiver's or child's benefit record can be accurately identified. Generally verbal notification of a death will be acceptable. This advice can be acted on when the relationship of the caller to the deceased caregiver or child is determined, and sufficient information to provide confirmation of the deceased's identity has been obtained.
Follow-up verification should generally be requested. A copy of the death certificate or a copy of the death notice is acceptable support documentation.
## Mandatory Reviews
There are no Mandatory Reviews of Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit when the caregiver or child (that Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid for) has died.
All other Mandatory Reviews, including Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit paid for another child, must still be completed.
The caregiver may be able to get an extension if they need more time to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the caregiver is unable to respond to the review (even if they had more time) based on their individual circumstances, they may qualify for an exemption.
## Child turns 18
When a caregiver or child (that Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid for) has died, the notice when a child turns 18 is not required to be responded to and Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit will not stop during the continuation of payment period.
However, if Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is continuing for up to 28 days because a child has died, and a different child in their care (that Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is also paid for) turns 18, the caregiver must respond to the notice or Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit for the 18-year-old will stop.

chunks.title: Deductions — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Deductions
In certain circumstances the Ministry of Social Development can be required to pay part of the client's benefit to another party.
The Ministry is legally required to make such deductions when served with a properly issued Deduction Notice or Attachment Order. In these cases, the consent of the caregiver is not required.
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others.

chunks.title: Examples of Mandatory Review outcomes — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: MSD must review a caregiver's Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit within 52-weeks of the commencement date of their benefit, or 52-weeks from when the caregiver's last Mandatory Review was completed. The Mandatory Review is completed when MSD has determined if the caregiver continues to qualify for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit and the rate payable (if applicable). When a caregiver responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined if the caregiver qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit to check the caregiver is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period - cancel the benefit and other assistance for the child if the caregiver no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: Outcomes of a Mandatory Review Examples Client declares no change Susan is getting Unsupported Child's Benefit for Isobel and her Mandatory Review is due on 14 August 2026. Susan responds to her Mandatory Review on 13 August 2026 and confirms she has had no change to her circumstances. Because Susan has declared no change in circumstances, MSD continues her Unsupported Child's Benefit for Isobel at the same rate. MSD completes Susan's Mandatory Review on 13 August and sets the next review date for 52 weeks later (12 August 2027). Client declares a change in circumstances Kellie is getting Unsupported Childs Benefit for Nala and her Mandatory Review is due on 10 May 2027. Kellie responds to her Mandatory Review on 5 May 2027 and tells MSD that on 1 April 2027 Nala got a $3,000 income payment from a trust and that it will be paid annually. Because Nala's trust income is less than 50% of the annual rate payable for Unsupported Child's Benefit, MSD determines that Kellie can continue getting Unsupported Child's Benefit paid at the same rate. MSD completes Kellie's Mandatory Review on 5 May 2027 and sets the next review date for 52 weeks later (3 May 2028). Not enough information to complete Mandatory Review Virginia is getting Orphan's Benefit for two children in her care, Melanie and Eric, and her Mandatory Review is due on 13 October 2027. Virginia responds to the Mandatory Review on 8 October 2027 and tells MSD that Eric is no longer in her care. Virginia has declared a change in circumstances that affects the rate payable for Orphan's Benefit. However, MSD does not have enough information to determine when Orphan's Benefit should be reviewed from as she has not confirmed the date Eric left her care. MSD cannot complete the Mandatory Review without requesting more information from Virginia. MSD sets a new reasonable deadline of 15 October 2027 for Virginia to provide further information. Virginia's Orphan's Benefit continues to be paid at the same rate during this time. If Virginia does not provide information before 15 October 2027, Orphan's Benefit will suspend on this date. Virginia contacts MSD on 14 October 2027 and confirms Eric left her care on 30 September 2027 to live with his grandparents.

chunks.title: Examples of outcomes that can occur — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: MSD determines that the rate of Orphan's Benefit will reduce when Eric is excluded and must use discretion to consider whether payment is able to continue for up to 28 days following the event. MSD completes Virginia's Mandatory Review on 14 October and sets the next review date for 52 weeks later (12 October 2028). Note when there is a change in circumstances that means they no longer qualify for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, MSD should consider if the caregiver qualifies for other types of assistance.

chunks.title: Financially independent — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Financially independent
A child is considered to be financially independent when the child:
- is in full-time employment
- gets a Student Allowance or
- gets a main benefit in their own right or
- gets a payment that is considered to be the equivalent of a main benefit
## Other situations where a child is considered to be financially independent
There may be other situations where all a child's financial needs (including the provision of accommodation and material needs) are being met by someone else or from some other source. For example:
- a family trust or
- the parent who is not acting as the caregiver
## Date of review
Generally, when a child becomes financially independent Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit should stop from the start of the pay period following the date the child became financially independent.
There is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the event to allow for a period of financial adjustment, generally to avoid hardship for the client.

chunks.title: Full-time employment — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Full-time employment
When a child starts full-time employment, the child is no longer a dependent child.
Note if the dependent child is temporarily working more than 30 hours per week during the school holidays and they are returning to school after the holidays, they are not considered in full-time employment.
## Date of review
Generally, Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit should stop from the start of the pay period following the date the child started work.
There is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the event to allow for a period of financial adjustment, generally to avoid hardship for the client.

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
If the caregiver or the child (that Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid for) is admitted to hospital there is no change to the rate of payment.
While the caregiver or child is in hospital MSD will need to check if the child continues to meet the definition of dependent child and the caregiver continues to be an eligible caregiver.
When a child is admitted to hospital (depending on the nature of the child's injury, illness or disability) the caregiver may be able to get Child Disability Allowance. Child Disability Allowance is a non-taxable allowance paid to an eligible caregiver of a child with a serious disability, who is in need of constant care and attention for a period longer than 12 months.
## Client in hospital during Mandatory Review
Generally, caregivers getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit must respond to their Mandatory Review before their review date or their payments will suspend.
However, when a caregiver or the child is in hospital and the caregiver needs more time to respond to the review, they may be able to get an extension.
In some situations, an exemption may be considered.
The caregiver must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension.

chunks.title: Inland Revenue deduction notices — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
Inland Revenue may request for a caregiver's unpaid taxes to be directly deducted from their benefit payments.
Note all Inland Revenue deduction notices are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
The instructions of the deduction notice will be to deduct the lowest of either:
- 10% of the total debt which Inland Revenue specify in the notice, on a weekly basis or
- 20% of the caregiver's gross earnings on a weekly basis
When there are insufficient funds to cover the deduction, the Ministry of Social Development must advise Inland Revenue immediately that the deduction will not start or will start at a reduced rate.
Inland Revenue deductions have a lower priority than Child Support deductions.
For more information see:
- Priority for deductions

chunks.title: Mandatory Review dates for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review dates for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit
MSD must review a caregiver's Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit within 52-weeks of the commencement date of the benefit, or within 52-weeks from when the caregiver's last Mandatory Review was completed.
The caregivers next review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD determined the caregiver continues to qualify for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit and the rate of benefit payable (i.e. when MSD completes the review).
Caregivers who are getting another benefit that is subject to a Mandatory Review will have their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit reviewed separately to that benefit, unless the caregiver is getting Disability Allowance for the child that Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid. In this case, Disability Allowance will be reviewed at the same time as their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
Note when MSD has an interaction with a caregiver that confirms all of the same circumstances as a Mandatory Review, this can push out the caregiver's Mandatory Review date by 52 weeks. This is known as a specific engagement.
## Initial Mandatory Review dates
Benefit commencement date
Mandatory Review dates
Benefit commenced before 1 July 2026
Caregivers whose Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit commenced before 1 July 2026 will have their initial Mandatory Review either:
- 52 weeks from the commencement date of the benefit
or
- 52 weeks from when their last periodic review was completed
Benefit commenced on or after 1 July 2026
If a caregiver's Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit commenced on or after 1 July 2026, their initial Mandatory Review date is either:
- 52 weeks from the commencement date of the benefit
or
- 52 weeks from the completion of a specific engagement

chunks.title: Mandatory Review not required — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review not required
There is no Mandatory Review for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit in the following circumstances:
- the caregiver has died
- the child (that Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid for) has died
- the caregiver is living in or visiting a region affected by an emergency or adverse event and they are unable to reasonably leave the area
- the caregiver is living in or visiting a region affected by an outbreak of a quarantinable disease and an epidemic notice has been given and is in force
or when:
- there is a system outage that prevents MSD from carrying out Mandatory Reviews
MSD will also stop the review for any caregivers who are in these circumstances after they have been notified about their Mandatory Review.
MSD will notify the caregiver when they are not required to complete the review. The Mandatory Review date is reset to 52 weeks in the future from the caregiver's review date.
Note a notification will not be sent when the caregiver or child has died.

chunks.title: Ministry of Social Development debt repayments — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Ministry of Social Development debt repayments
When a caregiver has a Ministry of Social Development debt, this can be recovered by regular deductions from their current benefit.
Note Income Related Rent historical Kāinga Ora debt should be given equal priority to Ministry of Social Development debt.
For more information see:
- Current client debt Negotiating repayment of debt

chunks.title: New caregiver applies for benefit — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## New caregiver applies for benefit
Where a new caregiver applies for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, MSD must obtain verification from the previous caregiver that the child is no longer in their care.
## Applications for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit
If the new caregiver meets all the qualifications, and there has been no change in the circumstances of the child's parents, then Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit can be paid to the new caregiver.
When any application for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is granted, entitlement to an Establishment Grant can be considered, and a Clothing Allowance for the child will be paid automatically.

chunks.title: Obligation to advise of departure from New Zealand — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Obligation to advise of departure from New Zealand
All caregivers getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit must tell MSD before they leave New Zealand.
If a caregiver does not tell MSD before they and/or the child (that Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid for) go overseas, their benefit payments will stop from the day after they leave New Zealand.
## Does not advise of departure
MSD has an Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service that identifies clients who have left New Zealand if they are getting a benefit.
MSD uses this information to stop a caregiver's Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit if they have not advised of their or the child's intended departure before leaving New Zealand.

chunks.title: Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit suspended before Mandatory Review date — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit suspended before Mandatory Review date
Clients getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit are generally notified about their Mandatory Review, even if their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is suspended, unless it is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison.
MSD must not undertake the Mandatory Review unless the client contacts MSD to resume their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
If the caregiver contacts MSD before their review date to resume their benefit, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to do their Mandatory Review. MSD can resume the benefit before the Mandatory Review has been responded to.
However, if the caregiver contacts MSD on or after the Mandatory Review date, the review must be completed before MSD can resume the benefit (if they still qualify).
Example
Dennis is getting Unsupported Child's Benefit for Ross, and his Mandatory Review is due on 2 April 2027.
Dennis and Ross left New Zealand to go on holiday on 29 March 2027 and did not tell MSD that they were leaving. His Unsupported Child's Benefit suspended on 30 March 2027.
On 14 April 2027 Dennis contacts MSD and advises that they arrived back in New Zealand on 7 April 2027.
MSD advises Dennis that he will need to respond to the Mandatory Review and confirm his circumstances before MSD can resume the Unsupported Child's Benefit.
On 16 April 2027 Dennis responds to his Mandatory Review and confirms that he has had no change in circumstances.
MSD determines that Dennis continues to qualify for Unsupported Child's Benefit for Ross at the same rate and resumes the Unsupported Child's Benefit from 7 April 2027.
MSD completes Dennis' Mandatory Review on 16 April 2027 and sets the next review date for 52 weeks later (14 April 2028).

chunks.title: Outcomes of a Mandatory Review — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: Caregivers must respond to their Mandatory Review before their Mandatory Review date, or their payments will suspend. When a caregiver responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined if the caregiver qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the caregiver is getting the correct rate - suspend if there is no benefit payable for a period - cancel the benefit if the caregiver no longer qualifies The Mandatory Review is complete when MSD makes a decision about the caregiver's eligibility for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit and the rate of benefit payable (if applicable). MSD may also carry out a separate review of Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit at any time, where there is good reason.

chunks.title: Caregiver declares no change — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: When a caregiver responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have had no change in circumstances, MSD must continue their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit at the same rate. The caregiver's next review date will be set for 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review.

chunks.title: Caregiver declares a change in circumstances — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: When a caregiver responds to the Mandatory Review with a change in circumstances, MSD must use the information provided to determine if the caregiver continues to qualify for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit and the rate payable. If a caregiver is also getting Disability Allowance for the child who Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid for, MSD will use that information to determine if they continue to qualify for Disability Allowance and the rate payable at the same time. MSD may request further information from the caregiver if it is unclear if the caregiver continues to qualify for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, or the child's Disability Allowance (if applicable). Date of change When a caregiver declares a change in circumstances, MSD will need to assess if the caregiver still qualifies for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit and the rate payable and from what date, depending on when the change in circumstances happened or will happen. Caregiver is also getting other assistance When the caregiver has provided information as part of the Mandatory Review that could affect their entitlement to or the rate payable of any other assistance, MSD may use this information to review that assistance. When the other assistance is affected by the outcome of the Mandatory Review, MSD must change the rate, suspend or cancel that assistance where appropriate. For example, a caregiver gets Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit for multiple children and the outcome of the Mandatory Review is that the caregiver is entitled to a different rate as one of the children has left their care, any other assistance paid for the child must be reviewed, and the rate may change or stop if they no longer qualify.

chunks.title: Further information is needed to complete the Mandatory Review — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: When a caregiver has responded to the review and further information is needed to determine if the caregiver continues to qualify for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, or that the rate of payment is correct, MSD must give a reasonable timeframe for the caregiver to provide it. The date the caregiver is given to provide the information by becomes the caregiver's new deadline to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the caregiver doesn't provide the information that was asked for before the deadline, MSD must suspend the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit on the new deadline date. If the caregiver provides the information that was asked for and MSD determines the caregiver continues to qualify for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit (including the rate payable), a future Mandatory Review date is set 52-weeks from the date MSD completed the review.

chunks.title: Completing the Mandatory Review when there are new costs — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: MSD can still complete the Mandatory Review when a caregiver also gets Disability Allowance for the child and has declared a new disability cost. This is because it doesn't affect the caregiver's eligibility for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit or the Disability Allowance for the child.

chunks.title: Part-time employment — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Part-time employment
Part-time employment does not make a child financially independent. Do not take the child's earnings into account when assessing the rate of Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit payments.
For more information on children's income see:
- Income

chunks.title: Permanent absence — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
If the caregiver or the child (that Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid for) is leaving New Zealand permanently, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit must be cancelled from the day after departure.
If the child is remaining in New Zealand:
- the new caregiver may meet the qualifications for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit or
- if the new caregiver is receiving a main benefit the child may be included as a dependent child in the benefit, unless the period of care is temporary.

chunks.title: Permanent return to parents' care — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Permanent return to parents' care
When a child returns to live with their parents permanently, and the parents resume primary responsibility for the child other than on a temporary basis, then the caregiver getting Unsupported Child's Benefit is no longer an eligible caregiver.
The Unsupported Child's Benefit should generally stop from the start of the pay period following the date of event.
However, there is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the event to allow for a period of financial adjustment, generally to avoid hardship for the client.

chunks.title: Priority for deductions — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Priority for deductions
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others; the following list gives the order of priority, highest to lowest:
Highest priority
- Child Support deductions made under the Child Support Act 1991
- Inland Revenue tax deductions
- Ministry of Social Development debt repayments including Liable Parent Contributions (LPC), child maintenance debts and Major Repairs Advances (MRA), Student Allowance debt, Student Loan debt converted to Ministry of Social Development debt, Income Related Rent historical Kāinga Ora debt, Income Related Rent Ministry of Social Development debt
- Attachment orders made under the Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Court attachment orders issued under the Summary Proceedings Act 1957
- Court attachment orders issued under the District Court Act 2016
- Student Loan repayments
Lowest priority
Determining the priority of deductions is necessary when a caregiver has more than one order issued in respect of their benefit. Each order and deduction notice is subject to its own protected earnings rule.
When you need to reduce deductions you adjust from the lowest priority up to those with a higher priority taking into account the protected earnings rules for each.
## Example
A caregiver has both Child Support and Ministry of Social Development debt deductions to be made from their benefit.
When the level of Ministry of Social Development debt would reduce the caregiver's benefit payments below the Child Support protected earnings rate, the Ministry of Social Development debt deduction must be reduced not any Child Support payments.
This is because Child Support deductions take priority over Ministry of Social Development debt repayments.

chunks.title: Protected earnings rate — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Protected earnings rate
Both the District Court Act and the Summary Proceedings Act provide that every Ministry of Justice attachment order must specify a 'protected earnings rate'. The protected earnings rate is usually 60% of the client’s net earnings after PAYE tax has been deducted or withheld.
If the attachment order will reduce the caregivers income below the protected earnings rate, then the order will not operate and you must cancel or return the attachment order to the Ministry of Justice.
Calculating the caregivers income differs between attachment orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act and the District Court Act, in that different benefits are taken into account. Therefore it is important to determine what type of attachment order has been issued.
Summary Proceedings Act 1957
For orders made under this act, the calculation of the caregivers income does not include Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support, Disability Allowance, Child Disability Allowance, Winter Energy Payment, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit
District Court Act 2016
For orders made under the District Court Act 2016, the caregivers income includes Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support and Disability Allowance but does not include Child Disability Allowance, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit
## Example
An attachment order is received from the Ministry of Justice for $120.00 per week. The order lists the protected income as $375.91 per week:
Sole parent support net rate (as at 1 April 2026)
$521.52
Plus Accommodation Supplement (Area 2)
$105.00
Total net earnings
$626.52
60% of total net earnings (= protected earnings)
$375.91
Calculate if Attachment Order will exceed protected earnings
Total net earnings
$626.52
Less Child Support
$55.00
Less Ministry of Social Development debt
$90.00
Sub total
$481.52
Less Attachment Order
$120.00
Total
$361.52
The court order takes the caregivers income to $361.52, which is below the protected income rate of $375.91. The attachment order will not operate, therefore you must return it to the Court, Ministry of Justice for the order to be amended.

chunks.title: Gets a Student Allowance — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Gets a Student Allowance
When a child gets a Student Allowance or an Independent Circumstances Allowance under the Student Allowances Regulations 1998 they are no longer a dependent child and Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit must generally stop from:
- the start of the pay period following the date of event or
- the date the child's Student Allowance is granted
whichever is earlier.
Wherever possible (and in appropriate circumstances) the date the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit stops and the commencement date of the Student Allowance should coincide.
Note there are specific rules for deciding whether a child is considered a dependent child when the child turns 18.
There is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days following the event to allow for a period of financial adjustment, generally to avoid hardship for the client.

chunks.title: Gets a Student Loan — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Gets a Student Loan
Getting a Student Loan (including the living cost component) does not mean a child is financially independent.
If the child continues to be the caregiver's primary responsibility and maintained as a member of their family and financially dependent (that is, the caregiver is meeting some of the costs for the child) the Orphan's or Unsupported Child's Benefit can continue to be paid until the start of the pay period following:
- the date they turn 18 or
- where the child is 18 and continuing in education, the earlier of: the date they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education orthe date the child is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required orthe date the child is financially independent orthe date the child leaves the parent or caregiver's care or31 December of the year they turn 18
- the date they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education or
- the date the child is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required or
- the date the child is financially independent or
- the date the child leaves the parent or caregiver's care or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18

chunks.title: Mandatory Review for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: MSD must review a caregivers Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit within 52-weeks of when their benefit commenced, or within 52-weeks from when the caregiver's last Mandatory Review was completed. Caregivers must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend. The purpose of a Mandatory Review is to: - check for any changes to the caregiver's or child's circumstances - determine if the caregiver still meets the qualifications for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit - determine if the child is still a dependent child - confirm the income (other than personal earnings) received by the child or on behalf of the child over the last 52 weeks and - review the rate of Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit payable

chunks.title: Caregiver is also getting Disability Allowance — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: When a caregiver is getting Disability Allowance for a child who Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid for, they will have their Disability Allowance reviewed at the same time as their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit. If a caregiver is getting Disability Allowance for someone else, they will have a Mandatory Review for their Disability Allowance at least once in a 52-week period, but it will be separate to the Mandatory Review for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Caregiver is also getting other assistance — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: If a caregiver is getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit and any other assistance (excluding Disability Allowance for the child the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid), the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit has a separate Mandatory Review at least once in a 52-week period. For any other assistance that has a Mandatory Review (excluding Disability Allowance for the child the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is paid), 26-week or 52-week reapplication, it is separate to the Mandatory Review for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit. Note When the caregiver has provided information as part of the Mandatory Review that could affect their entitlement to or rate payable of any other assistance they get for themselves or the child, such as a main benefit or extra help, MSD may use this information to review that assistance. Example Justin was granted Accommodation Supplement on 11 March 2026. He had his grandson Oliver come into his care and was granted Unsupported Child's Benefit on 5 May 2026. Because Mandatory Reviews for Unsupported Child's Benefit are done separately to Accommodation Supplement, Justin will have two Mandatory Reviews. The review date for Accommodation Supplement is based on its commencement date and set for 52 weeks from 11 March 2026 and the review date for Unsupported Child's Benefit is based on its commencement date and reset to 52 weeks from 5 May 2026.

chunks.title: Notice period for a Mandatory Review — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: Caregivers are notified at least 20 working days before their Mandatory Review date, unless their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison. The notice period allows sufficient time for caregivers to respond to the Mandatory Review. Note if a client's Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is suspended when the Mandatory Review notice is sent, they are not required to respond to their Mandatory Review until their Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is to be resumed.

chunks.title: Responding to the Mandatory Review — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: To respond to the Mandatory Review, the caregiver must: - confirm or provide current information about their circumstances and - provide further information to MSD if requested Caregivers must confirm the information MSD holds is correct or provide any new information before their review date. When a caregiver has responded to the Mandatory Review and MSD has determined they continue to qualify for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, their next review date is 52 weeks from the date their Mandatory Review was completed.

chunks.title: Caregiver does not respond to the Mandatory Review — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: When a caregiver does not respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit will suspend, as well as any other assistance they get for that child (excluding Child Disability Allowance, Childcare Subsidy, OSCAR Subsidy and Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment). If the caregiver does not respond to the Mandatory Review to confirm their circumstances within 8 weeks after their payments have suspended, the Orphan's Benefit, Unsupported Child's Benefit and any other assistance that was also suspended will be cancelled. A caregiver can still do their Mandatory Review during those 8 weeks. However, once the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit has cancelled, the caregiver will need to apply for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit if they still need this assistance. A client's Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit cannot be resumed before they have responded to their Mandatory Review during the 8-week suspension period.

chunks.title: Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit suspends — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: If a caregiver's Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit suspends as the result of the caregiver not responding to their Mandatory Review, all of the other assistance paid for that child will also suspend, except for the following payments: - Child Disability Allowance - Childcare Subsidy - OSCAR (Out of School Care and Recreational Subsidy) - Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment

chunks.title: When the Mandatory Review is completed — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: The Mandatory Review is complete when MSD makes a decision about the caregiver's eligibility for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit and the rate of benefit payable. MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the caregiver is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period - cancel the benefit if the caregiver no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Specific engagements — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Specific engagements
Specific engagements are interactions that can meet the same purpose as the Mandatory Review. These interactions can capture information that confirms if a caregiver still qualifies for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
Specific engagements are when a caregiver has an interaction with MSD, and this results in a full review of the caregiver's circumstances.
For example, specific engagements may include when a caregiver contacts MSD to:
- discuss a change in circumstances or
- apply for other assistance
If the specific engagement meets the same purpose as a Mandatory Review and the caregiver still qualifies, their Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from when the specific engagement was completed.

chunks.title: Temporary return to parents — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text:
## Temporary return to parents
In Unsupported Childs Benefit cases where the child leaves the care of the eligible caregiver and returns to their parents for a short period you will need to establish:
- the reason for the change
- the intended length of stay
- whether the child will return to the caregiver
- who made arrangements for the change
- whether it is likely to happen again and
- who will be providing the support, care and control of the child (that is, will the caregiver still be responsible for the child)
'Short period' is not defined. A decision whether to continue paying Unsupported Childs Benefit is to be made on the facts available. It is necessary to determine in these cases if the child is still the primary responsibility of the caregiver.
While Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid, the parents continue to be liable to pay their assessed Child Support.
## Return to parents for a trial period
When a child returns to their parents care for a trial period, Unsupported Childs Benefit continues to be paid to the eligible caregiver only.
## Transition to parents' care
When a child returns to their parents' care for part of a week, Unsupported Childs Benefit continues to be paid to the eligible caregiver only, as the child does not meet the definition of dependent child for the parents.
## Oranga Tamariki involvement
Where Oranga Tamariki has been funding a child's placement where other orders are in place, it is expected to continue to provide financial assistance.

chunks.title: When an extension or exemption can be given — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: When a caregiver needs more time to respond to the Mandatory Review, they may be able to get an extension. If a caregiver is unable to respond to the review, they may be able to get an exemption. Clients must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption. A caregiver cannot get an extension or exemption on or after the Mandatory Review date. Note even if a caregiver gets an extension or exemption, they must still advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit or the rate payable. Extension - caregiver needs more time to respond to review Caregivers may be able to get an extension if there is a good and sufficient reason why they cannot complete their Mandatory Review in time. When a caregiver needs more time to complete their review, they must let MSD know before their review date. The extension can only be granted before the review date. Good and sufficient reasons may include (but are not limited to): - the caregiver is unexpectedly hospitalised - death or illness in the caregiver's immediate family - the caregiver is experiencing or escaping a family violence situation If MSD determines the caregiver has a good and sufficient reason, the caregiver can get an extension of up to 20 working days. Note a caregiver can get multiple short extensions, however the maximum amount of time that can be given for an extension is a total of 20 working days from the caregiver's original review date. Exemption - caregiver is unable to respond to review A caregiver may be able to get an exemption when they are experiencing an unforeseen event or situation that is beyond their control, and this means they are unable to respond to their Mandatory Review (even if they had more time). The caregiver must let MSD know before their review date to discuss their circumstances. Exemption reasons may include (but are not limited to): - localised natural disaster that affects the caregiver but not the whole region (e.g. the caregiver's property is affected by a landslip) - unexpected serious illness or an accident affecting the caregiver or their immediate family member

chunks.title: When an extension or exemption can be given — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit > changes and reviews ob and ucb
chunks.text: Generally, an exemption would also apply when a caregiver's Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is ending within 28 days because the child no longer qualifies, e.g. change in caregiver. If MSD determines an exemption applies, the caregiver is not required to respond to their Mandatory Review, and the review date is reset to 52 weeks from their current review date. Example Beryl is getting Orphan's Benefit for her granddaughter Olive and has a Mandatory Review due on 12 July 2026. However, Beryl's home is damaged by a small-scale flash flood, and they cannot return home. Because Beryl has lost all her possessions and is focused on finding accommodation, MSD determines it is not reasonable for her to respond to her Mandatory Review by her review date. In this case, MSD grants an exemption. Beryl's next Mandatory Review is set for 52-weeks from the original review date.

chunks.title: Child discharged from Oranga Tamariki care — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Child discharged from Oranga Tamariki care
Where Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency has care, custody or sole guardianship of the child, and returns the child to the care of the immediate previous caregiver, the child can be considered a dependent child for benefit purposes. Unsupported Childs Benefit and Clothing Allowance may be paid.
Generally, Oranga Tamariki does not make payments for the child who is not in their care. However, in some situations the court may make an order for Oranga Tamariki to continue to make payments to the caregiver. These payments are not considered chargeable income for benefit purposes.
Where the relationship is not one of care, but more of a boarding arrangement, the young person may be able to get Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment.
Once a child has been discharged from the care of Oranga Tamariki, Unsupported Childs Benefit can be considered even when Oranga Tamariki or any other authorised agency involvement continues, for example:
- additional Guardianship Order
- Support Order or
- Services Order
These orders should be read carefully to ensure that the caregiver is eligible for benefit. Take care when dealing with services and support orders. The intention of the court in granting either of these orders may affect entitlement to Unsupported Childs Benefit.

chunks.title: Child in care of Oranga Tamariki — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Child in care of Oranga Tamariki
Where a child or young person is in the care, custody or sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, the cost of the child's care is the responsibility of Oranga Tamariki and it is responsible for making payments under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989. The child is not considered a dependent child and Unsupported Childs Benefit cannot be paid.
However, where there is a sole guardianship order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, but the child or young person is in the custody of the caregiver, the caregiver may be entitled to Unsupported Childs Benefit if all other criteria are met. Caregivers in this situation will also be automatically granted a Clothing Allowance when the Unsupported Childs Benefit is granted.
When Oranga Tamariki is involved, but there are no orders or agreements about care, the child can be considered a dependent child (for example when Oranga Tamariki provides services to family groups under a Family Group Conference plan only).
For information on different orders and whether they mean the child can be considered a dependent child while the order is still in place, see Oranga Tamariki order in place.
## Parents as caregivers
When a child is returned to the care of a parent by Oranga Tamariki the child can be considered as a dependent child and included in a main benefit that the parent is receiving.
This is regardless of whether or not the parent was the immediate previous caregiver of the child.

chunks.title: Child Support — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Child Support
Any person applying for Unsupported Childs Benefit may need to apply for Child Support through Inland Revenue.
When a carer is required to apply for Child Support, Inland Revenue works out the rate of Child Support entitlement. This is called a formula assessment.
The liable parents pay Child Support to Inland Revenue which is used to help pay for the Unsupported Childs Benefit the child's carer gets.
Any formula assessment excess Child Support will be paid to the carer and is not charged as income.
For more information see:
A carer may get Child Support paid to them for a child who they are getting Unsupported Child Benefit for, as well as another child in their care who they are not getting Unsupported Childs Benefit for.
If the Child Support is paid by the same liable parent, Inland Revenue pay both types of Child Support to the carer as one payment. This is known as a mixed Child Support payment and is treated the same as a formula assessment excess payment.
For more information see:
## Disclosure of the carer's details
MSD may get information from Oranga Tamariki about concerns a carer has for their safety when applying for Unsupported Childs Benefit and Child Support.
In these cases the disclosure of the carer's details on the Child Support application form can be replaced by using the first name only (or an alias first name) and writing the words 'surname withheld'.

chunks.title: Child's income — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Child's income
Personal earnings of the child do not affect the rate of payment of Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
A child in full-time employment and financially independent is not treated as a dependent child for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
## Other income
A child may receive other income that is not from personal earnings. Any other money received (other than personal earnings) that is more than 50% of the basic annual benefit rate reduces the benefit payable by $1.00 for every complete $1.00 of income.
Other income may include:
- interest from bank accounts
- trust income and
- payments from the Arthur Hall Fletcher Trust
If a caregiver receives an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for more than one child, the income is assessed separately for each child. This may mean different rates of benefit may apply to each child depending on their age and income levels.
## Example
For an example of assessing rate of payment where a child has income over 50% of the annual benefit rate see:
- Example
## Rate reduces below family tax credit rate
If the income received by a child reduces Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit to below the level of family tax credit that the caregiver can get, consider:
- cancelling the benefit and including the child as a dependent in a parent benefit or
- advising the caregiver to seek family tax credit payments through Inland Revenue
For more information see:
- Child starts work
- Income
- ACC child weekly compensation

chunks.title: Commencement Date — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Commencement Date
Payment of the Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit begins from either:
- the day the child comes into the care of the caregiver
- the date the child has been discharged from the care of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki or
- the date of application
whichever is the later.
From 1 July 2018 all caregivers receiving Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit will automatically be granted a weekly non-taxable Clothing Allowance for Orphans or Unsupported children.
For more information see:
- Clothing Allowance for Orphans and Unsupported children
When a new application for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is granted, review any benefits (including Extra help) received by the parents or previous caregiver and exclude the child.
Also review any benefits being made on behalf of the child, such as Child Disability Allowance and Disability Allowance.
For more information see:
- Child Disability Allowance
- Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Definition of discharged from Oranga Tamariki care — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Definition of discharged from Oranga Tamariki care
A child or young person is considered discharged from care when they are discharged from:
- the sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency
- the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency under a custody order made under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 or
- the care of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency under an agreement made under section 140 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989

chunks.title: Dependent child — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: To get Orphan’s Benefit or Unsupported Child’s Benefit, the caregiver must be the principal caregiver or the principal temporary caregiver of a dependent child. A dependent child for Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is a child who is: - primarily the responsibility of the client - maintained as a member of that family - financially dependent on that client - in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but has been returned to their parent's care A dependent child for Orphan’s Benefit or Unsupported Child’s Benefit does not include a: - child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 and - child for whom Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid for the following payments: Jobseeker SupportSole Parent PaymentYouth PaymentYoung Parent Payment (except in relation to that child's parent or step-parent). That is, a young person getting Young Parent Payment (and their child) cannot also be included in another main benefit as neither of them are considered a dependent child. See: Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step-parent examplesAccommodation Supplementthe hospital rate for clients who have been in hospital for more than 13 weeks - Jobseeker Support - Sole Parent Payment - Youth Payment - Young Parent Payment (except in relation to that child's parent or step-parent). That is, a young person getting Young Parent Payment (and their child) cannot also be included in another main benefit as neither of them are considered a dependent child. See: Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step-parent examples - Accommodation Supplement - the hospital rate for clients who have been in hospital for more than 13 weeks -  This means, when a caregiver is getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit and is also getting one of the payments above, they cannot include that child in both the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit payments and their other benefit. Sometimes, a child may be living away from home but is still considered dependent. The child may be involved or may have been previously involved with Oranga Tamariki.

chunks.title: Dependent child — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: If a child is not considered a dependent child for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit purposes - they are not a dependent child for any other benefit purposes. If the child is aged 16 or 17 years old, they may be able to get Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment.

chunks.title: Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step-parent examples — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step-parent examples
To help you identify when there is a "dependent child", please see the examples below:

chunks.title: Disclosure of the carers details (Oranga Tamariki arrangement) — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Disclosure of the carers details (Oranga Tamariki arrangement)
There may be cases when MSD may get information about a carer's safety concerns when applying for Unsupported Childs Benefit.
They may not be required to apply for Child Support.
If it is appropriate for them to apply for Child Support it would be inappropriate to disclose the carer's details on an Inland Revenue 'Application for Child Support' form.
When a carer applies for Child Support it is standard practice for Inland Revenue to send details of the caregiver recorded on an 'Application for Child Support' form to the parents who are liable in law to maintain the child.
In these cases, the carer will be advised by their Oranga Tamariki social worker to respond to question 5 of the Application for Child Support form, 'What name does the carer want the paying parent to know them by?', by using their first name only (or an alias first name) and writing the words 'surname withheld'.
Oranga Tamariki will provide a letter to the carer that supports the use of their first name only (or an alias first name), which needs to be attached to the Application for Child Support form.

chunks.title: Eligible caregiver — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Eligible caregiver
To get an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, the caregiver must be an eligible caregiver, which is either the principal caregiver or the principal temporary caregiver of the child.
Principal caregiver means the caregiver:
- has the primary responsibility for the day-to-day care of the child, other than on a temporary basis
- expects to be the principal caregiver for the child for at least 12 months or more and
- is not the natural or adoptive parent of the child, see also: Parent applies
Principal temporary caregiver means the caregiver:
- has the primary responsibility for the day-to-day care of the child
- expects to be the principal temporary caregiver for a short-term, unknown, or uncertain period and
- is not the natural or adoptive parent of the child, see also: Parent applies
When a child has been legally adopted the birth parents are no longer considered natural parents of that child.
In addition to this, for Unsupported Childs Benefit, the eligible caregiver must not be the step-parent of the child, see also: Parent applies
If a caregiver legally adopts the child, the child is regarded as their own and the caregiver cannot get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
The eligible caregiver cannot include:
- any organisation, any person who is the proprietor of, or employed in a residence established under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 or
- any other institution in which the child is being cared for
If the caregiver is applying for or already getting a benefit, they may be able to include the child and get a higher rate of payment instead of getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit.
You need to check which is most beneficial for the caregiver.

chunks.title: Establishment Grant — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Establishment Grant
The Establishment Grant is a non-taxable, non-recoverable payment to carers who are granted Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit for a child.
The caregiver, or their spouse or partner can only ever receive the Establishment Grant once for each Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit child.
The caregiver receiving Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is not required to apply for the Establishment Grant; this payment is made when the Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit has been granted.
The Establishment Grant will not be paid when a caregiver has been granted an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, if the caregiver, their spouse or partner (if any) has:
- previously received an Establishment Grant for that Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit child
or
- received or been approved to receive a payment for achieving Home for Life status for the Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit child
Note caregivers who are seeking Home for Life status but who have not been approved may be eligible for the Establishment Grant
## Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit regranted or child re-included
When the Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit has been regranted or the child is re-included, within 28 days of the previous Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit being cancelled for that child you cannot pay the Establishment Grant.
If the caregiver has been regranted an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit or the child is re-included after 28 days then the caregiver can receive an Establishment Grant, if the caregiver has never previously received an Establishment Grant for that child.
## Multiple children
An Establishment Grant can be paid for each child, when the caregiver had been granted an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for a number of children, and they meet the qualifications for an Establishment Grant.
## Payment
If a caregiver is eligible for an Establishment Grant, a payment of $350 will be made to the caregiver's bank account automatically. Only one payment of an Establishment Grant will be made per child.

chunks.title: Example - child's income — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Example - child's income
A 10 year old child gets trust income of $8,550.00 a year. The child's caregiver gets $17,012.32 annually (52 weeks at $327.16 per week, as at 1 April 2026).
As the child gets over 50% of the annual rate payable - $8,506.16, the rate of Orphans Benefit the caregiver will get is:
child's income
$8,550.00
less 50% of annual rate
$8,506.16
equals deduction
$43.84
The rate payable will be $17,012.32 less $43.84 equals $16,968.48 per year ($326.31 per week).
When clients are getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, they also get the following assistance:

chunks.title: Independent Assessment Provider — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: The Independent Assessment Provider is required to provide an assessment and recommendation to MSD for Unsupported Child's Benefit applicants. While the decision ultimately lies with MSD, the purpose of this assessment is to determine if there has been a family breakdown. Exception when there has been recent Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency involvement and evidence of the family breakdown is provided, an assessment is not required.

chunks.title: Involving parents — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: In all cases the Independent Assessment Provider will invite the parents to discuss the application for Unsupported Child's Benefit. If the applicant refuses to allow the parents to be interviewed without a satisfactory reason, and MSD does not have sufficient information to determine entitlement, MSD must advise the applicant their application will be declined. The Independent Assessment Provider will detail all contact and attempts at contact in the Unsupported Child's Benefit assessment report. Parental involvement is not required when: - care and protection concerns have been identified or - the child has been discharged from Oranga Tamariki care or has moved into permanency

chunks.title: Care and protection concerns — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: When considering whether a family breakdown has occurred it is important to consider any possible care and protection concerns for a child or young person. If MSD believes any child has been, or is likely to be harmed (physically, emotionally or sexually), ill-treated, abused, neglected, deprived or MSD has concerns about the wellbeing of the child, the case must be referred to Oranga Tamariki.

chunks.title: Disputes about recommendations made by the Independent Assessment Provider — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: MSD decides who can get an Unsupported Child’s Benefit using information from the: - application - assessment report and - recommendation of the Independent Assessment Provider If MSD is concerned about the assessment process or the recommendations made by the Independent Assessment Provider MSD should discuss any concerns with them. There are 2 scenarios when MSD may need to contact the Independent Assessment Provider before deciding whether to approve or decline an Unsupported Child's Benefit application. These are when MSD has: - extra information not included in the report that could impact the outcome of the assessment or - different information from the information included in the report that could impact the outcome of the assessment If MSD has concerns with the assessment report or doesn't agree with the recommendation MSD should: - fully document why MSD has reached a different conclusion to the Independent Assessment Provider and - include full notes of any discussion with the Independent Assessment Provider Note MSD can legally share the information it holds with the Independent Assessment Provider if the information being shared is related to whether MSD approves or declines an Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Request to access the Unsupported Child’s Benefit assessment report — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: The Unsupported Child's Benefit assessment report generally contains sensitive information provided by the parties in confidence. If one of those parties (i.e. a parent or guardian) requests a copy of the report, they may be able to access information about themselves in the report. MSD should take care to protect the other parties, particularly the child who the report is about, and in some circumstances, it may be appropriate to withhold the information requested. If MSD are unsure of whether to withhold some or all of the report and needs help, contact MSD's Privacy Officer.

chunks.title: Introduction — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit provide income support to the caregiver of a child whose parents cannot support them.
Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit are non-taxable benefits.
## For more information on Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit see:
- Qualifications
- Obligations
- Commencement Date
- Payment
- Establishment Grant
- Changes and reviews
Also see:
- Extra help Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit products

chunks.title: Multiple children — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Multiple children
Sometimes a caregiver will apply for Unsupported Childs Benefit for multiple children. How family breakdown is assessed depends on the relationship between the children.
## Siblings
Where the children are siblings they should be assessed for family breakdown together.
All the children must be referred to an Independent Assessment Provider for a family breakdown assessment.
## Not siblings
Generally, where the children are not siblings they should be assessed separately.
For more information see:
- Independent Assessment Provider
- Unsupported Child's Benefit - Guidelines for Interviews [no link find out why]

chunks.title: New child comes into care — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## New child comes into care
When a caregiver applies to include a new child that meets the qualifications for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, if the qualifications for an Establishment Grant are met, an Establishment Grant must be made.
If the child is included into the Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit between the first Monday after 10th of January and the last day of February, a School and Year Start-up Payment must also be paid if the caregiver applies for this payment and the qualifications are met.
All children are also entitled to a Clothing Allowance for Orphans or Unsupported children.

chunks.title: Obligations — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Obligations
Caregivers receiving Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit have the following obligations:
- they must advise us of any change in circumstances and
- they should apply for Child Support
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Child Support

chunks.title: Oranga Tamariki child discharged to caregiver — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Oranga Tamariki child discharged to caregiver
Where Oranga Tamariki has had care, custody or sole guardianship of a child, but the child is now in the legal custody of a carer, the child is considered to be in a permanent placement. This is referred to as 'in permanency' by Oranga Tamariki.
The caregiver may be able to receive Unsupported Child's Benefit or Orphans Benefit from the Ministry of Social Development.
Oranga Tamariki may be required by court order to provide financial support for a child in permanency. This financial support is not considered chargeable income for benefit purposes. Some of these court orders are renewable.

chunks.title: Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency documentation — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency documentation
Where there has been Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency involvement and a Family Group Conference or a hui or cultural service meeting held, you will need to obtain copies of the relevant documents from the caregiver. Note the caregiver may not have a copy of the Family Group Conference outcome unless they are directly affected by Family Group Conference decision or plan, or if the co-ordinator considers that they have a genuine and proper interest in the matter.
If the caregiver cannot show the required 'proof' of a breakdown in the child's family from Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency you will need to refer the applicant to an Independent Assessment Provider for a family breakdown assessment.
A supporting letter from Oranga Tamariki (or other authorised agency) alone is not proof of a breakdown but may provide supporting information relevant by confirming the continuation of placement with the alternative caregiver.
For more information see:
- Multiple children
## Relevant documentation from Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency
Relevant documentation from Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency, obtained via the caregiver, to prove a breakdown in the child's family has occurred include:
- a copy of the Family Group Conference outcome
- copies of all current Court Orders in respect of the child
- a copy of the court-approved plan
- an extract from a hui or cultural service meeting (signed by a social worker or an elder of the iwi or cultural service who attended the meeting)
These documents confirm current care arrangements and also include future care arrangements, including the reason that the child has come into the caregiver's care.
If the caregiver cannot show documentation, it will be necessary to refer to an Independent Assessment Provider for a family breakdown assessment.

chunks.title: Oranga Tamariki order in place — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: The following table identifies when Unsupported Childs Benefit can be paid and when it can't, depending on the type of order that is in place and section of Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 that applies. When to pay Unsupported Childs Benefit When not to pay Unsupported Childs Benefit section 139: Agreements for temporary care of child or young person by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 140: Agreements for extended care of child or young person by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 78: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, pending determination of court proceedings. If the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki has returned the child or young person into the care of the immediate previous caregiver. section 78: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, pending determination of court proceedings section 101: Custody order in favour of principal caregiver. Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki under section 110. section 101: Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 102: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 110(2) a: Sole Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. Section 101 Custody order in favour of principal caregiver and other dependent child criteria are met. Please refer case to your local solicitor for consideration. section 110(2)a: Sole Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 110(2) b: Additional guardianship Order, to any other guardian in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. section 112: Guardianship Order in favour of Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki for a specific purpose. Please refer case to your local solicitor for consideration. section 86: Services Orders that provide for particular services and assistance required by the child or young person (eg counselling fees, special education costs) section 86: Services Orders that provide for general financial support to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. section 91: Support Orders. The child may be considered a dependent child where the documentation states that specific financial support is to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. section 91:

chunks.title: Oranga Tamariki order in place — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: Support Orders. The child cannot be considered a dependent child where the documentation states that general financial support is to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. See your local solicitor if you receive a case in this category. When a child or young person is discharged from the care, custody or sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, always consider eligibility for Unsupported Childs Benefit

chunks.title: Orphans Benefit — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text:
## Orphans Benefit
For a caregiver to receive an Orphans Benefit, the child's natural or adoptive parents must not be able to provide care because they are:
- deceased
- suffering from a serious long-term illness or incapacity which makes them unable to care for their child or
- unable to be found (a decision will depend on whether they have been missing for some time. Active attempts must have been made to find the parents, for example, asking for police assistance.)
No Family Meeting is required and no application for Child Support should be taken.
Note when a child has been legally adopted the birth parents are no longer considered natural parents of that child.
## Orphaned girls
The Arthur Hall Fletcher Trust provides extra help for orphaned girls.

chunks.title: Other benefit assistance — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: Some caregivers getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit for a child, will apply for or be getting a main benefit, because they need financial assistance for themselves. In this situation, you will need to talk with the caregiver to determine what benefit they should be getting. You need to consider a number of factors including whether the caregiver: - has other dependent children in their care - can meet full-time work obligations - meets the principal caregiver definition, i.e. not caring on a temporary basis

chunks.title: Caring for a child on Jobseeker Support — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: A single or sole parent caregiver getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit may not qualify for Jobseeker Support if they are unable to be available for and seeking full-time work, due to their care of that child or children If the child for whom they are getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is under 14, the caregiver may qualify for Sole Parent Support if they choose not to get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit. Note the caregiver must meet the qualifications for Sole Parent Support, and generally be caring for the child long-term or permanently. For more information see: - Sole Parent Support Temporary care If the single caregiver or sole parent chooses to get Sole Parent Support, they cannot continue to get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for a child or children when they are included in their Sole Parent Support. However, they can exclude the child in the future and get Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit instead.

chunks.title: Emergency Benefit for caregivers of a child for whom Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is paid — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: If a caregiver does not qualify for Sole Parent Support, Jobseeker Support, or any other main benefit, Emergency Benefit may be considered. The hardship test applies to Emergency benefit in this situation. If the caregiver qualifies for Emergency Benefit (including meeting the hardship test), this should be granted at the Jobseeker Support rate they would have received if they were available for full-time work. They can continue getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for the care of the child. The caregiver should have conditions of grant assigned, that mirror the obligations they would have had based on the age of the youngest child (including the Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit child).

chunks.title: Things to consider when discussing benefit options with the caregiver — main benefits > orphans benefit and unsupported childs benefit
chunks.text: When discussing benefit options available to a caregiver you need to consider the impact the benefit type has on other types of assistance and obligations for the caregiver.
