A client receiving Sole Parent Support can continue to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason:
- when they are meeting their work-preparation obligations by attending and participating in employment related training and
- the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet these work obligations (eg during a semester or term break)
## Examples (but are not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
Client receiving Sole Parent Support with work preparation obligations who has been required to undertake an approved training course. During their term break from the course they are going to Australia to visit family.
The client is already meeting their work preparation obligations and therefore can be absent from New Zealand and continue to be paid their benefit for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
Client receiving Sole Parent Support who is in full-time study who wishes to go on holiday during the term break to visit family in Australia.
The client is already meeting their work preparation obligations and therefore can be absent from New Zealand and continue to be paid their benefit for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.

chunks.title: Examples include (but are not limited to) — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Examples include (but are not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A client receiving Sole Parent Support with work preparation but no activities assigned left New Zealand for a holiday in Australia. While she was in Australia there was severe flooding which meant she could not return to New Zealand on the day she was meant to return.
She contacts Work and Income. The client has been paid for 20 days in the previous 52 weeks while she was absent from New Zealand, leaving a balance of eight days.
The client cannot return due to circumstances that were not reasonably foreseeable and they were outside the client's control. Work and Income would extend the client's benefit for a reasonable period for her to be able to return.
This client can travel for any reason. If the client hadn't informed Work and Income, their benefit would continue to be paid up until the 29th day.
A client receiving Sole Parent Support has been overseas for five days to attend his father's funeral.
He is delayed in Sydney due to fog. He must remain a further three days.
The client cannot return due to circumstances that were not reasonably foreseeable and they were outside the client's control.
Work and Income would extend the client's benefit for a reasonable period for him to be able to return.
Also consider whether there is any grounds to pay for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Client obtains employment overseas — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Client obtains employment overseas
Where the client:
- is successful in their job prospect or job search overseas and
- they are not returning to New Zealand
the Sole Parent Support should be cancelled from the day after the notice of job appointment.
If the client returns to New Zealand for the period between getting the job and actually starting employment, the Sole Parent Support can be continued until they leave the country. The benefit must be cancelled from the day after they leave New Zealand to commence the job.

chunks.title: Client with an exemption from their work obligations — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Client with an exemption from their work obligations
A client cannot continue to receive their payment when they temporarily leave New Zealand if they have work obligations, unless they meet the criteria for approved travel. A client may have a full exemption from their work obligations.
## Client with an exemption from work obligations
A client with an exemption from their work obligations cannot continue to receive their payment when they temporarily leave New Zealand (unless they meet the criteria for approved travel). Where they meet the criteria for approved travel they can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- they have notified Work and Income of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
For more information see:
- Client with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption
- Approved travel reasons
- Exemptions

chunks.title: Client with work obligations — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Client with work obligations
A client cannot continue to receive their payment when they temporarily leave New Zealand if they have work obligations.
When they meet the criteria for approved travel they can continue getting their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- they have notified Work and Income of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
For more information see:
- Client with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption
- Client meeting their work obligations
- Client with an exemption from their work obligations
- Approved travel reasons

chunks.title: Client with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Client with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption
Whether a client receiving Sole Parent Support can be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment of their benefit depends on their work or work preparation obligations.
For more information see:
- Client with work preparation obligations
- Client with work obligations
- Client with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption

chunks.title: Client with work preparation obligations — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Client with work preparation obligations
A client with work preparation obligations may be able to continue to receive their benefit if absent from New Zealand. A decision about whether the benefit can be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period will depend on whether activities have been assigned.
## Client has work preparation activities assigned
A client receiving Sole Parent Support cannot continue to receive their payment when they temporarily leave New Zealand if they have work preparation obligations and have activities assigned (unless they meet the criteria for approved travel). Where they meet the criteria for approved travel they can continue to receive their payment for a period of up to 28 days in any 52 week period if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- they have notified Work and Income of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
## Client has no work preparation activities assigned
A client receiving Sole Parent Support who has work preparation obligations but has not had work preparation activities assigned can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period when they are absent from New Zealand if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- they have notified Work and Income of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Client with work obligations
- Client with an exemption from their work obligations

chunks.title: Contacting Work and Income on return to New Zealand — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Contacting Work and Income on return to New Zealand
Generally, it would be reasonable to expect a client to contact Work and Income within 10 working days of returning to New Zealand. However, you should consider whether the client's circumstances meant they were unable to inform Work and Income in this period.
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure
- Clients with work obligations, exemptions or deferral
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Examples of applying the Absence from New Zealand policy

chunks.title: Information that can be provided — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Information that can be provided
Work and Income can provide the Ministry of Justice with the last known address and telephone number of a client under section 126A of the Social Security Act 2018. This only applies when the Ministry of Justice is unable to locate a client who is in default of a court fine.

chunks.title: Date of review (including backdating) — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Date of review (including backdating)
Include the new born child in the benefit and pay family tax credit and Best Start tax credit from the:
- date of birth or
- date the client's benefit was granted
whichever is the later.

chunks.title: Death of a child — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Death of a child
When a dependent child dies, the child should be excluded from Sole Parent Support 28 days following the date of the child's death.
Payment of the benefit should continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child died. This provides a transition period for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.
## Best Start tax credit
Best Start tax credit will continue for 28 days following the child's date of death.
If the child's third birthday occurs in the 28-day period the best start tax credit payment will stop from the date of the third birthday.
## Child turns 18
Generally, clients getting Sole Parent Support must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will be excluded from their payments.
If Sole Parent Support and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a child has died, and that child turns 18 during that period, the child will not be excluded, and the client is not required to respond to the notice during the continuation of payment period.
However, if Sole Parent Support and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because the client's child has died and a different child in their care turns 18, the client must respond to the notice or the 18-year-old will be excluded from their payments.

chunks.title: Death of a client — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
Sole Parent Support can continue to be paid for 28 days following the death of a client.
The continuation of payment beyond the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit.
## Exception
When the death of the client was the result of an accident, entitlement to a lump sum ACC payment needs to be decided before terminal benefit can be paid.
If the child is entitled to a survivor's grant from ACC there is no entitlement to Sole Parent Support beyond the date of death.
When benefit payment has continued beyond the date of death, an overpayment should be established and recovery of the debt should be sought from the estate.
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the client's Sole Parent Support when the child turns 18 during the 28-day continuation of payment.

chunks.title: Debt recovery from arrears or terminal benefit — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Debt recovery from arrears or terminal benefit
When a client has benefit payment arrears owing to them at the time of their death and they have an outstanding debt balance, you should attempt to recover the debt, in full, from the final benefit payment.
## Terminal benefit
When a client has an outstanding debt balance and terminal benefit is payable, you should not recover the debt in full from the terminal benefit payment.
For more information see:
- Ongoing assistance for dependent children

chunks.title: Decision guidelines - sole parents — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines - sole parents
When a Sole Parent Support client is imprisoned it is important that financial assistance is available to support any dependent children.
While Sole Parent Support should generally be stopped when the client is imprisoned, there is discretion for payment to be continued and paid to the person who is caring for the client's dependent children.
To help you decide whether it is reasonable to pay the Sole Parent Support to a temporary caregiver while the client is in prison consider the following:
- has the period in prison already passed?
- is the client due to be released from prison shortly?
- is the likely period in prison less than twelve months?
- will the children return to the client's care on their release from prison?
- has the caregiver ceased work to care for the children?
- has the caregiver lost entitlement to their own benefit due to having children in their care?
For further help you can contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.
For more information see:
- Temporary caregiver
- Rate of payment
- Examples - sole parents
- Remanded in custody

chunks.title: Dependent child — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
A dependent child for Sole Parent Support is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of the client
- maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
- in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but has been returned to their parent's care
A dependent child for Sole Parent Support does not include a:
- child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989
- child for whom Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid and
- young person getting a Young Parent Payment and their child (see Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples)
## Principal responsibility
The client must be responsible for the day-to-day care of the child and be the person who makes the major decisions concerning the child's life (for example schooling and health care).
There are some situations where the person who has primary responsibility of a child is not clear.
## Maintained as a member of the family
The child should be an integral part of the family, participating in the usual family activities (for example outings and annual holidays).
Dependent children should be included in the assessment of Sole Parent Support.
In some situations, a child may not be living at home but is still considered to be a dependent child.

chunks.title: Discharge from hospital — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Discharge from hospital
Where a client is receiving the hospital rate and they are discharged from hospital:
- increase their benefit to the appropriate full rate from the date of discharge and
- review any Extra help from the same date
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.

chunks.title: Discharged from Oranga Tamariki care — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Discharged from Oranga Tamariki care
Where Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency has care, custody or sole guardianship of the child, and returns the child to the care of the immediate previous caregiver, they do not make payments for the child.
The child is then a dependent child and can be included in the Sole Parent Support.
Where the relationship is not one of care, but more of a boarding arrangement, the young person may be able to receive Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment.
Once a child has been discharged from care the child can be considered a dependent child even when Oranga Tamariki or any other authorised agency involvement continues, for example:
- Additional Guardianship Order
- Support Order or
- Services Order
When there is a Service or Support Order in place, you will need to make sure that the Court's intent allows you to consider the child as a dependent child.
For further details on what discharged from care means see:
- Definition of discharged from Oranga Tamariki care

chunks.title: Effect on benefit — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Effect on benefit
Any inclusion or exclusion of a dependent child from a client's benefit will result in a general review of the client's Sole Parent Support and any extra help they are getting.
You may need to review the following:
- Accommodation SupplementChanges to the family composition may result in a change to the Accommodation Supplement entry thresholds.
- Non standard benefit rateWhere a child is added or removed you may need to manually adjust the non-standard rate of payment.
- Special BenefitAny change to family circumstances will result in a review of Special Benefit. A child included or excluded from the Sole Parent Support may result in a change to the allowable costs for Special Benefit.
- Temporary Additional SupportAny change to family circumstances will result in a review of Temporary Additional Support. A child included or excluded from the Sole Parent Support may result in a change to the allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support.
- Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Family tax credit — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Family tax credit
As long as the child continues to be a dependent child, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments continue to be paid while the client is in hospital.
For Best Start tax credit payments will stop from the child’s third birthday.
## Winter Energy Payment
When a Sole Parent Support client is admitted to hospital, their benefit can continue at the full rate for the first 13 weeks.
The rate of payment will need to be reduced to the hospital rate after the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks (not after receiving a benefit for 13 weeks). However, a portion of the Sole Parent Support may be paid to the caregiver of the children and if this happens, the caregiver may receive Winter Energy Payment.
For more information see:
- Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Ending payment for client who can travel for any reason (within 28 day maximum) — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Ending payment for client who can travel for any reason (within 28 day maximum)
Where a client can travel for any reason their payments will suspend automatically on the 29th day in a 52 week period they have been absent from New Zealand and continued to receive a payment.
## Client may need to be absent for more than 28 days
A client may be required to be absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days.
For more information see:
- Paying for more than 28 days - delayed return
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason for travel

chunks.title: Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason to travel (within 28 day maximum) — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason to travel (within 28 day maximum)
Where the client is receiving their payments while they are absent from New Zealand because they have an approved travel reason their payments will suspend automatically on their agreed return date.
For example, a client has been approved travel to attend a job interview in Sydney. They are approved three days. The benefit will suspend automatically on the day they were meant to return.
Where the client is receiving their payments while they are absent from New Zealand because they have an approved travel reason and their return date changes, they must advise Work and Income from overseas, otherwise their payment will be stopped from the day they originally advised they would return to New Zealand.
## Benefit can be backdated once back in New Zealand in very limited circumstances
They may be able to have their benefit backdated if there is an unforeseen reason they cannot notify us while they are overseas.
For example, a client boards a plane to return home on schedule and the plane is held up due to fog. There is no way the client could notify Work and Income due to an event outside of their control. When the client contacts Work and Income once they are back in New Zealand, the benefit would be resumed from the original date they were due to return (this will be on the boarding pass and/or in the custom tab in WASP).
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Client not returned due to an unforeseeable event
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Essential travel — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Essential travel
A client not otherwise entitled to be paid their Sole Parent Support while they are absent from New Zealand may have their payments continue for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if they have to travel outside of New Zealand to attend a significant event relating to a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family).
These events are ones which the client would reasonably be expected to attend. That is, the travel is essential to them and where not attending the event would cause the person emotional distress. This may include, but is not limited to, travel that allows the client to:
- be with a seriously ill or dying person who is a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family)
- attend a funeral or an unveiling in relation to a family member
- pay respect to a family member of the deceased in the event of the client missing the funeral
- attend to legal matters in relation to the affairs of the deceased family member
- attend a birth of a family member or be with a family member around the time of their giving birth
- provide support to a party or witness to a court case
- attend a wedding of a family member - the client does not need to be a member of the bridal party or play a significant part in the wedding in order for the payment of benefit to continue while they are absent from New Zealand
- travel for a court ordered custody arrangement
For more information see:
- Definition of family member
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Job interviews or follow up on a job prospect
- Permitted travel reasons
- Paying benefit when client failed to advise of absence
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes (within a 28 day maximum)

chunks.title: Examples for paying more than 28 days for an approved reason — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text: The following examples show situations where we may pay for more than 28 days in any 52 week period (but are not limited to): Client's reason for travelling for 28 days within 52 week period Client's current reason for travel within 52 week period Outcome Essential travel reasons Essential travel reason eg a seriously ill family member Generally consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if reasonable in the circumstances Job interview or job prospect Essential travel reason eg a funeral Generally would consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if reasonable in the circumstances Sole Parent Support client with work obligations or work-preparation obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. The client wishes to be absent from overseas for another general holiday This is not an approved reason for paying for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. The client would not be able to receive a benefit while absent from New Zealand for this reason even if the travel will not prevent them meeting their obligations (eg they had further annual leave from their employment. Sole Parent Support client with work obligations or work-preparation obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. To provide aid or assistance to a family member immediately following a natural disaster or similar adverse event. Generally would allow further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. This is an unforeseen event and it is reasonable for them to help their family member. Sole Parent Support client with work obligations or work-preparation obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. Essential travel reason Generally would consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if the essential travel reason was unforeseen. Sole Parent Support client with work obligations or work-preparation obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. Needs to attend a wedding of a family member. Generally would not consider allowing a further period of payment for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. Weddings are usually known about in advance and this should have been planned for when they used the 28 days to go on holiday. However, where the wedding is genuinely unforeseen, consideration could be given to allowing travel for a period of more than 28 days in a 52 week period.

chunks.title: Examples for paying more than 28 days for an approved reason — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text: Sole Parent Support client with work obligations or work-preparation obligations had to spend four days at a funeral overseas. The client had booked a holiday prior to the attendance at the funeral overseas. This holiday was booked for 28 days because they are able to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with their obligations. The client does not have the full 28 days left Travelling for a general holiday is not an approved reason for paying a benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period The benefit will only be paid for the number of days the client has available.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text: Carlos contacts MSD on 19 November to advise that he has returned from travelling to Malaysia to be with his dying mother. He left in a hurry and didn't contact MSD before his departure. His Sole Parent Support stopped on 4 November, the day after he left the country. He returned to New Zealand on 14 November, but then had to organise a New Zealand-based funeral for his mother, as a large number of people are based in New Zealand. Carlos didn't advise MSD of his travel before leaving New Zealand, but he has a humanitarian reason that justifies his travel and the reason he didn't contact MSD before he left. Given Carlos' circumstances, he contacted MSD as soon as it would have been reasonable to expect him to and he meets the criteria for an approved travel reason. Carlos' Sole Parent Support can be backdated to 4 November.

chunks.title: Example 2 — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text: Sanjay left New Zealand for India on 7 December because his father had become suddenly seriously ill and been hospitalised. While in India, Sanjay's father passed away and Sanjay stayed in India for the funeral. Sanjay returned on 16 December, after staying for 2 weeks for the Hindu funeral and mourning period. On 19 December, Sanjay contacts MSD to explain that he has been overseas after learning of his father's illness, and that he stayed for the funeral. On return, Sanjay spent time mourning with his own family and has been distraught. He explains that he only realised last night that he had not informed MSD of his absence. Sanjay's reason for leaving New Zealand is a humanitarian reason and he meets the criteria for backdating his payment to the day after departure. Given Sanjay's circumstances, he informed MSD as soon as he reasonably could. Sanjay's Sole Parent Support can be backdated to 8 December, the date it was suspended.

chunks.title: Example 3 — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text: Tusila calls MSD on 5 October to tell them she will leave New Zealand on 7 October to help her sister, who just lost her house in a flood. When asked how long she will be gone for, Tusila says that she hasn't bought a return ticket yet and was considering staying on to catch up with family and see how her sister is going. MSD informs Tusila that she can only keep getting her Sole Parent Support if she is absent for essential travel. Helping her sister after a flood is considered essential travel, however, if she is going to stay longer for a holiday, she won't be able to get Sole Parent Support during the time she is on holiday. Tusila returns to MSD the next day with an airline quote showing that the cheapest return flight is on 14 October. She thinks it will take her a week to ensure her sister has sorted out insurance, medium-term accommodation, and access to basic goods like clothing and food. She has decided not to stay on for the holiday. MSD agrees this is reasonable and tells Tusila she can continue to get Sole Parent Support from 7 to 14 October, while she is overseas helping her sister.

chunks.title: Example 4 — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text: Christy is getting Sole Parent Support and contacts MSD to advise that her sister is getting married in Australia on 8 September. Christy is going to Australia to her sister's wedding but intends to stay on for a further 2 weeks to visit other family. Christy is leaving New Zealand on 4 September as she has to help her sister prepare. She will stay until 10 September to help clean up. Christy then begins the holiday leg of her trip, returning to New Zealand on 25 September. Christy's travel is divided as follows: - 5 September to 10 September period meets the essential travel criteria - 11 September to 24 September period is considered other travel (holiday) and does not meet the essential travel criteria Christy's Sole Parent Support can only be paid until 10 September, for the period that meets the essential travel criteria.

chunks.title: Example 5 — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text: Graeme left New Zealand on 16 August to help his sister in Australia after she lost her house in a fire. He returns to New Zealand on 23 August. A week later, on 30 August he attends an appointment and asks why he hasn't been getting his Sole Parent Support. His case manager informs him that his payments stopped when he left the country and asks why he didn't contact MSD sooner. Graeme explains that he left to help his sister after a house fire, and he meant to contact MSD once he had helped his sister sort out accommodation and insurance , but he forgot. The case manager explains that because he didn't contact MSD as soon as he reasonably could have been expected to (i.e. once he had helped his sister), his Sole Parent Support can only be backdated to 23 August, the date he returned to New Zealand.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Example 1
A client applies for benefit to be paid for 10 days when they are going to be absent from New Zealand.
In the past 52 weeks the client had 10 days absence from New Zealand and continued to be paid their benefit
Step
Calculation
Identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand.
14 September 2019
Count back 52 weeks from this date.
15 September 2018
Count the number of days the client has continued getting their benefit while they were overseas in this 52 week period.
Days client has continued to receive their benefit while absent from New Zealand between 14 September 2018 and 15 September 2019 = 10 days.
Subtract the number of days the client was paid their benefit while absent from New Zealand from 28 days.
28 - 10 days = 18 days available
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay the client for the days they have available.
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay them for the 10 days they are out of the country.
## Example 2
A client applies for benefit to be paid for 10 days when they are going to be absent from New Zealand.
In the past 52 weeks the client has had 20 days absent from New Zealand and continued to be paid their benefit.
Step
Calculation
Identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand.
14 September 2019
Count back 52 weeks from this date.
15 September 2018
Count the number of days the client continued getting their benefit while they were overseas in this 52 week period.
Days client continued being paid their benefit while absent from New Zealand between 14 September 2018 and 15 September 2019 = 20 days.
Subtract the number of days the client was paid their benefit while absent from New Zealand from 28 days.
28 - 20 days = 8 days available
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay the client for the days they have available.
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay them for the 8 days they are out of the country. For 2 of the days they are absent from New Zealand they will not get their payments.
Check if the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period - if they meet these criteria, they may be able to continue getting their payment for the additional 2 days of absence.

chunks.title: Date of review — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Date of review
Where a child becomes financially independent it should be excluded from the benefit payment from the start of the next pay period in which the child became financially independent.
There is discretion to continue payment for one payday following the event.
This discretion only applies when the exclusion of the child affects the rate of payment of Sole Parent Support and is generally used when processing deadlines have passed.
## Family tax credit
Stop family tax credit from the start of the next payday in which the child became financially independent, to avoid an overpayment (with Inland Revenue) for the client.
## Not financially independent
Generally, receipt of a Student Loan (including the living cost component) does not mean a child is financially independent.

chunks.title: Date of review — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Date of review
Exclude the child from the Sole Parent Support from the beginning of the next pay period in which the child started work.
## Family tax credit
Family tax credit should be stopped from the start of the next pay period in which the child starts full-time employment to avoid an overpayment (with Inland Revenue) for the client.
For more information see:
- Effect on benefit

chunks.title: Guidelines for paying a higher rate — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Guidelines for paying a higher rate
Payment can be increased above the hospital rate to a rate that (together with the client's other income) will be sufficient to meet the client's continuing commitments.
Use the following guidelines to assess whether the client's rate should be higher.
1. Have the client complete an Increased payment while you are in hospital form.
2. Accept stated expenses where they appear reasonable, but ask for proof if there is doubt.
3. If the client is a sole parent and has childcare costs:
- include the childcare costs when assessing whether a higher rate should be paid
- include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit as income (as these payments will continue)
4. Check that all possible action has been taken to reduce expenses. For example, giving up the lease on a flat where the hospital stay is indefinite.
5. If the increase in payment request is for one-off items such as clothing, you can pay the increase by:
- a backdated review of the benefit rate to create a lump sum payment or
- increasing the benefit rate for a limited time
## Example
Continuing commitments per week
$55.00
less other weekly income (bank interest)
$5.00
rate of increase
$50.00
plus hospital rate (net, at 1 April 2023)
$55.35
rate of benefit payable
$105.35
Add the rate payable as a non-standard rate on the SNSRA screen.
A parent benefit reassessment SPBR may also be required.

chunks.title: Exception — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Exception
A client's Sole Parent Support may have continued as a temporary caregiver was caring for the client's children. No stand-down will be imposed. The client's benefit will need to be reassessed and the agent will need to be removed.
For more information see:
- Prisoners no stand-down applies
- Temporary caregiver

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a Sole Parent Support client is admitted to hospital, their benefit can continue at the full rate for the first 13 weeks.
The rate of payment will need to be reduced to the hospital rate after the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks (not after receiving a benefit for 13 weeks).
## Care of the child
You will need to find out who is caring for the client's child and the length of time the client is likely to be in hospital. If requested, you can pay part of the benefit to the child's caregiver to cover the cost of alternative care or accommodation.
Where a portion of benefit amount is still being paid to the sole parent and being paid to the child’s caregiver, Winter Energy Payment can continue to be paid.
Where the child is not going to remain in the care of the client, check what the continuing care arrangements are for the child. If the child is no longer a dependent child you will need to stop the client's benefit. You will need to find out if the client qualifies for another benefit.
If there are no other continuing financial costs and it is likely that the client will remain in hospital long term, consider other means of income support for the children.
For example, the new caregiver may meet the qualifications for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, or the child may be able to be included as a dependent child if the new caregiver is receiving a main benefit.
## Hospital rate
The hospital rate allows for the cost of personal items, which patients are expected to provide for themselves. The net weekly hospital rate is $58.34 (as at 1 April 2026).
You can pay an amount above the hospital rate where there are financial circumstances to warrant paying at a higher rate.
Note you cannot pay an amount less than the hospital rate.
For more information see:
- Agents
- Date payment should be reduced
- Income
- Effect on Extra Help
- On leave from hospital
- Discharge from hospital
- Child admitted to hospital
- Private hospital and homes
- Qualifies for another benefit
- Winter Energy Payment - Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure
Where a client does not advise of their departure from New Zealand before they go, they may be able to have their benefit paid from the day after their departure date if the client has a humanitarian reason that justifies their reason for travel and their failure to tell Work and Income before they left.
Humanitarian reasons are:
- to provide aid or assistance to a family member (or a person to whom they have a relationship similar to a family member) immediately following a natural disaster (for example, flood, earthquake, bush fires) or similar adverse event (eg house fire)
- to be with a suddenly seriously ill, or dying family member (or a person to whom they have a relationship similar to a family member)
- to attend the sudden funeral of a family member (or a person to whom they have a relationship similar to a family member)
For more information see:
- Client not returned due to unforeseen circumstances (within 28 day maximum)
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes (within 28 day maximum)
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Backdating benefit to the day after departure date

chunks.title: Imprisonment — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
When a Sole Parent Support client is imprisoned or detained in custody, they generally are no longer entitled to receive the Sole Parent Support.
Generally, to receive a Sole Parent Support the client must be the parent of one or more dependent children.
As the client is in prison or remanded in custody the client generally is no longer the caregiver of dependent children.
The Sole Parent Support should stop from the day following the date of imprisonment.
MSD must decide whether to suspend or cancel the benefit after considering the likely period in prison and whether the client has dependent children.
## Exception
The client may be imprisoned for less than one year and a temporary caregiver will be caring for the client's dependent children. In this situation, all or part of the client's Sole Parent Support may continue and be paid to the temporary caregiver caring for the client's dependent children.
There is also discretion to continue payment if the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance.

chunks.title: In the care of Oranga Tamariki — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## In the care of Oranga Tamariki
When a child or young person is in the care, custody or sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, the cost of the child's care is the responsibility of Oranga Tamariki and they are responsible for making payments under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989. The child is not considered a dependent child and Unsupported Childs Benefit cannot be paid.
However, where there is a sole guardianship order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but the child or young person is in the care of the caregiver, the caregiver may be entitled to Unsupported Childs Benefit if all other criteria are met.
When Oranga Tamariki is involved, but there are no orders or agreements about care, the child can be considered a dependent child (for example when Oranga Tamariki provides services to family groups under a Family Group Conference plan only).
For information on different orders and whether they mean the child can be considered a dependent child while the order is still in place, see:
- Oranga Tamariki order in place.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Example 1
A client receiving a Sole Parent Support has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks. This client has other income which reduces the main benefit rate to $20.00 per week.
In this case we pay the rate $20.00 per week which is lower than the hospital rate of $58.34 (as at 1 April 2026).
## Example 2
A client receiving a Sole Parent Support has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks. This client has other income which reduces the main benefit rate to $70.00 per week.
In this case we pay the hospital rate of $58.34 per week (as at 1 April 2026) which is the lower rate.

chunks.title: Inland Revenue deduction notices — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
Inland Revenue may request for a client's unpaid taxes to be directly deducted from their benefit payments.
Note all Inland Revenue deduction notices are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
The instructions of the deduction notice will be to deduct the lowest of either:
- 10% of the total debt which Inland Revenue specify in the notice, on a weekly basis, or
- 20% of the client's gross earnings on a weekly basis
When there are insufficient funds to cover the deduction, Work and Income must advise Inland Revenue immediately that the deduction will not start or will start at a reduced rate.
Inland Revenue deductions have a lower priority than Child Support deductions.
For more information see:
- Priority for deductions

chunks.title: Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service
The Ministry of Social Development has an Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service with New Zealand Customs Service that identifies clients who have left New Zealand if they are getting a benefit.
Once identified, the client's eligibility to keep getting their benefit payments while they are absent from New Zealand is automatically determined by Ministry systems.
## Does not advise of departure
If the client did not tell the Ministry they were leaving New Zealand their benefit will be suspended immediately from the day after they left New Zealand.
The Integrity Intervention Centre will determine if there has been an overpayment, establish any debt and advise the client.
If a client questions the information match refer them to the Integrity Intervention Centre.
For more information see:
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Approved travel reasons
- Backdating benefit to the day after departure date
- Contacting Work and Income as soon as the client reasonably can
- Action on return to New Zealand
- Examples of applying the absence from New Zealand policy

chunks.title: On leave from hospital — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text:
## On leave from hospital
Sole Parent Support is paid at the full rate for any period of leave from hospital. Where the client has been receiving the hospital rate increase their benefit for any period they are on leave.
The benefit action to take, on the client's re-admission to hospital, will depend on how long they were on leave.

chunks.title: Ongoing assistance for dependent children — main benefits > sole parent support > changes and reviews sole parent support
chunks.text: When a surviving dependent child is to be cared for by a person other than a parent, the principal caregiver may be able to get an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit. For more information see: - Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit The provision to continue the benefit payment for 28 days following the date of death. is referred to as terminal benefit. Sole Parent Support is continued at the rate which was payable to the client at the date of death. A terminal benefit includes extra help being paid (for up to 28 days following the date of death) but does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments.

chunks.text: When the client's benefit was paid at a reduced rate at the date of death, the terminal benefit is also paid at the reduced rate. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed - Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenue - when a surviving partner or family member makes enquiries, refer them to Inland Revenue - court attachment orders - redirection to Kāinga Ora or a community housing provider When the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. For more information see: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client Note all of the above deductions will continue being made from the terminal benefit payments unless they are manually stopped before cancellation.
