chunks.title: Mandatory Review dates for Supported Living Payment — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review dates for Supported Living Payment
MSD must review a client's Supported Living Payment within 52 weeks of the commencement date of Supported Living Payment, or within 52 weeks from when the client's Mandatory Review was completed.
The next review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD determined the client continues to qualify for Supported Living Payment and the rate of benefit payable (i.e. when MSD completes the review).
Note when MSD has an interaction with a client that confirms all of the same circumstances as a Mandatory Review, this can push out the client's Mandatory Review date by 52 weeks. This is known as a specific engagement.
## Initial Mandatory Review dates
Supported Living Payment commencement date
Mandatory Review dates
Benefit commenced before 2 March 2026
Clients whose Supported Living Payment commenced before 2 March 2026 will have their initial Mandatory Review either:
- 52 weeks from the commencement date of the benefit
or
- 52 weeks from when their last periodic review was completed
or
- 52 weeks from when MSD last contacted the client to confirm if the information MSD holds about their circumstances is correct (annual circumstances letter)
Whichever date is later.
Benefit commenced on or after 2 March 2026
If a client's Supported Living Payment commenced on or after 2 March 2026, their initial Mandatory Review is either:
- 52 weeks from the commencement date of the benefit
or
- 52 weeks from the completion of a specific engagement
## Clients who have been notified to complete 26 week review before 2 March 2026
Clients who have an "in-flight" 26 week periodic review
On 2 March 2026, some clients will have an "in-flight" 26 week periodic review and must complete this.
This only applies to clients who have already been notified about the 26 week review before 2 March 2026.
Their initial Mandatory Review is set for 52-weeks from when their 26 week periodic review was completed.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review not required — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Mandatory Review not required
There is no Mandatory Review for Supported Living Payment for clients in the following circumstances:
- the client is hospitalised for more than 13 weeks
- the client is in residential disability care or rest home care
- the client has died
- the client is living in or visiting a region affected by an emergency or adverse event and they are unable to reasonably leave the area
- the client is living in or visiting a region affected by an outbreak of a quarantinable disease and an epidemic notice has been given and is in force
or when:
- there is a major system outage that prevents MSD from carrying out mandatory reviews of specified benefits
MSD will also stop the review for any clients who are in these circumstances after they have been notified about their Mandatory Review.
MSD will notify the client when they are not required to complete the review. The Mandatory Review date is reset to 52 weeks in the future from the client's original review date.
Note a notification will not be sent when the client has died.

chunks.title: Does not advise of departure — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Does not advise of departure
If the client did not tell the Ministry they were leaving New Zealand their benefit will be suspended immediately from the day after they left New Zealand.
The Integrity Intervention Centre will determine if there has been an overpayment, establish any debt and advise the client.
If a client questions the information match refer them to the Integrity Intervention Centre.
For more information see:
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Backdating benefit to the day after departure date
- Approved travel reasons
- Action on return to New Zealand
- Examples of applying the Absence from New Zealand policy
- Contacting Work and Income as soon as the client reasonably can

chunks.title: On leave from hospital — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## On leave from hospital
Supported Living Payment is paid at the full rate for any period of leave from hospital. Where the client has been receiving the hospital rate increase their benefit for any period they are on leave.
The benefit action to take, on the client's re-admission to hospital, will depend on how long they were on leave.

chunks.title: One-off environmental change is not sheltered employment — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## One-off environmental change is not sheltered employment
If the employer has made a one-off environmental change to the work place the client is not working in sheltered employment. For example a client would not be considered as working in sheltered employment if an employer made changes to the work place such as:
- installing a ramp to assist wheelchair users or
- purchasing specialised equipment such as an electronic hoist to carry heavy objects
For more information see:
- Guidelines for sheltered employment

chunks.title: Open employment for employment and training services — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Open employment for employment and training services
Open employment for employment and training services is different from open employment for Supported Living Payment purposes.
The definition of open employment for employment programmes and services is governed by the Social Security Act 2018. In the context of support for people with ill health and disabilities, open employment is a job available to anyone in the community who has an employment agreement attached as defined in the Employment Relations Act 2000.
This means that a client who is considered to be working in sheltered employment for Supported Living Payment purposes may also be considered to be working in open employment for employment programmes or services assistance.
## Example of a severely disabled client in open employment
A leading New Zealand freight company has advertised a position for a store person. John, who is severely disabled and was receiving Supported Living Payment, applied for and was successfully appointed as their new store person.
Because of John's disability, his new employer has substantially changed the working conditions to accommodate John.
In this situation, the degree of change to the conditions of John's employment means we can accept employment is sheltered for the purposes of John's entitlement to Supported Living Payment.
In addition, because the position has been advertised in the open market, the job is considered to be open employment. This means Work and Income can also consider programmes and services and financial assistance for clients with severe disabilities to achieve unsubsidised and sustainable employment.
For more information see:
- Employment and training services
- Deskfile Approved Business Enterprises
- Employment and training Clients who have a health condition, injury or disability

chunks.title: Oranga Tamariki order in place — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: The following table identifies when a child can be considered a dependent child and when it can't, depending on the type of order that is in place and section of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 that applies. When to include as a dependent child When not to include as a dependent child section 139: Agreements for temporary care of child or young person by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 140: Agreements for extended care of child or young person by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 78: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, pending determination of court proceedings. If Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki has returned the child or young person in to the care of the immediate previous caregiver. section 78: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, pending determination of court proceedings section 101: Custody order in favour of principal caregiver. Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki under section 110. section 101: Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 102: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 110(2)a: Sole Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. Section 101 Custody Order in favour of principal caregiver and other dependent child criteria are met. Please refer case to your local solicitor for consideration. section 110(2)a: Sole Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 110(2) b: Additional guardianship Order, to any other guardian in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. section 112: Guardianship Order in favour of Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki for a specific purpose. Please refer case to your local solicitor for consideration. section 86: Services Orders that provide for particular services and assistance required by the child or young person (e.g. counselling fees, special education costs) section 86: Services Orders that provide for general financial support to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. section 91: Support Orders. The child may be considered a dependent child where the documentation states that specific financial support is to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki.

chunks.title: Oranga Tamariki order in place — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: section 91: Support Orders. The child cannot be considered a dependent child where the documentation states that general financial support is to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. See your local solicitor if you receive a case in this category. When a child or young person is discharged from the care, custody or sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, always consider including the child in the clients Supported Living Payment or Unsupported Childs Benefit - The legislation referenced above is the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989

chunks.title: Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid
When a client is receiving an Orphans Benefit or an Unsupported Childs Benefit, the child is not treated as a dependent child and is not included in the assessment of Supported Living Payment.
The client's Supported Living Payment is assessed on their family circumstances excluding the child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid.

chunks.title: Outcomes of a Mandatory Review — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Clients must respond to their Mandatory Review before their Mandatory Review date, or their payments will suspend. When a client responds to the review, there are a number of outcomes that can occur. Once MSD has determined if the client qualifies, MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g. partner has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies The Mandatory Review is complete when MSD makes a decision about the client's eligibility for Supported Living Payment and the rate of benefit payable (if applicable). MSD may also carry out a separate review of the Supported Living Payment at any time, where there is good reason.

chunks.title: Client declares no change — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have had no change in circumstances, MSD must generally continue their Supported Living Payment at the same rate. The client's next review date will be set for 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review. Exceptions when a client declares no change When a client responds to their Mandatory Review and confirms they have no change in circumstances, there are some situations when MSD can request further information from the client before deciding whether to continue Supported Living Payment e.g. the client has had no change to their declared income amount for three consecutive years.

chunks.title: Client declares a change in circumstances — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When a client responds to the Mandatory Review with a change in circumstances, MSD must use the information provided to determine if the client continues to qualify for Supported Living Payment, or any other benefits they get that are subject to a Mandatory Review (excluding Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit) and the rate payable. MSD can request further information from the client where it's unclear whether the client continues to qualify for Supported Living Payment. Date of change When a client declares a change in circumstances, MSD must assess if the client still qualifies for Supported Living Payment and determine the rate payable and from what date, depending on when the change in circumstances happened or will happen. Client is also getting other assistance When the client has provided information as part of the Mandatory Review that could affect their entitlement to or the rate payable of any other assistance (e.g. Temporary Additional Support or Flexible Childcare Assistance), MSD may use this information to review that assistance. When the other assistance is affected by the outcome of the Mandatory Review, MSD must change the rate, suspend or cancel that assistance where appropriate. For example, if the outcome of the Mandatory Review is that the client is no longer entitled to Supported Living Payment, their Temporary Additional Support must be reviewed, and the rate may change or stop if they no longer qualify.

chunks.title: Further information is needed to complete the Mandatory Review — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: If further information is needed to determine if the client continues to qualify for Supported Living Payment or that the rate of payment is correct, MSD must give a reasonable timeframe for the client to provide it. The date the client is given to provide the information by becomes the client's new deadline to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client does not provide the information that was asked for before the deadline, MSD must suspend the Supported Living Payment from the new deadline date. If the client provides the information that was asked for and MSD determines the client continues to qualify for Supported Living Payment (including the rate payable), the future Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from the date MSD completed the review.

chunks.title: Completing the Mandatory Review when there are new costs — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: In some circumstances MSD can still complete the Mandatory Review when a client has declared a change in circumstances and this doesn't affect the client's eligibility for Supported Living Payment, e.g. the client has declared a new cost. Example 1 Davey is getting Supported Living Payment and has a Mandatory Review for his benefit. Davey responds to his Mandatory Review to confirm his circumstances. Davey tells MSD he now has accommodation costs but nothing else has changed. MSD completes the Mandatory Review and continues the Supported Living Payment at the existing rate as the change declared by Davey doesn't affect his eligibility for Supported Living Payment. Davey can apply for Accommodation Supplement based on his new accommodation costs. This application is separate to the Mandatory Review. Example 2 Billy is getting Supported Living Payment and Disability Allowance and has a Mandatory Review for both. Billy responds to the Mandatory Review to confirm their circumstances. Billy tells MSD they have a new disability cost but nothing else has changed. MSD completes the Mandatory Review and continues the Supported Living Payment and Disability Allowance at the existing rate. MSD advises Billy that they need to provide a medical certificate from their medical or nurse practitioner to confirm the additional cost, and they must provide proof of cost to have the new cost included in their Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Overseas medical treatment — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Overseas medical treatment
When a client is receiving assistance for overseas medical treatment from Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora - High Cost Treatment Pool, the client can continue to receive benefit payments for up to 2 years while absent from New Zealand.
Payment can also continue if the partner, dependent child, or sibling of a client is the person who is being assisted under the High Cost Treatment Pool. Payment may also continue for partners and siblings when they are required to accompany the client overseas.

chunks.title: Overseas vocational or disability assistance dog training — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Overseas vocational or disability assistance dog training
A client receiving Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability, or total blindness only) may need to travel overseas to:
- attend a specific vocational training course or
- receive disability assistance dog training
In these cases the client can continue to receive payment of their benefit during any period or periods of absence not exceeding two years in total.
The criteria for continuing payment are:
- the person is receiving Supported Living Payment on the grounds of their health condition, injury, disability or total blindness
and
- the vocational or disability dog training cannot be carried out in New Zealand during the period the client is absent
Training can be for guide dogs, hearing dogs or other disability assistance dogs as appropriate. Training is limited to dogs only. There may be some cases where a client applies to receive training for some other type of disability assistance animal. This training would not be appropriate and does not meet the criteria for continuation of payments.
## Proof
The client will need to provide proof that the vocational or disability assistance dog training is not available in New Zealand.
## Process
For more information contact Helpline.

chunks.title: Part-time employment — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Part-time employment
Part-time employment does not make a child financially independent. Nor do you take the child's earnings into account when assessing the rate of Supported Living Payment payments.
For more information on children's income see:
- Child income

chunks.title: Partner becomes sick — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Partner becomes sick
If the partner of a Supported Living Payment client has a health condition, is injured or disabled they may be exempt from meeting their work obligations until they are well again.
Where the partner's health condition permanently and severely restricts their ability to work, they may be able to receive a Supported Living Payment in their own right.
If the client (or partner) is admitted to hospital it may affect their rate of payment.
For more information see:
- Exemptions for partners
- Qualifications
- Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Partner donates a kidney or liver tissue — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Partner donates a kidney or liver tissue
When a partner is donating a kidney or liver tissue, they can keep getting their Supported Living Payment. Exempt the client from any work obligations during the recovery period.
Grant the partner the exemption 'Would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability'.
Manually record the exemption in the SWTDA screen in SWIFTT.
The exemption must not be more than 12 weeks.
Do not apply any obligations failures:
- for the maximum period of 12 weeks or
- until the partner has recovered from the operation
whichever is earlier.
## Partner has an obligations failure
If the partner currently has an obligations failure, donating a kidney or liver tissue is a ‘good and sufficient reason’.
The work obligations failure must be overturned in OBMAN. This will remove the failure from the client’s 12 month obligation failure count, and there is no sanction.
## Childcare assistance
Clients may be eligible for Childcare Assistance payments while they are recovering.
For more information and the additional qualifications see:
- Childcare Subsidy Temporary illness
- OSCAR Temporary illness
- Exemptions for partners
- Partners with no children or youngest child 14+ years
- Partner with youngest child between 3 and 13 years
- Would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability

chunks.title: Partners with children under 3 years old — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: A partner with their youngest child aged under 3 years old does not have to meet work obligations and can be a part-time or full-time student without it affecting their Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability).

chunks.title: Partners with work obligations — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Partners with no children or with their youngest child aged 3 years old or over, may be a part or full-time student without it affecting Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) eligibility if they have been granted an exemption from meeting their work obligations because they: - were part way through a course of study at the time that the client applied for an Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) - were part way through a course of study when their youngest child reached the age of 3 years A partner can be considered to be meeting their work obligations if their study timetable allows enough time for job search activity, for example, if the hours of the part-time study are outside of normal working hours. If a partner starts study and they can no longer meet their work obligations and they do not have an exemption from meeting their work obligations you may need to initiate an obligations failure. For more information see: - Work obligations - partners - Obligations failures

chunks.title: Partner engaged in full time study — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: If a partner is engaged in full-time study and does not meet the criteria for exemption they can apply for a Student Allowance. If the partner qualifies for a Student Allowance the client can be included in the Student Allowance when: - they are legally married, in a civil union or de facto relationship and - both are aged 24 years or more or - they have a dependent child Where the client cannot be included, the partner will be regarded as single and will receive the single rate of Student Allowance. For Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) we still regard them as a married, civil union or de facto couple. You will need to charge the Student Allowance against the married, civil union or de facto rate of Supported Living Payment and pay the client half of the abated benefit. Because the Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) and Student Allowance rules are different there are particular procedures to follow. There is a flowchart to help you, see: - Couple under 24 years - partner not granted an exemption in non approved study flowchart For more information see: - Work obligations - partners - Effect of sanctions on assistance - Exemptions for partners - Student Allowance - Student Allowance Students with a partner

chunks.title: Partner meeting their work obligation requirements — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: A client who is a partner of someone receiving Supported Living Payment can continue to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason: - when they are meeting their work obligations by being in paid employment and - the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet these work obligations (eg during a period of annual leave from employment)

chunks.title: Examples (but are not limited to) — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Client situation Outcome Partner of a person receiving Supported Living Payment has part-time work obligations. They are in employment 25 hours a week. They have taken annual leave from their employment to travel to Australia. The primary client can continue to be paid while overseas on a holiday as they have no work preparation obligations. The partner is already meeting their part-time work obligations by being in suitable employment of over 20 hours per week. Their benefit will continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand. A Supported Living Payment couple go overseas on holiday. The primary client does not have work preparation obligations. The partner has part-time work obligations and is meeting their obligations by working part-time for 24 hours per week. The holiday is taken while the partner is on annual leave. The primary client can continue to be paid while overseas on a holiday as they have no work preparation obligations. The partner is already meeting their part-time work obligations by being in suitable employment of over 20 hours per week. The partners share of the benefit will continue to be paid for up to 28 days in a 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand. The full rate of accommodation supplement can continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand.

chunks.title: Obligations change on 1 April 2016 — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: From 1 April 2016, partners will need an approved reason to travel if: - their youngest dependent child is 3 or 4 years old - they are working between 15 and 20 hours per week Discretion to continue payments while temporarily overseas is available for clients that: - will change from work preparation to part-time work obligations on 1 April 2016 because their youngest dependent child is aged 3 or 4 years old or - will no longer be meeting their part-time work obligations on 1 April 2016 because the definition of part-time work increased from 15 to 20 hours per week and - book overseas travel before they are aware of the changes to their work obligations that come into effect on 1 April 2016 and - would continue to receive their payment based on their obligations at the time they booked travel Note all other Absence from New Zealand policy applies when applying this discretion.

chunks.title: Partner meeting their work preparation activities — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Partner meeting their work preparation activities
A client who is a partner of someone receiving Supported Living Payment can continue to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason:
- when they are meeting their work preparation obligations by attending and participating in employment related training and
- the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet these work obligations (eg during a semester or term break)
## Examples (but are not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
Partner receiving Supported Living Payment with work preparation obligations who has been required to undertake an approved training course. During their term break from the course they are going to Australia to visit family.
The partner is already meeting their work preparation obligations and therefore can be absent from New Zealand and continue to be paid their benefit for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
Partner receiving Supported Living Payment who is in full-time study who wishes to go on holiday during the term break to visit family in Australia.
The partner is already meeting their work preparation obligations and therefore can be absent from New Zealand and continue to be paid their benefit for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.

chunks.title: Partner obtains employment overseas — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Partner obtains employment overseas
Where the partner:
- is successful in their job prospect or job search overseas and
- they are not returning to New Zealand
their portion of the Supported Living Payment should be cancelled from the day after the interview or notice of job appointment.
If the partner returns to New Zealand for the period between getting the job and actually starting employment, the Supported Living Payment can be continued until they leave the country. Their portion of the Supported Living Payment must be cancelled from the day after they leave New Zealand to commence the job.

chunks.title: Partner with a full exemption from work obligations — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Partner with a full exemption from work obligations
A partner who has a full exemption from their work obligations can continue to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
## Partner with a partial exemption from work obligations
A partner with a partial exemption from their work obligations cannot continue to receive their payment when they temporarily leave New Zealand (unless they meet the criteria for approved travel). Where they meet the criteria for approved travel they can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- they have notified Work and Income of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
For more information see:
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations
- Exemptions for partners
- Approved travel reasons

chunks.title: Partner with work obligations — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Partner with work obligations
A partner cannot continue to receive their payment when they temporarily leave New Zealand if they have work obligations unless they meet the criteria for approved travel.
Where they meet the criteria for approved travel they can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- they have notified Work and Income of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
For more information see:
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations
- Partner meeting their work obligations
- Partner with an exemption from their work obligations
- Approved travel reasons

chunks.title: Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption
Whether a partner of a Supported Living Payment client can be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment of their benefit depends on their work or work preparation obligations.
Note there is no partner rate for Supported Living Payment (caring for a person). A partner of someone receiving Supported Living Payment (caring for a person) may be receiving another main benefit and will need to meet that benefit criteria for absence from New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Partner with work preparation obligations
- Partner with work obligations
- Partner with an exemption from their work obligations

chunks.title: Partner has work preparation activities assigned — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Partner has work preparation activities assigned
A partner of someone receiving Supported Living Payment cannot continue to receive their payment when they temporarily leave New Zealand if they have work preparation obligations and have activities assigned (unless they meet the criteria for approved travel). Where they meet the criteria for approved travel they can continue to receive their payment for a period of up to 28 days in any 52 week period if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- they have notified Work and Income of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
## Partner has no work preparation activities assigned
A partner of someone receiving Supported Living Payment who has work preparation obligations but has not had work preparation activities assigned can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period when they are absent from New Zealand if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- the absences do not affect the client's eligibility for the benefit
- they have notified Work and Income of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Partner with work obligations
- Partner with an exemption from their work obligations

chunks.title: Partners of a main beneficiary who have youth activity obligations — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Young partners receiving a main benefit cannot generally be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment of their portion of their benefit. The Government's obligation to pay income support usually stops when the client leaves New Zealand. A young partner can continue to be paid their portion of their benefit for up to 28 days in a 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand: - if they have an approved travel reason or - for any reason if the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations (eg because they are attending school and the travel is during the school holidays or they are attending a training course and the travel is during a term or semester break, and they do not need to be in New Zealand to meet any of their other obligations during the travel period) or - overseas for medical treatment For more information see: - Approved travel reasons

chunks.title: Examples (but are not limited to) — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Client situation Outcome A young partner is meeting their education obligation by attending secondary school and they wish to travel to Australia during the school holidays. The client is not required by their Service Provider to undertake a budgeting course or attend any meetings with them during the period they wish to travel. The travel will not prevent the young partner from meeting any of their youth activity obligations so it will be approved. Therefore, the young partner can be absent from New Zealand for this reason and continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period. A young partner is meeting their education obligation by participating in a full time training course and decides to take time off from the course in the middle of the term so that they can holiday in Australia. The travel will not be approved as it will prevent the young partner from meeting their obligation to be in full-time education or training. A young partner is enrolled in a full-time training course, however, the course has not yet started, and the young person wishes to travel to the United States for a holiday before the course commencement date. The young partner does not have to be in New Zealand to meet any other obligations during the travel period (eg they do not have to attend a budgeting course during the time of the travel). The travel will not prevent the client from meeting any of their youth activity obligations so it will be approved. The young person can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand.. For more information see: - Young partner not yet subject to obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning - Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations - Absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days for an approved reason

chunks.title: Resuming benefit when client failed to advise of absence — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Resuming benefit when client failed to advise of absence
If a client contacts Work and Income after they have left New Zealand, and is not eligible to have their payment backdated, their benefit can only be resumed from:
- the date that they notified us of their absence and
- only if the travel is allowed (ie they meet the criteria to continue to be paid their benefit while overseas either because they meet the criteria for approved travel, or the requirement that travel be approved does not apply to them)
Otherwise, the client cannot have their benefit resumed until they return to New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Backdating benefit to day after departure date
- Action on return to New Zealand
- Approved travel reasons
- Payment when client or partner absent from New Zealand
- Examples of applying the Absence from New Zealand policy

chunks.title: Paying a higher rate — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Paying a higher rate
You can make payment at a rate higher than the hospital rate where the client cannot meet their continuing costs from the hospital rate of payment and any other income they receive.
You will need to take into consideration:
- the client's financial commitments and
- access to other income
When you are considering payment of benefit at a rate higher than the hospital rate, generally you do not take cash assets into account as rates of benefit payment are not subject to an assets test.
If a client is required to make Child Support payments and does not qualify for an exemption from Inland Revenue Child Support, you can increase the hospital rate to include any Child Support payments that are required to be apportioned from the benefit.
For more information about paying at a higher rate see:
- Carers who do not need to apply for child support
## Maximum amount payable
You can pay a rate higher than the hospital rate up to the maximum rate of Supported Living Payment that would otherwise be payable.
## When not to pay a higher rate
A client cannot be paid a higher rate of benefit (because of hospitalisation) than they would otherwise get. Where their usual benefit payment is less than the hospital rate, you don't increase their benefit to the hospital rate (or any other higher rate).
A benefit may be paid at less than the hospital rate because of:
- the client's income (if it continues while in hospital)
- maintenance deductions or
- overseas pension deductions

chunks.title: Examples — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Examples
A client who is absent from New Zealand for an approved reason may be prevented from returning by new unforeseen circumstances which could include (but are not limited to):
- travel delays due to unforeseen weather events eg fog, volcano, flooding, earthquakes, terrorism
- travel delays due to transport options being cancelled
- health condition or injury or hospitalisation preventing return
For more information see:
- Overseas for medical treatment
- Special Olympics or Paralympics
- Overseas vocational or disability assistance dog training
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes

chunks.title: Paying for more than 28 days for an approved reason — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Generally, a benefit cannot be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period when the client is absent from New Zealand. However there are limited circumstances where a benefit can be paid for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. To pay a benefit more than 28 days during any 52 week period of absence from New Zealand, the client must be travelling for one of the following reasons: - essential travel - to attend a significant event relating to a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family), that the client would reasonably be expected to attend (eg visit a person who is seriously ill, seriously injured or whose death is imminent, attend a funeral, provide support to a party or witness to a court case, travel required for a court ordered custody arrangement) - to attend a court case which the person is required to attend as a party or a witness - to attend a job interview or follow up on a job prospect - for clients with a disability, to receive vocational training or disability assistance-dog training not available in New Zealand during the period or periods of absence - for clients with a disability, to travel overseas for the sole or predominant purpose of competing in any overseas multinational or international Special Olympic or Paralympic Games competition - for clients with a disability, to travel overseas for the purpose to attend an approved disability forum - to provide aid or assistance to a family member immediately following a natural disaster (flood, earthquake, fire) or similar adverse event (eg house fire) and - Work and Income must be satisfied, when considering the client's reason for travel, that the length of the absence is no longer than necessary for the reason for travel. In addition, where the client has already been paid a benefit while absent from New Zealand in the 52 week period Work and Income must be satisfied that either: - the client could not have reasonably foreseen them needing to be absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in a 52 week period or - the client could not have rearranged their affairs to avoid being absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in a 52 week period and - it would be unreasonable for the benefit not to be paid Note generally we would not pay more than 28 days extra travel per absence. For more information see: - Examples for paying more than 28 days for an approved reason - Client not returned due to unforeseen circumstances (within 28 days maximum)

chunks.title: Paying for more than 28 days for an approved reason — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: - Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes (within 28 day maximum) - Paying for more than 28 days - delayed return - Calculating the period of absence

chunks.title: Paying for more than 28 days - receive support from family overseas (young partner) — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Generally, a benefit cannot be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period. However there are limited circumstances where a benefit can be paid for more than 28 days in a 52 week period where the young partner is travelling to receive support from a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family) who is residing overseas. For more information see: - Definition of 'support' from a family member residing overseas This applies (and is limited to a further 28 days in any 52 week period) when: - the young partner has already been paid a benefit while absent from New Zealand for one or more approved reasons for all or most of 28 days in a 52 week period and - the young partner will be absent from New Zealand for the purpose of obtaining support from a family member residing overseas and - the support that the young partner needs cannot reasonably be provided to the client by one of the family members in New Zealand and - the absence does not prevent the young partner from meeting their youth activity obligations because the absence is at a time when: they are not required to attend education, training or work-based learning (for example, they are exempt from meeting their obligationsthey are not yet required to be undertaking education, training or work-based learning because of the age of their youngest child orthey are undertaking education or training but it is semester or term break or they are between academic years) or the course has not yet started andthey are not required to be in New Zealand to meet any of their other obligations during the time of the absence (eg they do not need to attend a parenting or budgeting course during the time they will be overseas) - they are not required to attend education, training or work-based learning (for example, they are exempt from meeting their obligations - they are not yet required to be undertaking education, training or work-based learning because of the age of their youngest child or - they are undertaking education or training but it is semester or term break or they are between academic years) or the course has not yet started and - they are not required to be in New Zealand to meet any of their other obligations during the time of the absence (eg they do not need to attend a parenting or budgeting course during the time they will be overseas)

chunks.title: Cannot be paid for more than 28 days for purposes of obtaining support — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: The maximum amount of time that a young partner can continue to receive their payment while overseas on the grounds that the absence does not prevent them meeting their obligations is 28 days in any 52 week period. Therefore, if a client subject to youth activity obligations has already received their payment for 28 days while they were overseas on a holiday on the grounds that the travel did not prevent them meeting their obligations, they will not be able to travel and continue to receive their payment under the "obtaining support from a family member" circumstance. For more information see: - Examples of paying for more than 28 days for obtaining family support for young partners

chunks.title: Payment to partners — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Payment to partners
When a client with a partner (with no dependent children) has their Supported Living Payment reduced to the hospital rate, their partner in the community can from the same date:
- have their portion of benefit or pension increased by the difference between the maximum half married, civil union or de facto rate, and the single rate of that benefit or pension and
- get Special Disability Allowance
Note couples with dependent children do not have their rate reduced to the hospital rate.
## Partner is also in hospital
If the partner is also in hospital, the same rules apply as when the client is in hospital.
If the partner has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks their benefit or pension is also reduced to the hospital rate.
Note if the partner is getting Veteran's Pension and is in hospital for more than 13 weeks their payment must not be reduced to the hospital rate.This is because Veteran's Pension is not affected by hospitalisation. The partner of the Veteran's Pension client cannot have their payments increased or get Special Disability Allowance.
## Charging income
You need to charge any income the couple gets against the married, civil union or de facto rate before you can determine the amount to pay.
The partner in the community will get the half married, civil union or de facto rate (after charging income) plus the difference between the maximum half married, civil union or de facto rate, and the single rate.
The client in hospital will get the lesser of the:
- half married, civil union or de facto rate (after charging income) or
- hospital rate of payment

chunks.title: Payment when client or partner absent from New Zealand — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Payment when client or partner absent from New Zealand
There are some situations where the benefit payments will be affected when the client is absent from New Zealand. The action required by Work and Income will depend on the reason the client is absent from New Zealand and whether they are continuing to be paid a benefit.
For more information see:
- Client or partner remains in New Zealand
- Ending payment for client who can travel for any reason
- Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason for travel
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes (within 28 day maximum)
- Client not returned due to an unforeseeable event (within 28 day maximum)
- Child absent

chunks.title: Permanent absence — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
If a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, Supported Living Payment must be cancelled from the day after departure.
## Client receiving Supported Living Payment (caring for a person who requires full-time care and attention)
If the client is moving to Australia it is important that they are aware that they may not be able to receive a benefit until they have resided in Australia for two years after being granted permanent residence status.
If the client is moving to a country that has a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand they may qualify for a benefit or pension in that country.
## Client receiving Support Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
If a client receiving Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is moving to a country that has a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand they may qualify for a benefit or pension in that country, or they may be able to have their New Zealand Supported Living Payment paid overseas.
Moving to the United Kingdom
If the client is moving to the United Kingdom they qualify for a benefit or pension in that country.
Moving to Australia
If the client is moving to Australia it is important they are aware that they may not be able to receive their Supported Living Payment unless they meet the severely disabled medical criteria.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reciprocal agreements

chunks.title: Permanently and severely incapacitated to work — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Permanently and severely incapacitated to work
Clients receiving Supported Living Payment as they are permanently and severely incapacitated to work can have their benefit continue at the full rate for the first 13 weeks.
The rate of payment will need to be reduced to the hospital rate after the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks (not after receiving a benefit for 13 weeks).
If a partner has work obligations is hospitalised, exempt the partner from their work obligations by adding the 'sick/injured/disabled - partners - partial' exemption code (402) on the SWTDA screen in SWIFTT. You will also need to add an expiry date.
## Exception
Married, civil union or de facto couples with a dependent child do not have their benefit payment reduced regardless of how long they are in hospital.
Note if a client (or partner) is getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit for a child in their care, this child is regarded as a dependent child.
## Hospital rate
The hospital rate payment allows for the cost of personal items, which patients are expected to provide for themselves. The net weekly hospital rate is $58.34 net as at 1 April 2026.
You can pay an amount above the hospital rate where there are financial circumstances to warrant paying at a higher rate.
Note you cannot pay an amount less than the hospital rate.
For more information see:
- Date payment should be reduced
- Income
- Sole parents
- Effect on Extra Help
- Payment to partners
- On leave from hospital
- Discharge from hospital
- Child admitted to hospital
- Private hospital and homes

chunks.title: Permitted travel reasons — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Permitted travel reasons
A client or partner not otherwise entitled to be paid their Supported Living Payment while absent from New Zealand may have their payments continue for up to 28 days in any 52 week period, if their travel is for one (or a combination) of, the following permitted travel reasons:
- essential travel - to attend a significant event relating to a family member or a person who fulfils a role in relation to the client that is similar to that of a family member, that the client would reasonably be expected to attend
- to attend a court case which the person is required to attend as a party or a witness - this is to allow clients who are required by law to attend court and supports the maintenance of the law. A client would generally be expected to provide evidence that they are required to attend a court overseas. This would include documents from the court.
- to attend a job interview or follow up on a job prospect
- for clients with a disability, to receive vocational training or disability assistance-dog training not available in New Zealand during the time the client is absent
- for clients with a disability, to travel overseas for the sole or predominant purpose of competing in any overseas multinational or international Special Olympic or Paralympic Games competition
- for clients with a disability, to travel overseas for the purpose of attending an approved disability forum
- to provide aid or assistance to a family member immediately following a natural disaster (eg flood, earthquake, fire) or similar adverse event (eg house fire)
## Evidence of the client's situation
Although it may not be possible for the client to get proof of their situation, they should make a reasonable effort to do so.
For more information see:
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Definition of family member
- Essential travel
- Job interviews or follow up on a job prospect
- Absences that do not prevent partner meeting their obligations

chunks.title: Person temporarily leaves care — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: The basic qualification for Supported Living Payment - caring for a person is that the client is providing full time care and attention at home. However, the benefit can continue for a maximum of four weeks while the person being cared for is in some other person's care. This allows the client to have a break. For example, the person may enter respite care for up to four weeks to give the client a short break from caring responsibilities.

chunks.title: Person permanently leaves care — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When the person leaves the care of the client permanently, the client no longer qualifies for Supported Living Payment - caring for a person Unless the person has entered residential care or has been admitted to hospital permanently, the benefit should be cancelled from the beginning of the next pay period following the event. MSD needs to determine if the client qualifies for another benefit.

chunks.title: Person enters residential care or hospital — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Supported Living Payment - caring for a person may continue at the existing rate for 28 days from the date the person left the client's care. This is to allow a period of transition for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.

chunks.title: Death of the person being cared for — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When the person being cared for dies the client no longer qualifies for Supported Living Payment - caring for a person. The benefit may end 28 days following the date of event and can continue to be paid at the existing rate. At the end of the 28-day period MSD needs to determine if the client qualifies for another benefit. Note if the client has other changes of circumstances, such as a change in income, the rate of main benefit and extra help will need to be reassessed.

chunks.title: Mandatory Reviews — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Generally, clients getting Supported Living Payment on the ground of caring for a person must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date or their payments will suspend. If the person being cared for temporarily leaves the client's care and Supported Living Payment will continue, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to respond to the Mandatory Review. If the client is unable to respond to the review (even if they had more time) based on their individual circumstances, they may qualify for an exemption. Generally, when the Mandatory Review is only for Supported Living Payment and the benefit will stop at the end of the 28-day continuation period e.g. the person being cared for has entered residential care or hospital, or died, and the review is due, an exemption will apply. The client must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Generally, clients getting Supported Living Payment on the ground of caring for a person must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will be excluded from their payments. When the person being cared for is a dependent child who turns 18 while they have temporarily left care, the client must respond to the notice, or the child will be excluded from their payments. When the person being cared for is a dependent child who has entered residential care or hospital, or died, and that child turns 18 during that period, the client is not required to respond to the notice and the child will not be excluded during the continuation of payment period. However, if Supported Living Payment and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because the person being cared for has entered residential care or hospital, or died, and a dependent child turns 18 (who is not the person being cared for), the client must still respond to the notice or the child will be excluded from their payments.

chunks.title: Private hospital and homes — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Private hospital and homes
Supported Living Payment can be paid at the full rate regardless of the period of hospitalisation when a client is:
- admitted to a private hospital or
- admitted to a private home that provides residential care disability services
If the client receives Extra Help, this will need to be reviewed to see if their costs are continuing.
For more information see:
- Residential Care Subsidy
- Residential Support Subsidy

chunks.title: Process for decisions — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Process for decisions
Once you have received all the information you require from your client and their employer, you need to make an assessment and draft your decision. The case should then be referred to your Regional Disability Advisor or Regional Health Advisor for their comment.
When you have received comment from your Regional Disability Advisor or Regional Health Advisor you should finalise your decision and record the information on CMS.
For more information see:
- Guidelines for sheltered employment

chunks.title: Protected earnings rate — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Protected earnings rate
Both the District Court Act and the Summary Proceedings Act provide that every Ministry of Justice attachment order must specify a 'protected earnings rate'. The protected earnings rate is usually 60% of the client’s net earnings after PAYE tax has been deducted or withheld.
If the attachment order will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate, then the order will not operate, and you must cancel or return the attachment order to the Ministry of Justice.
Calculating the client's income differs between attachment orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act and the District Court Act, in that different benefits are taken into account. Therefore, it is important to determine what type of attachment order has been issued.
Summary Proceedings Act 1957
For orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act, the calculation of the client's income does not include Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support, Disability Allowance, Child Disability Allowance, Winter Energy Payment, and Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
District Court Act 2016
For orders made under the District Court Act, the client's income includes Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support and Disability Allowance but does not include Child Disability Allowance, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
## Example
An attachment order is received from the Ministry of Justice for $60 per week. The order lists the client's protected earnings rate as $317.76 per week:
Supported Living Payment single 18+ years net rate (as at 1 April 2026)
$424.60
Plus Accommodation Supplement (Area 2)
$105.00
Total net earnings
$529.60
60% of total net earnings (= protected earnings)
$317.76
Calculate if Attachment Order will exceed protected earnings
Total net earnings
$529.60
Less Child Support deduction
$85.00
Less Ministry of Social Development debt
$75.00
Sub total
$369.60
Less Attachment Order
$60.00
Total net income remaining for the client per week
$309.60
The client's income is $309.60, which is below the protected income rate of $317.76.
The attachment order will not operate, you must return it to the Ministry of Justice for the order to be amended.

chunks.title: Qualifies for another benefit — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Qualifies for another benefit
A client may qualify for another benefit due to a change in their circumstances. It is also important to determine if the client still qualifies for Supported Living Payment.
For example:
- if a client's health condition improves they may no longer qualify for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) and they would generally transfer to Jobseeker Support or
- if a person's (who requires full-time care and attention) health condition improves the client would no longer qualify for Supported Living Payment (caring for a person) and would transfer to another benefit or
- a client reaches the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation
If the client qualifies for more than one benefit they must be told which benefit is the most beneficial for their particular circumstances. You will need to advise them of:
- benefit rates
- the effect of any income they may receive (income reduction and any exemptions) and
- benefit obligations
The client must make the final decision on which benefit they receive after being given all relevant information.
For more information see:
- Supported Living Payment Qualifications
- Jobseeker Support Qualifications
- Sole Parent Support Qualifications
- New Zealand Superannuation Qualifications
- Processing standards Client transfers to another benefit type [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Rate of payment - sole parents — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Rate of payment - sole parents
If payment of Supported Living Payment is to continue while a sole parent client is in prison, you will need to determine the rate to pay to the temporary caregiver.
The Supported Living Payment should generally be paid at the equivalent rate of Unsupported Child's Benefit that would be payable if the caregiver qualified for this.
## Exception
However there is discretion to continue payment at the full sole parent rate.
You can consider including the following costs to calculate the rate to pay the temporary caregiver while the client is in prison:
- rent or outgoings if the children are being cared for in the client's home
- the client's other commitments if these costs are for essential items and they cannot be suspended, such as Child Support payments (where the client does not qualify for an exemption) or hire purchase for an essential item
The total amount paid to the temporary caregiver must not exceed the maximum amount of Supported Living Payment payable.
## SWIFTT
The Supported Living Payment and family tax credit and Best start tax credit should continue in the client's name and be paid to the caregiver as an agent in SWIFTT.
When the temporary caregiver is to be paid less than the maximum rate of Supported Living Payment, you will need to add this as a non-standard rate using the SNSRA screen in SWIFTT.
For more information see:
- Examples - sole parents
- Decision guidelines - sole parents
- Sole parents

chunks.title: Release from prison — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Release from prison
A client may be entitled to Supported Living Payment when they are released from prison. The date to recommence payment depends on the length of time the client has been in prison.
## Partner
When the partner of a person in prison has been receiving a benefit, this will need to be reviewed from the date of release.
For more information see:
- Transfer between benefits
- Prisoners no stand-down applies

chunks.title: Release on bail — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Release on bail
When a client is released on bail, Supported Living Payment can be paid from the date of release providing the client meets the qualifying criteria.
Note if the client has been in custody for more than 31 days an initial stand-down will be imposed.
For more information see:
- Prisoners no stand-down applies
- Qualifications

chunks.title: Remanded in custody — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Remanded in custody
Generally, when a client is remanded in custody awaiting a further court appearance their benefit should be stopped. However, there is discretion to continue payment of Supported Living Payment after taking the client's financial circumstances and commitments into account.
When deciding whether to continue paying Supported Living Payment for the period of remand for a particular client, consider the following:
- has the client been remanded pending further hearing or for sentencing
- does the client have continuing costs that cannot be avoided, such as rent and hire purchase for essential items
- does the client have client have a partner or dependent children
- what arrangements have been made for caring for the patient for Supported Living Payment - caring for a person
Every situation should be considered on a case-by-case basis.
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances of the client before making a decision.

chunks.title: Review of Annual Income — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: The Review of Annual Income ensures that clients getting Supported Living Payment have received the correct rate of payment for the past 52 weeks. Clients do not have a Review of Annual Income if their benefit has not been reduced at any point during the period that income is assessed (the 52-week review period). Clients who have not received any income during this period will also not have a review. Note the Review of Annual Income is a separate process to a Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Income received during the review period — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Income received during the 52-week period following the client's commencement date, and each 52 week period after that, is assessed against the benefit that was paid to the client during this time. Most types of income are charged against Supported Living Payment for the review year the income was earned in or the period it relates to. The relevant period may be a period in the past or a future date. Only income charged during the current review period is considered for the Review of Annual Income. If the client has transferred between benefits, but has continuously been getting a benefit that can have income charged annually, the commencement date is the date they first started getting an annual benefit.

chunks.title: Child Support income for Reviews of Annual Income — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Non-information share Child Support Non-information share Child Support payments are charged as income using the general charging rules that are used for most other types of income. Any non-information share Child Support payments charged as income during the current review period are included in the Review of Annual Income. Information share Child Support Information share Child Support payments are charged forward as income, using defined rules. The income charge is always for 4 or 5 weeks from when the client gets the payment, regardless of what period the payment relates to. Any information share Child Support payments charged as income during the current review period are included in the Review of Annual Income. Note the amount of information share Child Support payment charged as income may not be the same amount of Child Support a client got in the review period. This could happen if a client gets an information share Child Support payment shortly before the end of the review period. Only the income charged during the review period can be included in the Review of Annual Income. Example Desdemona gets Supported Living Payment and gets information share Child Support payments from her child's other parent. Desdemona's review period for her Review of Annual Income is 6 September to 5 September the following year. Desdemona gets an information share Child Support payment on 21 August. This payment is charged forward for 4 weeks, from the week beginning 19 August. Only the income charged from 19 August to 5 September will be included in this years' Review of Annual Income. The remainder of the 4-week income charge related to that Child Support payment will be included in the following year's review.

chunks.title: Mandatory Review for Supported Living Payment — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: MSD must review a client's Supported Living Payment within 52-weeks of when their benefit commenced, or within 52-weeks from when the client's last Mandatory Review was completed. Clients must respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, or their payments will suspend. The purpose of a Mandatory Review for Supported Living Payment is to: - check for any changes to a client's circumstances - determine if the client still meets the qualifications for Supported Living Payment (except for the medical qualifications, they are reviewed separately) and - review the rate of Supported Living Payment payable. The review checks a client's circumstances but is not a review of their health condition, injury or disability, known as a medical review. Medical reviews will take place separately. Note the Review of Annual Income is a separate process to a Mandatory Review.

chunks.title: Clients getting Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Clients also getting Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance have these reviewed at the same time as their Mandatory Review for Supported Living Payment. Example: client is getting Supported Living Payment and Accommodation Supplement Celia has been getting Accommodation Supplement since 1 December 2025. Celia applied for Supported Living Payment, which commenced on 10 April 2026. Because the initial Mandatory Review date is determined by the Supported Living Payment commencement date, the review date for both Accommodation Supplement and Supported Living Payment is reset to 52 weeks from 10 April 2026.

chunks.title: Clients getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: If a client is getting Supported Living Payment and Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit, they will have a Mandatory Review for their Supported Living Payment at least once in a 52-week period, but it will be separate to the Mandatory Review for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit. Note MSD may use the information provided to review any assistance the client is getting.

chunks.title: Notice period for a Mandatory Review — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Clients are notified at least 20 working days before their Mandatory Review date, unless their Supported Living Payment is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison. The notice period allows sufficient time for clients to respond to the Mandatory Review. Note if a client's Supported Living Payment is suspended when the Mandatory Review notice is sent, they are not required to respond to their Mandatory Review until their Supported Living Payment is to be resumed.

chunks.title: Responding to the Mandatory Review — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: To respond to the Mandatory Review, the client must: - confirm or provide current information about their circumstances and - provide further information to MSD if requested Clients must confirm the information MSD holds is correct or provide any new information before their review date. When a client has responded to the Mandatory Review and MSD has determined they continue to qualify for Supported Living Payment, their next review date is 52 weeks from the date their Mandatory Review was completed.

chunks.title: Client does not respond to Mandatory Review — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When a client does not respond to the Mandatory Review before their review date, the Supported Living Payment will suspend. If the client does not respond to the Mandatory Review to confirm their circumstances within 8 weeks after their payments have suspended, their benefit will be cancelled. A client can still do their Mandatory Review during those 8 weeks. However, once the benefit has cancelled, the client will need to reapply for Supported Living Payment if they still need this assistance. A client's Supported Living Payment cannot be resumed before they have responded to their Mandatory Review during the 8-week suspension period.

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment suspends — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: If a client's Supported Living Payment suspends as a result of the client not responding to their Mandatory Review, all of their assistance will also suspend, except for the following payments: - Child Disability Allowance - Orphan's Benefit - Unsupported Child's Benefit - Childcare Subsidy - OSCAR (Out of School Care and Recreational Subsidy) - Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment

chunks.title: When the Mandatory Review is completed — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: The Mandatory Review is complete when MSD makes a decision about the client eligibility for Supported Living Payment and the rate of benefit payable. MSD will either: - continue paying the benefit at the existing rate - adjust the rate of benefit so the client is getting the correct rate - suspend the benefit if there is no rate payable for a period (e.g. partner has variable income) - cancel the benefit if the client no longer qualifies

chunks.title: Mandatory Reviews for clients with partners — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When a client has a partner, both the client and partner's circumstances are included in the review. Changes to the partner's circumstances (e.g. income, employment, living arrangements and other factors) must be included in the Mandatory Review. However, if a client and their partner are getting Supported Living Payment in their own right, both clients have a Mandatory Review and are required to confirm their partner's circumstances.

chunks.title: Review of client's health condition — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When a client applies for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) supporting information is used to decide whether your client is both permanently and severely restricted in their capacity to work. When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) is granted, the supporting information is also used to determine if the client's capacity for work will be reassessed: - in 2 years or - never (if the client qualifies to be given simplified access) For more information see: - Simplified access to Supported Living Payment

chunks.title: Impact of their health condition or disability could improve over time — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: For some clients it is reasonable to expect the impact of their permanent health condition or disability may change over time and the client's capacity for work may improve.
