These clients will have their benefit reassessed in 2 years. The client's capacity to work may improve over time because the impact of the client's health condition or disability reduces. This could be because: - their condition improves or - the client becomes better at managing the impact on their capacity to work over time

chunks.title: Impact of their health condition or disability is unlikely to improve over time — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: A small number of clients will qualify to be given simplified access because the impact of their health condition or disability on their capacity for work is unlikely to ever improve enough that they could regularly work 15 hours per week or more in open employment. Clients who qualify to be given simplified access will never require medical reassessment.

chunks.title: Client requires reassessment at 2 years — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: All clients who are eligible for Supported Living Payment but do not qualify to be given simplified access will be reassessed in 2 years. For reassessment, clients will automatically be sent a letter asking them to provide recent information about their health condition or disability. This will be issued approximately 5 weeks before the previous medical certificate expires.

chunks.title: Acceptable recent information — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Your client must meet the medical qualifications for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) to be able to continue to receive the benefit on medical grounds. See: - Medical qualifications When reviewing entitlement for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability), your client can provide either a medical certificate from their health practitioner or suitable existing assessments. For more information see: - Deciding Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) from a medical certificate - Deciding Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) using existing assessments If your client does not have any of this information, they can be referred to see a designated health practitioner. For more information see: - Designated health practitioners

chunks.title: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
For information on the payment in shared care situations see:
- Family tax credit Shared care
- Best Start tax credit Shared care

chunks.title: Sheltered employment — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Sheltered employment
Sheltered employment, for Supported Living Payment eligibility purposes, is employment that:
- is a contracted business enterprise (formerly known as "sheltered workshops") or
- has been designed to cater for the needs of a person who is severely disabled
Sheltered employment provides an environment in which the person, who is severely disabled, can work, notwithstanding their physical or mental impairment.
Note open employment is any other employment. The need to review Supported Living Payment entitlement based on the hours of employment only applies if your client is regularly working in open employment.
Also note the meaning of open employment for employment programmes and services is different. This means a client working in sheltered employment and receiving Supported Living Payment may be eligible for open employment assistance under employment programmes and services.
For more information see:
- Open employment for employment and training services
## How to decide sheltered employment
You need to consider each client's working environment on a case by case basis to determine if they are in sheltered employment.
To decide if your client is working in sheltered employment, you will need to talk with your client and their employer. Your local Employment Co-ordinator may be the most appropriate person to talk to the employer.
Note all types of employees (e.g. full-time, self-employed, supported or contract workers) could be considered as being in sheltered employment if their employment conditions have been specifically designed to cater for the needs of a severely disabled employee.
For more information see:
- Guidelines for sheltered employment
- Process for decisions
- One-off environmental change is not sheltered employment

chunks.title: Single clients — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Single clients
Generally, Supported Living Payment should be suspended when a single client is imprisoned. This will enable the benefit to be resumed if the client is only in prison for a short period and re-applies for a benefit following their release.
Note the Supported Living Payment should be suspended from the date following imprisonment.
## Exception - remanded in custody
Although the Supported Living Payment should be stopped for any period during which the client is remanded in custody pending further court appearance, there is discretion to continue payment of all or part of the benefit.
For more information see:
- Remanded in custody

chunks.title: Sole Parents — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Sole Parents
When a Supported Living Payment sole parent is admitted to hospital their benefit can continue at the full rate for the first 13 weeks.
You will need to find out who is caring for the client's child and the length of time the client is likely to be in hospital. If requested, you can pay part of the benefit to the child's caregiver to cover the cost of alternative care or accommodation.
Where the child is not going to remain in the care of the client, check what the continuing care arrangements are for the child. If the child is no longer a dependent child you will need to exclude the child and review the client's Supported Living Payment.
## Client in hospital for more than 13 weeks
If the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks, their rate of payment will need to be reduced to the hospital rate. You can pay a rate other than the hospital rate where:
- the client's financial circumstances warrant paying a higher rate
If there are no other continuing financial costs and it is likely that the client will remain in hospital long term, consider other means of income support for the children. For example, the new caregiver may meet the qualifications for Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, or the child may be able to be included as a dependent child if the new caregiver is receiving a main benefit.
## Family tax credit
As long as the child continues to be a dependent child, family tax credit payments continue to be paid regardless of how long the client is in hospital.
For more information see:
- Agents
- Date payment should be reduced
- Effect on Extra Help
- On leave from hospital
- Discharge from hospital

chunks.title: Sole parents — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Sole parents
When a sole parent client is imprisoned the Supported Living Payment will generally need to be cancelled.
Note the Supported Living Payment should be cancelled from the day following imprisonment.
You may need to find out who is caring for the client's children and the length of time the client is likely to be in prison. For Supported living Payment- caring for you may need to find out who is caring for the patient and, the client's children; and the length of time the client is likely to be in prison. The length of time in prison can be obtained by contacting the prison liaison officer at the Department of Corrections.
Generally, the caregiver will need to apply for financial assistance in their own right.
They may be entitled to:
- have the children included as dependent children in their current benefit
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Emergency Benefit Single and caring for a child or
- family tax credit and Best Start tax credit through Inland Revenue
## Exception
There is discretion to pay all or part of the Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) to a temporary caregiver caring for the client's children. For Supported Living Payment (caring for a person), there is discretion to pay all or part of the Supported Living Payment to a temporary caregiver caring for the person and, the client's children.
There is also discretion to continue payment if the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance.
For more information to help you decide these cases see:
- Decision guidelines - sole parents
- Temporary caregiver
- Rate of payment - sole parents
- Examples - sole parents
- Remanded in custody

chunks.title: Special Disability Allowance — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Special Disability Allowance
A Special Disability Allowance is paid to the partner of a client who is receiving the hospital rate or Residential Care Subsidy. It is paid to the person not in hospital or residential care to help with the extra costs of their partner's hospitalisation, for example travel costs to visit the patient.
Note that Special Disability Allowance is:
- granted without the client having to apply
- paid separately from Disability Allowance and
- not income or asset tested
Special Disability Allowance can start from the date the client in the community starts receiving a single rate of benefit, and their partner starts receiving a hospital rate of benefit or becomes financially eligible for Residential Care Subsidy.
For more information see:
- Deskfile Special Disability Allowance rates
Special Disability Allowance should be stopped from the first available date if the person receiving it is also admitted to hospital.
## SWIFTT
In SWIFTT, grant Special Disability Allowance using code 838 on the SSUPI screen.

chunks.title: Special Olympics or Paralympics — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Special Olympics or Paralympics
A client receiving Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability, or total blindness only) may need to travel overseas to participate in a multinational or international Special Olympic or Paralympics competition.
In these cases the client can continue to receive payment of their benefit for up to six weeks when they are absent from New Zealand. These extra days absent from New Zealand is additional to the 28 days they can usually have in a 52 week period.
Note this does not apply to a partner with work obligations.
## Other benefits participating in Special Olympics or Paralympics
Clients and partners receiving other benefits and who are participating in the Special Olympics or Paralympics may be able to attend and be paid their benefit while they are attending these events if they meet the criteria for approved travel.
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
## Proof
The client will need to provide proof that they have been selected to complete in a multinational or international Special Olympic or Paralympics competition outside of New Zealand.
## Process
For more information contact Helpline.

chunks.title: Specific engagements — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Specific engagements
Specific engagements are interactions that can meet the same purpose as the Mandatory Review. These interactions can capture information that confirms if a client still qualifies for Supported Living Payment.
Specific engagements are when a client has an interaction with MSD, and this results in a full review of the client's circumstances.
For example, specific engagements may include when a client contacts MSD to:
- discuss a change in circumstances or
- apply for assistance
If the specific engagement meets the same purpose as a Mandatory Review, and the client still qualifies, their Mandatory Review date is set 52 weeks from when the specific engagement was completed.

chunks.title: Split care — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Split care
Split care is when parents with two or more children are living apart and each parent has the care of at least one of their children on a full-time basis.
The child(ren) that is living with the Supported Living Payment client can be included as a dependent child.
In split care situations, generally only one parent can receive Sole Parent Support. The other parent must qualify, in their own right, for another benefit.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support Split care

chunks.title: Start date of Sustainable Employment Trial — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Start date of Sustainable Employment Trial
The start date of a client's Sustainable Employment Trial is the day:
- the client starts work or
- when the client and Work and Income agree to the Sustainable Employment Trial, if the client is already in employment
whichever is the later date.
## Backdating start date
If a client is already in employment, the start date of their Sustainable Employment Trial cannot be backdated. This means the Sustainable Employment Trial cannot have a start date prior to the client having gained the agreement of their case manager to take part in the Sustainable Employment Trial.
The Sustainable Employment Trial provisions came into force on 1 July 2004.

chunks.title: Stopping the Sustainable Employment Trial early — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Stopping the Sustainable Employment Trial early
The Sustainable Employment Trial ends if the client is unable to sustain the employment and withdraws from the Sustainable Employment Trial.
You should also discuss with the client what the barriers were that caused them to stop the Sustainable Employment Trial. Establish what Work and Income can do to assist them to overcome those barriers.
For more information see:
- End of Sustainable Employment Trial

chunks.title: Student Loans — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Student Loans
Clients with a Student Loan must make repayments to Inland Revenue when the income they receive exceeds the 'income threshold'.
A person must make repayments to Inland Revenue when their income exceeds $464.00 gross per week ($24,128 gross per year) as at 1 April 2026. Note non-taxable Extra help such as family tax credit, Accommodation Supplement and Winter Energy Payment do not count as income in this instance.
If the client's income is over this income threshold, the Ministry of Social Development can make the required deduction. However, this is only done if the client requests it.
If the client's portion of benefit is below the income threshold, there is no provision to make voluntary repayments through SWIFTT.
The client can make voluntary payments direct to Inland Revenue at any time.
Note the following:
- Student Loan deductions can only be made from taxable benefits
- Student Loan deductions cannot be made if the client's benefit is below the income threshold
- when a client receives a married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit only the client's portion is taken into consideration when assessing Student Loan repayments
- when a client is receiving a reduced rate of payment due to other income, the Student Loan deduction is assessed on the net payment after income deduction
For more information on Student Loans see:
- Students Student Loan

chunks.title: Study — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Study
Clients (and partners) have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any change in their circumstances that may affect their qualification for Supported Living Payment, such as commencing study.
When a Supported Living Payment client intends to or has commenced study, you will need to find out:
- the date study starts and
- the type of study, that is part-time or full-time
This will help you decide the appropriate review action required.
The client may qualify for Education and employment-related training
For more information see:
- Client engaged in study
- Partner engaged in study

chunks.title: Suitability of Sustainable Employment Trial — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Suitability of Sustainable Employment Trial
You and the client need to agree that the client will take part in a Sustainable Employment Trial and the period of the Sustainable Employment Trial. As Work and Income want to encourage clients to trial work, in most cases it will be appropriate to agree to a client's request to undertake a Sustainable Employment Trial.
You may want to encourage the client to discuss their involvement in a Sustainable Employment Trial with their health practitioner or other relevant support professional. This may include discussions on whether the job is appropriate or their planned hours of work are realistic or could be gradually increased.
For more information see:
- Clients undertaking multiple Sustainable Employment Trials
- Length of Sustainable Employment Trial
- Start date of Sustainable Employment Trial
- Clients who can take part

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment suspended before Mandatory Review date — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment suspended before Mandatory Review date
Clients getting Supported Living Payment are always notified about their Mandatory Review, even if their Supported Living Payment is suspended, unless it is suspended due to the client being temporarily overseas or in prison.
MSD must not undertake the Mandatory Review unless the client contacts MSD to resume their Supported Living Payment.
If the client contacts MSD before their review date to resume their Supported Living Payment, they may be able to get an extension if they need more time to do their Mandatory Review. MSD can resume the benefit before the Mandatory Review has been responded to.
However, if the client contacts MSD on or after their Mandatory Review date, the review must be completed before MSD can resume the benefit (if they still qualify).
Example
Caleb is a single person with no dependent children getting Supported Living Payment. Caleb's Mandatory Review is due on 2 May.
Caleb left New Zealand to go on holiday on 25 April and did not tell MSD that he was leaving. His Supported Living Payment suspended on 26 April.
On 10 May Caleb contacts MSD and advises that he arrived back in New Zealand on 7 May.
MSD tells Caleb that he will need to respond to the Mandatory Review and confirm his circumstances before MSD can resume his Supported Living Payment.
On 11 May Caleb responds to his Mandatory Review and confirms that he has had no change in circumstances.
MSD determines that Caleb continues to qualify for Supported Living Payment at the same rate and resumes his benefit from 7 May (the day he returned to New Zealand).
MSD completes Caleb's Mandatory Review on 11 May and sets the next review date for 52 weeks from the date the review was completed. Caleb's next Mandatory Review date is 9 May 2028.

chunks.title: Sustainable Employment Trial — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Sustainable Employment Trial
The purpose of the Sustainable Employment Trial is to encourage and support Supported Living Payment clients who want to move into employment or increase their hours of work to establish whether they can sustain that employment and cease receiving that benefit.
Supported Living Payment clients, with the agreement of their case manager, can work 15 hours or more a week for an agreed period of up to 26 weeks, without losing their entitlement to Supported Living Payment. This is known as a Sustainable Employment Trial.
## No change to Supported Living Payment qualifications
The introduction of the Sustainable Employment Trial does not change the Supported Living Payment qualifications in that the client must be:
- permanently and severely restricted in their capacity to work because of a health condition, or injury or disability from accident or congenital defect
- these clients must be medically assessed as being incapable of regularly working 15 or more hours a week in open employment) or
- totally blind
- the Sustainable Employment Trial process does not apply to totally blind clients because they can already work 15 or more hours per week without their benefit entitlement being affected
## Charging income against benefit rate
Clients undertaking a Sustainable Employment Trial and earning income will qualify for a personal earnings exemption. They may also be eligible for a special exemption for severe disablement. Except for income to which an exemption applies, any income earned from the Sustainable Employment Trial is to be charged against the benefit; the benefit will be reduced as under existing rules.
Note any income earned by the client may affect their entitlement to Extra Help.
For more information see:
- Clients who can take part
- Suitability of Sustainable Employment Trial
- Start date of Sustainable Employment Trial
- Length of Sustainable Employment Trial
- Hours of work
- Charging income against benefit rate
- End of Sustainable Employment Trial
- Employment and training Employment Transition Assistance
- Sustainable Employment Trial: client agrees to start an employment trial [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Tax certificates — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Tax certificates
MSD does not issue tax certificates to clients.
If a client requests information about their tax details they must be referred to Inland Revenue to get a "Summary of Earnings" or a "Personal Tax Summary".

chunks.title: Tax codes — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Tax codes
Supported Living Payment is taxed at the 'M' rate.
Supported Living Payment is always considered the client's primary source of income regardless of the amount paid.
If the client has other income this is always considered the client's secondary income.
Clients can apply to Inland Revenue for a tailored tax code for other income.
## SWIFTT
MSD can view a client's current monthly tax details in STAXQ.
The client's tax history can be viewed in STAXI.

chunks.title: Taxation — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Taxation
Supported Living Payment is a taxable benefit. MSD makes payments to clients at the net rate after the deduction of tax. MSD passes the tax on to Inland Revenue.
Generally, MSD will request clients to give MSD their IRD number or evidence of their IRD number.

chunks.title: Temporary caregiver — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Temporary caregiver
When a client is imprisoned, you will need to find out who is caring for the client's children; and the length of time the client is likely to be in prison. This information can be obtained by contacting the prison liaison officer at the Department of Corrections.
If another person is caring for the client's dependent children or patient (Supported Living Payment - caring for a person only), generally the temporary caregiver will need to apply for financial assistance in their own right.
They may be entitled to:
- have the children included as dependent children in their current benefit
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Emergency Benefit Single and caring for a child or
- family tax credit through Inland Revenue
- the Supported Living Payment in their own right
## Exception
There is discretion to pay all or part of the Supported Living Payment a temporary caregiver caring for the client's children and the patient (Supported Living Payment- caring for a person).
There is also discretion to continue payment if the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance.
For more information to help you decide, see:
- Decision guidelines - sole parents
- Rate of payment - sole parents
- Examples - sole parents
- Remanded in custody
- Sole parent

chunks.title: Terminal benefit for a single client — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit for a single client
Generally, the Supported Living Payment stops from the date following the death of a single client with no children, however, there is some discretion to continue the payment of benefit for up to 28 days. When payment is continued after the date of death, it is referred to as terminal benefit.
Circumstances to consider for continued benefit payment beyond a single client's date of death include:
- when the deceased client's domestic situation results in a transition cost for a family member, causing hardshipExample: accommodation and other household costs when client has been sharing accommodation
or
- when there are exceptional and justified costs associated with the death of the clientExample: multiple deaths within one family
Payment should not continue for 28 days following the death of a single client to meet funeral expenses. A Funeral Grant is available for this purpose.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit payments to surviving partner or person caring for the children — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit payments to surviving partner or person caring for the children
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children.
## Surviving partner
When terminal benefit is being paid to a couple, both the deceased client's and the surviving person's portion of the benefit is paid. Payment is the total benefit as well as any ongoing extra help. It does not include family tax credit or Best Start tax credit.
The deceased person's portion of terminal benefit is paid to their bank account.
A surviving person can apply to have the deceased client's portion of terminal benefit paid to them. When an application is received, terminal benefit (or remaining unpaid balance) can be paid to that applicant.
The surviving person's benefit should be reviewed to determine the best option financially for the person.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit rate — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: The provision to continue the benefit payment for 28 days following the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit. Benefit payment is continued at the rate which was payable to the client and partner (if any) at the date of death. A terminal benefit includes any extra help being paid (for up to 28 days following the date of death), but does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments.

chunks.title: Benefit paid at a reduced rate — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When the client's benefit was paid at a reduced rate at the date of death, the terminal benefit is also paid at the reduced rate. Benefit payments may have been reduced due to: - hospitalisationThe deceased client's benefit was reduced as they were in hospital for more than 13 weeks. - income - debt repayments when there are benefit arrears due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit paymentdo not recover debts in full, from terminal benefit payments - when there are benefit arrears due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit payment - do not recover debts in full, from terminal benefit payments - Child Support if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable at the cannot be reviewedChild Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however, MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenuewhen a surviving partner or family member makes enquires, refer them to Inland Revenue - if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable at the cannot be reviewed - Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however, MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenue - when a surviving partner or family member makes enquires, refer them to Inland Revenue - court attachment orders - redirection of payment to Kāinga Ora or a community housing providerWhen the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. For more information see: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client Note all of the above deductions will continue to be made from the terminal benefit payments unless they are manually stopped before cancellation.

chunks.title: Changes to benefit rates payable — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Rates of main benefits being paid as part of Terminal benefit are adjusted to reflect changes in the rate payable arising from legislative amendments such as the Annual General Adjustment of benefit rates on 1 April each year.

chunks.title: Unclear if the client is regularly working 15 or more hours a week — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Unclear if the client is regularly working 15 or more hours a week
If it is unclear whether the client will be regularly working 15 or more hours a week, you should discuss the matter with the client and the employer, if the client gives permission. This will help to determine whether the employment is regular.
If a client is regularly working 15 hours or more a week in open employment, and the exceptions below do not apply, Supported Living Payment must stop. You will need to consider if the client qualifies for another benefit or invite the client to apply for non beneficiary assistance and advise them of possible entitlement to Working for Families Tax Credits through Inland Revenue.
## Exceptions
- clients who are totally blind are able to work 15 hours or more a week, without it affecting their qualification for Supported Living Payment
- clients undertaking an Sustainable Employment Trial with the prior agreement of their case manager
(These clients can work 15 hours or more a week for an agreed period of up to 26 weeks, without it affecting their qualification for Supported Living Payment during the agreed period)
If you are unable to determine whether the work will be regular at this time, Supported Living Payment should continue to be paid. However, you should arrange to reassess the matter at a later date. This will depend upon the individual client but a suggestion is to review their circumstances in one month.
If you are still unable to determine whether the work is regular at the next review, you should continue to meet with the client on a monthly basis until a decision can be made.
Note Supported Living Payment should continue until a decision is made that the employment is regular. No overpayment should be established as the client is entitled to Supported Living Payment until the decision is made that the work is regular.
For more information see:
- Client is regularly working 15 or more hours a week
- Guidelines for regular employment

chunks.title: Underpaid — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Underpaid
When a client has been underpaid Supported Living Payment and is owed arrears, MSD will work out the amount of tax and pass this on to Inland Revenue.
From 1 April 2024, if an arrears payment relates to a previous tax year, the arrears will not be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment. This means the client will not have to pay any more tax on the payment.
Only arrears payments related to the current tax year will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment.
Example
A client is paid arrears on 12 June 2025. This payment represents arrears for 25 March 2025 to 8 June 2025.
The arrears for 25 March to 31 March 2025 represent a past tax year, so they will not be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment. The arrears for 1 April to 8 June 2025 represent the current tax year, so they will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment.

chunks.title: Verification of annual income — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Verification of annual income
Depending on the client's circumstances, they will either need to:
- provide income verification for the 52 week period
- check if their information is correct.If it is correct, they do not need to do anything. If it is different they will need to provide verification as above.
If the client cannot provide verification (for example payslips) then you can contact the employer and ask them to complete the
- Employment and earnings information for reviews (V26) form
For further details on how to charge income see:
- Core Policy Income

chunks.title: Weekend leave — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Weekend leave
Supported Living Payment is paid for a seven day period, covering Monday to Sunday. Therefore, where the client is receiving the hospital rate and they are on weekend leave you should pay the appropriate full rate of benefit for the number of days the client is on leave and subsequently incurring additional expenses in the community.
## Example
Client is on leave from Friday to Monday, you will need to pay the appropriate full rate of benefit for four days. Generally, you will do this by completing a back dated review so that SWIFTT will pay the appropriate full rate of Supported Living Payment for four days.
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.

chunks.title: When an extension or exemption can be given — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: When a client needs more time to respond to the Mandatory Review, they may be able to get an extension. If a client is unable to respond to the review, they may be able to get an exemption. Clients must contact MSD before their review date to discuss their situation if they need an extension or exemption. A client cannot get an extension or exemption on or after the Mandatory Review date. Note even if a client gets an extension or exemption, they must still advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Supported Living Payment or the rate payable.

chunks.title: Extension - client needs more time to respond to review — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: Clients may be able to get an extension if there is a good and sufficient reason why they cannot respond to their Mandatory Review before the review date. When a client needs more time to respond to the review, they must let MSD know before their Mandatory Review date. The extension can only be granted before the review date. Good and sufficient reasons may include (but are not limited to): - the client is unexpectedly hospitalised - death or illness in the client's immediate family - the client is experiencing or escaping a family violence situation If MSD determines the client has a good and sufficient reason, the client can get an extension of up to 20 working days. Note a client can get multiple short extensions, however the maximum amount of time that can be given for an extension is a total of 20 working days from the client's original review date.

chunks.title: Exemption - client is unable to respond to review — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text: A client may be able to get an exemption when they are experiencing an unforeseen event or situation that is beyond their control, and this means they are unable to respond to their Mandatory Review (even if they had more time). The client must let MSD know before their review date to discuss their circumstances. Exemptions reasons may include (but are not limited to): - localised natural disaster that affects the client but not the whole region (e.g. the client's property is affected by a landslip) - unexpected serious illness or an accident affecting the client or their immediate family member - the client's benefit is ending because a child has left their care suddenly and the Mandatory Review is due during the 28-day continuation of payment - the client's benefit is ending because the person they are caring for has died or entered residential care or hospital and the Mandatory Review is due during the 28-day continuation of payment Generally, an exemption would also apply when a client's benefit is ending within 28 days because they no longer meet the medical qualifications. If MSD determines an exemption applies, the client is not required to respond to the Mandatory Review, and the review date is reset to 52 weeks in the future from their current review date. Example Danny is getting Supported Living Payment and has a Mandatory Review due on 15 October 2026. However, Danny's home is damaged by a landslip, and he cannot return home. Because Danny has lost all his possessions and is focused on finding accommodation, MSD determines it is not reasonable for Danny to respond to his Mandatory Review by his review date. In this case, MSD grants an exemption. Danny's next Mandatory Review is set for 52 weeks from the original review date.

chunks.title: Young partner not yet subject to obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Young partner not yet subject to obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning
A young partner of a main beneficiary with youth activity obligations who is not yet subject to the obligation to be in education, training or work based learning can continue to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason when the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations.
## Example (but not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A young person who is not yet subject to the education obligation as their youngest dependent child is less than 12 months (and there is no Teen Parent Unit place available for them) wishes to holiday in Australia.
As long as the travel will not prevent the young person from meeting their other obligations (eg their parenting and budgeting obligations) they can continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations
- Absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days for an approved reason
- Activity failures for young partners
- Youth activity obligations

chunks.title: Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations — main benefits > supported living payment > changes and reviews supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations
A young partner of a main beneficiary who is exempt from all of their youth activity obligations can continue to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason if the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations.
A young partner who is exempt from some of their youth activity obligations can continue to receive their payment for any reason for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations.
## Example (but not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A young person who is exempt from all of their activity obligations advises that they wish to travel to Australia to visit friends.
The young person is able to be absent from New Zealand and continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
Note that a client with a partial exemption is still subject to some obligations and therefore they can only be paid while they are overseas if the travel will not prevent them from meeting their obligations.

chunks.title: Charging income — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Charging income
Clients getting Supported Living Payment have a part-time income test, and income may be charged annually or weekly.
## Annual income charge
A client (and partner, if any) who has income charged annually can get up to $8,320 per year (as at 1 April 2022) before their income will affect their benefit.
For clients who get over $8,320:
- income between $8,320 and $13,000 per year reduces their benefit by 30 cents for each $1.00 of income
- income over $13,000 per year reduces their benefit by 70 cents for every $1.00 of income
## Weekly income charge
A client (and partner, if any) who has income charged weekly can receive up to $160 per week (as at 1 April 2022) before their income will affect their benefit.
For clients who receive over $160 per week:
- income between $160 and $250 per week their benefit is reduced by 30 cents for each $1.00 of income
- income over $250 per week their benefit is reduced by 70 cents for every $1.00 of income
## Charging income for couples
Charging income for a married, civil union or de facto couple against Supported Living Payment (caring for a person) is calculated differently to other benefits. See:
- Supported Living Payment (caring for a person) - charging income for couples
- Supported Living Payment (health condition) - partners income
- Supported Living Payment client with New Zealand Superannuation partner - income assessment
## Income exemptions
There are also specific income exemptions that apply to Supported Living Payment clients.
Clients getting Supported Living Payment can get the following income exemption:
- Exemption for severe disablement
Clients getting Supported Living Payment on ground of health condition, injury, disability or total blindness can also get:
- Personal earnings exemptions
Note clients who are totally blind may be able to get a Blind client's subsidy
## Income from Overseas Pensions
Income from overseas pensions is generally treated as a direct deduction from the benefit rate and this has a separate calculation to charging other types of income.

chunks.title: Child changes and social obligations — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Child changes and social obligations
Sometimes a client will have a change in circumstances that may mean the client is no longer required to comply with their social obligations. This includes where:
- a dependent child changes age and the social obligation that applied for the dependent child in their care is no longer relevant or
- child leaves care (for example starts to live with another parent or caregiver or goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki)

chunks.title: Child Disability Allowance assessment — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Child Disability Allowance assessment
MSD can consider granting Supported Living Payment from a Child Disability Allowance assessment when the information confirms the client meets the medical criteria for Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Child Disability Allowance
If a child getting Child Disability Allowance is now applying for Supported Living Payment, MSD can grant Supported Living Payment if there is medical evidence showing that the child is permanently and severely restricted in their capacity for work because of a health condition, injury or disability.
## Child Disability Allowance children that meet the medical criteria
Not all children who have been getting Child Disability Allowance will meet the medical criteria for Supported Living Payment.
For example, children who have been getting Child Disability Allowance for epilepsy or an eating disorder, may not be permanently and severely restricted in their capacity for work because of a health condition, injury or disability.
If the client was getting Child Disability Allowance for the following health conditions or impairments they are likely to qualify for Supported Living Payment:
- long standing, severe ill health (e.g. ongoing cancer, end-stage kidney disease, degenerative conditions such as muscular dystrophy)
- severe physical disabilities (e.g. tetraplegia, paraplegia, spina bifida, cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy)
- intellectual disability (e.g. Down Syndrome)
- blindness (if the information on the report meets the medical qualification for blindness)
- deafness
The client may also have other assessments such as NASC assessments, assessment from their specialist or have special education reports. MSD can use more than 1 assessment to establish eligibility to Supported Living Payment.
If it is unclear from the information the client has provided that they meet the medical criteria for Supported Living Payment, seek advice from the Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor [no link find out why] .

chunks.title: Client in hospital — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Client in hospital
A client's Supported Living Payment rate of payment can be different if they are in hospital.
## Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or total blindness)
The rate is reduced to the hospital rate when the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks (not after receiving a benefit for 13 weeks).
If a client is married, in a civil union or de facto relationship with dependent children do not reduce their rate.
The hospital rate allows for the cost of personal items, which patients are expected to provide for themselves.
## Exception
If the client has been in hospital for 13 weeks or more at the commencement date of the benefit, the rate of payment is the hospital rate.
For more information about the hospital rate for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury or disability) see:
- Hospitalisation
## Supported Living Payment (caring for a person)
The main qualification for Supported Living Payment (caring for a person) is that the client is providing full time care and attention at home. However, the benefit can continue for a maximum of 28 days while the patient is in some other person's care because the client is in hospital.
If the client is in hospital for more than 28 days, they will no longer qualify for Supported Living Payment (caring for a person). You will need to find out if the client qualifies for another benefit.
For more information about the qualifications for Supported Living Payment (caring for a person) see:
- Qualifications

chunks.title: Client is meeting their social obligations — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Client is meeting their social obligations
If, during any of the Contact Steps of engagement and support, you consider that the client is meeting their social obligations you will need to let the client know that:
- as they are meeting their social obligations, you do not require any more information or contact from them and
- if they require any support regarding their social obligations they can contact Work and Income at any time
The appropriate outcome for the specific social obligations that apply to each of the client's dependent children needs to be recorded in OBMAN.
For more information on the 3 step process of engagement see:
- Contact steps - social obligations [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Client leaves Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Client leaves Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre
No stand-down applies to the commencement of a benefit when a client has left the Mangere Refugee Resettlement Centre.
For more information see:
- Refugees and protected persons
- Commencement date
- No stand-down applies

chunks.title: Client's circumstances — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Client's circumstances
To be eligible for Supported Living Payment a client must be:
- both permanently and severely restricted in their capacity for work because of a health condition, injury or disability or totally blind
or
- caring for a person who requires full-time care and attention

chunks.title: Clients from overseas — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Clients from overseas
If the client was born in another country or has lived and worked overseas this needs to be recorded on CMS. International Services will follow up any entitlement to an overseas pension once the details are recorded in CMS.
## Cook Island, Niue and Tokelau clients
Clients born in the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau are automatically New Zealand citizens (by birth). Generally they will travel to New Zealand on a New Zealand passport.
However, they must still have lived continuously in New Zealand for 2 years at any one before they can receive the Supported Living Payment.
Other residents of the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau will be required to produce a proof of residence document and meet the 2 years continuous residence requirement in New Zealand.
## Australian clients
Australian citizens are lawfully allowed in New Zealand as they are deemed to hold a residence class visa. However, they must still meet the 2 years residence qualification to qualify for Supported Living Payment.
If a client does not meet the residence requirements for Supported Living Payment, they may be able to receive an Emergency Benefit.
## British clients
Clients of British nationality who arrived in New Zealand prior to 2 April 1974 were allowed residence in New Zealand without a visa or permit. However, they must still meet the residence requirement for Supported Living Payment.

chunks.title: Clients undertaking voluntary work — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Clients undertaking voluntary work
Clients undertake voluntary work provided they continue to meet their work or work preparation obligations.
Clients with work preparation or work obligations may have to give up some or all of their voluntary activities if a work preparation activity is required or if a suitable job becomes available.
For more information see:
- Voluntary Work [no link find out why]
- Suitable employment

chunks.title: Clients with a partner — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Clients with a partner
Clients with a partner can apply for Supported Living Payment (caring for a person who is not their partner), however, there is no couple rate of benefit. The partner will need to qualify for a benefit in their own right or have some other form of income.
When you assess the rate of Supported Living Payment payable you must take the partners income into account.
Some carers may be getting Funded Family Care payments. These payments are income when assessing the rate of benefit payable.

chunks.title: Clients with dependent children - 50% protection — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Clients with dependent children - 50% protection
Sanctions are applied differently for:
- sole parent clients who fail their obligations
- couples with dependent children who both fail their obligations
- couples where one person is youth money managed
Clients and partners in these situations with a financial sanction imposed do not have their whole benefit sanctioned. Instead, a maximum sanction of 50% of the total benefit may be imposed. The balance payable is known as 50% protection.
For more information, including treatment of supplementary assistance, see:
- Sanctions for sole parents
- Sanctions for a couple with dependent children - both fail their obligations
- Sanctions for young partners
Note if a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligation failures.
For more information see:
- Recompliance

chunks.title: Commencement date — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
To decide when the Supported Living Payment can start you must first find the entitlement date.
This is usually the date that a person no longer has a means of support.
For a list of these dates see:
- Entitlement Date
Supported Living Payment is subject to an initial stand-down of up to a maximum of 2 weeks after the entitlement date.
Generally the commencement date is:
- the day after the initial stand-down ends or
- the application date
whichever is the later.
However, if a client applies for Supported Living Payment within 28 days of their entitlement date, the commencement date rules are different, see:
- Twenty-eight day rule
## No stand-down applies
There are some situations when an initial stand-down is not imposed. When no stand-down applies, the commencement date of the benefit is:
- the entitlement date or
- the application date
whichever is the later.
For more information see:
- Core policy Application for benefit
- Initial stand-down
- No stand-down applies
- Absence from New Zealand
- Non-entitlement period for 13 weeks
A partner with work obligations can have a longer stand-down before they can get Supported Living Payment.

chunks.title: Community Work Experience — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Community Work Experience
Community Work Experience is a non-financial sanction that can be imposed on a partner of a client who gets Supported Living Payment instead of a Grade 1 financial sanction. It is intended to help build work-related skills and confidence, and also build connections in their community.
A partner will work with a community or voluntary organisation, for at least 5 hours a week, for 4 weeks.
A partner will have a 2-week search period before their Community Work Experience begins to find a suitable position and organisation.
MSD will need to confirm whether the organisation and position are suitable before the partner can begin.
Once the partner completes their Community Work Experience, they are considered to have recomplied with their obligation failure and do not need to complete any other recompliance activities.

chunks.title: Examples of transfers between benefits — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Examples of transfers between benefits
The following table outlines what happens to the failure count and sanction when a Youth client transfers benefit type.
From
To
Failure count
Sanction
Jobseeker Support
Young Parent Payment
Re-sets to zero
Re-sets to zero

Jobseeker Support (work obligations)
Carries over
Re-set to zero
Young partner aged 16 or 17 years getting Jobseeker Support
Young partner aged 16 or 17 years getting Supported Living Payment

Carries over
## Calculating continuous receipt of benefit
To calculate continuous receipt of benefit, any employment for less than 10 working days is disregarded.

chunks.title: Grade 1 and 2 sanctions — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Grade 1 and 2 sanctions
The primary client who has met their obligations will continue to get their portion of the assistance.
A first or second failure means suspension of the in-hand allowance and any incentive payments for the young partner, until they recomply with the obligations they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations).
The young partner can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and portion of Winter Energy Payment to which they are entitled.
If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks the whole of their benefit and any incentive payments are suspended along with their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Winter Energy Payment . The primary client can be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.
Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.
## Grade 3 sanction
The primary client who has met their obligations will continue to get their portion of the assistance. They will also be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.
If the young partner who is youth money managed fails their obligations for a third time:
- their portion of the benefit, and any incentive payments is cancelled immediately
- their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Winter Energy Payment is cancelled and
- the young partner is subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks from the date of cancellation
The young partner may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities.
If the young partner does not start a 6-week approved activity, they may reapply at the end of their non-entitlement period to get a benefit.
Note Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period.

chunks.title: Couple, young partner is youth money managed, primary client has work preparation obligations, dependent children, both fail — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Couple, young partner is youth money managed, primary client has work preparation obligations, dependent children, both fail
Couples with dependent children who both fail their obligations at the same time do not have their whole benefit sanctioned. Instead, a maximum sanction of 50% of the total benefit may be imposed.
If a client has more than one obligation failure initiated on the same day, only one sanction can be imposed on the client. For the sanction to be lifted, the client must successfully dispute or recomply with all the obligations failures.
Note family tax credit continues to be paid at the full rate.
## Grade 1 sanction
If the primary client fails their obligations for the first time, their portion of the benefit is reduced by 50% unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed. Extra help (including their portion of Winter Energy Payment) is not affected.
For more information on non-financial sanctions see:
- Non-financial sanctions
If the young partner fails for the first time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments will be suspended. Their Extra help (including their portion of Winter Energy Payment) is not affected.
## Grade 2 sanction
If the primary client fails their obligations a second time, their portion (50% of the couple's benefit) is reduced by 25%. Their portion of Extra help is also suspended. They will not get their portion of Winter Energy Payment.
If the young partner also fails for the second time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments will be suspended.
The young partner will continue to get their portion of any Extra help to which they are entitled. In effect the couple gets 50% of the total Extra help to which they are entitled. This is as they have 50% protection for the family unit.
The young partner will also continue to be paid the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: If the young partner fails their obligations for the first time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments are suspended, until they recomply with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations). The young partner can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and Winter Energy Payment to which they are entitled. Disability Allowance is payable throughout any non-entitlement period. The primary client will continue to get any 50% of the couple's benefit entitlement and their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and the Winter Energy Payment. If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks their portion of the benefit is suspended. Their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks, including their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. The primary client will continue to get 50% of their married rate of benefit and their portion of Temporary Additional Support and Accommodation Supplement. The primary client can be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment. Note family tax credit continues to be paid at the full rate.

chunks.title: Grade 2 sanction — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: If the young partner fails their obligations for the second time, their in-hand allowance and any incentive payments are suspended, until they recomply with the obligation they have failed (or obligations if they have failed to comply with one or more of their obligations). The young partner can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and Winter Energy Payment to which they are entitled. The primary client will continue to get 50% of the couples benefit entitlement and their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and the Winter Energy Payment. If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks their portion of the benefit is suspended. Their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended. Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks, including their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. The primary client will continue to get 50% of their married rate of benefit and their portion of Temporary Additional Support and Accommodation Supplement. The primary client can be paid the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: Grade 3 sanction — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: If the young partner fails their obligations for a third time, their portion of the benefit and extra help is cancelled. They are subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks. The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities. If they have not started a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of the non-entitlement period to get a benefit. The non-sanctioned primary client will continue to get 50% of the couple's benefit entitlement including Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support. The non-sanctioned primary client will be paid the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Grade 1 sanction
If the primary client fails their obligations for the first time, that person's portion of benefit is reduced by half (50%) until they recomply, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed.
For more information on non-financial sanctions see:
- Non-financial sanctions
The young partner will have their in-hand allowance of up to $50 and any incentive payments suspended.
The couple can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled.
They continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment as they are still getting a qualifying benefit. Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during any non-entitlement period.
After 4 weeks
If the young partner has not recomplied within 4 weeks, they will have their portion of the benefit and their portion of Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support suspended. Their incentive payments and in-hand allowance will remain suspended.
Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or the payment is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.
## Grade 3 sanction
If both people in a couple fail their obligations for a third time:
- their benefit and any incentive payments are cancelled immediately
- Extra help, including the Winter Energy Payment is cancelled and
- subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks from the date of cancellation
The client and young partner may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity.
If the client or young partner does not start a 6-week approved activity, they must reapply at the end of their non-entitlement period to get a benefit.

chunks.title: Grade 1 sanction — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Grade 1 sanction
The young partner who has met their obligations will continue to have their portion (50%) of their assistance paid as usual through youth money management. This will include their incentive payments where these are payable.
If the primary client fails their obligations for the first time, that person's portion of benefit is reduced by half (25%) until they recomply, unless they have a non-financial sanction imposed.
For more information on non-financial sanctions see:
- Non-financial sanctions
The couple can continue to get any Accommodation Supplement and Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled. They can continue to get the full couple rate of the Winter Energy Payment.
Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period.
If the client does not recomply within 4 weeks, they will have their portion of the benefit suspended (along with their portion of any Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled). Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period.
Their benefit will remain suspended until they recomply or their portion of the benefit is automatically cancelled after 13 weeks.
## Grade 3 sanction
The young partner who has met their obligations is due their portion of the main benefit (including their incentive payments) paid as usual.
The young partner can also continue to get their portion of any Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support to which they are entitled. The young partner can get the full couple rate of Winter Energy Payment.
If the primary client fails their obligations for a third time:
- their portion of the benefit is cancelled immediately
- their portion of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support and the Winter Energy Payment is cancelled and
- the client subject to a non-entitlement period for 13 weeks from the date of cancellation
The client may get a provisional benefit if they start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities.
If the client does not start a 6-week approved activity or programme of activities, they may reapply at the end of their non-entitlement period to get a benefit.
Note Disability Allowance can continue to be paid during a non-entitlement period.

chunks.title: Court imposed conditions — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Court imposed conditions
This exemption may apply to partners with work or work preparation obligations.
A partner serving a sentence of home detention, or who has conditions and requirements of a court sentence or court order that limits their ability to meet all their obligations can be exempt from meeting some or all of their work or work preparation obligations.
This can be a full or partial exemption depending on the conditions imposed by the Courts.
This includes partners who:
- are former prisoners who are subject to probation or parole conditions which means that they cannot meet all their work obligations and
- have work obligations and are required as part of a sentence of the court or other court order to attend programmes or other activities, or have conditions imposed upon them (e.g. bail conditions) which limit their ability to meet all their work obligations
Home detainees or former prisoners are case managed by their probation officer. Part of this case management includes undertaking appropriate job search and activities to improve their prospects of obtaining paid employment.
In all cases, the case manager should contact the probation officer to facilitate any meetings.
Note this can be a full or partial exemption depending on the conditions imposed by the Courts.
## Proof
The partner must provide proof from the Ministry of Justice, the Department of Corrections or the Department of Courts stating that they:
- are serving a sentence of Home Detention or
- are subject to probation or parole conditions which limit their ability to meet all their work obligations or
- are required to attend programmes or other activities which limit their ability to meet all their work obligations or
- have conditions imposed (e.g. bail conditions) which limit their ability to meet all their work obligations and
- the length of time the partner should be exempt

chunks.title: Duration — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Duration
The duration of the exemption can be for up to 12 months or for a period determined by the court order or conditions placed on the young partner by the Courts, whichever is earliest.
