chunks.title: Well Child or Tamariki Ora services and checks — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Well Child or Tamariki Ora services and checks
Well Child/Tamariki Ora services are a screening, education and support service offered to all New Zealand children and their families or whānau from birth to 5 years.
The services assist and support families and whānau to improve and protect their children's health. They are provided free to all children under 5 years by registered nurses and community health workers with specific training in child health.
First time parents and families requiring extra support are offered additional visits. Some visits are carried out in the home and others in clinics or community facilities.
Different providers run the Well Child/Tamariki Ora services, including:
- Plunket
- Māori health providers
- Pacific Island health providers
- Public Health Services - for example, public health nurses, community nurses, community health workers, social workers.
## When do the checks happen?
The Well Child/Tamariki Ora schedule includes 12 health checks (visits/contacts) with 8 of these offered to children aged from, 4 - 6 weeks to 5 years.
Only the 8 core Well Child checks are required to meet this social obligation.

chunks.title: Work Ability Assessment — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Work Ability Assessment
A Work Ability Assessment is an independent assessment to identify what work a client can do, and the support and services they need to gain and retain work. The assessment must be undertaken by a suitably qualified registered health practitioner (such as a psychologist or occupational therapist), who is experienced in assisting people into work.
To be considered for a Work Ability Assessment a client must:
- be receiving a benefit and
- have a health condition or disability that stops them from working full-time and
- be actively looking for work or be preparing for work
MSD cannot require clients to participate in a Work Ability Assessment if they are receiving Supported Living Payment and:
- are terminally ill, or have little or no capacity for work, and their condition is deteriorating or unlikely to improve or
- have been given simplified access to the Supported Living Payment at application or
- are former Invalid's Benefit clients who have been identified as meeting a similar criteria as based on a current medical certificate (signed by a registered medical practitioner, nurse practitioner or psychologist) or designated health practitioner report
## Requirements
Before referring a client for a Work Ability Assessment, MSD must have:
- completed a Self-Assessment with the client and
- been working proactively and intensively with the client to move them into employment and
- completed a Structured Interview with the client and
- reviewed all relevant information held about the client
MSD should consider if:
- the client is progressing towards employment in line with the existing service plan and the information contained on their Work Capacity Medical Certificates
- previous supports and services have been effective
- more information is needed to ensure the client is matched to the appropriate employment support and services
Before a referral for a Work Ability Assessment can be made, MSD's Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor must review the information and documentation held about the client and consider their suitability for a Work Ability Assessment.
If the client is a suitable candidate the Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor will identify the information to be provided as part of the referral and determine the provider or assessor the client will be referred to.
If the client is not a suitable candidate the Regional Health Advisory or Regional Disability Advisor will recommend alternative options to help the client progress towards employment in line with the existing service plan.

chunks.title: Work ability assessment obligation — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Work ability assessment obligation
Clients getting Supported Living Payment have a work ability assessment obligation that requires them, when asked, to attend and participate in:
- Self-Assessments
- Structured Interview
- Work Ability Assessment
## Purpose of a work ability assessment
A work ability assessment will help show what work a person is capable of doing and what Work and Income can do to help a client find and stay in work.
A work ability assessment will help determine:
- the client's work ability
- what suitable work or work preparation activities are appropriate for the client
- what assistance, services or support Work and Income and/or other agencies should be providing
As a result of a work ability assessment a client's work obligations or benefit entitlement may change.
## Clients required to participate in a work ability assessment
Generally, only clients who have a health condition, injury or disability with some capacity to work will be required to participate in a work ability assessment.
## Clients not required to participate in a work ability assessment
You cannot require clients to participate in a work ability assessment if they are getting Supported Living Payment and:
- are terminally ill, or have little or no capacity for work, and their condition is deteriorating or is unlikely to improve or
- who have been given simplified access to the Supported Living Payment at application or
- are former Invalid's Benefit clients who have been identified as meeting a similar criteria as based on a current medical certificate or Designated Health Practitioner report

chunks.title: Work obligations - partners — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: Full-time work obligations apply to: - partners with no dependent children and - partners with a youngest dependent child aged 14 years or over Part-time work obligations apply to: - partners with a youngest dependent child aged between 3 and 13 years Partners with work obligations must: - be available for, and take reasonable steps to obtain, suitable employment - accept any offer of suitable employment, including temporary employment or seasonal employment Note suitable employment can include employment that contains and employment trial. - attend and participate in an interview for any opportunity of suitable employment to which the partner is referred - when required to attend and participate in any interview with Work and Income or on behalf of Work and Income - when required to undertake planning for employment - report to Work and Income on progress in meeting their work obligations as often as required and - when required by Work and Income, undertake any activity to improve their work readiness and employment prospects, including: any work assessmentany programme or seminarany work experience or work exploration activityany employment related trainingrehabilitation (but not medical treatment) - any work assessment - any programme or seminar - any work experience or work exploration activity - any employment related training - rehabilitation (but not medical treatment)

chunks.title: Suitable employment — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: Partners with full-time work obligations must be available for, and take reasonable steps to find, suitable employment of at least 30 hours or more per week. Partners with part-time work obligations must be available for, and take reasonable steps to find, suitable employment of at least 20 hours per week. However, if suitable employment is available for hours other than 20 or 30 hours per week (as applicable), the partner can be required to accept an offer of this job. Work obligations can be applied on any day of the week provided it is suitable for the partner's circumstances. To help you decide if the job is suitable for the partner see: - Suitable employment - Hours range for suitable employment

chunks.title: Failing to comply — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: If a partner does not meet their work obligations, without a good and sufficient reason, you should initiate an obligations failure. You should consider the partner's individual circumstances before referring them to a job or an activity, to ensure that they can realistically meet their obligations. For more information see: - Meeting job search requirements - Informing clients of their obligations - Setting appropriate activities for clients - Employment trial period of up to 90 days - Drug test obligations - Work ability assessment obligation - Work with contracted service provider obligation - Reporting progress - Rehabilitation - Exemptions for partners - Table of Exemptions - Obligations failures

chunks.title: Work or work preparation obligations — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Work or work preparation obligations
Primary clients receiving Supported Living Payment may have work preparation obligations where they have been assessed as having capacity to prepare for work.
For more information see:
- Assessing capacity for work preparation obligation - primary client
Partners of clients receiving Supported Living Payment have full-time or part-time work obligations or work preparation obligations depending on the age of their youngest child but may qualify for an exemption in certain circumstances.
## Full-time work obligations
Full-time work obligations apply to:
- partners with no children and
- partners with a youngest dependent child aged 14 years or over
Partners with full-time work obligations must be available for, and take reasonable steps to find suitable employment of at least 30 hours or more per week.
## Part-time work obligations
Part-time work obligations apply to:
- partners with a youngest dependent child aged between 3 and 13 years
Partners with part-time work obligations must be available for, and take reasonable steps to find suitable employment of at least 20 hours per week.
## Work preparation obligations
Work preparation obligations apply to:
- partners with a youngest dependent child aged under 3 years
Note that if the partner is receiving Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, these children are not considered dependent children for rates purposes but they are treated as dependent children for setting work or work preparation obligations.
## Partners aged 16 to 19 years old
Young partners (aged 16 to 19 years old) of clients receiving Supported Living Payment have youth activity obligations and not work or work preparation obligations if they are:
- aged 16 to 17 years old without dependent children or
- aged 16 to 19 years old with a dependent child or children and
- married to, or in a civil union or in a de facto relationship with a person receiving Supported Living Payment
For more information see:
- Partners with no children or youngest child 14+ years
- Partners with youngest child between 3 and 13 years
- Partners with youngest dependent child aged under 3 years

- Work preparation obligations - partners
- Work obligations - partners
- Youth activity obligations
- Rehabilitation
- Drug test obligations
- Work ability assessment obligation
- Work with contracted service provider obligation

chunks.title: Work preparation obligations do not apply - primary client — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Work preparation obligations do not apply - primary client
Work preparation obligations will not apply to clients receiving Supported Living Payment who do not have capacity to undertake them.
When considering a person's capacity you should consider:
- the information contained in any Work Ability Assessment or
- if the client has indicated they would like to plan for work
Note the work ability assessment obligation will not be applied to Supported Living Payment clients who have:
- a terminal illness or
- no or little capacity to work and their condition is deteriorating or is unlikely to improve
For more information see:
- Work ability assessment obligation

chunks.title: Work preparation obligations - partners — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Work preparation obligations - partners
A person with work preparation obligations must take all reasonable steps to prepare for employment. When considering what is reasonable you must consider what is practical for their individual circumstances.
In addition, partners with a youngest dependent child aged under 3 years must:
- when required to undertake planning for employment
- when required to report to Work and Income on progress in meeting their work preparation obligations as often as required
- when required to attend and participate in any interview with Work and Income or on behalf of Work and Income and
- when required by Work and Income, undertake any activity to improve their work readiness and employment prospects, including: any work assessmentany programme or seminarany work experience or work exploration activityany employment related trainingrehabilitation (but not medical treatment)an education programme
- any work assessment
- any programme or seminar
- any work experience or work exploration activity
- any employment related training
- rehabilitation (but not medical treatment)
- an education programme
Work preparation obligations can be applied on any day of the week provided it is suitable for the partner's circumstances.
If a partner does not meet their work preparation obligations, without a good and sufficient reason, you should initiate an obligations failure.
For more information see:
- Informing clients of their obligations
- Setting appropriate activities for clients
- Reporting progress
- Rehabilitation
- Exemptions for partners
- Table of Exemptions
- Obligations failures

chunks.title: Work preparation obligations - primary client — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Work preparation obligations - primary client
Work preparation obligations can be applied to clients receiving Supported Living Payment where they have been assessed as having the capacity to prepare for work.
This includes meeting any of the following:
- undertake planning for employment
- report to Work and Income on progress in meeting their work preparation obligations as often as required
- attend and participate in any interview with Work and Income or on behalf of Work and Income and
- where required, undertake any activity to improve their work readiness and employment prospects requested by Work and Income, including: any work assessmentany programme or seminarany work experience or work exploration activityany employment related trainingrehabilitation (but not medical treatment)an education programme
- any work assessment
- any programme or seminar
- any work experience or work exploration activity
- any employment related training
- rehabilitation (but not medical treatment)
- an education programme
A client cannot be required to meet the work preparation obligation to take all reasonable steps to prepare for employment.
For more information see:
- Assessing capacity for work preparation obligation - primary client
- Informing clients of their obligations
- Setting appropriate activities for clients
- Reporting progress
- Rehabilitation

chunks.title: Working overseas and paying New Zealand tax on earnings — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Working overseas and paying New Zealand tax on earnings
A client applying for Supported Living Payment can be considered resident and present in New Zealand during periods of overseas employment when their employer (or other relevant person):
- deducted PAYE or source deductions from their wages and
- paid the deducted amount to Inland Revenue New Zealand
The period overseas that the client was considered resident and present can be used towards the 2 years residence requirement for Supported Living Payment.
A partner or any dependent child who was with the client while they were working overseas can also be treated as resident and present in New Zealand for the same periods.
If the client has a child born outside of New Zealand during the period they were working overseas, the child is deemed to have been born in New Zealand.
The residential qualifications do not apply to people who are self-employed and working overseas.
Clients should provide evidence of the periods they were employed overseas, and PAYE or source deductions paid to Inland Revenue in New Zealand during these periods.
If the employer (or other relevant person) has deducted the tax but failed to pay it to Inland Revenue New Zealand and the client did not contribute to the employer's failure to pay the tax, the period of employment overseas can still be regarded as residence and present in New Zealand.
Note if any person leaves New Zealand while getting a benefit, and returns to take up ordinary residence in New Zealand at any time within 5 years, they are not required to meet the residential qualifications for the same benefit type.

chunks.title: Workplace/industry training — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Workplace/industry training
Workplace/industry training includes courses such as:
- Skills for Industry [no link find out why]
These courses are generally less than 13 weeks.
Young people will be meeting their obligations where they are undertaking programmes linked to the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF) credits.
For more information see:
- Approved training (young partners)

chunks.title: Would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability
This exemption may apply to partners with work obligations.
If a partner meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support on ground of a health condition, injury or disability, they can be exempt from meeting some or all of their work obligations until their capacity for work improves.
The partner must be limited in their capacity to work because of a health condition, injury or disability and, depending on whether they have part-time or full-time work obligations be:
- unable to look for part-time work of at least 15 hours per week or
- losing earnings because they are unable to work for at least 15 or 30 hours a week
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support
This is a partial exemption and the partner is able to:
- plan for employment and
- undertake certain work related activities
## Evidence
To support their exemption, the partner must provide a Work Capacity Medical Certificate that is completed by their registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist or midwife where relevant).
The information required on the medical certificate is:
- a diagnosis (what the illness, injury or disability is) and
- the impact of the condition on their ability to work and
- the likely duration of the impact and
- their capacity for work planning, training and part-time work and
- any other information that is required
## Duration
The period of an exemption for partners who are limited in their capacity to work because of a health condition, injury or disability is based on the next reassessment date recorded by their registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist, or midwife where relevant).
This exemption should then be reviewed.
At the review MSD should consider their circumstances and whether it is appropriate to extend the exemption. MSD can ask the partner to provide evidence of the reason for the exemption to be extended.

chunks.title: Would qualify for Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Would qualify for Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability
This exemption may apply to partners with work obligations.
If a partner meets the qualifications for Supported Living Payment on ground of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness, they can be exempt from meeting some or all of their work or work preparation obligations.
The partner must be:
- both permanently and severely restricted in their capacity for work because of a health condition, or injury or disability, from an accident, or condition they have had since birth or
- totally blind
Note totally blind and legally blind are not the same.
This can be a full or partial exemption depending on the whether the partner can plan for a return to work.
MSD should discuss with the partner whether they can still:
- plan for employment and
- undertake certain work related activities
If it is unclear whether a full or partial exemption should be granted, seek advice from the Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor.
Note in all cases MSD should consider the partner's eligibility for Supported Living Payment.
## Evidence
The partner must provide a Work Capacity Medical Certificate or medical information from a registered medical practitioner, nurse practitioner or psychologist stating:
- a diagnosis (what the illness, injury or disability is) and
- the impact of the condition on their ability to work and
- the likely duration of the impact and
- their capacity for work planning training and part-time work and
- any other information is required

chunks.title: Young partner (no dependent children) turns 18 years old — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: Generally, when a young partner with no dependent children turns 18 years old the youth activity obligations no longer apply. However, there are 2 situations when the obligations will continue to apply after they turn 18 years old. These are when a young partner: - is aged under 18 years when they first have youth activity obligations applied and must undertake Youth Activity obligations for a minimum of 6 months, even if they turn 18 years during this 6 month period - chooses to continue to have youth activity obligations so they can remain in education, training or work-based learning When a young partner reaches the age of 18 and has already had youth activity obligations for 6 months and does not choose to continue to have these obligations because they are not in education, training or work-based learning, the youth activity obligations no longer apply. Instead they will have the work obligations applicable to the main benefit.

chunks.title: Choose to have youth activity obligations past 18 years of age — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: Generally, when a young partner turns 18 years old the obligations for them to comply with Youth Activity obligations will no longer apply. However, to give a young partner a chance to complete the qualification they have started while having youth activity obligations, a young partner can choose to continue to have youth activity obligations and continue to participate in the Youth Service after they turn 18 if they remain in education, training, or work-based learning. Attending secondary school When a young partner reaches the age of 18 years and is attending secondary school they will continue to have youth activity obligations and continue to participate in the Youth Service until the following 31 March. For example, a young partner attending school who turns 18 years old in June will continue in the Youth Service until the following 31 March. Attending tertiary education, training or work-based learning When a young partner is attending tertiary education, training, or work-based learning and they turn 18 years old, they may continue to have youth activity obligations and continue to participate in the Youth Service until their course finishes, unless their course ends in December. If their course ends in December, they will continue to have youth activity obligations and participate in the Youth Service until 31 March the following year. Examples: - a young partner is part-way through a training course when they turn 18 years old. The training course finishes on 20 November. The young partner will be exited from the Youth Service on 21 November - a young partner is part-way through a training course when they turn 18 years old. The training course finishes on 20 December. The young partner will continue to have Youth Activity obligations and remain in the Youth Service until the following 31 March

chunks.title: Must have Youth Activity obligations for 6 months — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text: A young partner who is aged under 18 years when they first have Youth Activity obligations applied must undertake these obligations for a minimum of 6 months even if they turn 18 years old during this period. This ensures that the young partner is able to have a reasonable chance to move towards a qualification by participating in education, training or work-based learning and other youth activity obligations before they focus on obligations attached to other main benefits. For example, a young partner first has Youth Activity obligations applied at the age of 17 years and 8 months old. When they turn 18 years old they will need to continue to have these Youth Activity obligations and participate in the Youth Service for another 2 months to complete the 6 month minimum period. After this point, the youth activity obligations will no longer apply and instead they will have the work obligations applicable as the partner of a Supported Living Payment client (unless they choose to continue to have youth activity obligations because they are in education, training or work-based learning).

chunks.title: Young partner would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Young partner would qualify for Jobseeker Support - health condition, injury or disability
If a young partner meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability, they can be exempt from meeting some or all of their activity obligations until their capacity for education, training and work-based learning improves.
The young partner must be limited in their capacity to undertake activities because of a health condition, injury or disability.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support
If the young partner is partially exempt they are able to:
- plan for education, training or work-based learning and
- undertake other activities such as budgeting
## Evidence
To support their exemption, the young partner must provide a medical certificate completed and signed by a registered medical practitioner or nurse practitioner (or dentist, or midwife where relevant).
The information required on the medical certificate includes:
- a diagnosis (what the illness, disability or health condition is) and
- the impact of the condition on their ability to undertake activity obligations and
- the likely duration of the impact and
- their capacity for education, training and work-based learning and
- any other information that is required

chunks.title: Young partner would qualify Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Young partner would qualify Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability
If a young partner meets the qualifications for Supported Living Payment on the ground of a health condition, injury, disability or total blindness, they can be exempt from meeting some or all of their activity obligations.
The young partner must be:
- both permanently and severely restricted in their capacity for education, training and work-based learning because of health condition, or injury or disability from an accident, or condition they have had since birth or
- totally blind
Note totally blind and legally blind are not the same.
This can be a full or partial exemption depending on the whether the young partner can plan for a return to education, training or work-based learning.
MSD should discuss with the young partner whether they can still:
- plan for education, training or work-based learning and
- undertake other activities such as budgeting
If it is unclear whether a full or partial exemption should be granted, seek advice from the Regional Health Advisor or Regional Disability Advisor.
Note in all cases MSD should consider the young partner's eligibility for Supported Living Payment.
## Evidence
The young partner must provide either a medical certificate or medical information signed by a registered medical practitioner, nurse practitioner, or psychologist stating:
- a diagnosis (what the illness, injury or disability is) and
- the impact of the condition on their ability to undertake activities and
- the likely duration of the impact and
- their capacity for planning and undertaking activities part-time and
- any other information that is required

chunks.title: Youngest dependent child is aged under 12 months — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Youngest dependent child is aged under 12 months
Youth activity obligations apply from the time the benefit is first paid except where the young partner is caring for their youngest dependent child, and that child is aged under 12 months old.
In these cases, the obligation to be in or available for full-time education, training or work-based learning begins to apply on the earlier of:
- the day the child becomes 6 months old if there is a suitable place available for the young partner in a teen parent unit andMSD is satisfied that there are no special circumstances justifying the obligation starting at a later date
- if there is a suitable place available for the young partner in a teen parent unit and
- MSD is satisfied that there are no special circumstances justifying the obligation starting at a later date
or
- the day on which the child becomes 12 months old
For more information see:
- Deciding if suitable place at Teen Parent Unit available
- Special circumstances justifying delay in activity obligation
- Deciding education, training and work-based learning activities
- Parenting obligations
- Exemptions for young partners

chunks.title: Youth activity obligations — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Youth activity obligations
A young partner is subject to youth activity obligations and not to the work or work preparation obligations if they are:
- aged 16 or 17 years old without dependent children or
- aged 16 to 19 years old with a dependent child or children and
- married to, or in a civil union or in a de facto relationship with a person receiving Supported Living Payment
Note young partners may be able to get an exemption from some or all of their obligations where it is unreasonable to expect them to meet their obligations for a specified period.

chunks.title: Youth activity obligations failures — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## Youth activity obligations failures
If a young partner fails to comply with their youth activity obligations, an activity obligations failure needs to be considered.
The service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service:
- must to be satisfied that the young partner would have had no good and sufficient reason for their failure and
- if the young partner has no good and sufficient reason, recommend an activity obligations failure be imposed
The Youth Service Support Unit (YSSU):
- makes the decision to apply a sanction, based on the recommendation of the service provider or Work and Income 'in-house' service and
- initiates the activity obligations failure in the system
If it is decided that the young partner has failed their activity obligations, the YSSU will initiate an activity obligations failure. The young partner will then be notified by text message (where they have consented to be contacted in this way) or letter that:
- an obligations failure has occurred
- a sanction has been imposed and
- they have five working days to recomply before their payments are affected
All young people have a five working day notice period to dispute or recomply before the sanction is imposed. If a young person recomplies within the five working day notice period their benefit is not sanctioned but the activity obligations failure is recorded.
For more information see:

chunks.title: No longer subject to youth money management — main benefits > supported living payment
chunks.text:
## No longer subject to youth money management
A young partner aged 16 or 17 years (with no children) or 16 to 19 years (with dependent children) will not be subject to youth money management and will have their full payment paid directly to them when they have:
- demonstrated continued compliance with their obligations and been assessed as being financially competent or
- opted out of youth money management because they turned 18 years (for young partners without dependent children) and have chosen to stay in the Youth Service and complete their course of study, training or work-based learning
For more information see:
- Redirection for young partners
- In-hand allowance
- Incentive payments
- Payment process for a young partner
- Extra help and other payments
- Opting out of youth money management
- Earning the right to receive payment directly
- Continued compliance with their obligations
- Assessed as financially competent
- Returned to youth money management
- Method of payment
- Youth money management activity

chunks.title: Abbeyfield houses — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Abbeyfield houses
Abbeyfield is an incorporated, non-profit organisation that provides housing for older people.
An Abbeyfield house is styled as a large family home, where each of the eight to ten residents has a separate bedroom with ensuite facilities. A live-in housekeeper/cook prepares the main meals and cares generally for the residents.
A client living in an Abbeyfield house may receive the single living alone rate as long as they meet the definition of living alone and the Abbeyfield house meets the definition of a boarding house.
Abbeyfield residents may also receive an Accommodation Supplement provided they meet the usual criteria.
For more information see:
- Definition of living alone
- Definition of a boarding house

chunks.title: Age — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Age
A veteran must have reached the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation of 65, in order to have entitlement to a Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Amount of income exemption — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Amount of income exemption
When you have determined that a client is severely disabled you must then consider if they should have all or part of their income from employment disregarded for benefit purposes.
The amount of the income exemption depends on the client's individual circumstances after considering the guidelines - for severe disablement and should be:
- a reasonable amount as an incentive to recognise the personal effort that a severely disabled person has made to participate or continue in employment
- any additional costs that a severely disabled person has incurred to participate or continue in employment
- a reasonable amount to ensure that a severely disabled person is not disadvantaged by participating or continuing in employment
The client may be entitled to receive other types of assistance, for example Disability Allowance for transport costs to work or employment assistance.
Fully document your decision by recording the reasons and the amount of the exemption in the CMS note template, Special exemption for severe disablement.
Contact Helpline if you need help with the assessment.
For more information see:
- Extra help

chunks.title: Bank account — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Bank account
Unless there are special circumstances, it is a condition of Veteran's Pension that the client provides or opens a bank account or membership to a credit union to receive their Veteran's Pension payment.
## Bank
An appropriate bank is:
- a private savings bank, a trustee savings bank or The Co-operative Bank or
- a registered bank which on the 31st March 1987 was a trading bank or
- any other registered bank or a building society approved by the Minister after consultation with the Minister of Finance
For more information see:
- Processing standards Bank account [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Boarding houses — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Boarding houses
Clients living alone in a room in a boarding house can receive the single living alone rate, as long as all other qualifications are met.
This can include houses that are styled as a large family home where the residents have a separate bedroom along with facilities for communal use by all the other residents, such as Abbeyfield Houses or some Selwyn Foundation community houses.
If you are unsure whether the premises, meets the definition of a boarding house, contact Helpline for advice.
For more information see:
- Definition of a boarding house
- Abbeyfield houses
- Assessing single living alone prior to 2 September 2013

chunks.title: Boats — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Boats
Clients, who are living alone on a boat or craft moored within New Zealand, can receive single living alone rate as long as all other qualifications are met. In this situation, New Zealand includes:
- the territorial sea around New Zealand and
- lakes, rivers, estuaries within New Zealand
The boat does not have to remain in the same location.

chunks.title: Caravan parks and motor camps — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Caravan parks and motor camps
A client living alone in a caravan park, motor camp or camping ground maybe eligible for a single living alone rate of Veteran's Pension.
This accommodation include cabins, flats and caravans. The unit of accommodation does not have to be self-contained; the client can share facilities.

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
Clients getting Veteran's Pension in their own right can be absent from New Zealand and continue getting their payments for up to 26 weeks.
If the client is overseas for more than 30 weeks they do not qualify for Veteran's Pension from when they left New Zealand.
However, they may qualify for their payments if the client's return to New Zealand is delayed due to circumstances beyond the client's control that they could not have expected before departure.
For grandparented couples getting the non-qualified rate of Veteran's Pension, the grandparenting ends if the qualified partner is absent from New Zealand and they do not qualify for payment during the period of absence or any part of the absence.
The client must remain ordinarily resident during any absence.
For more information see:
- Effect of absence overseas on grandparented clients
- When grandparenting ends
Clients may continue getting payments for a longer period if the reason they are absent overseas is for:
- Overseas medical treatment
- Humanitarian work
## Single living alone rate
The single living alone rate can keep being paid for absences overseas of up to 26 weeks provided the client still qualifies.
## Extra help
Clients absent from New Zealand can keep getting their ongoing Extra help payments for 28 days.
Extra help cannot continue for more than 28 days when the client is absent from New Zealand. See 'Absence from New Zealand' in the relevant Extra help.

chunks.title: 26 weeks or less — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## 26 weeks or less
The absence will not have effected payments.
## More than 30 weeks
If the client was overseas for 30 weeks or more there is no qualification from when the client left New Zealand unless the client's return to New Zealand was delayed due to circumstances beyond the client's control that could not have been foreseen before departure.
If the qualified client of a grandparented non-qualified couple is absent for more than 26 weeks the grandparented non-qualified partner rate will end. If the qualifiedclientis unavoidably delayed but entitled to payment for the first 26 weeks of their absence the grandparented rate for their partner will end from the beginning of the 27th week of absence.

chunks.title: Advises more than 14 days after the event — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Advises more than 14 days after the event
Clients have an obligation to advise Senior Services of any changes that may affect the rate of payment of Veterans Pension. It is expected that they will do so within a reasonable period. As a guideline, a reasonable period is considered to be within 14 days.
When a client advises of a change in living situation more than 14 days after the event you should generally reduce Veterans Pension from the actual date of the change in living situation and establish an overpayment where appropriate.
## Good and sufficient reason
Where there is a good and sufficient reason (for example, bereavement or illness) for the client not advising Senior Services of a change in living situation within 14 days you may reduce Veterans Pension from the first available date.
## False or misleading information
If the client gives false or misleading information you must review Veteran's Pension from the actual date of the change in living situation and establish an overpayment where appropriate.

chunks.title: Annual income due paid assessment over 27 September 2010 period — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Annual income due paid assessment over 27 September 2010 period
When completing a due paid assessment of Veterans Pension over the 27 September 2010 period you need to:
1. Calculate the income deduction for the weeks prior to 27 September 2010.
2. Calculate the income deduction for the weeks from 27 September 2010.
3. Add the two deductions from step 1 and 2 together to get the annual income deduction.
The income to be charged for each of these periods must be totalled and compared with actual income for the year to establish whether an underpayment or overpayment has occurred.
## Annual income prior to 27 September 2010
Prior to 27 September 2010:
- income less than $4,160 gross per year will not affect their benefit
- income over $4,160 gross per year reduced benefit by 70 cents for every $1.00 of income
For more information see:
- Example of due paid assessment over 27 September 2010 period
- Charging income

chunks.title: Assessing single living alone before September 2013 — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Assessing single living alone before September 2013
Living Alone Payment for the period 24 September 2007 to 1 September 2013 may be backdated to 24 September 2007 where:
- the client has made contact with MSD but did not complete an application and there was good and sufficient reason why an application was not completed, the living alone rate may be backdated to the date of first contact
- the client completed an application form for a benefit or other form of assistance it may be considered as an application for the single living alone rate of payment and may be backdated to the date of application

chunks.title: Avoiding a debt — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Avoiding a debt
When a single client with no dependent children dies, payment generally stops from the day after the date of death. You must take all possible steps to stop payments from this date.
When payment cannot be stopped from the day after the date of death there is discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days after the date of death. You can use this discretion to stop payment from the first available date, that is, the earliest date that you can stop payments from so that no overpayment is established.
If the period between the date of death and the first available date to cancel payment from (to avoid creating a debt) is more than 28 days, you will have to establish an overpayment from the 29th day after death.
When there has been a deliberate intent to delay advising Work and Income of the client's death you should stop payment from the day after the date of death and establish an overpayment.
Note under no circumstances can payment continue for more than 28 days after the date of death.
## SWIFTT
Cancel Veterans Pension payments from the earliest possible date (but not more than 28 days after the date of death) in SBFTZ.
The date of death entered in CMS must be the client's actual date of death. You must make full notes in CMS of your actions.
Wherever possible you should enter the next of kin or the executor of the deceased's estate on SWIFTT.
For more information see:
- Terminal benefit for a single client

chunks.title: Calculating the period of absence — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Calculating the period of absence
In all cases, when assessing the period of absence does not include:
- the date of departure from New Zealand and
- the date of return to New Zealand
As Veterans Pension payments do not cover any specific period, you must look at the pay days that fall within the 26 weeks when confirming payment.
For more information see:
- Departure from New Zealand
- Effect of absence overseas on grandparented clients
- Return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Change in living situation — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Change in living situation
MSD should review the rate of payment of Veterans Pension whenever there is a change in the clients living situation such as:
- change in relationship status (such as getting married, starting or ending a de facto relationship or a civil union)
- death of a partner
- partner enters long term residential care or hospital
- starts or stops living alone
- has a visitor who stays for more than 13 weeks in any 26 week period
- change in the number of children supported (child comes into or leaves their care)

chunks.title: Change of address — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Change of address
When a client advises that they have changed their address it is important to check that the move does not affect their entitlement to Veterans Pension.
If the client is receiving Extra Help this will need to be reviewed to take into account their new costs.
If the client has a portion of their benefit paid to Kāinga Ora or Te Puni Kokiri this may need to be changed or cancelled.
The change of address may also indicate a change in the client's circumstances.
Examples of changes that may affect entitlement are:
- client or partner commences or ceases employment (grandparented non-qualified partner included)
- change of relationship status
- dependent children who have come into or left their care

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client must advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Veteran's Pension or the rate payable.
MSD may also review the Veteran's Pension at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment (if applicable). Reviews for Veteran's Pension are done on a case-by-case basis.
## Mandatory Reviews for Accommodation Supplement and Disability Allowance
Veteran's Pension clients getting Disability Allowance or Accommodation Supplement will have a Mandatory Review for this assistance only.
MSD must complete a Mandatory Review within 52 weeks of the commencement date for Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance, or 52-weeks from the date their last Mandatory Review was completed.
There is no Mandatory Review of the Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Client becomes sick — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Client becomes sick
If a Veterans Pension client or grandparented non qualified partner becomes sick, injured or disabled they can continue to receive Veterans Pension. Transferring the client (or partner) to another benefit would usually financially disadvantage them.
Veterans Pension clients are entitled to the full rate of Veterans Pension if they are hospitalised.
If the partner of a Veterans Pension client is admitted to hospital their rate of payment is reduced if the veteran has a War Disablement Pension rating of less than 70%, or has a Whole Body Impairment rating of less than 52%.
## Exception
Where a grandparented non qualified partner cannot work due to health condition, injury or disability they may qualify for Jobseeker Support or Supported Living Payment.
Due to the different income reductions and exemptions that apply it may mean the client and partner are financially better off if the:
- client receives the married or civil union person rate of Veterans Pension and
- partner receives Jobseeker Support or Supported Living Payment at the half married or civil union rate
You will need to advise the client and partner of:
- benefit rates
- the effect of income (income reduction and any exemptions) and
- benefit obligations
The client and partner must make the final decision on which benefit they receive after being given all relevant information.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support
- Supported Living Payment
- Payment
- Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Surviving partner or dependent child — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Surviving partner or dependent child
When a client dies (and there is a surviving partner or dependent child) before a decision is made on an application or review for Veterans Pension you can continue the application or review process as if the client had not died.
## Funeral Grant
In situations when the decision to grant or review Veterans Pension is made after the date of death of the client, you decide any Funeral Grant as if the deceased client were getting Veterans Pension.

chunks.title: Client donates a kidney or liver tissue — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Client donates a kidney or liver tissue
Clients getting Veteran's Pension can keep getting their payments if they are donating a kidney or liver tissue.

chunks.title: Client or partner in prison — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Client or partner in prison
There is discretion to continue payments to Veteran's Pension for clients in prison, for 2 instalments following imprisonment.
There is further discretion to continue payments beyond the initial 2 instalments where the Ministry of Social Development can pay all or part of the Veteran's Pension to:
- the partner of the person in prison, on remand or an escapee or
- any person responsible for the spouse or partner or any dependent children of the person in prison or
- to the client in prison, or on remand beyond the 2 instalments that have already been paid
A decision on making payment beyond the date of imprisonment must consider the couples’ full circumstances.
## Grandparented non qualified partner included
When a client is imprisoned and has a grandparented non qualified partner included in their Veteran's Pension, the Veterans Pension will generally need to be cancelled from the day following imprisonment to enable the partner to get a benefit in their own right.
However, there is discretion to continue payment of the client's Veterans Pension beyond the date of imprisonment.
Note if the grandparented non-qualified partner rate ends, the qualifying partner cannot get it again.
## Partner qualifies for Veterans Pension
When a client is imprisoned and has a partner who qualifies for Veterans Pension in their own right, the client's Veterans Pension will generally be stopped from the day following imprisonment.
However, there is discretion to continue payment of the client's Veterans Pension beyond the date of imprisonment.

chunks.title: Cost of funeral — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Cost of funeral
The person responsible for the cost of the funeral is able to receive assistance from Veterans Affairs New Zealand (VANZ).
If Veterans Affairs New Zealand have already assisted with the funeral expenses there is no entitlement to a Funeral Grant as well.
If Work and Income grants an application for Funeral Grant before a request is made to Veterans Affairs New Zealand. VANZ may pay a top-up in addition to the Funeral Grant.
The combined amount of top-up and Funeral Grant must not be more than the maximum amount paid by Veterans Affairs New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Funeral Grant

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Veteran's Pension when the child turns 18 during the terminal benefit period.

chunks.title: Death of a client with a partner or child — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: Veteran's Pension can continue to be paid for 28 days after the death of a client when there is a surviving partner or child, and the surviving partner is not entitled to a survivor's grant from ACC. Veteran's Pension can also continue to be paid for 28 days after the death of a single client who is a: - liable person and paying Child Support Payments or - caregiver receiving Unsupported Child's Benefit or Orphan's Benefit Continuing payments after the date of death is known as a terminal benefit. When the benefit is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person and the surviving person's portion of the benefit continues to be paid. The total benefit, including the surviving person's portion, plus any ongoing extra help continues for 28 days.

chunks.title: Surviving partner will get more money on other assistance — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: Sometimes the surviving partner or the caregiver of the child would get more money (based on their new circumstances) on: - a new main benefit or - their existing benefit or pension at a higher rate instead of getting their portion of their current assistance for 28 days.

chunks.title: New benefit paid at a higher rate — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: If the surviving person's situation is reviewed and they qualify for a new benefit at a higher rate, they may be granted the new benefit instead of terminal benefit from the day after their partner's death. If the deceased person qualified for a terminal benefit, their portion will continue to be paid.

chunks.title: Current benefit paid at a higher rate — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: If the surviving person's Veteran's Pension or main benefit is reviewed and they qualify for a higher rate, their rate increases from the day after their partner's death. MSD pays this instead of their portion of terminal benefit as they will get more money. If the deceased person qualified for a terminal benefit, their portion will continue to be paid.

chunks.title: Changing benefits or the benefit rate — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: The effect the client's death has on the surviving partner's payments will depend on whether the surviving partner: - qualifies in their own right for Veteran's Pension or - is included in Veteran's Pension as a grandparented non-qualified partner If the surviving partner is a grandparented non-qualified partner they will need to apply for a main benefit as they will not qualify for the grandparented non-qualified rate of Veteran's Pension. If the surviving partner gets a main benefit the rate and type of benefit should be reviewed to check they are getting the correct benefit and rate of payment.

chunks.title: Surviving person is entitled to survivor's grant from ACC — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: When the death of the person was the result of an accident, entitlement to a survivor's grant from ACC needs to be decided before terminal benefit can be paid. If the surviving person or child is entitled to a survivor's grant from ACC there is no entitlement to terminal benefit. If the Veteran's Pension payments have continued after the date of death, an overpayment is established and the debt should be recovered from the estate.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Veteran's Pension when the child turns 18 during the 28-day continuation of payment.

chunks.title: Death of a single client — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Death of a single client
When a single client (with no children) dies, payment generally stops from the day after the date of death, but there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days.
Payment should stop from the first available date if we have been notified within 28 days of the date of death. This will avoid creating a debt.
Where there are other circumstances that justify payment of terminal benefit, payment should continue for the full 28 days after death.
For more information see:
- Avoiding a debt
- Terminal benefit for a single client
Note a single client who is a liable person and paying Child Support payments, or a caregiver getting Unsupported Childs Benefit or Orphans Benefit is regarded as having children.

chunks.title: Deciding if grandparented non-qualified partner would be better off getting terminal benefit or another benefit — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Deciding if grandparented non-qualified partner would be better off getting terminal benefit or another benefit
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children.
When Veteran's Pension is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person and the surviving person's portion of the Veteran's Pension should be paid if it is decided that terminal benefit is the best option for the surviving partner. Payment is the total Veteran's Pension including any ongoing Extra help. It does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit.
Sometimes the surviving person or the caregiver of the child would get more money (based on their new circumstances) on a new benefit instead of getting their portion of their current assistance for 28 days.
Compare the surviving person's potential new benefit and any ongoing Extra help (from the date after death) against the surviving person's portion of benefit and ongoing Extra help they were getting before their partner's death.
Generally, a client does not qualify for Veteran's Pension in their own right would get more money by getting terminal benefit.

chunks.title: Decision guidelines - married, civil union or de facto clients — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines - married, civil union or de facto clients
While Veteran's Pension should generally be stopped when the qualifying client is imprisoned, there is discretion for payment to be continued to the qualifying client in prison or in full or part to the partner not in prison.
This discretion allows payment of all or part of the Veteran's Pension to the partner.
If you feel that payment should be continued, and paid to the partner, this should generally be at the half married, civil union or de facto rate. However, you can pay the full married, civil union or de facto rate if you feel this is warranted after having regard to the particular circumstances of the client and their partner.
To help you decide whether it is reasonable to pay the Veteran's Pension to the client in prison or to the partner of client in prison consider the following:
- has the period in prison already passed?
- is the client due to be released from prison shortly?
- is the likely period in prison less than 6 months?
- does the partner qualify for a statutory benefit in their own right?
- do they intend to live together when the partner is released?
- has the partner in prison applied for Home Detention?
- are there exceptional circumstances that warrant paying the full married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit to the partner who is not in prison?
- are there exceptional circumstances to treat the partner in the community as single (eg the client does not intend resuming the relationship with their partner when they are released or has decided to end the relationship due to the imprisonment)?Note imprisonment can affect the grandparenting status of non-qualified partner couples
- For further help you can contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.

chunks.title: Departure from New Zealand — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Departure from New Zealand
A client should advise the Ministry of any change of circumstances that may affect the payment of their Veterans Pension, for example, if they are going to be absent from New Zealand.
When a client or their partner contacts you to advise that they intend travelling overseas you need to obtain the following information:
- date of departure (flight numbers if possible)
- date of return (flight numbers if possible)
Note you need to make sure that you have told the client about their portability options and their need to return to New Zealand within 26 weeks and if they do not return within 30 weeks they may be overpaid from the day after they left New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Permanent absence
- Temporary absence

chunks.title: Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital
When a Veterans Pension client has been remanded in custody, or is serving a term of imprisonment, is detained in or transferred to a psychiatric hospital they can receive Veterans Pension.
This will also apply to people who turn 65 while in prison and who are then transferred to a psychiatric hospital provided they meet the eligibility criteria.
People who are aged 65 or over and are not eligible for Veterans Pension or New Zealand Superannuation may be able to receive Emergency Benefit.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Person serving their sentence of imprisonment in a psychiatric hospital
Clients remanded in custody or serving a term of imprisonment who are temporarily hospitalised for treatment of an injury or health condition are still considered to be in prison and the Department of Corrections will meet their costs. An Emergency Benefit or any other financial assistance cannot be paid.
## Rate of payment
Veterans Pension is not reduced on admission to a psychiatric hospital and continues to be paid at the full rate.

chunks.title: Effective date of review due to change in relationship — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: Veteran's Pension should be reviewed when the client: - marries, starts a de facto relationship or enters a civil union - reconciles with a former partner - separates - qualified partner elects to cancel the grandparented non-qualified partner rate - has a partner who enters long-term residential care or - has a partner who dies

chunks.title: Couple rate of payment when client gets a partner or reconciles — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: The rate of Veteran's Pension should be changed to the couple rate from the first available date if the client has advised the change in circumstances within a reasonable time (generally within 14 days). You should only establish an overpayment if: - the client has failed to advise of a change in living situation within 14 days of the event or - they have deliberately misled the Ministry of Social Development Note if the couple getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate of Veteran's Pension separate, the grandparented non-qualified parter rate is cancelled (if they then reconcile again, they won't be able to be included again). The non-qualified partner will be able to apply for a main benefit relevant to their circumstances.

chunks.title: Single sharing accommodation rate of payment when the client becomes single — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: The single sharing accommodation rate of Veteran's Pension can be paid from the: - day after the client separates or - day that their partner enters long-term residential care (even when there is no change in their relationship status) If the relationship has ended, the partner who does not qualify for Veteran's Pension in their own right, will need to test their eligibility to other assistance.

chunks.title: Single living alone rate of payment when the client becomes single — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: When the client meets the definition of living alone, the single living alone rate of Veteran's Pension can be paid from the: - date the client meets the definition of living alone - day that their partner enters long-term residential care (though there is no change in the relationship status) - day after the relationship ends - day after their partner died or - 2 September 2013 whichever is the later.

chunks.title: Exception when partner died before 2 September 2013 — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: If the client was living alone before 2 September 2013 as their partner died and they contacted the Ministry of Social Development within 28 days from the date of death, the client may be able to get the Living Alone Payment from the day after the date of death. The client will need to complete a Living Alone Payment application form. If the application for Living Alone Payment is received more than 28 days following the partners death, or no application is received, the client will be paid the single living alone rate from: - the date the client meets the definition of living alone or - 2 September 2013 whichever is the later.

chunks.title: Example 1 — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: A client receiving Veterans Pension has a grandparented non-qualified partner who works for 12 hours each week and earns $13 per hour ($156 per week). Their annual income year began on 5 July 2010 and ended on 4 July 2011. 1. Calculate the weeks prior to 27 September 2010 (12 weeks). Client's annual gross income ($156 x 12 weeks) $1,872 Less income allowed before benefit is affected - $80.00 per week $1,872 - $960 ($80 x 12 weeks) $912 Equals annual income that will reduce benefit payment(income over $4,160) $912 Annual reduction in benefit rate: Income over $4,160 = 70% of every $1 (70% of $912) $912 x 0.70 = $638.40 Reduction in benefit rate $638.40 2 Calculate the weeks from 27 September 2010 (40 weeks). Client's annual gross income ($156.00 x 40 weeks) $6,240 Less income allowed before benefit is affected - $100 per week $6,240 - $4,000 ($100 x 40 weeks) $2,240 Equals annual income that will reduce benefit payment(income over $5,200) $2,240 Annual reduction in benefit rate: Income over $5,200 = 70% of every $1 (70% of $2,240) $2,240 x 0.7 = $1,568 Reduction in benefit rate $1,568 3. Add the Reduction in benefit rate from steps 1 and 2 to get the total annual reduction in benefit. $638.40 + $1,568 = $2,206.40

chunks.title: Example 2 — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: A client receiving Veterans Pension has a grandparented non-qualified partner who is self-employed and earns $14,500. Their annual income year began on 9 August 2010 and ended on 7 August 2011. 1. Calculate the weeks prior to 27 September 2010 (7 weeks). Clients annual gross income($14,500 divided by 52 x 7 weeks) $1,951.92 Less income allowed before benefit is affected - $80 per week ($4,160 annually) $1,951.92 - $560 ($80 x 7 weeks = $560) $1,391.92 Equals annual income that will reduce benefit payment(income over $4,160) $1,391.00 Annual reduction in benefit rate: Income over $4,160 = 70% of every $1 (70% of $1,391) $1,391 x 0.7 = $973.70 Reduction in benefit rate $973.70 2. Calculate the weeks from 27 September 2010 (45 weeks) Clients annual gross income($14,500 divided by 52 x 45 weeks) $12,548.08 Less income allowed before benefit is affected - $100 per week $12,548.08 - $4,500 ($100 x 45 weeks) $8,048.08 Equals annual income that will reduce benefit payment (income over $5,200) $8,048.00 Annual reduction in benefit rate: Income over $5,200 = 70% of every $1 (70% of $8,048) $8,048 x 0.7 = $5,633.60 Reduction in benefit rate $5,633.60 3. Add the Reduction in benefit rate from steps 1 and 2 to get the total annual reduction in benefit. $973.70 + $5,633.60 = $6,607.30

chunks.title: Client does not respond — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Client does not respond
If the client fails to make contact, the Integrity Intervention Centre will suspend the Veterans Pension from the first available date after the 10 working days have lapsed. Notes are added in CMS stating that the client needs to confirm their date of return to New Zealand before their Veterans Pension can be resumed.
If the client does not make contact within 2 pay cycles, the Integrity Intervention Centre will establish an overpayment from the day after the departure date.
## Client makes contact before Veterans Pension suspended
If a client contacts the Ministry when they received the first letter, that is, before the Veterans Pension is suspended, take the following action:
- confirm the date they returned to New Zealand
- make full notes in CMS to prevent the benefit being suspended at a later date by the Integrity Intervention Centre
- remind your client of their obligation to tell the Ministry of any change in their circumstances that may affect their Veterans Pension payments
- a grandparented non-qualified couple must be informed that their grandparented non-qualified partner rate will end if the qualified partner is not entitled to payment for the period absence or any part of the absence.
## Client makes contact after Veterans Pension suspended
If a client contacts after their Veterans Pension has been suspended it will also mean that a debt has been established by the Integrity Intervention Centre, from the day after the client left New Zealand up to the date their payments were suspended.
If the overpayment period is incorrect, ask your client the following information and forward it to the Integrity Intervention Centre:
- verification of travel dates, for example, using boarding passes, tickets etc
- any other relevant information
The Integrity Intervention Centre will reassess the overpayment if there is more information which suggest the overpayment is incorrect.
Note clients may be asked to provide proof of the circumstances of their absence.
If you need any help contact the Integrity Intervention Centre.

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualified partner becomes sick — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Grandparented non-qualified partner becomes sick
When a grandparented non qualified partner becomes sick, injured or disabled they can continue to receive Veterans Pension. Transferring the client (or partner) to another benefit would usually financially disadvantage them.
Veterans Pension clients are entitled to the full rate of Veterans Pension if they are hospitalised.
If the partner of a Veterans Pension client is admitted to hospital their rate of payment is reduced if the veteran has a War Disablement Pension rating of less than 70%, or has a Whole Body Impairment rating of less than 52%.

chunks.title: Home detention — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Home detention
A client may be in prison for a short time before being released on home detention.
Note Veterans Pension does not have an initial stand-down.
Where the partner of a person in prison has been receiving a benefit, this will need to be reviewed from the date of release.

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a veteran is admitted to hospital, their Veteran's Pension continues at the full rate and is not reduced after they have been in hospital for more than 13 weeks. This also applies to the partner of a veteran who is included as a grandparented non-qualified partner.
Note the partner of a veteran cannot have their payments increased or get Special Disability Allowance when the veteran is hospitalised.
## Partner's main benefit or New Zealand Superannuation is reduced
The partner of a veteran who is getting a main benefit (except Young Parent Payment) or New Zealand Superannuation will have their benefit or pension reduced to the hospital rate if they are in hospital for more than 13 weeks. If the veteran is also in hospital, their Veteran's Pension will continue at the full rate.
If the veteran is not in hospital, their Veteran's Pension must be increased by the difference between the maximum half married rate and the maximum single or single living alone rate of Veteran's Pension. Special Disability Allowance must also be paid.
Note if the hospitalised partner's benefit or pension is increased above the hospital rate, the rate paid to the veteran must be adjusted so the total amount paid to the couple does not exceed the maximum rate the couple would have been paid if one partner wasn't hospitalised.
## Special Disability Allowance
Special Disability Allowance is paid to a client when their partner is in hospital and reduced to the hospital rate. Special Disability Allowance helps the client in the community with the extra costs of their partner's hospitalisation, eg travel costs to visit them in hospital.
Note that Special Disability Allowance is:
- granted without the client having to apply
- paid separately from Disability Allowance and
- not income or asset tested
Special Disability Allowance can start from the date the client in the community starts getting a higher rate of Veteran's Pension, and their partner starts getting a hospital rate of benefit or pension.

chunks.title: Humanitarian work — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Humanitarian work
A client can receive payment while overseas if they are undertaking full-time voluntary and unpaid humanitarian work for a recognised aid agency, and
- the absence is not more than 156 weeks
- the work the client has been engaged in has not deprived another person of paid employment and
- the client has remained ordinarily resident in New Zealand during this time
If all the conditions are not met the usual absence overseas conditions apply.
If the client is overseas for more than 156 weeks, payments must stop from the day after departure from New Zealand.
## Recognised aid agency
A recognised aid agency is an organisation that has as its principal function 'the giving of aid and assistance to less advantaged communities in one or more other countries' or similar. Aid agencies would include (but are not limited to) organisations such as:
- Red Cross
- United Nations Volunteers
- Volunteer Services Abroad and
- World Vision
Whether an aid agency meets the criteria above, is determined by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. If you need assistance deciding if the agency is a "recognised aid agency" please contact Helpline
## Partners
Payment can continue up to 156 weeks for the partner of a married, civil union or de facto superannuitant if they are also undertaking humanitarian work.
If the partner is absent from New Zealand and not undertaking humanitarian work, they can only receive payment for up to 26 weeks, provided they return to New Zealand within 30 weeks.
## Advice of departure
When you have determined that payment can continue for up to 156 weeks you must make full notes in CMS.
For more information see:
- Single living alone rate and absence from New Zealand

chunks.title: Imprisonment — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
Generally, when a Veteran's Pension client is imprisoned or detained in custody, they are no longer entitled to get the Veteran's Pension.
Veterans Pension should stop from the day following the date of imprisonment. However, there is discretion to continue 2 payments following imprisonment.
Further ongoing payments for the period of imprisonment are also discretionary.
MSD must decide whether to suspend or cancel the benefit after considering the likely period in prison and whether the client has a partner and or dependent children.
In some circumstances Veteran's Pension can continue when the client is imprisoned.

chunks.title: Inland Revenue deduction notices — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
Inland Revenue may request that a client's unpaid taxes be directly deducted from their benefit payments.
All Inland Revenue deduction notices are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
The instructions on the deduction notice are to deduct the lowest of either:
- 10% of the total debt which Inland Revenue specify in the notice, on a weekly basis or
- 20% of the client's gross earnings on a weekly basis
Where there are insufficient funds to cover the deduction, Work and Income must advise Inland Revenue immediately that the deduction will not start or will start at a reduced rate.
Inland Revenue deduction notices for unpaid taxes have a lower priority than Child Support deductions.
For more information see:
- Priority for deductions
- Inland revenue deductions

chunks.title: Tax — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Tax
Veterans Pension and Veteran's Pension is part of a person's taxable income and must be taken into account when a person is calculating their tax rate.
Tax deductions are made in line with the tax code entered in the system and are the first priority for deductions.
For more information see:
- Tax codes
## Student Loan repayments
Veterans Pension clients with a Student Loan must use a tax code with the Student Loan ("SL") repayment code.
This will ensure that Student Loan repayments are deducted every pay period if required. Student loan repayments are part of a person's tax liability and are first priority for deductions.
For more information see:
- Student Loan repayments
## Inland Revenue deduction notices
These are notices that Inland Revenue issue when a person has a tax debt. They are separate from and additional to their current tax liability, and are second priority deductions.
For more information see:
- Inland Revenue deduction notices
Also see:
