- Priority for deductions

chunks.title: Lump sum payment on death — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Lump sum payment on death
When a veteran with a partner or a dependent child dies, the surviving family may be entitled to a lump sum payment on death.
The lump sum payment on death is made to assist with funeral costs. It is paid separately from any payment for Funeral Expenses the client may also be entitled to under the Veterans' Support Act 2014.
When a lump sum payment is made on death for a Veterans Pension client, there is no entitlement to a Funeral Grant under the Social Security Act 2018.
Terminal benefit is deducted from the lump sum payment.
There are 3 different types of lump sum on death payments and they are all non-taxable:
- death of a veteran who was getting a War Veterans Allowance before 1 April 1990 (a World War I veteran)
- death of any other veteran
- death of any veteran's partner
If the veteran had less than 52% disablement pension under the Veterans' Support Act 2014 or less than 70% war disablement pension under the War Pensions Act 1954 their partner or spouse is not entitled to a lump sum on death payment.
The lump sum payment is not payable when there is no surviving partner or dependent children.

chunks.title: Ongoing assistance for dependent children — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Ongoing assistance for dependent children
When a surviving dependent child is to be cared for by a person other than a parent, the caregiver may be able to receive an Orphan's Benefit or an Unsupported Child's Benefit.
The surviving dependent children of a veteran may qualify for a Children's Pension from Veteran's Affairs New Zealand. Check whether their caregiver has made contact with Veteran's Affairs.

chunks.title: Ongoing assistance for surviving partner — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: The effect the client's death will have on the surviving partner's payments will depend on whether the surviving partner is: - qualified in their own right or - a grandparented non qualified partner

chunks.title: Qualified in own right — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: When the surviving partner qualifies for Veteran's Pension in their own right, they can receive the single sharing accommodation rate or the single living alone rate from the day after their partner's death. Any Extra help should then be adjusted to the appropriate single rate. The rate of payment will depend on whether they: - are sharing accommodation with any person aged 18 years or over who is not a dependent child, or a visitor who stays less than 13 weeks in any 26 week period or - meet all the qualifications for the single living alone rate The surviving partner may also qualify for a pension from New Zealand Veterans' Affairs if the veteran's death was service related and they were getting a war disablement pension. This may affect any Extra help they receive. For more information see: - Single clients - Single living alone rate - Effective date of review due to change in relationship Note when the surviving client qualifies for Veteran's Pension in their own right and receives the single sharing accommodation or single living alone rate from the day after their partner's death, the deceased client is paid the payments they were getting at the date of their death. This includes if they were being paid the full amount of Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Winter Energy Payment for the couple.

chunks.title: Grandparented non qualified partner with no dependent children — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: When there are no dependent children, the surviving grandparented non qualified partner must apply for an appropriate benefit, in their own right. The surviving partner may be granted a new benefit (instead of terminal benefit) from the day after their partner's death if they will get more money.

chunks.title: Grandparented non qualified partner with dependent children — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: When a qualifying Veteran's Pension client dies and the surviving partner has a dependent child, they may be able to receive Sole Parent Support or Jobseeker Support, depending on the age of their youngest dependent child. The surviving partner or dependent children of a veteran may qualify for pensions from New Zealand Veterans' Affairs. Check that the partner or caregiver for the dependent children has made contact with New Zealand Veterans' Affairs to find out about possible entitlement. Note there is no initial stand-down when a partner applies for Sole Parent Support or Jobseeker Support within 28 days of the client's death. When the partner 28 days or more after the death of the client, there will be an initial stand-down.

chunks.title: Delay in granting ACC payments — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: When the death was the result of an accident, the surviving partner may be able to get weekly compensation payments from ACC. If there will be a delay in deciding their claim, the partner can apply for a benefit while they are waiting. The surviving partner must acknowledge, in writing, that benefit payments made will be refunded once weekly compensation payments are granted from ACC.

chunks.title: Partner donates a kidney or liver tissue — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Partner donates a kidney or liver tissue
Partners of clients receiving Veteran's Pension can keep getting their pension if they are donating a kidney or liver tissue.

chunks.title: Partner has left New Zealand permanently — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Partner has left New Zealand permanently
When a partner has left New Zealand permanently and the other partner remains in New Zealand, their qualification for Veterans Pension depends on whether they are:
- qualified in their own right or
- a grandparented non-qualified partner
## Both qualified in own right
When payment has stopped for a client, as they are overseas, the partner who remains in New Zealand can continue to get the married, civil union or de facto rate. The partner remaining in New Zealand cannot get the single rate unless there is a breakdown in the relationship.
## Grandparented non-qualified partner is overseas
When the grandparented non-qualified partner is overseas permanently, the qualified client remaining in New Zealand will continue getting half the couple rate.
If the grandparented non-qualified partner in not returning to New Zealand the grandparented non-qualified partner rate must end as the non-qualifying partner will not be ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Grandparented non-qualified partner remains in New Zealand
When the grandparented non-qualified partner remains in New Zealand and the qualifying partners Veterans Pension has stopped as they are overseas for more than 26 weeks the grandparented rate ends because the qualifying partner is not entitled to payment for their absence or any part of the absence.
The non-qualified partner can test their eligibility for a main benefit if they need financial assistance.

chunks.title: Permanent absence — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
Generally, if a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, payments must be cancelled from the day after the client leaves New Zealand.
If the client is moving to a country that has a Reciprocal agreement with New Zealand they may qualify for a benefit or pension in that country.
If the client is moving to country that New Zealand does not have a Reciprocal agreement with, they may be able to receive part of their Veterans Pension payments.
If the client wishes to receive part of their Veterans Pension overseas, then it is important that they apply for 'portability' before they leave New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Reciprocal agreements
- To or from overseas Payment overseas of Veterans Pension
- To or from overseas Special portability arrangements with Pacific countries

chunks.title: Person detained under a Public Protection Order — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Person detained under a Public Protection Order
A person who has a Public Protection Order may get Veteran’s Pension if they meet the qualifications.
A Public Protection Order is when a person has finished their sentence in prison but for public safety they must remain in a secure residence.
This is to protect members of the public from the almost certain harm from serious sexual or violent offences. Corrections fund the costs of the person being detained in a residence within the prison compound.
For more information see:
## Rate of payment
The hospital rate of Veteran’s Pension is paid from the date of grant.
## Entitlement date
The entitlement date for Veteran’s Pension for a person held under a Public Protection Order is generally the date of release. The usual stand-down provisions for prisoners apply when determining the commencement date.
## Emergency Benefit
A person who has a Public Protection Order may get Emergency Benefit if they meet the basic eligibility criteria.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Entitlement date
- Emergency Benefit Person detained under a Public Protection Order

chunks.title: Priority for deductions — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Priority for deductions
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others; the following list gives the order of priority, highest to lowest:
Highest priority
- Inland Revenue tax deductions (including Student Loan repayments)
- Child Support deductions made under the Child Support Act 1991
- Inland Revenue deduction notices (for unpaid taxes)
- Ministry of Social Development debt repayments including Liable Parent Contributions (LPC), child maintenance debts and Major Repairs Advances (MRA), Student Allowance debt, Student Loan debt converted to Ministry of Social Development debt, Income Related Rent historical Kāinga Ora debt, Income Related Rent Ministry of Social Development debt
- Attachment orders made under the Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Court attachment orders issued under the Summary Proceedings Act 1957
- Court attachment orders issued under the District Court Act 2016
Lowest priority
Determining the priority of deductions is necessary where a client has more than one order issued in respect of their benefit. Also each order and deduction notice is subject to its own protected earnings rule.
When you need to reduce deductions you adjust from the lowest priority up to those with a higher priority taking into account the protected earnings rules for each.

chunks.title: Protected earnings rate — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Protected earnings rate
Both the District Court Act and the Summary Proceedings Act provide that every Ministry of Justice attachment order must specify a 'protected earnings rate'.
The protected earnings rate is usually 60% of the client's net earnings after PAYE tax has been deducted or withheld.
If the attachment order will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate, then the order will not operate and you must cancel or return the attachment order to the Ministry of Justice.
Calculating the client's income differs between attachment orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act and the District Court Act, as different benefits are taken into account. Therefore it is important to determine what type of attachment order has been issued.
Summary Proceedings Act 1957
For orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act 1957, the calculation of the client's income does not include Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support, Disability Allowance, Child Disability Allowance, Winter Energy Payment, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
District Court Act 2016
For orders made under the District Court Act 2016, the client's income includes Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support and Disability Allowance but does not include Child Disability Allowance, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
## Example
An attachment order is received from the Ministry of Justice for $80.00 per week. The order lists the protected income as $396.09 per week.
We need to calculate whether adding the deduction of $80.00 will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate:
Calculate protected earnings rate
Veteran's Pension paid at the single living alone rate (net, as at 1 April 2026)
$555.15
Plus Accommodation Supplement (Area 2)
$105.00
Total net earnings
$660.15
60% of total net earnings (= protected earnings)
$396.09
Calculate if Attachment Order will exceed protected earnings
Total net earnings
$660.15
Less Child Support deduction
$60.00
Less Ministry of Social Development debts
$130.00
Sub total
$470.15
Less Attachment Order
$80.00
Total
$390.15
The attachment order takes the client's income to $390.15, which is below the protected earnings rate of $396.09.
The attachment order will not operate, therefore you must return it to the Ministry of Justice for the order to be amended.

chunks.title: Qualification if one partner remains in New Zealand — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Qualification if one partner remains in New Zealand
A client qualified for Veteran's Pension in their own right can be temporarily absent from New Zealand for up to 26 weeks and continue to get Veterans Pension.
When a partner has left New Zealand permanently and the other partner remains in New Zealand, their qualification for Veterans Pension depends on whether they are qualified in their own right or are a grandparented non-qualified partner.

chunks.title: Qualification starts during absence — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Qualification starts during absence
If a client applies for Veterans Pension and becomes qualified while overseas, their absence before qualification is not taken into account.
The allowable absence period starts from when the client qualified, not from when they went overseas and is treated the same as other clients.

chunks.title: Qualifications - Partner dies — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Qualifications - Partner dies
The lump sum payment on death is made to a veteran when their partner or spouse dies and the partner:
- met the age and residence qualifications for New Zealand superannuation and
- was getting Veterans Pension when they died and
- was ordinarily resident in New Zealand on the date of death

chunks.title: Qualifications - Veteran dies — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Qualifications - Veteran dies
The lump sum payment on death is made to the surviving partner or spouse or dependent children when a veteran dies and they:
- met the age and residence qualifications for New Zealand superannuation and
- were receiving Veterans Pension when they died and
- had a war disablement pension of 70% or more under the War Pensions Act 1954 or
- had a disablement pension of 52% or more under the Veterans' Support Act 2014 and
- were ordinarily resident in New Zealand on the date of death
If there is no surviving spouse or partner, the lump sum payment is apportioned between any dependent children of the veteran.
If there is no surviving spouse or dependent children, no lump sum is payable.

chunks.title: Release on bail — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Release on bail
When a client is released on bail, Veteran's Pension can be paid from the date of release providing the client still meets the qualifications for the Veteran's Pension and reapplies for Veteran's Pension immediately after their release.
A non-qualified partner cannot be reincluded on release if the grandparented non-qualified partner rate was cancelled due to imprisonment.
Note there is no initial stand-down when clients apply for Veteran's Pension. Veteran's Pension commences from:
- date of application or
- date of release

chunks.title: Remanded in custody — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Remanded in custody
Generally, when a client is remanded in custody awaiting a further court appearance the client's Veteran's Pension should be stopped. There is discretion to continue payment for 2 pay days following imprisonment.
There is also discretion to continue payment of Veteran's Pension after taking the client's financial circumstances and commitments into account.
When deciding whether to continue paying Veteran's Pension for the period of remand, consider the following:
- has the client been remanded pending further hearing or for sentencing
- does the client have continuing costs that cannot be avoided, such as rent and hire purchase for essential items
- does the client have a partner (either qualified in their own right or a grandparented non-qualified partner)
Every situation should be considered on a case-by-case basis.
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances of the client before making a decision.

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When the client returns to New Zealand you will need to confirm the following:
- date of return to New Zealand
- date of departure (if client did not advise before leaving New Zealand) and
- did the client apply for or get any benefit or pension in the country that they travelled to, or an increase in the benefit or pension that they already get from that country during their stay there?
Note couples getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate of Veteran's Pension will lose their grandparenting if the qualified client is not entitled to payment during their absence or any part of the absence.

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand is delayed — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand is delayed
If unexpected circumstances, beyond the client's control, prevent their return to New Zealand within 30 weeks, payment for the pay days that fall within the first 26 weeks of absence can be confirmed. The client must also either:
- return to New Zealand
- apply under a Reciprocal Agreement or
- apply for payment overseas
In no circumstances should payment continue beyond 26 weeks.
You will need to carefully investigate the circumstances that caused the delay. Circumstances beyond the control of the client would include (but are not limited to):
- aircraft breakdowns
- industrial disputes
- bereavement and
- illness/injury to the client, their partner or other relatives
You will need to find out whether or not travel arrangements were affected by such circumstances. Consider the following factors:
What were the booking arrangements before departure?
Was a return passage or flight within the allowable period arranged?
Could an earlier return have reasonably been expected despite the circumstances that arose?
When the extended absence was caused by unforeseen circumstances beyond the control of the client, payment can be confirmed for the pay days that fall within the first 26 weeks.
Note if the qualified client of a grandparented non-qualified couple is absent for more than 26 weeks, and is not entitled to payment for their absence, or any part of the absence the grandparented non-qualified rate ends.
## Single living alone rate
The single living alone rate can continue to be paid for absences overseas of up to 26 weeks provide the client is otherwise entitled to get it.

chunks.title: Single living alone rate and absences from New Zealand — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Single living alone rate and absences from New Zealand
The single living alone rate can continue to be paid during temporary absences from New Zealand if the client:
- still meets the definition of living alone and
- is eligible for and receiving Veterans Pension
## Not entitled to the single living alone rate
If the client is not entitled to the single living alone rate while they are absent from New Zealand, their Veterans Pension should be reduced to the single sharing accommodation rate from the day after departure from New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Single living alone rate
- Definition of living alone
- Absence from New Zealand
- Overseas medical treatment
- Humanitarian work

chunks.title: Student Loan repayments — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Student Loan repayments
Clients getting a Veterans Pension with a Student Loan debt must use a tax code with the Student Loan ('SL') repayment code. This will ensure that Student Loan repayments are deducted every pay period if required.
A Student Loan repayment is required when:
- the client's gross weekly payment of Veterans Pension is over the Student Loan repayment threshold or
- the client is on secondary tax code, regardless of the client's rate of payment
For more information see:
- Repayment thresholds (current)
If the client's Veterans Pension is over the Student Loan repayment threshold, the Student Loan repayment will automatically be deducted from their fortnightly payment.
Deductions are calculated weekly but made fortnightly.
If the client's Veterans Pension is below the Student Loan repayment threshold, no Student Loan repayment will be made from the client's payment, unless the client is on a secondary tax code.
Clients can make voluntary payments directly to Inland Revenue at any time.
For more information on Student Loans see:
- Students Student Loan

chunks.title: Study — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Study
If a Veterans Pension client (or partner) starts full-time or part-time study it does not affect their Veterans Pension.
For any study commencing on or after 1 January 2011:
- a client will not be able to receive Student Allowance if the client or their partner is receiving Veterans Pension
- a client will not be able to receive Student Loan Living Costs if the client is receiving Veterans Pension or is included in their partners' Veterans Pension
For more information see:
- Student Allowance Eligibility and Entitlement
- Student Loan Eligibility and entitlement criteria for a Student Loan

chunks.title: SWIFTT process to pay a partner — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT process to pay a partner
When you decide to continue payment of Veterans Pension to the partner of a client who has been imprisoned, you will need to determine the most appropriate SWIFTT process to enable payment to be made to the partner.
The process for payment will depend on the following:
- the period in prison is in the past
- the client is due to be released from prison shortly
- the client is likely to be in prison for more than four weeks and
- the rate of payment for the partner
Note there is discretion to pay the full married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit.
## Period in prison has passed or release is imminent
Generally you should use the SBDR screen in SWIFTT to:
- suspend the client's portion of Veterans Pension for the period in prison and
- pay the appropriate rate of Veterans Pension to the partner
## Period in prison exceeds 4 weeks
When the Veterans Pension is to continue, and be paid to the partner you will need to contact Helpline for advice regarding the SWIFTT process to use.

chunks.title: Tax Certificates — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Tax Certificates
Work and Income does not issue tax certificates to clients. If a client requests information about their tax details they must be referred to Inland Revenue to get a "Personal Tax Summary".
## Exception
Tax details can be issued if a client:
- dies - you can provide details to the estate solicitor, administrator, executor etc or
- is paid Veterans Pension overseas - details will automatically be sent to the client in April each year

chunks.title: Tax codes — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Tax codes
Veteran's Pension clients must choose a tax code appropriate to their circumstances. The client can change their tax code at any time.
All queries about correct tax codes must be referred to Inland Revenue.
As a general guideline:
- if Veteran's Pension is the client's highest or only source of income, the 'M' tax code should be used
- if Veteran's Pension is not the client's highest or only source of income, a secondary or 'S' tax code should be used or
- clients with a Student Loan must use a tax code with the Student Loan (SL) repayment code or
- a tailored tax code can also be used when the client has other income
## Tailored tax codes
Clients need to apply to Inland Revenue for a tailored tax code. The client needs to provide proof of their tailored tax code for example, a letter from Inland Revenue, for this to be added to their Veteran's Pension record.
A tailored tax code should only be added to a Veteran's Pension at grant if verification from Inland Revenue of the tailored tax code is provided by the client.
The tailored tax code only applies for the year in which it is issued. Each year all clients with a tailored tax code need to re-apply to Inland Revenue to get a tailored tax code.
Instructions are provided each year in March on the 'end of tax year' process required for clients with a tailored tax code.

chunks.title: Taxation — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Taxation
Veterans Pension is a taxable benefit. MSD makes payments to clients at the net rate after the deduction of tax. MSD passes the tax on to Inland Revenue.
Generally MSD will request a client or partner who are included (grandparented non-qualified partner) to provide MSD their IRD number or evidence of their IRD number.

chunks.title: Temporary absence — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Temporary absence
When a client is going to be temporarily overseas (ie they are still ordinarily resident in New Zealand) there are a number of options available to the client depending on how long they will be overseas.
You should also advise the client that while payment can continue for up to 26 weeks, provided they return to New Zealand within 30 weeks, they must remain ordinarily resident in New Zealand. In addition, if the client:
- leaves New Zealand temporarily, eg on holiday, but does not return to New Zealand and decides to live permanently overseas
- is simply returning to New Zealand every 26 weeks in order to remain qualified for New Zealand Superannuation but is no longer ordinarily resident in New Zealand and
- if they decide to remain overseas for longer than 30 weeks
an overpayment will be established.
As payments can continue for up to 26 weeks, provided the client returns to New Zealand within 30 weeks, you should advise a client intending to be overseas for more than 26 weeks that if they are staying in a country that:
- has a Reciprocal agreement with New Zealand they may qualify for a benefit or pension in that country or
- New Zealand does not have a Reciprocal agreement with, they may be able to receive part of their Veterans Pension payments
Note couples getting the grandparented non-qualified rate of Veteran's Pension will lose their grandparenting if the qualified client is not entitled to payment during their absence or any part of the absence.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit payments to a single client — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit payments to a single client
When a single client with no dependent children dies, payment generally stops from the day after the date of death.
There is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days. When payment is continued after the date of death, it is referred to as terminal benefit.
Circumstances where you might consider continued payment beyond a single client's date of death include:
- when the deceased client's domestic situation results in a transition cost for a family member, causing hardshipExample: accommodation and other household costs when client has been sharing accommodation
or
- when there are exceptional and justified costs associated with the death of the clientExample: multiple deaths within one family
You should not continue payment for 28 days following the death of a single client to meet funeral expenses.
## Cost of funeral
The person responsible for the cost of the funeral is able to receive assistance from Veterans Affairs New Zealand.
If Veterans Affairs New Zealand have already assisted with the funeral expenses there is no entitlement to a Funeral Grant as well.
If the Ministry of Social Development grants an application for a Funeral Grant before a request is made to Veterans Affairs New Zealand, Veterans Affairs may pay a top-up in addition to the Funeral Grant.
The combined amount of top-up and Funeral Grant must not be more than the maximum amount paid by Veterans Affairs New Zealand.
## SWIFTT
If you are paying terminal benefit for a single client you will need to manually calculate entitlement and make an adhoc payment.
There is no automatic provision for the payment of terminal benefit (for a single client) in SWIFTT. You should make notes in CMS with the adhoc amount and the period it represents.
Wherever possible you should enter the next of kin or the executor of the deceased's estate on SWIFTT.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit payments to surviving partner, or person caring for the children — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit payments to surviving partner, or person caring for the children
Terminal benefit is payable for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children. The surviving partner could be a grandparented non-qualified partner or getting a main benefit.
## Surviving partner
When Veteran's Pension is being paid to a couple, both the deceased person and the surviving person's portion of Veteran's Pension is paid. Payment is the total Veteran's Pension payment as well as any ongoing extra help.
The deceased person's portion of the terminal benefit is paid to their bank account.
A surviving person can apply to have the deceased person's portion of terminal benefit paid to them. Where an application is received, terminal benefit (or remaining unpaid balance) can be paid to that applicant.
The surviving partner's Veteran's Pension or main benefit should be reviewed to determine the best option financially for the person.
## Surviving children
When the deceased client has no surviving partner but has surviving children, the payment can be made to the person caring for the deceased client's children.
Where an application is received, the remaining unpaid balance of terminal benefit can be paid to the carer.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit rate — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: The provision to continue payment for 28 days following the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit. Benefit payment is continued at the rate which was payable to the client and partner (if any) at the date of death and includes supplementary assistance (for up to 28 days following the date of death).

chunks.title: Payments at a reduced rate — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: When the client's Veterans Pension payment is paid at a reduced rate at the date of death, the terminal benefit is also paid at the reduced rate. Payments may have been reduced due to: - hospitalisation (only paid to the partner of a veteran, if the veteran had a war disablement below the threshold) - income (only if a grandparented non-qualified partner is included or surviving partner is getting a main benefit) - debt offsets when there are benefit arrears due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit paymentdo not recover debts in full from the final terminal benefit payments - when there are benefit arrears due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit payment - do not recover debts in full from the final terminal benefit payments - Child Support if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies, however, MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenuewhen a surviving partner or family member makes enquiries, refer them to Inland Revenue - if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed - Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies, however, MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenue - when a surviving partner or family member makes enquiries, refer them to Inland Revenue - court attachment orders - redirection to Kāinga Ora or a community housing provider when the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. See: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client

chunks.title: Payments at a reduced rate — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text: - when the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. See: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client Note all of the above deductions will continue to be made from the terminal benefit payments unless they are manually stopped before cancellation.

chunks.title: Underpaid — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Underpaid
When a client has been underpaid Veteran's Pension and is owed arrears, MSD will work out the amount of tax and pass this on to Inland Revenue.
The amount is included in the end-of-year tax assessment for the current tax year, regardless of the period that the underpayment covers. This is different to how arrears payments for main benefits are taxed.
Example
A client is paid arrears on 12 June 2026. This payment represents arrears for 25 March 2026 to 3 June 2026.
The whole arrears payment will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (the current tax year).

chunks.title: Verification — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Verification
You must be satisfied that you can accurately identify the deceased client's Veterans Pension record.
Generally we will accept verbal notification of a client's death. This advice can be acted on when you determine the relationship of the caller to the deceased client and obtaining sufficient information to provide confirmation of the deceased's identity.
Follow-up verification should generally be requested. A copy of the death certificate or a copy of the death notice is acceptable support documentation.

chunks.title: Verification of changes — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Verification of changes
At the time of the annual review you should also check that the client has not had any other changes to their personal circumstances. It is the client's responsibility to provide appropriate verification of any changes in their circumstances for example:
- relationship status - the client may have commenced a new relationship
proof: marriage or civil union certificate; or personal statement from the client
- accommodation costs
proof: tenancy agreement, letter from landlord
- children left care
proof: personal statement from client
- children came into care
proof: letter from previous caregiver, birth certificate (if another child born to client)
- disability allowance new or increased costs
proof: a printout of prescription charges, receipts etc.
Note proof of disability costs is only required when the costs have increased or there is a new cost. Verification is no longer required for an existing cost that has decreased.

chunks.title: Verification of income — main benefits > veterans pension > changes and reviews veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Verification of income
At the time of the annual review the client is to provide verification of any income they have earned during the previous income year.
If the client cannot provide verification (for example payslips) then you must contact the employer to verify income details in the last 52 weeks. You will need to send a verification of earnings form (VO6) to the employer.
Once confirmed income details have been obtained a due/paid income assessment will need to be done.
For more information see:
- Types of income
- Definition of income
- Income

chunks.title: Charging income — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Charging income
Veteran's Pension is income tested when:
- the client is under 65 years of age
and
- was getting a Veteran's Pension when the War Pensions Act 1954 was replaced by the Veterans' Support Act 2014 on 7 December 2014 and
- has chosen to continue to get Veteran's Pension instead of weekly income compensation from Veterans Affairs
or
- a client aged 65 years or older has included their grandparented non-qualified partner
Note income is reduced from the gross rate of Veteran's Pension.
## Some income disregarded
Payments from a Friendly Society or similar organisation of up to $104 a year can be disregarded.
Deduct this amount from the client's gross income before abatement.
## Veteran under 65
Veteran's Pension clients who are under the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation have their income (and their partner's, if any) charged at the following rates:
- 30 cents is taken from the benefit for each $1.00 of combined income the client (and their partner) earn over $160 per week ($8,320 per year), but not more than $250 per week ($13,000 per year) and
- 70 cents for each $1.00 of combined income over $250 per week ($13,000 per year)
## Veteran with a grandparented non-qualified partner included
When a veteran who meets the age and service criteria for Veterans Pension has a grandparented non-qualified partner included in their Veteran's Pension, their income (and their partners) is charged at the following rate:
- 70 cents for each $1.00 of their combined of income over $160 per week
For more information see:
## Overseas benefits or pensions
When a veteran is getting an overseas social security benefit or pension, this is generally treated as a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension rate. This requires a different calculation to the chargeable income assessment.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's single living alone rate of Veteran's Pension.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Veteran's Pension from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Veteran's Pension for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier

chunks.title: Client meets qualifications while overseas — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Client meets qualifications while overseas
When a client qualifies for Veteran's Pension while they are absent from New Zealand, the commencement date is:
- the date of entitlement or
- the date of application
whichever is the later.
A client can be paid for up to the first 26 weeks of their absence if they return to New Zealand within 30 weeks of the Veteran's Pension commencement date.
If the client is absent from New Zealand and is absent for more than 30 weeks from the date they qualified to get Veteran's Pension, and they were not delayed from returning to New Zealand by circumstances outside their control that were reasonably unforeseeable before they left, they cannot get Veteran's Pension while they are absent.
Veteran's Pension can resume from the date the client returns to New Zealand.
## Living in Reciprocal Agreement countries
A client may meet the qualifications for Veteran's Pension while living in a country that has a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand.

chunks.title: Clients with a partner — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: If a client has a partner, the rate of payment depends on whether: - both clients get Veteran's Pension in their own right (both meet the age and residency qualifications) and - either client is entitled to get or is getting a deductible overseas benefit or pension and - the partner has a temporary entry visa or is in New Zealand unlawfully. Both clients meet the qualifications for Veteran's Pension - The couple's income is not taken into consideration when assessing the rate of payment. - Any overseas benefits or pension either partner may be getting or entitled to get, will only be directly deducted from their individual Veteran's Pension payments. - A client or partner's overseas benefit or pension may affect the rate of any on-going financial assistance if there is an excess. Only one client qualifies for Veteran's Pension. - The couple's income is not taken into consideration when assessing the rate of Veteran's Pension. Veteran's Pension is not income tested. - If the client getting Veteran's Pension gets or is entitled to get an overseas benefit or pension, it is directly deducted from their payments. - If the partner is getting or is entitled to get an overseas benefit or pension, it is not deducted from the client's Veteran's Pension payments. - A client or partner's overseas benefit or pension may affect the rate of any on-going financial assistance if there is an excess. Only one client qualifies Veteran's Pension and their partner has a temporary entry visa or is in New Zealand unlawfully. - The couples income is not taken into consideration when assessing the rate of payment for Veteran's Pension. Veteran's Pension is not income tested. - If the client getting Veteran's Pension gets or is entitled to get an overseas benefit or pension, it is directly deducted from their payments. - If the partner is getting or is entitled to get an overseas benefit or pension, it is not deducted from the client's Veteran's Pension payments. - A client or partner's overseas benefit or pension may affect the rate of any on-going financial assistance if there is an excess. - Pay the client the single rate of Veteran's Pension. Only one client meets the qualifications for Veteran's Pension and the partner is included (grandparented non-qualified partner) - Payment is income tested.

chunks.title: Clients with a partner — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: - If the client or partner is getting or entitled to get an overseas benefit or pension, it is directly deducted from the grand-parented non-qualified partner rate of Veteran's Pension. The balance is divided equally and paid to each partner. - A client or partner's overseas benefit or pension may affect the rate of any on-going financial assistance if there is an excess. In some situations, clients who are living apart from their partner can get the single rate of Veteran's Pension. Note from 9 November 2020 a partner who does not qualify for Veteran's Pension cannot be included in the client's Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Commencement date — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
Veterans Pension commences on:
- the date of entitlement or
- the date of application
whichever is later.
Note applications from the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau do not lapse after 20 days.
No stand-down applies to Veteran's Pension.
## Back payment
The back payment of Veteran's Pension is only allowed under the following circumstances:
- the veteran only has 'J-Force' service or
- the original decision was made in error

chunks.title: Couple separate or one partner dies — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Couple separate or one partner dies
If a grandparented non-qualified couple separate, or one partner dies, the grandparented non-qualified partner rate will end.

chunks.title: Couples income makes it advantageous to stop the non-qualified partner rate — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Couples income makes it advantageous to stop the non-qualified partner rate
When a couple get the grandparented non-qualified partner rate of Veteran's Pension, combined income above the viability amount of $41,081.49 (as at 1 April 2026) will reduce the rate to less than the amount that would be paid to the qualified partner in their own right.
A decision on whether to continue getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate must be made by the qualifying partner only.
Before a decision is made the qualifying partner must be given the following information to help them decide:
- the couple can continue getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate even though it is less than the qualified partner would get without a partner included. This will keep the grandparented non-qualified partner status
- whether the income is likely to reduce below the viability amount in the future - they could continue with the reduced rate until their income reduces
- if the qualified partner chooses to cancel the grandparented non-qualified partner rate they will not be able to apply for it in the future
- the grandparented non-qualified partner will only have the option of applying for a main benefit which is paid at a lower amount, is income tested and paid at a half married rate
- the grandparented non-qualified partner will not be able to continue using their SuperGold Card
- the overseas absence provisions for main benefits are more limited than they are for Veteran's Pension
The qualifying partner must decide whether to cancel or continue with the grandparented non-qualified partner rate.

chunks.title: Couples who are living apart — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Couples who are living apart
Couples who live apart but still regard themselves as a couple receive the married, civil union or de facto rate of payment.
Generally, when a couple is physically living apart only because one partner is in long-term care (but they still consider themselves to be in a marriage or civil union), they may be entitled to get the single sharing or the single living alone rate instead of the married, civil union or de facto rate.
There are some important exceptions to this.

chunks.title: Couples who have separated — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Couples who have separated
When couples who are married, in a civil union or de facto relationship have separated, they can be treated as single, and can get the single sharing accommodation or the single living alone rate of Veteran's Pension (provided they have not entered into another relationship).
The rate of payment will depend on whether they:
- share their accommodation with any person aged 18 years or over, other than a dependent child, or a visitor who stays more than 13 weeks in any 26 week period or
- meet all the qualifications for the single living alone rate
Note the single sharing accommodation or the single living alone rate, can be paid from the date the Veteran's Pension commences if the client meets the above criteria at their entitlement date.
For more information about the effective date to review if the client is already getting Veteran's Pension see:
- Effective date of review due to change in relationship
## What determines a separation?
For couples who are married or in a civil union, to be separated from their partner there must be a physical separation and an acceptance or recognition by one or both of the partners that the relationship has ended.
For a de facto couple to be separated their relationship must no longer be in the nature of marriage or civil union (a relationship in the nature of marriage or civil union means both a financial interdependence and emotional commitment).

chunks.title: Deciding ordinarily resident in New Zealand — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: Generally, a client must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they apply for Veteran's Pension. They must remain ordinarily resident in New Zealand to continue getting Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Attributes of being ordinarily resident — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: To meet the ordinarily resident qualifications in New Zealand, the client must have a close and clear connection to New Zealand on the date they apply for Veteran's Pension. - their physical presence in New Zealand is not casually or as a traveller - they are in New Zealand voluntarily because they want to be - there is some intention to remain in New Zealand for a settled purpose - despite temporary absences from New Zealand, they regularly or customarily live in New Zealand - they prefer residence in New Zealand to any other country (a client cannot be ordinarily resident in 2 counties at the same time). If there is reason to believe the client may no longer be ordinarily resident in New Zealand after Veteran's Pension is granted, the key attributes can also be considered at that point.

chunks.title: Not clear if a client is ordinarily resident — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: When it is not clear if a client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand, the client may need to be asked for more information. Some of the following considerations may help to make a decision: - if the client is, or going overseas, what their intentions towards New Zealand are (sighting return air tickets may be a good indication) - the length of time they spend in New Zealand compared to the length of time overseas, and the reasons they were overseas - property ownership (as this tends to suggest permanent ties with a place), including other asset ownership (e.g. boats, cars or caravans) - where their cash assets are principally held (New Zealand banks or investment entities or overseas based holdings) - is their income earned in New Zealand or overseas, and if they are a tax resident in New Zealand - if they are still on an electoral role and vote in central and local body elections, and if they vote anywhere overseas - what their personal commitment to New Zealand is compared to overseas (e.g. their involvement in their immediate and extended family, community, community events, clubs and other groups). If there is reason to believe the client may no longer be ordinarily resident in New Zealand after Veteran’s Pension is granted, the key attributes of being ordinarily resident can also be considered at that point.

chunks.title: Making a decision — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: To decide if a client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand consideration must be given to all the factors of each case. The client should show a close and clear connection to New Zealand. They should be asked for more information if clarification is needed. If it is still unclear if a client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand, you should seek advice to help you make a decision.

chunks.title: Moving overseas — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: When a client leaves New Zealand to live overseas permanently, they may be able to keep getting their Veteran’s Pension. See: Portability

chunks.title: Deciding ordinarily resident in New Zealand for eligible charitable work overseas — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: For a client who did eligible charitable work outside of New Zealand, to have the period counted, they must have remained ordinarily resident during the period they were doing their voluntary work overseas. For more information see: - Residency qualifications

chunks.title: Determining ordinarily resident before (and during) a client's full-time voluntary work overseas — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: To determine if a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand immediately before they started their eligible charitable work, a number of factors must be considered. Some of the key attributes that indicate that a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand before they left (and during the period they were absence) for their voluntary work include: - their physical presence in New Zealand was other than casually or as a traveller - they were in New Zealand because they wanted to be and they were here voluntarily - there was some intention to remain settled in New Zealand for a settled purpose - despite temporary absences from New Zealand they regularly or customarily lived in New Zealand before they left and still considered New Zealand home while they were doing their voluntary work - they preferred residence in New Zealand to any other country (a client cannot be ordinarily resident in 2 countries at the same time)

chunks.title: Not clear if the client is ordinarily resident — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: When it is not clear if a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand before they left, and during the period they were doing voluntary work overseas, the client may need to be asked for more information. The following could be considered: - when the client was going overseas what were their intentions towards New Zealand, did they intend to return? - what were their ties to other countries at the time? - were there any extended absences from New Zealand leading up to the voluntary work? - the length of time they spend in New Zealand before they left for their eligible charitable work, compared to their periods of absence and the reasons for the absences - property ownership in New Zealand and elsewhere (as this tends to suggest permanent ties with a place), including other asset ownership (e.g. boats, cars or caravans) - where their cash assets were principally held (New Zealand banks or investment entities or overseas based holdings) - was their income earned in New Zealand or overseas before they left for their voluntary work, and were they tax resident in New Zealand? The client may need to talk to Inland Revenue for this information - were they on an electoral role and voted in central and local body elections before they left for their voluntary work? - did they have a personal commitment to New Zealand (e.g. their involvement in their immediate and extended family, community, community events, clubs and other groups) before they left for their voluntary work? If there is reason to believe a client may no longer be ordinarily resident in New Zealand after Veteran's Pension has been granted, the key attributes of being ordinarily resident can also be considered at that point.

chunks.title: Making a decision — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: To decide if a client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand consideration must be given to all factors of each case. The client should show a clear and close connection to New Zealand based on the attributes of being ordinarily resident in New Zealand. They should be asked for more information if clarification is needed. If it is still unclear if a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand before they left for or during their time doing voluntary work, you should seek advice to help you make a decision.

chunks.title: Missionary postings before 9 November 2020 — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: Clients who were born overseas and began a missionary posting outside of New Zealand before 9 November 2020 must have been ordinarily resident in New Zealand immediately before they left for missionary work overseas. Clients who were born in New Zealand and began a missionary posting outside of New Zealand before 9 November 2020 had no requirement to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand before they left for missionary work overseas.

chunks.title: Missionary postings on or after 9 November 2020 — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: Clients who began a missionary posting outside of New Zealand from 9 November 2020 must have been ordinarily resident in New Zealand immediately before they left for missionary work overseas.

chunks.title: Determining a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand before they left for missionary work — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: To determine if a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand immediately before they started their missionary work, a number of factors must be considered. Some of the key attributes indicating a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand before they left for their missionary work include: - their physical presence in New Zealand was other than casually or as a traveller - they were in New Zealand because they wanted to be and they were here voluntarily - there was some intention to remain in New Zealand for a settled purpose - despite temporary absences from New Zealand they regularly or customarily lived in New Zealand before they left for their missionary work - they preferred residence in New Zealand to any other country (a client cannot be ordinarily resident in two countries at the same time)

chunks.title: Not clear if the client is ordinarily resident — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: When it is not clear if a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand before they left for their missionary work, the following could be considered: - when the client was going overseas what were their intentions towards New Zealand, did they intend to return? - what were their ties to other countries at the same time? - were there any extended absences from New Zealand leading up to the missionary work? - the length of time they spend in New Zealand before they left for their missionary work, compared to their periods of absence and the reasons for the absences - property ownership in New Zealand and elsewhere (as this tends to suggest permanent ties with a place), including other asset ownership (for example boats, cars or caravans) - where their cash assets were principally held (New Zealand banks or investment entities or overseas based holdings) - was their income earned in New Zealand or overseas before they left for their missionary work, and were they tax resident in New Zealand? The client may need to talk to Inland Revenue to get this information - were they on an electoral role and voted in central and local body elections before they left for their missionary work? - did they have a personal commitment to New Zealand and elsewhere (e.g. their involvement in their immediate and extended family, community, community events, clubs and other groups) before they left for their missionary work? If there is reason to believe the client may no longer be ordinarily resident in New Zealand after Veteran's Pension is granted, the key attributes of being ordinarily resident can also be considered at that point.

chunks.title: Making a decision — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: To decide if a client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand consideration must be given to all the factors of each case. The client should show a close and clear connection to New Zealand based on the attributes of being ordinarily resident. They should be asked for more information if clarification is needed. If it is still unclear if a client was ordinarily resident in New Zealand before they left for their missionary work, you should seek advice to help you make your decision.

chunks.title: Definition of a boarding house — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Definition of a boarding house
A boarding house is a residential premises containing one or more boarding rooms along with facilities for communal use by the tenants of the boarding house; and occupied, or intended by the landlord to be occupied, by at least 6 tenants at any one time.
Facilities means the facilities provided by the landlord of a boarding house for the shared use by tenants of the boarding house, such as:
- toilet and bathroom facilities
- cooking facilities
- general living, dining or recreational areas
- laundry facilities
- lifts and stairways
- rubbish storage and rubbish disposal facilities
- appliances for heating or cooling premises
- communication facilities
- lawns, gardens and outhouses
- any land or buildings intended for use for storage space or for the parking of motor vehicles
For more information see:
- Boarding houses

chunks.title: Definition of living alone — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Definition of living alone
Clients are considered living alone when they are living alone in their principal place of residence. This cannot include sharing their residence with any person aged 18 years or over unless that person is a:
- dependent child who is continuing in education and not financially independent (until the start of the pay period following the date they are no longer in education, are financially independent or 31 December of the year they turn 18) or
- visitor who stays less than 13 weeks in any 26-week period
If a client has a young person under 18 living with them, who is in full time employment, the client is still eligible to get the single living alone rate of Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Dependent child — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
A dependent child is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of that client
- maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
A dependent child for Veteran’s Pension does not include a:
- child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 and
- young person getting a Young Parent Payment and their child (see Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples)
In some situations, a child may not be living at home but is still considered to be a dependent child.

chunks.title: Effect of absence overseas on grandparented couples — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Effect of absence overseas on grandparented couples
Couples getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate who are both absent from New Zealand at the same time, will keep getting their grandparented rate provided the qualifying partner qualifies during the period of absence.
If the qualifying partner no longer qualifies during their absence on or after 9 November 2020 the grandparented non-qualified rate will end and the qualifying partner will not be able to include a non-qualifying partner again.
## Overseas absence where both partners are absent
Period of absence
Is Grandparenting retained?
Absence less than 26 weeks
Yes - the qualified client is entitled for the period of absence.
Absence is more than 26 weeks but less than 30 weeks due to unavoidable delay returning
No - from the 27th week of absence, the qualified partner no longer qualifies and neither does the non-qualified partner. Grandparenting ends from the 27th week of absence.
Absence more than 26 weeks - not unavoidably delayed in returning
No - they no longer qualify from the day after the date of departure from New Zealand. Grandparenting ends from the date following departure.
Note this also applies if the qualified partner is overseas while the non-qualified partner is in New Zealand.
## Grandparented non-qualified partner is absent
Grandparenting is not affected when the grandparented non-qualified partner is temporarily absent from New Zealand by themselves, as long as the client in New Zealand still qualifies.
Payments made to the grandparented non-qualified partner during their absence can continue for up to 26 weeks.

chunks.title: Effect of imprisonment on grandparented clients — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: Grandparented non-qualified couples may no longer qualify for the grandparented non-qualified partner rate when either the client or partner is: - in prison - in custody on remand or - an escapee from custody There is discretion to continue Veteran's Pension for the 2 instalments following imprisonment. Further ongoing payments for the period of imprisonment are also discretionary.

chunks.title: Qualified partner is imprisoned — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: The decision guidelines - married, civil union or de facto clients should be used to decide whether the qualified partners payments continue for the period of imprisonment. If payments will not continue during the period of imprisonment, the grandparented non-qualified partner rate will end and the qualifying partner will not be able to include a non-qualified partner again. The grandparented non-qualified partner will need to apply for a main benefit.

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualified partner is imprisoned — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: Use the decision guidelines - married, civil union or de facto clients to decide whether the grandparented non-qualified partners payments continue for the period of imprisonment. If payments continue to the grandparented non-qualified partner, or the full amount is paid to the partner not in prison, the grandparented non-qualified partner rate continues. If payments to the grandparented non-qualified partner stop, the grandparented non-qualified partner rate can only be paid again on release if the qualifying partner: - continues to qualify for Veteran's Pension for the period of imprisonment and - wants to continue getting the grandparented non-qualified partner rate When payments stop for the grandparented non-qualified partner, the qualified partner’s payments continue at the same rate paid before their partner's imprisonment. The qualified partner can decide to cancel the grandparented rate at any time.

chunks.title: Single sharing or single living alone rate for qualified partner — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text: The qualified partner may qualify for the single sharing or single living alone rate of Veteran's Pension while their grandparented non-qualified partner is in prison. This must be considered separately based on the client's full circumstances eg the partner may not intend resuming the relationship when their partner leaves prison, or may end the relationship due to the imprisonment. Note the client should be informed that they will not be eligible for the grandparented non-qualified partner rate in the future, if they cancel the grandparented non-qualified partner rate, eg because they are treated as single.

chunks.title: Eligible charitable work — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Eligible charitable work
In certain circumstances, time spent doing eligible charitable work outside New Zealand may be considered as residence and presence in New Zealand to meet the requirements for Veteran's Pension.
Eligible charitable work is:
- full-time voluntary humanitarian work for an entity which had giving aid and assistance to less advantaged communities in one or more countries as its main purpose and
- work as a volunteer appointed by Volunteer Service Abroad Incorporated
Note voluntary work meant that a client did work for or on behalf of the charitable entity and did not get a salary or wage for doing this work. However, they may have got a small allowance to help with basic living costs.
Depending on whether the full-time voluntary work was before or after 9 November 2020, the period of absence for eligible charitable work is treated differently for assessing periods of residence and presence to qualify for Veteran's Pension.
## Applications before 9 November 2020
A client who applied for Veteran's Pension before 9 November 2020 could only have periods overseas included as a period of being resident and present to qualify for Veteran's Pension if they:
- were doing work as an accredited volunteer appointed by Volunteer Service Abroad Incorporated and
- remained ordinarily resident during their time overseas
## On or after 9 November 2020
A client who began eligible charitable work outside of New Zealand on or after 9 November 2020 can have it included as a period of residence and presence to qualify for Veteran's Pension if they:
- were doing work as an accredited volunteer appointed by Volunteer Service Abroad Incorporated and
- remained ordinarily resident during their time overseas or
- were doing full-time voluntary work that is humanitarian work and
- were carrying out the voluntary work for an entity that is affiliated with or closely related to, a charitable entity registered in New Zealand under the Charities Act 2005 and
- were carrying out this voluntary work on behalf of a charitable entity which has as its primary function, giving aid and assistance to less advantaged communities and
- remained ordinarily resident during their time overseas
Note this also means that only time from when the Charities Act 2005 (1 July 2005) came into force can be counted where a client wants to include work for a charity that is not Volunteer Services Abroad.

chunks.title: Exemption for severe disablement — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Exemption for severe disablement
As an incentive for the personal effort of a severely disabled person to participate or continue in employment, you can use your discretion to disregard all or part of any income earned from employment as chargeable income for benefit purposes.
Consideration for this special income exemption should be given to clients with a severe disability who are extremely limited in their ability to participate in employment, the community and take care of themselves.
You must first consider whether or not the client is severely disabled. The Guidelines - exemption for severe disablement will help you do this.
Each case should be assessed on an individual basis.
If the client is severely disabled you should consider whether or not to disregard all or part of any income earned by the client. To help you do this, see Amount of income exemption.
Note clients who are not severely disabled cannot receive this exemption.
For more information see:
- Amount of income exemption

chunks.title: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
If a Veteran's Pension client has dependent children or a child born on or after 1 July 2018, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit is paid by Inland Revenue, not through SWIFTT.

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualified partner with a partner in residential care — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Grandparented non-qualified partner with a partner in residential care
A grandparented non-qualified partner living in the community who has a Veteran's Pension partner who is in, or moves into long-term residential care may get a different rate of payment.
Their rate of payment depends on their own living situation.
## Partner living alone
Clients in the community who live alone can get the Veteran’s Pension single living alone rate from the date their partner entered care.
## Partner not living alone
Clients in the community who are not living alone can get the single sharing accommodation rate from the date their partner entered care.
## Income
The client in the community will have their income included in their partner's Financial Means Assessment for Residential Care Subsidy.
However, any income included in their partner's Financial Means Assessment for Residential Care Subsidy is not included as chargeable income against the Veteran's Pension.
Note if the partner does not meet the asset test for Residential Care Subsidy all income is charged against the Veteran's Pension.
## Special Disability Allowance
Special Disability Allowance can be paid to the client in the community to assist with extra costs due to their partner being in long term residential care, if the partner in care qualifies for Residential Care Subsidy.
## Rate of payment for partner in care
The partner in care will get the half married, civil union or de facto rate of Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Grandparented Veterans' Pensions — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Grandparented Veterans' Pensions
Veterans under the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation, who had a current Veteran's Pension on 7 December 2014, remain entitled to Veteran's Pension under the new Act.
From 7 December 2014 veterans under the age of 65 who receive Veteran's Pension can be required to have medical assessments to determine whether their condition prevents them from working. If a veteran under 65 is medically assessed as fit for work, their Veteran's Pension may be cancelled.
Veterans under 65 who continue to receive a Veteran's Pension after 7 December 2014 have the right to have decisions about their health condition reviewed by the Medical Appeals Board, if the condition is not related to their NZDF service.

chunks.title: Grandparenting non-qualified partner couples — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Grandparenting non-qualified partner couples
From 9 November 2020, clients who qualify for Veteran's Pension in their own right cannot include their non-qualified partner in their payments. A non-qualified partner can apply for a main benefit in their own right.
To be eligible for the grandparented rate, the client must have chosen to include their non qualifying partner before 9 November 2020 and be entitled to this rate from a date before 9 November 2020.
All existing non-qualified partners that were current, suspended or expired on 8 November 2020 were grandparented from 9 November 2020.
Note couples getting the non-qualified partner rate who temporarily left New Zealand before 26 March 2020 and were not able to return to New Zealand before 9 November 2020 will not be grandparented. Assistance during their absence is covered by the New Zealanders Stranded Overseas Support Programme. Couples who left New Zealand after 26 March 2020 have their absence treated under the usual 26 week absence rules and must be entitled to payment as at 8 November 2020 to be grandparented.
## Client included non-qualified partner at Veteran's Pension application
When a person applied for Veteran's Pension and included their non-qualified partner in their payments at the same time, the non-qualified partner rate is grandparented if:
- the client was entitled to get Veteran's Pension in their own right before 9 November 2020 and
- they applied for the non-qualified rate before 9 November 2020 and
- they were entitled to the non-qualified rate before 9 November 2020

chunks.title: Hospitals — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Hospitals
If a single client is in hospital at the time they meet the qualifications for Veteran's Pension they can only receive the single sharing accommodation rate.
When a client is already receiving the single living alone rate of Veteran's Pension at the time they are admitted to a public hospital, the single living alone rate continues to be paid.
The rate of Veteran's Pension is not reduced after 13 weeks hospitalisation.
For more information see:
- Changes and reviews Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Documents issued from 29 November 2010 — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Documents issued from 29 November 2010
Documents issued from 29 November 2010 include:
- eVisa letter
- Limited visa
- New Zealand Citizenship certificate (issued by Department of Internal Affairs)
- New Zealand Citizen endorsement (in a foreign passport)
- Permanent resident visa
- Resident visa
- Student visa
- Visitor visa
- Work visa
Only the Permanent resident visa, Permanent resident eVisa, Resident visa and Resident eVisa show a person is a resident.
A visa may be a sticker in the client's passport.
## Documents issued before 29 November 2010
Documents issued before 29 November 2010 that allow a person to stay in New Zealand include:
- Limited purposes permit
- New Zealand Citizenship certificate (issued by Department of Internal Affairs)
- Residence permit (with or without returning resident's visa)
- Student permit
- Visitor permit
- Work permit
Only the residence permit (with or without returning resident's visa) was issued to residents.
A permit may be a sticker in the client's passport.
## Unable to provide visa or permit
When a client is unable to provide an immigration visa or permit they may provide other Immigration New Zealand documents to verify their immigration status.
With the consent of the client, MSD can undertake an immigration status check directly with Immigration New Zealand.
Note that Immigration New Zealand may be unable to verify immigration status for clients of British nationality who arrived in New Zealand before 2 April 1974 and do not have a passport.

chunks.title: Infirmity — main benefits > veterans pension
chunks.text:
## Infirmity

These depend on whether the veteran is entitled to a disablement pension or independence allowance or a lump sum for whole-person impairment of 52% or more (or a War Disablement Pension of 70% or more under the War Pensions Act 1954) as determined by Veteran's Affairs New Zealand (Veterans Affairs).
