chunks.text: If both clients can't reach an agreement or provide the requested evidence within 10 working days from being notified of the mismatch, both clients' Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit must be suspended. For the client who is a social housing tenant, if they can't reach an agreement or provide the requested evidence within 10 working days from being notified of the mismatch, MSD will notify the housing provider that the client's Income Related Rent must be set to market rent for the property. Community Housing Providers have a discretion not to set the client's rent to the market rent rate. The standard 60-day notice period will apply. If both clients agree and/or provide evidence confirming the correct additional occupant contribution payment information while the assistance is suspended or Income Related Rent is at the market rent rate, the details should be updated and any assistance resumed and reviewed accordingly. For more information see: - change in additional occupant contributions If the mismatch has not been resolved within 8 weeks of being suspended, the Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit will be cancelled. In this case, clients can reapply for the Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, however if the same mismatch of information is identified, the disputes process will start again.

chunks.title: Informing clients about their duty — duty to advise of changes in circumstances
chunks.text:
## Informing clients about their duty
Clients on the social housing register or who rent in social housing must understand:
- they generally have a duty to advise MSD of any change in circumstances
- the consequences of failing to meet this duty e.g. MSD may review whether they still qualify for social housing or the property they are renting, and failure to declare a change in circumstance could result in prosecution.
Note clients do not need to tell MSD when they get, or have a change to, information share Child Support payments.
You need to make sure clients are aware of their duty to advise any change of circumstances and the consequences of failing to do this. See:
- Information documents advising of duty.
There are documents that reinforce the need for clients to advise MSD of a change in circumstances. These include:
- the placement letter
- Income Related Rent annual review letters
- Information sheet attached to most housing letters.

chunks.title: Introduction — duty to advise of changes in circumstances
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Generally, all clients on the social housing register, or renting social housing, have a duty to advise MSD straight away of any changes in their circumstances or their household's situation that may affect the following:
- whether they still qualify for social housing while on the register
- the need to be allocated, assigned or let any particular social housing property
- whether they still qualify for social housing when they are a tenant
- the need for particular property requirements in the place they are renting
- their calculated rate of Income Related Rent
## Exception - Client's getting information share Child Support
Clients do not need to tell MSD when they get, or have a change to, information share Child Support payments.
## Clients waiting to be allocated social housing
Generally, when a client on the register is waiting for allocation of social housing they must tell MSD straight away of any changes in their circumstances, or the circumstances of their partner, that may affect whether they qualify for social housing or the type of property they need.
## Current tenants
Generally, all social housing tenants have a duty to tell us straight away of any change in their circumstances, and any change in the circumstances of applicable people, that may mean they no longer:
- qualify for social housing or
- have a need for the particular property they are renting
Generally, all social housing tenants paying an Income Related Rent also have a duty to advise us straight away of any change in their circumstances, and any change in the circumstances of applicable people, that may result in them paying a higher Income Related Rent.
## Clients paying Income Related Rent
Generally, clients must tell MSD within 14 calendar days of any change in their or their household's circumstances that may affect their calculated rate of Income Related Rent.
This includes changes to the client's, or another applicable person's, assessable income and additional occupant contributions.

chunks.title: Abating cap — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Abating cap
If the client's rate of Income Related Rent is greater than what they were paying as rent before the change and they were not receiving Tenure Protection Allowance or Special Transfer Allowance then they are eligible for an abating cap.
The cap is calculated as the difference between the Income Related Rent the client would have been charged on 1 December 2000, and the net rent they were paying.
When a client is eligible for an abating cap, the cap amount reduces by $5 per week at each review of Income Related Rent if the cap has not already been reduced in the 12 months prior to the review.
## Example of abating cap
Rent payable before 1 December 2000
$140
Accommodation Supplement
$42
Net rent on 1 December 2000
$98 = A
Income Related Rent calculated on 1 December
$180 = B
Cap (discount) (= B - A)
$82 = C
Abatement as at December 2014 (= $5 x 14 years)
$70 = D
Abated cap as at December 2014 (= C - D)
$12 = E
Cumulative Rent (= A + D)
$168 = F
Calculated rate of Income Related Rent on 14 April 2023
$200 = G
Rent charged as at 14 April 2023 (lesser of F and G)
$168
## Example 2 abating cap
Rent payable before 1 December 2000
$140
Accommodation Supplement
$42
Net rent on 1 December 2000
$98 = A
Income Related Rent calculated on 1 December
$250 = B
Cap (discount) (= B - A)
$152= C
Abatement as at December 2014 (= $5 x 14 years)
$70 = D
Abated cap as at December 2014 (= C - D)
$82 = E
Cumulative Rent (= A + D)
$168 = F
Calculated rate of Income Related Rent on 14 April 2023
$150 = G
Rent charged as at 14 April 2023 (lesser of F and G)
$150

chunks.title: Client on the social housing register — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Client on the social housing register
A client on the register can get Accommodation Supplement or Accommodation Benefit until the day before their start date of the tenancy in a social housing property.
## Client living in social housing
An applicable person who is living in a property owned or managed by a social housing provider, cannot get Accommodation Supplement or Accommodation Benefit.
A client paying a contribution to someone to live in a social housing may be able to get an Accommodation Supplement based on the amount they pay.
A client who is paying rent to a registered community housing provider for a property that is not contracted for Income Related Rent purposes can get Accommodation Supplement.

chunks.title: Applications for Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Applications for Income Related Rent
When a prospective tenant applies for social housing, details of their assessable income and additional occupant contributions are recorded during their assessment for social housing. These details are used to calculate an indicative weekly rate of Income Related Rent.
An indicative rate of Income Related Rent is a rate based on the prospective tenant and their partner's (if any) circumstances at the time they complete the assessment.
The indicative rate of Income Related Rent is not provided to the housing provider.
The rate may change when the prospective tenant is placed into a property if their circumstances have changed since applying. Prospective tenants are obliged to advise of changes in circumstances while they are on the register.
Calculating an indicative rate of Income Related Rent for a prospective tenant:
- provides an opportunity to identify the most appropriate housing option for a prospective tenantFor example, if the indicative rate is greater than the lower quartile market rent in the prospective tenant's preferred location, they may be better renting in the private market
- ensures all current assessable income and additional occupant contribution details required are held and
- allows us to advise the prospective tenant what further verification is required to confirm the rate at placement
The rate of Income Related Rent will be confirmed at placement, when MSD is satisfied that:
- a prospective tenant has declared their correct income details
- a correct rate of Income Related Rent can be calculated and
- the client wants to apply for an Income Related Rent
The housing provider is then notified of the rate of Income Related Rent.
The client is eligible to pay Income Related Rent from the commencement of the tenancy (the start date).

chunks.title: Assessable assets — income related rent
chunks.text: Assessable assets are assets of applicable people that can be easily converted into cash and include: - bills of exchange or promissory notes - building society shares - money in bank accounts, including fixed and term deposits with any bank, friendly society, credit union, or building society - money invested with or lent to any bank, or other financial institution - money withdrawn from a KiwiSaver scheme - mortgage investments and other long-term loans - shares, stocks, debentures, bonus bonds and bonds - the client's share in any partnership - prepaid funeral expenses (in some circumstances) - proceeds from the sale of the family home

chunks.title: Not included as assessable assets — income related rent
chunks.text: Assessable assets do not include: - personal effects - motor vehicle principally used by the client for private use - a caravan, boat or other vehicle with a net equity less than $2,000 or which is used by the person or a member of their family for day to day accommodation - Crown funds provided directly to clients to purchase Support Services and Direct Disability Support payments - MSD lump sum payments for the first 12 months after the payment is made - funds locked into KiwiSaver and other retirement scheme accounts - Māori land when the title is in tribal trust and individual ownership cannot be identified, the client cannot realise or readily convert the land into a cash asset - Christchurch mosques attack support payments - Payments of Accommodation Supplement arrears due to a system processing error from 1993 to 2014 for the first 12 months after payment is made - Payments of arrears to Special Benefit clients better off on Temporary Additional Support for the first 12 months after payment is made - Payments to clients whose Kāinga Ora tenancy was terminated due to methamphetamine contamination for the first 12 months after payment is made - Residential Care Subsidy historic review refunds for the first 12 months after the payment is made - specified Ex gratia and compensation payments - FamilyBoost Tax Credit payments for the first 12 months after payment is received Note a bank overdraft is not considered a cash asset or resource available to a client. Canterbury earthquake related payments Payments made by the Crown, Earthquake Commission, insurance companies or the Canterbury Earthquake Commission (Red Cross) relating to the Canterbury earthquake are generally excluded for the first 12 or 24 months following the date the client got the payment.

chunks.title: Information share Child Support — income related rent
chunks.text: When a client is getting information share Child Support payments MSD must determine whether the payments are considered a cash asset or assessable income. The cash asset exemption for the period the information share Child Support is being charged for income-tested financial assistance does not apply to social housing. In most cases, Child Support will be considered assessable income rather than a cash asset because it's paid for an income related purpose, and is likely to be used over the payment period.

chunks.title: Assessable income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Assessable income
Assessable income is the income used in the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent.
The assessable income is the estimate of a client's net weekly income (i.e. after tax) from all sources, and after the deduction of any Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) premiums or levies.
Assessable income includes:
- assessable income of applicable people, including income from assessable assets and
- a portion of the family tax credit, if the applicable people are entitled to get it
Note:
- Contributions from additional occupants are not included as assessable income. When calculating Income Related Rent, 62% of the total contributions are added to the calculated rent amount. For more information see: Contributions from additional occupants.
- Best Start tax credit and in-work tax credit are not included as assessable income
- from 1 July 2023, most types of Child Support are included as assessable income. For more information see: Child Support included as assessable income from 1 July 2023
## Combined income sources
The total amount of assessable income of all applicable people is included in determining the assessable income.

chunks.title: Assessing the amount of deprived asset — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Assessing the amount of deprived asset
The assessed amount of deprived asset is the actual value of the asset or the part of the asset that the applicable person has deprived themselves of.
The amount of the deprived asset must be included as assessable asset.
For example, if the client has sold a property for less than its value, then the difference between the amount received and the actual value would be the amount of the deprived asset.
If you consider deprivation has occurred, contact Helpline for advice.
For more information see:
- Assessing the amount of deprived income
- Deprivation of income
- Examples of deprivation of income

chunks.title: Assessing the amount of deprived income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Assessing the amount of deprived income
If deprivation of income has occurred and the deprived income is to be counted back in, then, generally the assessed amount of deprived income is the actual amount of income that the person has deprived themselves of or has previously been assessed to contribute.
The amount of the deprived income must be included as assessable income.
For example if money previously invested is transferred to a non-income earning account then the amount previously being earned on the investment would be deemed the deprived income.
If you consider deprivation has occurred, contact Helpline for advice.
For more information see:
- Assessing the amount of deprived asset
- Deprivation of income
- Examples of deprivation of income

chunks.title: Asset thresholds and formula to work out assessable income from assets — income related rent
chunks.text: The thresholds for income from assessable assets are: Household type Asset threshold Sole tenant household(a single client who has no spouse or partner and no dependent children) $2,700 All other household types $5,400 Only income from assets over the asset threshold is included as assessable income. If an applicable person has assets under the threshold, and those assets are earning interest, you should not charge this as income.

chunks.title: Formula to work out assessable income from assets — income related rent
chunks.text: The formula to determine the appropriate amounts is as follows: Step 1: Work out the after tax weekly amount of any actual income acquired from the asset: - get the total value of the assessable assets - get the total annual after tax income of the asset - divide the income amount by the asset amount = A - minus total amount of the asset by the appropriate asset threshold = B - multiply A by B - divide this amount by 52 Step 2: Work out the estimated value of any income from the asset you should: - get the total value of the asset - minus the applicable asset threshold - multiply this amount by 0.0284 or 2.84% - divide this amount by 52 Step 3: whichever is the greater amount should be included as assessable income for Income Related Rent purposes.

chunks.title: Example of determining income from assets — income related rent
chunks.text: John is a single client who has mortgage investments worth $80,000. John receives $734 after tax in dividends from the investment each year. The asset threshold for John is $2,700. Calculate the assessable income as follows: Determine the amount to include as assessable income Rate per week Step 1: Total value of the assets $80,000 = A Total annual after tax income of the asset $734.00 = B Divide the income amount by the asset amount (= B divided by A). This will give you the income per $1 of asset. $0.009 = C Minus total amount of the asset by the applicable asset threshold (= A minus $2,700) $77,300 = D Multiply C by D $695.70 = E Divide E by 52 $13.37 = F Step 2: Total value of the assets $80,000 = G Minus the applicable asset threshold (= G minus $2,700) $77,300 = H Multiply 0.0284 or 2.84% by H $2,195.32 = I Divide I by 52 $42.21 = J Get the greater amount of F or J $42.21 = weekly amount to include in assessable income

chunks.title: Deprivation of income — income related rent
chunks.text: Where a client has directly or indirectly deprived themselves of property, you can consider adjusting the value of their assessable assets.

chunks.title: Incomplete application - information received later — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Incomplete application - information received later
You may consider backdating a client's application for Income Related Rent to an earlier date when you get information at a later date.
You need to be satisfied that all necessary information has been received and it is correct.
You may backdate to any date between the date of the earlier incomplete application and the date the full and correct information is received.
Example
Maria was placed into a property on 8 October 2022, her application for Income Related Rent was incomplete, and Kāinga Ora charged the market rent for the property. Maria provides information on 5 November 2022 but the information is only full and correct from 22 October 2022.
In this situation the Income Related Rent should be backdated to 22 October 2022 as that is the earliest date that it can be properly calculated from.
## Backdating when no earlier application for Income Related Rent made
You may consider backdating an application for Income Related Rent to an earlier date (when a client never made an earlier application) if you are satisfied that:
- all necessary information to calculate the Income Related Rent as at that earlier date has been received and
- the information is correct and
- it was unreasonable in the circumstances to expect the application to have been made earlier

chunks.title: Being satisfied that a lower rate was appropriate — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Being satisfied that a lower rate was appropriate
You may consider backdating to an earlier date if you are satisfied that a lower rate was appropriate because:
- all necessary information to calculate a new rate of Income Related Rent as at that earlier date has been received and
- that information is accurate and
- where it was unreasonable to expect the information to have been provided earlier
Before issuing a refund, you must confirm with the client's housing provider whether the client has paid the previously calculated rate of rent over the refund period. You then need to decide whether to issue the refund to the tenant or housing provider.
For more information see:
- Deciding who the refund should be paid to
## Refund period
The refund period is from:
- the start date of the tenancy, but cannot be any earlier or
- the date that full and correct information was subsequently provided or
- the rent charge date following the date the change in circumstance occurred
The refund period is to the day prior to the rent effective date that the correct rate of Income Related Rent was applied.
Note a manager client service delivery or service manager client service support must approve all refund decisions over $3000.
## Refund amount
The refund is the difference between the higher rate of Income Related Rent previously calculated (that generally, the client has been required to pay in rent to their housing provider), and the new lower calculated rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Assessable income includes the following forms of assistance — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Assessable income includes the following forms of assistance
- Emergency Benefit
- Emergency Maintenance Allowance
- Jobseeker Support
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship
- Sole Parent Support
- Supported Living Payment
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veterans Pension
- Student Allowance
## Assessable income does not include
- Orphans Benefit
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Student Loan (all components)
- Military decoration payments
- Surviving spouse pension
- War Pensions
- Extra help including but not limited to: Accommodation SupplementChild Disability AllowanceDisability AllowanceParticipation AllowanceSeasonal Work AssistanceTemporary Additional Support
- Accommodation Supplement
- Child Disability Allowance
- Disability Allowance
- Participation Allowance
- Seasonal Work Assistance
- Temporary Additional Support
- Accommodation Benefit (paid with a Student Allowance for students who qualify)
Note Accommodation Supplement and Accommodation Benefit are included in the affordability assessment.
## Payments reduced due to deductions or sanctions
If an applicable person is getting a benefit, New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and the payment is reduced because of any deductions or sanctions (e.g. court fines or MSD debt), their assessable income must include the rate of assistance before any deductions are made or sanctions applied.
## Payment reduced due to income
If an applicable person is getting a benefit, or New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension with a grandparented non-qualified partner, and has income that reduces the rate payable, their assessable income must include the rate of assistance after the reduction for income is applied.

chunks.title: Calculating new rate for client paying market rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Calculating new rate for client paying market rent
Where a client that has been paying rent at the market rent rate has a change in circumstance (such as finishing employment) and you have sufficient information to determine the client's assessable income, you can calculate the rate of Income Related Rent.
Note a client in these situations does not need to have an assessment for eligibility completed.
For more information see:
- Examples of notice periods for housing provider to increase the rent
- Increasing the rate of Income Related Rent to the market rent rate

chunks.title: Calculating rate using household income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Calculating rate using household income
Generally, the rate calculated using the household's income will be higher than the rate calculated using the applicable Jobseeker Support rate when an applicable person is receiving:
- income from sources other than benefit assistance
- benefit assistance or
- benefit assistance and other income
Note if an applicable person is getting a reduced rate of benefit, due to income MSD must include the reduced rate of benefit (before any deductions are made or sanctions applied, e.g. court fines or MSD debt) and any other assessable income.
## Calculation formula
The rate of Income Related Rent calculated using the household income is the amount that is the total of:
- 25% of the assessable income, at or below the income threshold and
- 50% of the assessable income above the income threshold plus
- a portion of the tenant's and their partner's family tax credit entitlement plus
- 62% of contributions from additional occupants
Note the rate of Income Related Rent calculated is rounded down to the nearest dollar.

chunks.title: Calculating rate using Jobseeker Support rate — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Calculating rate using Jobseeker Support rate
Generally, the rate calculated using the applicable Jobseeker Support rate will be higher than the rate calculated using the household income when an applicable person is:
- not receiving any income or
- receiving income equal to or less than the applicable rate of Jobseeker Support
This calculation produces the minimum calculated rate of Income Related Rent.
## Calculation formula
The rate of Income Related Rent calculated using Jobseeker Support is:
- 25% of the net amount of the applicable rate of Jobseeker Support for the household type, plus
- a portion of the applicable person's family tax credit entitlement but not including any Best Start tax credits, plus
- 62% of contributions from additional occupants
Note the rate of Income Related Rent calculated is rounded down to the nearest dollar.
## Tenants aged under 20 years
For clients aged under 20 years, use the Jobseeker Support "single 20 - 24 years" rate.

chunks.title: Calculation of Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Calculation of Income Related Rent
The rate of Income Related Rent is calculated using either:
- the applicable rate of Jobseeker Support or
- the household income
whichever is the higher.
The rate of Income Related Rent needs to be calculated using both methods and then the higher rate selected.
For more information see:
- Calculating rate using Jobseeker Support rate
- Calculating rate using household income
- Rent rate charged is different from calculated rate
- Examples of calculating the rate of Income Related Rent

chunks.title: Cash assets gifted — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Cash assets gifted
An applicable person is not able to directly or indirectly deprive themselves of any income.
You can generally allow a client to gift small amounts of money to others. However, large sums of money gifted by a client should be treated as an assessable asset for Income Related Rent purposes.
There may be circumstances where any amount gifted (whether large or small) can be considered as an assessable asset.
## Guidelines
Generally, if an applicable person has gifted any sum of money in the last year over the asset thresholds, then the amount is treated as an assessable asset.
As a guideline, you should annually reduce the value of the gift by $1000 for a single client or couple without children and $2000 for a sole parent or a couple with one or more dependent children.
Example
A gift of $4000 was gifted by a single person. The next year this becomes $3000, then $2000 the following year and is then disregarded as an assessable asset from the third year as it is below the exemption level.

chunks.title: Ceasing employment — income related rent
chunks.text: If an applicable person is made redundant or is ceasing employment, a breakdown of their final pay is required. Payments received by an applicable person at the time they stop work are used when determining when the employment ceased and are included as assessable income. This includes: - holiday pay - sick pay - long service leave - pay in lieu of notice - pay in lieu of accumulated leave - payments made on the completion of fixed term contracts - bonus or gratuity payments - retirement payments

chunks.title: Redundancy pay — income related rent
chunks.text: Redundancy payments are not classed as income and are not included in determining the date employment ceased. However, any unused amount of redundancy payment must be included as an assessable asset for Income Related Rent purposes. Note income from assessable assets over the asset threshold is to be included as assessable income. See:

chunks.title: Determining when employment ceased — income related rent
chunks.text: Find out the number of days represented by the payments received and the last day the client worked. If the number of days represented is not clearly shown on the verification provided, you will need to estimate the period that the payments would cover using the most appropriate of the following formula: Formula 1 - Determine the assessable income from employment over the last 52 weeks of employment - Divide by 52 weeks = weekly rate of pay - Divide by 5 days = the daily rate of pay - Confirm total amount of holiday pay and other appropriate payments from the verification provided - Divide this amount by the daily rate of pay and round down to the nearest whole day = number of days pay - Add the number of days pay to the last day the client worked. This is the date of change in circumstanceNote do not count Saturdays and Sundays - use Monday to Friday weekdays only. If a client stopped work on a Friday, add the days from the following Monday. If the client has not worked with the employer for 52 weeks or more before their last day of work, you may use the pay received over the period of employment and appropriate number of weeks of employment in the calculation. Formula 2 - Determine the assessable income from the employment over last 4 weeks of employment - Divide by 20 (number of working days in 4 weeks) = daily rate of pay - Confirm total amount of holiday pay and other appropriate payments from the verification provided - Divide this amount by the daily rate of pay and round down to the nearest whole day = number of days pay - Add the number of days pay to the last day the client worked. This is the date of change in circumstanceNote do not count Saturdays and Sundays - use Monday to Friday weekdays only. If a client stopped work on a Friday, add the days from the following Monday. Only calculate the period covered by holiday pay using the client's last 4 weeks of income if it does not disadvantage the client. If the income earned in the last 4 weeks does not reflect what the client normally earned, you may need to use the pay received over a longer period of employment and appropriate number of weeks of employment. Note a change to the calculated rate of Income Related Rent cannot be activated until the date the change in circumstance occurs.

chunks.title: Example of determining when employment ceased — income related rent
chunks.text: The client had been earning $320 net per week but stopped working from Friday 7 April 2023 and received $640 net in holiday pay. This is the equivalent of 2 weeks' pay and, therefore, the date the client ceased employment would be considered to be Friday 21 April 2023. You would continue to include $320 net per week as assessable income for the period Monday 10 April 2023 to Friday 21 April 2023. Note a change to the calculated rate of Income Related Rent cannot be activated until the date the change in circumstance occurs.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — income related rent
chunks.text: Generally, clients must tell MSD within 14 calendar days of any change in their circumstances or their family's situation that may affect their calculated rate of Income Related Rent. This includes changes to assessable income, additional occupant contributions and the people living in the property. It is the client's responsibility to advise the change in circumstances of all applicable people. This includes changes in the client's circumstances or their partner's circumstances. Generally, clients waiting to be allocated social housing must advise us straight away of any change in their circumstances that may affect their eligibility for social housing or the particular property they need. All tenants in social housing also generally have a duty to advise us straight away of any change in their circumstances that may affect their continued eligibility for social housing or need for the particular property they are renting. Note clients do not need to advise MSD when they get, or have a change to information share Child Support payments.

chunks.title: Review due to a change in circumstances — income related rent
chunks.text: When an applicable person has a change in circumstance MSD will need to decide whether the change affects the rate of Income Related Rent. The change in circumstance may result in a change to the household type, additional occupant contributions or the assessable income - which may in turn affect the rate of Income Related Rent calculated. The client may be contacted to confirm their circumstances. If the client's circumstances: - can be confirmed, a decision may be made to not change the rate of Income Related Rent as a change to the rate would not make a material difference - can be confirmed, a decision may be made to increase or decrease the rate of Income Related Rent - cannot be confirmed, a decision may be made whether to increase the rate of Income Related Rent to the market rent rate Note not all changes in circumstances affect the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent, for example: - if the tenant has 3 dependent children and 1 leaves care, this would not result in a change to the tenant's household type - if the tenant's last dependent child turns 18 and is no longer continuing in education or financially dependent, this would result in a change to the tenant's household type

chunks.title: Child Support is assessable income at next review — income related rent
chunks.text: From 1 July 2023, most types of Child Support are included as assessable income when calculating the rate of Income Related Rent. For tenants in social housing, only Child Support that covers a payment or liability period on or after 1 July 2023 is included as assessable income when calculating the rate of Income Related Rent. Child Support is only included as assessable income at their next Income Related Rent annual review or unrelated change in circumstances on or after 1 July 2023.

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
If a client has told MSD before being absent from New Zealand that they are going to be absent for up to 8 weeks, it is not considered to be a permanent change in circumstances and they can have the same rate of Income Related Rent during the period of the absence.
After 8 weeks the rate of Income Related Rent should be reviewed.
If a client does not tell MSD they are going to be absent from New Zealand before they leave, the rate of Income Related Rent should be reviewed straight away.
## Reviewing the rate of Income Related Rent
The rate of Income Related Rent needs to be reviewed to confirm that the client's circumstances have not changed when the client has not told MSD they are going to be absent from New Zealand or when an advised absence has been 8 weeks or more.
If the client's circumstances:
- cannot be confirmed, you will need to decide whether to increase the rate of Income Related Rent to the market rent rate
- can be confirmed, you will need to decide whether to increase, decrease or retain the rate of Income Related Rent
When there is more than one applicable person in the household, whichever person is absent from New Zealand may be removed from the household type when the absence is permanent (that is longer than 8 weeks).
Note a signatory to the Tenancy Agreement must not be removed from the household until the housing provider has confirmed they have been released from the agreement.
If the client's partner is absent from New Zealand, you should review the rate of Income Related Rent from the date the assessable income changed or the date the partner left New Zealand - whichever is the later.
## Notifying the housing provider
The housing provider will be notified by MSD the client is absent from New Zealand when MSD is aware that this is the case and considers the change to be permanent.
The housing provider can decided whether to end or change a tenancy.
Housing providers have their own policies on tenants being absent from the property they are renting.

chunks.title: Annual general adjustment and assessable income — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Annual general adjustment and assessable income
A change in income due to the annual general adjustment is not included as assessable income until the next review of a client's Income Related Rent. This could be when there is:
- a change in circumstances review (eg a review due to a permanent change in income which is a material difference) or
- an annual review
## Annual reviews
A client's Income Related Rent may change at annual review, due to the annual general adjustment. When this happens, the housing provider will be notified of the annual review processing date.
The housing provider cannot increase the rent until the earliest rent effective date following the 60-day notice period.
## Increase to Income Related Rent income thresholds
The Income Related Rent income thresholds increase when there is an annual general adjustment of New Zealand Superannuation. This is because the income thresholds are calculated using a net rate of New Zealand Superannuation, shown in the table below.
Category
Income threshold
Sole tenant household (a single client who has no spouse or partner and no dependent children)
$555.15
(the net weekly single living alone rate of New Zealand Superannuation as at 1 April 2026)
All other household types
$854.08
(2x $427.04, the net weekly half-couple rate of New Zealand Superannuation as at 1 April 2026)
For some non-beneficiary clients, their Income Related Rent may decrease if their income threshold increases. This is because more of their assessable income will be below their Income Related Rent income threshold.
These clients will have their Income Related Rent reviewed at the next available review after the annual general adjustment. This will usually be when there is:
- a change in circumstances review or
- an annual review
If the client is due a refund because of the increase to the Income Related Rent income threshold, this refund should be backdated up to 1 April at the earliest (the date the income threshold changed).

chunks.title: Annual review of Income Related Rent — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Annual review of Income Related Rent
The annual review process ensures that a review of the calculated rate of Income Related Rent is completed every year, and that correct information is held about applicable people.
The annual review is a review of the calculated rate of Income Related Rent. It is not a review of the client's eligibility for social housing.
Clients must complete the annual review process within the 5-week period before the next scheduled review date. If a client does not do this, their Income Related Rent may increase.
## All clients in social housing complete an annual review
MSD may review a person's Income Related Rent at any time and this is done at least annually. The annual review is completed by all applicable people, including clients paying rent at the market rent rate, to prevent:
- an incorrect rate of Income Related Rent being calculated
- a client incorrectly having a rate of Income Related Rent calculated when they should be paying rent at the market rent rate and / or
- housing providers charging rent at the market rent rate to clients who are eligible for a lower rate of Income Related Rent
A client can choose not to participate in the annual review process and decide not to have their rate of Income Related Rent calculated.

chunks.title: Annual review process — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Clients are given 5-weeks to complete the annual review process. If a client does not complete the review, their Income Related Rent may be increased. Note a client does not need to provide verification of any financial assistance that they are receiving from MSD.

chunks.title: Initial notice letter to complete annual review — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: All social housing clients are automatically sent an initial notice letter informing them that they need to complete an annual review. The letter and form will be sent 5-weeks before the client's next scheduled review date. The client has 5-weeks to complete the annual review. This allows sufficient time to complete the annual review without any effect on the rate of their Income Related Rent. If a client has not completed the annual review process a reminder letter will be sent 7-working days before the next scheduled review date. For more information see: - Examples of annual review periods - Next scheduled review date

chunks.title: Client completes the annual review and has had a change of income or household type — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Generally, you should follow the process for applying changes to an applicable person's rate of Income Related Rent in the same manner you would during the review of a change in circumstances. For more information see: - Income Related Rent Notifying a new rate of Income Related Rent - Income Related Rent Client must be given notice of rent increase - annual review When the change in income is due to the annual general adjustment to the rates of financial assistance paid by MSD there are some differences in the way you process the annual review. For more information see: - Annual general adjustment and assessable income

chunks.title: Reviewing clients with a grandparented rate of Income Related Rent — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: The abating cap amounts may reduce at annual review (and at a change in circumstances review). For more information see: - Grandparented rate for Kāinga Ora clients

chunks.title: Insufficient information to calculate a correct rate or client does not complete the annual review in 5 weeks — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: You may consider that you do not have sufficient information to process annual review when: - an applicant has not declared their correct or relevant income details or - an applicant has not completed to your satisfaction the annual review form or - an applicant has not returned their annual review form and - you have insufficient information available to calculate a correct rate of Income Related Rent If the information received from the client is insufficient to complete the annual review you should attempt to contact the client to request the required information. The client should be given 10 working days to provide the information. After 10 working days, follow the process for applying changes to an applicable person's rate of Income Related Rent. For more information see: - Income Related Rent Increasing the rate of Income Related Rent to the market rent rate - Income Related Rent Housing provider gives a 60-day notice period

chunks.title: Processing an annual review without an annual review form — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: When a client receiving financial assistance from MSD has not completed the annual review form correctly, or has not returned the form, you should consider whether the information MSD already holds is sufficient to complete the annual review. If you consider the information MSD hold is sufficient, you can use this information to complete the annual review and you do not need to request more information or verification from the client.

chunks.title: Notifying the housing provider of the correct date — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: At the annual review of the rate of Income Related Rent, the housing provider will be notified of: - the processing date of the annual review, if the Income Related Rent changes are as a result of the annual general adjustment - the date of the change in circumstances, if the Income Related Rent changes are as a result of a change in circumstances processed at the annual review

chunks.title: Appeal Authority process — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Appeal Authority process
Step 1. Client's application for appeal is sent direct to the Social Security Appeal Authority.
Step 2. The Social Security Appeal Authority advises the appropriate MSD Appeals officer.
Step 3. Appeals officer advises and obtains relevant information from the business unit or office that made the original decision.
Step 4. Appeals officer completes report in accordance with the relevant regulations under the Public and Community Housing Management Act 1992 and Part 7 Reviews and appeals of the Social Security Act 2018.
Step 5. The Social Security Appeal Authority sets a hearing date. The hearing can be heard in person or on papers only. The MSD appeals officer or solicitor will represent MSD at the hearing. The staff member who made the original decision may be required to give evidence.
Step 6. The Social Security Appeal Authority will advise MSD and the client of the outcome.
Step 7. The appeals officer will advise the appropriate staff member of any benefit action to be taken.

chunks.title: Appeals to the Social Security Appeal Authority — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Appeals to the Social Security Appeal Authority
A client can appeal to the Social Security Appeal Authority when the Benefits Review Committee has upheld or upheld in part a decision of MSD including decisions in respect of:
- the assessment or re-assessment of: their eligibility or continued eligibility for social housingtheir housing needs
- their eligibility or continued eligibility for social housing
- their housing needs
- the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent
- the establishment and recovery of Income Related Rent debt
A client's application for appeal should be sent directly to the Social Security Appeal Authority.
Note when the Benefits Review Committee has declined to hear an out of time Review of Decision and the client applies for the matter to be heard by the Social Security Appeal Authority, forward the case to the Appeal Authority.

chunks.title: Change in additional occupant contributions — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Change in additional occupant contributions
Income Related Rent should be reviewed when an applicable person has a change in the contributions they get from additional occupants that is permanent (8 weeks or more).
Generally:
- a change in circumstances that will result in an increase in Income Related Rent will not be considered permanent until it has lasted 8 weeks or more
- a change in circumstances that will result in a decrease in Income Related Rent will be considered permanent when it is likely to last or has lasted 8 weeks or more
For more information see:
- Contributions from additional occupants
## Variable contributions
If a client gets variable payments the rate of Income Related Rent does not need to be reviewed each time they change, unless it is considered that the change in income:
- is a permanent change which lasts longer than 8 weeks and
- will make a material difference to the Income Related Rent when compared to the previous weekly estimate of assessable income
## Determining if a change in variable contributions is permanent
To determine if a change in variable payments is permanent, the payments from the last 16 weeks need to be considered.
If their average weekly payments from the most recent 8 weeks is different to the average weekly payments for the 8 weeks before that, the change should be considered permanent.
For example, the change would be determined to be permanent when a client with variable payments had an average amount over the most recent 8 weeks of $580 per week, and their weekly payments over the 8 weeks before that period was $510.
For more information see:
- Deciding if changes are permanent or temporary
- Material difference to the rate of Income Related Rent
## Mismatch of information
When the additional occupant who pays the contribution gets Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, MSD will check the details match what information is held. Where there is a mismatch of information, the mismatch process must be followed.
For more information see:
- Mismatch of additional occupant contributions and accommodation costs

chunks.title: Change in assessable income — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Assessable income can be reviewed when an applicable person has a change in income that is permanent (8 weeks or more). Generally: - a change in circumstances that will result in an increase in Income Related Rent will not be considered permanent until it has lasted 8 weeks or more - a change in circumstances that will result in a decrease in Income Related Rent will be considered permanent when it is likely to last or has lasted 8 weeks or more

chunks.title: Ceased work — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: When a client ceases work the rate of Income Related Rent should be reviewed if it is a permanent change in circumstances (i.e. where they are not expected to return to work within the next 8 weeks).

chunks.title: Variable income — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Some clients such as seasonal, self-employed, or casual workers can have varied or fluctuating income. If a client has variable income the rate of the Income Related Rent does not need to be reviewed each time the client's or their partner's (if any) income changes, unless it is considered that the change in income: - is a permanent change which lasts longer than 8 weeks and - will make a material difference to the Income Related Rent when compared to the previous weekly estimate of assessable income

chunks.title: Determining if a change in variable income is permanent — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: To determine if a change in a client's income is permanent when their weekly income is variable, their income from the last 16 weeks needs to be considered. If their average weekly income from the most recent 8 weeks is different to the average weekly income for the 8 weeks before that, the change should be considered permanent. For example, the change would be determined to be permanent when a client with variable earnings had an average income over the most recent 8 weeks of $580 per week, and their weekly income over the 8 weeks before that period was $510.

chunks.title: Net income from benefits — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Benefit rates are reviewed and adjusted as soon as there is a change of income and this can be as frequently as a weekly adjustment. Assessable income for Income Related Rent purposes uses a future estimate of weekly income and is only adjusted when a change in circumstance is permanent and will make a material difference. Where a client is receiving a benefit, the income charged against a benefit may not be the same income amount used as assessable income for calculating the rate of Income Related Rent at any given point in time. At the time a review of the rate of Income Related Rent is completed, the current weekly benefit rate needs to be obtained. The rate that is included as assessable income depends on whether the client is getting income in addition to their benefit. If a client is earning income: - under the benefit income thresholds, the benefit rate to include is the benefit rate the client is getting or - over the benefit income thresholds, the benefit rate to include is an average benefit rate (over an appropriate period)

chunks.title: Client and partner separate — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Client and partner separate
When a couple are paying Income Related Rent, if a client and their partner separate, the partner will be removed from the household type as the change to the relationship is considered as a permanent change.
Whenever a partner is removed from the household type you must review the Income Related Rent.
You must reassess the Income Related Rent from the date of the change in circumstances, which is the date:
- the partner no longer resides at the property or
- the assessable income reduced
whichever is the later.
The rate of Income Related Rent should be the rate calculated using the new household type.
Note a signatory to the Tenancy Agreement must not be removed from the household type until the housing provider has confirmed they have been released from the agreement. If the client and the partner are both on the Tenancy Agreement, the person leaving the tenancy must tell the housing provider, and be released from the agreement before they are removed from the household.
## Client and partner start relationship
If a client advises they are in a relationship you should review the Income Related Rent from the date the relationship started.
The partner's assessable income is included in the calculation of the new rate of Income Related Rent.
The client may make a request to their housing provider for their partner to be included into the Tenancy Agreement as a signatory.
If the partner will not be a signatory to the Tenancy Agreement, they can generally still be included in the household type.
## Notifying the housing provider
The housing provider will be notified by MSD when there has been a change in the client's relationship and MSD is aware this is the case.
The housing provider may decide on whether to end or change a tenancy.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
Generally, clients must tell MSD within 14 calendar days of any change in their circumstances or their family's situation that may affect their calculated rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Child changes in circumstances — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Any change to the circumstances of a dependent child may affect the household type or the rate of Income Related Rent, especially if it is the only dependent child included in the household.

chunks.title: Dependent child not living at home — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: If a dependent child is no longer living in the social housing property, for example, because they are attending boarding school, the rate of Income Related Rent is not reviewed unless the child is no longer considered to be dependent. The child will still be considered a dependent child if the client pays for some of the costs including school fees, pocket money, clothing or travel, and the child returns to the client for some of the school holidays.

chunks.title: Child turns 16 — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Where a child aged 16 or 17 leaves school or tertiary education, they can still be included in the household type if the child remains a dependent child. If they become financially independent they will no longer be a dependent child and would be excluded from the household type.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: If a dependent child turns 18 the rate of Income Related Rent is reviewed if they are no longer considered to be dependent. The child would be excluded from the household type. An 18-year-old child is still considered to be a dependent child for a limited period if MSD is satisfied they are: - continuing in education and - not financially independent

chunks.title: Additional child for a tenant or partner with no other dependent children — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Following the birth of a child or a dependent child coming into care, the rate of Income Related Rent may need to be reviewed. The child would be included in the household type. Note if the client or partner has other dependent children included in their care, this would not change the household type, but MSD must update the client's record and complete a review, due to the change in circumstances to check the rate of Income Related Rent is correct.

chunks.title: Dependent child starts work — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: A dependent child's income from personal earnings is not included as assessable income, providing the child still meets the definition of dependent child.

chunks.title: Client has other dependent children — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Not all child changes in circumstances affect the household type and therefore the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent. For example, if the tenant or their partner has three children and one leaves their care or is no longer a dependent child, this would not result in a change to the household type. MSD must update the client's record and complete a review due to the change in circumstances, to check the rate of Income Related Rent is correct.

chunks.title: Client advises change of circumstances of another tenant — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Client advises change of circumstances of another tenant
If a client advises of a change in circumstances of another tenant, you must try to contact the other tenant to confirm the information received.
If the information received affects another tenant's financial assistance being paid by MSD, you must contact the other tenant to confirm the information received before you process the change.
## Exception
If MSD already holds information about the other tenant (as the other tenant is a beneficiary) then you may use the existing information (when appropriate).
## Client reviews a decision made due to a change in circumstances of another tenant
A client may lodge a Review of Decision where the rate of Income Related Rent has changed due to a change in circumstances of another tenant or partner (if any).
The client who lodged the review may ask to see information the other tenant provided, and they may access this information.
You must make sure the other tenant is only provided with information relevant to the decision the client is reviewing.

chunks.title: Client no longer requires a particular property — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Client no longer requires a particular property
If a client no longer requires a particular property they will need to contact their housing provider.
The housing provider must confirm that a tenancy has ended before MSD can stop paying the Income Related Rent Subsidy or calculating the rate of Income Related Rent.
Sometimes, a client may contact us to request a transfer to another property that will suit their housing needs better.

chunks.title: Client no longer wants a rate of Income Related Rent calculated — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Client no longer wants a rate of Income Related Rent calculated
A client can decide not to have a rate of Income Related Rent calculated.
When a client advises that they do not want a rate of Income Related Rent calculated, you should discuss with the client their reasons why and ask them if they are considering moving from the social housing property.
The client will continue to be eligible for social housing and you should increase their rate of Income Related Rent to the rate equal to the market rent rate.
Note clients, who do not have a rate of Income Related Rent calculated for them, are still required to complete an annual review of Income Related Rent.
For more information see:
- Increasing the rate of Income Related Rent to market rent rate
- Annual review of Income Related Rent
- Change in circumstances

chunks.title: Acknowledge the client's request to withdraw — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Acknowledge the client's request to withdraw
You need to acknowledge the client's request to withdraw their application for Review of Decision in writing. There is a template letter available for you to do this on HIYA ROD.
For more information see:
- When to advise a client of their right to review
- Who can apply for a review or appeal
- Review of Decision [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Clients with suspended or expired benefit records — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Clients with suspended or expired benefit records
Assessable income can be reviewed when an applicable person has a permanent change in income.
Where an applicable person is getting a benefit and the benefit payments have reduced or stopped, the rate of Income Related Rent may be reviewed:
- when the client tells MSD of the change in circumstances or
- following the cancellation of the benefit
## Retrospective benefit review
When a client's benefit is reviewed and retrospectively adjusted, you may need to consider whether the rate of Income Related Rent needs to be reviewed.

chunks.title: Death of a sole tenant — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: On the death of a sole tenant the Tenancy Agreement terminates: - 21 days after the housing provider receives written notice from the tenant's next of kin of the tenant's death - 21 days after the housing provider gives the next of kin written notice to vacate the property - on a date agreed in writing by the landlord with the next of kin or - on the date determined as the termination date by the Tenancy Tribunal whichever is earliest. MSD must have confirmation from the housing provider before they can stop paying the Income Related Rent Subsidy or calculating the rate of Income Related Rent. The rate of and entitlement to an Income Related Rent would not be reviewed until the earliest of the above dates.

chunks.title: Sole tenant — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: A person is a sole tenant when they are the only tenant on the Tenancy Agreement. This does not necessarily mean they are the sole occupant of the property. However, no other people living in the property (such as additional occupants or other people) have ongoing rights to stay in the property after the tenant's death. For example, the adult children of a tenant living in a house do not have the right to the tenancy after their parent passes away unless they are on the Tenancy Agreement. For more information see: - Assessment of eligibility Death of a sole tenant

chunks.title: Death of a joint tenant — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: For the purposes of Income Related Rent, on the death of a joint tenant, the deceased person will be removed from the household type. Whenever a person is removed from the household type you must review the Income Related Rent for the remaining tenant(s). You must reassess the Income Related Rent from the date: - the tenant(s) assessable income reduced or - the deceased tenant died whichever is the later. The rate of Income Related Rent should be the rate calculated using the new household type. Exclude the deceased tenant's income from the date they died. Note the remaining tenant(s) must advise the housing provider of the death of a joint tenant and request a change to their Tenancy Agreement. If a tenant considers the property is no longer suitable for them to stay in, they may contact their housing provider in the first instance to request a transfer to another property that better suits their housing needs. The housing provider may refer the client to MSD to request a new assessment of housing need. For more information see: - Assessment of eligibility Death of a joint tenant MSD will tell the housing provider when there is a change to the rate of the Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Income Related Rent refunds — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Any remaining refund due to the client needs to be made to the tenant's estate. This is as it is money legally owed to the deceased, and the estate can legally pursue it. For more information see: - Deciding who the refund should be paid to

chunks.title: Notifying the housing provider — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: When MSD is aware a client has died they will let the housing provider know.

chunks.title: Ending Income Related Rent or Income Related Rent Subsidy — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Ending Income Related Rent or Income Related Rent Subsidy
MSD must have confirmation from the housing provider that a tenancy has ended before they can stop paying the Income Related Rent Subsidy or calculating the rate of Income Related Rent.
The tenancy will end at the:
- end of the notice period given by either the tenant or the housing provider or
- date specified in a termination order, if any, from the Tenancy Tribunal
Generally, the tenancy end date should align with the last rent charge date, however in some cases the last rent payment may be for a partial period.
The tenant is responsible for rent payments until the end of the notice period.
## Notice period to vacate a property
The notice to vacate a property begins when either the housing provider or the tenant receives written notice to vacate.
If a housing provider gives notice to vacate a property, the notice period is usually 90 days. However, shorter notice periods are possible in some cases.
When a tenant wishes to vacate a property, the notice period is usually 28 days.
However, shorter notice periods are possible in some cases, for example, a 2-day notice period can be given when the property is deemed uninhabitable, unless the Tenancy Agreement was breached.
A housing provider may also accept a shorter notice period when written notice is provided following verbal notice.

chunks.title: Example 1 — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Insufficient information to calculate a correct rate Jason was sent his annual review form on 14 April 2023, 5 weeks before his next scheduled review date of 19 May 2023. Jason currently pays Income Related Rent calculated at $150 per week and is paying rent to Kāinga Ora weekly on a Thursday (the rent charge date). The market rent rate for the property is $220 per week. Jason does not return his annual review form and MSD does not have any other recent information to verify his circumstances as there has been no contact since the last annual review, when the rent remained unchanged. MSD notifies the housing provider that Jason should be charged rent at the rate equal to the market rent rate for the property. Jason continues to not contact MSD. Week 1 Week 3 - Week 5 Week 6 - Week 7 Week 8 - Week 16 Week 17 14 April 2023 28 April 2023 19 May 2023 20 May 2023 22 May 2023 24 July 2023 31 July 2023 MSD sends initial notice to client to complete the annual review. MSD sends a reminder notice to client to complete the annual review. Next scheduled review date - review completed. MSD notifies housing provider that client should be charged rent at the market rent rate. Housing provider notifies the tenant of the change to their rent and the date that the new rate will apply from as soon as possible. Housing provider issues notice of change to rent amount. End of the 60-day notice period calculated by CMS. The new rent takes effect from the earliest rent effective date. The earliest rent effective date is the Thursday following the 60-day notice period CMS will calculate the 60-day period (+ service period + 1 system day) as 19 May 2023 to 24 July 2023.

chunks.title: Example 2 — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Sufficient information to calculate a correct rate, increase the rate of Income Related Rent Richard was sent his annual review form on 8 July 2023, 5 weeks before his next scheduled review date of 12 August 2023. Richard currently has a rate of Income Related Rent calculated at $89 per week and is paying rent to a community housing provider weekly on a Wednesday (the rent charge date). Richard returns his annual review forms on 27 July 2023 and advises his partner will be starting work on the 3 August 2023. MSD completes the annual review with no change to the rate of Income Related Rent. The information from the future change is recorded. The Income Related Rent is reassessed as $133 when the change is determined to be permanent at the appropriate 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start. Week 1 Week 3 Week 4 Week 6 Week 14 Week 22-23 8 July 2023 27 July 2023 3 August 2023 12 August 2023 7 October 2023 8 December 2023 9 December 2023 MSD send initial notice to client to complete the annual review. Annual review forms returned with information on a future change in circumstances - review completed (no change to Income Related Rent). Partner starts work 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start. Income Related Rent is not reviewed as there has not been a permanent change in circumstances - the income change from week 4 has not lasted for 8 weeks or more. Next 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start. MSD determines that the increase in income since 3 August 2023 is a permanent change, and reviews the client's Income Related Rent. Housing provider notifies the tenant of the change to their rent and the date that the new rate will apply from as soon as possible. End of 61-day period calculated by CMS. The new rent takes effect from the earliest rent effective date The earliest rent effective date is the Wednesday following the 61-day period. CMS will calculate the 61-day period (+ 1 system day) as 7 October 2023 to 8 December 2023.

chunks.title: Example 3 — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Sufficient information to calculate a correct rate, increase the rate of Income Related Rent Kerry was sent her annual review form on 4 August 2023, 5 weeks before her next scheduled review date of 8 September 2015. Kerry is paying rent to a community housing provider weekly on a Wednesday (the rent charge date) and her rent has not changed since the tenancy started over a year ago. Kerry returns her annual review forms on 17 August 2023. She has had no changes to her circumstances, but her Supported Living Payment has increased due to the annual general adjustment. MSD completes the annual review and activates an increase of the rate of Income Related Rent from the date they process the annual review. Week 1 Week 3 Week 4 - Week 12 Week 13 4 August 2023 17 August 2023 20 August 2023 21 August 2023 25 October 2023 28 October 2023 MSD send initial notice to client to complete the annual review Annual review forms returned Annual review forms processed - review completed Housing provider notified by MSD the rate of the Income Related Rent will increase due to an annual review, and the date of processing of the annual review. The housing provider notifies the tenant of the change to their rent and the date the new rate will apply from as soon as possible after the 60-day notice period. End of the 60-day notice period calculated by CMS. The new rent takes effect from the next rent effective date. The next rent effective date is the Wednesday following the 60-day notice period CMS will calculate the 60-day period (+ service period + 1 system day) as 20 August 2023 to 25 October 2023.

chunks.title: Hospitalisation or rest home care — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation or rest home care
If a client is going into hospital or rest home care for less than 8 weeks, they can have the same rate of Income Related Rent calculated for them during the period of their care.
After 8-weeks, the hospital or rest home care is considered to be permanent and the rate of Income Related Rent may be reviewed.
MSD must tell the remaining tenant or partner in the property should be advised to contact their housing provider to discuss the Tenancy Agreement (if applicable).
## Notifying the housing provider
The housing provider will be notified by MSD the tenant is in rest home care or hospital when MSD is aware that this is the case and considers the change to be permanent.
The housing provider will decide on whether to end or change a tenancy.

chunks.title: Imprisoned or held on remand for less than 8 weeks — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: If a client advises MSD before being imprisoned or being held on remand for less than 8-weeks, it is not considered a permanent change in circumstances and they can have the same rate of Income Related Rent calculated for them during their period of the imprisonment or remand. If the client is still imprisoned or held on remand after 8-weeks, the change in circumstances is considered permanent, and the rate of Income Related Rent should be reviewed. Note if a client does not advise MSD that they are going to prison or that they are being held on remand, the rate of Income Related Rent should be reviewed as soon as possible.

chunks.title: Imprisoned or held on remand for 8 weeks or more — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: If the client is imprisoned or is being to be held on remand for more than 8-weeks it is considered a permanent change in circumstances and the rate of Income Related Rent should be reviewed as soon as possible.

chunks.title: Other applicable person is imprisoned — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: If there is more than one applicable person in the household, the applicable person who is imprisoned or on remand may be removed from the household type following the review (when appropriate). Note a signatory to the Tenancy Agreement must not be removed from the household until the housing provider has confirmed they have been released from the Tenancy Agreement.

chunks.title: Reviewing the rate of Income Related Rent — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: The rate of Income Related Rent must be reviewed to check for any changes in the client's circumstances. The client will be contacted to confirm their circumstances. If the client's circumstances: - cannot be confirmed, MSD must decide whether to increase the rate of Income Related Rent to the market rent rate or - can be confirmed, MSD must decide whether to increase or decrease the rate of Income Related Rent Note if a single or sole tenant has additional residents or other people living in the property, the additional residents or other people cannot request a join-in to the Tenancy Agreement in this situation.

chunks.title: Released from prison — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: When the applicable person is released from prison, and they are still a client in a social housing property, MSD should review the Income Related Rent and include them back in the household type. MSD should review the Income Related Rent from the earlier of either, the date the: - assessable income increases or - the client was released

chunks.title: Notifying the housing provider — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: When MSD knows a tenant has been imprisoned or is on remand and considers this change in circumstances to be permanent, their housing provider will be notified. The housing provider decides whether to end or change a tenancy. Housing providers have their own policies on clients being absent from the property they are renting.

chunks.title: Leaving a tenancy or changes to a tenancy — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Changes to a tenancy or when a tenant wants to leave a property must be discussed with the housing provider first. MSD must have confirmation from the housing provider before they can stop paying the Income Related Rent Subsidy or calculating the rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Release from Tenancy Agreement (relinquishments) — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: A joint tenant can request to give up their share in a tenancy if all the clients that are on the Tenancy Agreement give consent. There are some circumstances where it is more appropriate for the remaining tenant to make this request so the joint tenancy can be ended and the tenancy re-let to the remaining tenant as the sole tenant. The most common situation is when the departing tenant has already left and cannot be located to sign a release form. Sometimes, clients request to be removed from the Tenancy Agreement, but remain at the property as an additional occupant. For example, an adult child could request to become an additional occupant rather than a tenant if all tenants agree.

chunks.title: Breaches of Tenancy Agreement — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: There are 2 types of breaches to a Tenancy Agreement. These are: - breaches that can be resolved with the housing provider (for example, rent arrears) and - breaches that cannot be resolved as they have already occurred (for example, anti-social behaviour)

chunks.title: Evictions — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: A housing provider will only commence an eviction of a tenant as a last resort. An eviction will only be initiated due to: - an inability to reach agreement with the tenant - mediation or - a decision of the Tenancy Tribunal Tenants will be offered a final opportunity: - to pay any debt to their housing provider in full - resolve any outstanding tenancy issues or - to leave on their own accord However, repaying the debt or resolving the tenancy issues does not of itself guarantee that the eviction will not proceed. Every case is looked at on its own merits. When the tenancy has been terminated for any reason and the tenant does not vacate the tenancy, an eviction can only proceed if the housing provider obtains a possession order. If the tenant does not vacate after being issued a 90-day notice, or any other notice to vacate, an application must be made by the housing provider to the Tenancy Tribunal for a possession order. If the tenancy was terminated by the Tenancy Tribunal then the termination order will also be a possession order.

chunks.title: Non-occupation of the property — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: All tenants are expected to occupy their tenancy continuously. A tenant must tell their housing provider if they will be absent from the property for more than 30-days, as per their Tenancy Agreement.

chunks.title: Step one - Mismatch identified — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: A mismatch of information will be identified when a clients accommodation type or amount differs from what a client who is a social housing tenant has declared they are getting, or an additional occupant has declared they are paying. MSD must try to contact both clients within one working day of identifying the mismatch to check and confirm the correct details.
