If one or both clients are uncontactable within one working day, but a message is left for the client/s to make contact, MSD must consider whether it is reasonable to allow the one working day to lapse before moving to the next step in the process. When one or both clients have been contacted, and it is clear the mismatch cannot be resolved within one working day, or one or both clients are uncontactable and a message cannot be left, MSD can continue to the next step in the process. Note the one working day ends on the close of the working day following the day the mismatch is identified. Example: Raphael is a tenant in a social housing property and pays Income Related Rent. Donatello boards with him as an additional occupant and gets Accommodation Supplement. On Wednesday 6 May, Donatello contacts MSD to advise of a change in circumstances. He is now paying Raphael $365 a week for board from Monday 4 May, an increase from the $355 he had been paying. The new value differs from what MSD holds in the system for the board Raphael gets from Donatello. Raphael has not yet advised MSD of this change. On Thursday 7 May (within one working day of identifying the payment amount mismatch), MSD contacts Donatello to confirm he intended to declare a change in his board amount. Raphael contacts MSD later that day to advise that Donatello's board as increased to $365 from Monday. MSD updates the details for both clients' and the mismatch has been resolved.

chunks.title: Step three - Response to the notification of mismatch — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text: Contact from client/s and mismatch resolved within 10 working days When the client/s make contact and confirm the correct details within 10 working days, the details should be updated and any assistance reviewed accordingly. This means the mismatch is now resolved. No contact from client/s When one or both clients don't make contact within 10 working days to confirm their additional occupant contribution payment information, the mismatch is unable to be resolved, and both clients Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit must be suspended. For the client who is a social housing tenant and the mismatch is not resolved, MSD will notify the housing provider that the client's Income Related Rent must be set to market rent for the property. Community Housing Providers have a discretion not to set the client's rent to the market rent rate. The standard 60-day notice period will apply. Example: Amanda is a social housing tenant and gets Income Related Rent. Bonnie boards with Amanda as an additional occupant and gets Accommodation Supplement. Bonnie gets a mandatory review for her Accommodation Supplement. On Tuesday 9 June, she responds before her review due date confirming that she pays $20 more in board to Amanda. The new amount is different from what MSD holds for Amanda. MSD checks with Bonnie on Wednesday 10 June (within one working day of identifying the mismatch) to see if she advised of the increase in error. She confirms the increase is correct. On Wednesday 10 June, MSD tries contacting Amanda to confirm the new rate, but she doesn't respond. On Thursday 11 June (after the one working day has lapsed), MSD sends both Amanda and Bonnie notification of the mismatch and provides 10 working days to resolve it and advise MSD. Amanda does not respond to the request for information by close of day Tuesday 23 June (within 10 working days). MSD notifies Amanda's housing provider that her Income Related Rent needs to increase to market rent. Bonnie's Accommodation Supplement is suspended from Wednesday 24 June (11th working day) as MSD is unable to confirm the information reported. If Amanda doesn't respond within 8 weeks, Bonnie's Accommodation Supplement will be cancelled.

chunks.title: Next scheduled review date — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Next scheduled review date
Clients must complete the annual review process 5 weeks before the next scheduled review date. If a client does not do this, their Income Related Rent may increase.
The 5-week period a client has to complete the annual review is triggered by the next scheduled review date.
The next scheduled review date for the annual review will be 12 months following either the:
- the start date of the tenancy
- date that the change in circumstances was activated or
- last scheduled review date used for annual review
whichever is the later.
## Next review date is reset
The next scheduled review date is reset after any review of Income Related Rent is activated.
Not all clients will complete an annual review annually (as their Income Related Rent has already been reviewed).
The next scheduled review date is also reset if a client transfers into a different social housing provider property.
## Example 1
Carol moved into a Kāinga Ora property on 3 December 2013.
In this situation the next scheduled review date for her annual review will be 3 December every year that she remains living in the property.
## Example 2
Chris moved into a community housing provider property on 16 April 2020. Chris has had no changes in his circumstances in the last 12 months.
In this situation the next scheduled review date for his next annual review will be 16 April every year that he is living in the property.
On 8 September, Chris has a change in circumstance that reduces his assessable income.
MSD reviews the rate of Income Related Rent calculated and decreases the rate.
The scheduled review date for his next annual review will change. It will now be on 8 September every year that he is still living in the property or until another review is completed.

chunks.title: Review of decision for Income Related Rent debts — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Review of decision for Income Related Rent debts
When an application for Review of Decision involves an Income Related Rent debt currently being recovered from the client, it is appropriate to suspend recovery until the review and appeal process is completed.
If the debt is currently being recovered from the client's benefit, the deductions will need to be suspended.
Where the client is not receiving a benefit you will need to advise Client Support – Debt Management that the client has lodged an application for a Review of Decision in respect of the Income Related Rent debt.
Note you do not refund any payments already deducted until the outcome of the review or appeal is known.

chunks.title: Review of decision - three stage process — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Review of decision - three stage process
There are 3 stages to the review and appeal process:
## Stage 1 - Internal review
This is an administrative process only. When a client applies for a Review of Decision, it is appropriate for MSD to take another look at the decision, review any new information, as well as that which was available at the time of the decision, and check the decision was in accordance with legislation.
## Stage 3 - Social Security Appeal Authority hearing
When the original decision is upheld (or partially upheld) by the Benefit Review Committee, the client can appeal to the Social Security Appeal Authority.
- Review of Decision [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Reviews and Appeals — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Reviews and Appeals
A client can apply for a Review of Decision when they have received formal notification of and disagree with a decision, including decisions relating to:
- the assessment or re-assessment of: their eligibility or continued eligibility for social housingtheir housing needs
- their eligibility or continued eligibility for social housing
- their housing needs
- the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent
- the establishment and recovery of Income Related Rent debt
A client can appeal to the Social Security Appeal Authority where they do not agree with a decision, which was upheld or upheld in part by the Benefits Review Committee under an application for Review of Decision.
## Exceptions
A client has no right of appeal to the Social Security Appeal Authority (and therefore no right to apply for a Review of Decision) if they disagree with:
- a decision not to review their housing need- however, you will need to ensure there is a good reason not to undertake a review of their housing needs
- any decision made by a housing provider regarding tenancy-related matters, such as: the determination of a market rent raterent arrearsdamages debt orwhether someone can join into a tenancy agreement
- the determination of a market rent rate
- rent arrears
- damages debt or
- whether someone can join into a tenancy agreement
The client has the right to apply for a Review of Decision at any time within 3 months of the original decision being advised.
When a client has applied for a hearing outside the 3-month time limit the Benefits Review Committee must decide whether or not to accept the application before it considers the decision under review.
A client has the right to have their decision reviewed once. If they wish to have the same decision reviewed again refer the case to Legal Services.

chunks.title: Notify decision in full — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Notify decision in full
When you advise a client of a decision, in particular an unfavourable decision, you should explain your decision in full and explain the relevant legislation.
Note it is not appropriate to just quote a section of the act verbatim, you should explain the relevant legislation to the client and how it applies to their situation.
For more information see:
- Who can apply for a review or appeal

chunks.title: Joint tenants — income related rent > changes and reviews income related rent
chunks.text:
## Joint tenants
Where there are joint tenants, each individual tenant can apply for a Review of Decision. Depending on the decision under review, any response about the decision or the review may be sent to all of the joint tenants.
## Persons not able to apply for a review or appeal
A third party, without authorisation, is not able to apply for a Review of Decision.
Example
- the parent or family member of a young person who is or was a tenant or
- an additional occupant
For more information see:
- When to advise a client of their right to review
- Client wishes to withdraw application for review
- Review of Decision [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Child Support included as assessable income from 1 July 2023 — income related rent
chunks.text: From 1 July 2023, most types of Child Support clients get are included as assessable income for all applicable persons in the household, when calculating the rate of Income Related Rent. Child Support is money paid by parents who do not live with their children, or who share care with someone else. These payments help with the cost of raising a child. Child Support can be paid through Inland Revenue or directly to the client through another payment arrangement. Child Support payments are non-taxable and paid to the client at a net rate. For more information about Child Support payments see: Child Support Introduction

chunks.title: Information share Child Support — income related rent
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about any Child Support payments clients get. These payments are called information share Child Support payments and are automatically included as income for clients who get income-tested financial assistance. Social Housing income assessments However, social housing assessments need to be reviewed manually to include Child Support payments as assessable income at their Income Related Rent annual review or next unrelated change in circumstances review after 22 August 2023. The information share with Inland Revenue does not include all Child Support payments paid. For more information see: Child Support Income Introduction Note before including information share Child Support as assessable income, MSD must send the client a notice of adverse action. This gives the client 10 working days to tell MSD if the information is incorrect.

chunks.title: Types of Child Support — income related rent
chunks.text: The following types of Child Support are included as assessable income: - Child Support payments paid to a receiving carer from Inland Revenue (formula assessment and voluntary agreement) - Private arrangements of Child Support - Foreign Child Support - Court-ordered lump sums of Child Support (if not considered a cash asset) - Unsupported Child's Benefit excess payments under a voluntary agreement The following types of Child Support are excluded as assessable income: - Offset Child Support payments - Unsupported Child's Benefit excess payments under a formula assessment - Mixed Child Support payments

chunks.title: Child Support is assessable income only for a payment or liability period on or after 1 July 2023 — income related rent
chunks.text: Only Child Support that covers a payment or liability period on or after 1 July 2023 is included as assessable income when calculating the rate of Income Related Rent. For more information about when to include Child Support as assessable income see:

chunks.title: Exception - When Child Support is the client's only income — income related rent
chunks.text: When Child Support is the client's only income it is included as assessable income when calculating the rate of Income Related Rent both before and after 1 July 2023.

chunks.title: Child Support is assessable income from next review on or after 1 July 2023 — income related rent
chunks.text: Child Support is only included as assessable income at the client's next Income Related Rent annual review or unrelated permanent change in circumstances (whichever occurs first) on or after 1 July 2023. An unrelated permanent change in circumstances is a change not related to Child Support and may include (but is not limited to) changes to an applicable people assessable income or assets, or to the number of people living at the property. The unrelated permanent change in circumstances does not need to result in a difference to the rate of Income Related Rent. For more information see:

chunks.title: Client gets Child Support through Inland Revenue — income related rent
chunks.text: If the client gets Child Support through Inland Revenue from 1 July 2023, we only include payments made to them on or after 22 August 2023 as assessable income. This is because Child Support paid by Inland Revenue is paid in arrears. Any Child Support paid by Inland Revenue on or before 22 August 2023 covers a liability period before July 2023 and is excluded. Example - unrelated permanent change in circumstances Tiana lives with her partner, 2 dependent children and her mother in social housing. She gets Jobseeker Support at the 'couple with children rate' and has been getting Child Support of $420 a month paid under a formula assessment from Inland Revenue since May 2023. The Child Support is not currently included as assessable income for the household's Income Related Rent. On 30 July 2023, Tiana contacts MSD to say her mother (who is a tenant) is moving into a rest home. This is a permanent change in circumstances and the rate of Income Related Rent for the household needs to be reviewed. Although there is an unrelated permanent change in circumstances, MSD will not include Tiana's Child Support as assessable income for the review. This is because her Child Support has not been paid for a period on or after 1 July 2023 at time of review.

chunks.title: Client gets Child Support but not through Inland Revenue — income related rent
chunks.text: When a client gets Child Support through another arrangement, e.g. a private arrangement you must determine what period the Child Support is paid for. If it is paid for a period on or after 1 July 2023, it is included as assessable income. Example - annual review Jim works full-time and has been getting private arrangement Child Support of $300 a month for over a year. However, last month (June) his ex-partner could not afford to pay him Child Support. On 12 July 2023, Jim's ex-partner pays him $600: $300 for June and $300 for July. On 14 July 2023, MSD does an annual review of Jim's Income Related Rent. When calculating Jim's rate of Income Related Rent for his annual review, MSD: - includes Jim's Child Support of $300 for July 2023, because it was paid for a period on or after 1 July 2023 and - excludes Jim's Child Support of $300 for June 2023, because it was paid for a period before 1 July 2023

chunks.title: Children in the household type — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Children in the household type
Only the dependent children of applicable people are included as children in the household type for the calculation of Income Related Rent.
A dependent child for social housing purposes is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of the client
- being maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on the client
A child is a single person under the age of 18 years, other than a person who is:
- 16 or 17 years old and
- financially independent
A child may also include a person who is 18 for a limited period if they are:
- continuing in education and
- not financially independent
## Child not to be included in household type
A child is not to be included in the household type when the:
- client has shared care/carer of the child and the child stays in the house for less than 6 overnight stays per fortnight
- child is a child for whom the Orphan's Benefit, Unsupported Child's Benefit, or Foster Care Allowance is being paid
- child is a dependent child of an additional occupant or
- child is 18 years or over and they fall outside the above guidelines for inclusion
Note although these children are not included in the household type for calculating Income Related Rent, they may be considered as dependent children or additional occupants for the purposes of eligibility for social housing and be allocated a bedroom.

chunks.title: Client does not apply for Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Client does not apply for Income Related Rent
A client can choose not to apply for an Income Related Rent. This is confirmed at the time they are placed into a property.
You should discuss with the client their reasons why they do not want to get an Income Related Rent.
When a client advises that they do not want to get an Income Related Rent, they may continue to be eligible for social housing and you must advise:
- Kāinga Ora that the rent for the property is the market rent or
- community housing providers that they may set the rent for the property themselves but it must not be greater than the market rent

chunks.title: Client must be given notice of rent increase - annual review — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Client must be given notice of rent increase - annual review
Following an annual review, the amount of the rent charged by the housing provider cannot increase until the earliest rent effective date following the:
- 14-day notice period (plus service period) or
- 60-day notice period (plus service period)
## Change in circumstance at annual review
A change in circumstance may happen during an annual review where a client has had a change before the annual review was initiated, or during the annual review process and the change has not yet been activated or notified.
The housing provider must use the 14-day notice period at annual review when an increase to the rate of Income Related Rent is due to a change in circumstances.
Note the new rent must not be charged by the housing provider at least 61 days after the date that the change in circumstances occurred.
For more information see:
- Clients must be given notice of an increase - change in circumstances
## Other changes at annual review
You will need to provide the housing provider with the date of processing if you are activating and notifying the housing provider of other changes to the rate of Income Related Rent during an annual review.
A housing provider must use the 60-day notice period at annual review when:
- the client is paying rent at the market rent rate and the housing provider increases the rate of market rent or
- following the annual review of the rate of Income Related Rent where the rate has been increased as a result of the annual general adjustment to the rates of MSD's financial assistance or
- when a client has not completed an annual review form or provided sufficient information to process an annual review
The housing provider will count the 60-day notice period from the date after the date of the processing of the annual review.
Note the new rent cannot be charged by the housing provider within 12 months of the day after:
- the day the rent last increased or
- the day the tenancy started

chunks.title: Clients must be given notice of Income Related Rent increase - change in circumstances — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Clients must be given notice of Income Related Rent increase - change in circumstances
Following a change in circumstances review, the amount of the Income Related Rent charged by the housing provider cannot increase until the earliest rent effective date following the:
- 61-day period from the date of change in circumstances or
- 14-day notice period plus the service period, when this period cannot be included within the 61 days from the date of change in circumstances
whichever is the later.
Increases to the rate of Income Related Rent are not backdated.
If a rent increase should have occurred before the earliest rent effective date, consideration must be given on whether a debt needs to be established.
The new Income Related Rent must be charged by the housing provider at least 61 days after the date that the change in circumstances occurred.
The 61-day period provides:
- a standard timeframe and certainty to the client on how often the rent can be increased and
- time for the client to adjust their circumstances to pay the increased rent and to establish the new rent payments
The 61-day period is counted from the day after the day that the change in circumstances occurred.
## Example - 61-day period
In this example, MSD has been notified at the point the change in circumstances occurs.
Day 0
Day 1 to day 61
The new calculated rate of Income Related Rent takes effect from the earliest rent effective date
There is a change in circumstances and the client notifies MSD
61-day period
14-day notice period calculated by CMS (+ service period + one system day)
The housing provider must give at least a 14-day notice period to the client before the rent is changed.
The housing provider must also allow a 'service period' to allow the client time to get the notice.
## Example - 14-day notice period
In this example, the change in circumstances has been notified late, a debt may be created.
- 170 days
Day 1 to day 19
The new calculated rate of Income Related Rent takes effect from the earliest rent effective date
Change in circumstances occurs
14-day notice period calculated by CMS (service period + one system day)
The housing provider must give at least a 14-day notice period to the client before the rent is changed.
The housing provider must also allow a 'service period' to allow the client time to get the notice.

chunks.title: Contributions from additional occupants — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Contributions from additional occupants
From 2 March 2026, when the applicable persons of the household get contributions from additional occupants, 62% of the total contributions are added to the calculated Income Related Rent.
Income Related Rent for existing social housing tenants will be re-assessed using the new calculation at the earlier of their next scheduled annual review, or next change in circumstances review, on or after 2 March 2026.
For clients on the housing register moving into a social housing property on or after 2 March 2026, Income Related Rent will be reassessed using the new calculation.
Any annual review, change in circumstances review, or reassessment that begins before 2 March 2026, including when someone moves into social housing, will use the previous settings.
## What are contributions?
Contributions means all payments made by an additional occupant, and the value of all goods and services provided or paid for by them, for any of the following reasons:
- as contributions towards the costs and expenses incurred by the applicable persons in the household or
- in consideration of goods or services provided by the applicable persons while the additional occupant is living in the household or
- in consideration of the resident being allowed to reside there
Board, which includes payment for food and/or service costs such as power costs would be considered a contribution.
An additional occupant making contributions towards accommodation costs may be able to get an Accommodation Supplement or Accommodation Benefit based on their contributions.
When the additional occupant who pays the contribution to a tenant who pays Income Related Rent gets Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, and/or Special Benefit, MSD will check the details match between the two clients. Where there is a mismatch of information, the mismatch process must be followed.
## Example
Vanessa is a social housing tenant, and she gets contributions from 3 additional occupants in her household; two pay $200 each per week and the other pays $70 per week.
Two of the additional occupants have young children. Vanessa stays at home and cares for the children.
The total contributions she gets from the additional occupants are $470 a week and $291.40 is included in the assessment of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Date of change in circumstance — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Date of change in circumstance
MSD needs to determine the date of the change in circumstances. This is either:
- the actual date that the change in circumstances occurred or
- the date it is considered that the client's assessable income or additional occupant contributions permanently reduced or increased
whichever is the later.
For more information see:
- Reviews of the rate of Income Related Rent
- Deciding if changes are permanent or temporary
- Change in circumstances
## Annual reviews
At the annual review of the rate of Income Related Rent, when activating and notifying the housing provider of a change other than a change in circumstance, provide the date of processing.

chunks.title: Client advises late of a change in circumstances — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Client advises late of a change in circumstances
Generally, the client should advise us within 14 days of any change in their circumstances so their circumstances can be reviewed and when applicable, a new rate of Income Related Rent can be calculated, activated and notified.
If a client does not advise us about their change in circumstances, and there is an under-calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent, an Income Related Rent debt may be established.
Note Income Related Rent debt is established once the housing provider has advised they have increased the client's rent. This is because MSD needs the rent effective date to establish the correct debt period.

chunks.title: Client getting financial assistance from MSD — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Client getting financial assistance from MSD
Income Related Rent debt owed by clients getting financial assistance from MSD can be repaid by regular deductions from the client's weekly or fortnightly entitlement from any of the following sources:
- main benefit
- New Zealand Superannuation (pension)
- Extra help – only with the client's agreement
- Student Allowance
## Rate of repayment
You will need to negotiate the rate of repayment with the client. The rate of repayment needs to be realistic, without causing hardship for the client.
You will need to take the client's full circumstances into account including any other commitments they have, for example, hire purchase repayments.
You need to consider MSD’s priority for deductions when deciding the repayment rate.
## Advance Payment of Benefit and Income Related Rent debt
Income Related Rent debt is not used when determining the amount of Advance Payment of Benefit available.

chunks.title: Establishing Income Related Rent debt — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Establishing Income Related Rent debt
There are specific circumstances that can result in an Income Related Rent debt being established. Income Related Rent debt may be created when a client has a rate of Income Related Rent calculated lower than they were entitled to.
This may be due to:
- client not advising of a change in their circumstances, for example, an increase in their assessable income
- undeclared information at the time of assessment or at any time during the tenancy, for example, partner's assessable income
- fraud, for example, undeclared income (self or partner's), subletting, falsified or deliberately misleading information
## Period over which to calculate the debt
Income Related Rent debt is established from 61 days after the date of the change in circumstances until the day before the client starts paying the correct rate of Income Related Rent (that is the day before the rent effective date).
Debt is established from 61 days after the date of change because there are specific notice periods for the client, before the amount of Income Related Rent they must pay to their housing provider increases.
## Exception for fraud debt
Income Related Rent debt established due to fraud is calculated from when the client first started paying Income Related Rent, or the date the fraud started to the period fraud ended or the day before the rent effective date (whichever is applicable).
Debt established as the result of a fraud investigation not included in the 61 day period.
## Income Related Rent debt not established
Income Related Rent debt is not established if the:
- change notified makes no material difference to the social housing provider and the rent change is not applied
- debt calculated is under $500
- rent change is not applied (for example, tenant dies or ends the tenancy before the rent effective date)
- debt was caused wholly or partly due to a mistake the debtor did not intentionally make
## Repayment of Income Related Rent debt
Recovery of Income Related Rent debt can start once the debt has been established and the rent charge date confirmed by the housing provider though the new rent is effective from a future date.

chunks.title: Example of debt as result of undeclared information — income related rent debt
chunks.text: The following examples are situations when Income Related Rent debt may be created as the result of a client not declaring information to MSD. These examples are based on 2 different debt provisions.

chunks.title: Example 1 - Undeclared household income — income related rent debt
chunks.text: The client's next scheduled review date for their annual review of Income Related Rent is 15 December 2016. During the review a client provides additional information showing they had a change in circumstances on 10 May 2020, which they did not tell MSD about at the time. The client's income increased by an additional $60 per week from 10 May 2020. An investigation by the Client Service Integrity ends on 30 January 2023, and finds the client had good and sufficient reason and had not intended to defraud MSD. The client's rate of Income Related Rent is recalculated, and they are notified along with their housing provider of the new calculated rate of Income Related Rent. The housing provider informs the client of the new rate of rent they will need to pay, and the date the new rent amount is to be paid from. This is the 22 February 2017, the first rent effective date after the 14 days' notice period plus the service period. Debt is established from 10 July 2020 (61 days from the date of the client's change in circumstances) to 21 February 2023 (the day before the rent effective date).

chunks.title: Example 2 - Undeclared information during social housing eligibility assessment — income related rent debt
chunks.text: On 20 April 2022 a client attends their social housing eligibility assessment and fails to declare details about their partner's assessable income. The client had several opportunities to advise MSD of their partner's income but on all those occasions they did not advise MSD their partner was in full-time employment. MSD gets information about the client's circumstances on 1 August 2022. An investigation by Client Service Integrity establishes on 3 October 2022 that the client's partner was in full-time employment when they first applied for social housing. The client's rate of Income Related Rent is recalculated and the client and their housing provider are told of the client's calculated rate of Income Related Rent. Income Related Rent debt is established from the start of the tenancy to 31 October 2022 (the rent effective date notified by the housing provider). The client was not given the 61-day period from the start of the tenancy because Client Service Integrity determined the client provided misleading information to MSD.

chunks.title: Example of debt due to late notice of change in circumstances — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Example of debt due to late notice of change in circumstances
A client starts part-time work on 18 February 2023 and does not advise MSD of the changes to their income until 2 July 2023.
The client's rate of Income Related Rent is recalculated, and they are notified along with their housing provider of the new rate of Income Related Rent.
The housing provider confirms the rent effective date for rent change as 24 July 2023 (which is the first rent effective date after the 14 days' notice period plus the service period.
MSD establishes an Income Related Rent debt 61 days after the date of the change in circumstances (20 April 2023) to 23 July 2023 (the day before the rent effective date).
The client's rent increase takes effect from 24 July 2023.

chunks.title: Examples of debt created as result of fraud investigations — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Examples of debt created as result of fraud investigations
The following examples are situations when Income Related Rent debt may be created as the result of fraud investigations.
## Example 1 - Undeclared income from subletting property
A client travelled overseas for 6 months (from 1 April 2022 to 1 October 2022) but did not notify their housing provider of their absence from the property and unlawfully sublet the property to a friend for the 6-month period.
During a routine visit to the property, a tenancy manager becomes aware of the subletting arrangement and advises MSD.
An investigation by the Client Service Integrity establishes the client received additional income from the subletting arrangement.
The client's rate of Income Related Rent is recalculated for the period from 1 April 2022 to 1 October 2022.
A debt is established for this period based on the additional assessable income the client got from the subletting arrangement.
## Example 2 - Misleading MSD
On 1 January 2022, a client tells MSD her partner has moved in with her but fails to declare her partner is working and did not give information about his income.
As the client must advise within 14 days of any change in circumstances that might increase their rate of Income Related Rent, this will be treated as deliberate omission of information for the purposes of misleading MSD.
On 9 October 2022, an allegation is received about the client's partner's employment situation.
On 14 December 2022, as the result of an investigation, the Client Service Integrity has information previously not available to MSD.
An Income Related Rent is recalculated for the client and their social housing provider is notified. A debt is established from 1 January 2022 until the client starts paying rent at the correct rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Kāinga Ora debt historical Income Related Rent debt — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Kāinga Ora debt historical Income Related Rent debt
Kāinga Ora is responsible for recovering any Income Related Rent debt established before 14 April 2014.
Kāinga Ora can issue a deduction notice to MSD to recover Income Related Rent debt owed to them by clients who are getting a benefit.
## Deduction of historical Kāinga Ora Income Related Rent debt
Historical Kāinga Ora Income Related Rent debt has the same repayment priority as Income Related Rent debt repayments to MSD.
This is as MSD Income Related Rent debt and historical Kāinga Ora Income Related Rent debt are both Crown debts and must be given equal priority for recovery.
For example, if a client has a historical Income Related Rent debt with Kāinga Ora and now has an Income Related Rent debt with MSD, the client will contribute equal repayment amounts to both debts as they are both Crown debts.

chunks.title: Income Related Rent debt due to undeclared circumstances — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Income Related Rent debt due to undeclared circumstances
It is an offence for a client not to provide information or to provide false or misleading information to MSD.
When it is determined a client has deliberately not provided information or provided misleading information, and, as a result, there is an under-calculation of their Income Related Rent rate, an Income Related Rent debt will be established from the date the offence was committed to the day before the client starts paying the correct rate of Income Related Rent.
However, if MSD finds that the client did not intentionally omit to declared information (for example at the time of assessment or any time during their tenancy), it will be treated as a change in circumstance.
Debt will be established 61 days after the date of the change in circumstances until the day before the client starts paying rent at the correct Income Related Rent rate (that is the day before the rent effective date).

chunks.title: Income Related Rent debt from fraud — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Income Related Rent debt from fraud
Only Income Related Rent debt cases investigated by Client Intervention Services can be considered fraud.
## Suspicion of fraud
When you suspect a client may be committing fraud - this is called fraud suspicion.
A fraud suspicion could come about due to an interview, a phone conversation or a processing action.
Some examples of client situations that may result in fraud suspicion include:
- undeclared partners
- undeclared or under declared income
- false identity or identity theft
- deliberate omission of information or
- falsified or misleading information
## Period over which to establish fraud debt
When a higher calculated rate of Income Related Rent has been established due to fraud, a debt can be established from:
- the start date of the tenancy - which is the date the rate of Income Related Rent was first calculated from or
- the date fraud commenced
until period end date, which is:
- the day before the rent effective date or the rent charge date or
- the date the fraudulent activity ended
whichever is applicable.

chunks.title: Income Related Rent debt under $500 — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Income Related Rent debt under $500
MSD has discretion to not establish Income Related Rent debt.
Currently any Income Related Rent debt under $500 is not established.
When an Income Related Rent debt is calculated due to a change in circumstances, and the amount of the debt is under $500, it is not established or recovered.
Note this provision does not apply to debts established in fraud cases (for example, debt established because client undeclared or under declared their income, client falsified or provides misleading information).
You must record your Income Related Rent debt calculations and the total amount of the debt on the client's record in CMS, as the debt will not be calculated automatically by the system.
## Example
During the annual review of Income Related Rent it is discovered that Sarah had a change in circumstances, which affects the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent. The debt is calculated as $490. The debt amount is recorded on Sarah's record in CMS. However, as this debt is under $500 no debt is established.

chunks.title: Insolvency, bankruptcy or death — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Insolvency, bankruptcy or death
In a joint tenancy, if one of the tenants dies or becomes insolvent or bankrupt, MSD may recover any outstanding debt from the remaining tenant(s) on the tenancy agreement.
## Income Related Rent debt is split for recovery
However, if the debt has been split due to systems restrictions, MSD will generally not try to recover the amount apportioned to the deceased/insolvent/bankrupt tenant from the remaining tenants.

chunks.title: Introduction — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Social housing tenants must tell us straight away of any change in their circumstances or their family's situation that may affect their rate of Income Related Rent.
MSD calculates a rate of Income Related Rent and tells the social housing provider and the client. The social housing provider sets the rate of rent to pay based on the rate they are given by MSD.
If MSD are told about a change in circumstances late the rent rate the client is paying could be too low and an Income Related Rent debt may be created.
Note Income Related Rent debt is not rent debt (i.e. it is not debt owed to a landlord). MSD does not establish or recover rent arrears or other tenancy related debt.
## Income Related Rent debt
Income Related Rent debt is created when a clients Income Related Rents rate of payment for social housing was calculated at less than they should have paid.
The debt for the client is the difference between the current correct rate of Income Related Rent and the rate of Income Related Rent calculated earlier for that period. The client will generally need to repay any debt established.
## Income Related Rent debt established on or after 14 April 2014
MSD is responsible for Income Related Rent debts established on or after 14 April 2014.
Debt established after 14 April 2014 may include periods from before 14 April 2014.
## Income Related Rent debt established before 14 April 2014
Kāinga Ora is responsible for Income Related Rent debt established before 14 April 2014.

chunks.title: Liability for Income Related Rent debt — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Liability for Income Related Rent debt
The signatory(s) on the tenancy agreement are liable for any Income Related Rent debt created for any period during the tenancy, not the applicable person(s).
## More than one signatory on the tenancy agreement
When an Income Related Rent debt is established for a period when there was more than one signatory on the tenancy agreement (that is, joint tenants) the tenants are jointly and severally liable for that debt. This is regardless of whether both or all tenants are current tenants at the time the debt is established.
Note jointly and severally means that joint tenants are collectively and individually responsible for the debt - repayment of the debt does not have to be shared equally.
When one of the signatories in a joint tenancy relinquishes their tenancy at a later date (that is, they are no longer a signatory on the tenancy agreement), that tenant will not be liable for any debt created after they have been removed as a signatory on the tenancy. Debt from that point belongs to the remaining tenant(s) on the tenancy agreement.
Note due to systems restrictions, the debt will usually be split equally and recovered from all clients individually.

chunks.title: Rent to pay unchanged — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Rent to pay unchanged
Income Related Rent debt cannot be recovered from a client if their housing provider does not change the amount of rent they must pay.
## Rent payments reduced
If a client has another change in circumstance after the rent change notification, and the rent increase is not being applied, the debt will be cancelled, and any money recovered will be refunded.

chunks.title: Repayment of Income Related Rent debt — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Repayment of Income Related Rent debt
Recovery of Income Related Rent debt can start once the debt has been established and rent effective date confirmed by the housing provider even if the new rent is effective from a future date.
Debt deduction arrangements depend on whether the client is getting financial assistance from MSD or not.
Income Related Rent debt can be recovered from:
- benefit
- Student Allowance
- extra help provided under a welfare programme
- or
- by issuing deduction notices For example, to a State Sector employer, a bank or a trust. MSD can deduct from weekly compensation for loss earnings or loss of potential earning capacity paid to the debtor by ACC.
Once an Income Related Rent debt is established and is to be recovered, it is manually added to TRACE.

chunks.title: Review of decision of Income Related Rent debt — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Review of decision of Income Related Rent debt
Clients can have a decision reviewed when they disagree with the establishment and recovery of any Income Related Rent debt.
## Debt recovery can be suspended
When an application for a Review of Decision involves a debt currently being recovered, in most cases it is appropriate to suspend repayments until the review and appeal process is completed.
You need to consider what part of the debt is being reviewed before you suspend recovery:
- when establishment of the whole debt or the decision to recover is under review, stopping recovery for the period of the Review of Decision is appropriate
- when there is more than one debt, continue recovering other debts not being reviewed
- when a client is reviewing a part of the debt (not the complete debt) you should continue recovering the part of the debt not under dispute
Note you do not refund any repayments already deducted until the outcome of the review or appeal is known.

chunks.title: Students and clients not getting financial assistance from MSD — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Students and clients not getting financial assistance from MSD
Income Related Rent debt recovery for students and clients not getting financial assistance from MSD will be administered by Client Support – Debt Management using their usual debt recovery procedures.

chunks.title: Table of Income Related Rent debt liability — income related rent debt
chunks.text:
## Table of Income Related Rent debt liability
Client situation
Income Related Rent debt created
Liability for Income Related Rent debt
Couple
Only one signed the tenancy agreement and the partner is an applicable person.
Debt created
Only the signatory is liable for the Income Related Rent debt
Joint tenants
All parties signed the tenancy agreement and then one is removed from the tenancy agreement at a later stage.
Debt created while all on the tenancy agreement
All tenants are liable for the Income Related Rent debt
Debt created after one of the tenants is removed from the tenancy agreement:
- Debt period during joint tenancy
All tenants are liable for the Income Related Rent debt
Debt created after one of the tenants is removed from the tenancy agreement:
- Debt period does not include joint tenancy
Only the person who is still a signatory to the tenancy agreement is liable for the Income Related Rent debt

chunks.title: Deciding if changes are permanent or temporary — income related rent
chunks.text: When a client has had a change in circumstances, you must consider whether the change is likely to be permanent or temporary. If the information provided is unclear you should discuss with the client whether the change is likely to be permanent or temporary. This consideration must occur regardless of whether the change is likely to result in a decrease or an increase to the rate of Income Related Rent. Whether you consider the change to be permanent or temporary depends on the individual circumstances of the client and the specific reason for the change. Generally, for the purposes of Income Related Rent, a change that is likely to last or has lasted: - less than 8-weeks is temporary - 8- weeks or more is permanent

chunks.title: Temporary changes — income related rent
chunks.text: Where you consider the change to be temporary you should note the changes in the client's record, including the expected duration of the change. This will enable a task to be generated for follow up.

chunks.title: Permanent changes — income related rent
chunks.text: Where you consider the change to be permanent you should review the rate of Income Related Rent, and activate any changes to the rate. Generally: - a change in circumstances that will result in an increase in Income Related Rent will not be considered permanent until it has lasted 8-weeks or more for example when a client starts new employment, the change will not be considered permanent until they have maintained the employment for 8-weeks or more - for example when a client starts new employment, the change will not be considered permanent until they have maintained the employment for 8-weeks or more - a change in circumstances that will result in a decrease in Income Related Rent will be considered permanent when it is likely to last or has lasted 8-weeks or more for example when a client indicates that their hours of work have reduced and this is expected to last for at least 8-weeks, the change can be considered permanent from the point the client notified MSD of the change or the date their income reduced, whichever is later - for example when a client indicates that their hours of work have reduced and this is expected to last for at least 8-weeks, the change can be considered permanent from the point the client notified MSD of the change or the date their income reduced, whichever is later

chunks.title: Permanent change when granting benefit, New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension — income related rent
chunks.text: When a client is granted a benefit, New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, this is considered a permanent change in circumstance from the start of the initial stand-down period, or if the initial stand-down is not imposed, from the commencement date of the assistance.

chunks.title: Permanent change when client gets Child Support under a formula assessment from Inland Revenue — income related rent
chunks.text: When a client gets Child Support under a formula assessment from Inland Revenue, or the assessed amount has changed, this is generally considered a permanent change in circumstances from the date the client gets their first payment under that assessment (or reassessment). This is because Child Support paid under a formula assessment is an annual entitlement paid to the client in monthly instalments and is likely to last (or may have already lasted) more than 8-weeks. Note Child Support is only included as assessable income at a client's next Income Related Rent annual review or unrelated permanent change in circumstances (whichever is first) on or after 1 July 2023.

chunks.title: Deciding who the refund should be paid to — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Deciding who the refund should be paid to
Where a decision has been made to backdate the rate of Income Related Rent, a refund needs to be established and issued.
The refund is the difference between the previously calculated rate of Income Related Rent (that generally, the client has been required to pay in rent to their housing provider) and the new lower calculated rate of Income Related Rent.
MSD will decide whether to issue the refund to the client or the housing provider.
MSD will check with the housing provider whether the client has paid the rent charged during the refund period.
## Client has paid a higher amount of rent
Where the client has paid the higher amount of rent that the housing provider has charged the refund is due to the client. See:
- Refunds - paying to the client
## Client has under paid their rent
Where the client has underpaid their rent to the housing provider the refund must be issued directly to the housing provider. See:
- Refunds - paying to the housing provider
## Client has paid some but not all of the rent charged
In some situations, you may need to issue the refund to the client and to the housing provider. This can happen when the client has paid some but not all of the rent charged to their housing provider. See:
- Refunds - paying to client and the housing provider
## Joint tenants due a refund
There may be situations where a refund is due to joint tenants. See:
- Refunds - paying to joint tenants

chunks.title: Dependent child's income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Dependent child's income
A dependent child's personal earnings are not considered assessable income for Income Related Rent.
The child is included in the household type, but their income is not included.
If a child aged 16 years or older starts working full-time (an average of 30 hours or more each week) or is granted a benefit in their own right they are no longer considered to be a dependent child.

chunks.title: Deprivation of income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Deprivation of income
Deprivation of income means where an applicable person has changed their financial arrangements to put themselves at a financial disadvantage.
This could have led to the applicable person accessing an Income Related Rent at a lower rate than it would have otherwise been.
Deprivation of income must be assessed on a case by case basis. If you consider that the applicable person has deprived themselves of income, you can include all or a portion of the deprived income as assessable income.
If you consider deprivation has occurred, contact Helpline for advice.
## Child Support
From 1 July 2023, an applicable person who does not apply for, or decides to end, a Child Support arrangement is not considered to be depriving themselves of income.
This includes Child Support paid under a formula assessment via Inland Revenue.

chunks.title: Determining portion of family tax credit to include — income related rent
chunks.text: Only a portion of the family tax credit is included in the calculation of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: How to determine the amount to include — income related rent
chunks.text: Step 1. Determine the total family tax credit rate that the applicable people are entitled to get. This is the actual amount they are entitled to get based on their family situation and not what they are getting. Step 2. Determine the portion to include using the following formula: - get the actual amount that the applicable people are entitled to get and multiply the rate by 25% (or 0.25) - get the rate of the family tax credit category 'eldest or only child', and multiply the rate by 25% (or 0.25) Note use the rate 'eldest or only child', regardless of the age or number of the children that the applicable people are getting or are entitled to get family tax credit for. Step 3. Whichever is the lesser amount of step 2 should be included in the calculation of Income Related Rent. Note when a client has a shared care/carer arrangement and the child stays in the house for overnight stays for 6 nights per fortnight or more, you will need to include a portion of the amount of family tax credit the client is entitled to get.

chunks.title: Examples of determining family tax credit amount — income related rent
chunks.text: Example 1 Leanne has 3 children, aged 4, 9 and 16 years. She is getting Sole Parent Support and is entitled to get family tax credits. Calculate the portion to include in the calculation as follows: Step 1 - Family tax credit entitlement (1 April 2026) Rate per week Eldest or only child, 16 years old $151.91 Second or subsequent child, 9 years old $123.78 Second or subsequent child, 4 years old $123.78 Total amount of family tax credit received $399.47 = A Step 2 - Determine the portion to include Rate per week 25% of rate of A (amount Leanne is entitled to get) $99.86 = B Eldest or only child $151.91 25% of rate 'eldest or only child' $37.97 = C Step 3 - Get the lesser amount of B or C $37.97 = weekly amount to include in the calculation of Income Related Rent Example 2 Simon has a shared care/carer arrangement for his 9 year old child and the child stays in the house for overnight stays, 4 nights per week. He is getting Sole Parent Support and entitled to get family tax credit. Calculate the portion to include in the calculation as follows: Step 1 - Family tax credit entitlement (1 April 2026) Rate per week Eldest or only child, 9 years old ($151.91 divided by 7 and multiplied by 4) $86.80 Total amount of family tax credit received $86.80 = A Step 2 - Determine the portion to include Rate per week 25% of rate A (eg amount Simon is entitled to get) $21.70 = B Eldest or only child $151.91 25% of rate 'eldest or only child' $37.97 = C Step 3 - Get the lesser amount of B or C $21.70 = weekly amount to include in the calculation of Income Related Rent Note the above rates of family tax credit are as at 1 April 2026.

chunks.title: Difference in notice periods given by housing providers — income related rent
chunks.text: The amount of the rent charged by the housing provider cannot increase until the earliest rent effective date following the: - 14-day notice period or - 60-day notice period Housing providers give notice to clients to ensure that they have time to adjust their circumstances to pay a higher rate of rent. Note the housing provider must decrease the rent from the earliest rent effective date following the notification (ie no 14-day notice period or 60-day notice period applies for rent decreases).

chunks.title: Guideline for the difference between notice periods — income related rent
chunks.text: 14-day notice period and the 61-day period 60-day notice period and the 12-month period Social housing providers must give tenants at least 14 days' notice of any increase in their rate of Income Related Rent that is due to a change in the household circumstances. The 14-day notice must be given before the rent effective date. It could be within the 61-day period, or in addition to it, depending on when the change of circumstance was notified or discovered. The 14-day notice period starts from the date the notice is deemed to have been given to the tenant. In other words, it is in addition to the service period that applies (depending on the method of delivery). The 61-day period ensures that, when a tenant has a change of circumstance, any increase in their rate of Income Related Rent cannot take effect until at least 61-days after the date that the change in circumstances occurred (regardless of when the change of circumstance was notified or discovered). The 61-day period is counted from the day after the day that the change of circumstances occurred. While housing providers are responsible for allowing for the 61-day period, MSD must take it into account when calculating debt in situations of late notification or discovery of a tenant's change in circumstances, and it is also relevant to the calculation of Income Related Rent subsidy payable to housing providers. The 61-day period and the 14-day notice period are counted in calendar days. The 60-day notice period ensures that a client receives at least 60 days' notice of an increase in their rent. The 60-day notice period will apply to all increases of rent where the 61-day period is not applicable. This will include situations where the client doesn't provide sufficient information to MSD to calculate or review the rate of Income Related Rent and generally their rent is to be increased to market rent. In situations where the 60-day notice period applies, the 12-month period also applies. The 12-month period ensures a client's rent cannot be increased: - within 12 months of the day after the rent last increased or - within 12 months after the day the tenancy started The 60-day notice period starts from the date the notice is deemed to have been given to the client. In other words, it is in addition to the service period that applies (depending on the method of delivery). It is counted in calendar days.

chunks.title: Guideline for the difference between notice periods — income related rent
chunks.text: When do housing providers use the 14-day notice period? The 14-day notice period is used when the rate of Income Related Rent following a change in circumstance, which includes changes to the applicable person's income, and changes to their household, type. When do housing providers use the 60-day notice period? The 60-day notice period is used: - following the annual review of the rate of Income Related Rent where the rate has been increased due to the annual general adjustment to the rates of MSD financial assistance - when a applicable person has not completed an annual review form or provided sufficient information to process an annual review - when a client has had a change in circumstances, but has not provided sufficient information to process the review within 10 working days of the information being requested - when the tenant is paying rent at the market rent rate and the housing provider increases the rate of market rent

chunks.title: Ending grandparenting provision when client no longer qualifies — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Ending grandparenting provision when client no longer qualifies
The Income Related Rent grandparenting provisions will end if the client:
- moves from the Kāinga Ora property where the reduction was included in the calculated rate of Income Related Rent
- is a sole tenant (who qualified for grandparenting) who dies or
- has an abated cap that is less than or equal to $0.00
## Exception
When the client initiates a transfer from a Kāinga Ora property to another Kāinga Ora property the Income Related Rent grandparenting provisions will end; however when Kāinga Ora initiates the transfer, the client will retain the appropriate grandparenting provisions.
The client will not retain the grandparenting provisions if they move from a Kāinga Ora property to a community housing provider property.

chunks.title: Estimating and adjusting net weekly income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Estimating and adjusting net weekly income
A client's assessable income is their estimated net weekly income (ie income after tax) from all sources after the deduction of any Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) premiums or levies. This includes income from assessable assets.
When estimating a client's net weekly income, the estimated total net income for the period will be averaged over:
- 52 weeks or
- a shorter period where appropriate
Note weekly income cannot be estimated from a period longer than 52 weeks.
## Estimating weekly income over a shorter appropriate period
If it is appropriate, you can use a period that is less than 52 weeks to estimate weekly income.
If a shorter period is used to estimate the client's weekly income, the best available estimate of total assessable income received from all sources over the period must be divided to get the net weekly amount.
Calculate the assessable income as follows:
- estimate the net income over the shorter period
- divide by the shorter period = weekly rate of assessable income
For example, if there is evidence of a permanent increase or decrease in pay, the total assessable income received since the permanent change could be divided to get an estimate of the weekly income.
## Treatment of tax and ACC deductions
If any part of an applicable person's income has not been reduced by the appropriate amount of income tax, ACC premium or ACC levy, you will need to adjust the weekly income to account for the estimated amount payable.
For example, if a client is paying a higher tax rate than necessary, you should adjust the income to what would be the correct net amount.
## Adjusting income
You may adjust the estimated weekly income if you consider that the client is depriving themselves of income.

chunks.title: Example 1 — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Example 1
Jane has been receiving Sole Parent Support since July 2021 and has been a social housing tenant since 2020.
In January 2023 MSD became aware that Jane was in a relationship. Her partner was living with her and earning income above the threshold for benefits and additional assistance. The benefit was stopped and, after investigation, it was determined that she had misled MSD about her relationship status since the benefit was granted and the relationship began in July 2022.
A debt is established for the benefit paid from July 2022 until January 2023 and is to be recovered by MSD
When completing the review of Income Related Rent for the period over which the benefit debt was established (July 2022 to January 2023), the household type must be updated to include Jane's partner who was living with her. Only the income earned by Jane's partner will be included as income for the period. The benefit paid to Jane, which she was not entitled to and will be recovered, is not included as income.
The Income Related Rent reviewed for the period will reflect what it would have been had she advised MSD of the change in her circumstances when it had occurred.

chunks.title: Example 1 — income related rent
chunks.text: Theresa is 36, and is working full-time as a manager in a bank. She earns $1,600 (after tax and ACC levies) per week, and also has a large inheritance which is generating income. Her household type is 'single 25 years and over'. She is living in a Kāinga Ora property. The market rent rate for the property is $220 per week. Note Theresa's rate of Income Related Rent is calculated using household income, as this produces a higher rate than the rate calculated using the Jobseeker Support rate. Net weekly income earned Assessable income Wages or salary $1,600 Assessable income from assets $100 Total of assessable income $1,700 Calculation Total Total of income under the income threshold - $555.15 (at 1 April 2026) $555.15 25% of the income under the threshold $138.78 = A Total of income over (the threshold) $1,144.85 50% of the income total over threshold $572.42 = B Portion of family tax credit n/a = C 62% of contributions from additional occupants n/a = D Total before rounding (= A + B + C + D) $711.20 Total calculated rate $711.00 The rate of the Income Related Rent is above the market rent rate. The rent that Kāinga Ora charges Theresa, must be the market rent rate of $220 per week.

chunks.title: Example 2 — income related rent
chunks.text: Suzanne is 28, and is working full-time as a call centre manager. She earns $2,200 (after tax and ACC levies) per fortnight from her job. Her household type is 'single 25 years and over'. She is living in a community housing provider property. The market rent rate for the property is $330 per week. Note Suzanne's rate of Income Related Rent is calculated using household income, as this produces a higher rate than the rate calculated using the Jobseeker Support rate. Net weekly income earned Assessable income Wages or salary $1,100 Total of assessable income $1,100 Calculation Total Total of income under the income threshold - $555.15 (at 1 April 2026) $555.15 25% of the income under the threshold $138.78 = A Total of income over (the threshold) $544.85 50% of the income total over threshold $272.42 = B Portion of family tax credit n/a = C 62% of contributions from additional occupants n/a = D Total before rounding (= A + B + C + D) $411.20 Total calculated rate $411.00 The rate of the Income Related Rent is more than the market rent rate. The community housing provider can set the rent that they charge, but it cannot be higher than the market rent rate for the property, so no higher than $330 per week.

chunks.title: Examples of backdating - at review — income related rent
chunks.text: Examples of how backdating would work and the periods the refund should be issued for.

chunks.title: Example 1 - change in circumstances review — income related rent
chunks.text: Tom finished his temporary contract for his job on 12 May 2023 and his income has reduced. Tom was unable to contact MSD straight away to tell them about this, as his father passed away and he had to travel for the funeral. Tom contacts MSD on 3 June 2023 and provides the information. Tom is paying rent to Kāinga Ora weekly on a Thursday (his rent charge date). The new rent takes effect from the next rent period after the notification from MSD. A refund would be paid for the period from the earliest possible rent charge date, following the change in circumstances, to the day prior to the rent effective date. Timeline: - 12 May 2023: Tom finishes his contract. - 18 May 2023: Date the rent charge was backdated to (start of refund period). If Tom had notified MSD of the change in time, the reduced rent would have taken effect from this date. - 3 June 2023: Tom tells MSD that his contract finished on 12 May. - 4 June 2023: MSD notifies housing provider of the new (lower) rate of Income Related Rent. - 5 June 2023: Housing provider notifies Tom the rent will change, and tells him the effective date of the change. - 8 June 2023: New rent effective date (a Thursday). The refund period is 18 May 2023 to 7 June 2023.

chunks.title: Example 2 - change to income threshold at annual general adjustment — income related rent
chunks.text: David and Leani both work full-time and do not get any ongoing assistance from MSD apart from their Income Related Rent. On 1 April 2025, the income thresholds for Income Related Rent increase, as part of the annual general adjustment. This increase means more of their assessable income now falls below the income threshold for their household type. On 23 June 2025, David and Leani return their completed annual review form to MSD. MSD reassesses the couple's Income Related Rent and determines their rent has decreased from $358 to $352 a week. This decrease is due to the change to the income threshold at the annual general adjustment. MSD must calculate a refund from 1 April 2025 as set out below. The couple pays rent to Kāinga Ora weekly on a Thursday (their rent charge date). The earliest rent charge date after 1 April is Thursday 3 April. The day before their next rent charge date is Wednesday 25 June. David and Leani have paid their rent in full (they have no rent arrears for the refund period). They are due a refund for this period as follows: - Income Related Rent rate per week that needs to be refunded: $358 minus $352 = $6 a week - Refund period: there are 12 weeks from 3 April until 25 June - Refund amount: $6 x 12 weeks = $72 refund due from MSD to David and Leani Timeline: - 1 April 2025: The Income Related Rent income threshold changes at annual general adjustment. - 3 April 2025: The decrease in rent would have taken effect from this date. This is the appropriate rent charge date to backdate to (start of the refund period). - 23 June 2025: David and Leani hand in their annual review. - 24 June 2025: Housing provider notified by MSD of the new rate of Income Related Rent. - 25 June 2025: Housing provider tells David and Leani the rent will change, and the effective date of the change. - 26 June 2025: The new rent effective date (a Thursday) . The refund period is 3 April 2025 to 25 June 2025.

chunks.title: Example 1 — income related rent
chunks.text: Luke is 26 and is getting Jobseeker Support on the ground of a health condition, injury or disability. He is living in a community housing provider property. Luke works as an actor part time and earns $204.83 net, ($248.28 gross, 'S' tax rate) per week. His household type is 'single tenant'. chunks.title: Examples of decreasing the rent — income related rent
chunks.text: A housing provider must always issue notice to a tenant of a change to the rent charged. However, in the case of a decrease to the amount of rent charged, there is no notice period applied. The housing provider must apply the decrease to the rent from the earliest rent effective date following the notification received. Note that these examples assume that the housing provider will send written notice to change the rent to their tenants by post within 2 days of receiving notification from MSD, however this may not always be the case. Below are examples of how the notice for a decrease works.

chunks.title: Example 1 — income related rent
chunks.text: Mary's hours of work decreased on 2 December 2022 and she notified MSD on 3 December 2022. The new rate of Income Related Rent is activated because the assessable income has reduced. Mary is paying rent to Kāinga Ora weekly on a Thursday (her rent charge date). The new rent takes effect from the next rent period after the housing provider receives the notification from MSD. 2 December 2022 3 December 2022 4 December 2022 10 December 2022 Change in circumstances occurs and Income Related Rent reviewed Housing provider notified by MSD the rate of Income Related Rent has decreased due to a change in circumstances on 3 December 2022 Housing provider notifies tenant that the rent will change and when The earliest rent effective date is a Thursday

chunks.title: Example 2 — income related rent
chunks.text: Stewart calls MSD as he was made redundant on 12 May 2023. Stewart received two weeks of holiday pay. His partner continues to work and the couple is not eligible for benefit. The new rate of Income Related Rent can only be activated once the assessable income has reduced, and therefore the date to use as the change in circumstance is 26 May 2023. Stewart is paying rent to Kāinga Ora weekly on a Wednesday (his rent charge date). The new rent takes effect from the next rent period after the housing provider receives the notification from MSD. 26 May 2023 27 May 2023 29 May 2023 31 May 2023 Change in circumstances occurs and Income Related Rent reviewed Housing provider notified by MSD the rate of Income Related Rent has decreased due to a change in circumstances on 26 May 2023 Housing provider notifies tenant that the rent will change and when The earliest rent effective date is a Wednesday

chunks.title: Example 3 — income related rent
chunks.text: Michelle voluntarily left her job on 14 December 2022. MSD determines Michelle has deprived herself of the income from employment by voluntarily leaving without a good reason and the income she would have otherwise earned is included as assessable income for a further 13 weeks. After 13 weeks, the new rate of Income Related Rent is activated because the assessable income has reduced. Michelle is paying rent to Kāinga Ora weekly on a Thursday (her rent charge date). The new rent takes effect from the next rent period after the housing provider receives the notification from MSD. 15 March 2023 17 March 2023 18 March 2023 19 March 2023 Change in circumstances occurs and Income Related Rent reviewed Housing provider notified by MSD the rate of Income Related Rent has decreased due to a change in circumstances on 15 March 2023 Housing provider notifies tenant that the rent will change and when The earliest rent effective date is a Thursday

chunks.title: Examples of deprivation of income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Examples of deprivation of income
Deprivation of income may have occurred when an applicable person in the following situations (but not limited to):
- has not ensured that they will continue to have the right to get income from assets they have transferred to a family trust or other entity
- re-arranges their financial circumstances which reduces their income or assets after having received written advice of the income contribution they are required to make
- loans significant amounts of cash interest free
- gifts significant amounts of assets in any one particular year
- transfers or gifts a property to a trust or family member
- does not seek income from their family trust
- disclaims an inheritance
- self-employed and using assessable income for business development purposes (when in excess of reasonable amounts)
- transferring shareholdings to children or other people
- has a previous income stream such as estate income or trust income that ceases
- invested in Bonus Bonds instead of an income-earning account or term deposit
- charges rent for their property to their children or other people for an amount less than the market rent rate for the property
From 1 July 2023, an applicable person who does not apply for, or decides to end, a Child Support arrangement is not considered to be depriving themselves of income. This includes Child Support paid under a formula assessment via Inland Revenue.

chunks.title: Examples of notice periods for housing provider to increase the rent — income related rent
chunks.text: A housing provider must always issue notice to clients when they are increasing the rent. Below are examples of how these notice periods work. Note these examples assume that the housing provider will send written notice to change the rent by post within 2 days of receiving notification from MSD, however this may not always be the case. These examples also assume that the service period is four working days.

chunks.title: Example 1 - Kāinga Ora tenancy — income related rent
chunks.text: Anna starts her new part-time job and notifies MSD of the change on 26 June 2023. Her Income Related Rent is not reassessed until the end of the next consecutive 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start that occurs after she has maintained the employment for at least 8 weeks. The next consecutive 8-weekly anniversary of her tenancy start date is 11 September 2023. This is the date at which her change in circumstances is determined to be permanent. MSD activate and notify the housing provider of a new rate of Income Related Rent. Anna is paying rent to Kāinga Ora weekly on a Wednesday (rent charge date). In this situation, the new rent takes effect from the next rent period after the 61-day period. This is because the service period and the 14-day notice period required to be given by the housing provider to increase a rent is within the 61-day period. 26 June 2023 11 September 2023 12 September 2023 13 September 2023 12 November 2023 15 November 2023 Anna starts part-time work Next 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start after 8 weeks of employment. Permanent change in circumstances determined and Income Related Rent is reviewed. Housing provider notified by MSD that the rate of the Income Related Rent has increased due to a change in circumstances on 11 September 2023. MSD notify Anna of the new rate of Income Related Rent. Housing provider notifies the tenant of the change to their rent and the rent effective date the new rate will apply from. End of 61-day period calculated by CMS (+ 1 system day) - new rent takes effect from the earliest rent effective date. The earliest rent effective date is the Wednesday following the 61-day period. CMS will calculate the 61-day period + 1 system day as 11 September 2023 to 12 November 2023.

chunks.text: Debbie starts a part-time job on 26 June 2023. On the 17 July 2023 Debbie informs MSD that she started work.
