Debbie is paying rent to a community housing provider weekly on a Tuesday (rent charge date). In this situation, the new rent takes effect from the next rent period after the 61 day period. This is because the 14 day notice period required to be given by the housing provider to increase a rent is within the 61 day period. Housing provider notified by MSD that the rate of the Income Related Rent has increased due to a change in circumstances on 4 September 2023. MSD notify Debbie of the new rate of Income Related Rent. Housing provider notifies the tenant of the change to their rent and the rent effective date that the new rate will apply from. End of 61-day period calculated by CMS (+ 1 system day - rent takes effect from this day.) . CMS will calculate the 61 day period + 1 system day as 4 September 2023 to 5 November 2023.

chunks.title: Factors to consider when backdating — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Factors to consider when backdating
When considering whether to backdate an Income Related Rent, consider whether the reason provided:
- was unforeseen, out-of-the ordinary and could not be planned for
- was beyond the client's control or
- sets the client apart from others in a similar situation
Examples include (but are not limited to):
- unforeseen hospitalisation
- seriously sick or injured
- bereavement of immediate family
- emergency or adverse event
- victim of violent crime (including family violence)

chunks.title: Formula for calculating rate of Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Formula for calculating rate of Income Related Rent
The rate of Income Related Rent is calculated using both:
- the applicable rate of Jobseeker Support and
- the household income
The rate of Income Related Rent needs to be calculated using both methods and then the higher rate selected.
Note the calculated rate of Income Related Rent is rounded down to the nearest dollar.
For more information see:
- Assessable income
- Contributions from additional occupants
- Household types and income thresholds
- Calculation of Income Related Rent

chunks.title: Frequency of rent change — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Frequency of rent change
There are no limits to the number of times a client's calculated rate of Income Related Rent could change in a year.
How many times a client has a change each year depends on:
- how frequently they have a permanent change in circumstance
- the impact of that change on the clients calculated rate of Income Related Rent or
- any changes to the market rent rate for the property
An appropriate notice period for a rent increase must be given by the housing provider for every new calculated rate of Income Related Rent.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Getting Supported Living Payment for total blindness — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Getting Supported Living Payment for total blindness
If an applicable person is getting Supported Living Payment as they are totally blind, the Supported Living Payment is assessed as income for Income Related Rent purposes.
Any income earned by the applicable person from wages or salary is also included as assessable income.
## Partner
The partner's portion of Supported Living Payment is also included as assessable income, even if the client is getting Supported Living Payment as they are totally blind.

chunks.title: Grandparented rate for Kāinga Ora clients — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Grandparented rate for Kāinga Ora clients
On 1 December 2000, Income Related Rent replaced all accommodation assistance that was paid to Kāinga Ora (previously Housing NZ) clients. To ensure that no clients were worse off due to the transition to Income Related Rent, these tenancies had their rent capped at the net rent level as at 18 November 2000. Net rent is the rent payable to Kāinga Ora, less any accommodation assistance.
Before 1 December 2000, a client could have received the following accommodation assistance from Service Delivery:
- Tenure Protection Allowance
- Special Transfer Allowance
- Accommodation Supplement or
- Accommodation Benefit
Clients whose calculated rate of Income Related Rent was greater than net rent were given a special rent rebate. There are 2 types of rent rebates, these are known as:
- Abating caps and
- Non-abating caps
## Cumulative rent
The cumulative rent is a client's net rent on 1 December 2000, adjusted for any abatement in their cap at the time the Income Related Rent is calculated. The cumulative rent is the maximum rent that the client will pay while subject to the Income Related Rent grandparenting provisions.
If the calculated rate of Income Related Rent is below the cumulative rent then the client will pay the calculated rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Honoraria, payments to board of trustee members or local body members — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Honoraria, payments to board of trustee members or local body members
Board of trustee and local board members are generally entitled to a meeting fee set by the board.
Inland Revenue have established a benchmark for these fees, known as commonly paid amounts.
Some boards pay more than this. Some members choose not to take any payment.
Generally the amounts paid are as follows:
Commonly paid amounts
Inland Revenue maximum amounts
Trustee or local body members
$55 per meeting
$605 per year (11 meetings)
Chairperson
$75 per meeting
$825 per year (11 meetings)
For Income Related Rent purposes, commonly paid amounts are excluded from the calculation. However payments are included as assessable income when:
- they are in addition to the commonly paid amount (for example, travel) or
- the amount paid is above the commonly paid amount (for example, additional meetings held)
## Example
Edith is a trustee on her school's board; she is paid $55 for each meeting or $605 per year. In addition to this she is paid $20 for travel to the meetings or $220 per year.
Calculate the assessable income as follows:
Attendance at each meeting (disregard)
$605
Travel to the meetings
$220 = A
Divide additional amount for travel amount by 52 weeks (divide A by 52)
$4.23 = weekly amount to include in assessable income

chunks.title: Household types and income thresholds — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Household types and income thresholds
The household type is used to determine:
- the income threshold for the calculation of Income Related Rent and
- the rate of Jobseeker Support to use in the calculation
Note the household type is automatically determined in CMS from information recorded at the assessment.
There are 2 household types:
- sole tenant household - a single client with no partner and no dependent children
- all other household types
## Sole tenant household type
A sole tenant household type is where there is only a single client with no dependent children who is:
- applying for Income Related Rent and who will have their name on the tenancy agreement or
- living in the house or
- for shared housing purposes, living in one bedroom
A sole tenant household type does not always mean that there is only one person living in the house, there could be additional occupants, other people, or children who are not considered to be dependent children living in the property.
For example, a person paying a contribution or a child for whom Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid. See: Children in the household type
## All other household types
All other household types is where there is:
- more than one tenant's name on the tenancy agreement (for example, a joint tenancy)
- a client with a partner (for example, where the partner's name is not on the tenancy agreement) or
- a sole parent
## Partner is not included
A partner is not included in the household type when the partner:
- does not meet the residence criteria, including a grandparented non-qualified partner of a client on benefit
- is overseas on a permanent basis
- is in prison on a permanent basis
- is in residential or rest home care on a permanent basis
In these circumstances, the household type will be:
- sole tenant - where there are no dependent children or
- other household type - where there are dependent children
Note that a partner who is not getting a benefit, but would otherwise qualify for a benefit will still be included in this household type.

chunks.title: Housing provider actions new rent calculated — income related rent
chunks.text: When a housing provider receives notification that the client has a new rate of Income Related Rent calculated, they must: - review the amount of rent charged - change the amount of the rent charged to the rate of Income Related Rent calculated and notified, unless: in their opinion it would not make any material difference to the rent currently charged orthe rate is higher than market rent rate for the property, in which case they may only charge up to market rent rate - in their opinion it would not make any material difference to the rent currently charged or - the rate is higher than market rent rate for the property, in which case they may only charge up to market rent rate - work out which is the correct notice period to give the client, which is either the 14-day notice period or the 60-day notice period - advise MSD that they are changing the amount of the rent charged and the new rent effective date and - notify their tenant about the change to the amount of rent, the new amount rent charged and the new rent effective date Generally, the rate that the housing providers charge as weekly rent will be the same as the weekly calculated rate of Income Related Rent. For more information see: - Client must be given notice of rent increase - annual review - Clients must be given notice of rent increase - change in circumstances - Tenant has subsequent change in circumstances after notice issued - Rent rate charged is different from calculated rate

chunks.title: Changes to the Tenancy Agreement — income related rent
chunks.text: The housing provider can set up the Tenancy Agreement so that it does not need to be amended where a housing provider makes a change to the rent. Clients living in social housing properties are made aware that their rent can change following any change to their circumstances or their annual review of Income Related Rent when they sign the Tenancy Agreement with the housing provider. Kāinga Ora currently use this form of Tenancy Agreement, community housing providers may also choose to do so.

chunks.title: Calculated rate of Income Related Rent is equal or higher than market rent — income related rent
chunks.text: If the rate of Income Related Rent is calculated at a rate that is equal to or higher than the market rent, the housing provider must charge the rent at a rate no greater than the market rent rate for the property.

chunks.title: Housing provider actions new rent for clients paying rent at the market rent rate — income related rent
chunks.text: A housing provider can change a client's rent when the client is paying rent at the market rent rate, according to their own policies, and within the limits of the Residential Tenancies Act 1986. The rent charged cannot be greater than the market rent rate at the time.

chunks.title: Housing provider gives 60-day notice period — income related rent
chunks.text: In certain situations the housing provider must give a 60-day notice period and advise the client of this in writing (not the 61-day period). A housing provider must use the 60-day notice period when: - notified by MSD that the rate of Income Related Rent is set at the market rent rate in the following circumstances: when a client has not completed an annual review form or provided sufficient information to process an annual reviewwhen a client has had a change in circumstances but has not provided sufficient information to process the review within 10-working dayswhen there is a mismatch of additional occupant contributions and accommodation costs, and it has not been resolved within 10 working days after the date of the mismatch being notified to both clients - when a client has not completed an annual review form or provided sufficient information to process an annual review - when a client has had a change in circumstances but has not provided sufficient information to process the review within 10-working days - when there is a mismatch of additional occupant contributions and accommodation costs, and it has not been resolved within 10 working days after the date of the mismatch being notified to both clients - notified by MSD that the rate of Income Related Rent has been increased at annual review due to the annual general adjustment to the rates of MSD's financial assistance - the client is paying rent at the market rent rate and the housing provider increases the rate of market rent

chunks.title: Notification requirements — income related rent
chunks.text: The amount of the rent charged by the housing provider cannot increase until the earliest rent effective date following the 60-day notice period. On getting such a notification (where applicable): - Kāinga Ora must charge the market rent for the housing or - community housing providers may set the rent themselves but must not charge more than the market rent for the housing and The 60-day notice period requires the housing provider to consider whether the rent has been increased within a 12-month period. If the rent has been increased within a 12-month period, the housing provider cannot further increase the rent until the 12-month period has finished. This means that in some limited situations, an increase to the market rent rate will not be applied to a social housing client (unless another change of circumstances review changes the rate of Income Related Rent): - within 12-months of the day after the rent increased last or - within 12-months after the day the tenancy started Note that MSD would continue to pay the housing provider the Income Related Rent subsidy during the 180 day period (or applicable part of the period).

chunks.title: Income considered on case by case basis — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Income considered on case by case basis
The following sources of income should be considered as assessable income on a case by case basis:
- funeral benefit income paid by Friendly Societies and Credit Unions
- payments from trust funds and assets held in trust
- debt, health or disability insurance income
- life insurance income or
- any insurance paid as weekly compensation for loss of earnings, or potential earning capacity must be considered as income. Lump sum payments must be treated as savings/investments unless they are Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) lump sum payments. See Income from assets
You should consider the following:
- the purpose and frequency of the payments and
- what the payment is being used or being made for, for example insurance payments that are being made for replacement income purposes may be considered to be assessable income
If you need help deciding whether assessable income is being generated from any of the above sources, contact Helpline for advice.
Note in addition to the types of income that are considered on a case by case basis, contributions from additional occupants are sometimes, but not always, required to be treated as assessable income.

chunks.title: Income from assets — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Income from assets
The income from applicable people's assets over the asset threshold is included as assessable income when calculating the rate of Income Related Rent.
Income from assets is:
- the value of any income acquired from the assessable asset or
- the estimated income (after income tax) that the assessable asset would generate
whichever is the greater.
Only income from assets over the asset threshold is to be included as a client's assessable income.
The income from assessable assets is included as assessable income in the Income Related Rent calculation as a weekly rate.
For more information see:
- Asset thresholds and formula to work out assessable income from assets
- Assessable assets
- Treatment of specific assets
- Deprivation of income

chunks.title: Income of additional occupants — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Income of additional occupants
The income of additional occupants is not included in the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent.
However, if the applicable persons of the household are getting contributions from additional occupants, the contributions will be included in the calculation of Income Related Rent for the household.
For more information see:
- Contributions from additional occupants

chunks.title: Increasing the rate of Income Related Rent to the market rent rate — income related rent
chunks.text: In certain situations MSD can make a decision that a client's rate of Income Related Rent should be set at the market rent rate. This may happen: - when a client has not completed an annual review form or provided sufficient information to process an annual review - when a client has had a change in circumstances but has not provided sufficient information to process the review within 10 working days of the information being requested - when there is a mismatch of additional occupant contributions and accommodation costs, and it has not been resolved within 10 working days after the date of the mismatch being notified to both clients Following this decision MSD will need to notify the housing provider that a rate of Income Related Rent cannot be calculated for the client and must: - provide the client with a statement that: they have provided insufficient information and the date MSD determined this (where applicable)MSD determined that the Income Related Rent should increase to the market rent rate for the property (where applicable)the client has the right to request a review of the decision to recalculate the rate of Income Related Rentwhile MSD has determined Income Related Rent should be set at the market rent rate, it is the housing provider who actually decides whether there will be a change in the rent charged and the rent effective datethe change to the rate of Income Related Rent is due to insufficient information being provided by the clientthe Income Related Rent is equal to market rent rate for the property andincludes the date MSD processed the change - they have provided insufficient information and the date MSD determined this (where applicable) - MSD determined that the Income Related Rent should increase to the market rent rate for the property (where applicable) - the client has the right to request a review of the decision to recalculate the rate of Income Related Rent - while MSD has determined Income Related Rent should be set at the market rent rate, it is the housing provider who actually decides whether there will be a change in the rent charged and the rent effective date - the change to the rate of Income Related Rent is due to insufficient information being provided by the client - the Income Related Rent is equal to market rent rate for the property and - includes the date MSD processed the change The market rent rate is the maximum rent a social housing client can be charged. The housing provider cannot charge a rent greater than the market rent rate for the property.

chunks.title: Insufficient information to calculate a correct rate — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Insufficient information to calculate a correct rate
Generally, if the information received from the client is insufficient to complete the review you will need to attempt to contact the client to provide the information required. The client should be given 10 working days to provide the additional information you require (from the date of the first request).
If a client is also a beneficiary and provides insufficient information you can consider whether the information MSD hold is sufficient to process the review without getting the client to provide additional information.
You may consider that information is not sufficient if you decide that:
- a client has not declared their correct or relevant income details or
- there is insufficient information on which to calculate a correct rate of Income Related Rent

chunks.title: Insufficient information to calculate Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Insufficient information to calculate Income Related Rent
A prospective tenant must provide all the necessary information required for the calculation of Income Related Rent.
You need to be satisfied that a prospective tenant has declared their correct and relevant circumstances.
If the rate cannot be confirmed at the time the client is placed in a property you should not delay the placement process for the housing provider. Instead you should notify the housing provider that a rate of Income Related Rent cannot be calculated.
When they get the notice:
- Kāinga Ora must charge the market rent rate for the property or
- the community housing provider may set the rent themselves but it must not be higher than the market rent rate for the property

chunks.title: Introduction — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Income Related Rent is a subsidised rent scheme for social housing tenants with low incomes.
Social housing providers include Kāinga Ora and approved community housing providers.
MSD calculates the rate of Income Related Rent and the social housing provider charges this rate as rent to the client.
The rate of Income Related Rent is calculated based on a client's assessable income, additional occupant contributions and their household type.
If the rate of Income Related Rent calculated is higher than the market rent rate for the property, the housing provider will charge the client the market rent rate.

chunks.title: Lump sum for impairment — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Lump sum for impairment
If an applicable person has received a lump sum paid under the Accident Compensation Act 2001, the asset threshold is increased by the amount of the lump sum payment for 12 months from the date the payment is received.
After 12 months the calculated rate of Income Related Rent must be reviewed and this amount will be included as income from an asset.
For more information see:
- Income from assets
- Asset thresholds and formula to work out assessable income from assets
- Lump sum payment of an independence allowance

chunks.title: Lump sum payment of an independence allowance — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Lump sum payment of an independence allowance
If an applicable person has received a lump sum payment of an Independence Allowance under the Accident Insurance Act 1998, the asset threshold is increased by the amount of the lump sum payment for 12 months from the date the payment is received.
After 12 months the calculated rate of Income Related Rent must be reviewed and this amount will be included as income from an asset.
For more information see:
- Income from assets
- Asset thresholds and formula to work out assessable income from assets
- Lump sum for impairment
- Income, Accident Compensation Independence Allowance

chunks.title: Material difference to the rate of Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Material difference to the rate of Income Related Rent
A change to the rate of Income Related Rent should only be activated and notified to the housing provider if the change makes a material difference.
The calculated rate of Income Related Rent is always rounded down to the nearest dollar.
## Change to the rate making a material difference
A material difference, during a change in circumstances review, is where the new calculated rate of Income Related Rent is:
- an increase to the rate of $5 or more per week or
- a decrease to the rate of more than a dollar per week
## Change to the rate making a material difference at annual review
A material difference, during an annual review, is where the new calculated rate of Income Related Rent is:
- an increase to the rate of a dollar or more per week or
- a decrease to the rate of more than a dollar per week
An increase to the rate of Income Related Rent of between a dollar and less than $5 per week is only activated and notified to a housing provider once a year. This is to ensure:
- that housing providers do not have to regularly change rents for very small increases during the year and
- that beneficiaries rate of Income Related Rent is not affected by small benefit rate changes
## Housing provider may also consider material difference
On receiving notification of a new rate of Income Related Rent, housing providers may decide not to increase the rent they charge if they consider it would not make a material difference to the rate of rent charged.

chunks.title: Minimum family tax credit — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Minimum family tax credit
For Income Related Rent purposes, the minimum family tax credit applicable people are entitled to get is included as assessable income.
Minimum family tax credit is a payment made to families with dependent children aged 18 or younger, so they have a minimum income each week after tax.
Generally, the assessment to estimate the minimum family tax credit is as follows:
- determine if the applicable people are entitled to get a minimum family tax credit
- determine their estimated after-tax annual income for wages and salary
- work out the annual rate they would be entitled to get from the minimum family tax credits - to do this: get the current Inland Revenue threshold for minimum family tax creditsubtract the annual income from the threshold rateinclude this amount in the assessable income
- get the current Inland Revenue threshold for minimum family tax credit
- subtract the annual income from the threshold rate
- include this amount in the assessable income
## Example of estimating minimum family tax credit
Rena is a sole parent with one child aged 14 years. She works 23 hours per week and earns $23,411.96 (net) per year, ($450.23 (net) per week).
Rena can get a minimum family tax credit to top up her net income to $703.00 per week (at 1 April 2026).
Calculate the minimum family tax credit to include as assessable income as follows:
Determine the amount to include as assessable income
Inland Revenue after tax threshold for minimum family tax credit (at 1 April 2026)
$36,604.00 = A
Less client's annual income (after tax)
$23,411.96 = B
Annual entitlement to minimum family tax credit (= A minus B)
$13,192.04 = C
Weekly entitlement (C divided by 52)
$253.69 = weekly amount to include in assessable income
## Minimum family tax credit and joint tenancies
The total amount of wage and salary income of all applicable people is included in the assessable income calculation.
Although an applicable person may be getting minimum family tax credit or family tax credit, the calculation may not include it as assessable income, if the total wage and salary income for all applicable people is over the Inland Revenue income thresholds.

chunks.title: Net equity in a property — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Net equity in a property
The net equity in a property is:
- house and/or land value
less
- outstanding mortgage only (no interest)
## Net equity in a vehicle, caravan or boat
Net equity in a vehicle, caravan or boat is the amount of money the applicable person would have if they sold their vehicle, caravan or boat after they had paid any debts owing on it.
## Example
Tom has a boat that has a market value of $4000 but he still owes the bank $1500, so the net equity would be $2500. This is the amount that Tom would get if he sold the boat at market value and paid the bank what it was owed.
For more information see:
- Property not used as home
- Net equity in former home

chunks.title: Net equity in former family home — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Net equity in former family home
When a client has separated they may own, or jointly own the family home.
In this case do not assess the client's net equity in the home until:
- a decision on the sale of the home is made or
- there is a Relationship Property Settlement (previously matrimonial property settlement) - under a Property Agreement or Property Order
whichever is earlier.
Note that any rent the applicable person receives from the property needs to be counted as assessable income.

chunks.title: Non-abating cap — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Non-abating cap
If the client's rate of Income Related Rent is greater than what they were paying as rent prior to the change and they were getting Tenure Protection Allowance or Special Transfer Allowance then they are eligible for a non-abating cap.
## Example of non-abating cap
Rent payable before 1 December 2000
$115
Tenure Protection Allowance paid
$11
Net rent on 1 December 2000
$104 = A
Income Related Rent calculated on 1 December
$180 = B
Cap (discount) (= B - A)
$76 = C
Cumulative Rent (= Net rent on 1 December 2000 as not abated)
$104 = D
Calculated rate of Income Related Rent on 14 April 2023
$200 = E
Rent charged as at 14 April 2023 (lesser of D and E)
$104

chunks.title: Notifying a new rate of Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Notifying a new rate of Income Related Rent
When you have completed a review of a client's calculated Income Related Rent, you need to decide whether to activate and notify the housing provider of a new rate.
A change to the rate of Income Related Rent should only be activated and notified to the housing provider if the change makes a material difference.
For more information see:
- Material difference to the rate of Income Related Rent
## Rate of Income Related Rent is not notified
If the calculated rate of Income Related Rent is not activated or notified to the housing provider then the rate of Income Related Rent stays the same as previously calculated.
The client is not advised in this situation.
## Notifying housing provider and client of rent change
When you activate and notify a new rate of the Income Related Rent you must provide the client with:
- an acknowledgement of the change in circumstances that has occurred
- the date that it was determined that the change in circumstances took effect from
- the new rate of Income Related Rent calculated
- a statement the client has the right to request a review of the decision to recalculate the rate of Income Related Rent and
- a statement making it clear that while the rate of Income Related Rent has been recalculated, it is the housing provider who actually decides whether there will be a change in the rent charged and the rent effective date
- advise the housing provider that: the change to the rate is due to a change in the applicable person's circumstances orthe change to the rate is due to insufficient information being provided by the applicable person andthe date that you determined that the change in circumstances has taken affect from andthe new rate of Income Related Rent calculated
- the change to the rate is due to a change in the applicable person's circumstances or
- the change to the rate is due to insufficient information being provided by the applicable person and
- the date that you determined that the change in circumstances has taken affect from and
- the new rate of Income Related Rent calculated
Note during an annual review the housing provider will need to know if the change to the rate of Income Related Rent is due to the annual review, and the date of processing of the annual review.

chunks.title: Other sources of income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Other sources of income
The following sources of income are treated the same as in Income support, Core policy. See:
- Accident Compensation
- Child Support payments
- Christchurch mosques attack support payments and income earned on the payment
- Crown funds provided directly to clients to purchase Support Services and Direct Disability Support payments
- Education paymentsStudent LoansHome education supervision allowance - from Ministry of EducationStudent support payment from Te Kura - Distance School
- Student Loans
- Home education supervision allowance - from Ministry of Education
- Student support payment from Te Kura - Distance School
- Employment related income
- Wages and salary (includes allowances)
- Commission work
- Compensation or damages
- Fees for jury service
- Goods, services, accommodation in lieu of money
- Green dollar trading
- Carer's allowances and other payments
- Parental leave payments
- Payments from family day care schemes
- Payments from friendly and like societies
- Reimbursement of expenses
- Sale of artworks
- Sponsorship
- Energy Trust Dividends and income earned on the payment for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Estate income and wills
- Ex gratia and compensation
- Gifts
- Home equity conversion schemes
- Insurance
- Kāinga Ora energy subsidy
- Lotteries prizes and gambling wins
- Money withdrawn from a KiwiSaver scheme
- MSD lump sum payments
- Payments of arrears to Special Benefit clients better off on Temporary Additional Support
- Payments to clients whose Kāinga Ora tenancy was terminated due to methamphetamine contamination
- Payments to victims of crime and their families
- Rental property income
- Residential Care Subsidy historic review refunds and income earned on the payment for the first 12 months after the payment is made
- Sale of assets
- Superannuation scheme accounts
For information about overseas pensions see:
- To or from overseas Payments from overseas

chunks.title: Overpayment of benefit — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Overpayment of benefit
When a client has been overpaid benefit and the resulting debt will be recovered by MSD, the client's Income Related Rent will be reviewed based on their circumstances over the period that the benefit debt has been established for.
The process for reviewing the rate of Income Related Rent once a benefit overpayment has been established involves:
- checking if the client's circumstances over the period the overpayment was incurred has affected their assessable income, additional occupant contributions and/or household type
- calculating the rate of Income Related Rent over the period the overpayment was incurred
- establishing an Income Related Rent debt or refund as appropriate
- calculating the client's current rate of Income Related Rent as appropriate
Note a client's current rate of Income Related Rent may not change as a result of a benefit overpayment.
## Benefit income over the period the overpayment was incurred
If a benefit has been overpaid and a debt established which is to be recovered by MSD, the amount of benefit income used when reviewing the Income Related Rent for that period will be the assessed rate of benefit:
- after entitlement has been reviewed for the period the overpayment was incurred and
- after any income reduction and
- before any deductions are made, deductions for court fines or Crown debt
Any amount of benefit established as an overpayment and to be recovered by MSD should not be included when reviewing Income Related Rent over the period the benefit overpayment was incurred.
For more information see:
## Current benefit income
When reviewing a client's current rate of Income Related Rent, the amount of benefit included as income will be the benefit payable:
- after any income reduction and
- before any deductions are made, such as failure to assist for Child Support, or deductions for court fines or Crown debt
Note when the benefit overpayment is established due to fraud, the Income Related Rent debt or refund is established by Client Service Integrity.
The Centralised Unit Housing will review the current rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Period of the backdate — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Period of the backdate
If the client meets the criteria, you can consider backdating to any earlier date you consider the client would have applied had they been able to. This may be between:
- the start date of the tenancy (the commencement of the tenancy), but cannot be any earlier and
- the date that full and correct information was subsequently provided
A refund must be issued for the period from the date you decide to backdate to and to the day before the last rent effective date.

chunks.title: Permanent change becomes a temporary change — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Permanent change becomes a temporary change
Generally, if a permanent change becomes a temporary change, review the rate of the Income Related Rent from the date considered that the assessable income or additional occupant contributions have reduced or increased.
This means, that the date of the change of circumstances would be date the change became a temporary change.
## Example
On 9 June Sarah-Louise was granted a benefit as her hours at work were decreasing permanently. Her rate of Income Related Rent was reviewed from this date and decreased accordingly. On 23 June Sarah-Louise phoned and advised that her hours had increased on an on-going basis and the benefit was stopped.
In this situation review the rate of Income Related Rent from the 23 June. Do not backdate the rate or create a debt for the period.
## Permanent changes and increases
Where a client advised that their change in circumstances was permanent and their rate of Income Related Rent was increased, and it is subsequently determined that the change was temporary, review the client's rate of Income Related Rent and decrease the rate.
Generally, in this situation, it is not needed to backdate the rate Income Related Rent or issue a refund.
## Permanent changes and decreases
Where a client advised that their change in circumstances was permanent and their rate of Income Related Rent was decreased, and it is subsequently determined that the change was temporary, review the client's rate of Income Related Rent and increase the rate.
Generally, no debt would be created unless it is considered that the client intentionally misled MSD by not provided the correct information about their circumstances.
For more information see:
- Deciding if changes are permanent or temporary
- Tenant has subsequent change but notice already issued
- Reviews of the rate of Income Related Rent
- Refunds and backdating a rate of Income Related Rent during a review
- Date of change in circumstances
- Social housing Income Related Rent debt

chunks.title: Prepaid funeral expenses — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Prepaid funeral expenses
A pre-paid funeral trust fund or account, is money put aside (usually in a trust) exclusively for the payment of funeral expenses.
If the money can be accessed by the client and used for other purposes, it is not considered exclusively for funeral expenses and this money is included as an assessable asset for Income Related Rent.
It is usually clear whether or not the trust fund or account has been genuinely set aside for funeral expenses.
Evidence that it has been set aside exclusively for funeral expenses include:
- the trust fund or account is only paid out on production of a death certificate
- the client cannot usually access the funds
- if a client can access the fund, there are limited conditions on withdrawal, such as re-locating overseas
- the trust fund or account is only payable to the funeral director or administrator of the client's estate
- the client cannot generally access the interest earned from the trust fund or account
Where the trust fund or account has been set aside for funeral expenses and cannot be accessed or converted into cash, then this money is not considered to be an assessable asset for Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Property not used as a home — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Property not used as a home
A client may have a property (including boats and caravans) they do not use as a home for themselves or their family. Consider whether that property is a realisable asset.
There is an expectation that clients will utilise their own resources to support themselves, including any property that they may own or have an interest in that is not their home property or land on which their home is situated.
Points to consider when determining whether the property should be considered as a realisable asset include:
- What was the property originally bought for?
- What is the client's intention with the property?
- Is the property on the market?
- Is the asking price realistic?
- Is the property listed with a real estate agent?
- What is the location of the property?
If the property is a realisable asset you must then decide what effect this has on the assessable income.
When assessing the value of any realisable asset (for example, a piece of land or a rental property) you will need to calculate the net equity that the client holds in the asset.
In general you should treat any realisable asset the way you would 'cash assets'. If the applicable people's combined cash assets and realisable assets exceed the asset threshold, then this would be included as an assessable asset when calculating the rate of Income Related Rent.
## Exception
A client's net equity in the former family home may be disregarded for a period of time when they have separated from their partner.
For more information see:
- Net equity in former home
- Net equity
- Core policy, Income Rental property income

chunks.title: Refunds and backdating a rate of Income Related Rent during a review — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Refunds and backdating a rate of Income Related Rent during a review
Income Related Rent is not a payment or a benefit; it is a calculated rate of subsidised rent.
Where a decision has been made to backdate the rate of Income Related Rent a refund needs to be issued.
The refund to the client represents the same amount of money that would have been paid as an Income Related Rent Subsidy to the housing provider had the correct rate of Income Related Rent been calculated for the earlier period in the first place.

chunks.title: Refunds - paying to client and the housing provider — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Refunds - paying to client and the housing provider
In some situations, you may need to issue the refund to the client and to the housing provider.
This can happen when the client has paid some but not all of the rent charged to their housing provider.
The refund remaining after the housing provider has been paid is due to the client.
A refund may be used to repay current MSD debt only if the client agrees to this. If the client does not agree, or you are not able to contact the client, the refund must be issued directly to the client.
## Example
The client's rate of Income Related Rent and rate of rent charged was $130 per week. A decision is made to backdate the rate of Income Related Rent and issue a refund. The new rate of Income Related Rent is $91 per week.
The refund period is between 12 August 2023 and 26 August 2023. During this period the client made three rent payments.
Refund period (12 August 2023 and 26 August 2023)

The difference between the rate of Income Related Rent and the new lower rate for the period is $117. This is the total refund amount for the period.
The client has under paid their rent by $90.
A refund of $90 would be issued to the housing provider and a refund of $27 would be issued to the client.

chunks.title: Refunds - paying to joint tenants — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Refunds - paying to joint tenants
The refund remaining after the housing provider has been paid may be due to joint tenants.
Where a decision has been made to issue a refund to a tenant in a joint tenancy situation, you must seek agreement from the joint tenants as to where and who the refund should be issued to. The refund can either be:
- issued to one of the tenants on the tenancy
- split between all the tenants on the tenancy or
- issued to a joint bank account
If you are unable to get agreement after contacting or attempting to contact each of the tenants on the tenancy:
- if you can identify what each tenant paid towards the Income Related Rent over the period, you should issue the refund to all of the tenants on the tenancy based on the portion of the Income Related Rent they paid
- if you cannot identify what each tenant paid towards the Income Related Rent over the period, you should issue the refund in equal portions to all of the tenants on the tenancy
A tenant's share of any refund may be used to repay current MSD debt only if the relevant tenant agrees to this. If the tenant does not agree, or you are not able to contact the tenant, the refund must be issued directly to the tenant.

chunks.title: Refunds - paying to the client — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Refunds - paying to the client
Where the client has paid the higher amount of rent that the housing provider has charged the refund is due to the client.
This is because the refund is essentially the same amount of rent the client has overpaid to the housing provider.
A refund may be used to repay current MSD debt only if the client agrees to this. If the client does not agree, or you are not able to contact the client, the refund must be issued directly to the client.
## Example
The client's rate of Income Related Rent and rate of rent charged was $100 per week.
A decision is made to backdate the rate of Income Related Rent and issue a refund. The new rate of Income Related Rent is $52 per week.
The client has paid the higher amount of rent to the housing provider.
The refund period is between 15 January 2023 and 5 February 2023. During this period the client made four rent payments.

The difference between the rate of Income Related Rent and the new lower rate for the period is $192. This is the total refund amount for the period. A refund of $192 would be issued to the client.

chunks.title: Refunds - paying to the housing provider — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Refunds - paying to the housing provider
Where the client has not paid, or has underpaid the rent to their housing provider for the same period that the refund is due, the refund should be issued directly to the housing provider.
This is because the client does not need to be compensated because they never paid the higher amount of rent.
Instead the refund is issued to the housing provider to compensate for the Income Related Rent Subsidy they didn't get for the same period due to the incorrect rate of Income Related Rent that was previously calculated.
The housing provider will confirm to MSD:
- the client has not paid the correct rent to the housing provider during the refund period
- the amount of rent arrears that has been accrued during the refund period
Note that a refund cannot be used to repay historical rent arrears that is outside of the refund period.
## Example
The client's rate of Income Related Rent and rate of rent charged was $260 per week. A decision is made to backdate the rate of Income Related Rent and issue a refund. The new rate of Income Related Rent is $65 per week.
The client has not paid the higher amount of rent to their housing provider.
The refund period is between 15 January 2023 and 5 February 2023. During this period the client made four rent payments.
