chunks.title: Relevant information was subsequently provided - at review — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Relevant information was subsequently provided - at review
When reviewing the rate of Income Related Rent and the client did not provide the required verification within 10-working days, but they have subsequently provided the information requested, and the information is accurate, you may consider backdating to the date they provided the information.
The refund is paid for the period between the dates they subsequently provided the information to the day prior to the rent effective date that the correct rate of Income Related Rent was applied.

chunks.title: Rent rate charged is different from calculated rate — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Rent rate charged is different from calculated rate
Housing providers can only charge a rate lower than the rate of Income Related Rent calculated where:
- there are special circumstances or
- there is no material difference between the rent charged and the rate calculated by MSD
## Special circumstances
Generally, the rate of Income Related Rent calculated by MSD will be the same rate that the housing providers charge as rent to their tenant.
In special circumstances, the housing provider can make a decision to charge a rent lower than the rate of Income Related Rent calculated.
Special circumstances can be considered where, for example, the housing provider is renovating a property or the property is not of 'market' quality.
Note housing providers cannot claim for additional Income Related Rent Subsidy when this decision is made.
## No material difference in the rent charged
Generally, the rate of Income Related Rent calculated by MSD will be the same rate that housing providers charge as rent to their tenants.
On receiving notification of a new rate of Income Related Rent calculated, housing providers may decide not to increase the rent they charge if they consider it would not make a material difference (to the rate of rent charged).
Note housing providers can claim for additional Income Related Rent Subsidy when this decision is made.
## Rate calculated is greater than the market rent rate
The housing provider cannot charge a rent greater than the market rent rate for the property, which is the maximum rent a social housing client can be charged.
The rate of Income Related Rent calculated can be higher than the market rent rate. In this situation housing providers must not charge more than the market rent rate.
The housing provider may increase the rent if the market rent rate increases, but the rent cannot be increased to a rate more than the last notified rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: What a retirement payment is not — income related rent
chunks.text:
## What a retirement payment is not
It is important to differentiate between the types of payments a person gets when their employment ends to know how they affect entitlement to Income Related Rent.
Retirement payments do not include:
- a payment solely due to a seasonal lay-off
- a payment that depends on the completion of: a fixed-term engagement oran engagement to complete work specified in a contract
- a fixed-term engagement or
- an engagement to complete work specified in a contract
- a payment instead of notice terminating the employment
- any payment (including holiday pay) if MSD considers that, but for the termination of the employment, it would have been paid as monetary remuneration of the person
- any payment made by a company, to a director of a company or
- any payment from a superannuation fund or other similar payment
Note some of these other payments may affect the date employment ceased.
## How retirement payments affect Income Related Rent payments
Retirement payments can be paid in one or more lump sums or on a periodical basis.
Payment received before Income Related Rent is granted
Retirement payments do affect the date employment ceased and are included as assessable income.
Note this does not apply to retirement payments received more than 52 weeks after the date the client's employment ceased. Those payments do not affect the date employment ceased and are only included as assessable assets.
Payment received after Income Related Rent is granted
When a client getting Income Related Rent has been working and then gets a retirement payment, this payment is not regarded as assessable income.
However, it will be regarded as an assessable asset for Income Related Rent purposes and may affect any Extra Help the client is getting.
## Not retiring
In some situations a person may cease their employment for a reason other than retirement and get a retirement payment as part of their final pay. For example, when a person resigns from their role voluntarily because they want to change careers or have a holiday.
Retirement pay received when a person is not retiring does not affect the date employment ceased.

chunks.title: Reviewing Income Related Rent following a permanent change — income related rent
chunks.text: At the end of each consecutive 8-week period following the anniversary of the tenancy start date, the client's circumstances and the circumstances for other members of the household may be reviewed to identify any permanent changes. Where a permanent change is identified at an 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start, the Income Related Rent will be reviewed.

chunks.title: Increase to Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text: Generally, where there is a change in circumstances that will result in an increase to Income Related Rent, the change is determined to be permanent once it has lasted for 8 weeks or more. At each consecutive 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start: - if there is evidence of a permanent change in circumstances that will result in an increase in Income Related Rent, the Income Related Rent will be reviewed (ie where a change has lasted for 8 weeks or more) - if there is no evidence of a permanent change in circumstances that will result in an increase in Income Related Rent, the Income Related Rent will not be reviewed (ie when there has not been a change that has lasted for 8 weeks or longer) If a change has not lasted for at least 8-weeks at the current 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start, but continues and at the end of the next 8-week period has lasted for 8-weeks or more, the Income Related Rent will then be reviewed.

chunks.title: Child Support — income related rent
chunks.text: If a client gets Child Support under a formula assessment from Inland Revenue and there is a change to that Child Support resulting in an increase to Income Related Rent, MSD will generally consider the change permanent from the date of change. The change does not need to have lasted for 8 weeks or more. Note when MSD gets Child Support details through the information share agreement with Inland Revenue, MSD must send the client a notice of adverse action before including the information share Child Support as assessable income after 10 working days. This also gives the client 10 working days to tell MSD if the information is incorrect.

chunks.title: Decrease to Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text: If there has been a change in circumstances that will result in a decrease in Income Related Rent, this is generally considered to be permanent if it is likely to last or has lasted for 8 weeks or more. At each consecutive 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start: - if there is evidence of a permanent change in circumstances that will result in a decrease in Income Related Rent, the Income Related Rent will be reviewed (ie a change that is likely to last or has lasted 8 weeks or more) - if there is no evidence of a permanent change in circumstances that will result in a decrease in Income Related Rent, the Income Related Rent will not be reviewed (i.e. there has not been a change that is likely to last or has lasted for longer than 8-weeks) When a client contacts MSD to notify of a change in circumstances that will result in a decrease in their Income Related Rent and the change is expected to last for 8 weeks or more, you can determine the change is permanent from the point of contact. For example: If you were able to confirm at the point of contact that the change is expected to last for more than 8 weeks, you would determine that it is a permanent change and review the Income Related Rent immediately. However, if you are unable to confirm that the change is expected to last for 8 weeks or more at the point of contact, you would not be able to determine if it is a permanent change and would wait until the next consecutive 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start to review the Income Related Rent if the change continued.

chunks.title: Example 1 — income related rent
chunks.text: A client with regular income has an increase in their weekly earnings. Week 1 to 8 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start Week 9 to 16 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start Anniversary of the tenancy start Week 6 - Client calls to declare increase in income (weekly income increases by $70). The change is recorded but the Income Related Rent is not reviewed until change has lasted for at least 8-weeks or more. Income Related Rent is not reviewed as there has been no permanent change in circumstances - the income change from week 6 has not lasted for 8-weeks or more. Increase to weekly income continues for the entire period. Income Related Rent is reviewed using the average weekly income from week 9 to 16.

chunks.title: Example 2 — income related rent
chunks.text: A client has had a permanent reduction in hours and their earnings have decreased. Week 1 to 8 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start Week 9 to 16 8-weekly anniversary of the tenancy start Anniversary of the tenancy start Week 6 - Client calls to declare a reduction in income that is expected to be permanent (weekly income decreases by $180) The change is recorded and the Income Related Rent is reviewed. Income Related Rent is not reviewed as there has been no further permanent change in circumstances. No further changes. Income Related Rent is not reviewed as there has been no permanent change in circumstances

chunks.title: Reviews of the rate of Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Reviews of the rate of Income Related Rent
A client's calculated rate of Income Related Rent can be reviewed to check whether:
- it remains correct or
- a different rate should have been calculated from an earlier date
A review of the rate of Income Related Rent will be undertaken at least annually.
Additional reviews can be undertaken:
- when the client has a permanent change in circumstances or
- there is a permanent change in circumstances for other members of the household, including dependent children or
- when the client requests a review
At each review MSD must consider whether:
- another rate of Income Related Rent is more appropriate and
- it is appropriate to backdate a lower rate of Income Related Rent to an earlier date and establish a refund or
- a higher rate of Income Related Rent should have been applied from an earlier date and if it is appropriate to establish a debt from that date
The process for reviewing the rate of Income Related Rent involves:
- determining whether any change in circumstances of an applicable person is a permanent or temporary change
- checking if any change in circumstances of an applicable person has affected their assessable income, additional occupant contributions or household type
- calculating the rate of Income Related Rent
- deciding if the new rate of Income Related Rent should be activated and notified to the housing provider
Note that social housing providers will decide the date when the new rate should be applied (the rent effective date).

chunks.title: Scholarships — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Scholarships
An applicable person may get an educational scholarship payment to assist with their study and associated costs. Depending on the scholarship agreement, some or all of the scholarship payment may be included as assessable income for Income Related Rent.
## When a scholarship is assessable income?
Any portion of a scholarship paid for living costs or that can be used as the recipient wishes will generally be considered assessable income for Income Related Rent purposes when it is paid for a period over which Income Related Rent is assessed.
Any portion of a scholarship paid for fees or course-related costs is generally not included as assessable income for Income Related Rent purposes.
Some scholarships may not include payments for both course costs and living costs. The terms and conditions of the scholarship will set out the period the scholarship covers, the types of costs it is paid for and the amount paid for each type of cost.
## Period the scholarship is awarded for
Scholarships are awarded for study in part of a year, a whole year, or more than one year. The assessable income from the scholarship payment is applied to the study period covered by the scholarship.
Where a scholarship is paid in instalments due to academic or study requirements, the assessable income from the scholarship is applied to the whole of the study period covered by the scholarship, and not just at the point the instalment is received.
## Example of a scholarship as assessable income
The TeachNZ Career Changer scholarship is paid to a student for living costs for each year of study up to 2 full-time years. The scholarship is paid fortnightly over a 32-week period. There are no course fees or course-related costs associated with the scholarship.
The TeachNZ Career Changer scholarship would be included as assessable income for Income Related Rent purposes for the 32-week period over which it is paid.

chunks.title: 4 working day service period for posted notices — income related rent
chunks.text:
## 4 working day service period for posted notices
All written notices of changes in rent sent by post are deemed to have been given to the client on the fourth working day after the date it was posted.
This means, that this 4 working day service period must be allowed in addition (and prior to) to any 14-day notice period or 60-day notice period, that must be given.
Some housing providers may give the client a longer service period.
Note all notices issued by Kāinga Ora are sent by post.
## 2 working day service period for notices delivered by fax, email, or in person
All notices of changes in rent delivered by fax, email, or in person to the tenanted property, are deemed to have been given to the tenant on the second working day after the date it was delivered.
This means, that this 2 working day service period must be allowed in addition (and prior to) to any 14-day notice period or 60-day notice period, that must be given.
Some housing providers may give the client a longer service period.
Note some notices issued by community housing providers are sent by email.

chunks.title: Shared housing and Income Related Rent — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Shared housing and Income Related Rent
For the purposes of shared housing, a rate of Income Related Rent must be calculated based on the household type and the applicable people living within the bedroom.
For example, the household type for a single person living in a bedroom is a sole tenant household type.
Note that a tenancy agreement will be signed by each tenant with their housing provider for each person living in each bedroom of the shared housing property. Where the client has a partner, the tenancy agreement will be for the couple living in the bedroom.

chunks.title: Agreed process for setting the market rent rate — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Agreed process for setting the market rent rate
The market rent rate for a social housing property is set by the housing provider using an agreed process.
In setting the appropriate market rent rate a housing provider will consider:
- the benchmark property rate (lower quartile of rents for properties of a similar type, size and location)
- the condition of property and level of amenities and
- any special property features
Generally, social housing properties will be in the lower quartile of rents for properties of a similar type, size and location.
## Benchmark property rate
The housing provider will look at similar properties in the area and what other landlords are charging in rents for them.
They may consider:
- advertised private rents, such as through adverts by real estate agencies and private rental companies
- what other social housing providers are charging
- TradeMe data (TradeMe holds a record of the price of rentals listed on the website)
- tenancy bond data (actual bonds lodged by private landlords with the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
Note that the housing provider may also hold benchmark rents for particular groups of properties with similar characteristics depending on the location, property type and size.
## Condition of property and level of amenities
The housing provider will take account of the individual property condition and level of amenities available in the property.
## Adjustments for special or individual property features
The housing provider may look at whether the property has any special features that require an additional investment by the landlord and determine an additional amount.
Generally, a 'special features' rate is considered when modifications have been made to a property, for example for mobility, access or a garage. These modifications will have required an investment by the landlord that might not otherwise be reflected in the benchmark rent.
## Total market rent rate
The housing provider will add the amounts together and get the market rent rate for the property.
## Example
Property benchmark rate Total market rent rate for the property Benchmark property Special property features $412 $20 $432
Property benchmark rate
Total market rent rate for the property
Benchmark property
Special property features
$412
$20
$432
For more information see:
- Market rent rate
- Market rent rate reviews

chunks.title: Agreed rent rate — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Agreed rent rate
Some social housing providers have tailored agreements. These can include a weekly agreed rent for their social housing property.
If a property has a weekly agreed rent rate, this is used to calculate the Income Related Rent Subsidy paid to the social housing provider.
The weekly agreed rent rate is the maximum amount per week the housing provider can receive for a specific property, which can be different to the market rent for the property.
The agreed rent does not affect the way the Income Related Rent is calculated and the amount of Income Related Rent paid by the tenant.
The rate of Income Related Rent will still be calculated based on a client's assessable income, their household type and the market rent for the property.
The maximum amount of Income Related Rent that the housing provider can charge for the property is the market rent rate.
## Review of Agreed Rent
The review of the weekly agreed rent rate is written into the Agreement between the Ministry of Social Development and the housing provider.
For more information see:

chunks.title: Calculating the Income Related Rent Subsidy — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Calculating the Income Related Rent Subsidy
Social housing providers are paid for the difference between the value of the Income Related Rent and the market rent rate or the agreed rent rate for the property.
This payment is called the Income Related Rent Subsidy and is paid by the Ministry of Social Development.
For more information see:
- Shared housing and Income Related Rent Subsidy
- Subsidy for Kāinga Ora
- Subsidy for community housing providers with market rent
- Subsidy for community housing providers with agreed rent
- Market rent rate

chunks.title: Clients paying market rent as Income Related Rent not currently calculated — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Clients paying market rent as Income Related Rent not currently calculated
A client may be paying the market rent rate for a property because they:
- have not applied for Income Related Rent or have chosen not to access it or
- had been paying rent based on a rate of Income Related Rent but subsequently the Ministry of Social Development has been unable to calculate a new rate because the client has not provided all the information it required
In these situations:
- Kāinga Ora must charge the market rent rate for the property or
- community housing providers may set the rent themselves but it must not be higher than the market rent rate for the property
Note if the client has not had a rate of Income Related Rent calculated, the housing provider cannot be paid an Income Related Rent Subsidy.
For more information see:
- Property improvements
- Increases to the rent for clients paying market rent
- Decreases to the rent for clients paying market rent rates
- Market rent rate determined by the Tenancy Tribunal
- Examples of effect of changes to market rent rates
- Market rent rate reviews

chunks.title: Decreases to the rent for clients paying market rent — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Decreases to the rent for clients paying market rent
Where a decrease to the market rent rate results in a market rent rate that is lower than the rent currently being paid by client and it is also lower than a rate of Income Related Rent that has been calculated in the last 52 weeks, a review of the rate of Income Related Rent is to be completed.
Where a rate of Income Related Rent has not been calculated in the last 52 weeks the client may need to request that a review of the rate of Income Related Rent be completed.
The decrease to the rent would be applied to the earliest possible rent charge date by the housing provider.
Note clients in this situation do not need to have an assessment for eligibility completed.
For more information see:
- Increases to the rent for clients paying market rent
- Property improvements
- Market rent determined by the Tenancy Tribunal
- Clients paying market rent as Income Related Rent not currently calculated
- Examples of effect of changes to market rent rates
- Market rent rate reviews

chunks.title: Examples of effect of changes to market rent rates — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text: The following are examples of the effect when the market rent rate changes for a property:

chunks.title: Example 1 — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text: Market rent rate increases, impacts on client as rent is reviewed by housing provider. Current rates Current calculated rate of Income Related Rent $183 Current market rent rate $160 Current rent charged by housing provider $160 Current rate of Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by housing provider $0 Effect of market rent rate increasing New market rent rate following review by housing provider $180 New rent charged by housing provider at the market rent rate $180 New rate of Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by housing provider $0 In this situation the change to the market rent rate has an impact on the client, because the client is paying rent at the market rent rate and the new market rent remains below the last calculated rate of Income Related Rent. The rate of the Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by the housing provider will remain at zero.

chunks.title: Example 2 — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text: Market rent rate increases, market rent rate change has no impact on client. Current rates Current calculated rate of Income Related Rent $90 Current market rent rate $220 Current rent charged by housing provider $90 Current rate of Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by housing provider $130 Effect of market rent rate increasing New market rent rate following review by housing provider $240 Rent charged by housing provider at calculated rate of Income Related Rent $90 New rate of Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by housing provider $150 In this situation the change to the market rent rate has no impact on the client. The rate of the Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by housing provider will increase.

chunks.title: Example 3 — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text: Market rent rate increases, impacts on client as rent is reviewed by the housing provider, client can have a rate of Income Related Rent calculated. Current rates Last calculated rate of Income Related Rent $180 Current market rent rate $160 Current rent charged by housing provider $160 Current rate of Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by housing provider $0 Effect of market rent rate increasing New market rent rate following review of market rent by housing provider $190 New rent charged by housing provider $180 New rate of Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by housing provider $10 In this situation the change to the market rent rate has an impact on the client, because the client is paying rent at the market rent rate, however, the last calculated rate of Income Related Rent is lower than the new market rent rate. This means that the housing provider can charge no more than the calculated rate of Income Related Rent and will claim the $10 difference in Income Related Rent Subsidy.

chunks.title: Example 4 — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text: Market rent rate decreases, impacts on client as rent is reviewed by housing provider. Current rates Last calculated rate of Income Related Rent $200 Current market rent rate $195 Current rent charged by housing provider $195 Current rate of Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed $0 Effect of market rent rate increasing New market rent rate following review of market rent by housing provider $150 New rent charged by housing provider $150 New rate of Income Related Rent Subsidy claimed by housing provider $0 In this situation the change to the market rent rate impacts on the client, because the client is paying rent at the market rent rate. The clients rent would decrease. For more information see: - Property improvements - Increases to the rent for clients paying market rent - Decreases to the rent for clients paying market rent - Market rent rate determined by the Tenancy Tribunal - Clients paying market rent as Income Related Rent not currently calculated - Market rent rate reviews

chunks.title: Increases to the rent for clients paying market rent — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Increases to the rent for clients paying market rent
An increase to the market rent rate can result in a rent increase when the client is paying rent at the market rent rate.
If the increase to the rate of market rent rate results in an increase to the rent the client is paying, the amount of the rent charged by the housing provider cannot be increased until the earliest rent effective date following the 60-day notice period.
In this situation, a housing provider can issue notice of the increase without the Ministry of Social Development reviewing the client's circumstances.
Note if a client is paying rent at a calculated rate of Income Related Rent and this rate is less than the market rent, there is no need to review the calculated rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Introduction — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Income Related Rent Subsidy is part of the Government's financial support for social housing.
Social housing providers are paid for the difference between the value of the Income Related Rent and the market rent rate or agreed rent rate for their social housing properties. This payment is called the Income Related Rent Subsidy.
Social housing providers are responsible for calculating the amount of the Income Related Rent Subsidy and claiming the amount from the Ministry of Social Development.
The Ministry of Social Development is responsible for processing the Income Related Rent Subsidy claims and paying the housing provider.
For more information see:
- Market rent rate
- Agreed rent rate
- Calculating the Income Related Rent Subsidy
- Subsidy claims
- Income Related Rent Rent rate charged is different from calculated rate

chunks.title: Market rent determined by the Tenancy Tribunal — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Market rent determined by the Tenancy Tribunal
A client can ask the Tenancy Tribunal to review the amount of rent payable under a tenancy agreement and the Tenancy Tribunal can make an order for the rent to be reduced if it is satisfied that it is substantially more than the market rent rate for the property.
While it is possible for social housing clients to request a review of their rent by the Tenancy Tribunal, because of the agreed process for setting market rent rates for social housing properties, it is unlikely that the Tenancy Tribunal would find that a rent for a social housing property was substantially higher than the market rent rate.
For more information see:
- Property improvements
- Increases to the rent for clients paying market rent
- Decreases to the rent for clients paying market rent
- Clients paying market rent as Income Related Rent not currently calculated
- Examples of effect of changes to market rent rates
- Market rent rate reviews

chunks.title: Market rent rate reviews — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Market rent rate reviews
Housing providers periodically review the market rent rates for individual properties.
The amount of money that clients can afford to pay to live in an area, and the demand to live in particular areas, have an effect on changes to market rents.
A market rent rate can be reviewed and:
- increased because of an upward market rent movement for the area
- decreased because of a downward market rent movement for the area
- increased as significant property improvements have been made or
- stay the same
## Effect of changes to the market rent rate
Changes to the market rent rate can affect the amount of:
- rent that a client is paying, where they are paying rent at the market rent rate
- Income Related Rent Subsidy paid to the housing provider and
- debt that is being established for the client
A change to the market rent rate could result in a client:
- who was paying rent at the market rent rate, now paying a higher or lower rent
- who was paying rent based on a rate of Income Related Rent, starting to pay rent at the market rent rate (where the new market rent is lower than the last notified rate of Income Related Rent)
- who was paying rent based on a rate of Income Related Rent continuing to pay the same rent (where the new market rent rate is still more than the rate of Income Related Rent) or
- having a rate of Income Related Rent calculated for them when the new market rent rate increases beyond the last notified rate of Income Related Rent
If the increase to the rate of market rent results in an increase to the rent the client is paying, the amount of the rent charged by the housing provider cannot be increased until the earliest rent effective date following the 60-day notice period.

chunks.title: Market rent rate — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Market rent rate
The market rent rate for a social housing property is set by the housing provider according to an agreed process. The market rent rate must be comparable to the rent charged for other properties of a similar type, size and location.
Generally, social housing properties will be in the lower quartile of properties of that type, size and location.
For more information see:
- Agreed process for setting the market rent rate
- Market rent rate reviews

chunks.title: Property improvements — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Property improvements
If significant property improvements have been made by the housing provider, the market rent rate can be reviewed.
The housing provider will advise the client prior to making improvements to the property that the improvements may result in a rent increase.
It is up to the housing provider whether the improvements will be made.
For more information see:
- Increases to the rent for clients paying market rent
- Decreases to the rent for clients paying market rent
- Market rent rate determined by the Tenancy Tribunal
- Clients paying market rent as Income Related Rent not currently calculated
- Examples of effect of changes to market rent rates
- Market rent rate reviews

chunks.title: Shared housing and Income Related Rent Subsidy — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Shared housing and Income Related Rent Subsidy
The market rent rate or agreed rent rate for a social housing property that is providing shared housing is set based on each bedroom.
For the purposes of shared housing, the Income Related Rent Subsidy is then paid for the difference between the rate of Income Related Rent calculated for the tenant and the market rent rate or agreed rent rate for the bedroom.

chunks.title: Subsidy claims — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Subsidy claims
Housing providers must submit claims fortnightly.
GST cannot be claimed, as GST does not apply to residential tenancies.
The claim period is a fixed 2 week period with the first 2 week period commencing on the first rent charge date.
## Initial claim period
On receipt of a completed claim from the housing provider, the Ministry of Social Development will pay the Income Related Rent Subsidy for the period between:
- the start date of the tenancy and
- the rent charge date
If the initial claim period is for a part week then the claim must be adjusted accordingly. To work out the part-claim period, the housing provider will divide the first weeks claim period by 7 days, and adjust the claim for the appropriate number of days.
For example the first rent charge date is a Thursday, but the start date of the tenancy is a Monday. The client pays 3 days rent as part of their rent in advance payment. The housing provider can claim for Income Related Rent Subsidy for the 3 days of broken rent.
## Change to the subsidy due to changes in the rate of Income Related Rent rate
For community housing providers the earliest possible rent effective date of the new rate of Income Related Rent that falls within the claim period will be the date from which the subsidy changes.
For Kāinga Ora the date that the new rate of Income Related Rent was first charged within the claim period will be the date from which the subsidy changes.
The Income Related Rent Subsidy can be paid for the period between this date and the next rent charge date.
## Ending the claim
When a client is no longer eligible to have a rate of Income Related Rent calculated, the housing provider is not eligible to be paid the Income Related Rent Subsidy.
The Income Related Rent Subsidy must end on the day after the last rent charge date or the tenancy end date whichever is appropriate.
For more information see:
- Calculating the Income Related Rent Subsidy
- Subsidy for Kāinga Ora
- Subsidy for community housing providers with market rent
- Subsidy for community housing providers with agreed rent

chunks.title: Subsidy for community housing providers with agreed rent — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Subsidy for community housing providers with agreed rent

- rate of Income Related Rent calculated and notified by Work and Income (being the notified rate that was required to be charged within the fortnightly claim period, starting from the earliest possible date that it could have been charged) and
- market rent rate for the property

chunks.title: Subsidy for community housing providers with market rent — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## Subsidy for community housing providers with market rent
The Income Related Rent subsidy that can be claimed by community housing providers is the difference between the:
- rate of Income Related Rent calculated and notified by Work and Income (being the notified rate that was required to be charged within the fortnightly claim period, starting from the earliest possible date that it could have been charged) and

chunks.title: When the change to the market rent rate applies — income related rent subsidy
chunks.text:
## When the change to the market rent rate applies
Housing providers periodically review the market rent rates for individual properties, they must advise the Ministry of Social Development when the market rent rate has changed for a property.
Kāinga Ora review rates on a quarterly basis and community housing providers review rates no more than twice a year.
## When the change applies to the Income Related Rent Subsidy
The housing provider will include the change to the market rent rate in the Income Related Rent Subsidy claim from the earliest possible rent charge date (following the date they changed the market rent)
When the change applies for clients paying rent at the market rent rate
An increase or a decrease to the market rent rate can result in a change to the rent for clients who are paying rent at the market rent rate.
For more information see:
- Housing provider gives a sixty day notice period
## When the change applies to the Income Related Rent record
The Ministry of Social Development will apply the new market rent rates to the client's record at the next change in circumstances review or annual review - whichever is the earlier.
Some changes to the market rent rate can trigger a change in circumstances review of the rate of Income Related Rent. This happens when:
- the new market rent rate is lower than the last notified rate of Income Related Rent
- the new market rent rate increases beyond the last notified rate of Income Related Rent
If change to the market rent rate results in a change to the rent then the usual review processes must be followed.
For more information see:
- Increases to rent for clients paying market rent
- Decreases to the rent for clients paying market rent

chunks.title: Funds deducted from pay for superannuation scheme contributions — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Funds deducted from pay for superannuation scheme contributions
A client’s assessable income is their estimated net weekly income (ie income after tax) from all sources after the deduction of any Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) premiums or levies.
When a client has deductions from their pay for Kiwisaver or other superannuation scheme contributions, the amount deducted is assessable income for Income Related Rent.
## Employer contributions
Generally, when an employer contributes to an employee’s Kiwisaver account or other superannuation scheme, this contribution is not assessable income for Income Related Rent.
Where an employer is making significant voluntary contributions to a client’s superannuation scheme rather than paying the client a higher wage, this may be considered deprivation of income. This depends on factors such as the size and frequency of those deposits and the individual circumstances of the client.
## Funds held in a superannuation scheme
Funds held in a KiwiSaver account or other superannuation scheme are not considered assessable income.
Note funds held in a KiwiSaver account or other superannuation scheme are not considered an assessable asset for Income Related Rent unless the person is able to withdraw them due to being over 65 years of age.
## Withdrawal of funds from a superannuation scheme
When a person reaches the age of 65 they can withdraw their funds from their KiwiSaver account and generally any other superannuation scheme.
Funds that are withdrawn or available to be withdrawn from KiwiSaver or any other superannuation scheme are an assessable asset.
## Significant lump sums deposited in a superannuation scheme
Depositing significant lump sum funds into a superannuation scheme may be considered deprivation of income. This depends on factors such as the size and frequency of those deposits and the individual circumstances of the client.

chunks.title: Temporary change becomes a permanent change — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Temporary change becomes a permanent change
Where a client advised that their change in circumstances was temporary and this became a permanent change, you will need to review the client's rate of Income Related Rent.
Generally, you would review the rate of the Income Related Rent from the date the change in circumstances was determined to be a permanent change.
You may consider backdating a lower rate of Income Related Rent and issuing a refund for the client for the appropriate refund period.
Generally, no debt would be created unless you consider that the client intentionally misled you by not providing earlier the correct information about their circumstances.
For more information see:
- Deciding if changes are permanent or temporary
- Reviews of the rate of Income Related Rent
- Refunds and backdating a rate of Income Related Rent during a review
- Date of change in circumstances
- Social housing Income Related Rent debt

chunks.title: Tenant has subsequent change but notice already issued — income related rent
chunks.text: If a housing provider has issued a notice to a tenant that they are going to change the rent charged, and that tenant has a subsequent permanent change in circumstances (during a notice period) which means the rate of Income Related Rent will change further, you need to activate the new rate of Income Related Rent.

chunks.title: Kāinga Ora (Housing New Zealand) — income related rent
chunks.text: Where the provider is Kāinga Ora and the subsequent change is an increase in Income Related Rent, the initial change will not be applied to the rent charged. Kāinga Ora will advise the tenant of the new rent amount and the effective date of the change. Kāinga Ora should also advise the tenant that the earlier notice of rent change no longer applies. If the subsequent change is a decrease to the rate of Income Related Rent, the reduction will be applied from the next rent effective date.

chunks.title: Community housing providers — income related rent
chunks.text: When there is an increase to the Income Related Rent, community housing providers will apply the initial change in rent charged from the first rent effective date after the initial notice period. The Community housing providers will advise that tenant of the subsequent change to the rent amount and this amount will be charged from the end of the second notice period. If the subsequent change is a decrease to the rate of Income Related Rent, the reduction will be applied from the end of the second notice period.

chunks.title: Types of income — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Types of income
Income that is used to calculate the rate of Income Related Rent is known as 'assessable income'.
Assessable income is the estimate of a client's net weekly income (i.e. after tax) from all sources, and after the deduction of any Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) premiums or levies.
The assessable income of all applicable people in the household is used to calculate the rate of Income Related Rent.
## Child Support
From 1 July 2023, most types of Child Support are included as assessable income. For more information see: Child Support included as assessable income from 1 July 2023.
## Contributions from additional occupants
Contributions from additional occupants are not included as assessable income. When calculating Income Related Rent, 62% of the total contributions are added to the calculated amount. For more information see: Contributions from additional occupants.

chunks.title: Unreasonable to expect the information to have been provided earlier — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Unreasonable to expect the information to have been provided earlier
When determining the date that the change in circumstances occurred, consider whether it was unreasonable to expect the tenant to have advised of the changes any earlier.
Consider whether the reason provided:
- was unforeseen, out-of-the ordinary and could not be planned for
- was beyond the client's control or
- sets the client apart from others in a similar situation
Examples include (but are not limited to):
- unforeseen hospitalisation
- seriously sick or injured
- bereavement of immediate family
- emergency or adverse event
- victim of violent crime (including family violence)
If you consider it was unreasonable for the information to have been provided earlier, the refund is paid for the period between earliest possible rent charge date (following the day the change in circumstance occurred) to the day prior to the rent effective date that the correct rate of Income Related Rent was applied.

chunks.title: Unsupported Child's Benefit excess payment — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Unsupported Child's Benefit excess payment
Unsupported Child's Benefit carers must generally apply for a formula assessment of Child Support. This rule applies unless they have a voluntary agreement in place before applying for Unsupported Child's Benefit.
For these carers, Inland Revenue keeps Child Support paid by liable parents to help pay for the Unsupported Child's Benefit the child's carer is getting.
When the amount of Child Support paid is more than the rate of Unsupported Child's Benefit, Inland Revenue pay the difference to the receiving carer. This is called an Unsupported Child's Benefit excess payment.
## Types of Unsupported Child’s Benefit excess payments
There are 2 types of Unsupported Child's Benefit excess payments:
- formula assessment excess (the most common type)
- voluntary agreement excess
Formula assessment excess payment
If the formula assessment is higher than the Unsupported Child's Benefit rate, Inland Revenue pays the difference to the receiving carer. This is called a formula assessment excess payment and is not assessable income when determining whether a client qualifies for social housing.
Voluntary agreement excess payment
If the Unsupported Child's Benefit carer has a voluntary agreement, and the formula assessment is lower than the voluntary agreement amount, Inland Revenue can only keep the amount of the formula assessment. The rest is paid to the receiving carer. This is called a voluntary agreement excess payment and is assessable income when determining whether a client qualifies for social housing.
## Mixed payments not assessable income
In some rare cases a receiving carer may get an excess payment and another type of Inland Revenue Child Support payment from the same liable parent.
This is called a mixed Child Support payment, and is not assessable income for social housing.

chunks.title: When the rate of Income Related Rent is decreased — income related rent
chunks.text:
## When the rate of Income Related Rent is decreased
Following a change in circumstances, when there is a decrease to the rate of Income Related Rent, the housing provider is notified of the decrease if it makes a material difference to the rate.
The housing provider must:
- review the amount of rent charged
- change the amount of the rent charged (unless in their opinion it would not make a material difference to the rent currently charged)
- advise us that they are changing the amount of the rent charged (or not) and the new rent effective date and
- advise the tenant about the change to the amount of rent and the new rent effective date
The housing provider must decrease the rent from the earliest rent effective date following the notification (ie, no 60-day notice period or 14-day notice period applies).
## Change to the rate does not make a material difference
A change to the rate of Income Related Rent will not be activated or notified to the housing provider if the change does not make a material difference.
For more information see:
- Material difference to the rate of Income Related Rent
## Backdating to a date prior to the earliest rent effective date
In the situation where you have made the decision to backdate the rate of Income Related Rent to a date that is prior to the next earliest rent effective date you must:
- activate the new rate of Income Related Rent and send the notification to the housing provider and then
- process the backdate and issue the refund for the appropriate refund period

chunks.title: Working for Families Tax Credits — income related rent
chunks.text:
## Working for Families Tax Credits
When assessing Income Related Rent the Working for Families Tax Credits included in the calculation are:
- a portion of the family tax credit and
- the full amount of minimum family tax credit
If an applicable person has dependent children and they are entitled to get these payments, then these payments are included in the calculation of Income Related Rent.
If the child is not dependent then they are not considered as a child for whom the family tax credit and the minimum family tax credit is paid.
The in-work tax credit and Best Start tax credit paid by Inland Revenue are not assessable income for Income Related Rent and Housing affordability assessments (and therefore are not included in the calculation).
## Family tax credits paid weekly or annually by Inland Revenue
A weekly amount of family tax credit and the minimum family tax credit is included in the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent, regardless of whether the tenant chooses to have it paid to them weekly or annually.

chunks.title: Application status — register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Application status
Only clients who are eligible to be allocated social housing are placed on the register and can be referred to social housing providers. A client's eligibility for social housing can be reviewed while they are on the register to ensure the client remains eligible.
## Client not available for referral
Clients whose current circumstances cannot be confirmed to determine if they are still eligible for social housing would not be referred to a housing provider.
Clients who have been referred to a property by a housing provider cannot be referred to another provider.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances at point of referral — register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Change in circumstances at point of referral
Clients applying for social housing must tell us straight away of any change in circumstances or their family's situation so that they can be referred to a suitable property that best meets their housing needs (property requirements).
However, there may be some instances where a client has a change in circumstances which is only identified when they have been referred to a social housing provider for a property viewing.
When the property no longer matches the client's new circumstances the provider will withdraw the offer and the client's eligibility for social housing needs to be reviewed.
While the client's eligibility for social housing is being reviewed they cannot be referred to a housing provider until their circumstances have been confirmed.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — register management and referrals
chunks.text: Before being allocated social housing, that is, while clients are on the register they must generally tell MSD straight away of any change in their circumstances or their family's situation that may affect their: - eligibility for social housing or - need to be allocated, assigned or let any particular social housing Note clients do not need to advise MSD when they get, or have a change to, information share Child Support payments. When a review of eligibility results in a change to a client's housing need (for example, assessed as low (priority D) or moderate (priority C) housing need) they are no longer eligible for social housing and they must be removed them from the register. The client may be eligible for other financial assistance and could be referred to an options and advice seminar to assist them with finding alternative housing solutions. Note tenants in social housing also generally have a duty to advise MSD straight away of any change in their circumstances that may affect their continued eligibility for social housing, the need for the particular property they are renting, or their calculated rate of Income Related Rent. For more information see: - Duty to advise of changes of circumstances Change in circumstances for current tenants - Income Related Rent Change in circumstances

chunks.title: Review must be completed — register management and referrals
chunks.text: The client's application must be reviewed when the change of circumstances changes: - their household composition (changes to the people living in the property) - their housing need (priority for a house) - their housing needs (property requirements) - the assessable income or - the accommodation income they get from additional occupants The client must be advised if the review changes their priority rating or housing needs (property requirements).

chunks.title: Change in circumstances has no effect — register management and referrals
chunks.text: Some changes in circumstances, may not affect a client's eligibility for social housing for example a change to a postal address, name or telephone number.

chunks.title: Client cannot be contacted — register management and referrals
chunks.text: When a client cannot be contacted during an application register review, we do not know if the client is still eligible to be allocated social housing. The client cannot be referred to a housing provider until their circumstances have been confirmed. When a client's eligibility cannot be confirmed, they must be removed from the register.

chunks.title: Review of decision — register management and referrals
chunks.text: Clients have the right to review decisions made about their eligibility for social housing, following a review due to a change in circumstances.

chunks.title: Decline request to review — register management and referrals
chunks.text: There are circumstances when a request to review a client's housing need (priority) or housing needs (property requirements) can be declined if there is reason to believe the client's circumstances have not significantly changed since their last review. A client cannot apply for a Review of Decision if they do not agree with the decision not to review their eligibility while on the register.

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
Clients on the register must advise MSD if they are leaving New Zealand as absence from the country may affect their need for housing and our ability to refer them to a housing provider to be matched to suitable housing.
## Client leaves New Zealand permanently
Clients leaving New Zealand permanently are not eligible to be allocated social housing as they are no longer ordinarily resident.
## Client leaves New Zealand temporarily
Clients leaving New Zealand for a temporary period must provide details of their travel dates and a contact address, ideally before departure if they want to remain available for referral during their time outside New Zealand.
For example, a client may need to travel:
- to a funeral
- to represent New Zealand at a sporting event
- to visit a sick relative or
- for a family emergency
Some clients will retain their level of housing need and may want to be considered for a property during their absence.
## Client remains on the register
When the client remains on the register, they will continue to be actively managed and their circumstances regularly reviewed (unless they are grandparented clients). If the client fails to respond when contacted and their eligibility cannot be confirmed they will be removed from the register.
However, if a client makes contact within 8 weeks of being removed from the register, their application can be reinstated following a review of their circumstances.

chunks.title: Appeal Authority process — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Appeal Authority process
Step 1. Client's application for appeal is sent direct to the Social Security Appeal Authority.
Step 2. The Social Security Appeal Authority advises the appropriate MSD appeals officer.
Step 3. Appeals officer advises and obtains relevant information from the business unit or office that made the original decision.
Step 4. Appeals officer completes report in accordance with the relevant regulations under the Public and Community Housing Management Act 1992 and part 7 of the Social Security Act 2018.
Step 5. The Social Security Appeal Authority sets a hearing date. The hearing can be heard in person or on papers only. The MSD appeals officer or solicitor will represent MSD at the hearing. The staff member who made the original decision may be required to give evidence.
Step 6. The Social Security Appeal Authority will advise MSD and the client of the outcome.
Step 7. The appeals officer will advise the appropriate staff member of any benefit action to be taken.

chunks.title: Appeals to the Social Security Appeal Authority — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Appeals to the Social Security Appeal Authority
A client can appeal to the Social Security Appeal Authority when the Benefits Review Committee has upheld or upheld in part a decision of MSD, including decisions in respect of:
- the assessment or re-assessment of: their eligibility or continued eligibility for social housingtheir housing needs
- their eligibility or continued eligibility for social housing
- their housing needs
- the calculation of the rate of Income Related Rent
- the establishment and recovery of Income Related Rent debt
A client's application for appeal should be sent directly to the Social Security Appeal Authority.
Note when the Benefits Review Committee has declined to hear an out of time Review of Decision and the client applies for the matter to be heard by the Social Security Appeal Authority, forward the case to the Appeal Authority.
For more information see:
- Appeal Authority Process

chunks.title: Benefit is cancelled or suspended — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Benefit is cancelled or suspended
When a client who is receiving income support has their benefit cancelled or suspended you will need to consider whether this will affect their eligibility for social housing or their indicative rate of Income Related Rent.
Generally, when a client's benefit is cancelled it will mean a change in their income and you will need to review their circumstances. For example, the client's benefit has been cancelled due to starting employment.
A review of the client's circumstances may not be necessary in some situations. For example, you would not complete a review where the client's benefit is suspended because they have failed to return their annual review of benefit forms on time.
For more information see:
- Client with suspended or expired benefit record
- Employment and income changes
- Changes and reviews
- Change in circumstances
- Income Related Rent
- Core policy Use of social housing, benefit and student information

chunks.title: Change in accommodation income from additional occupants — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Change in accommodation income from additional occupants
When there is a change in the amount of accommodation income a client gets from additional occupants it needs to be determined if the change is temporary or permanent.
If the change is permanent, the ability of the client to afford rental accommodation in the private housing market must be reviewed, as it may affect the client’s priority for Social Housing.
The client's indicative rate of Income Related Rent also needs to be reviewed.
Where an additional occupant who pays the client joins or leaves the household, this may change the household needs (property requirements) and must be reviewed.

chunks.title: Change of address — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Change of address
A change of address may affect a client's eligibility as they may no longer have a need for social housing.
You must update the client's record with the new information.
You also need to consider the type of house into which the client is moving in to. For example, if there is a risk of overcrowding in the new property, this may increase the client's housing need.
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Core policy Use of social housing, benefit and student information

chunks.title: Change to people in the household — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Change to people in the household
A change to the people in the client's household includes where the client requires another person or household to be added (example person or household join-in the tenancy agreement) or removed from their household unit.
This can also mean a change to the client's housing needs (property requirements) and the indicative rate of Income Related Rent calculated.
## New partner joins the household
Where a new partner joins the household, this may change the housing needs (property requirements) and the indicative rate of Income Related Rent calculated. For example, the new partner may have a health condition and require their own room, or they are working and their income must be included.
## Person leaves the household
Where a person leaves the household, the client's circumstances need to be reviewed. There may be no change to the household needs (property requirements) as the person may have been sharing a bedroom.
Where the move impacts the client's priority rating or housing needs (property requirements) the client must be advised of the outcome of the review.
## Additional occupant joins or leaves the household
Where an additional occupant joins or leaves the household, this may change the household needs (property requirements). If the client gets accommodation income from the additional occupant, it may also change the indicative Income Related Rent calculated and the client’s priority for social housing.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
Prior to a client being allocated social housing (that is, while they are on the register) a client must generally tell MSD straight away of any change in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to social housing.
Note clients do not need to advise MSD when they get, or have a change to, information share Child Support payments.
A change in circumstances may result in a change to the household composition, the housing need (priority), household needs (property requirements) and the indicative rate of Income Related Rent.
However, when a change in circumstances means the client is no longer at risk or has no serious housing need, they are removed from the register.
Where a client cannot be contacted during a register review, they must be removed from the register as the client's eligible social housing cannot be confirmed.
A letter to confirm must be sent.

chunks.title: Child changes — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Child changes
A client's eligibility for social housing may be affected when a child or dependent child leaves or come into their care. MSD must review their circumstances (this includes the birth or adoption of a child).
Examples of how child changes can affect eligibility include (but are not limited to):
- family composition and household type changes such as a single person becomes a sole parent
- an additional child may contribute to chronic overcrowding in current accommodation and increase housing need
- an additional child may have specific needs and requires certain modifications or an additional bedroom
- a change in the child's age may affect the rate of family tax credit payable and bedroom allocation
- a child turns 18, is no longer dependent and becomes a boarder may impact a bedroom allocation or indicative Income Related Rent
## Dependent child comes into care
Following the birth of a child or a dependent child coming into care, the rate of Income Related Rent may need to be reviewed. The child would be included in the household type.
Note if the client or partner has other dependent children included in their care, this would not change the household type and therefore no review is required (although MSD should update the client's record).
## Dependent child's income
A dependent child's personal earnings are not considered to be assessable income for the purposes of Income Related Rent.
The child is included in the household type, but their income is not included.
If a child aged 16 or older starts working full-time (an average of 30 hours or more each week) they would no longer be considered a dependent child.
## Child turns 16
When a child aged 16 or 17 leaves school, they can still be included in the household type if the child remains a dependent child.
If they become financially independent they will no longer be a dependent child and would be excluded from the household type.
## Child turns 18
If a dependent child turns 18 the rate of Income Related Rent is reviewed if they are no longer considered to be dependent (for example, if they are in full-time work or they are not continuing in education). The child would be excluded from the household type.

chunks.title: Client becomes sick — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Client becomes sick
When a client becomes sick, their priority for social housing may change. Where the client's health condition impacts on their employment, their indicative rate of Income Related Rent may be affected.
Examples include (but are not limited to) where:
- the urgency for social housing increases
- the client has no immediate need due to being hospitalised long term
- alternative housing arrangements being made such as moving in with a family member who can provide care
- the client's benefit type changes
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Changes and reviews
- Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Client does not want a rate of Income Related Rent calculated — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Client does not want a rate of Income Related Rent calculated
During the housing needs assessment applicable persons have their income and asset details taken into account and these details are used to calculate an indicative rate of Income Related Rent.
A client can decide not to have a rate of Income Related Rent calculated.
When a client advises that they do not want a rate of Income Related Rent calculated, you should discuss with the client their reasons why and you need to be satisfied with the reasons provided note this on the client’s record. For example, you need to know their full income details as part of the eligibility (income test).
The client may continue to be eligible for social housing and you should increase their indicative rate of Income Related Rent to the rate equal to the market rent rate.
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Changes and reviews

chunks.title: Client fails to advise of absence — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Client fails to advise of absence
Generally, clients on the register must advise us of their intention to leave New Zealand before their departure as absence from the country may affect their need for housing, and our ability to refer them to a housing provider to be matched to suitable housing.
When a client leaves New Zealand and they fail to advise us they may be identified through the MSD and New Zealand Customs Service data match.
Clients will be contacted and must respond within 10 days.
If the client responds and advises they want to remain on the register for a referral to suitable providers and their absence from New Zealand does not affect their eligibility to be allocated social housing, they will not be removed from the register.
If the client advises they do not want to be referred, but still need social housing and their absence from New Zealand does not affect their eligibility to be allocated social housing, their application will be put on hold.
They will not be referred to a social housing provider until they return to New Zealand.
Clients who fail to respond will be removed from the register as we cannot confirm their eligibility.
However, if a client makes contact within 8 weeks of being removed from the register, their application can be reinstated following a review of their circumstances.

chunks.title: Client goes into residential care — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Client goes into residential care
If a client on a register goes into residential care, you will need to establish if the admission is permanent or for a short duration.
## Short-term care
Clients on the register who enter into short-term residential care will remain on the register for referrals to housing providers if they are available for referral or have an agent or someone to act on their behalf with their housing provider.
Note although a client may want an agent or someone to act on their behalf for referral, some social housing providers may choose not to deal with anyone other than the client. You will need to advise clients in such situations to make a separate arrangement with the housing provider to allow for someone to act on their behalf.
## Long-term care
Clients going into long-term residential care would no longer have a housing need and would be removed from the register.
## Joint application
If the client going into residential care permanently is a part of a joint application, the application must be reviewed based on the housing need of the remaining applicants to determine their eligibility for social housing along with their indicative rate of Income Related Rent. The remaining applicants must be invited to apply.
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Changes and reviews
- Core policy Agents
- Hospitalisation

chunks.title: Acknowledge the client's request to withdraw — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Acknowledge the client's request to withdraw
You need to acknowledge the client's request to withdraw their application for Review of Decision in writing. There is a template letter available for you to do this on HIYA ROD.
For more information see:
- When to advise a client of their right to review
- Who can apply for a review or appeal
- Review of Decision

chunks.title: Client with suspended or expired benefit record — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Client with suspended or expired benefit record
Assessable income can be reviewed when a client or their partner (if any) has a permanent change in income.
When a client or their partner (if any) is getting a benefit and the benefit payments have reduced or stopped, the indicative rate of Income Related Rent calculated will be reviewed:
- when the client tells MSD of the change in circumstances or
- following the cancellation of the benefit at 8 weeks
## Retrospective benefit review
When benefit is reviewed and retrospectively adjusted, you may need to consider whether the indicative rate of Income Related Rent calculated needs to be reviewed.

chunks.title: Death of a client — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
When a client dies how you treat their application for social housing will depend on whether they are a:
- single applicant
- sole parent
- joint applicant
## Single applicant
When a single applicant dies, you will need to close their application and remove them from the register.
## Sole parent
If the client was a sole parent you must close their application for social housing and send a letter to the client's surviving dependent children aged 16 and over, to invite them to apply for social housing if they have a housing need.
## Joint applicants
If the client who died is part of a joint application, the application will need to be reviewed to determine the remaining applicant's eligibility for social housing and a new indicative rate of Income Related Rent calculated for that applicant. The application should be put on hold until the review has been completed. The remaining applicant will not be available for referral in the interim.
If the remaining applicants do not respond after reasonable attempts have been made to contact them, you should remove them from the register.
## Removal from the register
For sole parent and joint applications, MSD will send a letter 10 working days after they receive notification of the death. If no contact is made by the next of kin or applicable persons the client will be removed from the register.
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Changes and reviews

chunks.title: Employment and income changes — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Employment and income changes
When a client starts employment or has other changes in their income, it needs to be determined if the change is temporary or permanent.
The income threshold and the ability of the client to afford to rent accommodation in the private housing market must be reviewed.
Income changes affect the indicative rate of Income Related Rent and eligibility for social housing.
If an income change is permanent this may affect the client's eligibility for social housing when the client's income exceeds the income thresholds or changes the outcome of the affordability criteria.
If the change in income is permanent the client's indicative rate of Income Related Rent will need to be reviewed in line with their new income details.
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Changes and reviews
- Income Related Rent Deciding if changes are permanent or temporary
- Change in accommodation income from additional occupants

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a client on the register is admitted to hospital, how you treat their application status is determined by a number of factors including (but not limited to):
- the expected duration of the stay in hospital (long or short term stay)
- whether they are a single applicant, a joint applicant or they have an agent
- the likelihood of the client moving into an alternative housing arrangementFor example residential care
- ability to participate in a referralwhether they are available for a referral or do they have someone to act on their behalf such as, an applicable person included in their application for social housing or an agent
For more information see:
- In hospital for less than 30 days
- In hospital for more than 30 days

chunks.title: Imprisonment — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
When a client applying for social housing is imprisoned or detained in custody, MSD should decide how to treat their application for social housing after considering the likely period in prison.
## Client in prison for more than 30 days
Clients imprisoned or remanded in custody or longer than 30 days are removed from the register or joint applications. Clients will be sent a letter advising them of this.
Note in the case of joint applicants, MSD must send a letter to the other applicants advising that their application will be reviewed to determine their eligibility for social housing.
## Client in prison for 30 days or less
Clients imprisoned or detained in custody for less than 30 days are not removed from the register. Their application is put on hold until they are released from prison or custody.
They will not be referred to social housing providers until they are released (that is, their application status will remain on hold). Clients must make contact within 10 days of their release date for their circumstances to be confirmed.
If the client has an agent or someone to act on their behalf they can remain on the register and continue to be referred to social housing providers.

chunks.title: Single applicant — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Single applicant
If a single applicant is in hospital for less than 30 days and they have an agent or someone to act on their behalf, they can remain on the register and have their circumstances reviewed to establish if their housing need and housing needs (property requirements) have changed.
## Sole parent
If the client in hospital is a sole parent and they have an agent or someone to act on their behalf, they can remain on the register and their circumstances reviewed to establish if their housing need and housing needs (property requirements) have changed.
## Joint applicants
Where one of the parties to a joint application is in hospital for less than 30 days, they can remain on the register. An applicable person can act on their behalf.
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Changes and reviews
- In hospital for more than 30 days

chunks.title: Single applicant — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Single applicant
Where a single applicant is in hospital for longer than 30 days without someone to act on their behalf, they will not be referred to any social housing providers.
The client's application may be reinstated following a review of their housing need upon discharge from hospital if it is within eight weeks of their removal from the register. Otherwise they will need to make a new application for social housing.
## Sole parent
If a sole parent is in hospital longer than 30 days without someone to act on their behalf, they will not be referred to any social housing providers.
However, their application may be reinstated following a review of their housing need upon discharge from hospital if it is within eight weeks of their removal from the register. Otherwise they will need to make a new application for social housing.
## Joint applicant
In the case of a joint application, if the client in hospital is available to be referred or has someone to act on their behalf, the client can remain on the register and be referred to housing providers. Their circumstances will be reviewed upon discharge to confirm their housing need or housing needs (requirements).
For more information see:
- Change in circumstances
- Changes and reviews
- Client goes into residential care

chunks.title: Stage 1 - Internal review — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
chunks.text:
## Stage 1 - Internal review
This is an administrative process only.
When a client applies for a Review of Decision, MSD will take another look at the decision, review any new information, as well as the information available at the time of the decision, and check the decision was in accordance with legislation.

chunks.title: Reviews and Appeals — register management and referrals > changes and reviews register management and referrals
