A client on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship has been overseas for five days to attend his father's funeral. He is delayed in Sydney due to fog. He must remain a further three days.
The client cannot return due to circumstances that were not reasonably foreseeable and they were outside the client's control. Work and Income would extend the client's benefit for a reasonable period for him to be able to return. Also consider whether there is any grounds to pay for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Client or partner remains in New Zealand — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Client or partner remains in New Zealand
Qualification for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship may be affected for a married, civil union or de facto couple when one of them remains in New Zealand. This will depend on whether:
- it is the primary client or their partner who remains in New Zealand and
- payment has been approved to continue if it is the primary client overseas
## Client remains in New Zealand
If the primary client remains in New Zealand, they will continue to receive the half married, civil union or de facto rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship. If the partner is receiving any income while overseas this must be charged against the benefit.
Note you must continue to treat the couple as married or in a civil union unless they are living apart with the intention of ending their marriage or civil union.
## Partner remains in New Zealand
If the partner remains in New Zealand, they can continue to receive the half married, civil union or de facto rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship as long as payment to the primary client has been approved and is continuing to be paid while they are overseas for up to 28 days.
If payment will not continue to the primary client, or has been stopped, the partner will no longer qualify to receive any payment. You will need to determine if the partner qualifies for another benefit in their own right, or they may be able to receive an Emergency Benefit.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefits
Note the partner can only receive the half married, civil union or de facto rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship while the client is overseas, unless the couple are living apart with the intention of ending their marriage or civil union. If the primary client is receiving any income while overseas this must be charged against the benefit.
## Exception
However, there are some situations that allow Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client to be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment for a period of absence.
For details of these situations see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Overseas medical treatment

chunks.title: Client with work obligations, exemption or deferral — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Client with work obligations, exemption or deferral
Clients receiving Jobseeker Support cannot generally be absent from New Zealand and continue to receive payment of their benefits unless they have an approved reason for travel. This includes:
- clients exempt from work obligations
- clients deferred from their work obligations
- clients with part-time work obligations
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Client exempt from work obligations
- Client deferred from their work obligations
- Client with part-time work obligations
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption

chunks.title: Clients with a partner — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Clients with a partner
When a married, civil union or de facto client is imprisoned the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship will generally need to be cancelled to enable the partner to be granted a benefit in their own right.
The Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should be cancelled from the day after imprisonment.
If the primary client is imprisoned, the partner should be invited to apply for an alternative benefit in their own right, for example Sole Parent Support (where they have dependent children under the age of 14 years) or Jobseeker Support Student Hardship (when they have no children or their youngest dependent child is over 14 years of age). Where the partner has children they can be granted a sole parent rate of benefit while their partner is in prison, even if they are still in a relationship.
If the partner is imprisoned the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue provided the primary client is still able to meet their work obligations. The Jobseeker Support Student Hardship will be paid at the single or sole parent rate.
Where there are dependent children and the primary client is no longer able to meet the eligibility for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship because they are no longer available for and seeking full-time work, they will need to test their eligibility for another benefit, for example Sole Parent Support (where their youngest dependent child is under the age of 14 years).
## Exception
Where a client has a partner and/or dependent children there is discretion to continue payment of the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for a limited period in some circumstances.
There is discretion to pay all or part of the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship to the partner of the person who has been imprisoned. This will depend on the length of time imprisoned. Where the length of imprisonment is short, using discretion to continue to pay the benefit prevents having to re-grant the benefit.
There is also discretion to continue payment if the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance. For example, this may be considered where the client may end up receiving a sentence of home detention and needing to have their benefit re-granted to the couple anyway.
For more information to help you decide see:
- Work obligations
- Decision guidelines - clients with a partner
- SWIFTT process to pay a partner
- Remanded in custody

chunks.title: Commission work — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Commission work
If a primary client commences full-time commission work (even if there is no or minimum income being earned) they will no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
If the client has a partner who meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship in their own right, the partner can apply for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship as the primary client.
## Part-time commission work
If a primary client starts part-time commission work, they may still be able to get Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, as long as they continue to meet their job search requirements. Any offer of suitable employment takes precedence over any part-time activity or commission work that does not meet their work obligations.
For more information see:
- Suitable employment
## Partner
If the person who has commenced commission work (either part-time or full-time) is the partner, then the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue with their earnings being charged as income against the benefit.
This is regardless of whether the partner has work obligations.
Note if the partner has full-time work obligations and is working 30 hours per week, or has part-time work obligations and is working 20 hours or more, then they must be receiving an income from this employment to be meeting their work obligations. If they are not receiving any income from the commission work they must still be available for and actively seeking suitable employment.
For more information see:
- Employment related income
- Charging income
- Job search requirements

chunks.title: Contacting Work and Income on return to New Zealand — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Contacting Work and Income on return to New Zealand
Generally, it would be reasonable to expect a client to contact Work and Income within 10 working days of returning to New Zealand. However, you should consider whether the client's circumstances meant they were unable to inform Work and Income in this period.
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure
- Clients with work obligations, exemption or deferral
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Examples of applying the Absence from New Zealand policy

chunks.title: Information provided by the Court — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Information provided by the Court
The information that will be received from the Courts, Ministry of Justice will have:
- the client's name
- the amount to be deducted from the benefit
- the fine's reference number
If a client is suffering undue hardship because of the amount of the attachment order then they should be directed to a Registrar of the District Court for a reassessment of the rate.
For more information see:
- Court request for information

chunks.title: Court request for information — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Court request for information
The Courts, Ministry of Justice can request the following information when they are considering either making an attachment order or assessing the client's protected earnings rate under section 87AA of the Summary Proceedings Act 1957:
- the amount of any benefit paid to the client
- the amount of any attachment orders or deduction notices issued under the following Acts: Social Security Act 2018Family Proceedings Act 1980Child Support Act 1991Tax Administration Act 1994
- Social Security Act 2018
- Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Child Support Act 1991
- Tax Administration Act 1994
- any Ministry of Social Development debt that is being recovered from the client
- the composition of the client's family, including the number of family members who are dependent on the client, as known by Work and Income
This information is used to determine how much the client can reasonably be expected to pay each week on any outstanding fines.
For more information see:
- Protected earnings rate

chunks.title: Backdating — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Backdating
Where a client requests the backdated inclusion of a child and the previous caregiver was in receipt of a benefit for the child, you will need to review when the child was excluded from the previous caregivers benefit.
Note a child cannot be included in two benefits for the same period.
Have regard to all the circumstances and decide whether a debt should be established for the previous caregiver.
If the date you are including the child from is a date in the previous tax year, SWIFTT will only pay arrears of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit from the beginning of the current tax year, that is, 1 April. You will need to advise the client that any arrears of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit prior to this date will need to be claimed from Inland Revenue.
You will need to do a backdated review in the SBDR screen to pay any benefit arrears to the client for the previous tax year. A backdated review may be required for the current year if other rate changes have occurred - check the SRAUI screen for details.
For more information see:
- Processing standards Child changes [no link find out why]
- Best Start tax credit Commencement date

chunks.title: Date payment should be reduced — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Date payment should be reduced
The hospital rate is paid when the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks. Reduce the client's benefit to the hospital rate or appropriate higher rate from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation.
The rate of benefit paid to a couple with dependent children is not affected by the client's hospitalisation.
Note the rate of benefit payable to a sole parent is dependent on their circumstances.
For more information see:
- Sole Parents
## Absence of 28 days or less
Any periods of leave from hospital of 28 days or less are to be ignored when deciding the date from which the benefit is to be reduced. Calculate the period in hospital from the original admission date. If the client has been allowed out of hospital for more than 28 days, the calculation of the period in hospital begins again after the client has been re-admitted.
## Client formally discharged
If the client has been formally discharged from hospital and then readmitted to the same or a different hospital, even if the absence is less than 28 days, the 13 week calculation starts again.
However, if the client is formally discharged from one hospital with the intention that they immediately transfer to another hospital, the client is treated as not being discharged (transferred). Ensure that SHODA is updated to show the new hospital details.

chunks.title: Death of a child — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Death of a child
When a dependent child dies, the child should be excluded from a couple's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship from the start of the pay period following the date of the child's death.
When a dependent child dies they should be excluded from a sole parent's benefit 28 days following the date of death.
Payment of the benefit may continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child died.
This provides a transition period for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.
Note during the 28-day continuation of payment, if the client has other changes of circumstances e.g. a change in income, the rate of any benefit will need to be reassessed using the sole parent threshold rates.
## Child turns 18
Generally, clients getting a discretionary benefit such as Jobseeker Support Student Hardship must respond to their notice before the child's 18th birthday or the child will be excluded from their payments. The client must also complete a review of circumstances to determine if they continue to qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and the rate payable or their payments will suspend.
If Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a sole parent's child has died, and the child that died was due to turn 18 during that period, the client is not required to complete a review of circumstances.
However, if Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and any extra help is continuing at the existing rate for up to 28 days because a sole parent's child has died and a different child in their care turns 18, the client must still complete the review of circumstances or their payments will suspend.

chunks.title: New benefit paid at a higher rate — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## New benefit paid at a higher rate
If the surviving person's benefit is reviewed and they qualify for a new benefit at a higher rate, they may be granted the new benefit instead of terminal benefit from the day after a client's death.
If the deceased person qualified for terminal benefit their portion will continue to be paid.
## Current benefit paid at a higher rate
If the surviving persons current benefit is reviewed and they qualify for a higher rate, their benefit rate increases from the day after their partner's death. MSD pays this instead of their portion of the terminal benefit as they will get more money.
If the deceased person qualified for terminal benefit their portion of the benefit will continue to be paid.
## Surviving person is entitled to survivor's grant from ACC
When the death of a person was the result of an accident, entitlement to a survivor's grant from ACC needs to be decided before terminal benefit can be paid.
If the surviving person or child are entitled to a survivor's grant from the ACC, there is no entitlement to terminal benefit.
If Jobseeker Support Student Hardship payments have continued after the date of death, an overpayment is established and the debt should be recovered from the estate.
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship when the child turns 18 during the 28-day continuation of payment period.
The review of circumstances for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship when their child turns 18 is not required when the client has died.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A child will not be excluded from the parent or caregiver's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship when the child turns 18 during the terminal benefit period.
The review of circumstances for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship when their child turns 18 is not required when the client has died.

chunks.title: Death of a single client — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Death of a single client
When a single client (with no children) dies, payment generally stops from the day after the date of death, but there is some discretion to continue payment for up to 28 days.
Payment should stop from the first available date if we have been notified within 28 days of the date of death. This will avoid creating a debt.
When there are other circumstances that justify payment of terminal benefit, payment should continue for the full 28 days after death.
For more information see:
- Avoiding a debt
- Terminal benefit for a single client
Note a single client who is a liable person and paying Child Support payments, or a caregiver getting Unsupported Childs Benefit or Orphans Benefit is regarded as having children.
For more information see:
- Death of a client with a partner or child

chunks.title: Deciding if surviving person would be better off getting terminal benefit or a new benefit — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Deciding if surviving person would be better off getting terminal benefit or a new benefit
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children.

chunks.title: Decision guidelines - clients with a partner — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines - clients with a partner
While Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should generally be stopped when the primary client is imprisoned, there is discretion for payment to be continued and paid to the partner not in prison. This discretion allows payment of all or part of the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship to the partner.
If you feel that payment should be continued, and paid to the partner, this should generally be at the single or sole parent rate. However, you can pay the full married, civil union or de facto rate if you feel this is warranted after having regard to the particular circumstances of the client and their partner.
To help you decide whether it is reasonable to pay the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship to the partner while the client is in prison, and the rate to pay, consider the following:
- has the period in prison already passed
- is the client due to be released from prison shortly
- is the likely period in prison less than six months
- does the partner qualify for a statutory benefit in their own right
- do they intend to live together when the partner is released
- has the partner in prison applied for Home Detention
- are there exceptional circumstances that warrant paying the full married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit to the partner who is not in prison
For further help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.
For more information see:
- SWIFTT process to pay a partner

chunks.title: Decision guidelines - sole parents — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Decision guidelines - sole parents
When a sole parent Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client is imprisoned it is important that financial assistance is available to support any dependent children.
While Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should generally be stopped when the client is imprisoned, there is discretion for payment to be continued and paid to the person who is caring for the dependent children.
To help you decide whether it is reasonable to pay the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship while the client is in prison, you should consider the following:
- has the period in prison already passed
- is the client due to be released from prison shortly
- is the likely period in prison less than twelve months
- will the children return to the client's care on their release from prison
- has the caregiver ceased work to care for the children
- has the caregiver lost entitlement to their own benefit due to having children in their care
For further help you can contact the Helpline to discuss the circumstances before you make your decision.
For more information see:
- Rate of payment - sole parents
- Examples - sole parents
- Remanded in custody
- Sole parents

chunks.title: Definition of 'support' from a family member residing overseas — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Definition of 'support' from a family member residing overseas
'Support' means assistance that the young person could not reasonably obtain from a family member in New Zealand, and includes (but are not limited to):
- emotional support
- educational support
- mentoring/guidance
- any other assistance that is beneficial to the welfare of the young person
Note in assessing whether the young person could not reasonably obtain the support from a family member in New Zealand, you should consider:
- the type and nature of the relationship with the family member residing overseas
- whether there are features of the young person's relationship with that family member that are absent from their relationships with other family members residing in New Zealand (such as shared experiences and the nature of the relationship)

chunks.title: Dependent child — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Dependent child
A dependent child for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is a child who is:
- primarily the responsibility of the client
- maintained as a member of that family
- financially dependent on that client
- in the custody of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki but has been returned to their parent's care
A dependent child for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship does not include a:
- child getting payments under section 363 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989
- child for whom Orphan's or Unsupported Child's Benefit is being paid and
- young person getting a Young Parent Payment and their child (see Dependent children, young parents and the child's parent or step parent examples)
## Maintained as a member of the family
The child should be an integral part of the family, participating in the usual family activities (for example outings and annual holidays).
In some situations, a child may not be living at home but is still considered to be a dependent child.
Dependent children should be included in the assessment of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.

chunks.title: Continuing dependent partner's portion of benefit — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Continuing dependent partner's portion of benefit
When the partner of a Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client dies, the partner's portion of the benefit is continued for 28 days at the same rate that was being paid on the date their partner died. Benefit payments that continue after the day a client has died are called 'terminal benefit'.
## Dependent children
When there are dependent children included in the benefit, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments should be transferred to the primary client. Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments are not part of the terminal benefit.
A surviving client, with dependent children, can choose to remain on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship if they can meet their work obligations.
If their youngest child is under 14 years old they may be able to receive Sole Parent Support from the date following the death of their partner. It is important that the different entitlements of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and Sole Parent Support are explained to the client so they can make the best decision for their circumstances.
## No dependent children
A client would stay on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship if they have no dependent children.
Note clients staying on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship may be given an exemption from their work obligations to allow them time to adjust to their new circumstances.
## Date of review
When the surviving client remains on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, review the client's benefit from the date following the death of their partner.
You need to:
- increase their benefit to the single or sole parent rate and
- adjust any Extra help to the single or sole parent rate
When the client applies for (and is granted) Sole Parent Support, cancel their Jobseeker Support Student Hardship from the day after their partner's death.
Note when the surviving client decides to receive a new main benefit or their existing benefit at the increased rate, the deceased partner’s portion of the benefit continues for 28 days at the rate being paid at the date of death (if the deceased person qualifies for terminal benefit).

chunks.title: Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Detention in or transfer to a psychiatric hospital
When person who has been remanded in custody, or is serving a term of imprisonment is detained in or transferred to a psychiatric hospital you may be able to pay an Emergency Benefit at the hospital rate.
People who are remanded in custody or serving a term of imprisonment who are temporarily hospitalised for treatment of an injury or health condition are still considered to be in prison and the Department of Corrections will meet their costs. An Emergency Benefit or any other financial assistance cannot be paid.
For more information see:
- Emergency Benefit Person serving their sentence of imprisonment in a psychiatric hospital
- Release from prison

chunks.title: Discharged from Oranga Tamariki care — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Discharged from Oranga Tamariki care
Where Oranga Tamariki or other authorised agency has care, custody or sole guardianship of the child, and returns the child to the care of the immediate previous caregiver, they do not make payments for the child.
The child is then a dependent child and can be included in the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
Where the relationship is not one of care, but more of a boarding arrangement, the young person may be able to receive Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment.
Once a child has been discharged from care the child can be considered a dependent child even when Oranga Tamariki or any other authorised agency involvement continues, for example:
- Additional Guardianship Order
- Support Order or
- Services Order
When there is a Service or Support Order in place, you will need to make sure that the Court's intent allows you to consider the child as a dependent child.
For further details on what discharged from care means see:
- Definition of discharged from Oranga Tamariki care

chunks.title: Effect of income on Extra help — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Effect of income on Extra help
When income is added or changed you will also need to review any Extra help the client may be receiving.
Some Extra help is not income tested such as Child Disability Allowance. It is the client's obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances.
Income is charged against Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support, and Childcare Subsidy or OSCAR on a weekly basis.
- Temporary Additional Support Chargeable income
- Childcare Subsidy Income test
- Special Benefit Assessment of income deficiency
- Income change
- Extra Help

chunks.title: Effect on benefit — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Effect on benefit
Any inclusion or exclusion of a dependent child from a client's benefit will result in a general review of the client's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and any extra help they are getting.
You may need to review the following:
- Jobseeker Support Student HardshipPartner's work obligations may change.
When a single client has a child come into their care they may no longer be able to meet their work obligations. Depending on the age of the child, they may be able to get a Sole Parent Support or an Emergency Benefit - caring for a child who is not their own.
- Accommodation SupplementChanges to the family composition may result in a change to the Accommodation Supplement entry thresholds.
- Non standard benefit rateWhen a child is added or removed you may need to manually adjust the non-standard rate of payment.
- Special BenefitAny change to family circumstances will result in a review of Special Benefit. A child included or excluded from the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship may result in a change to the allowable costs for Special Benefit.
- Temporary Additional SupportAny change to family circumstances will result in a review of Temporary Additional Support. A child included or excluded from the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship may result in a change to the allowable costs for Temporary Additional Support.
- Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Accommodation Supplement — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Accommodation Supplement
For a single client stop the Accommodation Supplement from the beginning of the 14th week of hospitalisation. Check whether the client still has to meet their continuing accommodation costs. If so, increase the benefit rate above the hospital rate to meet the costs.
For a married , civil union or de facto client (without dependent children) you still treat the couple as married, in a civil union or de facto relationship and take into account the income and assets of both. You can pay the full Accommodation Supplement to the partner not in hospital.
For more information see:
- Dependent children
- Accommodation Supplement
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
As long as the child continues to be a dependent child, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments continue to be paid regardless of how long the client is in hospital.
Best Start tax credit payments will stop when the child turns three even if the client remains in hospital.
For more information see:
- Dependent child
- Best Start tax credit Child turns 3

chunks.title: Employment — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Employment
Clients must advise of any change in circumstances that affects their entitlement to Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, such as commencing employment.
When a client or partner (if any) advises that they have commenced employment, MSD must check that they are still entitled to Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and are getting the correct rate of payment.
To review the client’s Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, MSD needs to know:
- the date their employment commenced
- the type of employment, meaning: casual employmentpart-time employmentfull-time employment
- casual employment
- part-time employment
- full-time employment
- the name and address of the employer
- the hours will they be working
MSD will determine the appropriate review action based on this information.
For more information see:
- Full-time employment
- Part-time employment
- Self-employment
- Seasonal work
- Commission work
- Voluntary Work
- Income stops
- Goes on strike
- Reapplying for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship

chunks.title: Partner may need to be absent for more than 28 days — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Partner may need to be absent for more than 28 days
A partner may be required to be absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days.
For more information see:
- Paying for more than 28 days - delayed return
- Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason to travel
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period

chunks.title: Essential travel — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Essential travel
A client not otherwise entitled to be paid their Jobseeker Support Student Hardship while they are absent from New Zealand may have their payments continue for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if they have to travel outside of New Zealand to attend a significant event relating to a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family).
These events are ones which the client or partner would reasonably be expected to attend. That is, the travel is essential to them and where not attending the event would cause the person emotional distress. This may include, but is not limited to, travel that allows the client to:
- be with a seriously ill or dying person who is a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family)
- attend a funeral or an unveiling in relation to a family member
- pay respect to a family member of the deceased in the event of the client missing the funeral
- attend to legal matters in relation to the affairs of the deceased family member
- attend a birth of a family member or be with a family member around the time of their giving birth
- provide support to a party or witness to a court case
- attend a wedding of a family member - the client does not need to be a member of the bridal party or play a significant part in the wedding in order for the payment of benefit to continue while they are absent from New Zealand
- travel for a court ordered custody arrangement
For more information see:
- Definition of family member
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Job interviews or follow up on a job prospect
- Permitted travel reasons
- Absences that do not prevent partner from meeting obligations
- Paying benefit when client failed to advise of absence
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes (within a 28 day maximum)

chunks.title: Estimated income — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Estimated income
Clients must advise MSD of any change in their circumstances that affects their entitlement or rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, such as commencing employment.
If a client has one-off, fluctuating or casual income, it may be necessary to estimate their earnings to prevent a debt. When the client under or over estimates their income they should confirm the actual amount earned as soon as possible.
If the actual income is different to the estimated amount, it must be charged against the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for the week it was earned or the period that it represents.
This may result in arrears or a debt for the client.
For more information about income see:
- Income change
- Calculating the benefit rate
For information about debt recovery, see:
- Debt treatment procedures [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Examples for paying more than 28 days for an approved reason — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: The following examples show situations where a benefit may be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period (but not limited to): Client's reason for travelling for 28 days within 52 week period Client's current reason for travel within 52 week period Outcome Essential travel reasons Essential travel reason eg a seriously ill family member Generally consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if reasonable in the circumstances Job interview or job prospect Essential travel reason eg a funeral Generally would consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if reasonable in the circumstances Partners of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship with work obligations, or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. The client wishes to be absent from New Zealand for another general holiday This is not an approved reason for paying for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. The client would not be able to receive a benefit while absent from New Zealand for this reason even if the travel will not prevent them meeting their obligations (eg even if they had further annual leave from their employment or for partners even if the travel is at a time when they are not required to be in education, training or work-based learning) Partners of Jobseeker Support with work obligations or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. To provide aid or assistance to a family member immediately following a natural disaster or similar adverse event. Generally would allow further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period. This is an unforeseen event and it is reasonable for them to help their family member. Partners of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship with work obligations or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. Essential travel reason Generally would consider allowing further period of payment while absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period, if the essential travel reason was unforeseen. Partners of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship with work obligations or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with these obligations. Needs to attend a wedding of a family member. Generally would not consider allowing a further period of payment for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.

chunks.title: Examples for paying more than 28 days for an approved reason — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Weddings are usually known about in advance and this should have been planned for when they used the 28 days to go on holiday. However, where the wedding is genuinely unforeseen, consideration could be given to allowing travel for a period of more than 28 days in a 52 week period. Partners of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship with work obligations or work-preparation obligations or youth activity obligations had to spend four days at a funeral overseas. The partner had booked a holiday prior to the attendance at the funeral overseas. This holiday was booked for 28 days because they are able to travel for any reason if the travel will not interfere with their obligations. The client does not have the full 28 days left Travelling for a general holiday is not an approved reason for paying a benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period The benefit will only be paid for the number of days the client has available (that is, 24 days).

chunks.title: Example 1 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Carlos contacts MSD on 19 November to advise that he has returned from travelling to Malaysia to be with his dying mother. He left in a hurry and didn't contact MSD before his departure. His Jobseeker Support Student Hardship stopped on 4 November, the day after he left the country. He returned to New Zealand on 14 November, but then had to organise a New Zealand-based funeral for his mother, as a large number of people are based in New Zealand. Carlos didn't advise MSD of his travel before leaving New Zealand, but he has a humanitarian reason that justifies his travel and the reason he didn't contact MSD before he left. Given Carlos' circumstances, he contacted MSD as soon as it would have been reasonable to expect him to and he meets the criteria for an approved travel reason. Carlos' Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can be backdated to 4 November.

chunks.title: Example 2 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Sanjay left New Zealand for India on 7 December because his father had become suddenly seriously ill and been hospitalised. While in India, Sanjay's father passed away and Sanjay stayed in India for the funeral. Sanjay returned on 16 December, after staying for 2 weeks for the Hindu funeral and mourning period. On 19 December, Sanjay contacts MSD to explain that he has been overseas after learning of his father's illness, and that he stayed for the funeral. On return, Sanjay spent time mourning with his own family and has been distraught. He explains that he only realised last night that he had not informed MSD of his absence. Sanjay's reason for leaving New Zealand is a humanitarian reason and he meets the criteria for backdating his payment to the day after departure. Given Sanjay's circumstances, he informed MSD as soon as he reasonably could. Sanjay's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can be backdated to 8 December, the date it was suspended.

chunks.title: Example 3 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Tusila calls MSD on 5 January to tell them she will leave New Zealand on 7 January to help her sister, who just lost her house in a flood. When asked how long she will be gone for, Tusila says that she hasn't bought a return ticket yet and was considering staying on to catch up with family and see how her sister is going. MSD informs Tusila that she can only keep getting her Jobseeker Support Student Hardship if she is absent for essential travel. Helping her sister after a flood is considered essential travel, however if she is going to stay longer for a holiday, she won't be able to get Jobseeker Support Student Hardship during the time she is on holiday. Tusila returns to MSD the next day with an airline quote showing that the cheapest return flight is on 14 January. She thinks it will take her a week to ensure her sister has sorted out insurance, medium-term accommodation, and access to basic goods like clothing and food. She has decided not to stay on for the holiday. MSD agrees this is reasonable and tells Tusila she keep getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship from 7 to 14 January, while she is overseas helping her sister.

chunks.title: Example 4 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Christy is getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and contacts MSD to advise that her sister is getting married in Australia on 8 June. Christy is going to Australia to her sister's wedding but intends to stay on for a further 2 weeks to visit other family. Christy is leaving New Zealand on 4 June as she has to help her sister prepare. She will stay until 10 June to help clean up. Christy then begins the holiday leg of her trip, returning to New Zealand on 25 June. Christy's travel is divided as follows: - 5 June to 10 June period meets the essential travel criteria - 11 June to 24 June period is considered other travel (holiday) and does not meet the essential travel criteria Christy's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can only be paid until 10 June, for the period that meets the essential travel criteria.

chunks.title: Example 5 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Graeme left New Zealand on 16 December to help his sister in Australia after she lost her house in a fire. He returns to New Zealand on 23 December. A week later, on 30 December he attends an appointment and asks why he hasn't been getting his Jobseeker Support Student Hardship. His case manager informs him that his payments stopped when he left the country and asks why he didn't contact MSD sooner. Graeme explains that he left to help his sister after a house fire, and he meant to contact MSD once he had helped his sister sort out accommodation and insurance , but he forgot. The case manager explains that because he didn't contact MSD as soon as he reasonably could have been expected to (i.e. once he had helped his sister), his Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can only be backdated to 23 December, the date he returned to New Zealand.

chunks.title: Example 1 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Example 1
A client applies for benefit to be paid for 10 days when they are going to be absent from New Zealand. In the past 52 weeks the client had 10 days absence from New Zealand and continued being paid their benefit
Step
Calculation
Identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand.
13 September 2019
Count back 52 weeks from this date.
14 September 2018
Count the number of days the client has continued getting their benefit while they were overseas in this 52 week period.
Days client has continued getting their benefit while absent from New Zealand between 14 September 2018 and 13 September 2019 = 10 days
Subtract the number of days the client has been paid their benefit while absent from New Zealand from 28 days.
28 - 10 days = 18 days available
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay the client for the days they have available.
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay them for the 10 days they are out of the country.
## Example 2
A client applies for benefit to be paid for 10 days when they are going to be absent from New Zealand. In the past 52 weeks the client had 20 days absence from New Zealand and continued to be paid their benefit.
Step
Calculation
Identify the day after the client is intending to leave New Zealand.
13 September 2019
Count back 52 weeks from this date.
14 September 2018
Count the number of days the client has continued getting their benefit while they were overseas in this 52 week period.
Days client has continued getting their benefit while absent from New Zealand between 14 September 2018 and 13 September 2019 = 20 days
Subtract the number of days the client was paid their benefit while absent from New Zealand from 28 days.
28 - 20 days = 8 days available
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay the client for the days they have available.
If the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit while overseas, pay them for the 8 days they are out of the country. For 2 of the days they are absent from New Zealand they will not get their payments.
Check if the client meets the criteria to be paid their benefit for more than 28 days in a 52 week period - if they meet these criteria, they may be able to continue getting their payment for the additional 2 days of absence.

chunks.title: Example 1 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: A married client is getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and their partner works for 2 weeks earning $190.53 gross in the first week and $850.00 gross in the second week. To work out the income deduction: Week 1 Week 2 Gross income (excluding cents) $190.00 $850.00(over cut out point) Less income allowed before benefit is affected $160.00 $160.00 Equals income $30.00 $690.00 Income over $160 reduces benefit by 70 cents per $1.00 $30 x 0.7 $690 x 0.7 Amount benefit reduced on account of income $21.00 $483.00 To work out the benefit rate payable: Maximum benefit (net as at 1 July 2021) $453.62 $453.62 Less reduction due to income $21.00 $483.00 Benefit rate payable $432.62 $NIL

chunks.title: Example 2 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: A client is getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship at the half married, civil union or de facto rate as their partner has a voluntary unemployment stand-down imposed. The client is also working and earning $190.43 gross a week on a regular basis. To work out the income deduction: Gross income (excluding cents) $190.00 Less income allowed before benefit is affected $160.00 Equals income $30.00 Income over $160 reduces benefit by 35 cents per $1.00 $30 x 0.35 Amount benefit reduced on account of income $10.50 To work out the benefit rate payable: Maximum net benefit (as at 1 July 2021) $226.81 Less reduction due to income $10.50 Benefit rate payable $216.31

chunks.title: Example 3 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: A sole parent getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is working and earning $190 gross per week. To work out the income deduction: Gross income (excluding cents) $190.00 Less income allowed before benefit is affected $160.00 Equals income $30.00 Income over $160 reduces benefit by 30 cents per $1.00, and 70 cents per $1.00 over $250 $30 x 0.30 Amount benefit reduced on account of income $9.00 To work out the benefit payable: Maximum net benefit (as at 1 July 2021) $406.78 Less reduction due to income $9.00 Benefit rate payable $397.78 Income may be charged on a weekly or annual basis.

chunks.title: Example 1 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: A client has two casual part-time jobs both are paid on a weekly basis. - Job 1 $150 gross paid weekly earned for the period Wednesday 02/04/2014 to Friday 04/04/2014 - Job 2 $210.00 gross paid weekly earned for the period Sunday 06/04/2014 to Tuesday 08/04/2014 The client phones the contact centre and declares all of this income. Although the income declared is received from two different part-time jobs the amounts are added together for the week the income is earned and charged against the benefit as follows: Period income earned Monday 31/03/2014 to Sunday 06/04/2014 Job 1 02/04/2014 to 04/04/2014 = Job 2 06/04/2014 to 06/04/2014 = (1 day) $150.00 gross $70.00 gross Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for week 31/03/2014 to 06/04/2014 $220.00 gross Period income earned Monday 07/04/2014 to Sunday 13/04/2014 Job 2 07/04/2014 to 08/04/2014 = (2 days) $140.00 Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for week 05/04/2014 to 13/04/2014 $140.00

chunks.title: Example 2 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: A client's partner has two casual part time jobs. - Part-time Job 1 $95.73 gross for the period worked Tuesday 01/04/2014 to Friday 04/04/2014 paid on the following Thursday 10/04/2014. - Part-time Job 2 $750.00 gross for the period worked Wednesday 02/04/2014 to Tuesday 15/04/2014 paid fortnightly on Tuesday 15/04/2014 (10 working days). Client earns $15.00 per hour and works 5 hours per day. The client's partner phones the contact centre on Tuesday 15/04/2014 and declares all of this income. Although the income declared is received from two different part time jobs the amounts are added together for the week the income is earned and charged against the benefit as follows: Period income earned Monday 31/04/2014 to Sunday 06/04/2014 Job 1 = 01/04/2014 to 04/04/2014 = Job 2 = 02/04/2014 to 04/04/2014 = (3 days) $95.73 gross $225.00 gross Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for week 31/03/2014 to 06/04/2014 $320.73 gross Period income earned Monday 07/04/2014 to Sunday 13/04/2014 Job 2 = 07/04/2014 to 11/04/2014 = (5 days) $375.00 Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for week 07/04/2014 to 13/04/2014 $375.00 Period income earned Monday 14/04/2014 to Sunday 20/04/2014 Job 2 = 14/04/2014 to 15/04/2014 = (2 days) $150.00 Total income to be charged on Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for week 14/04/2014 to 20/04/2014 $150.00 For more information see: - Period over which to charge income

chunks.title: Examples of paying for more than 28 days for obtaining family support for young partners — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Examples of paying for more than 28 days for obtaining family support for young partners
Generally, a benefit cannot be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period while a client is absent from New Zealand.
However, there are limited circumstances where a benefit can be paid for more than 28 days in a 52 week period where the client is travelling to receive support from a family member (including any other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family) who is residing overseas.
## Young partner of main beneficiary may meet the requirements in some circumstances
However, they may be able to be paid their payment for more than 28 days for the purposes of obtaining support from a family member overseas if:
- the support they require can't be given by their partner because the main beneficiary themselves is absent from New Zealand or
- it is support the young partner cannot receive from their partner (for example, it is support from a parent or grandparent or the partner and the young person are having relationship difficulties)

chunks.title: Example 1 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Example 1
The temporary caregiver is to be paid Jobseeker Support Student Hardship - sole parent at the equivalent Unsupported Childs Benefit rate while caring for 1 child, aged 14 years, during the sole parent client's imprisonment.
Unsupported Child's Benefit (as at 1 April 2026)
$350.58
Less family tax credit (as at 1 April 2026)
$151.91
Equals amount to add as a non-standard rate
$198.67
## Example 2
The temporary caregiver is to be paid Jobseeker Support Student Hardship - sole parent at the equivalent Unsupported Childs Benefit rate while caring for 2 children, aged 14 and 10 years, during the sole parent client's imprisonment.
Unsupported Childs Benefit (as at 1 April 2026):
- $350.58 for 14-year old and
- $327.16 for 10-year old
$677.74
Less family tax credit (as at 1 April 2026):
- $151.91 for first child and
- $123.78 for second child
$275.69
Equals amount to add as a non-standard rate
$402.05
## Example 3
The temporary caregiver is to be paid Jobseeker Support Student Hardship - Sole parent while caring for 2 children aged 14 and 10 years during the sole parent client's imprisonment. It has been agreed to include the rent of the client's home of $150.00.
Unsupported Childs Benefit (as at 1 April 2026):
- $350.58 for 14-year old and
- $327.16 for 10-year old
$677.74
Plus rent on client's home
$150.00
Sub total
$827.74
Less family tax credit (as at 1 April 2026):
- $151.91 for first child and
- $123.78 for second child
$275.69
Equals calculated amount required to assist the temporary caregiver to care for the client's children (rent included)
$552.05
Maximum Jobseeker Support Student Hardship - sole parent rate (net as at 1 April 2026)
$521.52
In this case the amount payable is the maximum Jobseeker Support Student Hardship - sole parent rate of $521.52. You don't need to add a non-standard rate.

chunks.title: Other situations where a child is considered to be financially independent — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Other situations where a child is considered to be financially independent
There may be other situations where all a child's financial needs (including the provision of accommodation and material needs) are being met by someone else or from some other source. For example:
- a family trust or
- the non-custodial parent
## Date of review
Where a child becomes financially independent it should be excluded from the benefit payment from the start of the next pay period in which the child became financially independent.
There is discretion to continue payment for one payday following the event.
This discretion only applies when the exclusion of the child affects the rate of payment of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and is generally used when processing deadlines have passed.
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
Stop family tax credit and Best Start tax credits payments from the start of the next payday in which the child became financially independent, to avoid an overpayment (with Inland Revenue) for the client.

chunks.title: Date of review — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Date of review
Exclude the child from the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship from the beginning of the next pay period in which the child started work.

chunks.title: Primary client — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Primary client
If a primary client commences full-time employment, they will no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should be stopped from the date the client commences full-time employment.
When a client commences full-time employment they may qualify for Extra Help as a non-beneficiary, such as:
- Accommodation Supplement
- Disability Allowance
- Seasonal Work Assistance
- Transition to Work Grant [no link find out why] - Doogle
- Working for Families Tax Credits from Inland Revenue or
- Childcare Assistance Programme
Note if the client has outstanding debt when their benefit is cancelled, MSD is responsible for arranging repayments with the client. If a client is cancelling their benefit to commence full-time employment, their debt recovery can be suspended for a 3 month period provided the client remains in employment.
However, MSD can accept repayments if the client wishes to start paying the outstanding debt straight away.
For more information see:
- Debt recovery suspension [no link find out why]
- Arranging repayments at cancellation
To determine whether the benefit should be suspended or cancelled when a client commences full-time employment see:
- Guidelines for suspension or cancellation
## Partner
If the person who has commenced full-time employment is the partner, then the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue with the partner's earnings being charged as income against the benefit.
This is regardless of whether the partner is subject to work obligations.
Note if the partner has full-time work obligations and is working 30 hours per week or has part-time work obligations and is working 20 hours or more, then they will be meeting their work obligations.
For more information see:
- Treatment of income
- Charging income
- Income stops
- Employment related income

chunks.title: Guidelines for paying a higher rate — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Guidelines for paying a higher rate
Payment can be increased above the hospital rate to a rate (together with the client's other income) that will be sufficient to meet the client's continuing commitments.
Use the following guidelines to assess whether the client's rate should be higher.
1. Have the client complete an Increased payment while you are in hospital form.
2. Accept stated expenses where they appear reasonable, but ask for proof if there is doubt.
3. If the client is a sole parent and has childcare costs:
- include the childcare costs when assessing whether a higher rate should be paid
- include family tax credit and Best Start tax credits payments as income (as these payments will continue)
4. If a client is married, in a civil union or de facto relationship, do not include home outgoings or accommodation expenses. These are the responsibility of the partner not in hospital. (The partner may qualify for Accommodation Supplement or Temporary Additional Support.)
5. Check that all possible action has been taken to reduce expenses. For example, giving up the lease on a flat where the hospital stay is indefinite.
6. If the increase in payment request is for one-off items such as clothing, you can pay the increase by:
- a backdated review of the benefit rate to create a lump sum payment or
- increasing the benefit rate for a limited time

chunks.title: Guidelines for suspension or cancellation — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Guidelines for suspension or cancellation
If a primary Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client has commenced full-time employment they will no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship. Generally, their benefit must be suspended or cancelled from the date they commenced full-time employment.
If their full-time employment is for a limited period, there are different ways to treat the benefit depending on:
- the proposed length of the employment
- the client's circumstances
- whether the client would qualify for Seasonal Work Assistance
- whether they qualify for Extra help such as Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance, Family tax credit, Best Start tax credits or In-work tax credit
To determine whether the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should be suspended or cancelled, MSD will consider:
- if the employment is likely to last for less than 8 weeks
- if the client is no longer intending to study
- if the client qualifies for Extra help during the period of employment
- whether the client gets Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
- if the client qualifies for Working for Families Tax Credits from Inland Revenue
## Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit can be paid for a maximum of 8 weeks after a benefit is suspended or cancelled when a client commences employment. Payment of the tax credits will continue at the same rate that was paid while the client was getting a benefit.
For more information see:
- Family tax credit
## Extra help
If a client commences full-time employment they may qualify for Extra help as a non-beneficiary.
The client does not need to complete a new application if they were already getting the Extra help with their main benefit. If they continue to qualify the rate payable should be reviewed.
If the client qualifies for Extra help they are not already getting with their main benefit, a new application is generally required.

chunks.title: Home Detention — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Home Detention
A client may be in prison for a short time before being released on home detention.
Home detainees can apply for an exemption from their work obligations.
## Partner
When the partner of a person in prison has been receiving a benefit, this will be reviewed from the date of release.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship Court imposed conditions
- Transfer between benefits
- Release from prison

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client (or their partner) is admitted to hospital, their benefit can continue at the full rate for the first 13 weeks. The rate of payment will need to be reduced to the hospital rate after the client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks (not after getting a benefit for 13 weeks).
If a partner who has work obligations is hospitalised, exempt the partner from their obligations by adding the 'sick/injured/disabled - partners - partial' exemption code (402) on SWTDA. You will also need to add an expiry date.
## Hospital rate
The hospital rate allows for the cost of personal items, which patients are expected to provide for themselves. The net weekly hospital rate is $58.34 as at 1 April 2026.
You can pay an amount above the hospital rate where there are financial circumstances to warrant paying at a higher rate.
Note you cannot pay an amount less than the hospital rate.

chunks.title: Imprisonment — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Imprisonment
Generally, when a Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client is imprisoned or detained in custody, they are no longer entitled to receive the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should stop from the day following the date of imprisonment.
MSD must decide whether to suspend or cancel the benefit after considering the likely period in prison and whether the client has a partner and or dependent children.
In some circumstances Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue when the client is imprisoned.

chunks.title: Example 1 — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Example 1
A client getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks. This client has other income which reduces the main benefit rate to $20 per week.
In this case we pay the rate $20 per week which is lower than the hospital rate of $58.34 (as at 1 April 2026).
## Example 2
A client receiving a Jobseeker Support Student Hardship has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks. This client has other income which reduces the main benefit rate to $70 per week.
In this case we pay the hospital rate of $58.34 per week (as at 1 April 2026) which is the lower rate.

chunks.title: Income change — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Income change
Clients must advise MSD of any change in circumstances that affects their entitlement or rate of benefit payable, such as when they receive or earn income.
Any income that a Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client or their partner (if any) receives must be charged against the benefit for the period in which the income was earned or represents.
If income does not represent a specific period or if MSD cannot determine the actual period it represents, MSD must determine the most appropriate period to charge the income. This may be the week it is received, provided or supplied.
When a client or their partner (if any) declare a change in income, MSD must check that they still qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and reassess any Extra Help they get.
Note sole parents whose Jobseeker Support Student Hardship commenced before 1 July 2025 may be able to have their income charged annually.
For more information see:
- Sole parents whose benefit commenced before 1 July 2025
## Deductions or redirections
When adding income to a client's record MSD must check that there is enough benefit to cover any deductions or redirections. Any deductions or redirections may need to be reduced depending on the amount of benefit due.
For more information see:
- Redirection of benefit payment

chunks.title: Income for a past period — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Income for a past period
If a client declares income for a past period and there is either no income or there is a different amount previously declared for that period, the client's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should be reviewed for that period.
Income should be charged against the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for the week in which it is earned or the period it represents. Any Extra Help assistance should also be reviewed.
## Information share Child Support payments
Information share Child Support payments are treated differently as they are automatically charged forward as income for a period of 4 or 5 weeks.
For more information see:
- Information share Child Support payments
- Automated income charging rules
Note sole parents whose Jobseeker Support Student Hardship commenced before 1 July 2025 may be able to have their income charged annually.
For more information see:
- Sole parents whose benefit commenced before 1 July 2025

chunks.title: Income from employment — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Income from employment
Clients must advise MSD of any change in their circumstances that affects their entitlement or rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, such as commencing employment.
## Full-time employment
If the primary client commences full-time employment, the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship must be stopped from the date they commenced employment. This is because they will no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
If the client has a partner who meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship in their own right, the partner can apply for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship as the primary client.
If the person who has commenced full-time employment is the partner, then the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue with their earnings being charged as income against the benefit.
For more information see:
- Full-time employment
## Part-time employment
If a client or their partner commences part-time or casual employment that is less than 30 hours a week the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue. This is because the client or partner will still be able to meet their job search requirements.
The income from part-time or casual employment will be charged against the benefit for the week in which the income was earned or represents.
However, if the earnings from the part-time or casual employment reduce the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship to zero when charged against the benefit, the benefit must be suspended.
## Weekend work
If a client or partner is working weekends regularly, casually or 'one-off' the income is charged against the benefit from the previous Monday.
For more information see:
- Estimated income
For more information see:
- Types of income
- Definition of income
- Employment
- Self-employment
- Commission work
- Income reduces the benefit payable to zero
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship cut-out points (current)

chunks.title: Income reduces the benefit payable to zero — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Income reduces the benefit payable to zero
IIf the client or partner has earnings or income for a period that will reduce the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship payable to zero, then the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship will need to be suspended or cancelled.
Although the main benefit may be stopped, the client may still qualify for Extra help.
For more information see:
- Effect of income on Extra help
- Income from employment
- Income change
Note clients will not qualify for the Winter Energy Payment if their income reduces their benefit payable to zero.

chunks.title: Income stops — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Income stops
If a client or partner (if any) advises that their income has stopped MSD must review their Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and any Extra help they are getting from the day after the income stopped.
MSD will need to determine why the income has stopped for example, a client may advise that the interest payments from their investment have stopped. MSD must find out what the client has done with the money that was invested.
## Deprivation of income or assets
MSD has discretion to reduce or decline a benefit (and any Extra help) where clients have deprived themselves of income or assets.
For more information see:
- Core policy Income
## Ceases employment
If a client or partner (if any), ceases employment MSD needs to decide when to review their Jobseeker Support Student Hardship from.
MSD will need to find out:
- the date they ceased employment
- the reason they ceased employment
- final pay details (including any holiday pay, redundancy etc)
Note if the client or partner gets any holiday pay, the holiday pay should be charged as ongoing income over the period it represents.
## Example
Alan has been getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship with his partner Kodi included.
Kodi is working and has been earning $720 gross per week. He ceases work on 1 April 2024 and gets holiday pay of $1440.
Kodi's holiday pay is equivalent to 2 weeks pay. MSD continues to charge $720 per week as income against the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, for the 2 weeks from 1 April 2024.
For more information see:
- Reapplying for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship
- Income change
- Employment related income

chunks.title: Single clients and couples — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Single clients and couples
Clients whose weekly income is over $160 gross per week will have their benefit reduced by 70 cents for every $1.00 of income that is over that amount per week.
If a client is getting a half-married rate of benefit because their partner is:
- granted a main benefits in their own right or
- not entitled to get a benefit because they have a 13-week non-entitlement period, have a financial sanction imposed or they are on strike
Then, their benefit will be reduced by 35 cents for every $1.00 of the total combined income that is over $160.00 gross per week.
## Sole parents
Sole parents clients whose weekly income is over $160 gross per week will have their benefit reduced by:
- 30 cents for every $1.00 of income that is between $160 and $250 gross per week
- 70 cents for every $1.00 of income that is more than $250 gross per week.
Note sole parents whose Jobseeker Support Student Hardship commenced before 1 July 2025 may be able to have their income charged annually.
For more information see:
- Sole parents whose benefit commenced before 1 July 2025

chunks.title: IRD number for partner who is not apportioned assistance — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: As part of a review of benefit, MSD may make a written request to the client for evidence of their partner's IRD number when the: - partner is not apportioned the primary client's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, and - partner's income is relevant to a client's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.

chunks.title: Adverse Action Notice following an unsuccessful match — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: MSD has an agreement with Inland Revenue to share information about a partner's IRD number. When the IRD number information MSD holds does not match Inland Revenue's information or there's an error, MSD should ask the client (in writing) to provide evidence of their partner's IRD number, unless there are significant barriers to providing this. In the written request for evidence of the IRD number, MSD must include a notice in writing (adverse action notice): - advising that MSD has shared information (including IRD number and some personal details) with Inland Revenue, and the match was unsuccessful, and - giving the client or partner a minimum of 10 working days to provide their partner's IRD number evidence or the client's assistance may be suspended. Example Isla is receiving Jobseeker Support Student Hardship. Isla's partner, Ariki, has income that is included in MSD's income test to determine eligibility for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and MSD holds an IRD number for Ariki. The IRD number validation results in a No Match for Ariki's IRD number. As part of a review of Isla's benefit, MSD provides a notice in writing, giving 10 working days for Isla to provide evidence of Ariki's IRD number. MSD's decision to give 10 working days to provide evidence is based on: - Ariki already having an IRD number - Ariki not having any significant barriers to getting evidence of their IRD number - MSD's obligation to provide a minimum of 10 working days to provide the information.

chunks.title: MSD may suspend assistance if evidence is not received — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: MSD may suspend all taxable and/or income tested assistance the client is getting, including Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, if evidence of a partner's IRD number evidence is not provided within a reasonable timeframe (usually 10 working days) or within the extended period if this has been applied. In rare cases, depending on the client's circumstances, MSD may consider cancelling or varying the client's assistance. Note suspension does not apply to Childcare Assistance.

chunks.title: IRD number not requested in some circumstances — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: MSD may not ask for evidence of an IRD number when there are significant barriers to providing the evidence, including, but not limited to: - significant factors, that are outside the client's or partner's control, that would substantially delay providing evidence of the IRD number, e.g. a national emergency affecting Inland Revenue's ability to provide IRD number evidence, and - the client needs assistance to continue, before the evidence can be provided. A partner's IRD number and evidence of their IRD number does not need to be provided when they are not a New Zealand tax resident. MSD can determine at a later point to request evidence of the IRD number. For more information see: - Non-tax resident partner's IRD number not required Note there is different guidance for requesting evidence of an IRD number for clients and partners apportioned Jobseeker Support Student Hardship or when a client is applying for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.

chunks.title: Making an adhoc payment — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Making an adhoc payment
When you need to make a payment of Extra help by way of an adhoc payment you need to use the following process:
- Assess the rate of Extra help the client is entitled to as a non-beneficiary (using a DREW assessment to help you)
- Create an ADHOC payment for the amount of Extra help due by entering the SAHPI screen and then selecting the SAHPA screen
- In the SAHPA screen:
