enter the service code for Extra help (e.g. 471 for Accommodation Supplement, 425 for Disability Allowance);
enter the amount to be paid in the net amount field and
press 'enter'
Note an attention message will appear to advise that the payment requires authorisation
- Create a CMS note to record details of the adhoc payment e.g., type of Extra help, such as Accommodation Supplement, the period the payment represents and the amount
- Give details of the main benefit service code and the Extra help payment to an authorising officer for the payment to be authorised in the SATRI screen

chunks.title: Ministry of Social Development debt repayments — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Ministry of Social Development debt repayments
When a client has a Ministry of Social Development debt, this can be recovered by regular deductions from their current benefit.
Note Income Related Rent historical Kāinga Ora (previously Housing NZ) debt should be given equal priority to Ministry of Social Development debt.
For more information see:
- Current client debt Negotiating repayment of debt

chunks.title: Does not advise of departure — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Does not advise of departure
If the client did not tell the Ministry they were leaving New Zealand their benefit will be suspended immediately from the day after they left New Zealand.
The Integrity Intervention Centre will determine if there has been an overpayment, establish any debt and advise the client.
If a client questions the information match refer them to the Integrity Intervention Centre.
For more information see:
- Paying a benefit when the client has not advised before departure
- Approved travel reasons
- Backdating benefit to the day after departure date
- Action on return to New Zealand
- Examples of applying the absence from New Zealand policy
- Payment when client or partner absent from New Zealand

chunks.title: On leave from hospital — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## On leave from hospital
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is paid at the full rate for any period of leave from hospital. Where the client has been receiving the hospital rate increase their benefit for any period they are on leave.
The benefit action to take, on the client's re-admission to hospital, will depend on how long they were on leave.

chunks.title: Ongoing assistance for dependent children — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Ongoing assistance for dependent children
When a surviving dependent child is to be cared for by a person other than a parent, the caregiver may be able to get an Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit

chunks.title: Oranga Tamariki order in place — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: The following table identifies when a child can be considered a dependent child and when it can't, depending on the type of order that is in place and section of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 that applies. When to include as a dependent child When not to include as a dependent child section 139: Agreements for temporary care of child or young person by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 140: Agreements for extended care of child or young person by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 78: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, pending determination of court proceedings. If Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki has returned the child or young person in to the care of the immediate previous care giver. section 78: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, pending determination of court proceedings section 101: Custody order in favour of principal caregiver. Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki under section 110. section 101: Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 102: Interim Custody Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 110(2)a: Sole Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. Section 101 Custody Order in favour of principal caregiver and other dependent child criteria are met. Please refer case to your local solicitor for consideration. section 110(2)a: Sole Guardianship Order in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki section 110(2) b: Additional Guardianship Order, to any other guardian in favour of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. section 112: Guardianship Order in favour of Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki for a specific purpose. Please refer case to your local solicitor for consideration. section 86: Services Orders that provide for particular services and assistance required by the child or young person (e.g. counselling fees, special education costs) section 86: Services Orders that provide for general financial support to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. section 91: Support Orders. The child may be considered a dependent child where the documentation states that specific financial support is to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki.

chunks.title: Oranga Tamariki order in place — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: section 91: Support Orders. The child cannot be considered a dependent child where the documentation states that general financial support is to be provided by the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki. See your local solicitor if you receive a case in this category. When a child or young person is discharged from the care, custody or sole guardianship of the Chief Executive of Oranga Tamariki, always consider including the child in the clients Jobseeker Support Student Hardship or granting Unsupported Childs Benefit - The legislation referenced above is the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989

chunks.title: Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Orphans or Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid
When a client is receiving an Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit, the child is not treated as a dependent child and is not included in the assessment of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
The client's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is assessed on their family circumstances excluding the child for whom Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit is being paid.

chunks.title: Couple, both aged under 20 years old — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Couple, both aged under 20 years old
When clients who are married, in a civil union or de facto relationship and who are both aged under 20 years, apply to have a child included in their benefit they no longer meet the age qualification for Jobseeker Support. Both clients must apply for Young Parent Payment in their own right.
For more information see:
- Young Parent Payment Qualifications

chunks.title: Part-time employment — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Part-time employment
Part-time employment does not make a child financially independent. Do not take the child's earnings into account when assessing the rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship payments. For more information on children's income see:
- Child income

chunks.title: Part-time employment — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Part-time employment
When Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client or their partner commences employment that is less than 30 hours a week payment of the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue as the client will still be able to meet their job search requirements.
If the partner has commenced full time employment then the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue with the partner's earnings being charged as income against the benefit. This is regardless of whether the partner is subject to work obligations.
You will need to check whether family tax credit and Best Start tax credit should continue to be paid at the full rate, or refer the client to Inland Revenue to avoid an overpayment.
For more information see:
- Family tax credit
- Best Start tax credit
- Guidelines for suspension or cancellation
- Types of income Employment related income
- Treatment of income Income stops
- Charging income

chunks.title: Partners with children under 3 years old — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Partners with children under 3 years old
A partner with their youngest child aged under 3 years old has work preparation obligations and can be a part or full-time student without it affecting their Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
## Partners with work obligations
Partners with no children or with their youngest child aged 3 years or over, may be a part or full-time student without it affecting their Jobseeker Support Student Hardship if they have been granted an exemption from meeting their work obligations because they:
- were part way through a course of study at the time that the client applied for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship or
- were part way through a course of study when their youngest child reached the age of 3 years
A partner can be considered to be meeting their work obligations if their study timetable allows enough time for job search activity, for example, if the hours of the part-time study are outside of normal working hours.
If a partner starts study and they can no longer meet their work obligations and they do not have an exemption from meeting their work obligations you may need to initiate an obligations failure.
For more information see:
- Work or work preparation obligations
- Obligations failures
- In approved study before subject to work obligations
## Partner engaged in full-time study
If a partner is engaged in full time study and does not meet the criteria for an exemption they can apply for a Student Allowance. If they are qualified for a Student Allowance the client can be included in the Student Allowance when:
- they are legally married, in a civil union or de facto relationship and
- both are aged 24 years or more or
- they have a dependent child
Where the client cannot be included, the partner will be regarded as single and will receive the single rate of Student Allowance.
For Jobseeker Support Student Hardship purposes we still regard them as a married, civil union or de facto couple. You will need to charge the student allowance against the married, civil union or de facto rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and pay the client half of the abated benefit.
Because the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and Student Allowance rules are different in this situation there are particular procedures to follow. There is a flowchart to help you, see:
- Couple under 24 years - partner not granted an exemption in non approved study flowchart

chunks.title: Partner meeting their work obligation requirements — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Partner meeting their work obligation requirements
A client who is a partner of someone receiving Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue to be paid a benefit while they are absent from New Zealand for any reason:
- when they are meeting their work obligations by being in paid employment and
- the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet these work obligations (eg during a period of annual leave from employment)
## Examples (but not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
Partner of a person receiving Jobseeker Support Student Hardship with part-time work obligations is in employment for 22 hours per week. They have taken annual leave from their employment to travel to Australia.
The client is already meeting their part-time work obligations by being in suitable employment of over 20 hours per week. Their benefit will continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand.
A Jobseeker Support Student Hardship couple go overseas on holiday. The partner is meeting their obligations by working part-time for 24 hours per week. The holiday is taken while the partner is on annual leave.
The primary job seeker cannot continue to be paid while overseas on a holiday.
The partner is already meeting their part-time work obligations by being in suitable employment of over 20 hours per week. The partners share of the benefit will continue to be paid for up to 28 days in a 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand.
The full rate of accommodation supplement can continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand.

chunks.title: Partner with work obligations — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Partner with work obligations
A partner cannot continue getting their Jobseeker Student Hardship Support payments when they temporarily leave New Zealand if they have work obligations unless they meet the criteria for approved travel.
Where they meet the criteria for approved travel they can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period if:
- the benefit would continue to be paid except for them having left New Zealand
- they have notified the Ministry of Social Development of their intention to temporarily leave New Zealand
For more information see:
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption
- Partner meeting their work obligation requirements
- Partner with an exemption from their work obligations
- Approved travel reasons

chunks.title: Partners of a main beneficiary who have youth activity obligations — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Partners of a main beneficiary who have youth activity obligations can be absent from New Zealand for any reason and continue to receive their payment, if the absence does not prevent the young person from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations. This is limited to up to 28 days within any 52 week period.

chunks.title: Client may be sanctioned — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: If the young person travels overseas at a time when they are required to be in New Zealand to meet their youth activity obligations, and they don't have a good and sufficient reason for not meeting these, an obligations failure will apply and a sanction may be imposed. Generally if a young person is required to be overseas due to a situation that is covered by the permitted reasons, they would be considered to have a good and sufficient reason for not meeting their youth activity obligations and so would not be failed. For more information see: - Permitted travel reasons Note the Youth Service Support Unit will make a decision on whether to initiate the sanction process based on a recommendation from the young person's service provider.

chunks.title: Examples (but are not limited to) — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Client situation Outcome A young partner is meeting their education obligation by attending secondary school and they wish to travel to Australia during the school holiday period. The client is not required by their Service Provider to undertake a parenting or budgeting course or attend any meetings with them during the period they wish to travel. The travel will not prevent the young partner from meeting any of their youth activity obligations. Therefore, the young person can be absent from New Zealand for this reason and continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period. A young partner is meeting their education obligation by participating in a full time training course and decides to take time off from the course in the middle of the term so that they can holiday in Australia. The young person will be advised that they would be failing their activity obligations if they are absent from New Zealand for this reason and therefore their payments may be sanctioned. The young person can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they were absent from New Zealand if they meet one of the other permitted travel reasons. A young partner is enrolled in a full-time training course. The course has not yet started. The young person wishes to travel before the school/course commencement date. The young person is meeting their education obligation. As long as the travel will not prevent the client from meeting any of their other youth activity obligations (for example, their budgeting and parenting obligations) they can continue to receive their payment for up to 28 days in any 52 week period while they are absent from New Zealand. For more information see: - Young partner not yet subject to obligation to be in education, training or work-based learning - Young partners who are exempt from their Youth Activity Obligations - Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days for an approved reason - Obligations failures

chunks.title: Maximum amount payable — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Maximum amount payable
You can pay a rate higher than the hospital rate up to the maximum rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship that would otherwise be payable.

chunks.title: Paying benefit when client failed to advise of absence — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Paying benefit when client failed to advise of absence
Generally, clients receiving a main benefit must advise Work and Income of their intention to leave New Zealand prior to their departure to be eligible to continue to receive their payments.
If a client contacts Work and Income after they have left New Zealand, their benefit can only be resumed from:
- the date that they notified us of their absence and
- only if the travel is allowed
## Backdating benefit to departure date (while still absent from New Zealand)
Where a client does not advise Work and Income of their intention to travel overseas before they leave New Zealand their benefit may be backdated to their departure date if they:
- have a humanitarian reason that justifies their reason for travel and their failure to tell Work and Income before they left and
- contacted Work and Income as soon as reasonably possible after they departed (taking into account the circumstances of the client) and
- meet the criteria to continue to be paid their benefit while overseas (either because they meet the criteria for approved travel, or the requirement that travel be approved does not apply to them)
Note this only applies if a client has contacted Work and Income while overseas. Payments cannot be back dated if the client advises Work and Income once they return from overseas.
For more information see:
- Approved travel reasons
- Humanitarian reasons for backdating to day after departure
- Client with work obligations, exemption or deferral
- Partner with work or work preparation obligations or an exemption

chunks.title: Benefit can be backdated once back in New Zealand in very limited circumstances — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Benefit can be backdated once back in New Zealand in very limited circumstances
A client who is continuing to be paid while they are absent from New Zealand for an approved reason may be able to have their benefit backdated if there is an unforeseen reason they cannot notify Work and Income while they are overseas.
For example, a client boards a plane to return home on schedule and the plane is held up due to fog. There is no way the client could notify Work and Income due to an event outside of their control. When the client contacts Work and Income once they are back in New Zealand, their benefit would be resumed from the original date they were due to return (this will be on the boarding pass and/or in the custom tab in WASP).
For more information see:
- Overseas medical treatment
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes

chunks.title: Paying for more than 28 days - receive support from family overseas (young partner) — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Generally, a benefit cannot be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period while the client is absent from New Zealand. However, there are limited circumstances where a benefit can be paid for more than 28 days in a 52 week period where the young partner is travelling to receive support from a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family) who is residing overseas. For more information see: - Definition of 'support' from a family member residing overseas This applies (and is limited to a further 28 days in any 52 week period) when: - the young partner has already been paid a benefit while absent from New Zealand for one or more approved reasons for all or most of 28 days in a 52 week period and - the young partner will be absent from New Zealand for the purpose of obtaining support from a family member residing overseas and - the support that the young partner needs cannot reasonably be provided to the client by one of their family members in New Zealand and - the absence does not prevent the young partner from meeting their youth activity obligations because the absence is at a time when: they are not required to attend education, training or work-based learning (for example, they are exempt from meeting their obligationsthey are not yet required to be undertaking education, training or work-based learning because of the age of their youngest child orthey are undertaking education or training but it is semester or term break or they are between academic years) or the course has not yet started andthey are not required to be in New Zealand to meet any of their other obligations during the time of the absence (eg they do not need to attend a parenting or budgeting course during the time they will be overseas) - they are not required to attend education, training or work-based learning (for example, they are exempt from meeting their obligations - they are not yet required to be undertaking education, training or work-based learning because of the age of their youngest child or - they are undertaking education or training but it is semester or term break or they are between academic years) or the course has not yet started and - they are not required to be in New Zealand to meet any of their other obligations during the time of the absence (eg they do not need to attend a parenting or budgeting course during the time they will be overseas)

chunks.title: Cannot be paid for more than 28 days for purposes of obtaining support — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: The maximum amount of time that a young partner can continue to receive their payment while overseas on the grounds that the absence does not prevent them meeting their obligations is 28 days in any 52 week period. Therefore, if a client subject to youth activity obligations has already received their payment for 28 days while they were overseas on a holiday on the grounds that the travel did not prevent them meeting their obligations, they will not be able to travel and continue to receive their payment under the 'obtaining support from a family member' circumstance. For more information see: - Examples of paying for more than 28 days for obtaining family support for young partners

chunks.title: Payment to partners — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Payment to partners
When a client with a partner (with no dependent children) has their Jobseeker Support Student Hardship reduced to the hospital rate, their partner in the community from the same date can:
- have their portion of benefit or pension increased by the difference between the maximum half married, civil union or de facto rate and the single rate of that benefit or pension and
- receive a Special Disability Allowance
Note couples with dependent children do not have their rate reduced to the hospital rate.
## Charging income
You need to charge any income the couple gets against the married, civil union or de facto rate before you can determine the amount to pay.
The partner in the community will get the half married, civil union or de facto rate (after charging income) plus the difference between the maximum married, civil union or de facto rate and the single rate.
The client in hospital will get the lesser of the:
- half married, civil union or de facto rate (after charging income) or
- hospital rate of payment
For more information see:
- Payment
- Special Disability Allowance

chunks.title: Payment when client or partner absent from New Zealand — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Payment when client or partner absent from New Zealand
There are some situations where the benefit payments will be affected when the client is absent from New Zealand. The action required by Work and Income will depend on the reason the client is absent from New Zealand and whether they are continuing to be paid a benefit.
For more information see:
- Client or partner remains in New Zealand
- Ending payment for partner who can travel for any reason
- Ending payment for client who needs an approved reason for travel
- Client left New Zealand and reason for travel changes (within 28 day maximum)
- Client not returned due to an unforeseeable event (within 28 day maximum)
- Child absent

chunks.title: Period over which to charge income — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Period over which to charge income
Income must be charged against the benefit for the week that it is earned or the period it represents for example:
- a client gets interest payments from their term deposit once every 6 months. This represents the interest earned over the previous 6 months: MSD will charge this payment against their benefit over the previous 6 months that the payment representsif it is an ongoing investment the payment amount will also be added as ongoing estimated income for the next 6 months
- MSD will charge this payment against their benefit over the previous 6 months that the payment represents
- if it is an ongoing investment the payment amount will also be added as ongoing estimated income for the next 6 months
- a client works 13 hours every week and gets paid fortnightly. MSD will charge their fortnightly income for each week the wages represent
- a client works 2 days a week and gets paid their wages weekly. MSD will charge their income for the week that it is earned
- a sole trader who mows lawns invoices their customers monthly. MSD will charge their net profit before tax as income for the actual period it represents
If income does not represent a specific period or if MSD cannot determine the actual period it represents, MSD must determine the most appropriate period to charge the income. This may be the week it is received, provided or supplied.
In most cases, determining the period will be straightforward. If you are unable to determine the period that the income represents you should discuss the payment with Helpline.
Note sole parents whose Jobseeker Support Student Hardship commenced before 1 July 2025 may be able to have their income charged annually.
For more information see:
- Sole parents whose benefit commenced before 1 July 2025
For more information on specific types of income and how to charge them, see:
- Types of income
## Overlapping income
If a client has income from multiple sources that are paid for the same periods of time, then all of the payments are added together.
The total income will be charged against the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship over the period that the income represents.

chunks.title: Permanent absence — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence
If a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, Jobseeker Support Student Hardship must be cancelled from the day after departure.
## Moving to Australia
If the client is moving to Australia it is important that they are aware that they may not be able to receive a benefit until they have resided in Australia for two years after being granted permanent residence status.
For more information see:
- United Kingdom Reciprocal Agreement Jobseekers Allowance
- Australian Reciprocal Agreement Clients going to Australia
- To or from overseas Payments from overseas

chunks.title: Evidence of the client's situation — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Evidence of the client's situation
Although it may not be possible for the client to get proof of their situation, they should make a reasonable effort to do so.
For more information see:
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- Definition of family member
- Essential travel
- Job interviews or follow up on a job prospect
- Absences that do not prevent partner from meeting obligations

chunks.title: Example — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Example
A client's partner phones on Thursday 05/05/2022 to advise that they worked for the week Monday 14/02/2022 to Friday 18/02/2022 and earned $195.54 gross.
Manually assess the income deduction:
Gross income (excluding cents)
$195.00
Less income allowed before benefit is affected
$160.00
Equals income
$35.00
Amount benefit reduced on account of income (income over $160 reduces benefit by 70 cents per $1.00)
($35 x 0.7)
$24.50
To work out the benefit rate payable:
Maximum benefit couple rate (as at 1 July 2021)
$453.62
Less reduction due to income
$24.50
Benefit rate payable
$429.12
($214.56 each)
Once you have calculated the benefit due for this week add the income to INCMA. A backdated review SBDR for both the client and their partner needs to be completed for this week.
The following is the process:
SBDR
$214.56 for the week income earned 14/02/2022 to 18/02/2022
LSUM
a memo will be produced as a result of the backdated review with details of the debt amount to be added into the appropriate tax year. It is the net amount of debt which is added to SWIFTT
SDBTI
debt inquiry for the client (F4 for STAXI)
STAXI
select the appropriate year and DBT which will take you into the SDBTA screen
SDBTA
add the debt type, add the benefit/pension code, add the debt status and breach type, add the net debt amount. This will also adjust the tax record for the client. Add the period that the debt represents and add any comments where appropriate - remember to commence recovery of the debt via SOFSI

chunks.title: Priority for deductions — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Priority for deductions
Certain forms of deductions take priority over others; the following list gives the order of priority, highest to lowest:
Highest priority
- Child Support deductions made under the Child Support Act 1991
- Inland Revenue tax deductions
- Ministry of Social Development debt repayments including Liable Parent Contributions (LPC), child maintenance debts and Major Repairs Advances (MRA), Student Allowance debt, Student Loan debt converted to Ministry of Social Development debt, Income Related Rent historical Kāinga Ora debt, Income Related Rent Ministry of Social Development debt
- Attachment orders made under the Family Proceedings Act 1980
- Court attachment orders issued under the Summary Proceedings Act 1957
- Court attachment orders issued under the District Court Act 2016
- Student Loan repayments
Lowest priority
Determining the priority of deductions is necessary where a client has more than one order issued in respect of their benefit. Also each order and deduction notice is subject to its own protected earnings rule.
When you need to reduce deductions you adjust from the lowest priority up to those with a higher priority taking into account the protected earnings rules for each.

chunks.title: Private hospital and homes — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Private hospital and homes
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can be paid at the full rate regardless of the period of hospitalisation when a client is:
- admitted to a private hospital or
- admitted to a private home that provides residential care disability services
If the client receives Extra Help, this will need to be reviewed to see if their costs are continuing.
For more information see:
- Residential Care Subsidy
- Residential Support Subsidy

chunks.title: Protected earnings rate — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Protected earnings rate
Both the District Court Act and the Summary Proceedings Act provide that every Ministry of Justice attachment order must specify a 'protected earnings rate'.
If the attachment order will reduce the client's income below the protected earnings rate, then the order will not operate and you must cancel or return the attachment order to the Ministry of Justice.
Calculating the client's income differs between attachment orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act and the District Court Act, as different benefits are taken into account. Therefore it is important to determine what type of attachment order has been issued.
Summary Proceedings Act 1957
For orders made under the Summary Proceedings Act , the calculation of the client's income does not include Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support, Disability Allowance, Child Disability Allowance, Winter Energy Payment, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit
District Court Act 2016
For orders made under the District Court Act, the client's income includes Special Benefit, Temporary Additional Support and Disability Allowance but does not include Child Disability Allowance, Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit
## Example
An attachment order is received from the Ministry of Justice for $50.00 per week. The order lists the protected income as $280 per week:
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship single 25+ rate (as at 1 July 2021)
$278.50
Plus Accommodation Supplement (Area 2)
$105.00
Total income
$383.50
Less Child Support deduction
$25.00
$358.50
Less Ministry of Social Development debts
$40.00
Sub total
$318.50
Less Court Order
$50.00
Total
$268.50
The court order takes the client's income to $268.50, this is below the protected income rate of $280 per week. The attachment order will not operate, you must return it to the Ministry of Justice for the order to be amended.

chunks.title: Qualifies for another benefit — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Qualifies for another benefit
A client may qualify for another benefit due to a change in their circumstances. It is also important to determine if the client still qualifies for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
For example:
- if a client is aged under 19 years old and they apply to have a child included in their benefit, they would no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and they would need to apply for Young Parent Payment or
- a client reaches the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation
If the client qualifies for more than one benefit they must be told which benefit is the most beneficial for their particular circumstances. You will need to advise them of:
- benefit rates
- the effect of any income they may receive (income reduction and any exemptions) and
- benefit obligations
The client must make the final decision on which benefit they receive after being given all relevant information.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship Qualifications
- Sole Parent Support Qualifications
- Supported Living payment Qualifications
- Young Parent Payment Qualifications
- New Zealand Superannuation Qualifications
- Processing standards Client transfers to another benefit type [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Rate of payment - sole parents — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Rate of payment - sole parents
If payment of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is to continue while a sole parent client is in prison, you will need to determine the rate to pay to the temporary caregiver.
The Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should generally be paid at the equivalent rate of Unsupported Child's Benefit that would be payable if the caregiver qualified for this, see: Examples - sole parents
However, there is discretion to continue payment at the full sole parent rate.
You can consider including the following costs to calculate the rate to pay the temporary caregiver while the client is in prison:
- rent or outgoings if the children are being cared for in the client's home
- the client's other commitments if these costs are for essential items and they cannot be suspended, such as Child Support payments (where the client does not qualify for an exemption) or hire purchase for an essential item
The total amount paid to the temporary caregiver must not exceed the maximum amount of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship payable.
## SWIFTT
The Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and family tax credit should continue in the client's name and be paid to the caregiver as an agent in SWIFTT.
When the temporary caregiver is to be paid less than the maximum rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, you will need to add this as a non-standard rate using the SNSRA screen in SWIFTT.
For more information see:
- Examples - sole parents
- Decision guidelines - sole parents
- Sole parents

chunks.title: Reapplying for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Reapplying for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship
When a client reapplies for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship after ceasing employment, the length of time that they have been working will affect the date that their Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can recommence.
## In employment less than 26 weeks
If the client stops full-time work and reapplies for benefit within 26 weeks of their previous benefit stopping, they will need to complete a Re-application (within 52 weeks) form (M26).
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can be recommenced from the day after the employment ceased or the application date of benefit whichever is the later.
## In employment 26 weeks or more
If the client stops full-time work 26 weeks or more after their previous benefit ceased you will need to treat them as a new applicant for benefit. The client will need to complete an application form. An initial stand-down calculation will need to be completed and imposed if necessary.
For more information see:
- Temporary employment
- Voluntary unemployment or dismissal for misconduct
- No stand-down applies

chunks.title: Gets a Student Loan — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Gets a Student Loan
Getting a Student Loan (including the living cost component) does not mean the child is financially independent.
If the child continues to be the client's primary responsibility and maintained as a member of their family and financially dependent (that is the parent is meeting some of the costs for the child) the child can continue to be included in the benefit until the start of the pay period following:
- the date they turn 18 or
- when the child is 18 years old and continuing in education, the earlier of: the date they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education orthe date the child is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required orthe date the child is financially independent orthe date the child leaves the parent or caregiver's care or31 December of the year they turn 18
- the date they are no longer enrolled in school or tertiary education or
- the date the child is no longer attending school or tertiary education as required or
- the date the child is financially independent or
- the date the child leaves the parent or caregiver's care or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
Note a parent or caregiver getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship must complete a review of circumstances when a dependent child turns 18, and when the child is excluded (if they continued to be included in the parent or caregiver's benefit after the child turned 18).

chunks.title: Recording income — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Recording income
Any income a client receives, even when the income is less than $160.00 gross per week, must be added to the client's SWIFTT record on the INCMA screen. This is to ensure any Extra help is reviewed correctly and will create a permanent audit trail of all income details.
If the income is over the benefit cut out point and SWIFTT will not accept this information then a note on CMS should be added.
Ensure the following details are recorded:
- source of income, such as the employer's details
- gross (before tax) amount of income received
- period that the income represents and
- contact details for example phoned in by the client

chunks.title: Release from prison — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Release from prison
A client may be entitled to Jobseeker Support Student Hardship when they are released from prison. The date to recommence payment depends on the length of time the client has been in prison.
## Partner
Where the partner of a person in prison has been receiving a benefit, this will need to be reviewed from the date of release.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship Prisoners

chunks.title: Release on bail — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Release on bail
When a client is released on bail, Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can be paid from the date of release providing the client:
- is still able to meet their work obligations
- has been in custody for less than 31 days and
- reapplies for a benefit immediately after their release
If the client has been in custody for more than 31 days an initial stand-down will be imposed.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship Prisoners
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship Court imposed conditions

chunks.title: Remanded in custody — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Remanded in custody
Generally, when a client is remanded in custody awaiting a further court appearance their benefit should be stopped. However, there is discretion to continue payment of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship after taking the client's financial circumstances and commitments into account.
When deciding whether to continue paying Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for the period for a particular client, consider the following:
- has the client been remanded pending a further court hearing or for sentencing
- does the client have continuing costs that cannot be avoided, such as rent and hire purchase for essential items
- does the client have a partner and or dependent children
Every situation should be considered on a case-by-case basis.
For help contact Helpline to discuss the circumstances before making a decision.

chunks.title: Partner — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Partner
Where the partner of a person in prison has been receiving a benefit, this will need to be reviewed from the date of release.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship Court imposed conditions
- Special Needs Grants Steps to Freedom

chunks.title: Season ends — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Season ends
When the client ceases work at the end of the season they need to re-enrol as a job seeker with Work and Income and reapply for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
For more information see:
- Commencement date
- Reapplying for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship

chunks.title: Seasonal work — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Seasonal work
If a primary client commences full-time seasonal work they will no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
If the client has a partner who meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship in their own right, the partner can apply for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship as the primary client.
## Partner
If the person who has commenced seasonal work (either part-time or full-time) is the partner, then the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue with their earnings being charged as income against the benefit.
This is regardless of whether the partner has work obligations.
Note if the partner has full-time work obligations and is working 30 hours per week, or has part-time work obligations and is working 20 hours or more, then they will be meeting their work obligations.
For more information see:
- Assistance during seasonal work
- Season ends
- Employment related income
- Charging income
- Job search requirements

chunks.title: Full-time self-employment — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Full-time self-employment
If a primary client commences full-time self-employment (even if there is no or minimum income being earned) they will no longer qualify for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
If the client has a partner who meets the qualifications for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship in their own right, the partner can apply for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship as the primary client.
## Part-time self-employment
If a primary client starts part-time self-employment they may still be able to get Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, as long as they continue to meet their job search requirements. Any offer of suitable employment takes precedence over any part- time activity or self-employment that does not meet their work obligations.
For more information see:
- Suitable employment
## Partner
If the person who has commenced self-employment (either part-time or full-time) is the partner, then the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship can continue with their earnings being charged as income against the benefit.
This is regardless of whether the partner has work obligations.
Note if the partner has full-time work obligations and is working 30 hours per week, or has part-time work obligations and is working 20 hours or more, then they must be receiving an income from this employment to be meeting their work obligations. If they are not receiving any income from the self-employment they must still be available for and actively seeking suitable employment.

chunks.title: Single clients — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Single clients
Generally the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should be suspended when a single client is imprisoned. This will enable payment to be resumed if the client is only in prison for a short period and reapplies for a benefit following their release.
The Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should be suspended from the day after imprisonment.
Note SWIFTT will automatically cancel the record if it remains suspended for 8 weeks.
## Exception
Remanded in custody
Although the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should generally be stopped for any period during which the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance, there is discretion to continue payment of all or part of the benefit.
For more information see:
- Remanded in custody

chunks.title: Sole Parents — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Sole Parents
When a sole parent client is admitted to hospital, their benefit can continue at the full rate for the first 13 weeks.
You will need to find out who is caring for the client's child and the length of time the client is likely to be in hospital. If requested, you can pay part of the benefit to the child's caregiver to cover the cost of alternative care or accommodation.
When the child is not going to remain in the care of the client, check what the continuing care arrangements are for the child. If the child is no longer a dependent child you will need to exclude the child and review the client's Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
## Family tax credit
As long as the child continues to be a dependent child, family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments continue to be paid while the client is in hospital.
Best Start tax credit stops when the child turns three even if the client is in hospital.
For more information see:
- Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit qualifications
- Agents
- Date payment should be reduced
- Effect on Extra Help
- On leave from hospital
- Discharge from hospital
- Best Start tax credit Child turns 3

chunks.title: Sole parents — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Sole parents
When a sole parent client is imprisoned they will no longer be entitled to Jobseeker Support Student Hardship.
The Jobseeker Support Student Hardship should be suspended from the day after imprisonment.
You may need to find out who is caring for the client's children and the length of time the client is likely to be in prison. The length of the time in prison can be obtained by contacting the prison liaison officer at the Department of Corrections.
Generally, the caregiver will need to apply for financial assistance in their own right.
They may be entitled to:
- have the children included as dependent children in their current benefit
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Emergency Benefit Single and caring for a child or
- family tax credit and Best Start tax credit through Inland Revenue
## Exception
There is discretion to pay all or part of the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship to a temporary caregiver caring for the client's children.
There is also discretion to continue payment if the client is remanded in custody pending a further court appearance.
For more information see:
- Decision guidelines - sole parents
- Rate of payment - sole parents
- Examples - sole parents
- Remanded in custody

chunks.title: Special Disability Allowance — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Special Disability Allowance
A Special Disability Allowance is paid to the partner of a client who is receiving the hospital rate. It is paid to the person not in hospital to help with the extra costs of their partner's hospitalisation, for example travel costs to visit the patient.
Note that Special Disability Allowance is:
- granted without the client having to apply
- paid separately from Disability Allowance and
- not income or asset tested
Special Disability Allowance can start from when the partner's rate of benefit is increased to the single rate (and the patient's benefit is reduced to the hospital rate).
For more information see:
- Deskfile Special Disability Allowance rates
Special Disability Allowance should be stopped from the first available date if the person receiving it is also admitted to hospital.
## SWIFTT
Grant Special Disability Allowance using code 838 on the SSUPI screen.

chunks.title: Split care — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Split care
Split care is when parents with two or more children are living apart and each parent has the care of at least one of their children on a full-time basis.
The child(ren) that is living with the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client can be included as a dependent child.
Note that in split care situations, generally only one parent can receive Sole Parent Support. The other parent must qualify, in their own right, for another benefit.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support Split care

chunks.title: Student Loans — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Student Loans
Clients with a Student Loan must make repayments to Inland Revenue when the income they receive exceeds a pre-determined level. This level is called the 'income threshold'.
A person must make repayments to Inland Revenue when their income exceeds $464 gross per week ($24,128 gross per year) as at 1 April 2026. Note non-taxable Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit and Accommodation Supplement do not count as income in this instance.
If the client's income is over this income threshold, the Ministry of Social Development can make the required deduction. However, this is only done if the client requests it.
If the client's portion of benefit is below the income threshold, there is no provision to make voluntary repayments through SWIFTT. The client can make voluntary payments direct to Inland Revenue at any time.
Note the following:
- Student Loan deductions can only be made from taxable benefits
- Student Loan deductions cannot be made if the client's benefit is below the income threshold
- when a client receives a married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit only the client's portion is taken into consideration when assessing Student Loan repayments
- when a client is receiving a reduced rate of payment due to other income, the Student Loan deduction is assessed on the net payment after income deduction
## For more information on Student Loans see:
- Students Student Loans

chunks.title: Study — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Study
Clients (and partners) have an obligation to advise Work and Income of any change in their circumstances that may affect their qualification for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship, such as commencing study.
When Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client intends to or has commenced study, you will need to find out:
- the date study starts and
- the type of study, that is part-time or full-time
This will help you decide the appropriate review action required.
For more information see:
- Client engaged in study
- Partner engaged in study
- In approved study before subject to work obligations

chunks.title: Debt Repayment Orders — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Debt Repayment Orders
All Debt Repayment Orders are sent directly to the Central Processing Unit for processing.
Debt Repayment Orders are issued by the Ministry of Justice under the Insolvency Act 2006 and can be issued when the client is an un-discharged bankrupt.
Unlike other Ministry of Justice attachment orders, Debt Repayment Orders are not subject to any protected earnings rate. Payment is generally made to the supervisor of the debt but occasionally the District Court will act as an agent for collection of the debt.
Payment continues for 3 years or until further notice is received from either the supervisor or the District Court.
Unlike District Court attachment orders, Debt Repayment Orders are administered via the PYECI screen in SWIFTT, not through CORBI.

chunks.title: SWIFTT process to pay a partner — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT process to pay a partner
When you decide to continue payment of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship to the partner of a client who has been imprisoned, you will need to determine the most appropriate SWIFTT process to enable payment to be made to the partner.
The process for payment will depend on whether the:
- period in prison is in the past
- client is due to be released from prison shortly
- client is likely to be in prison for more than 4 weeks and
- rate of payment for the partner
Note that there is discretion to pay the full married, civil union or de facto rate of benefit.
## Period in prison has passed or release is imminent
Generally you should use the SBDR screen in SWIFTT to:
- suspend the client's portion of the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for the period in prison
and
- pay the appropriate rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship to the partner
## Period in prison exceeds 4 weeks
When the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is to continue, and be paid to the partner you will need to contact Helpline for advice regarding the SWIFTT process to use.
For more information contact Helpline or see:
- Decision guidelines - clients with a partner

chunks.title: Tax codes — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Tax codes
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is taxed at the 'M' rate.
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is always considered the client's primary source of income regardless of the amount paid.
If the client has other income this is always considered the client's secondary income. Clients can apply to Inland Revenue for a tailored tax code for other income.

chunks.title: Taxation — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Taxation
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is a taxable benefit. MSD makes payments to clients at the net rate after the deduction of tax. MSD passes the tax on to Inland Revenue.
Generally, MSD will request clients to give MSD their IRD number or evidence of their IRD number.

chunks.title: Extra assistance during temporary care — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Extra assistance during temporary care
Any assistance for additional costs due to temporary care situations should be met, in the first instance, by the custodial parent. Where this is not available, you can consider Special Needs Grants assistance for the client.
For more information see:
- Extra help Special Needs Grants

chunks.title: Terminal benefit for a single client — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit for a single client
Generally the Jobseeker Support Student Hardship stops from the date after the date of death for a single client with no children, however, there is some discretion to continue the payment of benefit for up to 28 days. When payment is continued after the date of death, it is referred to as terminal benefit.
Circumstances where you might consider continued payment beyond a single client's date of death include:
- when the deceased client's domestic situation results in a transition cost for a family member, causing hardship
Example: accommodation and other household costs when client has been sharing accommodation
or
- when there are exceptional and justified costs associated with the death of the client
Example: multiple deaths within one family
You should not continue payment for 28 days following the death of a single client to meet funeral expenses. A Funeral Grant is available for this purpose.
## SWIFTT
If you are paying terminal benefit for a single client you will need to manually calculate entitlement and make an adhoc payment.
There is no automatic provision for the payment of terminal benefit (for a single client) on SWIFTT.
Wherever possible you should enter the next of kin or the executor of the deceased's estate on SWIFTT.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit payments to surviving person, or person caring for the children — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Terminal benefit payments to surviving person, or person caring for the children
Terminal benefit is paid for 28 days when a client dies and has a surviving partner or children.

chunks.title: Terminal benefit rate — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: The provision to continue the benefit payment for 28 days following the date of death is referred to as terminal benefit. Benefit payment is continued at the rate which was payable to the client and partner (if any) at the date of death. A terminal benefit includes extra help being paid (for up to 28 days following the date of death), but does not include family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments.

chunks.title: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments do not form part of terminal benefit. If the deceased client was getting these payments and there is a surviving partner, transfer family tax credit and Best Start tax credit payments to the partner.

chunks.title: Benefit paid at a reduced rate — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: When the client's benefit was paid at a reduced rate at the date of death, the terminal benefit is also paid at the reduced rate. Benefit payments may have been reduced due to: - hospitalisationThe deceased client's benefit was reduced as they were in hospital for more than 13 weeks. - income - debt repayments when there are benefit arrears due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit paymentdo not recover debts, in full, from terminal benefit payments - when there are benefit arrears due at the date of death attempt to recover the debt payment in full from the final benefit payment - do not recover debts, in full, from terminal benefit payments - Child Support if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenuewhen a surviving partner or family member makes enquires, refer them to Inland Revenue - if a client had an information share Child Support payment being charged as income at their date of death, they may have been getting a reduced rate of benefit. The effect of the income charge for the information share Child Support will continue for the duration of the terminal benefit, as the rate payable cannot be reviewed - Child Support liability ends when the liable person dies; however MSD cannot remove a Child Support deduction from a benefit record without the authorisation of Inland Revenue - when a surviving partner or family member makes enquires, refer them to Inland Revenue - redirection of payment to Kāinga Ora or a community housing provider when the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. For more information see: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client - when the accommodation is being retained by a surviving partner or family member, continue the redirection to Kāinga Ora or the community housing provider. For more information see: Social housing, Assessment of eligibility Death of a client - court attachment orders

chunks.title: Benefit paid at a reduced rate — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text: Note all of the above deductions will continue to be made from the terminal benefit payments unless they are manually stopped before cancellation.

chunks.title: Treatment of income — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Treatment of income
When a client (or their partner) is receiving Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and declares any income you need to:
- determine the source and the amount of income
- the family circumstances of the client
- check the client still qualifies for the and meets the job search requirements
- check the client's income is below the cut-out point
- check the period over which to charge income
- check the client is still entitled to receive family tax credit and Best Start tax credit
- review the rate of payment, see Income test and Income change
- review any Extra help Effect of income on Extra help
- check any Exemption for severe disablement
For information on how to charge specific types of income for example, Accident Compensation Payments, see: Types of income
When a client (or their partner) advises that they have commenced employment, you will need to find out more specific information about their employment see: Changes and reviews Employment

chunks.title: Underpaid — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Underpaid
When a client has been underpaid Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and is owed arrears, MSD will work out the amount of tax and pass this on to Inland Revenue.
From 1 April 2024, if an arrears payment relates to a previous tax year, the arrears will not be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment. This means the client will not have to pay any more tax on the payment.
Only arrears payments relating to the current tax year will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment.
Example
A client is paid arrears on 12 June 2026. This payment represents arrears for 25 March 2026 to 8 June 2026.
The arrears for 25 March to 31 March 2026 represent a past tax year, so they will not be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment. The arrears for 1 April to 8 June 2026 represent the current tax year, so they will be included in the client's end-of-year tax assessment.

chunks.title: Voluntary Work — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Voluntary Work
A Jobseeker Support Student Hardship client or their partner may elect to participate in voluntary work to obtain work experience.
This is an acceptable activity however it should not take precedence over the primary client's availability for paid work.
When clients in receipt of a work obligated benefit engage in one of these activities it is essential that they continue to meet their job search requirements and obligations.
It is not sufficient to only be available for work. There is also the requirement to be actively seeking work.
Clients can undertake voluntary work while continuing to meet the job search requirements and obligations of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship. Each case has to be considered on its merits, but if the part-time 'non' job search activity reaches in excess of 12 to 15 hours per week, there should be careful scrutiny of the person's benefit eligibility.
A client's part-time voluntary work must allow enough time for them to actively seek work as required by their job search requirements.
For more information see:
- Job search requirements

chunks.title: Weekend leave — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Weekend leave
Jobseeker Support Student Hardship is paid for a seven day period, covering Monday to Sunday. Therefore, where the client is receiving the hospital rate and is on weekend leave you should pay the appropriate full rate of benefit for the number of days they are on weekend leave and subsequently incurring additional expenses in the community.
Note the dates of admission and discharge are not regarded as days spent in hospital.
## Example
If the client is on leave from Friday to Monday, you will need to pay the appropriate full rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for 4 days. Generally, you will do this by completing a back dated review so that SWIFTT will pay the appropriate full rate of Jobseeker Support Student Hardship for 4 days.

chunks.title: Example (but not limited to) — jobseeker support student hardship > changes and reviews jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Example (but not limited to)
Client situation
Outcome
A young person who is not yet subject to the education obligation as their youngest dependent child is less than 12 months (and there is no Teen Parent Unit place available for them) wishes to holiday in Australia.
As long as the travel will not prevent the young person from meeting their other obligations (eg their parenting and budgeting obligations) they can continue to be paid for up to 28 days in any 52 week period.
For more information see:
- Young partners who are exempt from their youth activity obligations
- Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days for an approved reason

chunks.title: Charging income — jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Charging income
A client (and their partner, if any) getting Jobseeker Support Student Hardship have their income assessed and charged weekly.
MSD must charge income for the period it is earned or relates to.
If a payment does not represent a specific period or if MSD cannot determine the actual period it represents, MSD must determine the most appropriate period to charge the income. This may be the week it is received, provided or supplied.
When a client declares any income MSD must:
- determine the source and the amount of income
- check the client still qualifies for Jobseeker Support Student Hardship and meets the job search requirements
- check if the client qualifies for Family Tax Credit or Best Start tax credit
## Single clients and couples
Clients whose weekly income is over $160 gross per week will have their benefit reduced by 70 cents for every $1.00 of income that is over that amount per week.
If a client is getting a half-married rate of benefit because their partner is:
- granted a main benefit in their own right or
- not entitled to get a benefit because they have a 13 week non-entitlement period, are subject to an obligations failure, or they are on strike
Then, their benefit will be reduced by 35 cents for every $1.00 of the total combined income that is over $160 gross per week.
For more information see:
- Charging income example - single clients and couples
## Sole parents
Sole parent clients whose weekly income is over $160 gross per week will have their benefit reduced by:
- 30 cents for each $1.00 of income that is between $160 and $250 gross per week
- 70 cents for every $1.00 of income that is more than $250 gross per week.
Note sole parents whose Jobseeker Support Student Hardship commenced before 1 July 2025 may be able to have their income charged annually.
For more information see:
- Sole parents whose benefit commenced before 1 July 2025
- Charging income example – sole parents
## Childcare costs income exemption
If a sole parent has to pay childcare costs because they are working, they can get an income exemption.
For more information see:
- Childcare cost income exemption - sole parents
## Income from overseas pensions
Income from overseas pensions is generally treated as a direct deduction from the benefit rate. This has a separate calculation to charging other types of income.

chunks.title: Child changes and social obligations — jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Child changes and social obligations
Sometimes a client will have a change in circumstances that may mean the client is no longer required to comply with their social obligations. This includes where:
- a dependent child changes age and the social obligation that applied for the dependent child in their care is no longer relevant or
- child leaves care (for example starts to live with another parent or caregiver or goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki)
For more information see:
- Changes and reviews Child changes
- Clients situation changes during regular engagement and support process

chunks.title: Deciding if a child is financially dependent — jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Deciding if a child is financially dependent
When a client states they are receiving payments for a child's expenses you must decide if the child is a dependent child of the client.
A child does not have to be solely financially dependent on a client to be considered a dependent child. All that is required is that the child is financially dependent on the person to some degree.
However, being financially dependent on a client is only part of the qualifications of a dependent child. The child must still meet all the qualifications to be considered dependent.
If another person or body is paying for the child's expenses, including payments for the care provided, the child is not financially dependent on the client.
If a client is receiving payments toward the expenses of a dependent child this is regarded as income for benefit purposes.

chunks.title: Childcare cost income exemption - sole parents — jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Childcare cost income exemption - sole parents
There is an additional $20 per week income exemption for a sole parent who is receiving Jobseeker Support Student Hardship when they have to pay childcare costs while they are working.
It is not necessary for the child to attend an approved childcare centre, private arrangements can be accepted.
Entitlement to a Childcare Subsidy or OSCAR must be assessed first. If the total cost of childcare is not covered by the subsidy the client can receive the additional income exemption.
The exemption would be the lesser of:
- the amount the client pays for childcare or
- the cost of childcare not covered by a subsidy or
- $20 per week
The exemption only applies for the weeks the sole parent pays for childcare while they are working.

chunks.title: Client accepts the results of a failed screening test — jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Client accepts the results of a failed screening test
A client will be asked by the employer, training provider or the drug test provider to confirm that they accept the result of the failed screening test. They can accept the result of the failed drug test by:
- signing the Pre-employment Drug Test Result Confirmation Form or
- verbally accepting the result
When a client has accepted the results, this means that they understand:
- there is no requirement to send the failed screening test sample to a laboratory for evidential testing
- this may result in a sanction being imposed and
- they may have to repay Work and Income for the cost of the failed drug test
Before you initiate an obligations failure for a client because they have failed a drugs test, without having a good and sufficient reason, you must receive confirmation from the employer that the client has failed the test.
Once you have received confirmation from the employer or training provider that a client has failed the screening test, and all testing has been completed, an obligations failure should be initiated.
Although the client can still dispute other parts of the decision, by providing a good and sufficient reason for the obligations failure, they cannot dispute the result of the screening drug test because they have already accepted the failed result.
For more information see:
- Drug test obligations failure
- Informing a client of the drug test obligation failure
- Drug test failures reimbursement to employers and debt recovery
- Drug test obligations failures - good and sufficient reasons
- Recompliance for drug test obligation failures

chunks.title: Client and partner fail their social obligations — jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Client and partner fail their social obligations
Where a client has a partner, the social obligations apply to the couple. This means that when a social obligation is not complied with the obligation failure is initiated on both the client and their partner's record.
If a client and partner are at different stages in the 24 month failure count they may have to complete different recompliance activities. This is because the client or partner may have failed other obligations such as work obligations in the past 24 months.
## Example 1
Client
Partner
Current 24 month failure count
Obligations failure 1
Obligations failure 2
Social obligations failure
Obligations failure 2
Obligations failure 3
In this situation the client will have to recomply by complying with all their social obligations. The partner will have to recomply by completing a six-week approved activity or programme of activities which includes complying with all their social obligations in order to be granted a provisional benefit.
## Example 2
Client
Partner
Current 24 month failure count
Obligations failure 2
Obligations failure 1
Social obligations failure
Obligations failure 3
Obligations failure 2
In this situation the client will have to recomply by complying with all their social obligations. The partner will have to recomply by completing a six week approved activity or programme of activities which includes complying with all their social obligations in order to be granted a provisional benefit.

chunks.title: Client has failed a screening drug test — jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Client has failed a screening drug test
If a client fails a screening drug test with an employer, training provider or drug test provider, they will be advised that they have failed and they will be asked if they:
- accept the results of the screening test or
- do not accept the results of the drug screening test
For more information see:
- Informing a client of the drug test obligation failure
- Client accepts the results of a failed screening test
- Client does not accept the results of a failed screening test
- Drug test obligations failures - Good and sufficient reasons

chunks.title: Client is meeting their social obligations — jobseeker support student hardship
chunks.text:
## Client is meeting their social obligations
If, during any of the three stages Contact Steps of engagement and support, you consider that the client is meeting their social obligations you will need to let the client know that:
