- Denmark
- Hellenic Republic (Greece)
- Ireland
- Jersey and Guernsey
- Republic of Korea
- Malta
- Netherlands
- United Kingdom

chunks.title: Review date — payments from overseas
chunks.text:
## Review date
A New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date a client is granted an overseas benefit or pension, or when the rate of an overseas benefit or pension is increased.
If you are having difficulty obtaining details of the overseas pension grant date you should contact International Services for advice.
Where an overseas benefit or pension is reduced, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the reduction.
For more information see:
- Direct deductions
- Taxation and Overseas benefits and pensions

chunks.title: Taxation and overseas benefits and pensions — payments from overseas
chunks.text:
## Taxation and overseas benefits and pensions
Clients who wish to know whether their overseas benefit or pension is liable for New Zealand income tax should be referred to Inland Revenue.
## Tax liability
Generally a client will be liable for tax if they are receiving New Zealand Superannuation and the overseas benefit is being paid direct to their own bank account. They will need to provide details of the overseas pension payments from their bank statements.
## Exemption from tax
If a client is receiving any other New Zealand benefit or pension and the overseas benefit or pension is being deducted from the New Zealand benefit, the overseas benefit or pension is generally exempt from tax.
The client must provide details of the overseas benefit or pension to Inland Revenue who will decide whether the overseas benefit or pension is liable for tax.
## Special Banking option
If a client's overseas pension is paid to the special banking option account and they are getting a New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, the tax deducted by SWIFTT will cover their New Zealand Superannuation and overseas pension tax liability.

chunks.title: Voluntary portion of overseas pension — payments from overseas
chunks.text:
## Voluntary portion of overseas pension
Voluntary contributions are additional payments people make into a country's social insurance scheme, which are over and above the regular compulsory contributions which everyone makes. Voluntary contributions can also occur where a person is working overseas, and they decide to make voluntary contributions to their home country's state pensions scheme. Not all countries have a voluntary contribution option.
Voluntary contributions can result in people getting a retirement pension from their home country which includes compulsory and voluntary contributions. The portion of their state pension which represents their voluntary contributions is not deducted from their New Zealand benefit, but the voluntary portion is treated as income for any income tested assistance.
## Example
Hans receives New Zealand Superannuation and an overseas pension from Germany of $NZ476.00 every four weeks. 60% of the client's overseas pension is attributed to voluntary contributions the client continued make to their German state pension scheme while working in Germany for 28 years.
- 60% of the four weekly pension is $285.60 or $71.40 a week
- the $71.40 is not deducted from their New Zealand Superannuation but is treated as income for their Disability Allowance
- the remainder of their German pension is deducted from their New Zealand Superannuation

chunks.title: War Pensions — payments from overseas
chunks.text:
## War Pensions
When a client is getting a war disablement or a war widows pension from overseas which is in the nature of a New Zealand War Pension it will be disregarded in assessing the rate of their New Zealand benefit or pension.
Other war pensions may be deductible depending on the reason for their payment and the paying organisation. You need to contact International Services in the first instance for advice once you have obtained the following information:
- type of pension and reason for payment details. Example recognition of service (where was service completed?), disablement or other reason for payment
- name and address of paying organisation
- rate and frequency of payment
If you are unsure of the type of pension the client is receiving and how it should be treated you can contact:
- International Services

chunks.title: Introduction — portability
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Client's getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension may be able to continue getting their payment while overseas under portability provisions if they are:
- residing in a country that New Zealand does not have a social security agreement with or
- travelling overseas for more than 26 weeks but not residing in any one country or
- leaving New Zealand for more than 52 weeks to live in certain Pacific countries
Grandparented non-qualified partners cannot be paid overseas.

chunks.title: Admission to institutions — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Admission to institutions
If a client is admitted to an overseas hospital, prison or other institution payment is continued at the same rate regardless of the period of confinement.

chunks.title: Applying for payment — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Applying for payment
Clients should apply for payment overseas before they leave New Zealand. Only in certain circumstances is a client able to apply for payment from overseas.
Applications for payment overseas are decided by International Services. Clients should be advised to apply 6 weeks before they leave New Zealand. Applications are made at Service Centres on form (WIS7W). The client must be interviewed at a Service Centre and a special interview sheet (WIF9W) completed.
Clients must bring the following documents to their interview to support their application:
- passports
- secondary identification
- air tickets or travel itinerary and
- bank account details (if different from SWIFTT)
It is important that International Services receives a detailed itinerary, where the client can provide one, to support that the client is going to spend time travelling. A detailed itinerary can include details supplied on the application for payment overseas. If the client has an itinerary from their travel agent, please obtain a copy with the application.
If a client's passport shows repeated departures from New Zealand, document all periods of absence and countries visited and the reasons for the repeated absences. Certain absences can be counted as residence in New Zealand when calculating the rate of payment so it is very important that the reason for any absence from New Zealand is provided. If you need help while taking an application please contact International Services.
It is very important that International Services is given accurate information regarding the client residency in New Zealand as this relates to the amount of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension a client may receive.
The completed application form, interview sheet and supporting documentation must be sent to International Services.
Do not cancel the client record. If you need to stop the client's payments, suspend the record only.

chunks.title: Applying for payment from overseas — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Applying for payment from overseas
A client who left New Zealand to go overseas for less than 26 weeks but who cannot return to New Zealand within 30 weeks, may, under certain circumstances apply for payments from overseas.
To accept an application for General Portability from overseas the client must:
- have left New Zealand with the intention of being absent for 26 weeks or less
- have been prevented from returning to New Zealand within 26 weeks due to circumstances beyond their control and
- the circumstances beyond their control could not reasonably have been foreseen before leaving New Zealand
Note a desire to extend an overseas travelling holiday may not meet these criteria. In any circumstances where a person overseas under the 26 weeks provision wishes to apply for portable payment to continue overseas travel or to begin residing overseas, special care must be taken to ensure that the application is valid. The exemption criteria must be met, or the application must be declined.
New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension payments should be suspended as soon as a client advises they are not returning to New Zealand.
If a Service Centre or the Veterans Pension Centre receives a request for payment from overseas they should send this to International Services.
Note a client must provide proof to support their application. Example, an airline ticket may provide evidence that the client intended to return within 26 weeks. A letter from the client's overseas treating health practitioner may confirm that an accident or health condition prevented the clients return.
In the case of a health condition it is important to consider whether the client may have had this condition before they left New Zealand.

chunks.title: Bank accounts — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Bank accounts
Payments can be made to any overseas bank account or a New Zealand bank account. The client will need to provide full bank account details on their application form, or on the overseas details form that will be sent to them by International Services.
The overseas bank account number must be verified by the overseas bank or by the client supplying acceptable bank verification. For any country covered by IBAN, the full IBAN number must be verified. If the client wishes to be paid into a Canadian bank account then the institute number, branch number and account number must be provided. For more information contact International Services
If the client wants to be paid into an overseas bank account but does not know the overseas bank account number before they leave New Zealand there are two options for the first payments:
- make the first few payments to a New Zealand bank account (the client is responsible for any overseas transfer) or
- suspend all payments until details of the overseas bank account are known and pay arrears to the overseas bank account
Payments to overseas banks are made every 4 weeks on a New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension payday. Work and Income will meet the bank transaction costs incurred in transferring the payment to the overseas bank account. Any other transaction costs are the responsibility of the client.
Note the overseas bank account does not have to be in the same country as a person is travelling or living in.
For more information see:
- Payments
- Changes to bank accounts
- Deskfile New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension rates
- Overseas pensions
- Details from overseas
- Extra help

chunks.title: Change of address — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Change of address
When a client changes their address International Services must check that the move does not affect the client's entitlement to payment overseas.
Clients must contact International Services to advise them of any change of address.
For more information see:
- Moving to a social security agreement country
- Moving to a Pacific country
- Moving to a country not covered by a social security agreement or special portability
- Temporary absence
- Return to New Zealand
- Obligations

chunks.title: Changes in circumstances and payment reviews — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Changes in circumstances and payment reviews
A client is obliged to advise Work and Income of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
International Services may review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
For more information see:
- Moving to a social security agreement country
- Moving to a Pacific country
- Moving to a country not covered by a social security agreement or special portability
- Moving between overseas countries
- Admission to institutions
- Change of address
- Changes to bank accounts
- Temporary absence
- Return to New Zealand
- Admission to institutions
- Life Certificates
- Overpayments
- Death of a client

chunks.title: Changes to bank accounts — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Changes to bank accounts
Each client has the choice to receive their payments into either a New Zealand bank account or an overseas bank account
Payments into New Zealand bank accounts are made fortnightly on each New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension payday.
Payments to overseas banks are made every 4 weeks on every second New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension payday. Work and Income will meet the bank transaction costs incurred in transferring the payment to the overseas bank account.
If a client changes bank accounts, they will need to provide proof of the new bank account. Clients should delay closing their old bank account until they receive the first payment into the new account. This will eliminate any delays in recovering payments sent to the old account and then paying them to the new one.

chunks.title: Commencement date — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
The commencement date of payment overseas is:
- the first New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension payday after departure, for clients applying before they leave New Zealand or
- the first New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension payday after Work and Income receive the application, for those who apply after leaving New Zealand
Note a person who has left New Zealand to go overseas for less than 26 weeks, who cannot return to New Zealand within 30 weeks, may, under certain circumstances apply for portable payments from overseas. However, they must meet certain criteria - most importantly, they must be unable to return because of circumstances that are:
- beyond their control and
- unforeseen at the time of their departure from New Zealand
For more information see:
- Payments
- Taxation
- Overpayments
- Applying for payment
- Applying for payment from overseas

chunks.title: Death of a client — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
Payments may continue for up to 28 days after the client's death regardless of their relationship status.
Payments for surviving partners are increased to the single rate from the day after their partner's date of death.

chunks.title: Details from overseas — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Details from overseas
International Services sends each client a 'Details from Overseas' form with their grant letter - which can be emailed on request. The client is required to return this form after they have arrived overseas.
This form asks for:
- details of the client's overseas bank account number which must be verified by the overseas bank and
- evidence that the client is travelling or residing in the country or countries which were stated in their application form
If this form is not returned by the client within 6 weeks of their arrival overseas, payments will be suspended by International Services until the form is returned and entitlement confirmed.
If a client wants to communicate with International Services via email, they should complete the 'Authorisation of E-mail address Form' that's part of the 'Application for New Zealand Payment Overseas' form.
For more information see:
- Qualifications
- Bank accounts

chunks.title: Entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation
Only clients who qualify in their own right can receive General Portability. Grandparented non-qualified partners have no entitlement and their New Zealand Superannuation stops once they leave New Zealand.
If a client is not already receiving New Zealand Superannuation they should make an application for New Zealand Superannuation and payment overseas before they leave New Zealand. This means a client must be entitled to New Zealand Superannuation before leaving New Zealand.
Case managers are responsible for assessing the New Zealand Superannuation application and whether a client is entitled to New Zealand Superannuation. This will involve deciding whether the client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand on the date of application.
A client is entitled to General Portability of New Zealand Superannuation if they:
- are entitled or will be entitled to receive New Zealand Superannuation before leaving New Zealand
- are ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand on the date they apply for payment overseas and
- make an application stating the country or countries in which they intend to reside and the period for which they intend to reside in each country or countries or
- make an application stating the country or countries in which they intend to travel
Note clients must complete an application form for payment overseas before they leave New Zealand. All applications for payment overseas and ongoing payments are processed by International Services.

chunks.title: Entitlement to Veterans Pension — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Entitlement to Veterans Pension
Only clients who qualify in their own right can receive General Portability. Grandparented non-qualified partners have no entitlement and their Veteran's Pension payments stop once they leave New Zealand.
If a client is not already receiving Veteran's Pension they should make an application for Veteran's Pension and payment overseas before they leave New Zealand. This means that a client needs to be entitled to Veterans Pension before leaving New Zealand.
Veterans Pension Centre is responsible for assessing the Veteran's Pension application and deciding whether a client is entitled to Veterans Pension. This may involve deciding whether the client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they make their application where that is a condition on their entitlement.
A client is entitled to General Portability of Veterans Pension if they:
- are entitled or will be entitled to receive Veterans Pension before leaving New Zealand
- are ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand on the date they apply for payment overseas and
- make an application stating the country or countries in which they intend to reside and the period they intend to reside in each country or countries or
- make an application stating the country or countries in which they intend to travel
Note clients must complete an application form for payment overseas before they leave New Zealand. All applications for payment overseas and ongoing payments are processed by International Services.
## For more information about ordinary residence see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Deciding ordinarily resident in New Zealand
- Applying for payment

chunks.title: Extra help — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Extra help
Clients receiving General Portability are not entitled to receive any Extra help such as:
- Temporary Additional Support
- Accommodation Supplement
- Disability Allowance
- Funeral Grants
- Residential Care Subsidy
- Special Needs Grants
For more information see:
- Payments

chunks.title: Going overseas for 26 weeks or less — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Going overseas for 26 weeks or less
If a New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension client wants to travel overseas but will be back in New Zealand within 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension payment can continue as normal.
Note if clients are not entitled to supplementary payments during their absence these payments should be suspended.
If a client travels overseas for more than 26 weeks but returns to New Zealand within 30 weeks, they can still get paid for the first 26 weeks.
If a client intended to return to New Zealand within 30 weeks but was prevented due to circumstances beyond their control that they could not have reasonably foreseen, payment can still be made for the first 26 weeks.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Absence from New Zealand

chunks.title: Going overseas for aid work — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Going overseas for aid work
A client may not need to apply for payments of General Portability if they are undertaking full-time voluntary and unpaid humanitarian work for a recognised aid agency and intend to be away for less than 156 weeks.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Humanitarian work
- Applying for payment

chunks.title: Going overseas for medical treatment — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Going overseas for medical treatment
There are special provisions for clients going overseas for medical reasons. Clients who do not qualify under these special provisions should be considered for payment overseas.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Overseas medical treatment

chunks.title: Going overseas for more than 26 weeks — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Going overseas for more than 26 weeks
If a New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension client would like to go overseas for more than 26 weeks, they may be able to receive payments while they are overseas.
For more information see:
- Going overseas for medical treatment
- Going overseas for aid work
- Travelling or residing overseas for more than 26 weeks

chunks.title: Grandparented clients on New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Grandparented clients on New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
Before 5 January 2010, clients who were receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension while residing in a non-agreement country or in a Pacific country not covered by the Special Portability Arrangement were only paid 50% of their gross entitlement.
The new rules allow clients receiving the 50% flat rate to have a higher of either their payments based on their New Zealand residence between the ages of 20 and 65 or the 50% flat rate.
This means that:
- clients who resided in New Zealand for less than 270 months can choose to remain on the 50% rate because they would be entitled to less under the new rules
- clients who resided in New Zealand for more than 270 months and would therefore be entitled to more than 50% can receive the higher rate
Note overseas pensions are only deducted from grandparented rates. Only clients who are receiving a grandparented General Portability rate should have overseas pensions deducted.
## Qualifying criteria (grand parenting)
To be eligible for the grandparented rate clients must have been receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension or entitled to New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in their own right (not by virtue of a reciprocal social security agreement or as a grandparented non-qualified partner) before they leave New Zealand and must:
- be intending to reside in an overseas country for more than 26 weeks
- be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand on the date they apply for payment overseas
- not be going to live in a country with which New Zealand has a social security agreement
- have made an application for payment overseas before 5 January 2010 and
- be receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension overseas at the 50% rate in a non-Agreement country before 5 January 2010

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualified partners — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Grandparented non-qualified partners
Grandparented non-qualified partners cannot be paid overseas, so their payments will be cancelled from the payday after the qualified partner's departure from New Zealand.

chunks.title: Introduction — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Introduction
Client's receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension may be able to receive payments while overseas.
Note the term General Portability applies where a person is receiving a payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and is residing overseas in a country that is not a country that New Zealand has a social security agreement with. It also applies where a person may be residing in a specified Pacific country but is not paid under the Special Portability Arrangement. General Portability also applies to people who travel overseas for more than 26 weeks but do not reside in any one country.
For more information see:
- Going overseas for 26 weeks or less
- Going overseas for more than 26 weeks
- Reciprocal agreements
- Special Portability
- Changes in circumstances and payment reviews

chunks.title: Life Certificates — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Life Certificates
All clients living overseas will automatically be sent Life Certificates every 52 weeks. These certificates are sent to establish whether a client's circumstances have changed, and are the responsibility of Senior Services - international. The form must be completed by the client and returned by post from overseas to International Services
If a change of circumstances affects the client's entitlement, International Services will review the payments.
Clients will be sent Life Certificates every 26 weeks if they:
- are over 80
- have an agent
- choose to travel away from the country where they live or
- have a New Zealand bank account
All other clients will be sent a Life Certificate every 52 weeks.
Note if the Life Certificate is not completed and received by International Services within 8 weeks, payments are automatically suspended. Payments may then be temporarily resumed until the Life Certificate has been received by International Services, if the client contacts International Services and they are satisfied that the clients' circumstances have not changed.

chunks.title: Travelling — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Travelling
If clients are entitled to payment overseas of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, they can get this payment while travelling to, in or between countries.
## Residing
If clients are residing in a non-agreement country and want to travel in or reside in other non-agreement countries, they can continue to be paid New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension at the same rate.
Some agreements allow clients to continue to be paid if they are absent from the agreement countries for 26 weeks or less (Canada, Denmark, Ireland, the Netherlands, Australia).
However, if clients are residing in an agreement country and want to travel or reside in a non-agreement country for more than 26 weeks, they will generally not be entitled to payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension from the date they leave the agreement country.
If a client is residing in one agreement country, then moves to reside in a second agreement country they will need to apply for payment under the second country's agreement.
Clients will generally not be entitled to payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension from the date they leave the first agreement country.

chunks.title: Moving to a country not covered by a social security agreement or special portability — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Moving to a country not covered by a social security agreement or special portability
If a client is receiving General Portability payments and has moved to a country that we don't have a social security agreement with or that is covered by the special portability arrangement, their entitlement and payments will usually continue.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Moving to a Pacific country — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Moving to a Pacific country
If a client has moved to a Pacific country that is covered by the special portability arrangement, their payments will normally continue under the General Portability provisions. A client receiving General Portability payments will not be able to transfer to the special portability arrangement.
There are special rules for Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau residents.
For more information see:
- Special Portability Applying from overseas
Clients are not entitled to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension under the special portability arrangement if they apply from overseas.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Moving to a social security agreement country — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Moving to a social security agreement country
New Zealand has Social Security Agreements with the following countries:
- Australia
- Canada
- Denmark
- Hellenic Republic (Greece)
- Ireland
- Jersey and Guernsey
- Malta
- Netherlands
- United Kingdom
A client will not have continuing entitlement to payment under the General Portability provisions if they have moved permanently to a country with which New Zealand has a social security agreement on social security to live.
If the client moves to an agreement country permanently they should be advised to apply for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension under the social security agreement. If a client has entitlement under the social security agreement, International Services will reassess their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension. Their General Portability payments are cancelled from the payday after the client's departure from their previous country of residence.
If a client has gone to live in the United Kingdom their payments will be cancelled from the payday after the date they left their previous country of residence. Clients should be advised to apply for a United Kingdom pension when they arrive in the United Kingdom.
Note if a client intends to reside in more than one overseas country, one of those countries being the United Kingdom, they need to be advised that the order of the countries in which they want to reside is important. They should schedule the United Kingdom last on the list of countries because, unless they intend to move to another agreement country, they will not be entitled to payment.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reciprocal Agreements

chunks.title: Obligations — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Obligations
Clients are obliged to advise Work and Income of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
Clients agree to this by signing the Veteran's Pension or New Zealand Superannuation application form, the payment overseas application form and the overseas details form.
Checking their tax liability with Inland Revenue in New Zealand or the tax agency in the country they are moving to is the responsibility of the client.
Clients must keep International Services up to date with their travel movements if they are travelling. Any evidence requested to support that a client is travelling must be given to International Services (especially relevant for a client travelling through a social security agreement country).
Clients must also advise International Services when they move between countries.
Examples of changes and how to deal with these can be found in Changes in circumstances and payment reviews

chunks.title: Ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand on date of application for payment overseas — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand on date of application for payment overseas
Clients must be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand on the date they apply for payment overseas.
Note generally New Zealanders who usually live overseas should not be regarded as ordinarily resident in New Zealand if they have recently returned to apply for New Zealand Superannuation.
Information held in the payment overseas application may help you to decide whether a client can be considered ordinarily resident in New Zealand. Contact International Services for more information.

chunks.title: Overpayments — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
An overpayment should be established for any period where a higher rate of New Zealand Superannuation was paid but not due to the client.
If a client has been overpaid New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension at the domestic rate, the overpayment is always established for the net amount. Inland Revenue will return the tax portion of the overpayment directly to Work and Income.
Overpayments for clients being paid overseas are established for the gross amount as these payments do not have tax deducted by Work and Income.
## Exception
Do not establish an overpayment for the first 26 weeks of absence, to a client who has applied from overseas if the client can show that the reason for their non-return was due to circumstances beyond their control that could not reasonably have been foreseen at the time of their departure from New Zealand.
For clients who left New Zealand with a grandparented non-qualified partner included in their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, this means that the debt should not be established for the primary client, or for their partner.
If portable New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension is granted and domestic payment at the full rate continued after 26 weeks, then establish an overpayment from that date and recover the debt from ongoing payments.

chunks.title: Overseas pensions — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Overseas pensions
Overseas pensions will not be deducted from a client's payments unless they are getting the grandparented 50% fixed rate of payment overseas.
Clients who are not grandparented and are travelling or residing in a country or countries and getting General Portability will not have an overseas pension deducted.
If a client is getting payment overseas at the grandparented rate of 50% of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and is getting an overseas benefit or pension, the rate payable is 50% of the gross amount payable after deduction of the overseas pension.
## Example
Gross weekly New Zealand Superannuation single sharing (as at 1 April 2026)
$595.57
minus the weekly rate of overseas pension (NZD$100)
$100.00
equals the gross weekly New Zealand Superannuation single sharing rate
$495.57
50% of the gross rate equals
$247.78
Note if a client's overseas pension is being paid into a Special Banking Option account, the account must be closed by International Services, as they are responsible for administering the Special Banking Option payment method.
The client must be advised to make arrangements to have the overseas agency pay the pension directly to their own bank account.

chunks.title: Payments — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Payments
Payments to a New Zealand bank account are paid on the same day as all New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension payments.
Clients wanting their payments made to an overseas bank account are paid every 4 weeks.
In general, payment must be made directly to the client. However, where there is good cause, the client's benefit can be paid to another person.
For more information see:
- Core policy Agents
Grandparented non-qualified partner's payments are cancelled from the payday after the qualified partner leaves New Zealand.

chunks.title: Periods of residence — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Periods of residence
The maximum amount of residence to be used when calculating the rate of payment a client receives is 540 months. All full months of residence between the ages of 20 and 65 are added together. If there are any extra days left over, these are added together, and then divided by 30 to make up any extra full months.
Certain absences from New Zealand can also be counted as residence when calculating the rate to be paid overseas.

chunks.title: Permanent return to New Zealand — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Permanent return to New Zealand
If a client has returned to live in New Zealand permanently, payments are stopped by International Services from the payday after their date of return.
To allow International Services to stop a client's overseas payments, the client must make an appointment at a Service Centre. At this appointment the client must complete a "Personal Details Form" to inform Work and Income whether they intend to remain in New Zealand, and the date they returned to New Zealand. The completed form should be forwarded to International Services along with a copy of the client's boarding pass or passport (to verify the date of return to New Zealand).
Once International Services have stopped the payments overseas they will contact the Service Centre or Veterans Pension Centre to arrange the resumption of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension. New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension entitlement must be reviewed by the Service Centre or Veterans Pension entitlement by the Veterans Pension Centre.
If the client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand payments can be increased to the relevant domestic rate from the payday after the client's date of return.

chunks.title: Qualifications — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
From 5 January 2010 the legislation changed to allow people going overseas to receive up to 100% of the gross New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension. The new rate of payment is based on the amount of residence a person has in New Zealand between the ages of 20 and 65. As with the previous payment rate, grandparented non-qualified partners cannot be paid overseas.
Clients who applied for payment overseas and were receiving payment overseas under General Portability before 5 January 2010 are entitled to the higher of the new rate of payment or the old 50% of the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
A client is entitled to payment overseas of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension if they:
- are entitled or will be entitled to receive New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension before leaving New Zealand
- are ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand on the date they apply for payment overseas and
- make an application stating the country or countries in which they intend to reside and the period for which they intend to reside in each country or countries or
- make an application stating the country or countries in which they intend to travel
Clients must complete an application form for payment overseas before they leave New Zealand. All applications for payment overseas and ongoing payments are processed by International Services.
Note where a client has qualified for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension using one of the social security agreements check the appropriate Agreement to see whether the client is eligible for portable payment of their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension if they intend to be absent for more than 26 weeks.
## Exception
A client can apply from overseas for General Portability only if they had left New Zealand with the intention of returning within 26 weeks or less but was prevented from returning due to circumstances beyond their control that they could not have reasonably foreseen. Any application from overseas will be assessed based on residence in New Zealand between the ages of 20 and 65 if it is received after 5 January 2010.

chunks.title: Rate of payment — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Rate of payment
The rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid overseas is based on the number of months the client resided in New Zealand between the ages of 20 and 65.
- if a client has resided in New Zealand continuously between the ages of 20 and 65 they will receive 100% of their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension entitlement
- if they have resided in New Zealand for less than 540 months (or 45 years) between the ages of 20 and 65 they will be paid a proportionate amount
Clients can get up to 100% of the gross rate of either the half married, civil union or de facto rate, or the single sharing accommodation rate, depending on the client's relationship status.
The grandparented non-qualified partner rate is not payable outside New Zealand.
Overseas pensions will not be deducted from a client's payments unless they are grandparented at the 50% fixed rate of payment overseas.
General Portability payments are made at a gross rate. This means they are not taxed in New Zealand.
If a person going overseas is not sure whether they will need to pay New Zealand tax while they are overseas, they should check with Inland Revenue in New Zealand.
Veteran's Pension recipients under the age of 65 will have an income test applied.
Note single living alone rate, grandparented non-qualified partner payments, and Extra help are not payable to a client getting General Portability. The rate of New Zealand Superannuation will be paid at the single sharing accommodation rate and the supplementary payments will be cancelled.

chunks.title: Rate on return to New Zealand — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Rate on return to New Zealand
If the client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand payments can be increased to the domestic rate from the payday after the client's date of return.

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
Clients may return to New Zealand permanently or on a temporary visit. The rate they are paid depends on whether they have returned permanently or temporarily.
For more information see:
- Permanent return to New Zealand
- Temporary return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Reviews and Appeals — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Reviews and Appeals
A client can apply for a Review of Decision when they have received formal notification of (and do not agree with) a decision which has been made under:
- the Social Security Act 2018 and Residential Care and Disability Support Services Act 2018
- Approved special assistance programmes section 101 Social Security Act 2018
- Part I of the Social Welfare (Transitional Provisions) Act 1990 or section 175 of the Veterans' Support Act 2014
- Part 1 of the New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001
- the Family Benefits (Home Ownership) Act 1964
- Regulations in force under section 437 Social Security Act 2018 or
- Regulations in force under section 74 Residential Care and Disability Support Services Act 2018
A client can appeal to the Appeal Authority where they do not agree with a decision, which was:
- upheld or upheld in part by the Benefits Review Committee under an application for Review of Decision or
- made by MSD
For more information see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Tax records — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Tax records
SWIFTT will produce a tax record certificate each year that shows the total gross New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid as General Portability for the past New Zealand tax year. This will be posted to the client's mailing address.
Note the amount shown on these certificates will not include any payments made before departure from New Zealand.

chunks.title: Taxation — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Taxation
General Portability payments are made at a gross rate. This means that the payments are not taxed in New Zealand for those clients who are going to reside or travel for more than 26 weeks in an overseas country or countries
Clients who are residing overseas and are paid into an overseas bank account may have a tax liability in the country they have moved to. They should contact the tax authority in the country they are moving to for more information.
If payments are being made into a New Zealand bank account, clients will need to contact New Zealand Inland Revenue to determine their tax liability.
Clients who are travelling overseas for more than 26 weeks will need to contact New Zealand Inland Revenue to determine their tax liability.
Note if a client intends to travel overseas for more than 26 weeks, we cannot pay their tax for them while they are overseas. They will need to contact Inland Revenue before they leave New Zealand to discuss their tax liability while they are overseas.
For more information see:
- Tax records
- Obligations
- New Zealand Superannuation Taxation

chunks.title: Temporary absence — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Temporary absence
Where a client has chosen to reside in another country and they are absent from that country for less than 26 weeks they can continue to receive their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
If a client intends to travel from the country they reside in for an extended period of more than 26 weeks to one or more countries they may be able to continue to receive their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
Note please ensure that you contact International Services if the client is in New Zealand, as they will need to ensure that the client is receiving the correct New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension entitlement.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Temporary return to New Zealand — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Temporary return to New Zealand
If the client is only returning to New Zealand temporarily, their payments will probably continue at the overseas rate as the client has not returned to New Zealand permanently.
For example, if the client has been receiving General Portability payments while travelling for more than 26 weeks overseas and travels back to New Zealand temporarily to attend an event or visit a person, their payments should continue at the same rate.
Note please ensure that you contact International Services if the client is in New Zealand, as they will need to ensure that the client is receiving the correct New Zealand Superannuation entitlement.
A client returning to New Zealand temporarily is entitled to a Community Services Card. Temporary cards can be issued. Someone who is not living in New Zealand permanently is not entitled to a SuperGold Card.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Qualifications
- New Zealand Superannuation Deciding ordinarily resident in New Zealand
- SuperGold Card Residence
- Overpayments

chunks.title: Travelling or residing overseas for more than 26 weeks — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Travelling or residing overseas for more than 26 weeks
In some instances New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension can be paid to clients who are leaving New Zealand to travel or reside overseas for longer than 26 weeks. Grandparented non-qualified partners cannot be paid overseas.
Clients can receive up to 100% of the gross New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension rate if they:
- want to travel overseas for more than 26 weeks but don't want to reside in an overseas country or countries or
- want to reside in one or more overseas countries that is not a Pacific country covered by the Special Portability Arrangement or a country that New Zealand has a social security agreement with
The single living alone rate and Extra help are not payable to a client receiving General Portability.
The term General Portability applies where a person is receiving a payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and is residing overseas in a country that is not a country that New Zealand has a social security agreement with. It also applies where a person may be residing in a specified Pacific country but is not paid under the Special Portability Arrangement. General Portability also applies to people who travel overseas for more than 26 weeks but do not reside in any one country.
Clients wishing to reside in a social security agreement country may be able to receive payment under a social security agreement.
Clients wishing to reside in one of 22 specified Pacific countries may be able to receive payment under the Special Portability rules if they are intending to reside in that Pacific country for more than 52 weeks.
If a client is going to a Pacific country that is not a specified Pacific country then they may still qualify for payment overseas under General Portability.
Note someone who intended to travel around the world, who was receiving payment overseas while travelling, may choose to settle in a specified Pacific country to live. They would continue to receive payment at the General Portability rate and cannot be transferred to Special Portability.

chunks.title: Treatment of periods of absence for residence qualification — portability > general portability
chunks.text:
## Treatment of periods of absence for residence qualification
If a client was absent from New Zealand when they were aged between 20 and 65, some reasons for their absence can still qualify towards residency.
The types of absence are:
- for special medical or surgical treatment (if there was good and sufficient reason for the client to leave New Zealand for this)
- vocational training (if there was good and sufficient reason for the client to leave New Zealand for this)
- seamen serving on a ship registered or owned in New Zealand and engaged in trading to and from New Zealand
- overseas service as a member of the naval, military or air force of any Commonwealth country. This includes war service as a member of any organisation attached to any of these forces, eg, YMCA, church, Red Cross
- full-time voluntary humanitarian work this must be carried out for an entity that is: a charitable entity that has as its main function the giving of aid and assistance to less advantaged communities in one or more countries) oraffiliated with or closely related to, a charitable entity that has as its main function the giving of aid and assistance to less advantaged communities in one or more countries
- a charitable entity that has as its main function the giving of aid and assistance to less advantaged communities in one or more countries) or
- affiliated with or closely related to, a charitable entity that has as its main function the giving of aid and assistance to less advantaged communities in one or more countries
- any capacity as an accredited volunteer appointed by Volunteer Service Abroad
- missionary work (defined as including 'the advancement of religion or education and the maintenance, care or relief of orphans, or the aged, infirm, sick or needy')
- when a person has worked overseas and their New Zealand income tax (PAYE) was paid to Inland Revenue New Zealand (or had it withheld but not paid to Inland Revenue New Zealand
Clients must have been ordinarily resident for the periods they worked overseas.

chunks.title: Admission to institutions — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Admission to institutions
If a client is admitted to a hospital, prison or other institution payment of Special Portability is continued at the same rate regardless of the period of confinement.

chunks.title: Clients living in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Clients living in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau
Clients living in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau can apply for Special Portability from these countries. They must apply for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, and Special Portability at the same time. Clients must meet the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, and Special Portability. See:
- New Zealand Superannuation Qualifications
- Veterans's Pension Qualifications
- Special Portability Qualifications
These applications do not lapse after 20 working days.
## Client living in another Pacific country
Clients intending to live in any other Pacific country covered by Special Portability must apply for Special Portability from New Zealand before they leave. If they are not already getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, they must apply for this and Special Portability at the same time.
These applications lapse after 20 days.
## Did not apply before leaving New Zealand
If a client did not apply for Special Portability before leaving New Zealand, they may sill qualify if they intended to return to New Zealand within 26 weeks and:
- are now living in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau or
- are living in another Pacific country and are unable to return due to circumstances beyond their control, eg an unexpected serious illness
If the client cannot show that they are now:
- living in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau or
- prevented from returning from another Pacific country because of circumstances beyond their control, they may qualify for General Portability.
## General Portability
The client must have been prevented from returning to New Zealand due to circumstances beyond their control which could not have been reasonably foreseen before their departure from New Zealand.
When an application for Special Portability has been made from overseas, entitlement to General Portability will be considered by International Services.

chunks.title: Applying in New Zealand — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Applying in New Zealand
Clients already getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension must generally apply for Special Portability before they leave New Zealand. Each partner of a couple must apply separately.
Clients who are not already getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension should make an application for New Zealand Superannuation and Special Portability before they leave New Zealand.
Applications for Special Portability are assessed by International Services.
## How to apply
Applications are made at service centres and should be made 6-8 weeks before the client leaves New Zealand.
The client must complete at the service centre the:
- Application for Payment Overseas form (WIS7W) and
- Application for Payment Overseas interview form (WIF9W)
Clients must bring the following documents to their interview:
- passports
- secondary identification
- air tickets or travel itinerary and
- bank account details if different from SWIFTT
If a client's passport shows repeated departures from New Zealand, document all periods of absence and countries visited and the reasons for the repeated absences. If you need help while taking an application please contact International Services.
The completed application form, interview sheet and supporting documentation must be sent to International Services.
Note do not suspend or cancel the client record. Place the client record on bring up to check International Services has either granted Special Portability or suspended the record.

chunks.title: Change of address — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Change of address
When a client changes their address International Services must check that the move does not affect the client's entitlement to Special Portability.
## Moving to another country
If a client has moved to another Pacific country they will have continued entitlement to Special Portability. This also applies to clients who applied for Special Portability from the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau.
If they have moved to a country not covered by the Special Portability Arrangement different rules apply and payments should be suspended until continuing entitlement is decided by International Services.
For more information see:
- Definition of specified Pacific country
- Moving to a reciprocal agreement country
- Moving to a general portability country
- Return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise the Ministry of Social Development of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to their Special Portability payments of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
International Services may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
For more information see:
- Admission to institutions
- Change of address
- Death of a client
- Extra help
- Life certificates
- Moving to a general portability country
- Moving to a reciprocal agreement country
- Overpayments
- Return to New Zealand
- Tax record certificates

chunks.title: Commencement date — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Commencement date
The commencement date depends on whether the client applied before leaving New Zealand or from the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau.
## Commencement date for clients who apply before leaving New Zealand
For clients who apply in New Zealand the Special Portability commencement date is the first, New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension payday after they leave New Zealand.
## Commencement date for clients who apply from the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau
For clients who apply from the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau, the Special Portability commencement date is:
- the date they qualify for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension or
- the date of application (when the client requests an application form)
whichever is later.Note applications from the Cook Islands Niue and Tokelau do not lapse after 20 days.

chunks.title: Death of a client — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Death of a client
Payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran’s Pension under the Special Portability Arrangement may continue for no more than 4 weeks after the client's death regardless of their relationship status.
If a surviving partner is receiving Special Portability their payments are increased to the single sharing Special Portability rate from the payday after the date of death of their partner.
For more information see:
- Life certificates

chunks.title: Definition of specified Pacific country — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Definition of specified Pacific country
The Special Portability Arrangement covers the following specified Pacific countries:
- American Samoa
- Cook Islands
- Federated States of Micronesia
- Fiji
- French Polynesia
- Guam
- Kiribati
- Marshall Islands
- Nauru
- New Caledonia
- Niue
- Northern Mariana Islands
- Palau
- Papua New Guinea
- Pitcairn Island
- Samoa
- Solomon Islands
- Tokelau
- Tonga
- Tuvalu
- Vanuatu
- Wallis and Futuna

chunks.title: Clients going to a specified Pacific country — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Clients going to a specified Pacific country
Only clients who qualify in their own right can receive payment overseas under the Special Portability rules. Grandparented non-qualified partners have no entitlement and their New Zealand Superannuation payments stop once they leave New Zealand.
If a client is not already receiving New Zealand Superannuation they should make an application for New Zealand Superannuation and Special Portability before they leave New Zealand unless they intend to reside in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau.
Case managers are responsible for deciding New Zealand Superannuation entitlement. Special consideration should be given when deciding if a client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they make their application.
Note generally New Zealanders who usually live overseas are not regarded as ordinarily resident in New Zealand if they have recently returned to apply for New Zealand Superannuation. Information held on the Special Portability application may assist when considering whether a client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Clients applying from Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau
Clients applying from the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau will be required to apply for New Zealand Superannuation and Special Portability. A client can apply ahead of the date they meet the qualification age.
The application for New Zealand Superannuation is to determine that they meet the qualifying age and have had 10 years residence and presence in New Zealand since the age of 20. This must include 5 years or more since age 50. Clients applying from the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau are not required to meet the ordinary residence in New Zealand requirement.

chunks.title: Clients going to a Pacific country — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Clients going to a Pacific country
Only clients who qualify in their own right can get payment overseas under the Special Portability rules.
Grandparented non-qualified partners have no entitlement and their Veteran's Pension payments stop once they leave New Zealand.
If a client is not already getting Veteran's Pension they should make an application for Veteran's Pension and Special Portability before they leave New Zealand, unless they intend to reside in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau.
The Veteran's Pension Centre is responsible for deciding Veteran's Pension entitlement. Special consideration should be given when deciding if a client is ordinarily resident when they make their application.
Note generally New Zealanders who usually live overseas are not regarded as ordinarily resident in New Zealand if they have recently returned to apply for Veteran's Pension.
Information held on the Special Portability application may assist when considering whether a client is ordinarily resident.
## Clients applying from Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau
Clients applying from the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau will be required to apply for Veteran's Pension and Special Portability at the same time.
The application for Veteran's Pension is to determine the client:
- has qualifying operational service and
- has attained the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation and
- meets the residential qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation
The client is not required to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
If needed contact Veterans Pension Centre

chunks.title: Extra help — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Extra help
A client getting Special Portability is not entitled to get any Extra help such as:
- Accommodation Supplement
- Disability Allowance
- Special Needs Grants
- Residential Care Subsidy or
- Funeral Grants
For more information see:
- Payment

chunks.title: Introduction — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The Special Portability Arrangement allows people getting New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension in their own right to live and get their payments in certain Pacific countries.
Clients must meet the Special Portability qualifications as well as the New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension qualifications.
The rate of payment is between 50% and 100% of the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
The rate depends on the number of years the client has lived in New Zealand since they turned 20.
## Pacific countries covered by Special Portability
American Samoa, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, New Caledonia, Niue, Northern Mariana Islands, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Pitcairn Island, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tokelau, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna.
## Special rules for the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau
Client's living in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau can apply for Special Portability and New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension from these countries.
They can apply for both at the same time.
Other clients must apply for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension first, and Special Portability before leaving New Zealand.
## May qualify for General Portability instead
Clients who do not qualify for Special Portability may qualify for General Portability.
International Services processes all applications and will look at what type of portability the client qualifies for.

chunks.title: Life certificates — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Life certificates
All clients receiving Special Portability will automatically be sent Life Certificates every 52 weeks. These certificates are sent to establish whether a client's circumstances have changed and are the responsibility of International Services. The form must be completed by the client and returned to International Services.
If a change of circumstances affects the client's entitlement, International Services will review the Special Portability payments.
Clients over 80, those with agents or those with New Zealand bank accounts, will be sent life certificates every 26 weeks and all other clients will be sent a life certificate every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Moving to a General Portability country — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Moving to a General Portability country
If a client has moved to a country that is covered by the General Portability provisions Special Portability will be cancelled from the payday after their departure from the Pacific country.
Clients are not entitled to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension under the General Portability rules if they apply from overseas in these circumstances.
For more information see:
- General portability

chunks.title: Moving to a reciprocal agreement country — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Moving to a reciprocal agreement country
Special Portability is cancelled from the payday after the client's departure from their Pacific country of residence.
For all countries with a reciprocal agreement except the United Kingdom, the client should be advised to apply for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension under the reciprocal agreement on social security with that country.
International Services will reassess their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
## United Kingdom
If a client has gone to live in the United Kingdom their payments will be cancelled from the payday after the date they left the Special Portability country. Clients should be advised to apply for a United Kingdom pension when they arrive in the United Kingdom.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Reciprocal agreements

chunks.title: Obligations — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Obligations
Although a client may no longer be living in New Zealand they must tell the Ministry of Social Development straight away of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
Clients agree to do this by signing the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension application form, the Special Portability application form and the overseas details form.
Examples of changes and how to deal with these can be found in:
- Changes and reviews

chunks.title: Overpayments — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
An overpayment should be established for any period where a higher rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension was paid, but not due to the client.
If a client has been overpaid New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension at the full rate, the overpayment is always established for the net amount.
Inland Revenue will return the tax portion of the overpayment directly to Work and Income.
Special Portability overpayments are established for the gross amount as these payments are not taxed in New Zealand.
For more information:
- Current client debt Debt recovery maximum

chunks.title: Overseas bank accounts — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Overseas bank accounts
Payments of Special Portability can be made to an overseas bank account. The client will need to provide full bank account details on their application form or on the overseas details form that will be sent to them by International Services.
The overseas bank account number must be verified by the overseas bank or by supplying acceptable bank verification.
If the client will not know the overseas bank account number before they leave New Zealand there are two options for the first payments:
- make the first few payments to a New Zealand bank account (the client is responsible for any overseas transfer) or
- suspend all payments until details of the overseas bank account are known and pay arrears to the overseas bank account
Payments to overseas banks are made every 4 weeks on the New Zealand Superannuation payday. The Ministry of Social Development will meet the bank transaction costs incurred in transferring the payment to the overseas bank account.
Note for payment to clients living in Tokelau see:
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension changes for Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau residents [no link find out why]
For more information see:
- Payment
- Processing standards Bank account [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Overseas details request — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Overseas details request
International Services sends each client a 'Details from Overseas' form with their grant letter. When the client has arrived in the overseas country they are required to complete and return this form to International Services.
This 'Details from Overseas' form provides:
- details of the client's overseas bank account number, which must be verified by the overseas bank
- evidence that the client is residing in the country to which their application relates
If this form is not returned by the client within 6 weeks of their arrival overseas, payments will be suspended by International Services until the form is returned and entitlement confirmed.

chunks.title: Overseas pensions — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Overseas pensions
If a client is getting an overseas benefit or pension that is deductible from their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, the overseas pension continues to be a deduction from the maximum gross rate payable.
The rate of payment of Special Portability is then assessed based on this reduced rate.
## Example - single client with 15 years New Zealand residence
Gross weekly single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation/Veteran's Pension (as at 1 April 2026)
$595.57
Less weekly rate of overseas pension (NZD$100)
$100.00
Maximum gross New Zealand Superannuation/Veteran's Pension
$495.57
Special Portability payment rate using formula:
Maximum gross New Zealand Superannuation/Veteran's Pension (from above)
$495.57
multiply by 15
$7,433.55
then divide by 20
equals gross rate payable
$371.67
## Special Banking option
If a client's overseas pension is being paid into the Special Banking Option account, the account must be closed by International Services, who are responsible for administering the Special Banking Option payment method.
The client must be advised to make arrangements to have the overseas agency pay the overseas pension directly to their own bank account.

chunks.title: Payment — portability > special portability
chunks.text: Special Portability payments to New Zealand bank accounts are paid on the same day as all New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension payments. Clients wanting their payments made to an overseas bank account are paid differently. In general, payment must be made directly to the client. However, where there is good cause, the client's benefit can be paid to another person. For more information see: - Core policy Agents Note for payment to clients living in Tokelau see: - New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension changes for Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau [no link find out why] Grandparented non-qualified partner's payments are cancelled from the payday after the qualified partner leaves New Zealand. The maximum rate payable is the single sharing accommodation rate or the married, civil union or de facto relationship rate depending on the client's circumstances. If the client is receiving the single living alone rate, they will need to be transferred to the single sharing rate from the payday after their departure from New Zealand. Payments are not taxed in New Zealand but may be subject to tax in a specified Pacific country.

chunks.title: Extra help — portability > special portability
chunks.text: Extra help is not payable to a client receiving Special Portability and these payments are cancelled from the payday after departure from New Zealand. Clients applying from the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau are not entitled to Extra help assistance.

chunks.title: Rate of payment — portability > special portability
chunks.text: The rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid under Special Portability including clients who have applied from the Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau depends on the client's number of year's residence in New Zealand since age 20. 20 years or more New Zealand residence since age 20 - the maximum gross half married, civil union or de facto rate or single sharing accommodation rate (less any overseas pension) Between 10 and 20 years New Zealand residence since age 20 The rate payable is based on the following formula: - base rate multiplied by whole number of years of New Zealand residence (since 20) divided by 20 The base rate is either the gross single sharing accommodation or half married, civil union or de facto rate, depending on the client's relationship status. See the following example. Example - A single client has 10 years New Zealand residence since age 20 Single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation (as at 1 April 2026) $595.57 gross multiply by 10 $5,955.70 then divide by 20 equals maximum gross rate payable $297.78 Any overseas pension is deducted from the maximum gross rate paid before the formula is applied.

chunks.title: Qualifications — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Qualifications
For client’s to qualify for Special Portability of their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, they must:
- qualify for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and
- be resident and present in New Zealand when they apply or
- if intending to live in the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau be resident and present in one of these countries when they apply and
- be living in a Pacific country when each payment is made and
- not residing in a country New Zealand has a social security reciprocal agreement with, or a general portability country
Note if a client qualified for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension using one of the social security reciprocal agreements, and they are intending to leave New Zealand for more than 26 weeks, we need to check whether they can get this payment under Special Portability in that country.
## Non-qualified partners
Non-qualified partners are not entitled to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran’s pension in their own right and their payments will stop when they leave New Zealand.

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
If a client returns to live in New Zealand Special Portability payments are stopped by International Services from the payday after the return date.
The client must produce evidence of their date of return to New Zealand and complete a statement advising their intentions regarding their residence in New Zealand. Service Centres should send copies of these documents to International Services.
New Zealand Superannuation entitlement must be reviewed by the service centre. If the client is ordinarily resident in New Zealand payments can be increased to the full rate from the payday after the client's date of return, once Special Portability has been cancelled by International Services.
Veteran's Pension payments must be reviewed by the Veterans Pension Centre from the payday after return.
Note If the client is only returning to New Zealand temporarily, their payments will continue at the Special Portability rate as the client is not ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Qualifications
- Veteran's Pension Qualifications
- New Zealand Superannuation Deciding ordinarily resident in New Zealand
- Overpayments

chunks.title: Tax record certificates — portability > special portability
chunks.text:
## Tax record certificates
Special Portability is paid at a gross rate and is not taxed in New Zealand. The client may need to pay tax in the country they are living in and they will need to contact the tax authorities of that country for information.
SWIFTT will produce a tax record certificate each year that shows the total gross New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid as Special Portability for the past tax year. This will be posted to the client's overseas address.
Note the amount shown on these certificates will not include any payments made at the full rate before departure from New Zealand.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Taxation
- Veteran's Pension Taxation

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements
chunks.text:
## Introduction
New Zealand has 10 Reciprocal Agreements which cover 11 countries.
The agreements help former residents of one country access certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.

chunks.title: Additional criteria for Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When a client from Australia does not meet the residence qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind), their residence in Australia can be regarded as residence in New Zealand if the client meets the following conditions: - is resident and present in New Zealand and intends to remain for at least one year or has been present in New Zealand for at least 6 months prior to application and - has a total of 2 years continuous residence in Australia and/or New Zealand and - meets the severely disabled medical criteria and - has been an Australian resident for 12 months of which at least 6 months must have been continuous and - was resident in Australia or New Zealand at the date of severe disablement and - was a resident of Australia for a period of not less than one year at any time prior to the date of severe disablement The date of severe disablement is: - the date a person who applies for a Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) (for the severely disabled) was first assessed as meeting the criteria for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) (for the severely disabled) or - where evidence supports, an earlier date (only Services Australia - International Services and International Services, New Zealand, may agree on an earlier date) The date of severe disablement is usually the date of application. When a client applies for New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) in these circumstances International Services will undertake the necessary investigations to determine eligibility for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) (for the severely disabled) under the Agreement with Australia. International Services will send the client the necessary application forms and will arrange for the client to undergo the necessary medical assessments. Where a person has no other means of income support, you may need to consider alternative assistance until the outcome of their entitlement under the agreement with Australia is known. If another benefit is granted details of the client's disability should be entered in CMS.
