International Services will receive down lists of all Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) registrations and declines and will screen for possible eligibility to Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) (for the severely disabled) for clients who have lived in Australia. For more information contact International Services or see: - Severely disabled medical criteria - Supported Living Payment from 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Admission to Hospital — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Admission to Hospital
When a client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced.
The Australian pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the Australian pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner and the rate of an Australian pension for one partner is more than the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension the excess amount of the Australian pension is deducted from the other partner's New Zealand benefit or pension payment.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Hospitalisation in relevant Main Benefit
- Changes and Reviews in relevant Main Benefit

chunks.title: Admission to hospital or prison — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital or prison
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Australia the rate of payment must not be reduced if the client is in hospital for more than 13 weeks.
The New Zealand benefit should not be stopped if the client is imprisoned in Australia.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Australian pensions paid in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Australian pensions paid in New Zealand
The agreement with Australia allows clients who have resided in Australia to receive the following pensions when they are living in New Zealand:
- Age Pension
- Disability Support Pension (for the severely disabled)
- Carers payment (for partners of severely disabled Disability Support Pensioners)
## Note
- Australian pensions can be paid directly to the client by the Direct Payment Method or to a Special Banking Option account
- Australian pensions that meet the overseas pension criteria set out in section 187 of the Social Security Act 2018 are directly deducted from the clients New Zealand benefit or pension under section 189 of the Act if they are paid by the Direct Payment Method
- third country (means a country other than New Zealand or Australia) pensions for clients who have less than 10 years New Zealand residence will be treated as income as part of the Australian income and asset test when assessing the rate of Australian pension to be paid. In this instance, third country pensions will not be directly deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension
- the system will compare the total amount of third country pensions to the Australian Notional Pension rate and will deduct the higher amount from the New Zealand benefit or pension.
- third country pensions will be directly deducted from the rate of New Zealand payment if the client has 10 years or more New Zealand residence
- when an Australian pension exceeds the main benefit rate, the amount that exceeds the main benefit rate will be directly deducted from the partner's New Zealand benefit or pension if they receive one or from any Accommodation Supplement the client may receive as a non-beneficiary
- the Australian authorities can ask that a client be medically examined periodically to check they are still entitled to Disability Support Pension (severely disabled)
- any medical examinations are arranged by International Services and the account is paid by International Services.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Clients receiving Australian pensions
- Clients entitled to Australian pensions
- Direct deductions
- Other payments
- Payment options
- Extra Help
- Review Date

chunks.title: Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in Australia the rate payable will be the lesser of: - the Proportional Rate or - the Notional Rate New Zealand will pay the lesser of the Proportional Rate or Notional Rate. A grandparented non-qualified partner will not be paid New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Australia. Clients in a relationship can be paid the married, civil union or de facto rate in Australia regardless of the sex or gender of either partner.

chunks.title: Proportional Rate — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: The Proportional Rate of payment is calculated using the following formula: - count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence from age 20 to age 65 (include time spent in third countries if the client is not a permanent resident of Australia) and divide by - 540 and multiply by - the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation

chunks.title: Maximum Proportional Rate — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: The maximum proportional rate is the single sharing accommodation rate, or the married, civil union or de facto relationship rate, depending on the client's circumstances, less 15%.

chunks.title: Notional Rate — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: If the client is not a permanent resident of Australia, the Notional Rate is the amount of Australian Age Pension that would be payable if the client was not entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension and/or a pension from a third country. If the client is a permanent resident of Australia, the Notional Rate is the amount of Australian Age Pension that would be payable if the client was not entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension.

chunks.title: Client is not an Australian Permanent Resident (Special Category Visa-Unprotected) — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: If the client is not a citizen or permanent resident of Australia, and they have working age residence in a third country, that residence is counted as residence in New Zealand when calculating the client's proportional rate. If the client going to/living in Australia is not a permanent resident of Australia, and is in receipt of a third country pension that is deductible, the third country pension is directly deducted from the New Zealand rate payable.

chunks.title: Australian Permanent Residents (Permanent Resident Visa and Special Category Visa-Protected) — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: If the person going to or living in Australia, is a citizen or permanent resident of Australia and they are receiving a third country pension that is deductible, the third country pension is not deducted from the New Zealand rate payable and Services Australia - International Services treats it as income when assessing the Australian pension rate. Any Services Australia - International Services pension is not directly deducted from the rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension payable in Australia. Contact International Services or:

chunks.title: Calculation for Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Calculation for Supported Living Payment
When Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) is paid to a client in Australia the rate payable will be the lesser of:
- the Proportional Rate or
- the Notional Rate
## Proportional Rate
The Proportional Rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence from age 20 to date of severe disablement and divide by
- the aggregate of the periods of working age residence (between the ages of 20 and the date of severe disablement) in Australia and New Zealand up until the date Services Australia - International Services assesses the person as severely disabled and multiply by
- the maximum rate of Supported Living Payment
## Notional Rate
The Notional Rate is the amount of Australian Disability Support Pension (for the severely disabled) that would be payable if the client was not entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Note
- any Services Australia - International Services pension is not directly deducted from the rate of New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) payable in Australia
- if the person going to/living in Australia is not a permanent resident of Australia, and is in receipt of a third country pension, this pension is directly deducted from the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled)
- if the person going to/living in Australia is a permanent resident of Australia and is in receipt of a third country pension, it will not be deducted from the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) payable, but Services Australia - International Services will treat it as income when assessing the Australian pension rate
- the New Zealand income test will not be applied to the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) made to clients in Australia
- Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Australia.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Methods of payment in Australia

chunks.title: Change in income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When a client is getting Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) that is being paid in Australia, the client will need to advise Services Australia - International Services when there is any change in their income.
Services Australia - International Services may need to take the income into account and adjust the rate of the client's Australian Disability Support Pension (for the severely disabled). This may result in the New Zealand rate changing.
## Income details
The client must provide Services Australia - International Services with details of all income they receive in Australia or New Zealand.
This includes any Child Support payments they get that are paid through Inland Revenue.
## For more information contact or see:
- International Services

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International Services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension paid in Australia when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a de facto relationship or
- a married or civil union client becomes single through separation; the marriage or civil union is dissolved; or the death of their partner
When a client enters or is already in a relationship they can be paid the married, civil union or de facto rate in Australia regardless of the sex or gender of either partner.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for Australian pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for Australian pensions
A client is obliged to advise Work and Income of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualification and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also required to provide any information required by the Australian authorities to ensure that they are still entitled to their Australian pension paid in New Zealand. Any such information provided to you by the client should be forwarded to International Services
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Admission to Hospital
- Clients going overseas
- Death of a client in New Zealand
- Reviews and Appeals
- Taxation in relevant Main Benefit

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Australia
Clients have an obligation to advise Services Australia - International Services and MSD when there is any change in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension or the rate payable such as:
- Admission to hospital or prison
- Change in income
- Change in relationship status
- Child turns 18
- Death in Australia
- Move to another country
- Overpayments
- Recovery of New Zealand debt from Australian pension
- Return to New Zealand
- Reviews and Appeals
MSD may also review a New Zealand benefit or pension in Australia at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
## Responsibilities
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions paid in Australia.
Clients getting New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) will need to complete a Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks and may be required to undergo medical examinations for review purposes.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment paid in Australia.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier.

chunks.title: Clients entitled to Australian pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Clients entitled to Australian pensions
A client must apply for any benefit or pension they may be entitled to from Australia if:
- they are in receipt of or applying for a New Zealand pension or benefit and
- they use the agreement to qualify for the New Zealand pension or benefit or
- they have lived in Australia at any time since the age of 20
International Services will decide whether a client needs to test their entitlement to an Australian pension and will contact the client direct if necessary.
Should the client contact you for help in completing or forwarding on the application it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation as listed in the Australian application form is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies)
If the client refuses to apply for any Australian pension to which they may be entitled you should contact International Services.
## Partners
Where the partner of a client says they have overseas residence that might give them entitlement to an overseas pension, you should also ask the partner to test their entitlement to an overseas pension. This is regardless of whether they are getting a New Zealand benefit or pension or not.

chunks.title: Clients from Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Clients from Australia
When a former resident of Australia applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they are receiving an Australian pension or if they may be entitled to one.
All clients who have lived in Australia for 1 year or more, regardless of where they were born, must complete the residence details section of the application form and this information must be entered in CMS.
This is irrespective of whether the client uses the agreement with Australia to qualify for a New Zealand benefit or pension, or qualifies under the New Zealand domestic legislation.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Australian pensions paid in New Zealand
- Clients entitled to Australian pensions
- Other payments
## Client applies on or after 1 July 2017
If a client applies for New Zealand Superannuation at age 65 on or after 1 July 2017 they will need to meet the residential qualifications based solely on their New Zealand residence.
If they do not have sufficient New Zealand residence, they will only be able to use their Australian residence at the date they reach the qualifying age for the residence at the date they reach the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension.
For more information see:
- Qualifying age for Australian Age Pension

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When a client is receiving an Australian pension or a New Zealand benefit or pension by virtue of the agreement, the normal absence provisions apply to the New Zealand benefit or pension they are receiving. If a client in receipt of New Zealand Superannuation, Veterans Pension or Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) intends going to Australia they may be able to receive payment of their New Zealand benefit or pension in Australia depending on how long they intend to go for. Applications for New Zealand Superannuation, Veterans Pension and Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) in Australia can be made in New Zealand or from Australia although it is preferable that they apply after arrival in Australia, as the New Zealand payment rate will depend on the rate assessed by Services Australia - International Services.

chunks.title: Note — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: Applications for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension to be paid in Australia must be made within 26 weeks after arrival in Australia and within 4 weeks of arrival for Supported Living Payment (severely disabled). If the Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) client intends to stay longer than the allowable 4 weeks, they can take their health practitioner or specialist reports with them to Australia, as this may help avoid any possible delays in their application for the Australian Disability Support Pension (severely disabled). From 1 July 2017, when a client leaves New Zealand for Australia, their continued entitlement while in Australia will depend on their age and their intention on the date of departure from New Zealand. If a client intends to live in Australia and wants their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension to continue they must apply for the Australian Age Pension within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand. They will need to contact Services Australia - International Services. If they already receive an Australian Age Pension they must advise Services Australia - International Services that they have arrived in Australia to live. New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension payments will continue for up to 26 weeks when applications were received before 1 July 2017. Applications we receive on or after 1 July 2017 and if the client has reached the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension, we will continue to pay New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension for up to 26 weeks. If the client has not reached the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension will stop from the day after their departure from New Zealand. They will need to lodge a new application under the 2017 Agreement when they have reached the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension. If a client goes to Australia for a holiday or visit but, they don't intend to live there then, their payments can continue for up to 26 weeks provided that they return to New Zealand within 30 weeks. If they don't return within 30 weeks their payments will stop and they may have to pay this amount back.

chunks.title: Applications for Supported Living Payment in Australia from 1 July 2017 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: If a client leaves New Zealand to live in Australia, their Supported Living Payment will continue to be payable for up to 4 weeks after their departure from New Zealand provided that they apply for Supported Living Payment overseas within 4 weeks of that date. We will back-date Supported Living Payment overseas up-to a maximum of 12 months from the date of the initial application being lodged with Services Australia - International Services.

chunks.title: For more information — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: Contact International Services or see: - New Zealand Benefits and Pensions in Australia - Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Clients receiving Australian pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving Australian pensions
When a client advises that they are receiving payments from Australia you will need to find out the type of payment in order to determine if the Australian pension should be a direct deduction from the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
It is important that the information is obtained as quickly as possible to enable the client's correct entitlement to be assessed. If a client refuses to provide information regarding their Australian pension their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or payment suspended.
If the client is unable to provide full documentation of the payments you will need to grant and suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension from application date until written verification is received. The client will need to contact Services Australia on freephone 0800 441 248 to request the written verification. You can suggest that the client request this information be faxed to them through your office to avoid delays in commencing payment.
The written verification must contain the following information:
- the rate and frequency of payment in Australian currency
- the reason for the grant, such as age, disablement, or war service
- the full name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment, such as Services Australia or the Australian Department of Veterans' Affairs
## Note
The client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Australian pension. If they do not or refuse to comply their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or payment can be suspended. This will be done by International Services.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- War Pensions
- Direct deductions
- Extra help

chunks.title: Commencement of payment in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Commencement of payment in Australia
When a client applies for their New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid in Australia before their departure from New Zealand, payments in Australia will start on the first payday after their departure from New Zealand.
When a client applies from Australia the New Zealand benefit or pension will start on:
- the date they become entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension
- the date they applied for the New Zealand benefit or
- the date the client applied for an Australian pension
whichever is the latest date.
Services Australia - International Services will forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Methods of payment in Australia
- Rate payable in Australia

chunks.title: Death in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Death in Australia
The normal procedures for cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions apply on the death of a client receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension in Australia.
Generally, Services Australia - International Services will advise International Services of the death of a client in Australia and International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Funeral Grants
A Funeral Grant is not payable for clients who were living in Australia at the time of their death.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on death follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients who were also receiving an Australian pension that has been recorded on SWIFTT.
The executor of the client's estate will need to contact the Australian authorities directly if they require any details of the Australian pension.
International Services will send the following information to the Australian authorities:
- the clients name
- date of death and
- the name and address of the administrator of the estate
## Note
- the executor of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen in SWIFTT so that International Services can advise the Australian authorities
- Terminal Benefit should be paid at the rate of the New Zealand benefit payable as at the date of death
## Changes to benefit rate payable
Rates of main benefits being paid as part of terminal benefit are adjusted to reflect changes in the rate payable arising from legislative amendments, such as the $25 net increase in main benefit rates on 1 April 2020 (only). This also includes when benefit rates change in the Annual General Adjustment that occurs on 1 April each year.

chunks.title: Decision Guidelines — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Decision Guidelines
To help you to decide whether a New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from:
- the date a client is granted an Australian benefit or pension or
- the first available date
Use the following guidelines:
- was the client aware that they may need to repay some of the New Zealand benefit or pension once an Australian benefit or pension was granted?
- did the client receive the payment of the Australian pension in good faith?
- has the client spent or committed the overseas payment without realising that it was liable to be directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit?
- is the Australian pension money still in their bank account?
- did the client deliberately or intentionally not advise that they were receiving an Australian pension?
- has there been a delay in reviewing the New Zealand benefit or pension after receiving advice of the grant of the Australian pension?

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
When a client is receiving an Australian pension paid by the Australian Government, the gross amount is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit if they are paid by the Direct Payment Option.
The Australian pension is deducted from:
- the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and
- the net rate of any other benefit, including Accommodation Supplement
When a client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Australian pension is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services
If you receive information from a client about an Australian pension, a fax should be sent to International Services with verification of the rate, type of Australian pension or benefit, the grant date and the name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already receiving an Australian pension at the time a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process.
Under the agreement with Australia a client can elect to:
- have their Australian pension paid to their own bank account and receive a reduced rate of New Zealand benefit or pension through the direct payment option or
- have the Australian pension paid through the Special Banking Option and receive the full rate of New Zealand benefit or pension
## Note
International Services must be advised of all clients who are receiving an Australian pension. It is International Services responsibility to carry out New Zealand benefit or pension reviews required when the Australian pension deduction is being up-dated or reviewed.
Any other reviews of the client's New Zealand benefit, such as a change of relationship status or a change of chargeable income, should be completed by the case manager.
War pensions cannot be paid via the Special Banking Option.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Payments from overseas Couples getting overseas pensions
Also see:
- Clients receiving Australian pensions
- Extra Help
- Payment options
- Review date

chunks.title: Direct Payment Option — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Direct Payment Option
If a client does not choose to have their Australian pension paid through the Special Banking Option, it will be paid directly to their own bank account.
Under this method of payment:
- Australian pension payments are made every 4 weeks
- payment will be converted at the rate of exchange applicable on the day the bank credits their account
- the client receives the gross rate of the Australian pension and is responsible for any tax liability on it
- the amount deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension will be based on the previous month's exchange rate for the Australian pension
- if the client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension the rate will be automatically recalculated in SWIFTT each month using the previous month's Australian exchange rate shown in SELXT
- if the client is receiving any other New Zealand benefit or pension International Services will manually review the rate on a monthly basis
- there is no due/paid assessment at the end of each year to take into account the exact exchange rate that the Australian pension was paid to the client
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Initial grant of Australian pension

chunks.title: Accommodation Supplement — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Accommodation Supplement
When a client is receiving a deductible Australian pension that exceeds the New Zealand main benefit rate, the excess amount will be directly deducted from any Accommodation Supplement the client receives.
You will need to calculate the amount that the client would be entitled to receive by way of a New Zealand benefit or pension and the rate of Accommodation Supplement that would be payable alongside that benefit or pension. The Australian pension should be deducted from the total New Zealand benefit and Accommodation Supplement, and the balance will be the actual rate of Accommodation Supplement payable.
## Manual deduction
You will need to manually deduct this amount in SWIFTT using the SNSRA screen.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Payments from Overseas Accommodation Supplement examples
## Disability Allowance
When a client is receiving a deductible Australian pension that is considered to be in the nature of a disability allowance, it will be directly deducted from any New Zealand Disability Allowance, before it is able to be deducted from any other New Zealand benefit.
The Disability Support Pension is not in the nature of a Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Initial grant of Australian pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Initial grant of Australian pension
When a client has signed an authority for the release of information and has agreed to have their Australian pension arrears paid to Work and Income, the Australian authorities will:
- provide details of any grant of an Australian pension to International Services and
- pay the Australian pension arrears to Work and Income
This will enable International Services to:
- add the Australian pension details to SWIFTT
- add the correct direct deduction amount to the New Zealand benefit or pension using the INCMA screen in SWIFTT
- review the New Zealand benefit or pension from the date of grant of the Australian pension and
- recover any overpayment of New Zealand benefit or pension paid for the same period as the Australian pension or
- pay the Australian pension arrears to the client
## Information not released
If the client has not signed an authority for the Australian authorities to release information, the client must provide verification of the Australian pension details or the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and Australia allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- Australian working age residence between 20 years of age and the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension (up to a maximum of 45 years) can be regarded as residence in New Zealand to help a client meet the residence qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- New Zealand working age residence between 20 years of age and the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension (up to a maximum of 45 years) can be regarded as residence in Australia to help a client meet the residence qualifications for some Australian pensions
- some Australian pensions and payments can be paid in New Zealand
- some New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid in Australia
- overpayments can be recovered by one country on behalf of the other country
- War pensions from either country are not included in the agreement, however, the New Zealand Veterans Pension is covered
- the agreement covers clients residing on or intending to reside on, or with residence on, Norfolk Island
If a client advises you that they are moving to Australia, thinking about moving to Australia, or looking at a long term trip to Australia you should contact International Services who will provide you with all the information needed to help clients make their decision and to ensure they receive their correct entitlement.
## Clients qualifying before 1 July 2017
A new Social Security Agreement between New Zealand and Australia is effective from 1 July 2017.
Clients who were receiving a New Zealand pension or benefit under the 2002 Agreement will continue to receive their payments under that Agreement. However, if their entitlement to a pension or benefit is cancelled on or after 1 July 2017, they will need to reapply under the provisions of the 2017 Agreement.
Clients who are moving to Australia or thinking about moving to Australia on or after 1 July 2017 will be covered by the 2017 Agreement.
Clients returning to New Zealand from Australia on or after 1 July 2017, who don't meet the New Zealand residence requirements in their own right, are covered by the 2017 Agreement. You should contact International Services who will provide you with all the information needed to help these clients.

chunks.title: Liaison agencies — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Liaison agencies
Australia and New Zealand each has its own agency for administering the "Agreement on Social Security between the Government of New Zealand and the Government of Australia" (which is part of the Social Welfare (Reciprocity with Australia) Order 2017 in New Zealand). These agencies are:
- Australia: Services Australia - International Services
- New Zealand: International Services, whose contact details are:
International ServicesMinistry of Social DevelopmentPO Box 27178Wellington 6146New Zealand
Freephone: 0800 777 227 - if calling from New Zealand
Freephone: 1800 150 479 - if calling from Australia
Fax: 64 4 918 0159

chunks.title: Methods of payment in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment in Australia
When a client receives a New Zealand benefit or pension in Australia they can:
- choose to have payments made by direct credit into a New Zealand bank account or
- to a bank account they hold in Australia
## New Zealand bank account
Payments made to a New Zealand bank account are credited fortnightly. If a client chooses to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account and then transferred to an overseas bank account, the client must pay the cost of the transfer of the funds.
## Australian bank account
Payments made to an Australian bank account are credited every 4 weeks. If a client chooses to have money paid directly to an Australian bank account, Work and Income meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
If a client applies to have their New Zealand benefit or pension paid in Australia before they leave New Zealand, there are three options for the first payment being made into an Australian bank account:
- payment can be made to an overseas bank account if the client has provided proof of their bank account
- the first payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the Australian bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the Australian bank account are given to International Services. Once account details are advised, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the Australian account with the first payment.
Contact International Services

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client intends to live in a country other than New Zealand or Australia for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
If a client living in Australia is getting a New Zealand pension or benefit and leaves Australia for more than 26 weeks at one time, their New Zealand payment will stop from the date they left Australia.
The client may still be entitled to get a New Zealand benefit or pension if:
- they qualify for the New Zealand benefit or pension due to their previous residence in New Zealand and
- they are moving to a country which has an agreement with New Zealand
Payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension must stop 26 weeks from the day the client leaves Australia. The client can check whether they qualify to get a New Zealand benefit or pension in the country they have moved to.
## Moving to a non-agreement country
New Zealand Superannuation, Veterans Pension and Supported Living Payment cannot continue being paid to a client, who leaves Australia to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand.
If the client is in New Zealand and is getting the New Zealand benefit or pension by using their Australian residence to meet the New Zealand residence qualification, they may not be entitled to have the New Zealand benefit or pension paid in another country. The client will need to check whether they will keep getting their benefit or pension in another country.
## Moving to a Pacific country
New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension clients need to be ordinarily resident in and present in New Zealand at the date they apply for payment overseas of a New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
Unless they move to and apply from the Cooks Islands, Niue or Tokelau under the Special Portability arrangement with Pacific countries.
## Or contact
- International Services

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions in Australia
Under the agreement with Australia the following New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid to former New Zealand residents who live or intend to live in Australia:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veterans Pension
- Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled)
The rules are different depending on whether the client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension and is moving to Australia, or if they are already living in Australia at the time they apply.
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Sole Parent Support
- Emergency Benefits
- Supported Living Payment (for care of sick or infirm)
- Jobseeker Support
- Unsupported Child's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Supported Living Payment clients living in Australia
- Supported Living Payment clients moving to Australia
- Supported Living Payment from 15 July 2013
- Superannuitants living in Australia
- Superannuitants moving to Australia
- Veterans living in Australia
- Veterans moving to Australia
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main Benefit

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
The agreement with Australia sets out additional conditions that a client must meet when they meet all the qualifications for the following New Zealand benefit or pension except for residence:
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind)
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veteran's Pension
The additional conditions are different for each benefit or pension so it is important that you check the conditions for each benefit or pension carefully.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Clients from Australia
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Australia
- Welfare reforms impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Australia
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefit
- Jobseeker Support
- Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit
- Sole Parent Support
- Supported Living Payment (for care of sick or infirm)
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
Case managers are responsible for determining eligibility for New Zealand benefits and pensions based on New Zealand legislation and the agreement with Australia in respect of people residing in New Zealand.
The only exception is New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) when the applicant has not had 2 years continuous residence within New Zealand. These claims must be decided by International Services.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When a client from Australia meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except for residence, they may qualify under the agreement with Australia. The agreement with Australia allows Australian residence between 20 years of age and the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension (up to a maximum of 45 years) to be regarded as residence in New Zealand to help a client meet the residence qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation. Australian residence that can be counted includes residence in Australia on a temporary residence visa or non-permanent visa. However, these clients must also meet the following additional criteria: - be resident and present in New Zealand and intend to remain here for at least 1 year or have been present in New Zealand for at least 6 months prior to application and - have a total of 10 years residence in Australia or New Zealand since the age of 20, 5 years of which must have been since the age of 50 and - have been an Australian resident for 12 months since the age of 20, of which at least 6 months must be continuous The client must also: - meet the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation and - qualify for an Australian pension under the Agreement This includes clients who qualify for an Australian pension at a zero rate of payment. Australian pensions that fall within the criteria of sections 187-191 of the Social Security Act 2018 and sections 118-136 of the Social Security Regulations 2018 will be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation. If a client is aged 65 or over and has been granted New Zealand Superannuation payments into Australia before 1 July 2017, they can continue to receive New Zealand Superannuation in Australia. If their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation stops after this date (eg. due to absence from Australia), then they will need to reapply under the 2017 Agreement. If a client turns 65 on or after 1 July 2017 and they are living in Australia, or intend to move there from New Zealand on or after that date, they will need to meet the qualifying age for the Australia Age Pension to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation payable under the 2017 Agreement.

chunks.title: Qualifying age for Australian Age Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: The qualifying age for clients is explained in the table below: Clients born between Qualify for the Australian Age Pension at age 1 July 1952 to 31 December 1953 65 years and 6 months* 1 January 1954 to 30 June 1955 66 years 1 July 1955 to 31 December 1956 66 years and 6 months* From 1 January 1957 67 years * 6 months means at the end of a 6-month period. For example: For a birthday on The 6-month period ends on And the qualifying date is 1 January 30 June 1 July 30 April 29 October 30 October 1 May 31 October 1 November 14 May 13 November 14 November 31 August 28 February or29 February in a leap year 1 March Calculating months when combining periods of residence A client's residence is used to calculate their entitlement to a New Zealand pension or benefit as well as the rate payable. Any incomplete months are rounded up for residence calculation purposes. For example, 45 months and 1 day becomes 46 months.

chunks.title: SWIFTT — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When New Zealand Superannuation is granted using the agreement with Australia you will need to enter the reciprocal entitlement code (13) in the NDTA screen. For more information contact International Services or see: - New Zealand Superannuation Residency - Clients from Australia - New Zealand benefit and pensions in Australia - Superannuitants living in Australia - Overpayments

chunks.title: Other payments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Other payments
When a client is receiving other payments, such as interest or rent from investments or properties they own in Australia, the payments will be treated in the same way as income earned in New Zealand.
You need to convert the income to New Zealand dollars by applying the current exchange rate using the SELXT screen in SWIFTT.
If you are unsure how the calculation works you should contact International Services by phone on 0800 777 227.
If a client is receiving a benefit or pension from a third country this will only be a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client has 10 years New Zealand residence.
For more information contact International Services by phone on 0800 777 227 or see:
- Payments from overseas

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand benefit or pension being paid in Australia is overpaid International Services will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment
- their review and appeal rights and
- the relevant legislation under which the debt is established
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deduction from any New Zealand benefit or pension that the client is receiving.
If the client is no longer receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension they will need to make arrangements to repay the debt.
## Note
- some overpayments may be able to be recovered from the client's Australian pension if a New Zealand benefit is no longer payable
- if a client applies for a review, or appeals a decision on the establishment of a debt or the rate of recovery, recovery action will be suspended until the outcome of that review or appeal is known
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Recovery of New Zealand Debt from Australian pension
- Review and Appeals

chunks.title: Payment options — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Payment options
When a client is receiving an Australian pension through Services Australia - International Services (the Australian liaison agency) later referred to as a Services Australia - International Services pension, they can choose to have their Australian pension paid by the:
- Direct Payment Option or
- Special Banking Option
## Note
Clients will be asked to select a payment option when they are sent an Australian pension application pack by International Services
- clients can change from one payment option to the other at any time but can generally only join the Special Banking Option once
- all payment option changes are completed by International Services
- a client can authorise the Australian authorities to pay arrears of their Australian pension direct to Work and Income regardless of the payment option they choose for regular payments
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Rate payable in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When a New Zealand benefit or pension is paid to a client in Australia, the rate of payment is calculated by a specific formula set out in the agreement with Australia. The calculation is based on the client's working age (between the ages of 20 and 65) residence in New Zealand. The formula for calculating New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension is different to the calculation for New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled).

chunks.title: Specific circumstances — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: - periods of working age residence in a third country can be regarded as periods of working age residence in New Zealand for the purposes of calculating the New Zealand rate payable if that person is not a permanent resident of Australia and they are applying for New Zealand Superannuation, Veterans Pension or Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) to be paid in Australia - the rate of Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) payable in Australia is calculated on the proportions of New Zealand and Australian residence. For example, if a person who lived in New Zealand for 10 years since the age of 20 and then moved to Australia and became severely disabled at age 35, New Zealand would be responsible for 10 of the 15 years, and would pay two thirds of the Supported Living Payment rate to that person - there is no provision to include payment for a grandparented non-qualified partner in a New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension. The partner can only be paid in Australia if they meet the qualifications in their own right - when Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) is paid in Australia the client's partner can be included - when a client enters or is in a relationship they can be paid the married, civil union or de facto rate in Australia regardless of the sex or gender of either partner - no payment is made to a client who has lived in New Zealand for less than 12 continuous months since the age of 20 - Supported Living Payment clients who are under the age of 21 will not be entitled to payment in Australia as they will not meet the 12 continuous months of New Zealand residence requirement - the New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Australian pension. The Australian pension is not directly deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension before payment is made in Australia - if the client is a permanent resident in Australia (i.e. an Australian citizen or the holder of an Australian permanent residents visa), any pensions from third countries are not directly deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension

chunks.title: Recovery of New Zealand debt from Australian pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Recovery of New Zealand debt from Australian pension
If a New Zealand benefit is no longer payable but the debtor is in receipt of a pension or benefit paid by Services Australia - International Services, the overpayment may be able to be recovered from the client's Australian pension.
The minimum debt amount that New Zealand can ask Australia to recover is Australian $400 or New Zealand's equivalent.
The debt must have been established within 5 years of the request for recovery being made and it must be a social security debt.
## Note
- Services Australia - International Services must be sent the appropriate debt recovery liaison form by International Services
- this must be accompanied by the certificate of debt compliance
- if debt recovery is appealed by the client, recovery must be suspended until the outcome of the review is known
- it is not possible to total a number of debts established over different dates in a 5 year period to reach the minimum debt amount. Each debt must have been established on the same date, or as part of the same review (eg where you have added some debts for a review on one day but have not completed adding debts until the next day)
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reviews and Appeals
- Client Support - Debt Management [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for an Australian pension. International Services will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not respond to requests to apply for an Australian pension.
International Services will talk to clients about the reasons why they must apply, including:
- it is their right as they have lived in Australia
- clients must claim any pension they may be entitled to in Australia if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from Australia
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate, and the rate of Australian pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended but the Australian pension will still be paid

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Australia and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, payment of the New Zealand benefit will continue to be paid at the same rate as when they were living in Australia. This is because the client will not be considered as ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
When a client receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Australia returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their benefit can be reviewed from the date of return to New Zealand.
If a client living in Australia moves back to New Zealand on or after 1 July 2017, they will qualify for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension at age 65 provided they can meet the New Zealand residential requirements. They can only count their Australian residence towards these requirements under the Agreement if they have met the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension. If they do not have the required New Zealand residence, they will qualify for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension when they have either accumulated this or reached the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension under the 2017 Agreement.
If a client returns to New Zealand for more than 26 weeks they should contact their local Work and Income office. They should be asked to complete a personal statement confirming the:
- date they left Australia
- date they intend to return to Australia
If their intention is to live in New Zealand they should be asked for the following:
- verification of their New Zealand bank account
- verification of their Inland Revenue number (if not already recorded)
The client will need to contact Services Australia - International Services to advise them of their intention to live in New Zealand.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Return to New Zealand in relevant Main benefit
- Qualifying age for Australian Age Pension

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Review date
International Services will review a New Zealand benefit or pension from the date a client is granted an Australian benefit or pension, or when the rate of an Australian benefit or pension is increased or decreased.
However, you can use the decision guidelines to review the New Zealand benefit or pension from the first available date.
If you have a case where you feel an overpayment should be established you should contact International Services to discuss it.
Where an Australian benefit or pension is altered, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the change.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Reviews and Appeals — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Reviews and Appeals
If a client is unhappy with any decision regarding their Australian pension being paid in New Zealand they will need to write to Services Australia - International Services. Reviews and appeals must be lodged with Services Australia - International Services within 13 weeks of receiving advice of the original decision. This is because if the review is decided in the client's favour, back payment can only be paid if the request is lodged within this 13 week period.
International Services is responsible for any reviews and appeals in regards to the interpretation of the agreement with Australia and the effect of Australian benefits and pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions.
The New Zealand review and appeal process applies to any other decision regarding New Zealand benefits or pensions such as charging income or change in relationship status.
For further information contact International Services or see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Severely disabled medical criteria — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Severely disabled medical criteria
When a client from Australia does not meet the residence qualifications for New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind), their residence in Australia can only be regarded as residence in New Zealand if they meet all of the additional criteria for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) including the severely disabled medical criteria.
The client needs to be medically assessed as severely disabled. Severely disabled means a person who:
- has a physical, psychiatric or intellectual impairment (or a combination of these) which makes the person, without taking into account any other factor, totally unable to work for at least the next 2 years and who is unable to improve their ability to participate in a programme of assistance or a rehabilitation programme within the next 2 years or
- is permanently blind
## Note
When a client applies for New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury disability or totally blind) in these circumstances International Services will test for Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) if necessary.
International Services will send the client the necessary application forms and will also arrange for the client to undergo the necessary medical assessments.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Special Banking Option — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option
When a client is receiving a Services Australia - International Services pension they can choose to have it paid into a Special Banking Option account by the Australian authorities. The client will then receive the full rate of their New Zealand benefit or pension.
The advantages of this option are:
- that payment is made every week or 2 weeks (depending on the pay cycle for their New Zealand Benefit)
- tax is already deducted
- the client is not affected by fluctuations in the exchange rate
## Note
- clients may elect to join the Special Banking Option at any time but cannot re-join once they have chosen to cancel the Special Banking Option (there are exceptions, contact International Services)
- when a client has a partner they must both choose the same payment option
- the Special Banking Option is not suitable for clients whose Australian pension is higher than (or likely to be higher than) the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Special Banking Option applications
- Initial grant of Australian pension

chunks.title: Special Banking Option applications — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option applications
When a client chooses the Special Banking Option for their Services Australia - International Services pension they will be sent an application pack from International Services containing:
- an application for the Special Banking Option
- an application for a Special Bank Account and
- an Authority to Release Information form (this form allows us to share information regarding pension entitlements with Services Australia - International Services)
All three forms must be fully completed and forwarded to International Services for processing.
## Note
- when a client has a partner they must both choose the same payment option
- the client can change from the direct payment method to the Special Banking Option at any time
- if the client has changed from the Special Banking Option to the Direct Payment Method generally they cannot re-join the Special Banking Option
- the client does not have access to the Special Banking Option account that the Australian pension is paid into as it is simply a holding account for funds that are to be paid to MSD

chunks.title: Superannuitants living in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Superannuitants living in Australia
Under the agreement with Australia a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation when they are living in Australia, provided they meet the Australian Age Pension qualifications.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Australia, they can get New Zealand Superannuation if:
- they meet the New Zealand Superannuation qualifications (except for being ordinarily resident in New Zealand) and
- they meet the qualifications for the Australian Age Pension (including the qualifying pension age)
- they are a New Zealand citizen and able to get an Australian Special Category Visa, an Australian citizen, or an Australian Permanent Resident (New Zealand Permanent Residence Visa holders will not automatically qualify) and
- they are resident in Australia and are either in Australia or New Zealand at the time they apply and
- they intend to live in Australia for at least 1 year or have been living in Australia for at least 26 weeks and
- they have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since age 20 and
- they have a total of 10 years residence in New Zealand and/or their Australia working age residence since the age of 20, 5 years of which must be since the age of 50 (Australian residence that can be counted includes residence in Australia on a temporary residence visa or non-permanent visa)
Note the qualifying pension age in Australia is different from the age for New Zealand Superannuation. The client must be the qualifying pension age in Australia to get their New Zealand Superannuation payments in Australia.
If the client is not entitled to an Australian Age Pension, the client is not entitled to any payments from New Zealand.
## Partners
If the client has a partner, the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
Clients in a relationship can be paid the married, civil union or de facto rate in Australia regardless of the sex or gender of either partner.
The client must let Services Australia - International Services and our International Services know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances. Especially if they intend to leave Australia to live in another country.
## International Services
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Superannuitants moving to Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: Under the agreement with Australia a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation when they are living in Australia, provided they meet the Australian Age Pension qualifications. When a New Zealand resident is moving to Australia, they can get their New Zealand Superannuation payments in Australia if they: - meet the New Zealand qualifications (except for being ordinarily resident in New Zealand) - meet the qualifications for the Australian Age Pension (including the qualifying pension age and income or asset criteria) - are a New Zealand citizen and able to get an Australian Special Category Visa, an Australian citizen, or an Australian Permanent Resident (New Zealand Permanent Residence Visa holders will not automatically qualify) - are present in Australia at the time they apply - intend to live in Australia for at least 1 year or have been living in Australia for at least 26 weeks - have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since age 20 and - have a total of 10 years residence in New Zealand and/or Australia working age residence since the age of 20, 5 years of which must be since the age of 50 (Australian residence that can be counted includes residence in Australia on a temporary residence visa or a non-permanent visa) Note the qualifying pension age in Australia is different from the age for New Zealand Superannuation. The client must be the qualifying pension age in Australia to get their New Zealand Superannuation payments in Australia. If the client is not entitled to an Australian Age Pension, the client is not entitled to any payment from New Zealand.

chunks.title: Payment in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: The client must contact Services Australia - International Services within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand to apply for the Australian Age Pension and for their New Zealand Superannuation to be paid in Australia. Their New Zealand Superannuation will continue being paid at the current rate until the beginning of the 27th week, or the date their Australian Age Pension payments start - whichever is the earliest date. If the client does not apply for payment of New Zealand Superannuation in Australia within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand, and they do not return to New Zealand within 30 weeks of leaving, they will have no entitlement for the whole period of absence from New Zealand. If the client is intending to move to Australia and is not currently getting New Zealand Superannuation, their application can be made after they have left New Zealand under the portable agreement provisions. However, entitlement must be established using New Zealand Superannuation qualifications before they can receive their payments in Australia.

chunks.title: Partners — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: If the client has a partner, the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right. Clients in a relationship can be paid the married, civil union or de facto rate in Australia regardless of the sex or gender of either partner.

chunks.title: Grandparented non-qualified partner — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: If a grandparented non-qualified partner is currently included in the client's New Zealand Superannuation, they will lose their grandparented non-qualified partner status after 26 weeks in Australia, or on the date the client starts getting their Australian Age Pension payments - whichever is the earlier date. If the grandparented non-qualified partner returns to New Zealand, they will not be eligible for New Zealand Superannuation until they qualify in their own right. For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When a client from Australia meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Australia. The agreement with Australia allows Australian residence to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind). However, these clients must also meet additional criteria and these applications must be decided by International Services The client must also: - meet additional criteria including different medical criteria and - qualify for an Australian pension that is payable under the agreement which will be directly deducted from New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) Single clients living in Australia can only continue to receive a Supported Living Payment until they meet the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension. At that time, they are required to apply for New Zealand Superannuation. They must contact International Services when they meet the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension Clients who are married, in a civil union or in a de facto relationship can continue to receive a Supported Living Payment until the younger partner reaches the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension. At that time, the clients are required to apply for New Zealand Superannuation. They must contact International Services when this happens. To apply for New Zealand Superannuation, they will need to contact International Services.

chunks.title: Applications for Supported Living Payment in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: If a client leaves New Zealand to live in Australia, their Supported Living Payment will continue to be payable for up to 4 weeks after their departure from New Zealand provided that they apply for Supported Living Payment overseas within 4 weeks of that date. We will back-date Supported Living Payment overseas for a maximum of 12 months up-to the date of the initial application being lodged with Services Australia - International Services. Under the Agreement, New Zealanders under the age of 21 and receiving a Supported Living Payment overseas cannot receive their Supported Living Payment overseas, or a Disability Support Pension, in Australia.

chunks.title: SWIFTT — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is granted using the agreement with Australia you will need to enter the reciprocal entitlement code (13) in the SDT1A screen.

chunks.title: For more information — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: Contact International Services or see: - Supported Living Payment Residence - Clients from Australia - New Zealand benefits and pensions in Australia - Supported Living Payment clients living in Australia - Supported Living Payment from 15 July 2013 - Qualifying age for Australian Age Pension

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment client moving to Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: Under the agreement with Australia a client can be paid the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) when they are living in Australia if they meet the severely disabled medical criteria. When a Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) client advises that they intend to move to Australia, the benefit can continue for up 4 weeks from the date the client leaves New Zealand if the client: - is leaving New Zealand with the intention of becoming ordinarily resident in Australia and - applies for the Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) under the agreement within 4 weeks of their departure from New Zealand by contacting Services Australia - International Services In some circumstances, a client's Australian Disability Support Pension application date can be used as the client's Supported Living Payment application date. This can only happen when the client applies for the: - Australian Disability Support Pension (for the severely disabled) within 4 weeks of leaving New Zealand, and - Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) under the agreement within 12 months of that Australian Disability Support Pension application Note a client who is getting Australian Disability Support Pension (for the severely disabled) when they leave New Zealand must apply for Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) under the agreement within 4 weeks from the date the client leaves New Zealand. If the client has not applied for the Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) within 4 weeks of their departure from New Zealand, they will have no entitlement to the benefit for any of the first 4 weeks of their absence from New Zealand. The Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) may continue for less than 4 weeks depending on when and what decision Services Australia - International Services makes about the client's Australian Disability Support Pension (for the severely disabled) application. Where MSD and Services Australia - International Services make a different decision about whether the client is severely disabled, they may dispute the different decision with each other.

chunks.title: Payment in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: The client must apply to Services Australia - International Services within 4 weeks of their departure from New Zealand to continue to get their New Zealand payment at their current rate for up to 4 weeks. The client will need to meet the following qualifications: - be present in Australia at the time they apply and - have the intention of remaining resident in Australia for at least one year and - have at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since age 20 and - have a total of 2 years continuous residence in New Zealand and or Australia and - meet the severely disabled medical criteria for an Australian Disability Support Pension (for the severely disabled) If the client is not yet getting the Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the New Zealand qualifications. International Services should be contacted before any current benefit is cancelled or suspended. If a client applies from Australia for New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) and they are not already receiving Supported Living Payment, they must have been living in Australia for at least 26 weeks prior to the date of application or have an intention to reside in Australia for at least one year. Note if the client does not notify MSD of their intended absence prior to their departure, their Supported Living Payment will stop from the day following their departure.

chunks.title: For more information — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: Contact International Services or see: - Commencement of payment in Australia - Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main Benefit - Supported Living Payment from 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment clients living in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment clients living in Australia
Under the agreement with Australia a client can be paid the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) when they are living in Australia.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Australia they can receive the Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) if:
- they are resident in Australia and are present either in Australia or New Zealand at the time they apply
- they have the intention of remaining resident in Australia for at least one year or have been living in Australia for at least 26 weeks and
- they have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since age 20 and
- they meet the severely disabled medical criteria for Supported Living Payment (severely disabled) as outlined in the agreement and
- they have a total of 2 years continuous residence in Australia and/or New Zealand
## Note
- if the client has a partner, the partner should be included and the Supported Living Payment (severely disabled) paid at the married or civil union rate
- the Australian authorities will arrange and pay for any medical examinations that are required for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (severely disabled) and the Australian Disability Support Pension (for the severely disabled) when a client is living in Australia
The client must let Services Australia - International Services and International Services know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Australia to live in another country.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in Australia
- Supported Living Payment clients moving to Australia
- Supported Living Payment
- Supported Living Payment from 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment from 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment from 15 July 2013
Qualifications for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) remain the same as those for the Invalids Benefit payable under the Social Security Agreement with Australia. The only change is a name change.
From 15 July 2013 references to Invalids Benefit in the Social Security Agreement must be considered to be a reference to Supported Living Payment. When corresponding with a client the new benefit name must be used.

chunks.title: Veteran's Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: When a client from Australia meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Veterans Pension except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Australia.
