For information on the qualifications required for Veterans Pensions contact the Veterans Pension Centre The agreement with Australia allows Australian residence between the ages of 20 years and the qualifying age for the Australian Age Pension (up to a maximum of 45) to be regarded as residence in New Zealand to help a client meet the residence qualifications for New Zealand Veterans Pension. Australian residence that can be counted includes residence in Australia on a temporary residence visa or non-permanent visa However, these clients must also meet the following additional criteria: - be resident and present in New Zealand and intends to remain for at least one year or have been present in New Zealand for at least six months prior to application and - have a total of 10 years residence in Australia and/or New Zealand since the age of 20, 5 years of which must have been since the age of 50 and - have been an Australian resident for 12 months since the age of 20, of which at least 6 months must be continuous The client must also: - meet the New Zealand service and disability qualifications - have reached age 65 and - qualify for an Australian pension under the agreement This includes clients who qualify for an Australian pension at a zero rate of payment. Australian pensions that fall within the criteria of sections 187-191 of the Social Security Act 2018 and sections 118-136 of the Social Security Regulations 2018 will be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation. When New Zealand Veterans Pension is granted using the agreement with Australia you will need to enter entitlement code (13) in the NDTA screen. If a client is aged 65 or over and has been granted Veteran’s Pension payments into Australia before 1 July 2017, they can continue to receive Veteran’s Pension in Australia. If their entitlement to Veteran’s Pension stops after this date (eg. due to absence from Australia), then they will need to reapply under the 2017 Agreement. If a client turns 65 on or after 1 July 2017 and they are living in Australia, or intend to move there from New Zealand on or after that date, they will need to meet the qualifying age for the Australia Age Pension to qualify for Veteran’s Pension payable under the 2017 Agreement.

chunks.title: Qualifying age for Australian Age Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: The qualifying age for clients is explained in the table below: Clients born between Qualify for the Australian Age Pension at age 1 July 1952 to 31 December 1953 65 years and 6 months* 1 January 1954 to 30 June 1955 66 years 1 July 1955 to 31 December 1956 66 years and 6 months* From 1 January 1957 67 years * 6 months means at the end of a 6-month period. For example: For a birthday on The 6-month period ends on And the qualifying date is 1 January 30 June 1 July 30 April 29 October 30 October 1 May 31 October 1 November 14 May 13 November 14 November 31 August 28 February or29 February in a leap year 1 March Calculating months when combining periods of residence A client's residence is used to calculate their entitlement to a New Zealand pension or benefit as well as the rate payable. Any incomplete months are rounded up for residence calculation purposes. For example, 45 months and 1 day becomes 46 months. For more information contact International Services or see: - Clients from Australia - New Zealand benefits and pensions in Australia - Veterans living in Australia

chunks.title: Veterans living in Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Veterans living in Australia
Under the agreement with Australia a client can be paid New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are living in Australia.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Australia they can receive Veterans Pension if:
- they are resident in Australia and present either in Australia or New Zealand at the time they apply and
- they have the intention of remaining resident in Australia for at least 1 year or have been living in Australia for at least 26 weeks and
- they have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since age 20 and
- their residence in New Zealand and/or Australia working age residence totals at least 10 years since the age of 20, 5 years of which must be since the age of 50 (Australian residence that can be counted includes residence in Australia on a temporary residence visa or a non-permanent visa and
- they meet the qualifications for New Zealand Veterans Pension except for having to meet the usual residence criteria of being ordinarily resident in New Zealand and
- have reached the qualifying pension age and
- they receive or are entitled to receive New Zealand Veterans Pension in their own right
For information on the qualifications required for Veterans Pensions please contact the Veterans Pension Centre
## Partners
If the client has a partner, the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right. If the partner is under the age of 65, they cannot be included in the client's payment.
Clients in a relationship can be paid the married, civil union or de facto rate in Australia regardless of the sex or gender of either partner.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let Services Australia - International Services and International Services know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Australia to live in another country.
## Under 65 years old
If the client is under the age of 65 they will need to apply for and be entitled to a Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) to receive ongoing payment into Australia.
## International Services
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in Australia
- Qualifying pension age

chunks.title: Veterans moving to Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: Under the agreement with Australia a client can be paid New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are living in Australia. When a Veterans Pension client advises you that they intend to live in Australia you will need to: - put a future suspension on the client's SWIFTT record for the beginning of the 27th week of absence from New Zealand (you must not cancel or suspend the payment) - suspend any extra help payments the client may be receiving from the day the client will leave New Zealand, as they are not entitled to receive these when they are leaving New Zealand with the intention of living in Australia - advise the client that they must apply for their New Zealand Veterans Pension to be paid in Australia and apply for an Australian Age Pension within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand (as this will affect the rate of the New Zealand payment) Note the Veterans Pension continues to be paid at the existing rate until the beginning of the 27th week, or the date payments in Australia commence - whichever is the earliest date. The application for New Zealand Veterans Pension to be paid in Australia and supporting documents must be sent to International Services for processing. Services Australia - International Services will decide whether the client is entitled to an Australian Age Pension. If the client is not entitled to an Australian Age Pension, the client will not be entitled to any payment from New Zealand. International Services will ensure that the record is either cancelled or changed to make ongoing payments into Australia.

chunks.title: Apply in Australia within 26 weeks — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text: The client must apply to Services Australia - International Services within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand to continue to receive their New Zealand payment at their current rate for up to 26 weeks The client will need to meet the following qualifications: - be present in Australia at the time they apply and - have the intention of residing in Australia for at least 1 year and - have had a least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since age 20 and - have a total of 10 years residence in New Zealand and/or Australian working age residence since the age of 20, 5 years of which must be since the age of 50 (Australian residence that can be counted includes residence in Australia on a temporary residence visa or non-permanent visa) and - meet the criteria for the Australian Age Pension and - have reached the qualifying pension age If the client is intending to move to Australia and is not yet receiving New Zealand Veterans Pension an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the New Zealand qualifications. For information on the qualifications required for Veterans Pensions please contact the Veterans Pension Centre. If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Australia for 1 year or more, they can continue to be paid their New Zealand rate of payment for up to 26 weeks after leaving New Zealand, provided they apply for payment in Australia within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand. If the client does not apply for payment in Australia within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand, and they do not return to New Zealand within 30 weeks of leaving, they will have no entitlement for the whole period of absence from New Zealand. Clients who are under the age of 65 will need to meet the qualifications for Supported Living Payment (for the severely disabled) to get ongoing payments into Australia. Clients in a relationship can be paid the married, civil union or de facto rate in Australia regardless of the sex or gender of either partner. For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: War Pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## War Pensions
When a client is receiving an Australian War Service Pension it will be directly deducted from any New Zealand benefit or pension.
When a client is receiving one of the following War pensions from the Department of Veteran's Affairs in Australia, it will not affect any New Zealand benefit or pension that the client receives.
## War Disablement Pension
Australian War Disablement Pensions can provide additional pension to compensate veterans for injuries or diseases caused or aggravated by War/Defence services.
## War Widow's Pension and Orphans Pension
The full amount of an Australian War Widow's Pension, including any amount paid for children, does not affect any New Zealand benefit or pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Australia — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal australia
chunks.text:
## Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Australia
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefits names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Australia.
## New Benefit categories
Jobseeker Support will replace:
- Unemployment Benefit (including Unemployment Benefit Student Hardship and Unemployment Benefit Training)
- Sickness Benefit (including Sickness Benefit Hardship)
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged 14 years or older, or have no children
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent and widowers with dependent children aged 14 years or older
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women alone
Sole Parent Support will replace:
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged under 14 years
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent and widowers with dependent children aged under 14 years
Supported Living Payment will replace:
- Invalid's Benefit
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Care of sick or infirm
The following benefits will remain:
- Emergency Benefit for clients in hardship (including Emergency Maintenance Allowance)
- Unsupported Child's Benefit and Orphan's Benefit
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
- Youth Payment
- Young Parent Payment
Note the changes do not affect New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension. The only change for people previously receiving the Invalid's Benefit will be that the name of the benefit they receive will change to Supported Living Payment. The rate of payment will remain the same.
For more information see:
- Supported Living Payment from 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Admission to hospital — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital
When a client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced.
The Canadian pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks, and the Canadian pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner and the rate of a Canadian pension for one partner is more than the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension the excess amount of the Canadian pension is deducted from the other partner's New Zealand benefit or pension payment.

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Canada the rate of payment is not reduced if the client is in hospital for more than 13 weeks.
## Imprisonment
The New Zealand benefit should not be stopped if the client is imprisoned.
This is as overseas institutions are not covered by the definitions of institutions in New Zealand legislation.

chunks.title: Applications for payment in Canada with entitlements before 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Applications for payment in Canada with entitlements before 15 July 2013
To decide if an application for portable Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Canada is decided and grandparented under the old rules the following will apply:
- the applicant must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or Canada on 14 July 2013 and
- an application for payment in Canada may be received before or after 15 July 2013 but there must be entitlement to Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers from a date before 15 July 2013
Provided these conditions are met an application may be granted under the old rules and the grandparenting provisions will apply. If any one of the conditions is not met the application must be decided under the new rules.

chunks.title: Benefit entitlements in Canada after 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Benefit entitlements in Canada after 15 July 2013
New applications for Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers under the agreement with Canada with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013, are to be considered as applications for Sole Parent Support.
In order to qualify the applicant must:
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or in Canada on 15 July 2013
- have a spouse who has died and
- have a dependent child under the age of 14 years
Entitlement to Sole Parent Support will cease when the dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Canada.
New applications for Invalids Benefits under the Agreement with Canada with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind). The only change to this benefit is the name change from Invalids Benefit to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Last child turning 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)

chunks.title: Calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension
When New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in Canada the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence since the age of 20 anddivide by
- the number for the date the client was born (see calculation table) andmultiply by
- the maximum benefit rate
The minimum payment that can be paid is:
- 1/40 to 1/45 of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation
The maximum rate that can be paid is 100% of the gross rate of either half married, civil union, de facto rate or the single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation depending on the client's circumstances.
There is no provision to pay the married, civil union or de facto rate of payment to same sex couples living in Canada unless they are legally married to each other. If they are not legally married to each other, each partner must be assessed on an individual basis and be paid at the single sharing accommodation rate.
Note the Reciprocal Agreement with Canada and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in Canada, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
## Extra help
Extra help such as Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance or Temporary Additional Support cannot be paid to clients living in Canada.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in Canada
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Calculation for other benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Calculation for other benefits
When a benefit other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in Canada use the following formula to calculate the rate of payment:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence since the age of 20 and
- divide this by 300 and
- multiply this by the maximum benefit rate
The minimum rate that can be paid is:
- 12 divided by 300 multiplied by the maximum benefit rate
The maximum rate of payment is the full net rate of the benefit the client is entitled to.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Canadian pension or other overseas pension being paid.
## Period of absence
A period of up to 26 weeks absence from New Zealand can be included as New Zealand residence, so long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Canada.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Canadian Life Certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Canadian Life Certificates
When a client is receiving a Canadian pension in New Zealand the Canadian authorities require them to complete life certificates.
The Canadian authorities will send the life certificate form directly to the client when it is due.
The client should complete the life certificate and return it directly to Canada.
If a client needs the life certificate witnessed it is important to check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
Return the life certificate to the client so that they can send it directly to the Canadian authorities.

chunks.title: Canadian pensions paid in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Canadian pensions paid in New Zealand
Canada has 2 social security programmes these are the:
- Old Age Security Programme and
- Canadian Pension Plan
Guaranteed Income Supplement and allowance are paid under the Old Age Security Programme. The other pensions are paid under the Canadian Pension Plan.
Pensions paid under the Canadian Pension Plan can be made anywhere in the world provided claimants meet the eligibility conditions.
Some of the following pensions may be paid when a client from Canada is living in New Zealand:
- Disability Pension
- Guaranteed Income Supplement (only paid for first 6 months after leaving Canada)
- Old Age Security Pension
- Orphans Pension
- Retirement Pension
- Spouse's Allowance
- Surviving Spouse's Pension
Canadian pensions are paid directly to the client on a monthly basis. Canadian pensions are directly deducted from the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
The Canadian Orphans Benefit is directly deducted from any New Zealand benefit or pension the client is getting.
## Extra help
Accommodation Supplement
When a Canadian pension is more than the main benefit rate, the amount over the main benefit rate is directly deducted from any Accommodation Supplement the client may get as a non-beneficiary.
Disability Allowance
If the Canadian pension is considered to be in the nature of a disability allowance, this will be directly deducted from any New Zealand Disability Allowance.
The Canadian authorities can require a client to be medically re-examined periodically, to check they are still entitled to the Disability Pension.
Any medical examinations are arranged by the case manager and the account is sent to International Services to arrange payment.
Contact International Services or:

chunks.title: Change in income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When a client is getting one of the following New Zealand benefits that is being paid in Canada it will still be income tested and the client will need to advise when there is any change in their income:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
The client must provide details of income they get in Canada or New Zealand.
This includes any Child Support payments they get from Inland Revenue.
## Annual reviews
The Confirming your Circumstances form will be sent for the client to complete and return to New Zealand every 52 weeks.
## For more information contact International Services or see:
- International Services

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International Services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension paid in Canada when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a relationship in the nature of marriage or
- a client becomes single through separation, the marriage or civil union is dissolved, or the death of their partner

chunks.title: Changes and Reviews for Canadian pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Changes and Reviews for Canadian pensions
A client is obliged to advise the Ministry of Social Development of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also required to provide any information required by the Canadian authorities to ensure that they are still entitled to their Canadian pension paid in New Zealand.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Canada
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension or the rate payable.
MSD may also review a New Zealand benefit or pension in Canada at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions paid in Canada.
## Life certificates
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Canada will need to complete a Life Certificate which will be sent to them every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances.
## Annual reviews
Clients getting other New Zealand benefits or pensions in Canada will need to complete the 'Confirming your Circumstances form' which will be sent to them every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment paid in Canada.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier.

chunks.title: Clients entitled to Canadian pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Clients entitled to Canadian pensions
Under the Social Security Act 2018 a client must apply for any pension that they may be entitled to from Canada if they are applying for a New Zealand benefit or pension.
If a client has Canadian creditable periods they will need to complete an application for a Canadian pension. Contact International Services to have an application pack sent to the client.
When the client completes the application it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies)
- the application form, bank authority form and both sides of the 'Authority to release information and adjust Canadian arrears' form are signed and dated
If the client refuses to apply for any Canadian pension to which they may be entitled you should contact International Services.

chunks.title: Clients from Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Clients from Canada
When a former resident of Canada applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they are receiving a Canadian pension, or if they may be entitled to one.
A client who has previously resided in Canada must show these details on their application form. These details must be entered into CMS.
Information about clients with overseas residence will be downloaded to International Services who will follow up whether the client has any overseas pension entitlement.
If the client is already receiving an overseas pension you should find out the details to establish whether this pension should be a deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Canadian pensions paid in New Zealand
- Clients entitled to Canadian pensions
- Changes and reviews for Canadian pensions
- Direct deductions
- Other income
- Payments from overseas

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Clients going overseas
When a client receiving a Canadian pension leaves New Zealand for a temporary absence the Canadian pension can continue to be paid.
The normal absence provisions apply to any New Zealand benefit or pension they are receiving.
If a client is going to Canada and intends to stay there for more than 26 weeks they may be able to receive payment of their New Zealand benefit or pension in Canada.
For more information see:
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main Benefit
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Canada

chunks.title: Clients getting Canadian pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Clients getting Canadian pensions
A client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Canadian pension that they are receiving. If they do not comply their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or payment can be suspended.
When a client is receiving payments from Canada you will need to find out the payment details in order to determine if the Canadian pension should be a direct deduction from the clients New Zealand or benefit.
It is important that the information is obtained as quickly as possible to enable the client's New Zealand benefit or pension entitlement to be assessed correctly.
If the client is unable to provide full documentation of the payments they will need to complete an Information Release Authority form.
The form must be sent to International Services for them to obtain and verify the following information:
- rate and frequency of payment in Canadian currency and whether it includes any amount in respect of the client's partner and any dependent children
- reason for the grant, such as age, widowhood, disablement, or war service
- the full name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment
- verification of any amount which is payment based on voluntary contributions
Contact International Services or:

chunks.title: Client applies for payment in Canada before they leave New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Client applies for payment in Canada before they leave New Zealand
When a client applies for their New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid in Canada before their departure from New Zealand, payments to Canada will start on the first payday after their departure from New Zealand.
Client applies for New Zealand portable payment into Canada from Canada
When a client applies from Canada, the commencement date will depend on whether the client is already getting a New Zealand benefit or pension, and whether they arrived in Canada direct from New Zealand or after residing in another country.
## Client is already getting a New Zealand benefit or pension payment
If the client is already getting a New Zealand benefit or pension and they apply for payment into Canada, the payments into Canada will start from:
- the first payday after their departure from New Zealand (if they arrive in Canada within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand) or
- the date they applied for the New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid into Canada or
- the date they applied for an equivalent Canadian benefit or pension or
- the date they arrived in Canada (if they did not arrive within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand) or
- the date the agreement with Canada came into force (1 May 1997)
whichever is the later.
## Client is not getting a New Zealand benefit or pension
If the client is not getting a New Zealand benefit or pension, the payment into Canada will start on:
- the date the client applied for a New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid into Canada or
- the date the client applied for an equivalent Canadian benefit or pension
Unless this date is before:
- the date of entitlement (eg when client turns 65 for New Zealand Superannuation /Veterans Pension) or
- the date the Agreement came into force (1 May 1997)
in these cases, we would use the later date.
The Canadian authorities forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services

chunks.title: Death in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Death in Canada
The normal procedures for cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions apply on the death of a client receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension in Canada.
Generally the Canadian authorities will advise International Services of the death of a client in Canada and International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
Note that Funeral Grants are not payable for clients who were living in Canada at the time of their death.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main Benefit

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on death follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients who were also receiving a Canadian pension that has been recorded in SWIFTT.
The executor of the client's estate will need to contact the Canadian authorities directly if they require any details of the Canadian pension.
International Services will send the following information to the Canadian authorities:
- the clients name
- date of death and
- the name and address of the administrator of the estate
Terminal benefit should be paid at the rate of the New Zealand benefit payable as at the date of death.
## SWIFTT
The executor of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen in SWIFTT so that International Services can advise the Canadian authorities.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Changes and reviews, Death of a client in relevant Main benefit
## Annual General Adjustment
Terminal benefit rates are adjusted to reflect changes made in the Annual General Adjustment. This occurs on 1 April each year.

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
When a client is receiving a Canadian pension or other payment, the gross amount is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit.
The Canadian pension is deducted from:
- the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and
- the net rate of any other New Zealand benefit (including Accommodation Supplement)
- if the Canadian pension is considered to be in the nature of a disability allowance, it will be directly deducted from any New Zealand Disability Allowance but not any other New Zealand benefit
When a client is already getting a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Canadian pension is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services.
A fax should be sent to International Services including the:
- verification of the rate
- frequency and type of Canadian pension
- grant date and
- name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already getting a Canadian pension at the time a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process.
## Reviews
International Services must be advised of all clients who are getting a Canadian pension as it is International Services' responsibility to carry out New Zealand benefit or pension reviews required, when the Canadian pension deduction is being up-dated or reviewed.
Any other reviews of the client's New Zealand benefit, such as a change of relationship status or a change of chargeable income, should be completed by the case manager.

chunks.title: Existing portable payments for Widows and Widowers in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Existing portable payments for Widows and Widowers in Canada
From 15 July 2013 onwards, people receiving existing portable payments of Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for Widowers in Canada will be grandparented on their existing rate and conditions.
References to the benefit names Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for Widowers are grandparented for existing clients and must still be used when administering these benefits payable under the Agreement with Canada and when corresponding with the client.
Grandparenting arrangements do not apply to the former Invalid's Benefit because the only change is the name change to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Grandparenting
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Canada

chunks.title: Accommodation Supplement — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Accommodation Supplement
When a client is receiving a Canadian pension that exceeds the New Zealand main benefit rate, the excess amount will be directly deducted from any Accommodation Supplement the client receives.
You will need to calculate the amount that the client would be entitled to receive by way of a New Zealand benefit or pension and the rate of Accommodation Supplement that would be payable alongside that benefit or pension.
The Canadian pension should be deducted from the total New Zealand benefit and Accommodation Supplement, and the balance will be the actual rate of Accommodation Supplement payable.
Note that you will need to manually add this amount in SWIFTT using the SASA screen.
## Disability Allowance
When a client is receiving a Canadian pension that is considered to be in the nature of a Disability Allowance, it will be directly deducted from any New Zealand Disability Allowance, but not any other New Zealand benefit.

chunks.title: Grandparenting — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Grandparenting
Grandparenting is a provision in which the old rules continue to apply to existing situations, while the new rules will apply to all future cases. The main benefit information for Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers will still be available if required by contacting seniors@msd.govt.nz.

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and Canada allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- Canadian creditable periods can be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- residence in New Zealand can be regarded as Canadian creditable periods to meet the residence qualifications for some Canadian benefits and pensions
- Canadian pensions can be paid in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid in Canada
## Benefit consolidation
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provided for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names, and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes had some impacts on the Agreement with Canada.

chunks.title: Last child turning 14 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Last child turning 14
Clients receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower will cease to be eligible for payments once their last dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Canada.
If the client returns to New Zealand after their last dependent child turns 14 they may be eligible for Jobseeker Support but will not be eligible for a New Zealand benefit if they remain in Canada.
Supported Living Payment clients with dependent children and grand parented Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers do not lose entitlement once their last dependent child turns 14.
For more information see:
- Main benefit Sole Parent Support

chunks.title: Methods of payment in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment in Canada
When a client is getting a New Zealand benefit or pension in Canada they can choose to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account or to a bank account in Canada.
## Canadian bank account
Payments made to a Canadian bank account are credited four weekly.
If a client chooses to have money paid directly to a Canadian bank account, Work and Income meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
There are 3 options for the first payment being made into a Canadian bank account:
- payment can be made to an overseas bank account if the client has provided proof of their bank account
- the first payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the Canadian bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the Canadian bank account are given to International Services. Once account details are advised, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the Canadian account with the first payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Rate payable in Canada

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client intends to live in a country other than New Zealand or Canada for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
The client may still be entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension if:
- they qualify for the New Zealand benefit or pension due to their previous residence in New Zealand and
- they are moving to a country which has an agreement with New Zealand
Payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension should stop from the payday after the client's departure from Canada until the client can test their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension in the country that they have moved to.
## Residence
New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension cannot be paid to a client who leaves Canada to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand as the client needs to be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand at the date they apply for payment overseas.
If the client is receiving the New Zealand benefit or pension by using their Canadian residence to meet the New Zealand residence qualification, they may not be entitled to have the New Zealand benefit or pension paid in another country depending on their circumstances.
Example
A client receiving New Zealand Superannuation has only three years New Zealand residence but sufficient Canadian creditable periods to enable them to meet the minimum residence requirement for New Zealand Superannuation. The client is not entitled to take payment overseas to a third country (unless it is a country that also has a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand).
For more information see:
- Reciprocal agreements
- General Portability
- Special Portability

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions in Canada
Under the agreement with Canada, the following New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid to former New Zealand residents who live, or intend to live, in Canada:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with child/ren under 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veterans Pension
The rules are different depending on whether the client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension and is moving to Canada, or if they are already living in Canada at the time they apply.
## The agreement does not cover the following
- Sole Parent Support - Sole parents
- Supported Living Payment for care of the sick or infirm
- Emergency Benefits
- Jobseeker Support
- Unsupported Child's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers living in Canada
- Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers moving to Canada
- Supported Living Payment living in Canada
- Supported Living Payment moving to Canada
- New Zealand Superannuation clients living in Canada
- New Zealand Superannuation clients moving to Canada
- Veterans living in Canada
- Veterans moving to Canada
- Applications for payment in Canada with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Canada after 15 July 2013
- Existing portable payment for widows and widowers in Canada
- Commencement of payment in Canada

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
The agreement with Canada allows Canadian creditable periods to be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualification for the following New Zealand benefits:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers (with dependent children under 14 years of age)
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veterans Pension
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefits
- Jobseeker Support
- Sole Parent Support - sole parents
- Supported Living Payment for care of sick or infirm
- Unsupported Child's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For more information see:
- Clients from Canada
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Canada
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Canada

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation
When a client from Canada meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Canada.
The agreement with Canada allows Canadian creditable periods from the age of 20 to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
The client must be the New Zealand qualifying age.
The client may also be entitled to a Canadian Pension, which may be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation.
A Canadian creditable period accumulated under the Old Age Security Act which coincides with a period accumulated under the Canada Pension Plan can only be taken into account once.
## SWIFTT
When New Zealand Superannuation is granted using the agreement with Canada you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 06 in the entitlement code field.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Residency
- Clients from Canada
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Canada
- New Zealand Superannuation clients living in Canada
- New Zealand Superannuation clients moving to Canada

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation clients living in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation clients living in Canada
Under the agreement with Canada a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation when they are living in Canada.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Canada they can receive New Zealand Superannuation if:
- they are ordinarily resident in Canada and present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Canada for at least 26 weeks
- they have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since the age of 20 and
- they meet the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except for ordinarily resident
## Payment to partners
If the client has a partner the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Canada to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or New Zealand Superannuation will stop.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in Canada

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation clients moving to Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation clients moving to Canada
Under the agreement with Canada a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation when they are living in Canada.
When a New Zealand Superannuation client advises that intend to live in Canada they will need to:
- complete an Application for Payment Overseas form (WIS7W)
- complete an Application for Payment Overseas Interview form (WIF9W)
- provide details of the total period of their residence in New Zealand
- provide two forms of identification one must be their passport and
- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to Canada
- verified bank account details if different than those on SWIFTT
The application form, interview form and supporting documents should be sent for processing to International Services
The client will need to meet the following qualifications:
- intend to be ordinarily resident in Canada, and be present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Canada for at least 26 weeks
- have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since age 20 and
- meet the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation
If the client is not currently receiving New Zealand Superannuation an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the qualifications. The client must be ordinarily resident in Canada, or intending to be ordinarily resident in Canada, and be present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply
Before any current benefit is cancelled or suspended you should contact International Services.
## Intending to live in Canada
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Canada for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Canada.
Example
A client may wish to take a four-month holiday in the United States of America before taking up residence in Canada. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Canada for benefit purposes.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in Canada

chunks.title: Other income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Other income
When a client is receiving other income, such as interest from investments or rent from properties they own in Canada, the payments will be treated in the same way as income earned in New Zealand.
You need to convert the income to New Zealand dollars using the current exchange rate. This can be found by using the SELXT screen in SWIFTT and entering the Canadian country code 028.
If you are unsure how the calculation works you should contact International Services
For more information see:
- Direct deductions
- Income and property Definition of income

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand benefit or pension being paid in Canada is overpaid you will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment
- their review and appeal rights and
- the relevant section of the legislation or article of the agreement
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deduction from any New Zealand benefit or pension that the client is receiving.
If the client is no longer receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension they will need to make arrangements to repay the debt.
Overpayments cannot be recovered from the client's Canadian pension.
## Reviews or appeals
If a client applies for a review, or appeals a decision on the establishment of a debt or the rate of recovery, recovery action will be suspended until the outcome of that review or appeal is known.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reviews and appeals
- Debt management [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Rate payable in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Rate payable in Canada
When a New Zealand benefit or pension is paid to a client in Canada, the rate of payment is calculated by a specific formula as provided for in Article VII and VIII of the agreement between New Zealand and the Canadian authorities.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Canadian pension or other overseas pension being paid.
## New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension
The calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension is different to the calculation for other New Zealand benefits.
There is no provision in New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension to include payment for a grandparented non-qualified partner. The partner can only be paid New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Canada if they meet the qualifications in their own right.
The maximum rate payable is the single sharing accommodation rate or the married, civil union, de facto relationship rate depending on the client's circumstances.
## Supported Living Payment
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is paid to a married or civil union client in Canada their partner can be included.
## Residence in New Zealand
No payment is made to a client who has lived in New Zealand for less than 12 continuous months.
Only periods of actual New Zealand residence are counted. Periods of residence in a country other than New Zealand are disregarded even if the country has a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand.
## Period of absence
Any period of absence from New Zealand for up to 26 weeks is regarded as New Zealand residence, as long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Canada.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension
- Calculation for other benefits

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for a Canadian pension. International Services will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not respond to requests to apply for a Canadian pension.
International Services will talk to clients about the reasons why they must apply, including that:
- it is their right as they have made contributions
- clients must claim any benefit they may be entitled to in Canada if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from Canada
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension may stop, however, payment of a Canadian pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 4 weeks their Sole Parent Support stops, however, payment of a Canadian pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 6 weeks their Supported Living Payment stops, however, payment of a Canadian pension may continue
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate, and the rate of Canadian pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended, however, the Canadian pension will still be paid

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Canada and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, payment of the New Zealand benefit will continue to be paid at the same rate as when they were living in Canada.
This is because the client will not be considered as ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Client returns to New Zealand permanently
When a client receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Canada, returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their benefit can be reviewed from the date of return to New Zealand.
International Services must be advised as they are responsible for stopping payment made under the social security agreement.
For more information contact International Services or refer to the instructions for the relevant New Zealand main benefit or pension.

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Review date
A New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date a client is granted a Canadian pension, or when the rate of a Canadian pension changes.
If you are having difficulties obtaining the details you should contact International Services for advice.
When a Canadian pension is reduced, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the reduction.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions
- Extra help
- SWIFTT process

chunks.title: Reviews and appeals — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Reviews and appeals
If a client is unhappy with any decision regarding their Canadian pension being paid in New Zealand they should call or write to the Canadian authorities.
For Canadian contact details go to overseas pension agencies contact details Canada.
## Time limits
Reviews and appeals must be lodged with the Canadian authorities within the following time period:
- 90 days for the Canadian Old Age Pension
- 12 months for the Canadian Retirement, Survivors or Disability Pensions
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
International Services is responsible for any reviews and appeals in regard to:
- the interpretation of the agreement with Canada
- the effect of Canadian pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions and
- New Zealand benefits and pensions being paid in Canada
The New Zealand review and appeal process applies to any other decisions regarding New Zealand benefits or pensions paid in New Zealand, such as charging income or change in relationship status.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
When a client from Canada meets the qualifications for the New Zealand Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower and the client's child or children were born in Canada, they may qualify under the agreement with Canada.
Under the agreement:
- dependent children born in Canada can be accepted as being born in New Zealand provided that the child was born before the death of the person's last deceased spouse or civil union partner
- Canadian creditable periods to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence criteria for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower
- in the case of widows, a child must have been conceived before the spouse or civil union partner's death
- in the case of a widower the child was born before the death of the person's last spouse
- Canadian creditable periods under the Canadian Pension Plan for the last deceased partner is regarded as a period during which that partner was ordinarily resident in New Zealand
- a client can use their own or their partner's Canadian creditable periods as periods of New Zealand residence to meet the residence criteria
- the client may also be entitled to a Canadian Pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Sole Parent Support
## SWIFTT
When Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers is granted using the agreement with Canada you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 06 in the entitlement code field.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Sole Parent Support Residence

- Applications for payment in Canada with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Canada after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers living in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers living in Canada
Under the agreement with Canada a widow or widower can be paid the New Zealand Sole Parent Support when they are living in Canada.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Canada they can receive Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower if:
- they are ordinarily resident in Canada, and are present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply
- they have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Canada for at least 26 weeks
- they have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since the age of 20 and
- they meet the qualifications for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower except the ordinary residence criteria
Sole Parent Support will cease once the last child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Canada.
If the client is still receiving Sole Parent Support at the time they reach the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension they will no longer be eligible for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower and must test their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
## Income
Sole Parent Support paid to a widow or widower in Canada is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Canada or New Zealand when they apply for the benefit or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Canada to live in another country.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
## For more information

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers moving to Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers moving to Canada
Under the agreement with Canada widows or widowers can be paid the New Zealand Sole Parent Support when they are living in Canada.
When a client is receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower and advises that they intend to live in Canada they will need to:

- complete an Application for Payment Overseas Interview form (WIF9W)
- provide details of the total period of their residence in New Zealand

- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to Canada
- verified bank account details if different from those currently on SWIFTT
The application form, interview form and supporting documents should be sent to International Services for processing.
The client will need to meet the following qualifications:

- meet the qualifications for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower
If the client is not currently receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower an application should be taken and entitlement assessed with the qualifications.
The client must be ordinarily resident in Canada, and be present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply.
Before any current benefit is cancelled or suspended contact International Services.
## Intending to live in Canada
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Canada for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Canada.
Example A client may wish to take a four-month holiday in the United States of America before taking up residence in Canada. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Canada for benefit purposes.
For more information contact International Services by phone or see:

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment
When a client from Canada meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Canada.
The agreement with Canada allows Canadian creditable periods to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
The client must meet the New Zealand medical criteria.
The client may also be entitled to a Canadian Pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
## SWIFTT

Note Supported Living Payment for the care of sick or infirm is not payable under the Canadian Agreement.

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment living in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment living in Canada
Under the agreement with Canada a client can be paid the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when they are living in Canada.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Canada they can receive Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) if:
- they are ordinarily resident in Canada and are present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply
