chunks.title: SWIFTT process - direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT process - direct deductions
When a client is getting a Canadian pension that is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit or pension, it is important this is processed correctly in SWIFTT.
You will need to add the following information in the SOPDA screen in SWIFTT:
- letter indicator (defaults to x)
- the rate of the Canadian pension in Canadian currency
- the frequency at which the payments are made
- any Canadian pension reference number
- whether the pension is a deductible pension Y/N
- country code 028
- whether the pension is a gross or net amount
- weekly amount of any bank fees allowed, contact International Services
The New Zealand dollar amount of the Canadian pension will be displayed on the SOPHI screen once the above details have been entered.
The New Zealand dollar amount showing on the SOPHI screen will need to be added to the 'O/seas Pen direct ded' field using the INCMA screen in SWIFTT.
If you need more information you should contact International Services.
## SWIFTT
International Services updates the exchange rate table in SWIFTT each month, and the exchange rate table is linked to the country codes.
When the Canadian pension details are correctly recorded SWIFTT will automatically calculate the Canadian pension deduction from the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension payable.
For New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pensions only, SWIFTT will:
- recalculate the rate of the New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension each month and
- send a letter to advise the client if the letter indicator in the SOPDA screen is set to Y
- if a client does not wish to receive their advice letters, the indicator in the SWIFTT SOPHC screen should be set to N
- only International Services can change the letter indicator after the initial grant of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
- International Services manually updates other New Zealand benefits and pensions periodically

chunks.title: Clients in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Clients in New Zealand
When a Canadian pension is being paid to a client in New Zealand, the pension will be taxed at a maximum of 15% in Canada before payment is made to the client.
As Canada has a tax exemption for clients who receive less than $10,000 per year in Canadian currency, the client should be encouraged to file a tax return to the Canadian tax authorities each year at:
Canada Customs and Revenue AgencyInternational Tax Services Office2204 Walkley RoadOttawa, ON K1A 1A8CANADA
Or contact by:
phone: 001 905 613 - 952 3741 (collect calls are accepted)fax: 001 905 613 - 941 2505
The client should also contact Inland Revenue New Zealand to discuss their New Zealand tax liability for the Canadian pension and any New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Clients in Canada
New Zealand benefits paid in Canada are not taxed in New Zealand but may be taxed in Canada.
The client must make their own tax arrangements with the Canadian tax authority.

chunks.title: Veterans living in Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Veterans living in Canada
Under the agreement with Canada a client can be paid New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are living in Canada.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Canada they can receive Veterans Pension if:
- they are ordinarily resident in Canada and present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply
- they have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Canada for at least 26 weeks
- they have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since the age of 20 and
- they meet the qualifications for New Zealand Veterans Pension
## Payment to partners
If the client has a partner, the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Canada to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the Veterans Pension will stop.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in Canada

chunks.title: Veterans moving to Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Veterans moving to Canada
Under the agreement with Canada a client can be paid New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are living in Canada.
When a Veterans Pension client advises that intend to live in Canada they will need to:
- complete an Application for Payment Overseas form (WIS7W)
- complete an Application for Payment Overseas Interview form (WIF9W)
- provide details of the total period of their residence in New Zealand
- provide two forms of identification one must be the clients passport and
- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to Canada
The application form, interview form and supporting documents should be sent for processing to International Services.
The client will need to meet the following qualifications:
- intend to be ordinarily resident in Canada, and be present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Canada for at least 26 weeks
- have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since age 20 and
- meet the qualifications for Veterans Pension
If the client is not currently receiving Veterans Pension an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the qualifications.
The client must be ordinarily resident in Canada, and be present either in Canada or New Zealand at the time they apply.
Before any current benefit is cancelled or suspended you should contact International Services

chunks.title: Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension
When a client from Canada meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Veterans Pension except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Canada.
The agreement with Canada allows Canadian creditable periods from the age of 20 to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Veterans Pension.
For advice on the qualifications for Veterans Pensions contact the Veterans Pension Centre
The client must meet the New Zealand service and disability qualifications.
The client may also be entitled to a Canadian Pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Veterans Pension.
A Canadian creditable period accumulated under the Old Age Security Act which coincides with a period accumulated under the Canada Pension Plan can only be taken into account once.
## SWIFTT
When Veterans Pension is granted using the agreement with Canada you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 06 in the entitlement code field
For more information contact International Services or the Veterans Pension Centre
For more information see:
- Clients from Canada
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Canada
- Veterans living in Canada
- Veterans moving to Canada

chunks.title: War Pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## War Pensions
When a client is receiving 1 of the following war pensions from Canada it will not affect any New Zealand benefit or pension the client receives.
Note the Reciprocal Agreement with Canada and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in Canada, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
## War disablement pension
Canadian war disablement pensions can provide an additional pension for the client's wife and any dependent children. The amount paid for the wife and any children does not affect any New Zealand benefit or pension.
## War widow's pension
The full amount of a Canadian War Widow's Pension, including any amount paid for children, does not affect any New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Compassionate grant to widows
Canadian pension legislation provides for a grant on compassionate grounds to the widow of an ex-serviceman whose death was not associated with war service. This grant does not affect any New Zealand benefit or pension.

chunks.title: Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Canada — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal canada
chunks.text:
## Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Canada
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefits names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Canada.
## New Benefit categories
Jobseeker Support will replace:
- Unemployment Benefit (including Unemployment Benefit Student Hardship and Unemployment Benefit Training)
- Sickness Benefit (including Sickness Benefit Hardship)
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged 14 years or older, or have no children
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole Parent and widowers with dependent children aged 14 years or older
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women Alone
Sole Parent Support will replace:
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged under 14 years
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole Parent and widowers with dependent children aged under 14 years
Supported Living Payment will replace:
- Invalid's Benefit
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Care of sick or infirm
The following benefits will remain:
- Emergency Benefit for clients in hardship (including Emergency Maintenance Allowance)
- Unsupported Child's Benefit and Orphan's Benefit
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
- Youth Payment
- Young Parent Payment
For entitlements arising from an Agreement occurring on or after 15 July 2013 references in the Agreement with Canada to the former benefit names must be considered as references to the new names. The name changes do not affect New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
For more information see:
- Existing portable payments for Widows and Widowers in Canada
- Applications for payment in Canada with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Canada after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Admission to hospital — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital
When a client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced.
The Danish pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the Danish pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner and the rate of a Danish pension for one partner is more than the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension, the excess amount of the Danish pension is deducted from the other partner's New Zealand benefit or pension payment.
For more information see:
- Hospitalisation in relevant Main benefit
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Denmark

chunks.title: Admission to hospital or prison — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital or prison
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Denmark the rate of payment does not change when the client is admitted to hospital or prison.
This is because overseas institutions are not covered by the definitions of institutions in New Zealand legislation.

chunks.title: Application lodged prior to departure — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Application lodged prior to departure
When a client advises that they intend to live in Denmark they will need to:
- complete an Application for Payment Overseas form (WIS7W)
- be interviewed by a case manager who must complete the interview form (WIF9W)
- provide verification of the total period of their residence in New Zealand
- provide two forms of identification one must be their passport and
- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to Denmark
- verified bank account details if different than those on SWIFTT
The application form, interview form and supporting documents should be sent to International Services for processing.
Note International Services should be contacted before any current New Zealand benefit is cancelled or suspended.
## New Zealand benefit application
If the client is not yet receiving a New Zealand benefit an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the qualifications for the particular benefit.
## Residence
The residency and ordinary residency requirements are addressed under the specific benefit that is being applied for.
The client can use their periods of residence in Denmark to meet the qualifications for the New Zealand benefit or pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Applications lodged in Denmark
- Commencement of payment in Denmark
- NZ benefits and pensions in Denmark

chunks.title: Applications for payment in Denmark with entitlements before 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Applications for payment in Denmark with entitlements before 15 July 2013
To decide if an application for portable Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Denmark is decided and grandparented under the old rules the following will apply:
- the applicant must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or Denmark on 14 July 2013 and
- an application for payment in Denmark may be received before or after 15 July 2013 but there must be entitlement to Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers from a date before 15 July 2013
Provided these conditions are met an application may be granted under the old rules and the grandparenting provisions will apply. If any one of the conditions is not met the application must be decided under the new rules.

chunks.title: Applications lodged in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Applications lodged in Denmark
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Denmark they will be entitled to receive a New Zealand benefit or pension if they use the provisions of the agreement to meet the qualifying criteria.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
The client will need to complete an Application for New Zealand Benefit form (NZ1) and this can be sent to Senior Services - international or lodged at a Danish Pensions Agency office.
Note there are special conditions relating to specific benefits and pensions.
## First payment
The first payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension will be made to the Danish authority.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Commencement of payment in Denmark
- NZ benefits and pensions in Denmark

chunks.title: Benefit entitlements in Denmark after 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Benefit entitlements in Denmark after 15 July 2013
New applications for Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers under the agreement with Denmark with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Sole Parent Support.
In order to qualify the applicant must:
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or in Denmark on 15 July 2013
- have a spouse who has died and
- have a dependent child under the age of 14 years
Entitlement to Sole Parent Support will cease when the dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Denmark.
New applications for Invalids Benefit under the Agreement with Denmark with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind). The only change to this benefit is the name change from Invalids Benefit to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Last child turned 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)

chunks.title: Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension
When New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in Denmark the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence since age 20 and
divide by
- the number for the date the client was born (see calculation table) and
multiply by
- the maximum benefit rate
The minimum payment that can be paid is:
- 1/40 to 1/45 of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension or
- 50% of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation if the client was already receiving this amount before 1 October 1997
The maximum rate that can be paid is:
- 100% of the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
The maximum rate of payment is the full gross rate of either the half married, civil union or de facto rate or the single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, depending on the client's circumstances.
There is no provision to pay the married, civil union or de facto rate of payment to same sex couples living in Denmark. Each partner must be assessed on an individual basis and be paid at the single sharing accommodation rate.
Note the Reciprocal Agreement with Denmark and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in Denmark, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension are paid in Denmark without regard to any Danish or other overseas pension being paid.
Clients who were already receiving payment in Denmark before 1 October 1997 may be entitled to a higher rate under the agreement but they cannot receive less than 50% of the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
## Extra help
Extra help such as Accommodation Supplement, family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Denmark.
For more information contact International Services
Or see:
- Commencement of payment in Denmark
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Calculation for other benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Calculation for other benefits
When a benefit other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in Denmark use the following formula to calculate the rate of payment:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence since age 20 and
- divide this by 300 and
- multiply this by maximum benefit rate
The minimum rate that can be paid is:
- 12 divided by 300 multiplied by maximum benefit rate
The maximum rate of payment is the full net rate of the benefit the client is entitled to.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Danish or other overseas pension being paid, but other income should be taken into account for income tested benefits.
A period of up to 26 weeks absence from New Zealand can be included as New Zealand residence, so long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Temporary Additional Support or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Denmark.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Change in income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When a client is getting one of the following New Zealand benefits or pensions that is being paid in Denmark it will still be income tested and the client will need to advise when there is any change in their income:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
The client must provide details of all income.
This includes any Child Support payments they get from Inland Revenue.
## Exception
Danish or other overseas pensions being paid are not taken into account.
## Review of Circumstances
A Confirming your Circumstances form will be sent for the client to complete and return to International Services every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International Services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension paid in Denmark when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a relationship in the nature of a marriage or
- a client becomes single through separation; the marriage or civil union is dissolved; or the death of their partner

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for Danish pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for Danish pensions
A client is obliged to advise the Ministry of Social Development of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also required to provide any information required by the Danish authorities to ensure that they are still entitled to their Danish benefit or pension paid in New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Admission to hospital
- Clients going overseas
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Denmark
- Danish Life Certificates
- Death of a client in New Zealand
- Reviews and Appeals
- Taxation

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Denmark
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension or the rate payable.
MSD may also review a New Zealand benefit or pension in Denmark at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions paid in Denmark.
## Reviews
Clients receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Denmark will need to complete a Life Certificate which will be sent to them every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances.
Clients receiving other New Zealand benefits or pensions in Denmark will need to complete a Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment paid in Denmark.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier.

chunks.title: Clients entitled to Danish pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Clients entitled to Danish pensions
Under the Social Security Act 2018 a client and their spouse or partner must apply for any benefit or pension that they or their dependants may be entitled to from Denmark if they are applying for or receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension.
If the client has Danish residence they will need to complete an application for a Danish benefit or pension. International Services will contact clients with residence in Denmark and ask them to apply for a Danish benefit or pension.
When the client completes the application it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies)
- the application form has been signed and dated
If the client refuses to apply for any Danish benefit or pension to which they may be entitled you should contact International Services.

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Clients going overseas
When a client receiving a Danish pension leaves New Zealand for a temporary absence the Danish benefit or pension may still be paid.
If a client is going to reside in a country other than Denmark they may qualify for payment overseas depending on the country they are going to and benefit type they are receiving.
If a client is going to Denmark and intends to stay there for more than 26 weeks they may be able to receive payment of their New Zealand benefit or pension in Denmark.
For advice about a client's entitlement overseas contact International Services
## Client moving to Denmark
If a client is considering moving to Denmark you should advise them to write to the Danish authorities to check their entitlement to a Danish benefit or pension. The client will need to send full details of their circumstances.
For The Danish Pensions Agency (Pensionsstyrelsen) contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies Denmark.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit
- NZ benefits and pensions in Denmark

chunks.title: Clients receiving Danish pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving Danish pensions
A client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Danish benefit or pension that they, their spouse or partner, or their dependants are receiving. If they do not comply their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or payment can be suspended.
When a client, their spouse or partner, or their dependant is receiving payments from Denmark you will need to find out the details of the payment in order to determine the effect it will have on the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
It is important that the information is obtained as quickly as possible to enable the client's New Zealand benefit or pension entitlement to be assessed correctly.
If the client is unable to provide full documentation of their Danish benefit or pension, International Services may be able to obtain and verify the following information with the Danish pension authorities:
- rate of payment in Danish currency and whether it includes any amount in respect of the client's partner and any dependent children
- reason for the grant, such as age, widowhood, disablement, or war service
- the name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions
- Other payments

chunks.title: Commencement of payment in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Commencement of payment in Denmark
When a client applies for their New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid in Denmark before their departure from New Zealand, payments will start on the first payday after their departure.
When a client applies from Denmark, the New Zealand benefit or pension will start on:
- the date they become entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension
- the date the agreement with Denmark came into force (1 October 1997) or
- the date of application
whichever is the latest date.
Note that the initial stand-down applies to clients who are applying for New Zealand benefits other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
The Danish authorities forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Rate payable in Denmark
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Danish Life Certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Danish Life Certificates
When a client is receiving a Danish benefit or pension in New Zealand they are required to complete life certificates by the Danish authorities.
The Danish authorities will send the life certificate form directly to the client when it is due.
The client should complete the life certificate and return it directly to Denmark.
If a client needs the life certificate witnessed it is important to check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
The life certificate is returned to the client to send directly to the Danish authorities.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Danish pensions in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Danish pensions in New Zealand
When a former resident of Denmark applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they, their spouse or partner, or their dependants are receiving a Danish pension, or if they may be entitled to one.
A client who has previously resided in Denmark must show their overseas residence on the application form when they apply for any New Zealand benefit or pension.
The overseas residence details must be entered on CMS. These details are used by International Services to determine whether the client may be entitled to a Danish pension.
If the client, their spouse or partner, or their dependant is already receiving an overseas pension you should find out the details to establish whether this pension should be a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension.
The following Danish benefits and pensions are covered by the agreement and may be payable to former Danish residents living in New Zealand:
- Anticipatory Pension
- Disability Benefit
- Labour Market Supplementary Pension (ATP)
- Old Age Pension
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Clients receiving Danish pensions
- Clients entitled to Danish pensions
- Other payments

chunks.title: Death in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Death in Denmark
The normal procedures for cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions apply on the death of a client receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension in Denmark.
Generally the Danish authorities will advise International Services of the death of a client in Denmark and International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
Note that Funeral Grants are not payable for clients who were living in Denmark at the time of their death.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on the death of a client follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients who were also receiving a Danish benefit or pension.
The executor of the client's estate will need to contact the Danish authorities directly if they require any details of the Danish benefit or pension, such as last payments due.
For The Danish Pensions Agency (Pensionsstyrelsen) contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies Denmark
International Services will send the following information to the Danish authorities:
- the clients name
- the date of death and
- the name and address of the administrator of the estate
## SWIFTT
The executor of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen in SWIFTT so that International Services can advise the Danish authorities.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
In general when a client is living in New Zealand and receiving a Danish state pension it will be directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit or pension. The amount to deduct is the rate of the benefit or pension after any deduction of tax in Denmark but before the deduction of any New Zealand tax.
The Danish benefit or pension is deducted from:
- the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and
- the net rate of any other New Zealand benefit, including Accommodation Supplement
When a client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Danish pension is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services
A fax should be sent to International Services with verification of the rate, type of Danish pension, the grant date and the name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already receiving a Danish pension at the time a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process.
If you are unsure whether an overseas pension is deductible or not, contact International Services for advice.
## Reviews
International Services must be advised of all clients who are receiving a Danish pension because it is International Services' responsibility to carry out New Zealand benefit or pension reviews required where the Danish pension deduction is being up-dated or reviewed.
Any other reviews of the client's New Zealand benefit, such as a change of relationship status or a change of chargeable income, should be completed by the case manager.

chunks.title: Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Denmark
From 15 July 2013 onwards, people receiving existing portable payments of Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Denmark will be grandparented on their existing rate and conditions.
References to the benefit names Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for Widowers are grandparented for existing clients and must still be used when administering these benefits payable under the Agreement with Denmark and when corresponding with the client.
Grandparenting arrangements do not apply to the former Invalid's Benefit because the only change is the name change to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Grandparenting
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Denmark

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and Denmark allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- residence in Denmark can be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- residence in New Zealand may be able to be regarded as residence and or periods of contributions in Denmark to meet the residence qualifications for some Danish pensions
- some Danish pensions can be paid in New Zealand
- some New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid in Denmark
- War pensions from either country are not included in the agreement, however, the New Zealand Veterans Pension is covered
## Note
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Denmark.

chunks.title: Last child turning 14 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Last child turning 14
Clients receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower will cease to be eligible for payments once their last dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Denmark.
If the client returns to New Zealand after their last dependent child turns 14 they may be eligible for Jobseeker Support but will not be eligible for a New Zealand benefit if they remain ordinarily resident in Denmark
Supported Living Payment with dependent children and grand parented Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers with dependent children do not lose entitlement when their last child turns 14.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support

chunks.title: Methods of payment in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment in Denmark
When a client is getting a New Zealand benefit or pension in Denmark they can choose to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account or to an overseas bank account.
Note that if the client applies from Denmark the first payment will be made to the Danish authorities.
## Overseas bank account
Payments made to an overseas bank account are credited four weekly.
If a client chooses to have money paid directly to an overseas bank account, the Ministry of Social Development meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
There are 3 options for the first payment being made into an overseas bank account:
- payment can be made to an overseas bank account if the client has provided proof of their bank account
- the first payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the overseas bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the overseas bank account are given to International Services. Once account details are advised, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the overseas account with the first payment
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client intends to live in a country other than New Zealand or Denmark for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
The client may still be entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension if:
- they are moving to a country which has an agreement with New Zealand and they qualify under that agreement
Payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension should stop from the payday after the client's departure from Denmark until the client can test their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension in the country that they have moved to.
## Residence
New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension cannot be paid to a client who leaves Denmark to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand as the client needs to be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand at the date they apply for payment overseas.
If the client is receiving the New Zealand benefit or pension by using their Danish residence to meet the New Zealand residence qualification, they may not be entitled to have the New Zealand benefit or pension paid in another agreement country depending on their circumstances.
Example
A client receiving New Zealand Superannuation with 6 months New Zealand residence has used their Danish period of insurance to meet the New Zealand Superannuation residence requirement.
The client now wants to live in Denmark but has no previous Canadian residence. Although New Zealand has an agreement with Denmark the client has insufficient New Zealand residence to be entitled to payment overseas.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reciprocal agreements
- General Portability
- Special Portability

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
Under the agreement with Denmark, residence and or periods of contributions in Denmark can be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualification for the following New Zealand benefits:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers (with dependent child/ren under 14 years of age)
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veterans Pension
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefits
- Jobseeker Support
- Sole Parent Support (sole parent)
- Supported Living Payment for care of sick or infirm
- Unsupported Child's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For more information see:
- Danish pensions in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Denmark
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Denmark
- Changes and reviews for Danish pensions
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Denmark

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation
When a client from Denmark meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Denmark.
The agreement with Denmark allows periods of residence in Denmark since the age of 20 to be regarded as residence and presence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
The client must be the New Zealand qualifying age.
The client may also be entitled to a Danish pension, which may be directly deducted from their New Zealand entitlement.
Note when New Zealand Superannuation is granted using the agreement with Denmark you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 10 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Residency
- Danish pensions in New Zealand
- NZ benefits and pensions in Denmark
- New Zealand Superannuation clients residing in Denmark

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation clients residing in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation clients residing in Denmark
Under the agreement with Denmark a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation while they are residing in Denmark.
The client can apply for New Zealand Superannuation to be paid in Denmark before their departure from New Zealand, or from Denmark. Payment cannot be backdated so clients should be encouraged to apply before they leave New Zealand.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving New Zealand Superannuation
- be ordinarily resident in Denmark or New Zealand and present in Denmark or New Zealand at the time they apply for payment from overseas
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Denmark for at least 26 weeks and
- have resided continuously in New Zealand for at least 12 months since age 20
The client can use their periods of residence in Denmark since the age of 20 to meet the residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
## Intending to reside in Denmark
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Denmark for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Denmark.
Example
A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Denmark. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Denmark for benefit purposes.
## Payment to partner
If the client has a partner the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Denmark to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the New Zealand Superannuation will stop.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Denmark
- Commencement of payment in Denmark

chunks.title: NZ benefits and pensions in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## NZ benefits and pensions in Denmark
Under the agreement with Denmark, the following New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid to former New Zealand residents who are residing or intend to reside in Denmark:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with dependent children under 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Veterans Pension
The rules are different depending on whether the client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension and is moving to Denmark, or if they are already living in Denmark at the time they apply.
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefits
- Jobseeker Support
- Orphans Benefit
- Sole Parent Support - sole parent, women alone, or care of sick or infirm
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
The following pensions are covered by the agreement and may be payable to former New Zealand residents residing in Denmark:
- Anticipatory Pension
- Disability Benefit
- Labour Market Supplementary Pension (ATP)
- Old Age Pension
Clients should contact Udenlandsk Pension for more information.

chunks.title: Other payments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Other payments
When a client is receiving other payments, such as interest or rent from investments or properties they own in Denmark, the payments will be treated in the same way as income earned in New Zealand.
You need to convert the income to New Zealand dollars using the current exchange rate. This can be found by using the SELXT screen in SWIFTT and entering the Danish country code 042.
If you are unsure how the calculation works you should contact International Services

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand benefit or pension being paid in Denmark is overpaid you will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment
- their review and appeal rights and
- the relevant section of the legislation or article of the agreement
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deductions from any New Zealand benefit or pension that the client is receiving.
If the client is no longer receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension the Danish authorities will recover the overpayment from any current Danish pension payments.
The Danish authorities will reimburse New Zealand each September for any overpayments recovered during the previous year.
If the client is no longer receiving any benefit or pension they will need to make arrangements to repay the debt themselves.
## Review or appeal
If a client applies for a review or appeals a decision on the establishment of a debt or the rate of recovery, recovery action will be suspended until the outcome of that review or appeal is known.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Reviews and appeals
- Debt management [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Rate payable in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Rate payable in Denmark
When a New Zealand benefit or pension is paid to a client in Denmark the rate of payment is determined by the number of months that the client has resided in New Zealand since the age of 20.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Danish or other overseas pension being paid. However, any other income the client or their partner receives may affect the rate of payment for income tested benefits.
## New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension
The calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension is different to the calculation for other New Zealand benefits.
There is no provision in New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension to include payment for a grandparented non-qualified partner. The partner can only be paid New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Denmark if they meet the qualifications in their own right.
The maximum rate payable is the single sharing accommodation rate or the married, civil union, de facto relationship rate depending on the client's circumstances.
## Supported Living Payment
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is paid to a married or civil union client in Denmark their partner can be included. The partner does not have to establish entitlement in their own right.
## Residence
No payment is made to a client who has lived in New Zealand for less than 12 continuous months.
Only periods of actual New Zealand residence are counted. Periods of residence in a country other than New Zealand are disregarded even if the country has a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand.
Any period of absence from New Zealand for up to 26 weeks is regarded as New Zealand residence, as long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Denmark.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension
- Calculation for other benefits

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for a Danish benefit or pension. International Services will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not respond to requests to apply for a Danish benefit or pension.
International Services will talk to clients about the reasons why they must apply, including:
- clients and their spouse or partner must claim any benefit or pension to which they, or their dependants may be entitled to in Denmark if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension
- it is their right as they have made contributions
- a New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from Denmark
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension may stop, but payment of a Danish pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 4 weeks their Sole Parent Support may stop but payment of a Danish benefit or pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 6 weeks their Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) may stop but payment of a Danish benefit or pension may continue
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate, and the rate of Danish benefit or pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended but the Danish benefit or pension may still be paid

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Denmark and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension will continue to be paid at the same rate as when they were living in Denmark.
This is because the client will not be considered as ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Client returns to New Zealand permanently
When a client receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Denmark, returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their benefit can be reviewed from the date of return to New Zealand.
International Services must be advised as they are responsible for stopping payment made under the social security agreement.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Review date
A New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date a client is granted a Danish benefit or pension, or when the rate of a Danish benefit or pension changes.
If you have difficulty obtaining details of the overseas pension grant date, contact International Services for advice.
When a Danish benefit or pension is reduced, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the reduction.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions
- SWIFTT process

chunks.title: Reviews and appeals — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Reviews and appeals
If a client is unhappy with any decision regarding their Danish pension being paid in New Zealand they will need to write to the Danish authorities.
For reviews in respect of Labour Market Supplementary Pension (ATP) the client will need to write to the ATP Appeal Board.
For the ATP Appeal Board contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies Denmark
For reviews of any other benefits and pensions from Denmark the client should write to The Danish Pensions Agency (Pensionsstyrelsen).
For The Danish Pensions Agency (Pensionsstyrelsen) contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies Denmark
Reviews and appeals must be lodged with the Danish authorities within 4 weeks of the receipt of the decision.
International Services is responsible for any reviews and appeals in regard to:
- the interpretation of the agreement with Denmark
- the effect of Danish pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions and
- New Zealand benefits and pensions being paid in Denmark
The New Zealand review and appeal process applies to any other decisions regarding New Zealand benefits or pensions paid in New Zealand, such as charging income or change in relationship status.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with dependent children under 14 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with dependent children under 14
Under the agreement with Denmark, a widow or widower may qualify for New Zealand Sole Parent Support if they meet all the qualifications.
Under the agreement:
- dependent children born in Denmark can be accepted as being born in New Zealand if the child was born before the death of the last deceased partner
- residence and/or periods of contributions in Denmark to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers
- the client can use their own or their last deceased spouse or civil union partner's residence and/or periods of contributions in Denmark as periods of New Zealand residence to meet the residence criteria
- for Sole Parent Support widows, the children must have been conceived prior to the last partner's death
- for Sole Parent Support widowers, the children must have been born before the death of the last deceased partner
- the client may also be entitled to a Danish Pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Sole Parent Support
## SWIFTT
When Sole Parent Support is granted using the agreement with Denmark you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 10 in the entitlement code field.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Sole Parent Support Residence
- Applications for payment in Denmark with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Danish pensions in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Denmark
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers residing in Denmark
- Care and protection concerns for a child or young person

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers residing in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers residing in Denmark
Under the agreement with Denmark a widow or widower can be paid the New Zealand Sole Parent Support when they are ordinarily resident in Denmark.
The client can apply for the Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower to be paid in Denmark before their departure from New Zealand, or from Denmark. Payment cannot be backdated so clients should be encouraged to apply before they leave New Zealand.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower with dependent children under 14
- be ordinarily resident in Denmark or New Zealand and present in Denmark or New Zealand at the time they apply for payment overseas
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Denmark for at least 26 weeks and
- have resided continuously in New Zealand for at least 12 months since age 20
## Income
Sole Parent Support paid to a widow or widower in Denmark is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Denmark or New Zealand when they apply for the benefit or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Denmark to live in another country.
When the client reaches the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension they will no longer be eligible for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower and must apply for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Denmark
- Commencement of payment in Denmark
- Last child turning under 14
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Denmark
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Denmark
- Benefit entitlements in Denmark after 15 July 2013
- Main benefits Sole Parent Support

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment
When a client from Denmark meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Denmark.
The agreement with Denmark allows periods of residence in Denmark to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
The client must meet the New Zealand medical criteria.
The client may also be entitled to a Danish Pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
Note when Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is granted using the agreement with Denmark you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 10 in the entitlement code field.

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment residing in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment residing in Denmark
Under the agreement with Denmark a client can be paid the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when they are residing in Denmark.
The client can apply for the Supported Living Payment to be paid in Denmark before their departure from New Zealand, or from Denmark. Payment cannot be backdated so clients should be encouraged to apply before they leave New Zealand.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- be ordinarily resident in Denmark or New Zealand and present in Denmark or New Zealand at the time they apply for payment from overseas
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Denmark for at least 26 weeks and
- have resided continuously in New Zealand for at least 12 months since age 20
The client can use their periods of residence in Denmark to meet the residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
## Payment to partners
Payment can be made to the partner of a qualifying client. The partner does not have to establish entitlement in their own right
## Medical examinations
The Danish authorities will arrange and pay for any medical examination that is required for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when a client is living in Denmark.
## Income
Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) paid in Denmark is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Denmark or New Zealand when they apply for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Denmark to live in another country.
When the client reaches the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension they will no longer be eligible for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) and must test their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Denmark
- Commencement of payment in Denmark
- Benefit entitlements in Denmark after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: SWIFTT process — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT process
When a client is getting a Danish benefit or pension that is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit or pension it is important that this is processed correctly in SWIFTT.
You will need to add the following information in the SOPDA screen in SWIFTT:Note some of these fields are only used by International Services
- letter indicator (defaults to x)
- the rate of the Danish benefit or pension in Danish currency
- the four-weekly amount of bank fees allowed (contact International Services)
- the frequency at which the payments are made
- the Danish benefit or pension reference number
- whether the overseas pension amount is gross or net
- country code 042
- whether the benefit or pension is a deductible pension Y/N
The New Zealand dollar amount of the Danish benefit or pension will be displayed on the SOPHI screen once the above details have been entered.
The New Zealand dollar amount showing on the SOPHI screen will need to be added to the 'O/seas Pen direct ded' field using the INCMA screen in SWIFTT.
When the Danish benefit or pension details are correctly recorded SWIFTT will automatically calculate the Danish benefit or pension deduction from the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension payable.
If you need further information you should contact International Services.
Note International Services up-dates the exchange rate table in SWIFTT each month and the exchange rate table is linked to the country codes.
For New Zealand benefits and pensions paid other than weekly SWIFTT will:
- recalculate the rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension each month and
- send a letter to advise the client if the letter indicator in the SOPDA screen is set to Y
- if a client does not wish to receive their advice letters, the indicator in the SWIFTT SOPHC screen should be set to N
- only International Services can change the letter indicator after the initial grant of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
International Services manually up-dates other New Zealand benefits and pensions periodically.

chunks.title: Clients in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Clients in New Zealand
Danish pensions are taxed in Denmark prior to being paid to the client in New Zealand.
The full amount of the Danish pension is subject to New Zealand tax but a tax credit will be allowed for any tax deducted in Denmark up to the maximum New Zealand tax liability on the benefit or pension income.
The client should be encouraged to file a tax return to the Danish tax authorities each year to The Danish Pensions Agency (Pensionsstyrelsen).
For The Danish Pensions Agency (Pensionsstyrelsen) contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies Denmark
The client should contact New Zealand Inland Revenue to discuss their New Zealand tax liability for the Danish pension and any New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Clients in Denmark
New Zealand benefits and pensions paid in Denmark are not taxed in New Zealand but may be taxed in Denmark.
The client must make their own tax arrangements with the Danish tax authority.

chunks.title: Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension
When a client from Denmark meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Veterans Pension, except residence, they may qualify under the agreement with Denmark.
The agreement with Denmark allows periods of residence in Denmark since the age of 20 to be regarded as residence and presence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Veterans Pension.
The client must meet the New Zealand service and disability qualifications.
The client may also be entitled to a Danish pension, which may be directly deducted from their New Zealand entitlement.
Note when Veterans Pension is granted using the agreement with Denmark you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 10 in the entitlement code field
For more information contact International Services or the Veterans Pension Centre or see:
- Danish pensions in New Zealand
- NZ benefits and pensions in Denmark
- Veterans residing in Denmark

chunks.title: Veterans residing in Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Veterans residing in Denmark
Under the agreement with Denmark a client can be paid the New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are residing in Denmark.
The client can apply for the Veterans Pension to be paid in Denmark before their departure from New Zealand, or from Denmark. Payment cannot be backdated so clients should be encouraged to apply before they leave New Zealand.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Veterans Pension
- be the age of entitlement for New Zealand Superannuation
- be ordinarily resident in Denmark or New Zealand and present in Denmark or New Zealand at the time they apply for payment from overseas
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Denmark for at least 26 weeks and
- have resided continuously in New Zealand for at least 12 months since age 20
The client can use their periods of residence in Denmark since the age of 20 to meet the residence qualification for Veterans Pension.
## Payment to partner
If the client has a partner each partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Denmark to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the Veterans pension will stop.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Denmark
- Commencement of payment in Denmark

chunks.title: Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Denmark — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal denmark
chunks.text:
## Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Denmark
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefits names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Denmark.
## New benefit categories
Jobseeker Support will replace:
- Unemployment Benefit (including Unemployment Benefit Student Hardship and Unemployment Benefit Training)
- Sickness Benefit (including Sickness Benefit Hardship)
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged 14 years or older, or have no children
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole Parent and widowers with dependent children aged 14 years or older
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women Alone
Sole Parent Support will replace:
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged under 14 years
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole Parent and widowers with dependent children aged under 14 years
Supported Living Payment will replace:
- Invalid's Benefit
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Care of sick or infirm
The following benefits will remain:
- Emergency Benefit for clients in hardship (including Emergency Maintenance Allowance)
- Unsupported Child's Benefit and Orphan's Benefit
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
- Youth Payment
- Young Parent Payment
For entitlements arising from an Agreement occurring on or after 15 July 2013 references in the Agreement with Denmark to the former benefit names must be considered as references to the new names. The name changes do not affect New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
For more information see:
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Denmark
- Applications for payment in Denmark with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Denmark after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Admission to hospital — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital
When a client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced.
The Greek pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the Greek pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner and the rate of a Greek pension for one partner is more than the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension the excess amount of the Greek pension is deducted from the other partner's New Zealand benefit or pension payment.
For more information see:
- Hospitalisation in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Hospitalisation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Hospitalisation
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Greece the rate of payment is not reduced if the client is in hospital for more than 13 weeks.
## Imprisonment
The New Zealand benefit should not be stopped if the client is imprisoned.
This is because overseas institutions are not covered by the definitions of institutions in New Zealand legislation.

chunks.title: Application lodged prior to departure — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Application lodged prior to departure
When a client advises that they intend to live in Greece they will need to:
- complete an Application for payment overseas form (WIS7W)
- complete an Application for payment overseas interview form (WIF9W)
- provide details of the total period of their residence in New Zealand
- provide their passport plus one other form of identification and
- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to Greece
The application form, interview form and supporting documents should be sent for processing to International Services
International Services should be contacted before any current New Zealand benefit is cancelled or suspended.
## New Zealand benefit application
If the client is not yet receiving a New Zealand benefit an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the qualifications for the particular benefit (except, for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind), the client does not need to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand).
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Applications lodged in Greece
- Commencement of payment in Greece
- Applications for payment in Greece with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece

chunks.title: Applications for payment in Greece with entitlements before 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Applications for payment in Greece with entitlements before 15 July 2013
To decide if an application for portable Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Greece is decided and grandparented under the old rules the following will apply:
- the applicant must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or Greece on 14 July 2013 and
- an application for payment in Greece may be received before or after 15 July 2013 but there must be entitlement to Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers from a date before 15 July 2013
Provided these conditions are met an application may be granted under the old rules and the grandparenting provisions will apply. If any one of the conditions is not met the application must be decided under the new rules.

chunks.title: Applications lodged in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Applications lodged in Greece
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Greece they are entitled to receive a New Zealand benefit or pension covered by the agreement if:
New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension
- the client must have lived in New Zealand for at least one continuous year since the age of 20 and intend to live in Greece for more than 26 weeks
Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- the client cannot apply from Greece because they need to be in New Zealand at the time they apply
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
Note there are special conditions relating to specific benefits and pensions.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Commencement of payment in Greece
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece
- Applications for payment in Greece with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers

chunks.title: Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013
New applications for Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for Widowers under the agreement with Greece with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Sole Parent Support.
In order to qualify the applicant must:
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or in Greece on 15 July 2013
- have a spouse who has died and
- have a dependent child under the age of 14 years
Entitlement to Sole Parent Support will cease when the dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Greece.
New applications for Invalids Benefits under the Agreement with Greece with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Supported Living Payment. The only change to this benefit is the name change from Invalids Benefit to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Last child turning 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)

chunks.title: Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension
When New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in Greece the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole years of New Zealand residence since the age of 20
- divide by 40 and
- multiply by the maximum benefit rate
The minimum payment that can be paid is:
- 1 divided by 40 multiplied by the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension that the client is entitled to or
- 50% of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension if the client was already receiving this prior to 01 April 1994
The maximum rate that can be paid is:
- the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension that the client is entitled to
The maximum rate of payment is the gross rate of either the half married, civil union or de facto rate or the single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, depending on the client's circumstances.
New Zealand Superannuation/Veterans Pension is paid without regard to any Greek Old Age Benefit payable.
Clients who were already receiving payment in Greece prior to 01 April 1994 may be entitled to a higher rate under the agreement but they cannot receive less than 50% of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, that the client is entitled too.
## Extra help
Extra help such as Accommodation Supplement, family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid to clients in Greece.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in Greece
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Calculation for other benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Calculation for other benefits
