For Sole Parent Support and Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when a benefit is paid to a client in Greece the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole years of New Zealand residence since the age of 20
- divide this by 25 and
- multiply this by the maximum benefit rate
The minimum rate that can be paid is:
- 1 divided by 25 multiplied by the maximum benefit rate that the client is entitled to
The maximum rate that can be paid is:
- the full rate of the benefit the client is entitled to
A period of up to 26 weeks absence from New Zealand can be included as New Zealand residence, so long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Orphans Benefit
The rate payable is the maximum rate payable in accordance with New Zealand legislation.
## Funeral Grant
The amount paid is that due under New Zealand legislation less any Funeral Grant paid under Greek legislation.
## Extra help
Other Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Greece.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Change in income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When a client is getting one of the following New Zealand benefits that is being paid in Greece it will still be income tested and the client will need to advise when there is any change in their income:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Orphans Benefit (child's income only)
The client must provide details of all income they get.
This includes any Child Support payments they get from Inland Revenue.
## Review of Circumstances
A Confirming your Circumstances form will be sent to the client every 52 weeks to complete and return to International Services.

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International Services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension paid in Greece when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a relationship in the nature of a marriage or
- a client becomes single through separation; the marriage or civil union is dissolved; or the death of their partner

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for Greek pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for Greek pensions
A client is obliged to advise Work and Income of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also required to provide any information required by the Greek authorities to ensure that they are still entitled to their Greek pension paid in New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Admission to hospital
- Clients going overseas
- Greek Life Certificates
- Death of a client in New Zealand
- Reviews and Appeals
- Taxation
- Changes and reviews for NZ benefits in Greece

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Greece
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension in Greece or the rate payable.
MSD may also review a New Zealand benefit or pension in Greece at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions paid in Greece.
## Life certificates
Clients receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Greece will need to complete and return a Life Certificate that will be sent to them every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances.
## Annual review
Clients receiving other New Zealand benefits or pensions in Greece will need to complete an Confirming your Circumstances form that will be sent to them every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment or have Orphan's Benefit paid for them in Greece.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment or are no longer eligible for Orphan's Benefit from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment or have Orphan's Benefit paid for them for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from Supported Living Payment or Orphan's Benefit must stop from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier.
Note if the caregiver also gets Orphan's Benefit for other children, the payments for the other children will not be affected by another child turning 18.

chunks.title: Clients entitled to Greek pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Clients entitled to Greek pensions
Clients are required to apply for any pension that they may be entitled to from Greece if they are applying for a New Zealand benefit or pension.
If the client has Greek residence they will need to complete an application for a Greek pension. International Services will contact clients with residence in Greece and ask them to apply for a Greek benefit or pension.
When the client completes the application it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies)
- the application form, bank authority form and both sides of the 'Authority to release information and adjust Greek arrears' form are signed and dated
If the client refuses to apply for any Greek pension to which they may be entitled you should contact International Services.

chunks.title: Clients from Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Clients from Greece
When a former resident of Greece applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they are receiving a Greek pension, or if they may be entitled to one.
A client who has previously resided in Greece must show their Overseas Residence on the application form when they apply for any New Zealand benefit or pension.
The overseas residence details must be entered on CMS. These details are used by International Services to determine whether the client may be entitled to a Greek benefit or pension.
If the client is already receiving an overseas pension you should find out the details to establish whether this pension should be a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Greek pensions paid in New Zealand
- Clients entitled to Greek pensions
- Other payments

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Clients going overseas
When a client receiving a Greek pension leaves New Zealand for a temporary absence the Greek pension may still be paid.
If a client is going to reside in a country other than Greece they may qualify for payment overseas depending on the country they are going to and benefit type they are receiving.
If a client is going to Greece and intends to stay there for more than 4 or 26 weeks they may be able to receive payment of their New Zealand benefit or pension.
For advice about a client's entitlement overseas contact International Services

chunks.title: Clients getting Greek Pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Clients getting Greek Pensions
A client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Greek pension that they are receiving. If they do not comply their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or payment can be suspended.
When a client is receiving payments from Greece you will need to find out the payment details in order to determine the effect it will have on the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
It is important that the information is obtained as quickly as possible to enable the client's New Zealand benefit or pension entitlement to be assessed correctly. As it can take some months to obtain information from the Greek authorities, it is preferable that the details are obtained from the client.
If the client is unable to provide full documentation of the payments they will need to complete an Information Release Authority form.
The form must be sent to International Services to enable them to obtain and verify the following information:
- the Greek Pension date of grant
- rate of payment in Greek currency and whether it includes any amount for the clients partner and any dependent children
- the frequency of the payment, eg: monthly, fortnightly etc
- reason for the grant, such as age, widowhood, disablement, or war service
- the name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment
- verification of any amount which is payment from voluntary contributions
Contact International Services or:

chunks.title: Commencement of payment in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Commencement of payment in Greece
When a client applies for their New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid in Greece before their departure from New Zealand, payments will start on the first payday after their departure from New Zealand.
When a client applies from Greece, the New Zealand benefit or pension will start on:
- the date they become entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension
- the date the agreement with Greece came into force (01 April 1994)
- the earlier of the date they applied for a New Zealand benefit or a Greek pension
whichever is the latest date.
Note the New Zealand domestic initial stand-down provisions apply to clients applying for New Zealand benefits other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
The Greek authorities forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Death in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Death in Greece
The normal procedures for cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions apply on the death of a client receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension in Greece.
Generally, the Greek authorities will advise International Services of the death of a client in Greece and International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
A New Zealand Funeral Grant can be paid in respect of clients who were living in Greece at the time of their death.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit
- Funeral Grant paid outside New Zealand

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on the death of a client follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients who were also receiving a Greek pension.
The executor of the client's estate will need to contact the Greek authorities directly at the following addresses if they require any details of the Greek pension, such as last payments due:
For either Social Security Institute (IKA) or Agricultural Insurance Organisation (OGA) contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies Greece
International Services will send the following information to the Greek authorities:
- the client's name
- the date of death and
- the name and address of the administrator of the estate
A lump sum benefit after death (funeral expenses) may be paid by the Greek authorities.
## SWIFTT
The executor of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen in SWIFTT so that International Services can advise the Greek authorities.
For more information see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit
- Funeral expenses
- New Zealand Funeral Grant

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
When a client is receiving a Greek pension the gross amount is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit.
The Greek pension is deducted from:
- the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension and
- the net rate of any other New Zealand benefit (including Accommodation Supplement)
When a client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Greek pension is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services
A fax should be sent to International Services with verification of the rate, type of Greek pension, the grant date and the name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already receiving a Greek pension at the time a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process
If you are unsure whether an overseas pension is deductible or not, contact International Services.
## Reviews
International Services must be advised of all clients who are receiving a Greek pension because it is International Services' responsibility to carry out New Zealand benefit or pension reviews required where the Greek pension deduction is being up-dated or reviewed.
Any other reviews of the client's New Zealand benefit, such as a change of relationship status or a change of chargeable income, should be completed by the Case Manager.

chunks.title: Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Greece
From 15 July 2013 onwards, people receiving existing portable payments of Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Greece will be grandparented on their existing rate and conditions.
References to the benefit names Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for Widowers are grandparented for existing clients and must still be used when administering these benefits payable under the Agreement with Greece and when corresponding with the client.
Grand parenting arrangements do not apply to the former Invalid's Benefit because the only change is the name change to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Grandparenting
- Welfare Reform impact on the Social Security Agreement with Greece

chunks.title: Funeral expenses — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Funeral expenses
When a client from Greece has died in New Zealand, they must meet all the qualifications for the New Zealand Funeral Grant.
Under the agreement a lump sum benefit after death (funeral expenses) may be paid by the Greek authorities to help with the funeral costs of a client from Greece who was living in New Zealand at the time of their death.
Any amount paid by the Greek authorities will be reduced by the amount of any Funeral Grant paid under New Zealand domestic legislation.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand Funeral Grant

chunks.title: Funeral Grant paid outside New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Funeral Grant paid outside New Zealand
Under the agreement with Greece a New Zealand Funeral Grant can be paid to a person who is living in Greece to help meet the funeral costs when:
- the deceased person or child had been ordinarily resident in New Zealand for a continuous period of at least 12 months at any time before their death and
- the deceased person has a surviving partner who is receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension under the agreement with Greece or
- the deceased child was a dependent child of a person who is receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension under the agreement with Greece
The amount of any assistance paid by the Greek authorities towards the cost of the funeral will be directly deducted from the New Zealand Funeral Grant.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Funeral Grant

chunks.title: Greek Life Certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Greek Life Certificates
When a client is receiving a Greek pension in New Zealand they are required to complete life certificates by the Greek authorities.
The Greek authorities will send the life certificate form directly to the client when it is due.
The client should complete the life certificate and return it directly to Greece.
If a client needs the life certificate witnessed it is important to check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
The life certificate is returned to the client to send directly to the Greek authorities.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Greek pensions paid in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Greek pensions paid in New Zealand
The agreement allows clients who have resided in Greece and made contributions to the Greek insurance scheme to get some Greek benefits or pensions.
Clients who have resided in Greece may be able to get the following assistance:
- Disability Pension
- Funeral Grant
- Orphans Pension
- Retirement Pension
- Survivor's Pension
## Payment
Greek pensions are paid directly to the client, generally on a monthly basis.
## Income
Greek pensions are directly deducted from the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
When a Greek pension is more than the main New Zealand benefit rate, the amount that exceeds the main benefit rate will be directly deducted from any Accommodation Supplement the client may get as a non-beneficiary.
## Medical requirements
The Greek authorities can require a client to be medically re-examined periodically, to check they are still entitled to their Greek Pension.
Any medical examinations are arranged by the Case Manager and the account is sent to International Services to arrange payment.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and the Hellenic Republic (Greece) allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- residence and or contributions to the national insurance scheme in Greece can be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- residence in New Zealand can be regarded as periods of residence and or contributions to the insurance scheme in Greece to meet the residence qualifications for some Greek benefits and pensions
- some Greek pensions can be paid in New Zealand
- some New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid in Greece
Note
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Greece.
For more information see:
- New Zealand benefits and pensions
- Welfare Reform impact on the Social Security Agreement with Greece
- Clients from Greece
- Greek pensions paid in New Zealand
- Changes and reviews for Greek pensions
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece
- Changes and reviews for NZ benefits in Greece

chunks.title: Last child turning 14 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Last child turning 14
Clients receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower will cease to be eligible for payments once their last child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Greece.
If the client returns to New Zealand after their last dependent child turns 14 they may be eligible for Jobseeker Support but will not be eligible for a New Zealand benefit if they remain in Greece.
Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) clients with dependent children or grand parented Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers with dependent children do not lose entitlement when their last child turns 14.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support Ending of Sole Parent Support when youngest child turns 14 years old

chunks.title: Methods of payment in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment in Greece
When a client is getting a New Zealand benefit or pension in Greece, they can choose to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account or to a bank account in Greece.
## Greek bank account
Payments made to a Greek bank account are credited four weekly.
If a client chooses to have money paid directly to a Greek bank account, Work and Income meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
There are three options for the first payment being made into a Greek bank account:
- payment can be made to an overseas bank account if the client has provided proof of their bank account
- the first payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the Greek bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the Greek bank account are given to International Services. Once account details are advised, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the Greek account with the first payment.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client intends to live in a country other than Greece for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
The client may still be entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension if they are moving to a country that has an agreement with New Zealand. The client will need to complete an application form for payment for the new country they are intending to reside in.
Note: The client must qualify for a New Zealand benefit or pension under that agreement, in order to be entitled to payment.
In other cases payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension should stop from the payday after the client's departure from Greece.
## Residence
If a client, resident in New Zealand, used their Greek residence to meet the New Zealand residence qualification, they would not be entitled to payment of their New Zealand benefit or pension when they move to another country unless:
- New Zealand has an agreement with that country and
- the client qualifies for the New Zealand benefit or pension under that agreement
## Payment cannot be made
New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension cannot be paid to a client who leaves Greece to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand or Greece as the client needs to be resident and present or ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand at the date they apply for payment overseas.
New Zealand benefits and pensions are not payable in the United Kingdom.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- General Portability
- Special Portability
- Return to New Zealand

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece
Under the agreement with Greece, the following New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid to former New Zealand residents who are residing or intend to reside in Greece:
- Funeral Grant
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Orphans Benefit
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with dependent children under 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Veterans Pension
The rules are different depending on whether the client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension and is moving to Greece, or if they are already living in Greece at the time they apply.
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Sole Parent Support - sole parent
- Emergency Benefits
- Jobseeker Support
- Supported Living Payment - care of sick or infirm
- Unsupported Child's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers going to or residing in Greece
- Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Greece
- Orphans going to or residing in Greece
- Superannuitants going to or residing in Greece
- Veterans going to or residing in Greece
- Applications for payment in Greece with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Greece
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Greece
- Funeral Grants paid outside New Zealand

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
The agreement with Greece allows residence in Greece and contributions to the Greek insurance scheme to be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualification for the following New Zealand benefits:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with dependent child/ren under 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally disabled)
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Orphans Benefit
- Veterans Pension
- Funeral Grant
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefits
- Sole Parent Support - sole parent
- Supported Living Payment - care of sick or infirm
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For more information see:
- Clients from Greece
- Greek pensions paid in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece
- Welfare Reform impact on the Social Security Agreement with Greece
- Changes and reviews for Greek pensions
- Changes and reviews for NZ benefits in Greece

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation
When a client from Greece meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except residence, they may qualify under the agreement with Greece.
The agreement allows periods of residence and/or contributions to the insurance scheme in Greece to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
If the client was born in Greece prior to the Second World War their birth certificate will show only the year of birth. The date of birth to use will be 1 July of the stated year.
The client may also be entitled to a Greek Pension, which may be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation.
## SWIFTT
When New Zealand Superannuation is granted using the agreement with Greece you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 08 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Residency
- Clients from Greece
- Greek pensions paid in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece
- NZ Superannuation clients going to or residing in Greece

chunks.title: Orphans going to or residing in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Orphans going to or residing in Greece
Under the agreement with Greece a client can be paid the New Zealand Orphans Benefit when they are residing in Greece.
The client can apply for the Orphans Benefit to be paid in Greece before their departure from New Zealand or from Greece.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Orphans Benefit
- intend to reside in Greece for more than 4 weeks and
- continue to be the principal caregiver of the child
The Orphans Benefit will be paid in Greece at the same rate that it is payable in New Zealand.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Greece to live in another country.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Greece
- Commencement of payment in Greece

chunks.title: Other payments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Other payments
When a client is receiving other payments, such as interest or rent from investments or properties they own in Greece, the payments will be treated in the same way as income earned in New Zealand.
You need to convert the income to New Zealand dollars using the current exchange rate. This can be found by using the SELXT screen in SWIFTT and entering the Greek country code 060.
If you are unsure how the calculation works you should contact International Services
For more information see:
- Charging income in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand benefit or pension being paid in Greece is overpaid you will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment
- their review and appeal rights and
- the relevant legislation (if the overpayment occurred as a result of a provision in the agreement, then the authority to establish an overpayment is contained in that Article of the agreement)
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deduction from any New Zealand benefit or pension that the client is receiving that is similar to the Greek benefit from which the overpayment arose.
If the client is no longer receiving payments from either country they will need to make their own arrangements to repay the debt.
International Services will provide details of the overpayment to the Greek authorities and follow up the recovery action.
## Review or appeal
If a client applies for a review or appeals a decision on the establishment of a debt or the rate of recovery, recovery action will be suspended until the outcome of that review or appeal is known.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reviews and appeals
- Debt management [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Rate payable in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Rate payable in Greece
When a New Zealand benefit or pension is paid to a client in Greece the rate of payment is determined by the number of years that the client has resided in New Zealand since the age of 20.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Greek Old Age Benefit being paid.
## New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension
The calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension is different to the calculation for other New Zealand benefits.
There is no provision in New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension to include payment for a grandparented non-qualified partner. The partner can only be paid New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Greece if they meet the qualifications in their own right.
The maximum rate payable is the single sharing accommodation rate or the married, civil union, de facto relationship rate depending on the client's circumstances.
## Supported Living Payment
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is paid to a married or civil union client in Greece their partner can be included.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Greece.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension
- Calculation for other benefits

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for a Greek pension. International Services will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not respond to requests to apply for a Greek pension.
International Services will talk to clients about the reasons why they must apply, including:
- clients must claim any benefit they may be entitled to from Greece, if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension
- it is their right as they have made contributions
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from Greece
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension may stop, but payment of a Greek pension may still continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 4 weeks their Sole Parent Support may stop but payment of a Greek pension may still continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 6 weeks their Supported Living Payment may stop but payment of a Greek pension may still continue
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate, and the rate of Greek pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended but the Greek pension will still be paid

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Greece and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, payment of the New Zealand benefit will continue to be paid at the same rate as when they were living in Greece.
This is because the client will not be considered as ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Client returns to New Zealand permanently
When a client receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Greece, returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their benefit can be reviewed from the date of return to New Zealand.
International Services must be advised as they are responsible for stopping payment made under the social security agreement.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Review date
A New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date a client is granted a Greek pension, or when the rate of a Greek pension changes.
If you have difficulty obtaining details of the overseas pension grant date, contact International Services for advice.
If you have a case where you feel an overpayment should be established you should contact International Services.
When a Greek pension is reduced, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the reduction.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions
- SWIFTT process

chunks.title: Greek pension paid in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Greek pension paid in New Zealand
If a client is unhappy with any decision regarding their Greek pension being paid in New Zealand they will need to write a letter to the Greek authorities and forward it to International Services at:
International ServicesP O Box 27 178Wellington
International Services will forward the client's letter to the Greek authorities.
International Services is responsible for any reviews and appeals in regard to the interpretation of the agreement with Greece and the effect of Greek pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions.
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
The New Zealand review and appeal process applies to any other decisions regarding New Zealand benefits or pensions, such as charging income or change in relationship status.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
Under the agreement with Greece a client may qualify for a New Zealand Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower if they meet all the qualifications.
Under the agreement:
- dependent children born in Greece can be accepted as being born in New Zealand
- periods of residence and/or contributions to the insurance scheme in Greece to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower
- the client may also be entitled to a Greek Pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Sole Parent Support
## SWIFTT
When Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers is granted using the agreement with Greece you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 08 in the entitlement code field.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Sole Parent Support Residence
- Applications for payment in Greece with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Clients from Greece
- Greek pensions paid in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece
- Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers going to or residing in Greece
- Care and protection concerns for a child or young person

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers going to or residing in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers going to or residing in Greece
Under the agreement with Greece a widow or widower can be paid the New Zealand Sole Parent Support when they are residing in Greece.
The client must apply for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower to be paid in Greece before their departure from New Zealand. New Zealanders already residing in Greece will not qualify.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they apply for payment overseas
- intend to live in Greece for more than 4 weeks and
- have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since the age of 20
## Change in circumstances
Sole Parent Support paid to widows or widowers in Greece is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Greece or New Zealand when they apply for the benefit or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Greece to live in another country.
Note Sole Parent Support payments will cease to be payable once the last dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Greece.
If the client is still receiving Sole Parent Support at the time they reach the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension they will no longer be eligible for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower and must test their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Greece
- Commencement of payment in Greece
- Welfare Reform impact on the Social Security Agreement with Greece
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Greece
- Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013
- Sole Parent Support

chunks.title: Superannuitants going to or residing in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Superannuitants going to or residing in Greece
Under the agreement with Greece a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation when they are residing in Greece.
The client can apply for New Zealand Superannuation to be paid in Greece before their departure from New Zealand or from Greece.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving New Zealand Superannuation
- intend to live in Greece for more than 26 weeks and
- have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20
## Partners
If the client has a partner the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement to a New Zealand benefit in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Greece to live in another country.
## Life certificates
The client will be sent a life certificate, either every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances, which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the New Zealand Superannuation will stop.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Greece
- Commencement of payment in Greece

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment
When a client from Greece meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) except residence, they may qualify under the agreement with Greece.
The agreement allows residence and/or periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Greece to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
The client must meet the New Zealand medical criteria.
The client may also be entitled to a Greek Pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
For more information see:
- Direct Deductions
## SWIFTT
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is granted using the agreement with Greece you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 08 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Supported Living Payment Residence
- Clients from Greece
- Greek pensions paid in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Greece
Under the agreement with Greece a client can be paid the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when they are residing in Greece.
The client must apply for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) to be paid in Greece before their departure from New Zealand. New Zealanders already residing in Greece will not qualify.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they apply for payment overseas
- intend to live in Greece for more than 6 weeks and
- have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since the age of 20
## Payment to partners
Payment can be made to the partner of a qualifying client. The partner does not have to establish entitlement in their own right.
## Medical examinations
The Greek authorities will arrange and pay for any medical examination that is required for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) while a client is living in Greece.
## Change in circumstances
Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) paid in Greece is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Greece or New Zealand when they apply for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Greece to live in another country.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Commencement of payment in Greece
- Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: SWIFTT process — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT process
When a client is receiving a Greek pension that is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit or pension it is important that this is processed correctly in SWIFTT.
You will need to add the following information in the SOPDA screen in SWIFTT:
- letter indicator (defaults to x)
- the rate of the Greek pension in Greek currency
- whether the overseas pension is a gross or net amount
- the frequency at which the payments are made
- the weekly amount of bank fees allowed (contact International Services)
- the percentage of any private pension that is included in the overseas pension
- any Greek pension reference number
- country code 060
- whether the pension is a deductible pension Y/N
Note some of these fields may not be applicable to all clients and some are only used by International Services
The New Zealand dollar amount of the Greek pension will be displayed on the SOPHI screen once the above details have been entered.
The New Zealand dollar amount showing on the SOPHI screen will need to be added to the 'O/seas Pen direct ded' field using the INCMA screen in SWIFTT.
If you need further information you should contact International Services.
## SWIFTT
International Services up-dates the exchange rate table in SWIFTT each month, and the exchange rate table is linked to the country codes.
When the Greek pension details are correctly recorded SWIFTT will automatically calculate the Greek pension deduction from the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension payable.
For benefits paid other than weekly, SWIFTT will:
- recalculate the rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension each month and
- send a letter to advise the client if the letter indicator in the SOPDA screen is set to Y
- if a client does not wish to receive their advice letters, the indicator in the SWIFTT SOPHC screen should be set to N
- only International Services can change the letter indicator after the initial grant of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
International Services manually up-dates other New Zealand benefits and pensions periodically.

chunks.title: Clients in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Clients in New Zealand
When a client is receiving a Greek pension in New Zealand, they are usually liable for New Zealand tax, unless their pension is a direct deduction from a New Zealand benefit other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
The client should contact Inland Revenue to discuss their New Zealand tax liability for the Greek pension and any New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Clients in Greece
New Zealand benefits paid in Greece are not taxed in New Zealand, but may be taxed in Greece.
The client must make their own tax arrangements with the Greek tax authority.

chunks.title: Veterans going to or residing in Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Veterans going to or residing in Greece
Under the agreement with Greece a client can be paid the New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are residing in Greece.
The client can apply for the Veterans Pension to be paid in Greece before their departure from New Zealand or from Greece.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving a Veterans Pension
- intend to live in Greece for more than 26 weeks and
- have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20
## Partners
If the client has a partner each partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension in their own right.
## Life certificate
The client will be sent a life certificate, either every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances, which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the Veterans Pension will stop.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Greece
- Commencement of payment in Greece

chunks.title: Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension
When a client from Greece meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Veterans Pension except residence, they may qualify under the agreement with Greece.
The agreement allows periods of residence and/or contributions to the insurance scheme in Greece to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Veterans Pension.
The client must meet the New Zealand service and disability qualifications.
If the client was born in Greece prior to the Second World War their birth certificate will show only the year of birth. The date of birth to use will be 1 July of the stated year.
The client may also be entitled to a Greek Pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Veterans Pension.
For more information see:
- Direct Deductions
## SWIFTT
When Veterans Pension is granted using the agreement with Greece you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 08 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or the Veterans Pension Centre or see:
- Clients from Greece
- Greek pensions paid in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Greece
- Veterans going to or residing in Greece

chunks.title: Welfare Reform impact on the Social Security Agreement with Greece — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal hellenic republic
chunks.text:
## Welfare Reform impact on the Social Security Agreement with Greece
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Greece.
## New Benefit categories
Jobseeker Support will replace:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent and widowers with dependent children aged 14 years or older
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women alone
- Sickness Benefit (including Sickness Benefit Hardship)
- Unemployment Benefit (including Unemployment Benefit Student Hardship and Unemployment Benefit Training)
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged 14 years or older or have no children
Sole Parent Support will replace:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole Parent and widowers with dependent children aged under 14 years
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged under 14 years
Supported Living Payment will replace:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Care of sick or infirm
- Invalid's Benefit
The following benefits will remain:
- Emergency Benefit for clients in hardship (including Emergency Maintenance Allowance)
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
- Unsupported Child Benefit and Orphan's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For entitlements arising from an Agreement occurring on or after 15 July 2013 references in the agreement with Greece to the former benefit names must be considered as references to the new names. The name changes do not affect New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
For more information see:
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Greece
- Applications for payment in Greece with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Greece after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Admission to hospital — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital
When a client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced.
The Irish benefit or pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the Irish benefit or pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner and the rate of an Irish benefit or pension for one partner is more than the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension the excess amount of the Irish benefit or pension is deducted from the other partner's New Zealand benefit or pension payment.

chunks.title: Admission to hospital or prison — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital or prison
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Republic of Ireland the rate of payment does not change when the client is admitted to hospital or prison.
This is because overseas institutions are not covered by the definitions of institutions in New Zealand legislation.

chunks.title: Application lodged before departure — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Application lodged before departure
When a client advises that they intend to reside in the Republic of Ireland they will need to:
- complete an Application for Payment Overseas form (WIS7W)
- complete an Application for Payment Overseas interview form (WIF9W)
- provide verification of the total period of their residence in New Zealand
- provide their passport plus one other form of identification and
- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to Ireland
The application form, interview form and supporting documents should be sent for processing to International Services
Before any current New Zealand benefit is cancelled or suspended you should contact International Services.
## Application for New Zealand benefit
If the client is not yet receiving a New Zealand benefit, and is living in New Zealand, an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the qualifications for the particular benefit. An application form for payment to be made in Ireland must also be completed.
The client can use their periods of insurance contributions in Ireland to meet the qualifications for the New Zealand benefit or pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Applications lodged in Ireland
- Commencement of payment in Ireland
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland

chunks.title: Applications for payment in Ireland with entitlements before 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Applications for payment in Ireland with entitlements before 15 July 2013
To decide if an application for portable Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Ireland is decided and grandparented under the old rules the following will apply:
- the applicant must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or Ireland on 14 July 2013 and
- an application for payment in Ireland may be received before or after 15 July 2013 but there must be entitlement to Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers from a date before 15 July 2013
Provided these conditions are met an application may be granted under the old rules and the grandparenting provisions will apply. If any one of the conditions is not met the application must be decided under the new rules.

chunks.title: Applications lodged in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Applications lodged in Ireland
When a former New Zealand resident is already residing in the Republic of Ireland they will be entitled to receive a New Zealand benefit or pension if they use the provisions of the agreement to meet the qualifying criteria.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
The client will need to complete an Application for New Zealand Benefit (NZ1).
There are special conditions relating to specific benefits and pensions.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged before departure
- Commencement of payment in Ireland
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland

chunks.title: Benefit entitlements in Ireland after 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Benefit entitlements in Ireland after 15 July 2013
New applications for Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers under the agreement with Ireland with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Sole Parent Support.
In order to qualify the applicant must:
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or in Ireland on 15 July 2013
- have a spouse who has died and
- have a dependent child under the age of 14 years
Entitlement to Sole Parent Support will cease when the dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Ireland.
New applications for Invalids Benefits under the Agreement with Ireland with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Supported Living Payment. The only change to this benefit is the name change from Invalids Benefit to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Last child turning 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)

chunks.title: Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension
When New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in the Republic of Ireland the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence since age 20
and divide by
- the number for the date the client was born (see calculation table)
and multiply by
- the maximum benefit rate
The minimum payment that can be paid is:
- 1/40 to 1/45 of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
- 50% of the maximum New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension rate if the client was already receiving this amount overseas before the agreement coming into effect (1 March 1994)
The maximum rate that can be paid is:
- 100% of the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
The maximum rate of payment is the full gross rate of either the half married, civil union or de facto rate, or the single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, depending on the client's circumstances.
There is no provision to pay the married, civil union or de facto rate of payment to same sex couples living in Ireland. Each partner must be assessed on an individual basis and be paid at the single sharing accommodation rate.
Note the Reciprocal Agreement with the Republic of Ireland and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in the Republic of Ireland, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension are paid without regard to any of the following Irish benefits:
- Retirement Pension
- Old Age (Contributory) Pension
- Widows (Contributory) Pension
- Invalidity Pension
Clients who were already getting payment in Ireland before 29 July 1993, may be entitled to a higher rate under the agreement, but they cannot get less than 50% of the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
## Residence
A period of up to 26 weeks absence from New Zealand can be included as New Zealand residence, so long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help eg, family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Ireland.

chunks.title: Calculation for other benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Calculation for other benefits
When a benefit other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in the Republic of Ireland use the following formula to calculate the rate of payment:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence since age 20
and
- divide this by 300
and
- multiply this by maximum benefit rate
The minimum rate that can be paid is:
- 12 divided by 300 multiplied by maximum benefit rate
The maximum rate of payment is the full net rate of the benefit the client is entitled to.
New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension are paid without regard to any of the following Irish benefits:
- Retirement Pension
- Old Age (Contributory) Pension
- Widows (Contributory) Pension
- Invalidity Pension
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Ireland.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Change in income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When a client is getting one of the following New Zealand benefits or pensions that is being paid in the Republic of Ireland it will still be income tested and the client will need to advise when there is any change in their income:
- Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
The client must provide details of all income they get in Ireland or New Zealand.
This includes any Child Support payments they get from Inland Revenue.
## Exception
Some Irish pensions are not taken into account.
## Review of Circumstances
A Confirming your Circumstances form will be sent for the client to complete and return to New Zealand every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International Services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension paid in the Republic of Ireland when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a relationship in the nature of a marriage or
- a client becomes single through separation; the marriage or civil union is dissolved; or the death of their partner

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for Irish benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for Irish benefits and pensions
A client is obliged to advise Work and Income of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also required to provide any information required by the Irish authorities to ensure that they are still entitled to their Irish benefit or pension paid in New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Admission to hospital
- Clients going overseas
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Ireland
- Irish Life Certificates
- Death of a client in New Zealand
- Reviews and Appeals
- Taxation

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Ireland
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension in the Republic of Ireland or the rate payable.
MSD may also review a New Zealand benefit or pension in Ireland at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions paid in Ireland.
## Life certificates
Clients receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Ireland will need to complete a Life certificate which will be sent to them every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances
## Review of Circumstances
Clients receiving other New Zealand benefits or pensions in Ireland will need to complete a Confirming your Circumstances form which will be sent to them every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment or have Orphan's Benefit paid for them in the Republic of Ireland.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment or are no longer eligible for Orphan's Benefit from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment or have Orphan's Benefit paid for them for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from Supported Living Payment or Orphan's Benefit must stop from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier.
Note if the caregiver also gets Orphan's Benefit for other children, the payments for the other children will not be affected by another child turning 18.

chunks.title: Clients entitled to Irish benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Clients entitled to Irish benefits and pensions
A client must apply for any benefit or pension that they may be entitled to from the Republic of Ireland if they are applying for or are receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension.
If a client has residence in Ireland they will need to complete an application for an Irish pension. International Services will contact clients with residence in Ireland and ask them to apply.
When the client completes the application it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies)
- the application form and the 'Authority to release information and adjust Irish arrears' form are signed and dated
If the client refuses to apply for any Irish benefit or pension to which they may be entitled you should contact International Services.
For more information see:
- Refusal to apply
- Payment options

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Clients going overseas
When a client receiving an Irish benefit or pension leaves New Zealand for a temporary absence the Irish benefit or pension may still be paid.
The normal absence provisions apply to any New Zealand benefit or pension they are receiving.
If a client is going to the Republic of Ireland and intends to stay there for more than 26 weeks they may be able to receive payment of their New Zealand benefit or pension in Ireland.
If the client is going to reside in any other country they may qualify for payment overseas depending on their circumstances. For advice about a client's entitlement overseas contact International Services
For more information see:
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland

chunks.title: Clients receiving Irish benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving Irish benefits and pensions
A client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Irish benefit or pension that they are receiving. If they do not comply their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or payment can be suspended.
When a client is receiving payments from the Republic of Ireland you will need to find out the details of payment in order to determine the effect it will have on the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
It is important that the information is obtained as quickly as possible to enable the client's New Zealand benefit or pension entitlement to be assessed correctly.
If the client is unable to provide full documentation of the payments they will need to complete an Information Release Authority form.
The form must be sent to International Services to enable International Services to obtain and verify the following information:
- rate of payment in Irish currency and whether it includes any amount in respect of the clients partner and any dependent children
- reason for the grant, such as age, widowhood, disablement, or war service
- the name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment
- verification of any amount which is payment from voluntary contributions
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Payment options
- Other income

chunks.title: Commencement of payment in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Commencement of payment in Ireland
When a client applies for their New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid in the Republic of Ireland before their departure from New Zealand, payments under the Irish Agreement will start on the first payday after their departure.
When a client applies from Ireland, the New Zealand benefit or pension will start on:
- the date they become entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension
- the date the agreement with Ireland came into force (1 March 1993)
- the earlier of the date they applied for a New Zealand benefit or an Irish pension
whichever is the latest date.
Note that the initial stand-down applies to clients applying for New Zealand benefits other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
The Irish authorities forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services
For more information International Services or see:
- Rate payable in Ireland
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Death in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Death in Ireland
The normal procedures for cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions apply on the death of a client receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Republic of Ireland.
Generally the Irish authorities will advise International Services of the death of a client in Ireland and International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
Note Funeral Grants are not payable for clients who were living in Ireland at the time of their death.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Change in relationship status
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on death follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients who were also getting an Irish benefit or pension.
The executor/administrator of the client's estate will need to contact the Irish authorities directly at Department of Social, Community and Family Affairs if they require any details of the Irish benefit or pension, such as last payments due. See:
- Overseas pension agencies Republic of Ireland
International Services will send the following information to the Irish authorities:
- the clients name
- date of death and
- the name and address of the executor/administrator of the estate
The executor/administrator of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen so International Services can advise the Irish authorities.
For more information see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
When a client is receiving or entitled to receive an Irish benefit or pension it will generally be directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit or pension.
The amount to deduct is the rate of the benefit or pension before the deduction of any New Zealand tax.
The Irish benefit or pension is deducted from:
- the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and
- the net rate of any other New Zealand benefit
When a client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Irish benefit or pension is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services.
A fax should be sent to International Services with verification of the rate, type of Irish benefit or pension, the grant date and the name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already receiving an Irish benefit or pension at the time a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process.
If you are unsure whether an overseas pension is deductible, contact International Services for advice.
## Reviews
International Services must be advised of all clients who are receiving an Irish benefit or pension because it is International Services' responsibility to carry out New Zealand benefit or pension reviews required where the Irish benefit or pension deduction is being up-dated or reviewed.
Any other reviews of the clients New Zealand benefit, such as a change of relationship status or a change of chargeable income, should be completed by the case manager.

chunks.title: Direct Payment Option — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Direct Payment Option
When a client is receiving an Irish benefit or pension they can choose to have the Irish benefit or pension paid directly to their own bank account.
Under this method of payment:
- clients can choose to have their Irish benefit or pension paid once every 4 or 13 weeks
- payment will be converted at the rate of exchange applicable on the day the bank credits their account
- the client receives the gross rate of the Irish benefit or pension and is responsible for any tax liability on it
- the amount deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension will be based on an average exchange rate for the Irish benefit or pension
- if the client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension the rate will be automatically recalculated in SWIFTT each month using an average of the Ireland exchange rates for previous month
- if the client is receiving any other New Zealand benefit or pension International Services will manually review the rate periodically or when the client requests it
- there is no due/paid assessment at the end of each year to take into account the exact exchange rate that the Irish benefit or pension was paid to the client
- when the Irish benefit or pension is payable at two pounds or less per week the client will be paid once a year in December unless they choose to have it paid at 4 or 13 weekly intervals
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Ireland
From 15 July 2013 onwards, people receiving existing portable payments of Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Ireland will be grandparented on their existing rate and conditions.
References to the benefit names Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for Widowers are grandparented for existing clients and must still be used when administering these benefits payable under the Agreement with Ireland and when corresponding with the client.
Grandparenting arrangements do not apply to the former Invalids Benefit because the only change is the name change to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Grandparenting
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Ireland

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and the Republic of Ireland allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- contributions to the Irish insurance scheme can be regarded as residence in New Zealand to meet the residence qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- residence in New Zealand can be regarded as periods of contributions to the Irish insurance scheme to meet the residence qualifications for some Irish benefits and pensions
- some Irish benefits and pensions can be paid in New Zealand
- some New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid in Ireland
- War pensions from either country are not included in the agreement
Note on 15 July 2013 new provisions provided for consolidation of benefits, with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes had some impacts on the Agreement with Ireland.
For more information see:
- New Zealand benefits and pensions
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Ireland
- Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand
- Changes and reviews for Irish benefits and pensions
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Ireland

chunks.title: Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand
