When a former resident of the Republic of Ireland applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they are receiving an Irish benefit or pension, or if they may be entitled to one.
A client who has previously resided in Ireland must show their Overseas Residence on the application form when they apply for any New Zealand benefit or pension.
The overseas residence details must be entered on CMS. These details are used by International Services to determine whether the client may be entitled to an Irish benefit or pension.
If the client is already receiving an overseas pension you should find out the details to establish whether this pension should be a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension.
The following Irish pensions are covered by the agreement and may be payable to former Irish residents living in New Zealand:
- Invalidity Pension
- State Pension (contributory)
- Guardian's Payment (contributory)
- State Pension (transition)
- Widows (Contributory) Pension
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Clients receiving Irish benefits or pensions
- Clients entitled to Irish benefits or pensions
- Other income
- Direct deductions
- Review date
- Payment options

chunks.title: Irish life certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Irish life certificates
When a client is receiving an Irish benefit or pension in New Zealand they are required to complete life certificates by the Irish authorities.
The Irish authorities will send the life certificate form directly to the client when it is due.
The client should complete the life certificate and return it directly to the Republic of Ireland.
If a client needs the life certificate witnessed it is important to check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
The life certificate is returned to the client to send directly to the Irish authorities.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Last child turning 14 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Last child turning 14
Clients receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower will cease to be eligible for payments once their last child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Ireland.
If the client returns to New Zealand after their last dependent child turns 14 they may be eligible for Jobseeker Support but will not be eligible for a New Zealand benefit if they remain in Ireland.
Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) clients with dependent children or grandparented Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers with dependent children do not lose entitlement when their last child turns 14.
For more information see:
- Main benefits Sole Parent Support

chunks.title: Methods of payment in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment in Ireland
When a client receives a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Republic of Ireland they can choose to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account or to a bank account in Ireland.
## Irish bank account
Payments made to an Irish bank account are credited four weekly.
If a client chooses to have money paid directly to an Irish bank account, Work and Income meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
There are 3 options for the first payment being made into an Irish bank account:
- payment can be made to an over seas bank account if the client has provided proof of their bank account
- the first payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the Irish bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the Irish bank account are given to International Services. Once account details are advised, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the Irish account with the first payment.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client intends to live in a country other than New Zealand or the Republic of Ireland for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
The client may still be entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension if:
- they are moving to a country, other than United Kingdom or Australia, which has an agreement with New Zealand
Payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension should stop from the payday after the client's departure from Ireland until the client can test their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension in the country that they have moved to.
## Residence
If the client is receiving the New Zealand benefit or pension by using their Irish periods of insurance to meet the New Zealand residence qualification, they may not be entitled to have the New Zealand benefit or pension paid in another agreement country depending on their circumstances.
## Payment cannot be made
New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension cannot be paid to a client who leaves Ireland to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand as the client needs to be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand at the date they apply for payment overseas.
New Zealand benefits or pensions are not payable in the United Kingdom.
Example
A client in receipt of New Zealand Superannuation with 12 months New Zealand residence has used their Irish period of Insurance to meet the New Zealand Superannuation residence requirement.
The client now wants to live in Canada but has no previous Canadian residence. Although New Zealand has an agreement with Canada the client has insufficient New Zealand residence to be entitled to payment overseas.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reciprocal agreements
- General Portability
- Special Portability
- Return to New Zealand

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland
Under the agreement with the Republic of Ireland, the following New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid to former New Zealand residents who are residing or intend to reside in the Republic of Ireland:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Orphans Benefit
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Veterans Pension
The rules are different depending on whether the client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension and is moving to Ireland, or if they are already living in Ireland when they apply.
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefit
- Jobseeker Support
- Sole Parent Support (sole parents)
- Supported Living Payment (care of sick or infirm)
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
The following pensions are covered by the agreement and may be payable to former New Zealand residents residing in Ireland:
- Old age (Contributory) pension
- Retirement pension
- Widows (Contributory) pension
- Invalidity Pension
- Orphans Contributory Allowance
Clients should contact the Irish Social Security Agency for more information.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers going to or residing in Ireland
- Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Ireland
- NZ Superannuation clients going to or residing in Ireland
- Veterans going to or residing in Ireland
- Orphans going to or residing in Ireland
- Applications for payment in Ireland with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Ireland after 15 July 2013
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Ireland
- Client going overseas
- Application lodged before departure
- Application lodged in Ireland
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
Under the agreement with the Republic of Ireland, periods of contributions to the Irish insurance scheme can be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualification for the following New Zealand benefits:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Orphans Benefit
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers (with dependent child/ren under 14)
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Veterans Pension
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefits
- Jobseeker Support
- Sole Parent Support (sole parent)
- Supported Living Payment (care of sick or infirm)
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For more information see:
- Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Ireland
- Changes and reviews for Irish benefits and pensions
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Ireland

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation
When a client from the Republic of Ireland meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Ireland.
The agreement with Ireland allows periods of contributions to the Irish insurance scheme since the age of 20 to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
The client must be the New Zealand qualifying age.
The client's contributions to the Irish insurance scheme together with any periods of New Zealand residence must total 10 years since the age of 20 and 5 years since the age of 50.
The client may also be entitled to an Irish benefit or pension, which may be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation.
## SWIFTT
When New Zealand Superannuation is granted using the agreement with Ireland you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 07 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Residency
- Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland
- NZ Superannuation clients going to or residing in Ireland

chunks.title: NZ Superannuation clients going to or residing in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## NZ Superannuation clients going to or residing in Ireland
Under the agreement with the Republic of Ireland a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation when they are residing in Ireland.
The client can apply for the New Zealand Superannuation to be paid in Ireland before their departure from New Zealand or from Ireland.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving New Zealand Superannuation
- be ordinarily resident and present in Ireland or New Zealand when they apply for payment overseas
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Ireland for more than 26 weeks and
- have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since the age of 20
The client can use their periods of insurance contributions in Ireland to meet the residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
## Partners
If the client has a partner the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Ireland to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate either every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the New Zealand Superannuation will stop.
## Intending to reside in Ireland
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Ireland for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Ireland
Example
A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Ireland. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Ireland for benefit purposes.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged before departure
- Application lodged in Ireland
- Commencement of payment in Ireland

chunks.title: Orphans Benefit — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Orphans Benefit
When a client from the Republic of Ireland meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Orphans Benefit except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Ireland.
The agreement with Ireland allows for birth in Ireland to be regarded as birth in New Zealand to meet the residence laws for Orphans Benefit.
The client may also be entitled to an Irish benefit or pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Orphans Benefit.
## SWIFTT
When Orphans Benefit is granted using the agreement with Ireland you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 07 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Orphans Benefit Residency
- Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland
- Orphans going to or residing in Ireland

chunks.title: Orphans going to or residing in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Orphans going to or residing in Ireland
Under the agreement with the Republic of Ireland a client can be paid the New Zealand Orphans Benefit when they are residing in Ireland.
The client can apply for the Orphans Benefit to be paid in Ireland before their departure from New Zealand or from Ireland.
In all cases the client must:
- be ordinarily resident in Ireland or intending to be ordinarily resident in Ireland for at least 26 weeks
- be present in Ireland or New Zealand on the date they apply
- be entitled to or receiving Orphans Benefit
- be an eligible caregiver or principal temporary caregiver of the child
The following conditions must also be met:
- the child must intend to live in Ireland for more than 26 weeks
- the event that gave rise to entitlement to Orphans Benefit must have occurred when the child was living in New Zealand and
- the child must have been born in New Zealand or
- the child has had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand
The Orphans Benefit will be paid in Ireland at the same rate that it is payable in New Zealand.
## For more information contact
- International Services
## Or see:
- Application lodged before departure
- Application lodged in Ireland
- Commencement of payment in Ireland

chunks.title: Other income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Other income
When a client is receiving other income, such as interest or rent from investments or properties they own in the Republic of Ireland, the income will be treated in the same way as income earned in New Zealand.
You need to convert the income to New Zealand dollars using the current exchange rate. This can be found by using the SELXT screen in SWIFTT and entering the Irish country code 075.
If you are unsure how the calculation works you should contact International Services
For more information see:
- Charging income in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand benefit or pension being paid in the Republic of Ireland is overpaid you will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment
- their review and appeal rights and
- the relevant section of the legislation or article of the agreement
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deductions from any New Zealand benefit or pension that the client is receiving.
If the client is no longer receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension the Irish authorities will recover the overpayment from any current Irish benefit or pension payments.
If the client is no longer receiving any benefit or pension they will need to make arrangements to repay the debt themselves.

chunks.title: Payment options — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Payment options
When a client is receiving a benefit or pension through the Republic of Ireland Social Welfare Services, they can choose to have their Irish benefit or pension paid by the:
- Direct Payment Option or
- Special Banking Option
Clients will be asked to select a payment option when they are sent an Irish pension application pack by International Services
Clients can change from one payment option to the other at any time but can usually only join the Special Banking Option once.
All payment option changes are completed by International Services.
A client can authorise the Irish authorities to pay arrears of their Irish pension direct to Work and Income regardless of the payment option they choose for regular payments.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Rate payable in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Rate payable in Ireland
When a New Zealand benefit or pension is paid to a client in the Republic of Ireland the rate of payment is determined by the number of months that the client has resided in New Zealand since the age of 20.
There is no calculation for Orphans Benefit, it is paid at the rate appropriate to the age of the child.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Irish benefit or pension being paid. Generally other overseas pensions are a direct deduction.
## New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension
The calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension is different to the calculation for other New Zealand benefits.
There is no provision in New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension to include payment for a grandparented non-qualified partner. The partner can only be paid New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Ireland if they meet the qualifications in their own right.
The maximum rate payable is the single sharing accommodation rate or the married, civil union, de facto relationship rate depending on the client's circumstances.
## Supported Living Payment
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is paid to a married or civil union client in Ireland their partner can be included.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Ireland.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for an Irish benefit or pension. International Services will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not respond to requests to apply for an Irish benefit or pension.
International Services will talk to clients about the reasons they must apply, including:
- clients must claim any benefit they may be entitled to from the Republic of Ireland if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension
- it is their right as they have made contributions
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from Ireland
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension may stop, but payment of an Irish benefit or pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 4 weeks their Sole Parent Support may stop but payment of an Irish benefit or pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 6 weeks their Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) may stop but payment of an Irish benefit or pension may continue
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate, and the rate of Irish benefit or pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended but the Irish benefit or pension will still be paid

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Republic of Ireland and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, payment of the New Zealand benefit will continue to be paid at the same rate as when they were living in Ireland.
This is because the client will not be considered as ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Client returns to New Zealand permanently
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Ireland and returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their benefit can be reviewed from the date of return to New Zealand.
International Services must be advised as they are responsible for stopping payment made under the social security agreement.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Review date
A New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date a client is granted an Irish benefit or pension, or when the rate of an Irish benefit or pension changes.
If you have difficulty obtaining details of the overseas pension granted contact International Services for advice.
When an Irish benefit or pension is reduced, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the reduction.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Reviews and appeals — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Reviews and appeals
If a client is unhappy with any decision regarding their Irish benefit or pension being paid in New Zealand they will need to write within 21 days of the decision being conveyed to the Social Welfare Appeals Office. For the contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies Republic of Ireland
The client should set out their grounds for disagreeing with the decision in the letter.
International Services is responsible for any reviews and appeals in regard to:
- the interpretation of the agreement with the Republic of Ireland
- the effect of Irish pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions and
- New Zealand benefits and pensions being paid in Ireland
The New Zealand review and appeal process applies to any other decisions regarding New Zealand benefits or pensions paid in New Zealand, such as charging income or change in relationship status.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
Under the agreement with the Republic of Ireland a client may qualify for a New Zealand Sole Parent Support as a widow and widower if they meet all the qualifications.
Under the agreement:
- dependent children born in Ireland can be accepted as being born in New Zealand
- a widow or widower's periods of contributions to the Irish insurance scheme to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Widows Benefit
a widow can use their own or their last deceased spouse or civil union partner's periods of contributions to the Irish insurance scheme as periods of New Zealand residence to meet the residence criteria.
- the client may also be entitled to an Irish benefit or pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Sole Parent Support
## SWIFTT
When Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers is granted using the agreement with Ireland you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 07 in the entitlement code field.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Sole Parent Support Residence
- Main benefit Sole Parent Support
- Applications for payment in Ireland with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland
- Sole Parent Support widows and widowers going to or residing in Ireland
- Care and protection concerns for a child or young person

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers going to or residing in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: Under the agreement with the Republic of Ireland a widow or widower can be paid the New Zealand Sole Parent Support when they are ordinarily resident in Ireland. The client can apply for the Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower to be paid in Ireland before their departure from New Zealand or from Ireland. In all cases the client must: - have the intention of living in Ireland for more than 26 weeks - be ordinarily resident and present in Ireland or New Zealand when they apply under the agreement - have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since the age of 20 and - meet the qualifications Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower Children born in Ireland can be regarded as born in New Zealand for Sole Parent Support.

chunks.title: Income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: Sole Parent Support paid to widows and widowers in Ireland is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Ireland or New Zealand when they apply for the benefit or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Intending to reside in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Ireland for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Ireland. Example A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Ireland. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Ireland for benefit purposes.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Ireland to live in another country. Sole Parent Support will cease when the client's last dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Ireland. If the client is still receiving Sole Parent Support at the time they reach the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension they will no longer be eligible for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower and must apply for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension. For more information contact International Services or see: - Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit - Application lodged before departure - Application lodged in Ireland - Commencement of payment in Ireland - Main benefit Sole Parent Support - Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Ireland - Benefit entitlements in Ireland after 15 July 2013 - Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Ireland

chunks.title: Special Banking Option — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option
When a client is receiving an Irish benefit or pension they can choose to have it paid into a Special Banking Option account by the Irish authorities. The client will then receive the full rate of their New Zealand benefit or pension.
The advantages of this option are:
- the client receives a regular payment
- tax is already deducted
- the client is not affected by fluctuations in the exchange rate
Clients may elect to join the Special Banking Option at any time but cannot re-join once they have chosen to cancel the option (there are exceptions, contact International Services).
The Special Banking Option is not suitable for clients whose Irish benefit or pension is higher than (or likely to be higher than) the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Partner
When a client has a partner they must both choose the same payment option.
For more information contact International Services, or see:
- Special Banking Option applications

chunks.title: Special Banking Option applications — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option applications
When a client chooses the Special Banking Option for their Irish benefit or pension they will be sent an application pack from International Services containing:
- an Application for the Special Banking Option
- an Application for a Special Bank Account and
- an Authority to Release Information form (this form allows us to share information regarding pension entitlements with the Social Welfare Services Office in the Republic of Ireland)
All three forms must be fully completed and forwarded to International Services for processing.
## Note
- when a client has a partner they must both choose the same payment option
- the client can change from the direct payment method to the Special Banking Option at any time
- if the client has changed from the Special Banking Option to the direct payment option they cannot re-join the Special Banking Option
- the client does not have access to the Special Banking Option account that the Irish benefit or pension is paid into as it is simply a holding account for funds that are to be paid to MSD

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment
When a client from the Republic of Ireland meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Ireland.
The agreement with Ireland allows periods of contributions to the Irish insurance scheme to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
The client must meet the New Zealand medical criteria.
The client's contributions to the Irish insurance scheme together with any period of residence in New Zealand must total 2 continuous years.
The client may also be entitled to an Irish benefit or pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
## SWIFTT
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is granted using the agreement with Ireland you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 07 in the entitlement code field.
Note Supported Living Payment for the care of the sick or infirm is not payable under the Irish Agreement.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Supported Living Payment Residence
- Main benefit Supported Living Payment
- Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland
- Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Ireland
- Benefit entitlements in Ireland after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: Under the agreement with the Republic of Ireland a client can be paid the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when they are ordinarily resident in Ireland. The client can apply for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) to be paid in Ireland before their departure from New Zealand or after their arrival in Ireland. In all cases the client must: - be entitled to or receiving Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) - be ordinarily resident in Ireland or New Zealand at the time they apply for payment from overseas - intend to reside in Ireland for more than 26 weeks - be present in New Zealand or Ireland at the time they apply - have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since the age of 20 Note the client can use their periods of insurance contributions in Ireland to meet the residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).

chunks.title: Medical examinations — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: The Irish authorities will arrange and pay for any medical examination that is required for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when a client is living in Ireland.

chunks.title: Income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) paid in Ireland is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Ireland or New Zealand when they apply for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Ireland to live in another country. When the client reaches the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension they will no longer be eligible for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) and must test their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.

chunks.title: Intending to reside in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text: If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of living in Ireland for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Ireland. Example A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Ireland. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Ireland for benefit purposes. For more information contact International Services or see: - Application lodged before departure - Application lodged in Ireland - Commencement of payment in Ireland - Benefit entitlements in Ireland after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Clients in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Clients in New Zealand
When a client is receiving an Irish benefit or pension in New Zealand paid directly to their own bank account, they may have to pay New Zealand income tax. This is unless the Irish benefit or pension is a direct deduction from a New Zealand Benefit other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
The client should contact Inland Revenue to discuss their New Zealand tax liability for the Irish benefit or pension and any New Zealand benefit or pension.
Note clients who have their Irish Pension paid to the special banking option account receive the full rate of New Zealand benefit or pension and tax is already deducted.
## Clients in Ireland
New Zealand benefits paid in the Republic of Ireland are not taxed in New Zealand but may be taxed in Ireland.
The client must make their own tax arrangements with the Irish tax authority.

chunks.title: Veterans going to or residing in Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Veterans going to or residing in Ireland
Under the agreement with the Republic of Ireland a client can be paid the New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are residing in Ireland.
The client can apply for the Veterans Pension to be paid in Ireland before their departure from New Zealand or from Ireland.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Veterans Pension
- be ordinarily resident and present in Ireland or New Zealand when they apply for payment under the agreement
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Ireland for at least 26 weeks
- have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since the age of 20
The client can use their periods of insurance contributions in Ireland to meet the residence qualification for Veterans Pension.
## Partners
If the client has a partner each partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Ireland to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate either every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the Veterans Pension will stop.
## Intending to reside in Ireland
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of living in Ireland for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Ireland.
Example
A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Ireland. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Ireland for benefit purposes.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged before departure
- Application lodged in Ireland
- Commencement of payment in Ireland

chunks.title: Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension
When a client from the Republic of Ireland meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Veterans Pension except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Ireland.
The agreement with Ireland allows periods of contributions to the Irish insurance scheme since the age of 20 to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Veterans Pension.
The client must meet the New Zealand service and disability qualifications.
The client may also be entitled to an Irish benefit or pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Veterans Pension.
## SWIFTT
When Veterans Pension is granted using the agreement with Ireland you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 07 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or the Veterans Pension Centre or see:
- Irish benefits and pensions in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Ireland
- Veterans going to or residing in Ireland

chunks.title: Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Ireland — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal ireland
chunks.text:
## Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Ireland
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Ireland.
## New Benefit categories
Jobseeker Support will replace:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent and widowers with dependent children aged 14 years or older
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women alone
- Sickness Benefit (including Sickness Benefit Hardship)
- Unemployment Benefit (including Unemployment Benefit Student Hardship and Unemployment Benefit Training)
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged 14 years or older, or have no children
Sole Parent Support will replace:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent and widowers with dependent children aged under 14 years
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged under 14 years
Supported Living Payment will replace:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Care of sick or infirm
- Invalids Benefit
The following benefits will remain:
- Emergency Benefit for clients in hardship (including Emergency Maintenance Allowance)
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
- Unsupported Child's Benefit and Orphan's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For entitlements arising from an Agreement occurring on or after 15 July 2013 references in the Agreement with Ireland to the former benefits names must be considered as references to the new names. The name changes do not affect New Zealand Superannuation, Veteran's Pension or Orphans Benefit.
For more information see:
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Ireland
- Applications for payment in Ireland with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Ireland after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Admission to hospital — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital
When a client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced.
The Jersey/Guernsey pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receive reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the Jersey/Guernsey pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner and the rate of a Jersey/Guernsey pension for one partner is more than the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension the excess amount of the Jersey/Guernsey pension is deducted from the other partner's New Zealand benefit or pension payment.

chunks.title: Admission to hospital or prison — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital or prison
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey the rate of payment does not change when the client is admitted to hospital or prison.
This is because overseas institutions are not covered by the definitions of institutions in New Zealand legislation.

chunks.title: Application lodged prior to departure — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Application lodged prior to departure
When a client advises that they intend to live in Jersey/Guernsey they will need to:
- complete an Application for Payment Overseas form (WIS7W)
- provide details of the total period of their residence in New Zealand
- provide their passport and one other form of identification and
- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to Jersey/Guernsey
The application and supporting documents should be sent to International Services for processing.
An interview form must be completed and sent to International Services.
Exception Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability) is not payable outside New Zealand.
If the client is not yet receiving a New Zealand benefit an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the qualifications for the particular benefit (except for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind), the client does not need to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand).
The client can use their periods of insurance in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the qualifications for the New Zealand benefit or pension.
The client can use their partners or former partner's periods of insurance in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the qualifications for the New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services should be contacted before any current New Zealand benefit is cancelled or suspended.
## For more information contact International Services or see:
- Applications lodged in Jersey/Guernsey
- Commencement of payment in Jersey/Guernsey
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey
- Benefit entitlements in Jersey/Guernsey after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Applications for payment in Jersey/Guernsey with entitlements before 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Applications for payment in Jersey/Guernsey with entitlements before 15 July 2013
To decide if an application for portable Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Jersey/Guernsey is decided and grandparented under the old rules the following will apply:
- the applicant must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or Jersey/Guernsey on 14 July 2013 and
- an application for payment in Jersey/Guernsey may be received before or after 15 July 2013 but there must be entitlement to Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers from a date before 15 July 2013
Provided these conditions are met an application may be granted under the old rules and the grandparenting provisions will apply. If any one of the conditions is not met the application must be decided under the new rules.

chunks.title: Applications lodged in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Applications lodged in Jersey/Guernsey
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Jersey/Guernsey they are entitled to receive a New Zealand benefit or pension covered by the agreement if:
- they are intending to live in Jersey/Guernsey for more than 26 weeks and
- they have lived in New Zealand for at least one continuous year since the age of 20
Only New Zealand Superannuation, Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers and Veterans Pension can be granted if a client applies in Jersey/ Guernsey. The Agreement does not enable a client to apply for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) from Jersey/Guernsey.
The client must meet all the qualifications for the New Zealand benefit except the requirement to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
The client can use their own and/or their partners (or former partners) periods of insurance in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the qualifications for a New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
The client will need to complete an Application for Payment Overseas form (WIS7W) and this can be sent to International Services or lodged at the Jersey or Guernsey Social Security authority.
There are special conditions relating to specific benefits and pensions.
The first payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension will be made to the Jersey/Guernsey authority.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Commencement of payment in Jersey/Guernsey
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: Benefit entitlements in Jersey/Guernsey after 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Benefit entitlements in Jersey/Guernsey after 15 July 2013
New applications for Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Sole Parent Support.
In order to qualify the applicant must:
- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or in Jersey/Guernsey on 15 July 2013
- have a spouse who has died and
- have a dependent child under the age of 14 years
Entitlement to Sole Parent Support will cease when the dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.
New applications for Invalids Benefits under the Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Supported Living Payment. The only change to this benefit is the name change from Invalids Benefit to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Last child turning 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)

chunks.title: Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Calculation for NZ Superannuation or Veterans Pension
When New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension is paid to a client in Jersey/Guernsey the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole years of New Zealand residence since the age of 20 and
- divide by 40 and
- multiply by the maximum benefit rate
The minimum payment that can be paid is:
- 1 divided by 40 multiplied by the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation or
- 50% of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension if the client was already receiving this amount before 1 April 1995
The maximum rate that can be paid is:
- 100% of the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation
The maximum rate of payment is the full gross rate of either the half married, civil union or de facto rate or the single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension, depending on the client's circumstances.
There is no provision to pay the married, civil union or de facto rate of payment to same sex couples living in Jersey/Guernsey unless they are legally married to each other. If they are not legally married to each other, each partner must be assessed on an individual basis and paid at the single sharing accommodation rate.
Note the Reciprocal Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in Jersey/Guernsey, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension are paid in Jersey/Guernsey without regard to any Jersey/Guernsey pension being paid.
A period of up to 26 weeks absence from New Zealand can be included as New Zealand residence, so long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
The living alone payment cannot be paid to clients in Jersey/Guernsey.
Clients who were already receiving payment in Jersey/Guernsey before 1 April 1995 may be entitled to a higher rate under the agreement but they cannot receive less than 50% of the New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Jersey/Guernsey.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in Jersey/Guernsey
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Calculation for other benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Calculation for other benefits
When a benefit other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension is paid to a client in Jersey/Guernsey use the following formula to calculate the rate of payment:
- count the number of whole years of New Zealand residence since the age of 20 and
- divide by 25 and
- multiply by maximum benefit rate
The minimum rate that can be paid is:
- 1 divided by 25 multiplied by maximum benefit rate
The maximum rate of payment is 100% of the benefit the client is entitled to.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Jersey/Guernsey or other overseas pension being paid.
A period of up to 26 weeks absence from New Zealand can be included as New Zealand residence, so long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Jersey/Guernsey.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Change in income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When a client is getting one of the following New Zealand benefits or pensions that are being paid in Jersey/Guernsey it will still be income tested, and the clients will need to advise when there is any change in their income:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
The client must provide details of income they earn in Jersey/Guernsey or New Zealand.
This includes any Child Support payments they get from Inland Revenue
Jersey/Guernsey benefits or pensions are not taken into account.

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International Services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension paid in Jersey/Guernsey when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a relationship in the nature of a marriage or
- a client becomes single through separation; the marriage or civil union is dissolved; or the death of their partner

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Jersey/Guernsey
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey or the rate payable.
MSD may also review a New Zealand benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions paid in Jersey/Guernsey.
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Jersey/Guernsey will need to complete a Life Certificate which will be sent to them every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances.
Clients getting other New Zealand benefits or pensions in Jersey/Guernsey will need to complete a Confirming your Circumstances form which will be sent to them every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise Work and Income of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also required to provide any information required by the Jersey/Guernsey authorities to ensure that they are still entitled to their Jersey/Guernsey pension paid in New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Admission to hospital
- Clients going overseas
- Death of a client in New Zealand
- Jersey/Guernsey Life Certificates
- Reviews and Appeals
- Taxation
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment paid in Jersey/Guernsey.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier.

chunks.title: Clients eligible for Jersey or Guernsey pensions or benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Clients eligible for Jersey or Guernsey pensions or benefits
Under the agreement regarding social security in Jersey and Guernsey a client must apply for any pension or benefit that they may be entitled to from Jersey or Guernsey if they are applying for a New Zealand pension or benefit.
If a client has residence, or previously had residence, in Jersey or Guernsey they will need to complete an application for a Jersey or Guernsey pension. International Services will contact the client and ask them to apply for one of these pensions.
When the client completes an application it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies)
- the application form and the Information Release form are signed and dated
If the client refuses to apply for any Jersey or Guernsey pension or benefit they may be eligible for, you should contact International Services.

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Clients going overseas
When a client receiving a Jersey/Guernsey pension leaves New Zealand for a temporary absence the Jersey/Guernsey pension can continue to be paid.
The normal absence provisions apply to any New Zealand benefit or pension they are receiving.
If a client is going to reside in a country other than Jersey/Guernsey they may qualify for payment overseas depending on the country they are going to and the benefit type they are receiving.
If a client is going to Jersey/Guernsey and intends to stay there for more than 26 weeks they may be able to receive payment of their New Zealand benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey.
If a client is considering moving to Jersey/Guernsey you should advise them to write to the Jersey/Guernsey authorities to check their entitlement to a Jersey/Guernsey benefit or pension. The client will need to send full details of their circumstances to:
Jersey Employment & Social Security Philip Le Feuvre House La Motte Street St Helier Jersey Channel Islands, JE2 8PE
Telephone 0044 1534 280 000
or
The Administrator Guernsey Social Security Authority Edward T Wheadon House Le Truchot, St Peter Port Guernsey Channel Islands, GY1 3WH
Telephone 0044 1481 732 500
For more information see:
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: Clients receiving Jersey or Guernsey pensions or benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving Jersey or Guernsey pensions or benefits
A client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Jersey or Guernsey pension or benefit that they are receiving. If they do not comply their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or payment can be suspended.
When a client is receiving payments from Jersey or Guernsey you will need to find out the type of payment in order to determine the effect it will have on the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
It is important that the information is obtained as quickly as possible to enable the client's New Zealand benefit or pension entitlement to be assessed correctly.
If the client is unable to provide full documentation of the payments they will need to complete an Information Release Authority form.
The form must be sent to International Services to enable International Services to obtain and verify the following information:
- rate of payment in Jersey or Guernsey currency and whether it includes any amount in respect of the client's partner and any dependent children
- reason for the grant, such as age, widowhood, disablement, sickness, invalidity, death or war service
- the name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Payment options
- Other payments

chunks.title: Commencement of payment in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Commencement of payment in Jersey/Guernsey
When a client applies for their New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid in Jersey/Guernsey before their departure from New Zealand, payments will start on the first payday after their departure.
When a client applies from Jersey/Guernsey, the New Zealand benefit or pension will start on:
- the date they become entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension
- the date the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey came into force (1 April 1995)
- the earlier of the date they applied for a New Zealand benefit or a Jersey/Guernsey pension
whichever is the latest date.
Note that the initial stand-down applies to clients who are applying for New Zealand benefits other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
The Jersey/Guernsey authorities forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Rate payable in Jersey/Guernsey
- Methods of payment
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Death in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Death in Jersey/Guernsey
The normal procedures for cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions apply on the death of a client receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey.
Generally, the Jersey/Guernsey authorities will advise International Services of the death of a client in Jersey/Guernsey and International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
Note that Funeral Grants are not payable for clients who were living in Jersey/Guernsey at the time of their death.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on the death of a client follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients who were also getting a Jersey/Guernsey pension.
The executor of the client's estate will need to contact the Jersey/Guernsey authorities directly at the following address if they require any details of the Jersey/Guernsey pension, such as last payments due:
Jersey Employment & Social Security Philip Le Feuvre House La Motte Street St Helier Jersey Channel Islands, JE2 8PE
Telephone 0044 1534 280 000
or
The Administrator Guernsey Social Security Authority Edward T Wheadon House Le Truchot, St Peter Port Guernsey Channel Islands, GY1 3WH
Telephone 0044 1481 732 500
International Services will send the following information to the Jersey/Guernsey authorities:
- the clients name
- date of death and
- the name and address of the administrator of the estate
## SWIFTT
The executor of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen so that International Services can advise the Jersey/Guernsey authorities.
For more information see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
When a client is living in New Zealand and getting a Jersey/Guernsey pension it will be directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit.
The gross amount of the Jersey/Guernsey pension is deducted from:
- the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension and
- the net rate of any other New Zealand benefit including Accommodation Supplement
When a client is already getting a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Jersey/Guernsey pension is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services
A fax should be sent to International Services with verification of the rate, type of Jersey/Guernsey pension, the grant date and the name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already getting a Jersey/Guernsey pension at the time a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process.
For advice if you are unsure whether the pension is deductible contact International Services.
International Services must be advised of all clients who are getting a Jersey/Guernsey pension because it is International Services responsibility to carry out New Zealand benefit or pension reviews required where the Jersey/Guernsey pension deduction is being up-dated or reviewed.
## Change in circumstances
Any other reviews of the clients New Zealand benefit, such as a change of relationship status or a change of chargeable income, should be completed by the case manager.

chunks.title: Direct payment option — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Direct payment option
When a client is receiving a Jersey or Guernsey pension or benefit they can choose to have the Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit paid directly to their own bank account.
Under this method of payment:
- clients can choose to have their Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit paid once every 4 or 13 weeks
- payment will be converted at the rate of exchange applicable on the day the bank credits their account
- the client receives the gross rate of the Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit and is responsible for any tax liability on it
- the amount deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension will be based on an average exchange rate for the Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit
- if the client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension the rate will be automatically recalculated in SWIFTT each month using an average of the Jersey/Guernsey exchange rates for the previous month
- if the client is receiving any other New Zealand benefit or pension International Services will manually review the rate periodically or when the client requests it
- there is no due/paid assessment at the end of each year to take into account the exact exchange rate that the Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit was paid to the client
- when the Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit is payable at two pounds or less per week the client will be paid once a year in December unless they choose to have it paid at 4 or 13 weekly intervals
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Jersey/Guernsey
From 15 July 2013 onwards, people receiving existing portable payments of Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in Jersey/Guernsey will be grandparented on their existing rate and conditions.
References to the benefit names Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for Widowers are grandparented for existing clients and must still be used when administering these benefits payable under the Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey and when corresponding with the client.
Grandparenting arrangements do not apply to the former Invalids Benefit because the only change is the name change to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Grandparenting
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the government of New Zealand and the government of the United Kingdom on behalf of the states of Jersey and the states of Guernsey, allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey can be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the contribution qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- residence in New Zealand can be regarded as periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the residence qualifications for some Jersey/Guernsey benefits and pensions
- some Jersey/Guernsey pensions can be paid in New Zealand
- some New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid in Jersey/Guernsey
- war pensions from either country are not included in the agreement
Note
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.
For more information see:
- New Zealand benefits and pensions
- Welfare Reform impact on the Social Security Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey
- Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand
- Changes and reviews
- NZ benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: Jersey/Guernsey Life Certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Jersey/Guernsey Life Certificates
When a client is receiving a Jersey/Guernsey pension in New Zealand they are required to complete life certificates by the Jersey/Guernsey authorities.
The Jersey/Guernsey authorities will send the life certificate form directly to the client when it is due.
The client should complete the life certificate and return it directly to Jersey/Guernsey.
If a client needs the life certificate witnessed it is important to check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
The life certificate is returned to the client to send directly to the Jersey/Guernsey authorities.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand
When a former resident of Jersey or Guernsey applies for a New Zealand pension or benefit it is important to know whether they are receiving a Jersey or Guernsey pension or benefit, or if they may be entitled to one.
A client who has previously resided in Jersey or Guernsey must show their Overseas Residence details when they apply for any New Zealand benefit or pension.
The overseas residence details must be entered on CMS. These details are used by International Services to determine whether the client may be entitled to an overseas pension.
If the client is already receiving an overseas pension or benefit you should find out the details to establish whether this pension or benefit should be a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension.
Clients who have resided in Jersey or Guernsey may be able to receive a range of benefits or pensions from Jersey or Guernsey when they are living in New Zealand including:
For Guernsey:
- Sickness Benefit
- Industrial Injury Benefit
- Industrial Disablement Benefit
- Death Grants
- Old Age Pension
- Widows Benefit
- Invalidity Benefit
For Jersey:
- Old Age Pension
- Widows benefits
- Invalidity benefit
- Sickness benefit
- Disablement benefit
- Death Grant
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Clients eligible for Jersey or Guernsey pensions or benefits
- Clients receiving Jersey or Guernsey pensions or benefits
- Other payments
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Jobseeker Support — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Jobseeker Support
When a client from Jersey/Guernsey meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability) except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.
The agreement with Jersey/Guernsey allows periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability).
Under the agreement the client must:
- have contributed to the Jersey/Guernsey insurance scheme for a minimum of 12 months and
- have undertaken paid employment in New Zealand for at least 30 hours per week for 8 weeks or more since their most recent arrival in New Zealand
The client can use their own or their partner's (or former partner's) periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the New Zealand residence qualification.
The client's period of residence in New Zealand plus the period of contributions to the Jersey/Guernsey insurance scheme can be totalled to meet the two years residence qualification for Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability).
The client may be entitled to a Jersey/Guernsey pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability).
Note although the Agreement enables periods of contributions to Jersey/Guernsey insurance schemes to meet the residential qualification for Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability) in New Zealand, the Agreement does not provide for Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability) to be paid to residents in Jersey/Guernsey.
## SWIFTT
When Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability) is granted using the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen and entering 05 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Jobseeker Support Residence
- Main benefits Jobseeker Support
- Applications for payment in Jersey/Guernsey with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand

chunks.title: Last child turning 14 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Last child turning 14
Client's receiving Sole Parent Support payments as a widow or widower will cease to be eligible for payments once their last dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.
If the client returns to New Zealand after their last dependent child turns 14 they may be eligible for Jobseeker Support but will not be eligible for a New Zealand benefit if they remain ordinarily resident in Jersey/Guernsey.
Supported Living Payment clients with dependent children and grandparented Widow's Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers with dependent children do not lose their entitlement when their last child turns 14.
For more information see:
- Main benefits Sole Parent Support
Legislation
- Expiry of sole parent support, and replacement with jobseeker support, when youngest dependent child turns 14 years old section 33 Social Security Act 2018
- Ending of benefits section 325-330 Social Security Act 2018

chunks.title: Methods of payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment
When a client receives a New Zealand benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey they can choose to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account or to a bank account in Jersey/Guernsey.
Note that if the client applies from Jersey/Guernsey the first payment will be made to the Jersey/Guernsey authorities.
## Jersey/Guernsey bank account
Payments made to a Jersey/Guernsey bank account are credited four weekly.
If a client chooses to have money paid directly to a Jersey/Guernsey bank account, Work and Income meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
There are three options for the first payment being made into a Jersey/Guernsey bank account:
- payment can be made to an overseas bank account if the client has provided proof
- the first payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the Jersey/Guernsey bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the Jersey/Guernsey bank account are given to International Services. Once account details are advised, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the Jersey/Guernsey account with the first payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Rate payable in Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client intends to live in a country other than New Zealand or Jersey/Guernsey for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
The client may still be entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension if:
- they are moving to a country which has an agreement with New Zealand
Payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension should stop from the payday after the client's departure from Jersey/Guernsey until the client can test their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension in the country that they have moved to.
New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension cannot be paid to a client who leaves Jersey/Guernsey to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand as the client needs to be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand at the date they apply for payment overseas.
A client living in New Zealand who has totalised under the Jersey/Guernsey Agreement to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension may be able to receive a portable rate if they move to a non-Agreement country.
A proportional portable rate may be paid if they have at any time after the age of 20 been ordinarily resident in New Zealand for more 12 months. The proportional rate will be based on the length of time they have been ordinarily resident in and resided in New Zealand after age 20
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reciprocal agreements
- General Portability
- Special Portability
- Return to New Zealand

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey
Under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey, the following New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid to former New Zealand residents who are residing in or intend to reside in Jersey/Guernsey:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers with dependent child/ren under 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Veterans Pension
The rules are different depending on whether the client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension and whether they are already residing in Jersey or Guernsey when they apply.
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefits
- Funeral Grant
- Jobseeker Support
- Orphans Benefit
