- Sole Parent Support (sole parent)
- Supported Living Payment (for care of sick or infirm)
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey
- Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey
- New Zealand Superannuitants going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey
- Veterans going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey
- Applications for payment in Jersey/Guernsey with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Jersey/Guernsey after 15 July 2013
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Jersey/Guernsey
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Jersey/Guernsey
- Clients going overseas

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
Under the agreement with Jersey and Guernsey, periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey can be regarded as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualification for the following New Zealand benefits:
- Jobseeker Support (on grounds of health condition, injury, or disability)
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with dependent child/ren under 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Veterans Pension
Note that the agreement does not cover the following:
- Jobseeker Support (payable to full-time jobseekers)
- Orphans Benefit
- Sole Parent Support (sole parent)
- Supported Living Payment (care of sick or infirm)
- Unsupported Childs Benefit
- War Pensions
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For more information see:
- Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey
- Changes and reviews
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation
When a client from Jersey/Guernsey meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.
The agreement with Jersey/Guernsey allows periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
Under the agreement the client must have contributed to the Jersey/Guernsey insurance scheme for a minimum of 12 months.
The client can use their own or their partner's (or former partner's) periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the New Zealand residence qualification.
The client may also be entitled to a Jersey/Guernsey pension, which may be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation.
## SWIFTT
When New Zealand Superannuation is granted using the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen and entering 05 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Residency
- Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey
- New Zealand Superannuitants going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuitants going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuitants going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey
Under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation when they are residing in Jersey/Guernsey.
The client can apply for the New Zealand Superannuation to be paid in Jersey/Guernsey before their departure from New Zealand or from Jersey/Guernsey.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving New Zealand Superannuation
- intend to live in Jersey/Guernsey for more than 26 weeks and
- have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20
Note the client can use their own and/or their partners (or former partners) periods of insurance in Jersey/Guernsey since the age of 20 to meet the residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
## Partner
If the client has a partner the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in their circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Jersey/Guernsey to live in another country
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the New Zealand Superannuation will stop.
## Intending to live in Jersey /Guernsey
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Jersey/Guernsey for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Jersey/Guernsey.
Example
A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Jersey/Guernsey. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Jersey/Guernsey for benefit purposes.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Jersey/Guernsey
- Commencement of payment in Jersey/Guernsey
- New Zealand Superannuation

chunks.title: Other payments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Other payments
When a client is receiving other payments, such as interest or rent from investments or properties they own in Jersey/Guernsey, the payments will be treated in the same way as income earned in New Zealand.
You need to convert the income to New Zealand dollars using the current exchange rate. This can be found by using the SELXT screen in SWIFTT and entering the country code of 202 for Jersey or 199 for Guernsey.
If you are unsure how the calculation works you should contact International Services
For more information see:
- Charging income in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand benefit or pension being paid in Jersey/Guernsey is overpaid you will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment
- their review and appeal rights and
- the relevant section of the legislation or article of the agreement
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deductions from any New Zealand benefit or pension that the client is receiving.
If the client is no longer receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension the Jersey/Guernsey authorities may be able to assist to recover the overpayment from any current Jersey/Guernsey pension payments.
If the client is no longer receiving any benefit or pension they will need to make arrangements to repay the debt themselves.
## Applies for a review or appeal
If a client applies for a review or appeals a decision on the establishment of a debt or the rate of recovery, recovery action will be suspended until the outcome of that review or appeal is known.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reviews and appeals
- Debt management [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Payment options — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Payment options
When a client is receiving a Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit, they can choose to have their Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit paid by the:
- Direct Payment Option or
- Special Banking Option
Clients will be asked to select a payment option when they are sent a Jersey/Guernsey pension application pack by International Services
Clients can change from one payment option to the other at any time but can usually only join the Special Banking Option once.
All payment option changes are completed by International Services.
A client can authorise the Jersey/Guernsey authorities to pay arrears of their Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit direct to International Services regardless of the payment option they choose for regular payments.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Rate payable in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Rate payable in Jersey/Guernsey
When a New Zealand benefit or pension is paid to a client in Jersey/Guernsey the rate of payment is determined by the number of whole years that the client has resided in New Zealand since the age of 20.
The calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans pensions is different to the calculation for other New Zealand benefits. Note that the maximum rate payable is the single sharing accommodation rate or the married, civil union or de facto relationship rate, depending on the client's circumstances.
No payment is made to a client who has lived in New Zealand for less than 12 continuous months.
Only periods of actual New Zealand residence are counted. Periods of residence in a country other than New Zealand are disregarded even if the country has a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Jersey/Guernsey or other overseas pension being paid.
## Grandparented non-qualified partner
There is no provision to include payment for a grandparented non-qualified partner. The partner can only be paid a benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey if they meet the qualifications for a New Zealand benefit or pension in their own right.
## Absence from New Zealand
Any period of absence from New Zealand for up to 26 weeks is regarded as New Zealand residence, as long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Jersey/Guernsey.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Calculation for NZ Superannuation/Veterans Pension
- Calculation for other benefits

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for a Jersey/Guernsey pension. International Services will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not respond to requests to apply for a Jersey/Guernsey pension.
These reasons are:
- it is their right as they have made contributions
- clients must claim any benefit they may be entitled to in Jersey/Guernsey if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from Jersey/Guernsey
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension may stop, but payment of a Jersey/Guernsey pension continues
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 4 weeks their Sole Parent Support may stop but payment of a Jersey/Guernsey pension continues
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 6 weeks their Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) may stop but payment of a Jersey/Guernsey pension continues
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate, and the rate of the Jersey/Guernsey pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended but the Jersey/Guernsey pension will still be paid

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, payment of the New Zealand benefit will continue to be paid at the same rate as when they were living in Jersey/Guernsey.
This is because the client will not be considered as ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
When a client receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in Jersey/Guernsey, returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their benefit can be reviewed from the date of return to New Zealand.
International Services must be advised as they are responsible for stopping payment made under the social security agreement.
For more information contact International Services or refer to the instructions for the appropriate benefit.

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Review date
A New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date a client is granted a Jersey/Guernsey pension, or when the rate of a Jersey/Guernsey pension changes.
If you have difficulty obtaining details of the overseas pension granted contact International Services for advice.
If you have a case where you feel an overpayment should be established you should contact International Services.
When a Jersey/Guernsey pension is reduced, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the reduction.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Reviews and appeals — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Reviews and appeals
If a client is unhappy with any decision regarding their Jersey/Guernsey pension being in New Zealand they will need to write to the Jersey/Guernsey authorities.
For Guernsey or Jersey contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies Guernsey or Jersey
International Services are responsible for any reviews and appeals in regard to:
- the interpretation of the agreement with Guernsey or Jersey
- the effect of Jersey/Guernsey pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions and
- New Zealand benefits and pensions being paid in Guernsey or Jersey
The New Zealand review and appeal process applies to any other decisions regarding New Zealand benefits or pensions paid in New Zealand, such as charging income or change in relationship status.
For more information contact International Services see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
Under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey a client may qualify for the New Zealand Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower if they meet all the qualifications.
Under the agreement:
- dependent children born in Jersey/Guernsey (or while parent temporarily absent from Jersey/Guernsey) can be accepted as being born in New Zealand
- the client must have contributed to the Jersey/Guernsey insurance scheme for a minimum of 12 months
- periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower
the client can use their own or their spouse or civil union partner's periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey as periods of New Zealand residence to meet the residence criteria
Note the client may also be entitled to a Jersey/Guernsey pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower.
## SWIFTT
When Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers is granted using the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 05 in the entitlement code field.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Sole Parent Support Residence
- Main benefits Sole Parent Support
- Applications for payment in Jersey/Guernsey with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey
- Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey
- Care and protection concerns for a child or young person

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: Under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey a widow or widower can be paid the New Zealand Sole Parent Support when they are residing in Jersey/Guernsey. The client must apply for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower to be paid in Jersey/Guernsey before their departure from New Zealand. New Zealanders already residing in Jersey/Guernsey will not qualify. In all cases the client must: - meet the qualifications for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower - be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they apply for payment overseas - intend to live in Jersey/Guernsey for more than 26 weeks and - have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20 Note the client can use their own and or their former partner's periods of insurance in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the residence qualification for Sole Parent Support. Sole Parent Support will cease once the last child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.

chunks.title: Income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: Sole Parent Support paid to a widow or widower in Jersey/Guernsey is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Jersey/Guernsey or New Zealand when they apply for the benefit or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Jersey/Guernsey to live in another country.

chunks.title: Qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: When the client reaches the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension they will no longer be eligible for Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers and must test their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension. Note Sole Parent Support payments will cease to be payable in the event of the last dependent child turning 14 before the client reaches the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Intending to live in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Jersey/Guernsey for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Jersey/Guernsey. Example A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Jersey/Guernsey. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Jersey/Guernsey for benefit purposes. For more information contact International Services or see: - Application lodged prior to departure - Application lodged in Jersey/Guernsey - Commencement of payment in Jersey/Guernsey - Last child turning 14 - Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey - Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Jersey/Guernsey - Benefit entitlements in Jersey/Guernsey after 15 July 2013 - Sole Parent Support

chunks.title: Special Banking Option — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option
When a client is receiving a Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit they can choose to have it paid into a Special Banking Option account by the Jersey or Guernsey authorities. The client will then receive the full rate of their New Zealand benefit or pension.
The advantages of this option are:
- the client receives regular payments
- tax is already deducted
- the client is not affected by fluctuations in the exchange rate
Clients may elect to join the Special Banking Option at any time but cannot re-join once they have chosen to cancel the option (there are exceptions, contact International Services).
The Special Banking Option is not suitable for clients whose Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit is higher than (or likely to be higher than) the rate of New Zealand pension or benefit.
## Partner
When a client has a partner, who is also receiving a New Zealand pension or benefit and a Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit, they must both choose the same payment option.
For more information contact International Services, or see:
- Special Banking Option applications

chunks.title: Special Banking Option applications — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option applications
When a client chooses the special banking option for their Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit they will be sent an application pack from International Services containing:
- an Application for the Special Banking Option
- an Application for a Special Bank Account and
- an Authority to Release Information form (this form allows us to share information regarding pension and benefit entitlements with the Social Welfare Services Authorities in Jersey/Guernsey)
All three forms must be fully completed and forwarded to International Services for processing.
## Note
- when a client has a partner they must both choose the same payment option
- the client can change from the direct payment method to the Special Banking Option at any time
- if the client has changed from the Special Banking Option to the direct payment option they cannot re-join the special banking option (however there are exceptions, for these please contact International Services)
- the client does not have access to the special banking option account that the Jersey/Guernsey pension or benefit is paid into as it is simply a holding account for funds that are to be paid to MSD

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment
When a client from Jersey/Guernsey meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.
The agreement with Jersey/Guernsey allows periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
Under the agreement the client must have contributed to the Jersey and Guernsey insurance scheme for a minimum of 12 months.
The client can use their own or their partner's (or former partner's) periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the New Zealand residence qualification.
The client may also be entitled to a Jersey/Guernsey pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
Note Supported Living Payment for the care of the sick or infirm is not payable under the Jersey/Guernsey Agreement.
## SWIFTT
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is granted using the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 05 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Supported Living Payment Residence
- Main benefits Supported Living Payment
- Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey
- Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey
- Benefit entitlement in Jersey/Guernsey after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: Under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey a client can be paid the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when they are residing in Jersey/Guernsey. The client must apply for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) to be paid in Jersey/Guernsey before their departure from New Zealand. New Zealanders already residing in Jersey/Guernsey will not qualify. In all cases the client must: - meet the qualifications for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) - be ordinarily resident in New Zealand when they apply for payment overseas - intend to live in Jersey/Guernsey for more than 26 weeks and - have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20 Note the client can use their own and/or their partners (or former partners) periods of insurance in Jersey/Guernsey to meet the residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).

chunks.title: Partner — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: If the client has a partner each partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.

chunks.title: Medical — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: The Jersey/Guernsey authorities will arrange and pay for any medical examination that is required for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) when a client is living in Jersey/Guernsey.

chunks.title: Income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) paid in Jersey/Guernsey is still income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in Jersey/Guernsey or New Zealand when they apply for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Jersey/Guernsey to live in another country

chunks.title: Qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: When the client reaches the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension they will no longer be eligible for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) and must test their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension

chunks.title: Intending to live in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text: If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Jersey/Guernsey for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Jersey/Guernsey. Example A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Jersey/Guernsey. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Jersey/Guernsey for benefit purposes. For more information contact International Services or see: - Application lodged prior to departure - Commencement of payment in Jersey/Guernsey - Main benefits Supported Living Payment - Benefit entitlements in Jersey/Guernsey after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Clients in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Clients in New Zealand
Jersey/Guernsey pensions are not taxed in Jersey/Guernsey prior to being paid to the client in New Zealand.
The client should contact Inland Revenue (IR) to discuss their New Zealand tax liability for the Jersey/Guernsey pension and any New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Clients in Jersey/Guernsey
New Zealand benefits paid in Jersey or Guernsey are not taxed in New Zealand but may be taxed in Jersey or Guernsey.
The client must make their own tax arrangements with the Jersey/Guernsey tax authority.

chunks.title: Veterans going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Veterans going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey
Under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey a client can be paid the New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are residing in Jersey/Guernsey.
The client can apply for the Veterans Pension to be paid in Jersey/Guernsey before their departure from New Zealand or from Jersey/Guernsey.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Veterans Pension
- intend to live in Jersey/Guernsey for more than 26 weeks and
- have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20
Note the client can use their own and/or their partners (or former partners) periods of insurance in Jersey/Guernsey since the age of 20 to meet the residence qualification for Veterans Pension.
## Partner
If the client has a partner, each partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Jersey/Guernsey to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the Veterans pension will stop.
## Intending to live in Jersey /Guernsey
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Jersey/Guernsey for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Jersey/Guernsey.
Example
A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Jersey/Guernsey. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in Jersey/Guernsey for benefit purposes.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension
When a client from Jersey/Guernsey meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Veterans Pension except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.
The agreement with Jersey/Guernsey allows periods of contributions to the insurance scheme in Jersey/Guernsey to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Veterans Pension.
The client can use their own or their partners (or former partners) periods of contributions to the Jersey/Guernsey insurance scheme to meet the New Zealand residence qualification.
The client must meet the New Zealand service and disability qualifications.
The client may also be entitled to a Jersey/Guernsey pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Veterans Pension.
## SWIFTT
When Veterans Pension is granted using the agreement with Jersey/Guernsey you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen and entering 05 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or Veterans Pension Centre or see:
- Jersey/Guernsey pensions or benefits in New Zealand
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in Jersey/Guernsey
- Veterans going to or residing in Jersey/Guernsey

chunks.title: Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal jersey guernsey
chunks.text:
## Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey.
## New Benefit categories
Jobseeker Support will replace:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent and widowers with dependent children aged 14 years or older
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women Alone
- Sickness Benefit (including Sickness Benefit Hardship)
- Unemployment Benefit (including Unemployment Benefit Student Hardship and Unemployment Benefit Training)
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged 14 years or older, or have no children
Sole Parent Support will replace:
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged under 14 years
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent and widowers with dependent children aged under 14 years
Supported Living Payment will replace:
- Invalids Benefit
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Care of sick or infirm
The following benefits will remain:
- Emergency Benefit for clients in hardship (including Emergency Maintenance Allowance)
- Unsupported Child's Benefit and Orphan's Benefit
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
- Youth Payment
- Young Parent Payment
For entitlements arising from an Agreement occurring on or after 15 July 2013 references in the Agreement with Jersey/Guernsey to the former benefits names must be considered as references to the new names. The name changes do not affect New Zealand Superannuation, Veteran's Pension or Orphans Benefit.
For more information see:
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Jersey/Guernsey
- Applications for payment in Jersey/Guernsey with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Benefit entitlements in Jersey/Guernsey after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Admission to hospital in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital in New Zealand
When a client has been in a public hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate. A Veteran's Pension is an exception to this and is not reduced if they are admitted to a public hospital and are in for longer than 13 weeks.
The Maltese pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the Maltese pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner and the rate of a Maltese pension for one partner is more than the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension, the excess amount of the Maltese pension is deducted from the other partner's New Zealand benefit or pension payment.
Note clients admitted to private hospitals do not have their benefit or pension reduced to the hospital rate.

chunks.title: Admission to hospital or prison — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital or prison
When a client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Malta the rate of payment does not change when the client is admitted to hospital or imprisoned.
This is because overseas institutions are not covered by the definitions of institutions in New Zealand legislation.

chunks.title: Application lodged prior to departure — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Application lodged prior to departure
When a client advises that they intend to live in Malta they will need to:
- complete an Application for New Zealand Payment Overseas form (WIS7W)
- provide details of the total period of their residence in New Zealand
- provide two forms of identification one must be their passport and
- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to Malta
- provide verified bank account details if different than those on SWIFTT
They also need to attend an interview where the case manager will complete an Application for New Zealand Payment Overseas interview form (WIF9W).
The application form, interview form and supporting documents should be sent to International Services for processing.
Note International Services should be contacted before any current New Zealand benefit is cancelled or suspended.
## New Zealand benefit application
If the client is not yet receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the qualifications for the particular benefit.
## Residence
The residency and ordinary residence requirements are addressed under the specific benefit that is being applied for.
The client can use their periods of contributions in Malta to meet the residency qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Applications lodged in Malta
- Commencement of payment in Malta

chunks.title: Applications lodged in Malta — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Applications lodged in Malta
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Malta they may be entitled to receive New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension if they use the provisions of the agreement with Malta to meet the qualifying criteria.
The client will need to complete an Application for New Zealand Benefit form and this can be sent to Senior Services - international or lodged at a Maltese National Social Security Office who will send it to International Services
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- maintaining client records
- reviewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
## All payments
All payments of the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension will be made to the client. This is because the agreement with Malta does not include a provision to recover a debt from the initial arrears.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Commencement of payment in Malta

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International Services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid in Malta when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a relationship in the nature of a marriage or
- a client becomes single through separation; the marriage or civil union is dissolved; or the death of their partner

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for Maltese pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for Maltese pensions
A client is required to advise details of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also obliged to provide any information required by the Maltese authorities to ensure that they are still entitled to receive their Maltese pension in New Zealand. This will mainly be in the form of Life Certificates.
Note Malta may also request details about any service pension or superannuation paid by a former employer. This allows Malta to assess entitlement to a non-contributory (means tested) scheme.
For more information see:
- Admission to hospital in New Zealand
- Clients going overseas
- Maltese life certificates
- Death of a client in New Zealand
- Changes and reviews for New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension in Malta

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension in Malta — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension in Malta
When a client is receiving their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Malta they must advise International Services when there is any change in their circumstances that may affect payment of their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension such as:
- Admission to hospital or prison in Malta
- Change in relationship status
- Death in Malta
- Move to another country
- Overpayments
- Return to New Zealand
## Reviews
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions in Malta.
Clients receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in Malta will need to complete a Life Certificate which will be sent to them every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances.

chunks.title: Clients entitled to Maltese pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Clients entitled to Maltese pensions
Under the Social Security Act 2018 a client and their partner and dependent (if any) must apply for any pension that they may be entitled to from Malta if they are applying for or receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension. This applies even if the New Zealand benefit is not included in the agreement with Malta.
If the client has Maltese residence they will need to complete an application for a Maltese pension. International Services will contact clients with residence in Malta and ask them to apply for a Maltese benefit or pension.
When the client completes the application it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies)
- the application form is signed and dated
If the client refuses to apply for any Maltese pension you should contact International Services.

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Clients going overseas
If a client receiving a Maltese pension leaves New Zealand for a temporary or permanent absence, they will need to contact the Maltese authorities to find out what Malta may pay.

chunks.title: Clients receiving Maltese pensions in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving Maltese pensions in New Zealand
A client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Maltese pension that they are receiving. If they do not comply any New Zealand benefit or pension they may already receive may be refused or suspended.
When a client is receiving payments from Malta you will need to find out the details of the payment in order to determine the effect it will have on the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
It is important that the information is obtained as quickly as possible to enable the client's New Zealand benefit or pension entitlement to be assessed correctly. This will also minimise any potential debt that could occur.
The following information needs to be obtained and forwarded to International Services:
- rate of payment in Euro and whether it includes any amount in respect of the client's partner and any dependent children
- whether the rate of payment is subject to tax in Malta and if so whether tax has been deducted from the payment
- reason for the grant (eg retirement)
- confirm whether any part of the pension is made up from periods of voluntary Maltese contributions (this may not apply and can be difficult to identify)
- if the client has made voluntary contributions ask how long they made voluntary contributions for (years)
- the name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment - this is usually the Competent institution or Liaison Agency
- the date the payment was granted from
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Commencement of payment in Malta — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Commencement of payment in Malta
When a client applies for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension to be paid in Malta before their departure payments will start on the first payday after their departure.
When a client applies from Malta, the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's pension will start on:
- the date they become entitled to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
- the date the agreement with Malta came into force or
- the earlier of the date they either applied for a New Zealand benefit or a Maltese pension
whichever is the latest date.
The Maltese authorities will forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Rate payable in Malta
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: Death in Malta — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Death in Malta
The normal procedures for cancellation of New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension apply on the death of a client in Malta.
Generally the Maltese authorities will advise International Services of the death of a client in Malta and International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
Note that Funeral Grants are not payable for clients who were living in Malta at the time of their death.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Death of a client

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on the death of a client follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients who were also receiving a Maltese pension.
International Services will send the following information to the Maltese authorities:
- the clients name
- the date of death and
- the name and address of the administrator of the estate
The executor of the client's estate will need to contact the Maltese authorities directly if they require any details of the Maltese pension.
Note the executor of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen in SWIFTT so International Services can advise the Maltese authorities.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Death of a client

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
In general when a client is living in New Zealand and receiving a Maltese state pension it will be directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit. The amount to deduct is the rate of the pension after any deduction of tax in Malta but before the deduction of any New Zealand tax.
The Maltese pension is deducted from:
- the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension and
- the net rate of any other New Zealand benefit, including Accommodation Supplement
When a client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Maltese pension is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services
Details should be sent to International Services with verification of the rate, type of Maltese pension, the grant date and the name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already receiving a Maltese pension at the time a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process.
Not all pensions received from an overseas country are deductible. You should contact International Services for advice on the deductibility of overseas pensions before applying the direct deduction.
When it is determined that an overseas pension is not deductible the pension must be treated as income and taken into account for any income tested assistance the client receives.
Note the Special Banking Option is not available for Maltese pensions.
## Reviews
International Services must be advised of all clients who are receiving a Maltese pension.
International Services is responsible for ensuring that New Zealand benefit or pension is reviewed as required where a Maltese pension is granted or where changes to the rate of a Maltese pension occur.
Any other reviews of the client's New Zealand benefit, such as a change of relationship status or a change of chargeable income, can be completed by a local services case manager.

chunks.title: Exchange of information — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Exchange of information
For the effective administration of the agreement with Malta there will be an exchange of information between New Zealand and Malta on changes in circumstances affecting individual clients and general adjustments of pension rates.
The process for the exchange of information and updating of client records is detailed in the Administrative Arrangements and Supplementary Administrative Arrangements which are subject to privacy compliance under the Privacy Act 2020.
Under these Arrangements:
- liaison forms must be used for all exchanges of client information
- liaison forms must be sent by mail or equivalent air courier service
- email and facsimile exchanges of client information are not permitted under the Administrative Arrangements
- only information included on Liaison forms can be exchanged - no other types of information can be exchanged
- a 100% check of the client's name, date of birth, Social Welfare Number, Maltese Social Security number and Maltese Identity Card number provided on Liaison forms must be made and confirmed before a client record can be updated with the new information
- if all of the matching criteria does not match with information already held you must check back with Malta to clarify the discrepancy
- liaison forms received from Malta must be destroyed within 60 days unless adverse action is taken on the client records
For more information see:
- Mutual assistance provisions for the exchange of information article 14 Social Welfare (Reciprocity with Malta) Order 2013
- Matching of information section 1 Administrative Arrangement for the application of the Agreement between New Zealand and the Republic of Malta on Social Security
- Destruction of liaison forms paragraph 9 Supplementary Administrative Arrangement for the Implementation of the Agreement between New Zealand and the Republic of Malta on Social Security
- Information to be exchanged section 7 Administrative Arrangement for the application of the Agreement between New Zealand and the Republic of Malta on Social Security
- Liaison forms section 3 Administrative Arrangement for the application of the Agreement between New Zealand and the Republic of Malta on Social Security
- Sending liaison forms section 2 Administrative Arrangement for the application of the Agreement between New Zealand and the Republic of Malta on Social Security

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and Malta allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- periods of Maltese contributions in Malta after the age of 20 can be regarded as periods of residence and presence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
- Working Age Residence in New Zealand can be regarded as periods of Maltese contributions to meet the qualifications for some Maltese benefits and pensions
- Maltese pensions paid in respect of retirement can be paid in New Zealand
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension can be paid in Malta
- War disablement pensions from either country are not included in the agreement with Malta

chunks.title: Maltese life certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Maltese life certificates
When a client is receiving a Maltese pension in New Zealand they may be required to complete life certificates by the Maltese authorities.
The Maltese authorities will send the life certificate form directly to the client when it is due.
The client should complete the life certificate and return it directly to Malta.
If a client needs the life certificate witnessed it is important to check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
The life certificate is returned to the client to send directly to the Maltese authorities.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Maltese pensions in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Maltese pensions in New Zealand
When a former resident of Malta applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they are receiving a Maltese pension, or if they may be entitled to one.
A client who has previously resided in Malta must complete details of their residence in Malta and any other country of residence on the application form when they apply for any New Zealand benefit or pension.
The overseas residence details must be entered in CMS. These details are used by International Services to determine whether the client may be entitled to a Maltese benefit or pension or pension from any other country.
If the client is already receiving an overseas pension you should find out the details to establish whether this pension should be a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Maltese old age pensions
The following Maltese old age pensions are covered by the agreement with Malta and may be payable to or are being paid to former Maltese residents living in New Zealand:
- Retirement Pension
- Non-contributory Old Age Pension (means tested)
## Other benefits and pensions
Some Maltese benefits not covered by the agreement with Malta may still be payable in New Zealand. These payments may be deductible under the Social Security Act 2018.
Totalisation of periods of contributions in Malta cannot be used to meet residence qualifications for a New Zealand benefit such as Jobseeker Support.
Note the agreement with Malta only allows for the exchange on information in relation to retirement and old age pensions. Information on other Maltese benefits and pensions cannot be exchanged between New Zealand and Malta. Any information will need to be provided by the client.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Clients receiving Maltese pensions in New Zealand
- Clients entitled to Maltese pensions

chunks.title: Methods of payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment
When a client receives a New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Malta they can choose to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account or to an overseas bank account.
Note all payments will be made directly to the clients bank account and not to the Maltese authority. This is because the agreement with Malta does not include a provision to recover any debt from the initial arrears.
## New Zealand bank account
Payments made to a New Zealand bank account are credited fortnightly.
If a client chooses to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account before transferring the funds to an overseas bank account, the client must pay the cost of the transfer of the funds.
## Overseas bank account
Payments made to an overseas bank account are credited four weekly.
If a client chooses to have money paid directly to an overseas bank account, the Ministry of Social Development meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
There are three options for the first payment being made into an overseas bank account:
- payment can be made to an overseas bank account if the client has already provided verification of their bank account that meets core processing standards
- the first payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the overseas bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the overseas bank account are given to International Services. Once account details are advised, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the overseas account with the first payment.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Rate payable in Malta

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension decides to move to another country other than New Zealand or Malta for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
The client may still be entitled to their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension if:
- they are moving to a country which has an agreement with New Zealand and they qualify under that agreement
Payment of the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension should stop from the payday after the client's departure from Malta until the client can test their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in the country that they have moved to.
## Residence
New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension cannot be paid to a client who leaves Malta to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand. This is because the client would need to be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand at the date they apply for payment overseas under either the General or Special Portability provisions.
If the client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension by using their periods of contributions in Malta to meet the New Zealand residence qualification, they may not be entitled to have the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid in another agreement country. Their entitlement will depend on the terms of the agreement between New Zealand and the new country the client has moved to.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reciprocal agreements
- General Portability
- Special Portability

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions in Malta — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions in Malta
Under the agreement with Malta, the following New Zealand pensions can be paid for former New Zealand residents who live, or intend to live, in Malta:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veteran's Pension
## Other benefits and pensions
- The agreement with Malta does not allow for any other New Zealand benefits or pensions to be paid in Malta.
## Totalisation
- A widow or widower living in Malta may be able to use their deceased spouse or partners New Zealand Working Age Residence in order to meet contributory requirements for widows payments in Malta.
Note the agreement with Malta only allows for the exchange of information in relation to retirement and old age pensions. Information on the Maltese Widows and Widowers cannot be exchanged between New Zealand and Malta. Any information will need to be provided by the client.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation clients moving to Malta
- Veterans Pension clients moving to Malta
- Commencement of payment in Malta
- Rate payable in Malta
- Methods of payment

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
New Zealand benefits included in the agreement with Malta are:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veterans Pension
The agreement does not cover any other benefits, funeral grants, or extra help assistance.
This means totalisation of periods of contributions in Malta cannot be used to meet residence qualifications for a New Zealand benefit such as Jobseeker Support.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation
When a client from Malta meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except residence they may qualify under the agreement with Malta.
To help a client meet the residence qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation the agreement with Malta allows:
- periods of contributions in Malta after the age of 20 to be regarded as a period when a person is both resident and present in New Zealand
- only periods of Maltese contributions after the age of 50, can be used to meet the requirement of 5 years of residence in New Zealand and presence in New Zealand after age of 50
The client may also be entitled to a Maltese Pension, which may be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation.
Note when New Zealand Superannuation is granted using the agreement with Malta you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 16 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation clients moving to Malta — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation clients moving to Malta
Under the agreement with Malta a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation while they are residing in Malta.
The client can apply for New Zealand Superannuation to be paid in Malta before their departure from New Zealand, or from Malta. Payment cannot be backdated so clients should be encouraged to apply before they leave New Zealand.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or be receiving New Zealand Superannuation at the time they apply
- be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand or Malta at the time they apply for payment
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Malta for at least 26 weeks and
- have at least 12 months Working Age Residence in New Zealand
The client can use their periods of contributions in Malta to meet the residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation (10 years residence and presence in New Zealand since age 20 with five years residence and presence since age 50).
## Intending to reside in Malta
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Malta for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Malta. This means they may go to Malta via another country or countries provided they arrive in Malta within 26 weeks of their date of departure from New Zealand.
Example
A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Malta. In this instance the client would be considered ordinarily resident in Malta for purposes of deciding their application for payment of New Zealand Superannuation into Malta.
## Payment to partner
There is no provision to pay for a grandparented non-qualified partner overseas. If the client has a partner the partner must also complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement and especially if they intend to leave Malta to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the New Zealand Superannuation will stop.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Malta

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension being paid in Malta is overpaid you will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment and
- their review and appeal rights
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deductions from the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension the client is receiving.
If the client is no longer receiving a New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension there is no provision in the agreement with Malta for the Maltese authorities to recover the overpayment on New Zealand's behalf. There is also no provision in the agreement with Malta for New Zealand to recover Maltese debts.
## Review or appeal
If a client applies for a review or appeals a decision on the establishment of a debt or the rate of recovery, recovery action will be suspended until the outcome of that review or appeal is known.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reviews and appeals

chunks.title: Rate payable in Malta — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Rate payable in Malta
When New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension is paid to a client in Malta the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand Working age residence and
divide by
- 540 months and
multiply by
- the full maximum rate of payment
The minimum payment that can be paid is:
- 12/540 of the maximum rate of payment or
- 50% of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation if the client was already receiving this amount under the General Portability provisions (in Malta) prior to the implementation of the agreement with Malta on 1 December 2013.
The maximum rate that can be paid is:
- 100% of the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
Note if the client has a third country pension it is not directly deducted from the rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension payable.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in Malta and should be cancelled from the day after departure.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for a Maltese pension. International Services will then contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services may suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not agree to requests to apply for a Maltese pension.
International Services will talk to clients about the reasons why they must apply, which will include the following factors:
- clients are required by legislation to apply for any benefit they may be entitled to in Malta if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension
- it is their right if they have periods of contributions to the Maltese social security scheme
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from Malta
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension may stop, but payment of a Maltese pension will continue and is not affected by the 26 week rule
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate. If the rate of any Maltese pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended but the Maltese pension will continue to be paid
Note that Veteran's Pension is not reduced if the client is in hospital for more than 13 weeks.

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When a client is receiving payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Malta and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, payment of the New Zealand benefit will continue to be paid at the same rate as when they were living in Malta.
This is because the client will not be considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Client returns to New Zealand permanently
When a client receiving payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Malta, returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their pension can be reviewed from the date of return to New Zealand.
International Services must be advised as they are responsible for stopping payment made under the social security agreement.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand Superannuation, Absence from New Zealand Return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Review date
A New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date a client is granted a Maltese pension and every time when the rate of a Maltese pension changes.
If you have difficulty obtaining details of the overseas pension grant date, contact International Services for advice.
When a Maltese pension is reduced, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the reduction.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions
- SWIFTT process

chunks.title: Reviews and appeals — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Reviews and appeals
If a client disagrees with any decision regarding their Maltese pension being paid in New Zealand they will need to write to the Maltese authorities.
International Services is responsible for any reviews and appeals in regard to:
- the effect of Maltese pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions and
- decisions made on New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension being paid in Malta
- other decisions made in terms of the agreement with Malta affecting a client's New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: SWIFTT process — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## SWIFTT process
When a client is receiving a Maltese pension that is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit or pension it is important that this is processed correctly in SWIFTT.
The following information is required to add a Maltese pension to the SOPDA screen in SWIFTT:
Note some of these fields are only used by International Services
- letter indicator (defaults to x)
- the rate of the Maltese pension in Maltese currency
- the weekly amount of bank fees allowed (contact International Services)
- the frequency at which the Maltese pension payments are made
- the percentage of any voluntary component that is included in the overseas pension
- any Maltese Social Security Number (essential for matching purposes)
- country code 097
- whether the pension is a deductible pension Y/N
The New Zealand dollar amount of the Maltese pension will be displayed on the SOPHI screen once the above details have been entered.
The New Zealand dollar amount showing on the SOPHI screen will need to be added to the 'O/seas Pen direct ded' field using the INCMA screen in SWIFTT.
When the Maltese pension details are correctly recorded SWIFTT will automatically calculate the Maltese pension deduction from the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension payable.
Note if the overseas pension is not deductible it must be treated as income and taken into account in assessing any other income tested assistance being received.
If you need further information you should contact International Services.
Note International Services up-dates the exchange rate table in SWIFTT each month and the exchange rate table is linked to the country codes.
For benefits paid other than weekly SWIFTT will:
- recalculate the rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension each month and
- send a letter to advise the client if the letter indicator in the SOPDA screen is set to Y
- if a client does not wish to receive their advice letters, the indicator in the SWIFTT SOPHC screen should be set to N
- only International Services can change the letter indicator after the initial grant of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
International Services manually updates other New Zealand benefits and pensions periodically.

chunks.title: Maltese pensioners in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Maltese pensioners in New Zealand
Maltese benefits and pensions are taxed in Malta prior to being paid to the client in New Zealand.
The amount of the Maltese pension to be deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension is the amount of the Maltese benefit after it is reduced by the Maltese tax levied on it.
The client should contact Inland Revenue to discuss their New Zealand tax liability for the Maltese pension.
## New Zealand pensions in Malta
New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension paid in Malta are not taxed in New Zealand but may be subject to tax under the tax laws in Malta.
A client must make their own arrangements for payment of any tax with the Maltese tax authority.

chunks.title: Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension
When a client from Malta meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Veteran's Pension except residence, they may qualify under the agreement with Malta.
The agreement allows:
- periods of contributions in Malta after the age of 20 to be regarded as a period when a person is both resident and present in New Zealand
- only periods Maltese contributions after the age of 50, can be used to meet the requirement of 5 years of residence and presence in New Zealand after age 50
A Veterans Pension client must be the New Zealand Superannuation qualifying age.
Note when Veterans Pension is granted using the agreement with Malta you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 16 in the entitlement code field
For more information contact International Services or the Veteran's Pensions Centre or see:

chunks.title: Veterans Pension clients moving to Malta — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension clients moving to Malta
Under the agreement with Malta a client can be paid the New Zealand Veterans Pension when they are residing in Malta.
The client can apply for the Veteran's Pension to be paid in Malta before their departure from New Zealand, or from Malta. Payment cannot be backdated so clients should be encouraged to apply before they leave New Zealand.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or receiving Veteran's Pension at the time they apply
- be aged 65 or older
- be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand or in Malta at the time they apply for payment from overseas
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Malta for at least 26 weeks and
- have at least 12 months Working Age Residence in New Zealand
The client can use their periods of contributions in Malta to meet the residence qualification for Veteran's Pension.
## Intending to reside in Malta
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Malta for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Malta.
Example
A client may wish to take a three-month holiday in the United Kingdom before taking up residence in Malta. In this example the client would still be considered ordinarily resident in Malta for benefit purposes.
## Payment to partner
If the client has a partner each partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right. If one partner is ineligible there is no provision to pay for a grandparented non-qualified partner overseas.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Malta to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the Veteran's pension will stop.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Application lodged prior to departure
- Application lodged in Malta
- Commencement of payment in Malta

chunks.title: Working age residence — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal malta
chunks.text:
## Working age residence
Under the agreement with Malta, Working Age Residence means a period when the client was both resident and present in New Zealand and aged 20 or more but less than 65.
Working age residence also includes a period when a client:
- was employed outside of New Zealand and liable to pay New Zealand income tax on those earnings or
- was with a spouse or partner who was employed outside of new Zealand and liable to pay New Zealand income tax on those earnings
provided the client returned to New Zealand on or after 23 June 1987 and during that period was aged 20 or more but less than 65.

chunks.title: Admission to hospital — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital
When a client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced.
The Netherlands pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the Netherlands pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner and the rate of a Netherlands pension for one partner is more than the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension the excess amount of the Netherlands pension is deducted from the other partner's New Zealand benefit or pension payment.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Admission to hospital or prison — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital or prison
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Netherlands the rate of payment does not change when the client is admitted to hospital or prison.
This is because overseas institutions are not covered by the definitions that are covered by New Zealand domestic legislation.

chunks.title: Applications for payment in the Netherlands with entitlements before 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Applications for payment in the Netherlands with entitlements before 15 July 2013
To decide if an application for portable Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in the Netherlands is decided and grandparented under the old rules the following will apply:
- the applicant must be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or the Netherlands on 14 July 2013 and
- an application for payment in Netherlands may be received before or after 15 July 2013 but there must be entitlement to Widow's Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers from a date before 15 July 2013
Provided these conditions are met an application may be granted under the old rules and the grandparenting provisions will apply. If any one of the conditions is not met the application must be decided under the new rules.
For more information see:
- Grandparenting
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Netherlands

chunks.title: Benefit entitlements in the Netherlands after 15 July 2013 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Benefit entitlements in the Netherlands after 15 July 2013
New applications for Widows Benefit or Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers under the agreement with the Netherlands with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Sole Parent Support.
In order to qualify the applicant must:
