- be ordinarily resident in New Zealand or in the Netherlands on 15 July 2013
- have a spouse who has died and
- have a dependent child under the age of 14 years
Entitlement to Sole Parent Support will cease when the dependent child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with the Netherlands.
New applications for Invalids Benefits under the Agreement with the Netherlands with an entitlement date after 15 July 2013 are to be considered as applications for Supported Living Payment. The only change to this benefit is the name change from Invalids Benefit to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
- Last child turning 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)

chunks.title: Calculation for NZ Superannuation and Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Calculation for NZ Superannuation and Veterans Pension
When New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension is paid to a client in the Netherlands the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence after the age of 20 and
divide by
- the number for the date the client was born (see calculation table) and
multiply by
- the maximum benefit rate
The minimum payment that can be paid is 1/40 to 1/45 of the maximum rate of New Zealand Superannuation
The maximum benefit rate is the full gross rate of either the half married, civil union or de facto rate or the single sharing accommodation rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, depending on the client's circumstances.
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension while living in the Netherlands may also be entitled to a Netherlands pension 'top-up' or supplementary payment under the Netherlands National Assistance Act.
Note clients aged 65 before 1 November 2003 must have 10 years actual New Zealand residence at any time.
## Same sex couples
There is no provision to pay the married, civil union or de facto rate of payment to same sex couples living in the Netherlands unless they are legally married to each other. If they are not legally married to each other, each partner must be assessed on an individual basis and be paid at the single sharing accommodation rate.
Note the Reciprocal Agreement with the Netherlands and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in the Netherlands, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in the Netherlands.
For more information you can contact International Services.

chunks.title: Calculation for other benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Calculation for other benefits
When a benefit other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's pension is paid to a client in the Netherlands use the following formula to calculate the rate of payment:
- count the number of whole months of New Zealand residence since attaining the age of 20 and
- divide this by 300
- then multiply this by maximum benefit rate
The minimum rate that can be paid is:
12 divided by 300 multiplied by maximum benefit rate
The maximum rate of payment is the full net rate of the benefit the client is entitled to.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Netherlands pension or other overseas pension being paid, but other income should be taken into account for income tested benefits.
## Period of absence
A period of up to 26 weeks absence from New Zealand can be included as New Zealand residence for the rate calculation, so long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in the Netherlands.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Payments in the Netherlands

chunks.title: Change in income — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Change in income
When a client is getting one of the following New Zealand benefits that is being paid in the Netherlands it will still be income tested and the client will need to advise International Services when there is any change in their income:
- Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
Note the client must provide details of all income they receive in the Netherlands or New Zealand.
This includes any Child Support payments they get from Inland Revenue.
## Review of Circumstances
A Confirming your Circumstances form will be sent the client every 52 weeks to complete and return to International Services.

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension paid in the Netherlands when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a de facto relationship or
- a married or civil union client becomes single through separation; the marriage or civil union is dissolved; or at the death of their partner
Single clients who enter a civil union or de facto relationship with a same sex partner should continue to receive payment at the single rate as the Agreement does not have provision to pay the married rate in these situations. If a client legally marries a same sex partner, they can be paid at the married rate.
Note the Reciprocal Agreement with the Netherlands and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in the Netherlands, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for Netherlands pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for Netherlands pensions
A client is obliged to advise Work and Income of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also required to provide any information required by the Netherlands authorities to ensure that they are still entitled to their Netherlands pension paid in New Zealand. Any such information provided to case managers by the client should be forwarded to International Services
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Admission to hospital
- Clients going overseas
- Death of a client in New Zealand
- Exchange of information
- Netherlands Life Certificates
- Reviews and Appeals
- Taxation

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand benefits in the Netherlands
Clients have an obligation to advise MSD of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension or the rate payable.
MSD may also review a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Netherlands at any time to check if the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions paid in the Netherlands.
## Life certificates
Clients receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in the Netherlands will need to complete a Life Certificate which will be sent to them every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Life certificates
## Review of Circumstances
Clients receiving other New Zealand benefits or pensions in the Netherlands will need to complete a Confirming your Circumstances form which will be sent to them every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Child turns 18 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Child turns 18
A dependent child must generally be under the age of 18 to be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment paid in the Netherlands.
When a child turns 18, they are generally no longer considered a dependent child and must be excluded from their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment from the start of the pay period following the child's 18th birthday.
However, if the 18-year-old child is continuing in education and is not financially independent, the child may continue to be considered a dependent child and be included in their parent or caregiver's Supported Living Payment for a limited period.
In these situations, the child must be excluded from the start of the pay period following:
- the date they no longer meet these criteria or
- 31 December of the year they turn 18
whichever is earlier.

chunks.title: Client must apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Client must apply
A client must apply for any pension that they may be entitled to from the Netherlands if they are in receipt of or applying for a New Zealand benefit or pension.
If a client has Netherlands residence or has made contributions to the Netherlands national insurance scheme they will need to complete an application for a Netherlands pension. International Services will decide whether a client needs to test their entitlement to a Netherlands pension and will contact the client direct if necessary.
Should the client contact you for help in completing or forwarding on the application, it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies) including signed special banking option forms, if the client has chosen to be paid via this option
- the application form is signed and dated
If the client refuses to apply for any Netherlands pension to which they may be entitled you should contact International Services.

chunks.title: Clients from the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Clients from the Netherlands
When a former resident of the Netherlands applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they are receiving a Netherlands pension, or if they may be entitled to one.
All clients who have previously resided in the Netherlands, regardless of where they were born, must complete the residence detail section of the application form when they apply for any New Zealand benefit or pension. This information must be entered in CMS.
This is irrespective of whether the client uses the agreement with the Netherlands to qualify for a New Zealand benefit or pension, or qualifies under the New Zealand domestic legislation.
Note the Netherlands authorities may advise International Services when a Netherlands pension is granted for a client who is living in New Zealand. If the client is not receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension International Services will record the information in CMS.
This will ensure there is a record of the Netherlands pension if the client subsequently applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Netherlands benefits and pensions paid in New Zealand
- Clients entitled to Netherlands pensions
- Clients receiving Netherlands pensions

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Clients going overseas
When a client receiving a Netherlands pension leaves New Zealand for a temporary absence the Netherlands pension can continue to be paid.
If a client is going to the Netherlands and intends to stay there for more than 26 weeks they may be able to receive payment of their New Zealand benefit or pension in the Netherlands under the social security reciprocal agreement.
Any New Zealand benefit or pension the client is receiving is subject to the absence from New Zealand provisions for that benefit if the client has no entitlement to payment overseas under a reciprocal agreement or the portability provisions.
As there are quite different entitlement conditions depending on the benefit type and the country the client is going to you should contact International Services for advice.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- New Zealand benefits and pensions in the Netherlands
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit
- Reciprocal agreements
- Portability

chunks.title: Information required from the client — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Information required from the client
A client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Netherlands pension that they, their partner, or their dependents are receiving. If they do not comply the grant of their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or, if already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension, their payments can be suspended.
## Payments from the Netherlands and how they affect entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension
When a client advises that they, their partner or their dependents are receiving payments from the Netherlands you will need to find out the payment details in order to determine if the Netherlands pension should be a direct deduction from the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
It is important that the information is obtained as quickly as possible to enable the client's New Zealand benefit or pension entitlement to be assessed correctly.
The part of the Netherlands pensions based on voluntary contributions and Netherlands Holiday Pay are not directly deducted from New Zealand benefits and pensions but are treated as income for income tested benefits and extra help.
## Client is unable to provide the information
If the client is unable to provide full documentation of the payments, you will need to grant and suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension from application date until written verification is received. International Services can obtain the pension details directly from the Netherlands authorities.
## Steps to take when documentation completed
The completed form must be sent to International Services to enable International Services to obtain and verify the following information:
- rate of payment in the Netherlands currency and whether it includes any amount in respect of the client's partner and any dependent children
- reason for the grant, such as age, widowhood, disablement, or war service
- the name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment
- verification of any amount which is payment from voluntary contributions and/or holiday pay
## Client does not comply with the request for information
The client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any Netherlands pension. If they do not or refuse to comply the grant of their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or, if they are already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension, their payments can be suspended. This will be done by International Services.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions
- Extra Help
- Other payments

chunks.title: Commencement of payment in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Commencement of payment in the Netherlands
When a client applies for their New Zealand benefit or pension to be paid in the Netherlands before their departure from New Zealand, payments overseas to the Netherlands will start on the first payday after their departure from New Zealand.
When a client applies from the Netherlands, the New Zealand benefit or pension will start on:
- the date they become entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension
- the date they applied for the New Zealand benefit or
- the date the client arrived in the Netherlands if they did not arrive within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand
whichever is the latest date.
If the client is not already in receipt of Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) or Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers then payment will commence after the applicable stand-down period has been applied.
The Netherlands authorities will forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services for processing.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Rate payable in the Netherlands
- Payments in the Netherlands

chunks.title: Death in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Death in the Netherlands
The normal procedures for cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions apply on the death of a client receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Netherlands.
Generally the Netherlands authorities will advise International Services of the death of a client in the Netherlands and International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
Note a Funeral Grant is not payable for clients who were living in the Netherlands at the time of their death.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on death follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients who were also getting a Netherlands pension that has been recorded on SWIFTT.
The executor/administrator of the client's estate will need to contact the Netherlands authorities directly if they require any details of the Netherlands pension.
International Services will send the following information to the Netherlands authorities:
- the clients name
- date of death and
- the name and address of the executor/administrator of the estate
## SWIFTT
The executor/administrator of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen in SWIFTT so International Services can advise the Netherlands authorities.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Death of a client in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
When a client is receiving a Netherlands pension, the gross amount (except for holiday pay and any portion of the pension that is based on voluntary contributions) is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit if they are paid by the Direct Payment Method.
The client can elect to have their Netherlands pension paid to their own bank account (called the direct payment method) or have their Netherlands pension paid to the Special Banking Option account.
When a client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Netherlands pension is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services
If you receive information from a client about a Netherlands pension, a fax should be sent to International Services with verification of the rate, type of Netherlands pension, the grant date and the name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already receiving a Netherlands pension at the time a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process.
## Exception
If the clients Netherlands pension is taxed in the Netherlands the net amount can be deducted from the clients New Zealand benefit or pension.
Holiday pay and voluntary contribution based portions of the pension are treated as income for income tested benefits and extra help.
Note International Services must be advised of all clients who are receiving a Netherlands pension. It is International Services' responsibility to carry out New Zealand benefit or pension reviews required when the Netherlands pension deduction is being up-dated or reviewed.
Any other reviews of the client's New Zealand benefit, such as a change of relationship status or a change of chargeable income, should be completed by the case manager.

chunks.title: Direct payment method — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Direct payment method
If a client does not choose to have their Netherlands pension paid through the Special Banking Option, it will be paid directly into their own bank account.
Under this method of payment:
- Netherlands pension payments are made every 4 weeks
- payment will be converted at the rate of exchange applicable on the day the bank credits their account
- the client is responsible for any tax liability on their Netherlands pension including holiday pay and any pension based on voluntary contributions
- the amount deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension will be based on the actual exchange rate on the 20th of the previous month)
- if the client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation, Veterans Pension or other benefit paid fortnightly the rate will be automatically recalculated in SWIFTT each month using the previous month's Netherlands exchange rate shown in SELXT
- if the client is receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension paid weekly International Services will manually review the rate on a monthly basis
- there is no due/paid assessment at the end of each year to take into account the exact exchange rate that was used by the bank to convert the Netherlands pension to New Zealand dollars
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Initial grant of Netherlands pension

chunks.title: Exchange of information — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Exchange of information
The social security agreement New Zealand has with the Netherlands has wider powers to exchange information than other agreements. New Zealand and the Netherlands exchange information by liaison form through their respective social security agencies.
In New Zealand International Services is the authorised agency and the Sociale Verzekerings Bank (SVB) and Uitvoering Werknemersverzekeringen (UWV) are the authorised Netherlands social security agencies.
As well as exchanging information about a client's New Zealand or Netherlands pension entitlement, both countries can also request information from the other country's tax authorities. If the Netherlands request information from New Zealand's Inland Revenue department, International Services is responsible for forwarding the request to Inland Revenue and returning any information to the Netherlands.
International Services will not view or copy the information.
For more information contact International Services.
## Requests for information
When a client makes application for a Netherlands pension the Netherlands authorities may send a request form to International Services for information such as:
- details of employment in New Zealand and periods on New Zealand benefits
- whether the client received a New Zealand benefit using the social security agreement with the Netherlands
International Services will obtain the relevant information and return the form to the Netherlands authorities.
None of this information will be copied or held by International Services.

chunks.title: Exchange rate example — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Exchange rate example
To convert overseas currency to New Zealand currency, take the foreign currency and multiply it by the New Zealand exchange rate.
The Netherlands exchange rate is shown on SELXT and is the actual rate for the payday the Netherlands make the payment. It is provided to International Services by the Netherlands authorities.
Note the Netherlands has one payday per month for all regular pension payments.
## Example - SWIFTT exchange rate
A client is receiving weekly payments of $50.00 per week Euro. The exchange rate for the Euro showing in SELXT screen is 1.5261 for the 20th of July 2012.
50.00 euro x 1.5261 = NZ $76.31
## Banks exchange rate
Clients may query the exchange rate as banks express their rates in a different way than SWIFTT does. The bank would express 1.5261 as 0.6553. This is calculated by dividing 1 by 1.5261 = 0.6553.
The bank calculates the exchange rate for overseas currency by dividing the overseas pension amount by the exchange rate instead of multiplying it as in the SWIFTT example above. When comparing the calculations using the 2 exchange rates there may be a small difference in the New Zealand dollar amounts. The difference is usually only one or two cents.
## Example
50.00 euro divided by 0.6553 = $76.30 (NZ)
In these examples there is only one cent difference in the New Zealand dollar amount of the overseas pension.

chunks.title: Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Netherlands
From 15 July 2013 onwards, people receiving existing portable payments of Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers in the Netherlands will be grandparented on their existing rate and conditions.
References to the benefit names Widows Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for Widowers are grandparented for existing clients and must still be used when administering these benefits payable under the Agreement with Netherlands and when corresponding with the client.
Grandparenting arrangements do not apply to the former Invalids Benefit because the only change is the name change to Supported Living Payment.
For more information see:
- Grandparenting
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Netherlands

chunks.title: Extra Help — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Extra Help
When assessing the amount of any Extra Help that the client may be entitled to, you must include the following in the calculation in the same way as income earned in New Zealand:
- holiday pay or
- any portion of the pension that is based on the clients voluntary contributions
## Accommodation Supplement
When a client is receiving a Netherlands pension that exceeds the New Zealand main benefit rate, the excess amount will be directly deducted from any Accommodation Supplement the client receives.
You will need to calculate the amount that the client would be entitled to receive by way of a New Zealand benefit or pension and the rate of Accommodation Supplement that would be payable alongside that benefit or pension. The Netherlands pension should be deducted from the total New Zealand benefit and Accommodation Supplement, and the balance will be the actual rate of Accommodation Supplement payable.
Note you will need to manually add the actual rate of Accommodation Supplement payable in SWIFTT using the SASA screen.
For more information contact International Services
Also see:
- Review date
- Exchange rate example

chunks.title: Initial grant of Netherlands pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Initial grant of Netherlands pension
When a client already getting a New Zealand benefit or pension is granted a Netherlands pension, the Netherlands authorities will:
- provide details of any grant of a Netherlands pension to International Services and
- pay the Netherlands pension arrears to Work and Income
This will enable International Services to:
- add the Netherlands pension details to SWIFTT
- add the Netherlands pension as a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension using the INCMA screen in SWIFTT
- review the New Zealand benefit or pension from the date of grant of the Netherlands pension and
- recover any overpayment of New Zealand benefit or pension paid for the same period as the Netherlands pension or
- pay the Netherlands pension arrears to the client
Note if the Netherlands authorities have not provided the Netherlands pension details, the client must provide verification or the New Zealand benefit or pension may be suspended.
For more information regarding this process you can contact International Services.

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and the Netherlands allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- periods of contributions to the Netherlands national insurance scheme after attaining the age of 20 years can be regarded as periods of residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- residence in New Zealand can be regarded as residence in the Netherlands in order to meet the residence qualifications for some Netherlands benefits and pensions
- some Netherlands pensions can be paid in New Zealand
- some New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid in the Netherlands
## Benefit changes from 15 July 2013
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories.
These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with the Netherlands.

chunks.title: Last child turning 14 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Last child turning 14
Client's getting Sole Parent Support payments as a widow or widower will cease to be eligible for payments once their last child turns 14.
Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14, as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with the Netherlands.
If the client returns to New Zealand after their last dependent child turns 14 they may qualify for Jobseeker Support but will not be eligible for a New Zealand benefit if they remain ordinarily resident in the Netherlands.
Supported Living Payment clients with dependent children and grandparented Widow's Benefit and Domestic Purposes Benefit for widowers with dependent children do not lose their entitlement when their last child turns 14.

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client intends to live in a country other than New Zealand or the Netherlands for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
The client may still be entitled to the New Zealand benefit or pension if:
- they qualify for the New Zealand benefit or pension due to their previous residence in New Zealand and
- they are moving to a country which has an agreement with New Zealand
Payment of the New Zealand benefit or pension should stop from the payday after the client's departure from the Netherlands until the client can test their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension in the country that they have moved to.
## Payment cannot be made
New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension cannot be paid to a client who leaves the Netherlands to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand as the client needs to be ordinarily resident or resident and present in New Zealand at the date they apply for payment overseas.
Other New Zealand benefits cannot be paid to a client who leaves the Netherlands unless they intend to live in a country that has a social security agreement with New Zealand, which covers the payment of New Zealand benefits.
## Residence
If the client is receiving the New Zealand benefit or pension by using their Netherlands residence to meet the New Zealand residence qualification, they may not be entitled to have the New Zealand benefit or pension paid in another country.
## Example
A customer is receiving New Zealand Superannuation with only three years New Zealand residence but sufficient Netherlands residence or contributions to the Netherlands insurance to enable them to meet the minimum residence requirement for New Zealand Superannuation. They will not be entitled to take payment overseas to a third country (unless they can qualify under another reciprocal agreement).
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reciprocal agreements
- Portability

chunks.title: Netherlands benefits and pensions paid in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Netherlands benefits and pensions paid in New Zealand
The agreement with the Netherlands allows clients who have resided in the Netherlands and/or who have paid contributions to the Netherlands national insurance scheme to receive the following Netherlands pensions when they are living in New Zealand:
- Children's Allowance
- Invalidity Benefit
- Old Age Pension
- Sickness Benefit
- Survivors Benefit
- Unemployment Benefit (in certain circumstances for seconded workers)
Netherlands pensions can be paid directly to the client by the Direct Payment Method or to a Special Banking Option account. For more information see:
- Direct Payment Method
- Special Banking Option
Netherlands pensions are directly deducted from the client's New Zealand benefit or pension if they are paid by the direct payment method except for holiday pay and any portion of the pension that is based on their voluntary contributions
When a Netherlands pension exceeds the main benefit rate, the amount that exceeds the main benefit rate will be directly deducted from the partner's New Zealand benefit or pension if they receive one or from any Accommodation Supplement the client may receive as a non-beneficiary.
## Medical examinations
The Netherlands authorities can require a client to be medically re-examined periodically to check that they are still entitled to a benefit or pension.
Any medical examinations are arranged by International Services
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Clients entitled to Netherlands pensions
- Clients receiving Netherlands pensions
- Initial grant of Netherlands pensions
- Direct deductions
- Extra Help
- Change and reviews for Netherlands pensions

chunks.title: Netherlands debt recovery — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Netherlands debt recovery
If a Netherlands benefit or pension is no longer payable but the debtor is in New Zealand the Netherlands authorities can ask International Services to assist in recovering the debt.
The following conditions must be met:
- the debt must be a social security debt
- the Netherlands must have pursued all means available to them in the Netherlands
- the Netherlands review/appeal timeframe must have passed
- the debt must amount to at least NZ $500 and
- no more than five years must have passed since the debt was established
- it is not possible to total a number of debts over different dates in a five year period to reach the minimum debt amount. Each debt must have been established on the same date, or as part of the same review (eg where you have added some debts for a review on one day but have not completed adding debts until the next day)
If the client is in receipt on a New Zealand benefit or pension the debt can be recovered from the clients benefit payments.
If the client is not in receipt of a New Zealand benefit or pension International Services will try to recover the debt by asking the client to make repayment. The Ministry of Social Development may refer the debt to a debt collection agency.
Note the Netherlands social security authorities must send International Services the appropriate debt recovery liaison form and this must be accompanied by a debt certificate.
The recovery of a Netherlands debt should not be done at the expense of the recovery of a New Zealand debt.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Netherlands debt recovery process
- Exchange of information

chunks.title: Netherlands debt recovery process — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Netherlands debt recovery process
Once the debt certificate and liaison form has been checked to ensure the recovery criteria has been met, International Services will:
## Debtor getting New Zealand benefit or pension
Contact the client and advise them of the request from the Netherlands and negotiate repayment of the debt.
If the debt is to be recovered from the clients New Zealand benefit or pension International Services will initiate the debt recovery process.
The overseas agency is added as a payee and the money due to the Netherlands will be remitted (by Crown Revenue) on a regular basis.
## Debtor not getting a New Zealand benefit or pension
International Services will locate the client, advise them of the debt and negotiate debt recovery. If the client is unable to be located or ignores debt repayment requests the debt may be referred to a debt collection agency.
The Netherlands authorities will have to provide their authority (once a quote for collection has been received) before a debt can be referred to a debt collection agency for collection.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Netherlands life certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Netherlands life certificates
When a client is receiving a Netherlands pension in New Zealand the Netherlands authorities require them to complete life certificates.
The Netherlands authorities will send the life certificate form directly to the client when it is due. The client should complete the life certificate and return it directly to the Netherlands.
If a client needs the life certificate witnessed it is important to check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
Return the life certificate to the client so that they can send it directly to the Netherlands authorities.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions in the Netherlands
Under the agreement with the Netherlands, the following New Zealand benefits and pensions can be paid to former New Zealand residents who live, or intend to live, in the Netherlands:
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with dependent child/ren under 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- Veterans Pension
The rules are different depending on whether the client is already receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension and is moving to the Netherlands, or if they are already living in the Netherlands at the time they apply.
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefits
- Jobseeker Support
- Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Sole Parent Support (sole parent)
- Supported Living Payment (care of sick or infirm)
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
The agreement with the Netherlands allows periods of Netherlands residence or contributions to the Netherlands national insurance scheme after attaining the age of 20 years to be regarded as periods of residence in New Zealand to meet the residence qualification for the following New Zealand benefits:
- Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers with dependent child/ren under 14
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Veterans Pension
Note where a person does not meet the New Zealand Superannuation residence requirement of 5 years over the age of 50, only periods of Netherlands residence or contributions to Netherlands national insurance scheme after the person attained age 50 can be used to meet this residential requirement.
The agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefit
- Jobseeker Support
- Orphans Benefit and Unsupported Childs Benefit
- Sole Parent Support - sole parent
- Supported Living Payment - caring for sick or infirm
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment

chunks.title: New Zealand life certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## New Zealand life certificates
When a client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in the Netherlands they are required to complete a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances.
International Services will send the life certificate form directly to the client.
Certificates can be issued every 26 weeks for clients considered a 'high risk'. That is clients who are using an agent, clients aged 80 years or over and clients continuing to have benefit paid into a New Zealand bank account.
It is the client's responsibility to complete the life certificate and return it directly to International Services. However, if the client needs the life certificate witnessed, the Netherlands authorities will check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
The life certificate will either be sent to International Services by the Netherlands authorities or it will be returned to the client so that they can send it directly to International Services.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation
When a client from the Netherlands meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except residence they may qualify under the agreement with the Netherlands.
The agreement with the Netherlands allows residence in the Netherlands after the age of 20 to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
Note only periods of residence in the Netherlands after the person attained the age of 50 years can be used for the residential requirement of being resident in New Zealand for 5 years after the age of 50.
The client must be the New Zealand qualifying age.
The client may also be entitled to a Netherlands Pension which will be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation.
## SWIFTT
When New Zealand Superannuation is granted using the agreement with Netherlands you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 12 (Netherlands 2002) in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Sole Parent Support Qualifications
- New Zealand Superannuation Residency
- Clients from the Netherlands

chunks.title: Other payments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Other payments
When a client is receiving other payments, such as interest or rent from investments or properties they own in the Netherlands, the payments will be treated in the same way as income earned in New Zealand.
You need to convert the income to New Zealand dollars using the current exchange rate. This can be found by using the SELXT screen in SWIFTT and entering the Netherlands country code 110.
Netherlands holiday pay is paid directly to the clients own bank account even if their Netherlands pension is paid to the special banking option account. Holiday pay should be treated as income the same way as income earned in New Zealand.
Netherlands pensions based wholly or partly on voluntary contributions are not treated as a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension but as income the same way as income earned in New Zealand. You should always check with International Services if a client claims their pension is based on voluntary contributions.
For more information on how to treat income from overseas or if you are unsure how the calculation works you should contact International Services or see:
- Charging income in relevant Main benefit
- Exchange rate example

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand benefit or pension being paid in the Netherlands is overpaid you will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment
- their review and appeal rights and
- the relevant legislation (if the overpayment occurred as a result of a provision in the agreement; then the authority to establish an overpayment is contained in that Article of the agreement)
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deduction from any New Zealand benefit or pension that the client is receiving.
If the client is no longer receiving a New Zealand benefit or pension they will need to make arrangements to repay the debt.
The Netherlands Social Security authorities may be able to assist in recovering the debt.
## Review or appeal
If a client applies for a review, or appeals a decision on the establishment of a debt or the rate of recovery, recovery action will be suspended until the outcome of that review or appeal is known.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Reviews and appeals

chunks.title: Payment options — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Payment options
When a client is receiving a benefit or pension from the Netherlands social security authorities, they can choose to have their Netherlands pension paid by the:
- Direct payment method or
- Special banking option
Clients will be asked to select a payment option when they are sent a Netherlands pension application pack by International Services. They can change from one payment option to the other at any time but can generally only join the special banking option once.
All payment option changes are completed by International Services.
Note a client can authorise the Netherlands authorities to pay arrears of their Netherlands pension direct to Work and Income regardless of the payment option they choose for regular payments.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct payment method
- Special Banking Option

chunks.title: Methods of payment in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment in the Netherlands
When a client receives a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Netherlands they can choose to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account or to an overseas bank account.
## Overseas bank account
Payments made to an overseas bank account are credited 4 weekly.
If a client chooses to have money paid directly to an overseas bank account, Work and Income meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
There are 3 options for the first payment being made into a Netherlands bank account:
- payment can be made to an overseas bank account if the client has already provided proof of their bank account
- the first payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the overseas bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the overseas bank account are given to International Services (once account details are advised, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the overseas account with the first payment)
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Rate payable in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Rate payable in the Netherlands
When a New Zealand benefit or pension is paid to a client in the Netherlands the rate of payment is calculated by a specific formula as provided for in article 8 and article 9 of the agreement between New Zealand and the Netherlands authorities.
The New Zealand benefit or pension is paid without regard to any Netherlands pension or other overseas pension being paid but other income should be taken into account for income tested benefits.
## New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
The calculation for New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension is different to the calculation for other New Zealand benefits.
If a client was entitled to receive New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension while residing in New Zealand without having to use Netherlands residence or contributions and moved to the Netherlands after 1 April 1990, the minimum they can be paid is 50%.
There is no provision in respect of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension to include payment for a grandparented non-qualified partner. The partner can only be paid New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in the Netherlands if they meet the qualifications in their own right.
The maximum rate payable is the single sharing accommodation rate or the married, civil union, de facto relationship rate depending on the client's circumstances.
## Supported Living Payment
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is paid to a married or civil union client in the Netherlands their partner can be included.
## Residence in New Zealand
New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension clients who are already age 65 on 1 November 2003 must have 10 years New Zealand residence. In other cases no payment is made to a client who has lived in New Zealand for less than 12 continuous months.
Only periods of actual New Zealand residence are counted. Periods of residence in a country other than New Zealand are disregarded even if the country has a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand.
Any period of absence from New Zealand for up to 26 weeks is regarded as New Zealand residence, as long as the client was considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the period of absence.
## Extra help
Extra help such as family tax credit, Best Start tax credit, Temporary Additional Support, Special Benefit or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in the Netherlands.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for a Netherlands pension. International Services will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not respond to requests to apply for a Netherlands pension.
International Services will talk to clients about the reasons why they must apply, including:
- it is their right as they have lived in the Netherlands or made contributions to the national insurance scheme
- clients must claim any pension they may be entitled to from the Netherlands if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from the Netherlands
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension may stop, payment of a Netherlands pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 4 weeks their Sole Parent Support may stop but payment of a Netherlands pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 6 weeks their Supported Living Payment may stop but payment of a Netherlands pension may continue
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate, and the rate of Netherlands pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended but the Netherlands pension may still be paid

chunks.title: Temporary return — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Temporary return
When a client is receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Netherlands and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, payment of the New Zealand benefit will continue to be paid at the same rate as when they were living in the Netherlands.
This is because the client will not be considered as being ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Permanent return
When a client, receiving payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension in the Netherlands, returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their benefit can be reviewed from the payday after they return to New Zealand.
International Services must be advised as they are responsible for stopping payment made under the Social Security Agreement.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Review date
International Services will review a New Zealand benefit or pension from the date a client is granted a Netherlands pension, or when the rate of a Netherlands pension changes.
When a Netherlands pension is altered, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the change.
Note when reviewing a New Zealand benefit or pension do not include the following Netherlands payments in the direct deduction assessment but include them as income for income tested benefits and extra help:
- holiday pay or
- any portion of the pension that is based on the clients voluntary contributions
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions
- Extra Help
- Exchange rate example

chunks.title: Review of Circumstances for benefit — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Review of Circumstances for benefit
Clients receiving one of the following New Zealand benefits paid in the Netherlands will be sent a Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks for them to complete and return to International Services:
- Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
International Services will process the review and renew the benefit for the following year.

chunks.title: Netherlands pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Netherlands pensions
If a client is unhappy with any decision regarding their Netherlands pension being paid in New Zealand they will need to contact the Netherlands authorities.
For Netherlands pension agencies contact details, see:
- Overseas pension agencies The Netherlands
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
International Services is responsible for any reviews and appeals in regards to the interpretation of the Agreement with the Netherlands and the effect of the Netherlands pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions.
The New Zealand review and appeal process applies to any other decisions regarding New Zealand benefits or pensions such as charging income or change in relationship status.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers
Under the agreement with the Netherlands a client may qualify for the New Zealand Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower if they meet all the qualifications.
Under the agreement a dependent child born in the Netherlands can be treated as having been born in New Zealand provided:
- in the case of a widow the child was conceived before the death of the applicant's last deceased spouse
- in the case of a widower the child was born before the death of the applicants last deceased spouse
- the client may also be entitled to a Netherlands Pension which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Domestic Purposes Benefit
For widows or widower's periods of Netherlands residence or periods of contributions to the Netherlands national insurance scheme after age 20 can be regarded as a period the applicant was both resident and present in New Zealand.
Specific to widows only who are ordinarily resident in New Zealand or Netherlands the residential qualification for Sole Parent Support can be met with:
- any accumulated periods of residence or contributions in the Netherlands by the last deceased spouse may be regarded as residence in New Zealand
- any accumulated periods of residence or contributions in the Netherlands by the last deceased spouse and the applicant may be regarded as residence in New Zealand but may be considered only once
- Netherlands periods of residence or contributions accumulated by a widow's last deceased spouse is deemed to be, for the purpose of determining if the spouse was ordinarily resident in New Zealand a period during which the deceased spouse was ordinarily resident in New Zealand
- the death of the last deceased spouse in the Netherlands is treated as if the death occurred in New Zealand
## SWIFTT
When Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers is granted using the agreement with Netherlands you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 12 in the entitlement code field.
## For more information
Contact International Services or see:
- Sole Parent Support Qualifications
- Sole Parent Support Residence
- Applications for payment in the Netherlands with entitlements before 15 July 2013
- Clients from the Netherlands
- Care and protection concerns for a child or young person

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers moving to the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text: Under the agreement with the Netherlands Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers can be paid to clients who move to and live in the Netherlands. When a client is receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower and advises they intend to live in the Netherlands they will need to: - complete an Application for Payment Overseas form (WIS7W) - be interviewed by a case manager and Interview form (WIF9W) completed - provide details of the total period of their residence in New Zealand - provide two forms of identification one must be their passport - provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm that they are travelling to the Netherlands and - provide verified bank account details if different than those currently in SWIFTT The application, interview form and supporting documents should be sent to International Services for processing. The client will need to meet the following qualifications: - intend to be ordinarily resident in the Netherlands, and be present either in the Netherlands or New Zealand at the time they apply - have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in the Netherlands for at least 26 weeks - have had at least 12 months continuous residence in New Zealand since the age of 20 and - meet the qualifications for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower If the client is not currently receiving Sole Parent Support an application should be taken and entitlement established in accordance with the qualifications for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower (except the client does not need to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand). The client should apply before leaving New Zealand to avoid any overpayment as any application made from overseas cannot be backdated. International Services should be contacted before any current benefit is cancelled or suspended.

chunks.title: Intending to live in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text: If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in the Netherlands for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in the Netherlands. If the client begins to be ordinarily resident in the Netherlands within that time, then they can be treated as being ordinarily resident from the date they departed New Zealand.

chunks.title: Example — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text: A client may wish to take a four-month holiday in the United States of America before taking up residence in the Netherlands. In this instance the client would be considered to be ordinarily resident in the Netherlands from the date they departed New Zealand for benefit purposes. For more information contact International Services or see: - Commencement of payment in the Netherlands - Applications for payment in the Netherlands with entitlements before 15 July 2013 - Benefit entitlements in the Netherlands after 15 July 2013 - Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers living in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support - widows and widowers living in the Netherlands
Under the agreement with the Netherlands Sole Parent Support for a widow or widower can be paid when they are living in the Netherlands.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in the Netherlands they can receive Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower if:
- they are ordinarily resident in the Netherlands, and are present either in the Netherlands or New Zealand at the time they apply
- they have lived, or are intending to live, in the Netherlands for at least 26 weeks
- they have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20 and
- they meet the qualifications for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower except the ordinary residence criteria
Sole Parent Support will cease once the last child turns 14. Clients cannot transfer to Jobseeker Support once their child has turned 14 as Jobseeker Support is not included as a benefit payable under the Agreement with the Netherlands.
If the client is still receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower at the time they reach the qualifying age for New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension they will no longer be eligible for Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower and must test their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension.
## Income
Sole Parent Support paid to a widow or widower in the Netherlands is income tested and the client will need to advise details of any income they receive in the Netherlands or New Zealand when they apply for the benefit or when they complete the Confirming your Circumstances form every 52 weeks.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave the Netherlands to live in another country.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in the Netherlands
- Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers moving to the Netherlands
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Netherlands
- Existing portable payments for widows and widowers in Netherlands
- Benefit entitlements in the Netherlands after 15 July 2013

chunks.title: Special Banking Option applications — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option applications
When a client chooses the special banking option for their Netherlands pension they will be sent an application pack from International Services containing:
- an Application for the Special Banking Option
- an Application for a Special Bank Account and
- an Authority to Release Information form (this form allows us to share information regarding pension entitlements with the Netherlands authorities)
All three forms must be fully completed and forwarded to International Services for processing.
## Note
- when a client has a partner they must both choose the same payment option
- the client can change from the direct payment method to the special banking option at any time
- if the client has changed from the special banking option to the direct payment option generally they cannot re-join the special banking option
- the client does not have access to the special banking option account that the Netherlands pension is paid into as it is simply a holding account for funds that are to be paid to MSD

chunks.title: Special Banking Option payment method — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option payment method
This payment method is not suitable for clients who receive part or their entire pension based on voluntary contributions.
When a client is receiving a Netherlands pension they can choose to have it paid into a special banking option account by the Netherlands authorities. The client will then receive the full rate of their New Zealand benefit or pension.
The advantages of this option are:
- the New Zealand benefit or pension is paid as usual at the full rate every week or 2 weeks (depending on the pay cycle for the client's New Zealand Benefit)
- tax is already deducted
- the client is not affected by fluctuations in the exchange rate
Clients may elect to join the special banking option at any time but cannot re-join once they have chosen to cancel the option (there are exceptions, contact International Services).
The special banking option is not suitable for clients whose Netherlands pension is higher than (or likely to be higher than) the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Payment of holiday pay
If the client is paid holiday pay this amount is transferred from the Special Banking Option account directly to the clients own bank account and the client is responsible for paying tax on this amount.
## Partner
When a client has a partner they must both choose the same payment option.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Special Banking Option applications
- Initial grant of Netherlands pension

chunks.title: Superannuitants living in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Superannuitants living in the Netherlands
Under the agreement with the Netherlands a client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation when they are living in the Netherlands.
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in the Netherlands they can receive New Zealand Superannuation if:
- they are ordinarily resident in the Netherlands and present either in the Netherlands or New Zealand at the time they apply
- they have lived, or are intending to live, in the Netherlands for at least 26 weeks
- they have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20 and
- they meet the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except being ordinarily resident
Note although periods of Netherlands insurance can be treated as residence in New Zealand in order to meet the residence qualifications for New Zealand superannuation, clients who are aged 65 years before 1 November 2003, must have 10 years actual New Zealand residence at any time.
## Partner
If the client has a partner, the partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
There is no provision to pay the married, civil union or de facto rate of payment to same sex couples living in the Netherlands unless they are legally married to each other. If they are not legally married to each other, each partner must be assessed on an individual basis and be paid at the single sharing rate.
Note the Reciprocal Agreement with the Netherlands and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in the Netherlands, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
## Change of circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave the Netherlands to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or their New Zealand Superannuation will stop.
## International Services
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- reviewing entitlement
- renewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Commencement of payment in the Netherlands
- New Zealand Superannuation

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment
When a client from the Netherlands meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) except residence they may qualify under the agreement with the Netherlands.
The agreement with the Netherlands allows residence in the Netherlands after the age of 20 to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
The client must meet the New Zealand medical criteria.
The client may also be entitled to a Netherlands pension, which may be directly deducted from the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).

chunks.title: Clients in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Clients in New Zealand
When a client gets New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, and a Netherlands pension paid in New Zealand, they will be liable to pay tax on the Netherlands pension. This is regardless of whether the Netherlands pension is paid into a New Zealand or Netherlands bank account.
If the Netherlands pension is paid into a Special Banking Option account, tax is deducted when the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension payments are made.
A client getting any other type of New Zealand benefit or pension and a Netherlands pension will be exempt from paying tax on the Netherlands pension in New Zealand (if the Netherlands pension is being deducted from their New Zealand benefit rate. This is because the gross Netherlands pension is directly deducted from the net New Zealand benefit or pension).
If the Netherlands pension is paid into New Zealand at a net rate the client should contact Inland Revenue to discuss their New Zealand tax liability.
Note clients can pay tax in the Netherlands on the Netherlands pension paid into New Zealand. They are only able to do this if they are a Netherlands citizen. If they are a New Zealand citizen only, they are not able to pay tax on their Netherlands pension in the Netherlands.
## Holiday pay and voluntary payments
Holiday pay and any portion of a Netherlands pension based on voluntary contributions are generally liable for tax in New Zealand. The client should contact Inland Revenue to discuss their tax obligations.
## Clients in the Netherlands
New Zealand benefits paid in the Netherlands are not taxed in New Zealand but may be liable for tax in the Netherlands.
The client must make their own tax arrangements with the Netherlands tax authority.

chunks.title: Veterans living in the Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:

- they are age 65 or over
- they are ordinarily resident in the Netherlands and present either in the Netherlands or New Zealand at the time they apply
- they have lived, or are intending to live, in the Netherlands for at least 26 weeks
- they have had at least 12 months residence in New Zealand since age 20 and
- they meet the qualifications for New Zealand Veteran's Pension
Note if the client is already age 65 years as at 1 November 2003, they must have at least 10 years actual New Zealand residence, at any time.
## Partner
The partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement in their own right.
There is no provision to pay the married, civil union or de facto rate of payment to same sex couples living in the Netherlands unless they are legally married to each other. If they are not legally married to each other, each partner must be assessed on an individual basis and be paid at the single sharing accommodation rate.
Note the Netherlands and the supporting legislation set the relationship criteria for payments to clients living in the Netherlands, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
## Change of circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave the Netherlands to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances which must be completed and returned to New Zealand or the Veteran's Pension will stop.

Contact the Veterans Pension Centre for help. The client should apply before leaving New Zealand to avoid any overpayment.
