chunks.title: Veterans Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension
When a client from the Netherlands meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Veteran's Pension except residence they may qualify under the agreement with the Netherlands.
The agreement with the Netherlands allows Netherlands residence or periods of contributions to the Netherlands insurance scheme after the age of 20 to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Veteran's Pension.
If the client's periods of Netherlands residence or contributions are to be taken into account and treated as New Zealand residence, the client must be at least 65 years of age.
The client must meet the New Zealand service and disability qualifications.
The client may also be entitled to a Netherlands Pension which will be directly deducted from the New Zealand Veteran's Pension.
## SWIFTT
When Veteran's Pension is granted using the agreement with Netherlands you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 12 (Netherlands 2002) in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services or the Veterans Pension Centre
Also see:
- Clients from the Netherlands

chunks.title: Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Netherlands — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal netherlands
chunks.text:
## Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with Netherlands
From 15 July 2013 new provisions provide for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit names and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes have some impacts on the Agreement with the Netherlands.
## New benefit categories
Jobseeker Support replaced:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole Parent and widowers with dependent children aged 14 years or older
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women Alone
- Sickness Benefit (including Sickness Benefit Hardship)
- Unemployment Benefit (including Unemployment Benefit Student Hardship and Unemployment Benefit Training)
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged 14 years or older, or have no children
Sole Parent Support replaced:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent and widowers with dependent children aged under 14 years
- Widows Benefit for clients with dependent children aged under 14 years
Supported Living Payment replaced:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Care of sick or infirm
- Invalids Benefit
The following benefits remain:
- Emergency Benefit for clients in hardship (including Emergency Maintenance Allowance)
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
- Unsupported Child's Benefit and Orphan's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For entitlements arising from an Agreement occurring on or after 15 July 2013 references in the Agreement with the Netherlands to the former benefits names must be considered as references to the new names. The name changes do not affect New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Admission to hospital in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital in New Zealand
When a client has been in a public hospital for more than 13 weeks the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate.
Veteran's Pension is the exception and is not reduced if the client is in a public hospital for more than 13 weeks.
The Korean pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital. SWIFTT will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension when a client has been in hospital for 13 weeks and the Korean pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
When the client has a partner qualified for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension and the rate of a Korean old age benefit is more than the hospital rate of their New Zealand benefit or pension, the excess amount of the Korean old age benefit is not deducted from the other partner's New Zealand Superannuation.
Note clients admitted to private hospitals do not have their benefit or pension reduced to the hospital rate.

chunks.title: Admission to hospital or prison — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital or prison
When a client is getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Korea the rate of payment does not change when the client is admitted to hospital or imprisoned.
This is because overseas institutions are not covered by the definitions of institutions in New Zealand legislation.

chunks.title: Applying before departure — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Applying before departure
When a client advises they intend to live in Korea they will need to:
- complete an Application for New Zealand Payment Overseas form (WIS7W)
- provide details of the total period of their residence in New Zealand
- provide two forms of identification one must be their passport and
- provide their air tickets or travel itinerary to confirm they are travelling to Korea
- provide verified bank account details if different than those on SWIFTT
They also need to attend an interview where the case manager will complete an Application for New Zealand Payment Overseas interview form (WIF9W).
The application form, interview form and supporting documents should be sent to International Services for processing.
Note contact International Services before any current New Zealand benefit is cancelled or suspended.
## New Zealand benefit application
If the client is not yet getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, take an application and establish entitlement based on the qualifications for the particular benefit.
## Residence
The residency and ordinary residence requirements are addressed under the specific benefit being applied for.
Clients can use their periods of coverage in Korea to meet the residency qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension only.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Applying in Korea — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Applying in Korea
When a former New Zealand resident is already living in Korea they may get New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension if they meet the qualifying criteria.
The client will need to complete an Application for New Zealand Benefit form and lodge it at a Korean National Pension Service office which will send it to International Services in New Zealand.
International Services is responsible for:
- assessing entitlement
- granting and declining applications
- maintaining client records
- reviewing entitlement and
- cancelling payment
## All payments
All initial payments of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension will be made to the client or their designated representative. The agreement with Korea does not include recovery of debt from the initial arrears, or any other debt recovery.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Change in relationship status — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Change in relationship status
International Services will review the rate of payment of a New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid in Korea when:
- a single client marries, enters a civil union, or starts living in a relationship in the nature of a marriage or
- a client becomes single through separation; the marriage or civil union is dissolved; or the death of their partner

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for Korean benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for Korean benefits
Clients must give us details of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
We can review a benefit at any time to make sure the client still meets the qualifications and is getting the correct rate of payment.
Clients must provide any information the Korean authorities need to make sure they are still entitled to get their Korean old age benefit in New Zealand. This is usually a Life Certificate.
Note Korea may also request details about any service pension or superannuation paid by a former employer. This allows Korea to assess entitlement to a non-contributory (means tested) scheme.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews for New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension in Korea — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews for New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension in Korea
Clients getting their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Korea must advise International Services when there is any change in their circumstances that may affect payment of their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
These include:
- Admission to hospital or prison in Korea
- Change in relationship status
- Death in Korea
- Move to another country
- Overpayments
- Return to New Zealand
## Reviews
International Services is responsible for reviews of New Zealand benefits and pensions being paid in Korea.
Clients getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Korea will need to complete a life certificate. These are sent out every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances.

chunks.title: Clients entitled to Korean benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Clients entitled to Korean benefits
Clients, their partner and dependents (if any) must apply for any pension or benefit that they may be entitled to from Korea if they are applying for or getting a New Zealand benefit or pension. This applies even if the New Zealand benefit they are applying for is not included in the agreement with Korea.
If the client has applicable periods of Korean contributions, they will need to complete an application for a Korean benefit.
International Services will contact clients with applicable periods of residence in Korea and ask them to apply for a Korean benefit.
When the client completes the application, it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all relevant questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached
- the application form is signed and dated
If the client refuses to apply for a Korean old age benefit or any other benefit or pension from Korea they may be entitled to contact International Services.

chunks.title: Clients getting Korean benefits in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Clients getting Korean benefits in New Zealand
Clients getting payments from Korea need to tell us the details of any payments they are getting to determine the effect they will have on the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
If they do not provide this information any New Zealand benefit or pension they are getting may be suspended.
It is important that information is provided as quickly as possible, so the client's New Zealand benefit or pension payments can be assessed correctly. This will also reduce the possibility of the clients getting a debt.
The following information needs to be provided by the client and forwarded to International Services:
- rate of payment in Korean Won and whether it includes any payments for the client's partner and any dependent children
- whether tax has been deducted from the payment in Korea before being sent - only required for the Korean old age benefit
- reason for the payment (e.g. retirement, disability etc)
- confirm whether any part of the benefit is made up from periods of voluntary Korean contributions (this may not apply and can be difficult to identify)
- the name of the organisation or authority that is making the payment - this is usually the Competent institution or their paying agency
- the date the payments started from and any changes in the rate of payment from the date the New Zealand payment is or was granted
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Clients going overseas — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Clients going overseas
If a client getting a Korean old age benefit or other Korean benefit or pension leaves New Zealand for a temporary or permanent absence, they will need to contact the Korean authorities to find out what they may pay during the absence.

chunks.title: Commencement of payment in Korea — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Commencement of payment in Korea
When a client applies for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension to be paid in Korea before their departure, payments will start on the first payday after they have left New Zealand.
When a client applies from Korea, the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's pension will start from the latter of:
- the date they are entitled to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
- the date the agreement with Korea came into force or
- the date they applied for New Zealand Superannuation Veteran's Pension or a Korean pension (whichever they applied for earliest)
The Korean authorities will forward the application form and supporting documentation to International Services.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Death in Korea — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Death in Korea
The Korean authorities will advise International Services of the death of a client in the Republic of Korea. International Services will complete the cancellation of the New Zealand benefit or pension which will include payment of any terminal benefit.
Note Funeral Grants are not paid for clients who were living in Korea at the time of their death.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Death of a client in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Death of a client in New Zealand
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on the death of a client follows normal procedures.
International Services gets reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled for clients also getting a Korean old age benefit.
International Services will send the following information to the Korean authorities:
- the clients name
- the date of death and
- the name and address of the administrator of the estate
This information cannot be sent to Korea for clients who receive a Korean benefit or pension not covered by the Agreement.
The executor of the client's estate will need to contact the Korean authorities directly if they require any details of the Korean pension.
Note the executor of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen in SWIFTT so that International Services can advise the Korean authorities.

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
In general, when a client is living in New Zealand and receiving a Korean old age benefit it will be directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit.
The amount to deduct is the rate of the benefit after any tax deductions in Korea but before any New Zealand tax deductions.
The Korean old age benefit is deducted from:
- the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension and
- the net rate of any other New Zealand benefit, including Accommodation Supplement
Note any other deductible benefit or pension from Korea that is not covered by the Agreement the gross amount should be deducted.
When a client is already getting a New Zealand benefit or pension at the time the Korean old age benefit is granted the deduction will be processed by International Services.
Details should be sent to International Services with verification of the rate, type of Korean benefit or pension, the grant date and the name of the organisation making the payment.
If the client is already getting a Korean old age benefit or other benefit or pension when a New Zealand benefit or pension is being granted the direct deduction can be added using the SWIFTT process.
Not all benefits and pensions received from an overseas country are deductible. You should contact International Services for advice on the deductibility of overseas benefits and pensions before applying the direct deduction.
When it is determined that the overseas benefit or pension is not deductible it must be treated as income and taken into account for any income tested assistance the client receives.
## Reviews
International Services must be advised of all clients who are receiving a Korean old age benefit or other benefit or pension. International Services is responsible for ensuring the New Zealand benefit or pension is reviewed when a Korean benefit is granted or when there are changes to the Korean payment rate.

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and Korea allows former residents of one country access to some benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
Under the agreement:
- periods of coverage in Korea are periods of contributions recognised and completed under the legislation of Korea. After the age of 20 the contributions can be regarded as periods of residence and presence in New Zealand to meet the residence qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
- periods of New Zealand working age residence can be taken into account for the purpose of establishing entitlement to Korean old age benefits
- Korean old age benefit paid for retirement can be paid in New Zealand
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension can be paid in Korea
Note War disablement pensions from either country are not included in this agreement.

chunks.title: Korean benefits in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Korean benefits in New Zealand
When a former resident of Korea applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they are getting or may be entitled to a Korean old age benefit or any other Korean benefit or pension.
A client who has previously resided in Korea must complete details of their residence in Korea, and any other country of residence on the application form when they apply for any New Zealand benefit or pension.
The overseas residence details must be entered in CMS. These details are used by International Services to assess whether the client may be entitled to a Korean old age benefit or any other benefit or pension from another country.
If the client is already getting an overseas pension you should find out the details to check whether this pension should be a direct deduction from their New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Korean old age benefits
The Korean old age benefit is the only benefit covered by the agreement with Korea.
## Other Korean benefits and pensions
Korean benefits not covered by the agreement may still be paid in New Zealand. These payments may be deductible from New Zealand Superannuation, Veteran's Pension or other New Zealand benefits. Periods of contributions in Korea cannot be totalised to meet residence qualifications for a New Zealand benefit such as Jobseeker Support.
Note the agreement with Korea only allows for the exchange of information in relation to the Korean Old Age Benefit, New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension. Information on other Korean benefits and pensions and New Zealand benefits cannot be exchanged between New Zealand and Korea. Any information will need to be provided by the client.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Korean life certificates — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Korean life certificates
When a client is getting a Korean pension in New Zealand they may be required to complete life certificates from the Korean authorities.
The Korean authorities will send the life certificate form directly to the client when it is due.
The client should complete the life certificate and return it directly to Korea.
If a client needs the life certificate witnessed, it is important to check that:
- the life certificate is fully completed, signed and dated
- the client's address has been verified and
- the certificate has been stamped with the office date stamp in the presence of the client
The life certificate is returned to the client for them to send directly to the Korean authorities.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Methods of payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Methods of payment
When a client gets New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Korea they can choose to have payments made to a New Zealand or overseas bank account.
Note all payments will be made directly to the client's bank account and not to the Korean authority. The agreement with Korea does not include recovery of debt from the initial arrears, or any other debt recovery.
## New Zealand bank account
Payments are made fortnightly to New Zealand bank accounts.
If a client chooses to have payments made to a New Zealand bank account before transferring the funds to an overseas bank account, the client must pay the cost of transferring funds.
## Overseas bank account
Payments to an overseas bank account are made every 4 weeks.
If a client chooses to have money paid directly to an overseas bank account, the Ministry of Social Development meets the cost of the initial transfer of funds.
There are 3 options for the first payment being made into an overseas bank account:
- payment can be made to an overseas bank account if the client has already provided verification of their bank account that meets core processing standards or
- payment(s) may be made to a New Zealand account until the overseas bank account details are supplied or
- payment is suspended until details of the overseas bank account are given to - International Services. Once account details are provided, any accumulated arrears will be paid to the overseas account with the first payment.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Move to another country — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Move to another country
When a client getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension moves to another country other than New Zealand or Korea for 26 weeks or more, this can affect their entitlement to New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
The client may still be entitled to their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension if:
- they are moving to a country with a reciprocal agreement with New Zealand and they qualify under that agreement or
- they are moving to the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau and they qualify under the Special Portability Provisions
Payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension should stop from the day after the client leaves Korea. The client needs to check if they can get New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in the country they have moved to.
## Residence
New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension cannot usually be paid to a client who leaves Korea to live in a country that does not have an agreement with New Zealand. This is because the client would need to be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand when they apply for payment overseas under either the General or Special Portability provisions. However, they may be able to be paid if they move to the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau where more flexible special portability provisions apply.
If the client is getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension by using their periods of contributions in Korea to meet the New Zealand residence qualification, they may not be entitled to have the New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid in another agreement country. Their entitlement will depend on the terms of the agreement between New Zealand and the new country the client has moved to.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits and pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits and pensions
New Zealand benefits included in the agreement with Korea are:
- New Zealand Superannuation and
- Veteran's Pension
The agreement does not include coverage for any other main benefits, funeral grants, or extra help assistance.
This means totalisation of periods of contributions in Korea cannot be used to meet residence qualifications for a New Zealand benefit eg Jobseeker Support.
Note New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension paid in Korea does not include payments for grandparented non-qualified partners.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation clients moving to or applying from Korea — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text: A client can be paid New Zealand Superannuation under the agreement while they are residing in Korea. Applications can be made from New Zealand or Korea. A client already receiving or entitled to payment of New Zealand Superannuation as a resident of New Zealand can apply for New Zealand Superannuation to be paid in Korea before they leave New Zealand. If they choose to apply from Korea their domestic New Zealand Superannuation payments should have stopped from the day after they left New Zealand. Payment cannot be backdated so clients should be encouraged to apply before they leave New Zealand. In all cases the client must: - be entitled to or be getting New Zealand Superannuation at the time they apply - be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand or Korea at the time they apply for payment - have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Korea for at least 26 weeks and - have had a continuous period of at least 12 months working age residence in New Zealand The client can use their periods of residence in Korea to meet the residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation (10 years residence and presence in New Zealand since age 20, with 5 years residence and presence since age 50).

chunks.title: Intending to reside in Korea — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text: If a client leaves New Zealand intending to reside in Korea for 26 weeks or more, they have up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Korea to be considered ordinarily resident in Korea on the date of departure from New Zealand. Clients may go to other countries before they get to Korea, but they must arrive in Korea within 26 weeks from the date they left New Zealand to be considered as ordinarily resident in Korea on the date they left New Zealand. Example A client may want to have a 3 month holiday in the United Kingdom before they start living in Korea. In this case the client would be considered ordinarily resident in Korea during those 3 months.

chunks.title: Payment to partner — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text: New Zealand Superannuation cannot be paid to include a grandparented non-qualified partner when they are living overseas.

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text: The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement and especially if they intend to leave Korea to live in another country. The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances. This must be completed and returned to New Zealand. If the client does not return the life certificate their New Zealand Superannuation payments will stop. For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation - Totalisation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation - Totalisation
When a client from Korea meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except residence, they may qualify for New Zealand Superannuation under the agreement with Korea.
The residence qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation in the agreement allows:
- periods of Korean contributions from the age of 20 can be used to meet the requirement for 10 years residence and presence in New Zealand from the age of 20
- periods of Korean contributions from the age of 50 can be used to meet the requirement for 5 years residence and presence in New Zealand from the age of 50
A client must also have not less than one year of continuous New Zealand working age residence, and be ordinarily resident and present in either New Zealand or Korea at the time they apply for a New Zealand benefit under the Agreement.
The client may also be entitled to a Korean old age benefit, which will be directly deducted from New Zealand Superannuation.
Note when New Zealand Superannuation is granted using this agreement you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 16 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
When a New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension being paid in Korea is overpaid you will need to advise the client:
- the reason for the overpayment
- the amount of the overpayment and
- their review and appeal rights
The overpayment can be recovered by regular deductions from the client's New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.
If the client is no longer getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, there is no provision in the agreement for the Korean authorities to recover the overpayment on New Zealand's behalf. There is also no provision in the agreement for New Zealand to recover Korean debts.
Contact clients directly to seek recovery of any overpayment.
## Review or appeal
If a client applies for a review or appeals a decision on the establishment of a debt or the rate of recovery, recovery action will be suspended until the outcome of that review or appeal is known.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Payment rate in Korea — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Payment rate in Korea
When New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension is paid to a client in Korea the rate of payment is calculated using the following formula:
- number of whole months of New Zealand Working age residence
multiply by
- maximum gross benefit
divide by
- 540 (months in 45 years)
## Minimum payment
The minimum payment that can be paid is:
- 12/540 of the maximum rate of payment
## Maximum payment
The maximum rate that can be paid is:
- 100% of the gross rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
Note 1 if the client has a third country pension it is not directly deducted from the rate of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension payable.
Note 2 clients with less than 12 months working age residence in New Zealand will not be eligible for payment in Korea.
## Extra help
Extra help such as Accommodation Supplement, Working for Families Tax Credits, Temporary Additional Support or Disability Allowance cannot be paid in the Republic of Korea and should be cancelled from the day after departure.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
If a client has possible entitlement to a Korean old age benefit or any other Korean benefit or pension but refuses to apply for it advise International Services. They will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services may suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client refuses to apply for a Korean benefit.
International Services will talk to clients about the reasons why they must apply. This discussion may include the following factors:
- clients must apply for any benefit they may qualify for in Korea if they are applying for a New Zealand benefit or pension
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to get from Korea. This is part of the cost-sharing arrangement for Social Welfare between Korea and New Zealand
- it is their obligation if they have applicable periods of contributions to the Korean Social Welfare scheme to apply for these payments
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension may stop, but payment of a Korean benefit will usually continue, so the client may be advantaged by their Korean benefit entitlement
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate the New Zealand payments will be suspended if the Korean benefit is more than the hospital rate. However, the Korean benefit will continue being paid to them in New Zealand, so they may be advantaged by their Korean benefit entitlement.

chunks.title: Return to New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Return to New Zealand
When a client is getting New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension paid in Korea and returns to New Zealand for a temporary period, their New Zealand payment will continue being paid at the same rate as when they were living in Korea.
This is because the client is not considered to be ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
## Client returns to New Zealand permanently
When a client getting payment of New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension in Korea, returns to live permanently in New Zealand, their pension can be reviewed from the date of return to New Zealand.
International Services must be advised as they are responsible for stopping payments made under the Social Security agreement.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Review date — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Review date
A New Zealand benefit or pension must be reviewed from the date a client is granted a Korean old age benefit or other benefit or pension and every time when the rate of payment changes.
If you have difficulty obtaining details of the overseas pension grant date, contact International Services for advice.
When a Korean old age benefit or other Korean benefit or pension is reduced, the New Zealand benefit or pension should be reviewed from the date of the reduction.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Reviews and appeals — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Reviews and appeals
If a client disagrees with any decision regarding their Korean old age benefit being paid in New Zealand they will need to write to the Korean authorities or to the MSD who can pass the notice of review to the Korean authority.
International Services is responsible for any reviews and appeals for:
- the effect of the Korean old age benefit and any other deductible Korean benefit or pension on New Zealand benefits and pensions and
- decisions made on New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension being paid in Korea
- other decisions made under the agreement with Korea affecting a client's New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: SWIFTT process — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text: When a client is getting a Korean old age benefit or other deductible benefit or pension that is directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit or pension it is important this is processed correctly in SWIFTT. The following information is required to add a Korean benefit or pension to the SOPDA screen in SWIFTT: letter indicator (defaults to x) - the rate of the Korean old age benefit or other benefit or pension in Korean currency - the amount of bank fees allowed (contact International Services) - the frequency of the Korean payments - the percentage of any voluntary component included in the overseas pension - any Korean Social Welfare Number (essential for information matching purposes) - country code 097 - whether the benefit or pension is a deductible pension Y/N Note some of the above fields are only used by International Services. The New Zealand dollar amount of the Korean old age benefit or other benefit or pension will be displayed on the SOPHI screen once the above details have been entered. The New Zealand dollar amount showing on the SOPHI screen will need to be added to the 'O/seas Pen direct ded' field using the INCMA screen in SWIFTT. When the Korean old age benefit or other benefit or pension details are correctly recorded SWIFTT will automatically calculate the amount of the deduction from the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension payable. Note if an overseas payment is not directly deductible it must be treated as income and taken into account in assessing any other income tested assistance being received. If you need further information you should contact International Services. Note International Services updates the exchange rate table in SWIFTT each month with adjusted exchange rates of applicable countries. Following these updates, for New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension, SWIFTT will: - recalculate the New Zealand benefit or pension rate each month and - send a letter to advise the client, if the client has only one overseas pension and is not in receipt of New Zealand Superannuation with a grandparented non-qualified spouse included, and the letter indicator in the SOPDA screen is set to Y (or X where the change in New Zealand Superannuation is of sufficient magnitude)Note if the indicator in the SWIFTT SOPDA is set to N no letter will be generated and only International Services can change the letter indicator after the initial grant of New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension

chunks.title: SWIFTT process — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text: For New Zealand benefits other than New Zealand Superannuation, a report is generated every month and International Services manually updates the overseas pension deductions of clients on this report as appropriate.

chunks.title: Korean pensioners in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Korean pensioners in New Zealand
The Korean age benefit is taxed in Korea before being paid to the client in New Zealand.
The amount to be deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension is the amount of Korean age benefit after it is reduced by the Korean tax levied on it. This only applies to the Korean age benefit. Any other deductible benefit payable from Korea reduces the New Zealand benefit or pension by the gross amount of the Korean benefit or pension.
The client should contact Inland Revenue to discuss their New Zealand tax liability for the Korean old age benefit.
## New Zealand pensions in Korea
New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension paid in Korea are not taxed in New Zealand but may be taxed under the tax laws of Korea.
A client must make their own arrangements with the Korean tax authority for payment of any tax.

chunks.title: Veteran's Pension clients moving to Korea — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Veteran's Pension clients moving to Korea
Under the agreement with Korea a client can be paid Veteran's Pension when they are living in Korea. Applications can be made from New Zealand or Korea.
A client already receiving/entitled to payment of Veteran's Pension as a resident of New Zealand can apply for Veteran's Pension to be paid in Korea before they leave New Zealand. If they choose to apply from Korea their domestic Veteran's Pension payments should have stopped from the day after they left New Zealand. Payment cannot be backdated so clients will be better off if they apply before they leave New Zealand.
In all cases the client must:
- be entitled to or getting Veteran's Pension at the time they apply
- be aged 65 or older
- be ordinarily resident and present in New Zealand or in Korea at the time they apply for payment from overseas
- have the intention of remaining ordinarily resident in Korea for at least 26 weeks and
- have a continuous period of at least 12 months working age residence in New Zealand
The client can use their periods of contributions in Korea to meet the residence qualification for Veteran's Pension.
## Intending to reside in Korea
If a client leaves New Zealand with the intention of residing in Korea for 26 weeks or more, they are allowed a period of up to 26 weeks to take up residence in Korea.
Example
A client may want to have a 3-month holiday in the United Kingdom before they start living in Korea.
In this case, the client is considered ordinarily resident in Korea during those 3 months.
## Payment to partner
If the client has a partner, each partner must complete an application form and establish entitlement. If one partner is not eligible we cannot pay Veterans Pension for a non-qualified partner overseas.
## Change in circumstances
The client must let us know immediately if there are any changes in their circumstances and especially if they intend to leave Korea to live in another country.
The client will be sent a life certificate every 26 weeks or 52 weeks depending on their circumstances. This must be completed and returned to New Zealand. If they do not return the life certificate their Veteran's Pension will stop.
For more information contact International services

chunks.title: Veterans Pension - Totalisation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Veterans Pension - Totalisation
When a client from Korea meets all the qualifications for the New Zealand Veteran's Pension except residence, they may qualify under the agreement with Korea.
The agreement allows:
- periods of Korean contributions from the age of 20 can be used to meet the requirement for 10 years residence and presence in New Zealand from the age of 20
- periods of Korean contributions from the age of 50 can be used to meet the requirement for 5 years residence and presence in New Zealand from the age of 50
A Veteran's Pension client must be the New Zealand Superannuation qualifying age of 65 years.
Note when Veteran's Pension is granted using the agreement with Korea you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 16 in the entitlement code field.
For more information contact International Services

chunks.title: Working age residence — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal republic of korea
chunks.text:
## Working age residence
Under the agreement with Korea, New Zealand working age residence means a period when the client was resident in New Zealand between the ages of 20 and 65 years.
New Zealand working age residence also includes a period when a client:
- was employed outside of New Zealand and their employer deducted and paid income tax on their earnings to Inland Revenue in New Zealand or
- was with their partner who was employed outside of New Zealand, and was paying New Zealand income tax on those earnings

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
When a client intends to travel overseas, the expected period of absence and the country they are travelling to, can affect:
- entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension the client is receiving
- entitlement to a benefit or pension in the country the client intends to visit and
- any United Kingdom benefit or pension they may be receiving
For more information see:
- Clients going to the United Kingdom
- Permanent absence
- Temporary absence
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Admission to hospital — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Admission to hospital
When a client has been in hospital for more than 13 weeks their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced.
The United Kingdom benefit or pension is still treated as a direct deduction from the hospital rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services get reports from SWIFTT of clients admitted to hospital and will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the United Kingdom benefit or pension is more than the hospital rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension.
Clients who have their United Kingdom benefit or pension paid through the Special Banking Option will have their United Kingdom benefit or pension released to them by International Services if their New Zealand benefit or pension is stopped.
When the client has a spouse or partner the rules are different.

chunks.title: Benefits and pensions in the United Kingdom — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Benefits and pensions in the United Kingdom
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom, residence in New Zealand can be regarded as periods during which contributions were made to the United Kingdom National Insurance scheme in order to meet the residence qualifications for a number of United Kingdom benefits and pensions.
Clients will need to contact the United Kingdom Authorities to confirm any entitlement they may have to a benefit or pension in the United Kingdom. The client will need to send full details of their circumstances including their full name, full address, date of birth, a list of all the countries they have lived in and, if possible, their National Insurance number.
For United Kingdom contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies United Kingdom
For an overview of the United Kingdom benefits and pensions that are included in the agreement see:
- Child Benefit
- Guardians Allowance
- Jobseekers Allowance
- Retirement Pension
- Widow's Pension and Widowed Mothers Allowance
For more information about United Kingdom benefits and pensions see:
- Working age benefits: GOV.UK benefits
- Age pensions: GOV.UK pension
Clients need to take evidence of their New Zealand residence, such as tax certificates, employer reference, travel documents or letters from 2 friends in New Zealand, with them to the United Kingdom. Applications can only be lodged when a client is in the United Kingdom.

chunks.title: Cancellations — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Cancellations
Follow normal cancellation procedures for the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled and the client was receiving a United Kingdom benefit or pension.
International Services will advise the client of any changes to the United Kingdom benefit or pension following cancellation of their New Zealand benefit or pension, such as changing the payment option for the United Kingdom benefit or pension if it is paid through the Special Banking Option.
For more information see the appropriate New Zealand benefit or pension:
- Jobseeker Support
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Orphans Benefit
- Sole Parent Support
- Supported Living Payment

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A client is obliged to advise the Ministry of Social Development of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to a New Zealand benefit or pension.
You may also review a benefit at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A client is also required to provide any information required by the United Kingdom Department for Work and Pensions to ensure that they are still entitled to their United Kingdom benefit or pension. Any such information can be forwarded to International Services to pass on to the United Kingdom authorities.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Absence from New Zealand
- Admission to Hospital
- Cancellations
- Death
- Last child turning 14
- Overpayments
- Reviews and Appeals
- Taxation
- United Kingdom requests for information

chunks.title: Child Benefit — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Child Benefit
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom periods of residence in New Zealand can be accepted as periods during which contributions were made to the United Kingdom National Insurance scheme.
The Child Benefit is similar to New Zealand family tax credit. It is paid to families with children under the age of 16 and can be continued until the child is 18, if the child is still at school.
## United Kingdom Social Security authorities
United Kingdom Social Security authorities decide entitlement to a United Kingdom pension.
If a client would like to know more about their entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension they will need to send full details of their circumstances including their full name, full address, date of birth, a list of all the countries they have lived in and, if possible, their National Insurance number.
For United Kingdom contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies United Kingdom
For more information you can contact International Services or see:
- Retirement Pension
- Widow's Pension and Widowed Mothers Allowance
- Guardians Allowance
- Jobseekers Allowance

chunks.title: Clients entitled to United Kingdom benefits or pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Clients entitled to United Kingdom benefits or pensions
A client must apply for any benefit or pension they may be entitled to from the United Kingdom if:
- they are in receipt of or applying for a New Zealand benefit or pension and
- they use the agreement to qualify for the New Zealand benefit or pension or
- they have made contributions to the United Kingdom scheme
You will need to contact International Services to have an application pack sent to the client.
There are different forms for the client to sign depending on the payment option they choose. The client will need to indicate their preferred method of payment, so that International Services can send the appropriate application pack to the client.
When the client completes the application it is important that you check the following details before forwarding it to International Services:
- all questions on the form have been answered
- all supporting documentation is attached (these should be sighted, photocopied, and authorised as true copies)
- the application form and both sides of the 'Authority to release information and adjust United Kingdom arrears' form are signed and dated and
- the bank authority form is completed by clients for the Direct Payment Method for the United Kingdom benefit or pension
If a client refuses to apply for any United Kingdom benefit or pension to which they may be entitled you should contact International Services.
For more information regarding United Kingdom benefits or pensions that can be paid in New Zealand contact International Services or see:
- Child Benefit
- Industrial Disablement Pension
- Retirement and Widows Pensions
- Service pensions
- War disablement pension
- War widows pension
- Widowed Mothers Allowance
- Refusal to apply

chunks.title: Clients going to the United Kingdom — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Clients going to the United Kingdom
Under the Agreement with the United Kingdom periods of residence in New Zealand can be treated as periods of contributions in the United Kingdom to qualify for some benefits and pensions when a client is in the United Kingdom.
When a client is intending to live in the United Kingdom for any period, either temporary or permanent, you should advise the client that they can apply for a United Kingdom benefit or pension in the United Kingdom.
If a client is considering moving to the United Kingdom you should advise them to write to the United Kingdom Department for Work and Pensions to check their entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension. The client will need to send full details of their circumstances including their full name, full address, date of birth, a list of all the countries they have lived in and, if possible, their National Insurance number. For United Kingdom contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies United Kingdom
## Note
If the client is already getting a United Kingdom benefit or pension in New Zealand they can apply for an increase while in the United Kingdom.
International Services receives a SWIFTT report of clients who are receiving a United Kingdom benefit or pension when their New Zealand benefit or pension is suspended or cancelled, and will follow up whether the United Kingdom pension is to be returned to the United Kingdom.
For more information see:
- Benefits and pensions in the United Kingdom
- Temporary absence
- Permanent absence
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Clients receiving United Kingdom benefits or pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Clients receiving United Kingdom benefits or pensions
When a client is receiving a benefit or pension from the United Kingdom you will need to find out the type of payment in order to determine the effect it will have on the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
It is important that the information is obtained promptly to enable the correct assessment of the New Zealand benefit or pension and to prevent or reduce any overpayment.
If the client is unable to provide full documentation of the payments they will need to complete an Information Release Authority form (WIF8).
The form must be sent to International Services to enable them to obtain and verify the following information:
- the rate of payment in United Kingdom currency and whether it includes any amount in respect of the clients spouse/partner and any dependent children
- the reason for the grant, such as age, widowhood, disablement, or war service
- the name of the organisation that is making the payment
- whether all or part of the payment is from voluntary contributions
A client is required to provide information regarding the rate of any overseas pension. If they do not comply their New Zealand benefit or pension can be refused or payment can be suspended.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- United Kingdom Child Benefit
- Direct deductions
- Industrial Disablement Pension
- Retirement and Widows Pensions
- Service pensions
- War disablement pension
- War widows pension

chunks.title: Death — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Death
The cancellation of New Zealand benefits and pensions on death follows normal procedures.
International Services receives reports from SWIFTT when a New Zealand benefit or pension is cancelled and the client was getting a United Kingdom benefit or pension that has been recorded in SWIFTT.
The executor/administrator of the client's estate will need to contact the United Kingdom authorities directly if they require any details of the United Kingdom benefit or pension, such as last payments due.
If the client has been getting a United Kingdom benefit or pension you should advise the executor/administrator of the estate that they will need to supply the following information to the United Kingdom Department for Work and Pensions:
- the client's name
- date of death
- United Kingdom National Insurance Number and
- the name and address of the executor/administrator of the estate
The executor/administrator of the estate should be added to the client's record using the SBFTZ screen in SWIFTT so International Services can advise the United Kingdom authorities.
## Special Banking Option
If the United Kingdom benefit or pension has been paid through the Special Banking Option, International Services will close the special banking account and return any payments to the United Kingdom.
For more information see, Main benefits, Changes and reviews in:
- Jobseeker Support
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Orphans Benefit
- Sole Parent Support
- Supported Living Payment

chunks.title: Direct deductions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Direct deductions
When a client gets a benefit or pension through the United Kingdom Social Security scheme it will be directly deducted from their New Zealand benefit, unless they qualify for dual entitlement.
The rate of the New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced by the gross rate of the United Kingdom benefit or pension.
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom a client can elect to:
- have the United Kingdom benefit or pension paid to their own bank account and get a reduced rate of New Zealand benefit or pension or
- have the United Kingdom benefit or pension paid through the Special Banking Option and get the full rate of New Zealand benefit or pension

chunks.title: Direct payment option — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Direct payment option
When a client is receiving a United Kingdom benefit or pension they can choose to have the United Kingdom benefit or pension paid directly to their own bank account.
Under this method of payment:
- clients can choose to have their United Kingdom benefit or pension paid once every 4 or 13 weeks
- payment will be converted at the rate of exchange applicable on the day the bank credits their account
- the client receives the gross rate of the United Kingdom benefit or pension and is responsible for any tax liability on it
- the amount deducted from the New Zealand benefit or pension will be based on an average exchange rate for the United Kingdom benefit or pension
- if the client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension the rate will be automatically recalculated in SWIFTT each month using an average of the United Kingdom exchange rates for the previous month
- if the client is receiving any other New Zealand benefit or pension International Services will manually review the rate periodically or when the client requests it
- there is no due/paid assessment at the end of each year to take into account the exact exchange rate that the United Kingdom benefit or pension was paid to the client
- when the United Kingdom benefit or pension is payable at two pounds or less per week the client will be paid once a year in December unless they choose to have it paid at 4 or 13 weekly intervals
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Initial grant of United Kingdom benefit or pension

chunks.title: Dual entitlement — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Dual entitlement
A client can receive full payment of their New Zealand Superannuation as well as their United Kingdom benefit or pension when:
- they were usually resident in New Zealand on 1 January 1970(usually resident, in relation to New Zealand means permanent residence, and, in relation to the United Kingdom means ordinarily resident) and
- they paid contributions to the United Kingdom National Insurance scheme before that date while usually resident in New Zealand and
- they have not had to use the agreement to qualify for New Zealand Superannuation
## Deciding dual entitlement
International Services will decide if a person has dual entitlement by:
- obtaining the date the client last paid contributions to the United Kingdom National Insurance scheme from the United Kingdom authorities
- verifying the date the client first arrived in New Zealand and the date they became a permanent resident in New Zealand
When dual entitlement is established International Services will note the client's record to show that the United Kingdom benefit or pension is not deducted from their New Zealand Superannuation.
A register of clients who have dual entitlement is maintained by International Services.

chunks.title: Example 1 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Example 1
A widow with 2 dependent children under the age of 14 has just arrived in New Zealand from the United Kingdom. The children were born in the United Kingdom and the husband died there.
The children can be accepted as dependent children (where they meet the criteria for dependent child) for the New Zealand Sole Parent Support as a widow under the agreement with the United Kingdom as:
- children born in the United Kingdom can be accepted as having been born in New Zealand and
- the husband's death can be accepted as having occurred in New Zealand
## Example 2
A widow has 2 dependent children under the age of 14 who were born in the United Kingdom. The family came to New Zealand 2 years ago and were granted permanent residence at that time. The husband died in New Zealand.
The children can be accepted as dependent children (where they meet the criteria for dependent child) for the New Zealand Sole Parent Support as a widow under the agreement with the United Kingdom as:
- children born in the United Kingdom can be accepted as having been born in New Zealand

chunks.title: Guardians Allowance — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Guardians Allowance
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom periods of residence in New Zealand can be accepted as periods during which contributions were made to the United Kingdom National Insurance scheme.
If a client has been receiving a New Zealand Orphan's benefit they may qualify for a Guardians Allowance in the United Kingdom.
The client must be supporting and caring for a child whose parents have died.
## United Kingdom Social Security authorities
United Kingdom Social Security authorities decide entitlement to a United Kingdom pension.
If a client would like to know more about their entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension they will need to send full details of their circumstances including their full name, full address, date of birth, a list of all the countries they have lived in and, if possible, their National Insurance number. For United Kingdom contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies United Kingdom
For more information you can contact International Services or see:
- Retirement Pension
- Widow's Pension and Widowed Mothers Allowance
- Child Benefit
- Jobseekers Allowance

chunks.title: Initial grant of United Kingdom benefit or pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Initial grant of United Kingdom benefit or pension
When a client has signed an authority for the release of information and adjustment of United Kingdom pension arrears form (BRI/WFI8) the United Kingdom authorities will:
- provide details of any grant of a United Kingdom benefit or pension to International Services and
- pay the United Kingdom benefit or pension arrears to the Ministry of Social Development direct to Finance or through the Special Banking Option account
This will enable International Services to:
- add the United Kingdom benefit or pension details to SWIFTT
- add the United Kingdom benefit or pension as a direct deduction from the New Zealand benefit or pension using the INCMA screen in SWIFTT
- review the New Zealand benefit or pension from the date of grant of the United Kingdom benefit or pension and
- recover any overpayment of New Zealand benefit or pension paid for the same period as the United Kingdom benefit or pension or
- pay the United Kingdom benefit or pension arrears to the client
## Information release
If the client has not signed an Information Release Form (WIF8) authority for the United Kingdom authorities to release information, the client must provide verification of the United Kingdom benefit or pension details or the New Zealand benefit or pension will be suspended.
For more information regarding this process you can contact International Services

chunks.title: Introduction — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Introduction
The social security agreement between the governments of New Zealand and the United Kingdom allows former residents of one country access to certain benefits and pensions under the other country's social security system.
The terms of the Agreement do not provide for New Zealand benefits to be paid to people residing in the United Kingdom.
Under the agreement:
- residence, birth or death in the United Kingdom can be regarded as residence, birth or death in New Zealand in order to meet the qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- payment of contributions to the United Kingdom scheme while residing outside of the United Kingdom can also be accepted as residence in New Zealand to meet the residence qualifications for some New Zealand benefits and pensions
- residence in New Zealand can be regarded as periods of contribution to the National Insurance scheme in the United Kingdom to qualify for some United Kingdom benefits and pensions
- birth or death in New Zealand can be regarded as birth or death in the United Kingdom
- some United Kingdom benefits or pensions can be paid to clients from New Zealand who are temporarily in the United Kingdom
- some United Kingdom benefits or pensions are payable anywhere in the world and are paid regardless of whether the client is living in a country which has an agreement with the United Kingdom
- War pensions from either country are not included in the agreement
For more information see:
- New Zealand Benefits
- Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with United Kingdom
- United Kingdom Benefits and Pensions in New Zealand
- Changes and reviews
- Benefits and pensions in the United Kingdom
- Direct Deductions

chunks.title: Jobseeker Support — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Jobseeker Support
When a client meets all of the qualifications for Jobseeker Support except for the period of residence they may qualify under the agreement with the United Kingdom.
The agreement with the United Kingdom allows periods of residence in the United Kingdom to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Jobseeker Support.
## Example
A client who has permanent residence in New Zealand but has only lived here for four months, and was previously residing or making insurance contributions in the United Kingdom for twenty months, will meet the 2 years residence requirement for Jobseeker Support.
## Overseas residence details form
The client must complete an 'Overseas Residence Details' form (WIF7W) and this should be sent to International Services to follow up whether the client may be entitled to a United Kingdom benefit or pension.
## SWIFTT
When Jobseeker Support is granted using residence in the United Kingdom you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 02 in the entitlement code field.
For more information see:
- Jobseeker Support Residence
- United Kingdom Benefits and Pensions in New Zealand

chunks.title: Jobseekers Allowance — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Jobseekers Allowance
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom periods of residence in New Zealand can be accepted as periods during which contributions were made to the United Kingdom National Insurance scheme.
The United Kingdom Jobseekers Allowance is payable for up to 182 days to clients who are unemployed and looking for work.
It is available to clients visiting the United Kingdom, as permanent residence is not needed.
## Entitlement to UK benefits and pensions
United Kingdom Social Security authorities decide entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension.
If a client would like to know more about their entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension they will need to send full details of their circumstances including their full name, full address, date of birth, a list of all the countries they have lived in and, if possible, their National Insurance number. For United Kingdom contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies United Kingdom
For more information you can contact International Services or see:
- Retirement Pension
- Widow's Pension and Widowed Mothers Allowance
- Guardians Allowance
- Child Benefit

chunks.title: Last child turning 14 — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Last child turning 14
Clients receiving Sole Parent Support as a widow will cease to be eligible for payments once their last dependent child turns 14 and will automatically be transferred to Jobseeker Support.
In some instances where there is some evidence the client will not be eligible for Jobseeker Support when their last child turns 14, the client may be invited to apply for Jobseeker Support to assess their entitlement.
For more information see:
- Sole Parent Support Qualifications

chunks.title: New Zealand benefits — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## New Zealand benefits
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom, residence and or periods of insurance contributions in the United Kingdom can be regarded as residence in New Zealand to meet the residence qualifications for New Zealand benefits covered by the Agreement.
The following benefits are included in the Agreement:
- Jobseeker Support
- New Zealand Superannuation
- Sole Parent Support for widows
- Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind)
Note that the agreement does not cover the following:
- Emergency Benefits
- Sole Parent Support (for sole parents who have lost the support of a partner, and widowers)
- Supported Living Payment for caring for the sick or infirm
- Unsupported Child's Benefit
- Veteran's Pension
- War Pensions
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## New Zealand Superannuation
When a client meets all the qualifications for New Zealand Superannuation except for the period of residence they may qualify under the agreement with the United Kingdom.
The agreement with the United Kingdom allows periods of residence in the United Kingdom to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for New Zealand Superannuation.
To be able to use their period of residence in the United Kingdom as residence for New Zealand Superannuation a client:
- must meet the New Zealand age of entitlement for New Zealand Superannuation
- must apply for any United Kingdom benefit or pension to which they may be entitled
- usually must have their United Kingdom benefit or pension directly deducted from their New Zealand Superannuation
## Dual entitlement
There are some instances when a client may have entitlement to both the full New Zealand Superannuation and their United Kingdom benefit or pension, see: Dual entitlement
When New Zealand Superannuation is granted using residence in the United Kingdom you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the NDTA screen in SWIFTT and entering 02 in the entitlement code field.
For more information see:
- New Zealand Superannuation Residency
- United Kingdom Benefits and Pensions in New Zealand

chunks.title: Overpayments — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Overpayments
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom a debt can be recovered when there are arrears of benefit or pension owing for the same period.
## Clients in the United Kingdom
Generally International Services does not ask the United Kingdom authorities to recover New Zealand debts. This is due to the difficulty in obtaining the client's authority and contacting the United Kingdom authorities before the arrears of the United Kingdom benefit or pension are paid to the client.
You should follow normal procedures to recover any overpayment from the client.
If this is unsuccessful, and you have an overseas address for the client, contact International Services for advice as to whether the debt may be recovered by the United Kingdom authorities.
## Clients in New Zealand
When a client has an overpayment of their New Zealand benefit or pension you will need to follow the normal debt recovery procedure.
If the client has an overpayment of their United Kingdom benefit or pension International Services may be able to recover the debt from any arrears of the United Kingdom benefit or pension that are held for the client.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Current client debt Negotiating repayment of debt

chunks.title: Payment options — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Payment options
When a client is receiving a benefit or pension through the United Kingdom Social Security scheme, they can choose to have their United Kingdom pension paid by the:
- Direct payment option or
- Special Banking Option
Clients will be asked to select a payment option when they are sent a United Kingdom pension application pack by International Services
Clients can change from one payment option to the other at any time but can usually only join the Special Banking Option once.
All payment option changes are completed by International Services.
A client can authorise the United Kingdom authorities to pay arrears of their United Kingdom pension direct to the Ministry of Social Development regardless of the payment option they choose for regular payments.
For more information contact International Services.

chunks.title: Permanent absence from New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Permanent absence from New Zealand
When a client leaves New Zealand for permanent residence in the United Kingdom you will need to cancel the New Zealand benefit or pension from the day after they leave New Zealand. Under the Agreement New Zealand benefits or pensions are not paid to persons going to or residing in the United Kingdom.
You will need to record the date of departure from New Zealand in CMS and give the client a letter to present to the authorities when they make application for a benefit or pension in the United Kingdom.
The letter should contain the following information:
- date of departure from New Zealand
- date of last payment
- the type of New Zealand benefit or pension the client was receiving
- whether entitlement to the New Zealand benefit or pension was under New Zealand legislation or an agreement
Note that if the client was receiving Orphan's benefit you will need to include:
- the name(s) and date(s) of birth of the child(ren)
- names of and dates of death of parents
- period of confirmed New Zealand residence of the last surviving parent and
- name and address of proposed guardian in the United Kingdom
International Services receives a SWIFTT report of clients who are receiving a United Kingdom benefit or pension when their New Zealand benefit or pension is suspended or cancelled, and will advise the United Kingdom Authorities of the client's departure from New Zealand.
The client will need to contact the United Kingdom authorities to arrange to have their United Kingdom benefit or pension paid directly to them.
For more information see:
- Benefits and pensions in the United Kingdom
- Temporary absence
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit

chunks.title: Refusal to apply — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Refusal to apply
Advise International Services if a client refuses to apply for a United Kingdom pension. International Services will contact the client to explain the reasons why they must apply.
International Services will suspend the New Zealand benefit or pension if the client does not respond to requests to apply for a United Kingdom benefit or pension.
The reasons why a client must apply for a United Kingdom benefit or pension are:
- it is their right as they or their husband have made contributions
- clients must claim any benefit or pension they may be entitled to in the United Kingdom if they are entitled to a New Zealand benefit or pension or their New Zealand benefit of pension can be refused or stopped
- a New Zealand benefit is reduced by the amount a client is entitled to receive from the United Kingdom
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 26 weeks their New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension may stop, but payment of a United Kingdom benefit or pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 4 weeks their Sole Parent Support for widows may stop but payment of a United Kingdom benefit or pension may continue
- if a client leaves New Zealand for more than 6 weeks their Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) may stop but payment of a United Kingdom benefit or pension may continue
- if a client is single and their New Zealand benefit or pension is reduced to the hospital rate and the rate of United Kingdom benefit or pension is more than the hospital rate, the New Zealand benefit/pension will be suspended but the United Kingdom pension may still be paid
Note criteria for the United Kingdom pensions are determined by the United Kingdom, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.

chunks.title: Retirement and Widows Pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text: The United Kingdom social security scheme is contribution based and some pensions are payable anywhere in the world. A client's contribution record determines their entitlement and not their residence in the United Kingdom. Clients may be entitled to a United Kingdom Retirement or Widows pension through their own contributions or a woman or widow can be entitled through her husband's contributions. The United Kingdom Retirement pension and the Widows pension are directly deducted from any New Zealand benefit or pension. The age of entitlement for a United Kingdom Retirement pension depends on the person’s date of birth, and whether they are a man or woman, if born on or before 6 December 1953. To check age eligibility to the United Kingdom State Pension see: Check your State Pension age Note criteria for the United Kingdom pensions are determined by the United Kingdom, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.

chunks.title: Extra help — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text: When the United Kingdom benefit or pension is directly deducted from the main benefit, it does not affect any Extra help that the client may be receiving.

chunks.title: Living in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text: When a United Kingdom benefit or pension is granted to a person who is living in New Zealand the rate of the United Kingdom benefit or pension is frozen and no increases are made. For more information contact International Services or see: - Direct deductions - Clients receiving United Kingdom benefits or pensions - Clients entitled to United Kingdom benefits or pensions

chunks.title: Retirement Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Retirement Pension
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom periods of residence in New Zealand can be accepted as periods during which contributions were made to the United Kingdom National Insurance scheme.
The United Kingdom Retirement pension can be paid to clients from New Zealand who are living in the United Kingdom and have reached the qualifying age.
It is available to clients visiting the United Kingdom, as permanent residence is not needed.
## Entitlement to a United Kingdom pension
