United Kingdom Social Security authorities decide entitlement to a United Kingdom pension.
If a client would like to know more about their entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension they will need to send full details of their circumstances including their full name, full address, date of birth, a list of all the countries they have lived in and, if possible, their National Insurance number. For United Kingdom contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies United Kingdom
To check age eligibility to the United Kingdom State Pension see: Check your State Pension age
For more information you can contact International Services or see:
- Widow's Pension and Widowed Mothers Allowance
- Guardians Allowance
- Child Benefit
- Jobseekers Allowance

chunks.title: Reviews and Appeals — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Reviews and Appeals
If a client is unhappy with any decision regarding their United Kingdom benefit or pension being paid in New Zealand they will need to write to the United Kingdom authorities.
They should include their full name, full address, date of birth, a list of all the countries they have lived in and, if possible their National Insurance number. For United Kingdom contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies United Kingdom
International Services are responsible for any reviews and appeals in regard to the interpretation of the agreement with the United Kingdom and the effect of United Kingdom benefits or pensions on New Zealand benefits and pensions.
The New Zealand review and appeal process applies to any other decisions regarding New Zealand benefits or pensions, such as charging income or change in relationship status.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Core policy Reviews and Appeals

chunks.title: Service pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Service pensions
There are numerous service pensions payable to former United Kingdom residents living in New Zealand. These can be War Service Pensions or private superannuation payments due to the client's voluntary contributions.
If the client receives a War Service pension this will be directly deducted from any New Zealand benefit or pension.
If the client receives a private superannuation this will be chargeable income for any income tested New Zealand benefit or pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Charging income Superannuation scheme accounts
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: Sole Parent Support for widows — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Sole Parent Support for widows
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom a client may qualify for Sole Parent Support for widows if they meet all the qualifications except for:
- the client's dependent child or children were born overseas
The agreement with the United Kingdom allows:
- periods of residence in the United Kingdom to be regarded as residence in New Zealand to meet the period of residence qualification for Sole Parent Support as a widow
- any period that the client's husband was resident in the United Kingdom to be included as residence for the widow
- children born in the United Kingdom can be accepted as having been born in New Zealand
- a husband who died in the United Kingdom to be regarded as having died in New Zealand
The Agreement does not enable a widower to use residence in the United Kingdom to qualify for Sole Parent Support as a widower in New Zealand.
## UK benefits or pension
- the client must test their entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension and
- any United Kingdom benefit or pension will be directly deducted from the New Zealand Sole Parent Support
When Sole Parent Support as a widow is granted using residence in the United Kingdom you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 02 in the entitlement code field.
Note criteria for the United Kingdom pensions are determined by the United Kingdom, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.

chunks.title: Special Banking Option — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option
When a client is getting a United Kingdom benefit or pension they can choose to have it paid into a Special Banking Option account by the United Kingdom authorities. The client will then receive the full rate of their New Zealand benefit or pension.
The advantages of this option are:
- the client receives a regular payment
- tax is already deducted
- the client is not affected by fluctuations in the exchange rate
Clients may choose to join the Special Banking Option at any time but cannot re-join once they have chosen to cancel the option, there are exceptions, contact International Services.
The Special Banking Option is not suitable for clients whose United Kingdom benefit or pension is higher than (or likely to be higher than) the rate of New Zealand benefit or pension.
## Partners must choose same option
When a client has a partner they must both choose the same payment option.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Special Banking Option applications
- Initial grant of United Kingdom benefit or pension

chunks.title: Special Banking Option applications — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Special Banking Option applications
When a client chooses the Special Banking Option for their United Kingdom pension they will be sent an application pack from International Services containing:
- an Application for the Special Banking Option
- an Application for a Special Bank Account and
- an Authority to Release Information form (this form allows us to share information regarding pension entitlements with the Department of Social Security in the United Kingdom)
All three forms must be fully completed and forwarded to International Services for processing.
## Note
- if the client has a partner who is also receiving a United Kingdom pension the client can only choose the Special Banking Option if the partner also chooses this option for payment of their United Kingdom pension
- the client can change from the direct payment method to the Special Banking Option at any time
- if the client has changed from the Special Banking Option to the direct payment option they cannot re-join the Special Banking Option
- the client does not have access to the Special Banking Option account that the United Kingdom pension is paid into as it is simply a holding account for funds that are to be paid to MSD

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Supported Living Payment
When a client meets all the qualifications for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) except for the period of residence they may qualify under the agreement with the United Kingdom.
The agreement with the United Kingdom allows periods of residence in the United Kingdom to be regarded as residence in New Zealand for a client to meet the period of residence qualification for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
## Example
A client who has permanent residence in New Zealand but has only lived here for six months, and was previously residing or making insurance contributions in the United Kingdom for 1 year and 6 months, will meet the 2 years residence requirement for Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) as long as they have not lived in another country in between moving.
## Medical assessment
The client must have a medical assessment and meet the medical qualifications for the New Zealand Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind).
Blindness or permanent incapacity originating in the United Kingdom is treated as if it occurred in New Zealand.
## SWIFTT
When Supported Living Payment (health condition, injury, disability or totally blind) is granted using residence in the United Kingdom you will need to add the reciprocal indicator by using the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT and entering 02 in the entitlement code field
For more information see:
- Supported Living Payment Medical qualifications
- Supported Living Payment Residence
- United Kingdom Benefits and Pensions in New Zealand

chunks.title: Taxation — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Taxation
When a United Kingdom benefit or pension is paid direct to the client it is paid at the gross rate with no tax deducted. It is the client's responsibility to pay any tax owed on their United Kingdom benefit or pension.
Generally a client will not have to pay tax on the United Kingdom benefit or pension when:
- they are getting a New Zealand benefit, other than New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans pension and
- the United Kingdom benefit or pension is directly deducted from the New Zealand benefit or
- the United Kingdom benefit or pension is being paid through the Special Banking Option
Inquiries about taxation of United Kingdom benefits or pensions should be referred to Inland Revenue.
Note clients can apply for a tailored tax code which, in most cases, can be used to pay the tax on both their New Zealand benefit and pension, and their United Kingdom benefit or pension.

chunks.title: Temporary absence — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Temporary absence
When a client is leaving New Zealand for a temporary absence in the United Kingdom you should advise the client that they can apply for a benefit or pension while they are in the United Kingdom.
If the client already receives a United Kingdom benefit or pension they can apply for an increase in this benefit or pension while they are in the United Kingdom.
The normal provisions for payment during periods of absence from New Zealand apply to the client's New Zealand benefit or pension.
When a United Kingdom benefit or pension is normally paid through the Special Banking Option the United Kingdom authorities may pay the benefit or pension directly to the client while they are in the United Kingdom.
## Overpayments
The client should be advised that if a United Kingdom benefit or pension is paid to their own bank account for any period that the New Zealand benefit is continued under the 4 or 26 week absence provisions an overpayment of the New Zealand benefit or pension will occur.
A client will be overpaid if they receive the full rate of their New Zealand benefit or pension for the same period that the United Kingdom benefit or pension is paid to their own account.
On return to New Zealand the client must provide details of any United Kingdom benefit or pension they received while they were in the United Kingdom and this information should be sent to International Services.
For more information see:
- Permanent absence
- Absence from New Zealand in relevant Main benefit
- Benefits and pensions in the United Kingdom

chunks.title: United Kingdom Benefits and Pensions in New Zealand — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## United Kingdom Benefits and Pensions in New Zealand
The United Kingdom scheme is based on contributions and not on residence and some United Kingdom benefits or pensions are payable anywhere in the world.
When a former resident of the United Kingdom applies for a New Zealand benefit or pension it is important to know whether they are receiving a United Kingdom benefit or pension, or if they may be entitled to receive one.
A client who has previously resided in the United Kingdom must complete an Overseas Residence Details form (WIF7W) when they apply for any New Zealand benefit or pension.
The form should be sent to International Services to follow up whether the client is entitled to a United Kingdom benefit or pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Clients receiving United Kingdom benefits or pensions
- Clients entitled to United Kingdom benefits or pensions

chunks.title: United Kingdom Child Benefit — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## United Kingdom Child Benefit
When a client from the United Kingdom intends to live in New Zealand for less than three years the United Kingdom Child Benefit can be paid for the first 26 weeks following their departure from the United Kingdom.
The Child Benefit will stop at the end of 26 weeks.
The Child Benefit will be directly deducted from any New Zealand Orphans Benefit payable in respect of the child.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: United Kingdom Industrial Disablement Pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## United Kingdom Industrial Disablement Pension
The United Kingdom Industrial Disablement Pension is regarded in the same way as accident insurance compensation payments under New Zealand legislation.
When calculating the rate of payment of a New Zealand benefit or pension, the Industrial Disablement Pension will be:
- disregarded when a client is receiving New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension in their own right
- chargeable income if the client is receiving income tested New Zealand Superannuation, Veterans Pension, or Extra help as a non-beneficiary
- directly deducted from any other benefit the client is receiving
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Types of income Accident compensation charging income
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: United Kingdom requests for information — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## United Kingdom requests for information
When a client makes application for a United Kingdom benefit or pension the United Kingdom authorities may send a request form to International Services for information such as:
- details of employment in New Zealand and periods on New Zealand benefits
- whether the client received a New Zealand benefit or pension using the agreement with the United Kingdom
International Services will get the relevant information and return the form to the United Kingdom authorities.

chunks.title: War disablement pensions — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## War disablement pensions
United Kingdom war disablement pensions include small elements paid concurrently for the wife and child(ren) of the pensioner.
There is also provision for concurrent payment of an unemployment supplement and other allowances such as:
- invalidity
- treatment
- attendants
- clothing
- comforts
- lower standard of occupation
- education and
- age
The War Disablement Pension, plus any additional allowances are disregarded in the assessment of a New Zealand benefit or pension.
Note criteria for the United Kingdom pensions are determined by the United Kingdom, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
## Invalidity Allowance and Unemployability Supplement
When a client is receiving an Invalidity Allowance and Unemployability Supplement these will be directly deducted from any New Zealand benefit or pension.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions

chunks.title: War widows pension — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## War widows pension
In addition to a basic War Widows Pension, United Kingdom war widows may receive:
- additional pension for a dependent child(ren)
- rent allowance
- war widows age allowance or
- elderly widows allowance
Disregard the War Widows Pension and any child element when assessing for a New Zealand benefit.
Note criteria for the United Kingdom pensions are determined by the United Kingdom, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.

chunks.title: Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with the United Kingdom — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Welfare Reform impacts on the Social Security Agreement with the United Kingdom
From 15 July 2013 new welfare reform provisions provided for consolidation of benefit categories with new benefit name changes and an increased focus on work expectations for some categories. These changes had some impacts on the Agreement with the United Kingdom.
## New Benefit categories
Jobseeker Support replaced:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent (and widowers with dependent children aged 14 years or older)
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Women alone
- Sickness Benefit (including Sickness Benefit Hardship)
- Unemployment Benefit (including Unemployment Benefit Student Hardship and Unemployment Benefit Training)
- Widows Benefit (for clients with dependent children aged 14 years or older, or have no children)
Sole Parent Support replaced:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Sole parent (and widowers with dependent children aged under 14 years)
- Widows Benefit (for clients with dependent children aged under 14 years)
Supported Living Payment replaced:
- Domestic Purposes Benefit - Care of sick or infirm
- Invalids Benefit
The following benefits have not changed:
- Emergency Benefit for clients in hardship (including Emergency Maintenance Allowance)
- New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
- Unsupported Child's Benefit and Orphan's Benefit
- Young Parent Payment
- Youth Payment
For entitlements arising from an Agreement occurring on or after 15 July 2013 references in the Agreement with the United Kingdom to the former benefits names must be considered as references to the new names. The name changes do not affect New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Widow's Pension and Widowed Mothers Allowance — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Widow's Pension and Widowed Mothers Allowance
Under the agreement with the United Kingdom periods of residence in New Zealand can be accepted as periods during which contributions were made to the United Kingdom National Insurance scheme.
The United Kingdom Widow's pension or the Widowed Mothers Allowance can be paid to clients from New Zealand who are living in the United Kingdom and were receiving the New Zealand Widow's benefit when last in New Zealand.
It is available to clients visiting the United Kingdom, as permanent residence is not needed.
## United Kingdom Social Security authorities
United Kingdom Social Security authorities decide entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension.
If a client would like to know more about their entitlement to a United Kingdom benefit or pension they will need to send full details of their circumstances including their full name, full address, date of birth, a list of all the countries they have lived in and, if possible, their National Insurance number. For United Kingdom contact details see:
- Overseas pension agencies United Kingdom
For more information you can contact International Services or see:
- Retirement Pension
- Guardians Allowance
- Child Benefit
- Jobseekers Allowance

chunks.title: Widowed Mothers Allowance — reciprocal agreements > reciprocal united kingdom
chunks.text:
## Widowed Mothers Allowance
The Widowed Mother's Allowance can be paid in New Zealand when the client has dependent children.
The Allowance will be directly deducted from any New Zealand benefit or pension.
It does not affect any Extra help that the client may be receiving.
Note criteria for the United Kingdom pensions are determined by the United Kingdom, including any specific rules relating to sex or gender.
For more information contact International Services or see:
- Direct deductions
- Clients receiving United Kingdom benefits or pensions
- Clients entitled to United Kingdom benefits or pensions

chunks.title: Activity obligations failures — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Activity obligations failures
If a young person fails to comply with their activity obligations, an activity obligations failure needs to be considered.
The service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service:
- must be satisfied that the young person did not have a good and sufficient reason for their failure and
- if the young person did not have a good and sufficient reason, recommend an activity obligations failure be imposed
The Youth Service Support Unit (YSSU):
- makes the decision to apply a sanction, based on the recommendation of the service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service and
- initiates the activity obligations failure in the system
For more information see:
- Obligations
- Good and sufficient reason for failing activity obligations
If it is decided that the young person has failed their activity obligations, the YSSU will initiate an activity obligations failure. The young person will then be notified by text message or letter that
- an obligations failure has occurred and
- they have five working days to recomply otherwise a sanction will be imposed
All young people have a five working day notice period to dispute or recomply before the sanction is imposed. If a young person recomplies within the five working day notice period their benefit is not sanctioned but the activity obligations failure is recorded. For more information see:
- When the sanction is imposed
- Counting previous activity obligations failures
For more information, see:
- Disputes or reviews of an activity obligations failure
- Recompliance Grade 1 and 2
- Recompliance (13 week non-entitlement period)
- Effect of sanctions on assistance

chunks.title: Activity requirements — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Activity requirements
A young parent applying for Young Parent Payment must be undertaking or available for a full-time course of:
- secondary education
- tertiary education
- approved training
- approved work-based learning
Generally the activity will lead to a NCEA level 2 qualification or an equivalent or higher qualification.
## Exemptions
If a young parent would be available for these activities but qualifies for an exemption, the exemption can apply from the start of the Young Parent Payment.
Note a young parent does not have to be available for full-time education, training or work-based learning until their youngest child is 6 months old and there is a suitable place in a Teen Parent Unit. Where there is no suitable place in a Teen Parent Unit, this obligation applies from the earlier of the date a suitable place becomes available or the youngest child is 12 months old.
For more information see:
- In or available for secondary education
- In or available for tertiary education
- In or available for approved training
- In or available for work-based learning
- Working part-time
- Exemptions from activity obligations
- Obligations Youngest dependent child aged under 6 months
- Obligations NCEA level 2 or equivalent or higher qualification

chunks.title: Age — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Age
Young people applying for Young Parent Payment must be aged:
- 16 to 19 years old
## Young person turns 20 years old
When a young person turns 20 years old the Young Parent Payment should stop, however in some circumstances Young Parent Payment can continue to be paid after the young person has turned 20 years old.
For more information see:
- Young person turns 20 years old

chunks.title: Applying for hardship assistance with money on payment card — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Applying for hardship assistance with money on payment card
A young person applying for hardship assistance generally won't qualify if they can meet their need from their own resources. This includes any money still on their youth payment card when they are no longer required to have their money managed.
If the young person has money on their card that will fully or partially cover the cost of the goods or services they are applying for, they need to apply for their remaining money.
This money could help them to meet or partially meet their needs.
It may be appropriate to decline an application for hardship assistance if a person refuses to apply for funds available on their youth payment card that will enable them to meet or partially meet their own need.

chunks.title: Approved budgeting programme activity — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Approved budgeting programme activity
Young people receiving Young Parent Payment are required to participate in and complete an approved budgeting programme.
The budgeting programme aims to provide young people with skills to help them competently manage their finances. It is expected that budgeting courses delivered as part of the Youth Service will generally meet the Ministry's guideline for an approved budgeting programme.
Young people must be referred to a provider from the list of authorised course providers contracted by the Ministry of Social Development.
The providers of the budgeting programme will provide a programme that is in line with the Youth Services Guidelines for the content of the approved budgeting programme.
In areas where there are no contracted budgeting providers, the Youth Service provider is expected to deliver the budgeting programme to the young people in their service.
Young people receiving Young Parent Payment are not subject to hardship obligations if they are accessing Special Needs Grants or Advance Payment of Benefit.
## Recognition of prior learning
Prior learning can be recognised for clients who have previously completed budgeting programmes.
The client can be assessed as having met the requirement to participate in an approved budgeting programme if they have completed at least two unit standards in financial literacy.
Applicable unit standards
The following unit standards can be considered for prior learning:
Level
Unit standard
1
24709 - Produce a balanced budget to manage personal finances
28088 - Demonstrate understanding of credit and debt on personal finances
2
28094 - Produce a balanced household budget and adjust the budget to reflect changing financial circumstances
28096 - Demonstrate understanding of insurance products for personal financial capability
3
28099- Analyse credit options and select strategies to manage personal finances
28100 - Develop a plan to achieve a long-term personal financial goal(s)
This list is not exhaustive. Other unit standards in financial literacy can also be considered.
Providers can consult the NZQA website to confirm if a young person has completed an appropriate unit standard in Financial Capability
## Incentive payments
Young people receiving Young Parent Payment can earn incentive payments for education and budgeting obligations if they meet certain criteria.
- Earning incentive payments
- Obligations

chunks.title: Approved parenting programme — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Approved parenting programme
An approved parenting programme is generally a programme that:
- a young person has been referred to by a service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service or
- is provided by the service provider themselves or
- follows the guidelines for parenting programmes
## Recognition of prior learning
Prior learning can be recognised for clients who have previously completed parenting programmes.
The client can be assessed as having met the requirement to participate in an approved parenting programme if they have completed a parenting course.
When a young person has prior learning, the provider must assess the past parenting course using Youth Service parenting programme guidelines. The provider will determine if the client is required to complete a full course or refresher training.
Refresher training
The refresher training should focus on any components not covered by a parenting programme previously completed by the client.
The content of the refresher course covered must be in line with the Youth Service guidelines. However the course can be completed in a shorter timeframe (for example: half a day) and in a less intensive manner.

chunks.title: Approved training — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Approved training
In a situation where a young person cannot return to secondary education, the next appropriate activity to consider is approved training.
For youth activity obligations purposes approved training is defined as employment-related training.
Generally they should be working towards a NCEA level 2 qualification or an equivalent or higher qualification.
Approved training must:
- be reputable and likely to teach the young person skills that will help them find work
- have an emphasis on training rather than study
- offer full-time training (at least 30 hours per week) and
- offer NCEA or New Zealand Qualification Framework (NZQF) credits
When advising a young person of approved training you need to consider their future goals and aspirations. You should try and match types of training that would be suitable for the young person and their career path.
A young person in full-time approved training must:
- regularly attend the programme
- complete assignments and
- complete other course requirements
## Employment-related training
Employment-training includes (but is not limited to):
- Special regional training courses
- Workplace/industry training
- Youth Guarantee courses
## Extra Help for young people in approved training
The following assistance is available for Young people in approved training:
- Course Participation Assistance [no link find out why]
## Incentive payments
Young people receiving Young Parent Payment can earn incentive payments for education and budgeting obligations if they meet certain criteria.
For more information see:
- Definition of 'full-time'
- NCEA level 2 or equivalent or higher qualification
- Earning incentive payments
- Qualifications In or available for approved training
- Obligations
- Deciding education, training and work-based learning activities
- Youngest dependent child is aged under 12 months

chunks.title: Assessed as financially competent — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Assessed as financially competent
A young person is generally considered to be financially competent where they have:
- earned their budgeting incentive and
- shown consistent, sound financial judgement which may include: the young person is spending their in-hand allowance on items that are appropriate for their situationany hardship assistance is justifiedthe young person has lowered their coststhe young person has found a part-time job and is managing the money they receive from that in a way that is appropriate for their situation
- the young person is spending their in-hand allowance on items that are appropriate for their situation
- any hardship assistance is justified
- the young person has lowered their costs
- the young person has found a part-time job and is managing the money they receive from that in a way that is appropriate for their situation
For more information see:
- Earning the right to receive payment directly
- Continued compliance with their obligations

chunks.title: Assistance during a non-entitlement period — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Assistance during a non-entitlement period
Young people who have a non-entitlement period cannot get an Emergency Benefit, Temporary Additional Support or Accommodation Supplement during this period.
## Exception
If a young person was receiving Accommodation Supplement paid as a non-beneficiary they can continue to receive this during the non-entitlement period.
## Recompliance assistance
If a young person undertakes a recompliance activity their benefit payment will be resumed from the date they start the activity.
For more information see:
- Recompliance (Grade 1 and 2)
Provisional Benefit
During a 13 week non-entitlement period a young person may be able to receive a provisional Young Parent Payment while they undertake an approved activity.
For more information see:
- Recompliance (13 week non-entitlement period)
## Transfers and exemptions
In some instances it may be appropriate to consider an exemption from the activity obligations or transfer to another benefit.
For more information on transfers and exemptions see:
- Exemptions from activity obligations
- Main benefits Supported Living Payment - medical qualifications
Also see:
- Assistance for partners
- Unable to recomply due to meeting the criteria for an exemption
- Special Needs Grant Assistance during a non-entitlement period

chunks.title: Assistance during an initial stand-down and/or benefit application process — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Assistance during an initial stand-down and/or benefit application process
Young people who have an initial stand-down cannot get an Emergency Benefit, Temporary Additional Support or Accommodation Supplement during the stand-down.
## Exception
If a young person was receiving Accommodation Supplement paid as a non-beneficiary they can continue to receive this during the initial stand-down.
## Special Needs Grants
If a young person is suffering hardship they may be able to receive a Special Needs Grant.
For more information see:
- Special Needs Grants Assistance during an initial stand-down and/or benefit application process

chunks.title: Assistance for partners — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Assistance for partners
The partner of a young person who has a non-entitlement period of 13 weeks can receive Young Parent Payment in their own right, but must meet all of the qualifications (age, residence and activity).
To decide whether or not the young person is in a de facto relationship see:
- Core policy Relationship status for benefit
## Partner has income
If the partner qualifies for the Young Parent Payment and either partner has income, the income is charged against the benefit at the following rate:
- 50 cents is taken from the benefit for each $1.00 of the combined income of the young person and their partner over $284.70 (before tax) a week (as at 1 April 2026)

chunks.title: Average weekly income — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Average weekly income
Young people can choose an income assessment period of either 26 or 52 weeks to calculate their average weekly income for the initial stand-down. Therefore you will need to calculate the average weekly income for both 26 weeks and 52 weeks.Income (before tax) can include, but is not limited to:
- normal salary/wages
- bonus payments paid at the time of termination
- Child Support received
- earnings-related accident insurance payments
- gross income from investments
- holiday pay
- interest from savings or investments
- other benefit payments
- Paid Parental Leave payments
- pay in lieu of notice
- pay in lieu of accumulated leave
- payments dependent on the completion of a fixed term contract
- redundancy payments
- rent
- retirement payments
- Student Allowance and student Accommodation Benefit and
- any other income (for example family trust income)
To calculate the average weekly income over a 26 week period, divide by 26, the total amount of income received by the young person in the 26 week period immediately before their entitlement date. If this is the one week minimum, then the stand-down period is one week, otherwise calculate the average weekly income over a 52 week period.
To calculate the average weekly income over a 52 week period, divide by 52, the total amount of income received by the young person in the 52 week period immediately before their entitlement date.
You should use the calculation that gives the young person a lesser stand-down period.
Note any overseas earnings received by the young person before their entitlement date must be included in the calculation of the young person's average weekly income.
## Partners
When the young person has a partner who has been working or is still working, use the higher of their two incomes over the previous 26 or 52 weeks to calculate the stand-down.
Do not combine their incomes.
To decide whether or not the young person is in a de facto relationship see:
- Core policy Relationship status for benefit
However, if the other partner's wages or holiday pay continues beyond the commencement date, charge this income against the benefit in the usual way.

chunks.title: Bank account — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Bank account
Unless there are special circumstances, it is a condition of every benefit that the young person provides or opens a bank account or membership to a credit union to receive their benefit payment.
## Bank
An appropriate bank is:
- a private savings bank, a trustee savings bank, or The Co-operative Bank or
- a registered bank which on the 31st March 1987 was a trading bank or
- any other registered bank or a building society approved by the Minister after consultation with the Minister of Finance
For more information see:
- Processing standards Bank account [no link find out why]

chunks.title: Calculating the commencement date for couples — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Calculating the commencement date for couples
Young people who are married, in a civil union or de facto relationship must qualify for Young Parent Payment in their own right.
When working out the commencement date of the payment, you must calculate the entitlement date and initial stand-down for each person using their individual circumstances.
## Example
A young couple with one dependent child apply for Young Parent Payment. Jane is attending college full-time. James left school 6 months ago, he has been doing casual work for his uncle but this has finished.
You can waive the stand-down for Jane as she is still at school.
You impose a 1 week stand-down for James.
For more information see:
- Entitlement date
- Twenty-eight day rule
- Initial stand-down
- No stand-down applies

chunks.title: Step 1 — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Step 1
Find out the number of days represented by the payment received. If this is not clearly shown on the 'verification of payments received' provided by the young person, use either of the following formula.
Note extra payments paid to the young person for example holiday pay, should not be included in the gross salary figure used to calculate the daily rate of pay. However these payments will be included in the young persons' last 26 and 52 weeks gross earnings.
Formula 1
Determine gross salary over last 52 weeks of employment
Divide by 52 weeks = weekly rate of pay
Divide by 5 days = daily rate of pay
Confirm total amount of holiday pay etc
Divide this amount by daily rate of pay = number of days pay
Formula 2
Determine gross salary over last 4 weeks of employment
Divide by 20 (number of working days in 4 weeks) = daily rate of pay
Confirm total amount of holiday pay etc
Divide by daily rate of pay = number of days pay
Note only calculate the period covered by holiday pay using the applicants' last four weeks income if it does not disadvantage the young person. If the income earned in the last four weeks does not reflect what the young person normally earned, you may need to request extra weeks or calculate the daily rate of pay using the last 26 weeks gross salary.
## Step 2
Add the number of days pay to the last day the young person worked.
This is the date that employment ceased.
Remember do not count Saturdays and Sundays - use Monday to Friday weekdays only. For example, if a young person stopped work on a Friday, add the days from the following Monday.

chunks.title: Cannot expect financial support from parents — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Cannot expect financial support from parents
To receive a Young Parent Payment a single young person must meet all of the qualifications and have a parental support gap. A 16 or 17 year old is considered to have a parental support gap when:
- they are living independently and
- you are satisfied that they have a good and sufficient reason why they cannot reasonably expect to be financially dependent on their parents or any other person
You must send the young person to an Independent Assessment Provider for an assessment and recommendation before granting Young Parent Payment.
If you are granting a young person Young Parent Payment due to other 'good and sufficient' reasons, add the reason in the Young Parent Payment comments field in the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT.
## When is it reasonable to expect support?
Consider it reasonable to expect financial support from the parents when the parents are willing and able to support the young person.
Ask the young person's parents this information (willingness to support and income details). Note they are not expected to provide proof of their income.
If the young person's parents have been living apart for some time, it is reasonable to ask if both parents are willing and able to financially support the young person.
If the parents say they will support the young person, you should work through the details of when payments start and other arrangements for this to take place before declining the benefit.
For more information see:
- When financial support is not expected
- Independent
- Definition of 'parents'
- Unsupported Childs Benefit was paid
- Examples of good and sufficient reason
- Independent Assessment Provider

chunks.title: Capacity issues prevent a young person meeting their parenting obligations — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Capacity issues prevent a young person meeting their parenting obligations
A young person may be granted a parenting incentive without meeting the criteria if:
- there are capacity issues preventing a young person from: undertaking a parenting programmeenrolling their dependent child/ren with a primary health organisationkeeping their dependent child/ren aged five years or under up-to-date with their Wellchild checkshaving their children under five years attends an approved early childhood education programme or being placed in other suitable child care which the young person is in education, training, work-based learning or part-time work
- undertaking a parenting programme
- enrolling their dependent child/ren with a primary health organisation
- keeping their dependent child/ren aged five years or under up-to-date with their Wellchild checks
- having their children under five years attends an approved early childhood education programme or being placed in other suitable child care which the young person is in education, training, work-based learning or part-time work
and
- the young person has agreed with their service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service on steps they must take to fulfil these obligations (for example being on a waiting list) and
- the young person has taken the agreed steps to the satisfaction of their service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service

chunks.title: Caring for a child with special needs — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Caring for a child with special needs
A young person can be exempt from some or all of their activity obligations if they are the principal caregiver of a dependent child or the foster parent of a foster child with special needs whose welfare would be unduly harmed if the young person attended education, training or work-based learning and for whom alternative care arrangements are not available, or are unable to be made.
The child must have a:
- physical or intellectual disability
- health condition
- chronic or recurring illness
- learning or behavioural difficulty
- be unable to attend childcare, school or other alternative care on a regular basis or
- be a foster child, aged 1 year or older, who is adjusting to a placement with a new foster carer
This can be a full or partial exemption.
## Proof
The young person must provide written proof from a health professional or social worker stating:
- what the child's illness is and its likely duration or
- an assessment of the child's behavioural difficulty and
- the need for full-time care
- the risk to the child if the young person is required to meet their activity obligations and
- that the child is unable to attend childcare, school or another alternative care arrangement
Note you should also consider eligibility to Child Disability Allowance but receipt of Child Disability Allowance alone does not meet the criteria for this exemption.
## Duration
This exemption can be granted for up to 12 months.
This exemption should then be reviewed. At the review you should discuss the young person's circumstances and consider whether it is appropriate to extend the exemption for a further period. You can ask the young person to provide proof that their exemption should be extended.
## SWIFTT process
Use SWIFTT exemption reason 'Child has special needs'.
## Receiving an incentive payment
If the young person is receiving an incentive payment and then qualifies for an exemption you will need to decide if they can continue to receive it.
For more information see:
- Full or partial exemptions
- Child Disability Allowance
- Obligations Incentive payments can continue

chunks.title: Caring for foster child under 12 months old — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Caring for foster child under 12 months old
In some cases a young person may be caring for a foster child under the age of 12 months who is in Oranga Tamariki care. Foster children are not considered to be dependent children.
This is a partial exemption only. The young person can be exempt from meeting their obligation to be in full-time education, training and work-based learning.
The budgeting and parenting obligations, along with the obligation to meet with their service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service still apply.
## Age
This exemption is only available to 18 year olds. It is unlikely that anyone younger than 18 will be approved by Oranga Tamariki as a caregiver.
## Proof
The young person must provide:
- confirmation of the care arrangement - for example, a letter from Oranga Tamariki
- confirmation of the age of the child
## SWIFTT process
Use SWIFTT exemption reason "UCB/OB Foster Child under 12 months".
## Receiving an incentive payment
If the young person is receiving an incentive payment and then qualifies for an exemption you will need to decide if they can continue to receive it.
For more information see:
- Full or partial exemptions
- Obligations Incentive payments can continue

chunks.title: Caring full-time for a partner with a health condition, injury or disability — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Caring full-time for a partner with a health condition, injury or disability
A young person may be caring for a spouse or partner who has a health condition, injury, or disability and who needs to be cared for on a full-time basis.
This can be a full or partial exemption.
## Proof
The young person must provide proof from a health professional:
- that their spouse or partner needs the young person's full-time care
- that without that care their spouse or partner would need hospital care and
- the length of time their spouse or partner will need that care
## Receiving an incentive payment
If the young person is receiving an incentive payment and then qualifies for an exemption, you will need to decide if they can continue to receive it.
For more information see:
- Full or partial exemptions
- Obligations Incentive payments can continue

chunks.title: Cash assets — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Cash assets
Cash assets mean the assets of the young person and their partner (if any) that can be easily converted into cash.
## Cash assets include
- bills of exchange or promissory notes
- building society shares
- money in bank accounts, including fixed and term deposits with any bank, friendly society, credit union, or building society
- money invested with or lent to any bank or other financial institution
- mortgage investments and other long term loans
- shares, stocks, debentures, bonus bonds, and other bonds
- the net equity held in any property or land not used as the person's home and
- the young person's share in any partnership
## Cash assets do not include
- a caravan, boat or other vehicle with a net equity less than $2,000, or is used by the young person or a member of their family for day to day accommodation
- motor vehicle principally used by the young person for private use
- personal effects
- the home property and the land on which it is situated
- FamilyBoost Tax Credit payments for the first 12 months after payment is received
Note a bank overdraft facility is not considered a cash asset or resource available to a young person.
Generally, ex gratia payments and compensation payments made by the Crown are excluded for the first 12 months following the date the young person received the payment. For more information see:
- Income Ex gratia and Compensation payments
In exceptional circumstances you can disregard some of the young person's cash assets see:
- Hardship exceptional circumstances

chunks.title: Change in circumstances — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Change in circumstances
Young people must tell their service provider or Work and Income straight away of any changes in their circumstances or their family's situation that may affect their entitlement to Young Parent Payment. Young people are made aware of their obligations by:
- signing the Young Parent Payment application form or
- selecting that they agree to the obligations when they submit the online application form for a Young Parent Payment
Examples of changes and how to deal with these can be found in Changes and reviews

chunks.title: Change in personal resources — young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Change in personal resources
Immigration New Zealand requires applicants to sign a Declaration of Personal Resources when applying for permanent residence under the following categories:
- Skilled/Business Stream and
- Family Stream
Note people do not have to sign a declaration if they are granted permanent residence under the categories of International/Humanitarian Stream which includes the:
- Refugee Family Support Category
- Pacific Access Category
- Samoan Quota Scheme
- Victims of family violence or
- various other special policies for specific countries
By signing the Declaration of Personal Resources, the client declares they are able to support themselves and family (if any) for the first two years residence in New Zealand.
The requirement for an immigrant to maintain themselves for the first two years does not mean they cannot access benefit assistance as a non-beneficiary. However, the client may not have entitlement to non-beneficiary assistance due to those resources.
For the above categories a client's permanent residence has been assessed on the following resources:
- a definite offer of employment (supported in writing)
- financial support from family members in New Zealand (supported in writing) and/or
- personal cash assets
Young Parent Payment on grounds of hardship is income and asset tested. To assess a client's entitlement to Young Parent Payment on grounds of hardship confirmation of the client's income and assets declared on application for permanent residence is required from the Immigration New Zealand. Confirmation of the client's current income and assets is also required. If there is a change in financial circumstances further investigation will need to be done to establish the client's entitlement to benefit assistance.

chunks.title: Absence from New Zealand — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Absence from New Zealand
All clients getting Young Parent Payment must tell the Ministry of Social Development before they leave New Zealand.
If the client does not tell the Ministry before they go overseas, their benefit payments will stop from the day after they leave New Zealand.
If the client tells us they will be absent from New Zealand, and they have an approved travel reason, they may be able to keep getting payments for up to 28 days.
## Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service
The Ministry of Social Development has an Approved Information Sharing Agreement with New Zealand Customs Service that identifies clients who have left New Zealand.
Once identified, the client's eligibility to keep getting their benefit payments while they are absent from New Zealand is automatically determined by Ministry systems.
## Does not advise of departure
If the client did not tell the Ministry they were leaving New Zealand their benefit will be suspended immediately from the day after they left New Zealand.
The Integrity Intervention Centre will determine if there has been an overpayment, establish any debt and advise the client.
If the client challenges the information match refer them to the Integrity Intervention Centre.

chunks.title: Absences that do not prevent client from meeting obligations — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Absences that do not prevent client from meeting obligations
Generally, a client receiving Young Parent Payment who has youth activity obligations cannot be absent from New Zealand and continue to be paid a benefit unless:
- it is for one of (or a combination of) the permitted travel reasons or
- the travel will not prevent them from continuing to meet their youth activity obligations (eg because they are attending school and the travel is during the school holidays or they are attending a training course and the travel is during a term or semester break, and they do not need to be in New Zealand to meet any of their other obligations during the travel period)
Note the Youth Service Support Unit will determine whether the young person meets the criteria to continue to be paid their benefit while they are absent from New Zealand based on a recommendation from the young person's service provider.
## Can be paid a benefit for a maximum of 28 days for reason of 'meeting obligations'
Young people receiving Young Parent Payment can continue to be paid a benefit for a maximum of up to 28 days in any 52-week period while they are absent from New Zealand on the grounds that the travel will not prevent them from meeting their obligations.
Example, if a Young Parent Payment client has already received their payment for 2 weeks while they were overseas because their travel did not prevent them from meeting their obligations, they will only be able to continue to get their payment for this reason, for 2 additional weeks in the same 52-week period.

chunks.title: Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Absent from New Zealand more than 28 days in any 52 week period
Generally, a benefit cannot be paid for more than 28 days in any 52 week period. However there are limited circumstances where a benefit can be paid for more than 28 days in a 52 week period.
These circumstances are:
- travel is required for an approved reason and, either: it is the client's first absence within 52 weeks and the permitted reason the client needs to be absent from New Zealand necessitates a period longer than 28 days orthe client has had other prior approved absences within the 52 week period and they require further approved absences which will require them to be absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- it is the client's first absence within 52 weeks and the permitted reason the client needs to be absent from New Zealand necessitates a period longer than 28 days or
- the client has had other prior approved absences within the 52 week period and they require further approved absences which will require them to be absent from New Zealand for more than 28 days in any 52 week period
- the client is absent from New Zealand for an approved travel reason and their return is prevented by a new circumstance which will require them to be absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period or
- the client is travelling to receive support from a family member (including other person who is treated by the client as a member of the client's family) who is residing overseas

chunks.title: Action on return to New Zealand — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Action on return to New Zealand
You will need to look at the circumstances of the client's absence from and subsequent return to New Zealand to decide when to recommence their benefit and when to treat it as a new application.
You will need to consider the following:
- the client's intention at the time of their departure for example, did they cancel their benefit before leaving New Zealand because they did not intend to return
- did the client remain ordinarily resident during the period of absence?
- the length of time that they have been absent
- the reason for the absence
- have their circumstances changed significantly during their absence
- is the client eligible to have their benefit backdated to the day after their departure date or date of return?
For more information see:
- Backdating benefit to day after departure date

chunks.title: Amount of income exemption — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Amount of income exemption
When it is determined that a client is severely disabled consider if they should have all or part of their income from employment disregarded for benefit purposes.
The amount of the income exemption depends on the client's individual circumstances after considering the guidelines - exemption for severe disablement and should be:
- a reasonable amount as an incentive to recognise the personal effort that a severely disabled person has made to participate or continue in employment
- any additional costs that a severely disabled person has incurred to participate or continue in employment
- a reasonable amount to ensure that a severely disabled person is not disadvantaged by participating or continuing in employment
Note the client may be entitled to receive other types of assistance, for example Disability Allowance for transport costs to work or employment assistance.
Fully document the decision by recording the reasons and the amount of the exemption in the CMS note template, Income exemption.
Contact Helpline if help is needed with the assessment.

chunks.title: Approved travel reasons — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Approved travel reasons
A client receiving Young Parent Payment is generally not able to continue to receive their main benefit payments while they are absent from New Zealand unless they meet the criteria for approved travel.
Approved travel includes:
- travel for a permitted reason
- travel where the absence will not prevent the client from continuing to meet all of their youth activity obligations
Clients are not required to meet their youth activity obligations while absent from New Zealand for approved travel.
## Length of travel for an approved travel reason
Clients can travel for up to 28 days on Young Parent Payment for an approved travel reason. Discuss with the client the amount of time that they need to be absent from New Zealand as a result of the approved reason. The client should explain the length of their intended absence.
Consider:
- the length of time the event or reason for travel will take and
- flight availability and travel time
Remember to advise clients that generally they are only able to continue to be paid their benefit for up to 28 days in a 52 week period. This should be taken into account when deciding the approved travel period.
## Client travelling for multiple reasons
Some clients may travel overseas for an approved travel reason but elect to stay longer for another reason that is not an approved travel reason. In this case, the client can generally only receive their main benefit payments for the period of time that the approved travel reason applies to.

chunks.title: Backdating benefit to day after departure date — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Backdating benefit to day after departure date
A client who leaves New Zealand without advising Work and Income of their travel can only have their benefit backdated to the day after their departure date if they:
- have a humanitarian reason that justifies their reason for travel and their failure to tell Work and Income before they left and
- contacted Work and Income as soon as they reasonably could after they departed (taking into account the circumstances of the client) and
- meet the criteria to continue to be paid their benefit while overseas (either because they meet the criteria for approved travel or the requirement that travel be approved does not apply to them)

chunks.title: Birth of a child — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Birth of a child
When a client applies to have their newborn child included in their benefit, the following information is required:
- full birth certificate of the child, or confirmation from Internal Affairs that the childs’ birth was registered online and permission was given to share the birth registration with MSD
- written statement from the client requesting inclusion of the child
If a child's birth certificate is not available immediately, YSSU can include the child in the benefit (without delay) when the client can provide:
- Plunket records
- birth notices
- confirmation from the client's midwife or doctor of the date of birth of the new child or
- hospital papers
Note the service provider or the MSD's 'in house' service must follow-up to make sure the client produces a copy of the birth certificate.
All information should be scanned into the Activity Reporting Tool (ART).
## Extra help
If a child is born with a mental or physical disability, needs constant care and attention because of a disability, or is likely to require care for at least 12 months, the client should test their eligibility for Child Disability Allowance.
When a child has ongoing additional costs because of a disability they may be able to receive a Disability Allowance.
For more information see:
- Date of review (including backdating)
- Dependent child
- Effect on benefit
- Family tax credit
- Best Start tax credit
- Child support
- Verification from Internal Affairs

chunks.title: Calculating the benefit rate — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Calculating the benefit rate
SWIFTT will automatically calculate the rate of benefit payable when the client's income is added on the INCMA screen.
If income is declared late it may be appropriate to complete a back dated review SBDR. SWIFTT will prompt staff when a back dated review is required. Check SRAUI to determine the period the review is required for.
The Income Assessment tab in DREW can be used to estimate the benefit rate with income for the client.
Income must be rounded down to the nearest dollar.
For more information see:
- Example of income assessment
- Recording income
- Income for a past period

chunks.title: Calculating the period of absence — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Calculating the period of absence
The period of an absence from New Zealand for which payment of Young Parent Payment can continue (if approved) is up to 28 consecutive days, that is, Saturdays and Sundays are included.
In all cases, when assessing the period of absence, do not include:
- the date of departure from New Zealand and
- the date of return to New Zealand
If a client is absent for more than 28 days in a 52 week period the benefit should be suspended from the 29th day (unless they meet the criteria to pay for longer than 28 days).
Note if a client is leaving New Zealand permanently, the benefit must be cancelled from the day after departure.

chunks.title: Carer arrangements — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Carer arrangements
Where parents of a child live apart and the child comes into the care of the other parent it is important to establish that the arrangements made have been agreed to by both parents before the child is included in the other parents benefit.
In some cases the arrangement between both parents may not be of a legal arrangement but the child has been placed with the other parent by mutual agreement.
## Verification
Written proof must be obtained of the new care arrangement. Written proof could be (but is not limited to):
- statement from the other parent
- court order or
- documentation from Oranga Tamariki
For more information see:
- Child comes into care

chunks.title: Change in age — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Change in age
Generally when a young person turns 20 years old the Young Parent Payment should stop. However there are two situations where the payment can continue to be paid after they turn 20 years old. These are where a young person:
- must receive Young Parent Payment for a minimum of six months and cannot receive another main benefit (excluding Supported Living Payment - health condition, injury or disability) until after this period
- chooses to continue to receive Young Parent Payment if they remain in education, training, or work-based learning
## Expiry automatic
An expiry is automatically set on SWIFTT for the benefit to stop on the later of:
- the young person's 20th birthday
- the 31 December in the year in which the young person reaches the age of 20 (when the young person is attending school)
- the course end date or 31 December in the year the young person reaches the age of 20 (whichever is the earlier) - when the young person is in tertiary education, training or work-based learning or
- the date after the young person has turned 20 years they have spent a minimum of six months receiving Young Parent Payment
For more information see:
- Must receive payment for six months
- Chooses to remain on Young Parent Payment past 20 years of age

chunks.title: Change of activity — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Change of activity
If a Young Parent Payment client has changed their education, training or work-based learning activity it is important to update their record in both SWIFTT, and ART. The activity code in SDT1A must be updated with the new activity code to reflect the activity that the young person is undertaking:
- training
- enrolled secondary education
- enrolled in tertiary education
- work-based learning
When you change the activity code in the SDT1A screen in SWIFTT you must also complete a benefit reassessment using the SPBR screen with the reason for reassessment code 340.
Note that if you do not complete the reassessment using the reason code 340, the benefit will expire from the beginning of the next pay period.
If the client has stopped doing an activity then you need to consider whether a sanction should be imposed.
## Example
A client was granted Young Parent Payment because they were enrolled full time in a course of secondary education. They have since left school and are now participating in a training course.
You will need to complete the following actions in SWIFTT:
- change the activity code in the SDT1A screen from 3 to 2 and add the course end date and add details into the 'training course type' field
- complete a benefit reassessment in the SPBR screen using the reason for reassessment code 340

chunks.title: Change of address — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Change of address
When a client advises that they have changed their address it is important to check that the move does not affect their entitlement to Young Parent Payment.
You will need to check the reasons for the move and ensure that they are still meeting all the qualifications for Young Parent Payment, and their youth activity obligations.
## Young person returns to live with their parents
If a single young person has returned to live with their parents they will no longer be entitled to Young Parent Payment and it should be cancelled.
Exception
A single young person aged 16 or 17 years old can receive Young Parent Payment when they are living at home with, or being financially supported by their parents or guardians and their parents or guardians earn less than the Family Tax Credit income cut-out point.
Note the service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service will need to update the address in ART and YSSU will need to update the address in CMS.
If the client is getting extra help, this will also need to be reviewed by YSSU.

chunks.title: Changes and reviews — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Changes and reviews
A young person is obliged to advise their service provider or Work and Income of any changes in their circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Young Parent Payment.
A benefit may also be reviewed at any time to ensure that the client still meets the qualifications and is receiving the correct rate of payment.
A change in a client's circumstances may also mean that the client qualifies for another benefit.
## Youth Service Support Unit (YSSU) role
The Youth Service Support Unit (YSSU) is responsible for making decisions on behalf of Work and Income and for the general administration of the Young Parent Payment.
## Service provider or Work and Income "in-house" service role
The service provider or the Work and Income "in-house" service work closely with the YSSU and will make recommendations to assist the YSSU to make decisions by:
- keeping the young person's information up to date in the Activity Reporting Tool (ART)
- notifying YSSU immediately of any change in the young person's circumstances that may affect their entitlement to Young Parent Payment or any Extra Help

chunks.title: Child absent — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Child absent
A dependent child who travels overseas can continue to be included in a benefit as long as they continue to meet the definition of dependent child.
Examples of when a dependent child can be absent from New Zealand are:
- child is overseas on an American Field Scholarship or other student exchange programme
- child is overseas visiting a parent who does not act as caregiver
For more information about the effect of absence from New Zealand for a client getting Orphans Benefit or Unsupported Childs Benefit see:
- Orphans and Unsupported Childs Benefit Absence from New Zealand

chunks.title: Child changes — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Child changes
The number of dependent children in a Young Parent Payment client's care and any change to the circumstance of a child can affect:
- the rate of family tax credit payable
- payment of Best Start tax credit
- the rate of extra help payable
- the client's obligations and
- (in some situations) the client's eligibility to the benefit, for example, last child leaves care
## Including a child in Young Parent Payment
For a child to be included in a client's Young Parent Payment the child must be a dependent child and generally ordinarily resident in New Zealand.
For more information see:
- Dependent child
- Deciding ordinarily resident
Where the child is not the client's natural or adoptive child, the client (where they are aged 18 years or over) may be able to get Unsupported Childs Benefit (instead of having the child included in their Young Parent Payment). This will depend mainly on the care arrangements.
## Changes to a child's circumstances
Change to a dependent child's circumstances is generally going to affect the client's Young Parent Payment.

chunks.title: Child comes into care — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Child comes into care
When a client has made an application to have another child included in their benefit and that child was in the care of another person the following information is required:
- full birth certificate of the childSee: Verification from Internal Affairs
- written statement from the applicant stating they are the principal caregiver and requesting inclusion in the Young Parent Payment
- (where appropriate) letter from previous caregiver confirming that child has left their careNote where the client cannot get written confirmation from the previous caregiver, the new caring arrangement can be confirmed by a referee such as a teacher, Plunket nurse, minister or a Justice of the Peace.
Any benefit payments the previous caregiver was getting for the child must stop.
## Date of review
Include the child in the benefit from:
- the date the child came into the client's care or
- the date the Young Parent Payment was granted
whichever is the later.
## Backdating
Where a client requests the backdated inclusion of a child and the previous caregiver was getting a benefit for the child, the benefit should be reviewed from the date the child was excluded from the previous caregivers benefit.
Generally, a child cannot be included in multiple benefits for the same period. In some situations, the previous caregiver may continue to get a benefit in respect of that child for up to 28 days.
Consider all the circumstances and decide whether a debt should be established for the previous caregiver.
If the date the child is being included from is a date in the previous tax year, MSD can only pay arrears of family tax credit and Best Start tax credit from the beginning of the current tax year, that is, 1 April. The client will need to apply for any arrears of tax credits before this date from Inland Revenue.
A review of entitlement needs to be completed to determine the amount of any benefit arrears owed to the client for the backdated period.

chunks.title: Child leaves care — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Child leaves care
When a dependent child leaves the client's care, the child should be excluded from the start of the pay period following the date the child leaves care. The client's benefit rate and the rates of any extra help the client gets should be reassessed to the appropriate rate where applicable.
If the child is the client's last dependent child Young Parent Payment must be cancelled. MSD will need to determine if the client qualifies for another benefit.
Note different rules apply when a child stops being a dependent child of a sole parent client because of a sudden change of circumstances beyond the control of the client.
## Example
A sole parent client getting Young Parent Payment with one dependent child included in their benefit.
The child leaves care to start living with another caregiver as planned and is excluded from the start of the pay period so the client does not incur a debt.
The client no longer meets the qualification for Young Parent Payment and MSD must determine if the client qualifies for another benefit.

chunks.title: Child leaves care suddenly — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Child leaves care suddenly
When a child stops being a dependent child of a sole parent client because of a sudden change of circumstances beyond the control of the client, payment of the benefit may continue at the existing rate for 28 days following the date the child stopped being dependent.
This is to allow a period of transition for the client to adjust to their change in circumstances.
For example when a child suddenly goes into the care of Oranga Tamariki, payment may continue for 28 days from the date the child is no longer dependent on the client.
Extra help payments that can be continued for 28 days are:
- Accommodation Supplement
- Child Disability Allowance
- Disability Allowance
- Temporary Additional Support
- Winter Energy Payment
The exception is Childcare Assistance, including Guaranteed Childcare Assistance Payment (GCAP) which must be stopped on the day after the client stopped caring for the dependent child.
During the 28 days continuation of payment, if the client has other changes of circumstances such as a change in income, the rate of main benefit and extra help will need to be reassessed.

chunks.title: Child not living at home — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Child not living at home
The child doesn't have to be living with the client to be a dependent child, consider the following:
- why the child is living away from home
- how permanent the arrangement is and
- what payments the client makes towards the child's care

chunks.title: Child should be included — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Child should be included
A client is obliged to tell their service provider or the Ministry of Social Development of all their circumstances including the number of children in their care.
If a child is considered to be dependent that child is included in the caregiver's benefit and the appropriate rate of benefit paid.
## Client doesn't want to include a child
In cases where the client has genuine concerns about including the child in their benefit (such as concerns about violence from the other parent) advise the client all information contained in their benefit record is confidential.
If there are any concerns regarding the welfare of a child, the case should be referred to Oranga Tamariki.
## Deciding if a child is financially dependent
When a client states that they are receiving payments for a child's expenses YSSU must decide if the child is a dependent child of the client.
A child does not have to be solely financially dependent on a client to be considered a dependent child. All that is required is that the child is financially dependent on the person to some degree.
However, being financially dependent on a client is only part of the qualifications of a dependent child. The child must still meet all the qualifications to be considered dependent.
If another person or body is paying for the child's expenses, including payments for the care provided, the child is not financially dependent on the client.
If a client is receiving payments toward the expenses of a dependent child this is regarded as income for benefit purposes.

chunks.title: Surviving partner — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Surviving partner
When a client dies (and there is a surviving partner) before a decision is made on an application or review for Young Parent Payment, the application or review process can be continued as if the client had not died.
## Single client
When there is no surviving partner the benefit application should generally be declined. However, if there is a request for the application to be decided or the circumstances of the situation merit it, consult the manager client service delivery for a decision.
## Funeral Grant
In situations when the decision to grant or review Young Parent Payment is made after the date of death of the client, any Funeral Grant can be decided as if the deceased client were in receipt of Young Parent Payment.

chunks.title: Client does not return — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Client does not return
If a client's benefit is suspended because they are absent from New Zealand and they do not return, their benefit record will automatically cancel in SWIFTT, eight weeks after the date of suspension.
Note if the client had been approved continued payment of benefit for the first 28 days of the absence, this is not established as a debt.
For more information see:
- Action on return to New Zealand

chunks.title: Client donates a kidney or liver tissue — young parent payment > changes and reviews young parent payment
chunks.text:
## Client donates a kidney or liver tissue
