chunks.title: Living in Australia if you get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension and plan to live in Australia, your payments may continue if you meet certain criteria. You need to contact our International Services team before you leave New Zealand and let them know the date you're leaving. International services There are certain rules for what happens with your NZ Super and Veteran's Pension while living in Australia. These rules are set out in the Social Security Agreement (SSA) we have with Australia. This page explains some of those rules. You'll need to read the information we have about the SSA with Australia for more detail around things like: - how much you'll get paid - how you'll be paid, and - when you'll be paid. Social Security Agreement with Australia - living in Australia

chunks.title: When your payments can continue
chunks.text: Your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension payment will keep being paid for up to 26 weeks after you leave New Zealand (NZ). For these payments to continue after 26 weeks, you need to do certain things.> - First, we look at whether you used an SSA country to meet the residence criteria. - Then what you need to do depends on whether you already get Australian Age Pension (AAP) or not.

chunks.title: If you used an SSA country to meet residence criteria
chunks.text: When you applied for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension, you may have had to use a Social Security Agreement (SSA) country to help you meet the residence criteria. This means you may have included time you spent: - living in a country that NZ has a SSA with, and/or - contributing to a SSA country's pension scheme. If you used time in Australia to meet the residence criteria, you can live in Australia. If you used another SSA country, you need to meet the residence criteria without using the time spent from that country. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super and Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: What to do if you don't already get Australian Age Pension
chunks.text: For payments to continue, you need to: - meet the criteria for AAP (this includes being age 67 or older on or before the day you leave NZ) - apply for the AAP within 26 weeks of leaving NZ, and - apply to continue getting your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension payment - you need to apply within 12 months of applying for AAP. If you don't apply for these payments within the required timeframes, you'll need to pay back any payments you received after you left NZ. If both of these applications are declined, your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension payments will stop from the date your AAP is declined. Who can get Age Pension (Services Australia)external

chunks.title: What to do if you already get Australian Age Pension
chunks.text: You have to apply to continue to get your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension payment. You need to apply within 26 weeks of leaving New Zealand. If you don't apply within this timeframe, your NZ payment will stop after 26 weeks. You'll need to pay back the 26 weeks of NZ payment you received after you left NZ.

chunks.title: Step 1 - Contact International Services
chunks.text: Contact our International Services team before you leave NZ. Let them know the date you're leaving. International services

chunks.title: What passport to use when travelling to Australia
chunks.text: When you go to Australia, it’s best to travel on either your: - New Zealand passport, or - Australian passport, if you have one. This will make it easier to work out whether you meet the criteria for Australian Age Pension.

chunks.title: Step 2 - Contact Services Australia
chunks.text: Contact Services Australia within the first 26 weeks of leaving NZ. You need to apply for an Australian Age Pension (AAP) from them. Once Services Australia have processed your AAP form, they'll send you a NZ payment application form. This form is to continue your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension payments. Contact Services Australiaexternal

chunks.title: Step 3 - Complete NZ payment application form
chunks.text: You need to complete this form and send it back to Services Australia. We'll get a copy of the form and use it to work out: - whether your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension payments can continue, and - how much you can be paid.

chunks.title: If Australian Age Pension is declined
chunks.text: If your Australian Age Pension application is declined because of: - your income or assets, we'll most likely decline your NZ payment application. - another reason, e.g. residency requirements, we may still approve your NZ payment application. If we decline your NZ payment application, your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension payments will stop from the date your AAP is declined. We'll then review the NZ payments you received since you left NZ. We do this to make sure you were getting the right amount of payment during this time.

chunks.title: If you've got the Special Banking Option
chunks.text: You may be getting an overseas pension paid into a Special Banking Option account. The Special Banking Option is only available if you live in New Zealand. You'll need to arrange with Centrelink to have your payments made to your own bank account. It's best to arrange this before you leave NZ. Once payments start going into your own bank account, let us know. That way we can make sure you're getting the correct payments from us.

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: You’ll get your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension at the same rate you would get if you lived in NZ. This rate will continue until you apply for Australian Age Pension (up to 26 weeks). Then your rate of payment may change. The amount we pay you may be less than what you got in NZ. This might be because: - you have a partner included in your payment, as once you leave NZ they can no longer be included - you get any other payments, eg, Disability Allowance or Accommodation Supplement, which you cannot get after you leave NZ - you have lived in a country other than New Zealand or Australia, or - you have income and/or assets that affect how much you can get for Australian Age Pension. (We can't pay more than what Services Australia tell us your Australian Age Pension would be). If your application is approved, we'll review your 26 weeks of payments. We do this to make sure you were getting the right amount of payment during this time. Details of how much you'll get are set out in the Social Security Agreement we have with Australia. Social Security Agreement with Australia - living in Australia

chunks.title: When your payment will start
chunks.text: You’ll get your NZ Super or Veteran's Pension at the same rate you would get if you lived in NZ. This rate will continue for up to 26 weeks. Changes to this rate will start once: - your Australian Age Pension (AAP) is approved, and - your NZ payment application is approved. These rate changes will then be backdated to the date you applied for AAP. For example, if you applied for AAP within one week of leaving NZ, your rate change will be backdated to week one.

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Australia - living in Australia
chunks.text: If you've lived in New Zealand and now live in Australia, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Australia to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen and have a Special Category visa - are an Australia citizen, or - have an Australian residence class visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Australian payments (paid by Centrelink). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability. Australian payments covered by this agreement are: - Australian Age Pension - Disability Support Pension - Carer Payment. It also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: Periods of residence
chunks.text: You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super, Veteran's Pension and Supported Living Payment. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Australian residence to meet this criteria. Centrelink will verify your Australian residence. If you want to use periods of residence in New Zealand to get an Australian payment, contact Centrelink.

chunks.title: Periods of residence for NZ Super and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: Find out if you can use your Australian residence for NZ Super and Veteran's Pension: Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super and Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Periods of residence for Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: To use your Australian residence for Supported Living Payment, you must have: - been living in Australia during that time, and - been an Australian resident for 12 months, of which at least 6 months were continuous.

chunks.title: NZ and Australian payments
chunks.text: If you're already getting an NZ payment and going to live in Australia, go to one of these pages to find out what you need to do: Living in Australia if you get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension Living overseas while on a benefit If you're not already getting a NZ or Australian payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in Australia if you meet the below criteria. You need to meet the eligibility criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. However, you will be ordinarily resident in Australia instead of NZ, the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau when you apply. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension If you're not ordinarily resident in Australia, you will need to either: - have been physically present in Australia for at least 26 weeks, or - intend to remain physically present in Australia for 1 year from when you apply. You also need to: - meet the criteria and have applied for the Australian Age Pension from Centrelink in Australia. You must be entitled to a rate that's more than $0. - have lived in New Zealand for at least 1 year continuously since age 20, and - are in Australia when you apply. For Veteran's Pension you also need to have the necessary service and disability qualifications. Who can get Age Pension (Centrelink)external Residence descriptions (Centrelink)external When you go to Australia, it’s best to travel on your NZ or Australian passport, if you have one. This will make it easier to work out whether you meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran’s Pension.

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: You may be able to get Supported Living Payment while you're living in Australia if you meet the below criteria. You need to meet the eligibility criteria for Supported Living Payment. However you will be ordinarily resident in Australia instead of NZ when you apply. Supported Living Payment If you're not ordinarily resident in Australia, you must intend to remain physically present in Australia for at least 1 year from when you apply. You also need to: - qualify for a rate of Disability Support Pension from Centrelink in Australia - have lived in New Zealand and/or Australia continuously for at least: 2 years since becoming a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident, and 1 year since turning 20, and - 2 years since becoming a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident, and - 1 year since turning 20, and - are in Australia when you apply. To qualify for Disability Support Pension, there are certain rules you need to meet, including medical rules. These rules are different to the criteria for Supported Living Payment. It's best to check you meet these rules before you leave NZ. Disability Support Pension (Centrelink)external Residence descriptions (Centrelink)external When you go to Australia, it’s best to travel on your NZ or Australian passport, if you have one. This will make it easier to work out whether you meet the criteria for Supported Living Payment.

chunks.title: Who can get Australian payments
chunks.text: You may be able to get Australian payments while you're living in Australia. Centrelink in Australia decides who can get the Australian payments. Contact us (Centrelink)external

chunks.title: Step 1 - Apply for an Australian payment first
chunks.text: You need to contact Centrelink. They will ask you to claim an Australian payment first. They'll let you know which one you need to claim. It depends what New Zealand payment you want to apply for. The Australian payment will need to be approved before you can apply for a New Zealand payment. Contact us (Centrelink)external

chunks.title: Step 2 - Then apply for a NZ payment
chunks.text: Centrelink will send you the appropriate New Zealand application forms. Then contact Centrelink to find out your next steps. Contact us (Centrelink)external

chunks.title: How much you'll get
chunks.text: Your total payment will be made up of: - a NZ payment - our International Services team calculates and pays the NZ payment, and - an Australian payment - Centrelink calculates and pays the Australian payment. Below is the information about how we calculate the NZ payment. Talk to Centrelink for information about how they calculate the Australian payment.

chunks.title: NZ Super/Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you've applied for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension, your NZ payment will be the smaller amount of either the: - NZ rate (how much you get is based on certain criteria), or - Australia rate (the maximum amount you would be paid by Centrelink if you didn't get a NZ payment). The NZ rate is based on the number of months you lived in NZ between the ages of 20 and 65. This is a total of 540 months (or 45 years). If you're not an Australian citizen or Australian permanent resident, then: - any months you've spent in another country (not NZ or Australia) between age 20 and 65, is counted as months you've lived in NZ, and - if you get a benefit or pension from another country (not NZ or Australia), this is deducted from your NZ payment. If you're single, we calculate the NZ rate this way: - number of months you've lived in NZ divided by 540, and then multiplied by $595.57 gross (the weekly single rate we use) = amount 1 - work out 15% of amount 1 = amount 2 - amount 1 - amount 2 = NZ rate. If you have a partner, we calculate the NZ rate this way: - number of months you've lived in NZ divided by 540, and then multiplied by $492.14 gross (the weekly couple rate we use) = amount 1 - work out 15% of amount 1 = amount 2 - amount 1 - amount 2 = NZ rate. In either situation, if the Australia rate is: - more than this, we would pay you the NZ rate, or - less than this, we would pay you the Australia rate. This rate will be your NZ payment. Centrelink calculates and pays the Australian payment This could be $0 depending on how they calculate it. For example: you're single and have lived in NZ for the whole 45 years (540 months) between age 20 and 65. You don't get a benefit or pension from another country. So the calculation would be: - 540 divided by 540 and multiplied by $595.57 gross = $595.57 gross (amount 1) - 15% of $595.57 = $89.33 (amount 2) - $595.57 - $89.33 = $506.24.

chunks.title: NZ Super/Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: This means the NZ rate would be $506.24 gross a week. If the Australia rate is more than this, we would pay you the NZ rate.

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: If you've applied for the Supported Living Payment, your NZ payment will be the smaller amount of either the: - NZ rate (how much you get is based on certain criteria), or - Australia rate (the maximum amount you would be paid by Centrelink if you didn't get a NZ payment). The NZ rate is based on the number of months you lived in NZ or Australia between: - age 20, and - the date you're assessed as severely disabled by Centrelink or International Services. If you get an overseas pension, we'll deduct this from your Supported Living Payment if: - you're not an Australian citizen or Australian permanent resident, and - the overseas pension is from another country (not NZ or Australia). We calculate the NZ rate this way: - number of months lived in NZ divided by the number of total months lived in NZ and Australia, and - multiplied by the Supported Living Payment net rate you would qualify for. Supported Living Payment cut-out pointsexternal If the Australia rate is: - more than this, we would pay you the NZ rate, or - less than this, we would pay you the Australia rate. This rate will be your NZ payment. Centrelink calculates and pays the Australian payment. This could be $0, depending on how they calculate it. For example: you lived in NZ for 10 years (120 months), moved to Australia at age 30 and became severely disabled at age 35. You've lived in NZ and Australia for a total of 180 months. You're single and don't get a benefit or pension from another country. So the calculation would be 120 divided by 180 and multiplied by $424.60 = $283.06. This means the NZ rate would be $283.06 a week. If the Australia rate is more than this, we would pay you the NZ rate.

chunks.title: How you'll be paid
chunks.text: If you're living in Australia, you can choose to have your payments made to either your: - Australian bank account every 4 weeks, or - NZ bank account every 2 weeks. If they go to your Australian bank account, we'll pay the initial cost of transferring the funds. You must pay for any other costs that your bank charges. You must pay the cost of any transfers if: - your payments go to your NZ bank account, and - you then transfer them to your Australian account.

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: We won’t deduct tax from your New Zealand payments while you're living in Australia. If your payments are put into: - an Australian bank account, you may have to pay tax on these payments in Australia. - a New Zealand bank account, you may need to pay tax on these payments in New Zealand and/or Australia. For more information, contact the tax authorities in the relevant countries.

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: We'll let you know what date your payment will start in the letter we send you, once your application's approved.

chunks.title: If you applied for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: Payment will usually start from the date of your application or the entitlement date. It will be whichever is later.

chunks.title: If you applied for Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: If you apply for this from Australia for the first time, there is a stand-down before we can pay you.

chunks.title: Travelling from Australia to another country (not NZ)
chunks.text: Before you leave Australia you need to contact: - our International Services team, and - Centrelink, if you get an Australian payment. Contact International Services Below are details of what will happen to your NZ payments. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call and tell you what you need to do. Talk to Centrelink for information about what will happen to your Australian payment.

chunks.title: NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you're leaving Australia for: - 26 weeks or less, your payments will continue while you're away. You must continue to be ordinarily resident in Australia while you're away. Your NZ payment will be paid at the same rate you're paid in Australia. - more than 26 weeks, your payments will stop from the day you leave Australia. You may be able to apply to get these payments while you're overseas. It depends if the country you're going to has a SSA or arrangement with NZ. You can apply through that country's social security agency to be paid in that country. If you're going to the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau, there is a specific way to apply. Apply for NZ Super from Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau If you qualify, the payment will start from the later of either: - the date of your application in that country, or - the date you become entitled to that payment. Social Security Agreements and special arrangements with Pacific countries Your NZ payment will stop from the day you leave Australia. If your payments aren’t stopped in time, you will need to refund any overpayments to us. When you come back to Australia, you'll have to re-apply to restart these payments.

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: If you're going to another country for: - 26 weeks or less, your payments will stop after 4 weeks. You must continue to be ordinarily resident in Australia while you're away. Your NZ payment will be paid at the same rate you're paid in Australia. - more than 26 weeks, your payments will stop from the day you leave Australia. You may be able to apply to get these payments overseas. It depends if the country you're going to has a SSA with NZ and what that agreement states. You may be able to apply to be paid in that country. It depends what the agreement states and if it covers you to be paid Supported Living Payment. If you qualify, the payment will start from the later of either: - the date of your application in that country, or - the date you become entitled to that payment. Social Security Agreements and special arrangements with Pacific countries Your NZ payment will stop from the day you leave Australia. If your payments aren’t stopped in time, you will need to refund any overpayments to us. When you come back to Australia, you'll have to re-apply to restart these payments.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ temporarily (less than 26 weeks)
chunks.text: You should talk to Centrelink before you travel to New Zealand. You will continue to get your New Zealand payments at the same rate you're paid in Australia. Contact us (Centrelink)external

chunks.title: Returning to NZ temporarily (more than 26 weeks)
chunks.text: You should contact our International Services team before you travel to New Zealand. Contact International Services You will continue to get your New Zealand payments, but the amount may change.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ permanently
chunks.text: You should talk to Centrelink before you travel to New Zealand. Let them know you're returning permanently. Contact us (Centrelink)external When you return to New Zealand, you need to contact us so we can assess your payments. Phone us

chunks.title: Tell us about changes
chunks.text: You still need to tell us about any changes to your circumstances when you're living in Australia. These changes may affect your payments. You also need to tell Centrelink about these changes. These changes could include: - entering a relationship, or - moving address. Contact International Services Contact us (Centrelink)external

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Canada - living in Canada
chunks.text: If you've lived in New Zealand and now live in Canada, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Canada to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Canadian payments (paid by Service Canada). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability - Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers. Canadian payments covered by this agreement are: - Old Age Security Pension - Canada Pension Plan (if you get the Quebec Pension Plan, this is not covered by the agreement). This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in NZ and Canadian creditable periods so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and Canadian payments
chunks.text: If you're already getting an NZ payment and going to live in Canada, go to one of these pages to find out what you need to do: Living overseas if you get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension Living overseas while on a benefit If you're not already getting a NZ or Canadian payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in Canada if you: - meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. However you will be ordinarily resident in Canada instead of NZ when you apply, and - have been resident in New Zealand for at least 1 year continuously from age 20 - intend to remain ordinarily resident in Canada for at least 26 weeks from when you apply, and - are in NZ or Canada when you apply. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Canadian creditable periods to meet this criteria. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: You may be able to get Supported Living Payment for a health condition, injury or disability while you're living in Canada if you: - meet the criteria for Supported Living Payment. However you will be ordinarily resident in Canada instead of NZ when you apply - are 21 or older, and - are in NZ or Canada when you apply. You need to have lived in New Zealand for at least 2 years to get Supported Living Payment. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Canadian creditable periods to meet this criteria. To use your Canadian creditable periods, you must have lived in NZ continuously for at least 1 year from age 20. Supported Living Payment

chunks.title: Who can get Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers
chunks.text: You may be able to get Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower while you're living in Canada if you: - meet the criteria for Sole Parent Support - are 21 or older, - are the parent of one or more dependent children whose other parent is deceased, and - are in New Zealand or Canada when you apply. You need to have lived in New Zealand for at least 2 years to get Sole Parent Support. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Canadian creditable periods to meet this criteria. You can also use your late partner's Canadian creditable periods that they contributed to the Canada Pension Plan. Any overlapping periods can only be counted once. Sole Parent Support To use your Canadian creditable periods, you must have lived in NZ continuously for at least 1 year from age 20.

chunks.title: Who can get Canadian payments
chunks.text: You may be able to get Canadian payments while you're living in Canada. These are the: - Old Age Security Pension - Canada Pension Plan. You may need to have lived in Canada for a certain amount of time to get a Canadian payment. If so, you may be able to use periods of residence in New Zealand to meet this criteria. Service Canada decides who can get these Canadian payments. Government of Canadaexternal

chunks.title: Applying from NZ
chunks.text: You need to contact International Services at least 4 weeks before you leave NZ. They will book an appointment for you to come in and see us. At the interview, you and your partner (if you have one) will complete an application form. This includes questions about your residence in NZ. We'll ask you to bring these documents to the appointment: - your passport - another form of ID, e.g: birth certificate driver's licence marriage certificate - birth certificate - driver's licence - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - your travel itinerary or tickets - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into - any documentation that shows your intent to live in Canada, e.g. an accommodation agreement. You may need to bring other documents, we'll let you know when you call us.

chunks.title: Applying from Canada
chunks.text: You need to contact Service Canada. You and your partner (if you have one) will need to complete an application form and provide proof of the time you lived in NZ. This proof can include: - testimonials - work references, and - letters from neighbours and friends. You'll also need to provide the following documents: - proof of your identity, e.g: birth certificate passport driver's licence, or marriage certificate - birth certificate - passport - driver's licence, or - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into, e.g: bank statement deposit slip. - bank statement - deposit slip. Contact the Government of Canadaexternal

chunks.title: How to apply for Canadian payments
chunks.text: You need to apply for Canadian payments when you're in Canada. Contact Service Canada to apply for these payments. Contact the Government of Canadaexternal

chunks.title: New Zealand payments
chunks.text: If your NZ payments are made to a Canadian bank account, the amount you get will change each time you're paid. This is because it depends on the exchange rate used to convert your payment from NZ dollars to Canadian dollars.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: How much you get is based on the number of months you lived in NZ from age 20. If you're born: - before 31 March 1936, contact us to find out how much you could get. Phone us - after 31 March 1936, we work out how much you could get using the steps below. Step 1: Confirm the number of months you've lived in New Zealand from age 20. Step 2: Divide this number by 540. Step 3: Take that answer and: - if you're single, multiply it by $1,191.14 (the single fortnightly gross rate we use), or - if you have a partner, multiply it by either: $1,968.56 if both you and your partner qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation), or $984.28 if only you qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation). - $1,968.56 if both you and your partner qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation), or - $984.28 if only you qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation). For example, you're single and you've lived in NZ for 240 months (20 years) from age 20. Divide 240 by 540 which is 0.44. Then multiply this by the single gross rate of $1,191.14. That gives a fortnightly payment of $524.10 gross. Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support How much you get depends on how many months you've lived in NZ from age 20. If you lived in New Zealand for: - 300 months (25 years) or more from age 20, you will get the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate or Sole Parent Support rate - less than 300 months (25 years) from age 20, you need to: confirm the number of years you lived in NZ from age 20 divide this number by 300, and multiply this answer by the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate or Sole Parent Support rate for your situation. - confirm the number of years you lived in NZ from age 20 - divide this number by 300, and

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: - multiply this answer by the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate or Sole Parent Support rate for your situation. If you have any other income, this will also affect your payments. chunks.text: Service Canada decides how much you will be paid. For more information, contact Service Canada. Contact the Government of Canadaexternal

If they go to an overseas bank account, we'll pay the initial cost of transferring the funds. You must pay for any other costs that your bank charges. If they go to a NZ bank account, you must pay the cost of any transfers overseas.

chunks.text: Your NZ payments don’t have any tax taken off them. For information about your tax obligations, contact the tax authorities in the relevant countries. Canada Revenue Agencyexternal Inland Revenueexternal

chunks.title: Send life certificates and renewal forms back to us
chunks.text: What type of form we'll send you and how often we send it depends on what NZ payment you get.

chunks.title: You get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you get NZ Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, we'll send you life certificates every 12 months. In some cases, we'll send you a life certificate every 6 months, e.g. if: - you use an agent, - your New Zealand Super or Veteran's Pension payments are made to a New Zealand bank account, or - you're over 80. You need to return the life certificate within 8 weeks otherwise your payments will stop.

chunks.title: You get Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support
chunks.text: If you get Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support, we'll send you a renewal form every 12 months. You need to return the renewal form within 8 weeks otherwise your payments will stop.

chunks.title: Travelling from Canada to another country (not NZ)
chunks.text: Before you leave Canada you need to contact: - our International Services team, and - Service Canada, if you get a Canadian payment. International Services Below are details of what will happen to your NZ payments. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call and tell you what you need to do. Talk to Service Canada for information about what will happen to your Canadian payment.

chunks.title: Temporarily visiting another country
chunks.text: If you're going to visit another country for 26 weeks or less, your payments will continue while you're away. If you're going to visit another country for more than 26 weeks, your payments will be affected from the date you leave Canada. You may have a debt which you'll need to repay.

chunks.title: Moving to another country
chunks.text: NZ has Social Security Agreements (SSAs) with 11 countries. If you move to one of these countries, you'll need to re-apply for your NZ payment under the relevant agreement. One of the countries NZ has a SSA with is the United Kingdom (UK). If you're moving to the UK, you can't get an NZ payment. You may be able to get a UK payment instead under the UK Social Security Agreement. Social Security Agreement with the United Kingdom (UK) - living in UK Social Security Agreements and special arrangements with Pacific countries If you move to a country that doesn't have a SSA with NZ, your New Zealand payment will stop.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ temporarily
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand for 26 weeks or less, you'll get the same rate of payment you were getting in Canada.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ permanently
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand permanently, you may be paid the full NZ rate less any payment you get from Canada or another country. You need to contact us when you return to NZ so we can assess your payments. Phone us

chunks.title: Tell us about changes
chunks.text: You still need to tell us about any changes to your circumstances while you're living in Canada. These changes may affect your payments. You also need to tell Service Canada about these changes. These changes could include: - entering a relationship, or - moving address. Contact our International Services team Contact the Government of Canadaexternal

chunks.text: If you're going to visit another country for 26 weeks or less, your payments will continue while you're away. If you're going to visit another country for more than 26 weeks, your payments will stop from the date you leave Denmark. You may have a debt which you'll need to repay.

chunks.title: Moving to another country
chunks.text: NZ has Social Security Agreements (SSAs) with 11 countries. If you move to one of these countries, you'll need to re-apply for your NZ payment under the relevant agreement. One of the countries NZ has a SSA with is the United Kingdom (UK). If you're moving to the UK, you can't get an NZ payment. You may be able to get a UK payment instead under the UK Social Security Agreement. UK Social Security Agreement Countries NZ has a Social Security Agreement with If you move to a country that doesn't have a SSA with NZ, your New Zealand payment will stop.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ temporarily

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Greece - living in Greece

This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Greek payments (paid by the Greek Social Security Institute). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability. - Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers - Orphan's Benefit - Funeral Grant. Greek payments covered by this agreement are: - Old Age Benefit - Invalidity Benefit - Survivors Benefit - Funeral Grants. This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and Greek payments
chunks.text: If you're already getting an NZ payment and going to live in Greece, go to one of these pages to find out what you need to do: Living overseas if you get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension Living overseas while on a benefit If you're not already getting an NZ or Greek payment, read the information below.

Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use time you've spent living in Greece from age 20 or contributing to the national insurance scheme to meet this criteria. To use this time, you must have been ordinarily resident in NZ for at least 1 year at any time before you apply. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

If you haven't, you may be able to use time you've spent living in Greece from age 20 or contributing to the national insurance scheme to meet this criteria. chunks.text: You may be able to get Orphan's Benefit while you're living in Greece if: - you meet the criteria for Orphan's Benefit. chunks.title: Applying from NZ
chunks.text: You need to contact International Services at least 4 weeks before you leave NZ. They will book an appointment for you to come in and see us. At the appointment, you and your partner (if you have one) will complete an application form. This includes questions about your residence in NZ. We'll ask you to bring these documents to the appointment: - your passport - another form of ID, e.g: birth certificate driver's licence marriage certificate - birth certificate - driver's licence - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - your travel itinerary or tickets - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into - any documentation that shows your intent to live in Ireland, e.g. an accommodation agreement. You may need to bring other documents, we'll let you know when you call us.

chunks.title: Applying from Ireland
chunks.text: You need to contact the local branch of the Irish Department of Social Protection. Contact the Department of Social Protection You and your partner (if you have one) will need to complete an application form and provide proof of the time you lived in NZ. This proof can include: - testimonials - work references, and - letters from neighbours and friends. You'll also need to provide the following documents: - proof of your identity, e.g: birth certificate passport driver's licence, or marriage certificate - birth certificate - passport - driver's licence, or - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into, e.g: bank statement deposit slip. - bank statement - deposit slip.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: How much you get is based on the number of months you lived in NZ from age 20. If you're born: - before 31 March 1936, contact us to find out how much you could get. - after 31 March 1936, we work out how much you could get using the steps below. Phone us Step 1: Confirm the number of months you've lived in New Zealand from age 20. Step 2: Divide this number by 540. For example, you're single and you've lived in NZ for 240 months (20 years) from age 20. Divide 240 by 540 which is 0.44. Then multiply this by the single gross rate of $1,191.14. chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Jersey - living in Jersey
chunks.text: If you've lived in New Zealand and now live in Jersey, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Jersey to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Jersey payments (paid by the Jersey Social Security Department). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability. - Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers. Jersey payments covered by this agreement are: - Old Age Pension - Sickness Benefit - Survivors Pension (formerly Widows Benefit) - Income Support Disablement - Incapacity Pension. This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in Jersey if you: - meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. However you will be ordinarily resident in Jersey instead of NZ when you apply - have been resident in NZ for at least 1 year from age 20 - are in New Zealand or Jersey when you apply, and - intend to be ordinarily resident in Jersey for at least 26 weeks from when you apply. If you haven't, you may be able to use your or your partner's time you've spent contributing to the Jersey insurance scheme to meet this criteria. To use this time, you must have: - been ordinarily resident in NZ for at least 1 year from age 20, and - contributed to the Jersey insurance scheme for at least 12 months. Supported Living Payment You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get Supported Living Payment. If you haven't, you may be able to use your or your partner's time you've spent contributing to the Jersey insurance scheme to meet this criteria. To use this time, you must have lived in NZ continuously for at least 1 year from age 20. Any overlapping periods can only be counted once.

chunks.title: Who can get Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers
chunks.text: You may be able to get Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower while you're living in Jersey if you: - meet the criteria for Sole Parent Support - are 21 or older - are the parent of one or more dependent children whose other parent is deceased - have lived in New Zealand for at least 1 year from age 20 - are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, and - intend to be live in Jersey for at least 26 weeks from when you apply. If you haven't, you may be able to use your or your late partner's time contributing to the Jersey insurance scheme to meet this criteria. To use this time, you must have lived in NZ continuously for at least 1 year from age 20. Any overlapping periods can only be counted once.

We'll ask you to bring these documents to the appointment: - your passport - another form of ID, e.g: birth certificate driver's licence marriage certificate - birth certificate - driver's licence - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - your travel itinerary or tickets - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into - any documentation that shows your intent to live in the Netherlands, e.g. an accommodation agreement. You may need to bring other documents, we'll let you know when you call us.

chunks.title: Applying from the Netherlands
chunks.text: You need to contact the relevant Netherlands social security agency (Sociale Verzekeringsbank or Uitvoering Werknemersverzekeringen). You and your partner (if you have one) will need to complete an application form and provide proof of the time you lived in NZ. This proof can include: - testimonials - work references, and - letters from neighbours and friends. You'll also need to provide the following documents: - proof of your identity, e.g: birth certificate passport driver's licence, or marriage certificate - birth certificate - passport - driver's licence, or - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into, e.g: bank statement deposit slip. - bank statement - deposit slip. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: How to apply for Netherlands payments
chunks.text: You need to apply for Netherlands payments when you're in the Netherlands. Contact the relevant Netherlands social security agency to apply for these payments. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: New Zealand payments
chunks.text: If your NZ payments are made to a Netherlands bank account, the amount you get will change each month. This is because it depends on the exchange rate used to convert your payment from NZ dollars to Euros.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: How much you get is based on the number of months you lived in NZ from age 20. If you're born: - before 31 March 1936, contact us to find out how much you could get. - after 31 March 1936, we work out how much you could get using the steps below. Step 1: Confirm the number of months you've lived in New Zealand from age 20. Step 2: Divide this number by 540. Step 3: Take that answer and: - if you're single, multiply it by $1,191.14 (the single fortnightly gross rate we use), or - if you have a partner, multiply it by either: $1,968.56 if both you and your partner qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation), or $984.28 if you only you qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation). - $1,968.56 if both you and your partner qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation), or - $984.28 if you only you qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation). For example, you're single and you've lived in NZ for 240 months (20 years) from age 20. Divide 240 by 540 which is 0.44. Then multiply this by the single gross rate of $1,191.14. That gives a fortnightly payment of $524.10 gross. Phone us

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support
chunks.text: How much you get depends on how many months you've lived in NZ from age 20. If you lived in New Zealand for: - 300 months (25 years) or more from age 20, you will get the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate or Sole Parent Support rate for your situation. - less than 300 months (25 years) from age 20, you need to: confirm the number of years you lived in NZ from age 20 divide this number by 300, and multiply this answer by the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate< or Sole Parent Support rate< for your situation. - confirm the number of years you lived in NZ from age 20 - divide this number by 300, and - multiply this answer by the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate< or Sole Parent Support rate< for your situation. Supported Living Payment rate (Manuals and Procedures)external Sole Parent Support rate (Manuals and Procedures)external

chunks.title: Netherlands payments
chunks.text: The Netherlands social security agencies (Sociale Verzekeringsbank and Uitvoering Werknemersverzekeringen) decide how much you will be paid. For more information, contact the relevant agency. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: Your NZ payments don't have any tax taken off them. For information about your tax obligations, contact the tax authorities in the relevant countries. Belastingdienst - Netherlands Tax Administrationexternal Inland Revenueexternal

chunks.title: Travelling from the Netherlands to another country (not NZ)
chunks.text: Before you leave the Netherlands you need to contact: - our International Services team, and - the relevant Netherlands social security agency, if you get a Netherlands payment. Below are details of what will happen to your NZ payments. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call and tell you what you need to do. Talk to the relevant Netherlands social security agency for information about what will happen to your Netherlands payment. International Services

chunks.title: Temporarily visiting another country
chunks.text: If you're going to visit another country for 26 weeks or less, your payments will continue while you're away. If you're going to visit another country for more than 26 weeks, your payments will be affected from the date you leave the Netherlands. You may have a debt which you'll need to repay.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ temporarily
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand for 26 weeks or less, you'll get the same rate of payment you were getting in the Netherlands.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ permanently
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand permanently, you may be paid the full NZ rate less any payment you get from the Netherlands or another country. You need to contact us when you return to NZ so we can assess your payments. Phone us

chunks.title: Tell us about changes
chunks.text: You still need to tell us about any changes to your circumstances while you're living in the Netherlands. These changes may affect your payments. You also need to tell the relevant Netherlands social security agency about these changes. These changes could include: - entering a relationship, or - moving address. Contact International Services Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Australia - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in Australia and now live in New Zealand, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Australia to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an Australian citizen, - have an Australian residence class visa, or - are an New Zealand citizen.

chunks.title: Periods of residence
chunks.text: You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super, Veteran's Pension and Supported Living Payment. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Australian residence to meet this criteria. Contact our International Services team if you want to talk about your situation. International Services

chunks.title: NZ and Australian payments
chunks.text: If you already get an Australian payment and move to NZ, contact Centrelink. They'll change the payment if needed. Contact us (Services Australia)external If you're not already getting a NZ or Australian payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in New Zealand. To get this you must meet the eligibility criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension If you don't meet the eligibility criteria, you may still qualify if you meet the following criteria: - you are 67 or older (the age criteria for Australian Age Pension) - you have lived in Australia (as defined by Centrelink) for at least 12 months between age 20 and age 67 (the age you qualify for Australian Age Pension), of which 6 months were continuous - you either: are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, or intend to remain in New Zealand for at least 1 year or have lived in NZ for at least 6 months before you apply, and are in New Zealand when you apply - are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, or - intend to remain in New Zealand for at least 1 year or have lived in NZ for at least 6 months before you apply, and are in New Zealand when you apply Ordinarily resident - you either: have lived in NZ for a certain number of years since you turned 20, with 5 years since the age of 50. How many years you need is based on your date of birth (you can work this out on our 'Who can get NZ Super' page). You can use time spent as an Australian resident between age 20 and age 67 (the age you qualify for Australian Age Pension) to count towards this, or are in New Zealand when you apply. - have lived in NZ for a certain number of years since you turned 20, with 5 years since the age of 50. How many years you need is based on your date of birth (you can work this out on our 'Who can get NZ Super' page). You can use time spent as an Australian resident between age 20 and age 67 (the age you qualify for Australian Age Pension) to count towards this, or - are in New Zealand when you apply. For Veteran's Pension you also need to have the necessary service and disability qualifications. Who can get Australian Age Pension (Services Australia)external Definition of Australian resident and living in Australia (Services Australia)external

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: You may be able to get Supported Living Payment while you're living in New Zealand. To get this you must meet the eligibility criteria for Supported Living Payment. If you don't meet the eligibility criteria, you may still qualify if you meet the following criteria: - you either: are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, or intend to remain in New Zealand for at least 1 year or have lived in NZ for at least 6 months before you apply, and are in New Zealand when you apply - are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, or - intend to remain in New Zealand for at least 1 year or have lived in NZ for at least 6 months before you apply, and are in New Zealand when you apply - you have a total of 2 years residence in New Zealand and/or Australia - you have lived in Australia (as defined by Centrelink) for at least 12 months, of which 6 months were continuous, and - you are medically assessed as 'severely disabled' - this means: you must either: be permanently blind, or have a physical, psychiatric or intellectual impairment that means you cannot work or benefit from any assistance or rehabilitation programme for the next 2 years, and the severe disablement happened while you were living in New Zealand or Australia. - you must either: be permanently blind, or have a physical, psychiatric or intellectual impairment that means you cannot work or benefit from any assistance or rehabilitation programme for the next 2 years, and - be permanently blind, or - have a physical, psychiatric or intellectual impairment that means you cannot work or benefit from any assistance or rehabilitation programme for the next 2 years, and - the severe disablement happened while you were living in New Zealand or Australia. Ordinarily resident Definition of Australian resident and living in Australia (Services Australia)external

chunks.title: Who can get Australian payments
chunks.text: You may be able to get Australian payments while you're living in NZ. CentreLink in Australia decides who can get the Australian payments. How to contact Services Australiaexternal

chunks.title: How to apply for Australian payments
chunks.text: Contact International Services to find out what Australian payments you can get. International Services They will send you an application form to complete. You need to fill it out and send it back to them. They will then forward your application to Centrelink in Australia who will process it. Once a decision has been made, International Services will be in touch with you to let you know the outcome.

chunks.title: How to apply for New Zealand payments
chunks.text: Use our Check What You Might Get tool to find out what NZ payments you can get and how to apply. Check what you might getexternal

chunks.title: How much you'll get
chunks.text: Your total payment will be made up of: - a NZ payment, and - an Australian payment - Centrelink calculates and pays the Australian payment.

chunks.title: NZ payment rates
chunks.text: For NZ payments, you'll get the NZ rates for the payment you qualify for. - NZ Super or Veteran's Pension rates - Supported Living Payment rates How much you can get for NZ Super Supported Living Payment (current)external If you or your partner qualify for an overseas pension, this could affect your NZ rate. The Australian payment from Centrelink is classed as an overseas pension. Overseas pensions

chunks.title: How you'll be paid
chunks.text: If you're living in NZ, you can choose to have your Australian payment paid by either the: - Direct Payment Method, or - Special Banking option. Payment options for overseas pensions

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: You may have to pay tax on your Australian payment in New Zealand if you: - are paid your Australian pension by the Direct Payment Method. This is regardless of whether it's paid to a bank account in Australia or NZ, and - get NZ Super or Veteran’s Pension. Make sure you keep copies of all your banking records. These may show your gross Australian pension payments required for tax purposes.

chunks.title: If you get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: If you're paid your Australian pension by Direct Payment Method, you do not have to pay tax. This is because your gross Australian payment is deducted directly from your net New Zealand entitlement. However if your Australian payments are more than the maximum Supported Living Payment, you will need to pay tax.

chunks.title: Special Banking option
chunks.text: If you have chosen the Special Banking Option, the tax is already paid before you get your payment. However, you may need to pay tax on any Australian payment you got prior to choosing the Special Banking Option. You can talk to Inland Revenue New Zealand about your tax liability. Inland Revenueexternal

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: NZ payments will start from the date of your application or the entitlement date - whichever is later. We'll let you know what date your payment will start in the letter we send you, once your application's approved. Centrelink decides when you get paid any Australian payments.

chunks.title: Travelling from NZ to another country (not Australia)
chunks.text: Before you leave NZ you need to contact: - our International Services team, and - Centrelink, if you get an Australian payment. International Services Below are details of what will happen to your NZ payments. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call and tell you what you need to do. Talk to Centrelink for information about what will happen to your Australian payment.

chunks.title: NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you're going to another country for: - 26 weeks or less, your payment may continue while you're away. There are certain criteria you'll need to meet. - more than 26 weeks, you may be able to apply to keep your payments going. Travelling overseas for 26 weeks or less

chunks.title: Going for more than 26 weeks
chunks.text: You may have had to use your Australian residence to help you meet the residence criteria for your NZ payment. If you used your Australian residence and: - still need to do this to meet the residence criteria, your payments will stop from the day after you leave New Zealand. When you come back to NZ, you'll have to re-apply to get this payment again. - no longer need to do this to meet the residence criteria, you may be able to apply to get some or all of your NZ payment. What you're paid depends on what country you go to. You need to apply before you leave NZ. If you qualify to be paid in that country, payment will be made from the first payment date after you leave NZ. Social Security Agreements and special arrangements with Pacific countries

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: If you're going to another country, your Supported Living Payment may continue. It depends if the country you're going to has a SSA with NZ and what that agreement states.

chunks.title: Going to a country that has a SSA with NZ
chunks.text: You may be able to apply to keep your payments going. It depends what the agreement states and if it covers you to be paid Supported Living Payment. You need to apply before you leave NZ, otherwise your payments will stop after you leave NZ.

chunks.title: Going to a country that doesn't have a SSA with NZ
chunks.text: If you move to that country, your payments will stop after you leave NZ. If you're going to that country temporarily, you may be able to keep getting your Supported Living Payment. It depends on why you're going there. Going overseas temporarily while on a benefit

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Malta - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in Malta and now live in New Zealand, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Malta to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: NZ and Maltese payments
chunks.text: If you already get a Maltese payment and move to NZ, contact the Maltese Department of Social Security. They'll change the payment if needed. Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security If you're not already getting a NZ or Maltese payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in Malta, and - you meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use time you've spent contributing to the Maltese insurance scheme to meet this criteria. To include this time, you must: - have at least 1 year of continuous NZ working age residence, and - be ordinarily resident in NZ. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Who can get Maltese payments
chunks.text: You may be able to get Maltese payments while you're living in NZ. These are the: - Retirement Pension - Survivor's Pension - Non-contributory Old Age Pension. You may need to have lived in Malta for a certain amount of time to get a Maltese payment. If so, you may be able to use periods of residence in New Zealand to meet this criteria. The Maltese Department of Social Security decides who can get these Maltese payments. Department of Social Security Maltaexternal Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security

chunks.title: How to apply for NZ payments
chunks.text: Use our Check What You Might Get tool to find out what NZ payments you can get and how to apply. You also need to apply for: - any Maltese payment that you may qualify for and - any other overseas payments that you may be able to get. Check What You Might Getexternal

chunks.title: How to apply for Maltese payments
chunks.text: You should apply through the Maltese Department of Social Security before you leave Malta. If you already live in New Zealand, contact our International Services team. They'll send you an application form to complete and you'll need to send it back to them. Then they'll forward that to the Maltese Department of Social Security. International Services The Maltese Department of Social Security will decide whether you can get a Maltese payment and let you know. This may take a few months. Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security

chunks.title: New Zealand payments
chunks.text: We'll decide how much you will be paid based on certain criteria. If you get an overseas pension, it's usually deducted from your New Zealand payment. Overseas pensions Generally, the amount you're paid is about equal to what you would be paid if you had lived all your life in New Zealand.

chunks.title: Maltese payments
chunks.text: The Maltese Department of Social Security decides how much you will be paid. Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security

chunks.title: NZ payments
chunks.text: NZ Super and Veteran's Pension payments are paid into your nominated NZ bank account fortnightly.

chunks.title: Maltese payments
chunks.text: Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security to find out how Maltese payments are paid. Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: - You have to pay NZ tax on your NZ payments. We'll withhold your NZ tax based on the tax code you're using and pay this directly to the NZ tax department, Inland Revenue. - You may have to pay NZ tax on your Maltese payment. This is regardless of whether it's paid to a bank account in Malta or NZ. - You may have to pay Maltese tax on your Maltese payment. For more information, talk to the Maltese tax authority. If your Maltese payment is liable for tax in Malta, you may be able to get a rebate on your New Zealand tax. We recommend you discuss your tax liabilities with the relevant tax agency. Inland Revenueexternal Tax & Customs Administration Maltaexternal

chunks.title: Keep copies of your bank records
chunks.text: Make sure you keep copies of all your banking records, as these may show your gross Maltese pension payments required for tax purposes.

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: NZ payments will start from the date of your application or the entitlement date - whichever is later. We'll let you know what date this will be in the letter we send you, once your application's approved. The Maltese Department of Social Security decides when you get paid any Maltese payments.

chunks.title: Travelling from NZ to another country (not Malta)
chunks.text: Before you leave New Zealand you need to contact: - our International Services team - the Maltese Department of Social Security, if you get a Maltese payment. International Services Department of Social Security Malta You may keep getting your NZ payment but it depends on: - where you're going - how long you're going for, and - what type of payment you're getting. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call. Talk to the Maltese Department of Social Security for information about what will happen to your Maltese payment.

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with South Korea - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in South Korea and now live in New Zealand, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with South Korea to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or South Korean payments (paid by the South Korean National Pension Service). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension. The only South Korean payment covered by this agreement is the Old-age Pension. This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and South Korean payments
chunks.text: If you already get the Old-age Pension and move to NZ, contact the South Korean National Pension Service. They'll change the payment if needed. South Korean National Pension Service If you're not already getting a NZ or South Korean payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in South Korea, and - you meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use time you've spent contributing to the Korean National Pension Scheme from age 20 to meet this criteria. To use this time, you must: - have at least 1 year of continuous NZ working age residence, and - be ordinarily resident in NZ. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Who can get Old-age Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get the Old-age Pension while you're living in NZ. You must have contributed to the Korean National Pension Scheme for a certain amount of time to get this payment. You may be able to use periods of working age residence in New Zealand to meet this criteria. The South Korean National Pension Service decides who can get the Old-age Pension. Contact the South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: How to apply for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: Use our Check What You Might Get tool to find out what NZ payments you can get and how to apply. Check What You Might Getexternal You also need to apply for: - any South Korean payment that you may qualify for and - any other overseas payments that you may be able to get.

chunks.title: How to apply for the Old-age Pension
chunks.text: You should apply through the South Korean National Pension Service before you leave South Korea. If you already live in New Zealand, contact our International Services team. They'll send you an application form to complete and you'll need to send it back to them. Then they'll forward that to the South Korean National Pension Service. The South Korean National Pension Service will decide whether you can get the Old-age Pension and let you know. This may take a few months. International Services Contact the South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: NZ Super and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: We'll decide how much you will be paid based on certain criteria. If you get an overseas pension, it's usually deducted from your New Zealand payment. Generally, the amount you're paid is about equal to what you would be paid if you had lived all your life in New Zealand. Overseas Pension

chunks.title: Old-age Pension
chunks.text: The South Korean National Pension Service decides how much you will be paid. Contact the South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: Old-age Pension
chunks.text: Contact the South Korean National Pension Service to find out how this payment is paid. Contact the South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: - You have to pay NZ tax on NZ Super and Veteran's Pension payments. We'll withhold your NZ tax based on the tax code you're using and pay this directly to the NZ tax department, Inland Revenue. - You may have to pay NZ tax on the Old-age Pension. This is regardless of whether it's paid to a bank account in South Korea or NZ. - You may have to pay South Korean tax on the Old-age Pension. For more information, talk to the South Korean tax authority. If the Old-age Pension is liable for tax in South Korea, you may be able to get a rebate on your New Zealand tax. We recommend you discuss your tax liabilities with Inland Revenue (New Zealand). Inland Revenueexternal South Korean National Tax Serviceexternal

chunks.title: Keep copies of your bank records
chunks.text: Make sure you keep copies of all your banking records, as these may show your gross South Korean pension payments required for tax purposes.

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: NZ payments will start from the date of your application or the entitlement date - whichever is later. We'll let you know what date your payment will start in the letter we send you, once your application's approved. The South Korean National Pension Service decides when you get paid the Old-age Pension.

chunks.title: Travelling from NZ to another country (not South Korea)
chunks.text: Before you leave New Zealand you need to contact: - our International Services team - the South Korean National Pension Service, if you get the Old-age Pension. You may keep getting your NZ payment but it depends on: - where you're going - how long you're going for, and - what type of payment you're getting. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call. Talk to the South Korean National Pension Service for information about what will happen to the Old-age Pension. International Services South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Canada - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in Canada and now live in New Zealand, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Canada to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Canadian payments (paid by Service Canada). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability - Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers Canadian payments covered by this agreement are: - Old Age Security Pension - Canada Pension Plan (if you get the Quebec Pension Plan, this is not covered by the agreement). This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in NZ and Canadian creditable periods so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and Canadian payments
chunks.text: If you already get a Canadian payment and move to NZ, contact Service Canada. They'll change the payment if needed. If you're not already getting a NZ or Canadian payment, read the information below. Contact the Government of Canadaexternal

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in Canada, and - you meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Canadian creditable periods to meet this criteria. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: You may be able to get the Supported Living Payment while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in Canada, and - you meet the criteria for Supported Living Payment. You need to have lived in New Zealand for at least 2 years to get Supported Living Payment. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Canadian creditable periods to meet this criteria. Supported Living Payment

chunks.title: Who can get Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers
chunks.text: You may be able to get Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in Canada, and - you meet the criteria for Sole Parent Support Sole Parent Support You need to have lived in New Zealand for at least 2 years to get Sole Parent Support. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Canadian creditable periods to meet this criteria. You can also use your late partner's 'Canadian creditable periods' that they contributed to the Canada Pension Plan. Any overlapping periods can only be counted once.

chunks.title: How to apply for NZ payments
chunks.text: Use our Check What You Might Get tool to find out what NZ payments you can get and how to apply. Check What You Might Getexternal You also need to apply for: - any Canadian payment that you may qualify for and - any other overseas payments that you may be able to get.

chunks.title: How to apply for Canadian payments
chunks.text: You should apply through Service Canada before you leave Canada. If you already live in New Zealand, contact our International Services team. They'll send you an application form to complete and you'll need to send it back to them. Then they'll forward that to Service Canada. Service Canada will decide whether you can get a Canadian payment and let you know. This may take a few months. International Services The Government of Canadaexternal

chunks.title: Have previously worked in Quebec
chunks.text: If you've previously worked in Quebec, you need to apply for the Quebec Pension Plan (if you're not already getting it). You need to apply to the last Canadian province you lived in. If the last province you lived in was: - Quebec, you can get an application form on the Régie de rentes Quebec website. - a Canadian province other than Quebec, contact our International Services team for an application form. International Services You'll need to provide proof of your Canadian residence. These must be original documents. If you don't have original documents, you'll need to apply to Immigration Canada for this information. The Quebec Pension Plan (Retraite Quebec)external Immigration and citizenship (The Government of Canada)external

chunks.title: New Zealand payments
chunks.text: We'll decide how much you will be paid based on certain criteria. If you get an overseas pension, it's usually deducted from your New Zealand payment. Generally, the amount you're paid is about equal to what you would be paid if you had lived all your life in New Zealand. Overseas Pensions

chunks.title: NZ payments
chunks.text: NZ payments are paid into your nominated NZ bank account. NZ Super and Veteran's Pension are paid fortnightly. All other NZ payments are paid weekly.

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: - You have to pay NZ tax on your NZ payments.
